titre: Multimodal rehabilitation for hard flaccid syndrome in a retrospective case series.
titre_fr: Multimodal rehabilitation for hard flaccid syndrome in a retrospective case series.
auteurs: Mendias Christopher L, Awan Tariq M
resume: Hard flaccid syndrome (HFS) is an emerging condition of male sexual dysfunction characterized by a persistent semi-rigid penis in the flaccid state, altered penile sensation, erectile dysfunction, and pelvic or perineal pain. Single-modality treatments have shown limited success, and multimodal protocols have been reported only in single-patient case studies. To describe clinical outcomes associated with completion of an integrative multimodal rehabilitation protocol in a retrospective case series of men with HFS. Thirty-two men with HFS completed a comprehensive protocol combining class IV laser therapy, dry needling, radial pressure wave shockwave therapy, therapeutic ultrasound, biofeedback training, manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, behavioral coaching, and daily oral tadalafil. Patient-reported outcomes were collected at treatment initiation and completion. Erection Hardness Scale (EHS), penile function satisfaction, PROMIS Interest in Sexual Activity, and PROMIS Global Health Physical and Mental Component scores. Median EHS increased from 2 to 4 and median penile satisfaction increased from 2 to 5 (both P < 0.01). All 32 patients achieved EHS ≥3 by treatment end, compared to 8 of 32 (25%) at baseline. PROMIS Interest in Sexual Activity, Global Physical Health, and Global Mental Health scores all improved significantly (P < 0.01). Common comorbid features included low back pain (53%), hip or groin pain (38%), pelvic floor pain (31%), and urinary symptoms (28%). In this retrospective case series, completion of a multimodal rehabilitation program was associated with improvements in erection hardness, penile satisfaction, sexual interest, and global health in men with HFS. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective controlled studies evaluating efficacy, durability, and component-specific effects.

titre: Triboelectric E-Skin Patch Decoding Silent Speech for Advanced Human-Machine Interaction and Augmented Virtual Communication.
titre_fr: Triboelectric E-Skin Patch Decoding Silent Speech for Advanced Human-Machine Interaction and Augmented Virtual Communication.
auteurs: Huo Ziwei, Xu Nuo, Fu Yixuan, Gu Rui, Liu Chao, Wang Zhong Lin, Sun Qijun
resume: Silent speech decoding (lip reading) represents an innovative hands-free communication method for individuals with laryngeal and lingual impairments, addressing critical daily communication challenges. Herein, a novel silent speech decoding system is proposed, which employs a self-powered, low-cost, and conformable triboelectric-based E‑skin patch and a well-trained multi-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) model. We systematically characterize the structural principles and electrical performance of the E-skin patch. A comparative analysis of labial kinematics during vocalized and silent speech is also conducted, which demonstrates strong consistency in time-frequency domain characteristics. The utilized CNN model is trained across 15 lexical categories (200 samples per category), achieving a high accuracy of 98.75% and demonstrating excellent recognition performance. Furthermore, by integrating human-machine interaction (HMI) and virtual reality (VR) technologies, we develop three representative applications, including a real-time lip language visualization system, an orofacial-controlled "Feeding Frenzy" interactive game, and a VR communication platform with avatar dialogue. This technology enables barrier-free communication for voiceless populations, demonstrating significant potential in HMI, augmentative communication systems, virtual reality integration, and biomedical rehabilitation.

titre: Adjunctive Immersive Virtual Reality for Urinary Incontinence-Related Quality of Life in Postmenopausal Women with Urinary Incontinence: A Non-Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial.
titre_fr: Adjunctive Immersive Virtual Reality for Urinary Incontinence-Related Quality of Life in Postmenopausal Women with Urinary Incontinence: A Non-Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial.
auteurs: Kołodyńska Gabriela, Cieślik Błażej, Piątek Aleksandra, Zalewski Maciej, Szczepańska-Gieracha Joanna, Andrzejewski Waldemar
resume: Background/Objectives: This study examined whether adding relaxation-oriented immersive virtual reality (VR) to pelvic floor muscle electrostimulation with electromyographic (EMG) biofeedback was associated with additional improvement in incontinence-related quality of life among postmenopausal women. Methods: In this exploratory non-randomized controlled pilot trial, 40 postmenopausal women received electrostimulation with EMG biofeedback alone (ES; n = 20) or the same intervention preceded by VR (VR + ES; n = 20). Participants completed eight sessions over 2 weeks and were assessed at baseline (T0), post-intervention (T1), and 2-week follow-up (T2); T1 was the prespecified primary assessment. The primary outcome was the Incontinence Quality of Life Questionnaire (I-QOL) total score. Secondary outcomes included pelvic floor EMG, bladder-diary variables, other quality-of-life measures, perceived stress, and self-esteem. Baseline-adjusted linear mixed models were used. The registry record was submitted before enrollment (NCT07070063). Results: Thirty-six participants contributed to the primary analysis. The adjusted between-group difference in I-QOL was -1.65 points at T1 (95% CI, -10.03 to 6.74; p = 0.70) and -4.00 points at T2 (95% CI, -12.38 to 4.39; p = 0.35). Adjusted contrasts were non-significant for the remaining questionnaire and EMG outcomes. Selected bladder-diary outcomes differed between groups, but these analyses were exploratory, unadjusted for multiple comparisons, and did not directly quantify urinary leakage. Conclusions: The study did not detect a statistically significant additional improvement in incontinence-related quality of life with adjunctive VR. Confidence intervals remained compatible with potentially meaningful effects in either direction. Given the small sample and non-randomized design, the findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating.

titre_fr: Rehabilitation in Pediatric Patients with Acute and Subacute Acquired Brain Injury: A Scoping Review on Non-Pharmacological Interventions.
auteurs: Cardile Davide, Marafioti Giulia, Tanner Giuliana, Cappadona Irene, Pagano Maria, Corallo Francesco, Rifici Carmela, Quartarone Angelo, Calabrò Rocco Salvatore
resume: Background: Acquired brain injury in children and adolescents may lead to long-term neurological, cognitive, motor, and behavioral impairments. However, pediatric-specific evidence on rehabilitation strategies remains limited. Objective: This review aimed to summarize current evidence on non-pharmacological neurorehabilitation interventions for children and adolescents with acute/subacute acquired or traumatic brain injury, including a subset of patients with disorders of consciousness. Methods: A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus. Eligible studies investigated non-pharmacological rehabilitation approaches in pediatric or adolescent patients with severe acquired brain injury, traumatic brain injury, stroke, or disorders of consciousness. Data on interventions, outcomes, and main findings were extracted. Results: The reviewed studies included heterogeneous interventions, such as multidisciplinary rehabilitation, constraint-induced movement therapy, virtual-reality-based training, speech therapy, parent-child interaction therapy, sensory stimulation, autonomic monitoring, and neuromodulation. Overall, these approaches were feasible and generally well tolerated, with reported improvements in motor, functional, behavioral, autonomic, and consciousness-related outcomes. Conclusions: Non-pharmacological rehabilitation may support recovery in children and adolescents with severe brain injury, although current evidence remains preliminary and heterogeneous. Further multicenter studies with standardized protocols and outcome measures are needed to guide pediatric-specific rehabilitation practice.

titre: Short-term vestibulo-ocular and postural effects of virtual reality in healthy young adults.
titre_fr: Short-term vestibulo-ocular and postural effects of virtual reality in healthy young adults.
auteurs: Turkoglu Enes, Altin Busra, Aksoy Songul
revue: Journal of vestibular research : equilibrium & orientation
resume: BackgroundVirtual reality can simulate the testing of cognitive, sensory, and motor skills using simulated environments. Eye stabilization is necessary to maintain visual acuity during rapid head movements; this is achieved through mechanisms such as the vestibulo-ocular reflex.ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the short-term effect of a passive, non-interactive virtual reality stimulus on dynamic visual acuity and postural sway in healthy young adults.Methods24 healthy young adults (9 males, 15 females) aged 20-39, with an average age of 26.08 ± 4.14 were included in the study. All participants underwent the Sensory Organization Test (SOT), Static Visual Acuity Test (SVAT), Perception Time Test (PTT), Dynamic Visual Acuity Test (DVAT), Gaze Stabilization Test (GST), and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) to assess symptoms that may arise from virtual reality. These tests were repeated for all participants after the virtual reality experience, and completed on the same day.ResultsStatistically significant differences were obtained in the balance score of the SOT (COMP, mean decrease 2.29 points, 95% CI 0.49-4.10, p = 0.015, Cohen's d = 0.54) and the left-side GST (mean increase 24.7 ms, 95% CI -45.82 to -3.64, p = 0.024, Cohen's d = -0.52) in the pre/post virtual reality experience comparison. Virtual reality had no statistically significant effect on SOT conditions 1-6 individually (all p > 0.05), although CON6 and PTT were borderline (CON6: p = 0.095, r = 0.34; PTT: p = 0.053, r = 0.40). No statistically significant differences were found between pre- and post-treatment in PTT and DVAT (both p > 0.05).ConclusionIt has been demonstrated that a passive, non-interactive virtual reality stimulus may affect balance and gaze stabilization by increasing postural sway over a short, same-day time frame. Clinicians and researchers should be aware of these possible short-term effects when using similar VR-based paradigms for vestibular assessment and rehabilitation.

titre: The value of promoting "Internet Plus" home-based pulmonary rehabilitation for university staff with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
titre_fr: The value of promoting "Internet Plus" home-based pulmonary rehabilitation for university staff with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
auteurs: Wei Jia, Zhang Haijun, Wang Yiwei, Su Qiaoli
resume: Pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) is a non-pharmacological intervention for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). "Internet-Plus" technologies create opportunities for home-delivered PR to overcome barriers of center-based rehabilitation, yet real-world implementation evidence among university staff with COPD remains scarce. This mini review synthesizes six major "Internet-Plus" home-based PR modalities: short message service (SMS)/telephone follow-up, social media platforms, video conferencing telerehabilitation, wearable devices and Internet of things (IoT) systems, smartphone applications and virtual-reality-integrated rehabilitation. Available evidence indicates that telehealth PR yields comparable clinical outcomes to center PR in many studies, though considerable heterogeneity across trials leads to inconsistent conclusions regarding exercise capacity, quality of life and hospitalization endpoints. Notably, no interventional studies have delivered telehealth PR specifically for university staff with COPD. We conceptually propose that university staff with high digital literacy and structured occupational settings, constitute a promising target population for translational research in this domain. The review concludes with a conceptual framework for designing precise, intelligent home PR management within university communities.

titre: Implementing Somalia's National Transformation Plan 2025-2029 for health-system reform: a policy and practice review of governance, financing, and institutional readiness.
titre_fr: Implementing Somalia's National Transformation Plan 2025-2029 for health-system reform: a policy and practice review of governance, financing, and institutional readiness.
auteurs: Osman Nor Haji, Mohamed Dahir Osman, Osman Hamdi Mohamud, Rage Abdifatah Nour, Abdi Abdiweli Mohamed, Iman Mohamed Ismael, Moallim Aweis Ahmed, Jimale Abdirahman Mohamed, Ali Mohamed Ahmed, Dahir Ahmed Ismail, Adam Abdikarim Abdi, Mohamud Abdirahman Ahmed, Dhakane Siham Mohamed, Mohamud Osman Mohamed
resume: Somalia's National Transformation Plan (NTP) 2025-2029 presents an ambitious health-reform agenda centred on maternal and child health, workforce development, health-system strengthening, regulation, financing, digitalisation, and emergency preparedness. The policy challenge is whether the institutional conditions required for implementation can be assembled in a fragile, federal, highly aid-dependent and predominantly mixed-provider health system. This Policy and Practice Review critically examines the implementation readiness of the NTP health chapter and proposes a sequenced framework for converting national commitments into measurable results. A structured narrative review was undertaken from June to July 2026 using peer-reviewed literature, national policy documents, and reports from governmental and international institutions. Evidence was interpreted through the health-policy triangle, the updated Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR), applied prospectively to anticipated determinants, and a health-system resilience lens. The synthesis generated six interdependent proposed readiness foundations: a negotiated federal-state governance compact; a technically validated, costed and sequenced operational plan; sustainable financing and strategic purchasing; workforce and regulatory capacity; integrated information, monitoring and public accountability systems; and shock-responsive adaptive management. Important policy strengths include explicit targets for service coverage, workforce expansion, hospital rehabilitation, regulation and digital health. Key risks include inconsistent or under-specified targets and baselines, uncertain fiscal pathways, weak federal-state role specification, and dependence on external resources and non-state providers. Comparative evidence suggests that contracting and pooled financing can expand services when stewardship, fiduciary safeguards, workforce integration, community accountability and learning systems develop concurrently. We propose a phased 2026-2029 pathway prioritising technical validation, essential-service continuity, subnational compacts, workforce payroll transition, interoperable data systems and annual public performance reviews. The proposed framework is prospective and has not yet been empirically validated; consultation with federal and subnational authorities, providers, partners, civil society and communities is required before formal adoption.

titre: Effectiveness of Gamified Rehabilitation Interventions in Patients with Post-Stroke Dysphagia: A Meta-Analysis.
titre_fr: Effectiveness of Gamified Rehabilitation Interventions in Patients with Post-Stroke Dysphagia: A Meta-Analysis.
auteurs: Cao Yongxin, Liu Xiaohan, Zhao Jing, Zhao Jie, Chang Hong
resume: To evaluate the effects of gamified or multicomponent gamified swallowing rehabilitation on functional oral intake and bedside swallowing function in patients with post-stroke dysphagia, and to explore feedback modality, post-stroke duration, and the robustness of the main findings. This meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, Web of Science, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, CNKI, Wanfang Data, VIP Data, and SinoMed were systematically searched for randomized controlled trials published through December 22, 2025. The Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS) was designated as the primary outcome and the Standardized Swallowing Assessment (SSA) as the secondary outcome. All pooled analyses used random-effects models, with exploratory subgroup analyses and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses. Seven RCTs involving 340 participants were included. Gamified or multicomponent gamified swallowing rehabilitation was associated with higher FOIS scores (MD=1.53, 95% CI: 0.58-2.49, P=0.002), with very high between-study heterogeneity (I<sup>2</sup>=96%). Pooled results from four RCTs showed lower SSA scores after gamified swallowing rehabilitation (MD=- 2.44, 95% CI: - 3.84 to - 1.04, P<0.001; I<sup>2</sup>=54%). The between-subgroup difference for FOIS according to sEMG use was not statistically significant (P=0.39), whereas the SSA subgroup difference was statistically significant (P=0.01). After excluding Hou et al. (2024) in the sensitivity analysis, the direction of the FOIS effect remained unchanged (MD=1.04, 95% CI: 0.46-1.61, P=0.0004; I<sup>2</sup>=85%). Current evidence suggests that gamified swallowing rehabilitation may improve FOIS and SSA outcomes in patients with post-stroke dysphagia. However, the number of included studies and participants was limited, heterogeneity for FOIS was very high, several studies had a high risk of bias, and multiple co-intervention components made the independent effect of gamification difficult to isolate. Findings from the sEMG and post-stroke-duration subgroups should therefore be considered exploratory. Further high-quality studies are needed to optimize intervention strategies and reduce heterogeneity.

titre: Brain-computer interfaces in pediatric populations: research advances, application challenges, and future directions.
titre_fr: Brain-computer interfaces in pediatric populations: research advances, application challenges, and future directions.
auteurs: Wang Shan, Wu Qian, Lei Qiaorong, Li Chunyang, Lei Fenfang
resume: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) establish direct communication pathways between the brain and external devices. Leveraging the unique neuroplasticity of the developing brain, BCIs have emerged as a novel rehabilitative technology for children with neurodevelopmental disorders, including cerebral palsy, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and perinatal brain injury. This review comprehensively examines five major BCI paradigms-P300, motor imagery (MI), steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEP), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), and multimodal hybrid systems-with respect to their pediatric adaptability, technical limitations, and optimization strategies. We summarize the existing evidence across four key clinical applications: augmentative and alternative communication (AAC), motor function rehabilitation, ADHD attention training, and ASD social-emotional intervention. Key intrinsic (cognitive and physiological) and extrinsic (device and environmental) variables affecting BCI performance in children are analyzed, along with general optimization approaches including personalized parameter tuning, pre-training neurofeedback, and lightweight hardware modifications. Furthermore, we examine multilayer barriers to pediatric BCI adoption, including user experience, clinical workforce readiness, translational pathways, and child-specific ethical considerations. Preliminary evidence suggests that non-invasive BCIs can be feasibly used in children above 5 years of age, although this finding is based on short-term studies with small sample sizes and requires further validation through larger longitudinal trials. However, the immature pediatric brain, short attention spans, and low device tolerance preclude direct translation of adult BCI systems. While evidence is more established for AAC and motor rehabilitation in cerebral palsy, large-scale long-term data are still lacking for ADHD and ASD interventions. Future efforts should prioritize child-specific lightweight wearable devices, multicenter longitudinal trials, immersive integration with virtual reality (VR) and social robots, standardized clinical service frameworks, and ethical guidelines for invasive pediatric BCIs, thereby facilitating the transition of BCI technology from laboratory to clinical and home settings and maximizing its value in promoting neurodevelopmental plasticity in children with special needs.

titre: Campagne de vaccination contre la grippe 2026 : le meilleur moyen de se protéger des formes graves
resume: La campagne de vaccination contre la grippe démarre aujourd’hui. Cette année encore, les personnes les plus à risque ont reçu l’invitation de l’Assurance Maladie pour se faire vacciner contre la grippe, avec la recommandation de se faire vacciner également contre le Covid-19. En Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur, 1,5 million de personnes sont considérées comme à risque et sont invitées à se faire vacciner. Pourtant, lors de la précédente campagne, seules 46 % de ces personnes à risque s’étaient fait vacciner dans la région. Une couverture encore insuffisante, alors que l’Organisation mondiale de la santé recommande un objectif de 75 % chez les personnes à risque.

resume: Depuis plus de 30 ans, le Baromètre de Santé publique France est une enquête, unique en son genre, qui permet de mesurer et suivre les comportements, attitudes, opinions et connaissances en lien avec la santé des personnes vivant en France.

titre: Résultats de l’édition 2024 du Baromètre de Santé publique France : mieux connaître et comprendre les comportements, connaissances et opinions de la population en lien avec la santé
resume: Depuis plus de trente ans, le Baromètre de Santé publique France est une enquête, unique en son genre, qui permet de disposer d’informations impossibles à recueillir par ailleurs : comportements individuels, opinions, connaissances, ou encore événements de santé qui ne sont pas collectés par les systèmes de surveillance existants. Désormais actualisés tous les deux ans, les résultats produits éclairent les enjeux de santé publique, enrichissent les connaissances sur l’état de santé et fournissent des informations nécessaires pour guider les politiques de prévention et aider à réduire les inégalités sociales et territoriales de santé.

titre: PLFSS 2027 : le Conseil de la CNSA alerte sur un financement de l’autonomie en retard sur les besoins et un risque de fragilisation de la branche Autonomie
resume: Réuni le 15 octobre en présence de Camille Galliard-Minier, ministre déléguée chargée de l’Autonomie et des personnes handicapées, le Conseil de la CNSA, présidé par Paul Christophe, a appelé à un changement de cap. Son constat est sans appel : les moyens prévus ne sont pas à la hauteur des besoins des personnes âgées, des personnes en situation de handicap, de leurs proches et des professionnels qui les accompagnent. Le Conseil demande des ressources nouvelles pour la branche Autonomie, la mobilisation effective des crédits votés et la suppression du transfert de 300 millions d’euros de CSG aux départements prévu par l’article 13 du projet de loi de financement de la Sécurité sociale.
source: CNSA (Caisse Nationale de Solidarité pour l'Autonomie)

titre: Résidences autonomie : 30 millions d’euros mobilisés en 2026 pour renforcer l’offre dans les territoires
resume: Face au vieillissement de la population et à l’évolution des aspirations des personnes âgées, les résidences autonomie apportent une réponse adaptée en proposant des logements individuels, sécurisés et ouverts sur leur environnement, qui contribuent à prévenir la perte d’autonomie et à lutter contre l’isolement. Pour soutenir la création de nouvelles places, la CNSA et l’Assurance retraite lancent une nouvelle édition de l’Initiative pour le développement des résidences autonomie (IDRA).
source: CNSA (Caisse Nationale de Solidarité pour l'Autonomie)

titre: Intelligence artificielle dans la branche Autonomie : un an après son lancement, 80 % de la feuille de route déjà déployée
resume: Recensement de plus de 100 cas d’usage, expérimentations en MDPH, outillage des médecins évaluateurs en EHPAD, acculturation des équipes… Un an après le lancement de sa feuille de route IA 2025-2026, la CNSA dresse un premier bilan des actions engagées au sein de la branche Autonomie.
source: CNSA (Caisse Nationale de Solidarité pour l'Autonomie)

titre: Digital Interventions for Post-Stroke Rehabilitation: A Scoping Review of Delivery Method, Content, and Outcome.
titre_fr: Interventions numériques pour la réadaptation post-AVC : examen de la portée de la méthode de prestation, du contenu et des résultats.
auteurs: Prasetyo Agus, Pramukti Iqbal, Kurniawan Titis, Emilliano Emilliano
resume: Digital technologies are increasingly used to extend post-stroke rehabilitation and recovery support beyond conventional face-to-face services. However, the evidence remains heterogeneous in delivery, intervention content, and outcomes assessed. To map the delivery method, intervention content, and reported outcomes of digital interventions supporting post-stroke rehabilitation and recovery. This scoping review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Scopus, EBSCOhost, Taylor and Francis Online, and ScienceDirect were searched, with the final search conducted on 26 January 2026, supplemented by manual searches of relevant reference lists. Eligible studies included adults aged ≥18 years post-stroke and digital interventions supporting rehabilitation or recovery. We extracted and analyzed 21 source-verified studies descriptively and narratively. Delivery methods were mapped using a two-dimensional framework. Based on the level of professional interaction, studies were classified as clinician-supported remote rehabilitation (n=8), hybrid or clinician-facilitated digital rehabilitation (n=9), or primarily self-directed or patient-facing interventions (n=4). The technological mechanisms were considered non-mutually exclusive and included digital content or applications, telecommunication, virtual reality or exergaming, wearable or motion-sensing technologies, physiological monitoring, automated feedback or cueing, and remote data monitoring. Intervention content was mapped to motor and mobility exercises, stroke education and self-management, balance and postural training, and task-oriented training or occupational therapy; one study reported remote functional assessment rather than active rehabilitation content (n=1). Reported outcomes were categorized into physical and functional outcomes; emotional, behavioral, and patient-reported outcomes; cognitive and knowledge outcomes; and clinical and health outcomes. Digital post-stroke interventions comprise diverse combinations of professional support, technological mechanisms, rehabilitation content, and outcomes. The evidence is best interpreted as a descriptive map rather than confirmation of effectiveness. Future studies should more clearly specify intervention components, standardize outcome assessment where appropriate, and examine long-term feasibility, accessibility, and scalability.
resume_fr: Les technologies numériques sont de plus en plus utilisées pour étendre le soutien à la réadaptation et au rétablissement après un AVC au-delà des services conventionnels en face à face. Cependant, les preuves restent hétérogènes en ce qui concerne la prestation, le contenu de l'intervention et les résultats évalués. Cartographier la méthode de prestation, le contenu de l'intervention et les résultats rapportés des interventions numériques soutenant la réadaptation et le rétablissement après un AVC. Cet examen de la portée a suivi Arksey et O'Malley framework et PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Scopus, EBSCOhost, Taylor et Francis Online, et ScienceDirect ont été recherchés, avec la recherche finale effectuée le 26 janvier 2026, complétée par des recherches manuelles dans les listes de références pertinentes. Les études éligibles comprenaient des adultes âgés de ≥18 ans après un AVC et des interventions numériques soutenant la réadaptation ou le rétablissement. Nous avons extrait et analysé 21 études vérifiées à la source de manière descriptive et narrative. Méthodes de livraisonont été cartographiés à l'aide d'un cadre bidimensionnel. Sur la base du niveau d'interaction professionnelle, les études ont été classées comme une réadaptation à distance soutenue par le clinicien (n=8), une réadaptation numérique hybride ou facilitée par le clinicien (n=9), ou principalement des interventions autogérées ou orientées vers le patient (n=4). Les mécanismes technologiques ont été considérés comme non exclusifs sur le plan mutuel et comprenaient le contenu ou les applications numériques, les télécommunications, la réalité virtuelle outechnologies exergaming, portables ou de détection de mouvement, surveillance physiologique, rétroaction ou repérage automatisé et surveillance à distance des données. Le contenu de l'intervention a été mappé aux exercices moteurs et de mobilité, à l'éducation et à l'autogestion des AVC, à la formation à l'équilibre et à la posture, à la formation axée sur les tâches ou à l'ergothérapie ; une étude a rapporté une évaluation fonctionnelle à distance plutôt qu'un contenu de réadaptation active (n=1). Les résultats rapportés étaient categoles résultats physiques et fonctionnels ; les résultats émotionnels, comportementaux et rapportés par les patients ; les résultats cognitifs et de connaissances ; et les résultats cliniques et de santé. Les interventions numériques après un AVC comprennent diverses combinaisons de soutien professionnel, de mécanismes technologiques, de contenu de réadaptation et de résultats. Les preuves sont mieux interprétées comme une carte descriptive plutôt que comme une confirmation de l'efficacité. Les études futures devraient clarifier davantagey spécifier les composantes de l'intervention, normaliser l'évaluation des résultats, le cas échéant, et examiner la faisabilité, l'accessibilité et l'évolutivité à long terme.

titre: Cognitive Stimulation in Activities of Daily Living for individuals living with mild-to-moderate dementia (CS-ADL): a feasibility study.
titre_fr: Stimulation cognitive dans les activités de la vie quotidienne pour les personnes atteintes de démence légère à modérée (CS-ADL) : une étude de faisabilité.
auteurs: Ryan Simone, Shiel Agnes, Brady Orla
resume: Cognitive Stimulation in Activities of Daily Living (CS-ADL) is an occupational therapist-led group cognitive stimulation program for people living with mild-to-moderate dementia that aims to enhance functioning of activities of daily living (ADLs). This study investigated the feasibility of CS-ADL and a randomised controlled design comparing the effect of CS-ADL to treatment-as-usual (TAU) on ADL outcomes. This feasibility study used a non-randomiseddesign. Recruitment took place primarily within healthcare settings and supplemented via community outreach, media and voluntary organisations. Due to recruitment challenges, randomisation was not possible and between-group comparisons were not appropriate. ADL functioning, cognition, communication, quality of life (QOL) and neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPS) were assessed at baseline and follow-up. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics. Sixteen participants were enrolled in the study, 12 of which completed follow-up assessments. Recruitment rates differed across intervention sites and affected the feasibility of study design. Thirteen participants were allocated to the intervention group (CS-ADL) and three were allocated to TAU. A reduction in caregiver distress from neuropsychiatric symptoms was observed in the intervention group at follow-up. No meaningful change at follow-up was identified in other secondary outcomes. This is the first study to evaluate the feasibility of a trial comparing CS-ADL to TAU. Several challenges were identified in relation to recruitment, study design and outcome measures that require modification to enhance feasibility and rigour of future trials. Preliminary results indicate CS-ADL may reduce caregiver distress related to neuropsychiatric symptoms. Further research is necessary to confirm these findings.
resume_fr: La stimulation cognitive dans les activités de la vie quotidienne (CS-ADL) est un programme de stimulation cognitive de groupe dirigé par un ergothérapeute pour les personnes atteintes de démence légère à modérée qui vise à améliorer le fonctionnement des activités de la vie quotidienne (ADL). Cette étude a examiné la faisabilité de la CS-ADL et un plan contrôlé randomisé comparant l'effet de la CS-ADL au traitement habituel (TAU) sur les résultats de l'ADL. Cette étude de faisabilité a utilisé un modèle non aléatoiremauvaise conception. Le recrutement a eu lieu principalement dans les établissements de santé et a été complété par la sensibilisation de la communauté, les médias et les organisations bénévoles. En raison des difficultés de recrutement, la randomisation n'a pas été possible et les comparaisons entre les groupes n'ont pas été appropriées. Le fonctionnement ADL, la cognition, la communication, la qualité de vie (QDV) et les symptômes neuropsychiatriques (NPS) ont été évalués à l'inclusion et au suivi. Les données ont été analysées à l'aide de statistiques descriptivescs. Seize participants ont été inscrits à l'étude, dont 12 ont effectué des évaluations de suivi. Les taux de recrutement différaient d'un site d'intervention à l'autre et affectaient la faisabilité de la conception de l'étude. Treize participants ont été affectés au groupe d'intervention (CS-ADL) et trois ont été affectés à TAU. Une réduction de la détresse du soignant due aux symptômes neuropsychiatriques a été observée dans le groupe d'intervention lors du suivi. Aucun changement significatif à suivre-up a été identifié dans d'autres critères de jugement secondaires. Il s'agit de la première étude à évaluer la faisabilité d'un essai comparant CS-ADL à TAU. Plusieurs défis ont été identifiés en ce qui concerne le recrutement, la conception de l'étude et les mesures des résultats qui nécessitent des modifications pour améliorer la faisabilité et la rigueur des futurs essais. Les résultats préliminaires indiquent que le CS-ADL peut réduire la détresse du soignant liée aux symptômes neuropsychiatriques. Des recherches supplémentaires sont nécessaires pour confirmer ces résultats.

titre: Validity and Reliability of the Activity Card Sort 3 in Persons With Thumb Carpometacarpal Osteoarthritis.
titre_fr: Validité et fiabilité de la carte d'activité Trier 3 chez les personnes atteintes d'arthrose carpométacarpienne du pouce.
auteurs: McGee Corey W, Lu Triet, Justen Jagur
revue: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
resume: ImportanceAlthough individuals with thumb carpometacarpal (CMC1) osteoarthritis (OA) commonly experience participation restrictions, participation-focused outcome measures remain underinvestigated, and clinicians primarily rely on assessments of impairments in body structures and functions.ObjectiveTo determine the concurrent validity, test-retest reliability, and precision of the Activity Card Sort 3 (ACS3) in individuals with nonoperative CMC1 OA.DesignSingle-cohort observational psychometric study with repeated measures over a 2-week interval.SettingRemote assessments conducted via videoconferencing.ParticipantsThirty-three adults with radiographically confirmed CMC1 OA completed two virtual assessments approximately 2 weeks apart.Outcomes and MeasuresConcurrent validity was examined by comparing ACS3 domain and total scores with the World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule 2.0 (WHODAS 2.0). Test-retest reliability of the "current," "previous," and "% retained" activities scores was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC<sub>3,1</sub>). Precision was assessed using the standard error of measurement and minimal detectable change.ResultsThe ACS3 demonstrated good concurrent validity through strong associations with conceptually related WHODAS 2.0 domains. "Current" and "% retained" scores demonstrated good-to-excellent test-retest reliability across all domains. "Current" scores consistently showed the highest reliability and precision. "Previous" scores demonstrated lower reliability and greater measurement error, suggesting recall bias. Carrying forward "previous" scores from session 1 to session 2 improved the reliability of "% retained" scores.Conclusions and RelevanceThe ACS3 is a valid and reliable measure of participation for individuals with nonoperative CMC1 OA. The "current" and "% retained" scores may support occupational therapy practitioners in conducting participation-focused assessment of persons with CMC1 OA.
resume_fr: ImportanceBien que les personnes atteintes d'arthrose carpométacarpienne du pouce (CMC1) subissent généralement des restrictions de participation, les mesures de résultats axées sur la participation restent sous-investigées et les cliniciens s'appuient principalement sur des évaluations des déficiences des structures et des fonctions corporelles.ObjectifPour déterminer la validité concurrente, la fiabilité du test-retest et la précision de la carte d'activité Sort 3 (ACS3) chez les personnes atteintes de CMC1 non opératoireOA.DesignEtude psychométrique observationnelle à une seule cohorte avec mesures répétées sur un intervalle de 2 semaines.EtablissementÉvaluations à distance effectuées par vidéoconférence.ParticipantsTrois adultes avec CMC1 OA confirmé par radiographie ont effectué deux évaluations virtuelles à environ 2 semaines d'intervalle.Résultats et mesuresLa validité actuelle a été examinée en comparant les scores du domaine ACS3 et les scores totaux avec l'évaluation de l'incapacité de l'Organisation mondiale de la santé Schedule 2.0 (WHODAS 2.0). La fiabilité test-retest des scores d'activités « courant », « précédent » et « % retenu » a été évaluée à l'aide de coefficients de corrélation intraclasse (ICC<sub>3,1</sub>). La précision a été évaluée à l'aide de l'erreur type de mesure et du changement minimal détectable. Résultats L'ACS3 a démontré une bonne validité concurrente grâce à de fortes associations avec les domaines WHODAS 2.0 conceptuellement liés. "Actuel" et "% retenu" scores démona assuré une fiabilité de test-retest allant de bon à excellent dans tous les domaines. Les scores « actuels » ont toujours montré la plus grande fiabilité et la plus grande précision. Les scores « précédents » ont démontré une fiabilité plus faible et une plus grande erreur de mesure, suggérant un biais de rappel. Le report des scores « précédents » de la session 1 à la session 2 a amélioré la fiabilité des scores « % retenu ».Conclusions et pertinenceL' ACS3 est une mesure valide et fiable de la participation àdividuals avec OA CMC1 non opératoire. Les scores « actuel » et « % retenu » peuvent aider les praticiens de l'ergothérapie à effectuer une évaluation axée sur la participation des personnes atteintes d'arthrose CMC1.
type_etude: Étude psychométrique / de validation (détection par mots-clés, à confirmer)

titre: Experiences and Perceptions of Arab Occupational Therapy Students Regarding Integrating Wheelchair Training into Academia.
titre_fr: Expériences et perceptions des étudiants arabes en ergothérapie concernant l'intégration de la formation en fauteuil roulant dans le milieu universitaire.
auteurs: Sarsak Hassan Izzeddin
revue: Advances in medical education and practice
resume: The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that over 80 million people globally require a wheelchair, yet access to appropriate wheeled mobility devices and skilled service delivery remains severely restricted, particularly in low- and middle-income regions. Academic rehabilitation programs frequently lack structured, evidence-based wheelchair service provision curricula. This study evaluated the implementation, efficacy, and student perceptions of integrating the International Society of Wheelchair Professionals (ISWP)-recognized Wheelchair Training Program (WTP) into Arab occupational therapy (OT) higher education. A mixed-methods study design was conducted across eight Arab countries (total sample size N = 282 undergraduate OT students). Data were analyzed by categorizing participants into three distinct operational groups: Group 1 comprised participants from countries with quantitative pre-post outcome data (Saudi Arabia, Jordan, United Arab Emirates; n = 118), using a 10-point validated test adopted from the ISWP WSTP competency examination; Group 2 comprised participants engaged in Focus Group Discussions (FGDs, n = 96); and Group 3 comprised participants engaged in Semi-Structured Individual Interviews (n = 68). Qualitative investigations (Groups 2 and 3) were conducted between February and May 2025 across Oman, Lebanon, Palestine, Syria, and Morocco. Quantitative evaluation in Group 1 (n = 117 matched pairs) demonstrated a significant baseline knowledge deficit (Pre-test mean = 3.71, standard deviation = 1.26) and substantial post-intervention written knowledge gain (Post-test mean = 7.84, standard deviation = 1.28; mean increase = +4.13 points, t = -36.741, p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 3.40). Significant gains were consistently achieved across Saudi Arabia (4.23 ± 1.32 to 8.09 ± 1.10, p < 0.001), Jordan (2.97 ± 0.92 to 7.36 ± 1.43, p < 0.001), and the United Arab Emirates (3.82 ± 1.09 to 8.05 ± 1.20, p < 0.001). Thematic synthesis of qualitative data from Groups 2 and 3 yielded four core themes: (1) Transformation from theoretical awareness to clinical self-efficacy; (2) Overcoming regional curricular deficits in seating biomechanics and adaptive technology; (3) Culturally responsive rehabilitation and person-first terminology; and (4) Structural barriers to institutional integration and academic sustainability. Integrating a standardized hybrid wheelchair training program into academic OT curricula significantly enhances student theoretical knowledge and self-reported clinical confidence, offering a scalable approach to address educational gaps across the Arab region. Institutionalizing standardized ISWP/WHO-aligned modules within entry-to-practice healthcare degrees is essential to guarantee equitable, high-quality assistive technology service delivery.
resume_fr: L'Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS) estime que plus de 80 millions de personnes dans le monde ont besoin d'un fauteuil roulant, mais l'accès à des appareils de mobilité à roues appropriés et à une prestation de services qualifiée reste sévèrement limité, en particulier dans les régions à revenu faible et intermédiaire. Les programmes de réadaptation académique manquent souvent de programmes de prestation de services en fauteuil roulant structurés et fondés sur des données probantes. Cette étude a évalué la mise en œuvre, l'efficacité et la perception des étudiantsns d'intégrer le programme de formation en fauteuil roulant (WTP)reconnu par la Société internationale des professionnels en fauteuil roulant (ISWP) dans l'enseignement supérieur arabe en ergothérapie (OT). Un plan d'étude à méthodes mixtes a été mené dans huit pays arabes (taille totale de l'échantillon N = 282 étudiants de premier cycle en TO). Les données ont été analysées en catégorisant les participants en trois groupes opérationnels distincts : Le groupe 1 comprenait des participants de pays avec des données quantitativesative pre-post outcome data (Saudi Arabia, Jordan, United Arab Emirates ; n = 118), using a 10-point validated test adopted from the ISWP WSTP competency examination ; Group 2 included participants engaged in Focus Group Discussions (FGDs, n = 96) ; and Group 3 included participants engaged in Semi-Structured Individual Interviews (n = 68). Des enquêtes qualitatives (groupes 2 et 3) ont été menées entre février et mai 2025 à travers Oman,n, la Palestine, la Syrie et le Maroc. L'évaluation quantitative dans le groupe 1 (n = 117 paires appariées) a démontré un déficit significatif de connaissances de base (moyenne avant le test = 3,71, écart type = 1,26) et un gain substantiel de connaissances écrites après l'intervention (moyenne après le test = 7,84, écart type = 1,28 ; augmentation moyenne = +4,13 points, t = -36,741, p < 0,001, d de Cohen = 3,40). Des gains significatifs ont été systématiquement réalisés dans toute l'Arabie saoudite (4,23 ±1,32 à 8,09 ± 1,10, p < 0,001), la Jordanie (2,97 ± 0,92 à 7,36 ± 1,43, p < 0,001) et les Émirats arabes unis (3,82 ± 1,09 à 8,05 ± 1,20, p < 0,001). La synthèse thématique des données qualitatives des groupes 2 et 3 a produit quatre thèmes principaux : (1) Transformation de la conscience théorique à l'auto-efficacité clinique ; (2) Surmonter les déficits scolaires régionaux en biomécanique des sièges et en technologie adaptative ; (3) Réadaptation adaptée à la culture etrson-première terminologie ; et (4) Obstacles structurels à l'intégration institutionnelle et à la durabilité académique. L'intégration d'un programme de formation hybride standardisé en fauteuil roulant dans les programmes académiques OT améliore considérablement les connaissances théoriques des étudiants et la confiance clinique autodéclarée, offrant une approche évolutive pour combler les lacunes éducatives dans la région arabe. Institutionnalisation des modules normalisés alignés ISWP/OMS dans le cadre de l'entrée en bourseles diplômes de soins de santé sur glace sont essentiels pour garantir une prestation de services de technologie d'assistance équitable et de haute qualité.
type_etude: Étude qualitative (détection par mots-clés, à confirmer)

titre: The Wheelchair Use Confidence Scale (WheelCon): Persian translation, adaptation, and validation.
titre_fr: L'échelle de confiance en matière d'utilisation des fauteuils roulants (WheelCon) : traduction, adaptation et validation en persan.
auteurs: Zamiran Sara, Amini Malek, Hamid Benyamin, Pashmdarfard Marzieh, Rushton Paula W
revue: Assistive technology : the official journal of RESNA
resume: This study translated and culturally adapted the Wheelchair Use Confidence Scale for Manual Wheelchair Users (WheelCon-M) and the Wheelchair Use Confidence Scale for Power Wheelchair Users (WheelCon-P) into Persian (Farsi) and examined their reliability and validity. Internal consistency and test-retest reliability were examined. The Persian translated versions of the WheelCon-M (WheelCon-M-P) and the WheelCon-P (WheelCon-P-P) were administered to 40 adult wheelchair users. Cronbach's α was 0.97 for the WheelCon-M-P and 0.98 for the WheelCon-P-P. Both instruments demonstrated high reliability in test-retest assessments, with ICC values of 0.985 for the WheelCon-M-P and 0.981 for the WheelCon-P-P. This study presents early evidence of effective tools for healthcare professionals to assess confidence in wheelchair use among Persian users.
resume_fr: Cette étude a traduit et adapté culturellement l'échelle de confiance en matière d'utilisation des fauteuils roulants pour les utilisateurs manuels de fauteuils roulants (WheelCon-M) et l'échelle de confiance en matière d'utilisation des fauteuils roulants pour les utilisateurs de fauteuils roulants motorisés (WheelCon-P) en persan (farsi) et a examiné leur fiabilité et leur validité. La cohérence interne et la fiabilité test-retest ont été examinées. Les versions traduites en persan du WheelCon-M (WheelCon-M-P) et du WheelCon-P (WheelCon-P-P) ont été administréeso 40 utilisateurs adultes de fauteuils roulants. L'α de Cronbach était de 0,97 pour le WheelCon-M-P et de 0,98 pour le WheelCon-P-P. Les deux instruments ont démontré une grande fiabilité dans les évaluations de test-retest, avec des valeurs ICC de 0,985 pour le WheelCon-M-P et de 0,981 pour le WheelCon-P-P. Cette étude présente les premières preuves d'outils efficaces pour les professionnels de la santé afin d'évaluer la confiance dans l'utilisation du fauteuil roulant chez les utilisateurs persans.
type_etude: Étude psychométrique / de validation (détection par mots-clés, à confirmer)

titre: The therapeutic relationship between occupational therapy practitioners, autistic children, and their caregivers is paramount: caregivers' perspectives and experiences.
titre_fr: La relation thérapeutique entre les praticiens de l'ergothérapie, les enfants autistes et leurs soignants est primordiale : les perspectives et les expériences des soignants.
auteurs: Bernhard Felicia B, Skubik-Peplaski Camille, Dorich Jenny M
resume: Caregivers of autistic children are critical to the therapeutic process. However, gaps exist in our understanding of caregivers' experiences, clinicians' comfort, and clinicians' skill sets when involving caregivers in the therapeutic relationship with their autistic child. This study aimed to explore the caregiver experience within the therapeutic relationship. Eight caregivers of autistic children aged 3-10 years old engaged in individual, semi-structured interviews sharing their experiences working with occupational therapists and their autistic children. Data was analyzed through thematic analysis following a descriptive qualitative approach. Three themes were generated. Caregivers emphasized that the therapeutic relationship, including connection and a sense of belonging, is paramount and precedes any work toward therapy goals. The second theme demonstrates the benefits of a positive therapeutic relationship and the caregiver's active role in the therapeutic process. The final theme outlined the roles and responsibilities of the caregiver and the occupational therapy practitioner within the therapeutic relationship. Occupational therapy practitioners must purposefully establish a therapeutic relationship, including connection and a sense of belonging, to support the therapeutic process with autistic children and their caregivers. Further research is needed to investigate the therapeutic relationship from the perspective of the autistic child.
resume_fr: Les soignants des enfants autistes sont essentiels au processus thérapeutique. Cependant, il existe des lacunes dans notre compréhension des expériences des soignants, du confort des cliniciens et des compétences des cliniciens lorsqu'ils impliquent les soignants dans la relation thérapeutique avec leur enfant autiste. Cette étude visait à explorer l'expérience du soignant au sein de la relation thérapeutique. Huit soignants d'enfants autistes âgés de 3 à 10 ans engagés dans des activités individuelles, semi- entretiens structurés partageant leurs expériences de travail avec les ergothérapeutes et leurs enfants autistes. Les données ont été analysées par analyse thématique selon une approche qualitative descriptive. Trois thèmes ont été générés. Les soignants ont souligné que la relation thérapeutique, y compris la connexion et le sentiment d'appartenance, est primordiale et précède tout travail visant à atteindre les objectifs thérapeutiques. Le deuxième thème démontre les avantages d'une approche positivee relation thérapeutique et le rôle actif du soignant dans le processus thérapeutique. Le thème final a décrit les rôles et les responsabilités du soignant et du praticien de l'ergothérapie au sein de la relation thérapeutique. Les praticiens de l'ergothérapie doivent établir délibérément une relation thérapeutique, y compris un lien et un sentiment d'appartenance, pour soutenir le processus thérapeutique avec les enfants autistes et leurs prochesivers. D'autres recherches sont nécessaires pour étudier la relation thérapeutique du point de vue de l'enfant autiste.
type_etude: Étude qualitative (détection par mots-clés, à confirmer)

titre: Testosterone Replacement Therapy and Associated Outcomes and Management of Trigger Finger.
titre_fr: Thérapie de remplacement de la testostérone et résultats associés et gestion du doigt déclencheur.
auteurs: Henein Carolyn, Liu Timothy P, Hamad Christopher D, Benhaim Prosper, Azari Kodi K, Wessel Lauren E
revue: Journal of hand surgery global online
resume: Testosterone replacement therapy is increasingly common but has been associated with poor treatment outcomes in tendon pathology, although its impact on conditions related to the hand is incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) and rates of operative and nonoperative intervention, repeat intervention, and complications in male patients with trigger finger. We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network (2014-2025). We identified men aged 40-90 years with trigger finger who were exposed to TRT within 6 months before diagnosis. A control cohort without TRT use was generated with 1:1 propensity score matching using age, body mass index, Charlson Comorbidity Index, and additional comorbidities. Outcomes of interest included rates of surgical release, corticosteroid injection, stiffness, postoperative triggering requiring intervention, and occupational therapy referrals. Kaplan-Meier analyses were conducted with hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). After matching, 7,337 patients were included in each cohort. TRT exposure was associated with a higher 2-year rate of A1 pulley release (16.3% vs 12.7%; absolute risk difference [ARD], 3.61%; HR, 1.42; 95% CI, 1.30-1.55; P < .001). Corticosteroid injection was more common in the TRT cohort (22.9% vs 21.5%, ARD 1.45%), although the proportional hazards assumption was not satisfied. Stiffness occurred in 0.4% of the TRT cohort and 0.2% of controls (ARD 0.20%) and was interpreted as exploratory. Rates of occupational therapy referral and postoperative triggering requiring intervention were not significantly different between the 2 groups. TRT exposure was associated with greater treatment utilization among older male patients with trigger finger, notably A1 pulley release. Because patients receiving TRT may have more frequent healthcare contact, these findings may reflect surveillance or treatment-utilization bias rather than a direct effect of TRT on trigger finger severity. TRT status may be a useful contextual factor for patient counseling, although these findings should not be interpreted as evidence that TRT independently alters trigger finger management. Therapeutic III.
resume_fr: La thérapie de remplacement de la testostérone est de plus en plus courante, mais elle a été associée à de mauvais résultats thérapeutiques en pathologie tendineuse, bien que son impact sur les affections liées à la main soit mal compris. Cette étude visait à étudier l'association entre la thérapie de remplacement de la testostérone (TRT) et les taux d'intervention opératoire et non opératoire, d'intervention répétée et de complications chez les patients masculins avec doigt de déclenchement. Nous avons effectuéune étude de cohorte rétrospective utilisant le réseau de recherche TriNetX (2014-2025). Nous avons identifié des hommes âgés de 40 à 90 ans avec un doigt de déclenchement qui ont été exposés à la TRT dans les 6 mois précédant le diagnostic. Une cohorte témoin sans utilisation de TRT a été générée avec une correspondance de score de propension 1:1 en utilisant l'âge, l'indice de masse corporelle, l'indice de comorbidité de Charlson et des comorbidités supplémentaires. Les résultats d'intérêt comprenaient les taux de libération chirurgicale, l'injection de corticostéroïdes, la raideurs, le déclenchement postopératoire nécessitant une intervention et les références en ergothérapie. Les analyses de Kaplan-Meier ont été réalisées avec des hazard ratios (HR) et des intervalles de confiance (IC) à 95 %. Après appariement, 7 337 patients ont été inclus dans chaque cohorte. L'exposition à la TRT était associée à un taux plus élevé de libération de la poulie A1 sur 2 ans (16,3 % contre 12,7 % ; différence de risque absolue [ARD], 3,61 % ; HR, 1,42 ; IC à 95 %, 1,30-1,55 ; P < 0,001). Injection de corticostéroïdes wcomme plus fréquents dans la cohorte TRT (22,9% vs 21,5%, ARD 1,45%), bien que l'hypothèse de risques proportionnels n'ait pas été satisfaite. La raideur est survenue dans 0,4% de la cohorte TRT et 0,2% des contrôles (ARD 0,20%) et a été interprétée comme exploratoire. Les taux de référence en ergothérapie et de déclenchement postopératoire nécessitant une intervention n'étaient pas significativement différents entre les 2 groupes. L'exposition à la TRT a été associée à une plus grande utilisation du traitement aparmi les patients masculins plus âgés avec un doigt de déclenchement, notamment la libération de la poulie A1. Étant donné que les patients recevant une TRT peuvent avoir des contacts médicaux plus fréquents, ces résultats peuvent refléter un biais de surveillance ou d'utilisation du traitement plutôt qu'un effet direct de la TRT sur la gravité du doigt déclencheur. Le statut TRT peut être un facteur contextuel utile pour le conseil aux patients, bien que ces résultats ne doivent pas être interprétés comme une preuve que TRT modifie indépendamment le déclencheur fgestion de l'inger. Thérapeutique III.

titre: Reattach-Informed Integrated Occupational Therapy In Persistent Post-Concussion Syndrome: A Pilot Case Series.
titre_fr: Reattach-Informed Integrated Occupational Therapy In Persistent Post-Concussion Syndrome : A Pilot Case Series.
auteurs: Reitsma Sieto, Mehrad Aida
resume: Persistent post-concussion syndrome (PCS) affects a substantial proportion of individuals after mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI). Persistent symptoms may reflect functional dysregulation - including altered autonomic and sensory processing - rather than irreversible structural damage. This pilot case series explored the feasibility and preliminary outcomes of a ReAttach-informed integrated occupational therapy protocol on symptom severity, perceived stress, and functional participation. Ten adults with post-concussion symptoms persisting more than six weeks post-injury received four 60-minute sessions over four weeks, combining ReAttach with occupational therapy coaching. Outcomes were assessed at baseline (T0), post-treatment (T4, week 4), and follow-up (T12, 12 weeks post-baseline; 8 weeks after treatment completion) using the Rivermead Post-Concussion Symptoms Questionnaire (RPQ-13), the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), and the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM). Data were analysed with the Friedman test; where the omnibus test was significant, Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank post-hoc comparisons were conducted. Kendall's W was reported as the effect size. All measures showed a significant omnibus effect (p < .01), with large effect sizes (Kendall's W = .55-.83). Under the Bonferroni-corrected threshold, symptom severity was significantly reduced at post-treatment and at follow-up, and perceived stress and satisfaction were significantly improved at follow-up; the remaining pairwise comparisons did not survive correction. Satisfaction with daily activities showed a stronger overall effect (W = .83) than performance (W = .55). Post-hoc results are reported separately from the omnibus tests, and pairwise comparisons that did not survive Bonferroni correction are interpreted with caution. These preliminary findings suggest that a ReAttach-informed occupational therapy protocol may be associated with substantial within-participant improvements in persistent PCS. Given the small, uncontrolled sample, the results are exploratory and require confirmation in larger controlled trials. Interpretations regarding autonomic regulation and predictive processing are offered as possible frameworks rather than demonstrated mechanisms, and any cost-related advantages are discussed as potential rather than established.

titre: Experiences of telehealth-delivered occupational performance coaching among Palestinian mothers of autistic children: a qualitative study.
titre_fr: Experiences of telehealth-delivered occupational performance coaching among Palestinian mothers of autistic children: a qualitative study.
auteurs: Salahat Mohammad Hassan, Sarsak Hassan Izzeddin, Al Adam Hatem Ahmad
resume: Families of autistic children in Palestine face substantial barriers to sustained, family-centred rehabilitation, including travel demands, fragmented services, financial pressures, digital inequalities, and recurrent movement restrictions. Occupational Performance Coaching (OPC) is a collaborative, occupation-focused approach that supports caregivers to analyse everyday participation challenges, identify priorities, generate contextually relevant strategies, and evaluate change. This study explored how Palestinian mothers experienced an eight-session OPC telecoaching intervention and how they perceived its acceptability, benefits, challenges, and contextual fit. A qualitative descriptive study was embedded within an explanatory sequential mixed-methods external pilot trial. All 12 mothers who completed OPC participated in a post-intervention semi-structured interview in Arabic via Zoom. The interview guide was informed by the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability (TFA) and included broader questions about intervention processes, perceived change, and contextual experience. Analysis of the complete Arabic interview dataset used reflexive thematic analysis. TFA provided deductive sensitizing concepts, while coding and theme development remained open to meanings arising from participants' accounts. Reflexive notes, cross-case comparison, attention to divergent accounts, peer debriefing, and an audit trail supported analytic reflexivity and transparency. COREQ guided reporting. Five interrelated themes were developed: (1) from receiving advice to becoming a reflective problem-solver; (2) coaching in the context of everyday life; (3) taking responsibility: empowering, but demanding; (4) context-responsive access with conditional digital and cultural fit; and (5) meaningful progress as partial, variable, and still unfolding. Mothers valued collaborative reasoning, individualized goals, and the ability to work within real family routines. Remote delivery reduced some travel, scheduling, cost, and safety burdens, but connectivity, time, caregiving demands, and wider structural conditions remained important constraints. Increased parental responsibility could be experienced as both meaningful and demanding, and perceived changes were not uniform across goals or families. Mothers valued OPC telecoaching not only as a means of remote access, but as a way of working collaboratively on occupational challenges within everyday family life. Telehealth reduced selected access burdens in the Palestinian context but did not remove digital, caregiving, or structural constraints. The findings support further evaluation of culturally and contextually responsive, participation-focused telecoaching within pediatric occupational therapy.

titre: Perception and satisfaction of injured workers toward rehabilitation services: A cross-sectional study.
titre_fr: Perception and satisfaction of injured workers toward rehabilitation services: A cross-sectional study.
auteurs: El-Shboul Omar, Al-Dekah Arwa M, Abuzaid Sajeda, Alnawaiseh Nedal, Jaber Ala'a F, Kanaan Saddam F, Al-Nawafleh Ahmad H, Al-Rawashdeh Israa, Keirallah Khalid A
resume: BackgroundWork-related injuries pose significant physical, psychological, and economic burdens on workers, their families, and society. Rehabilitation and return-to-work (RTW) programs are essential for recovery and reintegration into the workforce. However, little is known about injured workers' perceptions of and satisfaction with rehabilitation services in Jordan.ObjectiveThis study aims to explore and compare the perceptions and satisfaction of injured employees with rehabilitation services offered by the Social Security Corporation (SSC) and evaluate their outcomes of returning to work (RTW).MethodsThis cross-sectional survey evaluated perceptions and outcomes of return-to-work and satisfaction of a random sample of injured employees in Jordan in 2022. Phone interviews were conducted by trained interviewers using a five-part questionnaire on injury and rehabilitation experiences. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and inferential tests, including independent t-tests, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U tests, Kruskal-Wallis tests, and Spearman's rank correlation coefficient.ResultsA total of 400 injured workers were surveyed. The mean age of the respondents was 36.1 ± 10.3 years, with the majority being males (92.5%) and married (70.3%). Less than half (46.8%) received rehabilitative services. The type and cause of injury were strongly correlated with receiving rehabilitation (p < 0.001). The mean perception rating was 3.89 ± 0.49 (out of 5), and the mean satisfaction rating among those who underwent rehabilitation was 4.52 ± 0.53. Perception was significantly higher among higher-income workers and workers who had rehabilitation services. There was a positive correlation between perception and satisfaction (r = 0.328, p < 0.001). In general, 87.5% of those who were injured returned to work.ConclusionMost injured workers successfully returned to work and expressed generally positive perceptions of SSC rehabilitation services. Enhancing awareness among employers and employees about the value and benefits of rehabilitation could further improve understanding, engagement, and utilization of these services among injured workers.

titre: Implementing Mirror Therapy and Mental Imagery for Stroke Inpatient Rehabilitation: Adoption, Acceptability, and Feasibility.
titre_fr: Implementing Mirror Therapy and Mental Imagery for Stroke Inpatient Rehabilitation: Adoption, Acceptability, and Feasibility.
auteurs: Schmidt Jessica, Khoury Elizabeth, Sherburne Gretl, Dittburner Lauren, Rafferty Miriam R, Edelstein Jessica
revue: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
resume: ImportanceMirror therapy and mental imagery (MTMI) are evidence-based interventions for upper extremity motor recovery after stroke, yet they remain underused in clinical practice. Implementation science offers a systematic approach in improving uptake in real-world settings.ObjectiveTo evaluate the changes in clinician acceptability, feasibility, adoption, and patient reach of MTMI over 12 months.DesignProspective, single-site implementation evaluation guided by implementation science frameworks.SettingA free-standing inpatient rehabilitation hospital.ParticipantsOccupational therapists (n = 16) and adult inpatients with stroke or similar neurological conditions.InterventionA therapist-led, 60 min MTMI group was delivered two to three times weekly. Six implementation barriers were identified. Implementation strategies: clinician education, training, support, and infrastructure changes.Outcomes and MeasuresTherapist acceptability and feasibility were measured using the Acceptability of Intervention Measure (AIM) and Feasibility of Intervention Measure (FIM) at baseline, 4 months, and 12 months. Therapist adoption was assessed through training records and self-report. Patient reach was derived from attendance-tracking and hospital-admission data.ResultsAIM and FIM scores remained high across all time points (AIM 4.4-4.8; FIM 4.6-4.8). Adoption increased over time: therapists trained to lead MTMI rose from 11% to 61%, and self-reported MTMI use increased from 63% to 92%. The mean monthly patient reach was 39%.Conclusions and RelevanceMultimodal implementation strategies supported high acceptability, feasibility, and clinician adoption of MTMI in inpatient rehabilitation. Patient reach remained modest.What This Article AddsThis study provides practical, context-specific guidance for integrating MTMI into inpatient rehabilitation.

titre: Expanding the Occupational Therapy Workforce (1987-2001): A Qualitative Historical Study With Implications for the Future.
titre_fr: Expanding the Occupational Therapy Workforce (1987-2001): A Qualitative Historical Study With Implications for the Future.
auteurs: McCarthy Molly, Hogan Andrew J
revue: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
resume: ImportanceDocumenting the origins, activities, and responses to the American Occupational Therapy Association's (AOTA) Multicultural Affairs Program (MAP) provides lessons that can inform future efforts to enhance workforce diversity.ObjectiveDescribe the need for enhancing diversity in the OT workforce during the 1980s and 1990s, articulate AOTA's strategic and programmatic responses to that need, and explore colleagues' perceptions of MAP's work.DesignWe used a qualitative historical design. Primary sources were articles in OT Week (1987-1999) and OT Practice (2000-2001).ResultsThe need for a diverse workforce was related to staffing shortages, enhancing the culture of the profession, and meeting clients' needs. Data informed MAP's initiatives, which addressed recruitment, education, leadership, collaboration, and supporting organizational changes. MAP was discontinued abruptly in 1998 due to financial pressure. Colleagues valued MAP's work, as evidenced by attempts in 1999 to reinstate MAP and a report in 2001 requesting that AOTA develop infrastructure similar to MAP's.Conclusion and RelevanceAOTA's MAP engaged in important data-informed programmatic activities which were valued by colleagues. Given that diversity and inclusion remain important priorities for the profession of OT, future efforts in these areas could build on previously used strategies.ImpactLearning from past endeavors may enhance the sustainability and stakeholder engagement of modern-day efforts to improve workforce diversity and inclusion.

titre: Multidisciplinary implementation of self-directed therapy (My therapy) during inpatient rehabilitation: a RE-AIM evaluation across four allied health disciplines.
titre_fr: Multidisciplinary implementation of self-directed therapy (My therapy) during inpatient rehabilitation: a RE-AIM evaluation across four allied health disciplines.
auteurs: Peiris Casey L, Trussell Celeste, Lu Annie, Loughnan Elika, Devlin Alicia, Dorward Emma, Brusco Natasha K, Langford Jennifer
resume: To evaluate the implementation of the My Therapy program across physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech pathology and music therapy during inpatient rehabilitation, using the RE-AIM framework. A repeated cross-sectional implementation study. Baseline, post-implementation and 6-month sustainability audits were undertaken to determine reach (number of patients with programs and nursing encouragement of program practice), effectiveness (discharge FIM, adverse events), adoption (percentage staff using My Therapy), implementation fidelity (adherence to the four pillars of My Therapy) and maintenance (6 months). Data were collected from patients (n = 278), allied health and nursing staff (n = 61). Chi-squared tests and one-way ANOVA were used to assess change over time. The proportion of patients with occupational therapy and music therapy independent practice programs significantly increased over time (p < 0.001), while speech pathology increased early, and physiotherapy remained stable. Nursing encouragement of independent practice increased significantly (p < 0.001). Most (88%) staff adopted My Therapy, and fidelity to all four My Therapy pillars improved significantly over time (p < 0.05). FIM at discharge did not change (p = 0.681) and no My Therapy-related adverse events were reported. My Therapy was successfully implemented across four allied health disciplines. Broader multidisciplinary implementation enhanced opportunities for independent practice and contributed to holistic rehabilitation.

titre: Stroke Caregiver Education and Training in an Inpatient Sub-Acute Setting: A Retrospective Clinical Audit.
titre_fr: Stroke Caregiver Education and Training in an Inpatient Sub-Acute Setting: A Retrospective Clinical Audit.
auteurs: McCarthy Madelaine, Baker Nicky, Selenitsch Natasha A, den Berg Maayken van
revue: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
resume: Caregiver burden is a significant issue post-stroke. Caregivers demonstrate unmet needs throughout the rehabilitation phase, with limited literature that delves into the details of caregiver education and training (CGET) provision prior to discharge. To identify current practice of multidisciplinary team documentation of CGET following stroke on an inpatient subacute neurosciences ward. A retrospective clinical audit was conducted on 109 stroke admissions on an inpatient subacute neurosciences ward. Documented demographic information, admission and discharge Functional Independence Measure scores, and CGET from the multidisciplinary team were collected using a purpose-built audit tool. Descriptive analysis and sub-group comparison explored the findings against the Stroke Guideline recommendations. Data from 109 records were included, which identified 1398 episodes of CGET. Social work (SW) (79.9%) and occupational therapy (OT) (77.1%) documented CGET more consistently than other disciplines. CGET was significantly more likely to be documented for patients with cognitive impairment, yet only three of 28 (10.7%) individuals with memory impairment had documented CGET relating to memory strategies. Nursing staff documented minimal CGET across all domains, including management of continence. Inconsistent CGET was documented for stroke recovery relating to activities of daily living, mobility and cognition. Variable documentation practices highlighted challenges with interpretation. Further research is needed to determine whether functional limitations of patients are being matched with the appropriate CGET. multidisciplinary team caregiver education and training provision and documentation needs to be consistent, particularly relating to cognition, continence, mobility and activities of daily living.

titre: Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Psychometric Evaluation of the Occupation-Based Practice Measure in Japan.
titre_fr: Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Psychometric Evaluation of the Occupation-Based Practice Measure in Japan.
auteurs: Ohno Kanta, Hirose Takuya, Amano Satoru, Takahashi Kayoko, Kyougoku Makoto, Okita Yuho, Shibahashi Hirotomo, Khayatzadeh-Mahani Mohammad
resume: Occupation-based practice (OBP) is central to occupational therapy, yet its implementation remains inconsistent. This study translated and culturally adapted the OBP Measure into Japanese and evaluated its psychometric properties in 351 occupational therapists. Content validity, structural validity, internal consistency, test-retest reliability, measurement error, and measurement invariance were examined. Content validity was excellent (S-CVI = .97). Confirmatory factor analysis of the revised 33-item model showed mixed fit. Internal consistency was acceptable for four subscales, whereas Interest in OBP showed inadequate internal consistency and relatively weak test-retest reliability. Total-score test-retest reliability was high (ICC = 0.87), with an MDC95 of 1.94. Configural and metric invariance were supported across career stages, whereas scalar invariance was not fully supported. Overall, the OBPM-J showed promising psychometric properties, although its structural validity, Interest in OBP subscale, total-score interpretation, and comparability across career stages require further investigation.

Total-score test-retest reliability was high (ICC = 0.87), with an MDC95 of 1.94. Configural and metric invariance were supported across career stages, whereas scalar invariance was not fully supported. Overall, the OBPM-J showed promising psychometric properties, although its structural validity, Interest in OBP subscale, total-score interpretation, and comparability across career stages require further investigation.

titre: Health Behavior Goals Among Cancer Survivors in an Occupational Therapy Self-Management Program.
titre_fr: Health Behavior Goals Among Cancer Survivors in an Occupational Therapy Self-Management Program.
auteurs: Fukumura Yoko E, Lyons Kathleen D, Sleight Alix G
resume: Adopting health behaviors is critical for cancer survivors. Facilitating goal setting has been identified as an effective support for behavior change, but little is known about granular goal-setting behaviors. Further understanding of individual goal-setting behaviors may help identify individual support needs and further understanding of the impact of personalized intervention for cancer survivors. To describe participant-identified short-term goal-setting behaviors within a 12-week occupational therapy health behavior intervention for cancer survivors. Summative qualitative content analysis was conducted on short-term goals from therapy notes of a pilot study with 20 adult cancer survivors. Thirteen goal categories were identified from 480 short-term goals, with the majority of goals within Physical Activity (26.9%) and Diet (24.2%). Individual differences were noted in both goal-setting frequency and variety of goal content. Results indicate that goal-setting behaviors vary widely across individuals. Further study is needed to examine whether differences correspond with unique support needs.
