titre: Development of a therapist-supervised flexibility and resistance exercise intervention for adults aged 50 years and over with a distal radius fracture in the Wrist Injury Strengthening Exercise (WISE) trial.
titre_fr: Development of a therapist-supervised flexibility and resistance exercise intervention for adults aged 50 years and over with a distal radius fracture in the Wrist Injury Strengthening Exercise (WISE) trial.
auteurs: Sheehan Warren, Lamb Sarah E, Forde Colin P, Srikesavan Cynthia, Nicolson Phillipa J A, Tutton Elizabeth, Gould Jenny, Grant Richard, Achten Juul, Appelbe Duncan, Costa Matthew L, Keene David J
resume: The definitive Wrist Injury Strengthening Exercise (WISE) trial is a multicentre superiority randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating usual care advice plus a therapist-supervised flexibility and resistance exercise intervention versus usual care advice alone for adults aged ≥ 50 years with a distal radius fracture (DRF). This paper describes the development and delivery of the therapist-supervised exercise intervention evaluated in the definitive WISE RCT. The intervention was developed iteratively in accordance with Medical Research Council (MRC) guidance for complex interventions. UK DRF clinical guidelines, published rehabilitation RCTs, UK NHS patient information leaflets, common post-injury impairments, and exercise and behavioural theory were reviewed to inform candidate intervention components. Feedback from UK therapists and patient and public involvement partners then informed the design of the initial intervention. Two methods of intervention delivery were then evaluated in a multicentre feasibility RCT and embedded qualitative study involving 117 participants aged ≥ 50 years with a distal radius fracture. Review of guidelines and previous research highlighted uncertainty regarding the optimal rehabilitation after DRF and limited reporting of progressive exercise interventions. NHS patient information leaflets largely focused on flexibility exercises and self-management advice. Therapist and patient feedback informed the intervention content, progression, and participant materials. Findings from the feasibility RCT and embedded qualitative study supported a therapist-supervised delivery model with three sessions, rather than a single-session independent exercise approach. The final intervention comprised usual care advice plus up to three one-to-one sessions with a physiotherapist or occupational therapist over 12 weeks. Participants also received a workbook containing self-management advice, progressive flexibility and resistance exercises with resistance bands and therapeutic putty, and behaviour change strategies to support exercise adherence. Using an iterative MRC-informed process, a therapist-supervised rehabilitation intervention was developed and refined prior to definitive evaluation. Transparent reporting of intervention development and content should support interpretation, replication, and implementation.

titre: Associations of Combined Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation and Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation With Psychological and Functional Outcomes After Stroke: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
titre_fr: Associations of Combined Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation and Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation With Psychological and Functional Outcomes After Stroke: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
auteurs: Wu Yuehao, Shen Yusha, Huang Meng
resume: To examine whether combined transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), delivered with standard rehabilitation, was associated with post-stroke depression and anxiety symptoms and secondary neurological and motor outcomes. This retrospective cohort study included 180 patients classified according to treatment received in routine clinical practice: combined TMS + tDCS + standard rehabilitation (n = 60), standard rehabilitation alone (n = 60), TMS + standard rehabilitation (n = 30), or tDCS + standard rehabilitation (n = 30). Treatment selection reflected physician recommendations and patient preference. Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7-item scale (GAD-7) scores were primary outcomes; National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), modified Rankin Scale (mRS), and Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA) scores were secondary outcomes. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, 4 weeks, and 8 weeks. Generalized estimating equations adjusted for prespecified measured covariates assessed group, time, and group × time associations. Dunnett-adjusted comparisons used standard rehabilitation as the reference. No statistically significant differences were detected in the measured baseline characteristics (all p > 0.05). At 8 weeks, the combined group had lower median BDI scores [8.0 (6.0, 10.0) vs. 14.5 (11.5, 17.0)] and GAD-7 scores [6.0 (4.0, 8.0) vs. 9.0 (7.0, 11.0)] than the Standard Rehabilitation Group (both Dunnett-adjusted p < 0.001). Significant group × time associations were identified for BDI, GAD-7, NIHSS, mRS, and FMA outcomes (all p < 0.05). The combined group also had lower NIHSS and mRS scores and higher FMA scores than the standard rehabilitation group at 4 and 8 weeks. No severe adverse events were documented. Total recorded adverse-event rates were 8.3%, 5.0%, 3.3%, and 3.3% across the four groups, respectively, with no significant between-group difference (Fisher's exact p = 0.584). In this retrospective cohort, combined TMS and tDCS with standard rehabilitation was associated with lower depression and anxiety symptom scores and more favorable neurological and motor outcome trajectories than standard rehabilitation. Non-random treatment allocation and residual confounding preclude causal interpretation; prospective randomized studies are required.

titre: Patient-Perceived Adaptation to the Prosthesis and Social Participation After Prosthodontic Rehabilitation: Associations With Chewing Function and Oral Health-Related Quality of Life.
titre_fr: Patient-Perceived Adaptation to the Prosthesis and Social Participation After Prosthodontic Rehabilitation: Associations With Chewing Function and Oral Health-Related Quality of Life.
auteurs: Hassanein Fatma E A, Alzahrani Khaled M, Binrayes Abdulaziz, Alqahtani Abdulaziz S, Alsahhaf Abdulaziz, Alzaid Abdulaziz A, Binalrimal Sultan, Ahmed Yousra
resume: Patient-perceived adaptation to the prosthesis may provide information about rehabilitation outcomes beyond conventional prosthodontic assessment. Its relationships with oral function, oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) and social participation remain insufficiently understood. To examine the association between patient-perceived adaptation to the prosthesis and social participation and characterize indirect associations involving chewing difficulty and OHRQoL. This cross-sectional study included 300 adults receiving prosthodontic rehabilitation. Patient-perceived adaptation to the prosthesis was assessed using a study-specific 0-100 composite score comprising equally weighted ratings of comfort, speech, aesthetics and stability. Chewing difficulty, OHRQoL and social participation were assessed using standardized patient-reported measures. A recursive path model was adjusted for age, sex, prosthesis type, duration of prosthesis use and remaining natural teeth. Direct and indirect associations were estimated using 5000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples. Higher patient-perceived adaptation to the prosthesis was associated with lower chewing difficulty (β = -0.719, p < 0.001) and greater social participation (β = 0.283, p < 0.001). The total association with social participation was β = 0.649 (95% BC CI, 0.522-0.748), with a total indirect association of β = 0.366 (95% BC CI, 0.266-0.474), representing 56.4% of the total association. The serial indirect association through lower chewing difficulty followed by better OHRQoL was β = 0.199 (95% BC CI, 0.140-0.276; p < 0.001). Higher patient-perceived adaptation to the prosthesis was associated with greater social participation and better perceived chewing function and OHRQoL. These findings support incorporating patient-reported adaptation, oral function and OHRQoL into patient-centred prosthetic rehabilitation assessment. Indirect associations should not be interpreted causally.

titre: Point-of-Care Computer Vision for Postural Assessment in Brain Injury Rehabilitation.
titre_fr: Point-of-Care Computer Vision for Postural Assessment in Brain Injury Rehabilitation.
auteurs: Kirkby Elise, Burke Helen, Cline Stephanie, Karimpour Rana, Piyasena Arun, Travitz Karla, Kinney Stephen, Whitlock Annie, Evans Nicholas, Willingham T Bradley
revue: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
resume: To develop and preliminarily evaluate a clinician-led, computer vision (CV)-based system for point-of-care postural assessment in people with acquired brain injury (ABI) undergoing inpatient rehabilitation. Cross-sectional and longitudinal observational study incorporating clinician-led co-innovation, usability testing, feasibility assessment, clinical utility analysis, and analytical validation against three-dimensional motion capture. Tertiary inpatient neurorehabilitation hospital. Rehabilitation clinicians (n=10), individuals with ABI (n=20; 60% female; age 45.0 ± 17.7 years), and neurologically intact controls (n=12). Occupational therapists, physical therapists, engineers, and rehabilitation scientists co-developed a markerless CV workflow for seated and standing postural assessment. Usability, feasibility, therapy-related change, analytical validity, and associations with clinician-reported measures were evaluated. Clinicians reported excellent usability (System Usability Scale: 85.3 ± 12.3). All participants with ABI completed testing without adverse events, and all posture metrics were successfully acquired. During inpatient neurorehabilitation, seated cervical lateral flexion (β = -0.084°/day, 95% CI: -0.163 to -0.005, p = 0.037) and standing trunk lateral flexion (β = -0.096°/day, 95% CI: -0.152 to -0.040, p = 0.0008) decreased significantly over time, indicating improvements in postural alignment. CV metrics correlated with clinician-rated postural abnormalities, including unsupported sitting trunk displacement (ρ = 0.531, p = 0.023), pelvic displacement (ρ = 0.501, p = 0.034), and head/neck displacement (ρ = 0.482, p = 0.043). Agreement with motion capture was strong for cervical and trunk lateral flexion (ICC[A,1] = 0.83 for both). Clinician-led co-innovation produced a usable, feasible, and clinically meaningful CV tool that captured therapy-related postural change and aligned with clinician-reported impairments in ABI.

titre: Clinical Heterogeneity in Response to Exercise-Based Musculoskeletal Rehabilitation: A Critical Narrative Review and Staged Clinical Response Framework.
titre_fr: Clinical Heterogeneity in Response to Exercise-Based Musculoskeletal Rehabilitation: A Critical Narrative Review and Staged Clinical Response Framework.
auteurs: Shankar Ganesh G
revue: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
resume: Exercise produces a modest average benefit in musculoskeletal rehabilitation that varies by condition, comparator, and outcome, but this average conceals considerable clinical heterogeneity in baseline presentation, magnitude and direction of change, trajectory, and which outcomes improve. Evidence on this variation is dispersed across pain science, exercise physiology, psychology, and rehabilitation research, and is often translated prematurely into treatment-matching recommendations before the underlying evidence has been shown to modify treatment effect rather than simply predict outcome. To clarify the meaning and measurement of heterogeneous clinical response to exercise-based musculoskeletal rehabilitation, synthesise patient-related, intervention-related, and contextual determinants of response variation, distinguish prognostic factors from true treatment-effect modifiers, and propose a staged framework for evaluating apparent non-response. Critical narrative review; no protocol was registered. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception through 30 June 2026. Of 2675 unique records identified after deduplication, 229 were considered in full text and 60 were included, comprising direct and indirect evidence together with conceptual or methodological sources. Screening and selection were undertaken by a single author, disclosed as a limitation. Four overlapping forms of clinical heterogeneity are distinguished. Apparent non-response is frequently attributable to measurement artefact, incomplete treatment exposure, or a mismatch between the intervention and the patient's principal limitation rather than a fixed inability to benefit. Across seven candidate domains of determinants, most evidence is associative, prognostic, mechanistic, or indirect rather than confirmatory of validated treatment-by-characteristic interactions. A five-stage clinical response framework is proposed, linking baseline characterization, treatment-target specification, documented exposure, trajectory evaluation, and adaptation. Clinical heterogeneity in exercise-based musculoskeletal rehabilitation is multidimensional and explained mainly by prognostic, mechanistic, or contextual factors rather than confirmed treatment-effect modifiers. The proposed staged framework offers a testable, evidence-informed approach to evaluating apparent non-response, pending prospective validation.

titre: Longitudinal Recovery Trajectories of Instrumental Activities of Daily Living and Social Participation after Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Prospective Study.
titre_fr: Longitudinal Recovery Trajectories of Instrumental Activities of Daily Living and Social Participation after Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Prospective Study.
auteurs: Asai Koki, Iwata Kentaro, Sakimoto Fumio, Oba Jumpei, Shimomura Yoshimitsu
resume: As survival after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) continues to improve, supporting long-term functional recovery and successful community reintegration has become a key clinical priority. Prior survivorship research has largely emphasized physiological outcomes, including muscle strength and exercise tolerance, or global health-related quality of life (QOL). Nonetheless, these measures may not fully capture survivors' ability to manage complex daily activities or resume meaningful social roles in real-world settings. This study aimed to investigate the longitudinal trajectories of instrumental activities of daily living (IADL) and social participation during the 48 weeks after discharge in patients undergoing HSCT. We also explored potential differences in these trajectories by transplant type. This prospective observational study enrolled 61 patients undergoing HSCT, including 37 allogeneic recipients (median age, 56.0 years; 25/37 [67.6%] male) and 24 autologous recipients (median age, 63.0 years; 18/24 [75.0%] male). The primary outcome was IADL and social participation measured using the Frenchay Activities Index (FAI). Secondary outcomes included anxiety and depression symptoms, assessed using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale; fatigue, assessed using the Cancer Fatigue Scale (CFS); and quality of life, measured using the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30 (EORTC QLQ-C30). Longitudinal changes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. A significant main effect of time was observed for FAI scores (p < 0.001), whereas transplant type (p = 0.443) and the time × transplant type interaction (p = 0.342) were not significant. In the allogeneic group, FAI scores decreased from 19.0 (13.0-28.0) at baseline to 13.0 (10.0-20.0) at 4 weeks after discharge, then improved to 26.0 (21.0-29.0) at 48 weeks. In the autologous group, FAI scores exhibited more modest changes over time, from 19.5 (8.8-24.5) at baseline to 16.0 (8.0-23.0) at 4 weeks and 19.5 (15.8-30.5) at 48 weeks. Post hoc analyses demonstrated that FAI scores at 12, 24, and 48 weeks were significantly higher than those at 4 weeks (p < 0.01). For the secondary outcomes, QOL (EORTC QLQ-C30) also showed significant improvement over time, whereas fatigue (CFS) showed no comparable improvement over time. IADL and social participation declined early after discharge and subsequently improved over 48 weeks after HSCT. Recovery trajectories appeared broadly similar between allogeneic and autologous recipients; however, the modest sample size and attrition over follow-up limit conclusions regarding transplant-type differences. Repeated assessment may help identify delayed functional recovery and inform survivorship care and rehabilitation planning. These findings should be confirmed in larger multicenter studies.

titre: Trunk Acceleration and Lower-limb Kinematics after Cerebellar Stroke: Associations with Walking Speed and Clinical Ataxia Severity.
titre_fr: Trunk Acceleration and Lower-limb Kinematics after Cerebellar Stroke: Associations with Walking Speed and Clinical Ataxia Severity.
auteurs: Yamasaki Yuichiro, Mizuta Naomichi, Ohnishi Sora, Kai Takumi, Sato Hirofumi, Okuma Katsunobu, Kobayashi Yohei, Takaishi Shinjiro, Maruki Hideyuki, Morioka Shu
resume: The relationship between gait characteristics and clinical ataxia severity, after accounting for walking speed, remains insufficiently characterized following cerebellar stroke. We examined direction-specific trunk acceleration and lower-limb kinematics during comfortable walking. This multicenter cross-sectional study included 55 patients with subacute cerebellar stroke and 56 healthy controls. Inertial measurements quantified lower-limb kinematics, trunk acceleration root mean square (RMS; without speed normalization), and sample entropy (SampEn). Analyses included group-by-speed models, speed-matched one-dimensional statistical parametric mapping, and exploratory patient-only, speed-adjusted regressions and partial Spearman correlations with the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA). Patients walked more slowly, with lower anteroposterior and mediolateral RMS but higher anteroposterior and vertical SampEn. After speed adjustment, each five-point higher SARA score was associated with smaller peak limb flexion (- 1.01°; 95% confidence interval, - 1.99 to - 0.02) and less-negative extension (+ 1.21°; 0.08 to 2.34), both with Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted P = 0.045. None of the six full-cohort group-by-speed interactions met the adjusted significance criterion. In speed-matched comparisons (11 per group), significant waveform differences were confined to limb angles near the beginning and end of the gait cycle. In speed-adjusted rank analyses, vertical RMS correlated with SARA (partial ρ = 0.471) and limb angles, but the original-scale linear SARA coefficient remained uncertain. Vertical SampEn showed no clear association with SARA or limb kinematics. Higher ataxia severity was associated with smaller whole-limb excursions in speed-adjusted models. These exploratory findings support interpreting trunk acceleration magnitude and regularity alongside whole-limb movement and clinical severity.

After speed adjustment, each five-point higher SARA score was associated with smaller peak limb flexion (- 1.01°; 95% confidence interval, - 1.99 to - 0.02) and less-negative extension (+ 1.21°; 0.08 to 2.34), both with Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted P = 0.045. None of the six full-cohort group-by-speed interactions met the adjusted significance criterion. In speed-matched comparisons (11 per group), significant waveform differences were confined to limb angles near the beginning and end of the gait cycle. In speed-adjusted rank analyses, vertical RMS correlated with SARA (partial ρ = 0.471) and limb angles, but the original-scale linear SARA coefficient remained uncertain. Vertical SampEn showed no clear association with SARA or limb kinematics. Higher ataxia severity was associated with smaller whole-limb excursions in speed-adjusted models. These exploratory findings support interpreting trunk acceleration magnitude and regularity alongside whole-limb movement and clinical severity.

titre: Measurement properties of observational gait analysis tools in neurological disorders: a COSMIN meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Measurement properties of observational gait analysis tools in neurological disorders: a COSMIN meta-analysis.
auteurs: Etoom Mohammad, Almomani Saja, Bakhsh Hadeel R, Alwardat Mohammad, Manocchio Nicola, Geroin Christian, Elabd Omar M, Jahan Alhadi M, Lena Francesco, Abdullahi Auwal, Hawamdeh Ziad, Foti Calogero
resume: To investigate measurement properties of Observational gait analysis (OGA) tools among neurological populations. PRISMA-COSMIN guidelines were followed. Articles included measurement properties studies for OGA tools in neurologic populations were included. Studies were rated as sufficient, insufficient, or indeterminate. Results were synthesized by the population and OGA tool. Twenty-eight included articles performed 63 studies for 7 OGA tools that were synthesized in 42 results in stroke, multiple sclerosis and Parkison's disease. The Wisconsin Gait Scale (WGS), and Gait Assessment and Intervention tool (G.A.I.T) in stroke have been studied for all properties except measurement invariance, and all of them were sufficient except measurement error. Other OGA tools were tested in limited studies. All included tools have potential for recommendation; however, none was fully recommended for use. WGS and G.A.I.T in stroke have the best potential for recommendation. They can be used at only group-level or cross-sectional analysis due to their large measurement error. Standardized observation methods and measurement invariance studies should be prioritized. Both WGS and G.A.I.T measure gait deviations through 14 and 31 items respectively, WGS provides more feasible assessment while G.A.I.T provides more detailed biomechanical analysis.

titre: Assessment of fourth-year medical students' knowledge of post-acute care rehabilitation discharge options following a physical medicine and rehabilitation clerkship educational program.
titre_fr: Assessment of fourth-year medical students' knowledge of post-acute care rehabilitation discharge options following a physical medicine and rehabilitation clerkship educational program.
auteurs: Zhou Elaine, Engel-Haber Einat, Snider Brittany, Kirshblum Steven
revue: PM & R : the journal of injury, function, and rehabilitation
resume: Post-acute care (PAC) plays an increasingly critical role in the health care system due to an aging population, shorter hospital stays, and the complex needs of patients. However, studies show that medical students often lack essential knowledge of PAC options, which may compromise safe care transitions. In the United States, medical education provides limited training on PAC and the rehabilitation requirements associated with these settings. To assess fourth-year medical students' knowledge of and confidence in PAC options following a targeted educational program delivered within a physical medicine and rehabilitation (PM&R) clerkship. Pre- and postintervention surveys. A single institution U.S. allopathic medical school. Fourth-year medical students enrolled in the mandatory PM&R clerkship between January and May 2025. Of 104 eligible students, 53 completed both surveys and were included in the analysis. The mandatory 2-week PM&R clerkship included a didactic lecture that (1) reviewed admission and rehabilitation eligibility criteria for each PAC setting based on Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services guidelines; (2) highlighted differences in physician oversight, nursing care, and average length of stay; and (3) applied concepts through patient case scenarios. The change from medical students' baseline to postclerkship knowledge of and confidence in PAC options. Students showed statistically significant improvements in both knowledge of PAC eligibility criteria (p < .001) and self-reported confidence in PAC discharge planning (p < .001). A structured educational module on PAC in addition to clinical experiences in a mandatory PM&R clerkship was associated with improved medical students' knowledge and confidence in PAC discharge planning. These findings support incorporating PAC education into medical school curricula, particularly within PM&R rotations, to better prepare future physicians for the complexities of care transitions.

titre: Design of an adaptive lower limb rehabilitation system with virtual reality and multimodal biosignals.
titre_fr: Design of an adaptive lower limb rehabilitation system with virtual reality and multimodal biosignals.
auteurs: Kuang Xujia, Yin Zhiqiang, Wang Xiao, Ouyang Hongda
resume: To develop and evaluate a virtual-reality-enhanced lower-limb rehabilitation framework that combines EEG-based motor-intention detection, robotic gait assistance, trunk-motion assessment, and lumbar surface electromyography to support multimodal assessment, interactive training, and therapist-oriented performance monitoring. Nine healthy participants completed VR-enhanced EEG motor-imagery training, open-loop calibration, closed-loop exoskeleton-triggering, trunk-attitude assessment, and lumbar-sEMG evaluation in separate experimental sessions. A four-degree-of-freedom hip-knee exoskeleton was integrated with participant-specific CDF threshold calibration, treadmill synchronization, VR rehabilitation tasks, attitude sensing, and RMS/MPF analysis. Participant identity was consistent across modalities, although the signals were not acquired simultaneously. The seated VR motor-imagery condition produced the highest open-loop command accuracy of 75.35 ± 4.21 %. Mean closed-loop gait-triggering accuracy was 76.7 ± 10.0 %, ranging from 60 % to 90 %. Mean trunk-movement magnitudes were 30.8°, 30.7°, 91.3°, and 31.0° for left lateral flexion, right lateral flexion, forward flexion, and backward extension, respectively. System prompting increased mean RMS from 0.094759 to 0.103330 mV and reduced mean MPF from 111.2023 to 103.0729 Hz. The findings support the feasibility of integrating intention-driven exoskeleton control, VR interaction, postural assessment, and muscular-response monitoring within a unified rehabilitation framework for adaptive, multimodal rehabilitation.

titre: Within-Patient, Evaluator-Blinded, Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial to Assess the Efficacy of Microneedling for the Treatment of Hypertrophic Scars in Adult Burn Survivors.
titre_fr: Within-Patient, Evaluator-Blinded, Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial to Assess the Efficacy of Microneedling for the Treatment of Hypertrophic Scars in Adult Burn Survivors.
auteurs: Nedelec Bernadette, Marois-Pagé Elisabeth, Edger-Lacoursière Zoë, Sawicki Jakub, Calva Valérie, Schneider Geneviève, Malo-Leclerc Ingrid, Correa Maxime A, Correa José A
resume: Microneedling is a promising treatment for hypertrophic scars (HSc); however, documentation of its effects remains limited. The purpose of this study was to objectively quantify scar changes and patient-reported outcomes following microneedling compared with within-patient matched control scars. Thirty-six adult burn survivors with two similar HSc and who completed the study received five microneedling treatments at six-week intervals in addition to usual care on a randomly assigned HSc. The matched scar received usual care alone. Objective outcomes (elasticity, erythema, melanin, thickness, and transepidermal water loss (TEWL)) were assessed at baseline and at 6 and 12 weeks post-treatment. Participant perception was evaluated using the Patient Scar Assessment Scale at baseline and at 6 weeks post-treatment. Within-scar comparisons at both post-treatment time points demonstrated significant reduction of erythema and TEWL in treated scars and improvement of elasticity and thickness for both scars. Linear mixed-effects models adjusting for baseline values revealed a significant between-group difference favoring the control scar at 6 weeks only for elasticity and the microneedling for erythema and TEWL at 12 weeks. Patient-reported improvements in color, stiffness and thickness were observed for both scars. A significant between-group difference was observed solely for overall scar opinion. Microneedling may enhance specific aspects of scar maturation and improve overall scar opinion.

titre: Parenteral Nutrition as a Strategic Therapeutic Option for Onco-Geriatric Rehabilitation After Total Gastrectomy and Anastomotic Stenosis Complicated by an Aorto-Esophageal Fistula: A Case Report.
titre_fr: Parenteral Nutrition as a Strategic Therapeutic Option for Onco-Geriatric Rehabilitation After Total Gastrectomy and Anastomotic Stenosis Complicated by an Aorto-Esophageal Fistula: A Case Report.
auteurs: Belaid Houssam Eddine, De Carvalho João Gabriel, Gagliano Mariangela
resume: Background and Clinical Significance: The nutritional management of onco-geriatric patients after a total gastrectomy remains a challenge, especially in the context of postoperative complications, such as stenosis of the esophagojejunal anastomosis, and in the presence of an aorto-esophageal fistula. Parenteral nutrition is a relevant therapeutic option to maintain nutritional support and enable rehabilitation when oral and enteral feeding are no longer feasible in this specific clinical context; Case Presentation: We report here the case of a 76-year-old patient who underwent a total gastrectomy for gastric adenocarcinoma with several dilated and stented esophagojejunal anastomoses. During the first postoperative year, the nutritional adaptation facilitated rehabilitation and helped him recover well. However, the occurrence of an aorto-esophageal fistula and its treatment with thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) made oral and enteral feeding impossible. This was associated with persistent asthenia, physical deconditioning, sarcopenia, weight loss, exercise intolerance, and increased dependence for activities of daily living. Although parenteral nutrition allowed for nutritional stability and the beginning of rehabilitation, a suspected nosocomial infection involving the aortic endograft led to his death before his treatment was complete; Conclusions: This case highlights the relevance of parenteral nutrition as a therapeutic option to continue rehabilitation when enteral access is judged unacceptably risky. However, the risk of infectious complications in the context of malnutrition can compromise the prognosis, and any suspicion of infection involving prosthetic material should be documented microbiologically as completely as possible whenever compatible with the patient's care objectives. Onco-geriatric assessment to manage older patients with esophagogastric cancer is recommended.

titre: Adjunctive Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma Activated with Autologous Thrombin Serum for a Refractory Below-Knee Amputation Stump Wound: A Case Report.
titre_fr: Adjunctive Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma Activated with Autologous Thrombin Serum for a Refractory Below-Knee Amputation Stump Wound: A Case Report.
auteurs: Shara Khansa, AlAjmi Hasan, Baatiah Nada, Darag Sara, Bakhamis Renad, Abdelhakim Amr
resume: Background and Clinical Significance: Refractory below-knee amputation (BKA) stump wounds can delay prosthetic rehabilitation. This report describes wound healing during multimodal care that included autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) activated with autologous thrombin serum (ATS); Case Presentation: A 33-year-old man with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease and a persistent right BKA stump wound after surgical revisions underwent three PRP-ATS applications on 16 and 23 February and 8 March 2026. Collagen dressings were applied on 2 and 15 March, and compression was continued thereafter. The estimated wound volume decreased from 14.18 cm3 at baseline to 0.48 cm3 at week 3 (approximately 97%); advanced epithelialization was observed at week 4. Complete closure was documented on 16 April 2026, approximately eight weeks after treatment began. No treatment-related adverse events were reported. After closure, the patient was referred for prosthetic rehabilitation assessment; fitting and functional use were not documented; Conclusions: Healing was temporally associated with PRP-ATS as part of a multimodal treatment course. This single case supports the feasibility of the approach but cannot establish the independent efficacy of PRP-ATS.

titre: Walking Distance and Interlimb Gait Differences Across 51 kg of Weight Loss After Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Three-Session Wearable Sensor Case Report.
titre_fr: Walking Distance and Interlimb Gait Differences Across 51 kg of Weight Loss After Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Three-Session Wearable Sensor Case Report.
auteurs: Trindade Andrei Machado Viegas da, Rezende Leonardo Pinheiro, Junior Junichiro Sado, Resende Marcos Henrique Alves, Oliveira Claudia Santos
resume: Background and Clinical Significance: Longitudinal observations that combine major postoperative weight loss with limb-specific gait assessment after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) are uncommon. This case report describes three single-trial instrumented assessments in one patient and is intended as a descriptive observation; it does not establish causality, measurement stability, mechanical loading, or a clinically meaningful persistent deficit; Case Presentation: A man in his early sixties at the first assessment had undergone left TKA for end-stage osteoarthritis and subsequently underwent Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Three assessments were available from approximately 31 to 67 months after TKA. Body mass was 120, 88, and 69 kg (body mass index 43.03, 31.55, and 24.74 kg/m2), while two-minute walk distance (2MWT) was 67.8, 105.1, and 118.1 m. The third walk test was launched in the software's six-minute module and stopped at 1 min 58 s, so 118.1 m is the distance accumulated over 118 s and was neither adjusted nor extrapolated to 120 s. The operated limb showed longer stance duration than the non-operated limb by 3.04, 5.28, and 2.05 percentage points, and a proprietary propulsion index was lower on the operated side by 18.18%, 17.95%, and 14.06%; the direction of both differences was the same at every session but the magnitude was not, and the index has no published calculation or post-TKA interpretive threshold. Each session comprised one trial, and the third-session gait means were based on only five operated-limb and four non-operated-limb steps. Valid Timed Up and Go (TUG) totals were available for sessions 1 and 2 (13.41 and 14.95 s); the available source documentation did not contain a valid session-3 TUG result. Vendor-derived walk-test speed was excluded from primary interpretation because its calculation could not be reconciled with distance divided by test duration; Conclusions: Across these three observations, 2MWT distance increased while side-to-side differences in stance duration and the exploratory propulsion index were present at each session. These co-occurring changes cannot be attributed to weight loss specifically, because time since arthroplasty, rehabilitation exposure and repeated testing varied together with body mass. The findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating; confirmation requires prospective studies with repeated trials per session, an adequate number of analysed steps, and validated kinetic or limb-specific outcomes.

titre: Age-Stratified Comparison of Gait Biomechanics in People with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis and Healthy Individuals: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
titre_fr: Age-Stratified Comparison of Gait Biomechanics in People with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis and Healthy Individuals: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
auteurs: Righetti Anna, Carletto Alessia, Varalta Valentina, Rigoni Giulio, Spolaor Fabiola, Dalle Vacche Maria, Calabrese Massimiliano, Ziccardi Stefano, Evangelista Elisa, Filippetti Mirko, Smania Nicola, Sawacha Zimi, Picelli Alessandro
revue: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
resume: Background and Objectives: Gait impairment is a common and disabling manifestation of multiple sclerosis, affecting mobility, independence, and quality of life. However, gait differences between people with multiple sclerosis and healthy individuals have not been well characterized within corresponding age strata. Methods: This exploratory cross-sectional study included 23 participants with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis and 50 healthy individuals aged 20-69 years. Participants underwent instrumented gait analysis at self-selected walking speed using a Vicon motion-capture system synchronized with force plates. Spatiotemporal parameters, lower-limb and pelvic kinematics, and ground reaction forces were assessed. Between-group comparisons were performed within predefined age strata (20-39, 40-49, 50-59, and 60-69 years) using one-dimensional Statistical Parametric Mapping and non-parametric analyses. Results: Across age strata, participants with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis generally showed slower walking and shorter stride-related measures, together with phase-specific multi-joint kinematic and ground reaction force deviations. Estimated gait-speed and stride-length differences were largest in the youngest stratum, whereas mean stride width was 0.04 m greater in both the youngest and oldest strata; however, confidence intervals were wide, and no between-stratum contrast was tested. Exploratory threshold crossings were not interpreted as evidence that the underlying effects differed among strata. Conclusions: The age-stratified, participant-level analysis identified recurrent differences in forward progression, lower-limb and pelvic kinematics, and loading and propulsion. These findings provide a quantitative description that may support individualized gait assessment and hypothesis generation for adequately powered studies. They do not establish an independent effect of age or an age-by-disease interaction.

titre: Musculoskeletal Findings Following Pre-Participation Screening in Young Athletes: A Retrospective Observational Study.
titre_fr: Musculoskeletal Findings Following Pre-Participation Screening in Young Athletes: A Retrospective Observational Study.
auteurs: Vecchiato Marco, Palermi Stefano, Ancona Luisa, Barbaro Giulio, Brontesi Giampietro, Conte Rosario, Luca Fulvio De, Foccardi Giulia, Gerbino Luigi, Grassi Mattia, Pandolfi Vincenzo, Quinto Giulia, Sutto Carlo, Varponi Stefano, Bargellesi Stefano, Brugin Erica
revue: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
resume: Background: Pre-participation screening (PPS) is widely used to evaluate athletes before sport participation, traditionally focusing on cardiovascular risk prevention. However, musculoskeletal assessment performed during PPS may also allow early identification of biomechanical and structural abnormalities that can affect sport participation during growth. Objectives: This study aimed to describe the prevalence, clinical characteristics, and management pathways of musculoskeletal alterations detected during PPS in young athletes, with particular focus on referral patterns to pediatric Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PM&R) specialists. Methods: This retrospective observational study included athletes aged ≤15 years who underwent PPS between January 2022 and December 2023 at the Sports Medicine Unit of Noale (ULSS 3 Serenissima, Venice, Italy). Musculoskeletal screening was systematically performed during PPS. Athletes presenting newly detected abnormalities were either managed conservatively by the sports physician or referred for PM&R evaluation. Clinical indications for referral, imaging investigations, diagnoses, and treatment strategies were analyzed. Results: A total of 707 athletes underwent PPS during the study period. After applying exclusion criteria, 635 athletes were eligible for analysis. Musculoskeletal alterations were identified in 141 athletes (22.2%). Among them, 54 athletes were referred for PM&R evaluation and 40 completed the consultation. No statistically significant differences were observed between referred and non-referred athletes. The most frequent reasons for referral were suspected scoliosis (n = 22), foot alignment disorders n = 18), thoracic hyperkyphosis (n = 5), and lower limb length discrepancy (n = 4). Specialist evaluation resulted in conservative management in most cases, including corrective exercise programs and orthotic interventions, while one athlete required surgical treatment for congenital scoliosis. Conclusions: Musculoskeletal screening during PPS identified a broad spectrum of findings in young athletes, including clinically relevant abnormalities requiring specialist evaluation and management. These findings suggest that musculoskeletal assessment may provide an opportunity for early clinical identification within PPS; however, prospective studies are needed to evaluate diagnostic accuracy, long-term clinical benefit, injury prevention, and cost-effectiveness before routine implementation can be recommended.

After applying exclusion criteria, 635 athletes were eligible for analysis. Musculoskeletal alterations were identified in 141 athletes (22.2%). Among them, 54 athletes were referred for PM&R evaluation and 40 completed the consultation. No statistically significant differences were observed between referred and non-referred athletes. The most frequent reasons for referral were suspected scoliosis (n = 22), foot alignment disorders n = 18), thoracic hyperkyphosis (n = 5), and lower limb length discrepancy (n = 4). Specialist evaluation resulted in conservative management in most cases, including corrective exercise programs and orthotic interventions, while one athlete required surgical treatment for congenital scoliosis. Conclusions: Musculoskeletal screening during PPS identified a broad spectrum of findings in young athletes, including clinically relevant abnormalities requiring specialist evaluation and management. These findings suggest that musculoskeletal assessment may provide an opportunity for early clinical identification within PPS; however, prospective studies are needed to evaluate diagnostic accuracy, long-term clinical benefit, injury prevention, and cost-effectiveness before routine implementation can be recommended.

titre: Machine Learning Applications for Wearable Sensor Data in Tennis and Padel: A Systematic Review of Movement Recognition, Performance Monitoring, and Emerging Injury-Related Applications.
titre_fr: Machine Learning Applications for Wearable Sensor Data in Tennis and Padel: A Systematic Review of Movement Recognition, Performance Monitoring, and Emerging Injury-Related Applications.
auteurs: Moggio Lucrezia, Ammendolia Antonio, de Sire Alessandro, Marotta Nicola, Demeco Andrea, Mercurio Melania, Galasso Olimpio, Longo Umile Giuseppe, Mercurio Michele
revue: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
resume: Background: Wearable sensors combined with machine learning (ML) offer new opportunities for movement analysis and performance monitoring in tennis and padel. However, the current evidence and potential applications remain unclear. This systematic review aimed to summarize the applications of ML to wearable sensor data in tennis and padel, focusing on movement recognition, performance monitoring, workload and fatigue assessment, injury-related applications, and rehabilitation. Methods: PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception to 1 August 2026. Studies were eligible if they investigated tennis or padel, used wearable sensors, and applied ML or deep learning methods. Study selection and data extraction were independently performed by two reviewers. Risk of bias was assessed across domains related to participants, predictors, outcomes, and analysis/validation. Due to substantial heterogeneity, a qualitative synthesis was performed. Results: Of 393 records identified, 16 studies were included. Fourteen investigated tennis, one padel, and one included tennis data within a multisport study. IMU-based systems were the most frequently used technology. Most studies focused on movement and stroke recognition, while fewer addressed performance, workload, fatigue, or injury-related applications. Reported model performance was generally high, but validation strategies were heterogeneous, and participant-independent or external validation was uncommon. Nine studies presented some concerns, and seven were classified as having high risk of bias. Evidence directly addressing rehabilitation and return-to-sport was particularly limited. Conclusions: ML applied to wearable sensor data shows promising potential for movement recognition and performance assessment in tennis and padel. However, methodological limitations, small and selected cohorts, and limited external validation restrict current generalizability and practical translation. Future research should prioritize larger and more diverse cohorts, subject-independent and external validation, and prospective studies addressing injury prevention, rehabilitation, and return-to-sport.

titre: Precision in Complexity: Efficacy of VSP and Mock Surgery in Stock Prosthetic Reconstruction for TMJ Re-Ankylosis.
titre_fr: Precision in Complexity: Efficacy of VSP and Mock Surgery in Stock Prosthetic Reconstruction for TMJ Re-Ankylosis.
auteurs: Kumar S Hemanth, Mohammad Shadab, Singh Vibha, Singh Geeta
resume: Temporomandibular joint ankylosis (TMJA) management has evolved from gap arthroplasty to total joint replacement (TJR). TMJ re-ankylosis presents a significant challenge in achieving long-term treatment success. This study evaluates the effectiveness of virtual surgical planning (VSP) guided stock TJR in TMJ re-ankylosis. Prospective, single-arm clinical interventional study with 10 patients (mean age 20.3 ± 1.37 years, range 18-28 years; 5 males, 5 females) with TMJ re-ankylosis were prospectively evaluated. Preoperative workflow integrated VSP for 3D mass assessment, cutting guide fabrication, and ramal osteoplasty mapping, followed by physical 1:1 stereolithographic mock surgery validation prior to alloplastic stock TJR (OrthoMax®). Functional outcomes were analyzed over a mean follow-up of 60 months. This study showed statistically significant improvement in maximum interincisal opening (MIO) from 1.83 mm to 37.83 mm (p < 0.001), bite force from 0 kg to 10.31 kg (p < 0.001), masticatory efficiency, and diet consistency post-stock-TJR with a mean follow-up of 60 months. Mandibular range of movements and quality of life improved markedly with minimal postoperative complications. This study highlights the clinical success of the dual validation protocol by integrating VSP-guided stock-TJR in TMJ re-ankylosis. Mock surgery verified digital precision with intraoperative flexibility, ensuring optimal prosthesis fit, restored mandibular function, improvement in quality of life (QoL) and functional rehabilitation. With ongoing advancements, the VSP-guided stock-TJR protocol can be considered effective in TMJ re-ankylosis.

titre: Iterative Motor Phenotyping in Cerebral Palsy: A Conceptual Review.
titre_fr: Iterative Motor Phenotyping in Cerebral Palsy: A Conceptual Review.
auteurs: Ueda Keisuke
resume: Cerebral palsy (CP) is a non-progressive neurodevelopmental disorder in which motor features and their functional impact may change across development. Although longitudinal surveillance and multidisciplinary management are established components of CP care, motor phenotype is often treated as static. This narrative review proposes iterative motor phenotyping as a conceptual framework for repeatedly characterizing spasticity, dystonia, ataxia, hypotonia, and mixed motor features in relation to function, participation, comfort, safety, and child- and family-centered goals. Reassessment may be scheduled during follow-up or triggered by developmental transitions, functional changes, by pain, or by limited or unexpected treatment response. Updated characterization can inform individualized management and may prompt targeted diagnostic evaluation when emerging or atypical features raise concern for an alternative diagnosis. Iterative motor phenotyping is intended to complement, rather than replace longitudinal surveillance, rehabilitation, multidisciplinary care, and diagnostic evaluation. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether this framework improves treatment selection or functional outcomes.

titre: Identifying activities and participation domains with severe dependence using the ICF-based LIMOS-Br in chronic stroke.
titre_fr: Identifying activities and participation domains with severe dependence using the ICF-based LIMOS-Br in chronic stroke.
auteurs: Monteiro Bibiana Caldeira, Ottiger Beatrice, Janizello Gustavo Pietracatelli, de Castro Shamyr Sulyvan, Polese Janaine Cunha, Vanbellingen Tim, Silva Soraia Micaela
resume: To identify activities and participation domains with severe dependence based on LIMOS-Br (Lucerne ICF-based Multidisciplinary Observational Scale-Brazilian version) scores and to evaluate the clinical utility of the instrument in individuals with chronic stroke. This cross-sectional study included 100 post-stroke individuals. Functioning was assessed using the LIMOS-Br. Descriptive and severity-based analyses (scores 1-2; >20% frequency threshold) were performed to identify activities and participation domains with severe dependence. Clinical utility was assessed using the Clinical Utility Scale. Severity-based analysis revealed a discrepancy between prevalence and severity. While limitations in climbing stairs (90%) and changing body position (79%) were highly prevalent, others were characterized by both high prevalence and substantial severity, including walking long distances (82% prevalence; 33% severe dependence) and moving around (85% prevalence; 24% severe dependence). These, together with fine hand use (35%), complex domestic tasks (29%), and writing (28%), were identified as domains with severe dependence, all exceeding the 20% threshold. Community mobility, fine hand use, and complex domestic activities showed the greatest frequency of severe dependence in this sample. The LIMOS-Br showed preliminary evidence of clinical utility and provides a standardized ICF-based measure to complement rehabilitation planning in chronic stroke survivors.

titre: Reliability and validity of the ICF core elements scale for swallowing function assessment in stroke patients: a single-center study from Hunan, China.
titre_fr: Reliability and validity of the ICF core elements scale for swallowing function assessment in stroke patients: a single-center study from Hunan, China.
auteurs: Dong Yi, Tan Hao, Chen Junrong, Qin Pei, Yin Yuqi, Tao Xi
resume: To evaluate the reliability and validity of the 21-item ICF Core Category Scale for Dysphagia in Stroke (ICCSDS) in assessing swallowing disorders in Chinese stroke patients. Six experienced rehabilitation physicians evaluated the content validity of the scale. Two raters (a rehabilitation physician and a swallowing therapist) received standardized training. Rehabilitation physicians screened and enrolled 80 patients with suspected swallowing difficulties using the Toronto Bedside Swallowing Screening Test. A swallowing therapist subsequently performed the initial ICCSDS assessment using the Gugging Swallowing Screen (GUSS) as a practical reference standard. Four hours later, a rehabilitation physician conducted a second ICCSDS assessment at the same site to evaluate interrater reliability. Significant differences were observed between the high-score and low-score groups for all the ICCSDS items (all p < 0.01). The Cronbach's α coefficients for assessments performed by the rehabilitation physician and swallowing therapist were 0.864 and 0.829, respectively. The S-CVI value was 0.978, and the I-CVI values ranged from 0.83 to 1.00. Exploratory factor analysis revealed that the Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) values for assessments by the rehabilitation physician and the swallowing therapist were 0.887 and 0.848, respectively (both p < 0.01), with cumulative variance contributions of 75.69 and 73.65%, respectively. When the GUSS was used as the practical reference standard, the criterion-related validity coefficients of the ICCSDS assessed by the rehabilitation physician and the swallowing therapist were 0.790 and 0.683, respectively (both p < 0.01). Interrater reliability analysis revealed an ICC (2, 1) of 0.924 and an ICC (2, k) of 0.961. The weighted kappa coefficients exceeded 0.80 for 14 items, reached 0.799 for one item, and ranged from 0.420 to 0.547 for six items. The 21-item ICCSDS demonstrated acceptable internal consistency, content validity, and interrater reliability in Chinese patients with poststroke dysphagia. The preliminary evidence from the criterion-related validity analysis supports its association with clinical bedside assessment tools.

titre: Rehabilitation of paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity secondary to severe brain injury: A case report.
titre_fr: Rehabilitation of paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity secondary to severe brain injury: A case report.
auteurs: Xiang Shouchang, Gao Zhenzhen, Zhu Zhiwen
resume: Paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH) is a complication of severe brain injury (SBI), characterised by paroxysms of excessive sympathetic nervous system activity, with manifestations such as fever, tachycardia, hypertension, excessive sweating and abnormal high muscle tone. PSH can delay diagnosis and rehabilitation, impacting the functional recovery of patients. The present case report aims to explore rehabilitation management strategies and treatment effects for PSH. The case of a 31-year-old woman who presented with rapid onset of PSH following SBI is included in the report. The patient received comprehensive rehabilitation treatment after transfer to The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang Chinese Medical University (Zhejiang Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine, Hangzhou, China), 5 months after the initial brain injury. Neurological function recovery, symptom relief and changes in functional outcomes were evaluated. Management focused on autonomic nervous system dysfunction and an individualised rehabilitation programme. Following comprehensive rehabilitation, the PSH symptoms of the patient demonstrated notable improvement. The frequency of PSH episodes decreased from several times per week to once every 1-2 months, and episode duration shortened to <1 min. The PSH-assessment measure total score was 26 at initial diagnosis, 24 at rehabilitation admission and 4 after comprehensive rehabilitation treatment. The Glasgow Coma Scale score improved from E1VTM1 to E4VTM3. Brunnstrom stages of bilateral upper limbs, hands and lower limbs progressed from I-I-I to II-II-II. In conclusion, in the present patient with PSH secondary to SBI, a stepwise, multidisciplinary rehabilitation strategy was temporally associated with symptomatic improvement, recovery of neurological function and improvement in activities of daily living. These findings suggest the potential clinical feasibility of an integrated rehabilitation approach for managing PSH.

titre: Comparing the efficacy of LORETA neurofeedback versus cognitive rehabilitation on working memory in children with learning disorders: A double-blind clinical trial.
titre_fr: Comparing the efficacy of LORETA neurofeedback versus cognitive rehabilitation on working memory in children with learning disorders: A double-blind clinical trial.
auteurs: Alamdarifar Shayan, Kalantari Jala
revue: Journal of education and health promotion
resume: Nowadays, researchers emphasize the use of inexpensive and low-risk methods as preferred treatments for disorders in children and adolescents. The present study was conducted with the aim of comparing the effects of LORETA neurofeedback (NF) and cognitive rehabilitation on the working memory of children with learning disabilities. The present research design was a quasi-experimental with pretest, posttest with three-month follow-up. The population were all students with learning disorders and sample was 45 children aged between 7 and 10 with learning disabilities from schools in Shiraz. Three groups of 15 children were selected by convenience sampling. The intervention consisted of cognitive rehabilitation and LORETA NF training sessions. To measure outcomes, they used three assessment tools: the IVA (Integrated Visual Auditory Performance Assessment), Wechsler's Working Memory Test, and the Children's Clinical Assessment. Data were analyzed by MANCOVA using SPSS 28. The study's results revealed that participants who received LORETA NF treatment showed more significant improvements in their working memory compared to those who underwent cognitive rehabilitation (P < 0.05). This improvement was evident not only immediately after treatment but also persisted through the follow-up period, suggesting that NF had a more lasting positive effect than cognitive rehabilitation (P < 0.05). The results suggest that LORETA NF training could be an effective intervention for improving working memory in children who have learning disabilities. Therapists and neuropsychologists can use the results of this study to improve the cognitive functions of affected students.

titre: Efficacy of Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation (NMES) on Lower Limb Mobility and Activities of Daily Living in Post-Stroke Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
titre_fr: Efficacy of Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation (NMES) on Lower Limb Mobility and Activities of Daily Living in Post-Stroke Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
auteurs: Feng Yunhao, Zhang Chongrui, Chang Yanbo, Xiaoning Di
revue: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
resume: To assess the therapeutic efficacy of neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) in improving lower limb function and daily activities in post-stroke patients. Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov from database inception to April 20, 2025. Meta-analysis for continuous outcomes was performed using the inverse variance method under fixed- or random-effects models according to heterogeneity. Ten studies (579 patients) were included. NMES significantly improved Fugl-Meyer Assessment (MD=3.40, P=0.001), ankle dorsiflexion ROM (MD=1.56, P=0.04), TUG (MD=-1.96, P=0.03), BBS (MD=10.78, P=0.005), PASS (MD=5.05, P<0.00001), and MBI (MD=13.29, P=0.02). Sensitivity analysis confirmed result robustness. NMES effectively enhances motor function and activities of daily living in post-stroke patients, and may complement standard rehabilitation.

titre: Evaluating the Mental Fatigue Scale for long COVID: A content validity study.
titre_fr: Evaluating the Mental Fatigue Scale for long COVID: A content validity study.
auteurs: Riis-Djernæs Line M, Oestergaard Lisa Gregersen, Nielsen Trine Brøns, Sørensen Lotte, Schiøttz-Christensen Berit, Young Hannah, Sørensen Dorthe
resume: This study aimed to evaluate the content validity of the Mental Fatigue Scale (MFS) in individuals with long COVID. Content validity was assessed using COSMIN methodology through cognitive interviews with individuals with long COVID (n = 10) and focus groups with healthcare professionals (n = 8). The interviews were conducted at a Danish long COVID clinic and a community-based rehabilitation centre. MFS was generally perceived as relevant, comprehensive, and comprehensible for assessing mental fatigue in individuals with long COVID. Most participants found the items appropriate; however, some described experiences, such as word-finding difficulties and racing thoughts, not fully captured by the scale. Participants also compared symptoms to their pre COVID condition rather than to the previous month, suggesting that the timeframe may require adjustment. Several noted that the MFS reflects symptoms at the body-function level and offers limited insight into how mental fatigue affects participation in work, social, and family life. The MFS appears useful for assessing mental fatigue in individuals with long COVID but may benefit from supplementary items relevant to this population or from being combined with tools that capture broader participation-related and contextual factors. Future studies should adapt and evaluate the scale in this population.

titre: Dual-scale assessment of motor dysfunction in older adults with locomotor dysfunction and its association with gait and muscle activation.
titre_fr: Dual-scale assessment of motor dysfunction in older adults with locomotor dysfunction and its association with gait and muscle activation.
auteurs: Liu Wen, Lu Chunxiao, Qian Lifeng
resume: This study examined the reliability and validity of a combined 25-question geriatric locomotive function scale (GLFS-25) and Locomotion Dysfunction Grade scale (LDG) classification protocol in older adults with locomotor dysfunction, and explored which objective gait and muscle activation parameters were most strongly associated with GLFS-25 scores. The GLFS-25 and LDG were used to assess 289 older adults with locomotor dysfunction, of whom 60 underwent gait analysis and surface electromyography (sEMG). Reliability analysis yielded a Cronbach's α of 0.702 for the GLFS-25, indicating acceptable but modest internal consistency. Exploratory factor analysis extracted nine factors, accounting for 55.193% of the cumulative variance. Confirmatory factor analysis showed X2/df = 1.424, RMSEA = 0.038 (90% CI: 0.000-0.060), and SRMR = 0.055, indicating acceptable fit; however, CFI = 0.821, TLI = 0.801, and IFI = 0.830 were below 0.90, suggesting partial rather than strong construct validity. In exploratory ridge regression, the model showed an in-sample R2 of 0.858, which should be interpreted with caution. Step length showed a positive association with the GLFS-25 score, while knee flexion during swing and the ratio of pressure onset time of the middle foot showed negative associations (P < 0.05). However, individual coefficients should be interpreted cautiously. The GLFS-25 demonstrated acceptable but modest reliability and partial construct validity in this population. In exploratory analyses, its scores showed a strong in-sample association with objective gait and sEMG measures. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require external validation in independent cohorts. Objective measures remain complementary to, rather than substitutes for, subjective assessment. Registration: ChiCTR2400087701.

Step length showed a positive association with the GLFS-25 score, while knee flexion during swing and the ratio of pressure onset time of the middle foot showed negative associations (P < 0.05). However, individual coefficients should be interpreted cautiously. The GLFS-25 demonstrated acceptable but modest reliability and partial construct validity in this population. In exploratory analyses, its scores showed a strong in-sample association with objective gait and sEMG measures. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require external validation in independent cohorts. Objective measures remain complementary to, rather than substitutes for, subjective assessment. titre: Maternal Vitamin D Deficiency is Associated With Sex-Dependent Alterations in Neurodevelopment-Related Gene Expression, Particularly in the Hypothalamus.
titre_fr: Maternal Vitamin D Deficiency is Associated With Sex-Dependent Alterations in Neurodevelopment-Related Gene Expression, Particularly in the Hypothalamus.
auteurs: Saidi Lidia, Snacel-Fazy Emmanuel, Seipelt Eva, Haroun Nicole, Astier Julien, Couturier Charlène, Soltani Mohamed El, Sérée Eric, Sicard Flavie, Hammou Habib, Puceat Michel, Landrier Jean-François, Mounien Lourdes
resume: Vitamin D (VD) is essential for calcium homeostasis and bone metabolism but also for brain development and function. However, few data are available on the impact of maternal VD deficiency (VDD) on sex-specific brain development, particularly in specific structures such as hypothalamus. This study investigated the impact of maternal VDD on early brain development, neuronal and glial differentiation, and hypothalamic gene expression in mice. Maternal VDD was associated with increased mRNA expression of markers related to neuronal differentiation and synaptogenesis in both sexes, while mRNA expression of astrocyte-related markers remained largely unchanged. Male offspring exhibited broader transcriptomic alterations, including dysregulation of melanocortin-pathway and synaptic signaling genes, in the hypothalamus of early postnatal and adult mice. Maternal VDD was associated with sex-dependent changes in gene expression relevant to early brain development, with altered mRNA expression of markers involved in neuronal differentiation and synaptogenesis in both sexes. Male offspring exhibited transcriptomic changes, including altered expression of melanocortin-pathway and synaptic signaling genes, further suggesting greater susceptibility of hypothalamic gene expression to maternal VDD. These findings indicate that maternal VDD may influence neurodevelopmental gene expression during early life, potentially contributing to later alterations in synaptic function, metabolism, and behavior.

titre: Genetic Screening for Expanded FMR1 Alleles in a Moroccan Cohort With Unexplained Intellectual Disability.
titre_fr: Genetic Screening for Expanded FMR1 Alleles in a Moroccan Cohort With Unexplained Intellectual Disability.
auteurs: Souski Hajar, Benmakhlouf Yousra, Lepine Valérie, Bekkari Houda, Barakat Amina, Nourouti Naima Ghailani, Bilan Frédéric, Mechita Mohcine Bennani
revue: Journal of intellectual disability research : JIDR
resume: Intellectual disability (ID) constitutes a major neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD), arising from diverse genetic and environmental aetiologies. Fragile X syndrome (FXS), caused by CGG repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene, is one of the most common inherited causes of ID and autism. In Morocco, FMR1 molecular screening data are currently not available. This study provides the first characterisation of FMR1 mutations in Moroccan patients with nonsyndromic ID (NS-ID). One hundred children and adolescents (75 boys and 25 girls) were tested using AmplideX PCR/CE FMR1 Kit based on fluorescent triplet-primed PCR (TP-PCR) and capillary electrophoresis (CE) to determine CGG repeat sizes. A total of 92% of individuals (23 females and 69 males) carried an FMR1 allele within the normal CGG repeat range (< 44 repeats), two of which were diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome (KS). Two females (2%) presented intermediate alleles (45-54 repeats), both with 53 repeats. Six full-mutation males (6%) were identified with CGG repeats > 200. As the first molecular screening initiative targeting FXS in high-risk patients, our results demonstrate the utility of testing in this population highlighting the importance of future multicentre studies.

titre: Arhgef1 Deletion Disrupts Early Cortical Neurogenesis via PAK1 Overactivation and Causes Motor Dysfunction in Adulthood.
titre_fr: Arhgef1 Deletion Disrupts Early Cortical Neurogenesis via PAK1 Overactivation and Causes Motor Dysfunction in Adulthood.
auteurs: Li Liuren, Ma Xuanyue, Ding Zhenyu, Sun Bang, Liu Linglin, Yip Hei Matthew, Wang Wei, Wu Tianying, Guo Yuan, Peng Yinghui, Zhang Shiqing, Ip Jacque Pak Kan, Zhang Li, Li Keshen, Shi Lei
resume: Precise regulation of early cortical development is essential for the establishment of normal brain function, and its disruption can contribute to the pathogenesis of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Impaired motor function is a prominent early manifestation of various NDDs, yet the mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identified ARHGEF1, a Rho family guanine nucleotide exchange factor highly expressed during early corticogenesis, as a novel regulator in embryonic cortical neurogenesis and adult motor function. By Emx1-Cre-mediated forebrain deletion of Arhgef1 in mice (Arhgef1 cKO mice), early cortical neurogenesis is specifically disrupted, leading to reduced deep-layer cortical neurons. Mechanistically, Arhgef1 deficiency overactivates RAC1/CDC42-PAK1-Cofilin signaling in early cortical development, whereas pharmacological PAK1 inhibition within this critical window rescues the genesis of deep-layer cortical neurons. Importantly, Arhgef1 cKO mice exhibit remarkable motor learning and coordination deficits in adulthood, accompanied by altered neuronal morphology in the motor cortex and impaired neuronal activities in motor circuits. In all, we elucidate a critical developmental window when ARHGEF1 governs corticogenesis via negatively regulates PAK1-dependent pathway and further reveal an important role for ARHGEF1 in maintaining normal motor function in adulthood.

titre: Non-invasive skin trace elementomics reveals a characteristic pattern of essential element deficiency and toxic element accumulation in children with ADHD.
titre_fr: Non-invasive skin trace elementomics reveals a characteristic pattern of essential element deficiency and toxic element accumulation in children with ADHD.
auteurs: Lei Yan, Li Shujin, Sun Yanhui, Jiang Zhongqin, Liu Bin, Zhang Yong, Ling Yu, Li Li
revue: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine
resume: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is the most common neurodevelopmental disorder in childhood. Its clinical diagnosis primarily relies on behavioral assessments, lacking objective and non-invasive biological indicators. Trace elements are involved in neurotransmitter synthesis, myelin development, and prefrontal cortex function regulation, and their imbalance may be associated with the pathogenesis of ADHD. However, previous studies have mostly focused on single elements, lacking systematic evidence at the omics level. To analyze the differences in 30 skin element levels between children with ADHD and healthy controls, and to explore the associations of elemental imbalances with core symptoms, anxiety, and executive function, thereby providing a basis for non-invasive screening of childhood ADHD. A total of 549 children with ADHD and 963 healthy controls were enrolled. Skin element levels were measured using a non-invasive high-throughput technique. Behavioral assessments were performed using the CONNERS, SNAP‑IV, SCARED, and WEISS scales. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with age as a covariate was used to compare intergroup differences in element levels. Partial correlation analysis was applied to control for age as a confounding factor. The Benjamini‑Hochberg method was used to control the false discovery rate (FDR) for multiple comparison correction, with a significance threshold of q < 0.05. After adjusting for age and FDR correction, 28 elements showed significant differences between the ADHD group and the control group. In the ADHD group, essential/potentially beneficial elements such as Mg, Zn, I, Cr, Li and Ge were decreased, whereas B and harmful elements including Pb, Hg, Cd, As, Al, Be, and Ba were increased. Multiple elements exhibited stable associations with inattention, hyperactivity-impulsivity, anxiety, and risk-taking behavior. Children with ADHD displayed a complex network pattern of synergistic and antagonistic inter-element relationships. Children with ADHD exhibit a characteristic skin trace elementomic imbalance, characterized by decreased beneficial elements and increased harmful elements, which is closely associated with behavioral symptoms. Non-invasive skin elementomics may serve as a reference indicator for population-based risk screening of childhood ADHD and holds promise for population-based screening.

titre: A novel PGAP1 splice-site variant expanding the clinical and molecular spectrum of GPI-anchor disorders.
titre_fr: A novel PGAP1 splice-site variant expanding the clinical and molecular spectrum of GPI-anchor disorders.
auteurs: Hashemi Seyyed-Saleh, Moazzami Reza, Miri Ali
resume: Genetic defects affecting the biosynthesis and remodeling of glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchors constitute a recently recognized group of autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorders with highly variable clinical presentations. Among the genes involved in this pathway, PGAP1 encodes an endoplasmic reticulum-associated inositol deacylase that plays a critical role in the initial step of GPI-anchor remodeling. Pathogenic variants in PGAP1 have been reported in only a limited number of families worldwide and are associated with clinical features such as global developmental delay, intellectual disability, seizures, microcephaly, and variable systemic manifestations. Here, we describe a patient harboring a novel homozygous splice-site variant (NM_024989.4.1173 + 1G > A) with neurodevelopmental impairment. The potential effect on splicing was assessed using in silico tools (SpliceAI, HSF, and varSEAK), while the potential structural consequences were evaluated using AlphaFold and PyMOL. Segregation analysis was performed to assess the inheritance pattern and provide additional evidence for variant classification. A comprehensive review of previously reported cases was also conducted to broaden the known phenotypic spectrum. The novel variant, which was absent from all public databases, was classified as likely pathogenic according to ACMG guidelines. Computational analyses consistently predicted significant disruption of splicing, while structural modeling suggested conformational alterations associated with the predicted in-frame deletion. Our findings expand the phenotypic heterogeneity of PGAP1-related disorders and provide further insight into the molecular basis of GPI-anchor remodeling defects. The findings also highlight the utility of genomic analysis for establishing a molecular diagnosis in patients with unexplained neurodevelopmental abnormalities.

titre: O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine homeostasis in brain health and disease: From physiology to neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders.
titre_fr: O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine homeostasis in brain health and disease: From physiology to neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders.
auteurs: Di Domenico Fabio, Ashraf Laiba, Slawson Chad, Buccarello Lucia, Caruso Giuseppe, De Filippis Bianca, Lanzillotta Chiara
resume: Protein O-GlcNAcylation is a dynamic and reversible post-translational modification that functions as a central nutrient-sensing mechanism linking cellular metabolism to protein function. Controlled by the opposing activities of O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine transferase and O-GlcNAcase, O-GlcNAcylation regulates thousands of nuclear, cytoplasmic, synaptic, and mitochondrial proteins involved in gene expression, neuronal differentiation, synaptic plasticity, proteostasis, mitochondrial homeostasis, and neuroimmune signaling. The brain exhibits particularly high O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine activity, reflecting its exceptional metabolic demands and the need to rapidly couple nutrient availability with neuronal function. Emerging evidence demonstrates that precise regulation of O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine cycling is indispensable throughout the lifespan, from embryonic neurodevelopment to healthy brain aging. Conversely, disruption of O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine homeostasis caused by genetic defects, metabolic disturbances, or environmental stress contributes to neurodevelopmental disorders. In the aging brain, impaired glucose metabolism and insulin resistance reduce O-GlcNAcylation, promoting mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, proteostasis failure, and the accumulation of pathogenic proteins. Consequently, dysregulated O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine signaling has emerged as a convergent mechanism underlying brain disorders spanning neurodevelopment to neurodegeneration. Although clinical translation remains challenging, growing evidence supports O-GlcNAcylation as a master regulator of brain homeostasis and a promising therapeutic target for neurological disorders. Collectively, this review highlights O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine signaling as a molecular bridge connecting early brain development, adulthood, and aging, providing an integrated framework for understanding brain physiology and disease.
