titre: Global research trends and emerging hotspots in probiotics and children's neurodevelopment: a bibliometric and visualized analysis (1998-2026, partial year).
titre_fr: Global research trends and emerging hotspots in probiotics and children's neurodevelopment: a bibliometric and visualized analysis (1998-2026, partial year).
auteurs: Sun Guohui, Guo Tianwei, Lang Weihong, Peng Fangyuan, Jiang Xiling, Chen Jianxing
resume: Research on the role of probiotics in children's neurodevelopment has expanded rapidly, yet a quantitative synthesis of this interdisciplinary field is lacking. This study aimed to map global research trends, identify key contributors, and reveal emerging hotspots in the field of probiotics and children's neurodevelopment through bibliometric and visualized analysis. Publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection from 1998 to 2026 (partial year, search conducted on 21 May 2026) were retrieved using a predefined search strategy combining terms related to probiotics, children, and neurodevelopment. After screening and deduplication, 1,684 documents were included. Bibliometric indicators, including annual publication trends, productive authors and journals, keyword co-occurrence networks, temporal trends in keyword frequency, and the top 15 most frequently cited references, were analyzed using the bibliometrix R package, igraph, ggplot2, and wordcloud. Common keyword synonyms were merged prior to network construction. Annual publication output increased steadily from 1998 to 2015 and accelerated sharply after 2020, reaching a peak in 2025. The most frequent publication venues included Nutrients and Frontiers in Microbiology. Keyword co-occurrence analysis revealed a core network centered on Gut Microbiota, Autism Spectrum Disorder, Probiotics, and Gut-Brain Axis, with ADHD emerging as a distinct and increasingly prominent node in the 2020-2026 period. Temporal trends in keyword frequency indicated a shift from broad descriptive associations toward more specialized terms such as Dysbiosis, Fecal Microbiota Transplantation, Neuroinflammation, and Metabolomics. Highly cited documents and the top 15 most frequently cited references were anchored by seminal works on the gut-brain axis and microbiome-behavior relationships, forming a stable intellectual base. This study provides a comprehensive overview of the research landscape in probiotics and children's neurodevelopment. The field is shifting from observational studies toward mechanism-oriented and interventional research, with ADHD and multi-omics approaches representing important emerging directions. As a single-database analysis, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and future studies should integrate additional databases to validate and extend them. Translational implications include stratifying patients by neurodevelopmental diagnosis and microbial profile, and testing mechanism-guided probiotic or synbiotic formulations in future trials. These findings offer useful guidance for researchers seeking to understand the structure of the field and identify promising areas for future investigation. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05105-2.

titre: From Exome to Optical Mapping: Resolving a Complex 17q12 Rearrangement Underlying a Severe Neurodevelopmental Disorder.
titre_fr: From Exome to Optical Mapping: Resolving a Complex 17q12 Rearrangement Underlying a Severe Neurodevelopmental Disorder.
auteurs: Dardas Zain, Du Haowei, Calame Daniel G, Pehlivan Davut, Gulec Elif Yilmaz, Saad Ahmed K, Hastings P J, Posey Jennifer E, Gibbs Richard A, Grochowski Christopher M, Lupski James R
resume: Background Complex genomic rearrangements (CGRs) are significant contributors to neurodevelopmental disorders, yet their full structural architecture often eludes conventional diagnostic methods. We investigated the genetic basis of a 7-year-old boy presenting with severe intellectual and growth delay, immune deficiency, and multiple congenital anomalies. Methods We combined exome sequencing, array comparative genomic hybridization, short-read and long-read genome sequencing, droplet digital PCR, and optical genome mapping to characterize a chromosomal rearrangement identified in the proband and to assess segregation within the family trio. Results This integrated approach reconstructed the architecture of a highly complex duplication-triplication-quadruplication rearrangement on chromosome 17q12, encompassing the developmental and immune-regulatory genes DUSP14 , SYNRG , DDX52 , and HNF1B , consistent with the proband's phenotypic spectrum. Breakpoint mapping revealed microhomologies and inverted repeats, implicating a replication-based mechanism, such as microhomology-mediated break-induced replication, in the rearrangement's formation. Droplet digital PCR further uncovered low-level mosaicism in the asymptomatic father, indicating a potential germline transmission pathway relevant to familial recurrence risk. Conclusions Integrating multiple sequencing and optical mapping technologies can resolve complex structural variation, uncover parental mosaicism, and implicate candidate genes that conventional methods alone would miss. This approach improves molecular diagnosis and advances understanding of the mutational mechanisms underlying complex disease-associated rearrangements.

titre: Novel variant in KARS1 in a consanguineous family with Intellectual Disability and hearing impairment: WES and in silico protein analysis.
titre_fr: Novel variant in KARS1 in a consanguineous family with Intellectual Disability and hearing impairment: WES and in silico protein analysis.
auteurs: Shahatit Shadi, Hashhoysh Roaa, Alkhateeb Asem
resume: Intellectual Disability (ID) is a genetically heterogeneous neurodevelopmental disorder that imposes a substantial burden on families, with huge demands on healthcare services. Autosomal recessive forms are particularly prevalent in inbred populations, where rare homozygous variants often remain undiagnosed. Trio-based whole-exome sequencing (WES) has emerged as an effective diagnostic approach for resolving the etiology of unresolved cases. Herein, we report a homozygous missense variant in KARS1, a lysyl-tRNA synthetase (c.989 T > C, p.Leu330Pro), co-segregating with ID and hearing impairments in a consanguineous Arab family from Jordan. We integrated WES and in silico analyses to characterize the variant, including evolutionary, pathogenicity, splicing, stability, and comparative 3D modelling analyses. The variant was located in a highly conserved catalytic domain, and multiple pathogenicity classifiers predicted a deleterious impact. The molecular changes included a potential loss of the alpha helix and alterations to the catalytic/allosteric sites. Splicing analyses predicted disruption of exonic regulatory elements, forming a new enhancer motif and a net increase in exonic splicing enhancers. Additionally, the variant was predicted to be destabilizing, with decreased local interactions, including potential clashes with Glu301. The identified variant can potentially disrupt aminoacylation fidelity, and the impaired protein function may compromise both cytosolic and mitochondrial protein synthesis, leading to defective proteostasis, reduced energy production, and altered synaptic development. Our findings highlight the diagnostic value of trio-based WES and computational analyses in consanguineous populations, expand the genetic and phenotypic spectrum of KARS1-related dysfunctions, and support the inclusion of KARS1 in regional diagnostic panels for ID.

titre: How School-Based Interventions Shape the Developing Brain during 3-12 Years: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-analysis.
titre_fr: How School-Based Interventions Shape the Developing Brain during 3-12 Years: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-analysis.
auteurs: Li Jingwen, Huang Runke, Li Hui
resume: The effects of school-based interventions (SBIs) on children's neurodevelopment are poorly synthesized. This systematic review integrates neuroscientific evidence on how structured educational activities influence brain development in children aged 3-12 years. Following PRISMA guidelines, we identified 17 empirical studies (published 2014-2025) using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), electroencephalography (EEG), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), or magnetoencephalography (MEG). Of these, 8 studies were included in a random-effects meta-analysis and all 17 in a thematic synthesis. The meta-analysis revealed a preliminary association between SBIs and reduced amygdala activity during stress regulation tasks (r = -.28, 95% CI [-.50, -.02]), based on two studies, which should be interpreted as exploratory rather than confirmatory. No significant pooled effect for executive function, likely due to high heterogeneity. Thematic analysis distinguishes between mechanisms of plasticity and markers of intervention effectiveness: the first three characterize intra-individual mechanisms of experience-dependent plasticity, including (1) executive function interventions engaged prefrontal networks through both increased recruitment and enhanced neural efficiency; (2) socio-emotional programs modulated limbic-prefrontal circuits; (3) language and auditory programs shaped sensory-specific electrophysiological markers and cortical specialization; and the fourth theme identifies a neural marker of the effective process of intervention delivery, demonstrating that (4) teacher-child inter-brain synchrony was positively correlated with learning outcomes. By integrating findings across neural, cognitive, and affective domains, this review provides a conceptual framework linking pedagogical practices to neural plasticity and advances the understanding of the neurofunctional pathways through which educational experiences shape the developing brain.

titre: Beyond Newborn Screening: Clinical Outcomes and Genotypic Spectrum Underlying Maple Syrup Urine Disease in Mexico.
titre_fr: Beyond Newborn Screening: Clinical Outcomes and Genotypic Spectrum Underlying Maple Syrup Urine Disease in Mexico.
auteurs: Vela-Amieva Marcela, Reyna-Fabián Miriam Erandi, Fernández-Hernández Liliana, Guillén-López Sara, López-Mejía Lizbeth, Alcantara-Ortigoza Miguel Angel, Gonzalez-Del Angel Ariadna, Estandía-Ortega Bernardette, Ibarra-González Isabel, Paz-Castillo Laura, Fernández-Lainez Cynthia
resume: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) is a time-critical inborn error of metabolism in which early detection may prevent irreversible neurological injury, yet the success of newborn screening (NBS) depends on timely post-screening care. We retrospectively characterized the clinical, biochemical, and genotypic spectrum of 88 Mexican patients from 80 unrelated families evaluated between 1995 and 2026 and assessed the relationship between NBS, treatment timing, neurological outcome, and survival. Most patients had severe neonatal disease, and 73/88 (83%) presented with acute metabolic decompensation requiring hospitalization. Nine patients were identified by NBS: six received timely confirmatory diagnosis and treatment and maintained normal age-appropriate neurodevelopment during 10 years of follow-up, whereas three experienced delays in the diagnostic and therapeutic pathway, developed metabolic decompensation, and subsequently had severe neurological disability. None of the successfully screened patients died. Among 33 molecularly characterized unrelated patients, 31 distinct variants were identified in BCKDHA, BCKDHB, and DBT, with marked genotypic heterogeneity. These findings show that National NBS strategies should prioritize the inclusion of this time critical disorder and the shortening of the interval between a positive screening result and treatment initiation. MSUD NBS should serve as the entry point to an optimal continuum of care. Rapid confirmation, immediate referral, treatment initiation, and sustained specialized metabolic follow-up are essential for translating early detection into favorable outcomes.

titre: Efficacy and Safety of Multidisciplinary Sandwich Regimen in AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD With Preconception B-Cell Depletion During Perigravidity.
titre_fr: Efficacy and Safety of Multidisciplinary Sandwich Regimen in AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD With Preconception B-Cell Depletion During Perigravidity.
auteurs: Xiao Li, Lu Gengxin, Gao Qian, Wan Feiyan, Lu Zhenze, Qiu Wei, Xu Chengfang, Lu Yaxin, Xu Lejia, Xia Tingting, Chao Jiajing, Fu Yu, Chen Zhuanggui, Li Rui, Chang Yanyu, Wang Yuge, Qin Bing, Shu Yaqing
resume: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) predominantly affects women of childbearing age, accompanied by markedly elevated relapse risks during pregnancy and postpartum periods, bringing great challenges to perigravid management. At present, there is no standardized gestational therapeutic regimen for NMOSD worldwide, and data on perigravid application of B-cell depleting agents including rituximab and inebilizumab remain limited. For patients exposed to B-cell depleting agents before conception, balancing disease control and fetal safety is an urgent clinical problem to be solved. This multicenter prospective cohort study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a three-stage multidisciplinary "sandwich" management regimen in AQP4-IgG-positive pregnant women with NMOSD exposed to B-cell depleting agents before conception. Maternal disease activity, pregnancy outcomes, neonatal conditions, and offspring growth and developmental characteristics within the first year of life were analyzed. A total of 8 AQP4-IgG-positive pregnant women with NMOSD who received B-cell depleting agents within 9 months prior to conception were enrolled from multiple centers between January 2022 and October 2024, including 3 patients treated with inebilizumab and 5 patients treated with rituximab. All subjects received a unified three-stage intervention: B-cell depleting agents were discontinued upon confirmed pregnancy; low-dose azathioprine combined with low-dose glucocorticoids was administered during gestation; B-cell depleting agents were reinitiated at 2 weeks postpartum. Multidisciplinary teams consisting of neurology, obstetrics, clinical pharmacy, and neonatology departments conducted full-cycle monitoring and follow-up. Primary observation indicators included maternal relapse events, Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) scores, B-cell counts, gestational complications, gestational age at delivery, neonatal physical indicators, Apgar scores, congenital malformations, as well as offspring growth and neurodevelopment and vaccination safety from birth to 1 year of age. All subjects achieved term live births without severe obstetric complications. Seven patients remained relapse-free throughout pregnancy and postpartum period with stable or improved EDSS scores; one patient discontinued all medications during gestation and suffered a relapse at 1 month postpartum. Neonatal physical indicators and Apgar scores were generally normal, one neonate presented mild hypospadias and two developed transient neonatal abnormalities; neonatal B-cell counts at birth and 1 month of age were within normal ranges. One-year follow-up showed normal physical and neurodevelopment in all offspring with safe vaccination procedures. For AQP4-IgG-positive pregnant women with NMOSD exposed to B-cell depleting agents before conception, the multidisciplinary "sandwich" regimen featuring B-cell depletion before conception and postpartum plus gestational bridging therapy with low-dose azathioprine combined with glucocorticoids is safe and effective, reduces disease relapse risk and yields favorable overall maternal and fetal outcomes. This regimen may serve as a promising perigravid management strategy that warrants further validation in larger cohorts.

titre: Decoding Zmiz1: a key transcription coactivator in development and disease.
titre_fr: Decoding Zmiz1: a key transcription coactivator in development and disease.
auteurs: K C Rajan, Shenoy Anoushka, Siddika Most Ayesha, Patel Nehal R, Meadows Stryder M, Galazo Maria J
revue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
resume: ZMIZ1, a zinc finger MIZ-type transcriptional co-activator in the PIAS family, is emerging as a central regulator at the interface of development and disease. Through interactions with key signaling effectors, including NOTCH1, SMAD3/4, p53, estrogen receptor, and androgen receptor, ZMIZ1 shapes transcriptional programs that govern embryogenesis, vascular and lymphatic development, and cerebral cortex development. Disruption of these programs is increasingly linked to human pathology: pathogenic ZMIZ1 variants cause a syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder with autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability, and are associated with Hirschsprung disease, depression, and Lewy body disease. Beyond the nervous system, genetic and functional studies implicate ZMIZ1 in T-cell development and leukemia, multiple autoimmune diseases, type-2 diabetes, and a broad spectrum of cancers, including cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, prostate, breast, colorectal cancer, osteosarcoma, and glioblastoma. Despite this expanding disease spectrum, the cell type-specific and context-dependent mechanisms by which ZMIZ1 integrates activation state from different signaling pathways, chromatin regulation, and transcription activation remain poorly understood. In this review, we synthesize current knowledge of ZMIZ1 and molecular regulatory networks across developmental, neurological, immune, metabolic, and oncologic contexts. We highlight convergent themes in ZMIZ1 biology, outstanding mechanistic questions, and emerging evidence supporting ZMIZ1 and its downstream pathways as potential diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic targets in human disease. By integrating genetic, molecular, and systems-level evidence across diverse organs and diseases, this review proposes a working model of ZMIZ1 as a partner-directed, dosage-sensitive transcriptional rheostat, identifies experiments required to test it, and appraises the current, largely preclinical, evidence for its clinical potential.

titre: A zebrafish model of NEXMIF-related encephalopathy identified drivers of hyperlocomotion and provides a scalable platform for drug discovery.
titre_fr: A zebrafish model of NEXMIF-related encephalopathy identified drivers of hyperlocomotion and provides a scalable platform for drug discovery.
auteurs: Bernal-Bermúdez Beatriz, Martínez-Morcillo Francisco J, Fuentes-Martínez Inmaculada, Martínez-López Alicia, Cayuela María L, Mulero Victoriano, García-Moreno Diana
revue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
resume: X-linked Intellectual Disability type 98 (XLID-98) is a neurodevelopmental disorder with a broad phenotypic spectrum caused by pathogenic variants in the neurite extension and migration factor (NEXMIF) gene, formerly known as KIAA2022, KIDLIA, or XPN (OMIM 300524). To investigate the pathogenic mechanisms of XLID-98, a double knock-out zebrafish model (nexmifa/b -/-) was generated using CRISPR/Cas9 technology. Mutant larvae displayed limited morphological abnormalities, the most notable being an increase in total body length. They also exhibited a significant hyperlocomotor phenotype in the visual-startle OFF assay, which was attenuated by treatment with sodium valproate (VPA) and topiramate, thereby supporting the pharmacological validity of the model. Transcriptomic analysis of larval heads at seven dpf revealed 414 differentially expressed genes enriched in mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling, cell adhesion, and sodium transport pathways. Functional analyses demonstrated that simultaneous CRISPR/Cas9-mediated disruption of the upregulated genes entpd3 (ectonucleoside triphosphate diphosphohydrolase 3) and ddx43 (DEAD-box helicase 43) exacerbated the hyperlocomotor phenotype, suggesting that these genes may participate in a compensatory response, whereas reduced kbtbd7 (kelch repeat and BTB domain-containing protein 7) activity may contribute to phenotype severity. A targeted screen of 87 natural compounds identified kahweol acetate, veratridine, and rauwolscine as potent inducers of entpd3. However, despite robust transcriptional activation, rauwolscine failed to improve behavioral outcomes, suggesting that modulation of a single molecular target may be insufficient for phenotypic rescue. Collectively, these findings establish the first zebrafish model of NEXMIF-related encephalopathy, identify entpd3, ddx43, and kbtbd7 as candidate modulators of this behavioral phenotype, and provide a scalable platform for targeted therapeutic discovery in XLID-98.

titre: Neurodevelopment as blueprint: biological validation of the dual-architecture AGI framework.
titre_fr: Neurodevelopment as blueprint: biological validation of the dual-architecture AGI framework.
auteurs: Chen Nan
resume: Human intelligence does not develop linearly: it follows a precise phase sequence. This article presents the hypothesis that this neurodevelopmental timeline corresponds to the dual-architecture artificial general intelligence (AGI) system previously proposed by the author, covering the 10 architectural components. We hypothesize that AGI development may be constrained by similar phase sequencing, address key objections (see Sections 3.1, 5.4, 5.5, and 5.6 for explicit objection-response pairs) through formal arguments, and provide indirect supporting evidence for six individual mechanisms on the MuJoCo platform: four-method anti-forgetting comparison: elastic weight consolidation (EWC), synaptic intelligence (SI), memory-aware synapses (MAS), and Naive. Curiosity-driven exploration, training stability analysis, multimodal cross-prediction, and warm-start routing analysis reveal negative transfer in genuinely novel scenarios, and a multi-novelty gradient experiment spanning five gravity levels (1.0×-2.0×) identifies a crossover threshold at approximately 1.25×-1.50× gravity on HalfCheetah-v5. An appendix provides a formal mathematical theory of token migration with two formal sketches and one implication.

titre: Using Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis to Explore the Experiences of Mothers Who Have a Child With the Rare Genetic Disorder, HNRNPU-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: "Some Days, I Wear a Cape and I'm Super Mom and Some Days, I Have to Hide Under My Cape and I Can't Get Out for a Few Days".
titre_fr: Using Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis to Explore the Experiences of Mothers Who Have a Child With the Rare Genetic Disorder, HNRNPU-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: "Some Days, I Wear a Cape and I'm Super Mom and Some Days, I Have to Hide Under My Cape and I Can't Get Out for a Few Days".
auteurs: Overton I, Docherty F, Balasubramanian M
resume: HNRNPU-related neurodevelopmental disorder is an ultra-rare genetic condition characterised by developmental delay, intellectual disability, seizures and a range of complex health needs. Yet, little is known about how families experience and navigate life with this diagnosis. This study explored the lived experiences of seven mothers caring for a child with HNRNPU-NDD, using Interpretive Phenomenological Analysis of semi-structured interviews to gain an in-depth understanding of how they manage with daily life and sustain their well-being. Three group experiential themes (GETs) were generated: (1) From nurturer to care manager: how hypervigilance shapes daily life and maternal identity, (2) How mothers make sense of futures that no longer look as expected: grief, fear of future and reconstruction of hope, (3) Social worlds that 'no longer fit': experiences of isolation and disconnection. Together, these themes show the emotional duality, identity shifts and social challenges involved in raising a child with HNRNPU-NDD. They are discussed alongside existing literature on rare disease caregiving, highlighting shared challenges as well as aspects that appear distinctive to ultra-rare neurodevelopmental conditions. The findings illustrate that mothers require meaningful support acknowledging the emotional weight and relational shifts of caregiving, beyond the child's symptoms. This study aims to shed light into an under-researched condition and offer suggestions for future research which should include broader family perspectives (fathers and siblings) and the development of support systems tailored to the complex needs of this population.

titre: Beyond Observable Behavior: A Narrative Review of Integrated Clinical, Biological, and Functional Assessment in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
titre_fr: Beyond Observable Behavior: A Narrative Review of Integrated Clinical, Biological, and Functional Assessment in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
auteurs: Sanabria Florencia
resume: Assessment of children with autism spectrum disorder must characterize everyday functioning, co-occurring conditions, and individual support needs alongside diagnostic classification. This narrative review examines the evidence and clinical rationale for integrated clinical, biological, and functional assessment in pediatric autism and presents SMART-NB as a proposed framework for organizing these dimensions. The review combines selected clinical guidelines and research publications with conceptual analysis and a targeted literature update, distinguishing established assessment principles from the author-developed framework. Three findings emerge. First, standardized observational instruments contribute to diagnosis but require interpretation alongside developmental history, caregiver information, differential diagnosis, and clinical judgment. Second, co-occurring sleep disturbances, gastrointestinal symptoms, nutritional problems, sensory impairments, and pain can influence behavior and participation and warrant clinically directed evaluation; their association with autism does not establish causation. Third, symptom severity does not fully describe adaptive functioning, supporting assessment across functional domains and everyday contexts. SMART-NB proposes connecting clinical, medical and biological, and demand-related profiles with seven functional domains, individualized goals, and longitudinal reassessment. The demand dimension examines available capacity, physiological and emotional burden, environmental requirements, and supports. Its proposed contribution is to document how assessment findings inform care priorities. Existing multidimensional approaches already address overlapping aspects of this task; the incremental value of this particular organization remains untested. The reviewed evidence supports multidimensional assessment but does not establish the validity, reliability, or clinical utility of SMART-NB. This review is not systematic, and extension beyond autism remains a hypothesis requiring condition-specific evaluation. Development should proceed from operational specification, independent content assessment, and feasibility studies to the evaluation of measurement properties and comparative clinical outcomes.

titre: Quantification of Neuromotor Control in STXBP1-Related Disorders With Wearable Sensors.
titre_fr: Quantification of Neuromotor Control in STXBP1-Related Disorders With Wearable Sensors.
auteurs: Orlando Julie M, Bane Bintou, Chisari Torrey, Magielski Jan H, Pierce Samuel R, Cunningham Kristin Girardi, Woo Charlene, Tefft Sarah, Nolan Joeylynn, Ruggiero Sarah Mckeown, Boland Michael J, McKee Jillian L, Helbig Ingo, Prosser Laura A
resume: STXBP1-related disorders (STXBP1-RD) are a spectrum of neurodevelopmental conditions that present with motor impairments, which include involuntary movements, ataxia, and tremor that have been difficult to measure. The objective of this study was to use wearable sensors to characterize motor control abnormalities in individuals with STXBP1-RD, a spectrum of neurodevelopmental conditions that present with motor impairments affecting motor development. In this study, an exploratory analysis to quantify the clinical features of motor control impairment, including tremor, in 23 individuals with STXBP1-RD was conducted and compared these features with those of 18 typically developing control participants using inertial sensors during a reaching task. Clinical relevance of the sensor-derived metrics of motor control was evaluated in the context of traditional developmental clinical assessments collected during a prospective natural history study. Individuals with STXBP1-RD demonstrated slower reaching time, decreased arm acceleration intensity, less smooth reaching, and tremor frequency characteristics consistent with an unstable or irregular rhythmic movement pattern. More than 65% of individuals with STXBP1-RD presented with tremor in our sample. Combining features from all 4 upper limb sensors predicted tremor with the highest accuracy (area under the curve = 0.87), and multiple motor control metrics were significantly related to developmental assessment scores with reaching duration having the strongest correlation. Our study provides an understanding of motor control in a rare neurodevelopmental disorder and establishes a paradigm to quantify neuromotor control in individuals with developmental differences. Our observations demonstrate significant relations between motor control measures and developmental function, and a tremor prevalence that exceeds twofold what has been reported in historical, retrospective data sets.

Our observations demonstrate significant relations between motor control measures and developmental function, and a tremor prevalence that exceeds twofold what has been reported in historical, retrospective data sets.

titre: Case Report: A severe case of human parechovirus encephalitis in a neonate.
titre_fr: Case Report: A severe case of human parechovirus encephalitis in a neonate.
auteurs: Grimm A M, Heep A, Sentner Christiaan Peter, Fiedler K M
resume: Human parechovirus is a common pathogen causing respiratory and gastroenterological symptoms. Symptoms range from asymptomatic courses to rare encephalitis or sepsis-like symptoms. Studies regarding neurodevelopment after parechovirus encephalitis in infants are conflicting with indications of possible short or long term neurodevelopmental impairments. In this case report we describe an especially severe course of human parechovirus infection. A two-week-old infant presented with fever and developed seizures and apneic episodes after admission. Laboratory tests revealed leukopenia. A lumbar puncture revealed parechovirus via polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Recurrent seizures required extensive anticonvulsive therapy. Invasive ventilation for four days was necessary due to apneic episodes. Cranial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed white matter involvement. In neonates with a sepsis-like presentation and largely unremarkable laboratory and cerebrospinal fluid findings, parechovirus encephalitis is an important differential diagnosis. In this case, follow-up examinations showed age-appropriate neurodevelopment. However, owing to the severe clinical presentation and extensive neuroimaging abnormalities, long-term neurodevelopmental monitoring is warranted.

titre: Prenatal tobacco exposure and visual disorders in children.
titre_fr: Prenatal tobacco exposure and visual disorders in children.
auteurs: Bomze Zuzanna, Babik Karolina, Korniluk Joanna, Woiński Michał, Omidi Sara, Białas-Niedziela Dorota
resume: Maternal smoking during pregnancy is associated with adverse fetal and perinatal outcomes and may also affect visual system development in offspring. Increasing evidence suggests that prenatal tobacco exposure may also be associated with abnormalities of visual system development in children. However, the extent to which these associations reflect direct effects of tobacco exposure versus indirect pathways mediated by adverse perinatal outcomes remains uncertain. This narrative review summarizes the available evidence regarding the association between prenatal tobacco exposure and visual abnormalities in children, with particular emphasis on retinopathy of prematurity, strabismus, refractive errors, retinal nerve fiber layer abnormalities, and optic nerve hypoplasia. The most consistent evidence concerns retinopathy of prematurity and strabismus, although interpretation is complicated by prematurity, fetal growth restriction, neonatal morbidity, and residual confounding. Evidence regarding refractive errors and amblyopia is less consistent, while data on structural visual pathway abnormalities remain limited. Proposed mechanisms include vascular dysfunction, altered cholinergic signaling, oxidative stress, inflammation, and impaired neurodevelopment.Conclusion: Prenatal tobacco exposure may be associated with selected functional and structural abnormalities of the developing visual system. The strength of evidence varies substantially by outcome, and available data do not establish that prenatal tobacco exposure independently causes all reported visual disorders. Future studies should use objective exposure biomarkers, longitudinal designs and analytical approaches that distinguish direct effects from pathways mediated by prematurity and fetal growth restriction. Smoking cessation during pregnancy remains an important preventive intervention.

titre: Impact of altered heme oxygenase-1 in caring for preterm neonates: navigating the unknown.
titre_fr: Impact of altered heme oxygenase-1 in caring for preterm neonates: navigating the unknown.
auteurs: Kim Phoebe, Ozen Maide
resume: Heme-oxygenase-1 (HO-1) is a key regulatory factor in organ development, organ function, cellular metabolism, heme processing, and bilirubin production. HO-1 homeostasis is crucial for healthy pregnancy and fetus. Dysregulation of HO-1 adversely affects placentation, yolk sac development, cardiovascular development, immune function, angiogenesis, microcirculation, alters the oxidoreductive balance, and is associated with adverse respiratory outcomes and necrotizing enterocolitis. The impact of HO-1 on neonatal neurodevelopment is unknown and is currently being investigated by our laboratory. In this review, we will discuss the morbidities associated with HO-1 dysregulation and importantly, we will navigate the unknown. We will highlight how infection or inflammation affect HO-1 homeostasis, its implications on neonatal morbidities at the limits of viability, summarize the relevant basic, translational, clinical and epidemiologic studies. We will conclude with proposing new approaches for the future, filling the gap between what is currently known and unknown. IMPACT: What does this article add to the existing literature? HO-1 pathway is relevant to pregnancy, fetus, neonatal, and later life outcomes. Provides comprehensive organ systems-based evaluation of Heme-oxygenase-1 in pregnancy, fetus, extreme preterm, and periviable neonates. Highlights how environmental factors, including infection, inflammation resulting in systemic dysregulation of HO-1 affects major neonatal morbidities. Underscores that novel investigations to close the knowledge gap are forthcoming to transform the HO-1 field.

titre: Conserved SINE and lineage-variable LINE-1 depletion at neurodevelopmental disorder promoters.
titre_fr: Conserved SINE and lineage-variable LINE-1 depletion at neurodevelopmental disorder promoters.
auteurs: Sevilmiş Can
revue: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
resume: Developmental genes lie in transposon-poor regions, but whether that deficit is a conserved property of the promoters themselves remains unmeasured. Transposable element frequency was compared at neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD) promoters (TSS ±2 kb) in seven primates and two outgroups, contrasting a curated NDD gene set (SFARI and ClinGen; [Formula: see text]) with brain-expressed housekeeping genes ([Formula: see text]). Alu depletion was significant in every primate ([Formula: see text] to [Formula: see text]), including the mouse lemur at 70 Mya. Mouse B1 and B2, SINEs amplified independently of primate Alu, each showed the deficit; the AT-biased Can-SINEs of dog did not. LINE-1 depletion was weak against housekeeping promoters but comparable to or deeper than the SINEs against the genome baseline, and more lineage-variable. The signal survived permutation testing, CpG and GC stratification, and gene-density and recombination controls. It persisted for alignment-defined rather than annotation-defined promoter windows, and against each genome's own baseline in seven of nine, marmoset and dog excepted; the squirrel monkey showed no such exception. Against human controls matched on constraint, brain expression and GC it narrowed but persisted ([Formula: see text]); Alu density does not otherwise track constraint. Windows away from the start site separate two components: the surrounding 250 kb is itself Alu-poor, and a promoter-proximal deficit survives normalisation to it. Depleted promoters coincided with active cis-regulatory elements, preferentially fetal-brain ones. Low promoter SINE content is thus an old feature of NDD-associated loci; whether the elements were never inserted or inserted and later lost is unresolved.

titre: Neonatal brain network integration trajectories predict neurodevelopment in congenital heart disease.
titre_fr: Neonatal brain network integration trajectories predict neurodevelopment in congenital heart disease.
auteurs: Harasymiw Lauren, Kuang Amy, Xu Duan, Scheffler Aaron, George Elizabeth, Peyvandi Shabnam, McQuillen Patrick
resume: Infants with critical congenital heart disease (CHD) are at high risk for abnormal brain development and later neurodevelopmental impairment. We hypothesized that the trajectory of perioperative whole-brain network development would predict neurodevelopmental outcomes in early childhood. This prospective longitudinal cohort of neonates with critical CHD (n = 97) underwent preoperative and/or postoperative brain MRI with diffusion imaging. Whole-brain network measures were derived from structural connectomes from 80 infants, and 50 had neurodevelopment assessed at 1-4 years using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development. White matter injury was associated with a slower perioperative increase in global efficiency (p = 0.013), a measure of network integration, whereas cardiac physiology was not associated with network development. Infants with greater perioperative increases in global efficiency had higher cognitive (p = 0.001), language (p < 0.001), and motor (p = 0.008) scores. For each 1-standard deviation increase in the trajectory of global efficiency, cognitive scores increased by 8.2 points (95% CI: 3.64-12.78), independent of brain injury and socioeconomic factors. In infants with critical CHD, longitudinal whole-brain network development was associated with neurodevelopment across multiple domains. Early network development may serve as a biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience in this population. In infants with critical congenital heart disease, perioperative increase in whole-brain network integration was associated with cognitive, language, and motor outcomes in early childhood. White matter injury was associated with a slower increase in network integration, whereas cardiac physiology subtype was not associated with network development. This study extends prior work by showing that a longitudinal measure of neonatal whole-brain network development, rather than a single imaging timepoint, predicts neurodevelopment across multiple domains. These findings identify early network development as a potential biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience, and support future risk-stratification and intervention studies in this population.

titre: Associations between Prenatal Exposure to Perchlorate, Thiocyanate, and Nitrate and Child Neurodevelopment in the MARBLES Study.
titre_fr: Associations between Prenatal Exposure to Perchlorate, Thiocyanate, and Nitrate and Child Neurodevelopment in the MARBLES Study.
auteurs: Jang Hyuna, Bennett Deborah H, Tancredi Daniel J, Schmidt Rebecca J, Shin Hyeong-Moo
resume: Associations between prenatal exposure to perchlorate, thiocyanate, and nitrate and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) remain largely unexplored. We investigated these associations in the MARBLES cohort, a prospective cohort with an elevated familial likelihood of ASD. A total of 310 mothers provided 1916 urine samples during pregnancy, and their children were classified at age 3 years as typically developing (TD), ASD, or non-TD (developmental concerns not meeting ASD diagnostic criteria). We estimated relative risks for ASD and non-TD compared with TD using Poisson regression and assessed mixture effects using quantile G-computation and Bayesian kernel machine regression. Overall and mixture analyses showed no significant associations between prenatal exposure to these NIS inhibitors and the child neurodevelopmental outcomes. However, stratified analyses identified several context-specific associations according to child sex, trimester of exposure, maternal urinary iodine concentration, and passive smoking status, some of which remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. These findings suggest that susceptibility to prenatal exposure to perchlorate, thiocyanate, and nitrate may vary across population subgroups and exposure windows. Although these subgroup-specific associations should be considered hypothesis generating, they highlight the need for future studies integrating thyroid biomarkers and mechanistic approaches to better understand thyroid-related pathways underlying child neurodevelopment.

titre: Reconceptualising ADHD as a neurobiological spectrum: calibration-based perspective.
titre_fr: Reconceptualising ADHD as a neurobiological spectrum: calibration-based perspective.
auteurs: Kazgan Kılıçaslan Aslı
resume: Although attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) diagnosis requires a categorical decision, phenotypic, twin and molecular genetic evidence indicates that ADHD traits are continuously distributed, with clinical ADHD at the functionally impairing end of this distribution. This paper proposes conceptualising ADHD as a neurobiological spectrum while treating categorical and dimensional approaches as complementary. A calibration perspective is proposed to describe graded differences in the regulation of attention, arousal, motivation and cognitive control, and their context-dependent expression. Genetic findings support dimensional continuity, whereas neurobiological and cognitive findings are consistent with graded regulatory variation. Functional impairment remains central to translating this dimensional framework into diagnosis and treatment decisions.

titre: Prescribing psychostimulants for persons with schizophrenia spectrum disorders and attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder: practice with little guidance.
titre_fr: Prescribing psychostimulants for persons with schizophrenia spectrum disorders and attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder: practice with little guidance.
auteurs: Simpson Alexander I F, Picco Corina Ziara Dubon, Agid Ofer, Jones Roland M
resume: Psychostimulant prescribing for individuals with comorbid attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder and schizophrenia spectrum disorders appears increasingly common despite limited evidence to guide the practice. This commentary highlights diagnostic and treatment challenges, critiques the current evidence base and argues for cautious prescribing, greater attention to substance use and the development of pragmatic clinical guidance.

titre: Do psychiatrists have a spider-sense? Clinical impressions as violations of interpersonal Bayesian expectation.
titre_fr: Do psychiatrists have a spider-sense? Clinical impressions as violations of interpersonal Bayesian expectation.
auteurs: Amad Ali, D'Hondt Fabien, Gauld Christophe, Bertoux Maxime, Daoudi Mohamed, Fovet Thomas
resume: Psychiatric diagnosis depends on the clinician's ability to infer mental states from complex and dynamically evolving interpersonal signals. During the psychiatric interview, clinicians do not only collect explicit symptoms; they continuously sample a rich array of non-verbal and paralinguistic cues including gaze, prosody, affective reciprocity, and interactional timing. These signals are central to psychiatric assessment, yet their contribution to diagnostic reasoning remains poorly formalized. In this Review, we propose a computational account of clinical impressions in psychiatry. We integrate evidence from phenomenological psychopathology, social cognition, and computational neuroscience. We argue that such impressions may arise when the clinician's generative model of social interaction is persistently disconfirmed by subtle deviations in interpersonal behaviour, generating high-level social prediction errors experienced as a sense of incongruity or failed attunement. We formalize this process as VIBE: Violation of Interpersonal Bayesian Expectation. VIBE denotes a pre-reflective epistemic signal generated when observed interpersonal cues deviate from the clinician's expected model of social reciprocity. It is not a diagnostic criterion but orients hypothesis generation by drawing attention to disturbances in interpersonal predictability. We hypothesize that VIBE may constitute a transdiagnostic mechanism: different disorders, from schizophrenia to autism spectrum disorder and mood disorders, may disrupt distinct dimensions of interpersonal prediction. The Praecox Feeling, first described by Rümke in 1942, can be read as the earliest clinical formalization of this process and as its schizophrenia-spectrum instance, in which the profile of interpersonal violations is consistent enough to be clinically recognizable. This framework recasts the diagnostic impression as an embodied inferential process rather than an opaque subjective faculty. Teaching clinicians to articulate, examine, and recalibrate these impressions could strengthen diagnostic reasoning, reduce bias, and improve therapeutic attunement. VIBE provides a bridge between phenomenological psychopathology and computational neuroscience, and offers a tractable, empirically testable model for studying the neurocomputational basis of psychiatric clinical judgement.

titre: Effect of Probiotics on GI Symptom Management in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Trials.
titre_fr: Effect of Probiotics on GI Symptom Management in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Trials.
auteurs: Bagui Soumili, Nanda Ashutosh, Dey Gargi
resume: Autism spectrum disorder has increased worldwide over the past few decades. Medical comorbidities are common in patients with ASD, with gastrointestinal (GI) diseases being especially common. Involvement of the gut-brain axis that communicates between the enteric and central nervous systems has been confirmed by several studies that have reported abnormal microbiota profiles in ASD subjects. In this review, a systematic database search was conducted. Six trials were included in the subgroup analysis that compared probiotic therapy with single or multiple strains to a placebo with respect to gastrointestinal severity index. The pooled effect size model revealed a slight decrease in gastrointestinal symptoms that favored probiotic supplementation (SMD = -0.189; 95% CI = -0.398 to 0.020; Z = -1.773, p = 0.07; I<sup>2</sup> = 39.4%). There was a moderate level of heterogeneity among the included studies. Additionally, the effects of single-strain and multiple-strain probiotic formulations were compared to their respective placebo groups using subgroup analysis. The results demonstrated that single-strain probiotic medication reduced gastrointestinal symptoms when compared to the placebo group. However, there was no statistically significant difference between multiple-strain probiotic therapy and a placebo. To accurately establish the therapeutic effects of probiotics on ASD, more randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies are required.

titre: The Association Between Cognitive Flexibility and Eating Behaviors in Autistic Women With Eating Disorders.
titre_fr: The Association Between Cognitive Flexibility and Eating Behaviors in Autistic Women With Eating Disorders.
auteurs: Schröder Sabrina S, Danner Unna N, Spek Annelies, Elburg Annemarie van
resume: Reduced cognitive flexibility is a trait associated with autism and has also been implicated in eating disorders (EDs). However, most studies have not distinguished between autistic and non-autistic individuals in ED samples, potentially obscuring group-specific patterns. This study investigated self-reported cognitive flexibility and its association with eating behaviors (traditional ED pathology and ARFID symptomatology) across four groups: autistic women with EDs (ASD + ED), non-autistic women with EDs (ED), autistic women without EDs (ASD), and non-autistic controls. Participants included 30 ASD + ED, 30 ED, 29 ASD, and 60 control women (N = 149). All completed the Detail and Flexibility Questionnaire (DFlex), the Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire (EDE-Q), and the Nine Item ARFID Screen (NIAS). Group comparisons were conducted on self-reported cognitive flexibility (cognitive rigidity, attention to detail), ED pathology, and ARFID symptoms. Associations between cognitive flexibility and eating behaviors were examined across and within groups. ASD + ED and ASD groups showed significantly greater difficulties in self-reported cognitive flexibility than ED and control groups, which did not differ from each other. Associations between self-reported cognitive flexibility and eating behaviors varied across groups, with attention to detail showing the clearest pattern. Attention to detail was associated with ED pathology in the ASD + ED group and with ARFID symptomatology in the ASD + ED, ASD, and control groups, but not in the ED group. These exploratory findings suggest that self-reported cognitive inflexibility may be more strongly associated with autism than with EDs alone and highlight the importance of considering co-occurring autism when examining cognitive characteristics in ED populations. This study explored how cognitive traits - like attention to detail - relate to eating behaviors in autistic and non-autistic women with and without eating disorders. Findings suggest that certain thinking patterns may be more closely linked to autism than to eating disorders alone, underscoring the need for greater clinical awareness of autism-specific features when assessing and supporting individuals with disordered eating.

titre: Training Physicians to Prevent Diversion of Stimulant Medication for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial in Pediatric Primary Care.
titre_fr: Training Physicians to Prevent Diversion of Stimulant Medication for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial in Pediatric Primary Care.
auteurs: Molina Brooke S G, Kipp Heidi L, Pedersen Sarah L, Kolko David J, Lindstrom Rachel A, Bauer Daniel J, Howard Andrea L, Joseph Heather M
resume: ObjectivesEvidence-based methods to deter the misuse of stimulant medications for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) are lacking. Diversion is the most common means by which stimulants are obtained for non-medical use and prevention should begin early. The current study is the first randomized controlled trial testing whether brief training of pediatricians in Stimulant Diversion Prevention (SDP) can reduce diversion by their adolescent patients with ADHD.MethodsA cluster-randomized controlled trial was conducted across seven pediatric practices in the U.S. (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03080259). A detailed description of the study protocol is provided as well as results for pre-registered primary and secondary outcomes.ResultsThirty-two prescribing providers, 357 adolescent patients, and one parent or guardian for each patient participated. Three practices were randomly assigned to training, and four waves of electronic surveys were administered to all participants (at baseline and 6-, 12-, and 18-months post-training) with high retention (e.g., 89%-97% of providers, 92%-96% of patients). Methods for recruitment and retention and provider and staff training were successful: planned sample size at baseline was exceeded by 12% for providers and was 95% of planned patients; planned retention at 18-months was exceeded by 21% for providers and by 10% for patients; 99% of the patients' providers received training. Patient diversion, however, was infrequent at baseline, with only one endorsement in the treatment-as-usual (TAU) group and none in the SDP group. Diversion remained infrequent across follow-ups (6.7% TAU; 3.7% SDP), rendering tests of group differences under-powered for trustworthy statistical comparisons. Group differences were not found for any pre-registered a priori primary or secondary outcomes; one exploratory group difference emerged: perceived negative social consequences of diversion was higher among patients whose providers were trained.ConclusionsPediatric practices can be successfully recruited, retained, and trained with a brief workshop on stimulant diversion prevention with, as previously reported, high rates of satisfaction and sustained implementation. Future research might benefit from focusing on older adolescent samples to assess proximal effects of physician training on stimulant diversion. Longitudinal follow-up into early adulthood of the adolescent patients in this study might reveal later-emerging benefits of the SDP training.

titre: Genetic Liability to Psychiatric Disorder and Risk of Musculoskeletal Diseases: A Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization Study.
titre_fr: Genetic Liability to Psychiatric Disorder and Risk of Musculoskeletal Diseases: A Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization Study.
auteurs: Luo Xiaohai, Wu Ning, Wang Zhaofu, Ma Jingzu, Zhang Xiaoyu
resume: Psychiatric disorders, particularly major depressive disorder (MDD), are increasingly recognized as systemic diseases that may predispose individuals to a range of physical comorbidities. Epidemiological studies have reported associations between depression and musculoskeletal diseases; however, causal inferences remain limited due to confounding factors and reverse causation. This study aims to investigate the bidirectional causal relationships between common psychiatric disorders and musculoskeletal outcomes using a Mendelian randomization (MR) framework. A bidirectional two-sample MR analysis was conducted using summary statistics from a large-scale genome-wide association study (GWAS) in European ancestry populations. Genetic instruments for seven psychiatric disorders were obtained from the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium, while musculoskeletal outcomes were sourced from the IEU Open GWAS and UK Biobank. Causal effects were primarily estimated using an inverse variance weighted model, with sensitivity analyses conducted using the weighted median (WM) and MR-Egger methods. Established diagnostic methods were employed to assess horizontal pleiotropy, heterogeneity, and robustness, and false discovery rate (FDR) corrections were applied to account for multiple testing. The genetic liability to MDD showed the most consistent evidence of association with osteoarthritis (OA) and osteomyelitis (OM). The association with OA appeared to be the most stable overall, while the findings regarding OM should be interpreted more cautiously due to the relatively limited number of available instrumental variables. Nominal associations were also observed for fracture and osteoporosis (OP) in relation to MDD, as well as between autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and fracture risk and between anorexia nervosa (AN) and fracture risk; however, these findings were either modest in magnitude or did not remain significant after multiple-testing correction, and thus should be considered exploratory results. There was no strong evidence supporting a reverse causal effect of musculoskeletal diseases on psychiatric disorders. This MR study suggests that genetic liability to MDD may be associated with susceptibility to specific musculoskeletal diseases, particularly OA, and more cautiously, OM. These findings should be interpreted with caution, especially for associations based on limited instrumental support or modest effect sizes, and require replication in different populations.

titre: Association Among Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index, Vitamin D Status and Clinical Subtypes of ADHD: A Retrospective Investigation.
titre_fr: Association Among Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index, Vitamin D Status and Clinical Subtypes of ADHD: A Retrospective Investigation.
auteurs: Lu Tingting, Chen Yingying, Hu Feiping, Zhu Yingping
resume: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has been linked to immune dysregulation and nutritional imbalance. The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) is a composite inflammatory marker, while serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) reflects vitamin D status. Their joint association with paediatric ADHD remains incompletely characterised. In this retrospective case-control study, 78 treatment-naïve children with ADHD and 40 non-ADHD outpatient comparison children selected using frequency matching by age and sex were included. The most recent laboratory results available in the outpatient record were extracted. Given that some 25(OH)D values were derived from reports obtained outside our hospital, all available 25(OH)D records were manually re-checked against source documents and standardised to ng/mL prior to analysis. Group comparisons, whole-sample Spearman correlation analyses, logistic regression models including an interaction term between standardised SII and standardised 25(OH)D and exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed. Sensitivity analysis and Firth penalised logistic regression were additionally conducted. Compared with the comparison group, children with ADHD had significantly higher SII, C-reactive protein (CRP), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) levels, together with lower serum 25(OH)D. The ADHD group was more likely to fall into lower clinically defined 25(OH)D categories, whereas the comparison group was more frequently in the ≥30 ng/mL category; this pattern remained directionally consistent after stratification by season of blood draw. In the whole study sample, SII was positively correlated with attention, impulsivity and oppositional scores, whereas serum 25(OH)D was inversely correlated with these symptom dimensions; SII was also inversely correlated with 25(OH)D. In the parsimonious model, the interaction term between standardised SII and standardised 25(OH)D was statistically significant (odds ratio (OR) = 3.06, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.59-6.80, p = 0.002), and it remained significant in the broader sensitivity model and Firth penalised regression. In exploratory within-sample analysis, ROC curves yielded area under curves (AUCs) of 0.808 for SII, 0.781 for serum 25(OH)D and 0.836 for the parsimonious multivariable model. Paediatric ADHD was associated with high inflammatory burden and low serum 25(OH)D status in this retrospective outpatient sample. The statistically significant interaction between SII and 25(OH)D suggests a stable pattern of effect modification on the logistic model scale. These findings support a potentially relevant immuno-nutritional pattern in ADHD, but prospective validation is needed before causal interpretation or clinical implementation can be considered.

titre: The Big Move: Predictors of Residential Status and Age at Leaving the Family Home in Adults With Neurodevelopmental Disabilities.
titre_fr: The Big Move: Predictors of Residential Status and Age at Leaving the Family Home in Adults With Neurodevelopmental Disabilities.
auteurs: Singer Hannah, Clarke Elaine B, Lord Catherine
revue: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
resume: Living arrangements play essential roles in the lives of adults with autism and neurodevelopmental disabilities (NDDs). Many individuals with NDDs face challenges transitioning from the family home to long-term independent or supported living arrangements, but few studies have examined the ages at which residential transitions may occur within NDD adulthood, nor how residential transition ages differ by co-occurring intellectual disability (ID) status. This study examined predictors of residential status and residential transition ages among 134 American adults (52% with ID) diagnosed with NDDs, primarily autism, in childhood. Kaplan-Meier survival analyses revealed 37% of participants with ID moved from the family home by their mid-30s (predominantly to supported living), compared to 69% without ID (predominantly to independent living). Cox models indicated higher family income and irritability (behavioral difficulties) predicted earlier-aged transitions among participants with ID; these effects were stronger at younger ages. For participants without ID, greater autistic behaviors predicted later-aged transitions; these effects strengthened with age. Findings point to potential "windows of opportunity" to transition to independent or supported living between ages 18 and 22, though these windows may differ by adult symptom and family income profiles. Needs for early-aged, equitable access to residential planning services are discussed.Lay AbstractHousing is a major part of daily life. This study investigated the ages at which adults with autism or neurodevelopmental disabilities (NDDs) leave the family home to move into longer-term supported or independent living settings, and how those pathways differ for those with and without co-occurring intellectual disability (ID). Among 134 American adults diagnosed with NDDs (mostly autism) in childhood, 37% of participants with co-occurring ID had moved by roughly their mid-30s (predominantly to supported living, for example, group homes), compared to 69% of those without ID (predominantly to independent living). Different factors were linked to moving at different ages. Among people with ID, those with higher family income and those with more irritability (behavioral challenges) were more likely to move out earlier, especially around ages 18 to 22. Among people without ID, those with greater autistic behaviors tended to move later in adulthood; this pattern became stronger with age. These findings suggest neurodivergent adults with different support needs follow unique pathways to moving out of the family home, and that both individual traits, such as irritability and autistic behaviors, and family financial assets may shape these pathways in complex ways. However, for both adults with and without ID, there may be key "windows of opportunity" for moving out in early adulthood (around ages 18-22). These results highlight the need for more numerous and flexible supported housing models, and for equitable and earlier-aged access to supports (such as functional skills supports) that help adults with NDDs both with and without ID to make transitions to supported and independent living if and when they desire them.

titre: Psychosocial difficulties in children of parents with epilepsy: A pilot case-control study.
titre_fr: Psychosocial difficulties in children of parents with epilepsy: A pilot case-control study.
auteurs: Helvacı Çelik Fatma Gül, Aktaş Yunus Emre, Şahin Berkan, Korkmaz Ulaş, Şeker Demet
resume: Epilepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that may affect family functioning. Although the psychosocial impact on children of parents with several chronic medical and neurological disorders has been studied, a notable gap remains regarding epilepsy. This pilot study aimed to examine psychosocial outcomes in children aged 6-17 years whose parents have epilepsy and to explore emotional and behavioral difficulties within a multifactorial framework. This observational pilot case-control study was conducted between 2023 and 2025 at neurology departments in Giresun and Erzurum. The epilepsy group (n = 45) was compared with a control group (n = 48) recruited from the same hospitals for non neurological reasons. Assessments included the Conners Parent Rating Scale (CPRS), Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), and Perceived Stress Scale (PSS), analyzed as continuous measures. Small sample size and risk of model overfitting precluded multivariable covariate adjustment; the Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate procedure was applied to account for multiple testing. Children of parents with epilepsy had higher rates of chronic medical conditions and ADHD diagnoses than controls. They also had higher SDQ emotional symptoms and hyperactivity/inattention scores, as well as higher CPRS total and problem related subscale scores. No significant between group differences were observed in total SDQ or PSS scores. In exploratory analyses by parental gender, children of fathers with epilepsy had higher SDQ total, emotional, and hyperactivity/inattention scores, as well as higher CPRS total and executive functioning scores. Fathers with epilepsy also reported higher PSS scores than mothers with epilepsy. Longer breastfeeding duration was inversely associated with CPRS total, hyperactivity/impulsivity, conduct, and peer relationship scores. Children of parents with epilepsy showed differences in selected emotional and behavioral domains rather than global psychosocial impairment. Exploratory findings related to parental gender and breastfeeding duration should be interpreted cautiously. The small, non probability sample, baseline group differences, inability to control for key epilepsy specific clinical characteristics because of sample size constraints, limited assessment of epilepsy related factors, and potential residual confounding limit causal interpretation and generalizability. These preliminary, hypothesis generating findings warrant confirmation in larger longitudinal studies incorporating multiple informants and family related factors.

titre: Genetic and Biological Pathways Underlying the Relations between Executive Functioning and Externalizing Behaviors.
titre_fr: Genetic and Biological Pathways Underlying the Relations between Executive Functioning and Externalizing Behaviors.
auteurs: Spychala Kellyn M, Miller Alex P, Friedman Naomi P, Gizer Ian R
revue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
resume: Across phenotypic and genotypic studies, executive functioning (EF) has been shown to be associated with externalizing behaviors, including attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), aggression, and substance use, and is a proposed underlying mechanism of these behaviors. However, there is limited research on the shared biological mechanisms underpinning EF and externalizing behaviors, including their overlap at the level of genomic regions. The current study used genome-wide association study summary statistics of EF, ADHD, aggressive behavior, alcohol use, and alcohol use disorder to examine whether the heritability of these traits or the co-heritability between them is enriched for genes expressed in particular tissues or stratified by other annotation types. Additionally, the study examined the genomic regions contributing to the covariation between EF and the externalizing traits to identify genetic variants and genes that may be underlying their overlap. First, across all phenotypes, there was evidence for enrichment of genetic signals in DNase hypersensitive sites and H3K4me1 regions, and significant enrichment among genes expressed in the anterior cingulate cortex and frontal cortex. Second, when combining results across regional methods, there was evidence for associations between EF and each of the externalizing behaviors in regions on chromosomes 1, 11, and 15. These findings highlight biological pathways that may link the relations between EF and externalizing behaviors and provides additional evidence of EF as an underlying mechanism of externalizing behavior.

titre: Longitudinal trajectories of ADHD symptoms: relationships to early-childhood predictors and later outcomes.
titre_fr: Longitudinal trajectories of ADHD symptoms: relationships to early-childhood predictors and later outcomes.
auteurs: Rounds Emily, Kozlowski Michael, McCormack Shane, Ryabinin Peter, Nousen Elizabeth, Tipsord Jessica, Dieckmann Nathan F, Karalunas Sarah L, Herting Megan M, Faraone Stephen V, Nikolas Molly, Nigg Joel T, Mooney Michael A
revue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
resume: ADHD symptoms follow heterogeneous trajectories across childhood and adolescence, with important implications for later functioning. Early-life factors, including perinatal health, family environment, cognition, socioeconomic conditions, and community exposures, may contribute to this variability. The present study examined (1) early-life predictors of ADHD symptom trajectories, and (2) ADHD symptom trajectories as predictors of later substance use, suicidality, and new-onset psychiatric disorders. Growth models were used to fit longitudinal trajectories of inattention, hyperactivity, and irritability measures in two independent samples: the Oregon ADHD-1000 cohort (N=1,215; 49.17% ADHD; 39.9% female, ages 7-23) and a subsample of the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study (N=1,252; 33.3% ADHD; 31.6% female, ages 9-16). Regression analyses examined multiple risk factors as predictors of symptom growth parameters as well as associations between symptom trajectories and later adverse outcomes. In both cohorts, growth models fit well (CFI > .96, RMSEA < .04), with all symptoms decreasing over time ( p s < .001) and hyperactivity declining significantly faster than inattention. ADHD polygenic risk, family conflict, parenting, and cognition were associated with symptom intercepts in both cohorts ( p s < .001). In Oregon ADHD-1000, poorer baseline working memory and processing speed predicted slower declines in inattention ( p s < .001), but these effects did not replicate in ABCD; no other early-life factors predicted symptom trajectories. Increasing irritability trajectories predicted new disorder onset in both cohorts (ORs = 1.73-2.09, ps < .001), while more positive inattention slopes predicted new disorder onset in ABCD (OR = 3.07, p < .001) and showed a weaker association in Oregon ADHD-1000 (OR = 1.50, p = .007). While several early risk factors were associated with ADHD symptoms initially, none robustly predicted symptom trajectories over time. However, increasing irritability and inattention were robustly associated with increased risk for new disorder onsets later in adolescence. - ADHD symptoms decrease over time on average, with hyperactivity demonstrating the highest rate of decline.- ADHD polygenic risk, family conflict, parental stress, parenting style, and cognition were strongly associated with symptom levels at intercept, but no replicable associations between early-life risk factors and change in symptoms over time (slopes) were observed.- Irritability slope was robustly associated with new disorder onsets.

titre: Paired-pulse tactile stimulation enhances tactile perception in neurotypical but not autistic children.
titre_fr: Paired-pulse tactile stimulation enhances tactile perception in neurotypical but not autistic children.
auteurs: Balabanovska Matea, He Jason L, Powell Helen J, Edden Richard A E, Mostofsky Stewart H, Puts Nicolaas A
resume: Tactile sensory differences are common in autism. Sensory gating, a mechanism by which perception is filtered, is of relevance, yet it is unknown if atypical sensory filtering in autistic people directly impacts the perception of sensory stimuli. In this study we used a novel psychophysical protocol to examine the effect of pre-pulse sub-threshold stimulation on tactile detection thresholds in 8-12 year old autistic (n = 24) and neurotypical (n = 51) children. We used two pre-pulse conditions with either a 30 ms or 100 ms interval. We hypothesised, based on prior work, that sub-threshold stimulation would worsen detection threshold in neurotypical controls whereas the effect of sub-threshold stimulation would be absent in autism. We further hypothesised that the absence of gating would correlate with autism outcomes. Contrary to these expectations, we observed that both pre-pulse stimulation conditions significantly improved detection thresholds in neurotypical children but not autistic children. titre: Childhood adversity contributes more strongly than cognition to transdiagnostic mental health symptoms in young adults.
titre_fr: Childhood adversity contributes more strongly than cognition to transdiagnostic mental health symptoms in young adults.
auteurs: Komarnyckyj Mica, Litwinczuk Marta, Shepherd Ryan, Banaschewski Tobias, Bokde Arun L W, Brühl Rüdiger, Desrivières Sylvane, Flor Herta, Gowland Penny, Grigis Antoine, Heinz Andreas, Nees Frauke, Orfanos Dimitri Papadopoulos, Poustka Luise, Smolka Michael N, Holz Nathalie, Vaidya Nilakshi, Walter Henrik, Whelan Robert, Wirsching Paul, Schumann Gunter, Elliott Rebecca
resume: Childhood adversity is associated with a broad range of mental health problems and may contribute to transdiagnostic risk via effects on cognitive development. However, it remains unclear how adversity and cognition jointly contribute to symptoms. Using the IMAGEN community sample (n = 827, mean age = 18.5), we examined cross-sectional associations between adversity, cognition and current symptoms in young adults. Three partial least squares regression models were compared: Adversity-only (threat and deprivation derived from Childhood Trauma Questionnaire); Cognition-only (CANTAB® performance); and combined Adversity-and-Cognition. When modelling symptoms across nine disorders, adversity emerged as the dominant predictor; the Adversity-and-Cognition model provided only modest improvement over Adversity-only for within-sample (R² = 0.189 vs 0.181) and out-of-sample predictive performance (R² = 0.056 vs 0.054). Adversity-and-Cognition showed a disorder-specific predictive value for depression, conduct disorder and hyperactivity/inattention (ADHD symptoms). However, for social phobia, specific phobia, agoraphobia, OCD and PTSD, incorporating cognition did not improve predictive performance beyond adversity alone.

titre: Cellular and molecular census of the pleiotropic disease locus Negr1 in zebrafish.
titre_fr: Cellular and molecular census of the pleiotropic disease locus Negr1 in zebrafish.
auteurs: González-Suarez Andrés, Pola-Morell Laura, López-Schier Hernán
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: A major challenge in precision medicine is to understand the cellular origin of disease-causing genetic alterations. One prominent example is the Negr1 locus , where common non-coding variants are associated with an unusually broad range of human traits and conditions, including body mass index (BMI), major depression, schizophrenia, autism-spectrum conditions and anorexia. Yet, no coding loss-of-function allele has been established as causal. These observations suggest that distinct Negr1 -expressing cell populations underlie distinct traits. However, this hypothesis is difficult to test in tractable experimental systems without first determining where this gene may act. To overcome this limitation, we generated a knock-in reporter at the zebrafish Negr1 locus and combined single-cell transcriptomics with whole-brain registration and single-neuron projection mapping. We found that Negr1 is expressed in a graded manner across neuronal classes of the brain and retina, radial glia and astrocyte-like cells, and most consistently in oligodendrocyte progenitor cells. Projection mapping suggests three conserved hubs formed by olfactory bulb projection neurons, tectal periventricular projection neurons and cerebellar eurydendroid cells. Our findings are consistent with the idea that Negr1 pleiotropy arises from dose perturbation of a rather broadly expressed gene. More generally, this integrative approach to produce granular multimodal datasets should enable high-resolution etiological studies in models of human disease.

titre: Spatiotemporal AI modeling of gene regulation and variant effects in the developing human brain.
titre_fr: Spatiotemporal AI modeling of gene regulation and variant effects in the developing human brain.
auteurs: Hao Yun, Park Christopher Y, Theesfeld Chandra T, Troyanskaya Olga G
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: Understanding how genetic variation shapes gene regulation in the developing human brain remains a central challenge in neuroscience, particularly in transient cell types and developmental stages where data are limited. We present Seal, an interpretable AI transfer learning framework for genome-based modeling of gene expression and variant effects with spatiotemporal resolution across 26 brain regions, 30 cell types, and seven developmental stages. Seal predictions enable characterization of both germline and somatic brain variants, and provide mechanistic interpretation by linking sequence variants to transcriptional regulators in spatiotemporal context. Applying Seal to genome-wide association studies, we identify cell types and developmental windows relevant to neuropsychiatric disease risk, revealing shared and distinct regulatory architectures across six neuropsychiatric conditions that align with clinical trajectories. In the Simons Simplex Collection autism cohort whole genome data, Seal uncovers a significant burden of de novo regulatory variants in transient fetal excitatory neurons, revealing a cell-type and developmentally specific regulatory burden. By connecting genetic variation to spatiotemporal regulatory programs, Seal offers a general framework for uncovering mechanisms of human brain development and disease.
