titre: Tonotopic mapping in children shows an overrepresentation of high frequencies in autism.
titre_fr: Tonotopic mapping in children shows an overrepresentation of high frequencies in autism.
auteurs: Chen Bosi, Boxberger Alexandra, Mahmalji Judy, Do Tess, Herrera Meagan, Tuy Sabrena, De Oliveira Campos Giovanna Arantes, Sereno Martin I, Fishman Inna, Linke Annika C
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: Altered sensitivity to sounds despite normal peripheral hearing is common in neurodevelopmental disorders but the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we investigate tonotopic organization in 86 children (6-11 years) with autism spectrum and related neurodevelopmental disorders as well as typically developing (TD) peers, using a child-friendly, passive listening, functional magnetic resonance imaging design. In TD children, tonotopic maps in primary auditory cortex resembled the typical high-low-high frequency gradients previously reported in adults, while children with autism showed an overrepresentation of high frequencies consistent with what has been observed in animal models of autism. Higher frequency tuning further correlated with greater caregiver-reported sound but not touch sensitivities. Importantly, tonotopy is a core organizational feature of auditory cortex that develops early in life and remains relatively stable after the critical period of heightened plasticity ends. Thus, these results suggest that atypical auditory processing in autism may result from early disruption to tonotopic map formation. Longitudinal neuroimaging studies are needed to understand the genetic and environmental causes of altered auditory cortex topology and its long-term consequences for higher-level auditory, language, and social communication development.

titre: Synaptic density imaging associates with performance but not self-report in autism.
titre_fr: Synaptic density imaging associates with performance but not self-report in autism.
auteurs: Naples Adam J, Cayir Salih, Cukar-Capizzi Christine, Wolf Julie M, McClelland Jenna E, Robertson Emma C, Sawant Shivani S, Matuskey David, McPartland James C
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: Autism is a common neurodevelopmental condition with considerable between-person variability and unknown biological etiology. Diagnosis of autism in adults relies on measurement of performance (e.g., clinician rating of social behavior, standardized assessment of cognition) and self-report of autism features. Our prior work revealed a strong relationship between clinician ratings of social function in autism and in vivo measures of synaptic density as measured by [ 11 C]UCB-J PET (Matuskey et al., 2025). However, it is not understood how the measured aspects of the autism phenotype index underlying biology. Here, in a sample of 12 autistic adults, we address this question by relating synaptic density imaging to a range of performance measures, such as cognition and face recognition, in contrast to self-report measures. Our results identify a dissociation between these measurement types in that synaptic density correlates strongly with measures of performance but shows virtually no relationship with self-report. These findings suggest that, while self-report and performance measures share variance in characterizing phenotypes in autism, they diverge when mapping onto the underlying biology. Results suggest that higher synaptic density may index a general mechanism that facilitates social and cognitive performance across a range of tasks. These data also indicate that performance and self-report measures are not interchangeable in capturing brain-behavior correspondences in autism, a finding that can guide measure selection in future biomarker studies and clinical research.

titre: Identifying Register-Based Severity Trajectories in Anorexia Nervosa: Associations with Polygenic Scores, Psychiatric and Somatic Conditions.
titre_fr: Identifying Register-Based Severity Trajectories in Anorexia Nervosa: Associations with Polygenic Scores, Psychiatric and Somatic Conditions.
auteurs: Abdulkadir Mohamed, Larsen Janne Tidselbak, Zhang Zi-Ping, Clausen Loa, Musliner Katherine L, Bulik Cynthia M, Petersen Liselotte Vogdrup, Yilmaz Zeynep
revue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
resume: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a severe metabo-psychiatric disorder with heterogeneous outcomes and elevated mortality. Characterizing severity trajectories may improve early risk stratification and targeted intervention. To identify AN severity trajectories using a register-based severity index (AN-RSI) and examine their associations with polygenic scores (PGS), preceding (prior to AN diagnosis) as well as subsequent (5 years post AN diagnosis) psychiatric and somatic disorders. Population-based cohort study. Nationwide study in Denmark. Individuals born between 1969 and 2013 with diagnosed AN (N = 9,534 individuals). Genetic data were available in a subsample comprising 5,126 individuals. Forty-one PGS indexing traits relevant to AN, and psychiatric and somatic disorders prior to AN diagnosis. The main outcomes of interest were the AN-RSI trajectories and psychiatric and somatic disorders 5 years post AN diagnosis. Three trajectories were identified: "low and stable" (32.6%), "medium and stable" (53.5%), and "high increasing" (14.0%). The "low and stable" group was used as the comparison group for all analyses. Each 1 standard deviation (SD) increase in AN PGS corresponded with 13% greater odds of following the "high increasing" trajectory. Increases in BMI and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder PGS corresponded with 15% and 14% lower odds of following the "high increasing" trajectory, respectively. No preceding psychiatric or somatic disorders were significantly associated with trajectory assignment. In contrast, psychiatric and somatic disorders were more likely to occur subsequent to an AN diagnosis in those in the "high increasing" trajectory with odds ratios (OR) ranging between 1.73 and 3.81 for psychiatric disorders and between 1.61 and 5.38 for somatic disorders with a notable exception of obesity which showed a lower OR of 0.27. Our findings hold significant clinical relevance by demonstrating that individuals with AN follow distinct severity trajectories that have different genetic risk as measured by PGS and clear differences in post-diagnosis morbidity patterns but no discernable differences in pre-diagnosis psychiatric or somatic morbidity As the eating disorders genetics field progresses, incorporating PGS into comprehensive assessments at first presentation may aid in early identification, personalized intervention, and resource allocation for individuals at higher risk of developing a severe illness trajectory. Question: Do patients with anorexia nervosa follow distinct severity trajectories that are associated with specific genetic and morbidity risks?Findings: In this register-based study we identified three severity trajectories of anorexia nervosa. Those who followed the most severe illness trajectory had greater genetic liability to both lower body weight and anorexia nervosa and were at greater risk of developing subsequent psychiatric and somatic disorders.Meaning: Illness severity trajectories in anorexia nervosa marked by genetic risk may assist in early identification and intervention for those at greatest risk of severe illness course.

titre: Dose dependent impact of global Cc2d1a reduction on cognitive, social, and metabolic phenotypes.
titre_fr: Dose dependent impact of global Cc2d1a reduction on cognitive, social, and metabolic phenotypes.
auteurs: Heller Abigail T, Bhattacharya Aniket, Routray Pallavi, Rauf Shanzeh, Uppalapati Vinitha, Suzuki Emma, Weiss Susanna, Manzini M Chiara
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and Intellectual disability (ID) share an increased male prevalence, but the biological mechanisms underlying this male bias remain poorly understood. Mice deficient for CC2D1A, a protein scaffold mutated in ASD/ID, have shown multiple male-specific deficits both in ASD-like behaviors and in the regulation of neuronal intracellular signaling pathways. However, previous research relied on conditional knockout (cKO) models due to early postnatal lethality of global Cc2d1a KO strains. Thus, the ability to define the developmental impacts of CC2D1A LOF in mice has been limited. While generating a Cc2d1a knock-in strain with V5-HA epitope tags, we found that homozygous animals ( Cc2d1a VH/VH ) resulted in a hypomorph line that can be used to study developmental loss of CC2D1A. We assessed gross morphology, behavior, and intracellular signaling in male and female Cc2d1a VH/VH animals, where only ∼20% of CC2D1A is present. We then crossed this line with a null allele to obtain a more severe hypomorph ( Cc2d1a -/VH ) and explore phenotypic penetrance thresholds. In addition to the previous phenotypic characterization, we also assessed body composition, feeding, and molecular hallmarks of metabolic function in both sexes. We found that ∼80% CC2D1A reduction in Cc2d1a VH/VH mice did not recapitulate any of the behavioral or molecular disruptions seen in cKO models. In contrast, ∼90% CC2D1A reduction in Cc2d1a -/VH mice resulted in ASD/ID-like behavioral phenotypes in males, similar to those reported in cKO lines, with distinct intracellular signaling disruptions. Male and female Cc2d1a -/VH mice also showed subtle but significant adult weight deficits associated with distinct metabolic changes. These models still do not fully recapitulate the complete CC2D1A LOF found in patients. Due to the analysis of two independent strains over multiple metrics, these studies are not powered to compare statistical differences between sexes and data were analyzed in males and females independently. We identified a strikingly narrow CC2D1A expression threshold for the emergence of ASD/ID-like behavioral deficits in males. In addition, we revealed a novel role for CC2D1A in adult weight gain. These mouse strains will be useful to better understand CC2D1A LOF phenotypes.

titre: Functional deficits of the inhibitory control system in children with ADHD: A task-based fMRI meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Functional deficits of the inhibitory control system in children with ADHD: A task-based fMRI meta-analysis.
auteurs: Kammer Elizabeth, Patil Shwetha, Huynh Helena, Gao Zhiyao, Cai Weidong
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: Inhibitory control deficits have long been proposed as a central neurocognitive mechanism underlying childhood Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). However, neuroimaging findings remain heterogeneous, partly due to methodological variability across developmental samples and experimental paradigms. The present study aimed to characterize the neural architecture of motor response inhibition in typically developing (TD) children and identify reproducible functional abnormalities associated with pediatric ADHD using stringent, developmentally specific inclusion criteria. We conducted two coordinate-based meta-analyses using Activation Likelihood Estimation (ALE). Following a systematic literature search (up to August 2026), we identified 23 task-based fMRI studies reporting inhibitory-control-related activation in TD children (237 foci) and 17 studies comparing children with ADHD and TD peers (114 foci) during the Stop-Signal Task or Go/No-Go Task. All participants were younger than 18 years of age. Statistical significance was determined using cluster-level family-wise error (FWE) correction. In TD children, ALE revealed a robust inhibitory-control network encompassing the bilateral anterior insula (AI), inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), and the midline pre-supplementary motor area (preSMA) and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). This spatial organization closely resembled the canonical inhibitory-control network consistently observed in adults, suggesting that the core neural architecture supporting motor inhibition is already detectably organized during development. In the between-group analysis, children with ADHD exhibited significant hypoactivation primarily within the preSMA. Notably, this region demonstrated striking spatial overlap with the preSMA cluster reliably recruited in TD children during motor inhibition. These findings provide convergent support for inhibitory-control models of ADHD and identify altered preSMA recruitment as one of the most consistent functional abnormalities associated with pediatric ADHD. While the neural infrastructure supporting inhibitory control is broadly established during childhood, children with ADHD exhibit reduced recruitment of a key cortical node within this network during motor inhibition demands.

titre: Parkinsonism Co-occurrence Among Older Autistic Adults, Adults With Intellectual Disability, and a Control Sample of Adults in National Health Care Claims Data.
titre_fr: Parkinsonism Co-occurrence Among Older Autistic Adults, Adults With Intellectual Disability, and a Control Sample of Adults in National Health Care Claims Data.
auteurs: Wallace Gregory L, Klein Claire B, Tao Sha, Carey Meghan E, Shea Lindsay, Klinger Laura G
revue: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
resume: Emerging evidence suggests that Parkinson's Disease (PD)-related conditions (i.e., parkinsonism) co-occur more commonly with autism than in the general population. However, prior prevalence-based studies did not account for the influence of antipsychotic usage, which is linked to secondary parkinsonism as a possible side effect, or co-occurring intellectual disability (ID). In addition, no study of incidence rates of parkinsonism among older autistic adults has been completed to date. Prevalence and incidence were examined among 56,970,786 45+ year old persons across four groups (autism only, ID only, autism + ID, and control sample) utilizing U.S.-based, individually linked Medicaid and Medicare health care claims data from 2017 to 2019. Compared with the control sample (1.57%), highly elevated prevalence of co-occurring PD-related diagnoses was found across groups (autism only: 3.83%; ID only: 4.32%; autism + ID: 4.86%). This elevation in prevalence persisted after the exclusion of individuals prescribed antipsychotic medications. Whether examining broader or narrower (excluding secondary) parkinsonism, the age-standardized incidence or risk of newly documented co-occurring parkinsonism was highest in those with autism + ID, followed by those with autism only and those with ID only, all of which far outpaced control sample findings. Overall, elevated co-occurrence of autism and parkinsonism has significant scientific, clinical, and service-system implications.Lay AbstractSome studies find that people with autism are more likely to have co-occurring parkinsonism, or the core motor features linked to Parkinson's Disease, like tremors and slowed movements. However, previous prevalence (number of cases at any one point in time) studies usually did not account for the influence of antipsychotic usage, which is relatively high in autism and can be associated with parkinsonism symptoms. Prior studies also rarely examined the influence of intellectual disability (ID) on the co-occurrence of parkinsonism and autism. Finally, no study of incidence rates (i.e., newly emerging cases over time) of parkinsonism among older autistic adults has been completed to date. titre: Deep TMS modulates neurovascular responses and enhances dual-task computation in healthy adults.
titre_fr: Deep TMS modulates neurovascular responses and enhances dual-task computation in healthy adults.
auteurs: Zeng Baoyao, Wang Weining, Ding Zhengran, Wang Chen, Li Ce, Yuan Runzhe, Zhou Bao, Zhu Yulian
resume: Dual-task performance requires coordination between cognitive control and motor systems. This study examined how deep transcranial magnetic stimulation (DTMS) influences cortical responses and computational performance during dual-task processing. In a randomized crossover study, 19 healthy adults underwent DTMS targeting the bilateral prefrontal cortex and anterior cingulate cortex and sham stimulation in separate sessions, with functional near-infrared spectroscopy and dual-task assessments performed before and after each intervention. Compared with sham stimulation, DTMS increased task-related cortical activation in regions involved in cognitive-motor processing and improved computation number without affecting accuracy. Activation changes involving the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, secondary motor cortex, and language-related regions were associated with dual-task performance. These findings suggest that DTMS may modulate distributed cortical dynamics supporting cognitive-motor coordination and inform its potential application in populations with cognitive-motor impairments.

titre: Multimodal Neuroimaging and Behavioral Characterization of Aged Female APOE4 Knock-In Rats Reveals a Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease Phenotype.
titre_fr: Multimodal Neuroimaging and Behavioral Characterization of Aged Female APOE4 Knock-In Rats Reveals a Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease Phenotype.
auteurs: Cavallaro Noah J, Maheswari Ashwath, Chukwuemeka Tochi, Koganov Allen, Sundararaj Nithiyashree, D'Argenio Sydney, Stotland Harper, Weiss Deena, Botelho Gregorio, Kulkarni Praveen P, Ferris Craig F
resume: The apolipoprotein E ε4 allele (APOE4) is the strongest genetic risk factor for sporadic Alzheimer's disease (AD) and confers disproportionate risk in women, particularly after reproductive senescence. The brain changes preceding overt neurodegeneration in APOE4 carriers remain incompletely characterized. We conducted neuroimaging and behavioral studies in aged (18-month) female APOE4 humanized knock-in rats and APOE3 controls. Regional brain volumes across 197 areas were quantified by voxel-based morphometry (VBM); white and gray matter microstructure by diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), yielding fractional anisotropy (FA) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Spatial memory was assessed with the Barnes maze and motor coordination with the beam walk. APOE4 rats showed significantly larger regional brain volumes than APOE3 controls. DTI revealed increased FA in the thalamus, brainstem, and white matter tracts, and reduced FA in the sensorimotor cortex. Across most regions elevated FA was accompanied by reduced ADC, an inverse relationship consistent with cytotoxic edema. Behaviorally, APOE4 rats were significantly impaired on the Barnes maze. Aged female APOE4 knock-in rats exhibit a preclinical AD phenotype: widespread volumetric enlargement across white matter, sensorimotor, and limbic circuits, with microstructural alterations (elevated FA in brainstem, thalamus, and white matter; reduced FA in sensorimotor cortex). This mirrors the imaging and cognitive profile of cognitively normal human APOE4 carriers in preclinical AD and validates the model as a translationally relevant platform for investigating early APOE4-driven pathophysiology and testing preventive interventions.

titre: Preconception, Prenatal and Postnatal PM2.5 Exposure and Neurodevelopmental Disorder Risk among Medicaid Recipients.
titre_fr: Preconception, Prenatal and Postnatal PM2.5 Exposure and Neurodevelopmental Disorder Risk among Medicaid Recipients.
auteurs: Shupler Matthew, Qiu Xinye, Huybrechts Krista F, Hernandez-Diaz Sonia, Huang Wanyu, Choi Hayon Michelle, Leung Michael, Wei Yaguang, Schwartz Joel, Coull Brent, Papatheodorou Evgenia, McDougle Christopher J, Zanobetti Antonella, Weisskopf Marc, Papatheodorou Stefania
resume: Evidence linking ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure to childhood neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) remains mixed. We conducted a cohort study (2001-2013) of 1,547,244 Medicaid-enrolled mother-child pairs to assess associations between zip-code-level PM2.5 exposure during preconception (12-week), prenatal (37-week), and postnatal (3-year) periods and children's NDD risk. Cox proportional hazards models estimated risks of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), learning difficulty (LD), speech/language disorder, developmental coordination disorder (DCD), intellectual disability, and behavioral disorder, adjusting for demographics, meteorological characteristics, and area-level socioeconomic indicators. Distributed lag models assessed critical exposure windows and cumulative effects. A 10 μg/m3 increase in cumulative prenatal PM2.5 exposure was associated with higher ASD risk (Hazard ratio (HR):1.17; 95%CI:1.00,1.37). A critical exposure window for ASD existed during gestational weeks 23-31 (HR:1.09 95%CI:[1.02,1.17]). Cumulative prenatal PM2.5 exposure was associated with increased ID risk among Hispanic individuals (HR:1.57 95%CI:[1.02,2.43]) but not among other races/ethnicities. Postnatal PM2.5 exposure was associated with increased ADHD risk (HR:1.17 95%CI:[0.94,1.46]) at age 0 years and DCD risk (HR:1.72 95%CI:[0.97,3.07]) at age 1 year. No associations between PM2.5 exposure and other NDDs were found. Prenatal and postnatal PM2.5 exposure may increase the risk of some NDDs among low-income U.S. children.

titre: Systemic mitochondrial injection protects against methanol-induced optic neuropathy through restoration of mitochondrial function and attenuation of oxidative stress.
titre_fr: Systemic mitochondrial injection protects against methanol-induced optic neuropathy through restoration of mitochondrial function and attenuation of oxidative stress.
auteurs: Salimi Ahmad, Elyasi Behrooz, Delavari Hanieh, Karroubian Hamed, Zeynali Elahe, Zaki Salva, Dehghanypoor Mina, Jamali Zhaleh
resume: Methanol poisoning can cause severe and irreversible optic neuropathy, for which effective neuroprotective strategies remain limited. Mitochondrial dysfunction is important contributors to methanol-induced neuronal injury. Therefore, this study evaluated whether systemic mitochondrial injection could attenuate methanol-induced optic nerve injury. Adult rats were randomly assigned to control, methanol, methanol + single mitochondrial injection, and methanol + double mitochondrial injection groups. Following methanol intoxication, freshly isolated functional mitochondria (250 µg/kg) were administered intravenously. Motor and visual functions were evaluated using the beam walking and visual cliff tests. Mitochondrial dysfunction was assessed by flow cytometric analysis of mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. Oxidative stress was assessed by measuring reduced glutathione (GSH) and malondialdehyde (MDA), and optic nerve histopathology was also examined. Methanol exposure impaired motor coordination and visual performance (P < 0.05) and was associated with increased ROS formation (P < 0.001), lipid peroxidation (P < 0.01), MMP collapse (P < 0.001), and GSH depletion (P < 0.05), accompanied by histopathological alterations in the optic nerve. Mitochondrial injection attenuated these changes (P < 0.05) and improved functional and histopathological outcomes. Overall, the double mitochondrial injection was associated with a relatively greater improvement than the single administration in some of the evaluated parameters. Systemic mitochondrial injection attenuated methanol-associated mitochondrial and oxidative disturbances and was accompanied by improved behavioral and histopathological outcomes in this experimental model. Obtained finding in the current study support further investigations of mitochondrial-based approaches as potential strategies for methanol-induced optic neuropathy, while additional works are required to establish their underlying mechanisms, durability, and translational potential.

titre: Neuronal surface autoantibodies at cerebellar and brainstem synapses: mechanisms, phenotypes, and translational gaps.
titre_fr: Neuronal surface autoantibodies at cerebellar and brainstem synapses: mechanisms, phenotypes, and translational gaps.
auteurs: Li Yan, Li Wenyuan, Zhang Zhaoben, Hu Yuyuan, Ma Xinyu, Wang Zhijun, Zhang Wei, Wang Yanhong
resume: Pathogenic neuronal-surface autoantibodies can disrupt extracellular receptors, ion-channel complexes, and synaptic proteins, yet their regional neurological phenotypes differ substantially. This variability is particularly informative in the cerebellum and brainstem, where precisely timed excitatory and inhibitory signaling supports motor coordination, ocular-motor control, autonomic regulation, arousal, and respiration. In this Mini Review, we examine how antibody effector mechanisms, regional antigen distribution, and local synaptic physiology interact to shape cerebellar and brainstem manifestations of neuronal-surface-antibody disease. Autoimmunity against metabotropic glutamate receptor 1 (mGluR1) provides a model of cerebellar synaptic dysfunction because mGluR1 is strongly linked to Purkinje-cell signaling and synaptic plasticity, whereas glycine receptor (GlyR) autoimmunity illustrates how impaired inhibitory transmission can destabilize brainstem and spinal networks. NMDAR, AMPAR, GABA_A receptor, GABA_B receptor, LGI1, and CASPR2 autoimmunity provide mechanistic comparators showing that extracellular antigen accessibility alone does not determine neurological phenotype. Direct antibody-mediated synaptic dysfunction may be reversible, but persistent structural injury occurs in a subset of patients; current evidence does not determine whether such injury is attributable to sustained antibody exposure, accompanying T-cell inflammation, or both. Evidence from acute physiological experiments, individual follow-up cases, and heterogeneous cohorts comes from different settings and does not establish a uniform progression from synaptic dysfunction to atrophy.

titre: Ataxia Therapeutics: A Comprehensive Overview of the Clinical Development Pipeline.
titre_fr: Ataxia Therapeutics: A Comprehensive Overview of the Clinical Development Pipeline.
auteurs: Cappella Marisa, Locuratolo Nicoletta, Salvatore Marco, Polizzi Agata, Carbone Elena, Perrone Federica, Bellomo Guido, Vanacore Nicola, Lacorte Eleonora, Piscopo Paola
resume: Ataxias are a heterogeneous group of rare neurological disorders characterized by progressive impairment of motor coordination and balance, caused by a broad range of genetic, immune-mediated, and degenerative mechanisms. Despite significant advances in molecular diagnostics and disease characterization, effective disease-targeted treatments remain limited, with omaveloxolone currently representing the only approved therapy for Friedreich's ataxia. In this review, we provide a comprehensive and up-to-date overview of the clinical drug development pipeline for ataxias, based on a systematic analysis of international clinical trial registries up to April 2026. One hundred and fifty-four interventional pharmacological trials investigating 66 therapeutic agents across phases 1-3 were identified. The majority of ongoing clinical efforts focus on symptomatic and supportive therapies, which together constitute more than half of the pipeline and include the most developmentally advanced programs. Neuroprotective therapies represent a substantial portion of trials but have shown mixed efficacy to date. In contrast, disease-targeted approaches, including gene therapies, antisense oligonucleotides, cell-based therapies, and protein replacement strategies, account for a smaller share of the pipeline and remain largely confined to early-phase development. More than half of investigational agents are repurposed compounds, reflecting a pragmatic strategy to accelerate therapeutic progress in rare disorders. Overall, the ataxia therapeutic landscape is expanding but remains fragmented, underscoring the need for improved patient stratification, validated biomarkers, harmonized registries, and international collaboration to enable the successful translation of emerging therapies into clinical practice.

titre: Driving Simulation Methods for Assessing Post-Injury Driving Performance After Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Scoping Review.
titre_fr: Driving Simulation Methods for Assessing Post-Injury Driving Performance After Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Scoping Review.
auteurs: Stevenson Johnna, Rundus Christopher R M, Yang Jingzhen, Stavrinos Despina
resume: Driving is a cognitively demanding task that involves the continuous integration of attention, executive control, visual processing, and motor coordination. Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) may disrupt these functions and affect driving performance during recovery. Driving simulation is increasingly used to examine post-mTBI driving performance, yet substantial heterogeneity exists in simulator platforms, task designs, and outcome selection. This scoping review characterized driving simulation methodologies used to assess post-mTBI driving performance and examined patterns of mTBI-related findings across reported outcomes. A systematic search of seven electronic databases identified 12 eligible publications between 2017 and 2026. Publications were synthesized by participant characteristics, time since injury, simulator platform, task demands, and outcomes. Across publications, mTBI-related findings were most frequently reported for vehicle control metrics, particularly lane position variability and speed regulation. mTBI-related differences were most often condition-specific, including differences during curves, hazard events, and manipulated cognitive load or dual-task conditions. Cognitive measures also demonstrated mTBI-related differences and associations to driving performance, particularly those assessing executive functioning and processing speed domains. Differences were observed across all post-injury intervals, including ≥ 15 days, with a small number of related publications reporting performance differences after symptom resolution. However, the predominantly cross-sectional evidence does not establish whether these differences persist over time within the same individuals. Findings suggest that driving simulation can provide a useful controlled method for examining functional driving performance following mTBI across varying road environments and task demands. Future work should prioritize standardizing simulator outcomes and validating simulator performance against on-road, naturalistic-driving, and crash-related outcomes.

titre: Mobile EEG Reveals Age-Dependent Cognitive-Motor Interference with Increasing Motor Task Complexity- a cross-sectional study.
titre_fr: Mobile EEG Reveals Age-Dependent Cognitive-Motor Interference with Increasing Motor Task Complexity- a cross-sectional study.
auteurs: Wollesen Bettina, Winter Leoni, Gramann Klaus, Protzak Janna
resume: This study examined age-related differences in behavior and brain dynamics underlying cognitive-motor interference (CMI) during motor dual-tasks (DT) with increasing motor task complexity. Behavioral performance and electrocortical activity were assessed in 19 younger adults (11 males, 8 females; 25.5 ± 2.3 years) and 11 older adults (6 males, 5 females; 72.6 ± 4.6 years) using mobile electroencephalography (EEG). Participants performed an oddball choice-reaction task under three conditions: sitting, standing, and treadmill walking. Event-related potential (ERPs; P1, N1, P3) amplitudes and latencies, response times, postural sway, and gait parameters were recorded to evaluate CMI. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVAs with within-subject factors of motor condition and stimulus type and age group as a between-subject factor. Older adults exhibited reduced step length compared to younger adults, but no DT-related changes in gait or postural sway were observed. Response times were generally slower in older adults and increased from sitting to standing and walking whereas younger adults showed slowing only from sitting to standing. Early sensory ERP components (P1, N1) demonstrated increased amplitudes with higher motor demands. The P3 component was reduced in amplitude in both groups during walking, with delayed latencies in older adults. For both groups, P3 latencies were associated with prolonged response times. Our findings suggest that this slowing during walking reflects altered cognitive resource allocation, characterized by delayed central information processing and enhanced early visual processing, rather than impaired peripheral motor coordination.

titre: A PRMT5-ANGPTL4 axis in brain endothelial cells regulates cerebellar inhibitory synaptogenesis and motor coordination.
titre_fr: A PRMT5-ANGPTL4 axis in brain endothelial cells regulates cerebellar inhibitory synaptogenesis and motor coordination.
auteurs: Lu Jinjin, Zhang Yizhe, Hao Yijie, Ning Huimin, Fan Zizhao, Hao Shiqiang, Cui Yaxiong, Han Yuying, Cai Yunting, Liu Wenjia, Ao Haiou, Xiu Shunshun, Wang Jun, Yang Xiao
resume: Brain vasculature is essential for central nervous system function. Here, we found a cerebrovascular signaling axis in which the arginine methyltransferase PRMT5 in endothelial cells promoted proper inhibitory synaptogenesis and motor coordination in male mice. Cerebrovascular endothelial cell-specific deletion of Prmt5 in mice led to excessive inhibitory synaptic input onto Purkinje cells and progressive motor deficits. Mechanistically, Prmt5 deficiency epigenetically increased the expression of the gene encoding the secreted angiocrine ANGPTL4 through reduced symmetric dimethylation of Arg8 in histone H3 and Arg3 in histone H4, which coincided with increased acetylation of Lys9 in histone H3, at the Angptl4 promoter. Angptl4 deletion in brain endothelium normalized inhibitory synaptic input onto Purkinje cells and partially restored motor coordination in mice with a conditional Prmt5 deficiency. Together, these findings define the endothelial PRMT5-ANGPTL4 axis as a key regulator of cerebellar inhibitory circuitry and motor function, highlighting cerebrovascular mechanisms as potential therapeutic targets for motor coordination disorders.

titre: [Autism, selective mutism and mild intellectual disability explained by 17q12 microdeletion syndrome].
titre_fr: [Autism, selective mutism and mild intellectual disability explained by 17q12 microdeletion syndrome].
auteurs: Fernell Elisabeth, Bulmer Linda, Gillberg Christopher
resume: The patient had presented symptoms during preschool years with motor coordination difficulties, deviant reactions to sensory stimuli and separation anxiety. A language stagnation had occurred at the age of 1.5 to 2 years. At school start, she became completely mute during school hours but spoke at home. At assessment at the Child Neuropsychiatric Clinic at the age of 10, autism, selective mutism and ADHD/ADD were diagnosed. Her intellectual level corresponded to borderline intellectual functioning, and a similar test result was evident also at the age of 14 years. When transition to upper secondary school was planned, the cognitive assessment showed a mild intellectual disability. Then, medical investigations, including genetic SNP array, was carried out. This analysis showed a 17q12 microdeletion syndrome. Then, specific medical investigations were carried out due to the various medical conditions that need to be checked and followed up in patients with 17q12 microdeletion syndrome.

titre: Endogenously Triboenhanced Heterogeneous Piezoelectric Nanofiber Membranes for Self-Powered Electroluminescent Pressure Sensing.
titre_fr: Endogenously Triboenhanced Heterogeneous Piezoelectric Nanofiber Membranes for Self-Powered Electroluminescent Pressure Sensing.
auteurs: Tang Qi, Lin Yanxuan, Lv Xiaoshuang, Du Mingjuan, Mao Ziyan, Gao Yanlei, Xu Ziao, Wang Faqiang, Wang Caiyan, Yu Jianyong, Ding Bin, Li Zhaoling
resume: The innovation of sensing systems is increasingly evolving toward direct visualization, which demands real-time and high electromechanical output to drive reliable optical readout, yet most multimodal sensing systems rely on simple signal superposition. Here, an endogenous tribo-enhanced piezoelectric pressure sensing with visualization capability was developed by coupling a PAN/PVDF-HFP heterogeneous nanofiber membrane with a ZnS:Cu/PZT/Ecoflex electroluminescent layer. The nanofiber membrane features a skeleton-filling architecture in which PAN-rich and PVDF-HFP-rich domains create abundant heterogeneous interfaces for endogenous triboelectric charge generation. Incorporation of [BMIM][BF4] further promotes charge separation and transport, increasing the open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current to 8 V and 22.8 nA, respectively. The enhanced electromechanical output directly drives the electroluminescent layer, enabling the real-time visualization of handwriting, patterned indentation, and dynamic stretching. This work provides an interface engineering strategy for self-powered visual pressure sensing.

titre: Decoding attempted handwritten characters based on temporal endovascular neural features.
titre_fr: Decoding attempted handwritten characters based on temporal endovascular neural features.
auteurs: Kokorin Kirill, Mu Jing, Grayden David B, John Sam E, Yoo Peter E
resume: We evaluated temporal neural features for motor decoding using a minimally-invasive endovascular brain-computer interfaces (BCI). We hypothesised that relatively long compound movements generate distinct patterns of neural activity that are encoded by temporal features.Approach. A single participant implanted with the Stentrode endovascular BCI attempted to hand write English characters, which were then classified offline and online based on the recorded brain activity. The input to the model was a one-dimensional trajectory of high-gamma power, summed across all channels to isolate the effect of temporal information on decoding performance.Main results. A small number of classes across multiple months was reliably decoded, showing that temporal decoding could identify stable patterns of brain activity associated with each handwriting movement. Across four online sessions, where each session contained 20-30 trials/character and 80-180 rest trials, the best performing (3-class) model achieved a mean rest recall of 87% as well as character recall and precision of 65% and 59%, respectively. These results showed that attempted handwriting can be used in an online multi-class selection BCI and that temporal neural features capture the internal user context. Linear warping of trials to minimise temporal variability, where all trials were modified to have the same duration, led to significantly increased decoding performance compared to classifying raw trials.Significance. The results from our participant showed that decoding brain activity based on the differences between feature trajectories across time can be an effective strategy for discriminating different movements. Therefore, BCIs may be able to use temporal information to reduce their spatial footprint, likely making them less invasive. Overall, our study shows that further investigation of temporal decoding across multiple participants and other recording modalities is warranted. Strategies for automatic temporal alignment are likely to further improve the performance of these systems.

titre: Metachronous dural arteriovenous fistulas in a single patient: a 25-year evolution of three distinct lesions.
titre_fr: Metachronous dural arteriovenous fistulas in a single patient: a 25-year evolution of three distinct lesions.
auteurs: Liu Hon-Man
resume: A rare case of metachronous dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) over 25 years is presented. The patient initially developed a left transverse-sigmoid sinus DAVF causing pulsatile tinnitus, successfully treated with embolisation. 14 years later, he experienced pulsatile scalp lesions, numbness and muscle weakness on the right side, impairing his handwriting. Angiography revealed a superior sagittal sinus DAVF with cortical vein reflux and sinus thrombosis, treated with transvenous and transarterial embolisation, leading to significant symptom improvement. Five years later, he reported right occipital pain, retromastoid tenderness and occasional tinnitus. Imaging confirmed a new DAVF on the right transverse-sigmoid sinus (Cognard type I). He declined further treatment but remained clinically stable with unchanged MRI findings for 8 years. This case highlights the complexity of managing recurrent, metachronous DAVFs and the importance of long-term monitoring.

titre: Distinct handwriting kinematic profiles across Parkinson's disease subtypes.
titre_fr: Distinct handwriting kinematic profiles across Parkinson's disease subtypes.
auteurs: Onder Halil, Dinc Sibel, Yavuz Zehra, Comoglu Selcuk
resume: Handwriting impairment is common in Parkinson's disease (PD), but its relationships with clinical severity and motor phenotypes remain incompletely understood. To characterize handwriting kinematics in PD and examine their associations with clinical severity and motor phenotypes. Fifty-six patients with PD and 46 healthy controls (HC) performed a standardized digital handwriting task in the medication OFF state. Letter area, duration, pressure, writing speed, and the progressive micrographia (PM) index were analyzed. TD and AR subtypes were compared, and correlation and ROC analyses were performed. PD patients showed significant handwriting abnormalities compared with HC. Using a >30% reduction in mean letter area to define categorical progressive micrographia, PM was observed in 8.9% of patients with PD and 2.2% of healthy controls (p = 0.219). The continuous PM index and twenty-letter duration showed discriminative performance, with AUCs of 0.753 and 0.718, respectively (both p < 0.001). Compared with TD patients, AR patients exhibited smaller writing areas (initial five-letter area, p = 0.042; twenty-letter area, p = 0.013; final five-letter area, p = 0.024) and slower writing speed (p = 0.012). Twenty-letter duration correlated with HY stage (r = 0.290, p = 0.030) and MDS-UPDRS-III scores (r = 0.404, p = 0.006). Overall, temporal parameters, particularly letter duration, were more closely associated with disease severity, whereas spatial measures showed weaker clinical correlations despite clear between-group differences. Temporal measures were more closely associated with clinical severity, whereas spatial measures showed weaker and less consistent associations. Distinct handwriting kinematic profiles between TD and AR phenotypes suggest that quantitative handwriting analysis may provide complementary information on motor heterogeneity in PD.

titre: Literary Element Use in Written Narratives for Third-Grade Children Who Are Deaf and Hard of Hearing.
titre_fr: Literary Element Use in Written Narratives for Third-Grade Children Who Are Deaf and Hard of Hearing.
auteurs: Grey Brittany, Lund Emily A, Werfel Krystal L
revue: Language, speech, and hearing services in schools
resume: This study examined literary element use in third-grade written narratives to determine if children who are deaf and hard of hearing (DHH) and their peers with typical hearing (TH) met macrostructure writing proficiency expectations addressed in the Common Core State Standards. Participants included 134 children who completed third grade across three groups: children who used cochlear implants (CIs), children who used hearing aids (HAs), and children with TH. Given a picture prompt, participants composed a written narrative. Using the third-grade Common Core State Standards that addressed macrostructure, written narratives were scored with a rubric that outlined the criteria for meeting seven literary element categories: characters, actions, feelings, dialogue, topic, sequence, and plot. CI, HA, and TH children did not meet most macrostructure literary element criteria for narrative writing addressed in the third-grade Common Core State Standards. Literary element outcomes did not significantly differ between CI, HA, and TH groups, except for topic. DHH and TH third-grade students did not demonstrate strong macrostructure writing skills in their written narratives. To build a solid writing foundation, elementary students, regardless of hearing status, would benefit from general and genre-specific writing interventions that incorporate self-regulating strategies throughout their writing process to facilitate the transition from learning to write to writing to learn. https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34259406.

titre: Argentine Tango as an Integrative Therapeutic Approach: Bridging Dance Therapy and Melotherapy.
titre_fr: Argentine Tango as an Integrative Therapeutic Approach: Bridging Dance Therapy and Melotherapy.
auteurs: Kicsi Csongor
revue: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
resume: Argentine tango integrates rhythmic auditory information, adaptive locomotion, improvisation, and continuous partnered interaction within a complex dance practice. This review examines its therapeutic relevance with primary emphasis on neurological rehabilitation, particularly Parkinson's disease (PD), where tango-specific evidence is most developed. Particular attention is given to balance, functional mobility, gait adaptability, and motor-cognitive integration, while cognitive, emotional, and social outcomes are considered complementary dimensions rather than equivalent primary endpoints. This review examines mechanisms involving auditory-motor coupling, motor learning, embodied cognition, and interpersonal coordination, while distinguishing tango-based interventions from formal dance/movement therapy and music therapy. Particular consideration is given to Adapted Tango, including how task demands can be scaled while preserving defining characteristics of Argentine tango. Rather than claiming superiority over other dance forms, the review proposes that tango is therapeutically relevant because of its distinctive combination of walking-based multidirectional locomotion, musical interpretation, improvisational decision-making, and partner-derived sensory information. These relationships are integrated within the Argentine Tango Therapeutic Integration Model (ATTIM), proposed as a hypothesis-generating framework for future research.

titre: Core Cognition Walking: Recalling the Moment of Automatic Postural Control During Everyday Walking - A Hypothesis for Chronic Low Back Pain.
titre_fr: Core Cognition Walking: Recalling the Moment of Automatic Postural Control During Everyday Walking - A Hypothesis for Chronic Low Back Pain.
auteurs: Lee Dae-Young, Park Si-Young
resume: In chronic low back pain (CLBP), the anticipatory postural adjustment (APA) of transversus abdominis that precedes limb movement is delayed, and this impairment tends to persist after pain relief and after surgical decompression. Cognitive Functional Therapy addresses beliefs, motor control exercise trains voluntary deep-muscle activation, and the Alexander technique re-educates habitual postural responses in everyday activity. None specifies a procedure by which a patient recognizes the moment in which trunk control occurs and subsequently recalls it against a single defined target. We describe a maneuver observed in clinical practice and state a testable hypothesis. When a patient flexes and extends the arm slowly while walking, keeping speed and effort uniform, the lower abdomen activates without any instruction to brace, and foot landing softens. When uniformity breaks, the response is not observed. The observation arose during clinical practice between March and June 2026; no structured data were collected, and neither response rates nor effect sizes are reported. We interpret the maneuver not as teaching gait anew but as making momentarily accessible a control that a diminished APA had concealed, and as allowing the patient to recall that moment. This interpretation is a hypothesis and not an established mechanism. The object of recognition is the quiet stability of the lower abdomen; the arm movement is the procedure that elicits it. We propose a 12-week randomized trial with the Oswestry Disability Index and pain as primary outcomes, using a 2×2 control structure that separates uniform arm movement from sensory attention. Immediate response is measured before allocation and pre-specified as a treatment-effect moderator rather than used as an eligibility criterion. Foot-landing loading rate, APA timing, and lumbar proprioceptive accuracy are exploratory measures. Core Cognition Walking is offered as a falsifiable hypothesis that warrants testing.

titre: Treatment of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD): acute attacks, relapse prevention, and symptomatic care.
titre_fr: Treatment of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD): acute attacks, relapse prevention, and symptomatic care.
auteurs: Mahler João Vitor, Vilardo Marina, Silva Guilherme Diogo, Vishnevetsky Anastasia, Bilodeau Philippe-Antoine, Levy Michael, Matiello Marcelo
resume: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) is a distinct inflammatory demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system, and its diagnosis is guided by the 2023 International MOGAD Panel criteria. Its clinical spectrum includes optic neuritis, transverse myelitis, acute disseminated encephalomyelitis, and brainstem or cortical encephalitis, with a phenotype distribution that is strongly age-dependent. Although attacks are typically steroid-responsive and recovery is often good, roughly half of adults relapse, and it is the accumulation of incompletely recovered attacks, rather than a progressive phase, that drives long-term disability. Management therefore has three aims: to abort and reverse the acute attack, to prevent relapses in patients at risk, and to relieve residual symptomatic disability. This review synthesizes current evidence for acute treatment (high-dose corticosteroids, therapeutic plasma exchange, and intravenous immunoglobulin), the corticosteroid taper, and maintenance immunotherapy, with attention to when treatment should be started and when it may reasonably be stopped. We summarize comparative data favoring maintenance intravenous immunoglobulin, the emerging evidence for interleukin-6 receptor blockade, the more variable performance of B-cell depletion relative to AQP4-IgG-seropositive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, and the first phase 3 trials in the field (satralizumab and rozanolixizumab). We give particular attention to children, in whom acute disseminated encephalomyelitis predominates and in whom cognitive, academic, growth and skeletal outcomes must shape treatment decisions, and to the real-world availability of antibody testing and therapy outside high-income settings. Finally, we address symptomatic care: visual rehabilitation, neuropathic and spasticity-related pain, fatigue, bladder dysfunction, cognition, and mood.

titre: Feasibility of a Co-Designed Personalized Cognitive Reablement Program Delivered via Digital Voice Assistants for Older Adults Living With Early-Stage Dementia or Mild Cognitive Impairment: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: Feasibility of a Co-Designed Personalized Cognitive Reablement Program Delivered via Digital Voice Assistants for Older Adults Living With Early-Stage Dementia or Mild Cognitive Impairment: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Yiannis Tracy, Macpherson Helen, Scott David, Callisaya Michele, Chapple Celeste, Glavas Costas, Gourlay Caitlyn, Maddison Ralph, Gvozdenko Eugene, Jansons Paul
resume: Home-based reablement programs have improved everyday functioning for people living with early-stage dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI), but the substantial time commitment required for delivery by health professionals has created a barrier to widespread implementation. Digital technology could facilitate delivery, but traditional devices such as smartphones and tablets present usability challenges for this population. We have co-designed a cognitive reablement program, VOICE-COG, that can deliver personalized interventions broadcast via voice-controlled digital voice assistants (DVAs). This pilot nonblinded randomized controlled trial examined the feasibility and potential effectiveness of VOICE-COG for older adults living with dementia or MCI to guide the design of a full-scale trial. Older adults (aged 60-85 years) with a self-reported diagnosis of dementia or MCI (N=30) were recruited via Facebook or the StepUp-for Dementia Research database and randomized to either a DVA intervention (n=15) or control (n=15) group for 12 weeks. Each participant randomized to the intervention group and their care partner met with a psychologist via Zoom to select 2 or 3 personalized goals from the VOICE-COG program. The personalized program was input into the software (BuddyLink) by researchers for broadcast via a DVA (Amazon Alexa Show 8). Participants in the control group received enhanced usual care, consisting of treatment as usual, plus weekly informational emails. Primary feasibility outcomes were recruitment, retention, device-recorded adherence, and the System Usability Scale (SUS). Secondary outcomes were self-reported by the participant and care partner via web-based Qualtrics forms and included the Goal Attainment Scale-Light (GAS), changes in participant mood, cognition, and everyday functioning, and carer burden. The recruitment rate was 86% (30/35) and the retention rate was 97% (29/30), with 1 participant in the intervention group lost to follow-up. Adherence to the VOICE-COG program ranged from 29% to 100% (mean 70%, SD 17%). The VOICE-COG program was rated as marginally acceptable (mean SUS score 56.3, SD 18.1). After 12 weeks, 60% (9/15) of the intervention group reported having met or exceeded their goals (GAS-Light t-score ≥50; mean 57.6, SD 15.4). The intervention group had a significantly higher increase in Multifactorial Memory Questionnaire-Strategy subscale score compared with control, mean difference 5.0 (95% CI 0.03-10.1, P=.049), representing a medium effect size (d=0.55). There were no other significant differences between groups. This co-designed VOICE-COG program, delivered via DVAs, was feasible for older adults living with early-stage dementia or MCI, resulting in most participants meeting their reablement goals and increases in the use of memory strategies. System usability issues should be addressed in future adequately powered trials.

titre: Assistive and adaptive technologies for dyscalculia: a bibliometric review and narrative synthesis of AI-supported screening and learning support.
titre_fr: Assistive and adaptive technologies for dyscalculia: a bibliometric review and narrative synthesis of AI-supported screening and learning support.
auteurs: Serin Mehmet Koray, Bulut Aydin, Kepceoğlu İbrahim
resume: This study aimed to map the development of assistive and adaptive technology-supported approaches to dyscalculia between 2005 and 2025 and to clarify how artificial intelligence, adaptive learning, and assistive technologies are positioned within this research field. A bibliometric review, complemented by a narrative synthesis, was conducted using 83 unique journal publications indexed in Web of Science and Scopus. The analysis included keyword frequency analysis, title-term distribution, keyword co-occurrence networks, thematic mapping, thematic evolution, and country-level collaboration analysis. The findings show that early research was largely grounded in neurocognitive explanations of dyscalculia, particularly numerical processing, working memory, and developmental learning difficulties. Recent publications indicate a broadening towards digital interventions, adaptive learning environments, serious games, augmented reality applications, and AI-supported assistive technologies. Studies using machine learning, deep learning, and probabilistic models suggest potential uses of AI for early screening, personalised feedback, individualised support, and cognitive support. However, AI remains an emerging rather than fully central organising theme. The review identified international collaboration patterns across Asia, the Middle East, Europe, and North America, alongside methodological and ethical issues, including limited longitudinal evidence, variability in intervention designs, biases in database and keyword selection, data privacy, and algorithmic transparency. Technology-assisted dyscalculia research has expanded from cognitive and developmental explanations towards more intervention-oriented, adaptive, and assistive technology-informed approaches. AI-supported assistive technologies appear promising for early identification, accessibility, individualised learning support, and participation in mathematics-related activities, but require stronger empirical validation, ethical implementation, user-centred evaluation, and integration into educational and rehabilitation-related support contexts.
resume_fr: This study aimed to map the development of assistive and adaptive technology-supported approaches to dyscalculia between 2005 and 2025 and to clarify how artificial intelligence, adaptive learning, and assistive technologies are positioned within this research field. titre: Graded multisensory neurofeedback via the iNems system for comprehensive upper limb recovery after stroke: a multiple baseline study.
titre_fr: Graded multisensory neurofeedback via the iNems system for comprehensive upper limb recovery after stroke: a multiple baseline study.
auteurs: Kodama Takayuki, Kitai Ken, Mizomoto Yasuhisa, Nishigaya Kaichi, Hashimoto Shoutarou, Hiraga Riona, Shimizu Satomi, Kawabata Miki, Hirabayashi Yuumi, Ikesue Keita, Kako Hazime, Yasui Syouta, Ito Hiroki, Nishimoto Kazuhei, Katayama Osamu, Yamaguchi Hideaki, Nagano Hikaru, Inoue Mari, Murata Shin, Morita Kiichiro
resume: Post-stroke upper-limb recovery remains challenging, especially in the presence of sensory impairments. Conventional brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are constrained by binary feedback, single-modality stimulation, and exclusion of patients with sensory deficits. We developed the Imagery Neurofeedback-based Multi-sensory System (iNems), a neurofeedback system that provides graded multisensory (visual and electrical) feedback based on ERD magnitude. This study validated iNems' efficacy in motor function, self-reported numbness, and cognitive functions using a multiple-baseline design (MBD). Four participants with post-stroke upper-limb motor and sensory impairments underwent a multiple baseline design. The baseline phase (phase A) used random feedback; the intervention (phase B) used adaptive iNems. iNems quantified motor intention via sensorimotor EEG event-related desynchronization (ERD) and delivered graded visual and electrical feedback. Primary outcomes were the Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) and Box and Block Test (BBT). Secondary outcomes included body cognition, numbness, and neurophysiological (ERD/ERS) changes. All participants demonstrated significant improvement during the intervention. FMA-UE increased by 6-16 points. The BBT showed large effects (integrated Tau-U = 0.75). Body cognition improved significantly in both sense of agency (Tau-U = 0.80) and ownership (Tau-U = 0.89). Numbness was reduced in affected cases (Tau-U = -0.85). Neurophysiological changes correlated with functional gains, with some patterns suggesting increased neural efficiency. This first MBD-validated demonstration shows that graded, multisensory graded neurofeedback based on ERD magnitude can improve motor, self-reported numbness, and cognitive domains after stroke. These findings support adaptive closed-loop therapy as a promising, multifaceted rehabilitation strategy.

titre: Feasibility of a multidimensional interdisciplinary rehabilitation program for people with dementia and their informal primary caregivers - a randomized pilot trial with a caregiver focus.
titre_fr: Feasibility of a multidimensional interdisciplinary rehabilitation program for people with dementia and their informal primary caregivers - a randomized pilot trial with a caregiver focus.
auteurs: Conradsson Mia, Olofsson Birgitta, Holmberg Henrik, Lindelöf Nina, Nilsson Ingeborg, Gustafson Yngve, Littbrand Håkan
resume: To improve the situation of informal caregivers, both supportive efforts for caregiver and rehabilitation for the person with dementia, may be needed. This randomized controlled pilot trial evaluated, among caregivers, the feasibility of a person-centred multidimensional interdisciplinary rehabilitation program for community-dwelling people with dementia that incorporated an education and support intervention for informal caregivers. Informal caregivers were randomized alongside the person with dementia to an intervention group (n=36) or usual care (n=31). Multiprofessional team rehabilitation for individuals with dementia and support for caregivers, were offered for one 20-week and two 4-week follow-up periods after 5 and 14 months. Caregivers were offered assessments, participation in group sessions, and individual support. After the last group session, scheduled during the last four weeks of the 20-week period, a survey was distributed. Attendance at group sessions and uptake of individual support were recorded. Blinded assessments of caregiver burden (Caregiver Burden Scale, CBS), depressive symptoms (Geriatric Depression Scale 15-item version, GDS) and health-related quality of life (Short Form 36-Health Survey, SF-36), were performed at baseline and after 5, 12, 24, and 36 months. Thirty-seven participants (56%) were spouses and 26 (39%) were adult children. Participation rate in assessments of outcomes at 36 months was 100% and 87% for intervention and control group in GDS and SF-36, respectively, and 69% and 61% for CBS, respectively. Missing data were primarily due to mortality. All caregivers in the intervention group (n=36) were assessed, and all received individual interventions by team staff. Twenty-three caregivers attended group sessions, and 21 completed a survey after the last session. Twenty (95%) caregivers reported increased knowledge about supporting the person with dementia, and 19 (90%) improved coping strategies. No significant differences were observed between groups in depressive symptoms or caregiver burden, yet differences in favour of the control group were seen in subscales of health-related quality of life at 24 and 36 months. The program, combining rehabilitation for the person with dementia with caregiver support, seems feasible regarding caregivers' participation in the intervention and study evaluation, and thus further evaluation in an adequately powered randomized controlled trial seems relevant. A future definitive trial should evaluate continuous support over a longer period adapted to the caregiver and refine assessment procedures, including conducting assessments during ongoing interventions to provide greater insights into rehabilitation and caregiver-support effects. The study protocol is published online 04/11/2015 at http://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN59155421.

titre: Association between Neuropsychological Impairments and Adaptive Functioning in Stroke Survivors: A Cross-sectional Study.
titre_fr: Association between Neuropsychological Impairments and Adaptive Functioning in Stroke Survivors: A Cross-sectional Study.
auteurs: Kumar S Aravind, Ardhanaari M, Janakiram Ashwathi, Nappinnai N R
resume: Poststroke neuropsychological deficits are common and often impact cognition, adaptive functioning, and functional independence, which can hinder successful community re-entry. To assess the relationship between neuropsychological impairments and adaptive functioning in stroke survivors and to determine independent predictors of adaptive functioning. This cross-sectional study was conducted with 122 stroke survivors aged 30-60 years from July 2025 to March 2026. Neuropsychological functioning was evaluated with the Bender-Gestalt Test and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA); the Vineland Social Maturity Scale (VSMS) was used to assess adaptive functioning; the Functional Independence Measure (FIM) was used to assess functional independence; and the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) was used to assess neurological severity. The mean MoCA, VSMS composite, and FIM scores were 25.1 ± 2.8, 90.6 ± 8.4, and 94.2 ± 12.7, respectively. MoCA scores were significantly positively correlated with VSMS composite (r = 0.53) and FIM (r = 0.62), while NIHSS scores were significantly negatively correlated with all neuropsychological and functional measures (all P < 0.05). Of the factors considered, MoCA score was the best independent predictor of adaptive functioning, followed by FIM score. Cognitive, adaptive, and functional outcomes were significantly better for participants with ischemic stroke. Adaptive functioning is strongly linked with neuropsychological functioning following stroke, and global cognitive performance and functional independence are the main predictors of adaptive functioning. A thorough evaluation of skills could help in the development of a tailored rehabilitation plan and enhance long-term outcomes.

titre: New horizons in cooking and mealtime interventions for mild cognitive impairment and early dementia: a scoping review.
titre_fr: New horizons in cooking and mealtime interventions for mild cognitive impairment and early dementia: a scoping review.
auteurs: Bannon Sarah M, Elizalde Carrillo Renata, McCage Sydney, Shahab Muhammad Hamza, Allison Grace O, Aminpour Aida, Levinson Carrie, Presciutti Alexander M, Fishel Anne
revue: The journal of nutrition, health & aging
resume: Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRDs) are increasingly common conditions that are highly disruptive to individuals and families. ADRDs impact cognition and can undermine a person's ability to participate in cooking, preparing meals, and engaging in conversations. Mealtime participation implicates key determinants of adequate nutritional intake and social connectedness. However, engaging in mealtime routines amid challenges can also exacerbate the stress and burden felt by family caregivers. Behavioral interventions can mitigate these downstream impacts, though they are currently underdeveloped. To summarize the literature on cooking and mealtime interventions for community-dwelling people with dementia and their caregivers. Scoping review. We searched databases up to May 2025 for English-language publications that described qualitative and quantitative research surrounding interventions focused on cooking and mealtime interventions for individuals living with subjective cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment, and ADRDs. At least two reviewers independently identified publications and extracted population characteristics, intervention components, and intervention outcomes. Included articles were published between 2007-2024. Qualitative and mixed methods studies (n=12) highlighted potential mechanisms for intervention, including cultivating routines for mealtimes (e.g., eating together, minimizing distractions, adaptive tools) and caregiver coping skills and training (e.g., distress tolerance, communication to emphasize respect/dignity, and social routines). Intervention studies (n=10) included caregiver skills training, education and cognitive rehabilitation-integrated cooking. Interventions were generally feasible; however, few were evaluated in randomized trials, and none underwent efficacy testing. Cooking and mealtime interventions hold promise for addressing determinants of aging in ADRDs, though further randomized controlled efficacy trials are needed.

titre: Physical activity guidelines' impact on cognition in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
titre_fr: Physical activity guidelines' impact on cognition in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
auteurs: Murphy Tanner, Lauinger Alexa, Peters Joseph, Truong Ethan, Abou Libak
resume: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to determine the effects of meeting physical activity guidelines for people with multiple sclerosis (PAG-MS) on cognition in people with multiple sclerosis (MS). Meeting PAG-MS has shown to elicit numerous health benefits in people with MS; minimal work has examined the influence of PAG-MS on cognition. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, SPORTDiscuss, Scopus, and PsycINFO. Two independent reviewers assessed included studies for eligibility, extracted data, and evaluated risk of bias. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) including physical activity that met PAG-MS and assessed cognition were included. Twelve randomized controlled trials met the inclusion criteria with 462 total participants. Eleven studies showed improvement in at least one aspect of cognition. Meta-analyses indicated meeting PAG-MS significantly improved processing speed (SMD = 0.29; 95% CI 0.08-0.51; p = 0.008), visuospatial memory (SMD = 0.47; 95% CI 0.14-0.80; p = 0.005), and verbal memory (SMD = 0.75; 95% CI 0.27-1.23; p = 0.002). Meta-analyses indicated meeting PAG-MS significantly improved processing speed and memory. The findings were based on a limited number of studies with a high risk of bias and more RCTs that meet PAG-MS and examine cognition are needed.

titre: Interventions Supporting Functional Recovery After Traumatic Brain Injury in Public Safety Personnel: A Systematic Review of Outcomes and Work Reintegration Considerations.
titre_fr: Interventions Supporting Functional Recovery After Traumatic Brain Injury in Public Safety Personnel: A Systematic Review of Outcomes and Work Reintegration Considerations.
auteurs: Shahzad Maryam, Siddiqui Sana, Premji Raihana, Liu Jonathan Jiesheng, He Yiting, Mencia Ledo Javier, Nandan Sharada, Dos Santos André Luiz Fagundes Avila, Lau Hong Ki Chloe, Afkhamiaghda Nazaninzahra, Haq Adeel, Haq Minahil, Khan Sobiah, Tam-Seto Linna, Carleton R Nicholas, Nowrouzi-Kia Behdin
revue: The Journal of head trauma rehabilitation
resume: Public safety personnel (PSP) face a heightened risk of traumatic brain injury (TBI) and barriers in resuming daily activities and returning to work (RTW). Despite these risks, evidence on interventions targeting functional recovery and participation in this population is scarce. To synthesize evidence on interventions targeting functional recovery and RTW in PSP with TBI. MEDLINE, CINAHL, EMBASE, PsycINFO, and Scopus on January 23, 2026. Eligible studies included PSP with TBI such as armed forces and/or military personnel and law enforcement personnel. Randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies, observational studies, case studies, and mixed methods designs were included. Outcomes were classified using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health framework and synthesized narratively. Risk of bias was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Twenty-one studies were included (9 randomized controlled trial, 5 cohort, 4 quasi-experimental, 3 case studies). Most studies focused on military populations, with only 2 civilian PSP studies (firefighters and police). Interventions included cognitive rehabilitation, psychological/mental health, interdisciplinary programs, simulation-based training, and physical rehabilitation. Narrative synthesis showed mixed but generally positive, improvements in body function outcomes, and cognitive function within the activity domain. Participation-level outcomes such as RTW were inconsistently defined and underreported. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low for participation outcomes to moderate for functional cognition. Interventions for PSP with TBI may support modest, but consistent, improvements in cognitive function; however, there remains low certainty of evidence for meaningful improvements in the participation domains (eg, RTW). The evidence is highly heterogeneous in outcomes and focused on military populations, limiting generalizability across PSP roles.

titre: Characterization of distinct cognitive domain patterns in AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD: A MoCA-based factor analysis and risk profiling.
titre_fr: Characterization of distinct cognitive domain patterns in AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD: A MoCA-based factor analysis and risk profiling.
auteurs: Zhang Tingting, Ma Yizuo, Wei Lai, Su Yujie, Meng Fangxia, Zhu Wenli, Wei Ruili
resume: Cognitive impairment (CI) is common in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), yet subdomain-specific patterns, modifiable risk factors, and underlying cognitive structure remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize cognitive deficits in AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD patients in stable remission, identify correlates of domain-specific impairment, and explore the latent factor structure using MoCA subscales. Sixty-one definite AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD patients in stable remission were enrolled. Assessments included MoCA, MMSE, Digit Span Test, and Hamilton Depression/Anxiety Scales. Demographic and clinical data were collected. Pearson correlation, partial correlation (controlling for age, education, and mood), multiple regression, and exploratory factor analysis (PCA with varimax rotation) were performed. Overall, 63.9% of patients had CI (MoCA < 26). Episodic memory (delayed recall: 42.6%), language repetition (36.1%), and visuospatial/executive function (34.4%) were most affected. Education (β = 0.386, p = 0.003) was the only statistically significant independent predictor in multivariate analysis; age, EDSS, depression, and anxiety showed domain-specific associations. Factor analysis revealed three networks-visuospatial-executive-language, memory-abstraction, and naming-attention networks-explaining 63.2% of variance (Cronbach's α = 0.637), suggesting three distinct cognitive domain patterns; given the modest sample size, this solution should be considered exploratory. AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD patients in stable remission show a characteristic cognitive profile with predominant episodic memory, executive, and linguistic deficits. Lower education was the only significant independent predictor of cognitive performance, while age, disability, and mood disturbances showed domain-specific associations. The three-factor cognitive structure may support domain-specific screening and targeted rehabilitation in clinical practice. Routine MoCA assessment may be considered for NMOSD patients, with priority given to older, less educated individuals and those with higher disability or comorbid depression.

titre: Outcomes Analysis of Low Back Pain Patients Managed Through a Spine Center Clinical Care Redesign Pathway: An Initial Retrospective Cohort Study.
titre_fr: Outcomes Analysis of Low Back Pain Patients Managed Through a Spine Center Clinical Care Redesign Pathway: An Initial Retrospective Cohort Study.
auteurs: Nip Isabel, Sylvain Jonathan, Chhabra Jyoti, Seetharama Subramani
revue: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
resume: Back pain affects a large portion of the U.S. population, and delivering care in an efficient manner without compromising outcomes is of utmost importance for quality of life. One potential approach is to reinvent clinical pathways to streamline care and reduce the gaps evident between recommendation and actual practice, such as high uses of surgery and imaging. To compare outcomes of acute or acute-on-chronic low back pain patients treated through a value-based structured clinical care redesign spine pathway at The Hospital of Central Connecticut (THOCC) Spine Center versus patients treated by Hartford HealthCare (HHC) ambulatory care providers/clinics that did not participate in the clinical care redesign spine pathway. Retrospective cohort study in the setting of ambulatory care referrals from primary care or community providers, urgent care, emergency department, walk-ins, or self-referral within HHC. Acute or acute-on-chronic lumbar pain patients conservatively treated with at least three physical therapy (PT) visits OUTCOME MEASURES: Initial and follow-up Modified Oswestry Low Back Pain Disability Questionnaire (MDQ) and numeric pain rating scale scores; days of first provider to first PT visit, first provider visit to completion of the acute care episode; number of provider, PT, and outside specialist visits (orthopedics, neurosurgery, neurology), and imaging studies (x-rays) METHODS: Patients were identified by querying the rehabilitation outcomes management system (ROMS) database. Variables were collected via chart and ROMS database review. Mann-Whitney-U tests with α set at 0.05 were performed. Differences in dichotomous data between the two groups were analyzed with contingency Chi-square tests or Fisher's Exact tests. Because this was a retrospective analysis of an existing cohort, no a priori sample-size calculation was performed. The final sample represents all available patients meeting the prespecified eligibility criteria during the study period. There were no statistically significant differences between the 41 patients treated through the THOCC clinical care redesign spine pathway and the 33 patients treated in the standard non-spine care pathway regarding sex, race, ethnicity, diagnosis, initial pain or disability score, or Subgroups for Targeted Treatment (STarT) Back Tool risk category. Spine Center participants were significantly older than controls (median age 52 vs 43 years, p=0.0004, effect size 0.414).
