titre: The effect of breathing exercises on pain, range of motion and quality of life in frozen shoulder rehabilitation: A randomized controlled study.
titre_fr: The effect of breathing exercises on pain, range of motion and quality of life in frozen shoulder rehabilitation: A randomized controlled study.
auteurs: Çelik Benli Songül, Akçay Genal Burçin
revue: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
resume: ObjectiveThis randomized controlled trial evaluated the effects of breathing exercises as an adjunct to conventional physiotherapy on pain, range of motion (ROM), and quality of life (QoL) in patients with frozen shoulders.MethodsForty participants (mean age 48.2 ± 9.6 years) with adhesive capsulitis were randomly allocated to either: (1) an intervention group receiving 15 sessions of conventional physiotherapy plus diaphragmatic/costal breathing exercises (n = 20), or (2) a control group receiving conventional physiotherapy alone (n = 20). Conventional therapy included ultrasound, TENS, Codman exercises, and stretching. Primary outcomes included visual analog scale (VAS) for pain, digital goniometer-measured shoulder ROM, and SF-36 QoL questionnaire, assessed at baseline and post-intervention.ResultsBoth groups showed a significant within-group reduction in post-treatment VAS scores compared with baseline (p < 0.001); the between-group difference in pain was not significant, although a significant Group × Time interaction (p = 0.007) and a lower mean post-treatment pain score in the intervention group were observed. The intervention group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in shoulder abduction (p = 0.03) and external rotation (p = 0.04) compared to controls. SF-36 results revealed between-group differences favoring the intervention group in physical role (p = 0.02) and social functioning (p = 0.03) domains, with significant group-time interactions for physical functioning, emotional role, pain, and general health (all p < 0.05).ConclusionBreathing exercises combined with conventional physiotherapy provided additional benefits for improving shoulder mobility (particularly abduction/external rotation) and quality of life domains in frozen shoulder patients, though pain reduction was equivalent between groups. These findings support the integration of respiratory exercises as a complementary approach in frozen shoulder rehabilitation.

titre: Short-term effects of extracorporeal shockwave therapy and low-level laser therapy on clinical outcomes and ultrasonographic tendon thickness in lateral elbow tendinopathy.
titre_fr: Short-term effects of extracorporeal shockwave therapy and low-level laser therapy on clinical outcomes and ultrasonographic tendon thickness in lateral elbow tendinopathy.
auteurs: Başaran Pınar Özge, Doğan Ayşe Gülşen, Çiçek Aybüke Beyza, Askerden Şükriye
revue: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
resume: BackgroundThis study aimed to compare the short-term effects of extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) and low-level laser therapy (LLLT) on pain, elbow function, health-related quality of life, hand grip strength, and ultrasonographic extensor tendon thickness in patients with LET.ObjectiveIn this prospective, randomized, controlled, single-blind trial, patients with LET were randomly assigned to either ESWT or LLLT. Both groups received the same standardized home exercise program and lateral epicondylitis brace. Visual Analog Scale (VAS), the Patient-Rated Tennis Elbow Evaluation (PRTEE), Short Form-36 (SF-36), hand grip strength, and ultrasonographic evaluation were assessed before and after three weeks of randomisation.ResultsAt three weeks, the ESWT group demonstrated significantly lower post-treatment pain intensity (VAS) than the LLLT group (p = 0.004). ESWT was also associated with significantly better outcomes in PRTEE pain scores (p = 0.030), ultrasonographic tendon thickness (p = 0.021), and the Role Physical (p = 0.029) and General Health (p = 0.005) domains of the SF-36. No significant between-group differences were observed in hand grip strength, PRTEE function, PRTEE total score, or the remaining SF-36 domains.ConclusionWhen used as adjuncts to a standardized exercise program and LET brace, ESWT was associated with greater short-term pain reduction and more favorable outcomes in the PRTEE pain subscale, ultrasonographic tendon thickness, and selected domains of health-related quality of life compared with LLLT. These findings suggest that ESWT may offer greater short-term pain-related benefits than LLLT when both are added to exercise and bracing.

titre: The Role of Targeted Rehabilitation in Enhancing Recovery After Total Hip Arthroplasty with Anterior Minimally Invasive Surgery Approach: A Retrospective Pilot Study.
titre_fr: The Role of Targeted Rehabilitation in Enhancing Recovery After Total Hip Arthroplasty with Anterior Minimally Invasive Surgery Approach: A Retrospective Pilot Study.
auteurs: Giorgino Riccardo, Ciliberto Ricardo, Roumenova Mileva Sara, Del Re Matteo, Rossi Nicolò, Sosio Corrado, Sirtori Paolo, Peretti Giuseppe M, Mangiavini Laura
revue: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
resume: Background: Hip osteoarthritis is a highly prevalent degenerative condition and a leading indication for total hip arthroplasty (THA). As anterior approaches have gained popularity, optimizing postoperative rehabilitation according to the muscles involved in recovery has become increasingly relevant. However, evidence regarding muscle-specific rehabilitation following the Anterior Minimally Invasive Surgery (AMIS) approach remains limited. Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate whether rehabilitation protocols specifically targeting the hip flexors or abductors could improve postoperative functional recovery compared with standard rehabilitation following AMIS THA. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 29 patients aged 50-80 years with BMI < 30 kg/m2 undergoing unilateral THA through the AMIS approach. The cohort included 14 men and 15 women. Patients were non-randomly allocated according to clinical and organizational factors to standard rehabilitation (ST; n = 10), a hip flexor-focused protocol (SP1; n = 10), or a hip abductor-focused protocol (SP2; n = 9). Postoperative recovery was evaluated using clinical, functional, and patient-reported outcome measures. Rehabilitation was supervised by physiotherapists. Outcomes included goniometric hip range of motion, dynamometer-measured hip flexor and abductor strength, Timed Up and Go (TUG), Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), Harris Hip Score (HHS), Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (HOOS), and SF-12. Longitudinal outcomes were analyzed using two-factor models assessing time, rehabilitation group, and their interaction, with post hoc comparisons where appropriate. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results: Of the 29 initially enrolled patients, 26 completed the study assessments and were included in the final analysis (ST, n = 9; SP1, n = 10; SP2, n = 7). Significant improvements over time were observed for hip flexion and internal rotation ROM, abductor strength, TUG, VAS, HOOS, and HHS. No consistent superiority of either targeted protocol over standard rehabilitation was identified. Postoperative improvements in hip range of motion, muscle strength, mobility, pain, and functional performance were observed over time across the study cohort. Although no protocol demonstrated statistically significant superiority in range of motion or functional outcomes, all three groups showed postoperative improvement over time following AMIS THA. Conclusions: All rehabilitation groups improved during postoperative recovery, but neither the flexor- nor abductor-focused protocol demonstrated superiority over standard rehabilitation. Given the small sample size and non-randomized design, these findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered randomized studies. Because the targeted protocols also involved a greater overall number of prescribed exercises, the present design cannot distinguish the effects of muscle-specific targeting from those of greater exercise exposure.

titre: Nonpharmacological Interventions in Degenerative Cerebellar Ataxia: A Systematic Review.
titre_fr: Nonpharmacological Interventions in Degenerative Cerebellar Ataxia: A Systematic Review.
auteurs: Garg Divyani, Yomtoob Jacob, Opal Puneet, Pal Pramod Kumar
resume: A comprehensive synthesis of nonpharmacological interventions (NPI) in degenerative cerebellar ataxia will clarify their efficacy and inform clinical practice and trial design in a field with limited therapeutic options. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-compliant systematic review was conducted (PROSPERO CRD42025649802). PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to April 16, 2025. Randomized and nonrandomized interventional studies evaluating rehabilitation, speech therapy, noninvasive neuromodulation (repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), transcranial direct current stimulation [tDCS]), virtual reality, vibration therapy, biofeedback-based, assistive devices, and complementary approaches were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklists. Given substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were consolidated narratively. A total of 100 studies met inclusion criteria. Structured physical therapy, rTMS, and tDCS demonstrated statistically significant short-term reductions in ataxia severity (measured using Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia [SARA] or International Cooperative Ataxia Rating Scale [ICARS]). Improvements were most consistent in axial domains, including gait and postural control. Limited mechanistic studies reported restoration of cerebellar inhibitory modulation, increased cerebellar-frontal connectivity, and enhanced regional perfusion following tDCS. Evidence for speech therapy, virtual reality-based rehabilitation, vibration therapy and complementary approaches was limited. Across all modalities, durability beyond the short-term remained unclear. NPI may confer short-term symptomatic and functional benefits in degenerative cerebellar ataxia, particularly in axial motor domains, supported by the largest evidence for structured rehabilitation followed by neuromodulation, although heterogeneous. Future multicenter, biomarker-informed trials are required to define optimal dosing, durability and stage-specific therapeutic strategies.

titre: Functional surgery plus rehabilitation versus physical exercise alone for Charcot-Marie-Tooth cavovarus foot deformity: a retrospective cohort study.
titre_fr: Functional surgery plus rehabilitation versus physical exercise alone for Charcot-Marie-Tooth cavovarus foot deformity: a retrospective cohort study.
auteurs: Wei Zhuoqi, Cui Zengzhen, Cao Yuan, Li Xiuzhi, Fu Yuliang, Bai Liangyu, Zhou Fang, Si Gao, Lv Yang
revue: Foot and ankle surgery : official journal of the European Society of Foot and Ankle Surgeons
resume: Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) cavovarus foot deformity severely impairs walking. This study evaluated walking and functional outcomes in patients managed with functional surgery plus rehabilitation (FS) or physical exercise alone (PE). This retrospective matched cohort study included 109 CMT patients (55 FS, 54 PE) followed for 2 years. Primary outcomes were the 10-Meter and 6-Minute Walk Tests (10MWT, 6MWT). Secondary outcomes included walking disability (Walk-12, FADI), quality of life (SF-12), ankle mobility, and clinical symptoms. In the FS group, 10MWT improved significantly at 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years (all p < 0.05). In the PE group, 10MWT improved significantly only at 6 months. 6MWT improved significantly in both groups at all follow-up points. At 2 years, the FS group showed significant reductions in falls (-21.8%; p = 0.019), callus formation (-16.4%; p = 0.026), and mobility aid use (-25.4%; p = 0.002), whereas the PE group showed no significant changes in these symptoms. CMTES remained unchanged in both groups. In appropriately selected patients with CMT-related foot deformity, both treatments improved walking function in the short term. FS was also associated with sustained reductions in falls, calluses, and mobility aid use at 2 years, whereas PE showed no significant changes in these symptoms.

titre: Can the functional assessment of abdominal, diaphragmatic, and pelvic floor muscles reflect post-prostatectomy urinary incontinence severity?
titre_fr: Can the functional assessment of abdominal, diaphragmatic, and pelvic floor muscles reflect post-prostatectomy urinary incontinence severity?
auteurs: Meslin Manuel, Ndziha Salvatore Metanmo, Modestine Johan Rose Dite, Drame Moustapha, Kara Norelyakin, Minchaca Céline
resume: Post-prostatectomy incontinence can substantially impair patients' quality of life. While rehabilitation typically targets the pelvic floor muscles, the role of the diaphragm and deep abdominal muscles is under-explored. This study aimed to determine the utility of evaluating and managing the transversus abdominis (TrA), diaphragm, and levator ani muscle (LAM) to facilitate post-prostatectomy urinary incontinence recovery. This single-center observational cohort study included 90 patients. During post-prostatectomy rehabilitation, we regularly assessed muscle capacity using a standardized clinical examinations comprising nine tests. Capacity score ranges were 0-2, 0-3, and 0-4 for the TrA, diaphragm, and levator ani. Data were collected until continence was restored or improvement plateaued, generally by 8 months. Incontinence was classified as severe, moderate, mild, or corrected. Spearman's rho assessed associations between incontinence grade and muscle scores. Higher muscle scores were associated with lower incontinence severity. The most consistently significant correlation was with the TrA, followed by the diaphragm (p < 0.05). LAM scores were no longer significantly correlated with incontinence from month 4 onward. Only patients in the corrected-continence group passed both TrA tests. Improved functional capacity of the TrA, diaphragm, and LAM was associated with the recovery of urinary continence. This association was strongest for the TrA. Our findings support the functional assessment of these three muscles in the evaluation and management of post-prostatectomy urinary incontinence.

titre: Liposomal bupivacaine utilization in the pain management of postoperative selective dorsal rhizotomy patients.
titre_fr: Liposomal bupivacaine utilization in the pain management of postoperative selective dorsal rhizotomy patients.
auteurs: Scott Victoria A, Walker David, Khoury Issa, Hill Christine A, Mundluru Surya N, Hall Stacey L, Thakur Nivedita, Gautam Nischal, Chen Bingrui, Pedroza Claudia, Javaid Simra, Wilson Sarah M L, Fraser Stuart, Shah Manish N
resume: Selective dorsal rhizotomy (SDR) is a procedure commonly utilized to treat spasticity in children with cerebral palsy. Limited studies have evaluated postoperative pain management with the objective of opiate dosage reduction. This retrospective cohort study examined the role of liposomal bupivacaine (LB) in postoperative pain management and the outcomes of SDR patients. This retrospective study used the Pediatric Movement Disorders Center's prospective database to query electronic medical records for demographic, surgical, and postoperative data for all patients who underwent SDR from 2023 through 2025. Patients were divided into two groups: those treated with 0.25% bupivacaine HCl (comparison group) or a mixture of LB and bupivacaine HCl (LB group). Both modalities were administered via local infusion during closure of the SDR incision. All patients also received our previously developed protocol that includes infusion of dexmedetomidine during SDR surgery combined with perioperative gabapentin and scheduled acetaminophen and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs postoperatively, henceforth referred to as the dexmedetomidine infusion (INF) protocol. Operative duration, postoperative opioid and nonopioid medication administration, and therapy notes were collected for 41 patients. Patients who underwent SDR between May 2023 and July 2024 received our INF postoperative pain management protocol and bupivacaine HCl (comparison group [n = 20]). Patients who underwent SDR between October 2024 and July 2025 received INF along with a mixture of bupivacaine HCl and LB (LB group [n = 21]). Differences in demographic characteristics, preoperative Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) scores, operative duration, hospital length of stay (LOS), and postoperative opiate/nonopiate medication administration were recorded. When converted to morphine milligram equivalent, there were no significant differences in opioid dosage or total opioid use between groups. There was a trend toward significance, in that the comparison group participated in physical therapy for a longer duration than the LB group on postoperative day 2. This was attributed to differences in discharge dates between the two groups: the LB group was more likely to be discharged on postoperative day 2 than the comparison group due to changes in our center's rehabilitation pathway during this study. Local infiltration of LB mixed with standard bupivacaine, given at the conclusion of SDR surgery in conjunction with our established postoperative pain management protocol, was not associated with decreased use of postoperative pain medications when compared to the infusion of standard bupivacaine.

All patients also received our previously developed protocol that includes infusion of dexmedetomidine during SDR surgery combined with perioperative gabapentin and scheduled acetaminophen and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs postoperatively, henceforth referred to as the dexmedetomidine infusion (INF) protocol. Operative duration, postoperative opioid and nonopioid medication administration, and therapy notes were collected for 41 patients. Patients who underwent SDR between May 2023 and July 2024 received our INF postoperative pain management protocol and bupivacaine HCl (comparison group [n = 20]). Patients who underwent SDR between October 2024 and July 2025 received INF along with a mixture of bupivacaine HCl and LB (LB group [n = 21]). Differences in demographic characteristics, preoperative Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) scores, operative duration, hospital length of stay (LOS), and postoperative opiate/nonopiate medication administration were recorded. When converted to morphine milligram equivalent, there were no significant differences in opioid dosage or total opioid use between groups. There was a trend toward significance, in that the comparison group participated in physical therapy for a longer duration than the LB group on postoperative day 2. This was attributed to differences in discharge dates between the two groups: the LB group was more likely to be discharged on postoperative day 2 than the comparison group due to changes in our center's rehabilitation pathway during this study. Local infiltration of LB mixed with standard bupivacaine, given at the conclusion of SDR surgery in conjunction with our established postoperative pain management protocol, was not associated with decreased use of postoperative pain medications when compared to the infusion of standard bupivacaine.

titre: Management of fragile X-associated tremor ataxia syndrome: a review for clinicians.
titre_fr: Management of fragile X-associated tremor ataxia syndrome: a review for clinicians.
auteurs: Hall Deborah A, González David Andrés, Klusek Jessica, Todd Peter K, O'Keefe Joan A, Maltman Nell, Montanaro Federica Alice Maria, Protic Dragana, Scorr Laura, Malik Rabia, Turcano Pierpaolo, Meyers Matthew S, Seritan Andreea
resume: Fragile X-associated tremor ataxia syndrome (FXTAS) is a multi-faceted and progressive neurodegenerative disorder that manifests clinically with action tremor, gait ataxia, parkinsonism, peripheral neuropathy, and cognitive and psychiatric features. The disease is highly heterogeneous and there are no FDA approved medications for FXTAS as a specific indication. As such, treatment is symptomatic and must be tailored to the specific needs of a given patient. This review provides expert opinion-based treatment recommendations for the core and ancillary clinical features of FXTAS. Movement disorders, such as tremor, ataxia and parkinsonism may respond to symptomatic medications and therapies, but caution is required when considering surgical interventions such as deep brain stimulation. Cognitive decline can be responsive to medications developed for other cognitive disorders, but these medications work best when combined with non-medication based approaches and all patients should be screened for other reversible causes of memory decline. Psychiatric symptoms, including anxiety, depression, and psychosis, can be treated with psychotherapy and medications; but caution is required to avoid exacerbating clinical and subclinical movement disorder features with psychotropic medications. Rehabilitative therapies, such as speech therapy, occupational, and physical therapy, often enhance patient function and quality of life. Exercise and good nutrition are recommendations that are common to other cerebellar ataxias and adult neurodegenerative disorders and may have a positive impact on general health. A multi-disciplinary approach is recommended to address all components of FXTAS.

titre: Coordinating Pelvic Floor Physical Therapy Care Across the Perinatal Period.
titre_fr: Coordinating Pelvic Floor Physical Therapy Care Across the Perinatal Period.
auteurs: Dreisbach Caitlin
revue: Journal of obstetric, gynecologic, and neonatal nursing : JOGNN
resume: Perineal injury during childbirth can contribute to maternal morbidity through pain, impaired bowel control, and limitations in activities of daily living. Nurses can help patients access pelvic floor physical therapy during pregnancy and postpartum recovery. In this column, I examine evidence on pelvic floor interventions for birth preparation and rehabilitation after perineal injury. I describe opportunities for nurses to support pelvic floor care through patient education, assessment of barriers to care, and care coordination with physical therapists and obstetric clinicians. I also discuss interdisciplinary care models that nurses can adapt to support continuity of pelvic floor care across the perinatal period.

titre: Individually Prescribed In-Bed Exergaming Using Nintendo Ring Fit Adventure in Posttransplant Inpatients With Marked Functional Impairment After Intensive Care: Prospective Single-Arm Feasibility Study.
titre_fr: Individually Prescribed In-Bed Exergaming Using Nintendo Ring Fit Adventure in Posttransplant Inpatients With Marked Functional Impairment After Intensive Care: Prospective Single-Arm Feasibility Study.
auteurs: Koo Yong Hoe, Son Woo Chul, Woo In Ho, Kim Ye Ji, Yoon Soo Hoon, Kim Ji Hye, Song Young Cheon, Kim Ho Cheol, Jung Dong-Hwan, Ryu Jiwon, Shin Gwanseob, Choi Jaesoon, Kim Won
resume: Early rehabilitation is important after transplantation and critical illness, but profound weakness, fatigue, and motivational, psychological, and safety barriers may limit participation. Exergaming may facilitate rehabilitation, but the feasibility of full-body in-bed exergaming in this population remains unclear. We evaluated the feasibility and observed safety of individually prescribed in-bed exergaming using Nintendo Ring Fit Adventure (NFA; Nintendo Co, Ltd) in posttransplant inpatients after intensive care unit (ICU) care. This prospective, single-center, single-arm interventional feasibility study (October 2024-October 2025) enrolled 26 posttransplant adults with prior ICU care and Functional Ambulation Category (FAC) scores ≤3. Participants were referred after ward transfer by transplant-team advanced practice nurses, and the principal investigator confirmed eligibility based on prespecified inclusion and exclusion criteria. Ten individually prescribed, supervised in-bed NFA sessions, each scheduled for 30 minutes, including setup and operation, were planned alongside usual physical therapy. Data were obtained from medical records, standardized session logs, and prespecified clinical and questionnaire assessments. Outcomes included retention; session delivery, completion, and interruptions; exercise-item completion and interruptions; session-terminating adverse events; net exercise time; satisfaction; and exploratory strength, mobility, and health-related quality-of-life changes. Participants (mean age 53.0, SD 12.4 y; 14 men) included 23 liver and 3 bilateral lung transplant recipients. Mean ICU stay and mechanical ventilation duration were 24.3 (SD 11.0) days and 21.3 (SD 11.6) days, respectively; median baseline FAC and Medical Research Council Sum Score were 0.5 (IQR 0.0-1.0) and 38.0 (IQR 30.5-42.0), respectively. None had an FAC score above 2. Twenty completed the final assessment (20/26, 76.9%, 95% CI 57.9%-89%). Of 227 delivered sessions, 223 (98.2%, 95% CI 95.8%-100%) were completed. Of 2161 prescribed exercise items, 2072 (95.9%, 95% CI 93.4%-97.9%) were completed. No session-terminating adverse events were observed (0/227, 0%, 95% CI 0%-1.6%). Median within-participant net exercise time increased by 159.0 (IQR 35.5-296.3) seconds from sessions 1 to 10 (95% CI 81.0-284.0; Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P<.001). Friedman tests followed by Bonferroni-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (2-sided α=.05) showed baseline-to-final median within-participant changes of 8.0 Medical Research Council Sum Score points (IQR 2.3-10.3; 95% CI 4.0-10.0, P=.004), 2.0 Intensive Care Unit Mobility Scale points (IQR 1.0-4.3; 95% CI 1.0-3.5, P<.001), and 15.0 EQ-VAS points (IQR 0.0-30.0; 95% CI 5.0-25.0, P=.009). Questionnaire responses were favorable. Under therapist supervision, the individually prescribed in-bed NFA program showed favorable operational feasibility, with no session-terminating adverse events. By combining the accessibility of a commercial off-the-shelf exergame with individualized exercise prescription, the program extended bedside exergaming to posttransplant inpatients with substantial functional impairment after ICU care who had not achieved independent ambulation.

titre: Effects of different postoperative rehabilitation approaches following shoulder arthroplasty: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effects of different postoperative rehabilitation approaches following shoulder arthroplasty: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Zou Jiahui, Shi Yihong, Remis Andréas, Liu Shan, Hao Jie
resume: The optimal postoperative rehabilitation protocol after shoulder arthroplasty remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) aimed to compare the effectiveness of different rehabilitation interventions. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the PEDro scale and RoB 2 tool. Meta-analysis was performed with a random-effects model. Nine RCTs (793 patients) were included; PEDro scores ranged from 5 to 8. In reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA), home-based rehabilitation was non-inferior to outpatient physical therapy for range of motion, patient-reported outcomes, and pain at 1 year. Early mobilization improved forward flexion at 3 months, but this difference was no longer evident at 6 months; in one anatomic TSA trial, it was associated with a trend toward lower lesser tuberosity healing. Subscapularis-specific training did not confer additional benefits. Home-based or telerehabilitation is a safe, potentially cost-effective alternative after rTSA; limited evidence for anatomic TSA suggests similar trends. Early mobilization offers transient functional gains, and current evidence is insufficient to recommend subscapularis-specific training. These findings highlight the need for further high-quality trials, especially in anatomic TSA.

titre: Sleep, inflammation, and pain in musculoskeletal rehabilitation: a structured integrative review of neurobiological mechanisms and non-pharmacological pain management strategies.
titre_fr: Sleep, inflammation, and pain in musculoskeletal rehabilitation: a structured integrative review of neurobiological mechanisms and non-pharmacological pain management strategies.
auteurs: de Freitas Eder Moreira, Silva Andressa, Esteves Andrea Maculano
resume: Sleep disturbance, inflammation, and persistent pain may reinforce one another, compromising musculoskeletal rehabilitation. To synthesize evidence on mechanisms linking sleep, inflammation, and pain and identify relevant non-pharmacological interventions. This structured integrative review examined peer-reviewed studies published from January 2010 to December 2025, identified through PubMed, Scopus, PEDro, and SciELO. Reporting and synthesis were guided by SANRA and EQUATOR recommendations. Fifty-seven studies were included: 24 experimental or observational studies, 17 systematic reviews or meta-analyses, and 16 narrative or integrative reviews. Sleep restriction was associated with changes in interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and C-reactive protein, with responses varying across populations and protocols. Prostaglandins and bradykinin may promote nociceptive sensitization, while disrupted sleep may impair descending pain inhibition. Exercise, manual therapy, neuromuscular electrical stimulation, low-level laser therapy, and sleep-focused behavioral interventions showed mechanistic plausibility, although confirmatory trials remain limited. Sleep assessment and sleep-focused interventions should be considered within multimodal musculoskeletal pain management, while further controlled research clarifies clinical effectiveness.

titre: The content and reporting completeness of physical therapist-led interventions for glenohumeral osteoarthritis: a systematic review.
titre_fr: The content and reporting completeness of physical therapist-led interventions for glenohumeral osteoarthritis: a systematic review.
auteurs: Muhammad Daha G, Foster Nadine E, Pelaez Mickylle, O'Leary Karina, Ackerman Ilana N, Quicke Jonathan G
resume: This study synthesised the content and reporting completeness of published physical therapist-led interventions for glenohumeral osteoarthritis (GHOA). This systematic review undertook electronic database searches in PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane, CINAHL and PEDro (until June 2025) for any peer-reviewed articles/studies describing physical therapist-led interventions across non-surgical and perioperative settings for adults aged 45 years and over with GHOA. The content and reporting completeness were synthesized using the 22-item Template for Intervention Description and Replication for rehabilitation interventions (TIDIeR_Rehab). Overall, 134 articles/studies describing 156 physical therapist-led interventions were included, comprising mostly case series designs (n=47, 35.1%) or narrative reviews (n=38, 28.4%). Of the remaining 49 articles/studies, only 11 were studies reporting RCT results and three were protocols of RCTs in progress. Intervention content varied considerably, and the overall completeness of intervention item reporting was poor (only 18%). Interventions in non-surgical contexts commonly included strengthening exercises (n=33, 53.2%), range of motion (ROM) exercises (n=23, 37.1%), and electrotherapy modalities (n=16, 25.8%). Sling immobilisation was most reported in postoperative interventions (n=64, 72.7%). Many different proposed mechanisms of action were reported (n=49, 31.4%); but all were biomechanically orientated. Very few high-quality empirical studies evaluating physical therapist-led interventions for GHOA have been published. We found substantial heterogeneity in the content of published physical therapist-led interventions, and the reporting completeness was generally poor. This suggests considerable uncertainty regarding best practice physical therapy for GHOA in terms of intervention content. Future high-quality empirical research is needed, preferably using RCT designs that include clear descriptions of interventions.

titre: TeleBACK clinical trial: comparing the effectiveness of telerehabilitation and in-clinic physical therapy for patients with chronic low back pain - protocol for a multicentre, pragmatic, individually randomised group treatment trial.
titre_fr: TeleBACK clinical trial: comparing the effectiveness of telerehabilitation and in-clinic physical therapy for patients with chronic low back pain - protocol for a multicentre, pragmatic, individually randomised group treatment trial.
auteurs: McLaughlin Kevin H, Fritz Julie M, Minick Kate I, Hunter Stephen, Moffit Steven, Schneider Matthew, Lane Elizabeth, Ford Isaac, Romero Adrianna, Colantuoni Elizabeth, Wegener Stephen T, Skolasky Richard L
resume: Chronic low back pain (LBP) is a leading cause of disability and healthcare spending in the USA. While physical therapy (PT) has been shown to improve disability and pain as well as decrease the cost of care associated with LBP, only a small portion (<15%) of eligible patients with LBP ever attend PT. These low utilisation rates are likely influenced by logistical barriers to attending visits (eg, transportation, missed work time). Patients with chronic pain may also struggle to attend frequent clinic visits because of their symptoms. Telerehabilitation, which expanded substantially during the COVID-19 pandemic, can potentially address these barriers by allowing patients to receive PT remotely. However, the effectiveness of telerehabilitation for chronic LBP is unclear. This multicentre, pragmatic, individually randomised group treatment, non-inferiority clinical trial will compare synchronous, video-based telerehabilitation with standard in-clinic PT in 1000 adults with chronic LBP (≥3 months duration) receiving primary or specialty care across three healthcare systems in Maryland and Utah. Participants will be randomised 1:1 to receive eight PT sessions over 8 weeks via either video conferencing or in-clinic visits and will be assessed at baseline, 3 months, 6 months and 1 year. The primary outcome is 3-month change in LBP-related disability as measured by the Oswestry Disability Index using a non-inferiority margin of 6 points, based on the minimal clinically important difference for this measure. Secondary outcomes include changes in pain intensity, pain interference and physical function, and LBP-related opioid and healthcare utilisation. Exploratory measures include treatment satisfaction and therapeutic alliance. This study was approved by the Johns Hopkins Medicine Institutional Review Boards (IRB), which serves as the single IRB for this study. Once the study is complete, study data will be shared in compliance with guidelines from the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute. NCT06821607.

titre: Pre-stroke frailty in patients with first-ever acute stroke: Its associations with stroke subtype and impact on activities of daily living.
titre_fr: Pre-stroke frailty in patients with first-ever acute stroke: Its associations with stroke subtype and impact on activities of daily living.
auteurs: Iwasawa Tatsuya, Aoyagi Yoichiro, Sakamoto Yuki, Ohashi Miho, Ikeda Satoshi, Saito Tomonari, Shimoyama Takashi, Suda Satoshi
resume: Few studies have examined frailty in patients with first-ever stroke who were independent in activities of daily living (ADLs) prior to onset. This study aimed to investigate the characteristics of pre-stroke frailty and its impact on ADLs at discharge. In this prospective cohort study, 152 patients aged ≥65 years with first-ever stroke admitted to the stroke unit of a university hospital were enrolled. Pre-frailty/frailty was assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS). Associations between frailty status and clinical characteristics were evaluated. Multivariate regression analysis identified independent predictors of the Barthel Index (BI) at discharge. Pre-frailty/frailty was present in 35.5% of patients, and was associated with higher rates of atrial fibrillation (p = 0.043) and cardioembolic stroke (p = 0.001). Compared with the robust group, the pre-frailty/frailty group had significantly lower BI scores at both admission and discharge, as well as more extended hospital stays. Both groups, however, demonstrated significant improvement in BI at discharge (p < 0.001). Multivariate analysis revealed that NIH Stroke Scale score (p < 0.001), stroke type (p = 0.010), and CFS score (p = 0.044) independently predicted BI at discharge. Pre-stroke frailty is associated with a higher risk of cardioembolic stroke and poorer functional status during hospitalization. Nevertheless, patients with frailty still achieved significant ADL improvement with rehabilitation, underscoring the importance of active rehabilitation strategies in this population.

titre: Association of Early Energy Gap With Activities of Daily Living and In-Hospital Complications in Patients With Acute Stroke.
titre_fr: Association of Early Energy Gap With Activities of Daily Living and In-Hospital Complications in Patients With Acute Stroke.
auteurs: Murata Hiroyasu
resume: Early nutritional adequacy may influence functional recovery and complications after stroke, but the clinical relevance of the magnitude of early energy deficit relative to estimated requirements remains insufficiently characterized. This study examined the association between the energy gap during the first 7 days after admission and discharge activities of daily living and in-hospital complications in patients with acute stroke. This retrospective observational study included 304 patients with ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke (median age, 77 years [IQR, 66-85]; 46.7% male) who were admitted to a Japanese university hospital and hospitalized for at least 7 days. Energy gap was calculated as mean daily total energy intake, including oral, enteral, and parenteral nutrition, minus estimated energy requirements of 25 kcal/kg ideal body weight/day during the first 7 days after admission. The primary outcome was total Functional Independence Measure score at discharge, and the secondary outcome was the occurrence of in-hospital complications. Multivariable linear and logistic regression analyses were performed. The median energy gap was -2.7 kcal/kg/day. Patients with severe energy deficit had lower discharge Functional Independence Measure scores and a higher occurrence of in-hospital complications. In multivariable analysis, a higher energy gap was associated with a higher total Functional Independence Measure score at discharge (B = 0.54, 95% CI 0.17-0.91, P = 0.005) and lower odds of in-hospital complications (OR = 0.91, 95% CI 0.86-0.96, P = 0.001). The association with in-hospital complications remained consistent across sensitivity analyses. A lower early energy gap was associated with poorer functional status at discharge and a higher occurrence of in-hospital complications in patients with acute stroke. These findings suggest that early energy gap may provide clinically relevant information regarding nutritional adequacy and clinical status.

In multivariable analysis, a higher energy gap was associated with a higher total Functional Independence Measure score at discharge (B = 0.54, 95% CI 0.17-0.91, P = 0.005) and lower odds of in-hospital complications (OR = 0.91, 95% CI 0.86-0.96, P = 0.001). The association with in-hospital complications remained consistent across sensitivity analyses. A lower early energy gap was associated with poorer functional status at discharge and a higher occurrence of in-hospital complications in patients with acute stroke. These findings suggest that early energy gap may provide clinically relevant information regarding nutritional adequacy and clinical status.

titre: Balance confidence, balance, and gait capacity in chronic stroke: baseline and change correlations.
titre_fr: Balance confidence, balance, and gait capacity in chronic stroke: baseline and change correlations.
auteurs: Moon Hyun-Min
resume: Balance confidence is associated with selected balance and gait measures after stroke, but whether changes in confidence track concurrent changes in objective capacity is unclear. This prespecified secondary analysis included 168 independently ambulant adults with chronic stroke from a single-center randomized trial. Balance confidence was assessed with the Activities-specific Balance Confidence scale. Objective outcomes included center-of-pressure sway velocity, limits of stability, Berg Balance Scale, Timed Up and Go, 10-Meter Walk Test time, and instrumented spatiotemporal gait measures. Pearson correlations with 95% confidence intervals and false discovery rate correction were used; Spearman, intervention-arm-centered change, and height-normalized spatial gait analyses assessed robustness. At baseline, associations between ABC scores and objective balance and gait measures were small, and none were statistically significant after false discovery rate correction. Change-to-change associations were also small, and none remained significant after multiplicity adjustment. Intervention-arm centering eliminated the unadjusted treadmill-speed association observed in the pooled change analysis, whereas the small association with center-of-pressure sway velocity remained similar but did not survive false discovery rate correction. Height normalization of spatial gait measures did not materially alter the findings. Balance confidence was weakly coupled with measured balance and gait capacity at baseline and over time. The findings do not establish independence but support assessing perceived confidence and objective capacity as complementary outcomes after stroke.

titre: The impact of kidney dysfunction on functional outcomes in a convalescent rehabilitation ward: a retrospective cohort study.
titre_fr: The impact of kidney dysfunction on functional outcomes in a convalescent rehabilitation ward: a retrospective cohort study.
auteurs: Yabe Hiroki, Tabata Aki, Iio Shintaro, Kunieda Kenjiro, Shigematsu Takashi, Fujishima Ichiro
resume: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) impairs physical function and activities of daily living, yet the relationship between CKD severity and inpatient rehabilitation outcomes in patients who have not started dialysis remains unclear. We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of 10 832 patients admitted to a convalescent rehabilitation ward between April 2014 and March 2023. Patients were stratified by CKD stage based on estimated glomerular filtration rate and grouped into  mild or no kidney dysfunction (stages 1-3a) and advanced kidney dysfunction (stages 3b-5). Functional outcomes were evaluated using the Functional Independence Measure at admission and discharge. Key outcomes were functional independence measure gain, functional independence measure efficiency (functional independence measure gain per hospital day), functional independence measure effectiveness (proportion of potential improvement achieved) and length of stay. Between-group and stage-based comparisons were performed using analysis of covariance adjusting for confounders. Among the 10 832 patients (mean age 73.1 ± 14.9 years), 3361 (31.0%) had CKD stages 3a-5. Individuals in the kidney dysfunction group were older and had lower serum albumin and hemoglobin than those in the non-kidney dysfunction group. Compared to patients with mild or no kidney dysfunction, those in the kidney dysfunction group had shorter length of stay (52.6 ± 31.7 vs 59.6 ± 39.4 days, P < .001), lower gain in functional independence measure (14.6 ± 14.4 vs 16.9 ± 15.5 points, P < .001), and reduced functional independence measure effectiveness (0.34 ± 0.35 vs 0.40 ± 0.39, P < .001), whereas functional independence measure efficiency did not differ between groups (P = .98). Kidney dysfunction was independently associated with less functional improvement and worse functional independence measure effectiveness during convalescent rehabilitation, partially due to shorter hospitalization and reduced total rehabilitation dose. Tailored rehabilitation programs that address kidney dysfunction-related vulnerabilities, including nutritional and metabolic optimization, may enhance recovery outcomes in this population.

titre: Baseline serum 25 hydroxyvitamin D concentration does not predict functional recovery in intensive inpatient rehabilitation: a retrospective observational study.
titre_fr: Baseline serum 25 hydroxyvitamin D concentration does not predict functional recovery in intensive inpatient rehabilitation: a retrospective observational study.
auteurs: Bellone Federica, Alito Angelo, Turriziani Laura, Spadaro Giuseppe, Crescimone Simone, Catalano Antonino, Cipolla Eliana, Malacarne Fabio, Squadrito Giovanni, Basile Giorgio
resume: Vitamin D deficiency is highly prevalent among hospitalized patients, and its effects on skeletal muscle function and systemic inflammation suggest that baseline status might influence functional recovery; however, evidence specifically in intensive inpatient rehabilitation remains scarce. In this retrospective observational cohort study, 97 adults (mean age 65.0 ± 13.1 years) admitted to intensive inpatient rehabilitation were enrolled. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] obtained within 48 h of admission was analyzed both as a continuous variable and categorized into deficient, insufficient, and sufficient groups. The primary outcome was the Functional Independence Measure (FIM) at discharge adjusted for admission score; secondary outcomes included the Barthel Index (BI), Functional Ambulation Category (FAC), 6-min walk test (6MWT), and length of stay. Hierarchical linear regression was performed adjusting for admission functional status, age, comorbidity burden, and diagnostic group, with robust standard errors and bootstrap confidence intervals. Hypovitaminosis D affected 78.4% of patients. Despite substantial functional improvement across the cohort, baseline serum 25(OH)D was not associated with any outcome measure-neither as a continuous variable nor across vitamin D categories-in unadjusted or fully adjusted analyses. Admission functional status (i.e., FIM) was the dominant predictor in all models. Baseline serum 25(OH)D did not predict functional recovery during intensive inpatient rehabilitation, irrespective of outcome measure. Although hypovitaminosis D was highly prevalent and warrants correction for skeletal health, the present study did not find evidence to support the use of serum 25(OH)D as a prognostic marker of rehabilitation outcome.

titre: Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis with psychiatric manifestations and choreiform movements: a case report and literature review.
titre_fr: Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis with psychiatric manifestations and choreiform movements: a case report and literature review.
auteurs: Shen Han Yao, Chen Xin, Yu Run Ze, Wu Wei Jie, Dou Xing Ying, Fan Xing Juan
resume: To summarize the clinical manifestations, ancillary examination findings, treatment course, and prognosis of a patient with neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis presenting with prominent psychiatric disturbances and choreiform movements, and to review the literature on the clinical spectrum of this disease. A 52-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and biopsy-proven podocytopathy with a "full-house" immunofluorescence pattern showing diffuse positivity for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, and C1q, diagnosed in February 2026; however, a definitive diagnosis of lupus podocytopathy remained uncertain, as the patient lacked systemic lupus erythematosus manifestations. She was admitted on April 3, 2026, with a 5-day history of psychiatric disturbances and involuntary choreiform movements in all four limbs, preceded by significant psychological stress (bereavement). Neurological examination revealed slowed responses and impaired calculation. Cranial MRI showed only bilateral periventricular small ischemic foci (Fazekas grade 1) with normal SWI. Initial EEG demonstrated sharp waves and spike-and-wave complexes in the left parietal, occipital, and temporal regions. CSF analysis revealed leukocytosis (21/μl, 90% mononuclear cells), protein of 0.4 g/L, elevated IgG index of 0.76, and elevated 24-hour intrathecal IgG synthesis rate of 5.63 mg/dl. CSF mNGS detected 453 EBV sequences (RPM) with a relative abundance of 97.48%. Serum EBV VCA-IgG and EBNA-IgG were elevated with negative IgM. Autoantibody testing followed a stepwise approach: initial screening for conventional autoimmune encephalitis, paraneoplastic, and demyelinating antibodies was negative; subsequent tissue-based assay (TBA) of CSF revealed strong positive immunoreactivity, prompting expanded antibody panel testing, which ultimately detected anti-neurexin-3α antibodies in serum (titer 1:30) and CSF (titer 1:100), confirmed by both cell-based assay (CBA) and TBA. The patient's condition progressively deteriorated, requiring endotracheal intubation on April 21 and tracheostomy on April 30. She received methylprednisolone pulse therapy at 500 mg/day for 5 days followed by a stepwise taper, intravenous immunoglobulin at 0.4 g/kg for 5 days, and five sessions of plasma exchange from April 30 to May 8 due to poor initial response. Choreiform movements gradually resolved after plasma exchange. She was weaned from mechanical ventilation on May 19 and decannulated on May 27. During the ICU course, she developed pulmonary infection with carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, which was controlled after antibiotic adjustment. Repeat EEG normalized on June 1. She was discharged from rehabilitation on June 9 on oral methylprednisolone 32 mg/day. On June 26, 2026, follow-up serum TBA showed weakly positive immunoreactivity, with the serum antibody titer remaining at 1:30. She subsequently received four infusions of efgartigimod at 400 mg each for consolidation immunotherapy and was transitioned to ofatumumab for long-term maintenance. At follow-up on August 6, 2026, the patient had no residual psychiatric symptoms or choreiform movements, with muscle strength recovered to 4+ in all limbs, full independence in daily activities, ambulation without assistance, and only mild gait instability. Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis is a rare but treatable condition. Choreiform movements expand its clinical spectrum. The coexistence of podocytopathy raises a hypothesis of shared antigenicity between renal and neuronal neurexin family members, though this remains purely speculative. CSF EBV reactivation may represent a bystander phenomenon or epiphenomenon of severe immune dysregulation rather than a confirmed trigger. Tissue-based assay provides crucial diagnostic direction when conventional screening is negative. Early recognition, comprehensive immunotherapy, and meticulous ICU management are important determinants of favorable outcomes. Given the inherent limitations of a single case report, these findings warrant confirmation through larger cohort studies.

titre: Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation in Postoperative Recovery after Total Hip Arthroplasty and Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Narrative Synthesis.
titre_fr: Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation in Postoperative Recovery after Total Hip Arthroplasty and Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Narrative Synthesis.
auteurs: Ain Zikra, Gupta Govind Kumar, Rai Arpita, Ranjan Rakesh
resume: Lower limb arthroplasties, including total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA), are established surgical interventions for advanced degenerative joint diseases; however, patients frequently encounter persistent postoperative challenges such as pain, muscle weakness, restricted range of motion (ROM), impaired balance, and altered gait patterns. Proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) is increasingly utilised in orthopaedic rehabilitation to address these neuromuscular deficits, extending beyond its conventional neurological scope. This narrative review evaluates and consolidates evidence on the efficacy of PNF-integrated rehabilitation regarding pain management, functional recovery, muscular strength, joint ROM, balance, and gait performance in adult patients undergoing THA and TKA. We conducted a comprehensive literature search across multiple electronic databases up to June 2026, screening studies that evaluated preoperative or postoperative PNF interventions against standard care, conventional physiotherapy, or no intervention. We synthesised ten studies, including randomised controlled trials, non-randomised comparative trials, and case reports. The pooled evidence indicates that incorporating PNF into lower limb arthroplasty rehabilitation accelerates functional recovery, enhances muscular strength, facilitates early improvements in active and passive joint ROM, sharpens static and dynamic balance, mitigates fall risk, and optimises spatiotemporal gait parameters compared with standard protocols alone. In conclusion, PNF represents a clinically valuable modality in post-arthroplasty musculoskeletal care, and clinicians should consider embedding individualised, supervised PNF protocols early into rehabilitation pathways to optimise functional independence and long-term quality of life.

titre: Collaborative Nursing Integrating Cognitive Rehabilitation and Nutritional Management for Cognitive Impairment Associated with Neurological Disorders.
titre_fr: Collaborative Nursing Integrating Cognitive Rehabilitation and Nutritional Management for Cognitive Impairment Associated with Neurological Disorders.
auteurs: Fang Weiqing, Tan Lili
resume: This retrospective study aimed to examine whether receipt of an integrated collaborative nursing model centered on multidimensional cognitive rehabilitation was associated with cognitive, nutritional, and functional outcomes among patients with cognitive impairment due to neurological disorders. A total of 150 patients admitted between May 2024 and May 2026 were retrospectively included. According to the nursing model actually received during hospitalization, patients were classified into an observation group of 69 patients, who received integrated collaborative nursing centered on cognitive rehabilitation and integrated with nutritional risk management, daily living task training, family collaboration, and continued post-discharge follow-up, and a control group of 81 patients, who received routine neurological nursing. Implementation indicators were higher in the observation group, including cognitive training completion (88.41% vs. 56.79%) and post-discharge follow-up completion (86.96% vs. 67.90%). After adjustment for age, sex, education level, primary neurological diagnosis, disease course, cognitive impairment severity, and the corresponding baseline outcome, the observation group had higher post-intervention Montreal Cognitive Assessment (adjusted mean difference, 2.26 points; 95% CI, 1.68-2.84), Mini Nutritional Assessment-Short Form (MNA-SF) (1.22 points; 95% CI, 0.88-1.55), and Barthel index scores (9.62 points; 95% CI, 7.15-12.10), p < 0.001; adjusted Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), instrumental activities of daily living‌ (IADL), and functional independence measure (FIM) outcomes showed the same direction of association. These findings indicate short-term associations between the receipt of the integrated collaborative nursing model and improvements in implementation, cognitive, nutritional assessment, functional, and continuity-of-care outcomes; the retrospective, non-randomized design does not establish causality.

titre: Effect of epidural spinal cord stimulation combined with personalized neurorehabilitation in chronic motor-complete spinal cord injury: study protocol for the phase II single-arm feasibility RESTORES (RESToration Of Rehabilitative function with Epidural spinal Stimulation) trial.
titre_fr: Effect of epidural spinal cord stimulation combined with personalized neurorehabilitation in chronic motor-complete spinal cord injury: study protocol for the phase II single-arm feasibility RESTORES (RESToration Of Rehabilitative function with Epidural spinal Stimulation) trial.
auteurs: Wan Kai Rui, Ng Zhi Yan Valerie, Wee Seng Kwee, Misbaah Fatimah, Lui Wen Li, Phua Min Wee, Plunkett Tegan, Robinson Neethu, Phyo Wai Aung Aung, Guan Cuntai, Sidarta Ananda, So Rosa Qi Yue, Premchand Brian, Susanto Kezia, Cocchi Luca, Saffari Seyed Ehsan, Ker Rui Xin Justin, Ng Wai Hoe
resume: Chronic motor-complete spinal cord injury (SCI) results in profound neurological disability with minimal prospects for functional recovery using conventional rehabilitation strategies. Emerging evidence suggests that epidural spinal cord stimulation (eSCS) can activate dormant spinal locomotor networks and restore volitional and autonomic functions when combined with intensive activity-based training. However, systematic evaluation of multimodal neuromodulation approaches integrating advanced rehabilitation and computational neurophysiology remains limited. The RESTORES trial (RESToration Of Rehabilitative function with Epidural spinal Stimulation) is a prospective, single-arm Phase II feasibility study enrolling 15 adults with chronic (≥1 year) motor-complete SCI (American Spinal Injury Association Impairment scale (AIS) A or B) between C5 and T12. Participants will undergo implantation of an epidural spinal cord stimulator followed by a 24-week program of structured stimulation-coupled personalised neurorehabilitation (five sessions per week). Clinical outcomes will be evaluated using standardized neurological and functional measures including the AIS motor score, Spinal Cord Independence Measure version III (SCIM-III), Walking Index for Spinal Cord Injury II (WISCI-II), and Trunk Assessment Scale (TASS). Autonomic function and quality of life will also be assessed. Multimodal neurophysiological measurements-including surface electromyography (sEMG), electroencephalography (EEG), resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI), and computer-vision-based movement analysis-will be performed to investigate neural recovery mechanisms and inform the development of adaptive neuromodulation systems. The primary outcome is the safety of epidural spinal cord stimulation implantation, defined as the absence of device explantation for safety-related reasons within 6 months following implantation. Secondary outcomes include changes in AIS motor score, functional outcomes (SCIM, WISCI-II, TASS), autonomic function, quality of life, and neurophysiological biomarkers. This study integrates neuromodulation, advanced rehabilitation technologies, and multimodal computational neurophysiology to evaluate both clinical efficacy and neural mechanisms of recovery following chronic SCI. Findings from the RESTORES trial will provide critical safety and feasibility data to inform future multicenter trials and the development of closed-loop spinal cord stimulation systems. ClinicalTrials.gov, Identifier NCT05644171.

titre: A machine learning model for predicting cognitive improvement after scalp cluster needling therapy in patients with post-stroke mild cognitive impairment.
titre_fr: A machine learning model for predicting cognitive improvement after scalp cluster needling therapy in patients with post-stroke mild cognitive impairment.
auteurs: Hao Yican, Wei Xia, Zhao Pingli, Qin Hewei
resume: Cognitive recovery varies substantially among patients with post-stroke mild cognitive impairment (PSCI-MCI), whereas individualized models for predicting post-treatment cognitive improvement remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a machine learning model for predicting cognitive improvement after 1 month of scalp cluster needling therapy with prolonged needle retention (SCNT-PR) in patients with PSCI-MCI. This retrospective study included hospitalized patients diagnosed with PSCI-MCI between January 1, 2010, and January 1, 2023. Baseline data included demographics, vascular risk factors, stroke severity, imaging features, cognitive and functional assessments, emotional and sleep-related indicators, treatment-related variables, and laboratory findings. The outcome was defined as an increase of at least 2 points in the corrected Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score after treatment compared with baseline. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and the Boruta algorithm were used to identify key predictors. Seven supervised machine learning algorithms were applied to develop pretreatment prediction models. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used for model interpretation. A total of 750 patients were included and randomly assigned to a training set (n = 526) and a validation set (n = 224). Seven key predictors were identified from the intersection of LASSO regression and Boruta. Among the evaluated models, LightGBM showed the acceptable performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.759. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis indicated acceptable calibration and favorable clinical utility. SHAP analysis identified baseline corrected MoCA score, years of education, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale total score, Barthel Index score for activities of daily living, age, frontal lobe lesion, and diabetes as the major contributors to model prediction. resume_fr: Cognitive recovery varies substantially among patients with post-stroke mild cognitive impairment (PSCI-MCI), whereas individualized models for predicting post-treatment cognitive improvement remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a machine learning model for predicting cognitive improvement after 1 month of scalp cluster needling therapy with prolonged needle retention (SCNT-PR) in patients with PSCI-MCI. This retrospective study included hospitalized patients diagnosed with PSCI-MCI between January 1, 2010, and January 1, 2023. Baseline data included demographics, vascular risk factors, stroke severity, imaging features, cognitive and functional assessments, emotional and sleep-related indicators, treatment-related variables, and laboratory findings. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and the Boruta algorithm were used to identify key predictors. Seven supervised machine learning algorithms were applied to develop pretreatment prediction models. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used for model interpretation. A total of 750 patients were included and randomly assigned to a training set (n = 526) and a validation set (n = 224). Seven key predictors were identified from the intersection of LASSO regression and Boruta. Among the evaluated models, LightGBM showed the acceptable performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.759. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis indicated acceptable calibration and favorable clinical utility. SHAP analysis identified baseline corrected MoCA score, years of education, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale total score, Barthel Index score for activities of daily living, age, frontal lobe lesion, and diabetes as the major contributors to model prediction. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated consistent predictor patterns under alternative outcome definitions and predictor configurations. We developed and internally validated a machine learning model based on multidimensional pretreatment clinical data to predict cognitive improvement after SCNT-PR in patients with PSCI-MCI. This model may provide preliminary support for patient stratification and individualized clinical assessment, although external validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

titre: Digital technology acceptance among older adults: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses on theoretical perspectives, determinants, and evidence base.
titre_fr: Digital technology acceptance among older adults: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses on theoretical perspectives, determinants, and evidence base.
auteurs: Han Saihong, Huang Fei, Bai Zhangyunfan, Zhao Xianjin, Chan Alan Hoi Shou, Chen Ke
resume: Digital and assistive technologies can support independence and ageing in place, yet their potential benefits remain constrained by challenges in acceptance and sustained engagement. This umbrella review examined the theoretical foundations of technology acceptance research among older adults, synthesised determinants associated with acceptance, and explored variations across technologies, populations, and implementation contexts. Following PRIOR guidelines, six databases were systematically searched. Forty-eight systematic reviews encompassing 1,602 primary studies were included. Narrative synthesis, including framework-based mapping, integrated findings across reviews, while quantitative re-meta-analysis quantified the strength and consistency of associations where comparable estimates were available. More than half of the included reviews lacked an explicit theoretical framework, while most others relied on TAM/UTAUT-based models. Fifty-nine determinants were identified across five domains: individual characteristics, technology attributes, environmental factors, social and cultural influences, and process-related attributes. Re-meta-analysis showed highly suggestive evidence for associations involving perceived usefulness, ease of use, facilitating conditions, social influence, and anxiety, although substantial heterogeneity was observed. Limited reporting of participant characteristics and implementation stages constrained subgroup comparisons. Reviews of AI-enabled technologies emphasised anthropomorphic and interactive features but gave comparatively limited attention to accessibility, contextual integration, and user diversity. Technology acceptance in later life is dynamic and context-dependent, with current theoretical models and empirical evidence providing limited explanation of how acceptance develops and varies across users and implementation settings. Future research should move beyond accumulating determinants towards lifespan-informed approaches that explain the mechanisms through which acceptance develops and is sustained across diverse later-life contexts.

titre: Comparative effects and dose-response relationships of exercise for finger dexterity and upper-limb function in Parkinson's disease: a Bayesian network and model-based dose-response meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Comparative effects and dose-response relationships of exercise for finger dexterity and upper-limb function in Parkinson's disease: a Bayesian network and model-based dose-response meta-analysis.
auteurs: Liu Bu-Yu, Zhuang Yu-Xin, Zhuang Chang-Kuan, Ruan Hui
resume: Upper-limb impairment limits independence in Parkinson's disease (PD), but the comparative effects and dose-response profiles of exercise modalities remain uncertain. PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science, Scopus, and SPORTDiscus were searched from inception to June 20, 2026. Studies that qualified were randomized controlled trials of structured exercise or rehabilitation in adults with PD. Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis and model-based dose-response network meta-analysis were conducted separately for finger dexterity and upper-limb function. Weekly dose was expressed as metabolic equivalent of task minutes per week (MET·min/week), and evidence certainty was assessed using CINeMA. Thirty-six reports comprising 1,575 participants were included. Aerobic exercise training (Hedges' g 1.46, 95% CrI 0.26-2.69) and task-oriented finger-dexterity training (0.96, 0.23-1.67) improved finger dexterity versus usual care. Low-certainty evidence suggested that mind-body exercise may improve upper-limb function, although the unusually large estimate (Hedges' g = 6.90, 95% CrI 4.28-9.43) was based on only two small trials involving 53 participants in the relevant comparison arms. Given the sparse evidence and local inconsistency in the modality-specific dose-response analysis, this result should be regarded as exploratory and interpreted cautiously. Models fitted to mapped dose nodes suggested an approximately linear association for finger dexterity and diminishing incremental gains for upper-limb function. Predictions toward 1,800 MET·min/week partly extended beyond the highest representative dose nodes and remained uncertain. Exercise effects were outcome specific. The findings can inform exercise-modality selection and future dose-ranging trials, but they do not establish an optimal dose or justify a uniform clinical prescription. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261463560, identifier: CRD420261463560.

titre: Behavioural intervention and guided stepping training early post-stroke (BIG STEPS): protocol for a multicentre randomised controlled trial.
titre_fr: Behavioural intervention and guided stepping training early post-stroke (BIG STEPS): protocol for a multicentre randomised controlled trial.
auteurs: van Eeden Charmaine, Khan Aiza, Alemayehu Wendimagegn, Anderson Sharon, Buck Brian H, D'Amico Jessica M, Dukelow Sean P, Hayward Jake, McCabe Erin, Spence John C, Tandon Puneeta, Yu Jaime C, Ezeugwu Victor E
resume: Physical inactivity and prolonged sedentary time are associated with lower functional and quality of life outcomes after stroke, and may increase the risk of stroke recurrence. Yet, the best way to manage these movement behaviours after stroke remains uncertain. This study aims to test the effects of a 3-month behavioural intervention and guided stepping training early post-stroke (BIG STEPS) programme on daily step counts, sedentary time, timed walking outcomes and patient-reported fatigue, cognitive function and quality of life. This is a multicentre, assessor-blinded, waitlist-controlled, randomised controlled trial to be completed within 60 months from August 2026 to July 2031. A total of 150 participants in the early subacute stroke recovery phase (<3 months post-stroke), 50 years and older, who are able to walk at least 5 m will be recruited from six centres in Canada. Participants will be randomly assigned (1:1) to an early BIG STEPS intervention group or delayed BIG STEPS waitlist control group. Blinded assessors will complete in-person assessments at baseline and at 3, 6, 9 and 12 months post-baseline. BIG STEPS will be delivered by trained interventionists in a blended format (1 initial in-person +11 virtual sessions). The primary outcome will be daily step counts at 3 months post-baseline, measured with an activPAL accelerometer and inclinometer. In addition, changes over time in 24-hour movement behaviours, timed-walking tests and patient-reported outcomes will be evaluated. Ethical approval for this study was obtained from the Health Research Ethics Board at the University of Alberta, Edmonton, Canada (Approval Number: Pro00140017). The results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed open-access publications, scientific conferences, participating clinical sites and knowledge translation activities to contribute to the evidence base for behaviour change interventions after stroke. NCT07702643.

titre: Physical Exercise in Rehabilitation Nursing: Qualitative Analysis in the Portuguese Clinical Context.
titre_fr: Physical Exercise in Rehabilitation Nursing: Qualitative Analysis in the Portuguese Clinical Context.
auteurs: Novo André, Mendes Eugénia, Preto Leonel, Martins Maria Manuela, Schoeller Soraia
revue: Rehabilitation nursing : the official journal of the Association of Rehabilitation Nurses
resume: To analyze how the principles of Buen Vivir, interpreted through Axel Honneth's Theory of Recognition, are expressed in rehabilitation nursing practice through the use of physical exercise. Qualitative, exploratory-descriptive study. The study was conducted in Portugal between January and April 2025 with 13 Rehabilitation Nurse Specialists, purposefully selected. Semistructured interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using Bardin's content analysis technique, following a deductive approach, with double coding, investigator triangulation, and support from ATLAS.ti software. The analysis identified quotes related to physical exercise and organized them into two categories: principles of Buen Vivir (subcategories: harmony with nature; solidarity and reciprocity; cultural pluralism and diversity; collective well-being) and pillars of the Theory of Recognition (subcategories: love; rights; and solidarity). Beyond the clinical dimension, physical exercise is perceived by Rehabilitation Nurse Specialists as a practice that promotes reconnection with nature, community solidarity, and active citizenship. This perspective expands the international evidence by emphasizing environmental, social, and cultural dimensions. Rehabilitation Nurse Specialists demonstrate a transformative model of care centered on dignity, autonomy, and solidarity. The findings highlight the potential of physical exercise as a means to foster Buen Vivir and Recognition.

titre: Population epigenomics of plant DNA methylation: perspectives for molecular breeding.
titre_fr: Population epigenomics of plant DNA methylation: perspectives for molecular breeding.
auteurs: Long Xi, Zheng Juyun, Fang Lei, Zhao Ting
revue: Journal of Zhejiang University. Science. B
resume: DNA methylation, a key epigenetic modification, contributes to regulatory diversity in plants and plays important roles in phenotypic plasticity and environmental adaptation. Recent population epigenomic studies have revealed extensive methylation variation across plant genomes, characterized genomic distribution and genetic architecture, and demonstrated both its dependence on and partial independence from underlying DNA sequence variation. These studies have further linked methylation variation to gene expression regulation, domestication, local adaptation, and complex trait variation through integrative analyses and epigenome-wide association research. Advances in high-throughput sequencing have enabled the generation of population-scale plant methylomes across natural accessions, wild relatives, landraces, and breeding germplasm, providing new avenues to systematically investigate epigenomic diversity and its functional consequences. In parallel, public methylome resources, epigenomic databases, and multi-omics analytical platforms are accelerating comparative and cross-species analyses of plant epigenomic variation. Future efforts that integrate population methylomes with genomics, transcriptomics, chromatin accessibility, three-dimensional genome organization, deep learning-based analytical frameworks, and targeted epigenome editing are expected to facilitate the discovery of epigenetic breeding markers, promoting the application of epigenomic variation in crop improvement.

titre: Genome-wide characterization and evolutionary expansion of the BLVRB gene family in Parnassius butterfly species.
titre_fr: Genome-wide characterization and evolutionary expansion of the BLVRB gene family in Parnassius butterfly species.
auteurs: Zhu Wei, Li Yali, Tang Fan, Zhu Zhenyao, Hu Zeyu, Hu Zixian, Hao Jiasheng, Su Chengyong
resume: Despite the pivotal role of biliverdin reductase B (BLVRB) in redox homeostasis, its evolutionary history in insects remains poorly understood. Here, we characterized the BLVRB gene family across the representative lepidopteran species, revealing a lineage-specific expansion in the alpine butterfly genus Parnassius. The expansion, primarily driven by tandem duplications under purifying selection, exhibits gene length variations significantly correlated with accumulation of transposable elements (TEs). Moreover, multiple comparisons based on tissue-, intra- and inter-specific gene expression profiles revealed that while the ancestral BLVRB retained constitutive expression for homeostasis regulation, several duplicated paralogs have evolved inducible and lineage-specific transcriptional pattern, supporting that their adaptive functional specialization likely happened during post-duplication process. These findings suggested that both the TE-mediated gene expansion and potentially functional diversification of BLVRB genes synergistically provided the genetic substrate for local adaptation, and might play a critical role in facilitating the dispersal of Parnassius into novel high-altitude habitats.
