titre: Comparative effects of different exercise training modalities on exercise capacity, pulmonary function, and health-related quality of life in patients with interstitial lung disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Comparative effects of different exercise training modalities on exercise capacity, pulmonary function, and health-related quality of life in patients with interstitial lung disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
auteurs: Li Yaozong, Wang Jian, Zhang Shujuan, Wu Fan, Zhang Wei
resume: Exercise training is central to pulmonary rehabilitation for interstitial lung disease (ILD), but the comparative effects of different exercise modalities remain uncertain. We compared their effects on exercise capacity, pulmonary function, and health-related quality of life. Six databases were searched from inception to June 11, 2026. Randomized controlled trials of exercise training in adults with ILD were included. Interventions were classified as aerobic training (AER), aerobic plus resistance training (AER_RES), respiratory-focused training comprising breathing exercises or inspiratory muscle training (BREATH_IMT), aerobic plus resistance plus breathing training (AER_RES_BREATH), mind-body exercise (MIND_BODY), or control (CON). Frequentist random-effects network meta-analyses evaluated changes in 6-min walk distance (6MWD), percentage predicted forced vital capacity (FVC% predicted), and St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) total score. Mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated. RoB 2 and CINeMA were used to assess risk of bias and confidence in the evidence. Twenty-six trials involving 1,409 participants were included. Compared with CON, all active modalities improved 6MWD, with MDs ranging from 29.46 m for AER (95% CI 11.82-47.10) to 57.12 m for AER_RES_BREATH (95% CI 41.76-72.48). AER_RES_BREATH produced greater estimated improvements than AER (MD 27.67 m, 95% CI 4.25-51.08) and AER_RES (MD 25.18 m, 95% CI 6.69-43.68), although these comparisons relied mainly on indirect evidence. Only AER_RES_BREATH showed a small improvement in FVC% predicted versus CON (MD 3.08 percentage points, 95% CI 0.05-6.12), with limited robustness and low confidence. AER_RES, AER_RES_BREATH, and MIND_BODY improved SGRQ total scores (MDs 10.08-15.20 points). Findings for 6MWD were the most robust across sensitivity analyses. Exercise training improves functional exercise capacity and may improve health-related quality of life in adults with ILD. AER_RES_BREATH showed the strongest signal for 6MWD, but limited direct comparisons preclude its designation as the optimal intervention. Evidence for FVC% predicted was less robust and should not be interpreted as evidence of disease modification. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261399024, identifier PROSPERO CRD420261399024.

titre: Selected traditional Chinese medicines for treating amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: a Bayesian network meta-analysis based on randomised controlled trials.
titre_fr: Selected traditional Chinese medicines for treating amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: a Bayesian network meta-analysis based on randomised controlled trials.
auteurs: Shen Chen, Wu Xiao-Ti, Yin Heng, Zuo Jing-Ling, Zhang Chen-Hao, Cao Feng, Zhang Ying, Tian Zi-Yu, Robinson Nicola, Liu Jian-Ping
resume: To assess the effectiveness of specific Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) therapies for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) using Bayesian network meta-analysis. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, EMBASE, Web of Science, and four Chinese databases up to 15th December 2024 was searched, including RCTs on adult Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis patients treated with TCM therapies (Chinese herbal medicine, preparations, non-pharmacological treatments) alone or combined with conventional treatments. Controls included no intervention, placebo, conventional treatments, or combinations. Primary outcomes were functional status (ALSFRS, ALSFRS-R, AALSS, m-Norris scales). Bayesian network meta-analysis compared treatment effects and calculated SUCRA values. Thirty-five RCTs involving 27 TCM therapies were included. No significant differences in functional status or quality of life were found among TCM therapies, ICT, Riluzole alone, and Riluzole plus placebo. For functional status, Shenmai injection + ICT (SUCRA 0.735 for ALSFRS, 0.870 for ALSFRS-R), Jiweiling injection + placebo (SUCRA 0.868 for ALSFRS), Jiawei Sijunzi decoction alone (SUCRA 0.739 for ALSFRS-R), Acupuncture + rehabilitation exercises + Riluzole (SUCRA 0.928 for AALSS, 0.863 for m-Norris) and Shenzhe Jiangqi powder + placebo (SUCRA 0.860 for m-Norris) had the highest probabilities of being superior treatment. For quality of life, Thunder fire moxibustion + Riluzole and Jiweiling injection + placebo for ALSAQ-40 were favorable. Despite no significant differences in functional status among TCM therapies, ICT, Riluzole alone, and Riluzole plus placebo, Jiweiling injection, Shenmai injection, Jiawei Sijunzi decoction, and Shenzhe Jiangqi powder may be regarded as candidate preparations for ALS patients. Future research should focus on real-world data to explore long-term effects and practical benefits. https://inplasy.com/inplasy-2024-8-0050/, identifier INPLASY202480050.

titre: Effects of oral hygiene care on swallowing recovery in hospitalised patients with post-stroke dysphagia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effects of oral hygiene care on swallowing recovery in hospitalised patients with post-stroke dysphagia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Pojmonpiti Sungkrit, Meersschaut Mariska, Batens Katja, Baudelet Margot, De Herdt Veerle, Janssens Barbara
resume: To evaluate the effects of oral hygiene care on swallowing-related outcomes in hospitalised patients with post-stroke dysphagia (PSD). A systematic literature search was conducted in MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, CINAHL, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov up to May 2026. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and non-RCTs with a comparison group that reporting swallowing-related outcomes were included. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 for RCTs and ROBINS-I for non-RCTs. Where appropriate, meta-analyses were conducted using random-effects models to estimate mean differences (MDs), odds ratios (ORs) and risk differences (RDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The certainty of the evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. Nine studies, comprising 7 RCTs and two non-RCTs, were included, with risk-of-bias ratings ranging from low risk to some concerns for RCTs and moderate risk for non-RCTs. Oral hygiene care increased the odds of achieving independent oral intake compared with usual care (OR = 2.54, 95% CI, 1.80; 3.59; I2 = 0%), corresponding to a 13% absolute increase (RD = 0.13, 95% CI, 0.03; 0.23; I2 = 0%). Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS; scores 1-7), with higher scores indicating more independent and unrestricted oral intake, favoured oral hygiene care (MD = 0.40, 95% CI, 0.07; 0.72; I2 = 0%). Similarly, Gugging Swallowing Screen (GUSS; scores 0-20), assessing swallowing safety and dysphagia severity, favoured oral hygiene care (MD = 2.93, 95% CI, 1.01; 4.85; I2 = 0%). The certainty of the evidence for achieving independent oral intake was rated as high. Oral hygiene care supports swallowing recovery in patients with PSD, particularly independent oral intake and should be considered an active component of dysphagia rehabilitation.

titre: Effectiveness of interventions for caregiver burden and quality of life of informal caregivers of stroke survivors: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effectiveness of interventions for caregiver burden and quality of life of informal caregivers of stroke survivors: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Lin Meijuan, Xie Sicong, Wang Benguo, Siu Alice Kwai-Yee
resume: Informal caregivers, who play a pivotal role in post-stroke care, frequently report substantial caregiver burden and reduced quality of life (QoL), which may adversely affect caregiving capacity and stroke rehabilitation outcomes. However, evidence regarding effective interventions to lessen caregiver burden and improve the QoL of informal caregivers remains fragmented. This study aimed to synthesize evidence on the effectiveness of interventions for reducing the caregiver burden and improving the QoL of informal caregivers of stroke survivors. A systematic search of eight databases (PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, and PsycINFO) was conducted until June 18, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published in English were included if they investigated the caregiver burden or QoL of informal caregivers of stroke survivors. The revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (RoB 2.0) was used to assess the risk of bias in the eligible studies. Random-effects meta-analyses using the DerSimonian-Laird method were conducted to pool data on caregiver burden and QoL. Subgroup analyses were performed based on the defined intervention characteristics. Overall, 39 RCTs involving 3,096 informal caregivers of stroke survivors were included in this analysis. Meta-analyses showed that standalone (psycho)education yielded the largest effect size in reducing the caregiver burden (k = 12; Hedges' g = 0.87; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.52 to 1.23; I2  = 86.31%), followed by the medium effect size of (psycho)education plus skill building (k = 12; Hedges' g = 0.62; 95% CI: 0.28 to 0.97; I2  = 84.86%) and the small effect size of multicomponent interventions (the combination of (psycho)education, skill building, and support interventions; k = 3; Hedges' g = 0.27; 95% CI: 0.03 to 0.52; I2  = 0.00%). However, the combination of (psycho)education and support interventions was not significantly associated with caregiver burden (k = 4; Hedges' g = 0.23; 95% CI: -0.04 to 0.49; I2  = 0.00%). Standalone (psycho)education was the only intervention associated with significant improvements in the QoL of informal caregivers of stroke survivors (k = 7; Hedges' g = 1.11; 95% CI: 0.39 to 1.83; I2  = 94.09%). Subgroup analyses indicated that larger effect sizes for both caregiver burden and QoL tended to be observed when interventions exclusively targeted informal caregivers, were researcher-led, spanned both hospital and home settings, used hybrid delivery modalities (face-to-face and remote), and comprised 5-9 sessions. Standalone (psycho)education demonstrated the largest pooled effect estimate for reducing caregiver burden and improving the QoL of informal caregivers of stroke survivors. These findings hold important clinical and practical implications for healthcare professionals by informing the design and implementation of caregiver-support interventions. Further high-quality studies are warranted to confirm these findings and identify the optimal intervention package. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/register/TemplatePreview, identifier: CRD420251152425.

titre: Effects of transcranial direct current stimulation on patient-reported outcomes in chronic low back pain: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effects of transcranial direct current stimulation on patient-reported outcomes in chronic low back pain: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis.
auteurs: Wang Chenming, Zhou Nianting, Zhang Sizhuo, Chen Peng
resume: Growing evidence suggests that central nervous system alterations may contribute to the persistence of chronic low back pain (CLBP). Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) can effectively modulate cortical excitability and holds considerable potential for the rehabilitation of CLBP. However, evidence regarding its effects remains controversial. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the effects of tDCS on pain, disability, and psychosocial outcomes in individuals with CLBP. Five electronic databases were searched from their inception to January 20, 2026. Randomized controlled trials were included to evaluate the effects of tDCS in CLBP individuals. Meta-analysis was performed using the random-effects model implemented in the metafor package in R. Subgroup analyses were based on tDCS polarity, electrode placement, current intensity, treatment sessions, and comparison type. A total of 14 randomized controlled trials were included. Meta-analysis results showed that compared with the control group, the tDCS group reported significantly reduced pain (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -0.40, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.61 to -0.19, P < 0.001) and disability (SMD = -0.18, 95 CI: -0.34 to -0.03, P < 0.02) in individuals with CLBP. However, no significant effects were observed for follow-up pain (SMD = -0.19, 95% CI: -0.46-0.08, P = 0.173), follow-up disability (SMD = -0.10, 95% CI: -0.26-0.05, P = 0.194), quality of life (SMD = 0.17, 95% CI: -0.08-0.41, P = 0.179), anxiety (SMD = -0.04, 95% CI: -0.23-0.15, P = 0.659), or depression (SMD = -0.18, 95% CI: -0.49-0.12, P = 0.241). Subgroup analyses based on tDCS polarity, electrode placement, current intensity, treatment sessions, and comparison type showed variations in effect estimates, but no significant between-subgroup differences were detected. Current evidence suggests that tDCS may reduce pain and produce a small improvement in disability in individuals with CLBP. Given the low-to-moderate certainty of the available evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. identifier CRD420261286288.

titre: Optimizing exercise regimens for quality of life in patients with cancer: a network meta-analysis and dose-response study.
titre_fr: Optimizing exercise regimens for quality of life in patients with cancer: a network meta-analysis and dose-response study.
auteurs: Hui Zhengxin, Li Liang, Zhang Yinping, Fan Tonggang
resume: To systematically evaluate the effects and dose-response relationships of different exercise interventions in improving the quality of life of patients with cancer using a combined Bayesian network meta-analysis and network dose-response meta-analysis approach. Systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library (up to August 2026). Interventions were ranked using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA), and dose-response relationships were modelled using the Emax model. A total of 149 randomized controlled trials involving 13,004 patients with cancer were included. Network meta-analysis showed that Qigong/Tai Chi, high-intensity interval training (HIIT), and combined aerobic and resistance training were the highest-ranked interventions according to SUCRA. Model-based dose-response analysis suggested a nonlinear association between exercise dose and quality of life, with the model-estimated overall effect peaking at approximately 2000 MET-min/week. This study compared exercise modalities and dose-response characteristics, identifying model-derived dose estimates associated with the greatest quality-of-life improvements in patients with cancer. titre: The effects of telerehabilitation in patients with chronic low back pain: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
titre_fr: The effects of telerehabilitation in patients with chronic low back pain: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
auteurs: Liu Jingyi, Law Sheung Wai, Cheung Wing Hoi, Wong Ronald Man Yeung, Liu Chaoran
resume: ObjectiveLow back pain (LBP) represents a predominant cause of rehabilitation needs worldwide. Telerehabilitation has the potential to improve health systems by decentralizing clinical services and expanding healthcare accessibility. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to evaluate the effectiveness of telerehabilitation compared to face-to-face (FtF) rehabilitation or minimal interventions (e.g. usual care, educational booklets, advice to stay active) in treating chronic LBP based on existing worldwide data.MethodsPubMed, Web of Science, and EMBASE were searched from inception to February 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing telerehabilitation to face-to-face therapy or minimal interventions in adults with chronic LBP (ID: CRD420251083396).Results21 RCTs (2148 participants) were included. Telerehabilitation showed a statistically significant reduction in pain intensity (Hedges' g = -0.37, 95% CI: -0.68 to -0.06). No statistically significant effects were observed for disability level or kinesiophobia. Quality-of-life outcomes showed favorable descriptive trends in specific domains, although no consistent significant effects were observed across instruments. Subgroup analyses for pain intensity showed that a statistically significant reduction was exclusively captured in the 8-week duration (Hedges' g = -0.50, 95% CI: -0.93 to -0.07). 2 of 3 economic evaluations suggested potential cost savings in specific contexts. The certainty of evidence was rated as "low" for pain intensity and "very low" for all other outcomes, with wide prediction intervals.ConclusionsTelerehabilitation may reduce pain intensity compared to FtF rehabilitation or minimal interventions in adults with chronic LBP, with the greatest effect observed in the 8-week subgroup. No significant improvements were observed in disability level or kinesiophobia, while quality-of-life outcomes showed inconsistent effects across instruments. Given the low to very low certainty of evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Telerehabilitation may represent a clinically viable alternative for selected patients with chronic LBP.

titre: Impact of motor guided imagery therapy on stroke patients with pain symptoms: a three-level meta-analysis and systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
titre_fr: Impact of motor guided imagery therapy on stroke patients with pain symptoms: a three-level meta-analysis and systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
auteurs: Li Xinmo, Ni Hong, Cui Guangze, Wei Chen, Zhu Yongguo
resume: Post-stroke pain is a common and intractable complication that hinders neurorehabilitation progress. Motor Guided Imagery (MGI), an emerging rehabilitation technique based on brain-computer interaction principles, has shown potential in relieving post-stroke pain, yet high-quality evidence on its multi-dimensional efficacy remains insufficient. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the effects of MGI on pain, sensorimotor function, sleep quality, life status, and psychological mood in stroke patients using a three-level meta-analysis. This study aimed to quantitatively assess the therapeutic effects of Motor Guided Imagery for stroke-related pain and explore potential intervention moderators using a three-level meta-analysis framework. Eight Chinese and English databases were searched from inception to June 29, 2025, to collect randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of MGI for stroke patients with pain. A three-level random-effects model was adopted to pool Hedges' g effect sizes, accompanied by heterogeneity testing, moderator analysis, influence analysis, and publication bias assessment. Influence-based outlier detection was implemented; analyses retaining all effect-size observations were treated as the primary main analysis, while outlier-removed analyses were reported only as supplementary sensitivity checks. Motor-guided imagery training significantly relieved pain (g = -0.524, 95% CI -0.779 to -0.269, p = 0.0006; negative Hedges' g indicates clinical improvement for this outcome) and improved sleep quality (g = -1.658, 95% CI -2.115 to -1.201, p < 0.001; negative Hedges' g indicates clinical improvement for this outcome) in stroke patients. Meanwhile, it significantly enhanced motor function (g = 1.395, 95% CI 0.963 to 1.826, p < 0.001), life status (g = 1.757, 95% CI 0.966 to 2.549, p = 0.0012), and psychological-emotional status (g = 1.729, 95% CI 1.045 to 2.413, p = 0.0002); positive Hedges' g indicates clinical improvement for the latter three outcomes. Moderator analysis indicated that acute-phase intervention (≤4 weeks) and high-frequency regimens (>5 sessions/week) tended to produce better analgesic effects, while age, gender, single-session duration, and pain location had no significant moderating effects. MGI may produce beneficial rehabilitation effects that can alleviate post-stroke pain and synergistically improve motor function, sleep, daily-living ability, and psychological state of stroke patients. Exploratory subgroup trends indicated potentially larger effects for early implementation within the acute phase and high-frequency short-duration regimens. However, these observations should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating clues given non-significant overall moderator tests. Further high-quality research is required to confirm these findings. The systematic review protocol was retrospectively registered with PROSPERO under registration ID CRD420261278812, after literature search and full-text screening had been completed. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261278812; identifier: CRD420261278812.

titre: Mirror therapy for upper limb motor recovery after stroke: a meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Mirror therapy for upper limb motor recovery after stroke: a meta-analysis.
auteurs: Man Yi, Liu XiaoPei, Feng Xinyi
resume: To systematically evaluate the rehabilitation effect of mirror therapy (MT) on upper limb motor function in stroke patients, thereby providing evidence-based support for clinical rehabilitation decision-making. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating MT for upper limb dysfunction after stroke were retrieved from the PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and EMBASE databases. The risk of bias in the included studies was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool 2.0 (RoB 2.0). A meta-analysis was performed, and the grade of evidence was determined using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) system. A total of 21 RCTs were ultimately included. The meta-analysis showed that MT significantly improved the total score of the Fugl-Meyer Assessment Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) in stroke patients (Mean Difference [MD] = 5.45, 95% Confidence Interval [95% CI]: 3.50-7.41, p < 0.001). Hand function showed a statistically significant but clinically modest improvement (MD = 1.16, 95% CI: 0.03-2.29, p = 0.04); however, sensitivity analysis indicated that this statistical significance was not robust and depended on a small number of high-weight studies. A positive trend toward improvement was observed for shoulder-elbow-forearm function (MD = 1.79, 95% CI: -0.02 to 3.60, p = 0.05). However, no statistically significant improvement was found for wrist joint function (MD = 0.65, 95% CI: -0.17 to 1.47, p = 0.12). Heterogeneity was low across outcomes. No clear evidence of publication bias was detected; however, the number of studies was small for some outcomes, limiting the power of funnel plots and Egger's test. The overall quality of evidence was moderate to low. MT may improve global upper limb motor function in stroke patients, with a more modest and less robust effect on hand function. The statistical significance of the hand-function finding depended on a small number of high-weight studies, and the evidence for hand function is of low quality; the overall evidence is low-to-moderate. Therefore, these findings, especially those for hand function, should be interpreted cautiously, and further high-quality studies are warranted. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420261395137, PROSPERO registration number: CRD420261395137.

titre: Advances in physiotherapy for chronic low-back pain: a level I systematic review.
titre_fr: Advances in physiotherapy for chronic low-back pain: a level I systematic review.
auteurs: Migliorini Filippo, Maffuli Nicola, Schäfer Luise, Manocchio Nicola, Bossa Michela, Foti Calogero
revue: Journal of orthopaedics and traumatology : official journal of the Italian Society of Orthopaedics and Traumatology
resume: Non-pharmacologic management of chronic low back pain (cLBP) should be considered the first-line treatment. However, consensus guidelines and internationally accepted recommendations on the therapeutic algorithm are missing. The present level I systematic review presents a qualitative analysis of advancements in physiotherapy over the past decades to discuss the role of physical and rehabilitation medicine in the management of cLBP. In August 2025, the following databases were accessed: PubMed, Web of Science and Embase. All randomised controlled trials evaluating the efficacy of physiotherapy programs in patients with cLBP were assessed using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) criteria. The data extraction and risk-of-bias evaluation were performed independently by two authors. Data from 150 randomised controlled trials (RCTs) (12,773 patients) were collected. The mean symptom duration was 61.2 ± 51.0 months, and the mean follow-up was 4.3 ± 5.9 months. The mean age was 44.5 ± 9.4 years, and the mean body mass index (BMI) was 25.8 ± 2.9 kg/m2. Managing cLBP is challenging. While individual investigations highlight the efficacy of a specific intervention, most cLBP management strategies share common elements. Combining key elements from various approaches may prove crucial. Although this result is not decisive for treatment, it paves the way for further research that considers a more holistic and multidisciplinary approach.

titre: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the timing of rehabilitation training intervention for recipients of extracorporeal membrane oxygenators.
titre_fr: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the timing of rehabilitation training intervention for recipients of extracorporeal membrane oxygenators.
auteurs: Cheng Zhen, Du Liping, Zheng Shuangqin, Zheng Xiaoheng, Cheng Lingling, Zhang Mengfei, Shi Chenmo, Zhang Tianyu, Zheng Wei, Shi Aili
resume: To systematically evaluate the effects of early versus delayed rehabilitation training interventions (RTI) on clinical outcomes in patients receiving extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs), non-randomized controlled studies, and observational cohort studies comparing early and delayed RTI in patients receiving ECMO. We searched databases including Embase, PubMed, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, China Science and Technology Journal Database, and China Biology Medicine disc from inception to 1 April 2025. Study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment were performed independently by two reviewers. Outcomes included complications, intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay (LOS), duration of mechanical ventilation, ECMO duration, and in-hospital mortality. Twelve studies (five RCTs, four non-RCTs, and three cohort studies) were included. Compared with delayed RTI, early RTI significantly reduced the risk of complications [risk ratio (RR) = 0.43, 95% CI: 0.26-0.69, P < 0.001], shortened ICU LOS [mean difference (MD) = -1.12 days, 95% CI: -1.30 to -0.94, P < 0.001], and reduced hospital LOS (MD = -4.69 days, 95% CI: -8.11 to -1.27, P = 0.007). No significant differences were found in mechanical ventilation duration (MD = 0.14 days, P = 0.914), ECMO duration (MD = -1.77 days, P = 0.136), or in-hospital mortality (RR = 0.72, P = 0.097). Sensitivity analysis excluding one study demonstrated a greater reduction in hospital LOS significant (MD = -5.82 days, 95% CI: -9.34 to -2.30, P = 0.001), while other outcomes remained unchanged. Early RTI is associated with reduced complications and improved recovery outcomes (ICU/hospital stay) in ECMO patients compared with delayed RTI. However, due to the limited number and moderate quality of included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution. High-quality RCTs are needed to confirm these results. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420251025533, PROSPERO CRD420251025533.

titre: Predictive roles of inflammatory indicators (NLR, PLR, LMR and SII) in poststroke depression rehabilitation: a systematic review.
titre_fr: Predictive roles of inflammatory indicators (NLR, PLR, LMR and SII) in poststroke depression rehabilitation: a systematic review.
auteurs: Dai Hao, Cheng Ming
resume: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide. Almost all AIS survivors suffer physical disabilities and neuropsychiatric disturbances, among which poststroke depression (PSD) is a typical poststroke complication. The development of new tools to diagnose PSD at the early stage and predict its long-term outcome has attracted the attention of clinicians and researchers. Neuroinflammation has been increasingly considered a critical modulator of stroke evolution. Following an IS, an inflammatory response arises in the CNS, characterized by the activation of microglia; the recruitment of peripheral immune cells, including neutrophils, monocytes, and lymphocytes; and the release of proinflammatory cytokines. In this review, we present a comprehensive and critical examination of the diagnostic and predictive roles of inflammatory indicators, including the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), in PSD. A systematic literature search on PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, and CNKI was performed up to January 31, 2026. Quality assessment was conducted using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), and heterogeneity was evaluated using the I 2 statistic. Nine original studies involving 2,626 patients were included. Compared with non-PSD (NPSD) patients, PSD patients had a significantly greater NLR (MD = 0.47, 95% CI [0.39, 0.56], I 2 = 49%), PLR (MD = 20.79, 95% CI [12.25, 29.33], I 2 = 90%), and SII (MD = 123.92, 95% CI [68.85, 178.98], I 2 = 70%) and a significantly lower LMR (MD = -0.21, 95% CI [-0.34, -0.08], I 2 = 64%). Most included studies were rated as moderate-to-high quality on the basis of their NOS scores. These findings suggest that the NLR, PLR, LMR, and SII may serve as accessible peripheral blood biomarkers for early risk assessment of PSD, although further research is needed to establish optimal cutoff values and validate their predictive utility across different stroke subtypes.

titre: Nurse-led rehabilitation after total hip or knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of functional recovery, self-efficacy, and quality of life.
titre_fr: Nurse-led rehabilitation after total hip or knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of functional recovery, self-efficacy, and quality of life.
auteurs: Xu Ying, Chen Yan, Yin Yuan, Tang Mengxia, Luo Qin
resume: Nurse-led rehabilitation is increasingly embedded in postdischarge care after total hip or knee arthroplasty, but its effect on patient-reported recovery has not been quantified through meta-analysis. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of nurse-led rehabilitation versus usual care on functional recovery, self-efficacy, and quality of life after total hip or knee arthroplasty. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched (2010-2026; English only) for randomized controlled trials comparing nurse-led rehabilitation with usual care. Standardized mean differences (Hedges g) were pooled using random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was assessed with I 2 and prediction intervals, robustness with leave-one-out and subgroup analyses, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). Eleven trials (1,107 participants) were included. Nurse-led rehabilitation improved functional recovery (10 trials; g = 1.11, 95% confidence interval 0.42-1.81; I 2 = 94.5%), self-efficacy (five trials; g = 1.10, 0.00-2.20; I 2 = 93.8%), and quality of life (four trials; g = 0.77, 0.08-1.46; I 2 = 81.7%). The certainty of evidence (GRADE) was rated low for all three primary outcomes. Secondary outcomes were directionally favorable but imprecise. The functional recovery effect was robust to leave-one-out analysis, whereas self-efficacy was statistically fragile. Quality of life showed a homogeneous benefit after knee replacement (g = 1.12, I 2 = 0%) but not hip (between-subgroup p = 0.032), and functional recovery differed by delivery model (p = 0.012, largest for digital). Heterogeneity was substantial throughout, all prediction intervals crossed the null, and funnel plot asymmetry suggested possible small-study effects. Nurse-led rehabilitation after hip or knee arthroplasty was associated with improved function, self-efficacy, and quality of life, consistently favoring nurse-led care in direction but with evidence of low certainty, substantial between-study heterogeneity, prediction intervals that crossed the null, and possible small-study effects. Therefore, the magnitude of benefit remains uncertain. Adequately powered, outcome-blinded trials are needed. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261425216, PROSPERO CRD420261425216.
resume_fr: Nurse-led rehabilitation is increasingly embedded in postdischarge care after total hip or knee arthroplasty, but its effect on patient-reported recovery has not been quantified through meta-analysis. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched (2010-2026; English only) for randomized controlled trials comparing nurse-led rehabilitation with usual care. Standardized mean differences (Hedges g) were pooled using random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was assessed with I 2 and prediction intervals, robustness with leave-one-out and subgroup analyses, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). Eleven trials (1,107 participants) were included. Nurse-led rehabilitation improved functional recovery (10 trials; g = 1.11, 95% confidence interval 0.42-1.81; I 2 = 94.5%), self-efficacy (five trials; g = 1.10, 0.00-2.20; I 2 = 93.8%), and quality of life (four trials; g = 0.77, 0.08-1.46; I 2 = 81.7%). The certainty of evidence (GRADE) was rated low for all three primary outcomes. Secondary outcomes were directionally favorable but imprecise. The functional recovery effect was robust to leave-one-out analysis, whereas self-efficacy was statistically fragile. Quality of life showed a homogeneous benefit after knee replacement (g = 1.12, I 2 = 0%) but not hip (between-subgroup p = 0.032), and functional recovery differed by delivery model (p = 0.012, largest for digital). Heterogeneity was substantial throughout, all prediction intervals crossed the null, and funnel plot asymmetry suggested possible small-study effects. Nurse-led rehabilitation after hip or knee arthroplasty was associated with improved function, self-efficacy, and quality of life, consistently favoring nurse-led care in direction but with evidence of low certainty, substantial between-study heterogeneity, prediction intervals that crossed the null, and possible small-study effects. Therefore, the magnitude of benefit remains uncertain. Adequately powered, outcome-blinded trials are needed. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261425216, PROSPERO CRD420261425216.

titre: Comparative Effectiveness of Rehabilitation Nursing Interventions in Patients With Post-Stroke Dysphagia: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
titre_fr: Comparative Effectiveness of Rehabilitation Nursing Interventions in Patients With Post-Stroke Dysphagia: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
auteurs: Lai Rongrong, Jin Lingyun, Chen Shuoshuo, Li Ruru, Wang Miao, Zhang Liqing
revue: Japan journal of nursing science : JJNS
resume: To compare the effectiveness of rehabilitation interventions integrated into nursing care on swallowing function and safety in patients with post-stroke dysphagia. We searched Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, ProQuest, CINAHL, PubMed, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating rehabilitation nursing interventions for patients with post-stroke dysphagia, from database inception to September 2025. The primary outcomes were the Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS) and the Penetration-Aspiration Scale (PAS), while secondary outcomes included the Videofluoroscopic Dysphagia Scale (VDS) and the Swallowing Quality of Life Scale (SWAL-QOL). Seventeen RCTs were included. Rehabilitation nursing interventions were more effective than conventional care in improving FOIS, PAS, and VDS. For FOIS, kinesiology taping (KT) combined with neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) (surface under the cumulative ranking curve [SUCRA] = 78.7%, mean rank = 2.7) and respiratory muscle training (RMT) (SUCRA = 78.1%, mean rank = 2.9) ranked highest. For PAS, KT combined with NMES (SUCRA = 95.9%, mean rank = 1.3) and KT (SUCRA = 84.1%, mean rank = 2.1) ranked highest. Rehabilitation nursing interventions may improve swallowing function and safety in patients with post-stroke dysphagia. RMT, KT, and KT + NMES showed potential benefits for different aspects of swallowing recovery. However, the superiority of KT + NMES requires confirmation in high-quality multicenter RCTs with head-to-head comparisons and long-term follow-up. PROSPERO ID: CRD420251155222.

titre: Rebuilding confidence after workplace injuries: The role of self perception and job satisfaction in reintegration.
titre_fr: Rebuilding confidence after workplace injuries: The role of self perception and job satisfaction in reintegration.
auteurs: Kang Dongsuk
resume: BackgroundReturning to work after an occupational injury is a complex process that extends beyond physical recovery. While rehabilitation programs focus primarily on medical treatment and functional restoration, psychological and workplace-related factors significantly influence long-term reintegration. In South Korea, despite ongoing efforts to reduce industrial accidents through policies and legislation, over 100,000 workers annually experience occupational injuries, highlighting the need for a more comprehensive approach to post-injury recovery.ObjectiveThis study investigates the interplay between self-perception and workplace support in shaping the reintegration outcomes of injured workers. Rather than treating psychological traits as independent predictors, this study explores how workplace relationships and support mechanisms moderate the effects of self-perception on job and life satisfaction.MethodsThis study analyzes data from 540 workers who returned to their workplaces after an occupational injury. Using structural equation modeling approach (Partial Least Square), the study examines the relationships between self-esteem, self-efficacy, workplace support, and reintegration outcomes.ResultsThe findings reveal that self-esteem positively can help self-efficacy, which in turn enhances job and life satisfaction. Additionally, workers who perceive higher levels of workplace support can exhibit greater psychological resilience, leading to smoother reintegration and reduced job-related stress.ConclusionsThese results can highlight the importance of workplace culture and structured support programs in fostering successful post-injury reintegration. Employers and policymakers need to develop interventions that enhance workers' confidence, strengthen workplace relationships, and facilitate sustainable career recovery following occupational injuries.

titre: Social Participation in Community Dwelling Minority Stroke Survivors: Decolonizing Research.
titre_fr: Social Participation in Community Dwelling Minority Stroke Survivors: Decolonizing Research.
auteurs: Melifonwu Rita, Atwal Anita, Flood Chris, Wills Jane
resume: Minority stroke survivors experience difficulties in access to rehabilitation due to a combination of systemic factors; lack of understanding of their cultural beliefs by health professionals; their colonial thinking and experiences; and they are underrepresented in social participation research. To address the disparity, this paper discusses how research on social participation of community dwelling minority stroke survivors could embrace decolonization. Decolonization of research in social participation can be achieved when minority stroke survivors are engaged in genuine trust and co-production of knowledge with social science researchers. Improvements in uptake and continuation of social participation are sustained when such reciprocal relationships take place. There is a need for cultural competence and humility amongst healthcare professionals working in stroke rehabilitation with minority stroke survivors.

titre: Research-creation in the health sciences: A scoping review protocol.
titre_fr: Research-creation in the health sciences: A scoping review protocol.
auteurs: Ha C J, Fawaz Nathan Viktor, Dennett Liz, Armijo-Olivo Susan, Barlott Tim, Peers Danielle
resume: Research-creation is a methodological orientation that integrates creative and artistic processes with scholarly inquiry, positioning creative practice as a primary mode of knowledge generation. Originating largely within the arts and humanities in Canada, research-creation has increasingly appeared in health sciences contexts, including rehabilitation, mental health, health professions education, and community health research. However, no review has systematically mapped how research-creation is defined, conceptualized, or applied within health sciences scholarship, and significant ambiguity persists regarding the forms of data it generates, how those data are analyzed, and how creative outputs function within empirical research processes. This scoping review aims to map how research-creation is defined and conceptualized in health sciences literature; identify the purposes for which it is used and the health-related contexts in which it appears; describe the theories, methodological approaches, and creative methods employed; and examine what forms of health-related data are generated, how they are analyzed, and how knowledge is mobilized. Sources were included if they explicitly used the term "research-creation" (or its hyphenated and slash variants) to describe their method, approach, or project; focused on health, illness, care, healthcare systems, rehabilitation, mental health, public or community health, or health-related training; and generated empirical or experiential material analyzed or discussed in relation to health. No language limits were applied. A systematic search of 22 article databases was conducted from inception to Aug 2026. Grey literature searches included EBSCO Open Dissertations, and ProQuest Dissertations and Theses. Reference lists of included studies will be hand-searched. Data will be extracted independently by two reviewers using four structured charting tables capturing study characteristics, population, concept, and context. An expanded extraction framework was developed to accommodate the distinctive methodological features of research-creation, including creative processes, citational lineages, creative outputs, and forms of health-related data generated. Data will be analyzed using inductive qualitative content analysis. Extraction tools will be piloted on a subset of five included studies. The search identified 842 sources, with 577 remaining after duplicate removal. Title and abstract screening, full-text screening, and data extraction are currently underway. This scoping review will provide the first systematic mapping of research-creation within health sciences research and training. Findings may strengthen interdisciplinary dialogue between arts, social sciences, and health disciplines; support methodological transparency for researchers employing creative inquiry; and serve as a resource for researchers, trainees, practitioners, and supervisors seeking to understand how research-creation contributes to health-related knowledge production.

titre: Minimal-Burden Prosthodontics: Simple Care and Comprehensive Risk Assessment in Older Adults.
titre_fr: Minimal-Burden Prosthodontics: Simple Care and Comprehensive Risk Assessment in Older Adults.
auteurs: Molinero-Mourelle Pedro, Schimmel Martin, Mosaddad Seyed Ali
resume: Older adults represent a growing population in whom oral health impairment may affect comfort, nutrition, dignity, social participation, and quality of life. Conventional prosthodontic approaches, often guided by comprehensive rehabilitation, technical refinement, and long-term restorative ideals, require assessment of present and foreseeable functional, cognitive, and maintenance needs. This commentary discusses minimal-burden prosthodontics as an application of established gerodontology principles to independent and semi-dependent community-dwelling older adults. The concept does not imply that prosthodontic care can be burden-free. All prostheses carry biological, functional, temporal, psychological, and maintenance-related costs, and no prosthesis is permanent. These burdens should be explicitly identified, minimized, and justified by meaningful benefit. Building on rational dental care, geriatric dental assessment, the Seattle Care Pathway, minimal intervention dentistry, and patient-priorities-aligned care, comprehensive risk assessment should precede rehabilitation and establish a feasible maintenance plan. Proportional care serves as the ethical principle, prosthodontic sufficiency as the clinical objective, and contingency planning as a practical requirement if later frailty, cognitive decline, or loss of support makes treatment unmaintainable. Homebound patients require explicit arrangements for access and follow-up. When the patient's main wish is to eat comfortably and enjoy daily life, the goal should be the simplest suitable care that achieves that wish.

titre: Psychological needs in individuals with lower limb amputation: a narrative review of evidence for clinical practice across the rehabilitation continuum.
titre_fr: Psychological needs in individuals with lower limb amputation: a narrative review of evidence for clinical practice across the rehabilitation continuum.
auteurs: Walczak Emeline, Dervaux Benjamin, Dumortier Maxence, Bassement Jennifer
resume: To synthesize the psychological needs of individuals undergoing lower-limb amputation (LLA) and their association with overall adjustment across the rehabilitation continuum, in order to propose clinical recommendations spanning the entire continuum of care. A narrative review was conducted in accordance with the SANRA criteria, using MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, and PsycArticles. We identified peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and July 2025 that met the following criteria: original research; focused on individuals with LLA; examined psychological, emotional, or psychosocial dimensions throughout the rehabilitation continuum care journey; studies that explored how psychological factors influence overall adjustment; written in English. A total of 28 quantitative and 12 qualitative studies were included. Individuals undergoing LLA report significant psychological distress from limb threat to long-term rehabilitation care, including anxiety, depression, body image disturbance, impairment in social life and sexuality, low balance confidence, and cognitive impairment. Psychological distress is associated with poorer overall adjustment, confirming that mental health plays a key role in adaptation. The integration of structured psychological screening and personalized interventions targeting psychological and psychosocial needs may be beneficial throughout the rehabilitation continuum. Further studies are needed to assess the applicability for healthcare providers, and patient benefits of these recommendations.

titre: Effects of ChatGPT Use on Self-care Cardiac Rehabilitation Adherence in Patients with Coronary Artery Disease.
titre_fr: Effects of ChatGPT Use on Self-care Cardiac Rehabilitation Adherence in Patients with Coronary Artery Disease.
auteurs: Ift I Hac, Yet T Do An
revue: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
resume: To clarify the possible effects of ChatGPT use on self-care cardiac rehabilitation (CR) adherence in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD). Patients in the ChatGPT group participated in a standard cardiac rehabilitation program supplemented with personalized digital support via ChatGPT (n=48). The control group participated in conventional cardiac rehabilitation only, without AI-based support (n=48). Both groups completed a 6-month structured rehabilitation program supervised by a multidisciplinary team. Baseline demographic and clinical data, patient satisfaction assessed using a Likert scale, physical activity levels assessed using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ), and metabolic equivalent of task (MET) values were recorded. The postrehabilitation MET score was 1537 in the ChatGPT group and 1413 in the control group (P = 0.001). Similarly, the change in MET score after rehabilitation was greater in the ChatGPT group than in the control group (1029 vs. 875, P = 0.001). SF-36 parameters, including physical functioning, role-physical, mental health, bodily pain, and general health, were significantly higher in the ChatGPT group than in the control group (P < 0.05 for all). Program compliance was higher in the ChatGPT group than in the control group (91.7% vs. 75.0%, P = 0.028). Patient satisfaction was also higher in the ChatGPT group (4.5 vs. 3.8, P = 0.001). ChatGPT use during CR was associated with higher patient compliance rates. Moreover, ChatGPT-supported CR was associated with higher physical activity levels, greater patient satisfaction, and better selected quality-of-life scores.

titre: Embedding mental health within paediatrics: A comprehensive consultation consultation-liaison psychiatry service at The Children's Hospital at Westmead.
titre_fr: Embedding mental health within paediatrics: A comprehensive consultation consultation-liaison psychiatry service at The Children's Hospital at Westmead.
auteurs: You Daniel, Kozlowska Kasia, Koo Siew, Agoroudis Anna, Mahmood Dina
revue: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
resume: ObjectiveTo present a detailed description of the Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry service at The Children's Hospital at Westmead, illustrating its integration of proactive, clinical mental health care, workforce development, and systems collaboration.MethodsA narrative description was developed, drawing on clinical practice, service documents, and the experience of the multidisciplinary team.ResultsThe CHW CL service provides integrated inpatient, outpatient, and rehabilitation care for children and adolescents with chronic medical illness and functional neurological disorder. Key features include (i) a proactive acute psychiatric pathway for inpatients with acute mental health concerns; (ii) the Mind-body Program, an inpatient rehabilitation intervention for children disabled by functional neurological disorder symptoms; (iii) integration of consultation-liaison clinicians within paediatric subspecialties; and (iv) system level contributions through workforce training, supervision, and policy development. The service also extends its reach through statewide consultation and supervision. It has produced resources and training initiatives to build capacity beyond the tertiary setting.ConclusionThe Children's Hospital at Westmead Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry Service demonstrates how mental health care can be embedded within tertiary paediatrics through a model that combines clinical care with prevention, workforce development, and systems integration. This model may inform the design and refinement of consultation-liaison services in other paediatric hospitals nationally and internationally.

titre: Traumatic Brain Injury in First Responders: From Hidden Burden to Occupational Health Action.
titre_fr: Traumatic Brain Injury in First Responders: From Hidden Burden to Occupational Health Action.
auteurs: Caccese Jaclyn B, Williams W Huw, Smith Nicholas
revue: The Journal of head trauma rehabilitation
resume: Traumatic brain injury (TBI), including concussion, is an important but often underrecognized occupational injury among first responders. Despite frequent exposure to circumstances that increase the risk of TBI, law enforcement officers, firefighters, and emergency medical services personnel often lack consistent pathways for injury recognition, reporting, clinical assessment, rehabilitation, and safe return to duty. This topical issue of the Journal of Head Trauma Rehabilitation brings together emerging evidence on TBI prevalence, underrecognition, mental health, functional recovery, and occupational reintegration in first responder populations. Collectively, the articles demonstrate a substantial burden of TBI, persistent gaps in diagnosis and treatment, and the complex relationships among TBI history, psychological health, and occupational functioning. They also highlight the limited evidence available to guide rehabilitation and determine readiness to resume safety-sensitive duties. A multidisciplinary consensus statement included in this issue offers 28 recommendations addressing recognition and reporting, early assessment, return to duty, mental health, prevention, and organizational policies. Although first responder-specific evidence remains limited, these recommendations provide a practical framework for improving care while identifying priorities for future research. Advancing TBI care in first responders will require coordinated efforts among healthcare professionals, first responder organizations, researchers, and policymakers to establish supportive reporting systems, improve access to appropriate care, and develop and evaluate occupation-specific return-to-duty pathways. Addressing TBI in first responders requires moving beyond individual injury management toward a coordinated occupational health approach that protects first responders and the communities they serve.

titre: Mental Health Symptom Severity Is Positively Associated With Rehabilitation Needs in Veterans and Service Members With Polytrauma, Including Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Veterans Affairs Traumatic Brain Injury Model Systems Study.
titre_fr: Mental Health Symptom Severity Is Positively Associated With Rehabilitation Needs in Veterans and Service Members With Polytrauma, Including Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Veterans Affairs Traumatic Brain Injury Model Systems Study.
auteurs: Gilmore Natalie, Miles Shannon R, Sevigny Mitch, Klyce Daniel, Skop Karen M, Finn Jacob, Munger Eric, Perrin Paul B, Ryan Jessica L, Nakase-Richardson Risa, Silva Marc A
revue: The Journal of head trauma rehabilitation
resume: To assess the relationship between rehabilitation needs and mental health symptoms in Veterans and Service Members with polytrauma, including history of mild traumatic brain injury (TBI). Five Veterans Affairs (VA) Intensive Evaluation and Treatment Programs. Veterans and Service Members enrolled in the VA TBI Model Systems study who completed a follow-up greater than 6 months postprogram. Cohort study. Primary regression analyses included rehabilitation needs (Rehabilitation Needs Survey) and post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSD Checklist-Civilian version). Age, sex, months from rehabilitation to follow-up interview, preinjury mental health, disability level (Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended), and number of comorbidities were included as covariates. Secondary analyses applied the same model structure to assess the relationship between rehabilitation needs and anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7) and depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9) symptoms. Most Veterans and Service Members with polytrauma, including mild TBI, reported a current need for services to control physical symptoms (55%) and greater than one-third endorsed a current need for services to improve memory (46%), manage emotions (45%), improve health (44%), manage daily stress (42%), and solve daily problems (38%). Adjusted regression analyses revealed that rehabilitation needs were significantly and positively associated with post-traumatic stress, anxiety, and depression self-report symptoms. These relationships were maintained when analyses were repeated with mental health-related items removed from the Rehabilitation Needs Survey, suggesting the finding was not solely because of mental health needs. Higher comorbidity burden and disability were also independently associated with higher rehabilitation needs. Veterans and Service Members with polytrauma, especially those with elevated post-traumatic stress, anxiety, and/or depressive symptoms in the context of mild TBI, could benefit from ongoing access to evidence-based psychotherapies and other specialty care, rehabilitation, and support services to manage long-term care and rehabilitation needs in the chronic phase of injury.

Age, sex, months from rehabilitation to follow-up interview, preinjury mental health, disability level (Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended), and number of comorbidities were included as covariates. Secondary analyses applied the same model structure to assess the relationship between rehabilitation needs and anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7) and depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9) symptoms. Most Veterans and Service Members with polytrauma, including mild TBI, reported a current need for services to control physical symptoms (55%) and greater than one-third endorsed a current need for services to improve memory (46%), manage emotions (45%), improve health (44%), manage daily stress (42%), and solve daily problems (38%). Adjusted regression analyses revealed that rehabilitation needs were significantly and positively associated with post-traumatic stress, anxiety, and depression self-report symptoms. These relationships were maintained when analyses were repeated with mental health-related items removed from the Rehabilitation Needs Survey, suggesting the finding was not solely because of mental health needs. Higher comorbidity burden and disability were also independently associated with higher rehabilitation needs. Veterans and Service Members with polytrauma, especially those with elevated post-traumatic stress, anxiety, and/or depressive symptoms in the context of mild TBI, could benefit from ongoing access to evidence-based psychotherapies and other specialty care, rehabilitation, and support services to manage long-term care and rehabilitation needs in the chronic phase of injury.

titre: Effects of Virtual Reality-Based Rehabilitation on Postural Balance in Older Adults: A Systematic Review.
titre_fr: Effects of Virtual Reality-Based Rehabilitation on Postural Balance in Older Adults: A Systematic Review.
auteurs: Neiva Barbara O M, Martins Andressa Maysa S, Beze Murilo Antônio R, Oliveira Silvia Priscilla R, Afonso João Pedro R, Andraus Rodrigo Antônio C, Oliveira Rodrigo F, Oliveira Deise A A P, Fernandes Tiago V, Marconi Daniel G, Carvalho Karla Cristina N, Oliveira Claudia S, Silva Carlos Hassel M, Guedes Orlando A, Maia Luciana P, Capodaglio Paolo, Oliveira Miriã C, Oliveira Luis Vicente F
resume: Population aging has been accompanied by an increased incidence of falls, fractures, and functional disability, representing a major global public health challenge. In this context, virtual reality (VR)-based rehabilitation has emerged as an innovative therapeutic strategy providing multimodal sensory and motor stimulation, facilitating motor learning, and enhancing treatment adherence through gamified, interactive environments. To investigate the effectiveness of VR-based rehabilitation on postural balance training in older adults through a systematic review. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261303119). Comprehensive literature searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, LILACS, and SciELO to identify studies published between 2015 and 2026. Randomized and non-randomized clinical trials evaluating VR rehabilitation in adults aged 60 years and older, with postural balance as the primary outcome, were eligible. Methodological quality was assessed using the PEDro Scale, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Data were synthesized using a qualitative, descriptive approach. Nine clinical trials of moderate-to-good methodological quality were included, evaluating non-immersive commercial exergames, semi-immersive, and immersive rehabilitation-dedicated systems. Overall, findings indicated that VR was associated with improvements in static and dynamic balance and functional mobility. Between-group analyses showed no statistically significant differences between VR and conventional rehabilitation in several trials, whereas superior effects for VR were reported in others, alongside greater participant engagement and adherence. VR-based rehabilitation is an effective intervention for improving static and dynamic balance and functional mobility in older adults. As a complementary strategy in geriatric physiotherapy, VR has the potential to reduce fall risk, preserve functional independence, and enhance rehabilitation outcomes. Nevertheless, additional high-quality randomized controlled trials with standardized protocols and long-term follow-up are warranted to strengthen the current evidence.

titre: Health-Related Services Using Digital Devices for the General Public in Pragmatic Trials: A Scoping Review.
titre_fr: Health-Related Services Using Digital Devices for the General Public in Pragmatic Trials: A Scoping Review.
auteurs: Okumoto Ayaka, Yamakawa Miyae, Higami Yoko
resume: The rapid evolution of digital devices has significantly impacted the healthcare industry, necessitating an examination of their usability. To provide evidence-based services, it is crucial to validate the results of pragmatic trials utilizing digital devices for the general public. This scoping review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of pragmatic trials utilizing digital devices for the general public, elucidating device types and evaluation processes, specifically in the context of health-related services. We conducted the scoping review by using the PRISMA-ScR checklist. MEDLINE, CINAHL, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched without restrictions on publication dates. Our review examined published articles concerning health-related services utilizing digital health devices in pragmatic trials involving the general public. We retrieved 987 records, and 24 articles were reviewed. The studies included digital screening for early detection of arrhythmia by using smartwatches and patches, and tracking physical activity through pedometers, accelerometers, and smartwatches. Twelve studies involved outcome evaluation, with eight reporting effective results and four reporting ineffective results. Other studies included process evaluation, economic evaluation, author manuscripts, substudies, and pooled analysis results. Limitations identified in the review include the inability of some individuals to use digital devices and uncertainty regarding long-term effects. Health-related services for the general public through pragmatic trials aim to promote health and prevent diseases, detect diseases early, and facilitate rehabilitation. To implement evidence-based health services that promote good health, it is essential to conduct multifaceted evaluations, including economic evaluations for stakeholders, to address limitations and identify barriers to implementation.

titre: Age-Friendly Telegeriatrics: Evidence and a 5M-Based Framework for Hybrid Geriatric Care in Saudi Arabia.
titre_fr: Age-Friendly Telegeriatrics: Evidence and a 5M-Based Framework for Hybrid Geriatric Care in Saudi Arabia.
auteurs: Alsaad Saad M
resume: Population ageing is increasing demand for accessible, coordinated, and person-centered care, while many older adults face barriers to conventional services related to frailty, multimorbidity, cognitive or sensory impairment, functional dependency, and travel burden. Telehealth can extend specialist expertise beyond conventional clinical settings, but geriatric care cannot be reduced to transferring a standard outpatient consultation to video. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence on telegeriatrics, including virtual comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA), cognitive and functional assessment, medication review, chronic-disease monitoring, rehabilitation, home-based care, and caregiver-supported models, with particular attention to Saudi Arabia. Evidence supports the feasibility and acceptability of several telegeriatric applications, although clinical effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, and long-term outcomes remain heterogeneous. Important limitations include digital exclusion, sensory and cognitive barriers, restricted physical examination, interoperability challenges, and the risk of shifting additional work to family caregivers. Emerging Saudi evidence demonstrates both rapid expansion of virtual-care infrastructure and growing experience with telehealth among older adults, including multidisciplinary tele-CGA through Seha Virtual Hospital, but geriatric-specific outcome evidence remains limited. Based on the narrative synthesis, an author-proposed, evidence-informed conceptual framework is presented to illustrate how the Geriatric 5Ms may inform the integration of virtual and in-person geriatric care. This framework has not undergone formal consensus development, prospective validation, or effectiveness testing. It is intended to support discussion, inform future research, and provide a starting point for prospective feasibility and implementation studies rather than serve as a clinical practice recommendation.

titre: Case Report: An MDT-guided multimodal protocol for large-area stroke plateau - integrating neuromodulation with multimodal assessment.
titre_fr: Case Report: An MDT-guided multimodal protocol for large-area stroke plateau - integrating neuromodulation with multimodal assessment.
auteurs: Wu Xiao-Li, Xia Xiao-Qian, Ye Chang-Qing, Wang Yun-Lei, Li Xing-Zhu, Liu Li-Xu, Hang Fu-Biao, Liu Jing-Song, Song Yi-Chuan, Zhang Yue, Du Xiao-Xia
resume: This case report investigates the feasibility and potential value of an individualized precision rehabilitation protocol for large-area stroke, integrating multimodal neuromodulation under the guidance of a multidisciplinary team (MDT) and dynamic assessment. A 38-year-old male with right hemiplegia and global aphasia following large left hemispheric infarction underwent an 8-month MDT-managed program. A closed-loop "assess-decide-intervene-re-assess" framework was implemented, featuring periodic multimodal evaluations (clinical scales, DTI, fMRI, EEG, 3D gait analysis). The intervention dynamically combined conventional therapy with staged neuromodulation: repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) for aphasia and intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation (iTBS) for motor disorder, Brain-Computer Interface (BCI)-robotic training and task-oriented Virtual Reality (VR) for upper limb function, and biomechanical correction with custom insoles based on gait analysis. Notable functional improvements were observed: LOTCA increased by 16 points, CRRCAE subscale improved by 60%-90%, FMA increased from 20 to 56, FMA-B reached 12, and MBI improved from 40 to 91. Neuroimaging revealed increased fractional anisotropy (FA) in the corpus callosum and right corticospinal tract, and elevated ALFF/ReHo in right frontal-temporal areas. Event-related desynchronization (ERD) decreased during BCI training, and gait parameters improved. In this patient with large-area stroke who showed limited response to conventional rehabilitation, an MDT-guided, dynamically adjusted multimodal intervention was temporally associated with concurrent recovery across cognitive, language, motor, and daily living domains. The concomitant neural changes suggest possible trans-hemispheric network reorganization. These observations are hypothesis-generating and, while limited by the single-case design, provide a preliminary rationale for future investigations into precision neurorehabilitation approaches in similar complex cases. ChiCTR2300069203.

titre: Ethics of Telerehabilitation in Supportive Cancer Care Through a Responsible Innovation Lens.
titre_fr: Ethics of Telerehabilitation in Supportive Cancer Care Through a Responsible Innovation Lens.
auteurs: Lorenz Maria C, Sample Matthew, Alves Alberto J, Müller Jana, Steindorf Karen, Wengström Yvonne, Zopf Eva M, May Anne M, Stuiver Martijn M
resume: In recent years, remote exercise services ("telerehabilitation") have been increasingly explored and implemented, including in supportive cancer care, on the promise of greater convenience, access independent of geographic location, reduced infection risk, and cost savings. Ethical commentary on telehealth in general is substantial, but sustained discussion of questions specific to telerehabilitation remains comparatively sparse. As contributors to PREFERBALE-II, a European Union-funded project evaluating live-remote exercise for people recovering from cancer treatment, we sought practical guidance on how to deliver such services responsibly, and found little to work with. This prompted this viewpoint, which sets out our own position as researchers and clinicians engaged in this work. We draw on a purposive sample of professional guidance documents, which were assembled through our professional networks and a supplementary web search, and on a narrative reading of qualitative studies chosen to represent accounts of benefits as well as burdens. We read these documents through an analytical lens of responsible innovation. We make 3 arguments. First, the ethical content of current telerehabilitation guidance is largely confined to the products and processes of innovation, covering safety, privacy, consent, and compliance, while the question of purpose, that is, whether, for whom, and why remote rehabilitation should be offered at all, is left largely unasked. Anticipation appears only implicitly, and reflexivity, inclusion, and responsiveness barely at all. Responsibility is repeatedly delegated to individual professionals without commensurate structural support. Second, the situated experience of users and professionals forms part of the ethics of telerehabilitation and is not merely data to be assessed. Reported benefits and burdens depend on social context, including age, digital literacy, connectivity, caregiver availability, language, and sensory or cognitive impairment, so an equity claim made for the modality in general may not hold for the individual patient. Third, the ethics of telerehabilitation consequently has to be institutionalized across 3 overlapping domains: the interpersonal and experiential quality of remote care, the legal and institutional conditions of delivery, and the positioning of telerehabilitation within health systems. We address these arguments primarily to rehabilitation professionals and the associations and standard-setting bodies that issue guidance for them, and secondarily to digital health and ethical, legal, and social implications researchers, policymakers, and health-system decision-makers who commission or implement such services. We offer an agenda for a broader ethics conversation across professional societies, curricula, and affected publics, together with observations from a consortium put forward as hypotheses for study.

titre: Experiences of physiotherapists practicing cardiopulmonary telerehabilitation in digital health: a qualitative study.
titre_fr: Experiences of physiotherapists practicing cardiopulmonary telerehabilitation in digital health: a qualitative study.
auteurs: Onal Seyma Nur, Calik Ebru
resume: Cardiopulmonary telerehabilitation (CTR) is an innovative approach that improves access to care by allowing physical therapists (PTs) to provide remote monitoring. This study examines clinical practice and the advancement of telerehabilitation (TR) by enhancing understanding of experiences, barriers, and their effectiveness. A qualitative study was conducted with eight PTs between May and September 2025. A semi-structured interview technique, developed based on the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF), was conducted via video conference. Using this inductive approach together with prior texts and written notes, a preliminary coding framework was developed. The interviews were coded independently by two researchers using MAXQDA software, and intercoder reliability was high (Cohen's kappa = 0.82). The participants were all female physiotherapists; five held a PhD degree and three held a master's degree, with 5-11 years of professional experience and 8-18 months of telerehabilitation experience. The interviews identified thematic codes related to PTs' adaptability, job satisfaction, and challenges in CTR's digital transformation. Key themes included advantages like patient adherence, efficiency, satisfaction, motivation, and technological competence; factors seen as both advantages and disadvantages, such as time flexibility and accessibility; disadvantages like technical issues, reduced physical contact, managing high-risk patients, and virtualization; and recommendations for hybrid models, integrated systems, and national software infrastructures. Cardiopulmonary telerehabilitation was perceived as an effective and accessible approach that improved patient satisfaction and treatment adherence. However, PTs raised concerns about role transformation, ethical and legal responsibilities, and excessive virtualization. Their preference for a hybrid model highlights the need for face-to-face care, especially for high-risk patients, where safety is critical. The call for user-friendly national software and improved technological literacy underscores that successful CTR implementation requires both infrastructure and professional adaptation.

titre: Digital Technologies in Postsurgical Orthopedic Rehabilitation: Scoping Review Mapping Interventions to the CAMS Framework (2020-2025).
titre_fr: Digital Technologies in Postsurgical Orthopedic Rehabilitation: Scoping Review Mapping Interventions to the CAMS Framework (2020-2025).
auteurs: Lai Ngan Kuen, Huang Hai, Chen Tet Khuan, Nor'a Muhammad Nur Affendy, Sijore Jeffery, Chen Wei Yang, Luo YongSheng
resume: Digital technologies have become common in postoperative orthopedic rehabilitation. The tendency toward this adoption appeared in the past decade. However, no standard method exists to classify their functional capabilities. This absence hinders practical implementation. Clinicians currently lack a structured framework to distinguish between the functional capabilities of different digital rehabilitation technologies effectively. This scoping review aims to map digital interventions used in postsurgical orthopedic rehabilitation to a proposed Coordination, Alignment, Motivation, and Strength (CAMS) framework and to identify research trends, functional coverage, and gaps in current evidence. A systematic search was conducted across 5 databases: MEDLINE (via PubMed), Scopus, IEEE Xplore, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and the Physiotherapy Evidence Database (PEDro), following PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines. Studies were mapped to the proposed CAMS framework pillars. Multiple validated appraisal tools were applied descriptively according to study design: version 2 of the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2; n=32), the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) for observational studies (n=2), and the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS) for nonrandomized designs (n=1). A total of 35 studies met the inclusion criteria. Coordination was the most frequently addressed pillar (29/35, 83%), followed by Motivation (26/35, 74%). Alignment was addressed in 37% (13/35) of studies, while Strength was the least represented pillar (12/35, 34%). Overall, 49% (17/35) of studies were rated "low risk" overall on the primary appraisal tool, 46% (16/35) demonstrated "some concerns," and 6% (2/35) were rated "high risk," with performance bias identified as a consistent methodological characteristic across the corpus. Delivery models were predominantly hybrid (14/35, 40%) or home-based (13/35, 37%), with 8 studies (8/35, 23%) using an exclusively clinical model. Digital health has shown a notable increase in the kinematic monitoring feature, offering effective solutions to movement quality (Coordination and Alignment) and psychological engagement (Motivation). Nevertheless, there is a consistent gap in strength-related studies, as current decentralized tools lack the capability to quantify physiological load. The next phase of innovations should be a shift to integrated 4-pillar solutions that would coordinate resistance-based training with high-precision biomechanical monitoring. The CAMS framework is proposed as an exploratory classification tool to guide future research design and technology evaluation in postsurgical digital rehabilitation.
