titre: Variable task difficulty with augmented sensory feedback for motor training in virtual reality.
titre_fr: Variable task difficulty with augmented sensory feedback for motor training in virtual reality.
auteurs: Shi Yu, Dewil Sophie, Marvin Zachary, Harel Noam Y, Nataraj Raviraj
resume: This study examined how motor task difficulty and augmented sensory feedback (ASF) modality influence task performance, physiological responses, and perceptual experience during virtual reality (VR)-based upper-limb motor training. Building on related brace- and VR-based ASF platforms previously examined in neurotypical and spinal cord injury cohorts, the long-term goal is to support neurorehabilitation-oriented adaptive VR training; however, the present study used neurotypical participants as an initial validation step. Fourteen right-handed neurotypical participants used a supportive upper-limb brace and surface electromyography (EMG) for myoelectric control of a virtual robotic arm in a two-dimensional tracking task. A 2 × 2 within-subject design crossed ASF modality (visual feedback versus visual + haptic feedback) with task difficulty (straight-line versus sinusoidal trajectory). Outcomes included normalized path length, task completion time, movement jerk, alpha- and beta-band electroencephalogram (EEG) power over motor cortex, heart rate, EMG amplitude, EMG-displacement-based virtual work, and perceptual ratings of agency, motivation, and utility. Short-term pre-to-post percentage changes were computed for each measure. VHF straight-line training produced the largest reductions in normalized path length (-4.69%) and completion time (-6.12%), whereas VHF sinusoid training produced the largest reductions in movement jerk (-5.67%) and virtual work (-13.33%). ASF modality affected path length, completion time, jerk, EMG amplitude, and virtual work, whereas task difficulty modulated beta-band EEG power and the physiological index. Changes in path length were positively associated with changes in completion time and EMG amplitude. These findings suggest that ASF modality and task difficulty can differentially shape short-term behavioral, physiological, and perceptual responses in healthy participants. The exploratory distribution of participant-specific best-case conditions motivates future studies using independent trial subsets to evaluate whether behavioral and physiological measures can support individualized VR training.

VHF straight-line training produced the largest reductions in normalized path length (-4.69%) and completion time (-6.12%), whereas VHF sinusoid training produced the largest reductions in movement jerk (-5.67%) and virtual work (-13.33%). ASF modality affected path length, completion time, jerk, EMG amplitude, and virtual work, whereas task difficulty modulated beta-band EEG power and the physiological index. Changes in path length were positively associated with changes in completion time and EMG amplitude. These findings suggest that ASF modality and task difficulty can differentially shape short-term behavioral, physiological, and perceptual responses in healthy participants. The exploratory distribution of participant-specific best-case conditions motivates future studies using independent trial subsets to evaluate whether behavioral and physiological measures can support individualized VR training.

titre: Lessons learned from the COVID-19 pandemic for future cochlear implant service preparedness: a multicenter study.
titre_fr: Lessons learned from the COVID-19 pandemic for future cochlear implant service preparedness: a multicenter study.
auteurs: Alshehabi Mohamed, Elakkawi Salam, Alzahrani Musaed, Almuhawas Fida, Altamimi Fahad, Aldaijani Nader, Shami Ibrahim, Alghamdi Saeed, Badr Khalid, Saleh Essam, Alghamdi Fares, Thabet Elsaeid, Mony Jad, Aldhafeeri Ahmad, Abdelsamad Yaseen, Sivaramakrishnan Gowri
resume: Cochlear implantation (CI) is a highly effective intervention for severe-to-profound hearing loss; however, the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted established CI service delivery worldwide. Maintaining access to this resource-intensive procedure during public health emergencies is critical, particularly for pediatric patients in whom delays may compromise auditory and language development. This multicenter retrospective comparative study analyzed CI service delivery across seven centers in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, comparing pre-pandemic and pandemic periods over six months. Data included procedural volumes, waiting lists, committee activity, surgical workflows, intraoperative testing, and adoption of telehealth for fitting and rehabilitation.Generalized estimating equations were used to account for center-level clustering. A total of 984 CI procedures were analyzed. Overall implant volume was preserved during the pandemic, while waiting lists increased by 31%. Telehealth adoption expanded markedly, with all remote fitting sessions and nearly all remote rehabilitation sessions occurring during the COVID-19 pandemic. Unilateral operating time decreased significantly, reflecting streamlined surgical workflows. Committee activity and intraoperative testing practices demonstrated center-specific adaptations. CI services demonstrated resilience during the COVID-19 pandemic through rapid telehealth integration and surgical workflow optimization. However, increased waiting lists highlight critical vulnerability, particularly for pediatric candidates. Hybrid care models and contingency planning should be formally integrated into future CI service frameworks.

titre: Enhancing Universal Design Through Co-Design: Realising the Potential of Disability Lived Experience.
titre_fr: Améliorer la conception universelle grâce à la co-conception : réaliser le potentiel de l'expérience vécue par les personnes handicapées.
auteurs: Watchorn Valerie, Tucker Richard, Frawley Patsie, Hitch Danielle
revue: Studies in health technology and informatics
resume: Ensuring public buildings meet the needs of diverse users has increased interest in co-design, a process in which people without formal design training actively participate in design and decision-making [1]. Universal design provides principles for creating environments usable by all and advocates for the involvement of people with disability in their application [2, 3]. However, limited evidence exists on how co-design is applied in the context of universal design and how participatory processes are experienced by those involved, particularly people with disability. To advance conceptual and practical understanding on this topic, a collective case study research project comprising three qualitative studies was conducted in Australia [4-6]. Workshops and interviews with people with disability, design professionals, and health professionals explored how co-design and universal design are enacted in public building projects, outcomes achieved, and factors influencing participation. The research examined the what, who, when, where, and why of participation, identifying mechanisms that enable or constrain co-design practice. Five integrative themes were developed: (1) Redistributing expertise: Valuing lived experience as design knowledge; (2) Broadening participation: From tokenism to interprofessional collaboration; (3) Temporal justice: Embedding co-design across stages; (4) Contextual boundaries: Where co-design happens and where it does not; and (5) Transformative intent: Why co-design matters for design quality and social justice. Overall findings indicate that co-design can improve accessibility and usability while building capacity among individuals, professionals, and communities. The research proposes a reciprocal relationship between co-design and universal design, whereby each can strengthen application of the other. It highlights the importance of iterative collaboration, accessible methodologies, and critical reflection on power dynamics. Co-design is positioned as an interprofessional practice strengthened by the expertise of people with disability, design professionals, and inclusion-focused disciplines, such as occupational therapy. The findings provide practical and conceptual guidance for embedding meaningful participation of people with disability in the design of public buildings.
resume_fr: S'assurer que les bâtiments publics répondent aux besoins de divers utilisateurs a accru l'intérêt pour la co-conception, un processus dans lequel les personnes sans formation formelle en conception participent activement à la conception et à la prise de décision [1]. La conception universelle fournit des principes pour créer des environnements utilisables par tous et plaide pour l'implication des personnes handicapées dans leur application [2, 3]. Cependant, il existe peu de preuves sur la façon dont la co-conception est appliquée dans le contextede conception universelle et comment les processus participatifs sont vécus par les personnes impliquées, en particulier les personnes handicapées. Pour faire progresser la compréhension conceptuelle et pratique de ce sujet, un projet de recherche collectif d'études de cas comprenant trois études qualitatives a été mené en Australie [4-6]. Des ateliers et des entretiens avec des personnes handicapées, des professionnels de la conception et des professionnels de la santé ont exploré comment la co-conception et la conception universelle sontmis en œuvre dans les projets de bâtiments publics, les résultats obtenus et les facteurs influençant la participation. La recherche a examiné le quoi, qui, quand, où et pourquoi de la participation, en identifiant les mécanismes qui permettent ou limitent la pratique de la co-conception. Cinq thèmes intégratifs ont été développés : (1) Redistribuer l'expertise : valoriser l'expérience vécue en tant que connaissance du design ; (2) Élargir la participation : du tokenisme à la collaboration interprofessionnelle ; (3) Le ju temporelstice : Intégrer la co-conception à travers les étapes ; (4) Limites contextuelles : où la co-conception se produit et où elle ne se produit pas ; et (5) Intention transformatrice : pourquoi la co-conception est importante pour la qualité de la conception et la justice sociale. Les résultats globaux indiquent que la co-conception peut améliorer l'accessibilité et la convivialité tout en renforçant les capacités des individus, des professionnels et des communautés. La recherche propose une relation réciproque entre la co-conception et la conception universelle, chacun pouvant renforcer l'application de l'autre. Il souligne l'importance de la collaboration itérative, des méthodologies accessibles et de la réflexion critique sur la dynamique du pouvoir. La co-conception se positionne comme une pratique interprofessionnelle renforcée par l'expertise des personnes handicapées, des professionnels de la conception et des disciplines axées sur l'inclusion, telles que l'ergothérapie. Les résultats fournissent des orientations pratiques et conceptuelles pour l'embedding participation significative des personnes handicapées à la conception des bâtiments publics.

titre: Improving detection of candidates for botulinum toxin therapy in spasticity: an interprofessional screening approach.
titre_fr: Improving detection of candidates for botulinum toxin therapy in spasticity: an interprofessional screening approach.
auteurs: Rudelstorfer Melanie, Mayr-Pirker Brigitte, Trinka Eugen, Iglseder Bernhard, Radlberger Richard Friedrich
resume: Spastic movement disorders (SMD) are commonly treated with botulinum toxin, however, many patients who may benefit from treatment remain unrecognized in routine clinical practice. Early identification is particularly challenging in non-specialized settings. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of interprofessional screening tools for identifying patients with clinically relevant SMD requiring referral for specialist assessment. In this prospective, two-phase, single-center study, 124 patients who received care by departments of neurology and geriatrics were included. In phase 1, the Spastic Movement Disorder decision tree (SMD-DT) was applied independently by nurses, physiotherapists, and occupational therapists and compared with the clinical assessment of an experienced neurologist as the reference standard. Based on the findings, a simplified nursing screening tool, the Salzburg Nursing Questionnaire (SNQ), was developed and subsequently evaluated in independent cohorts in phase 2 of the study. The SMD-DT demonstrated high agreement with the reference standard in neurological rehabilitation settings, with a high degree of consistency across all professional groups compared with the expert, but showed substantially lower performance among nurses in non-specialized geriatric settings. In contrast, the SNQ consistently achieved high diagnostic accuracy in these settings (sensitivity of 1.00 and specificity of 0.96) considering treatment recommendation. The diagnostic performance of screening instruments for SMD depends strongly on both clinical context and professional background. These findings support the implementation of profession-specific screening strategies to improve early recognition of clinically relevant SMD, facilitating timely referral for specialist evaluation, and optimize access to botulinum toxin therapy in routine clinical practice.
resume_fr: Les troubles du mouvement spastique (SMD) sont couramment traités avec la toxine botulinique, cependant, de nombreux patients qui peuvent bénéficier d'un traitement restent méconnus dans la pratique clinique de routine. L'identification précoce est particulièrement difficile dans les milieux non spécialisés. Cette étude a évalué la performance diagnostique des outils de dépistage interprofessionnels pour identifier les patients atteints de SMD cliniquement pertinents nécessitant une référence pour une évaluation spécialisée.prospective, en deux phases, étude monocentrique, 124 patients ayant reçu des soins par les services de neurologie et de gériatrie ont été inclus. Dans la phase 1, l'arbre de décision du trouble du mouvement spastique (SMD-DT) a été appliqué indépendamment par les infirmières, les physiothérapeutes et les ergothérapeutes et comparé à l'évaluation clinique d'un neurologue expérimenté comme étalon de référence. Sur la base des résultats, un outil de dépistage infirmier simplifié, le Salzburg Nursing Questionnaire (SNQ), a été développé puis évalué dans des cohortes indépendantes dans la phase 2 de l'étude. Le SMD-DT a démontré une forte concordance avec la norme de référence dans les milieux de réadaptation neurologique, avec un degré élevé de cohérence dans tous les groupes professionnels par rapport à l'expert, mais a montré des performances nettement inférieures chez les infirmières dans les milieux gériatriques non spécialisés. En revanche, la SNQ a toujoursa atteint une précision diagnostique élevée dans ces paramètres (sensibilité de 1,00 et spécificité de 0,96) en tenant compte de la recommandation de traitement. La performance diagnostique des instruments de dépistage de la SMD dépend fortement du contexte clinique et du contexte professionnel. Ces résultats soutiennent la mise en œuvre de stratégies de dépistage spécifiques à la profession pour améliorer la reconnaissance précoce des SMD cliniquement pertinents, facilitant l'orientation en temps opportun pour SPECIAdresser la liste des évaluations et optimiser l'accès au traitement par la toxine botulique dans la pratique clinique de routine.

titre: Stimulus over expertise: what governs clinical visual attention in early health-vocational students.
titre_fr: Stimulus over expertise : what governs clinical visual attention in early health-vocational students.
auteurs: Yuksel Burcu, Tayyare Begüm Çapa, Eryilmaz Nurullah
resume: Eye tracking is increasingly used to investigate how health-profession students allocate visual attention to clinically critical regions of diagnostic and therapeutic images. However, whether disciplinary training produces a perceptual advantage for images within students' own fields remains unclear. This study examined whether students preferentially attended to critical regions in images from their own discipline compared with those from an unfamiliar discipline. A within-stimulus 2 × 2 mixed design was employed involving 34 Medical Laboratory Techniques (MLT) students and 29 Occupational Therapy (OT) students. Participants viewed clinical images from both disciplines while their eye movements were recorded. Within each image set, own-discipline and visiting viewers were compared on attention to predefined critical regions and related fixation and timing measures. The potential predictive roles of academic standing and cognitive and learning-style variables were also examined. No consistent own-discipline advantage was observed across the eye-tracking measures. Attention to critical regions did not favour students from the corresponding discipline in either image set, and statistically significant differences, where observed, favoured visiting rather than own-discipline viewers. In contrast, image identity consistently exerted a substantial effect on visual attention across all conditions. Neither academic standing nor cognitive or learning-style variables predicted attention to critical regions. The findings challenge the assumption that enrolment in a health-profession programme necessarily confers discipline-specific perceptual expertise. Instead, visual attention appears to be influenced more strongly by stimulus characteristics than by disciplinary background at this stage of training. These results suggest that discipline-specific perceptual expertise may develop through accumulated, deliberate clinical exposure rather than through programme enrolment alone.
resume_fr: Le suivi oculaire est de plus en plus utilisé pour étudier comment les étudiants de la profession de la santé allouent l'attention visuelle aux régions cliniquement critiques des images diagnostiques et thérapeutiques. Cependant, il n'est pas clair si la formation disciplinaire produit un avantage perceptuel pour les images dans les propres domaines des étudiants. Cette étude a examiné si les étudiants s'occupaient de préférence des régions critiques dans les images de leur propre discipline par rapport à celles d'undiscipline étrangère. Une conception mixte 2 × 2 à l'intérieur du stimulus a été employée impliquant 34 étudiants en techniques de laboratoire médical (MLT) et 29 étudiants en ergothérapie (OT). Les participants ont visionné des images cliniques des deux disciplines pendant que leurs mouvements oculaires étaient enregistrés. Au sein de chaque ensemble d'images, les spectateurs de sa propre discipline et les visiteurs ont été comparés en fonction de l'attention portée à des régions critiques prédéfinies et des mesures de fixation et de synchronisation associées. Le potentiel préditive rôles de la position académique et des variables cognitives et de style d'apprentissage ont également été examinés. Aucun avantage cohérent propre à la discipline n'a été observé à travers les mesures de suivi oculaire. L'attention portée aux régions critiques n'a pas favorisé les étudiants de la discipline correspondante dans l'un ou l'autre ensemble d'images, et les différences statistiquement significatives, lorsqu'elles étaient observées, ont favorisé les visiteurs plutôt que les téléspectateurs de leur propre discipline. En revanche, l'identité d'image s'est constamment exercéeun effet substantiel sur l'attention visuelle dans toutes les conditions. Ni le statut académique ni les variables cognitives ou de style d'apprentissage n'ont prédit l'attention sur les régions critiques. Les résultats remettent en question l'hypothèse selon laquelle l'inscription à un programme de profession de la santé confère nécessairement une expertise perceptuelle spécifique à la discipline. Au lieu de cela, l'attention visuelle semble être plus fortement influencée par les caractéristiques du stimulus que par les antécédents disciplinaires àcette étape de la formation. Ces résultats suggèrent que l'expertise perceptuelle spécifique à une discipline peut se développer par une exposition clinique accumulée et délibérée plutôt que par la seule inscription au programme.

titre: Use of screening assessments in identifying the need for occupational therapy in HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders.
titre_fr: Utilisation des évaluations de dépistage pour identifier le besoin d'ergothérapie dans les troubles neurocognitifs associés au VIH.
auteurs: Smith Elizabeth, de Witt Patricia Ann, Franzsen Denise
resume: People living with HIV (PLWHIV) present with an increased risk of cognitive dysfunction and dependence in daily activities. In South Africa, PLWHIV attending a neuropsychiatric clinic are screened using the International HIV Dementia Scale (IHDS) to determine the presence of HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder (HAND). It is unknown how effectively this screening identifies the need for rehabilitation in occupational therapy. This study determined the cognitive and daily living dysfunction in PLWHIV who scored <11 on the IHDS (Indicating the presence of HAND), using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and the World Health Organisation Disability Assessment Schedule 2.0 (WHODAS 2.0). A sample of 55 participants had a median score of 7 on the IHDS. The median score of 20 on the MoCA and 23.51% for daily living on the WHODAS 2.0 indicated mild dysfunction. The IHDS scores were moderately associated with the MoCA scores but not the WHODAS 2.0 scores. An IHDS score of 9 was associated with mild cognitive dysfunction, while an IHDS score of 7 or less was associated with moderate cognitive dysfunction and mild to moderate disability in daily living. It is suggested that PLWHIV with a score of ≤7 should be prioritised for referral for occupational therapy intervention.
resume_fr: Les personnes vivant avec le VIH (PVVIH) présentent un risque accru de dysfonctionnement cognitif et de dépendance dans les activités quotidiennes. En Afrique du Sud, les PVVIH qui fréquentent une clinique neuropsychiatrique sont dépistés à l'aide de l'échelle internationale de démence liée au VIH (IHDS) pour déterminer la présence d'un trouble neurocognitif associé au VIH (HAND). On ne sait pas dans quelle mesure ce dépistage identifie efficacement le besoin de réadaptation en ergothérapie. Cette étude détermidu dysfonctionnement cognitif et de la vie quotidienne chez les PVVIH qui ont obtenu un score <11 à l'IHDS (indiquant la présence de la MAIN), en utilisant le Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) et le World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule 2.0 (WHODAS 2.0). Un échantillon de 55 participants avait un score médian de 7 sur l'IHDS. Le score médian de 20 sur le MoCA et de 23,51 % pour la vie quotidienne sur le WHODAS 2.0 indiquait un dysfonctionnement léger. Les scores IHDS étaient moderaassocié aux scores MoCA mais pas aux scores WHODAS 2.0. Un score IHDS de 9 était associé à un dysfonctionnement cognitif léger, tandis qu'un score IHDS de 7 ou moins était associé à un dysfonctionnement cognitif modéré et à un handicap léger à modéré dans la vie quotidienne. Il est suggéré que les PVVIH ayant un score ≤7 soient prioritaires pour l'orientation vers une intervention d'ergothérapie.

titre: Integrating Functional Cognitive Rehabilitation With Activity-Based Stroke Telerehabilitation: Intervention Design and Development Study.
titre_fr: Integrating Functional Cognitive Rehabilitation With Activity-Based Stroke Telerehabilitation : Intervention Design and Development Study.
auteurs: Finetto Patricia, Woodbury Michelle L, Laura Julianne, Rishe Kelly, Garner Stephanie, McTeague Lisa M, Schwen Blackett Deena, Twamley Elizabeth W, Aghamoosa Stephanie
resume: Many stroke survivors experience chronic cognitive deficits that, together with motor impairments, negatively impact well-being and daily function. Critically, poststroke cognitive deficits can interfere with successful engagement in rehabilitation programs aimed at improving participation in home and community activities. To address this issue, we developed a new telehealth intervention that integrates brief, functional cognitive rehabilitation (COG) into an existing upper extremity-focused, activity-based occupational therapy (OT) telerehabilitation program. To describe the development and specification of a telehealth intervention (COG+OT) that integrates functional cognitive rehabilitation into activity-based stroke telerehabilitation. COG+OT was developed using a multi-disciplinary, theory-informed process guided by principles of functional cognitive rehabilitation. It is reported according to the Template for Intervention Description and Replication checklist for rehabilitation (TIDieR-Rehab). The intervention was developed by a team with expertise in stroke rehabilitation from the fields of OT, neuropsychology, clinical psychology, and speech-language pathology. Cognitive rehabilitation content was adapted from an evidence-based compensatory strategy program and condensed into a brief "primer" format. The COG component was iteratively integrated into an existing upper-extremity, activity-based OT telerehabilitation program to support engagement and transfer of strategies to real-world functional tasks. In this paper, we describe the intervention structure, content, delivery, and tailoring procedures. COG+OT is an 8-week, 13-session telehealth intervention delivered in three phases: (1) cognitive strategy training ("primer"; sessions 1-4), (2) review and guided application of strategies within OT activities (sessions 5-10), and (3) integration of strategies to support generalization to everyday contexts (sessions 11-13). The intervention combines individualized, strategy-based cognitive rehabilitation with goal-oriented OT using a titrated approach. Patient-facing materials, structured session workflows, and therapist-guided metacognitive strategies support tailoring and real-world application. COG+OT is a theory-informed, user-centered intervention that provides a structured approach for integrating functional cognitive rehabilitation into stroke telerehabilitation. This work establishes a well-specified, replicable intervention model and supports future feasibility, effectiveness, and implementation studies.
resume_fr: De nombreux survivants d'un AVC souffrent de déficits cognitifs chroniques qui, associés à des déficiences motrices, ont un impact négatif sur le bien-être et la fonction quotidienne. De manière critique, les déficits cognitifs post-AVC peuvent interférer avec un engagement réussi dans des programmes de réadaptation visant à améliorer la participation aux activités à domicile et communautaires. Pour résoudre ce problème, nous avons développé une nouvelle intervention de télésanté qui intègre une réhabilitation cognitive brève et fonctionnelle(COG) dans un programme de téléréadaptation en ergothérapie (OT) axé sur les activités et les membres supérieurs existant. Décrire le développement et la spécification d'une intervention de télésanté (COG+OT) qui intègre la réadaptation cognitive fonctionnelle dans la téléréadaptation d'AVC basée sur l'activité. COG+OT a été développé à l'aide d'un processus multidisciplinaire fondé sur la théorie et guidé par les principes de la réadaptation cognitive fonctionnelle. Il est signalé uncselon le modèle de description d'intervention et la liste de contrôle de réplication pour la réhabilitation (TIDieR-Rehab). L'intervention a été développée par une équipe experte en réadaptation après un AVC dans les domaines de l'OT, de la neuropsychologie, de la psychologie clinique et de l'orthophonie. Le contenu de la réadaptation cognitive a été adapté à partir d'un programme de stratégie compensatoire fondé sur des preuves et condensé dans un bref format « d'amorce ». Le composant COG WAest itérativement intégré dans un programme existant de téléréadaptation OT basé sur les activités des extrémités supérieures pour soutenir l'engagement et le transfert de stratégies vers des tâches fonctionnelles du monde réel. Dans cet article, nous décrivons la structure d'intervention, le contenu, la livraison et les procédures d'adaptation. COG+OT est une intervention de télésanté de 8 semaines, en 13 sessions, dispensée en trois phases : (1) formation à la stratégie cognitive (« amorce » ; sessions 1 à 4), (2) examen et orientationplication of strategies within OT activities (sessions 5-10), and (3) integration of strategies to support generalization to everyday contexts (sessions 11-13). The intervention combines individualized, strategy-based cognitive rehabilitation with goal-oriented OT using a titrated approach. Patient-facing materials, structured session workflows, and therapist-guided metacognitive strategies support tailoring and real-world application. COG+OT is une intervention basée sur la théorie et centrée sur l'utilisateur qui fournit une approche structurée pour intégrer la réadaptation cognitive fonctionnelle dans la téléréadaptation après un AVC. Ce travail établit un modèle d'intervention bien spécifié et reproductible et soutient les futures études de faisabilité, d'efficacité et de mise en œuvre.

titre: Outcomes of multidisciplinary cognitive and social communication traumatic brain injury rehabilitation in Qatar: a retrospective cohort study.
titre_fr: Outcomes of multidisciplinary cognitive and social communication traumatic brain injury rehabilitation in Qatar: a retrospective cohort study.
auteurs: Kareem Abughalieh Basim Mohammad Abdul, Al Barghothi Maram Bassam H
resume: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) often leads to long-term social and cognitive dysfunction, and even more so in Arabic-speaking communities due to the lack of culturally appropriate rehabilitation programs. This study examines the efficacy of a structured multidisciplinary cognitive-social rehabilitation program on cognitive functioning, communication, and vocational reintegration in TBI patients in Qatar. Retrospective analysis was performed on clinical data of TBI patients 15-65 years old admitted to the Adult Day Rehabilitation Unit, Qatar Rehabilitation Institute, from January 2022 to December 2024. All the participants had cognitive and communication impairment and were treated with a multidisciplinary rehabilitation program consisting of individualized speech-language therapy and occupational therapy. Outcome measures included the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) of cognitive function, Functional Communication Measures (FCMs) of social interaction and communication, "the Ability to participate in social roles and activities (Neuro-QoL short form)," and the Functional Independence Measure (FIM) of global functional status and return-to-work or school. The measures were assessed at baseline, mid-intervention, post-intervention, and follow-up. Post-rehabilitation evaluations reported improvement in all areas of outcome. Participants showed greater improvements in MoCA (+4.3 vs + 1.3, p < .001), FIM (+14.45 vs + 5.1, p < .002), the Neuro-QoL scores improved by (+11.23 points), and FCMs (+7.0 vs + 2.2, p < .001) pre and post program. Return-to-work was achieved in 68.8%. Effect sizes were large (Cohen's d > 1.0). The results suggest the effectiveness of combined cognitive-social rehabilitation for TBI patients, emphasizing concurrent speech and occupational therapist intervention benefits. The intervention also demonstrated functional improvement in daily life, supporting the significance of multidisciplinary interventions to recovery and social reintegration after TBI.

titre: Suspected Pasteurella Infection Associated With Catnip Exposure Leading to Finger Extensor Tendon Rupture: A Case Report.
titre_fr: Suspected Pasteurella Infection Associated With Catnip Exposure Leading to Finger Extensor Tendon Rupture: A Case Report.
auteurs: Couch Kennedy L, Heck Holly C, Ifetiha Amar, Kin Chloe, Kerr William A, Mustapha Abdulazim, Szymanski Kate, Eisenmann Kathryn M
resume: Pasteurella species commonly cause soft tissue infections following direct animal bites or scratches. However, transmission through indirect contact with contaminated materials remains underrecognized. We report an unusual, suspected case of Pasteurella multocida infection acquired through contact with catnip contaminated by feline saliva, resulting in progressive soft tissue infection and extensor tendon rupture in the hand of an otherwise healthy individual. Operative debridement, tendon repair, culture-directed antibiotic therapy, and structured occupational therapy resulted in functional recovery with grip strength equal to the uninjured hand, a residual 37° total extension deficit, and a Quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (QuickDASH) score of 4.55% at four months postinjury. This case emphasizes the importance of recognizing atypical transmission routes and implementing timely interventions to prevent severe complications.

titre: Sustained Psychosocial Benefits of Telehealth Occupational Therapy for Young Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: Long-Term Follow-Up of the Resilient, Empowered, Active Living-Telehealth (REAL-T) Randomized Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: Sustained Psychosocial Benefits of Telehealth Occupational Therapy for Young Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: Long-Term Follow-Up of the Resilient, Empowered, Active Living-Telehealth (REAL-T) Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Pyatak Elizabeth A, Nnoli Ngozi D, Mo Yujia, Lee Pey-Jiuan, Blanchard Jeanine, Leite Jaime D, Sideris John, Fox D Steven, Granados Gabrielle, Diaz Jesus, Tapia Valerie, Raymond Jennifer K
revue: The science of diabetes self-management and care
resume: The purpose of this study was to examine 12-month outcomes of the Resilient, Empowered, Active Living-Telehealth (REAL-T) intervention for young adults with diabetes. Young adults ages 18 to 30 years with type 1 diabetes ≥1 year and A1C ≥7.5% (≥58 mmol/mol) were randomized 1:1 to REAL-T (6 months of telehealth occupational therapy) or usual care. Continuous glucose monitor metrics, diabetes distress, and diabetes-related quality of life (DQoL) were assessed at baseline, 6, and 12 months, while A1C and hypothesized mediators were assessed quarterly. Linear mixed-effects models estimated longitudinal treatment effects. Of 209 randomized participants, 171 (82%) contributed 12-month data. No significant between-group differences were observed for glycemia. REAL-T participants showed greater improvements in emotional distress and diabetes self-efficacy than control group participants. Per protocol analyses excluding untreated participants yielded stronger effects, with significantly improved DQoL and regimen distress. A telehealth occupational therapy intervention produced durable improvements in emotional distress and self-efficacy over 12 months, supporting psychosocial outcomes as central treatment targets in young adults with type 1 diabetes.

titre: Comparing outcomes of conservative rehabilitation protocols for camptodactyly in pediatric patients: A retrospective cohort study.
titre_fr: Comparing outcomes of conservative rehabilitation protocols for camptodactyly in pediatric patients: A retrospective cohort study.
auteurs: Young Liam, Baek Joshua, Ebeda Dalia, Ho Emily S
revue: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
resume: Camptodactyly is a flexion contracture of the proximal interphalangeal joint initially presenting during early (Type I) or later (Type II) in childhood. Commonly, the contracture occurs in the small finger but may affect multiple digits with or without association to distal arthrogryposis. Conservative management is widely recommended as the primary form of treatment for camptodactyly; however, little is known about how treatment approaches differ for camptodactyly with and without association to distal arthrogryposis. To compare the outcomes of conservative management for proximal interphalangeal joint contracture of children with camptodactyly and distal arthrogryposis. Retrospective cohort design. The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids) database was reviewed to identify children diagnosed with camptodactyly or distal arthrogryposis. Diagnostic and outcomes data were extracted from health records. The primary analysis was paired comparison of the degree of proximal interphalangeal joint extension passive range of motion of affected digits pre- and post-treatment. Secondary analyses were outcome comparisons of the mean difference in proximal interphalangeal joint between Type I and Type II camptodactyly. Of 280 children reviewed, 95 (M:F, 47:48) were included in the study. Sixty-five (68%) were diagnosed with camptodactyly and 30 (32%) distal arthrogryposis; 55 (59%) had Type I and 38 (41%) had Type II camptodactyly. Significant reduction in proximal interphalangeal joint contractures were found in children with camptodactyly following conservative treatment, but were not significant in children with distal arthrogryposis. No significant difference was found between Type I and Type II. Contractures in children with distal arthrogryposis were found to have higher association with skin and soft tissue deficiencies than children with camptodactyly. Camptodactyly and distal arthrogryposis may require different hand therapy treatment. Conservative management is indicated in both conditions; however, interweaving interdisciplinary collaboration to provide conservative and surgical intervention is recommended for children with distal arthrogryposis.

titre: Rehabilitation to support leisure participation following stroke: a national survey of clinical practice in Australia.
titre_fr: Rehabilitation to support leisure participation following stroke: a national survey of clinical practice in Australia.
auteurs: Alves-Stein Serena, Lannin Natasha A, Jolliffe Laura, Kramer Sharon
resume: To describe how allied health clinicians assess and treat leisure participation after stroke and identify factors influencing their practice. Allied health clinicians working in health and disability settings completed an online survey. Assessment and intervention approaches were collected with survey questions aligned to the TIDieR checklist. Perceived barriers to providing leisure rehabilitation were captured using the 26-item Determinants of Implementation Behaviour Questionnaire. Among the 131 clinicians who completed the survey, the largest proportion of respondents were occupational therapists (35%), physiotherapists (35%), and speech pathologists (18%). Most referred to clinical guidelines to inform their leisure rehabilitation practice. Of the 105 assessments reportedly used, only seven included a leisure-specific item or scale. Common intervention approaches included targeting underlying impairments (upper limb [44%] and mobility [44%]) and modifying activities (54%). Barriers to providing leisure rehabilitation included limited funding, training and resources. Allied health clinicians rely on guidelines that do not meaningfully inform leisure rehabilitation, leaving practice dependent on individual reasoning and inconsistent access to resources. Further research to understand clinicians' clinical reasoning and training needs can inform the design of effective leisure-focused interventions and help address a clear gap in stroke rehabilitation.

titre: Estimating Functional Independence Measure Scores From Japanese Rehabilitation Notes Using a Large Language Model: Retrospective Study.
titre_fr: Estimating Functional Independence Measure Scores From Japanese Rehabilitation Notes Using a Large Language Model: Retrospective Study.
auteurs: Nishiyama Tomohiro, Mine Yudai, Itoh Norihide, Ikenoue Tatsuyoshi, Nagasaka Keima, Matsuo Naoko, Tatsuki Onishi, Aramaki Eiji
resume: The Functional Independence Measure (FIM) is a standard functional assessment tool in rehabilitation medicine; however, formal assessments are often conducted only at limited intervals. Free-text clinical notes contain more frequent observations of patients' functional status and may complement these assessments. This study aimed to estimate item-level FIM scores from Japanese free-text rehabilitation notes using a locally deployed large language model (LLM) and to evaluate estimation performance; item-level estimability; and differences across diseases, therapy types, and admission FIM severity groups. We retrospectively analyzed free-text notes from physical therapy (PT), occupational therapy (OT), and speech-language pathology (SLP) for patients hospitalized with cerebral infarction (CeI), hip fracture (HF), or vertebral fracture (VBF) at Saiseikai Moriyama Municipal Hospital between October 2019 and September 2024. Using zero-shot prompting, an LLM estimated all FIM items from each note. Estimated scores were matched to reference FIM scores recorded for the same patient on the same calendar date. Performance was evaluated using the mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error, and quadratic weighted kappa. Estimation rates and comparisons with modal-score and last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) baselines were also examined. Among 2,952,702 eligible note-item pairs from 164,039 retained rehabilitation-note-level outputs, the model produced 980,000 valid estimates, corresponding to an overall estimation rate of 33.2%. Among 170,744 note-item opportunities with an available same-day reference score, 57,246 (33.5%) were estimable, of which 77.7% (44,481/57,246) were within 1 point of the reference score. Estimates derived from OT notes had a lower MAE than those derived from PT notes in CeI and HF, whereas the difference was not significant in VBF. The LLM outperformed the modal-score baseline but had a higher MAE than the LOCF overall (0.825 vs 0.648). The locally deployed LLM shows the potential to derive item-level FIM estimates from Japanese rehabilitation notes. Among estimable note-item pairs with a same-day reference FIM score, 77.7% were within 1 point of the reference score. These findings support the potential use of LLM-based estimation to structure functional information contained in routine rehabilitation notes and complement periodic FIM assessments. Further integration of multidisciplinary clinical records and external validation are needed to improve estimability and evaluate its value for longitudinal functional monitoring.

titre: Effects of Occupational Therapy Interventions on Occupational Performance and Physical and Cognitive Fatigue in Adults with Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
titre_fr: Effects of Occupational Therapy Interventions on Occupational Performance and Physical and Cognitive Fatigue in Adults with Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
auteurs: Vásquez-Carrasco Edgar, Branco Braulio Henrique Magnani, Lopez-Andaur Roberto, Hernandez-Martinez Jordan, Burgos-Carrasco Sebastián, Ochoa-Martinez Laura, Sandoval-Vásquez Cristian, Peña Francisca, Valdés-Badilla Pablo
resume: Background/Objectives: Multiple sclerosis (MS) frequently limits participation in daily occupations and is associated with disabling fatigue. However, the effects of occupational therapy (OT) remain uncertain because available trials have evaluated heterogeneous interventions and outcomes. This systematic review synthesized evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on occupational performance and physical and cognitive fatigue in adults with MS. Materials and Methods: Seven bibliographic databases were searched from inception to 10 August 2026: MEDLINE via PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) via the Cochrane Library, Web of Science Core Collection, APA PsycINFO via EBSCOhost, CINAHL Complete via EBSCOhost, and ProQuest Central. Two independent reviewers performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment using RoB 2. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Given the clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively following the Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis guideline. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251115448). Results: Seven RCTs involving 488 randomized participants were included. Findings for occupational performance were inconsistent: one small waitlist-controlled trial reported large short-term benefits from occupational performance coaching, whereas an active-comparator trial found improvements in both groups without clear superiority. Other findings showed no comparative benefit or provided only indirect evidence. Fatigue findings were similarly inconsistent: one 20-participant pilot trial favored a sleep-targeted OT intervention, two trials found no comparative benefit, and one large trial transiently favored usual-care OT. The certainty of evidence was very low for both outcomes. Conclusions: The available evidence does not consistently establish that OT interventions improve occupational performance or reduce physical and cognitive fatigue in adults with MS. Larger, adequately powered RCTs using clearly defined OT interventions, standardized outcomes, and longer follow-up periods are required.

titre: Infantile Colic-Related Symptoms and Maternal Feeding Attitudes in Infants Aged 7-12 Months: Associations with Sensory Processing Characteristics in a Cross-Sectional Study.
titre_fr: Infantile Colic-Related Symptoms and Maternal Feeding Attitudes in Infants Aged 7-12 Months: Associations with Sensory Processing Characteristics in a Cross-Sectional Study.
auteurs: Tekeci Yasin, Tuğrul Enes, İkinci Kaya Melike Selin, Torpil Berkan
resume: Background/Objectives: Infantile colic is primarily recognized as an early-infancy condition, yet early regulatory difficulties may be associated with sensory processing and feeding-related characteristics later in infancy. This study examined associations among colic-related symptom scores, sensory processing characteristics, and maternal attitudes toward breastfeeding versus formula feeding in infants aged 7-12 months with a documented history of infantile colic. Methods: This cross-sectional correlational study included 100 infants aged 7-12 months with a clinically documented colic diagnosis in the first 4 months of life meeting Wessel's criteria. The Infant/Toddler Sensory Profile-2 (ITSP-2), Infant Colic Scale (ICS), and Iowa Infant Feeding Attitude Scale (IIFAS) were administered. Data were analyzed using Pearson correlations and two multiple linear regression models. Results: IIFAS scores were inversely correlated with ICS scores (r = -0.708, p < 0.001). ICS scores correlated most strongly with General Processing (r = 0.804), Low Registration (r = 0.749), Sensitivity (r = 0.737), and Seeking (r = 0.719; all p < 0.001). In regression analyses, ICS scores were independently associated with IIFAS score (β = -0.291), General Processing (β = 0.567), Sensation Avoiding (β = -0.146), and Auditory Processing (β = -0.125) (R2 = 0.728, adjusted R2 = 0.716), while IIFAS scores were independently associated with ICS score (β = -0.427) and Low Registration (β = -0.376) (R2 = 0.564, adjusted R2 = 0.555; all p < 0.05). Conclusions: In infants with a history of colic, sensory processing characteristics were associated with current colic-related symptom scores and maternal feeding attitudes and may warrant consideration in clinical evaluation. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal and causal nature of these associations.

In regression analyses, ICS scores were independently associated with IIFAS score (β = -0.291), General Processing (β = 0.567), Sensation Avoiding (β = -0.146), and Auditory Processing (β = -0.125) (R2 = 0.728, adjusted R2 = 0.716), while IIFAS scores were independently associated with ICS score (β = -0.427) and Low Registration (β = -0.376) (R2 = 0.564, adjusted R2 = 0.555; all p < 0.05). Conclusions: In infants with a history of colic, sensory processing characteristics were associated with current colic-related symptom scores and maternal feeding attitudes and may warrant consideration in clinical evaluation. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal and causal nature of these associations.

titre: Maternal Anxiety Symptoms, Sensory Processing, and Play Performance in Children Aged 4-6 Years with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Cross-Sectional Study.
titre_fr: Maternal Anxiety Symptoms, Sensory Processing, and Play Performance in Children Aged 4-6 Years with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Cross-Sectional Study.
auteurs: Akçay Sümeyye, Dinç Yavaş Arzu, Poyrazoğlu Hatice Gamze, Cesar Nil Su, Kaplan İkra Nur, Uğur Cevriye Ceyda
resume: Background: Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) often show atypical sensory processing and reduced play participation, and their mothers frequently report elevated anxiety. However, maternal anxiety symptoms, sensory processing, and children's play performance and playfulness have rarely been examined together, and the factors independently associated with maternal anxiety symptoms have not yet been clarified. Objective: This study examined relationships between maternal anxiety symptoms and children's sensory processing, play performance, and playfulness in children with ASD aged 4-6 years, and identified factors independently associated with maternal anxiety symptoms. Method: In this cross-sectional study, 58 mother-child dyads were recruited from a special education center in Istanbul, Türkiye. Maternal anxiety was assessed with the Beck Anxiety Inventory, sensory processing with the Dunn Sensory Profile, and play with the Revised Knox Preschool Play Scale and Test of Playfulness. Results: Maternal anxiety was negatively correlated with play performance (ρ = -0.564, p < 0.001) and playfulness (ρ = -0.492, p < 0.001), and positively correlated with low registration and sensation-seeking raw scores (ρ = 0.474, p < 0.001 and ρ = 0.343, p = 0.008, respectively; higher raw scores indicate more typical, less atypical processing). Children with comorbid ADHD had mothers with higher anxiety and lower play scores. In a multivariable model (R2 = 0.516), play performance (β = -0.411, p = 0.002) and, preliminarily, comorbid ADHD (β = 0.274, p = 0.027; only 10 children with ADHD) were independently associated with maternal anxiety; maternal education, employment, and school type were not. Conclusions: In young children with ASD, maternal anxiety symptoms were most strongly associated with the child's play performance, while a preliminary association with co-occurring ADHD requires confirmation in larger samples; these findings support considering maternal wellbeing in family-centered occupational therapy assessment.

titre: Changes in Functional and Health-Related Outcomes After a Disability-Delay Program Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
titre_fr: Changes in Functional and Health-Related Outcomes After a Disability-Delay Program Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
auteurs: Chen Yu-Chung, Li Yi-Chun, Hong Rong-Bin, Shih Yi-Chen, Chang Jer-Hao
resume: Background: Frailty, sarcopenia, and cognitive decline are associated with reduced functional independence and participation among older adults. Occupational therapy uses multidomain and participation-focused approaches to support functional independence and healthy aging; however, evidence regarding functional and health-related changes among community-dwelling older adults participating in structured multidomain programs remains limited. This study aimed to describe pre-post changes in functional and health-related outcomes and to explore associations among concurrent changes in these measures. Methods: This uncontrolled retrospective pre-post program evaluation analyzed routinely collected data from 60 community-dwelling older adults who participated in a 12-week occupational therapist-led multidomain community program at five community sites. The program was delivered once weekly for 2 h and incorporated cognitive, physical, and daily activity-related components. Functional ability, frailty, sarcopenia risk, grip strength, cognitive function, and health-related quality of life were assessed at baseline and program completion. Pre-post differences were examined using paired-samples t-tests, and separate age-adjusted linear regression models were used to examine associations between individual clinical change variables and concurrent changes in functional outcomes. Results: Pre-post differences were observed in activities of daily living, frailty, sarcopenia risk, grip strength, cognitive function, and health-related quality of life. In separate exploratory age-adjusted regression models, changes in frailty (SOF), sarcopenia risk (SARC-F), and cognitive function (SPMSQ) were associated with concurrent changes in selected functional outcomes. These associations were considered exploratory and should not be interpreted as evidence of independent prediction or causality. Conclusions: Pre-post changes in multiple functional and health-related outcomes were observed among community-dwelling older adults participating in the 12-week occupational therapist-led multidomain program. Given the uncontrolled retrospective pre-post design, the observed changes cannot be attributed to the program, and the associations among concurrent changes should not be interpreted as causal. These findings may inform occupational therapy practice and the development of community-based multidomain programs aimed at supporting functional independence and participation in daily life. Further prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings and determine whether such programs produce clinically meaningful changes in functional and health-related outcomes.

titre: Translation and Cultural Adaptation of the Home Graded Repetitive Arm Supplementary Program (Home-GRASP) for Stroke Survivors in Spain.
titre_fr: Translation and Cultural Adaptation of the Home Graded Repetitive Arm Supplementary Program (Home-GRASP) for Stroke Survivors in Spain.
auteurs: Soler-Pons Carlos, Casaña-Escriche Empar, García-Millán Pablo, Hurtado-Pomares Miriam, Valera-Gran Desirée, Navarrete-Muñoz Eva María
resume: Background/Objectives: Home-based rehabilitation programs can increase upper-limb practice after stroke and support recovery beyond formal therapy sessions. However, no Spanish version of the Home Graded Repetitive Arm Supplementary Program (Home-GRASP) participant exercise manual was available. This study aimed to translate and cross-culturally adapt the manual for use in Spain and evaluate its clarity, comprehensibility, and ease of use. Methods: The original Home-GRASP participant exercise manual was independently translated into Spanish by two translators, reviewed by an expert committee, culturally adapted, and pilot tested with 13 adults with subacute or chronic stroke-related upper-limb hemiparesis receiving outpatient rehabilitation in Spain. Clarity and comprehensibility were assessed through direct observation of exercise performance and a participant questionnaire. Results: The expert committee considered that forward translations preserved the underlying concepts and therapeutic intent of the original manual and required only minor linguistic modifications. Expert review resulted in adaptations to photographs, exercise instructions, and layout. During pilot testing, all 35 exercises were evaluated, resulting in 49 exercise performances. Seven execution errors were identified across four exercises and were mainly related to ambiguities in movement descriptions or visual instructions. Following revision of the affected exercises, no further errors were observed. All participants reported that the manual was easy to use, 92.3% found it easy to understand, and 76.9% reported being able to perform the exercises independently. Conclusions: The Spanish version of the Home-GRASP participant exercise manual was successfully translated and cross-culturally adapted for use in Spain. The adapted manual showed preliminary evidence of satisfactory clarity, comprehensibility, and ease of use, supporting its use as a culturally appropriate resource for home-based upper-limb rehabilitation after stroke.

titre: Opening the Black Box of Ayres Sensory Integration<sup>®</sup>: Clarifying Mechanisms of Change from Treatment Theory to Participation.
titre_fr: Opening the Black Box of Ayres Sensory Integration<sup>®</sup>: Clarifying Mechanisms of Change from Treatment Theory to Participation.
auteurs: Reynolds Stacey, Andelin Lauren, LaRocca Caterina
resume: Ayres Sensory Integration<sup>®</sup> (ASI) remains one of the most widely used and debated intervention approaches in occupational therapy and related disciplines. Recent advances in rehabilitation treatment specification and reporting frameworks, including the Rehabilitation Treatment Specification System (RTSS) and the Reporting Guideline for Intervention Description in Rehabilitation (GUIDE-Rehab), emphasize the need for precise articulation of treatment ingredients, mechanisms of action, and targets. However, interventions grounded in neurodevelopmental theories, such as Ayres' theory of sensory integration, are complex, and may present challenges when interpreted within linear causal models. This paper argues that ASI theory is best understood as a treatment theory targeting proximal sensory-motor capacities, while participation-level outcomes may be more comprehensively explained through an enablement framework. Integrating this perspective with data-driven decision making (DDDM) clarifies longstanding ambiguities in the ASI literature and strengthens intervention specification, evaluation, and interpretation.

titre: Teaching Direction Control in Horse Riding: A Pre-Post Intervention Proof-of-Concept Study Using Multi-Modal Motor Learning Techniques.
titre_fr: Teaching Direction Control in Horse Riding: A Pre-Post Intervention Proof-of-Concept Study Using Multi-Modal Motor Learning Techniques.
auteurs: Blignault Karin, Buys Tania, Ramkilawon Gopika, van Vollenhoven Elize
revue: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
resume: Many riders experience persistent communication problems with their horses, particularly in controlling speed and direction, despite extensive training. This proof-of-concept study employed a pre-test-post-test intervention design to examine the effectiveness of the Four-Step Riding Programme (FSRP) in developing clear rider-horse body language for direction control. Multi-modal motor learning techniques (MMLTs) were applied to five rider-horse dyads during four one-hour lessons to teach coordinated movement patterns necessary for directional accuracy. Rider-horse communication was evaluated before and after the intervention using video recordings of 13 riding exercises. Three independent assessors rated the performances on a 5-point Likert scale, and riders provided self-assessments on the same scale. Horse stride parameters, reflecting shoulder control, were visualised with the Alogo™ Move Pro electronic sensor. Significant improvements were observed between pre- and post-intervention scores across all assessors and participants (p < 0.05). These preliminary findings suggest that the FSRP holds promise for facilitating the acquisition of rider-horse body language necessary for precise direction control.

titre: The effect of regional disparities in access to rehabilitation services on mortality among stroke patients: A Korean nationwide population-based retrospective cohort study.
titre_fr: The effect of regional disparities in access to rehabilitation services on mortality among stroke patients: A Korean nationwide population-based retrospective cohort study.
auteurs: Yoo Dong-Yup, Baek Chang-Yoon, Choi Jung-Kyu
resume: This study aimed to analyze physical therapy (PT) and occupational therapy (OT) claims data to determine whether access barriers to rehabilitation services due to regional factors affect PT and OT accessibility. Furthermore, we investigated the mortality rate of stroke patients by region in South Korea using the National Health Insurance Service-National Sample Cohort database. This is a register-based, retrospective cohort study. Using data from the National Health Insurance Service database, we included patients who were newly diagnosed with stroke between 2005 and 2017. Of the 19,067 patients diagnosed with stroke, 2263 who died within 6 months were excluded. The final sample included 16,804 patients (51.3% men and 48.7% women). Residential regions were categorized into Capital, Capital area, Metropolitan, and Rural area. After adjusting for covariates, a logistic regression model was used to analyze the accessibility of rehabilitation services by residential region. The Kaplan-Meier method was employed to compare the survival rates of rehabilitation patients across different residential regions. A Cox proportional hazards model was used to estimate the independent contribution of each factor to mortality risk (hazard ratios [HRs] and 95% confidence interval [CIs]). Significant differences in mortality were observed according to sociodemographic factors and Charlson Comorbidity Index scores. Accessibility in Capital area and Metropolitan cities was comparable to the Capital. However, patients living in a rural area had significantly lower access to rehabilitation compared to those in the Capital (PT: OR = 0.889, 95% CIs: 0.809-0.987, P = .029; OT: OR = 0.802, 95% CIs: 0.726-0.886, P = .001). Notably, among those receiving inpatient rehabilitation, rural area residency was associated with a higher risk of death compared to the Capital (HRs = 1.288; 95% CIs, 1.015-1.635; P = .037). In contrast, no significant disparity was found in the outpatient group (HRs = 1.011; 95% CIs, 0.917-1.115; P = .820). Stroke patients living in rural area were less likely to receive rehabilitation services than those in the capital. This regional disparity in access, particularly in inpatient rehabilitation, is associated with an increased risk of long-term mortality after stroke. These findings suggest that improving inpatient rehabilitation infrastructure in rural area is critical to reducing survival gaps.

titre: Priority domains, design and contextual considerations for a rehabilitation program addressing the daily living functioning of people diagnosed with borderline personality disorder: a modified nominal group technique.
titre_fr: Priority domains, design and contextual considerations for a rehabilitation program addressing the daily living functioning of people diagnosed with borderline personality disorder: a modified nominal group technique.
auteurs: Tepper Dillon, Sellar Ben, Shipley Sheryl, Smith Rachel, Murray Carolyn M
resume: People diagnosed with borderline personality disorder (BPD) experience persistent functional impairment, yet no manualised rehabilitation program addressing daily living functioning currently exists, creating opportunity for program development. This study aimed to identify: 1) priority domains of daily living functioning to include in a rehabilitation program, and 2) how such a program could support functional recovery. Five focus groups using a modified nominal group technique captured consumer (n = 9), caregiver (n = 7), mental health clinician (n = 3) and occupational therapist (n = 5) perspectives. Priority domains were ranked to structure discussions. Transcripts were analysed using conventional content analysis. Seven priority domains were identified: 1) Finding purpose and identity through roles, values and milestones; 2) Sleep and energy management; 3) Coping strategies to support emotional regulation; 4) Relationships, social connection and interpersonal skills; 5) Structured routines and balanced living; 6) Self-care, household and financial management; and 7) Help-seeking and self-advocacy. Participants envisioned a modular, graded program adjunctive to psychotherapy, addressing foundational domains before values-aligned roles. Design considerations included caregiver involvement, facilitator training, and responsiveness to stigma and comorbidities. Findings provide priority domains, design and contextual considerations to inform co-production of a rehabilitation program.

titre: Home Assessment Instruments in Occupational Therapy: A Scoping Review.
titre_fr: Home Assessment Instruments in Occupational Therapy: A Scoping Review.
auteurs: Juan Guillén María, Fernández-Pires Paula, Espinosa-Sempere María-Cristina, Company-Devesa Verónica, Sánchez-Pérez Alicia, Prieto-Botella Daniel, Pastor-Zaplana José-Ángel, Moreno-Morente Gema, Peral-Gómez Paula
revue: Hong Kong journal of occupational therapy : HKJOT
resume: The home environment should foster the independence, participation, and safety of its inhabitants. However, the presence of environmental barriers, especially for individuals with disabilities, can negatively impact their functioning, reducing well-being and quality of life at home. Occupational therapy plays a crucial role in this context, offering holistic evaluation processes and strategies for effective home modifications to improve occupational performance. To our knowledge, no comprehensive mapping of these tools exists. Therefore, this study conducts a scoping review to map and critically describe the home assessment instruments currently used within the field of occupational therapy. A scoping review following a systematized approach was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR recommendations for scoping reviews, involving an online bibliographic search complemented by the consultation of grey literature. A two-phase screening process was performed to systematically identify the instruments referenced. Ninety-three articles were included, identifying twenty-nine home assessment tools applied in occupational therapy. These instruments presented notable differences in their format, target population, aspects assessed, and the degree of user participation during the evaluation process, among other characteristics. This scoping review mapped 29 home assessment tools, revealing a strong focus on environmental factors but a critical gap in assessing personal factors, occupations, and social roles. While most instruments demonstrate acceptable reliability and validity, there is an urgent need for more robust psychometric studies, tools validated as clinical outcome measures, and the cultural adaptation of holistic, person-centered assessments to effectively guide home modifications. https://osf.io/8bmu9.

titre: Intersection Rules Subtest Timing as a Predictor of DriveSafe DriveAware Outcomes: A Pilot Study.
titre_fr: Intersection Rules Subtest Timing as a Predictor of DriveSafe DriveAware Outcomes: A Pilot Study.
auteurs: Wong Hoi Lam Stephanie, O'Donnell Joan, MacKenzie Lynette, Johnston Belinda Joy, James Carole L
revue: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
resume: ImportanceIntersection Rules Subtest timing is a potential predictor of the DriveSafe outcome score in DriveSafe DriveAware (DSDA) assessment.ObjectiveTo examine whether Intersection Rules completion time is associated with DriveSafe outcome within the DSDA assessment.DesignRetrospective, observational pilot study using secondary data.SettingAustralian metropolitan fitness-to-drive clinic.ParticipantsOf 169 participants (median age = 80; 61.5% male), 104 categorised into non-pass group of DriveSafe subtest formed 'cases', whilst 65 who passed were 'controls'.Outcomes and MeasuresPrimary predictor: Intersection Rules Subtest completion time in seconds. Primary outcome: DriveSafe subtest outcome, categorised as pass/non-pass. Relationships analysed using logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.ResultsLonger Intersection Rules Subtest time significantly predicted lower DriveSafe subtest outcome (non-pass) scores, with each additional 60 s increasing odds of failure by 93.7% (odds ratio [OR] = 1.94, 95% confidence interval [CI] [1.40, 2.68], p < .001). A ROC curve analysis revealed an area under the curve of 0.73 (95% CI: [.654, .807]). An optimal cut-off of 213.5 s showed high specificity (86.2%) (95% CI: [75.3, 93.5]) but modest sensitivity (48.1%) (95% CI: [38.2, 58.1]) for a non-pass result.Conclusions and RelevanceIntersection Rules Subtest completion time was associated with DriveSafe outcome in this pilot study. The current findings support future study of this timing metric, which may have potential as a clinical decision-support indicator, a 'Detect and Pause' step, after prospective validation and DSDA protocol sequence modification.

titre: Actor-Partner Effects on Dyadic Adjustment, Relationship Satisfaction, and Well-Being after Spinal Cord Injury.
titre_fr: Actor-Partner Effects on Dyadic Adjustment, Relationship Satisfaction, and Well-Being after Spinal Cord Injury.
auteurs: Xiang Siqi, Teramoto Masaru, Terrill Alexandra L
revue: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
resume: ImportanceSpinal cord injury (SCI) extends beyond the injured individual to intimate partners, often altering shared occupations, relational roles, and well-being. Understanding dyadic processes is critical for occupational therapy practice.ObjectiveTo examine associations among dyadic adjustment, relationship satisfaction, and well-being in SCI dyads using an actor-partner interdependence model.DesignCross-sectional dyadic study using baseline data from an intervention trial (SupportGroove).SettingHealth care institutions and community-based settings.ParticipantsEighty-two community-dwelling SCI-partner dyads (164 adults; mean ages: SCI, 50.1 ± 15.7; partners, 48.5 ± 14.5 years), 3 months to 5 years postinjury.Outcomes and MeasuresSelf-report; Revised Dyadic Adjustment Scale, Couples Satisfaction Index-4, and Neuro-QoL Positive Affect and Well-Being.ResultsDyadic adjustment was significantly and positively associated with relationship satisfaction among SCI participants (β = 0.66, standard error [SE] = 0.09, p < .001), indicating a large effect. A similar significant positive association was observed among partners (β = 0.47, SE = 0.11, p < .001), reflecting a medium effect size. Additionally, partners' relationship satisfaction was significantly and positively related to their own well-being (β = 0.35, SE = 0.14, p = .010), with a medium effect. No other structural equation model paths reached statistical significance (p > .05).Conclusions and RelevanceDyadic adjustment influences how both members of the SCI dyad perceive their relationship. However, relationship satisfaction contributes to well-being primarily for partners rather than for individuals with SCI. These findings support a dyadic approach to occupational therapy and rehabilitation that considers relationship functioning and well-being in both members of the dyad.

titre: OT-Vision: A 3D depth sensing mobile application to aid clinician-led home environment assessments for falls prevention.
titre_fr: OT-Vision: A 3D depth sensing mobile application to aid clinician-led home environment assessments for falls prevention.
auteurs: Ibrahim Zear, Money Arthur G, Atwal Anita, Spiliotopoulou Georgia
revue: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
resume: BackgroundAccurate measurement of the home environment is a critical component of clinician-led falls-risk assessment in occupational therapy. However, traditional paper-based measurement approaches can be time-consuming and may introduce variability, particularly under real-world conditions. Advances in mobile depth-sensing technologies provide new opportunities to support clinicians during in-home assessment tasks.ObjectiveThis paper introduces OT-Vision, a mobile application integrating depth-perception for point-to-point measurement, designed to assist occupational therapists in performing falls-risk assessments within the home.MethodsA within-subjects counterbalanced mixed-methods design was employed with 37 trainee and practising occupational therapists within controlled simulation environments. OT-Vision was compared with the standard paper-based measurement booklet with respect to measurement bias, accuracy, and task completion time. Usability and user experiences were evaluated via the System Usability Scale and semi-structured interviews.ResultsOT-Vision demonstrated broadly comparable levels of measurement bias compared to the paper-based guidance and modestly greater measurement accuracy, with significantly lower absolute measurement error for two items, following Holm-Bonferroni correction. Participants completed most measurement tasks more efficiently using OT-Vision, and usability scores were higher for OT-Vision versus the paper-based booklet. Qualitative findings indicated perceived benefits in workflow efficiency and measurement confidence, alongside challenges associated with reflective surfaces and adoption within established practice.ConclusionsThe findings suggest that mobile depth perception-enabled measurement applications such as OT-Vision may support more efficient and reliable measurement during home environment falls-risk assessments. While further refinement is required to address interaction and surface-related challenges, OT-Vision shows promise as a digital tool to support contemporary occupational therapy assessment practices.

titre: Universal Design for Learning: Advancing Equity in Undergraduate Nursing Education.
titre_fr: Universal Design for Learning: Advancing Equity in Undergraduate Nursing Education.
auteurs: Charles Marie Lourdes, Berro Elizabeth A, Tokash Jennifer, Lopez Michele Lucille, Damiao John, Hernandez Joeleena, Macatangay Kristen
resume: BackgroundIndividuals with disabilities account for at least 15% of the world's population. Students with disabilities are underrepresented in nursing due to systemic barriers, misconceptions about abilities, and rigid technical standards.PurposeThis quality improvement project describes strategies of an ongoing initiative to improve accessibility and inclusion by implementing Universal Design for Learning (UDL), interprofessional collaboration, and evidence-based institutional practices.MethodsUDL served as the template to improve diversity and adopt inclusive practices in a Nursing Program in the Northeastern region of the United States. These principles facilitate flexible learning and assessment options that promote the development of academic and clinical competence. Strategies were aligned with requirements of the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education and the American Association of Colleges of Nursing and state that inclusive practice can coexist with rigorous competency expectations. A grant from the Josiah Macy Jr. Foundation supported a partnership between nursing and occupational therapy programs at a mid-sized university to integrate students with disabilities into the nursing curriculum. The project's primary goals included ensuring physical, instructional, and technological accessibility and revising policies that support an inclusive institutional climate.

titre: Phytoremediation potential of native plants in fly ash-contaminated sites: a review on heavy metal uptake and soil restoration strategies.
titre_fr: Phytoremediation potential of native plants in fly ash-contaminated sites: a review on heavy metal uptake and soil restoration strategies.
auteurs: Dhadse Sharda, Chole Achal
resume: Fly ash generated from coal-fired thermal power plants represents one of the largest industrial solid wastes worldwide and poses significant environmental challenges due to its high alkalinity, poor nutrient status, and elevated concentrations of potentially toxic elements such as arsenic (As), cadmium (Cd), chromium (Cr), lead (Pb), nickel (Ni), and mercury (Hg). The uncontrolled disposal of fly ash threatens soil quality, groundwater resources, ecosystem stability, and human health, highlighting the urgent need for sustainable remediation strategies. Among the available technologies, phytoremediation using native plant species has emerged as an environmentally friendly and potentially lower-input because indigenous plants are naturally adapted to local climatic and edaphic conditions, enabling long-term establishment and ecological restoration with minimal external inputs. This review critically synthesizes current knowledge on the physicochemical characteristics of fly ash, heavy metal speciation and bioavailability, and the physiological, biochemical, molecular, and rhizosphere-mediated mechanisms governing heavy metal uptake, translocation, detoxification, and sequestration in native plant species. Unlike previous reviews that primarily provide descriptive accounts of phytoremediation, this review integrates plant functional traits, rhizosphere interactions, soil microbial dynamics, and ecosystem restoration processes into a comprehensive framework for selecting suitable native species for fly ash rehabilitation. The review further discusses recent advances in microbiome-assisted phytoremediation, biochar-assisted remediation, omics technologies, artificial intelligence-assisted species selection, remote sensing, and ecological risk assessment as emerging tools for improving remediation efficiency and long-term restoration monitoring. Existing knowledge gaps, including limited long-term field validation, biomass disposal challenges, insufficient economic assessment, and the need for standardized evaluation criteria, are critically examined. Finally, the review proposes future research priorities and emphasizes the integration of phytoremediation with sustainable land management and environmental policy to support resilient ecosystem restoration and the long-term rehabilitation of fly ash-contaminated landscapes.
