Force analysis indicated that the proposed linkage mechanism reduced the operating force to approximately 10 N, corresponding to a 45.6% reduction in user effort. Furthermore, usability assessment yielded a mean System Usability Scale (SUS) score of 86.3/100, indicating excellent user acceptance. The findings demonstrate that the proposed STS wheelchair is a safe, mechanically robust, and cost-effective assistive mobility solution that enhances user independence, reduces caregiver burden, and improves the quality of life for individuals with mobility impairments, particularly in low-resource settings.

titre: Quality, source transparency, information reliability, and domain coverage of short video-based information on feeding guidance for people with dysphagia: a cross-sectional study on 4 major Chinese social media platforms.
titre_fr: Quality, source transparency, information reliability, and domain coverage of short video-based information on feeding guidance for people with dysphagia: a cross-sectional study on 4 major Chinese social media platforms.
auteurs: Chen Jiaying, Xiong Ting, Li Ying, Wang Yue, Yang Chen, Huang Jinghui, Fang Fanfu
resume: Standardized feeding guidance is valuable for people with dysphagia, helping prevent aspiration, improve nutritional status, and enhance quality of life. In recent years, short-video platforms have become a key avenue for the public to access health information, providing people with dysphagia with a convenient channel to learn about feeding management. However, the quality of online health information varies considerably, making it difficult for patients to effectively distinguish reliable information from potential misconceptions, which may negatively impact clinical outcomes. This study aims to systematically evaluate feeding guidance content for dysphagia on mainstream Chinese short-video platforms by analyzing its quality, the transparency of its information sources, the reliability of the information, and its coverage of relevant domains. This study retrieved and included 278 short videos on feeding guidance for dysphagia as research samples from four major Chinese mainstream short video platforms: Rednote, Bilibili, Douyin, and Kwai. Two independent rehabilitation therapists specializing in dysphagia rehabilitation evaluated the domain coverage of video content using 10 criteria derived from relevant clinical guidelines and expert consensus documents on feeding guidance for people with dysphagia. We assessed the transparency of the video's information sources, overall quality, and information reliability using the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) Benchmark Criteria, the Global Quality Score (GQS), and the modified DISCERN (mDISCERN) Score. We also compared video data from different content providers and upload platforms. Based on the identity of the video uploader, videos were classified into seven categories, comprising four categories of healthcare professionals (physiatrists, rehabilitation therapists, rehabilitation nurses, and healthcare professionals in related clinical departments) and three categories of non-healthcare professionals (non-profit organizations, individual science communicators, and people with dysphagia). The results indicated that the overall quality of feeding guidance videos for people with dysphagia was generally low (GQS median = 2, IQR = 2-3). The impact of uploader identity varied across assessment dimensions: healthcare professionals scored significantly higher than non-healthcare professionals on both the JAMA score (P < .001) and the mDISCERN score (P < .001), although the inter-group difference in the GQS score was not statistically significant; rehabilitation nurses performed best on the GQS dimension, healthcare professionals in related clinical departments achieved the highest scores on the mDISCERN dimension, and people with dysphagia scored the lowest on the JAMA dimension. Differences among platforms also exhibit dimensionality dependence: the GQS scores showed minimal variation, with only Bilibili and Kwai exhibiting a statistically significant difference (adjusted P < .05, r = .376); the JAMA scores demonstrated moderate variation, with Rednote, Douyin, and Bilibili all significantly outperforming Kwai (adjusted P < .0001, r = .387; adjusted P < .0001, r = .551; adjusted P < .05, r = .288); the mDISCERN scores showed the most pronounced differences (ε 2 = .503), with Douyin significantly surpassing Rednote, Bilibili, and Kwai (adjusted P < .0001, r = .771; adjusted P < .0001, r = .757; adjusted P < .0001, r = .595). In terms of domain coverage, food adjustment (77%) and swallowing posture adjustment (52%) had relatively high coverage rates. In contrast, high-risk domains such as medication management (4%), nutritional management (21%), and oral care (17%) exhibited severe supply gaps. Among current mainstream short-video platforms in China, the overall quality of educational content on feeding guidance for people with dysphagia still requires improvement. The reliability of this information depends on both content creators' professional backgrounds and platform ecosystems. The existing short videos currently lack sufficient support for safe decision-making and standardized self-management among people with dysphagia. There is an urgent need to implement coordinated interventions that incorporate professional expertise, platform algorithm governance, and multidimensional quality assessments to support the standardized development of a health science communication environment.

titre: Three-dimensional evaluation and optimization of breast cancer rehabilitation science popularization videos on mainstream video platforms: a cross-sectional study in Mainland China.
titre_fr: Three-dimensional evaluation and optimization of breast cancer rehabilitation science popularization videos on mainstream video platforms: a cross-sectional study in Mainland China.
auteurs: Wu Siqi, Chen Chang, Chen Ge, Wang Fuyou, Wang Jianxiong
resume: With the growing number of breast cancer survivors, rehabilitation has become a critical component of comprehensive cancer care. Mainstream video platforms have emerged as a primary channel for patients to access rehabilitation information, yet the quality of such content remains unevaluated. This study aimed to systematically assess the quality and dissemination characteristics of breast cancer rehabilitation-related videos on TikTok, MicroBlog, and Today's Headline. A cross-sectional design was employed. From June to July 2026, videos related to breast cancer rehabilitation were retrieved on three platforms using an account-free search mode. 450 valid samples (150 per platform) were selected and a three-dimensional evaluation system was established: content scientificity (modified DISCERN scale), dissemination presentation (Global Quality Scale), and source credibility (JAMA scale). Overall quality was the arithmetic mean of the three dimensions. Six evaluators conducted scoring; inter-rater reliability was tested by ICC(2,k). Post hoc power analysis confirmed sufficient power (>0.99) for detecting medium-effect differences. The overall quality score was 2.74 ± 0.85, with a pass rate (≥3.5) of only 19.8%; a sensitivity analysis using alternative cutoffs (≥3.0 and ≥4.0) yielded pass rates of 42.4% and 6.7%, respectively, confirming the robustness of the low-quality conclusion. TikTok's overall quality, content scientificity, and source credibility scores were significantly higher than MicroBlog and Today's Headlines (all P < 0.05, η 2 = 0.11-0.16), a difference partly attributable to TikTok's higher proportion of certified physicians. One-way ANOVA revealed significant overall differences among four creator types (F = 128.6, P < 0.001, η 2 = 0.46), with Tukey post hoc tests confirming certified physicians > rehabilitation nurses > health institutions > ordinary users. Subgroup analysis showed that sexual/reproductive rehabilitation videos had the lowest quality (2.45 ± 0.91). A weak negative association was observed between the engagement composite and quality (r = -0.18, 95% CI: -0.27 to -0.09, P < 0.001). The overall quality of breast cancer rehabilitation popular science videos on Chinese mainstream platforms was low. Patients should prioritize content from certified physicians and health institutions that cite guidelines and present balanced information. Platform-specific regulation and greater participation by certified oncologists and rehabilitation specialists are urgently needed. Level II; Cross-Sectional Study.

titre: Kinesiophobia following ACL reconstruction: a qualitative netnographic study of lived experiences shared on Reddit.
titre_fr: Kinesiophobia following ACL reconstruction: a qualitative netnographic study of lived experiences shared on Reddit.
auteurs: Kahve Yakup, Darben Azarsiz Yagmur, Aydin Serap, Aydin Tahsin, Gurhan Utku, Civan Kahve Aybeniz
resume: Kinesiophobia, broadly defined as fear of movement and vulnerability to (re)injury, is one of the most significant psychological barriers to functional recovery following anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction, yet its everyday, lived texture is not fully captured by structured psychometric instruments. Orthopedic clinicians frequently observe that patients who have achieved objective surgical and functional recovery nonetheless remain reluctant to resume movement. This study aimed to explore this phenomenon in patients' own words. We conducted a qualitative netnographic study of 50 first-person Reddit narratives shared by individuals with ACL injury, spanning the rehabilitation trajectory from preoperative anxiety to chronic post-return instability. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis by an interdisciplinary team of orthopedic surgeons and psychiatrists. Three interconnected themes emerged. First, a progressive loss of trust in the injured body, in which normal postoperative sensations were hypervigilantly monitored and catastrophically reinterpreted as signs of graft failure, persisting even after objective strength testing and medical clearance. Second, fear-driven disruption of functional identity and future planning, in which reinjury fear extended beyond the knee to threaten occupational continuity, financial security, and physical self-concept. Third, persistent uncertainty and compulsive reassurance-seeking, fueled by inconsistent rehabilitation guidance and unfavorable social comparison with peers' recovery timelines on social media. Psychological readiness for return to activity appears to be shaped by an interacting network of bodily, identity-related, and informational factors that extend beyond fear of reinjury as traditionally measured. Incorporating expectation management, structured reassurance, and psychologically informed communication into postoperative care protocols may benefit orthopedic and rehabilitation teams. Naturally occurring online narratives may serve as an ecologically valid source of insight into the psychological dimensions of ACL recovery, complementing structured psychometric assessment.

titre: TikTok Videos on the Medial Patellofemoral Ligament Have Low Educational Quality and Reliability.
titre_fr: TikTok Videos on the Medial Patellofemoral Ligament Have Low Educational Quality and Reliability.
auteurs: Conteduca Jacopo, Brindisino Fabrizio, Casto Alberto, Valentino Luigi, Scrimitore Angelo, Bernetti Andrea, Rollo Giuseppe
resume: To assess the quality, reliability, and engagement of TikTok videos addressing the material about medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL). Between November 2 and 24, 2024, a comprehensive search of the TikTok platform was performed using both keyword-based search ("MPFL," "medial patellofemoral ligament") and hashtag-based search (#MPFL) to maximize content capture. Videos were included if they addressed the MPFL with respect to anatomy, injury mechanism, clinical evaluation, surgical management, or rehabilitation. Each video was independently assessed using the DISCERN instrument, Journal of the American Medical Association benchmark criteria, Global Quality Scale, and Patient Education and Decision Support Score. Video characteristics, including duration, number of views, likes, shares, and shares, were recorded, and correlations between engagement metrics and quality scores were analyzed. Of 100 videos analyzed, 9% were posted by medical doctors, 3% by physiotherapists, and 88% by private users. Most videos focused on personal experience, representing 74% of the information type and 80% of the content type. The mean scores of DISCERN, Journal of the American Medical Association, Global Quality Scale, and Patient Education and Decision Support Score were 16.25 ± 4.07, 0.1 ± 0.4, 1.1 ± 0.5, and 0.6 ± 1.88, respectively. Videos uploaded by medical professionals achieved significantly higher quality scores across all metrics (P < .001). No significant differences were observed between physicians and physiotherapists (P = .173). Engagement metrics (views, likes, shares) showed moderate positive correlations with DISCERN (r = 0.31) and Patient Education and Decision Support Score (r = 0.39), whereas video duration showed no correlation with any quality index. TikTok videos related to the MPFL show low educational quality and limited reliability, with the most content produced by nonmedical users. Videos uploaded by health care professionals achieved significantly higher quality scores across all evaluated assessment tools. Patients with MPFL pathology frequently seek medical information on social media platforms. Awareness of the limited educational quality and reliability of MPFL-related content on TikTok may help clinicians better counsel patients regarding online health information.

titre: Turkish Adaptation and Psychometric Evaluation of the Measure of Processes of Care for Service Providers in Pediatric Care and Rehabilitation.
titre_fr: Turkish Adaptation and Psychometric Evaluation of the Measure of Processes of Care for Service Providers in Pediatric Care and Rehabilitation.
auteurs: Özal Cemil, Türker Duygu, Gunel Mintaze Kerem
resume: Background/Objectives: Family-centered services (FCSs) are a key approach in pediatric healthcare and rehabilitation that promotes collaboration between service providers and families. The Measure of Processes of Care for Service Providers (MPOC-SP) is widely used to evaluate family-centered services from the provider perspective; however, no validated Turkish version is available. This study aimed to translate and culturally adapt the MPOC-SP into Turkish and to examine its factor structure, internal consistency, test-retest reliability, measurement error, and supplementary model-based construct indices among Turkish-speaking service providers working in pediatric healthcare, disability, and rehabilitation settings. Methods: The MPOC-SP was translated and culturally adapted following a structured cross-cultural adaptation process. A total of 267 service providers from multiple professional disciplines, institutional settings, and 15 provinces of Türkiye participated in the psychometric evaluation. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega. Test-retest reliability was evaluated in 86 participants using ICC(2,1), and measurement error was examined using the standard error of measurement (SEM) and minimal detectable change at the 95% confidence level (MDC95). The hypothesized four-factor structure was evaluated in 267 participants using confirmatory factor analysis based on polychoric correlations and diagonally weighted least squares (DWLS). Composite reliability, average variance extracted, the Fornell-Larcker criterion, and the heterotrait-monotrait ratio were examined as supplementary model-based indices. Institutional-group comparisons were exploratory. Results: The four subscales demonstrated high internal consistency, with Cronbach's alpha coefficients ranging from 0.884 to 0.968 and McDonald's omega coefficients from 0.885 to 0.968. Test-retest reliability was good to excellent (ICC[2,1] = 0.819-0.963), although small systematic decreases were observed for SIS and CSI. SEM values ranged from 0.228 to 0.328 and MDC95 values from 0.633 to 0.908. The four-factor model showed a good fit (χ2(318) = 463.24, CFI = 0.998, TLI = 0.998, RMSEA = 0.041, 90% CI [0.033-0.049], SRMR = 0.057), with standardized factor loadings ranging from 0.761 to 0.933. Composite reliability ranged from 0.899 to 0.976, AVE from 0.640 to 0.800, and HTMT values from 0.372 to 0.664. No substantial ceiling effects were observed at the subscale level; however, 14 of 27 items exceeded the predefined 15% criterion for item-level ceiling effects. Conclusions: The findings provide initial evidence supporting the four-factor structure and reliability of the Turkish MPOC-SP in this sample of service providers. Interpretation should focus on the four established subscales rather than an overall total score. Further studies in independent and more balanced samples are needed to examine external construct validity, measurement invariance, responsiveness, and clinically meaningful change.

titre: Canadian French adaptation and validation of instruments measuring return-to-work expectations and recovery expectations: Exploring similarities and differences between the two concepts.
titre_fr: Canadian French adaptation and validation of instruments measuring return-to-work expectations and recovery expectations: Exploring similarities and differences between the two concepts.
auteurs: Larivière Christian, Zaki Philip, Negrini Alessia, Corthésy-Blondin Laurent, Mecheri Hakim, Hong Quan Nha
revue: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine
resume: The aims of this study were to (1) to perform the transcultural adaptation from English to Canadian French of four instruments measuring return to work (RTW) expectations and two on recovery expectations, (2) assess their construct validity, and (3) to test their underlying constructs. The instruments were translated and then adapted through pre-testing. Their construct validity was verified using hypothesis testing. Correlations between RTW and recovery-expectation instruments tested their conceptual overlap. The transcultural adaptation step was straightforward. Hypothesis testing supported three RTW-expectations and one recovery expectations' instruments. Their correlations were low, suggesting that RTW expectations and recovery expectations instruments do not measure the same constructs. Hypothesis testing allowed rejecting some instruments but supported others. Recovery expectations, referring to health and healing, should be differentiated from RTW-expectations, referring to work participation.

titre: Criterion validity of the Watt-max Test and Test Assessors' judgement of V..O2max achievement in Individuals with Heart Disease.
titre_fr: Criterion validity of the Watt-max Test and Test Assessors' judgement of V..O2max achievement in Individuals with Heart Disease.
auteurs: Sevel Claus Theilgaard, Maribo Thomas, Dalgas Ulrik, Brincks John Kodal, Larsen Ryan Godske
revue: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
resume: To evaluate the criterion validity of the Watt-max test for identifying attainment of maximal oxygen consumption (V̇O₂max) in individuals with heart disease in primary healthcare. A secondary aim was to assess the accuracy of test assessors' judgement of maximal effort during the Watt-max test. Cross-sectional validation study. Single-centre primary healthcare cardiac rehabilitation program. 202 adults with diagnosed heart disease enrolled in cardiac rehabilitation. Participants completed a cycle-ergometer Watt-max test simultaneously with indirect calorimetry, which served as the reference standard. The primary criterion for confirming V̇O₂max was the attainment of a plateau in oxygen uptake, defined as a ≤50 mL/min increase in oxygen uptake despite increased workload during the Watt-max test. Secondary criteria included respiratory exchange ratio (≥1.15), rating of perceived exertion (≥17), and maximal heart rate (≥92% of age-predicted maximal heart rate). Overall, 155 participants (77%) met the predefined criteria for V̇O₂max attainment. Of these, 60% demonstrated a V̇O₂ plateau, while an additional 17% met at least two secondary criteria. Assessors correctly identified 81.9% of tests in which V̇O₂max was attained during the Watt-max test. However, low specificity (34.0%) and negative predictive value (36.4%) suggest limited accuracy for ruling out maximal effort. The Watt-max test demonstrates acceptable criterion validity for identifying V̇O₂max in individuals with heart disease when conducted in a primary healthcare setting. Assessors showed fair ability to identify maximal effort, yet caution is warranted when maximal effort is assessed as not achieved.

Secondary criteria included respiratory exchange ratio (≥1.15), rating of perceived exertion (≥17), and maximal heart rate (≥92% of age-predicted maximal heart rate). Overall, 155 participants (77%) met the predefined criteria for V̇O₂max attainment. Of these, 60% demonstrated a V̇O₂ plateau, while an additional 17% met at least two secondary criteria. Assessors correctly identified 81.9% of tests in which V̇O₂max was attained during the Watt-max test. However, low specificity (34.0%) and negative predictive value (36.4%) suggest limited accuracy for ruling out maximal effort. The Watt-max test demonstrates acceptable criterion validity for identifying V̇O₂max in individuals with heart disease when conducted in a primary healthcare setting. Assessors showed fair ability to identify maximal effort, yet caution is warranted when maximal effort is assessed as not achieved.

titre: Translation, Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Preliminary Validation of the Italian Version of the Early Cognitive and Listening Links (EarlyCaLL) Framework.
titre_fr: Translation, Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Preliminary Validation of the Italian Version of the Early Cognitive and Listening Links (EarlyCaLL) Framework.
auteurs: Caragli Valeria, Genovese Elisabetta, Monzani Daniele, Soloperto Davide, Galeazzi Gian Maria, Pingani Luca
resume: Background/Objectives: Children with severe-to-profound hearing loss and additional disabilities, receiving cochlear implant (CI), require multidimensional outcome measures that extend beyond conventional assessments of auditory perception and spoken language. The Early Cognitive and Listening Links (EarlyCaLL) framework was originally developed by the Nottingham Auditory Implant Programme team, in the United Kingdom, led by Datta and colleagues, to support expectation counselling and to monitor post-cochlear implantation progress in children with CI and associated complex needs. The framework was designed to capture broader developmental outcomes, including cognition, social and emotional engagement, listening and understanding, vocalisations and early talk, and augmentative and alternative communication (AAC), alongside CI equipment use and signal tolerance. However, to date, no validated Italian version of the Framework has been available. This study aims to translate, culturally adapt, and perform a preliminary psychometric validation of the Italian version of the EarlyCaLL. Methods: A methodological study was conducted following international guidelines for translation and cross-cultural adaptation. The development phase included forward translation, expert committee review, back-translation, developer review, and pre-validation refinement. The validation phase involved 20 experienced professionals. Results: The expert panel demonstrated extensive clinical experience, with a 100% response rate. Face validity was excellent across all six domains (≥90% adequate ratings; Gwet's AC1 = 0.82). Ninety percent of experts considered the questionnaire acceptable without substantial modifications, and 10% recommended only minor revisions. All 25 descriptors achieved perfect content validity, while the overall scale indices also indicated unanimous agreement regarding the relevance and adequacy of the instrument. Conclusions: Our results support the face and content validity of the Italian version of the EarlyCaLL, supporting further clinical validation as a culturally adapted multidimensional observational instrument for evaluating rehabilitation outcomes in children with CI and additional disabilities. The framework provides a comprehensive assessment of functional development and may facilitate individualized rehabilitation, multidisciplinary collaboration, and family-centred care in pediatric CI.

titre: First Opioid Exposure During Adolescent Third Molar Surgery: A Neurodevelopmental Perspective on Opioid Stewardship.
titre_fr: First Opioid Exposure During Adolescent Third Molar Surgery: A Neurodevelopmental Perspective on Opioid Stewardship.
auteurs: Smiley Alayna B
revue: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery : official journal of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons
resume: Third molar extraction is commonly performed in adolescents and young adults and may represent an early exposure to prescription opioids. Observational studies have examined whether perioperative opioid prescribing in dentoalveolar surgery is associated with subsequent opioid use. This perspective evaluates epidemiologic findings regarding persistent opioid use after third molar extraction and considers relevant aspects of adolescent neurodevelopment. Retrospective cohort studies report increased adjusted odds of persistent opioid use among some opioid-naive adolescents receiving perioperative dental opioid prescriptions, although absolute risk remains low. Developmental neuroscience demonstrates continued maturation of prefrontal cortical networks during adolescence and heightened reward responsivity, providing biologic context for reinforcement sensitivity. Current evidence does not establish a causal relationship between short-course postoperative opioid prescribing and addiction. However, epidemiologic associations and developmental considerations support continued emphasis on multimodal, opioid-sparing analgesia in adolescent third molar surgery.

titre: Early-Life Polyethylene Microplastic Exposure Exacerbates ADHD-Like Behaviors in Mice via PI3K/AKT1/Nrf2 Signaling: Evidence From the Pilot Cohort and Multi-Omics Analyses.
titre_fr: Early-Life Polyethylene Microplastic Exposure Exacerbates ADHD-Like Behaviors in Mice via PI3K/AKT1/Nrf2 Signaling: Evidence From the Pilot Cohort and Multi-Omics Analyses.
auteurs: Luo Yufan, Xie Ruijin, Xu Hua, Xiao Xue, Xiao Wei, Pan Qiyang, Xu Shengjie, Liu Li, Xiao Zeliang, Zhou Yue, Sun Chenyu, Wu Yu, Liu Yueying
resume: Microplastic pollution may influence neurodevelopment, yet its relationship with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) remains unclear. We integrated a pediatric cohort, multi-omics analyses, network toxicology, and animal experiments to investigate polyethylene (PE) microplastic exposure in ADHD vulnerability. Among 90 children, PE was the predominant polymer detected in blood and was more abundant in children with ADHD. Higher PE burden was associated with greater symptom severity, increased IL-6, and reduced antioxidant capacity. Multi-omics and network analyses converged on PI3K/AKT1/Nrf2 signaling. In a perinatal nicotine mouse model, developmental PE co-exposure exacerbated ADHD-like behaviors, dopaminergic dysfunction, and oxidative injury. Melatonin partially alleviated these abnormalities by restoring PI3K/AKT1/GSK3β and Nrf2 signaling, whereas AAV-mediated PI3K knockdown weakened its protective effects. Collectively, the human findings identify circulating PE burden as an environmental correlate of ADHD-related neurodevelopmental vulnerability, while the animal experiments provide evidence that developmental PE co-exposure can aggravate ADHD-like abnormalities in a susceptible background.

titre: Antenatal multiple micronutrients versus iron-folic acid supplementation and infant neurodevelopment: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Antenatal multiple micronutrients versus iron-folic acid supplementation and infant neurodevelopment: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Nagpal Jitender, Tyagi Sarika, Rawat Swapnil, Yadav Ramasheesh
revue: The American journal of clinical nutrition
resume: Antenatal multiple micronutrient (MMN) supplementation reduces the risk of low birth weight and small-for-gestational-age birth compared with iron and folic acid (IFA), but whether the benefits extend to neurodevelopment remains uncertain. To estimate the effect of antenatal MMN compared with IFA on infant cognitive, motor, and language development up to 24 months of age. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, OpenGrey, Wiley Online Library, and trial registers through June 10, 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing antenatal MMN with IFA and reporting infant neurodevelopment. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty with GRADE. Hedges g estimates were pooled with a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model and Knapp-Hartung adjustment; cluster-trial variances were inflated by the design effect. Of 2,943 records, seven trials (8 reports; 5,331 infants for the cognitive comparison) were included. MMN and IFA did not differ in cognitive development (g = +0.02; 95% CI -0.06, +0.10; P = 0.53; I<sup>2</sup> = 13%) or motor development (g = -0.02; 95% CI -0.09, +0.05; P = 0.49; I<sup>2</sup> = 0%). Language showed a small, non-significant advantage for MMN that was not robust across sensitivity analyses (g = +0.07; 95% CI -0.00, +0.14; P = 0.06; I<sup>2</sup> = 0%). All pooled point estimates were below the conventional threshold for a small, standardized effect of 0.2. Certainty was moderate for cognitive and motor outcomes and low for language. Antenatal MMN supplementation was associated with little to no difference in infant cognitive or motor development compared with IFA up to 24 months of age. The small language difference was not statistically significant, was not robust across sensitivity analyses, and is unlikely to be clinically important. PROSPERO CRD420261392389. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261392389.

titre: Single-Nucleus RNA Sequencing Analysis of the MECP2-Deficient Marmoset Hippocampus Reveals Altered Maturation-Associated Transcriptional Programs in Hippocampal Granule Neurons.
titre_fr: Single-Nucleus RNA Sequencing Analysis of the MECP2-Deficient Marmoset Hippocampus Reveals Altered Maturation-Associated Transcriptional Programs in Hippocampal Granule Neurons.
auteurs: He Ching Chi Jimmy, Kishi Noriyuki, Sanosaka Tsukasa, Kohyama Jun, Okano Hideyuki
resume: Rett syndrome (RTT) is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder primarily caused by mutations in the methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MECP2) gene. Although rodent models have provided important insights into RTT pathogenesis, the cell type-specific consequences of MECP2 deficiency in the primate brain remain poorly understood. Here, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing of the hippocampus from MECP2-deficient common marmosets to characterize transcriptional alterations associated with RTT. Analysis of hippocampal nuclei identified major neuronal and glial populations, including the dentate gyrus neurogenic lineage. In the MECP2-deficient hippocampus, immature and mature granule neurons displayed the most pronounced abnormalities, whereas neural stem cells and neural progenitors exhibited relatively limited transcriptional changes. Differential expression and functional enrichment analyses revealed disruption of synaptic signaling, neuronal communication, and circuit organization pathways, accompanied by altered developmental programs. Co-expression network analysis identified maturation-associated modules and hub genes, including GABBR2, NRXN3, and NRG3. Astrocytes and microglia/macrophages also exhibited transcriptional alterations associated with metabolic, lipid-remodeling, phagocytic, and immune-related processes. Cross-species comparison with published Mecp2-mutant mouse dentate gyrus datasets identified a limited but biologically relevant set of shared transcriptional alterations, particularly among downregulated genes involved in synaptic and neuronal functions. These findings indicate that MECP2 deficiency preferentially alters maturation-associated transcriptional programs and synaptic network programs in granule neurons in the primate hippocampus and support partial conservation of abnormalities across rodent and primate RTT models.

titre: Timing matters: Maternal stress and mental health symptoms from pregnancy to postpartum in shaping infant development.
titre_fr: Timing matters: Maternal stress and mental health symptoms from pregnancy to postpartum in shaping infant development.
auteurs: Jarkas Dana A, Lalani Sharifa, Nausheen Sidrah, Babar Neelofur, Ghani Farooq, Islam Nazneen, Letourneau Nicole, Forcheh Ntonghanwah, Premji Shahirose S, McQuaid Robyn J
resume: Maternal perceived stress, mental health, and physiological dysregulation during pregnancy can alter the intrauterine environment, shaping infant development through fetal programming processes. Nonetheless, few longitudinal studies in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) have jointly examined psychological and biological factors in relation to infant outcomes. This longitudinal study followed 146 Pakistani mother-infant dyads at early to mid-gestation (T1), mid- to late gestation (T2), and postpartum (T3). Maternal perceived stress, depressive symptoms, and social support were measured across all timepoints, whereas pregnancy-related anxiety and an allostatic load index of physiological dysregulation were measured during pregnancy. Infant developmental outcomes across five domains were assessed using the Ages and Stages Questionnaire (ASQ-3). Perceived stress at each timepoint, depressive symptoms at T1 and T3, and allostatic load at T1 were associated with poorer infant fine motor skills. Perceived stress at T3 was linked to poorer infant problem solving. Communication, gross motor, and personal-social skills in infants showed no associations. Higher T3 social support attenuated the relationship between prenatal perceived stress and fine motor skills. Moreover, an exploratory interaction showed that T1 allostatic load related to lower fine motor skills when T3 stress is high. Psychological and biological pathways may link maternal prenatal risk to infant fine motor development, with the postpartum environment possibly influencing whether prenatal vulnerabilities translate into delays. Interventions strengthening social resources and reducing postpartum stress may help disrupt intergenerational stress transmission in LMICs.

titre: Odd- and branched-chain fatty acids in breast milk and neurodevelopment in early infancy: a prospective cohort study.
titre_fr: Odd- and branched-chain fatty acids in breast milk and neurodevelopment in early infancy: a prospective cohort study.
auteurs: Bi Yanrui, Xu Jian, Feng Yao, Song Lihua, Zhou Hong, Brenna J Thomas, Luo Zhong-Cheng, Gao Ying
resume: Odd-chain and branched-chain fatty acids (OCFAs and BCFAs; OBCFAs) have been linked to human microbiota and may influence neurodevelopment via microbiota-gut-brain axis. However, population-based evidence on OBCFAs and neurodevelopment is sparse. A prospective cohort of 120 healthy mother-infant pairs was studied. Breast milk samples were collected at 42 days and 8 months postpartum, with fatty acid profiles quantified using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. Infant neurodevelopment was assessed at 8 months of age using the Bayley Scales of Infant Development Third Edition, including cognitive and motor developmental quotients (DQs). Associations between OBCFAs and infant DQs were examined by linear regression. Infants' motor DQs were inversely associated with breast milk OCFAs levels at 42 days postpartum, including C15:0 (β = -4.27, P = 0.003), C17:0 (β = -4.67, P = 0.001), and total OCFAs (β = -5.07, P < 0.001), as well as total OBCFAs (β = -4.33, P = 0.002). Similar inverse associations were observed for infants' motor DQs and breast milk OBCFAs at 8 months postpartum (β = -5.37, P = 0.002), including C15:0 (β = -5.31, P = 0.002), C17:0 (β = -5.03, P = 0.004), total OCFAs (β = -5.49, P = 0.001), anteiso-C15:0 (β = -4.92, P = 0.005), and total BCFAs (β = -4.63, P = 0.008); all survived FDR correction (q < 0.05). Stronger inverse associations between OBCFAs and motor DQs were observed among infants born by cesarean delivery, infants with younger mothers (≤ 30y), and infants whose mothers had excessive gestational weight gain. Lower levels of breast milk OBCFAs were associated with better motor development in early infancy. Further research is needed to confirm and clarify the role of OBCFAs in neurodevelopmental programming. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR).

titre: Testing strategy for the identification of thyroid hormone system disrupting chemicals.
titre_fr: Testing strategy for the identification of thyroid hormone system disrupting chemicals.
auteurs: Axelstad Marta, Holmer Marie L, Ramhøj Louise, Wedebye Eva Bay, Scholze Martin, Köhrle Josef, Fini Jean-Baptiste, Meima Marcel, Svingen Terje, Hamers Timo
resume: Disruption of the thyroid hormone (TH) system during fetal and neonatal life poses a significant risk to human neurodevelopment, yet current regulatory assessments lack sufficiently sensitive and specific endpoints to identify chemicals causing TH system disruption (THSD). The ATHENA project aimed to develop an integrated framework combining in silico, in vitro, and in vivo approaches to improve the identification of substances causing THSD and support their assessment within a regulatory context. This testing strategy emphasizes increased use of the adverse outcome pathways (AOP) framework and read-across approaches to better predict and address adversity. It further provides recommendations for in silico and in vitro test batteries and targeted in vivo investigations to improve identification of chemicals causing THSD. In addition, we propose enhancements to current regulatory practice, including further standardization of test methods, improved integration of human epidemiological and cross-species evidence, and recognition of altered TH concentration in serum and brain in animal studies as predictors of adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in humans. Collectively, these measures are intended to strengthen chemical hazard assessment and improve protection of human and environmental health through more robust and efficient identification of THSD.

titre: Cognitive Functioning in Very Preterm Children and Links With Socio-Family Risk and Parenting.
titre_fr: Cognitive Functioning in Very Preterm Children and Links With Socio-Family Risk and Parenting.
auteurs: Sánchez-Sandoval Yolanda, Lacalle Laura, Lambrisca Agustina, Martínez-Shaw Melissa L, Ercegovac Ina Reić, Verdugo Laura
resume: Children born very preterm are at elevated risk of developing cognitive difficulties, yet the contribution of family and social factors to their neurodevelopment remains unclear. This cross-sectional study examines their cognitive performance relative to normative standards and uses an exploratory framework linking socio-family risk and intellectual functioning through potential indirect pathways via parenting styles. A sample of 135 children born before 32 weeks of gestation and/or very low birth weight (< 1500 g) (mean age = 8.67 years) was assessed using the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children-Fifth Edition (WISC-V). Socio-family risk was measured through a cumulative index, and parenting was evaluated using the Parenting Styles and Dimensions Questionnaire. Very preterm children showed significantly lower average scores across full-scale IQ (t(134) = -6.68, p < 0.001, d = -0.58) and all indices compared to the normative population. Fluid reasoning, working memory, and processing speed showed the greatest vulnerabilities. Mediation analyses suggested that an authoritative parenting style partially accounts for the association between socio-family risk and intellectual outcomes. These findings suggest that positive parenting was associated with better intellectual outcomes and support the potential value of family-centered interventions for very preterm children.

titre: Beyond monocular acuity: Resolving the amblyopia treatment paradox with mechanism-targeted outcomes and modern testing methods.
titre_fr: Beyond monocular acuity: Resolving the amblyopia treatment paradox with mechanism-targeted outcomes and modern testing methods.
auteurs: Gong Ling, Min Seung Hyun, Yu Xiaoning, Lou Lixia, Zhang Yidong, Sun Zhaohui, Tang Xiajing
revue: Advances in ophthalmology practice and research
resume: Amblyopia is a neurodevelopmental disorder affecting approximately 1%-5% of the population and has traditionally been treated based on reduced monocular visual acuity. However, growing evidence indicates that amblyopia involves broader deficits spanning low- and high-level visual processing, many of which persist even after successful acuity restoration and cannot be explained solely by acuity loss of the poor eye. Despite the expanded understanding and the development of binocular (dichoptic) therapies designed to rebalance interocular suppression, clinical trials over the past decade comparing binocular and occlusion therapies have remained largely focused on monocular visual acuity gains. Measures of binocular function were typically limited to coarse clinical stereoacuity tests, which lack the sensitivity needed to detect subtle yet meaningful functional improvements. This therapeutic paradox-targeting binocular mechanisms while evaluating outcomes mainly through monocular acuity-constrains our ability to properly assess emerging interventions. In this review, we summarize multilevel dysfunctions in amblyopia, evaluate outcome measures used in binocular therapy trials, and outline modern testing methods for rapid and clinically feasible assessment of binocular and higher-level visual functions. We also highlight the need for open-source tools, standardized protocols, and reproducible research practices to improve accessibility and cross-study comparability of different testing methods for evaluating multi-level impairments in amblyopia. Advances in the understanding of amblyopia and the development of mechanism-targeted binocular therapies require a corresponding shift in how treatment outcomes are evaluated. Reliance on monocular acuity alone is insufficient to capture the broader functional deficits and recovery processes associated with amblyopia. A flexible, mechanism-driven, and clinically feasible testing strategy using a battery of tests is needed to align outcome measures with therapeutic targets and to better evaluate functional recovery across multiple domains of visual processing.

titre: Regio-specific glycan expression within the mammalian brain and tumors.
titre_fr: Regio-specific glycan expression within the mammalian brain and tumors.
auteurs: Tulin Ea Kristine Clarisse, Noel Maxence, Pepi Lauren E, Florido Mary H, Muerner Lukas, Cielen Louie, von Gunten Stephan, Cummings Richard D
resume: The mammalian brain exhibits a complex glycan code that orchestrates neural connectivity, yet the spatial organization of functionally critical modifications of glycoproteins, such as fucosylation and sialylation, remains unclear. Using novel monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) designed for glycan detection, we mapped expression of glycan epitopes with unprecedented sensitivity, revealing non-overlapping expression patterns. Combined with targeted N-/O-glycan profiling, we found that expression of fucosylated and sialylated glycans occurs in anatomically distinct domains in both murine and human central nervous system (CNS). Key findings include fucosylated O-glycans marking brain endothelial cells, sialylated O-glycans decorating lecticans at the nodes of Ranvier, whereas the accessory olfactory bulb harbors unique fucosylated N-glycans. RNAseq and co-localization studies confirm regio-specific glycosyltransferase activity driving this partitioning. We also found that brain tumors are distinguished by upregulated expression of specific fucosylated/sialylated epitopes compared to normal tissue. The mAb-based approach uncovers regio-specific glycan expression with implications for neurodevelopment and cancer diagnostics.

titre: HNRNPH2-R114W remodels RNA splicing and neurodevelopmental gene programs in isogenic cerebral organoids.
titre_fr: HNRNPH2-R114W remodels RNA splicing and neurodevelopmental gene programs in isogenic cerebral organoids.
auteurs: Caiaffa Carlo Donato, Ghousifam Neda, Watkins Stephan Lloyd, Nakaya Helder I, Bowling Rodney A, Finnell Richard H, Cabrera Robert M
resume: Autism spectrum disorder has been linked to disrupted RNA processing during corticogenesis, yet variant-specific mechanisms remain difficult to resolve. Isogenic cerebral organoids derived from a patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) line carrying the HNRNPH2-R114W variant and its CRISPR-corrected counterpart serve as a human developmental model to investigate variant-associated RNA dysregulation. Imaging quantification and exploratory bulk RNA sequencing, performed at a single developmental time point on a pooled organoid RNA from each genotype, identify coordinated remodeling of neuronal and metabolic programs, along with junction-centered splicing dysregulation involving 6,310 differentially used junctions. Computational structural docking situates HNRNPH2 RNA recognition motifs (RRMs) 1-3 within a spliceosomal context and locates residue R114 near a predicted RNA-contact interface, indicating that the R114W substitution may alter RNA engagement. Integration of differential expression with event- and isoform-level analyses identifies regulatory hubs enriched for axon guidance and synaptic signaling pathways. Single-cell-reference-based deconvolution suggests modest compositional shifts that are unlikely to account for the extent of transcriptional and splicing alterations observed. Collectively, these findings imply HNRNPH2-R114W in widespread RNA rewiring and define candidate isoform-level endpoints for mechanistic and therapeutic investigation in human cortical organoids. These molecular signatures open new avenues to examine how HNRNPH2-associated RNA dysregulation evolves across developmental time and recurs across independent biological contexts, providing a foundation for further mechanistic studies of this rare neurodevelopmental disorder.

titre: Food allergy and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in children: evidence and implications for pediatric allergy practice.
titre_fr: Food allergy and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in children: evidence and implications for pediatric allergy practice.
auteurs: Lu Bingxue, Xie Yongmei
resume: Families of children with food allergies (FA) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) often ask whether the conditions are related and whether dietary changes could improve their children's attention or behavior. This narrative review examines FA-specific evidence and its implications for pediatric allergy practices, drawing on observational studies, reviews, clinical guidance, and contextual mechanistic research. One small FA-specific meta-analysis found no statistically significant association, whereas several individual observational studies reported positive associations. Differences in diagnostic definitions, reporting sources, temporal assessment, and confounder adjustment limited the ability to make comparisons. Studies of broader allergic phenotypes and Mendelian randomization provide no FA-specific causal estimate, and proposed microbiota-immune-brain pathways remain unconfirmed in humans. Restrictive or elimination diets should not be routinely recommended for ADHD because evidence of sustained benefit is limited, and additional restriction may compromise nutrition or worsen feeding difficulties, particularly in children already avoiding allergens. Pediatric allergy care should verify the FA diagnosis, preserve tolerated foods, monitor growth and dietary adequacy, and refer persistent attention or behavioral concerns for appropriate assessment. This review distinguishes direct FA evidence from broader allergy findings and relates these uncertainties to practical decisions about diagnosis, dietary restriction, and coordinated care.

titre: Recurrent Neurodevelopmental Disorder Associated With a Dominant-Negative TOP2B H63Y Variant.
titre_fr: Recurrent Neurodevelopmental Disorder Associated With a Dominant-Negative TOP2B H63Y Variant.
auteurs: Ha Zong Yi, Dinatto Leticia, Meagher Kirsten, Guimond Colleen, Friedman Jan M, Stirling Peter C, Patel Millan S
revue: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
resume: We describe a 7 year-old boy with severe neurodevelopmental disorder, medically-refractory epileptic encephalopathy, hyperkinetic movement disorder, hypotonia, cerebral and cerebellar atrophy and hypomyelination who was found to have a heterozygous de novo TOP2B NM_001330700.2:c.187C>T, p.(His63Tyr) variant. This is the third individual reported with the H63Y variant and severe neurodevelopmental disorder. The phenotype associated with the H63Y variant differs greatly from the TOP2B-related Immunodeficiency and Congenital Anomalies Spectrum (TICAS) syndrome that has been reported with heterozygous loss-of-function variants affecting the TOPRIM domain and adjacent regions of TOP2B. DNA topoisomerase II beta (TOP2B) is an essential enzyme that resolves DNA supercoils and knots to facilitate transcription and replication. To investigate the functional impact of this variant, we studied the homologous yeast variant, top2 H20Y (H20Y). Homozygous H20Y strains exhibited reduced viability, while heterozygous H20Y acted as a loss-of-function allele incapable of supporting growth. Overexpression of the chimeric human H63Y variant in yeast was lethal. Despite its dysfunction, H63Y retains partial enzymatic activity and appears to function as a dominant negative variant that induces DNA damage. Thus, this work establishes a novel gene-disease association between TOP2B-H63Y and a neurodevelopmental disorder we propose to name TOP2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder. Further studies should elucidate the pathogenic mechanisms underlying H63Y-associated phenotypes.

titre: Consistent unmet needs and fragmented care in Rett syndrome: insights from a multi-country European caregiver study.
titre_fr: Consistent unmet needs and fragmented care in Rett syndrome: insights from a multi-country European caregiver study.
auteurs: Pulles Tom, Jenner Becky, den Berg Mariëlle van, Rocha Pedro, Martini Angela De, Chamberlain Kees, Grandjean Harish
resume: Rett syndrome is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder associated with functional impairments that emerge in early childhood and persist throughout life. Despite improved understanding of its genetic basis and natural history, therapeutic options remain limited, and care frameworks across Europe are highly variable. This study aimed to characterize the lived experiences, unmet needs, and evolving challenges faced by individuals with Rett syndrome and their caregivers across multiple European countries. Sixty caregivers across eight countries completed five-day diaries, and thirty participated in in-depth interviews. The sample represented children (36%), adolescents (42%), and adults (22%) with Rett syndrome; 97% were female. Difficulty using hands (reported by 88% of caregivers) and difficulty communicating (78%) were the most frequently observed symptoms. Daily activities were heavily affected, with symptoms impacting 59% of activities for children, 61% for adolescents, and 38% for adults. Some comorbidities increased with age, including scoliosis (45% in children vs. 92% in adults) and pneumonia (54% in adults). Care demands were substantial, with caregivers of adults spending an average of 41 hours per week providing emotional support alone, along with high time requirements for feeding (20 hours), washing and bathing (8 hours), and administering medication (5 hours). Caregiver experiences across Europe reveal a consistent pattern of unmet needs, high symptom burden, and fragmented, poorly coordinated care for individuals with Rett syndrome. The changing needs across the lifespan underscore the importance of anticipatory, multidisciplinary care models and improved transition pathways into adulthood. As participants were recruited through patient advocacy groups, the study population may represent a comparatively informed and healthcare-engaged subgroup of caregivers, highlighting that unmet needs and care challenges across the broader RTT caregiver community may be even greater among families with less access to advocacy networks and specialized support resources. These findings highlight the need for system-level changes and the development of comprehensive, standardized care frameworks for Rett syndrome across Europe.

titre: Genotype and phenotype analyses of 689 individuals with PCDH19-clustering epilepsy.
titre_fr: Genotype and phenotype analyses of 689 individuals with PCDH19-clustering epilepsy.
auteurs: Grasso Kiara M, Corbett Mark A, Scheffer Ingrid E, Gecz Jozef
resume: PCDH19-clustering epilepsy (PCDH19-CE) is an infantile-onset neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by clusters of seizures, typically triggered by fever. PCDH19-CE follows an unusual X-linked inheritance pattern whereby heterozygous females, and males with X-chromosome disomy or pathogenic postzygotic mosaic PCDH19 variants, are affected, while hemizygous males are spared. We aggregate published PCDH19 variants and their corresponding PCDH19-CE phenotypes to analyse phenotype-genotype correlations. Data extracted from 110 publications identified 689/735 (94%) individuals with PCDH19 variants and the typical PCDH19-CE phenotype. Three hundred seventy-three unique PCDH19 variants were identified; 195 were not recorded in ClinVar. Seizure onset prior to 12 months of age was associated with more severe intellectual disability (p < 0.001) and the presence of psychiatric morbidity (p = 0.001). There were no phenotypic differences between missense, nonsense, and frameshift variants or between individuals of different geographical backgrounds, which was assessed as a proxy for ancestry. Twenty-nine hemizygous males with constitutive PCDH19 variants did not exhibit the typical PCDH19-CE phenotype, suggesting that the identification of variants in these individuals likely results from chance or ascertainment bias. The correlation between earlier seizure onset and poorer neurodevelopmental outcomes emphasises a critical window for therapeutic intervention. The lack of phenotypic difference between variant types demonstrates that loss of PCDH19 function underpins PCDH19-CE. Moreover, the identification of PCDH19 cytoplasmic domain variants in 78 affected individuals challenges the traditional view that PCDH19-CE is caused primarily by defects in cell-cell adhesion, as variants in this domain are expected to disrupt the nuclear function(s) of PCDH19.

titre: Examining the Relationship between Sluggish Cognitive Tempo and internalizing Symptoms in Attention Deficit Disorder with Hyperactivity Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Examining the Relationship between Sluggish Cognitive Tempo and internalizing Symptoms in Attention Deficit Disorder with Hyperactivity Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
auteurs: Yang Xinyu, Li Xiawei, Zhou Yu, Han Wenhao, Li Xin, Yan Fuli, Pang Wei, Gao Jing
resume: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder in children and adolescents, frequently comorbid with sluggish cognitive tempo (SCT) and internalizing symptoms (INT), with anxiety and depression as the core subtypes. Clarifying the relationship between SCT and INT in individuals with ADHD is essential for enhancing diagnostic and intervention strategies. Following the PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and CNKI for peer-reviewed observational studies published up to May 10, 2025. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed using Pearson's correlation coefficient (r) as the effect size measure. Subgroup analysis and meta-regression were conducted to explore sources of heterogeneity. The meta-analysis of nine studies (n = 1,767) revealed a significant, moderate positive correlation between SCT and INT (r = 0.426, 95% CI: 0.342, 0.503, P < 0.001), with substantial heterogeneity (I<sup>2</sup>= 77.5%). Subgroup analyses indicated a stronger correlation for self-reported INT (r = 0.436) compared to parent-reported INT (r = 0.387). The correlations between SCT and the core internalizing subdomains were both significant, with a pooled correlation of r = 0.397. Age, sex, or sample size did not significantly moderate the heterogeneity. Heterogeneity remained partly unexplained, likely due to differences in internalizing symptom instruments, informant sources, and sampling frames across studies. SCT is consistently associated with higher levels of internalizing symptoms in youth with ADHD, particularly when assessed via self-report. These findings support the integration of SCT screening within ADHD evaluations and underscore the importance of multi-informant assessment to improve identification and management of co-occurring internalizing problems.

titre: Case Report: Prenatal and postnatal clinical manifestations of 15q duplication syndrome: a single longitudinal case combined with pooled analysis of 35 prenatal cases.
titre_fr: Case Report: Prenatal and postnatal clinical manifestations of 15q duplication syndrome: a single longitudinal case combined with pooled analysis of 35 prenatal cases.
auteurs: Xu Ziqing, Ufei Mou, Chen Hongbo, Yang Shuo, Zou Peijun, Lu You, Xiong Fei, Li Jinrong
resume: 15q duplication (Dup15q) syndrome is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by early-onset hypotonia, developmental delay, intellectual disability, symptoms related to autism spectrum disorder and epilepsy. In the absence of specific treatment, prenatal diagnosis is of important clinical significance. However, most reported cases are postnatal cases, whereas prenatal cases are limited and often lack detailed clinical information, making prenatal recognition of this disorder challenging. In this study, we integrated prenatal and postnatal clinical information from the present case with a pooled analysis of published prenatal Dup15q syndrome cases, providing additional insights into the prenatal-to-postnatal phenotypic spectrum of Dup15q syndrome. We report a case of Dup15q syndrome with both prenatal and postnatal clinical data. Although prenatal ultrasound showed polyhydramnios, an abdominal circumference below the 10th percentile, and mild tricuspid regurgitation, no further prenatal genetic testing was performed. After birth, the patient presented with early hypotonia and developmental delay, and the diagnosis was established by genetic testing after a poor response to rehabilitation. We collected 34 prenatal Dup15q syndrome cases through literature review. The results showed that non-invasive prenatal screening (NIPS) may facilitate the prenatal identification of Dup15q syndrome. Prenatal ultrasound findings included polyhydramnios, fetal growth restriction (FGR), cardiac abnormalities, dysmorphic features, and abnormal ultrasound soft markers. The pooled analysis further provided an overview of the prenatal phenotypic spectrum of Dup15q syndrome and suggested that FGR and polyhydramnios, particularly in the presence of additional ultrasound abnormalities, positive NIPS results, or a positive family history, may warrant further etiological evaluation. Dup15q syndrome exhibits prominent clinical heterogeneity with nonspecific prenatal manifestations, predisposing patients to missed or delayed diagnosis. By integrating prenatal and postnatal clinical information with pooled prenatal cases, this study provides a broader understanding of the phenotypic spectrum of Dup15q syndrome and may facilitate prenatal counseling and early clinical recognition.

titre: Oxytocin receptor agonist improves social deficits by regulating hippocampal neural plasticity in Shank3 knockout mice.
titre_fr: Oxytocin receptor agonist improves social deficits by regulating hippocampal neural plasticity in Shank3 knockout mice.
auteurs: Wang Yunlei, Cheng Lingna, Li Xingzhu, Bai Chen, Jin Tianyu, Du Xiaoxia, Zhang Tong
resume: Autism spectrum disorder is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder lacking effective pharmacological agents targeting core socialbehavioral symptoms. Oxytocin receptor represents a promising therapeutic target, yet the clinical benefits of exogenous oxytocin remain limited and inconsistent. This study used Shank3 knockout mice as a model of autism spectrum disorder to evaluate the efficacy of Lit001, a selective oxytocin receptor agonist, in ameliorating social deficits and to investigate its underlying mechanisms. Wild-type (normal) and homozygous Shank3 knockout mice were assigned to six experimental groups treated with single-dose or repeated Lit001 administration, with an additional oxytocin receptor antagonist co-administration group included for pharmacological reversal validation. We found that Lit001 exerted neuroprotective effects in the hippocampus, attenuated pathological microglial activation, increased hippocampal acetylcholine receptor and dopamine receptor D2 expression, restored dendritic spine and nerve fiber integrity, and reversed transcriptional abnormalities associated with synaptic transmission and energy metabolism. Pretreatment with an oxytocin receptor antagonist abolished these therapeutic effects. Social motivation improved rapidly after short-term treatment but diminished within one month, whereas social novelty preference exhibited a delayed yet sustained improvement. Transcriptomic analysis further demonstrated that oxytocin receptor blockade reversed Lit001-induced transcriptional remodeling. Patch-clamp recordings confirmed that Lit001 increased the frequency of spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic currents. Distinct from exogenous oxytocin, Lit001 selectively activates oxytocin receptors without altering peripheral oxytocin levels. The selective oxytocin receptor agonist Lit001 ameliorates core social deficits in Shank3 knockout mice, potentially through oxytocin receptor-dependent neural regeneration and remodeling of hippocampal neural plasticity.

titre: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Treatment Pattern and Its Associated Outcomes Among Children Referred to Psychiatry and Mental Health Services in Malaysia: Protocol for a Retrospective Cohort Study.
titre_fr: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Treatment Pattern and Its Associated Outcomes Among Children Referred to Psychiatry and Mental Health Services in Malaysia: Protocol for a Retrospective Cohort Study.
auteurs: Muhamad Nor Asiah, Ling Ling Shiao, Maamor Nur Hasnah, Hussin Suria, Tengku Baharudin Shah Tengku Puteri Nadiah, Jamalluddin Nurul Hidayah, Leman Fatin Norhasny, Musa Nurul Syarbani Eliana, Yahya Fariza, Chemi Norliza, Abdullah Norni, Abdul Jabbar Norli, Ibrahim Nurashikin
resume: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder associated with significant impairments in academic, social, and daily functioning. Despite the availability of clinical practice guidelines in Malaysia, evidence on real-world treatment patterns and outcomes remains limited. The lack of multicenter data on treatment use and clinical outcomes hinders the evaluation of current ADHD care and opportunities for service improvement. The primary objective of this study is to observe treatment patterns among children with ADHD referred to psychiatry and mental health services in Malaysia after receiving treatment for 18 months. This study will also compare treatment outcomes between children with ADHD who do receive treatment and those who do not receive any ADHD treatment. This multicenter retrospective cohort study will use secondary data from clinical records of children aged 4 to 16 years with a confirmed diagnosis of ADHD. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, clinical features, ADHD subtype and comorbidities, treatment modalities, health care use, treatment trajectories, and clinical outcomes will be extracted using a standardized case report form and will be anonymized prior to analysis. Data collection will be undertaken by trained site investigators and medical officers across participating centers. Statistical analyses will be conducted using R software (R Foundation for Statistical Computing). Descriptive statistics will be used to summarize characteristics, treatment patterns, health care use, and clinical outcomes of children with ADHD. Treatment patterns will be characterized according to pharmacological and nonpharmacological interventions, treatment modifications, and service use. Comparative analyses will be performed to examine associations between treatment patterns and clinical outcomes across children with ADHD and clinical subgroups. This study will be funded through a Ministry of Health Research Grant obtained in August 2026. It will commence in August 2026 and end in December 2028. Based on the sample size calculation, a minimum of 2771 eligible children with ADHD records will be included in the study. The study will be reported in accordance with the STROBE (Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology) guidelines for retrospective cohort studies. The findings will be disseminated through presentations and article publications at the national and international levels. This study will address a critical evidence gap in ADHD care by providing comprehensive real-world data on treatment patterns and outcomes among Malaysian children with ADHD. Findings will identify variations in treatment approaches, treatment trajectories, and clinical outcomes across hospitals and regions, assess the alignment of real-world practice with national recommendations, and highlight potential disparities in access to ADHD specialist services. The findings are expected to support evidence-based clinical decision-making, guide strategic health care planning, optimize resource use, and contribute to the development of a more coordinated, efficient, and equitable system of ADHD care across diverse health care settings in Malaysia.

titre: Whether substituting high-fat dairy with low-fat dairy changes the risk of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder: A case-control study.
titre_fr: Whether substituting high-fat dairy with low-fat dairy changes the risk of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder: A case-control study.
auteurs: Keyhanpour Shayesteh, Shams Fatemeh, Najarian Maryam, Abbasi Khadijeh, Ghiasvand Reza, Rouhani Mohammad Hossein
resume: BackgroundAttention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder in children, with potential influences from modifiable dietary factors. Evidence on the differential effects of low-fat and high-fat dairy on ADHD risk is limited.AimTo examine associations between total, low-fat, and high-fat dairy intake and ADHD risk, and to assess the impact of substituting high-fat dairy with low-fat dairy in children.MethodsA case-control study was conducted on 150 Iranian children aged 4-12 years, including 62 with ADHD and 88 controls. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire. Logistic regression was used to examine the association between dairy intake and ADHD risk, adjusting for energy intake, body mass index, age, sex, and socioeconomic status. Substitution analysis evaluated the effect of replacing 1 g/day of high-fat dairy with low-fat dairy.SummaryChildren with ADHD consumed significantly less total and low-fat dairy than controls, whereas high-fat dairy intake did not differ significantly between groups. Higher total and low-fat dairy intakes were inversely associated with ADHD risk (odds ratio (OR) = 0.974 and 0.970, respectively; both P < 0.001). High-fat dairy intake was not significantly associated with ADHD risk after full adjustment. Substituting 1 g/day of high-fat dairy with low-fat dairy was associated with lower odds of ADHD (OR = 0.981; P = 0.029). These findings suggest that greater consumption of total and low-fat dairy, as well as replacing high-fat with low-fat dairy, may be associated with lower ADHD risk in children.

titre: Beyond seizures: the hidden burden of developmental epileptic encephalopathies.
titre_fr: Beyond seizures: the hidden burden of developmental epileptic encephalopathies.
auteurs: Dell'Isola Giovanni Battista, Sorrentino Michele, Massara Sara, Dini Gianluca, Salpietro Vincenzo, Ferrara Pietro, Striano Pasquale, Vigevano Federico, Verrotti Alberto
resume: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) are a group of severe childhood-onset disorders characterized by drug-resistant epilepsy and a broad spectrum of neurodevelopmental, behavioral, psychiatric, and systemic manifestations. Although seizure control has traditionally been the primary therapeutic goal, growing evidence indicates that non-seizure manifestations often represent the main determinants of long-term disability, quality of life, and caregiver burden. This review highlights the hidden burden of DEEs by focusing on three paradigmatic syndromes: Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS), Dravet syndrome (DS), and tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC). DS and LGS represent prototypical DEEs, whereas TSC is a multisystem genetic disorder that is frequently, although not invariably, associated with early-onset drug-resistant epilepsy and DEE-like neurodevelopmental trajectories. Across these conditions, the severity and progression of clinical manifestations are influenced by complex interactions between genetic, structural, developmental, and epileptic mechanisms, supporting the concept that epilepsy and associated manifestations represent interconnected features of a broader neurodevelopmental disorder. The review also emphasizes the substantial psychosocial, physical, and economic burden experienced by families and caregivers, which often exceeds the impact of seizures alone. Current management strategies should therefore extend beyond seizure reduction and adopt a multidisciplinary, life-course approach integrating early genetic diagnosis, syndrome-specific surveillance, developmental interventions, rehabilitation, behavioral support, and coordinated multidisciplinary care. Future research should prioritize disease-modifying therapies and personalized strategies aimed at addressing both epileptic and non-epileptic manifestations, ultimately improving functional outcomes and quality of life for individuals with DEEs and their families.

titre: A novel LARP7 variant expands the phenotypic spectrum of Alazami syndrome and reveals transcriptomic dysregulation of developmental and extracellular matrix pathways.
titre_fr: A novel LARP7 variant expands the phenotypic spectrum of Alazami syndrome and reveals transcriptomic dysregulation of developmental and extracellular matrix pathways.
auteurs: Hassan Mozan, Irshaid Manal, Batool Aalia, Aldhaheri Wadima, Qehaizel Latifa Ba, Alzaabi Shamma, Alnuaimi Shamma, Saeed Sara, Al Jasmi Fatma, Akawi Nadia
revue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
resume: LARP7 encodes a critical scaffold protein of the 7SK small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (7SK snRNP) complex that regulates RNA polymerase II transcriptional elongation. Biallelic loss-of-function variants in LARP7 cause Alazami syndrome, a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, growth restriction, and distinctive craniofacial features. However, the transcriptomic consequences of LARP7 deficiency in human cells remain poorly understood, and the phenotypic spectrum of the disorder is incompletely defined. We investigated a 6-year-old boy with clinically diagnosed Alazami syndrome who carried a novel homozygous LARP7 frameshift variant. Clinical evaluation and exome sequencing of blood-derived genomic DNA were performed, while quantitative PCR, Western blotting, and transcriptomic analysis were conducted using patient-derived dermal fibroblasts. Transcriptomic consequences of LARP7 deficiency were assessed by RNA sequencing, followed by single-subject differential expression, pathway enrichment, and network analyses. The patient presented with classical features of Alazami syndrome and tetralogy of Fallot, a cardiac manifestation not previously reported in the disorder. The novel homozygous LARP7 frameshift variant resulted in marked depletion of LARP7 transcripts and complete loss of full-length protein. Transcriptome-wide analysis identified 1,224 dysregulated genes involved in extracellular matrix organization, developmental remodeling, cell-cycle regulation, and immune signaling. Pathway and network analyses highlighted dysregulation of STAT3-associated signaling together with SMAD3-linked extracellular matrix and developmental programs, identifying candidate developmental and tissue-remodeling pathways that warrant further investigation in disease-relevant models. This study provides the first comprehensive transcriptomic characterization of genetically confirmed LARP7 deficiency in primary human cells and potentially expands the phenotypic spectrum of Alazami syndrome. The findings reveal widespread dysregulation of developmental and extracellular matrix pathways, offering new insight into the molecular basis of the multisystem manifestations of Alazami syndrome and providing a framework for future functional and genotype-phenotype studies.

titre: Perinatal elimination of genetically aberrant human cortical neurons.
titre_fr: Perinatal elimination of genetically aberrant human cortical neurons.
auteurs: Shao Diane D, Zhao Yifan, Brew Joseph, Adla Yahia, Ghosh Urmi, Viswanadham Vinayak V, Luquette Lovelace J, Zhao Sijing, Kriz Andrea J, Qian Xuyu, Taketomi Takumi, Coy Shannon, Santagata Sandro, Miller Michael, Tsuruta Fuminori, Park Peter J, Walsh Christopher A
resume: Human neurons are postmitotic and long-lived, requiring precise genomic regulation. Normal neuronal function is highly dosage-sensitive, with copy number variants (CNVs) and heterozygous point mutations associated with a host of neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric conditions<sup>1-4</sup>. Here we investigated somatic CNVs arising in single neurons to understand the dynamic processes that shape the normal neuronal genetic landscape. Altogether, we sequenced 2,357 single neurons from human postmortem brain from fetal to postnatal life. Two single-cell whole-genome sequencing approaches-Tn5-transposase-based amplification (1,526 neurons, 16 individuals) and primary template amplification<sup>5</sup> (831 neurons, 12 individuals)-showed that an average of 25.9% [12.7-46%] of prenatal cortical neurons have highly aberrant genomes, that is, widespread CNVs involving multiple chromosomes. This proportion reduced by about 4.5-fold after birth across the two single-cell whole-genome sequencing approaches (Fisher meta-analysis P = 3.5 × 10<sup>-</sup><sup>6</sup>). Neurons with widespread CNVs were mainly eliminated perinatally, timed roughly parallel to periods of programmed cell death<sup>6</sup>, whereas neurons with smaller CNV burdens declined slowly in frequency with postnatal age. CNVs in surviving neurons were depleted for dosage-sensitive genes and genes involved in neurodevelopmental disorders (hypergeometric test P < 0.05), suggesting selective elimination of neurons with these CNVs. Analysis of 44,861 nuclei with single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (snATAC) and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) showed that neurons with high CNV burdens exhibited abnormal synaptic gene expression, suggesting that abnormal synaptic gene regulation contributes to neuronal elimination. Elimination of defective neuronal genomes might represent an important developmental genome quality-control process that may be vulnerable in neurodevelopmental disease, and suggests purifying selection during human neurodevelopment.

titre: Exploring the neural correlates of mental health: associations between cortical folding and mental health problems in youth with prenatal alcohol exposure.
titre_fr: Exploring the neural correlates of mental health: associations between cortical folding and mental health problems in youth with prenatal alcohol exposure.
auteurs: Scholten Chloe, Gilchrist Courtney, Geeraert Bryce, McMorris Carly A, Gibbard W Ben, Pei Jacqueline, Beaulieu Christian, Landman Bennett A, Tortorelli Christina, Lebel Catherine
resume: Prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) can alter neurodevelopment and cause health and behavioral effects. Mental health challenges disproportionately affect individuals with PAE and are related to brain alterations. Cortical folding (gyrification) is associated with mental health in clinical populations and may help understand mental health difficulties in individuals with PAE. 161 datasets from 125 youth (57 PAE, 59 females) aged 7-21 years were included. T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging and the caregiver-report Behavior Assessment System for Children were collected at baseline and 2-year follow-up. Images were processed to extract local gyrification index (LGI) from 20 mental health-related regions. Linear mixed-effects models were used to test the effect of PAE on associations between LGI and mental health symptoms. Youth with PAE had more Externalizing Problems (60.7 ± 15.5) than unexposed youth (54.8 ± 11.1; p < 0.001). PAE moderated the relationship between Internalizing Problems and LGI in the left posterior orbital gyrus and the left subcallosal area, and between Externalizing Problems and LGI in the right frontal pole and left subcallosal area. Higher LGI was associated with higher Internalizing and Externalizing Problems in participants with PAE; this association was weaker or absent in unexposed youth. This indicates a potential neurobiological basis for mental health challenges in individuals with PAE.
