titre: Thyroid function characteristics and early growth and neurodevelopmental outcomes in NICU preterm infants: A retrospective cohort study.
titre_fr: Thyroid function characteristics and early growth and neurodevelopmental outcomes in NICU preterm infants: A retrospective cohort study.
auteurs: Li Guanming, Zhang Airun, Li Jiahong, Yu Chaonan, Li Miao, Fang Xiaoyi
resume: To investigate thyroid function characteristics in preterm infants during early life, identify risk factors for thyroid dysfunction, and analyze associations with physical growth and neurodevelopmental outcomes. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using clinical data from preterm infants admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2024. Thyroid function parameters within the first month were analyzed. Logistic regression was performed to identify risk factors for thyroid dysfunction. Physical growth and neurodevelopmental outcomes within 12 months were compared between infants with and without thyroid dysfunction using generalized estimating equations (GEE). The overall incidence of thyroid dysfunction was 59.7% (288/482). The incidence increased with decreasing GA, reaching 95% in those <30 weeks. GA was an independent risk factor, with each one-week increase associated with a 30.2% reduction in risk (OR = 0.698, 95% CI 0.568-0.859). Iodine exposure (OR = 2.572, 95% CI 1.046-6.326) was another independent risk factor. No significant group × time interactions were observed for physical growth (all P > 0.05). For neurodevelopment, significant group × time interactions emerged at 6 months (OR = 2.89, P = 0.020) and 12 months (OR = 4.05, P = 0.003), with the euthyroid group showing decreasing risk and the thyroid dysfunction group showing increasing risk; hyperthyrotropinemia, CH, and low T3 syndrome drove this association. Among infants with thyroid dysfunction, no significant differences were observed between LT4-treated and untreated infants in weight, head circumference, or neurodevelopmental outcomes, except for a modest treatment × time interaction for length at 12 months (β = 0.627, P = 0.034). However, these findings are limited by the single-center, retrospective design. Thyroid dysfunction was common in NICU preterm infants, driven primarily by small GA and iodine exposure. It is associated with divergent neurodevelopmental trajectories over time, particularly in hyperthyrotropinemia, CH, and low T3 syndrome, but not with physical growth. LT4 treatment did not demonstrate clear benefits.

titre: Restricted and Repetitive Behavior Subtypes Show Distinct Associations with Adaptive Functioning in Autistic Children.
titre_fr: Restricted and Repetitive Behavior Subtypes Show Distinct Associations with Adaptive Functioning in Autistic Children.
auteurs: Rozenblat Shir, Lapidot Rotem, Zachor Ditza A, Avni Einat, Zait Anat Zaidman, Koller Judah
resume: Restricted and repetitive behaviors (RRBs) are a core feature of autism spectrum disorder, yet their distinct impacts on adaptive functioning remain unclear. Adaptive functioning, including communication, socialization, and daily living skills, is critical for quality of life in autistic children. Here we performed exploratory factor analysis of the Repetitive Behavior Scale-Revised in 167 autistic children aged 3-12 years, identifying three RRB subtypes: sameness/ritualistic/restricted behaviors, stereotypic/self-injurious behaviors, and compulsive behaviors. In primary models adjusting for age and sex, sameness/ritualistic/restricted behaviors predicted lower socialization, whereas stereotypic/self-injurious behaviors predicted lower communication and daily living skills. In a sensitivity analysis additionally adjusting for IQ, in the subset of children with available cognitive data, only sameness/ritualistic/restricted behaviors remained a significant predictor across all three domains. These findings suggest that not all RRB subtypes are equally associated with adaptive functioning, underscoring the need to differentiate RRBs when designing interventions. Understanding subtype-specific associations may guide strategies that address behaviors hindering adaptive outcomes while considering those with potential regulatory functions.

titre: Gender Diversity in Pediatric Chronic Orthostatic Intolerance: Mental Health and Quality-of-Life Outcomes.
titre_fr: Gender Diversity in Pediatric Chronic Orthostatic Intolerance: Mental Health and Quality-of-Life Outcomes.
auteurs: Frye William S, Mauriello Daniel, Mitchell Brooke, Greenberg Brooke, King Callie K
resume: This retrospective medical record review examined the proportion of transgender and gender-diverse (TGD) youth within a multidisciplinary pediatric autonomic dysfunction clinic specializing in chronic orthostatic intolerance, compared quality-of-life (QoL) scores between TGD and cisgender youth, and identified opportunities to improve health equity in nonpharmacological recommendations. Data on gender identity, mental health conditions, and QoL scores, were collected over 2 years. Among 145 youth, 6.9% identified as TGD, a proportion higher than population estimates. Transgender and gender-diverse youth had a significantly lower total QoL, with lower scores in social and emotional domains, and demonstrated higher rates of depression and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder; all TGD youth had an anxiety diagnosis. Overall, TGD youth demonstrated more frequent mental health concerns and greater QoL impairments than cisgender peers. Future studies are needed to determine specific mental health needs and if individualized treatment plans or adaptations to standard nonpharmacological recommendations improve outcomes in TGD youth.
resume_fr: This retrospective medical record review examined the proportion of transgender and gender-diverse (TGD) youth within a multidisciplinary pediatric autonomic dysfunction clinic specializing in chronic orthostatic intolerance, compared quality-of-life (QoL) scores between TGD and cisgender youth, and identified opportunities to improve health equity in nonpharmacological recommendations. Data on gender identity, mental health conditions, and QoL scores, were collected over 2 years. Among 145 youth, 6.9% identified as TGD, a proportion higher than population estimates. Transgender and gender-diverse youth had a significantly lower total QoL, with lower scores in social and emotional domains, and demonstrated higher rates of depression and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder; all TGD youth had an anxiety diagnosis. Overall, TGD youth demonstrated more frequent mental health concerns and greater QoL impairments than cisgender peers. Future studies are needed to determine specific mental health needs and if individualized treatment plans or adaptations to standard nonpharmacological recommendations improve outcomes in TGD youth.

titre: Parenting Children With Externalizing Disorders: A Qualitative Study From South India.
titre_fr: Parenting Children With Externalizing Disorders: A Qualitative Study From South India.
auteurs: Dutta Dyuti, Saravanan Vaishalee, Aroor Shrikiran
resume: AimsExternalizing disorders are one of the most prevalent childhood disorders. This study aimed to understand the experiences of parents of children with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD), and Conduct Disorder (CD) in the Indian context, with an equal representation of both fathers and mothers.MethodA qualitative exploratory design was utilized. 6 mothers and 5 fathers of children diagnosed with either ADHD, ODD, or CD were recruited using purposive sampling from the Department of Paediatrics and the Department of Clinical Psychology of a private hospital in India. The interviews followed a semi-structured schedule and were analyzed using thematic analysis.ResultsSix main themes were identified: child's behavior and emotional responsiveness, parental strain, imbalanced roles in the parental dyad, societal perceptions, reflective coping in parents, and parental concerns for the future. Parenting children with externalizing disorders was reported to be challenging, with most mothers facing an unequal burden. Children's need for screentime was an emerging concern.ImplicationsThe study implies the significant need to adapt interventions for Indian parents, keeping in mind cultural beliefs, while also ensuring adequate involvement of fathers in the treatment process. Regulation of screentime could be an additional target of intervention.

titre: Efficacy and safety of pharmacologic therapies for irritability in pediatric autism spectrum disorder: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
titre_fr: Efficacy and safety of pharmacologic therapies for irritability in pediatric autism spectrum disorder: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
auteurs: Wang Zuojun, Fang Liwei, Wang Shunxin, Zhao Jingyi, Zhang Qiannuo, Zou Xinyu, Wu De
resume: Irritability is a common and clinically significant feature of pediatric autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) to compare and rank pharmacological interventions for irritability in this population. Multiple databases were searched up to September 1, 2025, for randomized controlled trials enrolling pediatric ASD with significant irritability. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2.0, and confidence in network estimates was evaluated with Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis. Pairwise meta-analyses, subgroup analyses, and frequentist NMA were performed for efficacy and safety outcomes. Forty-three RCTs involving 2711 participants, evaluating 35 drugs across 41 regimens, were included. Traditional pairwise meta-analysis suggested that pharmacotherapy improved irritability more than placebo, with greater effects in younger children (<12 years) and shorter trials (⩽8 weeks). In the NMA, risperidone (Ris; MD = 8.81, 95% CI: 6.01-11.61) and aripiprazole (MD = 5.53, 95% CI: 2.61-8.45) led to larger reductions in ABC-I scores compared with placebo, showing the highest probability among monotherapies (surface under the cumulative ranking curve: 98% and 85%). Among Ris combination regimens, the most favorable effect was observed for the addition of topiramate, with an MD of 7.55 (95% CI: 5.89-9.21) relative to Ris + placebo. In terms of safety, pharmacotherapy was associated with an absolute adverse events (AEs) risk increase of 0.08 versus placebo, with no severe events reported. Ris and aripiprazole had the highest ranking probabilities among monotherapies, and topiramate was the most promising Ris adjunct in the NMA. Pharmacotherapy carried a slightly elevated AE risk, with no severe events. However, rankings should be interpreted cautiously because most comparisons were indirect. Large high-quality head-to-head trials are needed to confirm comparative efficacy and long-term safety.

titre: The Cognitive Functions of Youth With Obesity: A Meta-Analysis.
titre_fr: The Cognitive Functions of Youth With Obesity: A Meta-Analysis.
auteurs: Lin Yi-Chun, Chang Chia-Chia, Chang Yu-Tzu, Liu Wei-Lin, Liao Yu-Chi, Lin Ro-Ting
resume: This meta-analysis examined the associations between obesity and performance across seven cognitive domains (inhibition, cognitive flexibility, working memory, verbal fluency, planning, attention, and intelligence quotient [IQ]) in youth under 18 years. Developmental stage (school-aged children vs. adolescents) and sample sex composition examined as moderators. Evidence on executive function in youth with comorbid obesity and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) was synthesized qualitatively. Following PRISMA guidelines, 22 studies comparing youth with obesity to normal-weight peers were included. Effect sizes (Hedges' g) were pooled using a random-effects model. Subgroup analyses compared school-aged children and adolescents; meta-regression examined age and proportion of female participants as study-level moderators. Youth with obesity performed significantly worse than normal-weight peers on inhibition (g<sup>+</sup> = -0.193), cognitive flexibility (g<sup>+</sup> = -0.499), working memory (g<sup>+</sup> = -0.652), verbal fluency (g<sup>+</sup> = -0.420), attention (g<sup>+</sup> = -0.526), and IQ (g<sup>+</sup> = -0.288); planning could not be estimated. School-aged children showed deficits on inhibition, working memory, and attention; adolescents on working memory and attention only. Between-subgroup tests were non-significant for all domains (p ≥ 0.26), so developmental differences should be interpreted with caution. Meta-regression showed that a higher proportion of female participants in a study sample, a study-level characteristic rather than an individual-level effect, was associated with larger working memory deficits (p = 0.002); age did not moderate any domain. Two ADHD-comorbidity studies received qualitative synthesis only. Obesity is associated with poorer cognitive performance in youth across several domains, with sex composition of the study sample emerging as a moderator of the working memory finding; differences between school-aged children and adolescents were not significant and should be interpreted cautiously. Substantial heterogeneity, predominantly observational designs, inconsistent BMI criteria, and limited ADHD-stratified data constrain causal inference. Future studies should standardize weight definitions, report age- and ADHD-stratified data, and consider bidirectional pathways.

titre: Parents' Diagnostic Resolution and Activation: Examining a Mediation Model on Emotional and Behavioral Outcomes in Autistic Children and Adolescents.
titre_fr: Parents' Diagnostic Resolution and Activation: Examining a Mediation Model on Emotional and Behavioral Outcomes in Autistic Children and Adolescents.
auteurs: Fatta Laura Maria, Di Tata Daniele, Bianchi Dora, Lonigro Antonia, Laghi Fiorenzo
resume: A diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder poses significant emotional and practical challenges for parents. Although diagnostic resolution and parent activation have been examined separately, little is known about whether parents' psychological adjustment relates to active caregiving and, in turn, to child outcomes. This study tested: (1) a mediation model linking diagnostic resolution to child emotional-behavioral difficulties through parent activation; (2) psychometric properties of the Italian Parent Activation Measure for Developmental Disabilities (PAM-DD). We hypothesized that diagnostic resolution would be indirectly associated with lower levels of children's emotional-behavioral difficulties through higher parent activation. Participants were 179 parents (87.7% mothers; Mage = 43.91; SD = 5.63) of autistic children aged 6-13 years (81.6% boys; Mage = 9.50; SD = 2.32). Diagnostic resolution was operationalized as a reliable reduction in negative emotional responses, and child difficulties were assessed using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ). Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) examined PAM-DD structure, and path analysis tested the mediation model, controlling for child age and time since diagnosis. CFA supported a two-factor model (activated and passive dimensions) with acceptable fit (CFI = .92, TLI = .90, RMSEA = .06, 90% CI [.05, .08], SRMR = .07). Resolution was associated only with the activated dimension (β = .19, p < .05), which was negatively related to children's emotional-behavioral difficulties (β = -.25, p < .01). Findings suggest that psychological integration of the diagnosis may foster action-oriented parental engagement, which is linked to fewer child emotional-behavioral difficulties, highlighting parent activation as a potential intervention target.

titre: Evaluation of a novel unstructured performance measure of executive functioning for university students.
titre_fr: Evaluation of a novel unstructured performance measure of executive functioning for university students.
auteurs: Rand Bailey M, Hussain Sarah, Miller Carlin J
revue: Journal of clinical and experimental neuropsychology
resume: Executive functions (EFs) are higher order cognitive skills implicated in various neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders, including ADHD. Yet, there is a range of strategies for measuring EFs, with commonly used objective performance-based measures and subjective rating scales often yielding weak associations. This discrepancy may reflect objective measures relying on highly structured test administration procedures and rating scales' greater ability to capture self-direction, everyday functioning, and emotional aspects of EF. The present study evaluated the concurrent validity of a novel unstructured performance task (UPT) designed to assess self-direction in university students. One hundred twenty-one university students were included in the study. Performance was compared across the UPT and commonly used EF objective measures and rating scales. The relations between each EF measure and mood symptoms were also assessed. Scores on the UPT were correlated with the performance measures (p < .05), though neither were correlated with the rating scale (p > .05). Unlike performance measure and rating scale scores, the UPT was unaffected by mood symptoms (p > .05). No evidence was found suggesting that the UPT better captures self-direction compared with traditional performance measures. However, the UPT may provide an alternative, unstructured EF measure that is relatively less related to mood symptoms.   .

titre: Limited Evidence for Non-Invasive Brain Stimulation as a Cognitive Enhancer in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Multilevel Meta-Analysis of Sham-Controlled Trials.
titre_fr: Limited Evidence for Non-Invasive Brain Stimulation as a Cognitive Enhancer in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Multilevel Meta-Analysis of Sham-Controlled Trials.
auteurs: Ying Jiangbo, Desarkar Pushpal, Rodak Terri, Yu Veronica Yan Kiu, Liang Vivian, Sie Joanna, Ameis Stephanie H, Rajji Tarek K, Ni Hsing-Chang, Lin Hsiang-Yuan
resume: Non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) is increasingly applied to ameliorate cognitive deficits in neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and intellectual disability, yet whether standardized scalp-based protocols produce reliable cognitive enhancement remains untested at scale. This study evaluates the transdiagnostic efficacy of NIBS on shared, non-core cognitive domains across NDDs, searching MEDLINE, PsycINFO, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from inception to January 2026. A three-level multivariate random-effects meta-analysis synthesized effect sizes while accounting for dependency among multiple outcomes contributed by the same study. From 9191 identified records (5237 after deduplication), 30 randomized sham-controlled trials yielding 178 effect sizes across seven cognitive domains were synthesized. NIBS did not significantly outperform sham for any domain: working memory (k=24; g=-0.16, 95% CI [-0.37, 0.05]), cognitive flexibility (k=11; g=-0.12 [-0.38, 0.13]), global executive function (k=8; g=-0.14 [-0.46, 0.18]), processing speed (k=8; g=-0.27 [-0.77, 0.23]), inhibitory control (k=4; g=-0.08 [-0.62, 0.46]), verbal fluency (k=5; g=-0.11 [-0.59, 0.38]), or self-monitoring/behavioral metacognition (k=4; g=0.13 [-0.60, 0.86]). The pooled cross-domain estimate reached nominal significance (g=-0.18, p=0.035) but fell below the small-effect threshold, and its wide prediction interval (95% PI [-1.01, 0.66]) spanned benefit and harm. Exploratory diagnosis-stratified analyses were likewise null in both ADHD and ASD (all p>0.10). Current unstandardized, "one-size-fits-all" NIBS protocols do not yield reliable cognitive enhancement across NDDs, exposing a translational bottleneck driven by methodological heterogeneity. Realizing NIBS therapeutic potential for cognition in NDDs will require a shift toward precision psychiatry, utilizing individualized neuro-navigation and state-dependent stimulation.

titre: Maternal immune activation and the dopaminergic system: Models, mechanisms, and links to psychiatric disorders.
titre_fr: Maternal immune activation and the dopaminergic system: Models, mechanisms, and links to psychiatric disorders.
auteurs: Chérouvrier Mathilde, Delhaye Célia, Le Magueresse Corentin
resume: Maternal immune activation (MIA) during pregnancy, triggered by infectious or non-infectious factors, is a significant risk factor for neurodevelopmental disorders such as schizophrenia (SZ) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD), which are associated with dysfunctions of the dopaminergic system. Animal models using immune challenges like LPS and Poly(I:C) during gestation recapitulate key behavioral and neurochemical phenotypes observed in these disorders. This review synthesizes current evidence from both human epidemiological studies and animal models, highlighting the links between prenatal inflammation and alterations in dopaminergic circuits. In animal models, MIA causes region-specific changes in dopamine (DA) metabolism, receptor expression, and dopaminergic neuron activity. Notably, hyperdopaminergic states in the striatum and hypodopaminergic states in the cortex have been reported in animal models of MIA, but with some variability across studies. Surprisingly, decreased activity of ventral tegmental area (VTA) dopaminergic neurons in vivo emerges as one of the most robust findings in animal models of MIA. We discuss the possible mechanisms underlying MIA-induced dopaminergic phenotypes, focusing in particular on the endocannabinoid system and on microglia-mediated synaptic refinement and complement system activation. This review underscores the complexity of MIA's impact on brain development and dopaminergic function, emphasizing the need for further research into region-specific mechanisms underlying neuropsychiatric vulnerability, as well as innovative methodologies to investigate how MIA leads to long-term changes in the dynamics of DA release in behaving animals.

titre: Automated attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder detection using an explainable EEGNet model based on electroencephalogram signals.
titre_fr: Automated attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder detection using an explainable EEGNet model based on electroencephalogram signals.
auteurs: Hoseini Reza, Shalbaf Ahmad
resume: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition where traditional diagnostics often suffer from subjective biases and a lack of objective biomarkers. In this study, we developed a novel, automated, and interpretable diagnostic framework using the specialized EEGNet model to extract spatio-temporal patterns directly from raw EEG signals, ensuring robust ADHD detection and model generalizability across a clinical lifespan ranging from 5 to 89 years. The primary innovation of this research lies in a specialized, lightweight EEGNet model that directly processes raw 5-second spatio-temporal EEG segments, eliminating the need for manual feature engineering or signal-to-image transformation. Our findings demonstrate that EEGNet achieves superior performance, reaching an average accuracy of 89.48% (±4.21%) and an AUC of 0.96 (±0.03), significantly outperforming the transfer learning models. A distinguishing feature of this work is the transition from black-box modeling to explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) by integrating Saliency Maps and SHAP values, which decoded the model's decision-making logic to identify key contributing channels (Fp1, Fp2, C3, T5, and A2) whose spatial attributions align with established neuroscientific literature on ADHD. The high ranking of the Fp1 (prefrontal) channel aligns with established neuroscientific evidence regarding executive dysfunction in ADHD. Furthermore, the implementation of a rigorous inter-subject evaluation demonstrates the preliminary clinical feasibility of this interpretable framework, providing a foundation for future validation on larger multi-center cohorts and offering a robust assistive tool for real-world neurological assessments.

titre: Non-Metric Dental Traits, Dental Caries Experience, Parental Perceptions, and Oral Hygiene Status of Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder-A Step Towards Sustainable Smiles.
titre_fr: Non-Metric Dental Traits, Dental Caries Experience, Parental Perceptions, and Oral Hygiene Status of Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder-A Step Towards Sustainable Smiles.
auteurs: Anu Vijayakumar, Devi Sujatha, Preethy Mukunthan
revue: Special care in dentistry : official publication of the American Association of Hospital Dentists, the Academy of Dentistry for the Handicapped, and the American Society for Geriatric Dentistry
resume: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is accompanied by poor oral health outcomes for children with ASD. To assess the occurrence of non-metric dental traits (NMDTs), dental caries experience, parents' perception, and oral hygiene status of children with ASD. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 150 children with ASD and their biological parents. Children with severe sensory or behavioural difficulties who were unable to cooperate for oral examination were excluded. A pre-validated questionnaire was used to assess parental perception. Oral hygiene index-Simplified (OHI-S), Decayed, Missing and Filled Teeth index (DMFT) for permanent and primary dentition was used to assess oral hygiene status and dental caries in children with ASD. Non-metric dental trait (NMDT) was assessed using ASUDAS (Arizona State University Dental Anthropology System). Chi-square test and multiple linear regression analysis were done. Most parents, 126 (84.0%) had a neutral perception score. The mean OHI(S) score for the children with ASD was 1.86 (SD 0.95). The prevalence of dental caries was 16% in deciduous dentition and 48% in permanent dentition. A statistically significant association was observed between palatogingival groove, cusp of Carabelli, and poorer oral hygiene status. Regression analysis showed that children with ASD whose mothers were employed showed a negative association with oral hygiene status (B = -0.533, p = 0.015). Higher maternal education was associated with lower DMFT scores (DMFT, B = - 1.044, p = 0.040 and for D, B = -1.319, p = 0.003). Parents' perceptions regarding oral health among children with ASD are neutral with both behavioral limitations and oral hygiene practices affecting oral health. This study recommends early NMDTs identification and a multidisciplinary approach involving dental professionals, along with targeted parental education and regular follow-up, that may improve oral health outcomes.

Most parents, 126 (84.0%) had a neutral perception score. The mean OHI(S) score for the children with ASD was 1.86 (SD 0.95). The prevalence of dental caries was 16% in deciduous dentition and 48% in permanent dentition. A statistically significant association was observed between palatogingival groove, cusp of Carabelli, and poorer oral hygiene status. Regression analysis showed that children with ASD whose mothers were employed showed a negative association with oral hygiene status (B = -0.533, p = 0.015). Higher maternal education was associated with lower DMFT scores (DMFT, B = - 1.044, p = 0.040 and for D, B = -1.319, p = 0.003). Parents' perceptions regarding oral health among children with ASD are neutral with both behavioral limitations and oral hygiene practices affecting oral health. This study recommends early NMDTs identification and a multidisciplinary approach involving dental professionals, along with targeted parental education and regular follow-up, that may improve oral health outcomes.

titre: Influence of oral sensory processing challenges on the maintenance of oral health in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD): a scoping review.
titre_fr: Influence of oral sensory processing challenges on the maintenance of oral health in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD): a scoping review.
auteurs: Karuna Y M, Shenoy R, Dutt A, Tong H J, Bhat S, Nayak A, Rao A
revue: European archives of paediatric dentistry : official journal of the European Academy of Paediatric Dentistry
resume: The present review was conducted (1) to explore how oral sensory processing challenges (OSPCs) affect oral health maintenance in individuals with ASD and (2) to identify and summarize sensory-informed strategies reported in the literature to address OSPC during routine oral healthcare. A scoping review was conducted using the Arksey and O'Malley framework and reported following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Six electronic databases were searched for studies published between January 2010 and January 2025 in English. Quantitative, qualitative, mixed-methods, and interventional studies linking SOR and oral health in individuals with ASD were included. Data were charted using the PCC framework and synthesized thematically. Methodological quality assessment was performed using the Crowe Critical Appraisal Tool. The search yielded 6476 articles. Following the application of predefined eligibility criteria and the removal of duplicates, 21 studies were included, comprising 11 quantitative, 7 qualitative, and 3 mixed-method studies. Thematic synthesis revealed three major themes: (1) OSPC was associated with challenges in home oral hygiene behaviours, including difficulties related to toothbrush use, toothpaste, environmental triggers, and delayed initiation of routines; (2) OSPC influenced the dental visits through enhanced dental anxiety, barriers to access care, and reduced tolerance to dental procedures; and (3) the included studies reported oral care and dental behavioural strategies to accommodate OSPC during oral care. Oral sensory processing challenges were found to influence oral health care maintenance among individuals with ASD. The review also identified sensory-informed strategies that may support oral health care, although further studies are needed to establish robust evidence on their effectiveness.

titre: Improving Descriptive Diagnostics of Autism in People With Moderate or Severe Intellectual Disabilities: A Qualitative Participatory Study.
titre_fr: Improving Descriptive Diagnostics of Autism in People With Moderate or Severe Intellectual Disabilities: A Qualitative Participatory Study.
auteurs: de Bildt Annelies, Jonker Josien, Damen Nicole, Alma Manna A
revue: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
resume: This study aimed to improve descriptive autism assessment for people with moderate to severe intellectual disabilities (ID) in the Netherlands. The goal was to co-design a framework including an overview of assessment instruments, and recommendations for evaluating broader functioning, for translating findings into daily care and for involving representatives and staff. We used a participatory design, involving parents/representatives, clinicians, care staff, and management from ID and mental health services. The process included a literature study of autism-related instruments, a Delphi study to reach consensus on suitable instruments, and four focus group discussions (FGDs) exploring stakeholder involvement and the role of assessment instruments in the diagnostic process. The literature study identified 20 relevant instruments, of which 13 were selected through the Delphi study (n=37, three rounds). Key selection criteria included low burden for individuals, use of multiple information sources, and strong psychometric quality. While quick assessments were preferred, concerns arose about oversimplifying the autism assessment. FGDs (n=5-12) highlighted eight themes on stakeholder involvement, focusing on timing, roles, and goals. Although no consensus emerged on an optimal combination of tools, clarity about an instrument's purpose and implications proved important. The final FGD identified five potentially overlapping phases in the diagnostic process. The co-designed framework provides an overview of instruments for the assessment of autism and emphasises early and continuous involvement of parents and caregivers. Their participation is essential for defining concerns, guiding assessment goals, sharing information, and applying diagnostic outcomes to improve daily care and support.

titre: The Differential Role of Executive Functions in Reading Fluency in Children With Reading Difficulties, Children With Autism and Typically Developing Children.
titre_fr: The Differential Role of Executive Functions in Reading Fluency in Children With Reading Difficulties, Children With Autism and Typically Developing Children.
auteurs: Horowitz-Kraus Tzipi, Mostofsky Stewart H, Deronda Alyssa, Crocetti Deana, Schlaggar Bradley L, Farah Rola, Rosch Keri S
revue: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
resume: Reading fluency depends in part on executive functions (EF). Dysfluent reading and reduced EF occur in both autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and reading disability (RD), but whether the EF-reading fluency associations established in RD also characterize ASD is unclear. We tested whether diagnostic group moderates these associations. Two hundred twenty-three English-speaking children aged 8-12 years with ASD (n = 35), RD (n = 99), and typical development (TD; n = 89) completed measures of single-word, pseudoword, and contextual reading fluency, working memory (Digit Span), and processing speed (Coding, Symbol Search). Welch's ANOVAs compared groups; linear models with Group×EF interactions and simple slopes tested moderation, with age covaried in sensitivity models. Both clinical groups showed lower reading fluency and EF than TD. Coding predicted word and pseudoword fluency most strongly in ASD (β = 0.40 and 0.43) and less strongly in TD, but not in RD. Digit span predicted word fluency in ASD, and pseudoword fluency in ASD and RD. For contextual fluency, a significant Group × Symbol Search interaction (p = .003) indicated that symbol search predicted performance in ASD (β = 0.52) and TD (β = 0.29) but not RD. Results were unchanged with age covaried. EF-reading fluency associations were strongest and most widespread in ASD, whereas in RD executive measures predicted decoding-level but not contextual fluency. Comparable dysfluency thus rests on distinct executive profiles, supporting the inclusion of EF measures in reading assessment for children with autism and cautioning against transferring RD-derived interventions without adaptation.

titre: A Cross-Sectional Study of Vocabulary and Listening Comprehension in Turkish-Speaking Preschoolers Aged 62-84 Months With and Without Autism Spectrum Disorder.
titre_fr: A Cross-Sectional Study of Vocabulary and Listening Comprehension in Turkish-Speaking Preschoolers Aged 62-84 Months With and Without Autism Spectrum Disorder.
auteurs: Gengeç Hilal, Toker Merih
revue: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
resume: To compare receptive vocabulary, expressive vocabulary, and listening comprehension in Turkish-speaking preschoolers with and without autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and examine vocabulary contributions to comprehension in the ASD group. This cross-sectional study included 44 preschoolers with ASD (62-84 months) and 44 typically developing preschoolers (62-74 months) from 12 state schools in three Turkish cities. Children with ASD attended inclusive classrooms. Eligibility required an estimated nonverbal mental age of 60-72 months on Raven's Coloured Progressive Matrices and mean length of utterance in words ≥ 2.00, calculated from 15-minute play-based language samples using Turkish Systematic Analysis of Language Transcripts. The standardized Early Literacy Test assessed these three skills individually, face-to-face, using a printed tabletop battery without a computer. Parents and teachers completed paper-and-pencil demographic and socioeconomic status (SES) forms. Analyses comprised multivariate analysis of variance, multivariate analysis of covariance, Pearson correlations, and hierarchical regression within the ASD group. The ASD group scored lower on all three skills, with the largest difference in listening comprehension. Differences remained significant after adjustment for age, gender, and SES. Within the ASD group, adding vocabulary to a model containing SES, age, and nonverbal mental age increased explained variance in listening comprehension by 26.3% points, to 37.4%. Findings support assessing vocabulary and listening comprehension together. Vocabulary instruction combined with supported story-listening warrants investigation; the present cross-sectional results do not establish intervention effectiveness.

titre: Improving Student-Teacher Relationships for Autistic Children: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial of a Professional Development Program.
titre_fr: Improving Student-Teacher Relationships for Autistic Children: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial of a Professional Development Program.
auteurs: Blacher J, Eisenhower A, Bolourian Y, Hamsho N, Ledoux Galligan M
revue: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
resume: While most autistic students are placed in general education classrooms, the majority of general education teachers report a lack of autism training. We examined the feasibility and efficacy of Smooth Sailing, a relationship-focused, neurodiversity-affirming, professional development (PD) program, in a small, randomized controlled trial. Participants were 32 general education teachers (kindergarten - 2nd grade) and their autistic students (one per teacher), randomly assigned to intervention or control groups. Teachers and caregivers completed measures at Time 1, Time 2, Time 3, and at the two-month follow-up. The intervention included structured, asynchronous modules, coaching (via Zoom), and in-vivo learning activities. Social validity was also examined throughout. Regarding efficacy, the program had medium to large effects on teacher-reported student-teacher relationship quality (d=0.79), teachers' autism knowledge and self-efficacy (ds=1.49, 1.50), and caregiver-teacher relationship quality (d=0.54). Effects on child emotional-behavioral, social, and academic adjustment were medium to large (ds=0.63, 0.42, and 0.91). Outcomes were generally sustained at 2-month follow-up. Regarding feasibility, observed and teacher-reported data indicate excellent acceptability, implementation fidelity, and sustainability. Findings demonstrate the capacity for this program to enhance relationships and autism knowledge for general education teachers and to improve school adjustment for autistic students.

titre: Sex- and age-specific trends in prescription medication use, 2005-2025: a nationwide repeated cross-sectional study.
titre_fr: Sex- and age-specific trends in prescription medication use, 2005-2025: a nationwide repeated cross-sectional study.
auteurs: Roland Noémie, Ernst Martin Thomsen, Linde Jesper James, Rasmussen Lotte, Pottegård Anton
resume: Previous studies have documented higher medication consumption among females than males; however contemporary sex-based differences across age and therapeutic classes remain poorly characterized. We used the Danish National Prescription Registry to identify all prescriptions redeemed by Danish adults in 2005, 2015 and 2025, assessing overall medication use by sex and age. For the 30 most prescribed therapeutic classes, age-adjusted rate ratios (aRRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated to compare use between sexes. Polypharmacy (≥ five medications redeemed within a calendar year) was also assessed by sex and age groups. In 2025, females accounted for 52% of total medication consumption (1.98 billion Defined Daily Doses (DDDs) among females vs. 3.82 billion DDDs overall), down from 60% (1.17 billion vs. 1.96 billion DDDs) in 2005. This female excess was confined to early adulthood; from age 55 onward, male consumption exceeded that of females. While some of the higher medication use reflected a higher prevalence of certain conditions among females (e.g., thyroid disorders, osteoporosis, depression), females also exhibited a higher use of mental health medications, including antipsychotics, and, newly in 2025, ADHD medications (aRR 1.25; 95%CI 1.16-1.34). Males more frequently used cardiovascular therapies (antithrombotic agents (0.64; 0.62-0.66), insulins (0.67; 0.65-0.69)). However, the historical male cardiovascular predominance was challenged in 2025: thiazide diuretics (1.19; 1.16-1.22) and non-insulin glucose-lowering drugs were more prescribed to females (1.08; 1.01-1.16). Polypharmacy was more common among females in early adulthood but converged after age 65. Sex-based differences in overall medication use have narrowed over time. There is a need for continued monitoring of persistent and emerging sex differences in prescribing. No specific funding.

titre: Exploring long noncoding RNAs as a molecular connection between immune response and autism spectrum disorder.
titre_fr: Exploring long noncoding RNAs as a molecular connection between immune response and autism spectrum disorder.
auteurs: Roschyk Anaya, Campbell Daniel B
resume: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition increasingly linked to immune dysregulation, with long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) emerging as potential regulators of both neural and immune processes. This study commenced by analyzing ten unique lncRNAs and integrated ASD whole-blood datasets using the online platform GTex to identify expression of lncRNAs in various tissues. Moreover, the platform Network Analyst was utilized to assess differentially expressed lncRNAs and associated transcriptomic networks. A total of 93 upregulated and 51 downregulated lncRNAs were identified in people with ASD with tissue specific enrichment observed for MSNP1AS and LNC01238 in immune related systems. The transcription factor CEBPA was shown to interact with the upregulated lncRNA MALAT1, which influenced immune cell differentiation, inflammation and cytokine signaling. Intriguingly CEBPA simultaneously interacted with downregulated lnc RNA MIR22HG. Comparatively, downregulated lncRNAs were associated with the transcription factors TEAD2, CEBPA, CTCF, E2F4, TFAP2C, HIF1A, ETS1, HNF4A, SNAPC4, STAT1, STAT2, TEAD2, FOXC1, BRCA1, AR, E2F4, EOMES, SPI1, DACH1, E2F1, TP63, HMAP1, KLF9, HDGF, and MAZ. Overall, the findings support a role for lncRNAs in ASD pathophysiology and immune dysregulation, pointing to their potential as biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets for future research.

titre: Targeted Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction Analysis of Gut Microbiota and Its Association With Feeding and Mealtime Behavior and Intestinal Permeability in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
titre_fr: Targeted Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction Analysis of Gut Microbiota and Its Association With Feeding and Mealtime Behavior and Intestinal Permeability in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
auteurs: Ali Walaa H, Omar Abdulmabod, Ali Amal H, Hefny Hesham M, Nabil Gehad, Mahmoud Yasmin, Nasr Asmaa Elsaudi Abdelgawad, Abdelhamid Salwa M, Amin Hala Mohammed, Omar Marwa Mohamed, El-Attar Lama M, Mohamed Fatma Saffeyeldin, Elgamal Rasha, Ibrahem Mohamed, Abdelmotogaly Hala S M
resume: Gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms and feeding and mealtime problems are common in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). It is important to note that the gut microbiome is a hypothesized mechanism of action, but it is not yet known if specific bacterial profiles and markers of intestinal barrier function predict feeding problems in the target group of ASD. This is a cross-sectional case-control study that examined 70 children with ASD (aged 3-12 years) and 70 matched neurotypical children. Autism was evaluated using the Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS), and mealtime behaviors were evaluated using the Brief Autism Mealtime Behavior Inventory (BAMBI). Six important bacterial taxa were quantified using real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and fecal zonulin and calprotectin were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Children with ASD had significantly higher levels of fecal zonulin and calprotectin than controls (both at P < 0.001) and lower abundances of beneficial taxa (Prevotella, Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus) and higher abundances of Clostridium difficile and Bacteroidetes (all P < 0.01). The overall BAMBI scores did not differ among the groups, but within the ASD group, feeding problem severity was highly correlated with lower Bifidobacterium (r = -0.68) and higher Clostridium difficile (r = 0.74) and was not significantly correlated with autism severity, zonulin, or calprotectin. Children with ASD have increased levels of gut dysbiosis and barrier dysfunction compared to their non-autistic peers, but the severity of their feeding and mealtime problems tracked the degree of gut microbial imbalance rather than the severity of their ASD symptoms in general. This suggests that feeding behavior is a characteristic that has been under-recognized as a component of the ASD phenotype and is related to the microbiome; if confirmed in longitudinal studies, these microbial associations could represent a candidate target for future gut-directed intervention research.

titre: Longitudinal relationship between sleep and emotional/behavioral problems in autism spectrum disorders: a cross-lagged panel analysis.
titre_fr: Longitudinal relationship between sleep and emotional/behavioral problems in autism spectrum disorders: a cross-lagged panel analysis.
auteurs: Dong Hanyu, Zhang Yuxin, Yu Xinnan, Du Lin, Jia Feiyong
resume: Sleep, emotional, and behavioral problems are common comorbidities associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Current longitudinal research on the temporal links between sleep problems and emotional-behavioral problems shows inconsistent results among preschool children with ASD. Hence, this longitudinal study aimed to examine the temporal associations between emotional-behavioral and sleep problems among preschool children with ASD across two time points. Among 124 enrolled preschool children with ASD, 70 completed follow-up and constituted the final analytic sample (mean age 36.7 ± 10.2 months at T1). They were evaluated for developmental quotient using the Griffiths Development Scales-Chinese version (GDS-C), ASD symptoms using Autism Behavior Checklist (ABC) and Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS), emotional and behavioral problems using the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL), and sleep problems using the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ) at time 1 (T1). The evaluations were replicated at a follow-up appointment 18 months after T1 (time 2; T2). The cross-lagged panel model (CLPM) was employed to examine the potential relationship between CBCL and CSHQ scores in the children. The total CBCL score at T1 could predict the CSHQ at T2 (β = 0.348, t = 3.105, p = 0.002), whereas the CSHQ at T1 could not predict the CBCL at T2 (β = 0.117, t = 1.083, p = 0.279). Findings remained robust across five sensitivity subsets after excluding subgroups with distinct rehabilitation exposure, younger age, higher development quotients, girls, or mild ASD symptoms.  Emotional-behavioral problems predict sleep problems 18 months later in preschool ASD children. Screening of these symptoms during follow-up supports early sleep-risk monitoring. • Sleep, emotional, and behavioral problems are common comorbidities associated with ASD. • Thus, researching their temporal correlation over time is necessary. • Emotional and behavioral problems indicate a positive temporal correlation at T1, which was also evident for sleep problems at T2, in children with ASD. • Emotional and behavioral problems in preschool children with ASD can forecast sleep problems that develop 18 months later, providing guidance for clinical decision-making.

They were evaluated for developmental quotient using the Griffiths Development Scales-Chinese version (GDS-C), ASD symptoms using Autism Behavior Checklist (ABC) and Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS), emotional and behavioral problems using the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL), and sleep problems using the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ) at time 1 (T1). The evaluations were replicated at a follow-up appointment 18 months after T1 (time 2; T2). The cross-lagged panel model (CLPM) was employed to examine the potential relationship between CBCL and CSHQ scores in the children. The total CBCL score at T1 could predict the CSHQ at T2 (β = 0.348, t = 3.105, p = 0.002), whereas the CSHQ at T1 could not predict the CBCL at T2 (β = 0.117, t = 1.083, p = 0.279). Findings remained robust across five sensitivity subsets after excluding subgroups with distinct rehabilitation exposure, younger age, higher development quotients, girls, or mild ASD symptoms.  Emotional-behavioral problems predict sleep problems 18 months later in preschool ASD children. Screening of these symptoms during follow-up supports early sleep-risk monitoring. • Sleep, emotional, and behavioral problems are common comorbidities associated with ASD. • Thus, researching their temporal correlation over time is necessary. • Emotional and behavioral problems indicate a positive temporal correlation at T1, which was also evident for sleep problems at T2, in children with ASD. • Emotional and behavioral problems in preschool children with ASD can forecast sleep problems that develop 18 months later, providing guidance for clinical decision-making.

titre: Spatial single-cell mapping of transcriptional differences across genetic backgrounds in mouse brains.
titre_fr: Spatial single-cell mapping of transcriptional differences across genetic backgrounds in mouse brains.
auteurs: Hemminger Zachary, Tam Gabriela, De Ocampo Haley, Wang Aihui, Underwood Thomas, Xie Fangming, Zhao Qiuying, Song Dongyuan, Li Jingyi Jessica, Dong Hongwei, Wollman Roy
resume: Genetic variation can alter organ structure and function. Comparative statistical analysis of organs across genetic backgrounds requires spatial, single-cell, atlas-scale data in replicates. Here we introduce atlas-scale transcriptome localization using aggregate signatures (ATLAS), a scalable tissue mapping method that learns transcriptional signatures from single-cell RNA sequencing data, encodes them in situ with tens of thousands of oligonucleotide probes and decodes them to infer cell types and imputed transcriptomes. We validated ATLAS against direct MERFISH measurements of marker genes and through quantitative comparisons to four other technologies. We profiled 40 million cells across more than 400 coronal sections from central brains of five male and five female C57BL/6J mice and five male BTBR T<sup>+</sup>tf/J mice, an idiopathic autism model. Our analysis revealed more than 40 significant differences in cell-type distributions and identified 16 regional composition changes across male-female and B6-BTBR comparisons. ATLAS thus enables systematic comparative studies, facilitating organ-level structure-function analysis of disease models.

titre: Extended high-frequency hearing and cognitive-motor coordination during speech-in-noise walking.
titre_fr: Extended high-frequency hearing and cognitive-motor coordination during speech-in-noise walking.
auteurs: Li Ming Ang, Zhang Qiqi, Li Wei
resume: Human speech perception in everyday environments requires continuous coordination between auditory processing, predictive cognition, and motor control. Although extended high-frequency (EHF) hearing sensitivity has been associated with rapid speech-in-noise perception, little is known about whether subtle EHF variability relates to cognitive-motor performance during concurrent locomotion and listening. This cross-sectional laboratory study examined whether EHF hearing sensitivity was associated with predictive speech recognition and gait stability during dual-task walking under noisy listening conditions. Forty-eight young adults with clinically normal conventional audiograms (0.25-8 kHz < 20 dB HL) completed EHF audiometric testing between 9 and 16 kHz, followed by a dual-task experiment integrating treadmill walking with an auditory gating paradigm. Participants listened to naturally coarticulated fricative-onset Mandarin words embedded in spatially diffuse multitalker noise while walking at preferred and increased walking speeds. Speech stimuli were presented in progressively increasing temporal gates to assess predictive spoken-word recognition from partial acoustic input. Simultaneously, wearable inertial motion sensors recorded stride variability, trunk stability, and dual-task locomotor performance during auditory processing. Results showed that lower EHF thresholds were associated with higher predictive speech-recognition accuracy during early gating windows, particularly for fricative stimuli containing greater high-frequency spectral energy. Better EHF sensitivity was also associated with lower gait variability and reduced dual-task interference during noisy walking conditions. In contrast, elevated EHF thresholds were associated with delayed early lexical recognition, greater stride instability, and higher subjective listening effort under increased auditory uncertainty. Associations between EHF sensitivity and gait stability remained significant after controlling for conventional pure-tone averages. These findings suggest that EHF hearing sensitivity may be associated with auditory-cognitive-motor functioning during dynamic listening situations. Better EHF sensitivity was associated with greater early-gate recognition accuracy and lower gait variability, consistent with a possible shared auditory-cognitive-motor mechanism. The study extends current research on EHF hearing by integrating auditory psychophysics with cognitive-motor assessment. It highlights the potential relevance of EHF sensitivity for understanding subtle individual differences in speech perception and mobility-related listening performance.

titre: A longitudinal study of rotenone-induced Parkinsonism in mice.
titre_fr: A longitudinal study of rotenone-induced Parkinsonism in mice.
auteurs: Joshi Prince, Fan Fan, Lou Xuelin
resume: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra. Environmental toxins such as rotenone are widely used to model PD pathology and evaluate new drugs in PD; however, the long-term consequences of toxin exposure remain poorly understood. Here, we performed a longitudinal mouse study to examine the onset, progression, and long-term outcomes of rotenone-induced PD-like phenotypes. A 21-day regimen of rotenone (2.5 mg/kg/day, intraperitoneal) produced robust Parkinsonism-like phenotypes by week 4, including impaired locomotion, anxiety-like behaviors, and deficits in motor coordination and learning, accompanied by reduced tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression and loss of TH<sup>+</sup> neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta. Unexpectedly, these behavioral and neuropathological deficits gradually resolved over time. After 12 months of toxin cessation, rotenone-treated mice exhibited behavioral performance and TH expression levels comparable to untreated controls. These findings reveal a previously underappreciated capacity for adaptive resilience within the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system following toxic injury.

titre: Leuprolide acetate, a GnRH agonist, preserves cerebellar integrity and motor coordination in a rat model of hepatic encephalopathy.
titre_fr: Leuprolide acetate, a GnRH agonist, preserves cerebellar integrity and motor coordination in a rat model of hepatic encephalopathy.
auteurs: Gutiérrez-Esparza Brenda Lizeth, González-Torres Marina Liliana, Quintanar-Stephano Andrés, Calderón-Vallejo Dennise, Saldaña Ma Consolación Martínez, Murillo-Sánchez Marlin Danlleli, Quintanar J Luis
resume: Patients with hepatic encephalopathy (HE) experience both cognitive and motor coordination alterations, which lead to a decrease in quality of life. During the progression of this disease, the cerebellum is one of the most affected brain regions due to elevated blood ammonia levels that cause neuronal damage and contribute to motor dysfunction. Leuprolide acetate (LA), a gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) receptor agonist, has demonstrated neurotrophic effects in various regions of the central nervous system. Therefore, this study evaluated the potential neurotrophic effect of LA on the cerebellum in a rat model of HE induced by portocaval anastomosis (PCA). For the experimental design, male Wistar rats were divided into three groups: SHAM, PCA with saline solution (PCA+SS), and PCA treated with LA (PCA+LA). Motor function was assessed using rotarod and open field tests. Histological assessment of the cerebellum was performed using H&E staining, while immunoreactivity of the apoptotic markers caspase-8 and caspase-3 were analyzed to evaluate apoptosis. In addition, the expression of proteins associated with neuronal integrity and recovery, including NF200, neurabin II, and BDNF, were examined. The results showed that LA administration significantly improved motor coordination. Treated animals exhibited reduced neuronal loss in the Purkinje and granular layers, decreased activation of caspase-8 and caspase-3, and increased expression of neurabin II and BDNF. Collectively, these findings indicate that LA has therapeutic potential to attenuate cerebellar neuronal damage and promote functional recovery during HE.

titre: Early-Life NO<sub>2</sub> Exposure and developmental coordination disorder in Preschool Children: A Cross-sectional Study.
titre_fr: Early-Life NO<sub>2</sub> Exposure and developmental coordination disorder in Preschool Children: A Cross-sectional Study.
auteurs: Jiang Liyan, Su Yuantao, Meng Xia, Cai Jing, Hua Jing
resume: Although air pollution is a potential neurotoxicant, evidence linking early-life nitrogen dioxide (NO<sub>2</sub>) exposure to motor development remains inconsistent, and large-scale studies are limited. This cross-sectional study investigated associations of prenatal and postnatal NO<sub>2</sub> exposure with motor coordination performance and suspected developmental coordination disorder (DCD) risk among 105,280 children aged 3-5 years from Chinese National Cohort of Motor Development. Motor coordination was assessed using the Little DCD Questionnaire (LDCDQ). NO<sub>2</sub> exposure was estimated using a high-resolution satellite-based random forest model. Linear mixed-effects models and generalized linear mixed models with a binomial distribution were applied to evaluate associations with LDCDQ scores and suspected DCD risk, respectively. Per interquartile range (IQR) increase in NO<sub>2</sub> during the first trimester and from birth to 36 months, LDCDQ scores decreased by 0.20 (95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.08, -0.31) and 0.10 (95% CI: -0.02, -0.19), respectively. Odds ratios for suspected DCD were 1.07 (95% CI: 1.03, 1.11) for first-trimester exposure and 1.04 (95% CI: 1.004, 1.07) for birth-to-18-month exposure. Among three LDCDQ subdomains, general coordination showed the strongest association. Associations appeared to be stronger among boys. These findings suggest that early-life NO<sub>2</sub> exposure may adversely affect motor coordination development of preschoolers, though the modest effect sizes were observed.

titre: Frontal-parietal event related potential correlates of motor planning deficits in children with developmental coordination disorder.
titre_fr: Frontal-parietal event related potential correlates of motor planning deficits in children with developmental coordination disorder.
auteurs: Gholami Saeed, Ghanaee Chaman Abad Ali, Mashhadi Ali, Green Dido, Namdar Tajari Somayeh
resume: Imitation and praxis deficits are key characteristics of developmental coordination disorder (DCD). Although behavioral impairments in imitation have been widely studied, less is known about motor preparation and attentional processes underlying thwillese difficulties. This study examined imitation of meaningless gestures to better understand motor planning deficits in children with DCD while controlling for involuntary mirror movements. Forty-nine children aged 7-10 years participated (DCD: n = 24; typically developing [TD]: n = 25). Participants performed meaningless hand and finger gestures within a two-step cue-target paradigm designed to assess event-related potentials (ERPs) related to preparatory attention and motor planning. After a visual cue, an imperative stimulus appeared 1100 ms later, prompting response execution. Offline video analysis measured mirror movements-defined as involuntary replication of the target posture in the non-task hand-and imitation errors during unilateral performance. Children with DCD showed significantly prolonged ERP latencies during preparatory and motor planning stages compared to TD peers, with no amplitude differences and no group differences in late attention positivity. Behavioral analyses revealed significantly more mirror movements across hand and finger postures in the DCD group (all p ≤ .002). Additionally, left-finger imitation errors were higher in the congruent condition for children with DCD (p < .001). Children with DCD demonstrate delayed neural processing during motor preparation and planning, indicating temporal inefficiency and impaired interhemispheric motor regulation. Increased mirror movements and imitation errors further reflect difficulties in coordinating voluntary and involuntary motor control.

titre: Measuring the functional impact of developmental coordination disorder beyond childhood: a COSMIN systematic review.
titre_fr: Measuring the functional impact of developmental coordination disorder beyond childhood: a COSMIN systematic review.
auteurs: Blanco-Martínez Nerea, Delgado-Lobete Laura, Ayán-Pérez Carlos
resume: Difficulties in daily performance and participation become increasingly relevant for the identification of Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD) beyond childhood. Several questionnaires have been developed to assess Criterion B in adolescent and adult populations; however, their measurement properties have not been systematically synthesized. This systematic review aimed to (1) identify instruments designed to assess Criterion B of DCD in adolescents and adults, (2) evaluate their measurement properties following COSMIN methodology, and (3) provide evidence-based recommendations for their use in clinical practice and research. A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA and COSMIN guidelines. Six electronic databases were searched from inception to August 2026. Methodological quality was assessed using the COSMIN Risk of Bias checklist, measurement properties were evaluated against the COSMIN criteria for good measurement properties, and the certainty of evidence was graded using the COSMIN-modified GRADE approach. Nineteen studies evaluating five instruments were included: the Adult Developmental Coordination Disorder/Dyspraxia Checklist (ADC), the Adolescents and Adults Coordination Questionnaire (AAC-Q), the Functional Difficulties Questionnaire-9 (FDQ-9), the Developmental Coordination Disorder Questionnaire (DCDQ), and the Adolescent Motor Competence Questionnaire (AMCQ). Internal consistency and construct validity were the most frequently examined properties, whereas measurement error, and measurement invariance were rarely or never assessed. The ADC was the most extensively investigated instrument; structural validity was insufficient with moderate-quality evidence, whereas sufficient evidence was found for content validity and some aspects of test-retest reliability and construct validity. The AAC-Q showed a promising overall psychometric profile, although evidence for content validity, structural validity and internal consistency remained inconsistent. Evidence for the AMCQ was generally weaker despite its sufficient content validity, while findings for the FDQ-9 and DCDQ were based on only two studies each. Evidence supporting instruments designed to assess Criterion B of DCD in adolescents and adults remains limited and heterogeneous. No single instrument currently has sufficiently robust evidence to support firm recommendations across populations and cultural contexts. Further COSMIN-aligned validation studies are needed to strengthen confidence in instrument selection for clinical and research use beyond childhood.

titre: WE PLAY | ON JOUE - Family-Centered Virtual Reality Games Room for Children with Developmental Disabilities and Their Families: A Feasibility Case Study.
titre_fr: WE PLAY | ON JOUE - Family-Centered Virtual Reality Games Room for Children with Developmental Disabilities and Their Families: A Feasibility Case Study.
auteurs: Ogourtsova Tatiana, Lamontagne Anouk, Mahmoudi Ebrahim, Pietrangelo Filomena
resume: To explore the feasibility, satisfaction with, enjoyment of, acceptability, and preliminary effects of joint virtual reality (VR) sessions targeting physical engagement in youth with disabilities and relaxation in caregivers. In a mini-ethnographic case study, four youth-caregiver dyads completed weekly 30-minute immersive VR sessions over four weeks. Youth (aged 10-20 years) with cerebral palsy (n = 2), autism with motor dyspraxia (n = 1), and CHARGE syndrome (n = 1) used the AstroSurfer app targeting motor functions. Caregivers simultaneously engaged with the TRIPP® app for relaxation and meditation. Pre- and post-intervention measures included the Trunk Control Measurement Scale and the Quality of Upper Extremity Skills Test (youth), the Parental Stress Scale and the Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale (caregivers). Enjoyment ratings (0-10, at each session) and exit interviews were completed. Although standardized motor outcomes showed limited overall change over the intervention period, improvements were observed in one youth participant. Reductions in stress were noted for three caregivers. Enjoyment ratings were high (7-10/10 for youth; 9-10/10 for caregivers), with engaging gameplay and relaxation identified as key benefits. Findings provide preliminary support for the potential feasibility and acceptability of family-centered VR interventions in pediatric rehabilitation, warranting evaluation in larger studies.

titre: Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound activates Piezo1 to restore brain lymphatic drainage and improve outcomes in traumatic brain injury mice.
titre_fr: Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound activates Piezo1 to restore brain lymphatic drainage and improve outcomes in traumatic brain injury mice.
auteurs: Wang Shuo, Wang Bo, Wang Yuchang, Nie Meng, Yuan Jiangyuan, Wu Chenrui, Mi Liang, Chen Bo, Liu Tao, Jiang Rongcai
resume: Meningeal lymphatic vessels (mLVs) are specialized lymphatic structures that drain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and facilitate immune surveillance of the central nervous system. This drainage system is impaired after traumatic brain injury (TBI); mLVs undergo structural regression, and CSF outflow to peripheral lymphoid tissues is markedly slowed. The resulting accumulation of hyperphosphorylated tau, amyloid-β, and inflammatory mediators drives sustained neuroinflammation and cognitive decline. The neuroprotective effect of low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) in TBI mice has been previously demonstrated, however, its impact on brain lymphatic drainage is unclear. Here, we employed a controlled cortical impact (CCI) mouse model of TBI combined with serial LIPUS stimulation to investigate its therapeutic potential for mLV function. LIPUS restored neurological function in TBI mice, improving motor coordination and spatial/recognition memory while attenuating tau pathology, Aβ burden, and astrocyte reactivity. Mechanistically, LIPUS activated Piezo1 on meningeal lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs), triggering a downstream signaling cascade that promoted LEC proliferation and migration in vitro and restored lymphatic coverage and drainage function in vivo. To identify the critical mediator of this process, we examined the pathway's downstream components and found that vascular endothelial growth factor C (VEGFC) served as the critical downstream effector: VEGFC overexpression rescued meningeal lymphatic restoration and CSF drainage. These results establish LIPUS as a non-invasive therapeutic strategy that functionally restores brain lymphatic drainage after TBI, representing a promising preclinical therapeutic strategy for proteinopathy-associated neurological diseases that warrants further optimization for clinical translation.

titre: Sedative Potential of L (+)-Tartaric Acid: Behavioral Evidence With In Silico Insights Into Possible GABAergic Interaction.
titre_fr: Sedative Potential of L (+)-Tartaric Acid: Behavioral Evidence With In Silico Insights Into Possible GABAergic Interaction.
auteurs: Bithi Sumaya Akter, Chakrabarty Anike, Akter Khadija, Saha Chinmoy Kumar, Alshahrani Mohammad Y, Hossain Md Arif, Mia Emon, Yana Noshin Tasnim, Ajmee Afiya, Mandal Proma, Al Hasan Md Sakib, Islam Muhammad Torequl
resume: Insomnia is a prevalent neurological disorder often caused by stress, anxiety, and imbalances in the GABAergic system. Although benzodiazepines like diazepam (DZP) are commonly prescribed, their long-term use is associated with adverse effects, including dependence and impaired coordination. Therefore, there is growing interest in natural alternatives with safer pharmacological profiles. This study aimed to investigate the sedative-like potential of L (+)-tartaric acid (LTA), a naturally occurring organic acid, through both in vivo and in silico approaches targeting the γ-aminobutyric acid A (GABA<sub>A</sub>) receptor. Sedative-like activity was evaluated in Swiss albino mice using thiopental sodium-induced sleeping time, open-field, and rotarod tests. LTA significantly reduced sleep latency and prolonged sleep duration in a dose-dependent manner, with the higher dose (240 mg/kg) producing a more pronounced effect. Co-administration of LTA with DZP further enhanced thiopental-induced hypnosis. In the open-field test, LTA reduced locomotor and exploratory activities, as evidenced by decreases in square crossings, rearing, and grooming behaviors. titre: AVIL is dispensable for baseline neurobehavioral and somatosensory function in mice.
titre_fr: AVIL is dispensable for baseline neurobehavioral and somatosensory function in mice.
auteurs: Lynch Sarah A, Glowczyk-Gluc Martyna, Wang Yiwei, Johnson Summer, Shi Xinrui, Gidado Abdul-Salam, Johnson Alexis, Deppmann Christopher, Lukens John, Li Hui
resume: Advillin (AVIL) is an actin-binding protein expressed in peripheral sensory neurons and Merkel cells, but aberrantly upregulated in several malignancies, including low-grade glioma, glioblastoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma. AVIL's oncogenic activity and restricted adult tissue expression make it an attractive therapeutic target; however, its physiological function and the safety of AVIL inhibition remain incompletely understood. We evaluated genetic and pharmacologic targeting of Avil using neurobehavioral and somatosensory assays in vivo. Constitutive and conditional Avil knockout mice, generated by exons 7 and 8 deletion, underwent behavioral testing assessing anxiety-related and exploratory behaviors, motor coordination, affective responses, and learning and memory. Nociceptive and tactile sensory function were evaluated alongside histologic analysis of peripheral mechanosensory architecture. In parallel, a first-in-class AVIL inhibitor was assessed in vivo. Avil-deficient mice exhibited normal exploratory and anxiety-related behavior, intact motor coordination, preserved affective responses, and unaltered learning and memory. Loss or pharmacologic inhibition of advillin did not impair nociceptive processing, tactile sensitivity, or peripheral mechanosensory architecture, and histologic abnormalities were not detected. Together, these findings show preserved baseline behavioral and sensory outcomes following lifelong Avil loss, with complementary evidence of tolerability following pharmacologic inhibition under the conditions tested, supporting AVIL as a potentially well-tolerated therapeutic target in cancer.

titre: Modeling Parkinson's Disease Through Combined DJ-1 Deficiency and Noradrenergic Degeneration.
titre_fr: Modeling Parkinson's Disease Through Combined DJ-1 Deficiency and Noradrenergic Degeneration.
auteurs: Ferreira-Antunes Filipa, Marote Ana, Campos Jonas, Borges Inês Feio, Monteiro-Fernandes Daniela, Barata-Antunes Sandra, Mendes-Pinheiro Bárbara, Salgado António J, Sampaio-Marques Belém
resume: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by progressive degeneration of the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system while increasing evidence indicates that early pathology also involves the locus coeruleus (LC) and the noradrenergic system. However, whether LC degeneration increases dopaminergic vulnerability in genetically susceptible background remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the impact of selective noradrenergic depletion on behavioral and neuropathological phenotypes in DJ-1 knockout (KO) mice, a model of familial PD. DJ-1 KO and wild-type (WT) mice received the selective LC neurotoxin DSP-4 (50 mg/kg) to induce noradrenergic degeneration, followed by a battery of motor and non-motor behavioral assessments and histological analysis of the LC and nigrostriatal system. DSP-4 induced approximately 80-85% LC neuronal loss, confirming effective noradrenergic lesioning. While DSP-4-treated WT mice displayed relatively mild behavioral alterations, its combination with DJ-1 deficiency produced marked impairments, including increased anxious- and depressive-like behaviors, enhanced contextual fear responses, and deficits in motor coordination and balance. At the nigrostriatal level, DJ-1 KO mice already exhibited reduced TH-positive neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc), whereas combined DJ-1 deficiency and DSP-4 treatment produced a further significant reduction in striatal TH density, without significant additional loss of SNc TH-positive neurons. These findings indicate that LC noradrenergic degeneration selectively exacerbates dopaminergic terminal pathology in the DJ-1-deficient background, suggesting increased vulnerability of the nigrostriatal system to noradrenergic loss. Overall, our data identify LC degeneration as a modifier of both motor and non-motor phenotypes associated with DJ-1 deficiency and provide experimental support for a functional interaction between the noradrenergic and nigrostriatal systems in PD.

titre: Early Administration of Methylene Blue Attenuates Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Cognitive Deficits in a Model of Huntington's Disease.
titre_fr: Early Administration of Methylene Blue Attenuates Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Cognitive Deficits in a Model of Huntington's Disease.
auteurs: Huerta-Cervantes Maribel, Peña-Montes Donovan J, López-Vázquez Miguel Ángel, Saavedra-Molina Alfredo, Pérez-Vega María Isabel, Olvera-Cortés María Esther
resume: Huntington's disease (HD) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder marked by progressive motor, cognitive, and psychiatric impairments, for which no disease-modifying therapies exist. Mitochondrial dysfunction is an early feature of HD, highlighting the need to target bioenergetic deficits early. We evaluated the neuroprotective effects of methylene blue (MB) in a 3-nitropropionic acid (3-NP)-induced HD-like rat model characterized by mitochondrial dysfunction and striatal injury. Male Wistar rats received MB for 14 days during 3-NP administration. Behavioral performance was assessed, followed by biochemical and histological analyses of the striatum. MB improved cognitive performance and partially improved specific aspects of motor coordination. At the mitochondrial level, MB restored Complex II activity, membrane potential index, reduced reactive oxygen species (ROS), and modulated mitochondrial function, but did not rescue Complex I. Histologically, MB attenuated striatal histopathological damage. These results suggest that methylene blue has neuroprotective effects in the early stages, particularly at the mitochondrial and cognitive levels. Its limited impact on other behaviors and systemic parameters could indicate that its efficacy depends on timing or duration. Overall, this study supports early mitochondrial targeting in HD therapy and shows methylene blue as a promising, though partial, disease-modifying candidate.

titre: TREM2/IGF-1 signaling axis-induced microglial senescence underlies benzo[a]pyrene-associated Parkinson's disease-like lesions.
titre_fr: TREM2/IGF-1 signaling axis-induced microglial senescence underlies benzo[a]pyrene-associated Parkinson's disease-like lesions.
auteurs: Wu Yingying, Shi Yuxin, Xiao Feifan, Liu Aixiang, Li Xin, Xia Na, Zhang Hongmei
resume: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder worldwide. Accumulating evidence has linked environmental polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), with benzo[a]pyrene (B[a]P) as a representative ubiquitous member, to elevated PD risk and disease pathogenesis. The present study aimed to investigate whether B[a]P can trigger typical PD-like lesions in mice, and further dissects the functional role of microglial senescence as well as its underlying regulatory mechanism, using complementary systems in vivo mouse model and in vitro BV2 microglia cell. Behavioral assessments revealed that B[a]P exposure induced significant, dose-dependent impairments in motor coordination and cognitive function compared with the control group. Moreover, the degree of functional impairments measured in the high-dose B[a]P group was comparable to that observed in the MPTP positive-control group. Following B[a]P treatment, brain-resident microglia cells exhibited signs of cell senescence, as evidenced by typical ultrastructural alterations, increased senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) activity, and elevated expression of the core senescence markers p16, p21, and p53 proteins. Consistent with these in vivo observations, B[a]P was confirmed to also induce cell cycle arrest in cultured BV2 microglia cells. This pro-senescent effect was significnatly attenuated by Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) overexpression, whereas it was markedly exacerbated following TREM2 knockout. Subsequent experiments further validated that insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), as a direct downstream effector regulated by TREM2, is functionally required for B[a]P-triggered microglial senescence. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that B[a]P exposure can induce PD-like lesions and microglial senescence, and which is primarily mediated via the TREM2/IGF-1 signaling axis.
