These findings should not be interpreted as establishing clinical efficacy. Although some comparative studies reported greater pain reduction with LLLT/PBM than with ultrasound, this finding should be interpreted cautiously because the number of studies was small and treatment protocols were heterogeneous. Therefore, current evidence does not establish the superiority of LLLT/PBM over therapeutic ultrasound.

titre: From Limb Salvage to Prosthetic Rehabilitation After Severe Traumatic Hand Injury Complicated by Complex Regional Pain Syndrome: A Case Report.
titre_fr: From Limb Salvage to Prosthetic Rehabilitation After Severe Traumatic Hand Injury Complicated by Complex Regional Pain Syndrome: A Case Report.
auteurs: Tot Ozana Katarina, Petričević Anja, Hnatešen Dijana, Cicvarić Ana, Dimitrijević Iva, Matković Vanja
resume: Background/Objectives: Severe traumatic injuries of the upper extremity present a major therapeutic challenge because of extensive tissue damage, severe pain, loss of function, and substantial psychosocial consequences. Continuous multidisciplinary rehabilitation that adapts to the patient's evolving clinical condition may optimize functional outcomes across the entire continuum of care. Methods: A 42-year-old man with no prior comorbidities sustained a severe work-related traumatic injury to his left hand. Despite reconstructive surgery and prolonged multidisciplinary treatment, he developed CRPS with persistent neuropathic pain, progressive functional deterioration, and psychological distress. Fourteen months after injury, the affected limb became completely nonfunctional, and elective transradial amputation was recommended after multidisciplinary evaluation. Results: Rehabilitation was delivered as a continuous, phase-adapted multidisciplinary program. Before amputation, treatment focused on pain control, reduction of edema and inflammation, preservation of joint mobility and muscle function, and management of CRPS using multimodal physical therapy combined with pharmacological treatment and psychological support. As amputation became inevitable, rehabilitation goals shifted toward pre-amputation preparation, promotion of adaptive neuroplasticity, and prevention of phantom limb pain. After transradial amputation, pain intensity markedly decreased, functional adaptation improved, and the patient successfully completed prosthetic rehabilitation. Conclusions: This case highlights the importance of a continuous, individualized multidisciplinary rehabilitation strategy extending from limb salvage through post-amputation recovery. Integrating multimodal physical therapy, neuroplasticity based interventions, psychological support, and prosthetic rehabilitation may improve pain control, facilitate functional recovery, and enhance long-term adaptation after severe traumatic upper extremity injury.

titre: Investigation of Quiet Quitting and Burnout Levels Among Physical Therapy and Rehabilitation Students: A Descriptive and Correlational Study.
titre_fr: Investigation of Quiet Quitting and Burnout Levels Among Physical Therapy and Rehabilitation Students: A Descriptive and Correlational Study.
auteurs: Yilmaz Ramazan Cihad, Demirtas Karaoba Dilan, Candiri Senol Busra, Percin Alper
resume: Background/Objectives: Quiet quitting is characterized by reduced commitment and reluctance to exceed expected role responsibilities, whereas burnout reflects the depletion of emotional resources due to work and educational demands. This study aimed to examine the relationship between quiet quitting and burnout among Physical Therapy and Rehabilitation (PTR) students and to determine whether these variables differ by gender, grade level, reason for choosing the program, and program satisfaction. Methods: A total of 225 students participated in this descriptive and cross-sectional study. Data were collected using the Personal Information Form, the Quiet Quitting Scale (QQS), and the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Student Form (MBI-SF). The data were analyzed using nonparametric statistical methods with the SPSS 27.0 software. Results: The mean QQS total score was 48.14 ± 9.80. The mean scores for the MBI-SF dimensions were 14.27 ± 4.66 for Exhaustion, 9.89 ± 3.65 for Cynicism, and 11.28 ± 2.98 for Professional Efficacy. QQS scores differed significantly according to grade level and reason for choosing the programme, whereas gender differences were observed only in the Self-Protection subscale (p < 0.05). MBI-SF dimensions did not differ according to gender, grade level, reason for choosing the programme, or programme satisfaction (p > 0.05). "Exhaustion" and "Cynicism" were positively correlated with QQS subscale and total scores (r = 0.307-0.639, all p < 0.001). The MBI-SF "Professional Efficacy" subscale showed a weak correlation with QQS "Lack of Motivation" (r = 0.143, p = 0.032). Conclusions: Quiet quitting and burnout were significantly associated among PTR students, with the strength of this relationship varying across burnout dimensions. These findings extend the limited evidence on these constructs in physiotherapy education and support further investigation of their academic and psychosocial context.

titre: The Golden Neuroplastic Period: A Framework for Standardised Patient-centred Stroke Rehabilitation.
titre_fr: The Golden Neuroplastic Period: A Framework for Standardised Patient-centred Stroke Rehabilitation.
auteurs: Paul Sudip, Das Hrishita, Kumar Vijay, Bhatia Dinesh
resume: The issue of stroke continues to pose a serious problem for the world community with forecasts of a 50% increase in stroke-associated mortality rate by 2050. Around 90% of patients who suffered from stroke have cognitive deficits. Post-stroke recovery is the fastest within three months, and an interdisciplinary approach including cognitive, nutrition and motor rehabilitation can significantly improve patients' quality of life. The current review highlights the latest advances in interdisciplinary stroke rehabilitation and reveals the key components which are required for precision rehabilitation and durable recovery. An electronic database search was done using the following databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar) until March 2026 according to the PRISMA guidelines. Based on screening of 235 studies, there were included 17 articles into the narrative review. For 43,000 stroke patients, interdisciplinary approach to treatment planning was associated with higher survival rate and functional independence compared with conventional care. Timely start of intervention and treatment within 14 days were connected with better motor results, and participation of neuropsychologists in the stroke team increased the cost-benefit ratio three times due to decrease in social care expenses. To move towards evidence-based treatment and precision rehabilitation, it is imperative to identify the 'active ingredients' of therapy: specific doses of exercise, dual-task complexity and specific timing for nutritional supplementation. Standardised and cost-effective models should be widely implemented to decrease the burden of caregivers and support long-term brain health.

titre: Segmental phase angle as predictor of activities of daily living and muscle health in patients with osteoporotic fracture A retrospective cohort study.
titre_fr: Segmental phase angle as predictor of activities of daily living and muscle health in patients with osteoporotic fracture A retrospective cohort study.
auteurs: Ito Yusuke, Yoshimura Yoshihiro, Nagano Fumihiko, Matsumoto Ayaka
resume: This study aimed to determine whether the segmental phase angle is associated with clinical outcomes such as activities of daily living (ADL), muscle strength, and skeletal muscle mass in patients with osteoporotic fractures. This was a retrospective cohort study of patients with osteoporotic fractures admitted to convalescent rehabilitation wards. The primary outcome was a Functional Independence Measure motor (FIM-motor) score at discharge, and secondary outcomes were handgrip strength and skeletal muscle mass index (SMI) at discharge. Multivariate analysis was used to adjust for confounders and to examine the association between segmental phase angle and outcome. A total of 115 subjects (97 women, age 81.0 ± 10.0 years) were included in the study. The median baseline phase angle was 3.6°. Multiple regression analysis adjusted for confounders showed that arm phase angle was independently positively associated with handgrip strength (β=0.250, P < 0.001) and SMI (β=0.215, P < 0.001) at discharge. Leg phase angle was independently positively associated with FIM-motor score (β=0.077, P = 0.045), handgrip strength (β=0.174, P < 0.001), and SMI (β=0.154, P < 0.001) at discharge. The leg phase angle was associated with ADL, muscle strength, and skeletal muscle mass in patients with osteoporotic fractures at discharge. Segmental phase angle may be a useful indicator for considering intervention methods in patients with osteoporotic fractures.

titre: Integrating medical psychology into long-term trauma care for older adults.
titre_fr: Integrating medical psychology into long-term trauma care for older adults.
auteurs: Toding Novita, Paembonan Yanni
resume: Recent evidence demonstrates that severe injury in older adults is associated with prolonged risks of mortality and institutionalization, highlighting the importance of long-term functional outcomes such as ageing in place. While current trauma care models primarily emphasize physical recovery and frailty status, emerging research suggests that cognitive processing, psychological resilience, and emotional regulation also play significant roles in recovery trajectories among older patients. Studies on cognitive frailty indicate strong associations with mortality, disability, and fall risk, while longitudinal findings after hip fracture show that depressive symptoms and cognitive status influence frailty progression over time. Furthermore, resilience has been consistently linked to successful ageing across physical and psychosocial domains. Integrating medical psychology perspectives into geriatric trauma pathways-through early psychological screening, cognitive-support interventions, and resilience-oriented rehabilitation-may help improve long-term independence and community dwelling among older trauma survivors. A biopsychosocial extension of current trauma care models is therefore warranted to optimize outcomes in ageing populations following severe injury.

titre: Comparison of the effects of artificial intelligence, virtual reality, and traditional balance training programs on balance and gait in older adults.
titre_fr: Comparison of the effects of artificial intelligence, virtual reality, and traditional balance training programs on balance and gait in older adults.
auteurs: Yousefi Babadi Saeed, Norasteh Ali Asghar, Shamsi Majelan Ali
resume: With ageing, the ability to maintain balance and gait declines, leading to falls and reduced independence. This trial compared an AI-generated, human-delivered exercise program (ChatGPT-4o), a virtual reality (VR) exergaming program, and a traditional balance (TB) training program on balance and gait in older adults residing in retirement homes. In this stratified, parallel-group, randomised controlled trial, 48 older adults aged 60-75 years were allocated 1:1:1 to VR (Xbox Kinect; n = 16), AI (ChatGPT-4o-generated program; n = 16), or TB (n = 16). All groups completed 60-min sessions, three times per week for 8 weeks, with a 2-month follow-up. Balance, mobility, balance confidence, gait speed, cadence, Gait Stability Ratio (GSR), and usability (System Usability Scale, SUS) were assessed at all three time points. All groups improved significantly over time (p < .001); group × time interactions were significant for all outcomes (ηp2 = .195-.631) except ABC (p = .063 after Greenhouse-Geisser correction). VR and AI produced greater gait-speed gains than TB (both p < .001, no VR-AI difference); VR produced the largest cadence gains and AI the largest GSR reduction. Usability was excellent for VR (SUS 82.4) and good for the instructor-delivered AI program (74.6). No adverse events occurred. AI-, VR-, and traditional balance training can each improve balance and gait in older adults, while technology-assisted programs provide additional gait benefits, supporting more personalised, hybrid rehabilitation approaches. IRCT20181113041645N2 (May 18 2025).

titre: Case Report: Electroencephalography-informed low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the supplementary motor area in severe functional movement disorder.
titre_fr: Case Report: Electroencephalography-informed low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the supplementary motor area in severe functional movement disorder.
auteurs: Takahashi Chiaki, Asahi Takashi, Kanda Motoki, Ohta Yoshihiko, Matsushita Isao
resume: Functional movement disorder (FMD) is increasingly being recognized as a condition associated with abnormal brain network connectivity; however, effective treatment strategies remain limited. We report the case of a patient with severe FMD that developed following an occupational injury and was characterized by functional tremors accompanied by migraines and prominent autonomic symptoms. Based on electroencephalography (EEG) network analysis, low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the supplementary motor area was administered, followed by staged rehabilitation incorporating visual feedback. The combined intervention reduced tremors and improved gait speed, activities of daily living, and EEG network connectivity. This case highlights the potential utility of combining EEG-guided neuromodulation with staged rehabilitation for the treatment of FMD and supports further investigation of this approach.

titre: Edentulism and functional disability in older adults: A longitudinal and cross-national study in England, the United States, and India.
titre_fr: Edentulism and functional disability in older adults: A longitudinal and cross-national study in England, the United States, and India.
auteurs: Tang Wanqi, He Libang, Zhang Min, Li Jiyao
resume: Edentulism may contribute to functional disability in older adults, yet cross-national evidence combining multiple analytic strategies and mechanistic assessment remains limited. This study examined the association between edentulism and disability in activities of daily living (ADL) and instrumental activities of daily living (IADL) across England, the United States, and India. We analyzed harmonized data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA; n = 9,102), the Health and Retirement Study (HRS; n = 22,156), and the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (LASI; n = 31,816) for adults aged 60 years or older. Cross-sectional associations were estimated using inverse probability weighting (IPW) and augmented IPW. Longitudinal Cox proportional hazards models were applied in ELSA and HRS. Mediation through grip strength, body mass index (BMI), and depressive symptoms was assessed with counterfactual causal mediation analysis on the risk-difference scale. Edentulism was associated with higher odds of ADL (pooled odds ratio 1.30, 95% confidence interval 1.20-1.42) and IADL disability (1.27, 1.11-1.45). Longitudinal analyses confirmed elevated hazard ratios for incident ADL (1.19, 1.09-1.30) and IADL disability (1.30, 1.19-1.43). Grip strength accounted for the largest proportion mediated (approximately 50% in ELSA and HRS, and 5-14% in LASI); BMI and depressive symptoms showed little mediation. In LASI, denture use among edentulous participants was associated with lower disability odds. Edentulism was consistently associated with functional disability across three countries, with grip strength partially accounting for this association, although the cross-sectional design precludes establishing temporality. Oral rehabilitation may partly buffer this risk and merits further prospective investigation.

titre: Meaning of work: Perception of employment among veterans with substance use disorders.
titre_fr: Meaning of work: Perception of employment among veterans with substance use disorders.
auteurs: Mugoya George Ct, Mumba Mercy N, Leghari Fatima A, Mudathir Dhikrullah, Owolabi Babatunde, Granger Teresa, Davis Lori L
resume: BackgroundEmployment plays a significant role among veterans including facilitating their transition into the civilian society and is an important indicator of treatment progression for veterans presenting with substance use issues. While the Veterans Health Administration has instituted programs aimed at increasing employment outcomes among veterans, unemployment continues to be a significant problem among veterans presenting with substance use disorders (SUDs) in the United States.ObjectiveThe present study explored the perception and experience of work among veterans with a substance use history with a goal of understanding the complex meanings participants ascribe to employment.MethodsThe study utilized a qualitative research design. 25 veterans with self-identified history of substance use participated in the study.ResultsFour overarching themes were identified through thematic analysis: (a) source of economic support and independence, (b) provides structure, purpose and sense of accomplishment, (c) contribute to society and social connection, and (d) consequences of drug use on employment.ConclusionOverall, our findings indicate that despite the high unemployment rates among veterans with SUD, they are conscious of the benefits associated with being employed, which transcends the conventional role of employment as a mere source of income. Rehabilitation counselors and other professionals involved in the care for veterans with SUD should utilize an integrative treatment approach to care that includes employment as a critical component of recovery.

titre: Motivations of nurses who re-entered during the COVID-19 pandemic to either stay or leave nursing practice: A follow-up interview study.
titre_fr: Motivations of nurses who re-entered during the COVID-19 pandemic to either stay or leave nursing practice: A follow-up interview study.
auteurs: Arts Aafke P M, Francke Anneke L, Noorland Sofie A
revue: International journal of nursing studies advances
resume: During the COVID-19 pandemic, former nurses were encouraged to return to the nursing profession to ease pressure on the healthcare system. Retaining re-entering nurses in the long term would offer an opportunity to mitigate the persistent nursing shortages. To provide insights into the motivations of nurses in the Netherlands who re-entered nursing during the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic to either remain in or leave nursing again. A qualitative research design using semi-structured interviews. The study was conducted in the Netherlands at various healthcare settings, including hospitals, nursing homes, rehabilitation centres, home care, COVID-19 units, and public health vaccination sites. Nurses who had re-entered nursing during the COVID-19 pandemic participated in this follow-up study. Thirteen individual semi-structured interviews were conducted in 2025. Verbatim interview transcripts were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The re-entering nurses were categorised into two groups: three 'stayers', who were still working in nursing in 2025, and 10 'leavers', who had left nursing again. For stayers, the following main themes emerged from the analysis: a meaningful job, professional development opportunities combined with favourable working conditions, and support from managers and employers. For leavers, the main themes identified were: lack of professional development opportunities, unfavourable working conditions, lack of support from employers and managers, limited professional autonomy and recognition, and the intensive trajectory for re-registration for registered nurses. Most motivations of re-entering nurses to either remain in or leave nursing reflected broader challenges affecting nurse retention. Addressing these challenges may help to retain re-entering nurses.

titre: Unveiling the potential of needle knife therapy for post-stroke spastic hemiparesis: a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
titre_fr: Unveiling the potential of needle knife therapy for post-stroke spastic hemiparesis: a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
auteurs: Hu ZeHao, Li Haoyang, Huang Qiuxuan, Li Zhanxin
resume: Post-stroke spastic hemiparesis is a common and disabling complication after stroke. It is associated with impaired motor function and activity limitation, and it places a substantial long-term burden on patients, families and health services. Needle knife, also known as acupotomy, is a minimally invasive technique that uses a blade-tipped needle and is widely used in China; it is intended to release soft-tissue adhesions and reduce abnormal muscle tone, with the aim of improving limb function. However, the effectiveness and safety of needle knife for post-stroke spastic hemiparesis have not been systematically evaluated. This protocol describes the methods for a systematic review and meta-analysis that will assess the efficacy and safety of needle knife treatment for post-stroke spastic hemiparesis. The following electronic databases will be searched from inception to 1 August 2026: CINAHL, MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, the Allied and Complementary Medicine Database, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Chinese Biomedical Literature Database, VIP Database and Wanfang Database. Randomised controlled trials evaluating needle knife alone or needle knife combined with routine rehabilitation for post-stroke spastic hemiparesis will be included. The primary outcomes will be spasticity measured by the Modified Ashworth Scale and the Clinical Spasticity Index. Secondary outcomes will include motor function measured by the Fugl-Meyer Assessment, muscle strength measured by Manual Muscle Testing, activities of daily living, quality of life and adverse events. Two reviewers will independently screen records, extract data and assess risk of bias using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool. Review Manager V.5.4 or later will be used for data synthesis. Risk ratios with 95% CIs will be calculated for dichotomous outcomes. Mean differences or standardised mean differences with 95% CIs will be calculated for continuous outcomes. Heterogeneity will be assessed using the χ<sup>2</sup> test and I<sup>2</sup> statistic. When meta-analysis is not appropriate, a structured narrative synthesis will be performed. The certainty of evidence will be evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. CRD42023464211.

titre: Safety and Efficacy of Anodal transcranial direct-current stimulation over the Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex in Post-Stroke Cognitive Impairment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
titre_fr: Safety and Efficacy of Anodal transcranial direct-current stimulation over the Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex in Post-Stroke Cognitive Impairment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
auteurs: Li Song, Huo Hong, Li Dongxia, Li Wenqiang, Hu Yunzhe, Wang Ao, Li Jingyi, Liu Yue, Wang Dongyan
resume: This meta-analysis evaluated the safety and efficacy of anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) over the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) for post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI). Eight databases were searched from inception to June 7, 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment using the revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool. Meta-analyses were conducted using Stata version 18, with subgroups stratified by control type and stimulation site. Twenty-three RCTs involving 1326 participants were included. Anodal tDCS over the DLPFC significantly improved global cognitive screening performance: Clinical Efficacy (odds ratio [OR] = 1.37, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.01-1.85, P =0.043), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score (weighted mean difference [WMD] = 3.17, 95% CI: 2.53-3.80, P = 0.000), and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score (WMD = 2.52, 95% CI: 1.81-3.22, P = 0.001). Subgroup analyses demonstrated superiority of active tDCS regardless of control condition: rehabilitation therapy (RT) plus sham tDCS (MoCA: WMD = 2.45, 95% CI: 1.60-3.30; MMSE: WMD = 2.40, 95% CI: 0.97-3.83) and RT alone (MoCA: WMD = 3.47, 95% CI: 2.81-4.12; MMSE: WMD = 2.72, 95% CI: 2.12-3.32). Benefits were also consistent across stimulation of the affected hemisphere (MoCA: WMD = 2.88, 95% CI: 2.05-3.71; MMSE: WMD = 2.59, 95% CI: 1.50-3.68) and the left hemisphere (MoCA: WMD = 3.42, 95% CI: 2.47-4.38; MMSE: WMD = 2.48, 95% CI: 1.45-3.51). Activities of daily living (ADL) measured by the Modified Barthel Index (MBI) also improved significantly (WMD = 10.75, 95% CI: 8.67-12.84, P = 0.000), with benefits maintained across all subgroups: RT plus sham tDCS (WMD = 11.18, 95% CI: 8.76-13.60), RT alone (WMD = 10.49, 95% CI: 7.67-13.32), affected hemisphere (WMD = 11.37, 95% CI: 7.83-14.91), and left hemisphere (WMD = 10.06, 95% CI: 8.00-12.13). Safety outcomes were infrequently reported. Anodal tDCS over the DLPFC may improve global cognitive screening performance and ADL in PSCI patients, yet low methodological quality and inadequate safety reporting limit the current evidence. Further high-quality RCTs with rigorous adverse event monitoring are warranted.

titre: Levodopa or dopamine agonists for enhancing motor function after stroke.
titre_fr: Levodopa or dopamine agonists for enhancing motor function after stroke.
auteurs: Jauslin Andrea S, Boos Lukas, Hirt Julian, Altersberger Valerian, Ewald Hannah, Kaufmann Josefin Emelie, Speich Benjamin, Hemkens Lars G, Traenka Christopher, Engelter Stefan T
revue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
resume: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide. There is a lack of evidence regarding pharmacological enhancement of stroke recovery with dopamine agonists or levodopa, in particular in terms of motor deficits. To assess the effects of dopaminergic agents, defined as levodopa or dopamine agonists, on improving motor function after stroke. We conducted an extensive database search on the Cochrane Stroke Group trials register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Science Citation Index Expanded, CPCI-S, BIOSIS Citation Index, ProQuest Dissertation and Theses Global up to November 2025. We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that enrolled participants with a clinical diagnosis of stroke, irrespective of age or stroke aetiology and without a pre-existing indication for the use of levodopa or dopamine agonists. Eligible trials compared levodopa or dopamine agonists with a comparator group who received placebo or no medication, with equivalent rehabilitative care in both groups, and aimed at enhancing motor function after stroke. Motor function was the critical benefit outcome. As a critical harm outcome, we assessed serious adverse events. Important outcomes consisted of death, recurrent stroke, disability, dependence, health-related quality of life, activities of daily living, total number of adverse events, and psychiatric adverse events. Two review authors independently assessed the risk of bias for each trial using the Cochrane Risk of bias tool (RoB 1). We synthesised results for each outcome using a standardised mean difference (SMD) or mean difference (MD) for continuous data and risk ratio (RR) for dichotomous results, with a random-effects model due to heterogeneity between the trials. For non-extractable trials due to missing numerical data, we synthesised the results narratively. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence for each outcome. We included 12 parallel-group RCTs involving 1860 participants. The trials were conducted in Europe, the USA and Asia, and were published between 2001 and 2025. All trials included participants with either ischaemic strokes only or both haemorrhagic and ischaemic strokes. The mean age of all included participants ranged from 55 to 78 years. Of the included trials, 10 were placebo-controlled and two compared levodopa or dopamine agonists against usual care. Eleven trials investigated levodopa as the intervention and one examined the dopamine agonist ropinirole. Across 12 included trials, complete data on motor function were available for six trials with continuous data (1258 participants) and for two trials with dichotomous data (615 participants), of which one trial assessed both continuous and dichotomous data. We detected no difference in motor function scores between levodopa or dopamine agonists and the comparator groups for continuous outcomes (SMD 1.42, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.20 to 3.05; 6 trials, 1258 participants; very low-certainty evidence). The wide confidence intervals indicate substantial imprecision in the effect estimate. Consistent with those results, we detected no difference for dichotomous motor function outcomes either (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.82 to 1.06; 2 trials, 615 participants; anticipated absolute event rate of having a favourable outcome of 581/1000 in the comparator group versus 540/1000 with levodopa/dopamine agonists; low-certainty evidence). Heterogeneity for the critical outcome motor function (continuously measured) was high (I<sup>2</sup> = 99%). However, a sensitivity analysis including only two trials with a low risk of bias in all domains, that accounted for the majority of the included patient population (1025 of 1258), showed no heterogeneity (I<sup>2</sup> = 0%), and a smaller confidence interval (SMD 0.02, 95% CI -0.10 to 0.14; 2 trials, 1025 participants), implying no difference between groups. Six trials assessed serious adverse events, including 1281 participants. There was no notable difference in the risk of serious adverse events between groups (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.83 to 1.27; anticipated absolute event rate of 302/1000 events in comparators versus 311/1000 events with levodopa/dopamine agonists; low-certainty evidence). All important outcomes showed no notable between-group differences. The certainty of evidence, according to GRADE, was very low for continuously measured scores of motor function, low for dichotomous motor function outcomes, and low for serious adverse events. Together with heterogeneity in both interventions and outcomes, inconsistency of findings, imprecision related to small sample sizes in some trials, and imprecision of summary effect, there are major limitations of the current evidence. Based on limited data, we did not find evidence that the use of levodopa or dopamine agonists improves motor function after a stroke. Given the low certainty of evidence due to limited data, wide confidence intervals, and heterogeneity across trials, further research may change this assessment and explore whether effects are different in specific subgroups of patients. Science funds [Wissenschaftsfonds] Department of Rehabilitation and Neurology, University Department of Geriatric Medicine, Felix Platter, University of Basel, Switzerland. This review had no external funding. Protocol available via https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD013416.

titre: Minimal important change (MIC) for the Clinical Functioning Information Tool (ClinFIT) in inpatient rehabilitation.
titre_fr: Minimal important change (MIC) for the Clinical Functioning Information Tool (ClinFIT) in inpatient rehabilitation.
auteurs: Martinez-De la Torre Adrian, Amatya Bhasker, Mukaino Masahiko, Selb Melissa, Stucki Gerold, Khan Fary
resume: To estimate the Minimal Important Change (MIC) for the Clinical Functioning Information Tool (ClinFIT) in inpatient rehabilitation. Admission and discharge ClinFIT scores were analyzed in a Royal Melbourne Hospital inpatient rehabilitation cohort. Anchors were the Functional Independence Measure (FIM), EQ-5D-5L index, and EQ visual analog scale (EQ-VAS). Anchor-based analyses included receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, within-patient mean change, and between-group contrasts. Distribution-based reference values were calculated as 0.2 and 0.5 times the baseline ClinFIT SD and 0.2 times the change-score SD. Among 257 patients, mean age was 63.0 years and 54.5% were male. ClinFIT scores improved from 167.0 (SD 59.2) at admission to 97.7 (SD 57.8) at discharge. ClinFIT change correlated most strongly with EQ-5D-5L index change (ρ = -0.68), compared with FIM (ρ = -0.31) and EQ-VAS (ρ = -0.32). ROC-derived thresholds ranged from -77 to -43 points, between-group differences from -76 to -20 points, and distribution-based reference values from -29.7 to -10.3 points. An exploratory range of approximately 50-70 points was proposed based primarily on the ROC-derived thresholds. The EQ-5D-5L-supported ClinFIT MIC threshold indicated a reduction of approximately 57 points, with a wide confidence interval. ROC-derived thresholds informed an exploratory 50-70-point range.

titre: Electromyography biofeedback therapy for spinal cord injury rehabilitation: a systematic review.
titre_fr: Electromyography biofeedback therapy for spinal cord injury rehabilitation: a systematic review.
auteurs: Liu Ming-Wei, Liu Zhong-Yuan, Zhang Bing-Can, Gao Shu-Ji, Peng Hui-de
resume: Electromyographic biofeedback (EMG-BF) is being increasingly used as an adjunct to rehabilitation after spinal cord injury (SCI), but the available evidence is limited by the small sample size, heterogeneous comparators, and variable outcome reporting. We aimed to systematically identify and narratively synthesize the evidence on the effects of EMG-BF in SCI rehabilitation. We searched the PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP and other databases from inception to 8 January 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data and assessed the risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity and inconsistent outcome-data types, we did not pool effect estimates; instead, we performed a structured synthesis without meta-analysis (SWiM) and graded the certainty of evidence using GRADE. Ten randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving 537 participants were included. All 10 studies reported a favorable direction of effect for EMG-BF, but the evidence for every outcome was of low or very low certainty. Across the five RCTs reporting surface electromyography (sEMG), all reported larger signal amplitudes in the EMG-BF arm, although the outcome data types varied (means vs. medians) and the muscle sites and comparators differed. Two RCTs reported greater lower-limb muscle strength with EMG-BF. One RCT reported a higher functional independence measure score, and two reported higher ASIA motor scores with the use of the EMG-BF. Four RCTs reported reduced spasticity (modified Ashworth scale, MAS), but MAS was reported inconsistently as ordinal grade distributions or as grade-derived scores, precluding any pooled estimate. Three RCTs reported higher Berg balance scale scores with the use of the EMG-BF. Only one pilot RCT reported pain, and it permitted only within-group comparisons. Low- to very-low-certainty evidence suggests that EMG-BF may improve sEMG signals, lower-limb muscle strength, functional independence, ASIA motor scores, spasticity and balance in patients with SCI, but these findings are preliminary. Large, well-designed RCTs with allocation concealment, blinding of outcome assessors, standardized comparators and prospective registration are needed. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261282923, Identifier: [CRD420261282923].

titre: Independence in activities of daily living for home-based geriatric rehabilitation after shortened inpatient rehabilitation: the "Better@Home" center prospective cohort study with a matched historical control group.
titre_fr: Independence in activities of daily living for home-based geriatric rehabilitation after shortened inpatient rehabilitation: the "Better@Home" center prospective cohort study with a matched historical control group.
auteurs: Gamble C J, Vaz M, de Waal M W M, Groen W G, Pol M C, van Dam van Isselt E F, Innocenti F, Zwakhalen S M G, van Haastregt J C M
resume: Population aging is increasing the demand for geriatric rehabilitation (GR). A transition towards home-based GR could potentially reduce the need for inpatient GR and better align rehabilitation with daily functioning at home. The aim of this study is to compare the level of independence in activities of daily living between patients receiving the "Better@Home" program and those undergoing conventional inpatient geriatric rehabilitation. The Better@Home study is a multicenter prospective cohort study with a matched historical control group. Eight GR facilities in the Netherlands implemented the Better@Home program, which is a five-component intervention in which home-based GR replaces part of inpatient GR. Data was gathered at GR admission and discharge through semi-structured interviews, registration forms, and electronic patient files. The Better@Home group was compared with a matched historical control group receiving conventional inpatient GR on independence in activities of daily living (ADL), assessed by the Barthel Index (BI). Data was analyzed using a Cox and linear mixed-effects (LMM) regression model. A total of 350 participants were included (Better@Home n = 110; control n = 240). Groups were comparable on all characteristics at baseline. The LMM analysis found no significant difference between the Better@Home and the control group on independence in ADL at discharge (mean BI difference: 0.48 points, 95% CI -0.323-1.282; p = 0.240). This study demonstrates that a structured home-based GR program, replacing part of inpatient GR, can achieve comparable levels of independence in activities of daily living to conventional inpatient GR.

titre_fr: Acute Care and Rehabilitation After Low-Trauma Hip Fractures in Older Adults-Pathways and Functional Outcomes: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
auteurs: Cioffi Eva, Müller Karl, Ivanova Silviya, Fava Altes Albert Antoni, Pfister Manuel, Frischknecht Valerie, Angelva Noora Emilia, Marcin Thimo, Wilhelm Matthias, Martinez-De la Torre Adrian, Nef Tobias, Bastian Johannes Dominik, Scheel-Sailer Anke
resume: Background/Objectives: This study describes, first, healthcare pathways, including inpatient rehabilitation, and, second, functional outcomes for these low-trauma hip fracture (LTHF) types (femoral neck (FN-F), trochanteric (Tr-F), and acetabulum/periprosthetic (Ac/Pp-F) fractures). Methods: This single-center, retrospective cohort study, 2020-2023, included patients aged ≥65 years, with FN-F, Tr-F, or Ac/Pp-F, admitted to inpatient rehabilitation. Pathways comprised acute care, inpatient rehabilitation, and temporary care homes, bounded by pre-fracture situation and discharge destination. Pairwise Standardized Mean Differences (SMDs) were calculated to determine between-group differences. Results: Of 294 individuals (mean age 81.0 ± 7.4 years; 191 (65%) women; 152 Tr-F, 118 FN-F, and 24 Ac/Pp-F), four main pathways were identified: (1) acute care to inpatient rehabilitation in 208 (70.7%) individuals, (2) temporary care home stays before rehabilitation in 25 (8.5%), (3) temporary care home stays after rehabilitation in 17 (5.8%), and (4) re-hospitalization in 44 (15.0%). Median pathway length was 33.0 days (IQR 26.0-40.0) for FN-F, 35.0 (IQR 29.0-46.0) for Tr-F, and 60.5 (IQR 37.0-86.5) for Ac/Pp-F. Between-group differences in pathway type were moderate to large (SMDs: FN-F vs. Tr-F = 0.47; FN-F vs. Ac/Pp-F = 1.25; Tr-F vs. Ac/Pp-F = 0.84), and for length, small to large (SMDs: FN-F vs. Tr-F = 0.36; FN-F vs. Ac/Pp-F = 1.2; Tr-F vs. Ac/Pp-F = 0.69). Overall, 246 (83.7%) returned to a permanent private living setting. A total of 88 (29.9%) required new or increased home support or care. At discharge from rehabilitation, among participants who completed the program, the Functional Independence Measure and the Timed Up and Go test showed small-to-moderate between-group differences. Conclusions: Individuals with FN-F, Tr-F, and Ac/Pp-F fractures follow healthcare pathways in different frequencies and have different pathway durations. The findings may support the identification of future opportunities to improve continuity of healthcare, including orthogeriatric management and specialized rehabilitation.

titre: Peripheral Nerve Conduction Abnormalities and Their Association with Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Unilateral Hemiplegia Secondary to Stroke.
titre_fr: Peripheral Nerve Conduction Abnormalities and Their Association with Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Unilateral Hemiplegia Secondary to Stroke.
auteurs: Özgözen Selen, Doruk Analan Pınar
resume: Background/Objectives: Peripheral nerve conduction abnormalities may occur after stroke, but their clinical relevance in chronic hemiplegia remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize these abnormalities and examine their associations with motor and functional outcomes. Methods: This single-center, cross-sectional observational study included 72 patients with unilateral hemiplegia ≥ 6 months after ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke. Bilateral lower-extremity nerve conduction studies (NCS) were performed in all participants. In participants without findings suggestive of distal symmetric polyneuropathy (DSP), bilateral upper-extremity NCS were also performed to assess focal entrapment neuropathies; when DSP was suspected from lower-extremity findings, one upper extremity was examined to confirm upper-extremity involvement. Clinical assessments included the Fugl-Meyer Assessment, Functional Independence Measure, Timed Up and Go test, and computerized posturographic fall-risk assessment. Associations between NCS findings and clinical outcomes were examined using adjusted regression analyses. Results: Mean age was 61.75 ± 12.56 years, and stroke duration was 42.85 ± 38.14 months. Normal NCS findings were present in 18 (25.0%) patients. Most participants (86.1%) had high posturographic fall-risk. DSP was identified in 38 participants (52.8%). The most frequent focal neuropathy was median nerve entrapment at the wrist (17/72, 23.6%). DSP was more frequent in participants with diabetes than in those without diabetes (85.7% vs. 31.8%; p < 0.001). Ulnar sensory nerve action potential amplitude was lower on the paretic side (adjusted p = 0.028). Neither DSP nor median nerve entrapment was significantly associated with motor function, functional mobility, or functional independence in adjusted analyses; posturographic fall-risk classifications also did not differ according to these NCS findings in unadjusted exact tests. Conclusions: Peripheral nerve conduction abnormalities, particularly DSP and median nerve entrapment, were common in ambulatory individuals with chronic post-stroke hemiplegia. Despite their frequency, no statistically significant associations with motor or functional performance were identified, although clinically meaningful associations cannot be excluded.

titre: Comparing Nerve Transfer Versus Tendon Transfer and Conservative Management for Restoring Finger Extension Following Tetraplegia: A Cost-Effectiveness Analysis.
titre_fr: Comparing Nerve Transfer Versus Tendon Transfer and Conservative Management for Restoring Finger Extension Following Tetraplegia: A Cost-Effectiveness Analysis.
auteurs: Arunachalam Sakthiyendran Naveen, Cushman Caroline J, Hernandez Evan J, Mackay Brendan J
resume: Background/Objectives: Cervical spinal cord injury (SCI) frequently causes tetraplegia and severe upper-limb dysfunction with substantial societal cost. Restoring finger extension is a priority, since even modest gains improve independence. Tendon transfer and supinator-to-posterior interosseous nerve transfer (SUP-PIN) both restore hand function, but their relative economic value is unclear. We assessed the lifetime cost-effectiveness of SUP-PIN versus tendon transfer and conservative management for finger extension in patients with mid-cervical SCIs who are candidates for both reconstructive strategies. Methods: A decision-analytic model combining a decision-tree front end with a lifetime Markov state-transition structure (one-year cycles, 3% annual discounting, half-cycle correction) compared SUP-PIN, tendon transfer, and conservative (nonoperative) care over a lifetime horizon, incorporating direct medical costs and indirect productivity losses. The outcomes were quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) accumulated over the horizon, using a willingness-to-pay threshold of $100,000/QALY. Success, complication, recovery, and return-to-work probabilities were drawn from the published literature. Deterministic, probabilistic, and two-way sensitivity analyses assessed robustness. Results: From the healthcare-sector perspective, conservative management was the least costly ($630.48; 14.84 QALYs) but least effective; nerve transfer was the most effective (18.55 QALYs) at $6485.84 and dominated tendon transfer, with an ICER versus conservative management of $1579/QALY, well below the $100,000/QALY threshold. From the societal perspective, nerve transfer was dominant, with the lowest lifetime cost ($903,937) and the highest effectiveness. Across the sensitivity analyses, nerve transfer was preferred under nearly all assumptions; tendon transfer was preferred only with ≥90% tendon success combined with ≤40% nerve-transfer success. Conclusions: In this decision-analytic model, SUP-PIN nerve transfer was projected to be economically favorable, yielding greater modeled effectiveness and lower lifetime costs than tendon transfer and conservative care under the stated assumptions. These modeled findings support further evaluation of nerve transfer in post-SCI rehabilitation algorithms and timely surgical referrals but do not, by themselves, establish clinical superiority, which requires a prospective comparative study.

titre: Neuro-behavioural modulatory and bio-disinfectant effects of standardised Peganum harmala L. extract on incubation performance and neonatal welfare in quail.
titre_fr: Neuro-behavioural modulatory and bio-disinfectant effects of standardised Peganum harmala L. extract on incubation performance and neonatal welfare in quail.
auteurs: Dogan E, Taskin A
resume: 1. The following study investigated the effects of a standardised Peganum harmala L. (PH) extract on post-hatch behaviour, environmental adaptation, incubation performance and eggshell disinfection in Japanese quail (Coturnix japonica).2. A total of 520 fertile eggs were utilised in the experiment, with 130 eggs randomly assigned to each of the four treatment groups: distilled water (P1), ethanol (P2), 1% PH extract (P3) or 5% PH extract (P4) appliedviaactive humidification on d 1, 3, 7 and 14 of incubation. Analysis by GC-MS was used to identify peganine and quinazoline alkaloids as the primary bioactive components of the PH extract.3. Behavioural assessments (Open Field and Runway tests) showed shorter behavioural latency and enhanced exploratory behaviour in chicks exposed to PH extract compared with controls.4. Microbial analysis showed that the 5% extract (P4) achieved the lowest bacterial load on day 10 compared with P1 (p < 0.05). The eggs in the P4 group had the highest fertile hatchability and chick quality scores among the treatment groups.5. Standardised PH extract represents a promising botanical disinfectant associated with favourable behavioural outcomes in newly hatched chicks, with potential applications for hatchery management.

titre: Integrated omics analyses reveal the environmental adaptation mechanisms of Ctenopharyngodon idella to saline water via salinity programming.
titre_fr: Integrated omics analyses reveal the environmental adaptation mechanisms of Ctenopharyngodon idella to saline water via salinity programming.
auteurs: Lei Caixia, Lan Xin, Song Hongmei, Du Jinxin, Zhu Tao, Tian Jing, Li Shengjie
revue: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part D, Genomics & proteomics
resume: Saline aquaculture can utilize underused saline water resources while alleviating freshwater aquaculture pressure, boosting food supply, and supporting ecological restoration. This study conducted environmental salinity programming on fertilized Ctenopharyngodon idella eggs to explore the adaptive mechanisms in response to high-salinity aquatic stress via transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling. The results showed that early environmental salinity programming improves the high-salinity tolerance of juvenile C. idella by remodeling energy supply, osmoregulation, immunity, and antioxidant defense capacity. Intestine uses mRNA surveillance, PPAR signaling, and insulin signaling pathways to respond to salinity programming, with pdchd3, fms, rnase, and fgf21 identified as core genes. These genes relieve salinity-induced damage by regulating indole-3-acetamide, anthranilic acid, and penicilloic acid accumulation through tryptophan metabolism, folate biosynthesis, and penicillin and cephalosporin biosynthesis. In comparison, gill differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were mainly enriched in arachidonic acid metabolism, cardiac muscle contraction, and virion-adenovirus pathways, with oma1 and ph4ha2 as key genes modulated N-palmitoylsphingosine, vinblastine, and L-glutathione levels to strengthen C. idella immunity against high-salinity stress. Seven shared genes (h1.10, 18 s rRNA, ivlg1, vsig8a, serpinf1, pdk4, phlda2) involved in genetic virion-adenovirus pathway, together with one metabolite (anthranilic acid) involved in metabolic tryptophan metabolism pathway, jointly mediated the environmental adaptive response in the two tissues. Notably, the gene-metabolite pair pdk4-anthranilic acid showed a remarkable correlation with salinity adaptation. These findings provide a mechanistic framework whereby early salinity programming remodels the environmental plasticity of C. idella at both transcriptional and metabolic levels, offering theoretical support for the saline-alkali water exploitation and the aquatic ecosystem remediation.

titre: EquIPP-AT: a framework proposition for examining equity and inclusion in assistive technology assessment.
titre_fr: EquIPP-AT: a framework proposition for examining equity and inclusion in assistive technology assessment.
auteurs: Beckett Angharad E, Encarnação Pedro, Smith Emma M
resume: Assistive technology (AT) assessment shapes access to products, services and supports. Although discussed as a clinical, technical and user-centred process, it has been less systematically examined as an equity and inclusion process. This article proposes EquIPP-AT, a provisional AT-specific adaptation of the Equity and Inclusion in Policy Processes framework. This first-stage development adapts EquIPP to AT assessment through evidence synthesis and expert judgement, informed by AT service delivery and outcome literature, Critical Disability Studies, epistemic injustice, the capabilities approach, and comparison with EquiFrame and ARISE. Cases from Norway and Brazil and donation-mediated wheelchair provision in Kenya and the Philippines are used illustratively across provision contexts. EquIPP-AT is organised across three analytical levels: assessment governance and rules, assessment practices, and lived experience of assessment. It applies nine equity dimensions: participation and involvement; individual needs and circumstances; accessibility and reasonable adjustments; leadership, governance and accountability; data, evidence and monitoring; organisational commitment and culture; experiential expertise and co-production; communication and influence; and partnership and collaboration. Four contextual axes are identified: structural variation, marginality and precarity, cultural-epistemic difference, and temporality. It applies across professional-led, peer-supported, collaborative, commercial and self-directed assessment routes. EquIPP-AT is a provisional analytical framework, not a validated instrument. It supports systematic inquiry into how AT assessment processes include, exclude, recognise, constrain or enable AT users. Its levels, dimensions and axes remain propositions requiring testing and refinement through consultation and participatory development with AT users and Disabled People's Organisations, followed by empirical piloting across contrasting contexts.

titre: Massilia danxiaensis sp. nov., a novel bacterium isolated from red sandy conglomerate of Danxia Mountain with an experimentally supported complete tryptophan biosynthesis pathway.
titre_fr: Massilia danxiaensis sp. nov., a novel bacterium isolated from red sandy conglomerate of Danxia Mountain with an experimentally supported complete tryptophan biosynthesis pathway.
auteurs: Sun Ming-Man, He Huan-Huan, Guo Dan-Yuan, Han Jia-Rui, Hu Chao-Jian, Chen Fang, Zhou Ting, She Ting-Ting, Lin Hai-Wei, Fang Su-Qin, Li Wen-Jun, Dong Lei
resume: Strain SYSU DXS3249<sup>T</sup> was obtained from a sandy conglomerate sample originating from the red-bed geological formation of Danxia Mountain, PR China. The isolate is an aerobic, Gram-stain-negative bacterium that grows at pH 6.0-9.0 (optimum, pH 7.0), 15-37 °C (optimum, 28 °C), and in the presence of 0-1% NaCl (w/v; optimum 0%). Phylogenetic analyses based on 16S rRNA gene sequences and core genome datasets placed the strain within the genus Massilia, exhibiting highest 16S rRNA gene similarity to Massilia suwonensis CGMCC 1.12743<sup> T</sup> (98.8%), followed by Massilia haematophila CCUG 38318<sup> T</sup> (98.3%). The genomic DNA G + C content was 65.8%. The respiratory quinone of strain SYSU DXS3249<sup>T</sup> was Q-8. The polar lipid profile consisted mainly of phosphatidylglycerol, diphosphatidylglycerol and phosphatidylethanolamine, and the major cellular fatty acids (> 10%) were C<sub>16:0</sub>, C<sub>16:1</sub> ω7c and C<sub>16:1</sub> ω6c. Genomic analysis revealed a complete tryptophan biosynthesis module (M00023), and its functionality was experimentally supported by growth in M9 minimal medium without exogenous tryptophan. This trait may be ecologically relevant, as tryptophan is a precursor of auxin and other indole metabolites, and warrants future investigation of environmental adaptation and plant-microbe interactions. Based on the polyphasic characterization, strain SYSU DXS3249<sup>T</sup> represents a novel species of the genus Massilia, for which the name Massilia danxiaensis sp. nov. is proposed. The type strain of the proposed novel isolate is SYSU DXS3249<sup>T</sup> (= MCCC 1K09422<sup>T</sup> = KCTC 8716<sup> T</sup>).

titre: Genomic insights into environmental adaptation and metabolic versatility of Acinetobacter junii IK2 isolated from marine biofilm.
titre_fr: Genomic insights into environmental adaptation and metabolic versatility of Acinetobacter junii IK2 isolated from marine biofilm.
auteurs: Rajendran Thirugnanasambandam, Dhinakarasamy Inbakandan, Amith Vimal, Kumar Ragavendhar, Bhoopathy Subashni, Chandrasekar Anu, Varadharajan Ramesh Kumar, Louis Stanley Abraham, Sivaraj Aditya, Viswanathan Jeevankumaar, Baskaran Sabarish, Chandrasekaran Kumar
resume: Biofilm formation is ubiquitous in the marine environment, driven by microbial colonization on submerged surfaces, and poses ongoing challenges to maritime industries. In this study, whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was carried out for Acinetobacter junii IK2, a strain isolated from the biofilm formed on stainless steel coupons immersed in a seawater microcosm setup to elucidate its genomic features and biofilm-forming potential. The genome consists of 3,215,808 bp with a GC content of 38.63%, assembled from Illumina-generated sequencing data. A total of 2990 protein-coding sequences (CDS), 10 rRNA genes, and 63 tRNA genes were predicted. Functional annotation through COG, GO, and KEGG databases resulted in the classification of 2909, 2389, and 2960 unigenes, respectively. Genome analysis identified the presence of thirteen genes associated with biofilm development, including the pgaABC operon, two-component systems (barA, ompR), and global regulators (crp, csrA, dksA), suggesting potential for biofilm formation. Genes such as oxyR, yfiB, yiaD, and pal further support oxidative stress resistance, adhesion, and envelope stability. The biofilm-forming ability of Acinetobacter junii IK2 was further validated using a crystal violet microtiter plate assay, confirming its ability to form biofilms. Additionally, 35 virulence genes, 6 multidrug resistance genes and 25 insertion sequences suggest enhanced survival, pathogenicity and genetic plasticity, reinforcing biofilm-mediated persistence. These genomic features provide insights into potential adaptive mechanisms that may contribute to the environmental adaptation of A. junii IK2 and offer insights into its role in the marine environment.

Genome analysis identified the presence of thirteen genes associated with biofilm development, including the pgaABC operon, two-component systems (barA, ompR), and global regulators (crp, csrA, dksA), suggesting potential for biofilm formation. Genes such as oxyR, yfiB, yiaD, and pal further support oxidative stress resistance, adhesion, and envelope stability. The biofilm-forming ability of Acinetobacter junii IK2 was further validated using a crystal violet microtiter plate assay, confirming its ability to form biofilms. Additionally, 35 virulence genes, 6 multidrug resistance genes and 25 insertion sequences suggest enhanced survival, pathogenicity and genetic plasticity, reinforcing biofilm-mediated persistence. These genomic features provide insights into potential adaptive mechanisms that may contribute to the environmental adaptation of A. junii IK2 and offer insights into its role in the marine environment.

titre: The Fusion of AI and AT: The Demands of Inclusive Education vs the Possibilities of Technology.
titre_fr: The Fusion of AI and AT: The Demands of Inclusive Education vs the Possibilities of Technology.
auteurs: Boland Trevor
revue: Studies in health technology and informatics
resume: Universal Design works on the environment and curriculum from the outset, proactively removing barriers for everyone [1]. AI is emerging in the educational environment, and a recent Irish national policy focuses on Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Higher Education (HE). This AI policy links to a problem of practice (PoP) in my Assistive Technology (AT) role in HE. The fusion of AI and AT has raised issues that will be explored using the Bachi [2] 'What's the Problem Represented to Be' (WPR) thinking paradigm, which interrogates the governmental rationales that inform governing practices. This paradigm will explore how the presence of AI has created new possibilities for Students with Disabilities (SWDs), and emerging challenges are also evident. A WPR analysis will reveal the effects of an AI policy linked to my PoP, and the hindering and facilitating factors for its implementation and enactment, and any indicators of impact.

titre: From Function to Meaning: Co-Designing Bodily Extensions with Children with Congenital Upper Limb Difference. A Play-Based Participatory Approach to Identity, Agency, and Prosthetic Meaning Making.
titre_fr: From Function to Meaning: Co-Designing Bodily Extensions with Children with Congenital Upper Limb Difference. A Play-Based Participatory Approach to Identity, Agency, and Prosthetic Meaning Making.
auteurs: Kuźmiński Marek
revue: Studies in health technology and informatics
resume: Designing bodily extensions for children with Congenital Upper Limb Difference (CULD) requires attention not only to functional interaction but also to identity, agency, and lived social experience. While Universal and inclusive design frameworks provide important foundations for accessibility and participation, general design principles may not fully capture the highly situated, experiential, and imaginative perspectives involved in personalised assistive technologies for children. This paper presents a qualitative Research through Design study exploring a participatory, play-based approach [1,2] to co-designing upper-limb bodily extensions with children and their parents, followed by an exploratory development phase involving engineering collaborators. The study introduces a structured role-play framework positioning children as primary knowledge holders and decision-makers within the design process. Two 2.5-hour workshops were conducted in Katowice and Warsaw, Poland, involving 10 children aged 4-9 and 11 parents. Participants were recruited through the "In Our Hands" Facebook parent-support group for families of children with upper-limb differences. Across workshops conducted in Poland, children engaged in storytelling, drawing, role-play, and hands-on making to explore bodily extensions as part of their lived and imagined worlds. Findings suggest that structured role-play enabled children to integrate emotional, functional, and symbolic dimensions within unified design expressions, framing bodily extensions as identity-related and expressive artefacts rather than purely corrective tools. The approach also supported more reflective parental engagement and, during the subsequent engineering phase, provided collaborators with insights into the affective and social dimensions of children's assistive technology preferences. The study argues that bodily extensions can be understood as meaning-making artefacts that participate in identity construction. It proposes a participatory framework [1,2] that complements inclusive design through structured role-play, narrative framing, and child-led co-creation.

titre: Co-Designing a Transitional Co-Housing for People with Disabilities.
titre_fr: Co-Designing a Transitional Co-Housing for People with Disabilities.
auteurs: Salvador Elena, Montanari Carlo, Motolese Maria Rosaria, Hoogerwerf Evert-Jan, Mincolelli Giuseppe, Imbesi Silvia, Urbani Elisabetta, Malavasi Massimiliano
revue: Studies in health technology and informatics
resume: Transitional co-housing is an emerging model supporting the independent-living pathways of young adults with disabilities. Such facilities, however, often rely on standard accessibility compliance that addresses physical barriers while overlooking sensory, cognitive and behavioural needs. This paper presents the co-design methodology of CASA CARE, a publicly funded transitional residence in Calderara di Reno, Italy, where young adults with mild motor and/or cognitive disabilities prepare for autonomous living. Adopting a Universal Design approach, enacted through human-centred design, the project engaged social-health professionals, end users, family caregivers and companies across nine co-design workshops, adapting traditional co-design methods to improve accessibility for neurodiverse participants and beyond. Needs, insights, constraints and solutions were systematised through a traceable categorisation framework and translated into spatial, technological and service-model decisions informed by the ASPECTSS framework for neurodiversity. Usability tests assessed selected apps and devices with end users. The paper focuses on the methodology and its transferability, offering a replicable model that links universal design principles to technical specification and service-model development. In particular, it contributes a structured framework for translating stakeholder evidence into design decisions and demonstrates how co-design methods can be adapted to support the meaningful participation of neurodiverse users in housing projects.

titre: Beyond Housing Type: Rethinking Universal Design Through Affordable Retrofitting of Ageing Homes in India.
titre_fr: Beyond Housing Type: Rethinking Universal Design Through Affordable Retrofitting of Ageing Homes in India.
auteurs: Goyal Gunja
revue: Studies in health technology and informatics
resume: Ageing in place is increasingly important in India, where many older adults live in homes not designed for changing mobility and support needs. Although Universal Design (UD) provides a basis for inclusive housing, extensive retrofitting may be difficult in existing homes. This paper uses a qualitative, literature-informed comparison of high-rise apartments, independent homes and compact urban housing across five parameters: mobility stress, behavioural familiarity, operational resilience, safety vulnerability and incremental adaptability. The comparison identifies housing-specific vulnerabilities and feasible retrofit priorities, including small changes to lighting, surfaces, support features and everyday spatial use. Based on these findings, a Realistic Adaptability Framework is proposed to connect residents' needs with housing constraints, affordability and incremental intervention. The approach applies UD principles to existing homes while recognising the practical limitations within which ageing in place occurs.

titre: A balancing act: Passive ankle exoskeletons alter neuromuscular function and postural stability during balance.
titre_fr: A balancing act: Passive ankle exoskeletons alter neuromuscular function and postural stability during balance.
auteurs: Po Jemima C N, Williamson James L, Yee Jordan, Farris Dominic J, Dick Taylor J M
resume: Spring-loaded passive ankle exoskeletons have the potential to modulate neuromuscular function during standing balance by altering the mechanical demands placed on the muscle-tendon units spanning the ankle joint. This study investigated the effect of exoskeleton assistance on postural stability and neuromuscular function across balance conditions of varying difficulty. We hypothesised that assistance would improve postural stability and reduce ankle plantar flexor muscle activity during balance tasks, although these benefits may vary with balance task complexity. Participants performed standing balance tasks of varying difficulty with and without rotational stiffness provided by spring-loaded ankle exoskeletons. Balance tasks included (i) quiet standing with eyes open (EO), (ii) eyes closed (EC), and (iii) reduced base of support (RBOS). We recorded centre of pressure (COP)-based postural sway measures, lower limb joint kinematics, muscle activation data from the medial (MG) and lateral gastrocnemii (LG), soleus (SOL), and tibialis anterior (TA), and MG fascicle behaviour. Exoskeleton assistance reduced LG and SOL activation but also altered joint kinematics and coordination. Ankle-based adjustments were most evident with assistance during simpler balance tasks (EO and EC), whereas assistance during the most challenging task (RBOS) was associated with increases in COP sway velocity, COP variability and TA activation. Our results suggest that despite the potential energetic benefits from offloading the plantar flexors, passive ankle exoskeletons may induce unintended effects that hinder the control of standing balance, particularly during more challenging conditions. Further work is needed to determine the mechanisms underlying these effects.

titre: Spatial Gene Expression in Fungi: mRNA Localization, Condensates, and Beyond.
titre_fr: Spatial Gene Expression in Fungi: mRNA Localization, Condensates, and Beyond.
auteurs: Otterdijk Sander van, Wang Zixu, Arends Roan, Tutucci Evelina
resume: Polarized growth and cellular asymmetry are broadly conserved properties of fungal life, from transient bud-site selection in unicellular yeasts to sustained hyphal extension in filamentous and coenocytic species. While vesicle trafficking, cytoskeletal organization, and cell-wall remodeling are well-established contributors to these processes, the role of mRNA localization is only beginning to be fully appreciated. In this review, we examine how the spatial regulation of mRNAs and their translation contributes to fungal polarity, morphogenesis, and environmental adaptation. We discuss current knowledge around three interconnected layers contributing to mRNA localization: active cytoskeletal transport-actin-based in compact yeasts and microtubule-based in long hyphae; partitioning into biomolecular condensates such as P-bodies and Whi3-mRNA assemblies; and cytoplasmic-scale architectural features including bulk flow, nuclear positioning, and nuclear heterogeneity that become increasingly important in multinucleate and coenocytic systems such as arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi. Together, these mechanisms establish spatial gene expression as an integral component of fungal polarity, with implications for fungal development, host-pathogen interactions, and ecological adaptation, and for our broader understanding of polarized growth in eukaryotic cell organization.

titre: Impact of hearing loss on visual selective attention: Evidence from N2pc and resting-state networks.
titre_fr: Impact of hearing loss on visual selective attention: Evidence from N2pc and resting-state networks.
auteurs: Zeng Tongao, Bu Xiaoou, Zhu Han, Liu Ziyao, Xiao Hongli, Li Fuxiang, Zhang Wenjun, Yang Fuyi, Chen Jie, Ma Hailin
resume: Efficient visual attention is fundamental to environmental adaptation and social interaction. While previous studies have observed alterations in visual processing among deaf individuals, findings remain controversial regarding whether these changes stem from hearing loss (sensory compensation vs. cognitive deficit) or sign language experience. To address this issue, the present study provides task-related and resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) evidence to disentangle the specific drivers of visual selective attention plasticity. A visual search task was used to examine selective attention in 95 participants (34 prelingual deaf, 27 hearing signers, and 34 hearing nonsigners). Compared to both hearing groups, deaf individuals exhibited significantly lower hit rates and diminished N2-posterior contralateral (N2pc) amplitudes. Hearing signers and nonsigners showed comparable behavioral performance, N2pc amplitudes, and resting-state network topology, whereas the deaf group was further characterized by a degraded resting-state alpha network topology, evidenced by reduced clustering coefficients, global efficiency, and weakened frontal-occipital connectivity. N2pc amplitude correlated significantly with resting-state network properties and behavioral accuracy. These results suggest that deaf individuals may suffer from an imbalance in the regulation of visual selective attention, most clearly indexed by the evoked N2pc and by intrinsic alpha-network organization, and likely linked to increased resource competition following the loss of auditory monitoring. Our findings provide neurophysiological evidence that these attentional deficits are associated with hearing loss rather than with sign-language experience, offering a new perspective for understanding the boundaries of cross-modal plasticity in the human brain.

titre: Weissella cibaria EFEL4000 as a novel probiotic starter culture for kimchi fermentation with anti-inflammatory properties.
titre_fr: Weissella cibaria EFEL4000 as a novel probiotic starter culture for kimchi fermentation with anti-inflammatory properties.
auteurs: Kwak Min Jeong, Pyeon Geum Na, Jo Na Gyeong, Choi Yuri, Seong Hyunbin, Byun Woobean, Ryu Byung Hee, Han Nam Soo
resume: The recent approval of Weissella species as food ingredients in Korea has expanded their application as probiotic starter cultures for kimchi fermentation. Here, we evaluated Weissella cibaria EFEL4000 as a novel kimchi starter culture by investigating its fermentation performance, probiotic characteristics, safety, and anti-inflammatory activity. As a starter culture, EFEL4000 reached approximately 9.0 log CFU/mL and pH 4.42 after 3 days of fermentation at 10 °C and produced major sulfur-containing volatiles, including dimethyl disulfide, methyl propyl disulfide, and methyl 2-propenyl disulfide. As a probiotic, EFEL4000 showed a favorable strain-level safety profile and tolerance to acidic and bile salt conditions. It also exhibited a Caco-2 adhesion rate of 33% and maintained TEER at 74.11% following H₂O₂-induced oxidative stress. Additionally, heat-killed EFEL4000 significantly reduced NO production and the expression of IL-6, IL-1β, iNOS, and COX-2 in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages. Genome analysis identified genes associated with environmental adaptation and probiotic functions, while no biogenic amine-producing, acquired antibiotic resistance, or virulence genes were detected. Collectively, these findings provide scientific evidence for the industrial application of W. cibaria as a probiotic starter culture and support the development of functional plant-based fermented foods.

titre: Natural Variation in CYCLIC NUCLEOTIDE-GATED ION CHANNEL 16 Controls Fruit Weight in Tomato.
titre_fr: Natural Variation in CYCLIC NUCLEOTIDE-GATED ION CHANNEL 16 Controls Fruit Weight in Tomato.
auteurs: Wang Xiang, Huang Yixuan, Miao Huaiqi, Dai Ying, Wang Youwei, Ding Ziyuan, Li Nanyi, Wu Gang
resume: Fruit weight is a crucial agronomic trait influencing yield and quality in tomato domestication. Although numerous quantitative trait loci (QTLs) controlling fruit weight have been reported, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely unresolved. Here, we identify natural variation in the promoter region of CYCLIC NUCLEOTIDE-GATED ION CHANNEL 16 (CNGC16) associated with both fruit weight and gene expression differences via genome-wide association study (GWAS) in tomato accessions. Geographical and subpopulation analyses reveal that the large-fruit CNGC16 haplotype was selectively favoured during domestication and may contribute to local environmental adaptation. Functional assays demonstrate that CNGC16 regulates fruit weight by promoting cell division and maintaining cytosolic Ca<sup>2+</sup> homeostasis in fruit cells. Mechanistically, CNGC16 physically and genetically interacts with calmodulin 6 (CaM6) to mediate calcium signalling that controls fruit size. These findings uncover a novel calcium-dependent pathway regulating tomato fruit weight and propose CNGC16 and CaM6 as promising molecular targets for crop improvement.

titre: Integrating environmental adaptation, breeding, and rhizobia bioinoculants for soybean expansion in Europe.
titre_fr: Integrating environmental adaptation, breeding, and rhizobia bioinoculants for soybean expansion in Europe.
auteurs: Jacott Catherine N, Wilkinson Helen, López-Beltrán María, Rotundo José L, Couzigou Jean-Malo, Goormachtig Sofie, Del Cerro Pablo, Hungria Mariangela, Khazaei Hamid
resume: Europe's heavy dependence on imported protein is environmentally and strategically costly. Soybean (Glycine max) offers a great opportunity to close this gap. Soybean cultivation can reduce reliance on synthetic nitrogen (N) fertiliser through its symbiosis with N-fixing bacteria (rhizobia). Nevertheless, it remains a relatively new crop across much of Europe and establishing it in the continent's diverse environments raises challenges of climate adaptation, symbiotic N fixation, and crop management. We argue that these challenges must be addressed together rather than separately, because yield stability, N fixation, and environmental stress resilience emerge from the interactions between plant genotype, rhizobial strain, environment, and soil and crop management practices. Drawing on lessons from major soybean-producing regions, we review environmental adaptation through maturity-group selection and stress-resilience breeding, rhizobia inoculant design, and the management practices that shape symbiotic and crop performance. We further examine genetic, genomic, and computational resources that make these interactions predictable and optimisable and identify priorities for future research and practice.

titre: The plant nuclear mechanome: nuclear envelope-chromatin mechanics in environmental stress sensing, memory and recovery.
titre_fr: The plant nuclear mechanome: nuclear envelope-chromatin mechanics in environmental stress sensing, memory and recovery.
auteurs: Ali Sajid, Naseem Muhammad Tahir, Zaman Wajid
resume: Plant responses to drought, salinity, heat and mechanical loading are usually interpreted through hormones, redox signals and transcriptional networks, but these frameworks incompletely capture the physical state of the nucleus. In wall-bounded, turgor-driven plant cells, environmental and growth-derived forces can be transmitted through the cytoskeleton to the nuclear envelope, nucleoskeleton and chromatin. Evidence from osmotic and heat-stress studies indicates that nuclear shape, stiffness, lamina organization, peripheral chromatin tethering and three-dimensional genome architecture are stress responsive. We synthesize these findings into the concept of the plant nuclear mechanome: an integrated system comprising nuclear geometry, viscoelasticity, envelope-cytoskeleton coupling, lamin-like scaffolds, nuclear pores, chromatin organization and nuclear-body dynamics. We propose that this system acts as a tunable interface that can buffer, transmit or amplify mechanical inputs and thereby influence chromatin accessibility, transcriptional competence, acclimation, stress memory and recovery. Particular attention is given to nuclear envelope and nucleoskeletal modules that may connect force transmission with genome regulation. We distinguish established observations from mechanistic hypotheses and outline experiments combining realistic stress treatments, live nuclear imaging, quantitative mechanics, targeted genetic perturbation, single-nucleus omics and physiological validation. This framework positions nuclear mechanics as a testable dimension of plant cell biology and environmental adaptation.
