titre: Psl exopolysaccharide regulates biofilm formation and environmental adaptation in Pseudomonas fluorescens PF07.
titre_fr: Psl exopolysaccharide regulates biofilm formation and environmental adaptation in Pseudomonas fluorescens PF07.
auteurs: Lu Zhong, Zhou Zhulin, Feng Lifang, Zhu Junli
resume: Pseudomonas fluorescens PF07, a prevalent psychrotrophic spoilage bacterium, relies heavily on robust biofilm formation to persist in food environments and exert spoilage effects. Nevertheless, the distinct contributions of exopolysaccharides to its biofilm maturation and stress adaptation remain unclear. Herein, we systematically characterized the genetic determinants and biological functions of three exopolysaccharides (Psl, alginate and PNAG) in modulating PF07 biofilm development and resistance to food-processing-associated stressors. Single, double, and triple deletion mutants targeting the pslB, alg8, and pgaC genes were constructed to evaluate the contributions of these biosynthetic systems, and transcriptomic analysis was performed to explore the underlying responses. Deletion of pslB markedly impaired biofilm formation, pellicle development, and extracellular matrix production, whereas deficiency of alg8 or pgaC caused only minor phenotypic changes compared with the wild-type strain, indicating that Psl is the primary structural determinant of the PF07 biofilm matrix. Furthermore, double- and triple-mutants lacking pslB exhibited more severe reductions in biofilm biomass and thickness, suggesting that alginate and PNAG make supplementary but secondary contributions to the Psl-dominated biofilm matrix. In addition, ΔpslB exhibited substantially reduced biofilm formation under low temperature and ionic stress and decreased tolerance to sodium hypochlorite and benzalkonium chloride, in contrast with limited alterations for the Δalg8 and ΔpgaC mutants. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed significant changes in genes associated with stress adaptation and metabolism, including the upregulation of aqpZ, the downregulation of osmY, and alterations in multiple metabolism-related genes. titre: Role of the nagZ Gene in Antibiotic Resistance and Environmental Stress Tolerance of Yersinia enterocolitica.
titre_fr: Role of the nagZ Gene in Antibiotic Resistance and Environmental Stress Tolerance of Yersinia enterocolitica.
auteurs: Pan Qianwen, Dong Yumeng, Chen Qixin, Li Ruohan, Yue Zhuo, Tian Xiaoya, Chen Jingyu
resume: NagZ is a glycoside hydrolase that regulates AmpC β-lactamase and biofilm formation in Gram-negative bacteria, and its inhibitors show promise as antibiotic adjuvants. However, the role of nagZ in the important foodborne pathogen Yersinia enterocolitica, which exhibits strong environmental adaptability and increasing rates of antibiotic resistance, remains unclear. This study investigated the impact of NagZ on antibiotic resistance and environmental tolerance in Y. enterocolitica. The minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of relevant strains against ampicillin, ceftazidime, and fosfomycin sodium were determined. Since NagZ hydrolyzes peptidoglycan fragments bearing N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc), the synergistic effects of exogenous GlcNAc on resistance phenotypes were further evaluated. Environmental stress assays were also performed to evaluate the contribution of NagZ to environmental tolerance. The results showed that deletion of nagZ produced a pronounced increase in susceptibility to ampicillin, whereas MIC shifts for ceftazidime and fosfomycin sodium were within the experimental error. For ampicillin, exogenous GlcNAc reduced the MIC from 64 µg/mL (WT) to 16 µg/mL and further to 2 µg/mL in the nagZ mutant background. The ΔnagZ mutant also displayed impaired biofilm formation with 23.91%, 25.42%, and 16.46% reductions relative to WT at 24, 48, and 72 h. Compared with WT, the ΔnagZ mutant exhibited relative survival reductions of 32.59% (42 °C), 31.91% (4 °C), 36.37% (SDS), and 71.27% (oxidative stress). These findings indicate that NagZ may represent a critical node in the regulatory network linking antibiotic resistance and environmental adaptation, highlighting its potential as a novel target for controlling this foodborne pathogen.

titre: Genome-Wide Identification and Analysis of Brassica napus Nonexpressor of Pathogenesis-Related Genes Family and Functional Analysis of BnaNPR3.A02 in Clubroot Resistance.
titre_fr: Genome-Wide Identification and Analysis of Brassica napus Nonexpressor of Pathogenesis-Related Genes Family and Functional Analysis of BnaNPR3.A02 in Clubroot Resistance.
auteurs: Zheng Lin, Zhao Feixue, Li Ye, Xu Ke, Guo Zhiting, Nie Junwei, Ma Yongji, Chen Ziyuan, Sha Hongyu, Li Ruiheng, Li Keqi, Sun Weinan, Huang Zhen
resume: Nonexpressor of pathogenesis-related (NPR) proteins are key regulators of salicylic acid (SA)-mediated plant immunity, functioning as transcriptional co-regulators. In this study, we aimed to comprehensively identify NPR family members in Brassica napus and its diploid progenitors, investigate their evolutionary dynamics and expression profiles, and functionally characterize the role of BnaNPR3.A02 in clubroot resistance. We identified 23, 12, and 12 NPR genes in B. napus, B. rapa, and B. oleracea, respectively, which were phylogenetically divided into six conserved subfamilies (I-VI). Structural characterization showed that these genes possess conserved ankyrin repeats, BTB-POZ domains or the DUF3420 domains, and exhibit diversified exon-intron structures. Spatiotemporal expression profiling uncovered tissue-specific expression patterns of NPRs under normal conditions. Promoter cis-element analysis and transcriptomic profiling in response to phytohormones and abiotic stresses suggested broad involvement of BnaNPRs in environmental adaptation. GO annotation revealed that NPR1-4 members are enriched in jasmonic acid/salicylic acid-mediated defense pathways, whereas NPR5/6 members are associated with floral development. qRT-PCR analysis of 11 expressed BnaNPR1-4 genes was performed in resistant (R) and susceptible (S) rapeseed plants upon P. brassicae infection. BnaNPR3.A02 showed the greatest expression divergence, with significant induction in R plants but consistent suppression in S plants. Because NPR3 is a negative feedback regulator of SA signaling, the induction of BnaNPR3.A02 in R plants likely reflects feedback attenuation after immune activation, whereas its suppression in S plants may indicate a defective SA signaling node. Heterologous overexpression of BnaNPR3.A02 in Arabidopsis significantly increased disease severity and pathogen biomass, whereas Arabidopsis npr3 knockout mutants showed enhanced resistance, supporting a conserved negative regulatory role of NPR3 in this heterologous system. Protein-protein interaction and co-expression analyses further revealed that BnaNPR3.A02 is embedded in a stress- and defense-related network. These findings provide a foundation for understanding the evolutionary and functional divergence of the NPR family and identify BnaNPR3.A02 as a candidate target for future functional validation and breeding of clubroot-resistant B. napus varieties.

titre: Bacterial Community Structural Dynamics and Predicted Functional Potential in Loxostege sticticalis.
titre_fr: Bacterial Community Structural Dynamics and Predicted Functional Potential in Loxostege sticticalis.
auteurs: Ye Cheng, Chen Yuxuan, Gu Huimin, Cheng Yunxia, Xie Dianjie, Liang Zhong, Lin Jun, Li Xuan, Zhang Lei, Jiang Xingfu, Kong Hailong
resume: Symbiotic bacteria contribute to insect physiology and environmental adaptation, yet their dynamics and potential functions in the major migratory pest Loxostege sticticalis remain poorly understood. We characterized bacterial community composition, diversity, and predicted functional potential across developmental stages, tissues and frass samples, and environmental conditions. In laboratory-reared insects, Enterococcus and Staphylococcus predominated from the second to fifth instars, whose predicted functions emphasized carbohydrate and nucleotide metabolism. Adults were instead dominated by Pseudoalteromonas and Asaia, with predicted profiles showing greater representation of lipid and amino acid metabolism and transport and catabolism. First-instar larvae exhibited an adult-like community structure. Among sample types, Enterococcus predominated in the midgut, whereas Staphylococcus was overrepresented in the epidermis and frass. Epidermal and frass communities emphasized cellular processes and genetic information processing, whereas midgut and other internal tissue communities showed greater predicted potential for membrane transport and metabolism. Wild-caught larvae harbored distinct communities consistently enriched in Stenotrophomonas and Ralstonia, with predicted profiles shifting toward carbohydrate, amino acid, and lipid metabolism and environmental adaptation in later instars. Overall, these findings demonstrate that the symbiotic bacterial communities of L. sticticalis vary markedly with development, tissue niche, and environment, providing a basis for further studies of host-microbe interactions.

titre: Repeat-Rich Architecture and Gene Duplication Characterize the Expanded Genome of the Chestnut Gall Wasp.
titre_fr: Repeat-Rich Architecture and Gene Duplication Characterize the Expanded Genome of the Chestnut Gall Wasp.
auteurs: Ren Ye-Song, Lv An-Kang, Zeng Yang, Zhu Dao-Hong
resume: Dryocosmus kuriphilus, the chestnut gall wasp, is a globally invasive pest that reproduces by thelytokous parthenogenesis. Despite the absence of conventional sexual recombination, the species has spread widely and persists under diverse environmental conditions, but the genomic features associated with this capacity remain poorly understood. Here, a chromosome-level assembly of D. kuriphilus was compared with seven representative insect genomes, with emphasis on repetitive sequences, orthogroups, and gene-duplication patterns. The 2.28-Gb D. kuriphilus genome contained 79.7% repetitive sequences, including 62.3% transposable elements (TEs), most of which occurred in intergenic regions. OrthoFinder assigned 13,271 D. kuriphilus genes to multi-copy orthogroups, representing 61.5% of the protein-coding gene set. Independent MCScanX analysis classified genes into mutually exclusive dispersed, proximal, tandem, and segmental duplication modes, with segmental and dispersed representing the two largest duplicated-gene classes. D. kuriphilus contained substantially more segmental duplicates than the other species examined. Synonymous-substitution distributions revealed low- and high-Ks components representing different levels of synonymous divergence among duplicated genes, and genes in these components showed distinct functional profiles. Numerous local duplications were found near TEs and included genes involved in host recognition, nutrient utilisation, xenobiotic metabolism, and energy production. Compared with the closely related gall wasp Belonocnema kinseyi, D. kuriphilus has a broader reported distribution and host range and contains higher copy numbers in several gene families associated with chemosensation, detoxification, metabolism, and stress responses. Together, these findings show that the expanded D. kuriphilus genome is characterized by extensive repeat accumulation and increased gene copy number, whereas duplication at multiple scales increased and reshaped the functional gene repertoire. These genomic features identify candidate mechanisms that may contribute to genomic and ecological plasticity, although their adaptive significance requires expression, evolutionary, and functional validation.

titre: Population Genomic Insights into Genetic Differentiation and Environmental Adaptation of the Asian Honey Bee (Apis cerana) in Sichuan, China.
titre_fr: Population Genomic Insights into Genetic Differentiation and Environmental Adaptation of the Asian Honey Bee (Apis cerana) in Sichuan, China.
auteurs: Xu Xiangcheng, Ma Dingyuan, Liu Bingrong, Yang Mingxian, Lai Kang, Yang Jiandong
resume: The Asian honey bee (Apis cerana) is a key native pollinator in Asia, contributing substantially to both natural and agricultural ecosystems. However, climate change and human activities increasingly threaten its pollination services and long-term survival. Understanding patterns of genetic differentiation and local adaptation is therefore essential for protecting native populations. Sichuan Province in China, with its complex mountains, deep valleys, and pronounced climatic heterogeneity, offers an excellent natural laboratory for studying these processes in A. cerana. We collected 139 worker bees from 22 locations across Sichuan and generated whole-genome resequencing data. By integrating these data with genomes from eight well-established subspecies, we show that bees from Xinlong, Jiuzhaigou, and Kangding form three genetically differentiated populations that are distinct from all known subspecies. These populations display moderate to high genetic differentiation and unique demographic histories relative to previously described subspecies. Selective-sweep analyses further identified 200-300 candidate genes under positive selection in each population. These genes are enriched in functions related to chemical sensing, flight musculature, cell-cycle regulation, osmotic balance, and stress response, consistent with adaptation to patchy nectar resources, a short spring reproductive window, and large diurnal temperature swings. Our findings uncover three previously unrecognized genetic resources of A. cerana and provide genomic insights into their local adaptation, offering a valuable foundation for conservation and breeding programs.

titre: A Virtual Pulmonary Rehabilitation Program to Address Gaps in Pulmonary Rehabilitation: Retrospective Observational Study.
titre_fr: A Virtual Pulmonary Rehabilitation Program to Address Gaps in Pulmonary Rehabilitation: Retrospective Observational Study.
auteurs: Beschloss Alexander, Ostrovsky Andrey
resume: Traditional brick-and-mortar pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) programs remain substantially underused, with only 2.7% of Medicare beneficiaries completing PR within 12 months following hospitalization for a COPD exacerbation. Given the critical role of PR in improving exercise tolerance, quality of life, and reducing readmissions, innovative delivery models are needed to address this massive utilization gap. Virtual PR platforms have emerged as a potential solution, offering scalable, and home-based rehabilitation. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a novel virtual PR program on functional, psychosocial, and cardiometabolic outcomes among adults with COPD. This retrospective observational study analyzed outcomes among patients enrolled in a structured, multidisciplinary virtual PR program between 2022 and 2024. Participants completed individualized exercise and education sessions remotely, supported by a multidisciplinary team including Physicians and Clinical Exercise Physiologists. Baseline and postprogram measures were compared using Cohen d to assess effect sizes across clinical domains. Primary outcomes included changes in maximum metabolic equivalents (METs), Duke Activity Status Index (DASI), and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores. Other measures included changes in blood pressure (systolic and diastolic), smoking status, and prevalence of hypertension. Among 2444 patients completing the program, the largest effect size improvements were observed in maximum METs achieved, DASI, and PHQ-9 scores. The program was also associated with decreased smoking rates and a lower prevalence of hypertension post intervention. Notably, 91% of the studied population self-identified as having a "fixed income," underscoring the potential for virtual PR to extend access to patients with lower incomes in the United States. Virtual PR appears to be a promising and potentially more scalable alternative to traditional facility-based PR for patients with COPD. Significant improvements in exercise capacity, mood, and cardiovascular parameters suggest clinical benefit, while reductions in smoking and hypertension further highlight potential for broader health impact. Given the high proportion of participants on fixed incomes, virtual PR may represent an effective strategy to expand access and equity in chronic respiratory care delivery across the United States.

titre: Repeated sprint training in hypoxia as a post-surgical rehabilitation strategy: A case study in an elite badminton player.
titre_fr: Repeated sprint training in hypoxia as a post-surgical rehabilitation strategy: A case study in an elite badminton player.
auteurs: Tee Chris Chow Li, Chong Mee Chee, Yeap Ming Wei, Yeo Wee Kian
resume: Badminton is a racquet sport that imposes high demands on both aerobic and anaerobic capacity and involves repetitive, high-intensity movements, increasing the risk of non-contact injuries to joints and muscle-tendon units. Returning to sport-specific conditioning after injury, particularly post-surgery, presents challenges for deconditioned athletes seeking to restore aerobic capacity while minimising mechanical stress imposed on the injured parts. This case study evaluated the feasibility of integrating short-term repeated sprint training in hypoxia (RSH) as a supplementary modality within a late-stage post-lower back surgery rehabilitation program to support aerobic reconditioning before return to sport-specific conditioning. An elite men's singles badminton athlete completed 4-week RSH (FiO<sub>2</sub> ~ 16.5%), alongside his regular rehabilitation schedule. The intervention consisted of 20 × 4-s all-out cycling sprints interspersed with 30-56-s recovery, performed once weekly. Post-intervention lactate profiling suggested a rightward shift in the blood lactate curve, with estimated increases of 33% and 10% in power output at the aerobic and anaerobic thresholds, respectively, indicative of aerobic reconditioning. However, the present findings should be interpreted cautiously due to observed stage-to-stage blood lactate variability, single-case design, and concurrent rehabilitation. Overall, the present study supports the feasibility of incorporating hypoxic RSH in late-stage rehabilitation to facilitate return to sport-specific conditioning.

titre: Interactive Acupuncture for Poststroke Dysphagia: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: Interactive Acupuncture for Poststroke Dysphagia: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Zhao Zhiheng, Li Junjie, Zhao Manlin, Shao Changjun, Xu Mingjie, Zhang Yintao, Ren Yueqiao, Zhou Zhen, Gao Fangfang
resume: Poststroke dysphagia (difficulty swallowing) is a common disabling complication of stroke and is associated with malnutrition, aspiration pneumonia, impaired quality of life, and mortality. Conventional swallowing rehabilitation and instrumental assessment are useful but may be limited by equipment dependence and inconsistent accessibility. Interactive acupuncture is a dynamic acupuncture procedure in which short needling stimulation at selected nape acupoints is synchronized with active swallowing tasks. This protocol describes a multicenter, parallel-group randomized controlled trial that will evaluate whether interactive acupuncture improves swallowing function in patients with poststroke dysphagia compared with conventional acupuncture at the same acupoints. A total of 100 participants with poststroke dysphagia will be randomized 1:1 to an interactive acupuncture group or a conventional acupuncture control group. Both groups will receive routine conventional medical care and standardized acupuncture therapy for stroke. The intervention course comprises 14 sessions delivered 6 times per week followed by a 1-month follow-up. The registered primary outcome is the water swallowing test (WST) grade; the primary efficacy comparison is the change in WST grade from baseline to immediately after the 14th treatment session. Secondary outcomes include the Standardized Swallowing Assessment, Functional Oral Intake Scale, Swallowing Quality of Life Questionnaire, instrumental and physiological assessments, inflammatory markers, safety outcomes, and a supportive WST responder analysis. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline; after sessions 3, 7, and 14; and at 1 month after treatment completion, where applicable. The current amended protocol was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of Hengshui Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine on August 25, 2026 (approval 2026-KY-09), and separate institutional ethics approval was obtained from the Second Affiliated Hospital of Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine (approval Y2025-053-01). The study was funded in June 2025. The trial was registered with the International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry on December 30, 2025. Recruitment began on January 1, 2026; as of July 6, 2026, a total of 36 participants had been enrolled. Primary outcome data analysis has not yet begun. Recruitment is expected to continue until June 1, 2027, with final follow-up anticipated by July 2027 and submission of the primary results planned for September 2027. This trial will clarify whether adding a task-synchronized interactive acupuncture procedure to the same acupoint prescription provides incremental benefit over conventional acupuncture for poststroke dysphagia and will provide a manualized, fidelity-monitored protocol for future clinical implementation.

The current amended protocol was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of Hengshui Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine on August 25, 2026 (approval 2026-KY-09), and separate institutional ethics approval was obtained from the Second Affiliated Hospital of Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine (approval Y2025-053-01). The study was funded in June 2025. The trial was registered with the International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry on December 30, 2025. Recruitment began on January 1, 2026; as of July 6, 2026, a total of 36 participants had been enrolled. Primary outcome data analysis has not yet begun. Recruitment is expected to continue until June 1, 2027, with final follow-up anticipated by July 2027 and submission of the primary results planned for September 2027. This trial will clarify whether adding a task-synchronized interactive acupuncture procedure to the same acupoint prescription provides incremental benefit over conventional acupuncture for poststroke dysphagia and will provide a manualized, fidelity-monitored protocol for future clinical implementation.

titre: Clinical and behavioral delineation of cochlear implant non-users: a 20-year retrospective descriptive analysis.
titre_fr: Clinical and behavioral delineation of cochlear implant non-users: a 20-year retrospective descriptive analysis.
auteurs: Jang Jeong Hun, Ha Jungho, Kim You-Jeong, Park Hun Yi, Choung Yun-Hoon
resume: Although cochlear implants (CIs) effectively restore hearing, device abandonment ('non-use') remains a critical challenge limiting long-term auditory rehabilitation. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, clinical and radiological characteristics, and patient-reported reasons for CI non-use, comparing pre-lingually and post-lingually deafened individuals to inform long-term retention strategies. We retrospectively reviewed 545 CI recipients implanted between 2002 and 2023 (excluding 24 patients lost to follow-up or with incomplete data). Clinical features, temporal bone CT, internal auditory canal MRI, and speech-language therapy records of 36 non-users were analyzed. Overall non-use rate was 6.6% (36/545), comprising 8.7% (25/287) in pre-lingual and 4.3% (11/258) in post-lingual recipients. Inner ear anomalies were identified in 11 pre-lingual non-users, including two with isolated cochlear nerve deficiency. Primary non-use reasons were sound maladaptation (48.0% pre-lingual vs. 36.4% post-lingual) and lack of subjective listening effect (48.0% vs. 18.2%). Post-lingual non-users presented distinct adult-specific psychosocial barriers (27.3%), including depression and cognitive decline. CI non-use is driven by distinct physiological, psychological, and socioeconomic factors depending on deafness onset. Delineating these onset-specific profiles provides essential guidance for tailored preoperative counseling and age-appropriate post-implantation monitoring to minimize long-term device abandonment.

titre: Severe Propofol Infusion Syndrome Managed With Multimodal Critical Care: A Case Report.
titre_fr: Severe Propofol Infusion Syndrome Managed With Multimodal Critical Care: A Case Report.
auteurs: Power Rachael, El Katan Mohamed, Wibrow Bradley, Anstey Matthew H
resume: Rapid cardiovascular collapse with severe metabolic derangement during propofol sedation should raise concern for propofol infusion syndrome (PRIS). A 21-year-old man with previous traumatic brain injury presented with refractory status epilepticus requiring mechanical ventilation and prolonged propofol sedation. Following four days of infusion, he developed abrupt bradycardia, cardiogenic shock, severe high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, acute kidney injury, hypertriglyceridemia, and significant left ventricular dysfunction. The combination of prolonged propofol exposure and rapidly evolving multiorgan failure was considered consistent with PRIS. Propofol was discontinued immediately. Management included administration of multiple vasoactive infusions, sodium bicarbonate, calcium chloride, dual high-effluent continuous renal replacement therapy via two dialysis circuits, high-dose euglycemic insulin, and enteral L-carnitine. Hemodynamic improvement occurred within approximately six hours, followed by recovery of cardiac and renal function. He was discharged from the intensive care unit on day 30 and later returned home after rehabilitation without dialysis dependence. This case highlights the importance of early recognition of PRIS and rapid escalation of individualized organ support in severe presentations, while acknowledging that the contribution of individual adjunctive therapies cannot be determined from a single case.

titre: Senescence Biomarkers Predict Physical Function and Clinical Outcomes After Heart Failure Hospitalization: Insights From REHAB-HF.
titre_fr: Senescence Biomarkers Predict Physical Function and Clinical Outcomes After Heart Failure Hospitalization: Insights From REHAB-HF.
auteurs: Semelka Charles T, Ehrig Molly R, Pajewski Nicholas M, Kritchevsky Stephen B, Kramer Philip A, Peters Anthony E, Mentz Robert J, Pastva Amy M, Whellan David J, Kitzman Dalane W
revue: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
resume: Acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) is the most common cause of hospitalization in older adults. Cellular senescence, a hallmark of aging biology, has been implicated in heart failure pathophysiology and functional decline via the pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). We evaluated the association between SASP and physical function in older adults hospitalized for ADHF. REHAB-HF was a trial of older adults hospitalized for ADHF randomized to a novel physical rehabilitation intervention or attention control. We measured a panel of 18-SASP analytes at in-hospital baseline and at 3-month follow-up. Outcomes included short physical performance battery (SPPB) and 6-minute walk distance (6MWD). Statistical analysis included principal component analysis (PCA) of log- and z-transformed SASP values. Associations were evaluated with multivariable regression models adjusted for age, sex, and intervention arm. Samples were available for 226 (65%) of the REHAB-HF participants with mean age (SD) 72.3 (8), 53% female, 52% HFpEF, and 53% assigned to rehab intervention. Principal Component 1 (PC1) reflected a coordinated signal across biomarkers of inflammation and immune signaling. PC1 was associated with poorer function at baseline [(SPPB -0.46 [-0.77, -0.14]; p = 0.004 and 6MWD -19.7 meters [-32.7, -6.7]; p = 0.003)]. Increasing SASP over time was associated with clinically significant reduced physical function improvement (ΔSPPB -1.80 [-2.58, -1.03]; p < 0.001 and Δ6MWD -49.7 meters [-77.2, -22.1]; p = 0.001). Higher SASP levels were associated with poorer physical function recovery in older patients hospitalized for ADHF. These findings suggest that inflammatory SASP biomarkers may improve risk stratification and potentially guide therapeutic strategies. NCT02196038.

titre: Improving outcomes in the management of acute external laryngotracheal trauma.
titre_fr: Improving outcomes in the management of acute external laryngotracheal trauma.
auteurs: Mathews Suma Susan, Sargunaraj J Justin Ebenezer, Chetan Sheth Meet, Boaz Rashmi Tanya, Paul Roshna Rose, Gurushekar Preethi Rose, Karuppusami Reka, Albert Rita Ruby A
revue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
resume: To highlight the presentation, management, and functional outcomes of subjects with acute laryngotracheal trauma, managed by a dedicated laryngology unit in a tertiary care hospital in South India. A retrospective review of the medical records of acute laryngotracheal trauma cases from 1st January 2014 to 31st August 2023 was carried out. Data collected included demographics, mechanism of trauma, age, and sex, presentation, time of injury to intervention, investigations, Schaefer-Fuhrman (SF) grade, management (airway access, surgical techniques & conservative methods) and outcomes. Complications (via a graded complication classification grouped into mild, moderate , severe), functional airway, voice and swallowing outcomes were analysed separately as well as at the end of one year follow up. Sixty-eight subjects (57 males and 11 females) with laryngotracheal trauma were managed during this study period. All but 2 subjects received definitive management within 48 hours of the trauma. 91.2% (n=62) of them were managed within 24 hours of the injury. We encountered 2 deaths and one subject developed Hypoxic Ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE) during emergent management. Main mode of injury was motor vehicular accident (41%, n=28). SF group III and IV was observed in 33.8% (n=23) and 29.4% (n=20) subjects. The endolaryngeal mucosal repair as well as reduction and stabilisation of fractured cartilage segments were done using absorbable polyglactin (vicryl). Of the 54 who required surgery only 16 % (n=11) required stenting. Successful decannulation was achieved in 96% of the tracheostomised subjects (n=48/50) and successful rehabilitation from assisted to oral feeding was possible in 90.7 % (n=39/43). Poor voice, airway and swallowing outcomes were seen in 11%, 3% and 3% of our subjects during 1 year follow up. Long -term major complications were seen in 6% (n=4) and minor ones in 15.4 % (n=10). Early intervention remains pivotal for successful management of laryngotracheal trauma. This single institutional study, characterized primarily by early definitive management by an experienced team; was able to achieve favourable outcomes even with the use of simple, readily available, inexpensive materials like - absorbable sutures for mucosal and cartilage approximation, and modified endotracheal tube as stents.

titre: Motor manifestations of kernicterus spectrum disorder: Diagnosis and treatment.
titre_fr: Motor manifestations of kernicterus spectrum disorder: Diagnosis and treatment.
auteurs: Can Afra, Gelineau-Morel Rose
resume: Kernicterus Spectrum Disorder (KSD) is a chronic neurologic condition resulting from bilirubin neurotoxicity and remains a leading global cause of dyskinetic cerebral palsy (CP). Injury to the globus pallidus and related neural networks leads to characteristic movement disorders, most commonly dystonia and choreoathetosis, which often emerge months after the episode of hyperbilirubinemia. This delay contributes to underrecognition and missed opportunities for early intervention. In this review, we summarize motor manifestations of KSD and evaluate current approaches to early diagnosis and treatment. Available predictive and diagnostic tools include the modified Bilirubin-Induced Neurologic Dysfunction (BIND) score, brain magnetic resonance imaging, dystonia rating scales, and the KSD diagnostic toolkit. Although evidence for treatment of movement disorders specific to KSD remains limited, management can be informed by the broader literature on dyskinetic CP and acquired dystonia. Current interventions include oral medications, botulinum neurotoxin injections, intrathecal baclofen, deep brain stimulation (DBS), and rehabilitation therapies. Interventions should be individualized according to motor phenotype, functional goals, and patient priorities. Future research is needed to define effective interventions, identify individuals most likely to benefit from specific therapies, and develop personalized treatment strategies.

titre: Social participation after community stroke rehabilitation: individual and intervention factors in a retrospective cohort study.
titre_fr: Social participation after community stroke rehabilitation: individual and intervention factors in a retrospective cohort study.
auteurs: Poyet Alix, Vielotte Soléane, Dalmon Lisa, Mandigout Stéphane, Bernikier David, Salle Jean-Yves, Compagnat Maxence, Daviet Jean-Christophe
revue: Annals of physical and rehabilitation medicine
resume: Improving social participation is a key objective of poststroke rehabilitation, yet determinants of successful outcomes in Community Stroke Rehabilitation Teams (CSRT) remain poorly understood. In particular, the respective contributions of person-related and intervention-related factors need clarification. To identify person-related and intervention-related factors associated with improvement in social participation following a home-based CSRT rehabilitation program. We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 534 patients with stroke managed by a CSRT between 2019 and 2024. Social participation was assessed using the Frenchay Activities Index (FAI) at baseline and after intervention. Responders were defined as a FAI score increase ≥7 points. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors among patient characteristics and intervention components. Seventeen percent of participants achieved an improvement in FAI ≥7 points. Independent person-related factors included younger age (OR 0.975; P = 0.010) and higher baseline functional status (Barthel Index) (OR 1.027; P = 0.005). Regarding intervention-related factors, programs including adapted physical activity (OR 2.01; P = 0.023), mobility-focused interventions (OR 3.21; P = 0.043), communication (OR 2.15; P = 0.035), and work reintegration support (OR 2.17; P = 0.015) were significantly associated with FAI improvement. Participation in therapeutic education workshops was more frequent among Responders (88%vs 60%, P < 0.001), particularly those focused on adapted physical activity, mobility retraining, and communication. Responders also showed greater improvement in quality of life. Personal and stroke-related factors show limited ability to predict improvement in social participation. In contrast, key interventions targeting mobility, physical activity, communication, and work reintegration are significantly associated with an improvement in social participation. This study was a retrospective observational study based on routine clinical care and was not prospectively registered in an international trial registry.

titre: Efficacy and implementation of augmented reality in healthcare: a scoping review in randomized controlled trials.
titre_fr: Efficacy and implementation of augmented reality in healthcare: a scoping review in randomized controlled trials.
auteurs: Nuraini Tuti, Bestari Rifqi Alifa, Chou Kuei-Ru, Fajarini Melati, Pujasari Hening, Putri Tissa Aulia, Utami Fadhilah Rizka, Yulianti Eka Putri
resume: Despite medical advances, significant challenges in routine practice persist, including diagnostic variability from traditional two-dimensional (2D) imaging, surgical risks due to anatomical uncertainty, and poor patient comprehension that contributes to perioperative anxiety. Augmented Reality (AR) offers a solution by overlaying three-dimensional (3D) digital information onto the real-world environment, providing real-time guidance to address these clinical gaps. However, while AR's clinical efficacy is increasingly proven, its practical integration into standard clinical workflows remains fragmented. This study presents a scoping review restricted to RCT-level evidence to systematically map the scope, distinct clinical capabilities, implementation limitations, and ethical frameworks of AR-based healthcare systems. A systematic search was conducted across PubMed and Embase to identify randomized controlled trials involving AR interventions in healthcare. Methodological quality was appraised using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist. A total of 25 Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs) were analyzed and categorized based on clinical domains (education, diagnosis, intervention, and rehabilitation) and their functional roles (delivering or assisting). AR was associated with improvements in surgical precision, reductions in perioperative anxiety and better functional outcomes in rehabilitation. In education, AR 3D models fostered patient engagement and shared decision-making. However, widespread adoption is impeded by technical constraints, physiological side effects like cybersickness, high initial costs, and inherent methodological difficulties in blinding. While AR demonstrates distinct capabilities to enhance clinical interventions and empower patient care, technical, logistical, and ethical hurdles persist. Future research must prioritize seamless interoperability with Electronic Health Records (EHR), integration with Artificial Intelligence (AI) decision support, robust health data architectures, and optimized human-computer interaction (HCI) factor design to prevent exacerbating the socioeconomic digital divide.

titre: Depression, Anxiety, and Healthcare Utilization in Adults with Uncontrolled Asthma.
titre_fr: Depression, Anxiety, and Healthcare Utilization in Adults with Uncontrolled Asthma.
auteurs: Yohannes Abebaw Mengistu, Rane Dhanashree, Hannania Nicola Alexander
resume: Uncontrolled asthma is often associated with recurrent acute exacerbations, progressive and chronic systemic inflammation and decreased lung function, impaired quality of life, and healthcare utilization. A considerable proportion of adult patients with uncontrolled asthma exhibit comorbid elevated symptoms of depression and anxiety. These symptoms are often underrecognized and undertreated in adults with asthma. We examined and synthesized the available literature on the efficacy of pulmonary rehabilitation, cognitive behavioral therapy, and antidepressant drug therapy, and healthcare utilization in adults with uncontrolled asthma with comorbid depression and anxiety. The prevalence of anxiety in adults with uncontrolled asthma ranges from 25 to 54%, and depression ranges from 14 to 50%. To date, the available literature on the efficacy of pulmonary rehabilitation, cognitive behavioral therapy, and antidepressant drug therapy in the treatment of anxiety and depression is limited. Untreated depression and anxiety are associated with recurrent episodes of acute exacerbations, hospitalizations, poorer quality of life, longer hospital stays, and emergency healthcare utilization. Therefore, well-controlled randomized controlled trials are needed to improve the evidence base for optimal care of adults with uncontrolled asthma and ideally to reduce healthcare utilization.

titre: Predictors, risk factors and management of intestinal failure in crohn's disease: A narrative review.
titre_fr: Predictors, risk factors and management of intestinal failure in crohn's disease: A narrative review.
auteurs: Shah Dhruvi, Alzamani Meena, Sehgal Tanisha, Sharma Vishal, Goyal Manjeet Kumar
resume: Intestinal failure in Crohn's disease is a preventable complication arising from primarily three pathways: progressive inflammatory bowel destruction, cumulative surgical loss, and postoperative septic complications. Crohn's disease is one of the most common benign causes, with a cumulative incidence of approximately 8.5% at 20 years after initial surgery. Postoperative abdominal sepsis accounts for over half the cases, highlighting the importance of perioperative optimization. Several predictors such as young age at diagnosis, penetrating disease behavior, upper gastrointestinal localisation, cumulative inflammatory burden, residual small intestinal length less than 200 cm, and non-use of biologic therapy. Prevention should be the focus of management. Modern treat-to-target interventions aiming for endoscopic and transmural healing, early effective biologic therapy, timely surgical intervention with bowel-sparing techniques including strictureplasty and the Kono-S anastomosis, and structured perioperative optimization with nutritional rehabilitation collectively address each of the three pathways to intestinal failure. Management of established intestinal failure requires multidisciplinary intestinal rehabilitation encompassing parenteral nutrition, pharmacological intestinotrophic therapy with glucagon-like peptide-2 agonists, active Crohn's disease management, autologous gastrointestinal reconstruction and intestinal transplantation in refractory cases. This narrative review synthesizes the current evidence through unifying framework that intestinal failure in Crohn's disease is preventable at each step of the disease trajectory and proposes a risk stratification model and management algorithm to guide clinical decision making.

titre: Effects of primary somatosensory cortex high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation combined with core stability training on pain and glutamate levels and neuromuscular function in chronic low back pain: a randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Effects of primary somatosensory cortex high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation combined with core stability training on pain and glutamate levels and neuromuscular function in chronic low back pain: a randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Li Kai, Ou Luyuan, Zhang Xiangsheng, Zhang Siyun, Huang Ziyan, Yu Qiuhua, Yang Jiajia, Cheng Xue, Yan Takyu, Ding Minghui, Wang Hongjiang, Wang Chuhuai
resume: Chronic low back pain (CLBP) involves pain-related changes in sensory processing, motor control, and broader neurobiological function. The primary somatosensory cortex (S1) is a relevant neuromodulation target because it contributes to sensory-discriminative pain processing and exhibits maladaptive plasticity in chronic pain states. However, S1-targeted high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation (HD-tDCS) has been insufficiently studied in CLBP. titre: The effect of early rehabilitation nursing on the recovery of cardiac function in patients with acute myocardial infarction.
titre_fr: The effect of early rehabilitation nursing on the recovery of cardiac function in patients with acute myocardial infarction.
auteurs: Feng Zhiwei, Zhang Mingke, Qin Qingzhu
revue: Journal of health, population, and nutrition
resume: This study aimed to investigate the effect of implementing early rehabilitation nursing on the recovery of cardiac function indices and prognosis after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) treatment in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Patients diagnosed with AMI and treated with PCI between March 2020 and May 2024 were selected as the study participants. This was a prospective randomised controlled trial; patients were randomly allocated to an observation group and a control group using a random number table method (157 cases per group). The control group received routine nursing after surgery, whereas the observation group received structured early rehabilitation nursing. After 6 months of intervention, cardiac function indices, the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and quality of life were compared between the two groups. Cardiac function indices included stroke volume (SV), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) and 6-minute walking distance (6MWD). The World Health Organization Quality of Life Measurement Brief Form was used to evaluate quality of life. After nursing intervention, the levels of SV, LVEF and 6MWD in the cardiac function indices of the observation group were higher than those of the control group, whereas the levels of LVEDV were lower than those of the control group; the differences between the two groups were significant (p < 0.05). The total incidence of MACE in the observation group was lower than that in the control group (p < 0.05). In the comparison of quality-of-life scores, the observation group scored higher than the control group in five domains (p < 0.05). Early rehabilitation nursing for patients with AMI can effectively improve patients' cardiac function indices and reduce the risk of MACE, thereby improving their quality of life. ISRCTN18094960.

titre: The effect of acupuncture-rehabilitation therapy on brain functional plasticity in motor aphasia after ischemic stroke: a randomized clinical neuroimaging trial.
titre_fr: The effect of acupuncture-rehabilitation therapy on brain functional plasticity in motor aphasia after ischemic stroke: a randomized clinical neuroimaging trial.
auteurs: Liu Tian-Tian, Ren Meng, Wang Jiening, Wang Yuehua, Wang Chao-Jie, Tang Qiang, Yang Feng, Hou Xin-Lei
resume: Motor aphasia is the most prevalent type of aphasia following ischemic stroke (IS). This study aims to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and underlying neural mechanisms of acupuncture-rehabilitation (A-R) therapy on motor aphasia after IS. Twenty-six patients with post-IS motor aphasia were randomly assigned to either the A-R group or the Conventional Rehabilitation (CR) group in a 1:1 ratio, and matched by age and gender with 26 healthy controls (HCs). The CR group received standard treatment and language training, while the A-R group additionally underwent scalp acupoint cluster acupuncture. Behavioral assessments and Blood Oxygenation Level Dependent functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (BOLD-fMRI) scans were conducted before and after the four-week intervention to evaluate therapeutic outcomes and underlying mechanisms. Compared to HCs, patients exhibited decreased Amplitude of Low Frequency Fluctuations (ALFF) in the right precuneus (p < 0.05) and reduced Regional Homogeneity (ReHo) in the left precuneus/postcentral gyrus (p < 0.05). Enhanced functional connectivity (FC) was observed in regions including the left Broca's area and right superior temporal gyrus, left Broca's area and right inferior frontal orbitalis gyrus, left Broca's area and right precentral gyrus, left Broca's area and right postcentral gyrus (p < 0.05). After intervention, significant improvements were observed in Aphasia Quotient (AQ) scores and sub-item performance in both patient groups (p < 0.05), with the A-R group showing greater gains in AQ and spontaneous speech scores compared to the CR group (p < 0.05). FMRI results indicated a significant increase in mean ALFF (mALFF) in the left inferior temporal gyrus after A-R treatment (p < 0.05) compared to before, and higher szReHo in the left anterior central gyrus compared to the CR group (p < 0.05). FC between the left Broca's area and right precentral gyrus decreased in the A-R group (p < 0.05). Additionally, a negative correlation was observed between the right anterior central gyrus and listening comprehension (r = -0.574, p = 0.020). The findings suggest that both A-R and CR therapies enhance language function in patients with motor aphasia post-IS, with A-R therapy demonstrating superior efficacy. The therapeutic mechanism of A-R likely involves activating left hemisphere brain regions, suppressing right hemisphere activity, and restoring hemispheric balance to facilitate functional recovery.

titre: Beyond the clinic: a six-month home-based exercise and respiratory rehabilitation program improves functional capacity, respiratory muscle strength, and fatigue in chronic heart failure.
titre_fr: Beyond the clinic: a six-month home-based exercise and respiratory rehabilitation program improves functional capacity, respiratory muscle strength, and fatigue in chronic heart failure.
auteurs: Ciołkiewicz Mariusz, Wojciuk Mariusz, Kuryliszyn-Moskal Anna, Dakowicz Agnieszka, Sawicka-Śmiarowska Emilia, Kamiński Karol
resume: Optimal models of rehabilitation dedicated for patients with heart failure (HF) remain under investigation. The aim of this study was to assess the safety and effectiveness of a 6-month home-based rehabilitation program in patients with HF. 63 patients with stable HF were randomized, 28 patients from intervention group completed the study and were included in the analysis. Assessments including the 6-minute walk test, respiratory muscle strength, and quality of life measures (SF-36 and Fatigue Severity Scale - FSS) were conducted at baseline and after 6 months. Additionally, adverse events and adherence to the training protocol were monitored. Due to objective challenges caused by the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak, the course and final outcomes of the study differed from the original protocol; the control group was not assessed after 6 months. In the intervention group, 6 months of rehabilitation resulted in statistically significant improvements: the 6-minute walk distance increased by 37.86 meters (p = 0.001), maximal inspiratory pressure (PImax) improved by 20.21 cmH₂O, and maximal expiratory pressure (PEmax) by 20.75 cmH₂O (both p < 0.01). A significant reduction in fatigue was observed, as measured by FSS, with a mean decrease of 0.68 points (p = 0.029). Adherence to the exercise protocol averaged 91.5 ± 15.3%. No serious adverse events were reported. The home-based rehabilitation program, including respiratory muscle training, is safe and effective for patients with chronic HF. It improves functional capacity and reduces fatigue levels. https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT03780803, ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03780803. Registered 19/12/2018.

titre: Rhythmic auditory stimulation combined with split-belt treadmill training improves spatiotemporal gait parameters in hemiparetic stroke patients: a randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Rhythmic auditory stimulation combined with split-belt treadmill training improves spatiotemporal gait parameters in hemiparetic stroke patients: a randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Du Minghui, Zhang Wei, Xia Liang, Xia Xiaowu, Qiu Chenglin, Zhan Yixin, Zhang Zhiyuan, Chen Longwei
resume: Split-belt walking training (SWT) primarily ameliorates spatial gait asymmetry after stroke, yet its effect on temporal gait parameters remains limited. Rhythmic auditory stimulation (RAS) enhances cadence and rhythmicity via auditory-motor coupling. This study examined whether combining RAS with SWT yields greater walking benefits than SWT alone or conventional rehabilitation. Thirty patients with post-stroke hemiparesis were randomized to RAS+SWT (n = 11), SWT alone (n = 8), or conventional rehabilitation (control, n = 11). Interventions were delivered for three weeks (five sessions/week). Primary outcomes were spatiotemporal gait parameters: walking speed, cadence, step length, and limping index. Linear mixed-effects models were used, with Hedges' g for effect sizes. No dropouts occurred. Significant time-group interactions were found for walking speed (F = 10.68, p < 0.001), cadence (F = 5.01, p = 0.014), and affected-side step length (F = 6.21, p = 0.006). The RAS+SWT group showed greater improvements than controls in walking speed (mean difference = 0.167, 95% CI [0.090, 0.245]), cadence (mean difference = 9.340, 95% CI [4.456, 14.223]), and step length (unaffected: mean difference = 0.077, 95% CI [0.039, 0.116]; affected: mean difference = 0.081, 95% CI [0.035, 0.127]), and greater walking speed improvements than the SWT group (mean difference = 0.110, 95% CI [0.022, 0.197]). For the limping index, a significant main effect of group was observed (F = 5.41, p = 0.011); however, the time-by-group interaction was not significant (F = 0.430, p = 0.655). RAS combined with SWT is more effective than conventional rehabilitation in improving multidimensional spatiotemporal gait parameters-including walking speed, cadence, and affected-side step length-in patients with post-stroke hemiparesis. Compared with SWT alone, the combined intervention yielded greater improvements in walking speed, while no significant between-group differences were observed for cadence or step length. The combined protocol is feasible and safe. ChiCTR2600121963.

titre: Sense of Coherence in Patients After Intensive Care Treatment: A 1-Year Follow-Up Cohort Study.
titre_fr: Sense of Coherence in Patients After Intensive Care Treatment: A 1-Year Follow-Up Cohort Study.
auteurs: Austenå Mona, Rustøen Tone, Hagen Milada Cvancarova, Valsø Åse, Sunde Kjetil, Tøien Kirsti
resume: Patients endure physical, mental and cognitive symptoms after critical illness, and coping is vital to their healing process. Little research exists on associations between sense of coherence (SOC) and patients' health improvements after intensive care unit (ICU) discharge. To describe the trajectory of SOC and how demographic, clinical and psychosocial variables affect SOC in discharged ICU patients during 12 months of follow-up. A prospective cohort substudy of a neutral randomized controlled trial in Norway involving discharged ICU patients receiving nurse-led follow-up consultations or standard care. Data were collected in the ward (baseline) and after 3, 6 and 12 months. Univariate and multivariate linear mixed models for repeated measures were fitted with SOC-13 score as the dependent variable. We included 523 patients with a median of three ICU days, median age 57 years, 47% females, 54% receiving mechanical ventilation and stable SOC during follow-up. Higher SOC was associated with increased age (B = 0.12, 95% CI [0.05, 0.18]), no prior mental health problems (B = 6.69, 95% CI [4.19, 9.19]), no prior use of psychotropics (B = 2.37, 95% CI [0.16, 4.58]) and lower post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) at baseline (B = 5.56, 95% CI [3.50, 7.61]). Low educational level (B = -2.25, 95% CI [-4.10, -0.40]), higher pain interference at baseline (B = -0.46, 95% CI [-0.84, -0.08]) and less social support 3 months later (B = -5.93, 95% CI [-7.87, -3.99]) were associated with lower SOC. During 12 months after ICU discharge, SOC remained stable. Higher age, no previous mental health problems or use of psychotropics, and lower PTSS were associated with higher SOC. Low education, more pain and low social support were associated with lower SOC. More vulnerable patients deserve greater attention during general rehabilitation after ICU treatment due to low SOC.

titre: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation paired with a 3D-printed ankle-foot orthosis for ankle-foot dysfunction among older adults following subacute stroke: clinical findings and exploratory neurophysiological analyses.
titre_fr: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation paired with a 3D-printed ankle-foot orthosis for ankle-foot dysfunction among older adults following subacute stroke: clinical findings and exploratory neurophysiological analyses.
auteurs: Zhang Yuting, Chen Hehe, Xu Rui, Zhu Lingyu, Song Siyuan, Zhu Weixin
resume: This work evaluated clinical effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) plus custom-made 3D-printed ankle-foot orthosis (AFO) for older adults living with post-stroke ankle-foot impairment. Neurophysiological assessments were also carried out for exploratory purposes, drawing exclusively on indirect physiological readouts. Sixty older participants with ankle-foot dysfunction after subacute stroke were randomized into three parallel groups: conventional-only rehabilitation, 3D-printed AFO therapy, and combined rTMS-AFO intervention (n = 20 per group). Evaluations including ankle active range-of-motion (AROM), resting motor threshold (RMT), integrated surface electromyography (iEMG), Clinical Spasticity Index (CSI), Fugl-Meyer Assessment of the Lower Extremity (FMA-LE), Berg Balance Scale (BBS), and 10-Metre Walking Test (10MWT) were performed at baseline and four-week post-intervention time-point. Noticeable within-group functional improvements emerged in all three study arms upon completion of treatment (p < 0.001). Participants assigned to combined therapy achieved greater functional improvements compared with those receiving standalone 3D-printed-AFO or conventional rehabilitation (p < 0.05). The conventional rehabilitation group produced the weakest magnitude of functional recovery across measured endpoints. Compared with single-modality rehabilitation approaches, adding rTMS to 3D-printed AFO therapy brought measurable improvements in ankle mobility, muscle recruitment, balance and walking performance. These clinical benefits occurred alongside elevated excitability within the ipsilesional corticospinal tract. Explanations regarding sensorimotor integration and afferent-efferent circuit regulation should be regarded as exploratory hypotheses because direct neural measurements were not obtained in this investigation. Further independent research is needed to test these mechanistic assumptions.

titre: Home-based nurse-led self-management support for heart failure: a randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Home-based nurse-led self-management support for heart failure: a randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Çelik Hakan, Özen Betül
resume: To evaluate the effect of a nurse-led, stage-tailored home-based self-management and follow-up programme on self-care behaviour in people with heart failure. People with heart failure require ongoing education, symptom monitoring, and self-management support after specialist assessment. However, access to structured centre-based cardiac rehabilitation may be limited. A nurse-led home-based model may help bridge the gap between specialist cardiology care and community-based long-term support, particularly where rehabilitation services are unavailable. In this parallel-group randomized controlled trial, adults aged 40-75 years with New York Heart Association class I-III heart failure and ejection fraction >30% were allocated to a 12-week home-based programme or usual care. The intervention was delivered through nurse-led home visits and telephone follow-up for clinically stable patients who could not access structured centre-based rehabilitation. The intervention group received home visits and telephone follow-up (n = 32), while the control group received usual care (n = 31). The primary outcome was self-care behaviour. Secondary outcomes were quality of life, self-efficacy, and physical capacity. Exploratory clinical outcomes were body composition, ejection fraction, and HbA1c level. At 12 weeks, the intervention group had better self-care scores than the control group (17.78 ± 2.93 vs 40.00 ± 6.49). Secondary outcomes also favoured the intervention group, with better quality of life scores, higher self-efficacy scores, and greater 6-minute walk distance. Exploratory clinical outcomes showed changes in some parameters, including ejection fraction and body-fluid values. Most intervention participants reached the Transtheoretical Model action stage, and New York Heart Association class improved significantly. This primary health care-relevant home-based model was associated with improved self-care behaviour and may support continuity of care for people with heart failure after specialist cardiology assessment when centre-based rehabilitation is unavailable. The programme improved self-care in people with heart failure and showed potential to support home-based self-management when centre-based cardiac rehabilitation was unavailable.

The intervention group received home visits and telephone follow-up (n = 32), while the control group received usual care (n = 31). The primary outcome was self-care behaviour. Secondary outcomes were quality of life, self-efficacy, and physical capacity. Exploratory clinical outcomes were body composition, ejection fraction, and HbA1c level. At 12 weeks, the intervention group had better self-care scores than the control group (17.78 ± 2.93 vs 40.00 ± 6.49). Secondary outcomes also favoured the intervention group, with better quality of life scores, higher self-efficacy scores, and greater 6-minute walk distance. Exploratory clinical outcomes showed changes in some parameters, including ejection fraction and body-fluid values. Most intervention participants reached the Transtheoretical Model action stage, and New York Heart Association class improved significantly. This primary health care-relevant home-based model was associated with improved self-care behaviour and may support continuity of care for people with heart failure after specialist cardiology assessment when centre-based rehabilitation is unavailable. The programme improved self-care in people with heart failure and showed potential to support home-based self-management when centre-based cardiac rehabilitation was unavailable.

titre: Comparative effectiveness of three splints for rehabilitation after finger flexor tendon repair (FIRST): randomised controlled trial.
titre_fr: Comparative effectiveness of three splints for rehabilitation after finger flexor tendon repair (FIRST): randomised controlled trial.
auteurs: Bamford Emma, Berntsson Hannah, Beale Suzanne, Marks Freya, Desoysa Lauren, Dias Joseph, Hamer-Kiwacz Sienna, Head Charlotte, Hind Daniel, Johnson Nick, Loban Amanda, Malloy Kaye, Morvan Emma, Rombach Ines, Selby Anna, Turtle Chris, Walters Stephen, Young Tracey, Drummond Avril
resume: To compare the clinical effectiveness of three splints after repair of zone 1 and 2 flexor tendons: forearm based (long), Manchester short (short), and relative motion flexion (mini) splints. Prospective, randomised, parallel group, pragmatic, superiority, clinical trial. 26 UK hospitals. 430 participants (aged ≥16 years) requiring rehabilitation after primary repair of zone 1 and 2 flexor tendons in one or two fingers of the hand according to British Society for Surgery of the Hand guidelines. Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to the long, short, or mini splint. Splints were worn continuously for five weeks and intermittently for a further week at night and in vulnerable situations such as public environments. Masking participants was not possible owing to the nature of the intervention. The primary outcome was the mean post-randomisation score on the patient-rated wrist and hand evaluation (PRWHE) instrument at 6, 12, 26, and 52 weeks, analysed by intention to treat. 430 participants were randomised to the long splint (n=143), short splint (n=140), or mini splint (n=147) and 403 were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. Adherence, defined as wearing the splint for a minimum of five weeks, was 83% (118/143) for the long splint, 76% (106/140) for the short splint, and 78% (115/147) for the mini splint. Mean post-randomisation PRWHE scores were 24.5 (standard deviation 15.5) in the long splint group, 23.5 (16.7) in the short splint group, and 22.4 (15.0) in the mini splint group, with adjusted between group differences of 0.3 (98.3% confidence interval -4.0 to 4.6, P=0.88) for the long versus short splint, 2.3 (-1.9 to 6.5, P=0.19) for the long versus mini splint, and 2.0 (-2.2 to 6.3, P=0.25) for the short versus mini splint. Serious adverse event rates occurred in 10% (14/143) of participants in the long splint group, 11% (15/140) in the short splint group, and 11% (16/147) in the mini splint group. This trial found no statistically significant difference in clinical effectiveness between the long, short, and mini splint. Apart from some small differences, secondary outcomes were comparable across all three groups. ISRCTN Registry ISRCTN10236011.

titre: The effect of dual task-oriented circuit training on neuroplasticity and walking adaptability in subacute stroke patients: A pilot and feasibility study.
titre_fr: The effect of dual task-oriented circuit training on neuroplasticity and walking adaptability in subacute stroke patients: A pilot and feasibility study.
auteurs: Arisanti Farida, Ropii Bejo, Ghaida Saniy, Tristiana Dewi Tsuchiya, Poernomo Bernadeta Cahyo Setianingrum, Sribudiani Yunia, Amalia Lisda, Engkasan Julia Patrick, Biben Vitriana
resume: Stroke remains a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide, with a substantial proportion of survivors experiencing persistent limitations in functional mobility. Although many individuals regain the ability to walk in structured clinical environments, only a minority achieve independent community ambulation due to cognitive-motor interference (CMI). The subacute phase is characterized by heightened neuroplastic potential and responsiveness to rehabilitation. Dual Task-Oriented Circuit Training (DTOCT) integrates task-oriented circuit training with concurrent cognitive challenges and may provide a functionally relevant approach to addressing cognitive-motor interference. However, its feasibility, safety, and preliminary effects in subacute stroke remain unclear. This three-arm, participant-blinded, randomized pilot and feasibility trial will recruit 36 individuals with subacute stroke and allocate them equally to DTOCT, Task-Oriented Circuit Training (TOCT), or Dual Task Training (DTT). Participants will receive three supervised sessions per week for 4 weeks (12 sessions). Primary outcomes will assess feasibility and safety, including adherence, retention, adverse events, heart rate, blood pressure, and perceived exertion. Secondary exploratory outcomes will include walking endurance assessed using the 6-Minute Walk Test, gait speed using the 10-Meter Walk Test, walking adaptability using the Standardized Walking Obstacle Course, and serum brain-derived neurotrophic factor as an exploratory peripheral biomarker associated with neuroplasticity. This pilot study is designed to determine the feasibility and safety of DTOCT and to generate preliminary effect estimates for clinical and neurobiological outcomes. The findings will inform primary outcome selection, intervention refinement, and sample-size estimation for a subsequent adequately powered randomized controlled trial rather than establish definitive efficacy or superiority. ClinicalTrials.gov. Identifier: NCT07494357 (registered prospectively). Protocol ID: IKFR-202603.01).

titre: An Exploratory Randomized Clinical Trial to Assess the Effects of Vitamin D and Leucine-Enriched Whey Protein Supplementation on Inflammaging and Gut Eubacterial Biomass in Cardiac Rehabilitation Patients.
titre_fr: An Exploratory Randomized Clinical Trial to Assess the Effects of Vitamin D and Leucine-Enriched Whey Protein Supplementation on Inflammaging and Gut Eubacterial Biomass in Cardiac Rehabilitation Patients.
auteurs: Gheri Chiara Francesca, Luisi Maria Luisa Eliana, Lucarini Laura, Biffi Barbara, Madiai Sara, Roccotelli Angela, Zipoli Renato, Sgambellone Silvia, Provensi Gustavo, Macchi Claudio, Masini Emanuela, Ceccherini Maria Teresa
resume: Whey protein (WP) supplementation could affect low-grade inflammation (inflammaging) and gut microbiome dysbiosis, both of which play key roles in non-communicable diseases (NCDs). Twenty-seven cardiac rehabilitation patients were randomly allocated to two groups: the case group (CA) (n = 14) received 80 g/die vitamin D and leucine-enriched WP supplement, combined with a standard hospital diet, while the control group (CO, n = 13) received the standard hospital diet alone. Blood and stool samples were collected at baseline (T0) and after two weeks (T1). At T1, serum levels of interleukin 6 (IL-6) and C-reactive protein (CRP) significantly decreased in the CA group. Ferritin levels significantly decreased within both groups and between the two groups. No significant differences were observed for IL-1β, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), or IL-10. A clear difference in the bacterial intestinal microbiome composition between the case group at T1 (CAT1) and at T0 (CAT0), and control group at T0 (COT0) and at T1 (COT1), was observed. The eubacterial rpoB copy number, which was quantified by qPCR, significantly increased between CAT0 and CAT1, in contrast to the Lactobacillus spp. rpoB copy number. Our exploratory results showed that vitamin D and leucine-enriched WP supplementation could have a potential effect on chronic inflammation and gut microbiota composition in cardiac rehabilitation patients.

titre: Effects of grip strengthening combined with scapular stabilization exercise on shoulder muscle strength and functional outcomes in individuals with subacromial pain syndrome: A randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Effects of grip strengthening combined with scapular stabilization exercise on shoulder muscle strength and functional outcomes in individuals with subacromial pain syndrome: A randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Lee Jae-Hyun, Chung Eunjung, Lee Byoung-Hee
resume: Subacromial pain syndrome (SAPS) is one of the most common causes of shoulder pain and is frequently associated with rotator cuff dysfunction. Recent evidence suggests a close relationship between hand grip strength and rotator cuff muscle function, indicating that grip-strengthening exercises may enhance shoulder rehabilitation outcomes. To investigate the effects of grip strengthening combined with scapular stabilization exercise on shoulder muscle strength, grip strength, and functional outcomes in individuals with SAPS. Thirty-six individuals with SAPS were randomly assigned to an experimental group (scapular stabilization exercise combined with grip strengthening; n = 18) or a control group (scapular stabilization exercise alone; n = 18). Both groups participated in exercise sessions 3 times per week for 4 weeks. Shoulder muscle strength, grip strength, and functional outcomes using the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index were assessed before and after the intervention. Both groups showed significant improvements in shoulder muscle strength, grip strength, and Shoulder Pain and Disability Index scores (P < .001). Significant Time × Group interaction effects were observed for all outcome measures (P < .001), indicating greater improvements in the experimental group. Grip strengthening combined with scapular stabilization exercise may provide additional benefits for improving shoulder muscle strength, grip strength, and functional outcomes in individuals with SAPS.

titre: Clinical study of isokinetic training with joint control tasks on lower limb function in stroke patients with proprioceptive impairment: a preliminary randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Clinical study of isokinetic training with joint control tasks on lower limb function in stroke patients with proprioceptive impairment: a preliminary randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Zhang Zhendong, Yu Huixian, Li Ping, Li Na, Zhang Yumei
resume: To investigate the effects of isokinetic training with joint control tasks on lower limb proprioceptive and motor function in stroke patients with proprioceptive impairment. A randomized controlled trial design was adopted. Stroke patients with proprioceptive dysfunction who were admitted to the Department of Rehabilitation Medicine, Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Capital Medical University, between April 2025 and November 2025 were prospectively and consecutively enrolled. Participants were randomly assigned to an experimental group or a control group using a random number table. Both groups received conventional rehabilitation for 4 weeks, while the experimental group additionally underwent isokinetic training with joint control tasks during the same intervention period. General demographic and clinical data were collected. Before and after intervention, proprioception, motor function, and activities of daily living (ADL) were assessed. Based on the predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, 58 eligible patients were finally enrolled and randomly allocated into two groups (29 patients per group). Within-group comparisons showed that both groups exhibited significant post-intervention improvements in proprioceptive function, motor function, and activities of daily living (ADL) (all P < 0.05). In the control group, the Modified Nottingham Sensory Assessment (NSA), Joint Position Reproduction (JPR) tests at 30°, 45°, and 60°, Threshold to Detect Passive Motion (TTDPM), Berg Balance Scale (BBS), Fugl-Meyer Assessment for the lower extremity (FMA-LE), and Modified Barthel Index (MBI) scores all improved significantly compared with baseline (P < 0.05). Similarly, in the experimental group, all aforementioned indicators demonstrated significant improvements after intervention (P < 0.05). Between-group comparisons revealed that improvements in proprioceptive, motor, and ADL functions were significantly greater in the experimental group than in the control group. Specifically, the changes in NSA, JPR (30°, 45°, 60°), and TTDPM scores were significantly higher in the experimental group (P < 0.05). Furthermore, the experimental group exhibited larger gains in BBS and FMA-LE scores (P < 0.05), as well as greater improvements in MBI scores (P < 0.05). Isokinetic joint control training combined with conventional rehabilitation was associated with improvements in proprioceptive function, lower-limb motor performance, and activities of daily living in stroke patients with proprioceptive impairment. These findings suggest that this approach may serve as a useful adjunct to stroke rehabilitation; however, further studies with more rigorous designs are required to confirm these results.

titre: Preserved anabolic skeletal muscle capacity in response to exercise and protein intake after critical illness.
titre_fr: Preserved anabolic skeletal muscle capacity in response to exercise and protein intake after critical illness.
auteurs: Fischer-Hammerschmied Arabella, Tardif Nicolas, Mandić Mirko, Gustafsson Thomas, Apro William, Helleberg Johan, Amouzandeh Mariam, Grip Jonathan, Seldén Dag, Rooyackers Olav, Sundström Rehal Martin
resume: Low muscle mass and persistent weakness are common after critical illness, but the mechanisms behind impaired recovery are incompletely understood. The aim of this study was to investigate the skeletal muscle anabolic response to combined resistance exercise and protein intake in intensive care unit (ICU) survivors, compared to matched controls without a history of critical illness. We hypothesised that residual anabolic resistance limits muscle regeneration after ICU stay. Former patients were enrolled within 3 to 6 months of intensive care unit discharge. Muscle biopsies were obtained before and after resistance exercise using a flywheel leg extension ergometer, combined with ingestion of 24 g hydrolysed protein. Muscle protein fractional synthetic rate was determined from the incorporation of [ring-²H₅]phenylalanine into mixed-muscle protein during a primed continuous intravenous infusion. Anabolic and proteolytic pathways were measured using standard assays. Group-by-time differences were analysed using linear mixed models. The primary comparison was the between-group difference in pre-to-post change in muscle protein synthesis. Twenty ICU survivors (60 ± 12 years, 30% female, BMI 26.9 (IQR 22.9-28.7), SAPS 3 62.3 ± 15.8) and 20 age- and sex-matched controls were included. ICU survivors had significantly lower quadriceps muscle thickness (p = 0.02) and handgrip strength (p = 0.04) than controls. In ICU survivors, muscle protein synthesis from plasma precursor amino acids was higher at baseline than in controls (0.041%/hour vs. 0.030%/hour, p = 0.009), but increased less (Δ 0.031 vs. Δ 0.040%/hour, p = 0.04). Post-intervention muscle protein synthesis was similar between groups (0.071%/hour vs. 0.070%/hour, p = 0.70). At baseline, ICU survivors showed lower activation of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway. In both groups, the intervention increased anabolic signalling, decreased initiation of autophagy and increased parts of the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. In ICU survivors with persistent muscle loss and weakness, the increase in muscle protein synthesis after combined resistance exercise and protein intake was smaller than in controls, in the context of a higher baseline fractional synthetic rate. Post-intervention muscle protein synthesis rates were similar between groups. These findings provide the first mechanistic support for structured exercise-nutrition rehabilitation to promote muscle recovery after critical illness. This study was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05261984), 2022-02-20.
