titre: Impact of malnutrition and protein-enriched oral nutrition on early recovery after fragility fractures in older adults: the NuTra trial.
titre_fr: Impact of malnutrition and protein-enriched oral nutrition on early recovery after fragility fractures in older adults: the NuTra trial.
auteurs: Vogel Carolina, Heyl Moritz, Vollmer Louis, Schuhmacher Julia, Demissie Johanna, Haas Dannik, Braun Benedikt J, Herath Steven C, Histing Tina, Rollmann Mika F
resume: Malnutrition is highly prevalent in geriatric trauma patients and is associated with impaired recovery, complications, and reduced likelihood of returning home. Nonetheless, the impact of a targeted protein-enriched diet during the acute hospital stay on patient outcome and rehabilitation remains to be investigated. This single-center randomized controlled study enrolled patients ≥ 70 years with fragility fractures admitted to a Level I trauma center. Nutritional status was assessed using the Nutritional Risk Screening 2002 and Mini Nutritional Assessment. Patients screened positive in ≥ 1 tool were classified as being at nutritional risk and randomized to a protein-enriched diet (Group A) or standard diet (Group B); patients with negative screening served as observational reference group without nutritional risk (Group C). The intervention targeted 1.5-2.0 g/kg/day protein. Primary outcomes were in-hospital medical complications, surgical site infections and functional mobility at discharge. Secondary outcomes included length of stay, discharge destination, and in-hospital mortality. Multinomial logistic regression assessed independent associations with discharge destination. Of the 218 patients (mean age 81.8 ± 6.9 years; 72.0% female), 100 (45.9%) screened positive for being at nutritional risk and were randomized to intervention (A, n = 46) or control (B, n = 54), while 118 (54.1%) patients without nutritional risk served as reference group (C). Patients at nutritional risk showed higher comorbidity burdens, higher ASA classes, and greater frailty than group C. Medical complications occurred in 45.0% of patients, with no significant differences between groups. Serum albumin decreased and CRP increased during hospitalization, without differences among the groups. Patients in reference group C were more often independently mobile and discharged home, whereas all patients at nutritional risk more frequently required institutional care. In multivariable analysis, a higher age-adjusted CCI was independently associated with discharge destination, whereas no independent effect of the nutritional intervention was observed. In this geriatric trauma cohort, being at nutritional risk was closely linked to frailty and multimorbidity. A protein-enriched diet during the acute hospital stay did not translate into measurable short-term benefits regarding complications, functional mobility, length of stay or discharge destination. Nutritional risk should therefore be considered within the broader context of overall vulnerability, and nutritional care may need to be embedded in comprehensive longitudinal rehabilitation strategies extending beyond the acute in-hospital phase. The study was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov on 12 May 2026 (NCT07582575).

titre: A Remotely Delivered Exercise-Based Rehabilitation Program for Patients with Persistent Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy (EX-CIPN): A Phase I Feasibility Trial.
titre_fr: A Remotely Delivered Exercise-Based Rehabilitation Program for Patients with Persistent Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy (EX-CIPN): A Phase I Feasibility Trial.
auteurs: Antonen Eric M, Nadler Michelle B, Langelier David M, Campbell Kristin L, Flamer David, Cho Jang Hyuk, Capozza Scott, Avery Lisa, Bland Kelcey A, Leatherdale Scott, Manthorne Jackie, Al-Khaifi Muna, Jones Jennifer M
resume: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) affects two-thirds of patients who receive neurotoxic chemotherapy. In almost half of these patients, CIPN is persistent, with limited treatment options. Exercise-based rehabilitation shows promising results in improving CIPN-related outcomes, but high-quality research is needed with CIPN symptoms and disability as primary endpoints. We conducted a phase I single-arm, multi-method pilot study of a 10-week remotely delivered exercise-based rehabilitation program (EX-CIPN) for adult (≥18-years) cancer survivors experiencing CIPN symptoms ≥6 months post-chemotherapy. titre: Little league shoulder revisited: a systematic review of the last decade.
titre_fr: Little league shoulder revisited: a systematic review of the last decade.
auteurs: Lenz Annika, Johnson Luke, Riederer Mark, Provance Aaron
resume: Physeal stress injuries involving the shoulder epiphyseal growth plate complex, known as Little League Shoulder (LLS), occur primarily in skeletally immature overhead athletes. This systematic review included research on LLS published within the last 10 years, from 1 January 2015 through 23 September 2025, from four electronic databases (Embase, PubMed, SPORTDiscus, Cochrane Library) focusing on diagnosis, management, imaging, and criteria for return-to-sport. LLS is mainly described in male, skeletally immature overhead athletes aged 11-15. Early specialization, multi-team participation, and inadequate rest are reported risk factors. LLS commonly presents with throwing-related shoulder pain, proximal humeral physis tenderness, posterior capsule tightness, and scapular dyskinesia. X-rays remain first-line imaging, demonstrating lateral physeal widening and irregularity. Throwing cessation for 2-4 months, followed by rehabilitation and gradual return-to-throwing yields excellent short-term outcomes, with low rates of growth disturbance. Prevention strategies include pitch-counts, rest, proper throwing mechanics, and delayed specialization. The prevalence of LLS remains unknown due to variable diagnostic criteria, imaging use, and underreporting. Recurrence and long-term sequelae are inconsistent across studies, and the reasons athletes discontinue baseball remain uncertain. Evidence is conflicting regarding the benefits of formal rehabilitation compared with rest alone. Advanced imaging demonstrates structural remodeling of the shoulder, suggesting that repetitive loading during skeletal immaturity impacts long-term morphology and mechanics. Prospective studies using clinical and imaging criteria may help define the incidence, severity, risk factors, sport-specific patterns, and to clarify symptom resolution, humeral remodeling, and factors influencing attrition. Longitudinal studies should compare rest versus structured rehabilitation and varying return-to-throwing protocols.

titre: A comparison of the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants with low molecular weight heparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: A comparison of the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants with low molecular weight heparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Mohammad Hasan R, Rahman Azmi, Muhammad Ibrahim M, Gill Saran Singh, Selim Amr, Thomas Geraint, Murray David W, Griffin Xavier L
resume: To evaluate differences in the efficacy and safety of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) used for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after elective total hip arthroplasty (THA). This systematic review and meta-analysis reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from conception to 13 December 2025, for any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the efficacy (VTE risk) and safety (bleeding risk) of LMWH and DOACs after elective THA. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) of VTE, bleeding, reoperation, and mortality risks were assessed. A total of 22 RCTs involving 28,112 participants were included. The risk of VTE in the DOAC group was lower compared with the LMWH group (OR 0.62 (95% CI 0.47 to 0.82); p = 0.002), driven by a reduction in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) risk (OR 0.60 (95% CI 0.42 to 0.86); p = 0.008). The findings remained consistent in the subgroup analysis restricted to anticoagulants and dosages licensed for use in the UK. Overall bleeding risk was higher in the DOAC group (OR 1.19 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.38); p = 0.023), but no difference was seen when comparing only UK-licensed anticoagulants and doses (OR 1.06 (95% CI 0.95 to 1.18); p = 0.279). Reoperation risk (OR 1.21 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.93); p = 0.351) and mortality (OR 1.03 (95% CI 0.46 to 2.33); p = 0.937) did not differ between groups. DOACs reduce the risk of VTE and DVT following elective THA compared with LMWH without increasing bleeding risk, for UK-licensed agents and doses. Switching to DOACs could save the NHS £8.6 million per year. New clinical trials are needed to compare the safety and efficacy of UK-licensed DOACs and LWMH with modern postoperative rehabilitation protocols.

titre: Remote supervised exercise- and physical activity-based rehabilitation for post-stroke depression, anxiety, and quality of life: a systematic review, evidence map, and exploratory quantitative synthesis.
titre_fr: Remote supervised exercise- and physical activity-based rehabilitation for post-stroke depression, anxiety, and quality of life: a systematic review, evidence map, and exploratory quantitative synthesis.
auteurs: Zhang Cheng, Zhou Zhou, Cai Jie, Li Yuanyuan
resume: Depression, anxiety, and reduced quality of life are common after stroke and may interfere with rehabilitation engagement and long-term recovery. Remote supervision can support home-based exercise or physical activity, but the available programs are complex packages that may also include coaching, caregiver involvement, education, and psychological support. We aimed to synthesize randomized evidence on depression, anxiety, and quality of life after remotely supervised exercise- or physical activity-based stroke rehabilitation, accounting for comparator type and co-interventions. This systematic review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261394314) and reported according to PRISMA 2020. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, SPORTDiscus, Cochrane Library, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception to 1 March 2026. Randomized studies of remotely supervised exercise- or physical activity-based rehabilitation after ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke were eligible if depression, anxiety, or quality-of-life outcomes were extractable. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, certainty was evaluated using GRADE, and a co-intervention sensitivity analysis examined the evidence remaining after exclusion of interventions with explicit psychological support. Six randomized studies involving 483 participants were included. Interventions, comparators, outcome instruments, and study designs were heterogeneous, precluding a primary pooled meta-analysis. The only directly analyzable depression effect against standard care came from Sun et al., a 12-week multidisciplinary telerehabilitation program that included online psychological counseling; the aligned Hedges g was 0.93 (95% CI 0.64 to 1.22), conventionally large, but certainty was very low. After this trial was excluded, no directly analyzable depression effect against standard care remained. Active-vs-active depression or distress findings did not establish superiority. Quality-of-life signals varied across instruments and comparators; no separable patient anxiety effect was available. The included evidence concerns complex remote rehabilitation packages rather than exercise alone. A possible depression benefit is supported principally by one trial with a psychological-support co-intervention and is therefore fragile. Remote programs should not be regarded as stand-alone treatments for post-stroke depression or anxiety. Confirmatory trials should recruit or stratify participants by baseline psychiatric symptoms, prespecify psychiatric outcomes, and separate exercise from psychological and implementation components. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261394314, identifier CRD420261394314.

titre: Clinical guidelines for the management of osteoporosis in China: a systematic review.
titre_fr: Clinical guidelines for the management of osteoporosis in China: a systematic review.
auteurs: Wei Ting, Xu Lizheng, Xiong Shangzhi, Zhang Xinyi, Tian Maoyi, Yang Minghui, Wang Yongcheng, Chen Mingsheng, Abbott Penelope, Wong Peter K K, Kolt Gregory S, Si Lei
resume: The rising prevalence of osteoporosis and related fractures contributes substantially to the clinical and economic burden in China, particularly in the context of an ageing population. In response, various Chinese medical specialties and organisations have developed clinical guidelines for osteoporosis management, specifically tailored to the needs of the Chinese population. This systematic review aimed to compare and evaluate the consistency and divergence among these guidelines. A systematic search of Medline, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science was conducted for English-language papers. As well, a search of Chinese databases (China National Knowledge Infrastructure and Wanfang) and Chinese government websites was conducted. The search included documents published up to 13 August 2026. Article screening and data extraction were conducted by two independent reviewers. Management guidelines for primary osteoporosis in Chinese adults were included. Exclusion criteria were guidelines for secondary osteoporosis, guidelines for osteoporotic fractures that did not address osteoporosis management, previous versions of guidelines, and management protocols specific to local hospitals, organisations, communities, or rehabilitation centres. The methodological quality of guidelines was evaluated with the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research & Evaluation II (AGREE II). Our search yielded 8,100 records, from which 32 guidelines produced by over 60 professional societies across multiple medical specialties were included. While there was consensus on the definition of osteoporosis, diagnostic criteria, prevention strategies, and the inclusion of both pharmacological and non-pharmacological treatment approaches, notable differences emerged in specific treatment recommendations. These discrepancies often reflected differences in the clinical focus of individual disciplines, such as orthopaedics, endocrinology, and geriatrics, particularly regarding diagnosis, treatment or rehabilitation, and patient populations. Unlike other international guidelines, fracture liaison services and health economic considerations, including cost-effectiveness analyses, were addressed in only some of the included guidelines. This systematic review synthesises current osteoporosis management guidelines in China and highlights important inconsistencies in recommendations. The findings underscore the need for high-quality, context-specific research and greater incorporation of health economic evidence to inform the development of more coherent and evidence-based national guidelines. https://osf.io/j83s4/, identifier j83s4.

titre: Quality of osteoporosis management guidelines produced in China: a systematic review.
titre_fr: Quality of osteoporosis management guidelines produced in China: a systematic review.
auteurs: Liu Xiaonan, Ge Mengya, Wu Caie, Shen Kai, Yang Jin, Sun Shunxia
resume: This study employed the AGREE II and AGREE-REX instruments to assess the methodological rigor and recommendation quality of Chinese clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for osteoporosis care. A systematic search was conducted across CNKI, SinoMed, Wanfang, VIP, Medlive, and the Chinese Medical Association website for CPGs published between January 2014 and December 2025. AGREE II was used to evaluate methodological quality, while AGREE-REX was applied to guidelines scoring ≥50% in at least three AGREE II domains. A total of 13 CPGs were analyzed. The median overall quality score was 54% (IQR: 49%-71%). The rigor of development domain scored the lowest [38% (25%-94%)], whereas stakeholder involvement and clarity of presentation scored the highest [72% (44%-72%) and 72% (61%-83%), respectively]. Ten guidelines met the threshold for AGREE-REX assessment, with a median recommendation quality score of 56% (32%-63%). A positive correlation was found between AGREE-REX and AGREE II overall scores (r = 0.665). The methodological and recommendation quality of Chinese osteoporosis CPGs is moderate. Recommendations focusing on functional assessment, diet and exercise, rehabilitation, and environmental modifications are valuable. Furthermore, traditional Chinese medicine exercises may offer a reference for CPG development in other countries. https://ebn.nursing.fudan.edu.cn/myRegisterList, identifier, ER20240722.

titre: Comparative Effectiveness of Digital Exercise-Based Interventions for Improving Balance in Older Adults: Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis With GRADE Certainty of Evidence.
titre_fr: Comparative Effectiveness of Digital Exercise-Based Interventions for Improving Balance in Older Adults: Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis With GRADE Certainty of Evidence.
auteurs: Li Fangbo, Li Xuecheng, Li Qingfang, Gong Xiaoqin, Shi Kexin, Huang Yongyu, Feng Xiaowei, Zhang Dong
resume: Technology-based rehabilitation is increasingly used for balance training in older adults. A 2023 network meta-analysis (NMA) found only exergaming with motion capture superior to no treatment; however, the evidence has since expanded, and no GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) appraisal has been applied. This study aimed to update the comparative effectiveness of 5 technology categories-exergaming with balance platforms (EBP), exergaming with motion capture (EMC), other serious games, interventions with wearables, and telerehabilitation (Tele)-versus conventional exercise (CE), and no treatment (NT), applying GRADE adapted for NMA. A systematic search of 4 databases from inception through April 2025, with an identical supplementary update search to January 31, 2026, identified 60 randomized controlled trials (N=3469; mean age 73.1, SD 5.2; range 63.3-86.2 y). Fifty-seven trials (2758 analyzed participants) contributed to 4 prespecified networks (all balance, functional scales, Timed Up and Go [TUG] test, and gait speed). A random-effects NMA was fitted using multivariate meta-regression. Treatment hierarchies were summarized by the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) and the probability of being best; certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE adapted for NMA. In the all-balance network, Tele (standardized mean difference [SMD] 0.69, 95% CI 0.08-1.29; P=.03), EBP (SMD 0.63, 95% CI 0.31-0.95; P<.001), EMC (SMD 0.58, 95% CI 0.22-0.95; P=.002), and CE (SMD 0.35, 95% CI 0.03-0.68; P=.03) were superior to NT, with consistent findings in the TUG network (EBP 0.81, 95% CI 0.42-1.20; Tele 0.82, 95% CI 0.16-1.49; EMC 0.79, 95% CI 0.36-1.21; all P<.05). Tele ranked first by SUCRA (76.3%), but its probability of being best was only approximately 41%, and the estimate rested on 5 trials (n=198). No technology-based intervention was superior to CE in any network. Certainty of evidence was moderate for EBP versus NT and EMC versus NT in the TUG network only; the 37 other comparisons were low or very low. Dropout did not differ between technology-based and control arms (odds ratio 1.10, 95% CI 0.87-1.40; P=.41). Tele, EBP, and EMC were each associated with improved balance versus NT, although none exceeded CE. The first-place SUCRA ranking of Tele is preliminary. Certainty was moderate only for EBP and EMC versus NT on the TUG test; the remaining evidence is too uncertain for firm clinical recommendations. As no included trial reported falls, these findings are not direct evidence of fall prevention. Larger trials with standardized comparator intensity and posttraining follow-up are required.

titre: Long-term quality of life, rehospitalization risks, and economic viability of remote cardiac rehabilitation: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Long-term quality of life, rehospitalization risks, and economic viability of remote cardiac rehabilitation: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Pei Hui, Li Hengrui, Hu Miaomiao, Liu Boyan, Hu Dali, Li Yuanmin, Xiao Qiang
resume: Although remote cardiac rehabilitation (RCR) is a promising alternative to traditional center-based care, evidence regarding its exact impact on health-related quality of life (HRQoL), cardiovascular safety, and economic viability remains fragmented, necessitating a comprehensive synthesis to guide clinical implementation. This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to evaluate the HRQoL, cardiovascular safety, and economic viability of RCR versus standard center-based care in cardiovascular disease, with subgroup analyses based on follow-up duration and high-risk patient cohorts. Literature searches were conducted across multiple databases, including PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by manual screening of relevant references to identify clinical studies on RCR up to July 2026. Two independent review teams performed data extraction and risk of bias assessment using the RevMan software. Meta-analyses were conducted employing random-effects models to calculate pooled effect sizes with corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was assessed using the Cochrane Q test and I 2 statistic, and potential publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test. To evaluate the robustness of the pooled results and explore potential heterogeneity, subgroup and fixed-effects sensitivity analyses were conducted, supplemented by trial sequential analysis (TSA). A total of 45 randomized controlled trials were included in this meta-analysis. RCR significantly improved HRQoL across multiple scales (MacNew: MD = 0.17; MLHFQ: MD = -5.38; P < 0.05), while maintaining SF-36 and HADS outcomes comparable to standard care. Exploratory analyses indicated statistically significant improvements in mental health at 6 months (MD = 1.73, P = 0.03) and physical functioning at 12 months (MD = 1.48, P = 0.0002). Regarding cardiovascular safety, RCR was not associated with a statistically significant increase in the risk of MACEs, all-cause mortality, or adverse events (P > 0.05) compared to conventional care. RCR significantly reduced the risk of cardiac rehospitalization (RR = 0.70, P = 0.01), with exploratory stratified analyses indicating that this favorable association was evident in the hardware-integrated interventions subgroup (RR = 0.59, P = 0.02) and 6-month observation subgroup (RR = 0.38, P < 0.00001), alongside a non-significant numerical protective trend among high-risk patients (RR: 0.59 vs. 0.74, P = 0.15). The economic viability of RCR remains uncertain, critically depending on initial setup outlays, patient scaling, and subsequent healthcare utilization. RCR may serve as an effective and safe alternative to conventional care that improves physical and psychological well-being, was associated with a lower risk of cardiac rehospitalization, and may provide economic value in certain healthcare systems. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261374977, PROSPERO CRD420261374977.

This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to evaluate the HRQoL, cardiovascular safety, and economic viability of RCR versus standard center-based care in cardiovascular disease, with subgroup analyses based on follow-up duration and high-risk patient cohorts. Literature searches were conducted across multiple databases, including PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by manual screening of relevant references to identify clinical studies on RCR up to July 2026. Two independent review teams performed data extraction and risk of bias assessment using the RevMan software. Meta-analyses were conducted employing random-effects models to calculate pooled effect sizes with corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was assessed using the Cochrane Q test and I 2 statistic, and potential publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test. To evaluate the robustness of the pooled results and explore potential heterogeneity, subgroup and fixed-effects sensitivity analyses were conducted, supplemented by trial sequential analysis (TSA). A total of 45 randomized controlled trials were included in this meta-analysis. RCR significantly improved HRQoL across multiple scales (MacNew: MD = 0.17; MLHFQ: MD = -5.38; P < 0.05), while maintaining SF-36 and HADS outcomes comparable to standard care. Exploratory analyses indicated statistically significant improvements in mental health at 6 months (MD = 1.73, P = 0.03) and physical functioning at 12 months (MD = 1.48, P = 0.0002). Regarding cardiovascular safety, RCR was not associated with a statistically significant increase in the risk of MACEs, all-cause mortality, or adverse events (P > 0.05) compared to conventional care. RCR significantly reduced the risk of cardiac rehospitalization (RR = 0.70, P = 0.01), with exploratory stratified analyses indicating that this favorable association was evident in the hardware-integrated interventions subgroup (RR = 0.59, P = 0.02) and 6-month observation subgroup (RR = 0.38, P < 0.00001), alongside a non-significant numerical protective trend among high-risk patients (RR: 0.59 vs. 0.74, P = 0.15). The economic viability of RCR remains uncertain, critically depending on initial setup outlays, patient scaling, and subsequent healthcare utilization. RCR may serve as an effective and safe alternative to conventional care that improves physical and psychological well-being, was associated with a lower risk of cardiac rehospitalization, and may provide economic value in certain healthcare systems. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261374977, PROSPERO CRD420261374977.

titre: Psychological factors as predictors of compliance and outcome in non-operative management of Achilles tendon rupture: a systematic review.
titre_fr: Psychological factors as predictors of compliance and outcome in non-operative management of Achilles tendon rupture: a systematic review.
auteurs: Maffulli Nicola, Spiezia Filippo
resume: Non-operative management of acute Achilles tendon rupture (ATR) with early functional rehabilitation produces functional outcomes equivalent to surgery, but its effectiveness depends critically on patient compliance with bracing, weight-bearing and physiotherapy. Psychological factors, including motivation, self-efficacy, kinesiophobia, and social support, are plausible determinants of compliance and outcome, yet have received minimal systematic attention. Seven databases were searched from inception to June 2026 without language restriction. Studies of adults with ATR managed non-operatively, with any psychological assessment reporting compliance, re-rupture rate, Achilles Tendon Total Rupture Score (ATRS) or return to sport, were eligible. Six studies met the inclusion criteria (797 non-operative patients in total), and two further non-operative randomized controlled trials were used for functional benchmarking only. Data were synthesized narratively (SWiM framework). Non-operative management with early functional rehabilitation yields ATRS scores of 72-86 at 6-12 months, comparable to operative cohorts, with re-rupture rates of 5%-12% under functional bracing. Treatment success depends on patient compliance, and functional deficits persist for years irrespective of the management modality. Surgery continues to carry a lower re-rupture incidence than conservative management, although the absolute difference has narrowed with early functional rehabilitation. Whether pre-treatment psychological profiling should inform the choice between operative and non-operative management remains unvalidated, and no included study reported compliance as a formal outcome or its association with any psychological factor. Kinesiophobia, anxiety, and depression are present throughout the first year of non-operative rehabilitation, and kinesiophobia scores above the clinical cut-off were observed in most participants of the only dedicated non-operative cohort. Kinesiophobia and readiness-to-return scores do not appear to differ between operatively and non-operatively managed patients, supporting a common psychological assessment framework. Qualitative evidence identifies motivation and social support as key facilitators of recovery. Future non-operative ATR randomized trials should incorporate the I-PRRS, TSK-11, and a validated motivation measure as pre-specified secondary outcomes, together with guideline-based compliance definitions. A prospective cohort study of baseline psychological profile as a predictor of compliance and re-rupture should be prioritized, followed by evaluation of simple psychological screening within consent and treatment-selection pathways.

titre: Non-Invasive Neuromodulation for Post-Stroke Anxiety Symptoms: An Umbrella Review and Evidence Mapping of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses.
titre_fr: Non-Invasive Neuromodulation for Post-Stroke Anxiety Symptoms: An Umbrella Review and Evidence Mapping of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses.
auteurs: Li Tiantian, He Lijuan, Li Fenghui, Zhang Jianyun
resume: Post-stroke anxiety can impair rehabilitation, participation, and quality of life. This umbrella review mapped systematic reviews on non-invasive neuromodulation for anxiety symptoms after stroke. PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Embase were searched from inception through June 1, 2026. Published reviews with quantitative anxiety results were eligible, including reviews in which anxiety was secondary to pain, sleep disturbance, or depression. Reporting completeness, methodological quality, and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement, A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews 2 (AMSTAR 2), and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, respectively. Seven reviews were mapped, comprising six pairwise meta-analyses and one Bayesian network meta-analysis. Selected estimates suggested symptom improvement, whereas others showed no clear difference. All reviews had low or critically low methodological quality. Interpretation was limited by overlapping trials, small outcome-specific sample sizes, heterogeneous interventions, and inconsistencies across source reports. Anxiety-score changes in populations recruited for other post-stroke conditions do not establish a direct effect on clinically defined post-stroke anxiety. Source-level population eligibility and certainty judgments require particular scrutiny when mixed neurological populations contribute to pooled estimates. Non-invasive neuromodulation remains investigational for post-stroke anxiety. Current evidence does not support routine use of a specific protocol or replacement of standard multidisciplinary stroke care. Future trials should prospectively define anxiety, standardize stimulation and sham procedures, and assess sustained benefit and safety.

titre: Effects of exercise on balance in people with Parkinson's disease: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials.
titre_fr: Effects of exercise on balance in people with Parkinson's disease: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials.
auteurs: Yuan Yuning, Ran Hui, Song Youyou, Xu Shiyan, Chen Kangcheng
resume: Postural instability and impaired balance are disabling, levodopa-resistant features of Parkinson's disease (PD) and leading contributors to falls. Many systematic reviews and meta-analyses (SR/MAs) report that exercise improves balance, but they differ in modality, comparator, instrument and rigor and have not been synthesized and graded as a whole. We conducted an umbrella review of meta-analytic evidence on exercise and balance in PD. Following PRISMA 2020 and umbrella-review methodology, PubMed and Web of Science were searched from inception to 8 June 2026. Pairwise SR/MAs of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) reporting balance performance (Berg Balance Scale [BBS], Mini-BESTest), mobility (Timed Up-and-Go [TUG]) or falls in PD were eligible; network meta-analyses were supporting evidence only. We extracted the pooled random-effects estimates as reported by each review (no re-pooling of individual-trial data), harmonized their direction, and interpreted standardized effects as small/moderate/large. Methodological quality, primary-study overlap and certainty were appraised with AMSTAR-2, the corrected covered area (CCA) and GRADE. From 161 unique records, 20 pairwise meta-analyses were included, spanning aerobic, resistance, aquatic, dance, VR/exergaming, traditional Chinese exercise, and home-based and group formats. Exercise improved balance in most modalities, though not universally (resistance training and one mixed-exercise review were non-significant). Because estimates came from separate meta-analyses, they are not directly comparable; standardized balance-performance effects ranged from small (g = 0.33, 95% CI 0.11-0.55) to large (aerobic, BBS g = 0.99, 0.76-1.23). Evidence on falls was inconsistent (proportion of fallers unchanged; fall rate reduced). Between-review overlap was very high at the BBS node (CCA = 16.8%). AMSTAR-2 confidence was moderate in 9, low in 10 and critically low in 1; GRADE certainty was moderate-to-very-low. Exercise is associated with small-to-large improvements in clinical balance in PD, but evidence on falls is inconsistent, and the underlying meta-analyses are mostly of low-to-moderate quality, highly overlapping, and of moderate-to-very-low certainty. Aerobic, mind-body and game-based modalities show relatively consistent signals, but this umbrella review cannot establish superiority of any modality. Larger, blinded, registered RCTs with standardized balance and prospectively ascertained fall outcomes are needed.

titre: Effect of implant number on patient-reported outcomes in the edentulous maxilla: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effect of implant number on patient-reported outcomes in the edentulous maxilla: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Palmer Pascal, Wolfart Stefan, Kern Jaana-Sophia
resume: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated changes in patient-reported outcomes following implant-supported rehabilitation of the edentulous maxilla and their association with implant number. Five databases were searched through August 2026. Randomized controlled and prospective clinical studies including ≥ 10 patients and reporting patient-reported outcomes before and after treatment were eligible. Retrospective studies, studies without baseline PROM assessment, and studies involving mandibular or simultaneous maxillary and mandibular implant treatment were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, ROBINS-I, or MINORS, as appropriate. Hedges' g was analyzed using multi-level random-effects meta-analysis, with sensitivity analyses for OHIP- and VAS-based outcomes. Eleven studies were included. Patient-reported outcomes improved across all implant groups. Pooled effects were largest for ≥6 implants (g = 2.34; 95% CI: 1.85-2.83), followed by four implants (g = 1.13; 95% CI: 0.53-1.73); only one effect-size estimate was available for two implants. Improvement was significantly greater with ≥6 than with four implants (difference in g = 1.22; 95% CI: 0.40-2.04; p = 0.003) and remained significant when restricted to removable prostheses. Fixed and removable prostheses supported by six implants did not differ significantly. VAS-based outcomes showed a more pronounced difference than OHIP-based outcomes. Implant-supported rehabilitation substantially improves patient-reported outcomes in the edentulous maxilla. The greatest improvements were observed with ≥6 implants, with a significant advantage over four implants, although effect magnitude varied by PROM type. Evidence for two implants remains limited.

titre: Effectiveness of Wrist-Worn Wearable-Guided Cardiac Rehabilitation Delivered Through Fully Remote or Hybrid Programs in Patients With Cardiovascular Disease: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
titre_fr: Effectiveness of Wrist-Worn Wearable-Guided Cardiac Rehabilitation Delivered Through Fully Remote or Hybrid Programs in Patients With Cardiovascular Disease: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
auteurs: Choi Jun Hwan, Lee So Young, Seo Kyung Cheon, Lee Sang Yoon, Lee Hyo Kyung, Heo Dongbin, Ryu Hyun, Kim Jong Hoon, Kwon Jeong Eul, Kim Bo Ryun, Lee Michael Y
resume: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, yet participation in cardiac rehabilitation (CR) remains suboptimal. Wrist-worn wearables may support fully remote or hybrid CR through activity monitoring and individualized feedback, but the effectiveness and consistency of benefits remain uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of wrist-worn wearable-guided CR delivered through fully remote or hybrid programs initiated during phase II or III CR in patients with CVD. A total of 8 databases were searched for randomized controlled trials published from January 1, 2015, through August 7, 2026. Eligible trials enrolled adults with CVD and integrated a wrist-worn wearable into fully remote or hybrid CR. Studies focused primarily on heart failure or using wearables only for outcome measurement were excluded. Primary outcomes were peak oxygen consumption (VO<sub>2</sub>), 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), and daily steps. Random-effects meta-analyses used mean differences (MDs), except for quality of life, which used standardized MDs. Between-study variance was estimated using the DerSimonian-Laird method, pooled-effect CIs used the Knapp-Hartung adjustment, and 95% prediction intervals (PIs) used the Nagashima-Noma-Furukawa parametric bootstrap method. Risk of bias was assessed with Cochrane Risk of Bias 2. Subgroup and univariable meta-regression analyses explored study and intervention characteristics. A total of 18 trials involving 1993 randomized participants, reported in 20 publications, were included; 17 contributed to meta-analysis. Pooled estimates favored wearable-guided CR for peak VO<sub>2</sub> (10 studies; 591 participants; MD 1.69, 95% CI 0.46-2.92, 95% PI -2.21 to 5.39 mL/kg/min), 6MWD (9 studies; 1094 participants; MD 31.03, 95% CI 7.66-53.92, 95% PI -62.11 to 123.18 m), and daily steps (8 studies; 474 participants; MD 1062.8, 95% CI 383.5-1825.0, 95% PI -503.0 to 2860.0 steps/day). All 3 PIs included the null, indicating uncertainty about consistency across future comparable settings. No clear pooled effects were observed for anaerobic threshold, BMI, waist circumference, grip strength, or quality of life. Subgroup differences were not statistically significant. In univariable meta-regression, a higher proportion of female participants was associated with greater peak VO<sub>2</sub> improvement, although this aggregate-level finding was exploratory. Wrist-worn wearable-guided CR delivered through fully remote or hybrid programs may improve average exercise capacity and physical activity in patients with CVD. However, PIs included the null, indicating uncertainty about consistency across future settings. These programs may extend activity monitoring, individualized feedback, and behavioral support beyond center-based CR, but their multicomponent nature prevents attributing effects to wearables alone. Larger, rigorously designed trials with standardized protocols and outcomes should identify the patients and program components most likely to benefit. Future research should also evaluate long-term adherence, safety, equity, and implementation within routine multidisciplinary CR across diverse health systems.

titre: Efficacy of digital interventions for patients with post-stroke aphasia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Efficacy of digital interventions for patients with post-stroke aphasia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
auteurs: Shi Junjie, Sun Yue, Zhang Jingyi, Yang Zeyu, Hu Jia, Zhi Liang, Zhang Qingfang, Wang Yulong, Long Jianjun
resume: Digital interventions show potential for improving language function in post-stroke aphasia (PSA), but contradictory evidence leaves the optimal strategy unclear. This study aims to evaluate the effects of different digital interventions on language function and quality of life in patients with PSA, and to provide evidence-based support for clinical rehabilitation decisions. A systematic search across PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Embase, Scopus, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) (inception to May 2026) identified randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating digital interventions (e.g., virtual reality [VR], computer-assisted language therapy [CALT], telerehabilitation [TR]) for adults with PSA. Eligible studies reported Western Aphasia Battery or Stroke and Aphasia Quality of Life Scale-39 (SAQOL-39) outcomes. Data were extracted independently. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 1 (RoB 1) tool. Network meta-analysis was performed using R 4.5.2, incorporating a consistency model, a random-effects model, and I<sup>2</sup>statistics to assess heterogeneity. Sources of heterogeneity were analyzed through sensitivity analyses, subgroup analyses, and meta-regression. Intervention efficacy was ranked using Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking Curve (SUCRA). Robustness was validated via the Egger test and sensitivity analyses. Evidence quality was assessed using the GRADE framework. Twenty-five RCTs involving 1,069 participants were included. Compared to conventional therapy (C), VR showed significant superiority in aphasia quotient (mean difference [MD] = 10.77, 95% CI 9.48 to 12.06; SUCRA = 89.57%), spontaneous speech (MD = 2.35, 95% CI 1.71 to 2.99), auditory comprehension (MD = 1.47, 95% CI 0.81 to 2.13), and repetition (MD = 1.98, 95% CI 1.19 to 2.76); Ranking was VR > CALT>TR > C. For naming, CALT ranked highest (MD = 1.41, 95% CI 0.79 to 2.03; SUCRA = 89.87%); Ranking was CALT>VR > C > TR. For SAQOL-39, VR showed the best effect (MD = 0.51, 95% CI 0.33 to 0.70; SUCRA = 96.40%). Ranking was VR > TR > C > CALT. Digital interventions effectively improve language function in PSA. VR demonstrated potential advantages for aphasia quotient, speech, comprehension, repetition, and SAQOL-39, whereas CALT provides targeted advantages for naming impairments. Caution is warranted due to study heterogeneity, bias risks, and limited sample sizes. Future research should optimize intervention protocols, integrate neuromodulation or traditional therapeutic techniques, and explore cost-effective implementation strategies. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261373199, Identifier CRD420261373199.

titre: Conservative and Minimally Invasive Treatments for Temporomandibular Disorders Versus Inactive Controls: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
titre_fr: Conservative and Minimally Invasive Treatments for Temporomandibular Disorders Versus Inactive Controls: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
auteurs: Țănculescu Oana, Țarevici Eugenia-Larisa, Bodnar Petronela, Chiriac Alice-Teodora, Iordache Marina Cristina Iuliana, Doloca Adrian, Proca Vlad-Ștefan, Tatarciuc Monica Silvia, Pendefunda Alice-Arina, Foia Georgeta Liliana, Săveanu Cătălina Iulia, Fala Valeriu, Cheptănaru Olga, Bordeniuc Gheorghe, Apostu Alina-Mihaela
resume: Background/Objectives: Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are musculoskeletal conditions in which rehabilitation aims to reduce pain and restore mandibular mobility and function. We estimated the between-group effects of conservative and minimally invasive treatments versus inactive controls and examined important sources of variation. Methods: We included randomized controlled trials published in 2015-2025 in adults diagnosed with RDC/TMD or DC/TMD. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus and CENTRAL were searched, with the final searches completed in January 2026. The review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251250251). We synthesized comparisons of conservative and minimally invasive treatments with inactive controls in adults with TMD. Random-effects meta-analyses used REML and modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Two human reviewers independently assessed risk of bias with RoB 2 and certainty with GRADE. Results: Thirty-five studies contributed to 69 effects. Compared with inactive controls, short-term pain was 1.31 points lower on a 0-10 scale (95% CI 0.62-2.00; 23 studies; very-low certainty) and 0.94 points lower (95% CI 0.15-1.74) after high-risk results were excluded. Mouth opening was 1.96 mm greater (95% CI 0.33-3.60; 26 effects from 25 studies; very-low certainty) and 0.75 mm greater (95% CI -0.62 to 2.12) after high-risk results were excluded; the latter confidence interval included no difference. Prediction intervals included no benefit. Evidence for jaw function, oral-health-related quality of life and longer-term effects was sparse. None of the 73 result-specific risk-of-bias assessments was low risk, and 25 were high risk. Conclusions: The average short-term pain benefit was modest and decreased after high-risk results were removed. The mouth-opening difference became inconclusive after high-risk results were excluded. These descriptive pooled estimates support transparent discussion of uncertainty in rehabilitation practice but should not be used to rank treatments or predict an individual response.

titre: Impact of Cataract Surgery on Postural Control and Fall Risk in Adults and the Elderly: A Systematic Review.
titre_fr: Impact of Cataract Surgery on Postural Control and Fall Risk in Adults and the Elderly: A Systematic Review.
auteurs: Pereira Juliano, Oliveira Rodrigo Franco de, Sudré Tamyris Mendes de Faria, Costa Matheus André R da, Oliveira Bruna A Pires Franco de, de Oliveira Pereira Amélia, Pereira Gabriel de Oliveira, Oliveira Luis V F, Silva Carlos Hassel Mendes da, Oliveira Deise Aparecida de A P, Freitas Diego Galace
resume: Background: Cataracts are a major cause of reversible visual impairment worldwide, particularly among older adults. Visual deterioration associated with cataracts may compromise spatial perception, postural control, and balance, thereby increasing the risk of falls. In this context, cataract surgery has emerged not only as an effective intervention for visual rehabilitation but also as a potential strategy to improve mobility and functional performance in aging populations. Objective: The objective of this study was to systematically evaluate the impact of cataract surgery on postural control, balance, and fall risk in adults and older individuals by comparing preoperative and postoperative outcomes. Methods: A systematic review was conducted following a protocol registered in PROSPERO. Searches were initially conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and Scopus on 20 October 2025, and rerun on 10 March 2026, which was considered the final search date. Twelve studies were included, encompassing prospective cohorts, retrospective population-based analyses, and comparative studies. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE framework, and the methodological quality of individual studies was evaluated using JBI critical checklists. Results: The included studies generally reported improvements in visual function following cataract surgery, while several studies also reported favorable changes in postural stability, functional balance, and fall-related outcomes. However, findings varied according to study design, outcome definition, surgical timing, and follow-up period. Some studies reported more favorable fall-related and postural outcomes after second-eye surgery; however, the observational nature of the evidence and heterogeneity across studies preclude determining whether bilateral surgery itself caused these improvements. Conclusions: Cataract surgery appears to be associated with improved visual and postural function and, in several studies, with reduced fall incidence, particularly after bilateral correction. However, due to substantial heterogeneity, the predominance of observational evidence, and discordant findings on severe injurious outcomes, the certainty of this effect remains limited. The procedure should be regarded as a component of visual rehabilitation that may coincide with reduced fall risk in selected contexts, rather than a universal prevention strategy. Further prospective studies with standardized outcomes are needed to clarify the relationship between cataract surgery, visual function, postural control, and fall-related outcomes.

titre: The Relationship Between Overdose Experience and Social Functional Impairment in Individuals With a History of Substance Use.
titre_fr: The Relationship Between Overdose Experience and Social Functional Impairment in Individuals With a History of Substance Use.
auteurs: AlMusailhi Jawaher, Shahjahan Zayed B, Schütz Christian G
resume: Substance-use disorders can profoundly affect nearly every aspect of an individual's life. The threat of drug overdoses, driven primarily by illicit fentanyl, remains a major public health crisis. Functional disability refers to limitations in performing everyday tasks and participating in life situations. We examined the association between overdose experiences (such as naloxone administration, medical intervention, unintentional fentanyl exposure, or recent overdoses) and functional disability, manifested in both social and family domains, in a population of individuals with a history of substance use. Overdose experiences, functional disability, and sociodemographic factors were analyzed from selected survey instruments, including overdose Questionnaire, Sheehan Disability Survey, and Demographics Survey, administered as part of a battery of questionnaires in a prospective longitudinal multisite cohort study of individuals with severe mental health and substance-use disorders (ROAR CANADA). Impairment in social life and family responsibilities were examined in relation to various overdose experiences among individuals with substance-use disorder backgrounds. Female sex was the strongest and most consistent correlate of disability, with higher adjusted odds of greater social (OR=2.61: CI: 1.75, 3.89) and family disability (OR=2.47; CI: 1.65, 3.67). Unintentional fentanyl consumption was associated with greater social disability (OR=1.63; CI: 1.07, 2.48) and remained a stable predictor of markedly impaired social and family functioning across Elastic Net resampling analyses. Among treatment-seeking individuals with severe concurrent mental health and substance-use disorders, greater functional disability was most consistently associated with female sex, while unintentional fentanyl exposure was associated with greater social disability. These cross-sectional findings identify clinically relevant correlates of impaired social and family functioning and support longitudinal research to clarify temporal relationships and evaluate targeted functional assessment and rehabilitation approaches.

titre: An ICF-Based Assessment Tool: The ICF-Application.
titre_fr: An ICF-Based Assessment Tool: The ICF-Application.
auteurs: Traina Ivan, Pasqualotto Luciano, Lascioli Angelo
revue: Studies in health technology and informatics
resume: This paper presents a trial aimed at developing an assessment tool based on the International Classification of Functioning (ICF) framework, designed to define the Biopsychosocial Functional Profile of persons with disabilities, including the elderly and those with mental health disorders. This tool comprises an open-access online platform designed to disseminate an evidence-based approach in social, educational, and rehabilitation contexts through the use of the ICF. Aligned with the conceptual framework of Universal Design (UD) and the UN STGs 3 and 4, the ICF Application platform offers targeted guidance for identifying and analysing barriers, environmental and personal factors that impact human functioning and necessitate intervention to support individuals' empowerment within their living contexts. With the information collected through the ICF questionnaire, the platform allows the development of functional profiles that serve as comprehensive assessment tools, facilitating the generation of indicators for the planning, evaluation, and implementation of interventions tailored to specific population targets. The trial demonstrated that employing the biopsychosocial assessment provides evidence regarding individual support needs and the design of accessible environments from the UD perspective. Furthermore, the platform offers tools for education, rehabilitation, and social-care professionals to apply the principles of the ICF for designing person-centred interventions.

titre: The need for supportive policies: connecting individual placement and support to the domains of employment and mental health care.
titre_fr: The need for supportive policies: connecting individual placement and support to the domains of employment and mental health care.
auteurs: van Weeghel Jaap, Fioritti Angelo, Jaeckel Dorothea, Johnston Gary, Mazzetti Greta, Ahola Minna, Bejerholm Ulrika, Bergmans Cris, Debroas Frédéric, de Winter Lars, Einarsdottir Soffia Erla, Guglielmi Dina, Jónasson Hlynur, Kárníková Anna, Koatz Débora, Kropeit Julia, Lunder Arvesen Anne Lise, Manchisi Denise, Markerink Jan, Nan Lium Kine, Sipilä Noora, Twomey Una, Van Audenhove Chantal
resume: Individual placement and support (IPS) is an effective vocational rehabilitation programme for people with mental illness. This article analyses national policies that directly promote IPS and broader employment-related policies on mental health in 13 European countries. IPS alone cannot address the broader workplace and policy conditions that influence sustainable employment. Therefore, creating mentally healthy working conditions also requires action by employers, healthcare systems, and policymakers. Recurring barriers and facilitators were identified across countries, alongside variation in governance and implementation contexts. IPS services often operate in isolation, with limited access to consistent training, data, and cross-sector coordination. A national infrastructure for IPS is therefore needed to offer implementation support, intersectoral collaboration should be strengthened and employers need to be supported to advance equity, diversity and inclusion. IPS practice will benefit from policies addressing poor mental health conditions in the workplace, and policies endorsing a recovery-oriented mental healthcare system. IPS can build a solid bridge between mental healthcare and employment when integrated into recovery-oriented services and supported by policies that promote inclusive, mentally healthy workplaces.

titre: Importance of Audiologist Screening for Suicidal Ideation in Individuals With Hearing Loss.
titre_fr: Importance of Audiologist Screening for Suicidal Ideation in Individuals With Hearing Loss.
auteurs: Mathialakan Jeyajeevan Dharmarajan
resume: Hearing loss is increasingly recognized as a chronic health condition with psychosocial consequences that extend beyond impaired auditory function, including social isolation, loneliness, reduced quality of life, and depression. Emerging epidemiological evidence suggests that individuals with hearing loss may also be at an increased risk of suicidal ideation, particularly when communication difficulties coexist with depression and social withdrawal. Despite these findings, the role of audiologists in identifying individuals at risk has received limited attention. This viewpoint aims to present an evidence-based rationale for the role of audiologists in the early identification of suicidal ideation among individuals with hearing loss and to propose a practical framework for targeted suicide risk screening within audiology practice. Audiologists, through their ongoing involvement in hearing assessment, rehabilitation, tinnitus management, and long-term follow-up, are well positioned to recognize psychological distress and facilitate timely referral for comprehensive mental health evaluation. We advocate for a targeted, rather than universal, suicide risk screening approach using brief validated instruments among individuals presenting with established psychosocial or clinical risk factors. Importantly, screening is proposed as a means of identifying patients who require referral and should not be interpreted as replacing comprehensive mental health assessment or expanding the audiologist's scope into psychiatric diagnosis or treatment. Integrating such approaches into audiology services may meaningfully contribute to broader suicide prevention efforts.

titre: Chinese ethnic traditional sports as mind-body interventions for psychiatric recovery.
titre_fr: Chinese ethnic traditional sports as mind-body interventions for psychiatric recovery.
auteurs: Zhao Fang, Liu ChuChen
resume: Chinese ethnic traditional sports (CETS)-a family of culturally embedded physical practices encompassing traditional Chinese mind-body exercises (e.g., Tai Chi, Qigong, Baduanjin, Yijin Jing, Wuqinxi) and intangible cultural heritage folk sports (e.g., dragon-lion dance)-have attracted growing interest as accessible, low-cost mind-body interventions for mental health. This narrative review examines which mental health outcomes are associated with participation in different types of CETS and to what extent the available evidence supports their role in psychiatric recovery. The review synthesizes 68 studies published between January 2000 and June 2026, identified through multi-database searches of Web of Science, PubMed, and Scopus. Thematic synthesis identified four interconnected dimensions of mental health burden addressed by CETS: (a) affective disorders; (b) trauma-related disorders; (c) sleep-wake disturbances; and (d) cognitive and psychosocial dysfunction. Across these dimensions, individual randomized controlled trials consistently report moderate reductions in depressive and anxiety symptoms, with larger effects when CETS are delivered in supervised groups at moderate intensity for 12-24 weeks; however, most evidence derives from subclinical or non-psychiatric samples and measures symptom severity rather than functional recovery. The review therefore concludes that CETS are a promising, low-cost, culturally congruent adjunct to conventional psychiatric care-warranting rigorous, disorder-specific trials-rather than established stand-alone treatments for psychiatric recovery.

titre: Analysis and Prediction of Relapse Risk Factors in Community-Dwelling Individuals With Schizophrenia: Retrospective Cohort Study.
titre_fr: Analysis and Prediction of Relapse Risk Factors in Community-Dwelling Individuals With Schizophrenia: Retrospective Cohort Study.
auteurs: Zhang Weibo, Zhu Dian, Wang Xiaolan, Li Ruilan, Jiang Hong, Liu Yanli, Cai Jun, Liu Zhao, Wang Ling
resume: Schizophrenia is a severe mental disorder characterized by high disability and relapse rates, posing significant challenges to public safety and community-based mental health management. This study aimed to develop and validate a model for identifying hospitalization-related severe relapse risk among individuals with schizophrenia and to determine the key factors associated with this risk. A total of 44,804 electronic records of community-managed individuals with schizophrenia were extracted from an information management system between January 1, 2022, and December 31, 2023. The dataset included demographic information, clinical records, interview data, policy support, and management indicators to construct a comprehensive feature system. A Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) machine learning algorithm was used for model development, with cost-sensitive learning applied to address class imbalance. Model interpretability was enhanced using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) to identify the most influential predictors of relapse risk. After screening, a total of 39,818 community-dwelling individuals with schizophrenia were included in this study, of whom 3717 (9.33%) experienced hospitalization-related severe relapse. The dataset was randomly divided using stratified sampling into a training set (n=31,854, 80%) and an independent test set (n=7964, 20%). Among the 6 machine learning models evaluated, LightGBM showed leading and balanced performance, yielding an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.95, an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.79, a relapse-class recall of 0.77, a precision of 0.71, and an F1-score of 0.74 in the independent test set. SHAP-based interpretability analysis identified medication persistence (23.30%), specialist recommendation: medication adherence training (19.74%), number of follow-ups (7.38%), age (3.72%), and educational attainment (3.58%) as the most influential predictors. Higher hospitalization-related severe relapse risk was generally associated with interrupted or refused medication use, more frequent follow-ups, younger age, and higher educational attainment, whereas sustained medication use, better occupational functioning and productive work, greater social participation, and better social functioning were associated with lower predicted risk. This study developed a hospitalization-related severe relapse risk identification model that integrates multidimensional factors reflecting the clinical and functional complexity of schizophrenia. The findings provide an evidence-based foundation for risk identification, targeted intervention, and the optimization of community mental health services to reduce hospitalization-related severe relapse risk and support long-term recovery.

titre: ANCHOR: Communication Partner Training for Maintaining Friendships After Aphasia.
titre_fr: ANCHOR: Communication Partner Training for Maintaining Friendships After Aphasia.
auteurs: Azios Jamie H, Archer Brent, Douglas Natalie F, Strong Katie A, Eller Mary Ann, Silverman Maura, Simmons-Mackie Nina, Worrall Linda
revue: International journal of language & communication disorders
resume: Aphasia significantly disrupts social relationships, with friendship loss occurring early after stroke and continuing into chronic stages. Despite friendships being prioritised by people with aphasia and families, they rarely receive explicit focus in rehabilitation. Communication partner training is an intervention with potential to keep friendship bonds strong after aphasia. This paper describes the development of ANCHOR (Aphasia: Nurturing Connection, Honoring Ongoing Relationships), a communication partner training intervention protoype designed specifically for people with aphasia and their pre-existing friends-and the foundational elements of ANCHOR and how they informed its design and components, and then situates ANCHOR within the broader communication partner training literature with attention to partner type, candidacy and real-world delivery in service settings. ANCHOR represents the first communication partner training intervention explicitly targeting friendship maintenance after aphasia. Development was grounded in a systematic research progression including lived experience research, relational competence theory and the behaviour change wheel, and a planned cycle of refinement across a two-year development period. Key distinguishing features include a hybrid delivery model that combines self-paced digital modules with in-person coaching sessions, universal 'talking tools' accessible to friends with minimal aphasia knowledge, first-year post-stroke timing to prevent relationship deterioration, and explicit attention to implementation barriers. By grounding communication partner training design in lived experience, relationship theory and implementation science, ANCHOR is designed as a comprehensive, implementable approach to sustaining friendships after aphasia, thereby addressing a critical gap in post-stroke rehabilitation with potential to reduce social isolation and support mental health. ANCHOR is an intervention prototype and its core functions, forms and implementation supports will be refined as feasibility and trial data accrue. What is already known on this subject Aphasia greatly impacts the ability for people to maintain a strong social network. People with aphasia often lose most of their pre-stroke friends early in the recovery journey. Friends of people with aphasia need access to interventions that can help them understand aphasia and its impact on communication. What this study adds to the existing knowledge We developed a communication partner training program called ANCHOR based upon lived experience research involving people with aphasia and their friends and theories and relationship maintenance and behaviour change. ANCHOR is different than other communication partner training programs which target family members or healthcare providers in that it is limited to three face-to-face sessions, includes a self-guided digital component, and focuses on a standard package of communication strategies. What are the potential clinical implications of the study? ANCHOR continues to be refined and evaluated. It is our hope that ANCHOR will be a clinically feasible and person-centered communication partner training program that is effective in improving communication and relationships for people with aphasia and their friends.

Friends of people with aphasia need access to interventions that can help them understand aphasia and its impact on communication. What this study adds to the existing knowledge We developed a communication partner training program called ANCHOR based upon lived experience research involving people with aphasia and their friends and theories and relationship maintenance and behaviour change. ANCHOR is different than other communication partner training programs which target family members or healthcare providers in that it is limited to three face-to-face sessions, includes a self-guided digital component, and focuses on a standard package of communication strategies. What are the potential clinical implications of the study? ANCHOR continues to be refined and evaluated. It is our hope that ANCHOR will be a clinically feasible and person-centered communication partner training program that is effective in improving communication and relationships for people with aphasia and their friends.

titre: The Unbroken Integrative Psycho-Trauma Care Model: Health System Implementation in Wartime Ukraine.
titre_fr: The Unbroken Integrative Psycho-Trauma Care Model: Health System Implementation in Wartime Ukraine.
auteurs: Berezyuk Oleh, Rubinstein Dori, Duek Or, Amen Shelley, Samchuk Oleg, Krynytska-Berezyuk Ulyana, Filts Oleksandr, Svirchuk Mariana, Herych Hnat, Paolini Laritta, Patsalides Hofmann Beatrice, Bluvshtein Marina, Umarbekov Askar, Philip Noah S, Harpaz-Rotem Ilan
resume: The ongoing war in Ukraine has generated an unprecedented burden of psychological trauma, frequently compounded by posttraumatic stress disorder, traumatic brain injury, severe physical injury, and the psychiatric consequences of captivity among former prisoners of war. In large military conflicts, civilian hospital systems are essential for delivering trauma-informed mental health care at scale while managing patients with complex, overlapping medical and psychiatric conditions under active conflict, with limited implementation guidance. This Special Communication describes the implementation and clinical workflow of the Unbroken Integrative Psycho-Trauma Care Model, a multidisciplinary health system approach embedded in the Lviv First Medical Union in Western Ukraine to organize trauma-informed mental health care within a wartime civilian hospital. From February 24, 2022, through December 31, 2025, the Lviv First Medical Union treated more than 15 000 individuals for war-related injuries and cared for more than 400 former prisoners of war. During this period, 7538 unique individuals received psychiatric care through the Unbroken Model, including 4165 who received trauma-focused psychotherapy. The model was implemented through proactive psychiatric rounds across medical and surgical departments, structured triage into 4 clinical pathways, stabilization-first care sequencing, and longitudinal case management integrated with neurological, surgical, and rehabilitation services. This organization of care enabled early identification of trauma-related distress, continuity between medical and psychiatric treatment, and adaptive delivery of trauma-focused psychotherapies within a high-volume conflict setting. The Unbroken Model demonstrates how trauma-informed mental health care can be delivered at scale within a civilian hospital during active conflict. Its primary innovation lies in the organization of care delivery, integrating proactive outreach, triage-driven pathways, multidisciplinary coordination, and stabilization-first sequencing into a unified, scalable framework. This approach may be applicable to conflict-affected and postconflict health systems worldwide.

titre: Observed Service Utilization Differences and Audiometric Profiles Among Adults With Hearing Loss in Eastern Coastal Provinces in China.
titre_fr: Observed Service Utilization Differences and Audiometric Profiles Among Adults With Hearing Loss in Eastern Coastal Provinces in China.
auteurs: Chen Min, Quan Haoyu, Li Fang
resume: : Hearing loss is a major public health concern that hampers communication, social participation, and quality of life. To date, large-scale demographic and audiometric characteristic data for adults seeking hearing care services in China are limited. We aimed to assemble demographic and audiometric profiles for adults requesting hearing care services for the first time in selected eastern coastal provinces of China, with a focus on service- and region-specific patterns in observed service utilization. : This multicenter retrospective study included 2,413 adult first-time patients who initially sought hearing care services between January and June 2025, including 2,242 patients who visited public hospitals and 171 patients who visited private hearing aid clinics. Demographic and audiometric data were extracted from institutional databases. Hearing loss severity was assessed using better-ear four-frequency average hearing loss scores. Differences between groups were analyzed using analysis of variance and chi-square tests. Multiple linear regression was performed to identify factors associated with hearing loss severity. : Mean patient age was 55.65 years (51.1% were male). Patients attending private hearing aid clinics were significantly older than those visiting public hospitals and had more severe hearing loss. Sensorineural hearing loss was the most common (56.8%), followed by normal hearing (29.1%), mixed hearing loss (12.4%), and conductive hearing loss (1.7%). Regional differences in sex distribution and hearing loss profiles were observed. : This multicenter retrospective study describes observed service utilization and service-specific audiometric profile differences among adults presenting at selected hearing care institutions in Chinese eastern coastal provinces. Patients attending participating private hearing aid clinics operated by one provider were generally older and had more severe hearing loss, whereas public hospitals received a broader and more heterogeneous patient population. These findings should be interpreted descriptively and may help encourage earlier hearing screening, referral coordination, and integration of diagnostic and rehabilitation-oriented hearing care services.

titre: Exploring the Intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Metaverse Realities: Implications for Digital Mental Health Services.
titre_fr: Exploring the Intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Metaverse Realities: Implications for Digital Mental Health Services.
auteurs: Pesqueira Antonio
resume: Background/Objectives: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Metaverse Realities into Digital Mental Health Services presents novel opportunities for clinical assessment, therapeutic intervention, and continuous rehabilitation. Grounded in dynamic capabilities and sociotechnical systems theories, this study evaluates strategic pathways for integrating Artificial Intelligence and Metaverse Realities into Digital Mental Health Services, analyzes core bioethical and data privacy challenges, and examines the prospective impact of immersive virtual environments on patient engagement and therapeutic outcomes. Methods: An iterative three-round Delphi inquiry was conducted with an international panel of 36 multidisciplinary experts spanning clinical psychiatry, Artificial Intelligence and Metaverse Realities software development, digital ethics, and healthcare policy. Standardized, neutral visual scenarios prompted expert evaluations across 14 Digital Mental Health Services sub-areas. Panel consensus, rating dispersion, and domain interrelationships were quantified using Kendall's coefficient of concordance (W), non-parametric Spearman rank-order correlation analysis, and descriptive dispersion metrics (median, interquartile range, standard deviation), complemented by reflexive thematic qualitative synthesis. Results: Expert agreement converged significantly from Round 1 to Round 3. High consensus emerged for AI-enhanced initial screening (mean = 4.7, SD = 0.5) and comprehensive VR assessments (mean = 4.5, SD = 0.8). While AI-managed crisis services showed high perceived probability (95%), findings highlighted the necessity of strict human-in-the-loop architectures over full autonomy to mitigate psychiatric triage hazards. Conclusions: Artificial Intelligence and Metaverse Realities present viable adjunctive pathways for personalized psychiatric assessment and therapy, provided that systems implement strict clinician-in-the-loop safeguards, real-time dynamic consent, and end-to-end data encryption. Utilizing a Dynamic Capabilities framework enables healthcare organizations to systematically sense technological innovations, seize clinical opportunities, and reconfigure governance structures, thereby ensuring equitable, safe, and ethical digital mental health delivery.

titre: Quality of Life and Well-Being of Syrian Refugees: Insights from Spain and Jordan.
titre_fr: Quality of Life and Well-Being of Syrian Refugees: Insights from Spain and Jordan.
auteurs: Al-Hourani Dalia, Al-Wriekat Mahmoud, Alvarado-Omenat Jorge Juan, García-García Daniel, Llamas-Ramos Rocío, Llamas-Ramos Inés
resume: Syrian refugees face numerous challenges, including conflict, displacement, family separation, human rights violations, limited access to basic needs, and exposure to violence and torture. These experiences significantly affect their physical, psychological, social, and environmental quality of life (QoL). The aim of this study was to assess the QoL of Syrian refugees in Spain and Jordan and to examine the association between sociodemographic characteristics, living conditions, and experiences of discrimination with different QoL domains. This study used a cross-sectional correlational design in Syrian refugee centers, homes, and camps across Spain and Jordan. A convenience sample of Syrian refugees with confirmed status in the past ten years was recruited. Demographic data were collected via a demographic form, and the World Health Organization Quality of Life-Brief Questionnaire (WHOQOL-BREF) was used to assess their quality of life. Data analysis included descriptive statistics, Chi-square tests, one-way ANOVA, and independent t-tests. The two hundred participants were predominantly aged 18-29 (43%), female (52.5%), married (51.5%), with secondary school education (46.5%), and unemployed (70%), with low monthly family income (60.5%). While 69% experienced low levels of discrimination, 33% were satisfied with their health, and 47.5% rated their QoL as neutral. Refugees in Spain reported higher QoL across physical, psychological, social, and environmental domains compared to those in Jordan (p < 0.05). The QoL was related to socio-demographic factors: higher among married participants (p = 0.044), urban residents (p < 0.001), and recent immigrants (<5 years, p < 0.001), but lower among those with low income (p = 0.011). Gender differences showed that males had better physical (p = 0.001) and psychological (p = 0.032) QoL than females. Lower discrimination levels and employment were associated with higher QoL across multiple domains. This study highlights the lasting association of the Syrian conflict on refugees' QoL, emphasizing the need for holistic healthcare that addresses physical, psychological, social, and environmental challenges both before and after displacement. Findings call for comprehensive support systems, including early mental health interventions, anti-discrimination efforts, and community inclusion programs, to enhance refugees' resilience and integration. The study identifies specific subgroups at greater risk of lower QoL-including women, older adults, those with low income, the unemployed, camp residents, and those experiencing discrimination-providing actionable insights for policymakers to target resources and interventions effectively. Tailored rehabilitation and psychological care are essential for empowering refugees to rebuild their lives and fostering social cohesion in host communities.
