titre: Employment and life participation in patients with kidney disease: a narrative review.
titre_fr: Employment and life participation in patients with kidney disease: a narrative review.
auteurs: Lyons Teresa M, Cavanaugh Kerri L, Pappadis Monique R, Erickson Kevin F
revue: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension
resume: People living with kidney disease consistently rank employment and the ability to participate in life activities among their most important outcomes, yet employment among working-aged U.S. patients at dialysis initiation has remained at 20-24% for more than two decades. This review synthesizes recent evidence on why patients with kidney disease stop working and what may help them remain employed. Job loss begins well before dialysis: only about one-third of working-aged U.S. patients are employed 6 months before starting dialysis, and employment is lowest among patients receiving in-center hemodialysis, recovering only partially after transplantation. Employment is associated with better survival, greater access to transplantation, improved mental health, social connectedness, and protection from illness-related financial insecurity. Patients stop working for multiple reasons, including symptoms, treatment time and travel, employer inflexibility, and benefit structures that penalize work. Flexible dialysis options (home dialysis, evening shifts), psychosocial support, exercise, and vocational rehabilitation may help patients remain employed. Employment is a modifiable, patient-prioritized outcome. Restoring patient-level employment reporting in national registries and directly testing employment-focused interventions in kidney disease are priorities for research and quality improvement.

titre: Rehabilitation before discharge: A retrospective service evaluation of group-based rehabilitation in an Italian acute inpatient mental health unit.
titre_fr: Rehabilitation before discharge: A retrospective service evaluation of group-based rehabilitation in an Italian acute inpatient mental health unit.
auteurs: Camera Paolo
resume: Acute inpatient mental health units often prioritize containment, risk management, and pharmacological stabilization while deferring rehabilitation until after discharge. This retrospective service evaluation examined program reach and associations between group attendance and clinician-rated outcomes. We analyzed 480 consecutive admissions to an Italian acute inpatient mental health unit during 2018-2019. Daily newspaper and fairy-tale groups and weekly music and cinema groups were embedded in care. Newspaper-group attendance was the primary exposure. The outcomes were the Clinical Global Impression-Severity, Clinical Global Impression-Improvement, and Health of the Nation Outcome Scales. Robust regression and length-of-stay sensitivity analyses were conducted. At least one activity was attended during 406 admissions (84.6%); newspaper-group attendance occurred during 384 (80.0%). No group-related adverse events were documented in retrospectively reviewed records. Sensitivity analyses showed that the Clinical Global Impression-Severity association attenuated to nonsignificance under several flexible length-of-stay specifications, whereas the Health of the Nation Outcome Scales and Clinical Global Impression-Improvement associations were comparatively stable. In primary adjusted models, each 10-percentage-point attendance increase was associated with Health of the Nation Outcome Scales change of -0.296 points (95% CI [-0.410, -0.182]), Clinical Global Impression-Improvement of -0.057 points (95% CI [-0.082, -0.033]), and Clinical Global Impression-Severity change of -0.035 points (95% CI [-0.058, -0.012]); the Clinical Global Impression-Severity estimate should therefore be interpreted cautiously. Early group-based rehabilitation can be integrated into acute inpatient care. The outcome associations are hypothesis generating, not causal, because attendance accrued during admission, ratings were unblinded, and participation may reflect stability or engagement. Prospective studies should use time-varying exposure, independent ratings, language-access measures, patient-reported outcomes, and longer term recovery endpoints. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

titre: Geographical Location and Response to Trismus Rehabilitation Following Head and Neck Cancer Treatment: A Secondary Analysis of the Restorabite Trials.
titre_fr: Geographical Location and Response to Trismus Rehabilitation Following Head and Neck Cancer Treatment: A Secondary Analysis of the Restorabite Trials.
auteurs: Ricketts Virginia, Charters Emma, Frowen Jacqui, Poke Sarah, Gleeson Siobhan, Pryor Lee, Heng Caleb, Adshead Briony, Lai Megan, Boehm Jessica, Natsis Lydia, Dunn Masako, Clark Jonathan R
resume: Trismus is a common and disabling complication following head and neck cancer (HNC) treatment, particularly after multimodal therapy. Survivors in regional areas face barriers to accessing specialist rehabilitation. This study explored whether a patient's geographical location of residence influenced their response to trismus therapy. Secondary analysis of pooled data from three Restorabite trials (2021-2024) was performed. Adults with HNC-related trismus (maximal interincisal opening [MIO] ≤ 35 mm) completed a 10-week individualized rehabilitation program incorporating manual therapy, daily jaw exercises, and weekly speech pathology review delivered in person or via telehealth. Most participants (96.6%) received all or part of their intervention via telehealth. Outcomes included MIO and Gothenburg Trismus Questionnaire (GTQ) scores. Longitudinal change was modeled using generalized estimating equations. A total of 175 participants with a broad range of HNC subsites, tumor stage, and treatment modalities were included. MIO improved by an average of 1.2 mm/week and GTQ scores by -2.7 points/week after 10 weeks of trismus rehabilitation (both p < 0.001). While multimodal treatment had a negative effect on both MIO and GTQ, geographical residence was not associated with change in MIO or GTQ in adjusted models (p = 0.5 and p = 0.1, respectively). For geographically dispersed patients, geographical residence was not associated with poorer trismus outcomes within a predominantly telehealth-supported model of care, supporting the use of telehealth to facilitate access to specialist trismus rehabilitation.

titre: Upper Limb Neurorehabilitation Using a Hybrid Technology-Enabled Therapy Approach-A Scoping Review.
titre_fr: Upper Limb Neurorehabilitation Using a Hybrid Technology-Enabled Therapy Approach-A Scoping Review.
auteurs: Tornatore Giovanna, Fleming Jennifer, Scarff Shannon, Riba Marcos, Gullo Hannah
resume: There is growing evidence of benefits for a multimodal or 'hybrid' technology approach where more than one technology type is applied for upper limb (UL) neurorehabilitation. However, translation of this approach into real world clinical settings remains unclear. Exploration of multimodal technology use for UL neurorehabilitation in hospital settings is warranted to determine practice trends, efficacy, benefits and barriers. A scoping review was conducted to explore hybrid technology-enabled rehabilitation approaches for UL neurorehabilitation focusing on combined use of robotics, virtual reality and sensor-based therapy. Seven electronic databases were searched for studies on adult participants with neurological UL impairment who participated in hospital rehabilitation and used two or more technology devices. Of 25 333 articles screened, full text review was completed on 20 articles with nine progressed for data extraction. An additional article found from hand searching was included for data extraction resulting in ten articles in total. Included studies found hybrid technology-enabled UL rehabilitation was used mainly with stroke participants ranging from 25 to 91 years in a hospital setting. Most studies were observational or pilot in nature and focused on clinical feasibility. All studies showed positive patient outcomes and feasibility studies reported on factors to support implementation in the clinical setting. Further research is warranted to determine impact on participation, long-term outcomes, sustainability, and economic impacts in the clinical hospital setting.

titre: Rationale and design of RECOVER - a prospective, longitudinal cardiac rehabilitation registry.
titre_fr: Rationale and design of RECOVER - a prospective, longitudinal cardiac rehabilitation registry.
auteurs: Riess Jan, Schmidt Elisa Alba, Petrasch Gloria, Brito Da Silva Hadassa, Sichler Sarah, Sartori Pietro, Carluccio Eleonora Di, Haberfellner Cornelia, Senftinger Juliana, Albus Miriam, Bieri Kathrin, Rhyner Claudio, Hametner Greta, Prechtl Luisa M, Distler Meike, Jellestad Lena, D'Ascenzi Flavio, Sokolowska Milena, Rodriguez Cetina Biefer Hector, Dzemali Omer, Von Moos Roger, Twerenbold Raphael, Loidl Martin, Tanner Felix C, Lustenberger Caroline, Eijsvogels Thijs M H, Bakker Esmée A, Tomczak Corey R, Baggish Aaron, Kraler Simon, Aigner Elmar, Carter Alex W, Bauer Nicole, Röösli Martin, Haddad Imad El, Häuptli Daniel, Latshang Tsogyal D, Steffel Jan, Haykowsky Mark J, Blankenberg Stefan, Vontobel Jan, Ziegler Andreas, Niederseer David
revue: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
resume: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) has been performed in a structured manner since the 1970s, supported by a substantial body of evidence demonstrating its benefits across the heterogeneous pool of cardiac patients. Although therapeutic interventions, pharmacological options, and patient-centered recommendations keep emerging, the majority of CR programs have not changed accordingly. Hence, they are becoming less capable of accounting for an increasingly diverse patient cohort. With a prospective long-term cohort, we aim to achieve an in-depth characterization of CR patients, enabling the delivery of more personalized care in the contemporary era. In this non-interventional, monocentric, prospective cohort study named RECOVER (Cardiac REhabilitation COhort at the Medicine Campus DaVos to invEstigate Recovery), we plan to include 10,000 patients over 10 years across a broad spectrum of cardiovascular conditions (e.g., cardiac surgery, myocardial infarction, heart failure) with data collected across the full spectrum of inpatient CR. Data acquisition is complemented through extensive biobanking allowing detailed phenotyping and biomarker profiling of patients. Follow-up assessments are conducted at 3 and 6 months, and yearly thereafter, up to 10 years. By harnessing novel devices, digital monitoring is employed to continuously capture a wealth of health-related parameters, such as blood pressure and accelerometry-based physical activity. Given the substantial research gap in personalized CR, the RECOVER study provides the opportunity to systematically evaluate recovery patterns and treatment response across distinct cardiovascular subgroups. Due to the unique and highly innovative infrastructure available at the recruiting site, the monocentric design enables performance of an extensive standardized assessment. By incorporating digital technologies in conjunction with deep phenotypic and biomarker data, RECOVER holds promise to enable tailored CR strategies.
resume_fr: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) has been performed in a structured manner since the 1970s, supported by a substantial body of evidence demonstrating its benefits across the heterogeneous pool of cardiac patients. Although therapeutic interventions, pharmacological options, and patient-centered recommendations keep emerging, the majority of CR programs have not changed accordingly. Hence, they are becoming less capable of accounting for an increasingly diverse patient cohort. With a prospective long-term cohort, we aim to achieve an in-depth characterization of CR patients, enabling the delivery of more personalized care in the contemporary era. In this non-interventional, monocentric, prospective cohort study named RECOVER (Cardiac REhabilitation COhort at the Medicine Campus DaVos to invEstigate Recovery), we plan to include 10,000 patients over 10 years across a broad spectrum of cardiovascular conditions (e.g., cardiac surgery, myocardial infarction, heart failure) with data collected across the full spectrum of inpatient CR. Data acquisition is complemented through extensive biobanking allowing detailed phenotyping and biomarker profiling of patients. Follow-up assessments are conducted at 3 and 6 months, and yearly thereafter, up to 10 years. By harnessing novel devices, digital monitoring is employed to continuously capture a wealth of health-related parameters, such as blood pressure and accelerometry-based physical activity. Given the substantial research gap in personalized CR, the RECOVER study provides the opportunity to systematically evaluate recovery patterns and treatment response across distinct cardiovascular subgroups. Due to the unique and highly innovative infrastructure available at the recruiting site, the monocentric design enables performance of an extensive standardized assessment. By incorporating digital technologies in conjunction with deep phenotypic and biomarker data, RECOVER holds promise to enable tailored CR strategies.

titre: From physical healing to psychological readiness: Integrating virtual reality-based CBT into post-crash rehabilitation.
titre_fr: From physical healing to psychological readiness: Integrating virtual reality-based CBT into post-crash rehabilitation.
auteurs: Riandika Marfu'i Lucky Nindi, Lestari Ida Dwi
resume: This Letter to the Editor responds to Erdogan-Yildirim et al.'s review on the psychological and behavioral consequences of physical injuries after road traffic crashes. While the review highlights posttraumatic stress symptoms, driving-related avoidance, trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy, and virtual reality-based exposure, the operational integration of these components into post-crash rehabilitation requires further clarification. The novelty of this perspective lies in reframing recovery as a staged transition from physical healing to psychological readiness. We propose that virtual reality-based CBT may reduce post-crash psychological distress by modifying catastrophic driving-related appraisals, decreasing avoidance behavior, and strengthening driving self-efficacy through graded, therapist-guided driving simulations. This approach could be embedded after medical stabilization through early psychological screening, brief CBT, controlled virtual exposure, and gradual return-to-mobility planning. Future studies should test whether reduced driving avoidance and improved self-efficacy mediate psychological recovery after road traffic crashes.

titre: Barriers and facilitators of cardiac rehabilitation focusing on underserved groups: a mixed-methods systematic review.
titre_fr: Barriers and facilitators of cardiac rehabilitation focusing on underserved groups: a mixed-methods systematic review.
auteurs: Humoud Hanan A, AbuElkhair Ahlam A, Mbolo Ghislaine D, Buckley Benjamin J, Williams Nefyn H, Lane Deirdre A
resume: To identify and synthesise the barriers and facilitators influencing the uptake, adherence and completion of cardiac rehabilitation (CR) programmes among underserved populations globally. Mixed-methods systematic review. MEDLINE (Ovid), PubMed, CINAHL, PsycINFO and Scopus were searched from 1 January 2000 to 9 September 2025. Reference lists and grey literature were also screened. Qualitative, quantitative and mixed-methods studies examining barriers and/or facilitators to CR or physical activity participation among adults with cardiovascular disease from underserved populations (eg, women, ethnic minority groups and individuals with low socioeconomic status). Conference abstracts, editorials and studies without full text were excluded. Study selection, data extraction and quality appraisal were conducted independently in duplicate. Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed-Methods Appraisal Tool. Qualitative findings were synthesised thematically and mapped to the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behaviour model and Theoretical Domains Framework. Quantitative findings were summarised using frequency-based vote counting. 85 studies (54 quantitative, 22 qualitative and 9 mixed-methods studies) involving 228 660 participants were included. Frequently reported barriers included comorbidities and fatigue, limited awareness of CR, communication difficulties, long travel distance, transportation and cost barriers, time constraints and inconsistent referral practices. Key facilitators included structured or automatic referral, health professional recommendation, family and social support, perceived physical and psychological benefits, improved self-efficacy and flexible delivery models such as home-based, telehealth or hybrid programmes. Barriers and facilitators to CR participation among underserved populations operate across individual, social and health system levels. Strategies that incorporate systematic referral, patient education, behavioural support and flexible delivery models may improve equitable access and sustained engagement with CR. CRD42024502384

titre: Toward Culturally Responsive Clinical Practice: Intercultural Speech-Language Pathology Services for Acquired Pragmatic Communication Disorders in Traumatic Brain Injury and Right-Hemisphere Damage.
titre_fr: Toward Culturally Responsive Clinical Practice: Intercultural Speech-Language Pathology Services for Acquired Pragmatic Communication Disorders in Traumatic Brain Injury and Right-Hemisphere Damage.
auteurs: Brown Warren C, Fullwood Shanika Phillips, Fannin Danai Kasambira, Hardin Kathryn Y, Minga Jamila
resume: Acquired pragmatic communication disorders following traumatic brain injury and right-hemisphere damage can disrupt patient-provider interactions that are essential for effective health care. This clinical focus article explores how these disorders intersect with sociocultural factors such as race, language access, and health literacy, contributing to disparities in health care engagement and outcomes to offer culturally specific considerations. This clinical focus article integrates evidence from neurogenic communication disorders, intercultural pragmatics, and health disparities to inform assessment and intervention considerations for acquired pragmatic communication disorders across diverse cultural communication contexts and structural barriers in health care systems. Impairments in pragmatic communication can affect discourse management, conversational participation, and comprehension, reducing opportunities for shared understanding during clinical encounters. When these impairments intersect with cultural communication differences or limited health literacy, patients may experience greater difficulty navigating health care systems and participating in medical decision making. Current speech-language pathology assessment practices and rehabilitation models often fail to capture these contextual influences on communication. Considerations for speech-language pathology service improvements related to assessment and treatment are offered. Advancing equitable neurogenic rehabilitation requires integrating intercultural pragmatics and sociocultural perspectives into assessment and treatment. Approaches such as dynamic assessment, holistic assessment, and telehealth offer practical pathways to improve assessment practices for individuals with acquired social communication disorders.

titre: Development of CaReScreen, a Digital Health Tool for Assessing Late Effects and Cancer Rehabilitation Needs in Cancer Survivors: Protocol for a Qualitative Development and Formative Design Study.
titre_fr: Development of CaReScreen, a Digital Health Tool for Assessing Late Effects and Cancer Rehabilitation Needs in Cancer Survivors: Protocol for a Qualitative Development and Formative Design Study.
auteurs: Kulosman Maja, Engan Harald Kåre, Fagerli Unn Merete, Reinertsen Kristin Valborg, Sand Kari, Sandmæl Jon Arne, Solberg Arne, Tandstad Torgrim
resume: Due to advances in cancer diagnostics and treatments, life expectancy after cancer and the number of cancer survivors are increasing. Symptoms and late effects frequently occur in cancer survivors, with a negative impact on functioning and participation in society. Digital health tools might be helpful to systematically assess symptom burden of late effects and rehabilitation needs. This paper describes the objectives, design, and current status of the Cancer Rehabilitation Screening (CaReScreen) project. The aims are (1) to report the completed development phase of the digital health tool CaReScreen, comprising the exploratory work, the establishment of the interdisciplinary team, the selection of the assessment instrument, and the development of the initial prototype, and (2) to define the objectives, design, and timelines of the ongoing validation of the scoring manual and of the planned large-scale feasibility study. Development followed an iterative, qualitative, and participatory design approach guided by established frameworks for digital health development. It was informed by exploratory qualitative work comprising 40 interviews (9 group and 31 individual) involving 72 informants across Norway, which identified systematic assessment of late effects and navigation of rehabilitation services as the primary unmet needs in cancer survivorship follow-up. A 105-item patient-reported outcome measure (European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer [EORTC] QLQ-SURV100, supplemented with 5 EORTC QLQ-C30 items) was selected as the main assessment instrument. This paper reports the completed development phase; the ongoing validation study and the planned feasibility study are described in terms of objectives, design, and timelines, but their results are not reported here. An initial prototype was developed with health care professionals and cancer survivors as intended end users. It consists of a digital report that identifies and graphically visualizes a panoramic view of multidimensional needs, based on a traffic light scoring system: green indicates low symptom burden and high functioning, yellow moderate symptom burden and moderate functioning, and red high symptom burden and low functioning. The project is funded for the period 2022 to 2028. The development phase is completed, as well as early prototype usability and usefulness testing. Validation of the scoring manual is ongoing, with 800 participants included to date and reporting expected in spring 2027. A large-scale feasibility study is planned to commence in 2027. The CaReScreen interdisciplinary team has developed an initial digital health tool prototype with the main aim of enabling systematic assessment of late effects, functioning, and unmet rehabilitation needs in cancer survivors. The prototype now proceeds to validation and feasibility testing, which will determine its clinical utility and support regulatory approval under the European Medical Device Regulation.

titre: Digital and technology‑enabled approaches for post‑stroke fatigue: A scoping review protocol.
titre_fr: Digital and technology‑enabled approaches for post‑stroke fatigue: A scoping review protocol.
auteurs: Huang Xiangdong, Xu Jiangmei, Wang Lingmin, Huang Shiting, Zhu Xiaoping
resume: Post‑stroke fatigue (PSF) affects approximately 50% of stroke survivors and is one of the most common and disabling post‑stroke sequelae. Digital and technology‑enabled approaches have attracted increasing attention in the field of stroke rehabilitation, including mobile health applications (mHealth), wearable devices, virtual reality (VR), remote rehabilitation, artificial intelligence (AI), and neuromodulation technologies. However, no comprehensive scoping review has systematically mapped the full spectrum of evidence on digital and technology‑enabled approaches for PSF. This scoping review will follow the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews, be guided by the Population, Concept, Context (PCC) framework, and be reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta‑Analysis Protocols (PRISMA‑P) and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta‑Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA‑ScR). Eight electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, Cochrane CENTRAL, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and PsycINFO) and five gray literature sources (OpenGrey, ProQuest Dissertations and Theses Global, ClinicalTrials.gov, the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform, and Google Scholar) will be searched. Two reviewers will use NoteExpress to remove duplicates and manage references, and will independently screen titles, abstracts, and full texts. After pilot testing, data will be extracted independently by the two reviewers. Synthesis will involve descriptive numerical summaries and inductive qualitative content analysis. Inter‑rater agreement will be assessed during a calibration phase. The expected output is an evidence map organized by approach category and purpose (assessment, monitoring, prevention, and treatment), which will identify knowledge gaps and guide future research. This protocol has been registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF). Registration DOI (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/4WMEK).

titre: AI-Enabled Patient Profiling for Personalized Nursing Care and Health Support: Scoping Review.
titre_fr: AI-Enabled Patient Profiling for Personalized Nursing Care and Health Support: Scoping Review.
auteurs: Zhang Jingyan, Zhang Fengyi, Guo Youpeng, Zhang Jingwen, Zhong Hongmei, Guo Xuemei, Tan Min
resume: AI-enabled patient profiling has been proposed to organize heterogeneous patient data and support personalized nursing care and health support. Given the growing use of AI, machine learning, large language models (LLMs), digital phenotyping, and digital twins in health care, it is important to clarify how patient profiling has been conceptualized, applied, and evaluated in nursing-relevant contexts. This scoping review aimed to examine and report the available evidence on AI-enabled patient profiling for personalized nursing care and health support. This scoping review was conducted using the Joanna Briggs Institute methodological framework and the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews). Chinese and English databases were searched from inception to May 18, 2026, including China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, VIP Database, Chinese Biomedical Literature Database, PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Embase. Eligible studies used AI or computational intelligence methods to construct, classify, apply, validate, or evaluate patient profiles or related patient representations relevant to personalized nursing care or health support. Two reviewers independently screened records, assessed full texts, and charted data using a predefined form. Data were synthesized descriptively and narratively using an input-process-output framework. A total of 61 studies were included. AI-enabled patient profiling was represented through patient profiles, patient or user personas, digital phenotypes, patient segments, clinical subtypes, digital twins, and LLM-enabled personalization. Included studies used diverse data sources, including electronic health records, nursing records, patient-reported outcomes, questionnaires, mobile app data, wearable and sensor data, engagement logs, and textual or conversational data. Common AI approaches included machine learning, clustering, deep learning, natural language processing, recommender systems, knowledge graphs, digital twin modeling, and LLMs. Applications focused on personalized education, self-management support, rehabilitation, chronic disease management, remote monitoring, decision support, follow-up care, and shared decision-making. Most studies evaluated algorithmic performance, feasibility, usability, or system development, whereas fewer studies examined profile validity, actionability, equity, workflow integration, or long-term nursing-sensitive and patient-centered outcomes. Existing evidence positions AI-enabled patient profiling as an emerging data-to-action mechanism for personalized nursing care and health support rather than as a mature clinical intervention. Future research should strengthen conceptual clarity, validate the profile, establish explicit pathways linking profiles to actions, incorporate nurse and patient involvement, assess equity and safety, and evaluate implementation in real-world nursing settings. OSF Registry mey4u; https://osf.io/mey4u.

titre: Development process and user experiences of an online support program for first-time hearing aid users.
titre_fr: Development process and user experiences of an online support program for first-time hearing aid users.
auteurs: Ahlberg Sandra, Ivarsson Linda, Brännström K Jonas, Öberg Marie, Thorén Elisabet Sundewall
resume: Many with hearing loss do not recognize their need for support or may struggle to acknowledge and accept their hearing difficulties, and when one receives hearing aids for the first time, many feel the need for more information and support during their rehabilitation process. The present article describes the development process of an online program in Swedish that supports first-time hearing aid users in an interleaved manner with the traditional audiological rehabilitation at the clinic. In this formative evaluation study, the outline and content of the program was inspired by existing literature and informed by clinical expertise. The program was implemented within the Swedish national health portal. At the end of an iterative development process, four first-time and seven experienced hearing aid users evaluated the program in parallel to the provision of their new hearing aids and provided structured feedback on comprehension, relevance, manageability and ease of use to inform further development. Participant feedback identified the need for some minor changes but that the program was considered useful to first-time hearing aid users, comprehensible, relevant and manageable. The evaluation from the end-users demonstrated that all parts of the online support program were relevant for first-time hearing aid users, and that it was manageable and easy to use. However, content regarding assistive listening devices was deemed less relevant and some participants experienced difficulties with logging in to the national health portal.

titre: Independent AI pipelines for rehabilitation exercise assessment and cognitive status classification: a retrospective proof of concept study.
titre_fr: Independent AI pipelines for rehabilitation exercise assessment and cognitive status classification: a retrospective proof of concept study.
auteurs: Wang Guoyu, Ren Guoliang, Zhu Jiaju
resume: Digital rehabilitation can extend remote exercise monitoring and cognitive health support, but available public datasets often capture these functions separately. This study evaluates two independent machine learning pipelines within a conceptual telerehabilitation architecture rather than a clinically validated integrated system. The physical pipeline used the WLU Rehabilitation Posture dataset. After quality control and removal of exact duplicates, we retained 315 unique videos of arm raise, knee extension, and sit-to-stand with dataset-defined correct or incorrect labels. We converted 24 video frames into 182 privacy-preserving features: appearance, shape, gradient, optical flow, temporal, and metadata. We compared candidate algorithms using stratified five-fold cross-validation within the training data, reserving a 20% holdout set for final evaluation. The cognitive pipeline analyzed 5,000 records from the Community Elderly Cognitive Health dataset using 14 demographic, clinical, lifestyle, psychological, and cognitive-assessment predictors. Because target generation is not independently documented and MMSE and GDS are target-proximal, this module is interpreted as concurrent cognitive status classification rather than as independent risk prediction. Random forest achieved video-level physical six-class accuracy of 0.857, balanced accuracy of 0.846, macro F1 of 0.849, and Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.829; because participant and session identifiers were unavailable, these estimates do not represent participant-independent validation. Exercise identity accuracy was 0.984, whereas correct versus incorrect execution accuracy was 0.857. Extra Trees achieved cognitive status accuracy of 0.936, balanced accuracy of 0.918, macro F1 of 0.923, and ROC AUC of 0.978. MMSE, GDS, physical activity, and glucose level were influential cognitive predictors. The two pipelines produced strong technical discrimination and interpretable outputs, but we evaluated them on independent, unlinked datasets. The physical cohort was not confirmed as geriatric; participant- or session-level groupings were unavailable, and the provenance of the cognitive data and the target construction remain uncertain. The findings therefore support a retrospective proof of concept for separate clinician-supervised decision-support components, not for patient-level multimodal fusion, diagnosis, treatment effectiveness, recovery, or autonomous care.

titre: Speeded motor training leads to fMRI changes during imagined hallway walking conditions in adults with traumatic brain injury.
titre_fr: Speeded motor training leads to fMRI changes during imagined hallway walking conditions in adults with traumatic brain injury.
auteurs: Damiano Diane L, Weerasooriya Amanda, Horovitz Silvina
resume: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) often leads to persistent deficits in multiple functional domains. fMRI data were collected in an 8-week trial of rapid resisted elliptical training in ambulatory adults with chronic TBI to promote motor, cognitive and behavioral function and adaptive brain plasticity. Nine participants with chronic TBI and 9 uninjured adults were used for comparison of gait and fMRI data. Gait speed during treadmill walking down a virtual‑reality hallway with (cluttered) or without (uncluttered) distractions. Hallway videos at individualized speeds were displayed during fMRI while participants imagined walking through them before and after the intervention. We hypothesized that brain activation outcomes would differ between groups, conditions, and after training, and would relate to balance outcomes reported previously. Cluttered hallway conditions activated more brain regions than uncluttered ones. Uninjured adults initially had greater activation in the primary motor cortex and in regions involved in visuospatial processing and postural control. Post-intervention, those with TBI demonstrated increased activation, minimizing group differences, particularly in motor-related regions. Post-training, improvements in postural control related directly to increased cerebellar activation. Speed-focused motor training successfully induced brain plasticity related to improved balance in participants with chronic TBI, reinforcing the benefits of regular exercise in this population.
resume_fr: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) often leads to persistent deficits in multiple functional domains. fMRI data were collected in an 8-week trial of rapid resisted elliptical training in ambulatory adults with chronic TBI to promote motor, cognitive and behavioral function and adaptive brain plasticity. Nine participants with chronic TBI and 9 uninjured adults were used for comparison of gait and fMRI data. Gait speed during treadmill walking down a virtual‑reality hallway with (cluttered) or without (uncluttered) distractions. Hallway videos at individualized speeds were displayed during fMRI while participants imagined walking through them before and after the intervention. We hypothesized that brain activation outcomes would differ between groups, conditions, and after training, and would relate to balance outcomes reported previously. Cluttered hallway conditions activated more brain regions than uncluttered ones. Uninjured adults initially had greater activation in the primary motor cortex and in regions involved in visuospatial processing and postural control. Post-intervention, those with TBI demonstrated increased activation, minimizing group differences, particularly in motor-related regions. Post-training, improvements in postural control related directly to increased cerebellar activation. Speed-focused motor training successfully induced brain plasticity related to improved balance in participants with chronic TBI, reinforcing the benefits of regular exercise in this population.

titre: Multicentre phase III randomised controlled trial to evaluate effectiveness of the Both EARS (BEARS) virtual reality training package to maximise hearing abilities in children and young people with bilateral cochlear implants: the BEARS protocol.
titre_fr: Multicentre phase III randomised controlled trial to evaluate effectiveness of the Both EARS (BEARS) virtual reality training package to maximise hearing abilities in children and young people with bilateral cochlear implants: the BEARS protocol.
auteurs: Vickers Deborah, Buelt Lisabeth, Arram Liz, Picinali Lorenzo, Salorio Corbetto Marina, Chowdhury Kashfia, Clarke Caroline S, Freemantle Nick, Jiang Dan, Parmar Bhavisha, Early Frances, Driver Sandra, Bordea Ekaterina, Hill Teresa, Cullington Helen, Kukiewicz Fiona, Rocca Christine, Kitterick Padraig, Corbett Fleur, Nightingale Ruth, Blackstone James, Ahmed Norin, Somerset Sarah, Zalk Nejra, Mahon Merle
resume: Deafness is the most common human sensory deficit. Cochlear implantation is the primary intervention for severe to profound deafness. Currently, over 7000 people have bilateral cochlear implants (CIs) in the UK most of whom are children. Patient feedback suggests that for children with bilateral CIs, everyday communication is challenging and tiring, with extra effort required to integrate information from two ears, especially in noise and that current rehabilitation techniques are not engaging or appropriate to their lifestyles. To address these issues, researchers developed the Both EARS (BEARS) training package comprised three virtual reality games to improve sound localisation and listening in noise. This protocol describes the design and methodology of a multicentre phase III randomised controlled trial (RCT) to evaluate whether use of the BEARS training package alongside usual care compared with only receiving usual care improves speech-in-noise perception, hearing experiences, vocabulary and quality of life and reduces listening effort in children and young people (aged 8–16 years (inclusive)) with bilateral CIs. This RCT is currently underway in 16 clinical CI departments in National Health Service (NHS) or university hospitals across the UK. The intervention involves 3 months of spatial-listening training delivered via the BEARS training package in addition to any routine rehabilitation. The control is ‘usual care’ (routine rehabilitation clinical care pathway). The primary outcome is the difference between the intervention groups in speech-in-noise perception score at 3 months derived from the spatial speech in noise (SSiN-VA) test. Recruitment ended on 31 July 2026, and end of data collection is 31 October 2026. Data analyses will begin 30 November 2026, and first results will be reported by 31 March 2027. The BEARS trial was reviewed and approved by the Yorkshire & The Humber–Sheffield Research Ethics Committee (Integrated Research Application System project ID: 319903; REC reference: 23/YH/0046). It is also registered on the UK’s clinical study registry (ISRCTN92454702). Trial results will be submitted to peer-reviewed journals and presented at scientific conferences and will be disseminated regardless of the direction of effect. NCT05808543.

titre: Development of a Wearable Torsion Sensor Utilizing a Geometric Model and a Hysteresis-Compensated Calibration Engine.
titre_fr: Development of a Wearable Torsion Sensor Utilizing a Geometric Model and a Hysteresis-Compensated Calibration Engine.
auteurs: Koo Bonhak, Yu Seonghun, Chang Hojong, Kang Chansol, Sim Jeehyun
resume: Measuring torsional movement is crucial for tracking human kinematics in applications such as virtual reality, biomechanics, rehabilitation, and soft robotic joints. However, continuous, non-invasive torsion measurement remains challenging due to multi-axial deformations, where existing methods rely heavily on empirical data fitting or computationally expensive deep learning models requiring vast training datasets. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a training-free, highly precise torsion estimation framework that converts soft resistive strain sensor data into forearm rotation angles using closed-form kinematic-geometric modeling. Two geometric representations-the Cylinder Model and Truncated Cone Model-are established to analytically map non-linear tensile strain to torsion angles. Additionally, an online calibration algorithm is integrated to mitigate cumulative measurement drift caused by viscoelastic hysteresis. Under static conditions, the proposed models achieved a high coefficient of determination (R2 = 0.9888) against reference IMU data. In dynamic trials, the hysteresis compensation algorithm maintained robust tracking performance (R2 = 0.8033), achieving an angular root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 4.12° and a cycle peak prominence relative error of 0.42% for the Truncated Cone Model. In this single-subject proof-of-concept feasibility study (n = 1), the proposed framework demonstrated the feasibility of continuous torsional motion tracking through a training-free geometric approach, providing a preliminary foundation for future evaluation in wearable systems and soft robotics.

titre: Multimodal Sensing and Digital Biomarkers in Virtual Reality-Based Cognitive Rehabilitation: Clinical Validation, Adaptive Systems, and Real-World Translation.
titre_fr: Multimodal Sensing and Digital Biomarkers in Virtual Reality-Based Cognitive Rehabilitation: Clinical Validation, Adaptive Systems, and Real-World Translation.
auteurs: Rundo Francesco, Musso Sabrina, Buono Serafino, Recupero Marilena, Ferri Raffaele
resume: Virtual reality (VR) is evolving from a platform for cognitive exercises into an instrumented rehabilitation environment capable of simultaneously delivering treatment and quantifying behavior. This critical narrative review examines how behavioral, ocular, kinematic, physiological, and neurophysiological signals can be transformed into clinically meaningful digital measures, candidate biomarkers, adaptive interventions, and real-world functional outcomes. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore were searched from database inception to 20 September 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation searching and targeted searches. Clinical, methodological, validation, and directly relevant technical studies were considered, including studies in healthy participants when methodologically informative. Of 690 records identified, 145 duplicates were removed; 545 unique records were screened and 303 formed the candidate evidence pool for critical narrative appraisal. Behavioral and interaction-derived measures are the most established, while eye tracking, kinematic sensing, autonomic monitoring, EEG, and fNIRS provide complementary information on attention, strategy, workload, and engagement. Quantitatively, combined hand- and eye-tracking features distinguished mild cognitive impairment from healthy controls with 93.3% accuracy, 100% sensitivity, and 83.3% specificity, while immersive VR life-skills training produced real-world functional gains of d = 1.00 post-training and d = 1.12 at 1-week follow-up. However, most sensor-derived variables remain digital measures or candidate biomarkers rather than clinically validated biomarkers; physiology-informed closed-loop adaptation is uncommon, and evidence that such adaptation produces sustained ADL or assisted-living benefits is lacking. Progress now depends on standardized reporting, external and multicenter validation, clinically interpretable adaptive models, and objective demonstration of real-world transfer.

titre: 5 764 décès en excès en France durant la période de canicule du 17 juin au 2 juillet
resume: Santé publique France publie les données relatives à l’excès de mortalité toutes causes, observé durant la période de canicule du 17 juin au 2 juillet 2026 exposant la quasi-totalité de la population à de très fortes chaleurs dans une période encore importante d’activités scolaires et professionnelles. 5 764 décès toutes causes en excès (+ 36 %) ont été estimés pour les périodes et départements concernés par des records de températures historiques. Mercredi 24 et jeudi 25 juin ont été les journées les plus chaudes jamais enregistrées en France, atteignant pour la première fois les 30 °C en moyenne sur 24h selon Météo France. La chaleur a ainsi atteint des niveaux extrêmes avec des valeurs de températures maximales record dans plusieurs régions (42,5 °C à Bordeaux, 40,1 °C à Paris, 42,7 °C à Niort, 43 °C à Brive, 43,8 °C à Saintes …).Toutes les classes d’âge à partir de 15 ans sont également concernées. Cet excès de mortalité toutes causes, souligne l’impact sanitaire lié à l’intensité remarquable et la durée de l’exposition à la chaleur de la population sur le territoire hexagonal, sans toutefois atteindre celui de 2003. Ces données constituent une première estimation de l’impact de la canicule sur la mortalité toutes causes, réalisée et publiée 3 semaines après la fin de la vague de chaleur et sont donc non consolidées. Elles devront être confirmées par les analyses plus précises du bilan de fin de période de surveillance estivale, à l’automne.

titre: Augmentation marquée des recours aux soins d’urgences liée à l’épisode de canicule précoce de mai 2026 : les autorités sanitaires rappellent la nécessité d’adopter les bons gestes pour se protéger de la chaleur
resume: Cette année, un premier épisode de vigilance canicule particulièrement précoce a été observé. Météo France a activé la vigilance orange canicule pour 17 départements de 5 régions hexagonales (Bretagne, Ile-de-France, Normandie, Nouvelle-Aquitaine et Pays-de-la-Loire) du 26 au 30 mai soit 26 % de la population française concernée par au moins un jour de vigilance orange canicule. Durant cet épisode, Santé publique France a observé une hausse significative des recours aux soins d’urgence liés à certains indicateurs de santé surveillés et associés à la chaleur (hyperthermies, déshydratations, hyponatrémies et malaises). Les passages aux urgences et les hospitalisations consécutives ainsi que les consultations SOS Médecins pour les indicateurs de santé suivis ont augmenté dès le 22 mai atteignant un pic le 26 mai. Santé publique France publie le premier bulletin national Canicule et Santé, et les bulletins régionaux pour les 5 régions concernées. A l’occasion de ce premier épisode de chaleur survenu précocement dans la saison, les autorités sanitaires ont anticipé les dispositifs de prévention afin de limiter les risques pour la santé. Elles rappellent la nécessité d’adopter les comportements individuels adaptés et d’adapter les milieux de vie pour se prémunir des effets de la chaleur, dans un contexte où de nouveaux épisodes pourraient se produire au cours de la saison estivale.

titre: Experiences and visions for physiotherapy and occupational therapy in oncological rehabilitation: results from a transdisciplinary research workshop programme with people living with and beyond cancer and health professionals.
titre_fr: Expériences et visions de la physiothérapie et de l'ergothérapie en réadaptation oncologique : résultats d'un programme d'ateliers de recherche transdisciplinaire avec des personnes vivant avec et au-delà du cancer et des professionnels de la santé.
auteurs: Ley Clemens, Wenzel Claudia, Ebner Susanne, Müller Alexander, Subhieh Miriam, Masel Eva Katharina, Tatzer-Hanten Verena C
resume: Physiotherapy and occupational therapy can improve quality of life and help to manage complex cancer and treatment-related side effects, but these rehabilitation services remain underutilised. This study aimed to co-produce knowledge for improving patient-centred services in the oncological rehabilitation continuum in Austria. A 3-days transdisciplinary workshop programme was facilitated in a world café format with 36 participants: people living with and beyond cancer (n = 13), relatives (n = 1), health professionals (n = 11) and researchers (n = 11). Based on the participatory paradigm and co-production principles, a range of participatory research techniques were employed co-producing, analysing, and interpreting data (in-situ thematic analysis). Four main themes emerged: (a) physiotherapy and occupational therapy in the oncological rehabilitation continuum; (b) relationship-building; (c) continued and interconnected services; and (d) visions for an ideal rehabilitation. The findings display a vast diversity of lived experiences and illness trajectories as well as opportunities for improving services and enabling human agency. Physiotherapy and occupational therapy should be better integrated in all care settings, interconnected across all rehabilitation continuum phases, person-centred and tailored to diverse experiences, needs and rehabilitation trajectories. Peer-support, information and guidance for patients must be provided early from diagnosis and continuously throughout the care pathways for promoting continuity.
resume_fr: La physiothérapie et l'ergothérapie peuvent améliorer la qualité de vie et aider à gérer les cancers complexes et les effets secondaires liés au traitement, mais ces services de réadaptation restent sous-utilisés. Cette étude visait à coproduire des connaissances pour améliorer les services centrés sur le patient dans le continuum de réadaptation oncologique en Autriche. Un programme d'ateliers transdisciplinaires de 3 jours a été animé dans un format café mondial avec 36 participants : des personnes vivantavec et au-delà du cancer (n = 13), les parents (n = 1), les professionnels de la santé (n = 11) et les chercheurs (n = 11). Sur la base du paradigme participatif et des principes de coproduction, une gamme de techniques de recherche participative a été utilisée pour coproduire, analyser et interpréter des données (analyse thématique in situ). Quatre thèmes principaux ont émergé : (a) la physiothérapie et l'ergothérapie dans le continuum de la réadaptation oncologique ;(b) l'établissement de relations ; (c) des services continus et interconnectés ; et (d) des visions pour une réhabilitation idéale. Les résultats montrent une grande diversité d'expériences vécues et de trajectoires de maladie, ainsi que des possibilités d'améliorer les services et de permettre l'action humaine. La physiothérapie et l'ergothérapie devraient être mieux intégrées dans tous les milieux de soins, interconnectées à toutes les phases du continuum de réadaptation, centrées sur la personne et adaptéesà diverses expériences, besoins et trajectoires de réadaptation. Le soutien par les pairs, l'information et l'orientation des patients doivent être fournis dès le diagnostic et de manière continue tout au long des parcours de soins afin de promouvoir la continuité.

titre: Self-Reported AI Competency and Educational Needs for Integrated AI and Digital Rehabilitation Education Among Occupational Therapy Students: A Cross-Sectional Survey.
titre_fr: Self-Reported AI Competency and Educational Needs for Integrated AI and Digital Rehabilitation Education Among Occupational Therapy Students : A Cross-Sectional Survey.
auteurs: Park Yun-Hee, Kim Deok-Ju
resume: The growing use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare calls for occupational therapy education that combines critical appraisal, clinical reasoning, and digital rehabilitation. This study aimed to examine students' interest in AI, perceived AI competency, and needs for integrated AI and digital rehabilitation education, and identified factors associated with educational content needs. An exploratory cross-sectional survey using convenience sampling and five researcher-developed scales without full psychometric validation was conducted among occupational therapy students from three universities. A total of 250 questionnaires were submitted, and 230 complete responses were analyzed. Descriptive statistics, reliability tests, Welch group comparisons, Pearson correlations, and hierarchical multiple regression with sensitivity analyses were used. Mean scores were 3.64±0.77 for AI interest, 3.42±0.67 for self-reported AI competency, 3.93±0.68 for educational content needs, 3.95±0.63 for educational priority, and 3.82±0.64 for instructional method preference. All five domains were positively correlated. Educational priority and instructional method preference showed the strongest correlation (r=0.701). AI interest (β=0.490, p<0.001) and self-reported AI competency (β=0.154, p=0.015) were associated with educational content needs in the conventional regression; the final model explained 34.3% of the variance. The competency association was sensitive to robust inference (HC3 p=0.0504). Students expressed preferences for integrated, practice-oriented education addressing AI use, occupational therapy clinical reasoning, client-appropriate tool selection, assessment, and intervention planning.
resume_fr: L'utilisation croissante de l'intelligence artificielle générative (IA) dans les soins de santé nécessite une formation en ergothérapie qui combine évaluation critique, raisonnement clinique et réadaptation numérique. Cette étude visait à examiner l'intérêt des élèves pour l'IA, la compétence perçue en matière d'IA et les besoins en matière d'éducation intégrée à l'IA et à la réadaptation numérique, et à identifier les facteurs associés aux besoins en matière de contenu éducatif. Une enquête transversale exploratoire utilisantun échantillonnage de commodité et cinq échelles développées par des chercheurs sans validation psychométrique complète ont été menées auprès d'étudiants en ergothérapie de trois universités. Au total, 250 questionnaires ont été soumis et 230 réponses complètes ont été analysées. Des statistiques descriptives, des tests de fiabilité, des comparaisons de groupes de Welch, des corrélations de Pearson et une régression multiple hiérarchique avec des analyses de sensibilité ont été utilisés. Les scores moyens étaient de 3,64±0,77pour l'intérêt de l'IA, 3,42±0,67 pour la compétence en IA autodéclarée, 3,93±0,68 pour les besoins en contenu éducatif, 3,95±0,63 pour la priorité éducative et 3,82±0,64 pour la préférence de la méthode pédagogique. Les cinq domaines étaient positivement corrélés. La priorité éducative et la préférence de méthode pédagogique ont montré la corrélation la plus forte (r=0,701). L'intérêt pour l'IA (β=0,490, p<0,001) et la compétence en IA autodéclarée (β=0,154, p=0,015) ont été associés à l'éducation cbesoins ontents dans la régression conventionnelle ; le modèle final expliquait 34,3% de la variance. L'association de compétences était sensible à une inférence robuste (HC3 p=0,0504). Les élèves ont exprimé leurs préférences pour une éducation intégrée et axée sur la pratique portant sur l'utilisation de l'IA, le raisonnement clinique en ergothérapie, la sélection d'outils adaptés au client, l'évaluation et la planification des interventions.

titre: Comment on "Perceived value of physiotherapy and occupational therapy among people with multiple sclerosis: insights from a qualitative interview study".
titre_fr: Commentaire sur « Perceived value of physiotherapy and ergotherapy among people with multiple sclerosis : insights from a qualitative interview study ».

titre: Effects of Cognitive Orientation to Daily Occupational Performance (CO-OP) Intervention on Executive Functioning for Activities of Daily Living in Patients With Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: Effects of Cognitive Orientation to Daily Occupational Performance (CO-OP) Intervention on Executive Functioning for Activities of Daily Living in Patients With Stroke : A Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Bak Down, Kim Su-Kyoung, Cha Tae-Hyun, Kim Hee
revue: Hong Kong journal of occupational therapy : HKJOT
resume: This study aimed to examine the effects of the Cognitive Orientation to Daily Occupational Performance (CO-OP) intervention on executive functioning to promote the performance of activities of daily living in patients with stroke using a randomized controlled trial. Thirty-eight patients with stroke who met the inclusion criteria were randomly assigned to either an experimental (n = 19) or a control (n = 19) group using a computer-generated randomization program. The experimental group received the CO-OP intervention, whereas the control group received conventional occupational therapy. Both interventions were delivered over 12 sessions, 5 times per week, with each session lasting 60 min. The Executive Function Performance Test - Korean version, Canadian Occupational Performance Measure, Performance Quality Rating Scale, Korean version of the Modified Barthel index, and Korean version of the Instrumental Activities of Daily Living Scale were administered for pre- and post-intervention assessments. Both groups showed significant improvements in executive function, occupational performance, and activities of daily living following the interventions (p < .001). However, when comparing the magnitude of change between the two groups, the experimental group demonstrated significantly greater improvements across all measures (p < .05, p < .01, p < .001). These findings indicate that the CO-OP intervention led to statistically greater enhancement than conventional occupational therapy. This study provides evidence that the CO-OP approach in occupational therapy can effectively improve executive function, occupational performance, and activities of daily living in patients with stroke. Therefore, the CO-OP intervention, as a client-centered and evidence-based approach, may be a valuable therapeutic method in future clinical practice.
resume_fr: Cette étude visait à examiner les effets de l'intervention CO-OP (Cognitive Orientation to Daily Occupational Performance) sur le fonctionnement exécutif afin de promouvoir la performance des activités de la vie quotidienne chez les patients victimes d'un AVC à l'aide d'un essai contrôlé randomisé. Trente-huit patients victimes d'un AVC qui répondaient aux critères d'inclusion ont été assignés au hasard à un groupe expérimental (n = 19) ou à un groupe témoin (n = 19) à l'aide d'un Rando généré par ordinateurle groupe expérimental a reçu l'intervention COOPÉRATIVE, tandis que le groupe témoin a reçu l'ergothérapie conventionnelle. Les deux interventions se sont déroulées sur 12 séances, 5 fois par semaine, chaque séance durant 60 min. Le test de performance de la fonction exécutive - version coréenne, la mesure canadienne de la performance professionnelle, l'échelle d'évaluation de la qualité de la performance, la version coréenne de l'indice Barthel modifié et la version coréenne del'échelle des activités instrumentales de la vie quotidienne a été administrée pour les évaluations pré et post-intervention. Les deux groupes ont montré des améliorations significatives de la fonction exécutive, de la performance professionnelle et des activités de la vie quotidienne après les interventions (p < 0,001). Cependant, en comparant l'ampleur du changement entre les deux groupes, le groupe expérimental a montré des améliorations significativement plus importantes pour toutes les mesures (p < 0,05,p < .01, p < .001). Ces résultats indiquent que l'intervention COOPÉRATIVE a conduit à une amélioration statistiquement plus importante que l'ergothérapie conventionnelle. Cette étude fournit des preuves que l'approche COOPÉRATIVE en ergothérapie peut améliorer efficacement la fonction exécutive, la performance professionnelle et les activités de la vie quotidienne chez les patients victimes d'un AVC. Par conséquent, l'intervention COOPÉRATIVE, en tant qu'approche centrée sur le client et fondée sur des données probantes, peut être uneprécieuse méthode thérapeutique dans la pratique clinique future.
