titre: Performance-Based Versus Informant-Reported IADL in Dementia: A Person-Environment-Occupation Perspective for Occupational Therapy Outcome Selection.
titre_fr: Performance-Based versus Informant-Reported IADL in Dementia : A Person-Environment-Occupation Perspective for Occupational Therapy Outcome Selection.
auteurs: Chen Hui-Mei, Huang Hung-Chia, Chang Chun-Wei, Lin Hsiu-Fen, Chen Cheng-Sheng
revue: Hong Kong journal of occupational therapy : HKJOT
resume: Selecting an instrumental activities of daily living (IADL) outcome is important in occupational therapy intervention for older adults with dementia. Inspired by the Person-Environment-Occupation (PEO) framework, this study compared older adults with AD and non-AD dementia on performance-based and informant-reported IADL outcomes and examined correlates by group. Eighty older adults with mild-to-moderate dementia (49 AD; 31 non-AD: 17 vascular dementia, 14 dementia with Lewy bodies) and 30 controls were recruited in Taiwan. Cognition, physical performance, neuropsychiatric symptoms, and caregiver distress were assessed with the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), modified Physical Performance Test, and Neuropsychiatric Inventory. IADL was measured using Taiwan Performance-based IADL (TPIADL) and the Disability Assessment for Dementia-IADL (DAD-IADL). ANCOVA was used to compare groups, hierarchical regression was used to examine correlates, and Pearson correlations was used to examine within-group TPIADL-DAD-IADL associations. AD and non-AD participants had comparable cognitive, physical, and neuropsychiatric profiles. Non-AD participants had poorer DAD-IADL scores (p = .019), whereas TPIADL did not differ (p = .256). TPIADL and DAD-IADL were correlated in AD (r = -.697, p < .001) and non-AD dementia (r = -.374, p = .038). MoCA was the only consistent correlate of TPIADL (β = -.66 to -.87). For DAD-IADL, MoCA was the primary correlate in AD (β = .57), whereas hyperactivity (β = .59) and caregiver distress (β = -.58; ΔR2 = .287) were identified in non-AD. Performance-based and informant-reported IADL measures may provide complementary information about occupational performance in older adults with dementia. Their associations may be interpreted within the PEO framework as reflecting person-related and contextual influences.
resume_fr: Le choix d'un résultat des activités instrumentales de la vie quotidienne (IADL) est important dans l'intervention en ergothérapie pour les personnes âgées atteintes de démence. Inspirée par le cadre Personne-Environnement-Occupation (PEO), cette étude a comparé les adultes âgés atteints de démence AD et non AD sur les résultats IADL basés sur la performance et rapportés par les informateurs et a examiné les corrélats par groupe. Quatre-vingts personnes âgées atteintes de démence légère à modérée (49 AD ; 31 non AD : 17 dementia, 14 démences à corps de Lewy) et 30 témoins ont été recrutés à Taïwan. La cognition, la performance physique, les symptômes neuropsychiatriques et la détresse du soignant ont été évalués avec l'évaluation cognitive de Montréal (MoCA), le test de performance physique modifié et l'inventaire neuropsychiatrique. L'IADL a été mesuré à l'aide de l'IADL basé sur la performance de Taiwan (TPIADL) et de l'évaluation du handicap pour Dementia-IADL (DAD-IADL). ANCOVA a été utilisé pour comparer les groupes,la régression hiérarchique a été utilisée pour examiner les corrélats, et les corrélations de Pearson ont été utilisées pour examiner les associations TPIADL-DAD-IADL au sein du groupe. Les participants atteints de MA et non atteints de MA avaient des profils cognitifs, physiques et neuropsychiatriques comparables. Les participants non AD avaient des scores DAD-IADL plus faibles (p = 0,019), alors que les TPIADL ne différaient pas (p = 0,256). TPIADL et DAD-IADL ont été corrélés dans la MA (r = -.697, p < .001) et la démence non MA(r = -.374, p = .038). Le MoCA était le seul corrélé cohérent du TPIADL (β = -.66 à -.87). Pour le DAD-IADL, le MoCA était le principal corrélé dans la MA (β = .57), tandis que l'hyperactivité (β = .59) et la détresse du soignant (β = -.58 ; ΔR2 = .287) ont été identifiées dans la MA non. Les mesures IADL basées sur la performance et rapportées par les informateurs peuvent fournir des informations complémentaires sur la performance professionnelle chez les personnes âgées atteintes de démence.peuvent être interprétées dans le cadre de la PEO comme reflétant des influences liées à la personne et au contexte.

titre: A New Canadian Agenda for Occupational Therapy Education Research.
titre_fr: A New Canadian Agenda for Occupational Therapy Education Research.
auteurs: Duncan Andrea, Gill Monique, Jarus Tal, Roberts Mary Roduta, Smith Kirsten, VanderKaay Sandra
revue: Canadian journal of occupational therapy. Revue canadienne d'ergotherapie
resume: Background: Research on education is essential to train and educate future occupational therapists. While there may be institutional or geographical initiatives, there is no national set of priorities. Purpose: This study sought to develop a research agenda that outlines key priorities for Research on Education in occupational therapy in Canada. Methods: This study used a modified Delphi approach to identify researchers' and educators' priorities for occupational therapy research on education in Canada. Data were collected through two survey rounds and one in-person discussion. Findings: Education researchers identified teaching and learning, curriculum development, student preparedness and equity, and diversity as key research priorities. Included in these categories were a desire for research on the role of technology, hybrid and distributed campus models, integration of classroom and fieldwork learning, and professional identity formation. Approaches to new evidence creation include critically evaluating innovation and developing national evidence-informed frameworks to guide future research. Conclusions: This study highlights the need for a coordinated national research agenda in occupational therapy education. This acts as a call to action for clinicians, educators, researchers, administrators, funders, associations, and regulatory bodies to promote Canadian research on education efforts that are aligned with these priorities.
resume_fr: Contexte : La recherche sur l'éducation est essentielle pour former et éduquer les futurs ergothérapeutes. Bien qu'il puisse y avoir des initiatives institutionnelles ou géographiques, il n'y a pas d'ensemble national de priorités. Objectif : Cette étude visait à élaborer un programme de recherche qui décrit les principales priorités de la recherche sur l'éducation en ergothérapie au Canada. Méthodes : Cette étude a utilisé une approche Delphi modifiée pour identifier les chercheurs etpriorités des éducateurs pour la recherche en ergothérapie sur l'éducation au Canada. Les données ont été recueillies lors de deux cycles d'enquête et d'une discussion en personne. Constatations : Les chercheurs en éducation ont identifié l'enseignement et l'apprentissage, l'élaboration de programmes d'études, la préparation et l'équité des élèves et la diversité comme des priorités de recherche clés. Parmi ces catégories figurait un désir de recherche sur le rôle de la technologie, des modèles de campus hybrides et distribués, intégration de l'apprentissage en classe et sur le terrain, et formation à l'identité professionnelle. Les approches de la création de nouvelles données probantes comprennent l'évaluation critique de l'innovation et l'élaboration de cadres nationaux fondés sur des données probantes pour guider les recherches futures. Conclusions : Cette étude souligne la nécessité d'un programme de recherche national coordonné en matière de formation en ergothérapie. Cela agit comme un appel à l'action pour les cliniciens, les éducateurs, les chercheurs, les administrateurstors, bailleurs de fonds, associations et organismes de réglementation pour promouvoir la recherche canadienne sur les efforts d'éducation qui sont alignés sur ces priorités.

titre: Correction: the role of dynamic Lowenstein occupational therapy and cognitive assessment scale for the elderly with Parkinson's disease.
titre_fr: Correction : le rôle de l'ergothérapie dynamique de Lowenstein et de l'échelle d'évaluation cognitive pour les personnes âgées atteintes de la maladie de Parkinson.
auteurs: Yaman Fatıma, Akkoyun Arıkan Fatma, Soylu Esra Aysu, Pekşen Elif, Akdeniz Leblebicier Merve, Özlü Aysun, Gökpınar Hasan Hüseyin, Yenen Barış, Kavuncu Vural

titre: Social Isolation in Japanese Adolescents and Young Adults with Hematologic Malignancies: A Focus on Peer Relationships and Occupational Therapy Implications.
titre_fr: Social Isolation in Japanese Adolescents and Young Adults with Hematologic Malignancies : A Focus on Peer Relationships and Occupational Therapy Implications.
auteurs: Sekihara Hinako, Kawama Kennosuke, Takeda Kazunori
revue: Journal of adolescent and young adult oncology
resume: Adolescents and young adults (AYAs) with hematologic malignancies in Japan face unique psychosocial challenges, particularly in maintaining peer relationships. Despite the critical role of peer interactions in this developmental stage, research remains limited. This study aimed to examine the characteristics of social isolation in this population and explore its implications for occupational therapy (OT). A mixed-methods design was employed, involving quantitative surveys (n = 55) and qualitative analysis using Steps for Coding and Theorization (SCAT) of semistructured interviews conducted with five participants. Psychological assessments included the Object Relations Scale, Parent-Child Trust Scale, Multidimensional Empathy Scale, Affiliation Motive Scale, the Japanese version of the PedsQL Cancer Module, and the Cancer Fatigue Scale. Cluster and factor analyses were conducted on quantitative data, and themes were extracted from the interview narratives. Two psychosocial clusters were identified in this study. Cluster 2 exhibited greater difficulties in peer relationships, mental fatigue, and appearance-related issues. Factor analysis revealed two domains: psychosocial burden and physical/cognitive impact. Qualitative data highlighted disruptions in friendships, ambivalence toward illness disclosure, and shifts in relational values. Mixed-methods integration revealed that participants with higher psychosocial and cognitive burdens reported more strained peer experiences. Peer relationship challenges among AYAs with cancer are shaped by reciprocal social dynamics and not solely by individual vulnerabilities. These findings underscore the need for OT in Japan to expand beyond inpatient physical rehabilitation to include developmentally appropriate community-based psychosocial interventions that support social reintegration.
resume_fr: Les adolescents et les jeunes adultes (AJA) atteints de tumeurs malignes hématologiques au Japon sont confrontés à des défis psychosociaux uniques, en particulier pour maintenir des relations avec leurs pairs. Malgré le rôle critique des interactions entre pairs à ce stade de développement, la recherche reste limitée. Cette étude visait à examiner les caractéristiques de l'isolement social dans cette population et à explorer ses implications pour l'ergothérapie (OT). Une conception à méthodes mixtes a été utilisée, INVlving quantitative surveys (n = 55) and qualitative analysis using Steps for Coding and Theorization (SCAT) of semistructured interviews conducted with five participants. Les évaluations psychologiques comprenaient l'échelle des relations objet, l'échelle de confiance parent-enfant, l'échelle d'empathie multidimensionnelle, l'échelle des motifs d'affiliation, la version japonaise du module PedsQL sur le cancer et l'échelle de fatigue liée au cancer. Des analyses de grappes et de facteurs ont été menées surdonnées quantitatives et les thèmes ont été extraits des récits d'entretien. Deux groupes psychosociaux ont été identifiés dans cette étude. Le groupe 2 présentait de plus grandes difficultés dans les relations avec les pairs, la fatigue mentale et les problèmes liés à l'apparence. L'analyse factorielle a révélé deux domaines : la charge psychosociale et l'impact physique/cognitif. Les données qualitatives ont mis en évidence des perturbations dans les amitiés, une ambivalence envers la divulgation de la maladie et des changements dans les relationsvaleurs onales. L'intégration de méthodes mixtes a révélé que les participants ayant des fardeaux psychosociaux et cognitifs plus élevés ont signalé des expériences plus tendues avec leurs pairs. Les défis des relations entre pairs parmi les AJA atteintes de cancer sont façonnés par une dynamique sociale réciproque et pas seulement par les vulnérabilités individuelles. Ces résultats soulignent la nécessité pour l'OT au Japon d'aller au-delà de la réadaptation physique des patients hospitalisés pour inclure une approche communautaire adaptée au développementinterventions psychosociales qui soutiennent la réinsertion sociale.

titre: Clinical Interpretation of the Occupational Therapy-Drive Home Maze Test in Fitness-to-Drive Assessment.
titre_fr: Interprétation clinique du test de labyrinthe à domicile de l'ergothérapie dans l'évaluation de l'aptitude à conduire.
auteurs: Johnston Belinda J, Wesson Jacqueline, O'Donnell Joan M, Mackenzie Lynette
resume: This study examined the diagnostic accuracy and clinical interpretation of the Occupational Therapy-Drive Home Maze Test (OT-DHMT) in an Australian fitness-to-drive assessment pathway. Participants were 136 drivers referred because of age-related or neurological fitness-to-drive concerns. Maze completion time and error count were recorded before an occupational therapy on-road assessment. On-road outcomes were dichotomized as pass, indicating eligibility for an unrestricted license, or fail, indicating not meeting criteria for an unrestricted license. Drivers who failed completed the OT-DHMT more slowly and made more errors than those who passed. Completion time showed fair discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] = .74), whereas error count showed poor discrimination (AUC = .68). An empirically derived threshold of >38.5 s provided more balanced sensitivity and specificity, whereas a locally used >60 s threshold was highly specific but had low sensitivity. Findings suggest that the OT-DHMT may support clinical reasoning but should not be used as a standalone predictor of on-road outcome.
resume_fr: Cette étude a examiné la précision du diagnostic et l'interprétation clinique du test OT-DHMT (Occupational Therapy-Drive Home Maze Test) dans une voie d'évaluation australienne de l'aptitude à conduire. Les participants étaient 136 conducteurs référés en raison de problèmes d'aptitude à conduire liés à l'âge ou neurologiques. Le temps d'achèvement du labyrinthe et le nombre d'erreurs ont été enregistrés avant une évaluation de l'ergothérapie sur route. Les résultats sur route ont été dichotomisés comme pass, indiquant eligibilité pour une licence sans restriction, ou échec, indiquant qu'il ne répond pas aux critères d'une licence sans restriction. Les conducteurs qui ont échoué ont terminé l'OT-DHMT plus lentement et ont fait plus d'erreurs que ceux qui ont réussi. Le temps d'achèvement a montré une discrimination équitable (aire sous la courbe [ASC] = 0,74), tandis que le nombre d'erreurs a montré une mauvaise discrimination (ASC = 0,68). Un seuil empiriquement dérivé de >38,5 s a fourni une sensibilité et une spécificité plus équilibrées, alors qu'unle seuil utilisé localement >60 s était très spécifique mais avait une faible sensibilité. Les résultats suggèrent que l'OT-DHMT peut soutenir le raisonnement clinique, mais ne doit pas être utilisé comme un prédicteur autonome des résultats sur route.

titre: Navigating Outdoor Activities During Heatwaves: Heat Resilience Insights from a Focus Group Study with Urban-Dwelling Older Adults in Sweden.
titre_fr: Navigating Outdoor Activities During Heatwaves : Heat Resilience Insights from a Focus Group Study with Urban-Dwelling Older Adults in Sweden.
auteurs: Kvarnström Börsbo Sofia, Johansson Johanna, Rosenberg Lena, Gustafsson Susanne
resume: Climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of heatwaves, posing significant health risks for older adults. In Sweden, older adults have historically not needed to consider heat during outdoor activities, but rising temperatures make such considerations increasingly important. Urban environments with limited vegetation and high heat exposure exacerbate these risks and are restricting their participation in society. To promote Age-friendly Cities and Communities, more knowledge is needed about how heatwaves influence urban-dwelling older adults' outdoor activities. Therefore, this study aimed to provide insight into how older adults reason about activities in urban outdoor environments during heatwaves. Data were generated from three focus groups involving a total of 19 older adults and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Four themes were created: individual adaptations to outdoor activities; the significance of social networks; society's responsibility to act on the challenges posed by heatwaves; and opportunities and barriers in the urban outdoor environment. Outdoor activities were influenced by factors at individual, group, and societal levels. These included personal habits, social networks, and environmental opportunities and barriers. Heat resilience requires age-friendly urban planning and tailored preparedness strategies, grounded in a holistic understanding of older adults' everyday lives. Supporting habit adaptation, identifying persons at risk of heat-related health impacts, and addressing high-risk environments are essential. Occupational therapists could assume an important preventive role that strengthens participation, autonomy, and resilience among older adults in a changing climate.
resume_fr: Le changement climatique augmente la fréquence et l'intensité des vagues de chaleur, ce qui pose des risques importants pour la santé des personnes âgées. En Suède, les personnes âgées n'ont historiquement pas eu besoin de tenir compte de la chaleur pendant les activités de plein air, mais la hausse des températures rend ces considérations de plus en plus importantes. Les environnements urbains avec une végétation limitée et une forte exposition à la chaleur exacerbent ces risques et limitent leur participation à la société. Promouvoir le vieillissementen ce qui concerne les villes et les communautés, plus de connaissances sont nécessaires sur la façon dont les vagues de chaleur influencent les activités de plein air des personnes âgées vivant en milieu urbain. Par conséquent, cette étude visait à donner un aperçu de la façon dont les personnes âgées raisonnent sur les activités en milieu urbain extérieur pendant les vagues de chaleur. Les données ont été générées à partir de trois groupes de discussion impliquant un total de 19 personnes âgées et analysées à l'aide d'une analyse thématique réflexive. Quatre thèmes ont été créés : adaptatio individuelns aux activités de plein air ; l'importance des réseaux sociaux ; la responsabilité de la société d'agir sur les défis posés par les vagues de chaleur ; et les opportunités et les obstacles dans l'environnement urbain extérieur. Les activités de plein air ont été influencées par des facteurs aux niveaux individuel, de groupe et sociétal. Il s'agissait notamment des habitudes personnelles, des réseaux sociaux et des opportunités et obstacles environnementaux. La résilience à la chaleur nécessite une planification urbaine adaptée aux personnes âgées et une planification sur mesuredes stratégies de préparation, fondées sur une compréhension holistique de la vie quotidienne des personnes âgées. Il est essentiel de soutenir l'adaptation aux habitudes, d'identifier les personnes à risque d'impacts sur la santé liés à la chaleur et de s'attaquer aux environnements à haut risque. Les ergothérapeutes pourraient assumer un rôle préventif important qui renforce la participation, l'autonomie et la résilience des personnes âgées dans un climat changeant.
type_etude: Étude qualitative (détection par mots-clés, à confirmer)

titre: Artificial intelligence and clinical work: Designing GenAI mentoring to support decision making in cognitive rehabilitation.
titre_fr: Intelligence artificielle et travail clinique : Concevoir le mentorat GenAI pour soutenir la prise de décision en réadaptation cognitive.
auteurs: Zlotnik Sharon, Levy Meira, Hadar Ethan, Hadar Irit
resume: BackgroundOccupational therapists working in cognitive rehabilitation may face high cognitive demands, and professional isolation. Although AI is used for information retrieval and decision support, its role in supporting reflective clinical reasoning remains insufficiently conceptualized. As scholarly attention shifts from automation toward augmentation of professional judgment, the next step is to understand how AI may support reflective reasoning in complex rehabilitation work.ObjectiveTo examine key challenges in cognitive rehabilitation and explore how these needs may inform a conceptual design for GenAI-mediated mentoring within clinical work.MethodsA qualitative study grounded in Design Thinking methodology was conducted with 30 female occupational therapists (age range 24-64 years, M = 41.26, SD = 10.35) with wide range of clinical experience (less than one year to more than 20 years) from diverse settings. They completed a demographic questionnaire and participated in two Design Thinking workshops (n = 14; n = 16). Seven participants subsequently engaged in follow-up interviews to refine design implications. All sessions were audio-recorded, transcribed, and analyzed thematically.ResultsThe thematic analysis yielded four themes: (A) The Therapist's role (B) Challenging therapist-client interactions, (C) Loneliness of the Therapist (D) Expectations for guidance or support aspects. These findings informed the conceptualization of a GenAI mentoring framework grounded in real-world clinical demands.ConclusionsThe findings support the design of generative AI systems as dialogic, context-sensitive tools intended to strengthen professional judgment, warranting further examination of their integration within real-world clinical workflows.

titre: Reconceptualizing the impostor phenomenon as an occupational experience: a scoping review and framework synthesis of qualitative evidence guided by the model of human occupation.
titre_fr: Reconceptualizing the impostor phenomenon as an occupational experience: a scoping review and framework synthesis of qualitative evidence guided by the model of human occupation.
auteurs: Pandey Latika, Yasmin Fathima, Gibin Rinshidha, Fathima Mehar, Jabeen Suman, Sharieff Asniyah, Ktk Junaid, Das Ranajit
resume: The Impostor phenomenon is characterized by persistent feelings of self-doubt and difficulty internalizing accomplishment despite being competent. Although its psychological consequences among healthcare professionals have been extensively studied, the influences of impostor phenomenon on occupational functioning remains underexplored. This scoping review synthesized qualitative evidence to examine the experiences of healthcare professionals with impostor phenomenon through the Model of Human Occupation (MOHO), providing an occupational science perspective on impostor phenomenon. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute approach and reported following the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews. The protocol was pre-registered on the Open Science Framework. PubMed/MEDLINE, ProQuest Central, and Web of Science databases were searched for English-language qualitative studies published between 2015 and 2025. Data were charted and a framework synthesis was conducted using the Framework Method, with MOHO as the a priori analytical framework. Eleven studies met the inclusion criteria. Within volition, participants demonstrated a competence-confidence disconnect, attributional challenges and gradual reconstruction of perceived competence, while values remained largely intact despite self-doubt. Habituation reflected disrupted professional identity formation, role transitions and compensatory occupational patterns including concealment, overpreparation and perfectionistic work routines. Performance capacity was characterized by altered subjective experiences of occupational performance, including emotional distress, cognitive burden and perceived inadequacy despite evidence of competence, with consequences for learning, participation and performance. Environmental influences included supportive mentorship, constructive feedback and psychologically safe workplaces, whereas hierarchical cultures, discrimination, workload pressures and organizational expectations could potentially reinforce IP. Interpreted through MOHO, the findings suggest that IP may be experienced across interconnected occupational processes, encompassing perceived competence, and professional role development, patterns of doing and influence of the environment. These interpretations require further cross-professional and longitudinal evidence. This review highlights the value of occupation-centered approaches for understanding and addressing IP and identifies opportunities for occupational therapy, healthcare education and organizational interventions that support healthy professional development. OSF, registration DOI: https://osf.io/xrbpd.

Data were charted and a framework synthesis was conducted using the Framework Method, with MOHO as the a priori analytical framework. Eleven studies met the inclusion criteria. Within volition, participants demonstrated a competence-confidence disconnect, attributional challenges and gradual reconstruction of perceived competence, while values remained largely intact despite self-doubt. Habituation reflected disrupted professional identity formation, role transitions and compensatory occupational patterns including concealment, overpreparation and perfectionistic work routines. Performance capacity was characterized by altered subjective experiences of occupational performance, including emotional distress, cognitive burden and perceived inadequacy despite evidence of competence, with consequences for learning, participation and performance. Environmental influences included supportive mentorship, constructive feedback and psychologically safe workplaces, whereas hierarchical cultures, discrimination, workload pressures and organizational expectations could potentially reinforce IP. Interpreted through MOHO, the findings suggest that IP may be experienced across interconnected occupational processes, encompassing perceived competence, and professional role development, patterns of doing and influence of the environment. These interpretations require further cross-professional and longitudinal evidence. This review highlights the value of occupation-centered approaches for understanding and addressing IP and identifies opportunities for occupational therapy, healthcare education and organizational interventions that support healthy professional development. titre: Primary Care Pediatrician's Experiences Caring for Children With Disabilities.
titre_fr: Primary Care Pediatrician's Experiences Caring for Children With Disabilities.
auteurs: Kirby Caroline A, Houtrow Amy, Burr William H, Foster Carolyn C, Somberg Chloe A, Kuo Dennis Z
resume: Pediatricians have raised concerns about the time and resources needed to support children with disabilities (CWD). This study examines the experiences of pediatricians who provide services for CWD, including relationships between pediatrician characteristics, practice characteristics, and barriers to providing care. This study analyzes American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) 2023 Periodic Survey data (33.0% response rate; data weighted to account for nonresponse bias). Respondents reported experiences and barriers to caring for CWD. In addition to descriptive and bivariate statistics, we used multivariable logistic regression to examine pediatrician and practice characteristics associated with prescribing practices and reported barriers. Survey respondents included 323 primary care pediatricians. While most pediatricians reported providing care for children with a range of disabilities (80.1% gross motor disability, 72.3% fine motor, 88.2% communication) more than half of pediatricians reported CWD made up a small portion (≤6%) of their patient panel. Most respondents reported prescribing physical therapy (78.1%), occupational therapy (78.4%), and speech therapy (88.6%) "often/very often," with few prescribing mobility aids (13.7%). Common barriers to caring for CWD included time limitations (74.9%), inadequate payment (63.3%), and lack of formal education/training (45.5%). Pediatricians with access to care coordinators were significantly less likely to identify inadequate payment and lack of formal education/training as barriers to care. Most pediatricians provide care to CWD, but much of the care for CWD may be congregating among a small number of pediatricians. Equitable care access for CWD may entail medical home initiatives that combine support, consultation, and payment strategies.

titre: Knowledge and awareness of occupational therapy and associated factors among healthcare professionals in Rwanda: a cross-sectional study.
titre_fr: Knowledge and awareness of occupational therapy and associated factors among healthcare professionals in Rwanda: a cross-sectional study.
auteurs: Ishimwe Didier, Nsengimana Elysee Aubaine, Biracyaza Emmanuel, Turikumana Pierre Damien, Niyonkuru Felix, Uwihoreye Potien, Cloete Lizahn G
resume: Occupational therapy (OT) is a client-centered health profession that supports health and wellbeing by enabling individuals to engage in daily activities. In many low- and middle-income countries, including Rwanda, limited awareness and knowledge of OT among healthcare professionals (HCPs) hinder collaboration and access to services. Therefore, this study aimed to determine HCPs' awareness and knowledge of OT and identify associated factors. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 201 HCPs from five teaching hospitals in Rwanda. Data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire and the Knowledge and Attitude Toward OT Practice Tool. Bivariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to determine factors associated with awareness and knowledge of OT. Associations were reported using adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs), and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Of the 201 HCPs, 102 (50.7%) were female, 74 (36.8%) were aged 31-40 years, and 40 (19.9%) were mental health nurses. Overall, 151 (75.1%) participants were aware of OT, while more than half (n = 104, 51.7%) exhibited poor knowledge. Physiotherapists [aOR = 6.3, 95% CI (1.6-25.5), p = 0.010], general nurses [aOR = 5.6, 95% CI (1.7-18.1), p = 0.004], and mental health nurses [aOR = 5.8, 95% CI (1.8-18.7), p = 0.003] reported higher likelihoods of awareness of OT than medical doctors. Awareness of OT was significantly associated with working in habilitation/rehabilitation services [aOR = 3.8, 95% CI (1.9-7.5), p < 0.001] and positive perceptions of OT. Similarly, good knowledge of OT was associated with profession, previous professional practice outside Rwanda, awareness of OT, and a positive perception of OT. Specifically, physiotherapists [aOR = 8.2, 95% CI (2.5-27.0), p = 0.001], ophthalmic clinical officers [aOR = 8.6, 95% CI (1.5-49.4), p = 0.016], general nurses [aOR = 3.2, 95% CI (1.2-8.6), p = 0.024], and mental health nurses [aOR = 2.7, 95% CI (1.1-7.3), p = 0.045] had higher odds of good knowledge of OT than medical doctors. Although awareness of OT was relatively high among HCPs, more than half demonstrated poor knowledge of the profession. Greater awareness and knowledge were associated with professional background, involvement in habilitation or rehabilitation services, previous professional practice outside Rwanda, direct experience working with occupational therapists, and positive perceptions of OT. Considering these results, our study highlights the need for strengthening interprofessional education and continuing professional development to improve understanding and integration of OT within the Rwandan healthcare system.

titre: Occupational Therapy in LGBTQ + Affirming Primary Care: Referral, Intervention, and Outcomes.
titre_fr: Occupational Therapy in LGBTQ + Affirming Primary Care: Referral, Intervention, and Outcomes.
auteurs: LeRoy Michelle, Farrell Bridget, Sayers Colton
revue: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
resume: ImportanceLGBTQ + clients experience healthcare barriers that may shape daily routines, health management, and participation. Little is known about occupational therapy referral pathways and outcomes in LGBTQ + affirming primary care.ObjectiveTo describe referral characteristics, occupational performance concerns, intervention focus, and client-reported outcomes among LGBTQ + clients referred to occupational therapy.DesignRetrospective pilot program evaluation using clinical documentation and outcome data from July 2025 through March 2026, with a June 2026 analysis cutoff.SettingTwo Midwestern primary care settings where occupational therapy screening and referral processes were developed; ongoing intervention occurred through outpatient occupational therapy.ParticipantsThirty-nine referred clients were included in descriptive analyses; 38 received intervention beyond evaluation; 21 had complete baseline and follow-up Canadian Occupational Performance Measure data.InterventionIndividualized outpatient occupational therapy focused on client-identified concerns.Outcomes and MeasuresReferral and treatment characteristics, occupational performance concerns, coded occupational focus, and Canadian Occupational Performance Measure Performance and Satisfaction ratings.ResultsCommon concerns included instrumental activities of daily living (94.9%), health management/self-management (92.3%), activities of daily living (82.1%), and work or school participation (82.1%). The most common primary intervention focus was health management and chronic condition self-management (65.8%). Among participants with outcome data, COPM Performance scores improved by 2.29 points and Satisfaction scores improved by 2.58 points.Conclusions and RelevanceOccupational therapy may support LGBTQ + clients referred from primary care by addressing needs related to health management, routines, self-care, and participation through individualized outpatient intervention. Prospective multisite research is needed.

titre: Development and Validation of a ChatGPT-Based Assessment for Conversation-Related Clinical Skills in Occupational Therapy OSCEs.
titre_fr: Development and Validation of a ChatGPT-Based Assessment for Conversation-Related Clinical Skills in Occupational Therapy OSCEs.
auteurs: Wang Yi-Ching, Chen An-Ju, How Mon-Jane, Yang Chih-Wei, Lee Ya-Chen, Huang Sheau-Ling, Hsieh Ching-Lin
revue: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
resume: ImportanceConversation-related clinical skills are central to Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) in occupational therapy. However, real-time examiner scoring is resource-intensive and may overlook students' specific skills. Transcript-based scoring with Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT) may address these limitations.ObjectiveTo develop a ChatGPT-based assessment for chief-complaint interview OSCEs (G-ACE) and examine criterion validity against expert-consensus ratings, test-retest reliability, and inter-rater reliability.DesignSecondary analysis of de-identified transcripts from 8-min chief-complaint interviews with a simulated patient with stroke during an OSCE.SettingsA university in northern Taiwan.ParticipantsFifty-eight de-identified transcripts from undergraduate occupational therapy students.ResultsCriterion validity was acceptable for "Primary Symptoms and Related Feelings" and "Impact on Daily Life" items (weighted kappa ≥ 0.60), but lower for "Rehabilitation Expectations" and "Communication Skills" items (0.18-0.59). For domain and total scores, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) were 0.17 to 0.78 and percentages of mean absolute errors (MAE%s) were 4.6% to 20.7%. Test-retest reliability was acceptable at the item level (weighted kappa = 0.68-1.00), and acceptable to good at the domain and total score levels (ICC = 0.65-0.85; MAE% = 2.3%-9.1%). Inter-rater reliability was acceptable for most domain and total scores (ICCs = 0.52-0.78; MAE%s = 1.3%-12.0%), except for the "Rehabilitation Expectations" domain (ICCs = 0.17-0.30; MAE%s = 1.3%-7.3%).Conclusion and RelevanceThe G-ACE demonstrated generally acceptable test-retest reliability and small absolute differences from expert ratings for domain and total scores. Because some items showed lower consistency with expert ratings, formative feedback should be interpreted cautiously based on transcript evidence.

titre: Nonpharmacological and rehabilitative interventions for adults with myotonic dystrophy type 1: a systematic review.
titre_fr: Nonpharmacological and rehabilitative interventions for adults with myotonic dystrophy type 1: a systematic review.
auteurs: Lazogkas Zisis, Tsiakiri Anna, Papadimas George, Vlotinou Pinelopi
revue: International journal of rehabilitation research. Internationale Zeitschrift fur Rehabilitationsforschung. Revue internationale de recherches de readaptation
resume: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) has historically been managed cautiously with respect to physical exercise, out of concern that loading might accelerate dystrophic muscle breakdown. This systematic review synthesizes the evidence on nonpharmacological and rehabilitative interventions in adults with genetically confirmed or clinically well-defined DM1. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to 17 July 2026, without language or date restrictions; controlled and uncontrolled interventional studies were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (Cochrane risk of bias 2 for randomized trials; ROBINS-I for nonrandomized studies). Given heterogeneity in modality, dosing, and outcomes, narrative synthesis was used without meta-analysis. Sixteen publications reporting 13 independent studies were included across five modality families: resistance/strength training (eight publications from five studies), aerobic/cycling (three studies), hand-based occupational therapy (two), electrical stimulation (two), and behavioral rehabilitation (one). Resistance training dominates the evidence, reflecting a shift away from early concerns that loaded exercise harms dystrophic muscle. Aerobic training improved cardiorespiratory fitness in single-arm studies, but the only randomized trial found no between-group differences in walking or mobility; single-sex resistance-training cohorts, absent sex-disaggregated reporting, and inconsistent outcome measures recurred across studies. Nonpharmacological rehabilitation in DM1 appears feasible and potentially efficacious, with supervised progressive resistance training currently having the most substantial evidence base. Optimal modalities, timing, and patient-selection criteria remain unclear, and larger trials using standardized outcome sets are needed before other modalities can be recommended with confidence in clinical practice.

titre: Measurement properties of instruments used to measure children's and adolescents' engagement during rehabilitation sessions: a systematic review protocol.
titre_fr: Measurement properties of instruments used to measure children's and adolescents' engagement during rehabilitation sessions: a systematic review protocol.
auteurs: Srinivasan Sudha, Omonode Alaina, VanDerWoude Molly, Hood Jennifer, Guillot Ashley, Metcalf Emily, Kenyon Lisa K
resume: This systematic review will critically appraise and summarize the measurement properties of instruments used to measure children's and adolescents' engagement during rehabilitation sessions in both clinical and research contexts. A secondary objective will be to assess the suitability of these instruments for clinical and research use. Engagement in the therapeutic process is a critical mediator of therapeutic change during rehabilitation interventions. Yet there is little information on valid and reliable measures to holistically assess engagement during rehabilitation. The populations of interest will be children and adolescents ≤21 years, with any diagnosis, in any setting, participating in occupational therapy, physical therapy, or speech-language therapy sessions. This review will follow the Guideline for Systematic Reviews of Outcome Measurement Instruments. A search strategy will be developed for the following databases: PubMed, CINAHL Complete, Web of Science Core Collection, PsycINFO, and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Global. Methodological quality of included studies will be assessed through the COSMIN Risk of Bias tool and the COSMIN checklist. The measurement properties of the identified instruments will be graded using the modified GRADE approach and the COSMIN Criteria for Good Measurement Properties. Measurement properties (validity, reliability, and responsiveness), clinical feasibility (ease of administration, training needed, completion time, ease of score calculation, required equipment, and instrument cost), and interpretability (threshold values, floor and ceiling effects, percentage of missing items/scores, distribution of scores in the population, change scores for subgroups of children and adolescents, minimal important change or difference) for each instrument will be described. PROSPERO CRD420261277455.

titre: Parenting in the Shadow of Enduring Health Conditions: Experiences of Parenting, Participation and Support.
titre_fr: Parenting in the Shadow of Enduring Health Conditions: Experiences of Parenting, Participation and Support.
auteurs: Sheehan Lillian Kathy, Quirke Dearbhla Anne, Codd Yvonne, McGrath Margaret
resume: Parenting is a central occupation that may be disrupted by enduring health conditions, yet how parents experience the interaction between health, parenting demands and support systems remains underexplored. This study explored parents' experiences living with an enduring health condition, focusing on participation, support needs and service access. Qualitative data were drawn from open-ended questions within a national cross-sectional e-survey of parents with enduring health conditions in Ireland. Responses from 218 participants were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Four themes were identified: impact on parenting roles, centrality of informal support networks, engagement with formal services and future service design. Parenting participation was influenced by fluctuating symptoms, environmental barriers and social expectations. Informal supports enabled participation but were often inconsistent, while formal services were frequently fragmented and difficult to access. Parenting is shaped by interacting health, environmental and systemic factors, highlighting the need for strengths-based, family-centred occupational therapy approaches.

titre: Mapping the Interplay Between Functional Autonomy, Executive Functions, Self-Management, and Social-Emotional Strengths in Adolescents.
titre_fr: Mapping the Interplay Between Functional Autonomy, Executive Functions, Self-Management, and Social-Emotional Strengths in Adolescents.
auteurs: Fogel Yael, Landes Efrat, Porath Merav, Lamash Liron
resume: Functional autonomy reflects adolescents' participation across daily occupations. This cross-sectional study examined associations between functional autonomy, executive functions, self-management, and social-emotional strengths in 88 typically developing adolescents within a strength-based, multidimensional framework. Participants completed the Participation Activities Rating for Teenagers (Take PART) and standardized self-report measures (Teenage Executive Functioning Inventory, Self-Control and Self-Management Scale, and Social Emotional Health Survey-Secondary). Regression analyses identified inhibition and engaged living as primary factors associated with overall autonomy (R2 = .25), with domain-specific contributions from working memory and emotional competence. Cluster analysis revealed two functional profiles reflecting higher (Cluster 1) and lower (Cluster 2) cognitive-regulatory-emotional profiles. Inhibition and engaged living showed the strongest associations with overall autonomy. Functional autonomy was associated with executive functions, self-management, and social-emotional strengths. These findings support a multidimensional understanding of functional autonomy during adolescence and may inform individualized occupational therapy assessment and intervention planning.

titre: Development of a Single-Camera Markerless Motion Capture System for Assessing Upper Limb Function Post-Stroke (FULMA).
titre_fr: Development of a Single-Camera Markerless Motion Capture System for Assessing Upper Limb Function Post-Stroke (FULMA).
auteurs: Fisher Jarrad, Bunn Christopher, Li Wanqing, Hurden Alexandra, Barnhart Molly, Black Ross, Anderson Craig, Chen Xiaoying
resume: Upper limb impairment is common after stroke. Standardised measures such as the Action Research Arm Test and Fugl Meyer Assessment are widely used but may show inter-rater variability and limited sensitivity to subtle motor changes. To develop and evaluate the Functional Upper Limb Movement Assessment (FULMA) system, a single-camera markerless motion capture tool for objective movement analysis of upper limb function with clinician facing outputs after stroke. A prospective observational study included 39 stroke participants and 19 healthy controls. Participants completed 9 functional tasks recorded with a LiDAR depth camera. Kinematic features were analysed using machine learning models to predict an ordinal task performance score anchored to Action Research Arm Test scoring descriptors. Predictions were compared with independent occupational therapist ratings, and automated kinematic commentary was generated. The multilayer perceptron achieved a mean accuracy of 83.3%, with task level accuracies of 75.0% to 91.7% and weighted kappa values of 0.67 to 0.88. The support vector machine achieved a mean accuracy of 78.5%, with task level accuracies of 72.2% to 89.0% and weighted kappa values of 0.59 to 0.83. Performance varied across tasks, with the strongest results for cup to mouth and hair brushing. Commentary highlighted prolonged movement time, reduced smoothness and increased trunk displacement. This developmental study showed preliminary agreement between automated ordinal score predictions and therapist ratings within a controlled dataset. External validation and evaluation of measurement properties are required before clinical use. Kinematic commentary should be considered exploratory rather than a validated clinical interpretation.

A prospective observational study included 39 stroke participants and 19 healthy controls. Participants completed 9 functional tasks recorded with a LiDAR depth camera. Kinematic features were analysed using machine learning models to predict an ordinal task performance score anchored to Action Research Arm Test scoring descriptors. Predictions were compared with independent occupational therapist ratings, and automated kinematic commentary was generated. The multilayer perceptron achieved a mean accuracy of 83.3%, with task level accuracies of 75.0% to 91.7% and weighted kappa values of 0.67 to 0.88. The support vector machine achieved a mean accuracy of 78.5%, with task level accuracies of 72.2% to 89.0% and weighted kappa values of 0.59 to 0.83. Performance varied across tasks, with the strongest results for cup to mouth and hair brushing. Commentary highlighted prolonged movement time, reduced smoothness and increased trunk displacement. This developmental study showed preliminary agreement between automated ordinal score predictions and therapist ratings within a controlled dataset. External validation and evaluation of measurement properties are required before clinical use. Kinematic commentary should be considered exploratory rather than a validated clinical interpretation.

titre: Functional status of children with myelomeningocele and the burden of their informal caregivers: a cross-sectional study.
titre_fr: Functional status of children with myelomeningocele and the burden of their informal caregivers: a cross-sectional study.
auteurs: das Neves Fernanda Petrini Rodrigues, Salmen Isabel Cristina Drago Marquezini, Dos Santos JanaÃna Senhorini, Mazzo Alessandra
resume: To evaluate the functional performance of children with myelomeningocele undergoing rehabilitation and its association with the perceived burden of their informal caregivers. A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted at a rehabilitation center with eight child-caregiver dyads representing the entire population of children with myelomeningocele receiving care at the institution. Child functionality was assessed using the Pediatric Evaluation of Disability Inventory - Computer Adaptive Test, and caregiver burden was measured using the Informal Caregiver Burden Assessment Questionnaire. Sociodemographic and clinical data were also collected. Descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation analyses were performed between the domains of both instruments. Caregivers were all mothers, most with low household income and full-time caregiving responsibilities. Most children exhibited functional performance below age expectations in the domains of Mobility, Daily Activities, and Social and Cognitive Skills. Only three participants achieved normative percentiles above 50 in more than one domain. The lowest continuous scores were observed in Responsibility, followed by Daily Activities and Mobility. Financial Burden and Family Support showed the highest mean caregiver burden scores. Strong negative correlations were identified between functional performance and subjective burden domains, indicating that lower functionality was associated with greater emotional burden, stronger reactions to caregiving demands, and lower perceptions of efficacy and control. Functional deficits in children with myelomeningocele are associated with increased emotional and practical burden among informal caregivers. These findings highlight the importance of rehabilitation strategies aimed at improving children's functional independence while also incorporating caregiver support as an essential component of care.

titre: Gait Adaptability Rehabilitation: Perspectives From Individuals With Motor Incomplete Spinal Cord Injury.
titre_fr: Gait Adaptability Rehabilitation: Perspectives From Individuals With Motor Incomplete Spinal Cord Injury.
auteurs: Cesca Nicole, Condo Marissa, Gabison Sharon, Musselman Kristin E
revue: Journal of neurologic physical therapy : JNPT
resume: Following motor incomplete spinal cord injury (SCI), gait adaptability, which is the ability to modify one's gait pattern in response to task/environmental demands, is likely impaired. Despite rehabilitation, many individuals with motor incomplete SCI face ongoing walking challenges and view safe walking as an unmet goal. This study explored the perceived importance and appropriateness of addressing gait adaptability during SCI rehabilitation from the perspectives of community-dwelling adults with subacute, motor incomplete SCI. A qualitative study using semi-structured interviews was conducted. The interview guide was structured around the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation-Behaviour (COM-B) model, which examines the physical, social, and psychological factors influencing behavior. Questions queried participants' perspectives on current rehabilitation practices aimed at improving gait adaptability. Interviews were conducted 3 to 6 months post-inpatient discharge, audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using interpretive description. Fourteen individuals with motor incomplete SCI who completed walking training in inpatient rehabilitation were interviewed (9 males/men, 5 females/women). Three themes highlighting participant perceptions were identified: (1) gait adaptability is important for community reintegration, (2) perceived gait adaptability training and assessment practices: training is variable, with progress commonly measured by distance, and (3) real-world walking is complex: Training should reflect where people walk. Each theme included 2 subthemes, with participants highlighting the importance of real-world walking exposure, outdoor practice, and the role of personal goals in driving motivation. This study highlights the perceived importance of gait adaptability training for individuals with motor incomplete SCI, emphasizing its role in fostering confidence and independence post-inpatient discharge.

titre: Effects of adjunctive craniosacral therapy to conventional physiotherapy on postural responses and autonomic function in individuals with multiple sclerosis: a randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Effects of adjunctive craniosacral therapy to conventional physiotherapy on postural responses and autonomic function in individuals with multiple sclerosis: a randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Aslan Hilal, Vural Gönül, Aksoy Songül, Tekin Rabia Tuğba
resume: Craniosacral Therapy (CST) has emerged as a complementary approach in neurological rehabilitation, but its effects in multiple sclerosis (MS) remain unclear. To investigate the effects of adding CST to conventional physiotherapy on postural control and autonomic function in patients with MS. Thirty patients with relapsing-remitting MS were randomly assigned to a CST group (n = 15) or control group (n = 15) in this single-blind randomized controlled trial. Both groups received conventional physiotherapy twice weekly for 8 weeks; the CST group additionally received weekly CST. Assessments were conducted at baseline, post-treatment, and 2-month follow-up using Computerized Dynamic Posturography (CDP) and Heart Rate Variability (HRV). Significant group × time interactions were found for Adaptation Test (toes-down) and Motor Control Test (back-small) latency measures, with greater reductions in response latency over time in the CST group (ADT toes-down: p = .034, η2 = 0.129; MCT back-small: p = .006, η2 = 0.166). However, no significant between-group differences were observed at any assessment point. For HRV, although the CST group showed within-group improvements after treatment, no significant group × time interactions were detected (all p > .05). CST added to conventional physiotherapy may influence specific postural response parameters in patients with MS. However, no between-group superiority was demonstrated, and no significant treatment effect on autonomic function was observed. Further studies with larger samples are needed to confirm these findings.

titre: Volar Versus Dorsal Approach for Scaphoid Nonunion: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Task-Specific Wrist Kinematics.
titre_fr: Volar Versus Dorsal Approach for Scaphoid Nonunion: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Task-Specific Wrist Kinematics.
auteurs: Aydın Ahmet Serhat, Demirel Mehmet, Altaş Okyar, Durmaz Hayati, Ayık Ömer, Balcı Halil İbrahim, Çamlıbel Burcu Tunç, Büyüksaraç Bora
resume: The optimal surgical approach for scaphoid nonunion remains debated. This study compared task-specific wrist kinematics following volar versus dorsal reconstruction using wearable inertial sensors, with operated-healthy side difference as the primary endpoint. In this single-center prospective randomized controlled trial, 21 patients with waist-type scaphoid nonunion eligible for either approach were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to volar or dorsal reconstruction; 18 patients (9 per group) completed 12-month follow-up and were included in the analysis. Surgical fixation, distal radius bone grafting, and rehabilitation were standardized. The primary outcome was the operated-healthy side difference in peak wrist extension during a simulated phone-handling task at 12 months, measured using wearable inertial measurement units. Secondary outcomes included Patient-Rated Wrist Evaluation (PRWE), scapholunate angle correction, and goniometric wrist motion. All fractures achieved union at a mean follow-up of 12 months. The operated-healthy side difference in peak wrist extension was -11.5° in the volar group and -1.0° in the dorsal group (between-group difference, -10.5°; 95% CI, -22.5° to 1.5°; P = .083), indicating a numerically smaller extension asymmetry in the dorsal group. Patient-Rated Wrist Evaluation, radiographic correction, and standard goniometric extension were comparable between groups. Secondary kinematic analyses suggested task-specific differences in other planes of motion. Both approaches yielded similar union and patient-reported outcomes. The dorsal group demonstrated a numerically smaller extension asymmetry during a functional task, although this between-group difference did not reach statistical significance. Wearable sensor-based assessment may reveal clinically meaningful functional asymmetries not captured by traditional outcome measures. Larger adequately powered studies are needed to determine whether these exploratory differences are reproducible and clinically meaningful. Therapeutic Level I.

titre: Roadmap for cognitive neurorehabilitation: challenges and opportunities.
titre_fr: Roadmap for cognitive neurorehabilitation: challenges and opportunities.
auteurs: Sokolov Arseny A, Allain Philippe, d'Honincthun Peggy, Pignat Jean-Michel, Serino Andrea, Slama Hichem, Takani Kenza, Vallat-Azouvi Claire, Willems Sylvie
resume: Cognitive deficits affect 40-50% of patients after acquired brain injury, with a profound impact on participation, work capacity and quality of life. Cognitive neurorehabilitation is a relevant and promising approach to promote cognitive recovery, but the evidence remains limited. This review discusses the clinical state-of-the-art, open questions in clinical research, and outlines a roadmap for future development of this rapidly evolving domain. While optimal contemporary cognitive neurorehabilitation is multimodal and interprofessional, the currently available evidence is diluted by heterogeneous treatment content and patient characteristics, as well as by inadequate methodology and reporting. Several questions remain open: the optimal dose and frequency of therapy, the preferable sequence of treatments, and the factors that moderate treatment effects. We highlight the pressing need for rigorously designed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with active control conditions, everyday-relevant outcome measures, time by group interaction analyses and long-term follow-up. Future development of cognitive neurorehabilitation depends on RCTs and single-case experiments using cutting-edge methodology. We propose a roadmap with four tiers: mechanisms and efficacy, assessment of moderating factors, clinical validity as well as consideration of socio-economic impact and implementation from the outset. International collaboration in designing, developing and validating the approaches is warranted to ensure standardization and broad uptake. These efforts will promote the quality and accessibility of cognitive neurorehabilitation.

titre: Coping strategies and health literacy among Jordanian patients with myocardial infarction.
titre_fr: Coping strategies and health literacy among Jordanian patients with myocardial infarction.
auteurs: Alrababah Deyaaldeen M, Martin Penelope, Mayers Pat M
resume: Patients with myocardial infarction require adaptive coping skills and adequate health literacy levels to improve their health and reduce morbidity, cost of care and mortality. This study examined the association between commonly used coping strategies and health literacy levels among Jordanian patients with myocardial infarction. A descriptive cross-sectional survey design was used. Systematic random sampling was used to recruit 140 patients with myocardial infarction from four hospitals in Jordan. Respondents completed two scales: the Arabic versions of the Brief COPE (AR-BC) and the 16 items European Health Literacy Survey Questionnaire (HLS-EU-Q16). The research process followed ethical principles and measures. Respondents had low scores of engaging in coping activities. Emotion-focused coping and religious strategies were most used. Less than half (39.3%, n = 55) had adequate health literacy. The highest score was for the dimension Applying Information and the lowest was for Information Processing. Positive associations were found between health literacy levels and positive coping strategies (planning, acceptance, active coping, emotional support and positive reframing) and negative associations between negative coping strategies (venting) and health literacy levels. Patients with myocardial infarction had low health literacy and made more use of emotion-focused strategies rather than problem-focused coping strategies. Higher health literacy levels may be associated with the use of more adaptive coping strategies. Health literacy assessment and patients' use of adaptive coping strategies should be fundamental to the nursing care of patients with myocardial infarction.Contribution: Jordanian patients post-myocardial infarction have limited health literacy and use mainly emotion-focused coping strategies. To promote patients' adaptive, problem-focused coping, we recommend that health literacy training is included in nursing education curricula and HL screening is included in cardiac rehabilitation programmes.

titre: Service Providers' Perspectives on Family-Centred Practice Frameworks in Paediatric Disability Services: A Scoping Review.
titre_fr: Service Providers' Perspectives on Family-Centred Practice Frameworks in Paediatric Disability Services: A Scoping Review.
auteurs: Liu Yanlin, Shiel Agnes, Killeen Hazel
resume: Family-centred practice (FCP) is a core principle of paediatric disability and rehabilitation services. Although many frameworks, models, programmes and tools have been developed to support FCP, translating these approaches into routine practice remains complex. Service providers play a key role in implementation, yet evidence on how they perceive, use and experience FCP frameworks across paediatric disability-related services remains fragmented. This scoping review mapped the literature on service providers' perspectives of FCP frameworks for children with disabilities and their families. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with established guidance and reported following the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews checklist. Searches were conducted in CINAHL Complete, APA PsycINFO, SocINDEX with Full Text, Academic Search Complete, Scopus and MEDLINE via PubMed. Full-text empirical journal articles were included if they reported service providers' perspectives on FCP frameworks in paediatric disability-related contexts. Data were charted and synthesised descriptively and narratively. Twenty-one studies were included. The studies examined conceptual and guiding frameworks, service delivery models, coaching and relational approaches, intervention and training models and assessment and collaborative planning tools. Six themes were identified: professional role transformation, relational and communication competencies, collaborative goal setting, barriers to implementation, training and professional support needs and the influence of context and service delivery. Service providers generally valued FCP frameworks for supporting collaboration and meaningful goal setting. Implementation was constrained by time pressure, workload, tensions with expert-led practice, limited training, resource demands and contextual fit. FCP frameworks can support service providers to operationalise family-centred principles, but in isolation, they are not sufficient to ensure practice change. Implementation requires professional role development, relational competencies, training, supervision, organisational support and service conditions that enable sustained collaboration with families.

titre: [The novelties of adult advanced life support and post-resuscitation therapy according to the 2025 European Resuscitation Council guidelines].
titre_fr: [The novelties of adult advanced life support and post-resuscitation therapy according to the 2025 European Resuscitation Council guidelines].
auteurs: Válint Andrea, Bárszki László, Bukor Barbara, Pávó Mihály, Zima Endre, Kovács Enikő
resume: The European Resuscitation Council published its updated Guidelines for Resuscitation in 2025. The revised guidelines highlight advanced life support and post-resuscitation care, as well as post-resuscitation rehabilitation, as the third and fourth links in the updated Chain of Survival. In this review, we summarize the key updates and principal messages of the new guideline on advanced life support and post-resuscitation care. Although the Advanced Life Support guidelines do not represent a paradigm shift, they place a stronger emphasis on delivering high-quality, timely resuscitation. High-quality chest compressions remain the cornerstone of resuscitation, complemented by early, safe, and correctly performed defibrillation with minimal interruptions, appropriate drug administration, and prompt identification and treatment of the underlying cause of cardiac arrest. The updated guidelines also address emerging topics, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation-induced consciousness, the specific considerations for cardiac arrest occurring in closely monitored patients, and the introduction of physiology-guided resuscitation. Similarly, the post-resuscitation care guidelines introduce no major changes compared with previous recommendations. Instead, they reinforce the importance of delivering high-quality post-resuscitation care, with particular emphasis on neuroprotection. The key components of the stabilization, diagnostic, and optimization phases include an ABCDE approach to patient assessment, optimization of oxygenation, ventilation, and hemodynamic status, seizure management, prevention of fever during the first 72 hours after return of spontaneous circulation, and identification and treatment of the underlying cause of cardiac arrest. The indications for immediate coronary angiography following successful cardiopulmonary resuscitation have been further refined, and the guidelines also clarify the diagnostic approach when a non-cardiac cause of cardiac arrest is suspected. Greater emphasis is placed on multimodal neuroprognosis and post-resuscitation rehabilitation. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(45): 1810-1824.

titre: Configurations Associated with High Self-Regulatory Fatigue in Patients with Stroke: A Fuzzy-Set Qualitative Comparative Analysis.
titre_fr: Configurations Associated with High Self-Regulatory Fatigue in Patients with Stroke: A Fuzzy-Set Qualitative Comparative Analysis.
auteurs: Tian Xinran, Lin Yinglu, Wu Siyuan, Xu Changxin, Fu Mengxue, Lu Panting, Zhang Huafang
resume: Self-regulatory fatigue is common among patients with stroke and may adversely affect rehabilitation. Previous studies have mainly examined individual factors associated with self-regulatory fatigue, but how multiple stressor-related and resource-related conditions combine into distinct configurations of high self-regulatory fatigue remains unclear. To identify configurations associated with high self-regulatory fatigue among patients with stroke using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), guided by Conservation of Resources theory. A total of 288 patients with stroke were recruited from the neurology wards of a tertiary hospital in Zhejiang Province, China. Data were collected using validated instruments assessing self-regulatory fatigue, depressive symptoms, sense of coherence, perceived social support, stroke health literacy, activities of daily living, and neurological impairment. Necessity and sufficiency analyses were conducted using fsQCA to identify conditions and configurations associated with high self-regulatory fatigue. No single condition was necessary for high self-regulatory fatigue. Five configurations were identified, with an overall solution consistency of 0.937 and an overall solution coverage of 0.640. The configurations were categorised into three types: psychological-emotional resource depletion type, functional-social resource depletion type, and multi-resource synergistic depletion type. Robustness analyses supported the stability of the configurational findings. High self-regulatory fatigue among patients with stroke is associated with distinct configurations of psychological, functional, social, and health-management resource deficits rather than any single condition. These findings support multidimensional assessment and coordinated multidisciplinary care tailored to patients' resource profiles.

titre: Effects of virtual reality and exergame interventions on cognitive function in Chinese older adults with cognitive impairment: A three-level meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effects of virtual reality and exergame interventions on cognitive function in Chinese older adults with cognitive impairment: A three-level meta-analysis.
auteurs: Shen Yan, Zhong Yingying, Lin Anqi
resume: Technology-based cognitive interventions, such as virtual reality (VR) and exergames, have emerged as promising tools for cognitive rehabilitation. This meta-analysis evaluated their effects on cognitive outcomes among Chinese older adults with cognitive impairment and examined potential moderators. A systematic search of English- and Chinese-language databases identified eligible studies on VR and exergame interventions in Chinese older adults with cognitive impairment. To address data dependency, effect sizes were synthesized using a three-level random-effects meta-analysis estimated by restricted maximum likelihood estimation, with study-level cluster-robust variance estimation incorporating CR2 small-sample correction and Satterthwaite approximation. Sensitivity analyses, subgroup analyses, publication bias analyses, and GRADE assessment were also conducted. Thirty-eight studies involving 2873 participants and 202 effect sizes were included, of which 34 were randomized controlled trials (RCTs). In the primary RCT-only analysis, the pooled effect was significant (Hedges' g = 0.817, 95% CI [0.602, 1.032], p < 0.001). The pooled effect across all studies remained significant (Hedges' g = 0.738, 95% CI [0.530, 0.946], p < 0.001). Significant positive effects were observed across all four cognitive domains, but between-group differences in subgroup analyses were not statistically significant. Heterogeneity was substantial, and the prediction interval crossed zero. Leave-one-out analyses supported the stability of the findings. Modified Egger's regression suggested possible small-study effects, although publication bias could not be determined conclusively. The certainty of evidence was rated as low. VR and exergame interventions were associated with a significant positive average effect on cognitive outcomes among Chinese older adults with cognitive impairment. However, substantial heterogeneity, a prediction interval crossing zero, possible small-study effects, and low certainty of evidence limit firm conclusions regarding the consistency and clinical importance of this effect. More rigorously designed randomized trials with longer follow-up are needed.

titre: A 2025 survey of UK-practising veterinary surgeons on veterinary physiotherapy recommendations, perceptions, and follow-up during treatment of canine cranial cruciate ligament disease.
titre_fr: A 2025 survey of UK-practising veterinary surgeons on veterinary physiotherapy recommendations, perceptions, and follow-up during treatment of canine cranial cruciate ligament disease.
auteurs: de Jasay Theodora, Blake Roberta
resume: This cross-sectional online survey investigated UK-practising small-animal and mixed-practice veterinary surgeons' (VS) recommendations, behaviours, and perceptions regarding veterinary physiotherapy (VPT) during canine cruciate ligament disease (CCLD) management. Secondary aims explored perceptions of the evidence base and outcome assessment methods both in-practice and in research. A pilot questionnaire followed by the final questionnaire was distributed using non-probability sampling through veterinary practices, professional organisations, the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons' mailing list and personal contacts. Data were collected over a 10-week period from December 2024 to February 2025; 236 qualified VS at varying clinical levels, including general practitioners and specialists, completed the survey. Data were analysed descriptively and using Pearson's Chi-squared or Fisher's exact tests. Surgical management remained the preferred treatment approach. Most respondents (62.3%) always recommended formal physiotherapy post-CCLD-surgery, a higher proportion than reported in a previous international survey with different eligibility criteria. Respondents generally reported strongly positive perceptions of the potential effects of VPT, but only moderately positive perceptions of the supporting evidence-base, potentially reflecting variable evidence strength in CCLD-specific rehabilitation research. Significant associations with small to small-moderate effect sizes existed between always recommending VPT and rehabilitation-specific CPD, age range, years in-practice, and workplace business-structure. Most respondents used compliance-increasing and compliance-monitoring measures; however, follow-up assessments commonly declined beyond 8 weeks post-surgery. Respondents generally perceived biomechanical assessments as less useful in clinical practice than veterinary- or owner-reported measures. While VPT appeared increasingly integrated into respondents' CCLD management approaches, findings suggested clinician-specific contextual factors may influence rehabilitation integration and reinforced the need for clinically feasible, standardised post-operative rehabilitation and monitoring guidelines relevant to CCLD.

titre: Long COVID: A Modified Delphi Consensus on Definition, Burden, Diagnosis and Management in Southeast Asia.
titre_fr: Long COVID: A Modified Delphi Consensus on Definition, Burden, Diagnosis and Management in Southeast Asia.
auteurs: Burhan Erlina, Chew Huck Chin, Isbaniah Fathiyah, Jogulu Sathya Rao, Leong Chee Loon, Leong Hoe Nam, Manosuthi Weerawat, Nguyen Viet Nhung, Roman Arthur Dessi, Tan-Reyes Michelle Angela, Le Thuong Vu, Wongsurakiat Phunsup, Cheong Ervin, Taysi Bulent Nuri, Thakkar Karan
resume: Long COVID is a heterogeneous post-infectious condition following acute severe acute respiratory syndrome-coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection. Ongoing uncertainty around its definition, burden, diagnosis and management complicates clinical recognition and care in Southeast Asia. A modified Delphi consensus study was conducted with twelve experts from six Southeast Asian countries to develop regional guidance on long COVID. Consensus was predefined as ≥ 80% agreement, corresponding to at least 10 of 12 experts selecting the same response in multiple-choice questions or indicating agreement on Likert-scale questions (e.g. agree/strongly agree, most important/more important, relevant/highly relevant). Questions that reached consensus were removed from the subsequent round, while unresolved questions were revised, consolidated, or expanded. In the final round, a post hoc descriptive category, 'moderate endorsement', was applied to Likert-scale questions that had not reached consensus, with 'important' as the midpoint category of the five-point importance scale ('most important' to 'least important'), to capture responses judged important but falling short of the consensus threshold. Consensus was reached for all 'definition', 'burden' and 'management' theme questions and most 'diagnosis' questions. Experts defined long COVID as unexplained symptoms persisting for > 3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, distinct from post-acute COVID-19, with no minimum severity threshold requirement. Long COVID was recognised as affecting approximately 6%-10% of individuals after SARS-CoV-2 infection, consistent with published WHO and KSID estimates; clinical evaluation and symptom-guided testing were recommended for its diagnosis. Hospitalisation during acute COVID-19 was identified as a risk factor for developing long COVID. The experts recommended multidisciplinary, symptom-directed care, rehabilitation, pacing and follow-up. Vaccination and reinfection prevention were supported as important long COVID risk-reduction strategies, and early antiviral treatment should be considered to prevent severe acute illness and hospitalisation in high-risk individuals. Consensus was not reached on the past medical history required for diagnosis; moderate endorsement was observed for booster status, absence of early antiviral treatment, pre-COVID health assessment and standardised patient-reported outcome tools. This Delphi study provides a practical regional consensus framework for long COVID in Southeast Asia.
