titre: Reversible severe functional decline in an older patient with Alzheimer's dementia: A case report.
titre_fr: Reversible severe functional decline in an older patient with Alzheimer's dementia: A case report.
auteurs: Millman Rabbi Asher
revue: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
resume: Enteral feeding via percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) is generally discouraged in advanced dementia, because it has not been shown to improve survival, aspiration risk, or functional outcomes. However, these recommendations assume accurate disease staging. Reversible conditions such as metabolic encephalopathy and severe malnutrition may mimic terminal-stage dementia, leading to premature limitation of potentially beneficial nutritional support. This case highlights the importance of individualized reassessment before concluding that enteral feeding is futile. An 85-year-old woman with an 8-year history of Alzheimer dementia developed profound functional decline over 3-4 months, including mutism, inability to ambulate, incontinence, and minimal oral intake. At a routine visit with her primary care clinician (PCC), she was presumed to have progressed to advanced dementia, and no further evaluation was pursued, because current guidelines discourage artificially administered nutrition and hydration in advanced dementia. After transitioning to home-based primary care, her new PCC investigated the unusually rapid decline. Laboratory testing revealed severe hypernatremia (sodium, 158 mmol/L), acute kidney injury, and severe malnutrition (body mass index [BMI], 16.1). She was diagnosed with metabolic encephalopathy superimposed on moderate-stage Alzheimer dementia. Nutritional assessment confirmed severe malnutrition by Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria. Following transdisciplinary evaluation and shared decision-making with the patient's daughter, her designated health care proxy, PEG placement was performed. Nutritional rehabilitation normalized laboratory values, restored BMI to 21-22, and resulted in marked cognitive and functional improvement. Severe malnutrition and metabolic derangements may produce a reversible syndrome that mimics advanced dementia. Careful evaluation of reversible contributors to rapid decline is essential before forgoing nutritional support, thus allowing for individualized, goal-concordant decisions and avoiding inappropriate therapeutic nihilism.

titre: Preschool-to-school-age changes in daily-life upper-limb activity and hand function outcomes in children with unilateral cerebral palsy: a secondary longitudinal follow-up study.
titre_fr: Preschool-to-school-age changes in daily-life upper-limb activity and hand function outcomes in children with unilateral cerebral palsy: a secondary longitudinal follow-up study.
auteurs: Hwang Youngsub, You Eunchae, Kwon Jeong-Yi
resume: To compare within-child changes in daily-life bilateral wrist actigraphy and standardized and caregiver-reported hand function outcomes from preschool to school age in children with unilateral cerebral palsy (UCP). This secondary longitudinal observational study linked harmonized pre-intervention assessment waves from two prospective upper-limb rehabilitation trials. Thirteen children with UCP who participated in both studies and had complete actigraphy and hand-function outcome data at both T0 assessments were included. At each wave, MACS level was determined from contemporaneous information on the child's usual manual performance, and children underwent 3-day bilateral wrist actigraphy during habitual daily life and standardized assessment with the Assisting Hand Assessment (AHA) and Melbourne Assessment 2 (MA2), together with caregiver report using the Pediatric Motor Activity Log-Revised (PMAL-R). The mean follow-up interval was 3.82 ± 0.37 years (range, 2.91-4.36 years), and all 13 children retained their baseline MACS level at follow-up reassessment. Mean participant-level percentage changes in less-affected, affected, and bilateral activity counts were -20.2%, -23.6%, and -21.5%, respectively (all p < .001). No statistically detectable group-level change was observed in magnitude ratio (p = .273), AHA scores (p = .635), or PMAL-R How Often scores (p = .068). Mean PMAL-R How Well and all MA2 domain scores were higher at follow-up (all p ≤ .021). In this secondary follow-up sample, mean daily-life upper-limb activity counts were lower at follow-up, whereas no statistically detectable group-level change was observed in magnitude ratio or AHA scores; mean PMAL-R How Well and MA2 domain scores were higher at follow-up. These findings suggest that absolute movement volume and relative interlimb use may reflect different patterns of between-wave change. Reductions in raw activity counts should therefore be interpreted cautiously in the context of treatment exposure, maturation, and changes in daily routines and environments. The parent trials were registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04904796 and NCT06272760).

titre: Traumatic Anterior Shoulder Dislocation Associated With Bankart Lesion, Hill-Sachs Lesion, and Concomitant Pectoralis Major Rupture During Water Polo: A Case Report.
titre_fr: Traumatic Anterior Shoulder Dislocation Associated With Bankart Lesion, Hill-Sachs Lesion, and Concomitant Pectoralis Major Rupture During Water Polo: A Case Report.
auteurs: Pantos Panagiotis, Kosmas Vasileios, Koukos Christos, Papadimitriou Georgios, Mazis Georgios
resume: Concomitant rupture of the pectoralis major tendon and traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation is an exceptionally rare injury pattern. Although anterior shoulder dislocation is a common orthopaedic injury and pectoralis major rupture is increasingly recognized in athletic populations, the simultaneous occurrence of these injuries has been reported only rarely. This case is important because associated soft tissue injuries may be overlooked during the evaluation of shoulder instability, potentially delaying diagnosis and treatment. The present report contributes to the limited literature describing this combined injury pattern and its successful surgical management. A 47-year-old male recreational water polo athlete sustained a traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation during a water polo match following a forceful abduction and external rotation mechanism while contesting the ball overhead. Clinical examination demonstrated pain, anterior shoulder instability, weakness of adduction and internal rotation, and deformity of the anterior axillary fold. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed an anterior-inferior labral tear, a Hill-Sachs lesion, and complete rupture of the pectoralis major tendon. Surgical treatment consisted of arthroscopic repair of the anterior-inferior labrum, arthroscopic remplissage of the humeral head defect, and open repair of the pectoralis major tendon using suture anchors and non-absorbable sutures. A structured rehabilitation program was followed postoperatively. At final follow-up, the patient demonstrated restoration of shoulder stability, recovery of pectoralis major contour and strength, and return to recreational sports without recurrent instability. This case highlights the importance of careful assessment for associated tendon injuries in patients presenting with traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation, particularly following high-energy sporting mechanisms involving abduction and external rotation. Recognition of this uncommon injury combination allows timely treatment and may improve functional outcomes. This report adds to the orthopaedic literature by documenting a rare concomitant injury pattern and demonstrating that combined arthroscopic and open surgical management can achieve successful restoration of shoulder stability and function.

titre: Management of a Rare Complex Elbow Injury: Anatomic Reconstruction of the Triceps Footprint Combined with Radial Head Arthroplasty - A Case Report.
titre_fr: Management of a Rare Complex Elbow Injury: Anatomic Reconstruction of the Triceps Footprint Combined with Radial Head Arthroplasty - A Case Report.
auteurs: Georgiadis Nikolaos, Manidakis Nikolaos, Topaloglou Alexandros, Asteriadis Konstantinos, Kalyvas Efstathios
resume: Distal triceps tendon rupture is a rare injury that may coexist with other traumatic lesions around the elbow. The combination of distal triceps tendon rupture and radial head fracture is particularly uncommon and may be difficult to diagnose and treat. We report the case of a 60-year-old woman who presented with pain, swelling, and inability to actively extend the left elbow after a fall onto an outstretched hand. Clinical examination showed tenderness over the radial head and a palpable gap at the triceps insertion. Radiographs demonstrated a radial head fracture and the Fleck sign, suggestive of distal triceps avulsion. Computed tomography confirmed a comminuted intra-articular Mason type III radial head fracture. The patient underwent single-stage surgical treatment consisting of knotless anatomic triceps footprint repair with intraosseous sutures and press-fit radial head arthroplasty. Post-operative rehabilitation was progressive and protected. Combined distal triceps tendon rupture and radial head fracture is a rare complex elbow injury that may be overlooked. Thorough clinical and radiological assessment is essential. Single-stage treatment of all associated lesions may restore elbow stability and provide satisfactory functional outcome.

titre: Second and Third Carpometacarpal Joint Dislocation in a Polytrauma Patient: Successful Closed Reduction and 2-Year Follow-Up.
titre_fr: Second and Third Carpometacarpal Joint Dislocation in a Polytrauma Patient: Successful Closed Reduction and 2-Year Follow-Up.
auteurs: Salam Nabiel, Kaganur Raghavendra, Dwajan Anirudh, Harshith S, Arunachalam A, Bandi Issac
resume: Carpometacarpal joint dislocations are rare injuries that may be overlooked, particularly in high-energy trauma. Second and third carpometacarpal dislocations are especially uncommon due to the inherent stability of these joints. A man in his 20s sustained second and third carpometacarpal joint dislocations following a high-energy road traffic injury, with an associated femoral head fracture-dislocation. Following urgent management of the hip injury, closed reduction of the carpometacarpal dislocations was performed. Stable anatomical reduction was confirmed clinically and radiographically. The hand was immobilized for 4 weeks followed by structured rehabilitation. At 2-year follow-up, the patient remained pain-free with full function and maintained joint congruity without instability or degenerative changes. Second and third carpometacarpal dislocations require careful clinical and radiographic assessment, particularly in polytrauma. When stable anatomical reduction is achieved, conservative treatment can provide excellent long-term functional outcomes.

titre: Congenital Unilateral Terminal Transverse Deficiency with a Rudimentary Distal Osseous Anlage in a Treatment-Naïve Adult: A Case Report.
titre_fr: Congenital Unilateral Terminal Transverse Deficiency with a Rudimentary Distal Osseous Anlage in a Treatment-Naïve Adult: A Case Report.
auteurs: Shawer Mohamed Ibrahim Aly, Ahmad Shakil, Kindi Mohammed Nasser Said Al
resume: Congenital terminal transverse limb deficiencies are rare, with complete terminal arrest representing an uncommon form of congenital limb deficiency. The existing literature predominantly focuses on pediatric management, including surgical reconstruction and prosthetic rehabilitation, while the natural functional outcomes in untreated adults remain poorly documented. We report a case of congenital unilateral terminal transverse deficiency with a rudimentary distal osseous anlage in a treatment-naïve adult, highlighting the long-term functional adaptation in the absence of surgical or prosthetic intervention. A 44-year-old woman presented with a congenital unilateral left terminal transverse deficiency characterized by rudimentary soft-tissue nubbins and a distal osseous anlage. She had received no previous surgical reconstruction, prosthetic fitting, or formal rehabilitation. Clinical evaluation included goniometric assessment of range of motion, radiographic analysis, and the quick disabilities of the arm, shoulder, and hand questionnaire to assess long-term spontaneous functional and biomechanical adaptation. Despite the congenital deficiency and absence of prior intervention, she demonstrated substantial functional adaptation of the affected limb, enabling effective performance of activities of daily living. This case demonstrates the considerable capacity for spontaneous functional and biomechanical adaptation in an adult with congenital terminal transverse limb deficiency who remained treatment-naïve into adulthood. Despite the absence of surgical reconstruction, prosthetic use, or formal rehabilitation, the patient achieved substantial functional independence in activities of daily living. These findings highlight the importance of individualized assessment of functional requirements and patient expectations when considering reconstructive or prosthetic interventions in congenital limb deficiencies.

titre: Limb Salvage of a Flail Neuropathic Ankle in Congenital Insensitivity to Pain with Anhidrosis Using a Hindfoot Superconstruct.
titre_fr: Limb Salvage of a Flail Neuropathic Ankle in Congenital Insensitivity to Pain with Anhidrosis Using a Hindfoot Superconstruct.
auteurs: Tholgapiyan T, Sivakumar Senthilkumar, Athmanathan Madhan, Kumar T Dilip
resume: Congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis (CIPA) is a rare autosomal recessive neurological disorder, with an estimated incidence of 1 in 125 million. The condition is characterized by a clinical feature of unexplained pyrexia, global insensitivity to pain, anhidrosis, intellectual disability, and self-mutilating behavior. While musculoskeletal complications, such as fractures and joint dislocations are common, severe neuropathic arthropathy represents one of the most debilitating skeletal manifestations; however, its specific incidence remains unrecorded in present medical literature. titre: Concomitant Achilles Tendon Rupture and Ankle Fracture in a Snowboarder Managed with Early Rehabilitation: A Case Report.
titre_fr: Concomitant Achilles Tendon Rupture and Ankle Fracture in a Snowboarder Managed with Early Rehabilitation: A Case Report.
auteurs: Curran John A, Pappas Michael W, Grimm Nathan L, Curran Andrew R
resume: Achilles tendon rupture and ankle fracture are each common in isolation, but their simultaneous occurrence in the same limb is rare. Because the two injuries share overlapping signs of pain, swelling, and functional limitation, one is often missed on initial evaluation, and a low threshold for combined clinical and sonographic or magnetic resonance imaging assessment is warranted in high-energy ankle trauma. Furthermore, while early functional weight-bearing is increasingly favored for isolated Achilles ruptures, its safety and implementation in combined injuries remain poorly defined. A 34-year-old male sustained a closed Weber B bimalleolar ankle fracture and a complete Achilles tendon rupture during a high-energy snowboarding accident. Both injuries were identified preoperatively by clinical examination (palpable tendon defect, positive Thompson, and Matles tests) and ultrasonography. One week after injury, he underwent open reduction and internal fixation of the lateral malleolus with a lateral approach followed by repair of the Achilles using a Krackow-type suture-tape repair docked to the calcaneus with two SwiveLock anchors (Arthrex, Naples, FL). This was done through a separate posterior longitudinal incision. Intraoperative external rotation stress testing demonstrated no talar shift or medial malleolar fracture displacement, confirming stability and avoiding unnecessary medial fixation. At 1 week postoperatively, the patient was transitioned from a posterior splint to a boot with a heel wedge, and active range of motion was initiated. At 2 weeks, the patient was allowed to bear full weight in the boot with a heel wedge. Formal physical therapy began at 4 weeks. Concomitant Achilles tendon rupture and ankle fracture require a high index of suspicion for both injuries. Intraoperative stress testing after fibular fixation can guide the decision to forgo medial malleolar fixation. In addition, an early, protected rehabilitation protocol can be successfully implemented in patients with a combined Achilles rupture and malleolar fracture.

titre: Serious game-based interventions for pediatric asthma management: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Serious game-based interventions for pediatric asthma management: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Wu Liping, Deng Jia, Zhang Shun, Bai Yongqi
resume: Childhood asthma is a common chronic respiratory disease that can affect physical functioning, daily activities, and quality of life. Poor adherence and inadequate self-management remain important challenges in long-term asthma care. Serious games (SGs) combine game elements with health education, behavioral support, or rehabilitation and have been increasingly used in children with asthma. However, evidence regarding their clinical value has not been clearly established. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of SG-based interventions on pulmonary function, asthma-related knowledge, inflammatory biomarkers, healthcare utilization, engagement, adherence, and safety in children with asthma. PubMed, Scopus, Embase via Ovid, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, Science Direct, SinoMed and CNKI were searched from inception to June 1, 2026. Studies examining SG-based interventions in children with asthma were eligible for inclusion. Study selection, data extraction, and methodological assessment were conducted independently by two reviewers. Pulmonary function outcomes that were sufficiently comparable across studies were pooled by meta-analysis, whereas the remaining outcomes were summarized narratively. Eight studies were included. The interventions were classified as educational/self-management SG interventions or exercise/rehabilitation SG interventions. Meta-analyses included four studies for forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1), four studies for FEV1/forced vital capacity (FVC), three studies for FVC, and three studies for maximal mid-expiratory flow (MMEF). Pooled analyses showed higher FVC [mean difference (MD) =4.48, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.14 to 8.82] and MMEF (MD =8.41, 95% CI: 6.63 to 10.19) following SG-based interventions. No statistically significant differences were found for FEV1 (MD =1.90, 95% CI: -0.97 to 4.78) or FEV1/FVC [standardized mean difference (SMD) =-0.03, 95% CI: -0.26 to 0.20]. However, the certainty of evidence was limited by the small number of studies, small sample sizes, heterogeneity among interventions, and methodological limitations. SG-based interventions may serve as a complementary approach to pediatric asthma management, particularly for selected pulmonary function outcomes and self-management-related behaviors. The finding for MMEF was relatively consistent, whereas the evidence for FVC was less robust. Interpretation is limited by the small number of available studies, small sample sizes, differences in intervention protocols, and methodological limitations. Larger, well-designed studies using standardized outcomes and longer follow-up are needed before the clinical value of SG-based interventions can be established.

titre: Mitoribosome dysfunction in sensorineural hearing loss: genetic mechanisms and clinical implication.
titre_fr: Mitoribosome dysfunction in sensorineural hearing loss: genetic mechanisms and clinical implication.
auteurs: Cai Luhang, Chen Chao, Chen Jia, He Jianguo, Guan Min-Xin
resume: Mitochondrial translation depends on coordinated contributions from the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes and is essential for oxidative phosphorylation. Disruption of this system can cause isolated sensorineural hearing loss or auditory impairment within multisystem disease. This review examines how mitochondrial rRNA variants, nuclear-encoded mitoribosomal protein defects, and environmental exposures converge on mitochondrial translation to impair hearing. The mitochondrial 12S rRNA 1555A>G and 1494C>T mutations alter decoding-site architecture and increase susceptibility to aminoglycoside ototoxicity, whereas pathogenic variants in nuclear mitoribosomal protein genes can compromise subunit assembly, stability, or abundance. Nuclear modifiers, particularly TRMU, and secondary mitochondrial tRNA variants illustrate how RNA modification and tRNA function influence the consequences of a primary rRNA defect. We propose mitochondrial translational reserve as a testable framework for incomplete penetrance and cochlear vulnerability, while recognizing that its quantitative relationship to hearing outcomes remains unresolved. Current clinical applications include molecular diagnosis, genotype-informed aminoglycoside prescribing, cascade testing of maternal relatives, and individualized hearing rehabilitation. Patient-derived auditory models and genetic rescue studies provide opportunities to clarify disease mechanisms and evaluate interventions, although modifier correction and pharmacological otoprotection remain experimental. Integrating molecular mechanisms with clinical assessment can strengthen prevention of avoidable ototoxicity and guide care for mitochondrial hearing loss.

titre: Voice rehabilitation after thyroid cancer surgery: a narrative review of current evidence and clinical practice.
titre_fr: Voice rehabilitation after thyroid cancer surgery: a narrative review of current evidence and clinical practice.
auteurs: Zhang Chunhua, Shao Jinlan, Zhu Xiaofan, Sun Qianhui, Wang Meixiang, Zhang Liuliu, Hu Tingting
resume: Voice impairment is common after thyroid cancer surgery and can significantly affect quality of life, even in the absence of recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) injury. Voice rehabilitation has been recognized as beneficial, but current guidelines lack thyroid cancer-specific protocols regarding assessment, timing, intensity, and long-term follow-up. This review critically appraises current evidence on voice rehabilitation after thyroid cancer surgery to inform clinical decision-making and identify practice gaps. PubMed and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from January 1, 2015 to July 31, 2026. Eligible studies included clinical decisions, guidelines, expert consensus, systematic reviews, and original clinical studies addressing postoperative voice assessment, rehabilitation, or follow-up in adults after thyroidectomy for thyroid cancer. Evidence was synthesized narratively across nine domains: mechanisms and natural history; assessment tools and timing; timing and risk stratification; voice therapy; surgical rehabilitation; special populations; tele-rehabilitation and long-term follow-up; multidisciplinary collaboration and patient education; and evidence gaps. Post-thyroidectomy voice dysfunction is multifactorial and heterogeneous. Most patients improve within 3-6 months, but approximately 20% have persistent dysfunction at 1 year. Multidimensional assessment combining patient-reported outcomes, perceptual evaluation, acoustic measures, and laryngeal imaging is recommended. Early voice therapy within 4 weeks may improve outcomes. Surgical rehabilitation, including injection laryngoplasty (IL), laryngeal framework surgery, and recurrent laryngeal nerve reinnervation (RLNR), is indicated for persistent paralysis. Tele-rehabilitation and multidisciplinary care are promising but understudied. Evidence remains limited by heterogeneity, small sample sizes, and lack of standardized outcome measures. Voice rehabilitation after thyroid cancer surgery should be individualized, multidimensional, and initiated early for high-risk patients. Future research should prioritize core outcome sets (COSs), multicenter randomized trials, and validation of tele-rehabilitation and digital tools to improve long-term voice outcomes.

titre: Measuring Meaning and Purpose in Rehabilitation: Validating the Presence of Meaning Subscale in Adults With Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.
titre_fr: Measuring Meaning and Purpose in Rehabilitation: Validating the Presence of Meaning Subscale in Adults With Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.
auteurs: Covington Natalie V, Pei Yalian, Radomski Mary Vining
resume: Unexpected life events, such as a brain injury, can result in a disrupted sense of purpose and meaning in life. Meaning and purpose in life have been identified as potentially modifiable protective factors in promoting health and well-being. At present, meaning and purpose are not widely assessed in allied health research or clinical practice, nor have measures of these constructs been validated for use after brain injury. Consideration of meaning and purpose in brain injury management may improve long-term outcomes of rehabilitation. To support assessment of meaning and purpose in rehabilitation, we examined the psychometric properties of the Meaning in Life Questionnaire-Presence of Meaning (MLQ-P) subscale in adults with a history of mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI). Sixty-two people with mTBI completed the Meaning in Life Questionnaire, the Life Engagement Test, the Work and Social Adjustment Scale, and the Purpose Status Question. We evaluated the five-item MLQ-P subscale for (a) construct validity and internal structure using exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, (b) convergent validity by examining relationships between MLQ-P and related constructs, and (c) internal consistency reliability using Cronbach's alpha. The MLQ-P's internal structure was unidimensional, consistent with previous findings in the general population. Scores on the MLQ-P were strongly correlated to the Life Engagement Test, a related measure of purpose in life. The MLQ-P demonstrated strong internal consistency reliability. The MLQ-P is a valid measure of meaning and purpose in adults with mTBI. Future work should incorporate consideration of meaning and purpose into research and clinical practice for mTBI management.

titre: The effectiveness of virtual reality-based rehabilitation in patients with neck pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis of randomized controlled trials.
titre_fr: The effectiveness of virtual reality-based rehabilitation in patients with neck pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis of randomized controlled trials.
auteurs: Jike Amu, Zhang Xiang, Liu Hao, Yu Anyun
resume: Neck pain is a widespread condition impacting daily functioning and quality of life. Virtual Reality (VR) technology has gained attention as a non-pharmacological intervention in rehabilitative medicine, offering potential benefits for pain management. This study systematically reviewed and conducted a meta-analysis on the effectiveness of VR rehabilitation for neck pain. Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive literature search was performed across databases (e.g., PubMed) up to October 1, 2024, targeting randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing VR-based rehabilitation with alternative interventions for neck pain. Data extraction focused on outcomes like the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) and Neck Disability Index (NDI). Quality and bias were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool, and the GRADE approach evaluated evidence certainty. Trial Sequential Analysis (TSA) was also employed to ensure robustness in conclusions. This protocol was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD42022334319). The meta-analysis, which included 11 randomized controlled trials with 476 participants, demonstrated that virtual reality-based rehabilitation significantly reduced VAS scores [471 patients, mean difference (MD) -0.70, p = 0.01] and NDI scores (411 patients, MD -3.06, p < 0.0001) within the first week. Furthermore, significant reductions in VAS (315 patients, MD -1.00, p < 0.05) and NDI scores (315 patients, MD -3.81, p = 0.005) were observed from the first week to 6 months in the VR-based rehabilitation group. Trial sequential analysis further confirmed the statistical strength and reliability of these findings. Improvements in cervical mobility were observed, as evidenced by increased neck flexion and extension. VR-based rehabilitation shows promise as an effective strategy for managing neck pain, improving both pain levels and functional capacity. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42022334319, identifier PROSPERO (CRD42022334319).

titre: Lower limb lymphedema: reliability of four non-imaging measurement modalities.
titre_fr: Lower limb lymphedema: reliability of four non-imaging measurement modalities.
auteurs: Salim David, Bučan Amar, Wittenkamp Merete Celano, Vinther Anders, Frendø Martin, Asirvatham Gjørup Caroline, Rosenkrantz Hölmich Lisbet
resume: To assess intra- and inter-rater reliability of four non-imaging measuring modalities in lower limb lymphedema (LLL): perometry (PM), circumferential tape measurements (CTMs), bioimpedance spectroscopy (BIS), and tissue dielectric constant (TDC). In this study, 51 adults with LLL were assessed by two physiotherapists. Measurements were completed within 45 min in alternating order. Reliability was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC<sub>2,1</sub>), standard error of measurement (SEM), 95% confidence limits for SEM (SEM<sub>95</sub>), smallest real difference (SRD%), and Bland-Altman analysis. PM, CTM, and BIS demonstrated excellent reliability (ICC<sub>2,1</sub> ≥ 0.900) while TDC showed good to excellent reliability (ICC<sub>2,1</sub>: 0.761-0.933). SEM<sub>95</sub> was lowest for PM (263-282 mL), with greater error for CTM (505-767 mL), BIS (6.0-7.2 lymphedema-index (L-Dex score) units), and TDC (3.6-7.8%PWC). SRD values demonstrated a required change of 4% with PM, 7-11% with CTM, 8-10 L-Dex points with BIS, and 12.4-26.2% with TDC to exceed measurement error. PM, CTM, and BIS provide reliable LLL assessment. TDC showed greatest site-dependent variability, necessitating cautious interpretation. Our findings support PM as the most precise volume measure, CTM as a practical alternative, and BIS and TDC as complementary tools for quantifying extracellular and localized tissue fluid.

titre: Validation and reliability testing of the Persian translation of the Vertigo Handicap Questionnaire.
titre_fr: Validation and reliability testing of the Persian translation of the Vertigo Handicap Questionnaire.
auteurs: Reyhani Yousef, Adel Ghahraman Mansoureh, Jalali Mir Mohammad, Nemati Shadman, Jalaie Shohreh
revue: Journal of research in medical sciences : the official journal of Isfahan University of Medical Sciences
resume: The Vertigo Handicap Questionnaire (VHQ) is a well-established instrument for assessing the physical and psychosocial impact of vertigo. To facilitate its use in Persian-speaking populations, this study aimed to translate, culturally adapt, and validate the Persian version of the VHQ. The VHQ was culturally adapted into Persian using forward-backward translation, expert review, and cognitive interviews. Psychometric evaluation included 470 patients and 101 controls. Validity assessed face, content, construct (exploratory factor analysis then confirmatory factor analysis [CFA] with path diagram), discriminant (t-test/analysis of covariance/receiver operating characteristic), and convergent (correlation with Dizziness Handicap Inventory [DHI]) validity. Reliability was measured by internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha/omega) and test-retest (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC (3,1)] over 1 week; n = 128). The Persian Version of the VHQ (VHQ-P) showed a four-factor structure (restriction of activity, social anxiety, fear of vertigo, and severity of vertigo). CFA confirmed good model fit (χ2/df = 2.85, comparative fit index = 0.95, root mean square error of approximation = 0.063) with standardized factor loadings ranging from 0.65 to 0.95 (P < 0.001). Discriminant validity was excellent (AUC = 0.99; cutoff = 19.5; sensitivity = 97%, specificity = 100%). Convergent validity was supported by strong correlations with DHI subscales (ρ = 0.88-0.90). Test-retest reliability was excellent (ICC [3,1] = 0.98), and internal consistency was outstanding (Cronbach's α = 0.985; subscales: 0.898-0.972). The Persian version of the VHQ is a valid and reliable tool for clinical use. The efficacy of medical or surgical treatment of vertigo can be assessed using VHQ-P. The VHQ-P appears to be an appropriate tool for evaluating patients' perceived handicaps and advantages after rehabilitation interventions.

The Persian Version of the VHQ (VHQ-P) showed a four-factor structure (restriction of activity, social anxiety, fear of vertigo, and severity of vertigo). CFA confirmed good model fit (χ2/df = 2.85, comparative fit index = 0.95, root mean square error of approximation = 0.063) with standardized factor loadings ranging from 0.65 to 0.95 (P < 0.001). Discriminant validity was excellent (AUC = 0.99; cutoff = 19.5; sensitivity = 97%, specificity = 100%). Convergent validity was supported by strong correlations with DHI subscales (ρ = 0.88-0.90). Test-retest reliability was excellent (ICC [3,1] = 0.98), and internal consistency was outstanding (Cronbach's α = 0.985; subscales: 0.898-0.972). The Persian version of the VHQ is a valid and reliable tool for clinical use. The efficacy of medical or surgical treatment of vertigo can be assessed using VHQ-P. The VHQ-P appears to be an appropriate tool for evaluating patients' perceived handicaps and advantages after rehabilitation interventions.

titre: Willingness to adopt gene therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: barriers, facilitators, and multidisciplinary readiness.
titre_fr: Willingness to adopt gene therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: barriers, facilitators, and multidisciplinary readiness.
auteurs: García-Uzquiano Rocío, Branas-Pampillón María, Medina-Cantillo Julita, García-Palop Beatriz, Ruiz-Beato Elena, Maurino Jorge, Poveda-Andrés José Luis
resume: Management of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is shifting toward genotype-specific, disease-modifying interventions, including adeno-associated virus-mediated micro-dystrophin gene transfer. Grounded in established technology adoption frameworks, this study evaluated healthcare professionals' (HCPs) willingness to adopt advanced gene therapies, identified critical systemic barriers and facilitators, and mapped multidisciplinary familiarity and quality perceptions regarding functional outcome measures. We conducted a cross-sectional, web-based study evaluating 53 HCPs actively involved in DMD care across Spain: 37 pediatric neurologists, 11 rehabilitation physicians, and 5 hospital pharmacists. Using ad-hoc questionnaires and validated psychometric instruments, we evaluated technical knowledge, functional scale perceptions (including sensitivity to change and specificity), behavioral intent, and implementation challenges. Multivariate logistic regression identified independent predictors of high adoption willingness. Receptivity was high, with 67.6% of pediatric neurologists demonstrating strong willingness to adopt gene therapy. Clinicians ranked acute post-infusion safety concerns (mean rank: 2.30; lower values indicate greater relevance) and uncertainty regarding long-term efficacy (mean rank: 2.70) as primary clinical barriers, followed by institutional cost constraints (mean rank: 3.38). Conversely, the availability of robust clinical trial evidence was the primary operational facilitator (86.5%). In the multivariate model, a clinician's perception of the Six-Minute Walk Test as an objective and sensitive instrument emerged as the sole independent predictor of high adoption intent (OR = 15.23, 95%CI: 1.58-146.67, p = 0.018). HCPs demonstrate high theoretical receptivity to DMD gene therapy. However, clinical translation remains constrained by operational bottlenecks, acute safety risks, and technical gaps in functional outcome mastery. Because clinician readiness depends on diagnostic confidence in outcome measures, health authorities must prioritize standardized safety surveillance protocols, interprofessional training on scale psychometrics, and transparent reimbursement frameworks prior to broader deployment.

titre: Discriminant and Prognostic Validity of the Multimodal Exertional Test (MET) for Athletes with Concussion.
titre_fr: Discriminant and Prognostic Validity of the Multimodal Exertional Test (MET) for Athletes with Concussion.
auteurs: Pyndiura Kyla L, Di Battista Alex P, Richards Doug, Reed Nick, Lawrence David W, Hutchison Michael G
resume: Exertional tests have become an informative tool to assist with clinical concussion management and return-to-sport medical decisions. However, current tests are resource intensive and thus, we developed a widely accessible, multimodal exertional test (MET). The objectives of this study were: (1) To evaluate the discriminant validity of the MET by examining sex-stratified differences in symptoms, heart rate (HR), and performance metrics between concussed and healthy athletes; and (2) To assess the predictive (prognostic) validity of the MET by determining whether week 1 MET performance predicts time to medical clearance. This study was conducted at a single academic institution and affiliated sport medicine clinic in Toronto, Canada, with participants recruited between August 2022 and November 2024. 115 interuniversity athletes (female n=49, male n=66) completed the MET at off-season and 55 interuniversity athletes with concussion (female n=37, male n=18) completed the MET up to six times at 1-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 6-, and 8-weeks post-injury. Average and maximum HR, symptoms, performance metrics, and MET pass/fail status were measured prior to and during the protocol. Probabilistic hierarchical models were implemented to estimate differences between concussion and healthy athletes (discriminant validity) and negative binomial analyses were used to examine whether MET performance predicted time to medical clearance (predictive validity). At 1-week post injury, concussed athletes exhibited greater symptom provocation during the MET compared to healthy athletes, with differences after each task. MET failure rates were highest during weeks 1 (63%) and 2 (49%) and declined through week 8. Athletes who passed the MET at week 1 recovered 20.6 days faster (90% Credible Interval [CrI] = 4.9-36.8 days, posterior probability [pprob] > 0 = 97.7%) than those who failed. The MET demonstrates discriminant validity by eliciting greater symptom provocation in athletes with concussion compared to healthy athletes. Improvements in symptoms and completion rates over 8 weeks indicate recovery-related gains in exertional tolerance. The MET also demonstrates predictive validity, as passing the test at week 1 was associated with faster time to medical clearance, supporting its potential utility as an early prognostic tool in concussion management.

titre: The measurement structure of the Mayo-Portland Adaptability Inventory-4 (MPAI-4) in individuals with acquired brain injury: Evidence from Rasch analysis and classical test theory in a Japanese cohort.
titre_fr: The measurement structure of the Mayo-Portland Adaptability Inventory-4 (MPAI-4) in individuals with acquired brain injury: Evidence from Rasch analysis and classical test theory in a Japanese cohort.
auteurs: Oyama Nozomi, Crawford Fay, Wada Shinichi, Saito Kaoru, Bateman Andrew
resume: The Mayo-Portland Adaptability Inventory-4 (MPAI-4) is widely used to assess comprehensive outcomes following acquired brain injury (ABI). Although a Japanese version is available, its psychometric properties have not been evaluated. This study examined the measurement properties of the Japanese MPAI-4. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 163 participants receiving post-discharge rehabilitation between June 2024 and June 2025 at rehabilitation facilities in Japan. Rasch analyses examined reliability, unidimensionality, item fit, category functioning, targeting and differential item functioning. Classical Test Theory analyses assessed internal consistency and factor structure. The Japanese MPAI-4 demonstrated a Person Separation Index of 0.89 and high internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.91). Rasch analysis identified departures from model assumptions, including multidimensionality and disordered category thresholds. Exploratory factor analysis suggested a multifactorial structure, although it did not clearly align with the original three-domain model. These findings indicate that the Japanese MPAI-4 captures multiple aspects of post-ABI functioning, reflecting the complexity of outcomes in community rehabilitation. Although measurement issues should be considered when interpreting scores, the study provides initial psychometric evidence for the Japanese MPAI-4. These findings may support its clinical use for comprehensive assessment of post-ABI functioning in Japan, while contributing to the cross-cultural evidence base for the MPAI-4.

titre: Clinical performance of additively manufactured interim complete-arch dental prostheses for immediate implant loading: A retrospective observational study.
titre_fr: Clinical performance of additively manufactured interim complete-arch dental prostheses for immediate implant loading: A retrospective observational study.
auteurs: Tirone Federico, Rolando Erik, Rodi Donata, Pozzatti Laura, Salzano Stefano
resume: To evaluate framework fracture and early implant survival of immediately loaded implant-supported fixed complete dental prostheses (IFCDPs) fabricated from additively manufactured interim resin using a novel integrated digital prosthetic protocol. This retrospective multicenter observational study included 63 consecutive patients (77 arches) treated at four clinical centers. Overall, 320 implants were placed and immediately loaded. The primary outcome was the prosthesis-level framework fracture proportion during the interim-prosthesis observation period. Secondary outcomes were prosthetic screw loosening during the same period and implant failure, which was assessed over a 6-month retrospective follow-up. Generalized estimating equation (GEE) models were used to evaluate associations between framework fracture and patient/prosthetic variables while accounting for clustering of arches within patients. A multinomial logistic regression model was used to explore the association between implant failure and mechanical complications, and the Mann-Whitney U test was used to compare the number of fractures between arch types (α = 0.05). Fifteen of 77 IFCDPs experienced at least one framework fracture (19.5%). Overall, 33 fracture events occurred, including recurrent fractures in 13 arches after replacement prostheses were reprinted from the original files. Male sex was associated with a higher fracture rate than female sex in the arch-level GEE clustered by patient analysis (37.5% vs 9.7%; RR = 3.71; 95% CI, 1.01-13.60; p = 0.048). Five screw-loosening events occurred in 4 IFCDPs (5.2%). Three of 320 implants failed, yielding an early implant survival rate of 99.06%. Mechanical complications were not significantly associated with implant loss (p = 0.101). Additively manufactured resin interim IFCDPs showed a relevant prosthesis-level fracture proportion (19.5%) with frequent recurrence after reprinting, despite high early implant survival. Male sex was associated with a higher fracture rate, although this finding should be interpreted as exploratory. Fractured designs should be structurally reassessed before remanufacturing. Controlled prospective studies are required to validate design and manufacturing parameters. Additively manufactured interim resin prostheses allow for a fully digital provisionalization with favorable early implant survival. However, the observed fracture proportion and frequent recurrence after reprinting indicate that mechanical reliability remains a relevant limitation. Careful structural planning, design reassessment after fracture, and close clinical monitoring are therefore required.

titre: Anterior Middle Cingulate Cortex Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid Level Is Elevated in Children With Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder With and Without Prenatal Alcohol Exposure.
titre_fr: Anterior Middle Cingulate Cortex Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid Level Is Elevated in Children With Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder With and Without Prenatal Alcohol Exposure.
auteurs: Alger Jeffry R, Gupta Ishika, Farkouh Lea, Korthas Jennifer, Shah Ankita, Silverberg Arjun B, Salamon Noriko, Schneider Benjamin N, Joshi Shantanu H, O'Connor Mary J, O'Neill Joseph
resume: Prior neuroimaging suggests brain differences between children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and prenatal alcohol exposure (ADHD+PAE) and non-exposed children with ADHD due to non-PAE causes (ADHD-PAE). There has been interest in regional brain levels of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and glutamate (Glu) measured in vivo with magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) as possible indicators of local inhibitory, respectively, excitatory activity in ADHD. For the first time, we report here a comparison of GABA and Glu in ADHD+PAE vs. ADHD-PAE. At 3 Tesla, we used J-difference-edited single-voxel MRS to assay GABA and Glu in 27 children with ADHD+PAE, 21 with ADHD-PAE, and 28 typically developing (TD) controls, all aged between 7 and 14 years. MRS was sampled from midline anterior middle cingulate cortex (aMCC), the "cognitive cingulate" considered functionally relevant to ADHD. Spectra were fit with custom software, including a unique technique for isolating the GABA signal from the confounding macromolecular baseline (MMBL). aMCC GABA was higher in ADHD+PAE and ADHD-PAE than in TD. GABA increased with age in TD, but not in ADHD+PAE or ADHD-PAE. Similar effects were observed for the ratios GABA/Glu and GABA/Glx. For GABA+MMBL (GABA+) these effects were not seen; rather, GABA+ and MMBL increased with age for the ADHD+PAE group only. No significant effects were found for Glu or Glx. GABA in the aMCC does not distinguish the two etiologies of ADHD; rather, elevated GABA that follows an abnormal development appears to be common to both. High GABA may reflect increased inhibition of the aMCC impairing its cognitive functions. GABA+ results in ADHD may not track reliably with underlying GABA values. Negative results for Glu and Glx should be reexamined at shorter echo-times.

titre: Tracheostomy and Home Invasive Ventilation in Severe Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia: A Scoping Review of Indications, Timing, Outcomes and Transitional Care.
titre_fr: Tracheostomy and Home Invasive Ventilation in Severe Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia: A Scoping Review of Indications, Timing, Outcomes and Transitional Care.
auteurs: Mahindrakar Neha, Bhandari Prakreeti, Vorakunthada Yuttiwat, Lilitwat Weerapong
revue: Journal of paediatrics and child health
resume: To map the literature on tracheostomy and home invasive ventilation in infants and children with severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), including indications, timing, respiratory outcomes, comorbidities, complications, growth, neurodevelopment, social determinants and transitional care. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and CINAHL/EBSCO from inception to 30 June 2026. Search terms combined BPD or chronic lung disease of prematurity with tracheostomy or tracheotomy. Eligible studies included infants or children with BPD who underwent tracheostomy, received chronic invasive ventilation or were discharged on home mechanical ventilation. Conference abstracts without full-text articles, duplicate precursor abstracts, reviews and editorials were excluded from primary synthesis. Forty-one studies were included. Evidence was mainly retrospective, including cohorts, administrative database studies, multicentre registries and single-centre observational studies. Tracheostomy was generally considered for persistent invasive ventilation, failed extubation, high respiratory support needs, pulmonary hypertension, airway malacia, growth failure, sedation burden or limited developmental progress. Timing varied widely across centres. Pulmonary hypertension was associated with illness severity and mortality risk, although many children receiving home ventilation improved over time. Among survivors, ventilator liberation and decannulation were common but often occurred over several years. Airway complications, readmissions and operative airway interventions were frequent. Evidence also highlighted centre-level variation, racial and social disparities and limited caregiver-centred data. Tracheostomy and home invasive ventilation in severe BPD represent a prolonged care trajectory. Future work should define consensus indications, optimise timing, standardise transitional care and prioritise family-centred and equity-focused outcomes.

titre: Integrated Multi-omics Reveals Molecular Signatures of Rett Syndrome, Informing Future Biomarker Discovery.
titre_fr: Integrated Multi-omics Reveals Molecular Signatures of Rett Syndrome, Informing Future Biomarker Discovery.
auteurs: Issar Jasmeen Kaur, Hertzog Ashley, Pang Ignatius, Graham Mark E, Aryamanesh Nader, Riley Lisa G, Piras Ignazio S, Hansen Nathaniel P, Finney Caitlin A, Shvetcov Artur, Gloss Brian, Bandodkar Sushil, Dale Russell C, Sun Qin, Ellaway Carolyn, Tolun Adviye A, Ho Gladys, Kaufmann Walter E, Gold Wendy A
resume: Rett syndrome (RTT) is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder primarily caused by pathogenic variants in the X-linked methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MECP2) gene. Despite numerous clinical trials being conducted, there are limited disease-modifying options available for individuals with RTT. This paucity of effective treatments can in part be attributed to the lack of clinically useful biomarkers that can objectively assess treatment response. Moreover, diagnosis of RTT continues to be clinical, when clinical manifestations are apparent, precluding early therapeutic approaches. Thus, clinical biomarkers of disease stage could improve diagnosis and enable real-time monitoring of response to treatment, providing the earliest possible indications of therapeutic efficacy. Given MeCP2's role as a key regulator of gene transcription, we used an untargeted omics approach to evaluate transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolic profiles in blood from individuals with RTT (n = 9) and age- and sex-matched controls (n = 8). In addition to characterising differential expression at each omic layer, to understand the shared biology and coordinated molecular signals across all omic datasets, we used the unsupervised machine learning framework Multi-Omics Factor Analysis version 2 (MOFA2). The individual omic data consisted of a robust upregulation of genes involved in ribosomal structure and translation together with a downregulation in vesicle trafficking genes. An upregulation in ribosomal machinery and mitochondrial function together with a concomitant downregulation of critical epigenetic regulators, immune-signalling molecules, and cytoskeletal structural anchors was observed in the proteomics, which was supported by the phosphoproteomics. Notably, plasma metabolomics pointed towards alterations in energy substrates and lipid/cholesterol handling, suggesting systemic downstream consequences of primary intracellular disturbances. The integrated MOFA2 data supported the individual omic data revealing a central disease axis principally shaped by the proteome and transcriptome and supported by the metabolome and phosphoproteome, identifying potential biomarkers, including latent biological processes that distinguish RTT from controls (Latent Factor 1) and correlates of clinical severity (Latent Factor 2). Overall, our data reveal a distinctive 'disease state' molecular signature that distinguishes individuals with RTT from controls, where the findings in RTT blood cells are consistent with previously reported altered translational and mitochondrial function and disrupted chromatin regulation, cytoskeletal dynamics, and metabolic signalling. Our integrated multi-omics analyses revealed that PBMC's LTN1, ATRX, CHD8, SPTB, DMTN, PRF1, CD40LG, and PTPRCAP and plasma glutamate are the most promising disease-state (complementary diagnostic) candidate biomarkers while sphingomyelin, RTN3, and MMP1 appear to be the most suitable biomarkers of disease severity. Here, we demonstrate that blood from individuals with RTT reflects the molecular systemic consequences of MeCP2 dysfunction.

titre: Association of Neuronal Cell Adhesion Molecule (NrCAM) Gene with Autism Spectrum Disorder in Indian Cohorts.
titre_fr: Association of Neuronal Cell Adhesion Molecule (NrCAM) Gene with Autism Spectrum Disorder in Indian Cohorts.
auteurs: Chandrakala Elumalai, Nagaraj Kakanahalli
resume: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is the most complex neurodevelopmental disorder with impairments in communication, social interaction and stereotyped behaviours. ASD has been found to increase immeasurably in India, with estimates ranging from 1 in 68 to 1 in 100 children. Genetically, more than 1,000 genes have been linked with ASD. Among them, the neuronal cell adhesion molecule (NrCAM) gene is one of the candidate genes and is important for its critical role in the development and function of the nervous system, particularly in wiring the brain through axon guidance and organising myelinated nerve structures. Disruptions in this gene are associated with various neurodevelopmental, psychiatric and cancer-related disorders. The present study aimed to understand the association of the NrCAM gene with ASD. titre: Biallelic BECN1 variants cause neurodevelopmental disorders via AMPA receptor dysregulation.
titre_fr: Biallelic BECN1 variants cause neurodevelopmental disorders via AMPA receptor dysregulation.
auteurs: Kuramoto Kenta, Ullah Farid, Liang Pingdong, Ramirez Idalis M, AlAbdi Lama, Feng Bing, Sakurai Minami, Kang Myung-Su, Dong Huancheng, Oyeyemi Motunrayo J, Qin Zuoheng, Coghlan Meghan A, Sharma Abhineet, Mercier Angelique, McRae Anne, Belmadani Abdelhak, Contractor Anis, Abuyousef Omar, Hashem Mais O, Alhashem Amal, Maddirevula Sateesh, Alkuraya Fowzan S, He Yanlin, Davis Erica E, He Congcong
revue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
resume: Genetic regulation of neurodevelopmental disorders that impair brain development and social interaction is complex and poorly understood. Although emerging evidence suggests a link between neurodevelopmental disorders and autophagy deficits, congenital autophagy gene disorders are rare in humans, and underlying molecular mechanisms remain unknown. Here we demonstrate that the autophagy protein BECN1 is a regulator of neuronal and social development in vertebrate species. We identify rare deleterious biallelic BECN1 variants that cause neurodevelopmental disorders in two unrelated families. Becn1 disruption also causes neuronal and social developmental defects in mouse and zebrafish models. BECN1 serves as an adaptor to recruit Arc to the E3 ubiquitin ligase UBE3A for polyubiquitination and degradation, thereby maintaining postsynaptic AMPA receptor (AMPAR) stability, AMPAR-mediated excitatory neurotransmission, and normal social interaction. Thus, our study illustrates new biology and a non-canonical mechanism by which BECN1 regulates neurodevelopment in humans, mice and zebrafish, via a crosstalk with the ubiquitin-proteasomal machinery.

titre: Normative transcriptomic clues to thalamic developmental vulnerability in C9orf7 2-FTLD.
titre_fr: Normative transcriptomic clues to thalamic developmental vulnerability in C9orf7 2-FTLD.
auteurs: So Isis, Bouzigues Arabella, Ferry-Bolder Eve, Cullen Eva, Russell Lucy L, Foster Phoebe H, Farley Sophie, Convery Rhian, van Swieten John C, Jiskoot Lize C, Seelaar Harro, Galimberti Daniela, Vandenberghe Rik, Laforce Robert, Bruffaerts Rose, Bertoux Maxime, Lebouvier Thibaud, Solje Eino, Levin Johannes, di Fede Giuseppe, Thompson Alexander, Ber Isabelle Le, Migliaccio Raffaella Lara, Körtvélyessy Peter, Schroeter Matthias L, Logroscino Giancarlo, Otto Markus, Uzelac Zeljko, Illán-Gala Ignacio, Krüger Johanna, Nacmias Benedetta, Gerhard Alexander, Langheinrich Tobias, Ducharme Simon, Santana Isabel, Tartaglia Maria Carmela, Masellis Mario, de Mendonça Alexandre, Rowe James B, Graff Caroline, Moreno Fermin, Synofzik Matthis, Borroni Barbara, Sanchez-Valle Raquel, Rademakers Rosa, Brushaber Danielle, Forsberg Leah K, Heuer Hilary W, Kantarci Kejal, Kolander Tyler, Mester Carly, Boeve Bradley F, Boxer Adam L, Rosen Howard J, Lee Suzee E, Rohrer Jonathan D, Andrews Tallulah S, Finger Elizabeth C
revue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
resume: C9orf72 encodes a protein that is important for both typical neurodevelopment and homeostatic processes across the lifespan. Pathogenic C9orf72 repeat expansions constitute the most common genetic cause of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD). Collectively, preclinical models and clinical neuroimaging studies have observed smaller thalamic volumes in C9orf72 -associated FTLD, including in asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 repeat expansion carriers across 18 to 30 years old, supportive of potential neurodevelopmental origins. However, it is unknown whether asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers demonstrate volume differences in specific thalamic nuclei, as reported in older asymptomatic carriers and symptomatic patients; if so, normative transcriptomic patterns could reveal relevant neurodevelopmental and/or FTLD-related neurodegenerative processes. This study investigated volumetric MRI differences of the thalamic nuclei in asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers, and examined spatial associations with normative thalamic transcriptomics from 8 weeks post-conception through middle age. Young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers ( n =72) and non-carriers ( n =48) were enrolled in the Frontotemporal Dementia Prevention Initiative across Europe, Canada, and the USA (ages: 18-30 years; sex: 57% female). Spatial associations between young adult thalamic nuclei volumes and normative transcriptomics from the Allen Human Brain Atlas were examined using complementary data-driven and hypothesis-driven approaches. Spatial expression patterns of transcripts of interest were characterized across prenatal and postnatal neurodevelopment using BrainSpan data. Smaller volumes of the pulvinar, mediodorsal, and lateral nuclei were observed in young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers. These nuclei showed higher normative expression of transcripts involved concurrently in neurodevelopmental and C9orf72 -associated FTLD neurodegenerative processes (including lysosomal, autophagic, and small GTPase functions), and lower normative expression of CALB1 , a marker of prenatal human thalamic development. Normative expression of CALB2 (another human thalamic development marker) yielded positive correlations with C9orf72 across prenatal development to adulthood. These findings identify candidate transcripts that may provide insight into the molecular architecture leading to smaller thalamic nuclei volumes in C9orf72 -associated FTLD.

titre: A foundation model for brain organoid network dynamics uncovers intrinsic computation and convergent disease phenotypes.
titre_fr: A foundation model for brain organoid network dynamics uncovers intrinsic computation and convergent disease phenotypes.
auteurs: Schweiger Hunter E, Robbins Ash, Hernandez Sebastian, Moreno-Ochando Avelina, Cline Isabel, Doganyigit Kivilcim, Mouzaya Matilda, Hussain Kamran, Pang Zhiping P, Duan Jubao, Salama Sofie R, Pollen Alex A, Bhaduri Aparna, Haussler David, Teodorescu Mircea, Mostajo-Radji Mohammed A
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: Brain organoids develop self-organizing neural networks that can be used to model neurodevelopment and disease. Here we introduce PULSE, a foundation model developed using over 900 hours of high-density microelectrode array recordings of in vitro and ex vivo neural tissue. We show that this single model can address two open questions: how disease-associated variants alter network development, and how naive circuits encode information. PULSE revealed accelerated network maturation in held-out human 16p11.2-deletion organoids. It also revealed a change in network coordination shared with SHANK3 deficiency. Because organoids develop without sensory input, they let us ask how circuits encode information before any representation is learned. Closed-loop control of a virtual inverted pendulum engaged existing spontaneous activity patterns rather than creating new ones. PULSE provides a common reference frame for neural circuits across genotypes, protocols and tasks.

titre: Adolescent prodromal phenotypes of psychiatric disorders: insights from a novel DISC1-perturbed monkey model.
titre_fr: Adolescent prodromal phenotypes of psychiatric disorders: insights from a novel DISC1-perturbed monkey model.
auteurs: Lan Ziguo, Onoe Hirotaka, Tsukiyama Tomoyuki, Iwatani Chizuru, Chen Chih-Yang, Okita Keisuke, Ishizuka Koko, Endo Ryo, Nakai Risako, Imamura Keiko, Hikishima Keigo, Tsuchiya Hideaki, Nakaya Masataka, Fang Yang, Kobayashi Atsushi, Shinto Yuta, Yamaguchi Reona, Matsunaga Mami, Oe Kengo, Omori Koichi, Ozeki Yuji, Tomoda Toshifumi, Miura Kenichiro, Urayama Shin-Ichi, Oishi Naoya, Okada Tomohisa, Tanaka Motomasa, Inoue Haruhisa, Takahashi Jun, Sawa Akira, Isa Tadashi
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: Neurodevelopmental deficits frequently lead to mild but significant adolescent social and cognitive changes, representing prodromal manifestations of adult-onset psychiatric disorders in a cross-disease manner. Although experimental medicine utilizes animal models to address the mechanisms, rodent brains lack critical structures for human higher brain functions such as the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. To fill this translational gap, we generated monkeys with an impaired DISC1 gene locus, targeting the multifunctional protein essential for neurodevelopment and involved in transdiagnostic mental health risks. Here we analyze the F0 animals by minimizing mosaicism. At ages equivalent to human adolescence, these monkeys exhibited blunted responsiveness to social stimuli and increased internal drives, mirroring altered social behaviors in the prodromal stage in humans. Resting-state functional MRI data indicated disrupted global functional connectivity and reorganization of network topology, marked by a shift in the dominance of brain hubs from prefrontal regions to sensory areas. This primate model provides a unique platform for studying psychiatric disorders, such as schizophrenia, across the developmental trajectory.

titre: A human model of the neurodevelopmental metabolic shift.
titre_fr: A human model of the neurodevelopmental metabolic shift.
auteurs: Pettit Sydney N, Kornfeld Ariella T, Morales Celeste, Meffert Mollie K
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: The neurodevelopmental metabolic shift transitions the metabolic pathways used by neurons to generate energy in order to critically support survival, growth, and functional maturation. To better understand metabolic regulation during human neuronal development and to facilitate the study of early neurodevelopmental disorders impacting this time window, establishing a combination of effective human model systems will be required. We report that a streamlined strategy using the genetic induction of neuronal differentiation by NGN2 expression recapitulates hallmarks of metabolic reprogramming associated with neurodevelopment. The approach is refined to increase the uniformity of differentiation, allowing reproducible high-throughput assessments. We validate appropriate readouts of metabolic function, including gene expression, cellular respiration, and mitochondrial morphology, which can be combined to present a cohesive assessment of metabolic status and reliance on oxidative phosphorylation relative to glycolysis. Collectively, the strategy presented will enhance the ability of investigators to gather foundational and disease-related insights into regulatory mechanisms of the metabolic shift critical to successful neuronal differentiation. Establishes a model of the neurodevelopmental metabolic shift using human i <sup>3</sup> Neurons Characterizes metabolic correlates across neuronal differentiationDemonstrates strategies to assess cellular metabolism and bioenergetics in hPSCs and neuronsProvides a uniform system to probe metabolic deficiencies in neurological disorders. Several approaches to investigate human neurodevelopmental metabolic reprogramming have been previously reported. However, prior strategies have largely relied on extrinsic factors to provide neurodevelopmental cues, which can impact the uniformity of differentiation as well as being costly, time-consuming, and often technically challenging. As impairments impacting cellular respiration impede proper neuronal development and metabolic deficiencies have been linked to neurodegenerative, neuropsychiatric, and neurodevelopmental disorders, there is a need for efficient and robust models to investigate these early developmental mechanisms. Here, we report a strategy, incorporating an established neuronal differentiation model using induction of stably integrated Neurogenin-2 (NGN2) for rapid generation of excitatory neurons (i <sup>3</sup> Neurons), which we demonstrate can synchronously recapitulate changes associated with the neurodevelopmental metabolic shift.

titre: Effects of maternal exposure to 2,6-dichloro-1,4-benzoquinone during pregnancy and lactation on the gut microbiota and neurodevelopment in offspring rats.
titre_fr: Effects of maternal exposure to 2,6-dichloro-1,4-benzoquinone during pregnancy and lactation on the gut microbiota and neurodevelopment in offspring rats.
auteurs: Gao Zihui, Liu Ting, He Ziqiao, Zhang Xu, Chen Xin, Sun Lanchao, Cong Yan, Kou Jingwen, Yang Shuran, Li Jinhua
resume: 2,6-dichloro-1,4-benzoquinone (DCBQ), as an emerging drinking water disinfection byproduct, has been widely detected in drinking water and pose potential risks. However, there are relatively few reports on their potential neurodevelopmental toxicity, especially the lack of in vivo studies as the most direct evidence. A rat model was established for the entire gestation and lactation period to study the neurodevelopmental toxicity of DCBQ in offspring rats, through evaluating gut microbiota, neurotransmitters and neurobehaviors. Maternal rats were administered with DCBQ at 0.5, 5, and 50 mg/kg body weight via gavage throughout gestation and lactation. Our results showed that maternal DCBQ exposure induced prolonged neural reflex behavior, decreased motor activity, and increased anxiety-like behavior in offspring rats. And the levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factors and neurotransmitters, especially glutamate and dopamine, in serum and hippocampus were significantly decreased in offspring rats after maternal DCBQ exposure. Maternal DCBQ exposure induced imbalance of intestinal microbiota in a gender-specific way. In addition, maternal DCBQ exposure induced significant changes of 123 metabolites, affecting multiple metabolic pathways, such as mTOR pathway. In particular, the altered gut microbiota showed strong associations with altered metabolites, neurotransmitters and neurobehaviors after maternal DCBQ exposure. Our findings suggest that maternal DCBQ exposure may impair neurodevelopment and disrupt gut microbiota and fecal metabolite profiles of offspring rats, indicating a potential gut microbiota-metabolome-neurochemical link. Our study highlights the importance of evaluating the neurodevelopmental toxicity of disinfection byproducts in future.

titre: SHANK3 drives abnormal neurodevelopment in iPSC-derived 2D and 3D brain models of Phelan-McDermid Syndrome.
titre_fr: SHANK3 drives abnormal neurodevelopment in iPSC-derived 2D and 3D brain models of Phelan-McDermid Syndrome.
auteurs: Gao Meng, Huo Meng, Zhang Hongxia, Wang Xingcui
resume: Phelan-McDermid Syndrome (PMDS) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by 22q13.3 deletion involving SHANK3. While SHANK3 is critical for synapses, its role in early human neurodevelopment remains elusive. Here, we generated induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived 2D neuronal cultures and 3D cerebral organoids from two twin Phelan-McDermid syndrome patients with a 1.7 Mb 22q13 deletion encompassing SHANK3 gene. PMDS organoids showed reduced volume due to impaired neural progenitor cells (NPCs) proliferation. PMDS NPCs exhibited biased differentiation with decreased excitatory neurons but increased GFAP<sup>+</sup> astroglia and GABAergic neurons. PMDS neurons displayed simplified morphology, reduced synapse density and diminished excitability. Importantly, lentiviral-mediated SHANK3 overexpression largely rescued these defects. Our findings identify SHANK3 as a key regulator of early neurodevelopment and provide mechanistic insights into PMDS pathogenesis.

titre: Isolated Hyperchlorhidrosis Caused by Novel Biallelic CA12 Variants Mimicking Pseudohypoaldosteronism.
titre_fr: Isolated Hyperchlorhidrosis Caused by Novel Biallelic CA12 Variants Mimicking Pseudohypoaldosteronism.
auteurs: Kahraman Hülya, Durmaz Durmus, Gunay Aylin, Eltan Mehmet, Güran Tülay
resume: Isolated hyperchlorhidrosis (HYCHL; OMIM 143860) is caused by biallelic CA12 variants encoding carbonic anhydrase XII (CA XII), a transmembrane enzyme that mediates sodium and chloride reabsorption in sweat glands, leading to excessive salt loss. Clinically, HYCHL presents in infancy with recurrent hyponatremic dehydration secondary to excessive salt loss, often mimicking pseudohypoaldosteronism (PHA) or cystic fibrosis (CF). A 5-month-old girl presented with irritability, lethargy, poor feeding, severe hyponatremia (110 mEq/L), and hyperkalemia (7.1 mEq/L). Congenital adrenal hyperplasia was excluded by endocrine evaluation. Markedly elevated plasma renin activity and aldosterone initially suggested PHA; however, low urinary sodium excretion during hyponatremia indicated an extrarenal source of salt loss. Three further episodes occurred, predominantly during summer. Although the parents consistently reported a salty taste of the infant's skin. Clinical exome sequencing identified two unreported compound heterozygous CA12 missense variants, c.823C>T p.(Arg275Trp) and c.694C>A p.(Pro232Thr), with parental testing confirming trans inheritance. No pathogenic variants were detected in CFTR or PHA-associated genes. By 19 months of age, the patient had remained free of hyponatremic episodes for nine months without disease-specific treatment, with normal growth and neurodevelopment. This case expands the mutational spectrum of isolated hyperchlorhidrosis by identifying two unreported variants in CA12 and highlights the importance of considering isolated hyperchlorhidrosis in infants with recurrent salt-wasting when routine evaluation does not support PHA or CF.

titre: Is histone H2B deubiquitylation via ATXN7L3-dependent enzymes a new mechanism disrupted in neurodevelopmental disorders?
titre_fr: Is histone H2B deubiquitylation via ATXN7L3-dependent enzymes a new mechanism disrupted in neurodevelopmental disorders?
auteurs: Anand Abhinav, Bustos Francisco
resume: Neurodevelopmental disorders are lifelong debilitating conditions that affect cognition and originate during embryonic development. Being heterogeneous and with a variety of etiologies, most of these disorders have no targeted treatment or cures, due to our lack of knowledge on the underlying molecular mechanisms disrupted in their pathogenesis. An emerging epigenetic mechanism recently associated with neurodevelopmental disorders is ubiquitylation of histone H2B. This posttranslational modification controls gene expression during neurodevelopment, where histone H2B ubiquitylation levels are tightly regulated by multiple deubiquitylase protein complexes ensuring correct gene expression. Components of deubiquitylase complexes regulating histone H2B ubiquitylation are the protein scaffolds ATXN7L3 and ENY2, and the deubiquitylating enzymes USP22, USP27X, and USP51. Recent clinical studies have highlighted a potential role of H2B ubiquitylation in human neurodevelopment, including the identification of neurodevelopmental disorders associated with gene variants in the ATXN7L3, USP27X and USP51 genes. Here, we summarize our knowledge of the functions of deubiquitylase complexes that regulate histone H2B ubiquitylation and their components in neurodevelopment, and describe ATXN7L3, USP27X, and USP51-associated disorders, proposing future directions on the required research on their fundamental biology that could lead to targeted therapies.

titre: Network analysis of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder traits and mental health indicators in Brazilian adults.
titre_fr: Network analysis of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder traits and mental health indicators in Brazilian adults.
auteurs: Quintanilha Daniel de Freitas, Pereira Diogo Fagundes, Abramov Dimitri Marques
resume: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by behavioral traits such as inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity, has been widely associated with mental health impairments. However, the presence of these traits alone does not determine diagnosis, as they must also cause significant functional impairment for the individual to fulfill diagnostic criteria. Therefore, this study aimed at exploring how ADHD traits are associated with mental health indicators in general population adults regardless of whether participants met full diagnostic criteria for the disorder. The Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS) was used to screen ADHD traits in an online survey that also addressed mental health indicators such as excessive preoccupation, lack of meaning in life and substance use. titre: Mixture of Plasticizer Chemicals and Child Intelligence: A Weight-of-Evidence and Meta-Analysis-Informed Bayesian Approach in a Cohort with Improved Exposure Assessment.
titre_fr: Mixture of Plasticizer Chemicals and Child Intelligence: A Weight-of-Evidence and Meta-Analysis-Informed Bayesian Approach in a Cohort with Improved Exposure Assessment.
auteurs: Mustieles Vicente, Rolland Matthieu, Pérez-Cantero Ainhoa, Bayat Sam, Valmary-Degano Séverine, Thomsen Cathrine, Sakhi Amrit K, Slama Rémy, Guichardet Karine, Philippat Claire
resume: Early-life exposure to plasticizer chemicals can affect child neurodevelopment. However, accurately characterizing exposure to these short-lived chemicals remains challenging. To address knowledge gaps, we examined the association between prenatal and infant exposure to a plasticizer mixture and child intelligence quotient (IQ) in a cohort with improved exposure assessment, informing the statistical analysis using the existing toxicological and epidemiological evidence. This work included 380 mother-infant pairs from the SEPAGES study, a French new-generation population-based birth cohort recruited between 2014 and 2018. Sixteen phenols and phthalate metabolites were quantified in pools of multiple urine samples collected at four time points during pregnancy and infancy (up to 21/week). Children's IQ was assessed using the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence at age 3. A structured review of the toxicological and epidemiological evidence was conducted to prioritize the chemicals with the highest weight of evidence (WoE) to be analyzed as a mixture. Meta-analyses of the retrieved epidemiological studies were performed and used as priors in single-chemical Bayesian regression models. Of 1189 references screened, we retrieved data from 30 toxicological and 57 epidemiological studies supporting the prioritization of bisphenol A and S, diethylhexyl phthalate metabolites, monoethyl phthalate (MEP), mono-n-butyl phthalate (MnBP), and mono-isobutyl phthalate (MiBP). Each quartile increase in maternal third-trimester concentrations of the high-WoE plasticizer mixture was associated with decreased full-scale (β: -2.86; 95% Credibility Interval, CrI: -5.05, -0.91), visual-spatial (-2.79; 95% CrI: -5.39, -0.82) and verbal (-1.95; 95% CrI: -3.84, 0.00) child IQ scores. Bayesian single-chemical models informed by meta-analysis-based priors also found that third-trimester concentrations of four of the six prioritized chemicals (bisphenol A, MEP, MnBP, and MiBP) were associated with reduced IQ scores. This novel evidence-based framework increased the biological plausibility and external validity of results, supporting that pregnancy exposure to a mixture of common plasticizers affects child IQ and represents a public health concern. The findings underscore the need to protect fetuses and children from plastic-associated chemicals and regulate them by class.

titre: Bilateral, Asynchronous, Inferior Shoulder Dislocation in a Multidisabled Patient: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
titre_fr: Bilateral, Asynchronous, Inferior Shoulder Dislocation in a Multidisabled Patient: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
auteurs: Ali Fawzi E, Ali Yasmina F
resume: Inferior glenohumeral dislocation, or luxatio erecta humeri (LEH), is an exceptionally rare injury accounting for approximately 0.5% of all shoulder dislocations. It typically results from high-energy trauma through hyperabduction or direct axial loading, forcing the humeral head inferiorly and locking the arm in abduction. While unilateral presentation is rare, bilateral occurrence is extraordinary. Diagnostic or therapeutic delays can cause severe, permanent neurovascular and musculoskeletal sequelae. A 42-year-old male with profound neurodevelopmental disabilities - including cerebral palsy, intellectual disability, total blindness, and epilepsy - residing in a long-term care facility presented with an acute right LEH. Attempted closed reduction at an orthopedic center was unsuccessful, and the patient was discharged against medical advice without definitive intervention. Four years later, at age 46, the patient presented with a neglected, chronic left LEH. Due to the chronic, fixed nature of the bilateral injuries, the dislocations were deemed un-reducible, resulting in a profound and permanent accumulation of orthopedic disability. Managing LEH in patients with severe developmental disabilities presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Cognitive and communication barriers often cause diagnostic overshadowing, leading to missed or severely delayed presentations. Furthermore, management is frequently complicated by patient uncooperativeness, high-risk anesthesia profiles, and increased risks of operative failure.
