titre: Maternal serum retinol, vitamin K, and ferritin profiles during pregnancy, gestational diabetes mellitus, and offspring neurodevelopment: a prospective case-control study.
titre_fr: Maternal serum retinol, vitamin K, and ferritin profiles during pregnancy, gestational diabetes mellitus, and offspring neurodevelopment: a prospective case-control study.
auteurs: Jiang Changke, Pang Yulu, Yu Jinfeng, Yan Shiling, Liu Xiaoqing, Li Tingyu
resume: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with adverse offspring neurodevelopment, but the role of maternal circulating biomarkers-specifically serum retinol, serum vitamin K, and serum ferritin-in relation to offspring neurodevelopmental performance remains unclear. This study examined trimester-specific levels of these biomarkers in GDM vs. participants without GDM and their associations with infant neurodevelopmental outcomes at 12 months. In this prospective case-control study, 240 mother-infant pairs who were enrolled during pregnancy, classified according to GDM status after OGTT screening, and followed through delivery and offspring assessment at 12 months. Maternal serum retinol, serum vitamin K, and serum ferritin were measured in each trimester. Offspring neurodevelopment was assessed using the Gesell Developmental Schedules, with suboptimal neurodevelopmental performance defined as Total Gesell Score < 85. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for maternal age, pre-pregnancy BMI, years of formal education, gestational age at delivery, infant sex, and maternal HbA1c. Linear regression models included the same covariates together with maternal CRP and IL-6. Participants with GDM had significantly lower serum retinol and serum vitamin K concentrations and higher serum ferritin concentrations across all trimesters compared with control participants (all p < 0.001). Offspring in the GDM group had lower Total Gesell Scores (90.4 vs. 95.9, p < 0.001) and higher prevalence of Total Gesell Score < 85 (72.5% vs. 31.7%, p < 0.001) compared with offspring in the control group. Although the mean differences were statistically significant, the group means remained within broadly similar interpretive ranges, and the < 85 threshold includes borderline scores. In fully adjusted logistic regression, higher serum ferritin was independently associated with increased odds of suboptimal neurodevelopmental performance (OR = 1.22 per 10 ng/mL, 95% CI: 1.004-1.34, p = 0.036), while vitamin A and K were not significant. An exploratory composite Nutritional Risk Score of 1, indicating the presence of any one of the three prespecified sample-specific quartile-defined biomarker categories (serum retinol in the lowest quartile, serum vitamin K in the lowest quartile, or serum ferritin in the highest quartile), was associated with a nearly five-fold higher odds of suboptimal neurodevelopmental performance (OR = 4.92, 95% CI: 1.65-14.64, p = 0.004; however, the association was not monotonic across higher score categories. Linear regression confirmed ferritin as a significant negative predictor of Total Gesell Score (β = -0.05, p = 0.003). In participants with GDM, higher maternal ferritin-but not vitamins A or K-is independently associated with offspring suboptimal neurodevelopmental performance. A simple composite nutritional risk score may help identify at-risk infants. These findings support monitoring ferritin and considering overall nutritional risk beyond glycaemic control in GDM care.

titre: Phase Separation Contributes to Pathogenicity for Nonsense Mediated Decay-Escaping Variant Alleles.
titre_fr: Phase Separation Contributes to Pathogenicity for Nonsense Mediated Decay-Escaping Variant Alleles.
auteurs: Xu Jiaoyang, Schmidt Jacob, Campbell Amy, Bozkurt-Yozgatli Tugce, Egab Iman, Mestroni Luisa, Taylor Matthew, Posey Jennifer E, Gibbs Richard A, Boerwinkle Eric, de Vries Paul, Morrison Alanna, Yi S Stephen, Shaw Chad A, Carvalho Claudia M B, Lupski James R, Jagannathan Sujatha, Timucin Emel, Coban-Akdemir Zeynep
revue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
resume: Premature termination codons (PTCs) usually trigger nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), but PTCs in the final exon or within 50 base pairs of the last exon-exon junction escape surveillance and can yield stable truncated or altered proteins whose disease mechanisms remain poorly defined. Screening pathogenic and likely pathogenic ClinVar variants, we identified 134 autosomal dominant disease genes enriched for NMD-escape frameshift (N=94) or stopgain (N=64) variants. At the gene level, these genes were indistinguishable from length-matched controls in dosage sensitivity, interaction-network centrality and tissue specificity; only the stopgain class showed greater overlap between its NMD-escape regions and protein-protein interaction interfaces (log-odds ratio +1.22). Comparing pathogenic with benign variants in the same genes, pathogenic alleles truncated further upstream and therefore spanned more post-translational modification sites, nuclear localization signals, protein-protein interaction interfaces and disordered regions; after adjusting for truncation position, pathogenic stopgain variants still overlapped interaction interfaces and Pfam domains more often than benign ones. The two classes remodelled the C-terminus differently: pathogenic frameshift alleles generated novel tails that were less positively charged with a higher phase-separating disordered-region fraction in their divergent segment (q = 0.028), whereas pathogenic stopgain alleles removed longer, more disordered and interaction-prone C-terminal sequence, leaving a truncated protein enriched in arginine and positive charge. NMD-escape disease genes were over-represented among neurodevelopmental-disorder risk genes (35 observed versus 25 expected; odds ratio 1.6, P = 1.3 × 10⁻²), and an NMD-escape truncating variant in RARB (microphthalmia, syndromic 12; MIM 615524) formed aberrant condensates in cells. Together, these results define NMD-escape alleles as a mechanistically distinct class of dominant disease variants in which remodelling of interaction-prone, phase-separation-competent C-terminal sequence, rather than transcript loss, drives pathogenicity.

titre: Exploratory brain-wide analyses predicting binge drinking: A machine learning and targeted causal inference pipeline in two adolescent cohorts.
titre_fr: Exploratory brain-wide analyses predicting binge drinking: A machine learning and targeted causal inference pipeline in two adolescent cohorts.
auteurs: Visontay Rachel, Byrne Hollie R, Devine Emma K, Sunderland Matthew, Fan Lei, Wen Wei, Perica Maria I, Tapert Susan, Clark Duncan B, Nooner Kate, Afzali Kamran, Squeglia Lindsay M, Mewton Louise
revue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
resume: A sizeable literature has found that neuroanatomical differences predict alcohol use outcomes in adolescence. However, due possibly to small samples and inconsistent/limited methodologies, it is still unclear which specific morphometric features are most predictive and if they are also causally implicated in binge drinking onset. To differentially predict abstinence from binge drinking by age 16-17, a SuperLearner ensemble algorithm was fit to structural and diffusion MRI features at age 9-10 in the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development cohort (ABCD). A separate model was fit using the National Consortium on Alcohol and NeuroDevelopment in Adolescence (NCANDA), in which the MRI predictors were measured later (ages 12-17) but the developmental outcome (binge drinking by age 18) remained similar. The top ten predictors were extracted from each model, and the causal role of these features scrutinised using targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE). Predictive performance in ABCD was poor (AUC=.585) but was stronger in NCANDA (AUC=.695). There was little overlap in predictive feature rankings between the cohorts. TMLE did not reveal a causal effect of the top ten morphological predictors on binge drinking in either cohort. No evidence was found for causal contributions of any discrete macrostructural/microstructural brain feature in late childhood or adolescence to binge drinking. Using more sophisticated metrics of brain structure and function may yield better insights. Adding to previous evidence from youth cohorts, neuroanatomy may have greater predictive value for identifying those at risk of adolescent binge drinking when measured in adolescence, rather than late childhood.

titre: Systematic Functional Interrogation of Neurodevelopmental Disorder Risk Variants.
titre_fr: Systematic Functional Interrogation of Neurodevelopmental Disorder Risk Variants.
auteurs: Gomez Alejandro, McAfee Jessica C, Min Hyunggyu, Ulloa Avila Tatiana, Jones Sean, Bell Jessica L, Gao Yangzhenyu, Hu Ellen, Li Haoyue, Lee Sool, Sadovnik Ratchell, Fan Zheng, Yang Nan, Beltran Adriana S, Won Hyejung
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) are highly polygenic, yet the functional consequences of most associated non-coding variants remain unclear. We used a massively parallel reporter assay (MPRA) to test 727 NDD-associated non-coding variants in human neural progenitors, identifying 38 expression-modulating variants (emVars) with regulatory activity. These emVars were predicted to alter transcription factor binding motifs linked to neurodevelopmental signaling and cellular metabolism. We mapped emVars to candidate target genes using expression quantitative trait loci and activity-by-contact (ABC) models. We then used CRISPR droplet sequencing (CROP-seq) in human pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons to identify endogenous target genes and characterize their downstream transcriptional effects. CROP-seq preferentially supported ABC predictions, identified additional regulatory relationships, and revealed convergence on developmentally regulated programs involving neuronal connectivity, synaptic function, and mitochondrial biology. Together, these results connect NDD risk variants to endogenous target genes and shared neurodevelopmental transcriptional programs.

titre: Exposure to Maternal Pre- and Postnatal Psychological Distress: Associations With Brain Structure in 5-Year-Old Children.
titre_fr: Exposure to Maternal Pre- and Postnatal Psychological Distress: Associations With Brain Structure in 5-Year-Old Children.
auteurs: Pulli Elmo P, Audah Hilyatushalihah K, Svensk Amira, Eskola Eeva, Nordenswan Elisabeth, Rosberg Aylin, Alvajärvi Silja, Juntunen Pauliina, Wigley Isabella L C Mariani, Kumpulainen Venla, Silver Eero, Copeland Anni, Saukko Ekaterina, Merisaari Harri, Korja Riikka, Kataja Eeva-Leena, Karlsson Linnea
resume: Maternal mental health is an important contributor to child neurodevelopment. While there are multiple studies on prenatal exposure, early postnatal exposure has received little attention in neuroimaging research. Five-year-old children (n = 161) were recruited from the FinnBrain Birth Cohort study. Maternal distress was assessed using questionnaires on depressive and anxiety symptoms at 14, 24, and 34 gestational weeks and postnatally at 3, 6, and 24 months. T1-weighted structural images were processed using a voxel-based morphometry pipeline to map associations between maternal distress exposure and regional gray matter (GM) volumes. Whole-brain voxel-wise general linear models were used, accounting for potential confounders. Additionally, a latent class mixed model approach was used to model longitudinal trajectories of distress exposure. We found widespread associations between maternal postpartum distress symptoms and offspring brain morphology. Postnatal distress at 3 months was negatively associated with GM volumes in the left supplementary motor cortex, right cerebellum/fusiform gyrus, and left anterior insula/frontal operculum. Postnatal distress at 6 months was positively associated with GM volumes in the right cuneus and lingual gyrus, right insula/operculum, and right inferior occipital gyrus, while distress at 24 months was negatively associated with GM volumes in the left inferior/middle frontal gyrus. There were no structural brain differences between the latent classes. This study provides support for hypotheses proposing that early-life exposure to maternal distress can influence the structural development of the brain. It highlights the role of the early postnatal period and calls for further research into this so far overlooked period and the developmental pathways that explain these associations.

titre: Narrowing margins: exploring how MeCP2 deficiency degrades precision, timing, and adaptability in motor circuits.
titre_fr: Narrowing margins: exploring how MeCP2 deficiency degrades precision, timing, and adaptability in motor circuits.
auteurs: Dant Ayden Matthew, Namdarzadeh Behnaz, Pandkar Madhura R, Gonzalez Alvaro Rodriguez, Subedi Suresh, Byiers Breanne J, Joshi Amit S, Lamichhane Rajan, Lau Billy You Bun, Merbler Alyssa, McCord Rachel Patton, Phillips Mary L, Krishnan Keerthi
resume: The X-linked gene methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MECP2) is a critical epigenetic regulator with important roles in neuronal gene regulation and neuronal plasticity during sensitive periods of development and beyond. Mutations in MECP2 result in Rett syndrome (RTT), a neurodevelopmental disorder predominantly affecting females. Motor dysfunction is among the most consistently disrupted domains in RTT. The literature on this domain is under-synthesized and a cohesive framework to explain the neurobiological underpinnings of the varied motor phenotypes by sex, allele and age is lacking. In this review, we focus on the literature on motor dysfunction in RTT and propose a convergent-constraint model, in which MeCP2 loss compromises mitochondrial capacity, GPCR signaling, and calcium handling in high-energy-demand neuronal populations, with perineuronal nets acting as a structural node that reinforces this constraint. This model accounts for a recurring pattern across the intervention literature: genetic, viral, pharmacological, and behavioral approaches consistently produce partial, overlapping rescue rather than full correction, consistent with circuits operating below capacity rather than missing a single essential component. We identify testable hypotheses and gaps in the field, including the temporal sequence of these constraints and the absence of motor-specific mechanistic data for current and emerging therapies, that offer potential avenues for combinatorial therapeutic targets for RTT.
resume_fr: The X-linked gene methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MECP2) is a critical epigenetic regulator with important roles in neuronal gene regulation and neuronal plasticity during sensitive periods of development and beyond. The literature on this domain is under-synthesized and a cohesive framework to explain the neurobiological underpinnings of the varied motor phenotypes by sex, allele and age is lacking. In this review, we focus on the literature on motor dysfunction in RTT and propose a convergent-constraint model, in which MeCP2 loss compromises mitochondrial capacity, GPCR signaling, and calcium handling in high-energy-demand neuronal populations, with perineuronal nets acting as a structural node that reinforces this constraint. This model accounts for a recurring pattern across the intervention literature: genetic, viral, pharmacological, and behavioral approaches consistently produce partial, overlapping rescue rather than full correction, consistent with circuits operating below capacity rather than missing a single essential component. We identify testable hypotheses and gaps in the field, including the temporal sequence of these constraints and the absence of motor-specific mechanistic data for current and emerging therapies, that offer potential avenues for combinatorial therapeutic targets for RTT.

titre: Pre-pregnancy maternal steatotic liver disease and offspring neurodevelopmental disorders: a nationwide cohort study.
titre_fr: Pre-pregnancy maternal steatotic liver disease and offspring neurodevelopmental disorders: a nationwide cohort study.
auteurs: Chung Goh Eun, Cho Anna, Kim Da Hye, Yu Su Jong, Kim Yoon Jun, Yoon Jung-Hwan, Han Kyungdo, Cho Eun Ju
resume: Maternal metabolic health before pregnancy is increasingly linked to offspring neurodevelopment, but metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), the most common chronic liver disease worldwide, has not been examined in this context. We investigated whether maternal steatotic liver disease (SLD) phenotypes identified before pregnancy are associated with offspring neurodevelopmental disorders. In this nationwide Korean cohort of 778,401 mother-child pairs, maternal pre-pregnancy phenotypes (no SLD, MASLD, and alcohol-involved SLD) were defined using the fatty liver index (FLI), cardiometabolic criteria, alcohol intake, and diagnostic codes. Offspring were followed through 2022 for registration-confirmed intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and for claims-based attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Cox regression estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with and without adjustment for body mass index (BMI), diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia in addition to other covariates. Without this adjustment, MASLD was associated with intellectual disability (HR 1.72, 95% CI 1.52-1.96), ASD (1.42, 1.22-1.66), and ADHD (1.22, 1.15-1.30). After this adjustment, HRs were 1.05 (0.89-1.24), 1.18 (0.98-1.44), and 1.09 (1.01-1.17), respectively. The ADHD estimate was smaller when at least two separate claims were required (1.06, 0.98-1.15). Estimates for alcohol-involved SLD were imprecise. Pre-pregnancy MASLD was associated with higher risks of offspring neurodevelopmental disorders in analyses without adjustment for maternal BMI and metabolic conditions. These associations were substantially attenuated after adjustment; a modest ADHD association remained only under the least stringent claims-based definition and should be interpreted with caution. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant confirmation with pregnancy-specific exposure assessment and sibling-comparison designs.

titre: Narrative Review of the Advantages and Clinical Data to Support Evening Dosing for Delayed-Release and Extended-Release Methylphenidate for the Treatment of Attention-deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Prescriber Perspective.
titre_fr: Narrative Review of the Advantages and Clinical Data to Support Evening Dosing for Delayed-Release and Extended-Release Methylphenidate for the Treatment of Attention-deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Prescriber Perspective.
auteurs: Brashier Karah, Peppers Katherine H, Shafer Stephanie
revue: Journal of pediatric health care : official publication of National Association of Pediatric Nurse Associates & Practitioners
resume: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder typically treated first-line with stimulants. This review provides guidance to prescribers by presenting an overview of available treatment options, along with clinical and real-world evidence for delayed-release and extended-release methylphenidate (DR/ER-MPH). Traditional long-acting stimulants differ in duration of effect, leading to gaps in symptom control during the afternoon and evening. DR/ER-MPH is a unique treatment option, administered in the evening and absorbed in the colon, producing a gradual rise and fall in stimulant concentration and a dose-dependent duration of effect, making it a good option for patients across the lifespan. The safety profile of DR/ER-MPH is consistent with other methylphenidate formulations. With the guidance provided here, prescribers can ensure optimal outcomes when transitioning patients with ADHD to DR/ER-MPH treatment.

titre: Effects of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation on Core Symptoms and Sleep Disturbances in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
titre_fr: Effects of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation on Core Symptoms and Sleep Disturbances in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
auteurs: Wang Mingchen, Yang Meimei
resume: This meta-analysis was designed to determine whether transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) confers measurable benefits for selected behavioral features of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and for sleep problems in pediatric ASD populations. A comprehensive literature retrieval was conducted across eight electronic databases-PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Embase, CNKI, CBM, VIP, and Wanfang-covering the period from each database's inception through June 1, 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) in patients with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The methodological quality of the included trials was appraised using the Cochrane Risk of Bias assessment instrument. Quantitative synthesis was performed with RevMan 5.4 and Stata 17.0, following the PRISMA statement for systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Ultimately, seven studies qualified for inclusion in this systematic review. Pooled analyses showed that tDCS was associated with lower ATEC scores (mean difference [MD] = -8.81, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -12.06 to -5.56, p < 0.00001), ABC scores (MD = -12.08, 95% CI: -21.75 to -2.41, p = 0.01), and CSHQ scores (MD = -4.95, 95% CI: -8.66 to -1.24, p = 0.009). However, no statistically significant difference was observed for CARS scores (MD = -1.12, 95% CI: -4.15 to 1.91, p = 0.47). tDCS, most commonly delivered at 1 mA over the DLPFC, was associated with improvements in some ASD-related behavioral outcomes; preliminary evidence also suggested a potential benefit for sleep disturbances, although this finding was based on only two low-certainty studies and warrants cautious interpretation.

titre: Optimizing Inpatient Care for Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Multidisciplinary and Sensory-Informed Approach.
titre_fr: Optimizing Inpatient Care for Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Multidisciplinary and Sensory-Informed Approach.
auteurs: Drewry Melissa, Gross Elise, Jakubowski Erin, Zalewski Kristina, Scheid Andrea
resume: Pediatric hospitalists continue to optimize inpatient care for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), their families, and caregivers. The unfamiliar and overstimulating hospital environment frequently heightens distress, contributing to challenging behaviors and resistance to medical care. This review explores multidisciplinary and sensory-informed approaches to deliver evidence-based, patient- and family-centered care for children with ASD. Evidence supports early identification of sensory needs through standardized screening and implementation of structured care pathways that continue through hospitalization. Key interventions include sensory toolkits, caregiver input, and specialized care teams. Utilizing principles of behavior analysis enables proactive communication instead of reactions to challenging situations. Procedural adaptations and expert pharmacologic treatment enhance care delivery. Despite implementation barriers, hospitals can reduce distress, improve safety, and foster more positive health care experiences for children with ASD in the least restrictive environments by improving staff education, strengthening interdisciplinary communication, and integrating family expertise into care planning.

titre: Effects of Zumba dance to enhance motor skills of children with autism spectrum disorder.
titre_fr: Effects of Zumba dance to enhance motor skills of children with autism spectrum disorder.
auteurs: Varghese Jensy, Naomi G Victoria
resume: Motor difficulties are common among children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and may affect participation in everyday activities. Structured physical activity incorporating rhythmic movement may provide an engaging approach to motor-skill development. This study evaluated the effect of a 12-week Zumba-based intervention on motor proficiency in children with ASD. Sixty children with ASD aged 6-12 years were assigned to an experimental Zumba group (n = 30) or a control group (n = 30). The experimental group participated in 45-minute Zumba sessions three times per week for 12 weeks. Motor proficiency was assessed before and after the intervention using the Bruininks-Oseretsky Test of Motor Proficiency (BOT-2). Within-group changes were examined using paired-samples t-tests, and baseline differences were examined using an independent-samples t-test. Baseline motor-proficiency scores did not differ significantly between the Zumba and control groups (6.83 ± 3.42 vs. 7.43 ± 1.59; t(58) = 0.870, p = .388). The Zumba group demonstrated a significant increase from 6.83 ± 3.42 to 14.83 ± 2.98, representing a mean improvement of 8.00 points (117.1%; t(29) = 23.597, p < .001). The control group also showed a significant but smaller increase from 7.43 ± 1.59 to 8.53 ± 1.28, corresponding to a mean improvement of 1.10 points (14.8%; t(29) = 5.674, p < .001). The reported within-group effect size for the experimental group was approximately 2.49. A 12-week Zumba program was associated with substantial improvement in motor proficiency among children with ASD. Larger controlled studies with blinded assessment and long-term follow-up are needed to establish intervention-specific and sustained effects.

titre: Innovating Early Autism Diagnosis: A Telemedicine Model in Primary Care for Children Under 3 Years.
titre_fr: Innovating Early Autism Diagnosis: A Telemedicine Model in Primary Care for Children Under 3 Years.
auteurs: Rea Corinna J, Hayes Makeyla, Cox Joanne E, Cortina Christopher, Gray Kathryn P, Lesch Kayla, Poirier Samantha, Chaves McDonald Anna
revue: Journal of developmental and behavioral pediatrics : JDBP
resume: Children with suspected autism spectrum disorder (ASD) currently experience significant delays before receiving a developmental evaluation, which in turn delays initiation of services. We aimed to implement and evaluate a novel telemedicine model for diagnosing ASD in children under 3 years at 2 primary care sites. Children under 3 years with a concern for ASD were referred to the program by their primary care providers. Families completed an adaptive behavior scale and a structured telemedicine observation administered by a trained program coordinator. A psychologist reviewed all materials and made a diagnosis of ASD if appropriate. Indeterminate cases were scheduled for in-person assessment. Results were sent to primary care providers, who gave feedback to families. Families were asked to complete a survey after evaluation. Between October 2022 and March 2024, 189 patients were evaluated and 146 diagnosed with ASD by telemedicine, whereas 38 required in-person assessment. The median time to evaluation was 32 days, and there was 99% diagnostic concordance among patients seen by a specialist. There were no disparities in time to evaluation by language, race, ethnicity, or insurance type. Overall, parents and providers gave positive feedback about the model, although almost two-thirds of parents expressed a preference for in-person assessment. In this primary care-based telemedicine autism diagnosis program patients under age 3 years were diagnosed quickly and accurately with ASD. However, families still expressed a preference for in-person evaluation. Future work should focus on how to improve acceptability while maintaining efficiency, and the impact of the program on the timing of service connectivity.

titre: Dance Interventions Designed by Allied Health Professionals to Improve Health-Related Outcomes of Children and Youth with Disabilities: A Scoping Review.
titre_fr: Dance Interventions Designed by Allied Health Professionals to Improve Health-Related Outcomes of Children and Youth with Disabilities: A Scoping Review.
auteurs: Yee Maria L, Pacey Verity, Clutterbuck Georgina L, Wen Eugeenia, Johnston Leanne M
resume: To systematically map the design, purpose, and outcomes of dance, circus, and physical theater programs designed by allied health professionals for children and youth with disabilities. Following PRISMA-scoping review guidelines, seven databases were searched up to April 2026 for studies published in peer-reviewed journals. Intervention design was reported using the "INgredients iN ArTs in hEalth" framework. Twenty studies were included, featuring ballet (n = 4), dance therapy (n = 4), Indian dance (n = 2), mixed dance styles (n = 5), adapted dance (n = 2), belly dance, hip hop, and tap (each n = 1). Participants ranged from 3 to 23 years of age. Seventy percent of studies focused on school-aged children with cerebral palsy, Down syndrome, and autism. Programs spanned 6-36 sessions (4-54 h). All studies reported improvements in physical outcome measures. Allied health professional designed dance programs may positively influence physical outcomes in children and youth with disabilities. Future research should expand on the scope of health conditions, include preschool children and older youth, and focus on higher quality studies that include standardized intervention reporting, address project sustainability, and participant-focused outcomes.

titre: Kinematic Features of Handwriting Speed: A Comparative Study of Autistic and Non-Autistic Youth.
titre_fr: Kinematic Features of Handwriting Speed: A Comparative Study of Autistic and Non-Autistic Youth.
auteurs: Orefice Camilla, Cardillo Ramona, D'Antrassi Pierluigi, Mammarella Irene C
revue: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
resume: Handwriting has received limited attention in Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), making systematic investigation crucial. Digital assessments enable deeper analysis of handwriting characteristics and challenges in autistic children and adolescents. This study examined kinematic predictors of handwriting speed in autistic individuals without intellectual disability compared to non-autistic peers. Two hundred and four participants (White ethnicity, 8-17 years, autistic = 68 [54 M], M<sub>age</sub> = 12.08 (2.42); non-autistic = 136 [96 M], M<sub>age</sub> = 11.97 (2.00), matched for age, IQ, handedness, and sex, completed a tablet-based sentence-copying task under maximum accuracy (MA) and speed (MS) conditions. Completion time and kinematic measures (path length, pressure, pen angle, and writing/total time ratio) were recorded. Autistic participants were slower than non-autistic peers in both conditions (p<sub>s</sub> ≤ 0.006, d<sub>s</sub> ≥ 0.47), with distinct kinematic profiles. In MA (pseudo R<sup>2</sup> = 0.41, p = 0.017), shorter completion time (CT) was linked to greater writing-time proportion for all participants (B = -0.09, p = 0.012), with higher pressure being associated to longer CT only in autism (B = -0.157, p = 0.021). In MS (pseudo R<sup>2</sup> = 0.40, p = 0.05), shorter CT related to larger handwriting (i.e., longer path length) in autism (B = 0.20, p < 0.001) and to greater writing-time proportion in the non-autistic group (B = -0.30, p < 0.001). Findings underscore the importance of handwriting in functional assessment and support the need for tailored educational accommodations for autistic students.

titre: Reduced hypoxanthine Ameliorates LPS-triggered autism-like stereotyped behaviors in intestinal Tlr4 knockout mice via the DRN ROS-5-HT axis.
titre_fr: Reduced hypoxanthine Ameliorates LPS-triggered autism-like stereotyped behaviors in intestinal Tlr4 knockout mice via the DRN ROS-5-HT axis.
auteurs: Luo Ruifang, Liu Yi, Yan Junyan, Hu Riqiang, Lin Fang, Yuan Binlin, Xiang Xueli, Yang Ting, Sun Zhujun, Xiao Lu, Chen Jie
resume: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) involves social deficits and severe stereotyped behavior. While central serotonin (5-HT) systems and Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) activation are known to be implicated in ASD, how gut TLR4 affects central 5-HT and stereotyped behavior remains unknown. This study demonstrated that prenatal lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced social deficits in offspring of both intestinal Tlr4 knockout (Tlr4<sup>△IEC</sup>) and Tlr4<sup>fl/fl</sup> mice. However, the stereotyped behaviors and the inhibition of dorsal raphe nuclei (DRN) 5-HT were reduced in Tlr4<sup>△IEC</sup>-LPS mice compared with those in Tlr4<sup>fl/fl</sup>-LPS mice. By intersecting metabolites present in both colonic and cerebrospinal fluid, and selecting those exclusively changing in the colon of Tlr4<sup>fl/fl</sup>offspring, hypoxanthine was identified as a metabolite that can cross the blood-brain barrier and mediate the effects of intestinal Tlr4 knockout on DRN 5-HT signaling. Remarkably, hypoxanthine and xanthine oxidase were increased in the serum of ASD children compared to typical development (TD) children. In vivo and in vitro experiments confirmed that hypoxanthine increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) and reduced 5-HT production, thereby promoting 5-HT neuron apoptosis. The inhibition of both the PI3K/AKT and 5-HT pathways in H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>-treated PC12 cells was rescued by glutathione pretreatment in vitro. Meanwhile, the above LPS-induced DRN changes were significantly different in the Tlr4<sup>fl/fl</sup> offspring, and were reversed in the Tlr4<sup>△IEC</sup> mice after LPS exposure. Collectively, intestinal Tlr4 knockout reduces LPS-induced stereotyped behaviors, and the mechanism involves reduced hypoxanthine production and ROS-mediated inhibition of PI3K/AKT signaling, thereby decreasing 5-HT neuronal apoptosis by elevating the 5-HT level in DRN.

Collectively, intestinal Tlr4 knockout reduces LPS-induced stereotyped behaviors, and the mechanism involves reduced hypoxanthine production and ROS-mediated inhibition of PI3K/AKT signaling, thereby decreasing 5-HT neuronal apoptosis by elevating the 5-HT level in DRN.

titre: Effects of Lovastatin on Autism-Like Behavioral, Metabolic, and Neuroinflammatory Alterations in Male BTBR T+ Tf/J Mice.
titre_fr: Effects of Lovastatin on Autism-Like Behavioral, Metabolic, and Neuroinflammatory Alterations in Male BTBR T+ Tf/J Mice.
auteurs: Jayaprakash Petrilla, Thomas Shilu Deepa, Salleh Hazizul, Abdullah Haniulhanif, Al Dhaheri Dana, Baniyas Shamsa, Al Derei Mahra, Al Rahbi Fatema, AlKaabi Alyazia, Al Shamsi Noura, Al Houqani Shaikha, Oz Murat, Sadek Bassem
resume: Statins inhibit 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase, thereby reducing cellular cholesterol and isoprenoid biosynthesis. In addition to lowering serum cholesterol, statins exert pleiotropic neuroprotective effects, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory actions mediated through the mevalonate pathway. Statins are increasingly being explored for drug repurposing in neuropsychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders. This study evaluated the therapeutic potential of lovastatin in the BTBR T+ tf/J mouse model of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), a well-established idiopathic model exhibiting core behavioral deficits and dysregulated cholesterol homeostasis characterized by elevated serum cholesterol and reduced brain cholesterol, consistent with reports of altered cholesterol metabolism in ASD. BTBR mice received lovastatin (10, 20, and 40 mg/kg, i.p. for 21 days) and were assessed for repetitive behaviour, cognitive performance and social interaction. Cholesterol-related markers, HMG-CoA reductase levels and neuroinflammatory markers were also examined. BTBR mice exhibited increased marble-burying behaviour, reduced spontaneous alternation and social interaction, elevated HMG-CoA reductase levels, decreased brain free cholesterol, increased serum cholesterol, and heightened brain levels of TNF-α and IL-6 compared with C57BL/6J controls. Lovastatin was associated with improvements across the evaluated autism related behavioral outcomes. The 40 mg/kg dose of Lovastatin showed the largest observed behavioral effects overall. Following 21 days of treatment, lovastatin reduced brain HMG-CoA reductase levels at all tested doses and reduced elevated serum cholesterol levels. Exploratory neuroinflammatory analyses showed that lovastatin at 40 mg/kg significantly lowered brain TNF-α and IL-6 levels in BTBR mice. Lovastatin was associated with improvements in autism related behavioral outcomes in male BTBR mice, while modulating systemic cholesterol dysregulation and neuroinflammatory responses. These findings provide preclinical evidence supporting further investigation of lovastatin in ASD-related phenotypes.

titre: Cognitive Emotion Regulation in Early Adolescents with ADHD: Sex Differences in Adaptive Strategies.
titre_fr: Cognitive Emotion Regulation in Early Adolescents with ADHD: Sex Differences in Adaptive Strategies.
auteurs: Cash Annah R, Baron Olivia, Miller Melissa C, Breaux Rosanna, Becker Stephen P
resume: Emotion regulation (ER) difficulties are common among youth with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), yet little is known about the cognitive strategies they use to regulate emotions or whether these associations differ by sex. We examined adaptive and maladaptive cognitive ER in 341 early adolescents (ages 10-12; M  = 10.90; SD  = 0.80), 47.8% of whom met diagnostic criteria for ADHD and 52.2% of whom were female. ADHD diagnosis was established using a semi-structured diagnostic interview administered to caregivers, and adolescents completed self-report measures of cognitive ER and internalizing symptoms. Regression models controlled for internalizing symptoms, age, family income, and medication use. Sex did not moderate the association between ADHD status and maladaptive cognitive ER. In contrast, sex moderated the association between ADHD and adaptive cognitive ER ( b = -0.32, p = .045). Simple slopes analysis indicated ADHD status was associated with less frequent use of adaptive strategies among females ( b = -0.304, p = .011) but was unrelated for males ( b  = 0.02, p = .882). Exploratory analyses of specific adaptive strategies indicated a significant ADHD × sex interaction for acceptance (i.e., acknowledging/coming to terms with what has occurred; p = .032), with the same pattern of simple slopes as observed for adaptive strategies. Findings suggest that ADHD-related differences in adaptive cognitive ER may be particularly relevant for females during early adolescence and highlight the importance of considering sex when examining ER in ADHD. Acceptance may warrant further investigation as a specific cognitive ER strategy relevant to females with ADHD.

titre: Developmental rewiring of EHMT1 function during human cortical neurogenesis.
titre_fr: Developmental rewiring of EHMT1 function during human cortical neurogenesis.
auteurs: Kasliwal Kritika, Chatterjee Kaushiki, Bocchi Vittoria Dickinson, Mahmood Syed R, Uyehara Christopher M, Marchese William, Laguillo-Diego Alejandra, Goetzler Emily, Theis Gabriel, Minotti Andrew, Walsh Ryan, Polyzos Alexander, Apostolou Eftychia, Sidoli Simone, Studer Lorenz, Stadtfeld Matthias
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: Ubiquitously expressed chromatin regulators orchestrate cell-type-specific gene expression programs, yet how they acquire distinct regulatory functions during development remains fundamentally unresolved 1,2 . Using temporally controlled protein depletion during human cortical neurogenesis in vitro , we show that the autism-associated histone methyltransferase EHMT1 3,4 is developmentally repurposed from epiblast to cortical neurons. Broadly expressed zinc finger proteins recruit EHMT1 to distinct cis-regulatory elements within changing chromatin landscapes associated with lineage-specific transcription factor activity, with extensive remodeling of EHMT1 enhancer occupancy during neural induction dependent on ZNF462. This genomic rewiring is accompanied by a fundamental shift from restraining premature developmental gene expression in pluripotent cells to supporting neuronal programs, with distinct transcriptional consequences of EHMT1 loss across neural progenitors and excitatory and inhibitory neuronal subtypes. Timed depletion and recovery experiments identify the neural progenitor stage as the onset of a developmental period during which EHMT1 is required for faithful neuronal maturation. Remarkably, EHMT1 can re-engage stage-specific targets after prolonged deficiency, allowing extensive transcriptional recovery with only limited molecular scarring. These findings reveal how ubiquitous epigenetic machinery acquires developmental specificity while demonstrating the resilience of developmental gene regulatory programs to prolonged disruption, with implications for neurodevelopmental disorders.

titre: Exome-wide rare variant genetic load is associated with cognition, intellectual disability and psychiatric disorders in population-based cohorts.
titre_fr: Exome-wide rare variant genetic load is associated with cognition, intellectual disability and psychiatric disorders in population-based cohorts.
auteurs: Ahangari Mohammad, Moore Spencer, Schleede Justin, Anomaly Jonathan, Young Alexander Strudwick, Wolfram Tobias
revue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
resume: Rare protein-truncating variants (PTVs) and damaging missense variants in constrained genes are enriched among people with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), schizophrenia and related conditions, but most studies used clinical cohorts. In European-ancestry participants of the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study (ABCD, 3,523 children) and the All of Us Research Program (AoU, 302,421 adults), we summed, separately for rare PTVs and damaging missense variants, the selection coefficients of affected genes into genetic loads (GLs). In ABCD, one additional typical constrained gene with a PTV was associated with 0.22 SD lower cognition and with ASD (odds ratio 1.80). In AoU, it was associated with ASD (1.34), schizophrenia (1.51) and intellectual disability (ID, 2.02). Missense GL showed smaller, concordant associations. Risk rose with gene constraint, to almost ninefold odds of ID in the most constrained genes, and carriers of a constrained PTV (12% of AoU participants) made up 31% of ID, 20% of schizophrenia and 17% of ASD cases. GL was essentially uncorrelated with polygenic scores. In African-ancestry participants, PTV GL retained 71-125% of its European-ancestry effect, versus 23-62% for matched polygenic scores. Constraint-weighted rare variant load contributes measurably to cognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes in population cohorts.

titre: p70 ribosomal protein S6 Kinase (p70S6K) as a potential peripheral biomarker for autistic symptoms in 16p11.2 deletion and duplication syndromes.
titre_fr: p70 ribosomal protein S6 Kinase (p70S6K) as a potential peripheral biomarker for autistic symptoms in 16p11.2 deletion and duplication syndromes.
auteurs: Morella Ilaria, Hall Jessica, Butter Charlotte, Goldie Caitlin, Evans Georgia, Ali Nabila, Burlinson-Diaz Natalia, Burkitt-Wright Emma, Caraiscos Isabella, Morè Lorenzo, Green Jonathan, van den Bree Marianne B M, Brambilla Riccardo
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) encompass cognitive, motor, and psychiatric manifestations that require extensive assessments spanning different clinical domains. Individuals with syndromes caused by micro-deletions and -duplications in the proximal region of 16p11.2 have increased likelihood of neurodevelopmental and mental health symptoms, as well as cardiometabolic disorder. However, considerable phenotypic variability complicates prediction of risk, disease trajectory and treatment response. The identification of biomarkers in easily accessible tissues, such as Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMCs), could help diagnosis and prognosis, yet remains an unmet clinical need. Converging evidence implicates dysregulation of ubiquitous signalling pathways, including ERK and mTOR cascades, in altered protein synthesis across NDDs of both idiopathic and genetic origin. Here, using a hypothesis-driven approach, we examined candidate peripheral biomarkers in individuals with 16p11.2 proximal deletion and duplication syndromes. We established increased psychopathology and cognitive deficits in individuals with 16p11.2 deletion and duplication syndromes, compared to sibling controls. Furthermore, we identified a significant reduction of p70 S6 kinase (p70S6K) levels in PBMCs across both genotypes compared to controls. Notably, the magnitude of p70S6K reduction correlated with the severity of autistic symptoms independent of CNV genotype. In contrast, MAPK3/ERK1 protein levels mirrored the gene dosage, showing increased expression in individuals with the duplication and reduced levels in those with the deletion. These findings suggest that peripheral alterations in p70S6K may relate to variation in autism-related traits within individuals with 16p11.2 deletion and duplication syndromes, indicating that it may represent a potential biomarker of autism-associated symptom severity in this genetically at-risk group.

titre: Long-read sequencing and benchmarking of saliva against blood for genomic variant detection in autism.
titre_fr: Long-read sequencing and benchmarking of saliva against blood for genomic variant detection in autism.
auteurs: Sui Yang, Campos Gabriele, Kwon Youngjun, Wong Isaac, Koundinya Nidhi, Munson Katherine M, Hoekzema Kendra, Ayllon Marcelo, Wang Tianyun, Neuhaus Emily, Eichler Evan E
revue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
resume: Autism is highly heritable, yet many cases remain genetically unsolved even after short-read sequencing (SRS). Long-read sequencing (LRS) increases sensitivity for pathogenic variant discovery, especially for complex structural variants (SVs) in repetitive regions missed by SRS. However, LRS largely relies on blood-derived DNA; whether saliva can support genome-wide LRS at population scale remains to be seen. We report the first systematic evaluation of saliva-derived DNA for genome-wide LRS in autism, benchmarking 105 new saliva samples against 68 new blood samples and integrating 189 previously published LRS blood samples to expand the autism cohort and improve ultra-rare pathogenic variant discovery. A matched blood-saliva quad provided direct comparisons of variant detection between sample sources. Saliva samples contained substantially more nonhuman DNA than blood (mean 10% versus 0.005% of reads), reducing mean effective genome coverage from an estimated 28X to 24X after removal of nonhuman reads, compared with 34X in blood samples. Despite this reduction, saliva and blood samples yielded comparable numbers of validated (22,591 versus 23,064) and rare (209 versus 213) SVs per sample, which was also observed in the quad when matching coverage. Saliva LRS identified four new pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants missed by SRS. We report variants affecting MECP2 , DNMT3A , CHD8 , LMBRD2 , POGZ , and PHF3 ; four additional candidates with potential relevance to autism; and an increase of diagnostic yield of 9-18%. Saliva-derived DNA support blood-comparable discovery of pathogenic variants missed by SRS, including SVs, with increased sequencing coverage compensating for nonhuman DNA contamination and reduced assembly contiguity, thus showing saliva DNA collection as a feasible strategy for large-scale LRS studies of patients and population-scale sequencing of cohorts.

titre: A clinical laboratory test-wide association scan of polygenic scores identifies biomarkers of psychiatric disorders.
titre_fr: A clinical laboratory test-wide association scan of polygenic scores identifies biomarkers of psychiatric disorders.
auteurs: Reed Makayla L, Feuer Kyra L, Kember Rachel L
revue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
resume: Psychiatric disorders pose a significant public health burden, and their complex genetic architecture underlies multiple biological pathways, contributing to a lack of diagnostic biomarkers. Laboratory-Wide Association Studies (LabWAS) leverage electronic health record laboratory data as intermediary phenotypes to link genetic risk to physiology. Polygenic Scores (PGS) for 25 health-related, psychiatric, and substance use phenotypes were generated for individuals of African (AFR; N=10,473) and European (EUR, N=35,131) ancestry from the Penn Medicine Biobank. Laboratory data was prepared using the LabWAS pipeline, encompassing 78 laboratory tests and 6 vital signs. Linear regression models tested the association of each lab value with PGS adjusting for sex, age, and ten within-ancestry genetic principal components. Four PGS were significantly associated with at least one laboratory value in AFR individuals and 22 PGS in EUR individuals. In EUR individuals, psychiatric PGS partitioned into three physiological profiles: anxiety, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, major depressive disorder, and post-traumatic stress disorder shared a metabolic/inflammatory signature (higher BMI, glucose, and monocytes; lower high density lipoprotein cholesterol and oxygen saturation); anorexia nervosa, obsessive compulsive disorder, and schizophrenia were characterized by lower BMI; and bipolar disorder demonstrated a more circumscribed profile with lower electrolytes and renal makers. Substance use disorder PGS similarly clustered: tobacco use disorder and externalizing showed metabolic/inflammatory profiles; alcohol-related phenotypes showed lower red blood cell indices; and cannabis use disorder had a more circumscribed profile. LabWAS reveals physiologic signatures associated with genetic risk for psychiatric disorders, offering new biological insights into their pathology.

titre: Longitudinal Pain Profiles and Their Clinical and Genetic Correlates in 624,996 U.S. Veterans.
titre_fr: Longitudinal Pain Profiles and Their Clinical and Genetic Correlates in 624,996 U.S. Veterans.
auteurs: Davis Christal N, Shi Mingjian, Gunawan Tommy, Toikumo Sylvanus, Gray Joshua C, Kranzler Henry R
revue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
resume: Pain varies in its intensity and course, yet much of our understanding of pain is based on cross-sectional assessments or longitudinal studies of selected clinical populations. Routinely collected electronic health record data may enable characterization of longitudinal pain patterns at scale. To identify longitudinal pain profiles among U.S. Veterans and characterize their clinical and polygenic correlates. Cohort study using electronic health record and genomic data from the Million Veteran Program, with up to 16 years of pain assessments collected between 2000 to 2025. U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs health care system. Million Veteran Program participants assigned to African-like, Admixed American-like, East Asian-like, European-like, or South Asian-like genetically inferred ancestry groups who have at least three years of outpatient numeric rating scale pain records. Outpatient pain ratings and polygenic scores for psychiatric, sleep, and substance use traits. Pain profiles were identified using Gaussian finite mixture modeling of pain intensity, directional change, and within-person variability. Profiles were characterized by pain, psychiatric and substance use diagnoses, opioid exposure, body mass index, and polygenic scores. Among 624,996 participants (Mean [SD] age at first pain rating=53.4 [13.5] years; 568,833 [91.0%] male), 51,731,567 outpatient pain ratings were analyzed. Three profiles were identified: stable no pain, stable mild pain, and mild-to-moderate increasing pain. Compared with the stable no pain profile, the increasing pain profile had higher odds of chronic pain (OR=21.14 [95% CI: 18.96-23.57]), opioid use disorder (OR=9.32 [95% CI: 8.31-10.45]), opioid exposure (OR=8.61 [95% CI: 8.41-8.83]), major depressive disorder (OR=3.77 [95% CI: 3.67-3.87]), and posttraumatic stress disorder (OR=3.72 [95% CI: 3.61-3.84]). Associations were attenuated but remained after adjustment for mean pain severity. Polygenic scores for depression, insomnia, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and tobacco use disorder were the most consistent predictors of increasing pain across the three largest genetically inferred ancestry groups. Longitudinal modeling of routinely collected pain scores identified pain profiles associated with clinical burden and polygenic liability. These profiles captured clinically meaningful information beyond mean pain severity alone, highlighting the value of longitudinal pain phenotyping in electronic health record data. Question: Can pain scores collected in outpatient care identify clinically meaningful pain profiles among U.S. Veterans?Findings: In this cohort study of 624,996 Veterans with more than 51 million pain ratings across up to 16 years, three pain profiles were identified: stable no pain, stable mild pain, and mild-tomoderate increasing pain. Profiles differed in clinical burden even after accounting for mean pain severity and were associated with polygenic liability for psychiatric, sleep, and substance use traits.Meaning: Routinely collected pain scores can be used to characterize heterogeneity in the course of pain and factors associated with more burdensome pain patterns.

titre: Surrogate variables and the risk of overfitting in neuropsychiatric gene expression analyses.
titre_fr: Surrogate variables and the risk of overfitting in neuropsychiatric gene expression analyses.
auteurs: Hoang Dung T, Thompson Ryan C, Lund Anina N, Kritzer Eli, Buxbaum-Grice Ariela S, John Divya, Nadkarni Girish N, Golestani Negar, Charney Alexander W, Beckmann Noam D
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: The reproducibility crisis in biomedical research calls for re-evaluation of how common analytic approaches affect results. One such approach, surrogate variable analysis (SVA), is widely used to adjust for unmeasured drivers of variation in transcriptomic differential expression analyses. We systematically quantified the impact of SVA using synthetic data with known ground truth and fourteen brain RNA-seq and microarray datasets spanning Alzheimer's disease, autism spectrum disorder, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and Parkinson's disease. In synthetic data, SVA usage frequently led to high false positive rates. This issue was not revealed by standard diagnostics nor resolved by strategies such as maximizing cross-dataset signal correlation. In real data, using SVA reduced cross-cohort reproducibility of differential expression signatures regardless of the number of surrogate variables included. These findings show that SVA risks inducing overfitting at realistic signal levels, advocating for a cautious, case-by-case application, with a preference for modeling known covariates.
resume_fr: The reproducibility crisis in biomedical research calls for re-evaluation of how common analytic approaches affect results. One such approach, surrogate variable analysis (SVA), is widely used to adjust for unmeasured drivers of variation in transcriptomic differential expression analyses. We systematically quantified the impact of SVA using synthetic data with known ground truth and fourteen brain RNA-seq and microarray datasets spanning Alzheimer's disease, autism spectrum disorder, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and Parkinson's disease. In synthetic data, SVA usage frequently led to high false positive rates. This issue was not revealed by standard diagnostics nor resolved by strategies such as maximizing cross-dataset signal correlation. In real data, using SVA reduced cross-cohort reproducibility of differential expression signatures regardless of the number of surrogate variables included. These findings show that SVA risks inducing overfitting at realistic signal levels, advocating for a cautious, case-by-case application, with a preference for modeling known covariates.

titre: Linking anterior cingulate sulcal variability to attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder behavior.
titre_fr: Linking anterior cingulate sulcal variability to attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder behavior.
auteurs: Hadveck Robin F, Paras Abigail, Anctil Megan, Martinez Enrique, Gallardo Charley M, Maboudian Samira A, Willbrand Ethan H, Weiner Kevin S
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: The anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) is consistently implicated in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). ACC variability, including its most variable structure, the paracingulate sulcus (PCGS), has been known since the late 1800s, and since then, has been linked to cognitive control, impulsivity, and psychiatric conditions comorbid with ADHD, including autism spectrum disorder and schizophrenia. Yet, the role of the PCGS in ADHD remains unexamined at the individual level. We characterized PCGS incidence, asymmetry, and morphology in 247 children and adolescents (144 ADHD: 10.9 ± 2.73 years old, 75% male; 103 neurotypical: 12.2 ± 3.17 years old, 50% male) from the ADHD-200 dataset. The PCGS was manually identified in FreeSurfer cortical surface reconstructions. Morphometric measures, including sulcal length, depth, and cortical thickness, were extracted and normalized to hemisphere-wide variables. Between-group analyses tested whether PCGS presence, asymmetry, and quantitative morphology differed by diagnosis, while behavioral analyses examined associations with inattention, hyperactivity-impulsivity, and cognitive measures. Age and gender were included as covariates. Analyses revealed that, in both NT and ADHD individuals, there was significant leftward asymmetry in PCGS presence. Between groups, the PCGS was less likely to be present in individuals with ADHD in the left hemisphere. Leftward PCGS absence was also associated with significantly higher ADHD index and hyperactivity-impulsivity scores. These findings advance understanding of how early neurodevelopmental variation in cortical folding may serve as a structural intermediary between genetic liability and the behavioral expression of ADHD.

titre: Effects of Physical Activity and Sports Type on Executive Functions and Socioemotional Skills of Children and Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorder: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
titre_fr: Effects of Physical Activity and Sports Type on Executive Functions and Socioemotional Skills of Children and Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorder: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
auteurs: Gomes Aline, Di Martino Giulia, Costa Rochelle, Ben-Soussan Tal Dotan, Pesce Caterina, Lamas Leonardo
resume: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized evidence on the effects of physical activity and sports on executive functions and socioemotional skills in autistic youth, according to the intervention cognitive-motor engagement. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, 32 studies were analyzed using random-effects models with Hedges' g. Subgroup analyses and meta-regressions examined the effects of study design, intervention type, and dose. Physical activity and sports interventions showed beneficial effects on inhibitory control, communication, socialization, stereotyped behaviors, and social impairment. Physically conditioning, cognitively engaging, and combined interventions all showed positive effects, with larger effects generally observed for combined interventions. Team sports were particularly promising, showing significant effects for inhibition and socioemotional outcomes. Meta-regressions suggested domain-specific dose associations, with total intervention minutes predicting inhibition gains and total intervention weeks predicting effects on cognitive flexibility. Successful interventions often featured close supervision, progressive task difficulty, and structured social interaction. Findings support physical activity and sports as a promising, mechanism-informed approach for autistic youth.

titre: Methylphenidate-associated brain structural changes and neuroimaging predictors of treatment response in youth with ADHD: a systematic review.
titre_fr: Methylphenidate-associated brain structural changes and neuroimaging predictors of treatment response in youth with ADHD: a systematic review.
auteurs: Reneman Liesbeth, van der Pal Zarah, de Smidt Daniëlle, Bipat Shandra
resume: Methylphenidate (MPH) is a psychostimulant widely prescribed to children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Although its clinical efficacy is well established, its lasting effects on the developing brain remain unclear. This systematic review aimed to examine associations between long-term MPH treatment and brain structure in children and adolescents with ADHD using structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), distinguishing longitudinal treatment-effect studies from cross-sectional medication-history comparisons and baseline neuroimaging predictors of treatment response. A systematic search was conducted in MEDLINE and Embase databases. Studies were included if they investigated structural brain changes (gray matter volume, white matter integrity and cortical thickness) after at least four weeks of MPH treatment in children with ADHD. Data extraction and quality assessment were performed using the NIH quality assessment tool. Eight studies met the inclusion criteria: three longitudinal studies using repeated MRI to assess within-subject treatment effects, two cross-sectional comparisons based on medication history, and three studies using baseline neuroimaging to predict subsequent treatment response. Greater putamen volume was associated with medication status ad volume with better treatment response in the cross-sectional and predictive analyses, while cortical effects were less consistent and mainly age-dependent in frontal areas. White matter findings were subtle and inconsistent across studies, and cortical thickness evidence-limited to one study-suggests short-term, possibly transient effects in children. MPH treatment is associated l with age-dependent differences in brain structure in children and adolescents with ADHD; however, the limited number of included studies varied substantially in design, (cross-sectional and predictive studies alongside longitudinal treatment-effect studies), methodology, and reported outcomes, making firm causal conclusions difficult. Future research should prioritize larger, standardized, long-term longitudinal studies that account for developmental factors.

titre: Higher education adjustment and support needs among Chinese university students with ASD, ADHD, and SpLD: a call for comprehensive reassessment and support.
titre_fr: Higher education adjustment and support needs among Chinese university students with ASD, ADHD, and SpLD: a call for comprehensive reassessment and support.
auteurs: Au Jason Ka-Hei, Tso Ricky Van-Yip, Lai Tony Tai-Sum, Li Chin-Wa, Leung Angel Nga Man, Yeung Kitty Kit-Yu, Yeung Pui-Sze
resume: Students with ASD, ADHD, and specific learning difficulties (SpLD) often experience difficulties adjusting to higher education (HE), yet transition support remains limited. To better understand the support needs of university students in Hong Kong with SEN, this study profiled their cognitive, socio-emotional, and Chinese literacy characteristics and examined how these were associated with adjustment in HE. 104 Chinese university students, including typically developing (TD) students and students with ASD, ADHD, or SpLD completed questionnaires and tasks assessing cognitive, socio-emotional, and Chinese literacy characteristics. Seven functional domains were derived for analysis: ASD symptoms, ADHD symptoms, SpLD symptoms, executive functioning (EF), social functioning, socio-emotional functioning, and Chinese literacy. Regression analyses and exploratory moderation and relative importance analyses examined shared and group-specific associations with academic, social, personal-emotional adjustment, and institutional attachment. University students with ASD, ADHD, and SpLD showed poorer adjustment than TD. Regression analyses indicated that academic adjustment was associated with ASD symptoms and ADHD symptoms; social adjustment with social functioning; personal-emotional adjustment with socio-emotional functioning; and attachment with social functioning. Moderation analyses found no evidence that these associations differed statistically significantly across groups. Relative importance analyses further suggest potential distinct patterns of domain salience among students with ASD, ADHD, and SpLD. University students with SEN demonstrated both shared and group-specific support needs across adjustment outcomes in higher education. These findings suggest a preliminary layered support framework that combines transdiagnostic support with diagnosis-informed assessment to better address the needs of students with SEN.

titre: Autistic matrescence as dynamic person-environment fit: a theoretical model of regulatory resources and support usability.
titre_fr: Autistic matrescence as dynamic person-environment fit: a theoretical model of regulatory resources and support usability.
auteurs: Steinbrück Pia-Cecilia
resume: Matrescence is a developmental transition involving bodily, psychological, relational, and social change. Research on autistic pregnancy and early parenthood documents sensory overload, communication barriers, disrupted routines, professional scrutiny, and limited recovery alongside attachment, commitment, competence, and self-knowledge. Such divergence requires a model treating neither autism nor parenthood as sufficient explanations of psychological outcomes. This theoretical paper reuses the 25-publication corpus of a published mapping review on autistic pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum experience, infant feeding, and early parenting. It develops a distinct theoretical synthesis by integrating that corpus with theories of stress, resource loss, functioning, and person-environment-occupation fit; it does not report a new review or formal study-quality appraisal. The paper proposes that proximal psychological outcomes are shaped by dynamic person-environment fit among transition demands, state-dependent regulatory resources, and environmental demands and affordances. Its specific extension is the distinction between support availability and usability. Support usability is modelled as a staged conversion process through which available support must be accessed, processed, trusted, and implemented to become psychologically effective. The model specifies boundary conditions under which minority stress, trauma, psychopathology, acute clinical complications, or structural violence should be treated as primary explanations. Five propositions address within-person variation, sensory and communication moderation, recovery mediation, support usability, and reciprocal developmental feedback. Candidate measures are mapped onto instruments, including the Glasgow Sensory Questionnaire, state anxiety, perceived stress, the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, parenting confidence, parenting styles, and preliminary autistic-burnout measures. Generalization beyond autistic matrescence is presented as a transfer hypothesis rather than an established contribution.

titre: NeuroD1-induced fate conversion partially restores GABAergic neuronal identity in Huntington's disease.
titre_fr: NeuroD1-induced fate conversion partially restores GABAergic neuronal identity in Huntington's disease.
auteurs: Lee Siwoo, Notario Geneva Rose, Seo Jung Hwa, Cho Sung-Rae
revue: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
resume: NeuroD1 is a master transcription factor governing neuronal differentiation and subtype specification, yet its potential to restore striatal identity in Huntington's disease (HD) remains unresolved. In HD, striosomal D2 striatal projection neurons (SPNs) represent the earliest and most selectively vulnerable population, leading to early collapse of striatal compartmental organization. Here, we show that astrocyte-targeted expression of NeuroD1, via AAV9-mediated delivery of NeuroD1 under the GFAP promoter in a transgenic murine model of HD, reinstates hallmarks of inhibitory neuronal maturation, synaptic proteins, and chloride homeostasis in the striatum. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing further revealed selective recovery of striosomal D2 transcriptional programs and compartment-specific molecular signatures. NeuroD1 treatment promoted the partial reorganization of striosome-matrix compartmental distinctions, including the restoration of MOR1-defined striosomal domains. These cellular and circuit-level restorations were accompanied by significant amelioration of functional deficits in motor coordination and clasping behaviors. Together, these findings establish astroglial NeuroD1-mediated identity reinforcement as a potential strategy to counter subtype- and compartment-specific circuit disintegration in HD.

titre: Proanthocyanidin ameliorates BCCAO-induced neuroinflammation in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) in rats by targeting NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome pathway.
titre_fr: Proanthocyanidin ameliorates BCCAO-induced neuroinflammation in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) in rats by targeting NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome pathway.
auteurs: Pachauri Pradeep Kant, Panda Siva Prasad
resume: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) is a major cause of mortality and long-term neurological disability, characterized by excessive oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and neuronal degeneration following the restoration of cerebral blood flow. The present study investigated the neuroprotective effects of proanthocyanidin (PAC) against bilateral common carotid artery occlusion (BCCAO)-induced cerebral ischemia in Wistar albino rats, with particular emphasis on the NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome signaling pathway. Rats subjected to BCCAO received PAC at two dose levels or standard therapy (aspirin + clopidogrel). Neurological and cognitive functions were evaluated using the rotarod, actophotometer, and elevated plus maze tests. Biochemical assays were performed to determine oxidative stress markers and antioxidant enzyme activities, while histopathological examination assessed neuronal integrity. The molecular mechanism was further investigated by Western blot analysis and densitometric quantification of NF-κB (p65), NLRP3, and caspase-1 protein expression. BCCAO significantly impaired motor coordination, locomotor activity, and memory retention, accompanied by increased lipid peroxidation, myeloperoxidase, and acetylcholinesterase activities, depletion of endogenous antioxidants (glutathione, superoxide dismutase, and catalase), and marked neuronal degeneration in the hippocampal and cortical regions. PAC treatment significantly improved behavioral performance, restored antioxidant defense, reduced oxidative stress and biochemical alterations, and preserved neuronal architecture in a dose-dependent manner. Western blot analysis demonstrated that PAC markedly downregulated the overexpression of NF-κB (p65), NLRP3, and caspase-1 proteins, indicating suppression of NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated neuroinflammation. Overall, PAC exhibited significant neuroprotective efficacy comparable to aspirin plus clopidogrel, suggesting that its beneficial effects are mediated through the attenuation of oxidative stress and the inhibition of NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome signaling. These findings support PAC as a promising phytotherapeutic candidate for the management of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.

titre: The positive allosteric modulator of the GABA<sub>B</sub> receptor, ASP8062, attenuates alcohol self-administration in female Sardinian alcohol-preferring rats.
titre_fr: The positive allosteric modulator of the GABA<sub>B</sub> receptor, ASP8062, attenuates alcohol self-administration in female Sardinian alcohol-preferring rats.
auteurs: Maccioni Paola, Carai Mauro A M, Corelli Federico, Colombo Giancarlo
resume: Four-day intragastric treatment with the positive allosteric modulator of the GABA<sub>B</sub> receptor, ASP8062 (1, 3, and 10 mg/kg), suppressed operant oral alcohol self-administration in male and female Sprague Dawley (SD) rats (Haile et al., Psychopharmacology 238:2587-2600, 2021). Conversely, in a double-blind placebo-controlled trial, 6-week treatment with ASP8062 (25 mg/day, corresponding to the 3-mg/kg rat dose) failed to attenuate alcohol craving and consumption in individuals with moderate or severe alcohol use disorder (AUD) (Schacht et al., Alcohol Clin Exp Res 48:2352-2363, 2024). Reverse-translational dose-ranging studies in animal models of AUD were suggested. In keeping with this purpose, the present study tested ASP8062 on operant oral alcohol self-administration in selectively bred Sardinian alcohol-preferring (sP) rats, a validated animal model of AUD. Female sP rats were trained to lever-respond for alcohol under the fixed ratio 5 schedule of reinforcement. Once lever-responding for alcohol was high and steady, rats underwent a 4-day intragastric treatment with ASP8062 (3, 10, and 17 mg/kg). Only the 17-mg/kg dose reduced, by approximately 40%, lever-responding for alcohol and estimated amount of self-administered alcohol. No dose of ASP8062 altered motor-coordination, as indicated by the results of a concurrent inverted-screen test. ASP8062 in sP rats was remarkably less potent compared to previous observations in SD rats, suggesting that higher doses of ASP8062 may be needed in rats modeling AUD. If ideally transposed to humans, these data suggest that future clinical studies should consider testing higher doses of ASP8062 before reaching definitive conclusions on its therapeutic potential.

titre: Loss of SEZ6L2 disrupts synaptic architecture and drives progressive behavioral deficits.
titre_fr: Loss of SEZ6L2 disrupts synaptic architecture and drives progressive behavioral deficits.
auteurs: Granato Julia M, Silver Nina, Hobbins Alison, Randolph John, Stout Angela, Gelbard Harris A, Gunnersen Jenny M, Mackenzie Samuel J, White Patricia M, Hammond Jennetta W
resume: The SEZ6 family, composed of SEZ6, SEZ6L, and SEZ6L2, plays essential roles in neurodevelopment, synaptic maintenance, and complement regulation. However, the unique contribution of SEZ6L2 to brain development and function remains largely unexplored. In this study, we provide a comprehensive behavioral characterization of Sez6l2 knockout (KO) mice and directly compare their phenotype with wild-type and Sez6 triple knockout (TKO) mice, which lack all three Sez6 family genes. Sez6l2 KO mice exhibit impairments across multiple behavioral domains, including motor coordination, gait, sociability, sensory processing, and goal-directed repetitive behaviors. Several phenotypes, particularly motor deficits, worsen with age. Male Sez6l2 KO mice also demonstrate enhanced fear learning and increased prepulse inhibition, revealing sex-specific alterations in sensorimotor gating. At the synaptic level, Sez6l2 KO mice show reduced dendritic spine length and decreased expression of key postsynaptic proteins consistent with impaired excitatory synaptic connectivity. In comparison,Sez6 TKO mice display more severe impairments across most measures. To examine the contribution of complement signaling, complement component C3 was deleted in Sez6 TKO mice. This manipulation rescued dendritic spine length and partially improved select gait parameters but did not restore broader behavioral outcomes. These findings indicate that complement-dependent mechanisms contribute to specific structural and motor phenotypes but are not sufficient to explain the full behavioral deficits. SEZ6L2 therefore emerges as a critical regulator of synaptic integrity and behavior, providing a framework for understanding how SEZ6 family dysfunction may contribute to neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders.
