titre: Distinct Subgroups Emerge in Autistic Males and Females: Insights Into Sex Differences From a Large-Scale Nationwide Cohort.
titre_fr: Distinct Subgroups Emerge in Autistic Males and Females: Insights Into Sex Differences From a Large-Scale Nationwide Cohort.
auteurs: Landau Emily, Wodka Ericka L
revue: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
resume: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is diagnosed more frequently in males, with male-to-female ratios typically around 3:1 or 4:1. As such, autistic females are underrepresented in research, limiting the understanding of their unique profile. Sex differences contribute to diagnostic disparities, as females often present with either more subtle or impactful traits. This study aims to identify clinically meaningful subgroups of autistic youth and examine sex-based differences and co-occurring diagnoses across subgroups. This study included 13,543 autistic individuals (10,497 male, 3,046 female; ≤15 years) from the SPARK cohort. Latent profile analysis was conducted using age at ASD diagnosis, adaptive functioning, autism symptoms, repetitive behaviors, and motor coordination. Post hoc analyses examined subgroup differences in sex distribution and parent-reported co-occurring diagnoses, including ADHD, anxiety, depression, and intellectual/cognitive disability. Latent profile analysis revealed four distinct subgroups. Profile 1, with proportionally more females than other groups, had the latest age of diagnosis and highest rates of anxiety, depression, and ADHD. Other profiles did not differ in sex ratio. Profile 2 was clustered around the sample mean, Profile 3 had the highest support needs and the greatest prevalence of intellectual disability, and Profile 4 included individuals with lower support needs. Findings highlight heterogeneity in ASD and sex-related differences in functional profiles and diagnostic timing. Females with co-occurring conditions are at risk of diagnostic overshadowing, where mental health or attentional concerns delay autism identification. Results highlight the need for improved diagnostic tools and assessment approaches that differentiate autism from co-occurring conditions.
resume_fr: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is diagnosed more frequently in males, with male-to-female ratios typically around 3:1 or 4:1. As such, autistic females are underrepresented in research, limiting the understanding of their unique profile. Sex differences contribute to diagnostic disparities, as females often present with either more subtle or impactful traits. This study aims to identify clinically meaningful subgroups of autistic youth and examine sex-based differences and co-occurring diagnoses across subgroups. This study included 13,543 autistic individuals (10,497 male, 3,046 female; ≤15 years) from the SPARK cohort. Latent profile analysis was conducted using age at ASD diagnosis, adaptive functioning, autism symptoms, repetitive behaviors, and motor coordination. Post hoc analyses examined subgroup differences in sex distribution and parent-reported co-occurring diagnoses, including ADHD, anxiety, depression, and intellectual/cognitive disability. Latent profile analysis revealed four distinct subgroups. Profile 1, with proportionally more females than other groups, had the latest age of diagnosis and highest rates of anxiety, depression, and ADHD. Other profiles did not differ in sex ratio. Profile 2 was clustered around the sample mean, Profile 3 had the highest support needs and the greatest prevalence of intellectual disability, and Profile 4 included individuals with lower support needs. Findings highlight heterogeneity in ASD and sex-related differences in functional profiles and diagnostic timing. Females with co-occurring conditions are at risk of diagnostic overshadowing, where mental health or attentional concerns delay autism identification. Results highlight the need for improved diagnostic tools and assessment approaches that differentiate autism from co-occurring conditions.

titre: Comparing the impact of recess duration on motor coordination and psychological variables: An exploratory study.
titre_fr: Comparing the impact of recess duration on motor coordination and psychological variables: An exploratory study.
auteurs: von Borck Hailey G, Esposito Phillip, Braun-Trocchio Robyn, Wagner Lauren M, Rhea Deborah J
resume: Recess serves as a productive environment for children to play independently of adults, which promotes physiological and psychological development. However, current recess durations in schools across the United States (U.S.) are frequently insufficient in providing opportunities for physical activity (PA) to promote developmental improvements. One of the most well-studied evidence-based recess interventions, the LiiNK Project®, has demonstrated that when children receive 60 minutes of recess daily, motor coordination (MC) is significantly better than when children receive 30 minutes daily. However, child outcomes are lacking when schools modify the recess intervention duration in older grades to 30 minutes daily while continuing to practice the protocols and procedures from the full intervention. Therefore, the primary purpose of this study was to explore observed physiological (MC) and psychological (self-esteem and perceived physical ability) differences and associations between fourth and fifth grade children who received a modified version of the LiiNK intervention (n = 120) and children who did not receive the modified intervention (n = 98) at two-time points in one school year. The Körperkoordinationstest für Kinder (KTK) was used to assess MC, while the KID-KINDL self-esteem subscale and the Perceived Physical Ability Scale (PPASC) were used to assess the psychological variables. Grade, sex, race, and body fat percentages were collected to describe any group differences for a better interpretation of the groups. A mixed two-way repeated measures MANOVA analysis identified a between-group PPASC difference (p < 0.001), while the control group reported higher scores at both time points, suggesting a pre-existing group difference rather than a modified intervention change. Further, significant within-subjects time-related improvements were observed for single-leg hop (SH) and sideways stepping (SS), while a significant time-related decline was observed for self-esteem. Lastly, 2 x 2 Pearson chi-square analysis of "Normal-to-Great" and "Below Normal" MQ classifications was conducted separately at each time point. Although there were no significant findings, descriptively, both groups at Time 1 (85.8% of the modified intervention group and 90.8% of control group) were classified as "Normal-to-Great" MQ, improving to 88.3% and 95.9%, respectively, at Time 2. The "Below Normal" MQ classification decreased from 14.2% to 11.7% and 9.2% to 4.1% in the two groups respectively. Overall, these results provide preliminary insights into observed patterns of physiological and psychological outcomes for fourth and fifth grade children with similar recess minutes, but different protocols daily. However, these results provide no evidence that the modified intervention benefits the children any better than having 30 minutes of recess without the modified protocols. Future studies should compare the modified 30-minute intervention with a larger sample of children in the full LiiNK intervention (60 minutes) to assess these same variables, as well as collect the second data point in May instead of February.

titre: Comparative and combined neurotoxic effects of lithium carbonate and lead acetate in rats: From clinical alterations to molecular insights.
titre_fr: Comparative and combined neurotoxic effects of lithium carbonate and lead acetate in rats: From clinical alterations to molecular insights.
auteurs: Harsh R Patel, Urvesh D Patel, Maunik D Prajapati, Dhaval T Fefar
resume: Heavy metal contamination in soil and water is a global concern with significant ecological and health implications. Lithium (Li), increasingly used in electric vehicles, and lead (Pb), a well-established pollutant, poses neurotoxic risks to animals and humans. This study evaluated the individual and combined effects of lithium carbonate (Li; 20 mg/kg) and lead acetate (Pb; 20 mg/kg) administered orally for 28 days in adult rats. Forty-eight rats were divided into four groups: control, Li, Pb, and Li + Pb. Clinical signs included hair loss, diarrhoea, dehydration, dullness, and foul-smelling faeces, with Li + Pb rats showing greater feed reduction and weight loss than single-exposure groups. Behavioural assessments revealed impaired motor coordination, anxiety-like behaviour, and significantly increased grip strength in Li + Pb as compared to the control group. Oxidative stress markers demonstrated significantly reduced Superoxide Dismutase (SOD), catalase, glutathione, and total antioxidant capacity, along with significantly elevated Malondialdehyde (MDA) and Nitric Oxide (NO) levels in the Li + Pb group compared with the control group. Brain AChE activity was significantly reduced in the Pb and Li + Pb groups compared with the control group. Gene expression analysis revealed significant downregulation of apoe (3.93-fold), app (6.15-fold), and ache (4.75-fold) genes, alongside bax (4.98-fold) upregulation in the Li + Pb group compared with the control group, indicating enhanced apoptosis, impaired antioxidant defense, and Alzheimer's-like neurodegeneration. Gross pathology revealed mild cerebral congestion in the Li and Pb alone groups, and marked congestion in the Li + Pb rats. Histopathology confirmed neuronal degeneration, Purkinje cell loss, perineuronal space widening, and astrocytic proliferation, with the Li + Pb group exhibiting the most severe lesions. Collectively, these findings suggest that co-exposure to lithium and lead exerts more pronounced neurotoxic effects, mediated by oxidative stress, apoptosis, and gene alterations linked to neurodegeneration.

titre: Electroacupuncture Inhibits Neuronal Ferroptosis in MCAO/R Model Mice by Regulating the GSK-3β/NRF2 Signaling Pathway.
titre_fr: Electroacupuncture Inhibits Neuronal Ferroptosis in MCAO/R Model Mice by Regulating the GSK-3β/NRF2 Signaling Pathway.
auteurs: Xia Wenxin, Zhao Rui, Li Xiaoxiao, Xu Chenchen, Dong Jianjian, Li Shujie, Xu Yun, Han Yongsheng
resume: Neuronal ferroptosis following acute ischemic stroke (AIS) contributes to ischemic brain injury and is regulated by nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2), a key regulator of antioxidant defense and iron homeostasis. Whether electroacupuncture (EA) suppresses neuronal ferroptosis by regulating NRF2 stability and nuclear translocation through upstream glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta (GSK-3β) remains unclear. We investigated whether EA inhibits neuronal ferroptosis and alleviates ischemic brain injury by modulating the GSK-3β/NRF2 axis. Middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) models were established in C57BL/6 and conditional Nrf2-knockout mice. The GSK-3β inhibitor laduviglusib (CHIR-99021; CHIR), the ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1), and conditional Nrf2 knockout were used to investigate the anti-ferroptotic mechanism of EA and the regulatory hierarchy between GSK-3β and NRF2. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), western blotting, and immunofluorescence were used to examine the GSK-3β/NRF2 pathway and ferroptosis-related molecules. NRF2 nuclear localization, neuronal nuclei (NeuN) /acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) double immunofluorescence, and co-immunoprecipitation were used to assess NRF2 nuclear translocation, neuronal ferroptosis, and the GSK-3β-NRF2 interaction, respectively. EA inhibited GSK-3β activity after MCAO/R, restored NRF2 protein expression, promoted nuclear accumulation, and upregulated NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1). EA also downregulated ACSL4 and transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1), upregulated glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11), reduced NeuN/ACSL4-colocalized neurons, decreased ferrous iron (Fe<sup>2+</sup>) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and increased superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, glutathione (GSH) content, and the GSH/oxidized glutathione (GSSG) ratio. CHIR and Fer-1 produced similar anti-ferroptotic effects, and co-immunoprecipitation confirmed GSK-3β-NRF2 interaction. Conditional Nrf2 knockout did not affect EA- or CHIR-mediated GSK-3β phosphorylation but markedly attenuated their effects on NQO1, SLC7A11, GPX4, and TfR1. EA also alleviated mitochondrial ultrastructural damage, reduced cerebral infarction and Fluoro-Jade B (FJB)-positive neurons, and improved neurological function and motor coordination in MCAO/R mice. These findings identify the GSK-3β/NRF2 axis as an important regulatory mechanism of regulating neuronal ferroptosis after MCAO/R and support EA as a potential therapeutic strategy for alleviating neuronal ferroptosis and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury through GSK-3β inhibition and NRF2 activation.

titre: Effects of an embodied music intervention on executive function, emotion regulation and psychophysiological well-being in children: the role of movement-rhythm synchronization and self-regulation.
titre_fr: Effects of an embodied music intervention on executive function, emotion regulation and psychophysiological well-being in children: the role of movement-rhythm synchronization and self-regulation.
auteurs: Shu Qian
resume: Music participation engages auditory processing, temporal prediction, attention, and motor coordination, but the additional contribution of structured bodily engagement to children's cognitive and emotional development remains unclear. This randomized controlled trial examined whether a 12-week embodied music intervention produced greater changes in executive function, emotion regulation, movement-rhythm synchronization, and psychophysiological well-being than non-embodied music participation or usual activity. A total of 180 children aged 8-11 years were randomly assigned to embodied music (n = 60), non-embodied music (n = 60), or usual-activity control (n = 60). The two music conditions were matched for duration, musical exposure, instructor contact, and session frequency; the embodied condition additionally incorporated whole-body rhythmic coordination, movement inhibition, rule switching, spatial movement, and cooperative synchronization. Assessments were conducted at baseline (T0), week 6 (T1), week 12/post-intervention (T2), and 3-month follow-up (T3). Primary outcomes were executive function and emotion regulation; secondary outcomes included movement-rhythm synchronization, psychological well-being, resting heart rate variability indexed by RMSSD, and sleep problems. Linear mixed-effects models showed significant Group x Time interactions for executive function, chi-square(6) = 78.60, p < 0.001; emotion regulation, chi-square(6) = 51.40, p < 0.001; and movement-rhythm synchronization, chi-square(6) = 129.30, p < 0.001. At T2, embodied music showed larger model-estimated improvements than non-embodied music in executive function [adjusted difference in change = 6.40, 95% CI (3.80, 9.00), p < 0.001], emotion regulation [4.30, 95% CI (2.00, 6.60), p < 0.001], and movement-rhythm synchronization [10.90, 95% CI (8.20, 13.60), p < 0.001]. Benefits were largely maintained at follow-up. Changes in psychological well-being and RMSSD were more moderate, and sleep effects were smaller. Exploratory indirect-effect analyses were statistically consistent with the hypothesized association among embodied music, synchronization, executive function, emotion regulation, and later well-being [standardized serial indirect effect = 0.022, bootstrap 95% CI (0.009, 0.043)]; because the proposed mediators were not fully separated in time, these analyses do not establish temporal or causal mediation. Overall, the randomized comparisons support benefits of embodied music for several proximal outcomes, while the proposed mechanisms require further confirmatory study.

titre: Effects of Maternal Ligature-Induced Periodontitis on Brain in Offspring.
titre_fr: Effects of Maternal Ligature-Induced Periodontitis on Brain in Offspring.
auteurs: Imai C, Ohsugi Y, Lin P, Toyoshima K, Hirota T, Sekiguchi M, Shiba T, Iwata T, Uesaka N, Katagiri S
resume: The combined effects of chronic maternal periodontitis on offspring gut microbiome and brain outcomes remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of maternal oral microbiome disruption on brain function and gut microbiome in offspring. Periodontitis was induced in 11- to 12-wk-old parous C57BL/6J mice by maintaining ligatures around both sides of the maxillary second molars for 4 wk, followed by breeding with naïve male mice. Maternal oral and gut microbiome, as well as the offspring gut microbiome, was analyzed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Male offspring were evaluated at 7 to 8 wk of age via a set of analyses, including behavioral tests, microbiome profiling, RNA sequencing, immunohistochemistry for glial cell populations, and in vivo calcium imaging. Cerebellar DNA methylation was assessed at embryonic day 18.5 to examine early epigenetic alterations. Maternal periodontitis significantly reduced microbial diversity in the maternal oral microbiome and altered the composition of the maternal gut microbiome. In offspring, α-diversity was reduced in the gut microbiome. Behavioral analyses revealed impaired social interaction and reduced spontaneous locomotion, while motor coordination and memory-related behaviors were preserved. RNA sequencing identified region-specific changes in gene expression, particularly in the cerebellum, highlighting its vulnerability to maternal inflammatory conditions. DNA methylation analysis revealed epigenetic alterations during the fetal stage, suggesting early programming effects. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated a significant increase in astrocyte density in the cerebellum and frontal cortex, whereas oligodendrocytes and microglia were unaffected. Furthermore, calcium imaging revealed disrupted neuronal synchrony among Purkinje cells without significant changes in individual neuronal activity parameters. Maternal oral microbiome disruption induces coordinated alterations in maternal and offspring microbiomes and leads to persistent neurobehavioral, molecular, and cellular changes in offspring. These findings provide new insights into the link between maternal oral health and offspring neurodevelopment, highlighting the potential role of microbiome-mediated mechanisms in shaping brain function.

titre: The Red Nucleus in Motor Control and Autism Spectrum Disorder.
titre_fr: The Red Nucleus in Motor Control and Autism Spectrum Disorder.
auteurs: Wang Jiani, Pollick Frank, Delafield-Butt Jonathan
resume: Neuromotor differences of motor coordination, timing, postural regulation, and prospective motor control are common and emerge early in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). However, their underlying neural mechanisms remain incompletely understood, with existing research emphasising cortical and cerebellar systems. This review re-examines the red nucleus (RN), a midbrain structure embedded within cortical, cerebellar, and olivary motor pathways, as an underexplored component of distributed sensorimotor networks. We synthesise evidence from comparative neuroanatomy, animal experiments, human neuroimaging, movement disorders, and autism research, distinguishing direct RN findings from broader circuit-level inferences. Neuroimaging studies have reported RN-region susceptibility differences in autistic children, including an exploratory association with fine-motor development, but reproducible links to specific motor processes and RN-related causal mechanisms remain unestablished. We therefore propose a testable hypothesis that differences in RN structure, function, or connectivity may be associated with specific dimensions of motor function in autism. Error-related sensorimotor adaptation provides a primary experimental target, complemented by prospective motor control. Future investigations combining RN-sensitive neuroimaging, quantitative motor assessment, and transdiagnostic comparisons with developmental coordination disorder may determine whether RN-related measures provide explanatory information beyond sensorimotor systems. This framework positions the RN as a candidate component of autism-related motor networks.

titre: Neuroprotective potential of cardamonin in reserpine- and haloperidol-induced mice models of Parkinson's disease.
titre_fr: Neuroprotective potential of cardamonin in reserpine- and haloperidol-induced mice models of Parkinson's disease.
auteurs: Bhor A P, Ghaisas Mahesh M, Shete R V, Borate S R
resume: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by degeneration of dopaminergic neurons, resulting in tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia and poor motor coordination. The present study was aimed to evaluate anti-Parkinsonian activity and neuroprotective potential of cardamonin in reserpine and haloperidol induced experimental models of Parkinsonism in mice. Cardamonin is a naturally occurring chalcone that has been reported to possess antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities and may modulate biological processes associated with oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. Motor and cognitive functions were assessed using behavioral tests including open-field, pole-climbing, catalepsy and novel object recognition tests. Biochemical estimations of lipid peroxidation and endogenous antioxidants status were performed. Further, the tissue levels of dopamine were estimated. Brain tissues were subjected to routine histopathological investigation. Results showed that cardamonin significantly improved motor activity, decreased oxidative stress, enhanced the status of endogenous antioxidants and increased tissue levels of dopamine. Histopathological examination showed attenuation of general histological changes in treated animals. To summarize, the results support the anti-Parkinsonian activity and neuroprotective potential of cardamonin under the experimental conditions. However, direct preservation of dopaminergic neurons was not demonstrated because dopaminergic neuron-specific markers were not evaluated.

titre: Comparative study of acute-phase traumatic brain injury in rats of different weeks of age under identical impact force.
titre_fr: Comparative study of acute-phase traumatic brain injury in rats of different weeks of age under identical impact force.
auteurs: Chen Diyou, Wang Peng, Zhang Letian, Qiu Jinlong, Zhu Xiyan, Xiang Hongyi, Wang Qiushi, Guo Yu, Zhao Hui, Xiong Kunlin
resume: The closed head injury (CHI) model in rats is widely used in preclinical research, yet this model exhibits certain variability, partly due to the use of rats of different ages in experiments. To explore this variability, we selected rats of commonly used ages (8, 10, and 12 weeks) and induced brain injury under the same impact strength, comparing biomechanical responses, behavioral changes, and neuropathological outcomes. The results indicated that with increasing age, linear acceleration and rotational acceleration significantly decreased, and the younger age group (8 weeks) exhibited more severe neurological deficits and behavioral impairments, particularly in motor coordination and anxiety-like behaviors. Histological analysis showed the most severe neuronal loss and disorganization in the cerebral cortex and hippocampus in the 8-week group, with more extensive axonal injury. In contrast, the 10-week and 12-week groups showed milder pathological changes and better-preserved neuronal morphology. Molecular analysis revealed higher expression levels of glial fibrillary acidic protein, cleaved caspase-3, and interleukin-1 beta in younger rats, suggesting a positive correlation between these molecular markers and injury severity. Overall, this study reveals the significant impact of age differences in rats on TBI outcomes, highlighting the importance of age in TBI experiments and providing a basis for reducing experimental variability and enhancing the translational relevance to clinical applications.

titre: Task-Related Differences in Lip Motor Performance Between Children and Adults During Blowing and Sucking: A Composite Sensor Study.
titre_fr: Task-Related Differences in Lip Motor Performance Between Children and Adults During Blowing and Sucking: A Composite Sensor Study.
auteurs: Kusashio Nao, Hozawa Mio, Nakamura Yuki, Sotome Tetsuya, Tsukuno Saeko, Yonemoto Yuki, Hayasaki Haruaki
resume: Objective assessments of lip-closing function in children are increasingly of interest, but the task-specific, age-related characteristics of lip motor coordination remain unclear. To compare the lip motor performance of adults and children during blowing and sucking using a composite sensor (CS) that simultaneously measures lip-closing pressure (LP), intraoral pressure (IP) and upper orbicularis oris electromyographic (EMG) activity. In this cross-sectional study, 30 children (mean age 8.7 ± 1.7 years) and 25 adults (mean age 27.4 ± 3.9 years) performed blowing and sucking tasks. LP, IP and EMG activity were recorded simultaneously using a CS. Integral values of LP, IP and EMG were calculated and the relationships between pressure and EMG activity were analysed to identify any task- and age-related differences. LP and IP were lower in the children than in the adults during both tasks. During blowing, LP correlated with EMG activity only for children, whereas IP correlated with EMG activity for both groups. During sucking, LP correlated with EMG activity only for adults and IP showed no significant correlation with EMG activity. Lip motor performance differs between children and adults in a task-related manner. The distinct relationships among EMG activity, LP and IP imply qualitative age-group differences in perioral motor coordination rather than simple differences in strength. The evaluation of lip motor performance under multiple conditions may provide a more comprehensive means of assessing age-related variations in lip motor function in clinical settings.

titre: Neural and behavioral signatures of live and video demonstrations in bimanual interpersonal coordination: An EEG and kinematic study.
titre_fr: Neural and behavioral signatures of live and video demonstrations in bimanual interpersonal coordination: An EEG and kinematic study.
auteurs: Doosti Masoumeh, Tahmasebi Boroujeni Shahzad, Shirzad Araghi Elham
resume: Neural oscillations in the mu (8-12 Hz) and high-beta (21-30 Hz) bands are established markers of interpersonal coordination. However, the influence of social context-live versus video modeling - on sensorimotor engagement during coordinated action remains poorly understood. This study investigated how model type and engagement mode (execution vs. observation) shape neural and behavioral responses during an interpersonal motor coordination task. Twenty right-handed females (25.47 ± 3.4 years) were randomly assigned to train with either a live or video model (n = 10 per group). The same model performed 30-s sequences of elbow flexion-extension. Participants observed and executed the task with both live and video models across three phases (pre-test, post-test, and retention). During practice following the pre-test, participants trained coordinately with the model for 30 min. EEG activity was recorded from C3, Cz, and C4 electrodes, and spectral power was analyzed in the mu (8-12 Hz) and high-beta (21-30 Hz) bands. Kinematic coordination was quantified using vector coding of coupling angles between the participant and the model during execution. Results indicated significant desynchronization in both mu and high-beta bands during execution trials. Compared with the video-model condition, live-model interaction produced stronger high-beta suppression and more stable kinematic coupling. Additionally, mu suppression during observation increased across practice phases from pre-test to post-test and retention. Social context shapes interpersonal synchronization; physical presence may enhance perception-action coupling and predictive motor coding underlying joint action.

titre: A comprehensive review of detection, optical character recognition, and structuring methods for herbarium label digitization.
titre_fr: A comprehensive review of detection, optical character recognition, and structuring methods for herbarium label digitization.
auteurs: Abbad Hiba, Ariouat Hanane, Turenne Nicolas, Chenin Eric, Sebaa Abderrazak, Prifti Edi, Zucker Jean-Daniel, Sklab Youcef
resume: Global herbarium digitization has produced over 50 million specimen images, many of which contain handwritten or printed labels with rich metadata such as species names, collection dates, localities, and ecological notes. Manual transcription of this information is labor intensive, error prone, and not scalable, which has motivated the development of automated solutions. This systematic review examines studies published between 2018 and 2026, identified through electronic database searches and backward reference screening, focusing on deep learning and computer vision approaches for herbarium label digitization. The reviewed methods include convolutional neural networks, transformer-based models, large language models, and open-source pipelines for optical character recognition and structured metadata extraction from historical and handwritten botanical records. The results highlight significant advances in label detection, text recognition accuracy, and metadata structuring enabled by deep learning techniques, although reported performance varies considerably depending on dataset quality, handwriting complexity, and domain adaptation strategies. Despite this progress, substantial challenges remain in handling historical handwriting styles, heterogeneous label layouts, and multilingual collections. Future research should emphasize the creation of curated benchmark datasets and the development of scalable, robust artificial intelligence (AI) pipelines to enhance the reliability, efficiency, and generalizability of automated herbarium digitization systems.

titre: Are clinician-administered ataxia scales truly culture-free? Rethinking contextual validity in diverse populations.
titre_fr: Are clinician-administered ataxia scales truly culture-free? Rethinking contextual validity in diverse populations.
auteurs: Narzari Hina, Yadav Ravi, Srivastava Achal Kumar, Pal Pramod Kumar, Garg Divyani
resume: Hereditary cerebellar ataxias are genetically and phenotypically heterogeneous progressive neurodegenerative disorders characterized by substantial functional impairment. With the emergence of disease-modifying therapies and gene-targeted clinical trials, standardized and reliable clinical outcome measures are essential for assessing disease severity and progression. Among the available scales, two are widely used by clinicians to assess ataxia: The Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA) and the International Cooperative Ataxia Rating Scale (ICARS). Given considerable linguistic, educational and sociocultural heterogeneity across the globe, we opine that it may pose challenges to the uniform application and cross-cultural comparability of these instruments. Published translations and adaptations were also examined to determine whether cultural adaptation extended beyond linguistic translation. Among all the identified adaptations, reported processes predominantly comprised forward and backward translation, expert review and assessment of linguistic, conceptual or cultural equivalence. These findings suggest that linguistic translation alone may not be sufficient to ensure that clinician-rated ataxia scales retain equivalent meaning and measurement across diverse populations. We therefore introduce the concept of "contextual validity" emphasizing that language, educational heterogeneity, literacy, graphomotor familiarity, cultural practices and testing environments that may influence performance independently of cerebellar dysfunction. This perspective outlines considerations for developing contextually adapted and psychometrically validated Indian-language versions of SARA and ICARS to improve measurement accuracy and support equitable clinical assessment and participation in global clinical trials.

titre: Growth Curves and Predictors of Touch-Typing Fluency in 12-13-Year-Old Students With and Without Dyslexia.
titre_fr: Growth Curves and Predictors of Touch-Typing Fluency in 12-13-Year-Old Students With and Without Dyslexia.
auteurs: Košir Janja, Košir Andrej, Podlesek Anja
resume: Students with dyslexia often have difficulties with higher and lower-level writing skills. Research shows that they have lower transcription speed and accuracy compared to their peers. A commonly recommended educational adjustment for addressing writing difficulties of these students is the use of a computer and typing instead of handwriting. However, there is evidence that students with language-based handwriting problems can also type slowly. As dyslexia is also associated with difficulties in procedural learning, these students may have difficulties in learning touch-typing. This study investigated how Slovenian students aged 12-13 years with dyslexia (n = 21) learn touch-typing on a keyboard home-row compared to their peers without dyslexia (n = 21). The growth curves for typing fluency were analysed using linear mixed modelling. The results showed that students with dyslexia achieved significantly lower typing fluency and slower learning progress at all learning stages. Students without dyslexia reached a learning plateau earlier. The achieved touch-typing fluency was best predicted by simple finger typing fluency, pre-existing typing technique fluency, and non-word decoding fluency. Our study enhances understanding of the touch-typing acquisition in students with dyslexia, though further research is needed to explore how this development unfolds across all phases of learning touch-typing.

titre: Interfacial Hydrogen-Bond Regulation by Phytic Acid and SiO2 for Constructing Robust Dual-CrossLinked Nanocomposite Hydrogels.
titre_fr: Interfacial Hydrogen-Bond Regulation by Phytic Acid and SiO2 for Constructing Robust Dual-CrossLinked Nanocomposite Hydrogels.
auteurs: Feng Yujiao, Zhang Xinbin, Zhang Shaohua, Zhong Linlin, Xu Wenlong
revue: Langmuir : the ACS journal of surfaces and colloids
resume: Conventional hydrogels generally suffer from insufficient mechanical strength and structural stability due to limited intermolecular interactions. Herein, a phytic acid (PA)/SiO2 synergistic hydrogen-bond network engineering strategy is proposed to fabricate poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/polyacrylamide (PAM)/PA/SiO2 nanocomposite hydrogels. Unlike traditional PVA/PAM hydrogel systems, PA serves as an interfacial hydrogen-bond-mediating agent to couple SiO2 nanofillers with the PVA/PAM polymer network. The phosphate and hydroxyl groups in PA can simultaneously interact with both the PVA/PAM chains and the silanol groups on the SiO2 surface. Additionally, PA enhances the dispersion stability of SiO2, thereby introducing additional nanoscale interaction sites and forming a synergistic hydrogen-bonding network. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and complementary characterizations confirm the formation of extensive intermolecular hydrogen-bonding interactions, revealing the structural regulation mechanism of the hydrogel network. Benefiting from the optimized network architecture, the nanocomposite hydrogel exhibits enhanced mechanical strength, fatigue resistance, antibacterial activity, and highly sensitive strain-sensing performance. Furthermore, an intelligent handwriting recognition system is developed by integrating the hydrogel sensor with machine learning algorithms. This work provides an effective strategy for engineering high-performance multifunctional hydrogels for intelligent sensing applications.

titre: Gradient-structured allyl cellulose ball arrays for high performance piezoresistive sensors and intelligent handwriting recognition.
titre_fr: Gradient-structured allyl cellulose ball arrays for high performance piezoresistive sensors and intelligent handwriting recognition.
auteurs: Chen Wei, Zhang Yu, Ji Xingxiang, Li Nan
resume: Developing flexible pressure sensors that combine ultralow detection limits, high sensitivity, and environmental sustainability remains challenging, particularly using bio-based alternatives to petroleum-derived polymers. We present ultra-sensitive pressure sensors based on multi-scale allyl cellulose ball (ACB) arrays. ACBs were fabricated through syringe-based droplet formation in a saturated NaCl bath and UV-mediated crosslinking of allyl cellulose (AC), yielding a dual-network architecture comprising physically entangled chains from salt-induced phase separation and covalently crosslinked allyl groups that imparts mechanical robustness with controlled diameters (1.2, 1.5, and 2.2 mm). The sensor features a gradient architecture where different-sized ACBs create sequential activation mechanisms: larger balls deform first under low pressure, followed by progressive engagement of smaller balls, achieving ultrahigh sensitivity (27.2% kPa<sup>-1</sup>), ultralow detection limit (8 Pa), rapid response/recovery (38/40 ms), broad detection range (8 Pa-10 kPa), and exceptional stability (less than 5% drift over 6500 cycles). The approach eliminates expensive lithographic fabrication while surpassing human tactile thresholds. We demonstrated practical applications including flexible electroluminescent devices with programmable patterns and an intelligent handwriting recognition system capable of real-time character classification with 99.3% accuracy. This work establishes a gradient architecture strategy for biodegradable cellulose-based flexible sensors, offering a scalable and cost-effective pathway toward next-generation sustainable wearable electronics and intelligent human-machine interfaces.

titre: Temporal dynamics of central and peripheral processes in novel word acquisition: Evidence from co-registration of EEG and kinematics in natural handwriting.
titre_fr: Temporal dynamics of central and peripheral processes in novel word acquisition: Evidence from co-registration of EEG and kinematics in natural handwriting.
auteurs: Fu Yang, Enrique Jan Cordón Damian, Bermúdez-Margaretto Beatriz, Wang Huili, Domínguez Alberto
revue: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior
resume: Current models of handwriting production posit a hierarchy of cognitive subprocesses through which linguistic information cascades from central lexical encoding to peripheral motor execution. Yet it remains unclear how such cascaded coordination supports the formation of new memory traces for novel words. Here, we combined simultaneous electroencephalography and handwriting kinematics in native Spanish speakers (n = 63) to track word learning dynamics across repeated handwritten production. Event-related potentials (ERPs) time-locked to stimulus onset and kinematics-related potentials (KRPs) evoked by the motor execution of the critical letter revealed temporal coordination between central and peripheral learning effects as a function of repeated exposure, with exposure-driven modulation in the 173-309 msec after stimulus onset within a centro-frontal cluster and a comparable effect in the 133-286 msec post pen-down window over posterior sites. While orthographic encoding approached an asymptote after four exposures, motor refinement followed a more protracted trajectory across all encounters, indicating that the central and peripheral processes do not cascade to the same extent. The ongoing neural-kinematic coupling further revealed a parallel unfolding of motor planning and orthographic processing. Critically, the magnitude of exposure-induced neural modulation during learning predicted the strength of subsequent lexical competition in a masked priming lexical decision task after overnight consolidation. These findings substantiate the automatic nature of neural memory-trace formation coupled with cognitive and motor dynamics. The motor system continuously operates on partially specified linguistic information, establishing word-level orthographic representations before refining the letter-level graphomotor details on which lexical competition depends.

titre: Altered Cognitive Control and Cortical Oscillatory Dynamics in Athletes With ACL Reconstruction During Decision-Making Under Uncertainty.
titre_fr: Altered Cognitive Control and Cortical Oscillatory Dynamics in Athletes With ACL Reconstruction During Decision-Making Under Uncertainty.
auteurs: Jiménez-Martínez Jesús, Gutiérrez-Capote Alejandro, Alarcón-López Francisco, Cárdenas-Vélez David
revue: The American journal of sports medicine
resume: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury induces neuroplastic changes within the central nervous system (CNS) that may persist beyond reconstruction and rehabilitation. The purpose was to compare neurocognitive performance and cortical oscillatory activity between open-skill athletes (eg, soccer, basketball, or handball players) without ACL injury history and athletes with ACL reconstruction (ACLR) during a probabilistic go/no-go task. It was hypothesized that athletes with ACLR would exhibit poorer behavioral performance and less efficient oscillatory dynamics, particularly higher theta and lower suppression of beta and alpha power oscillations after goal stimulus onset. Controlled laboratory study. A total of 90 open-skill athletes (45 non-ACLR, 45 ACLR) performed a probabilistic go/no-go task while electroencephalographic recording was performed. Time-frequency analysis targeted midfrontal theta (4-7 Hz), left-lateralized central beta (15-25 Hz), and posterior alpha (8-12 Hz) oscillations during prestimulus and target stimulus windows. Linear mixed-effects models examined group differences in cognitive performance and oscillatory power. Athletes with ACLR showed slower response times and lower accuracy (d = 0.75-1.09). Midfrontal theta power was attenuated for the ACLR group during the prestimulus phase (d = 0.60) yet elevated during target phase trials (d = 0.48), indicating a shift from proactive to reactive cognitive control in athletes with ACLR. Left-lateralized central beta (d = 0.61) and posterior alpha suppression (d = 0.55) were reduced, reflecting impaired motor cortical disinhibition and less efficient visual-attentional resource deployment, especially under high uncertainty conditions. Athletes with ACLR showed persistent alterations in the cortical oscillatory mechanisms associated with conflict monitoring, motor preparation, and attentional allocation under uncertainty. These neurocognitive alterations may compromise adaptive motor responses in sport contexts characterized by high uncertainty and cognitive mental demand, potentially increasing reinjury risk. These findings support the integration of neurocognitive assessment into return-to-sport protocols. Alterations in cortical oscillatory dynamics during decision-making under uncertainty may reflect reduced efficiency in cognitive control, motor preparation, and attentional allocation, which are not detected by standard assessments. Exercise professionals should consider integrating these assessments into return-to-sport protocols to address the persistent CNS alterations that may underlie reinjury risk in athletes with ACLR.

titre: Cross-sectoral gerontopsychiatric treatment and rehabilitation in nursing homes (SGB Reha)-study protocol for a stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial.
titre_fr: Cross-sectoral gerontopsychiatric treatment and rehabilitation in nursing homes (SGB Reha)-study protocol for a stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial.
auteurs: Mierzwa Nora, Gradel Björn, Förstner Bernd R, Deeken Friederike, Desch Anke, Schroth Jennifer M, Du Manuel, Dierbach Oskar, Holmberg Christine, Hauptmann Michael, Rapp Michael, Häusler Andreas
resume: Demographic changes in Germany have increased the need for care to 5.7 million people, with around 800,000 living in residential care facilities. Nursing home residents are vulnerable, suffering from multimorbidity and cognitive impairments, with prevalent use of psychotropic medication linked to negative outcomes like sedation and hospitalizations. So far, there is little research on multimodal rehabilitation programs in nursing homes. The SGB Reha study aims to implement a cross-sectoral rehabilitation model to improve activities of daily living (ADLs), cognition, and quality of life for nursing home residents, reducing hospitalizations and treatment costs, and increasing the chance of residents returning home post-care. The study is conducted in 12 nursing homes located in North Rhine-Westphalia and Hamburg. It employs a cluster-randomized stepped-wedge design with randomization at the facility level. Data collection occurs at three consecutive measurement points, at 0, 3, and 6 months. The recruitment target includes 720 nursing home residents across four six-month study phases. Nursing home residents aged 65 years and older who had been admitted to the nursing home within the previous 12 months-either as a routine admission or following a hospital stay-and who have a care level of at least 2 are eligible for inclusion. The intervention integrates therapeutic and rehabilitative nursing practices. Structured multidisciplinary case conferences (including neurologists/psychiatrists, and consulting pharmacists) establish objectives, assess progress, adapt personalized care, develop therapeutic strategies, and systematically evaluate medications, especially emphasizing the reduction of psychotropic drugs and polypharmacy prevention. A multidisciplinary team delivers the intervention, supported by study nurses coordinating processes. resume_fr: Demographic changes in Germany have increased the need for care to 5.7 million people, with around 800,000 living in residential care facilities. titre: Neurological and functional recovery despite persistent skull defect after decompressive hemicraniectomy: a case report.
titre_fr: Neurological and functional recovery despite persistent skull defect after decompressive hemicraniectomy: a case report.
auteurs: Iwata Koki, Takami Syunta, Onishi Kozue, Saito Atsuo, Furuta Ryoichi, Sasaki Takeshi, Sugawara Kazuhiro
resume: Decompressive hemicraniectomy is a life-saving procedure for malignant cerebral infarction with severe edema. Although cranioplasty is performed to enhance neurological recovery, longitudinal descriptions of recovery with a persistent skull defect remain scarce. In such patients, syndrome of the trephined (SoT) may impact neurological function during upright activity. We present a patient who showed neurological and functional improvement beyond 6 months after stroke onset despite a persistent skull defect following bone flap removal due to infection. To describe longitudinal neurological and functional progression beyond 6 months after stroke onset in a patient with a persistent skull defect after decompressive hemicraniectomy. A 60-year-old man with right internal carotid artery occlusion underwent decompressive hemicraniectomy with extensive internal decompression. Cranioplasty performed on hospital day 40 was complicated by infection, necessitating removal of the bone flap. Intensive inpatient rehabilitation included postural control training, transfer practice, activities of daily living training, and cognitive-perceptual interventions, with monitoring. Beyond 6 months after stroke onset, consciousness, cognition, and mobility improved. No reproducible posture-dependent neurological worsening suggestive of clinically manifest SoT was observed during upright activity. From admission to the inpatient rehabilitation unit to discharge, the Glasgow Coma Scale score improved from 12 to 14, the Hasegawa's Dementia Scale-Revised score from 13 to 23, the Behavioral Inattention Test score from 20 to 72, and the Scale for Contraversive Pushing score from 2.5 in sitting and 3 in standing to 0.25 in both positions. At discharge, wheelchair transfers and toileting required minimal assistance. Neurological and functional improvements were observed beyond 6 months after stroke onset, despite extensive cortical resection and a persistent skull defect. Although the contributions of biological recovery and rehabilitation could not be distinguished, this case illustrates adaptation of rehabilitation goals and priorities in response to evolving clinical and functional barriers.

titre: Academic Functioning and Service Utilization After Sport-Related Injury in College Students: Comparing Concussion and Musculoskeletal Injury Experiences.
titre_fr: Academic Functioning and Service Utilization After Sport-Related Injury in College Students: Comparing Concussion and Musculoskeletal Injury Experiences.
auteurs: Kennedy Mary R T, O'Brien Katy H
resume: College student athletes commonly experience concussion and related cognitive and academic difficulties; however, the extent to which these difficulties are associated with engagement in rehabilitation and academic support services remains unclear. This study compared academic functioning, symptom burden, and support service utilization between college student athletes with sport-related concussion (SRC) and those with musculoskeletal (MSK) injuries to identify potential gaps in postinjury care relevant to return to learn. In this cross-sectional retrospective study, 63 student athletes (41 SRC, 22 MSK) completed the College Survey for Students With Concussion and Other Injuries. Outcomes included self-reported academic functioning, total and domain-specific symptom burden (cognitive, physical, emotional), and utilization of support services (medical, rehabilitation, disability, counseling). Group differences were examined using nonparametric tests, and associations among symptoms, academic functioning, and service utilization were evaluated using correlational analyses. Compared with the MSK group, student athletes with SRC reported greater academic difficulties and higher total symptom burden, particularly for cognitive and physical symptoms. Despite these differences, overall service utilization did not differ between groups. Physical therapy was used more frequently by the MSK group, whereas other services were rarely accessed by either group. Within the SRC group, greater symptom burden was associated with more self-reported academic challenges and a higher likelihood of service use, indicating greater help-seeking among highest need participants despite overall very low utilization. Findings suggest a mismatch between concussion-related academic and cognitive difficulties and engagement with rehabilitation and other services in college student athletes. Results highlight the need to investigate the need for and pathways to support services, including speech-language pathology and other cognitively focused interventions within collegiate concussion management and return-to-learn frameworks. https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34925325.

titre: Good Science, Real Constraints: Ethics-Based Approaches to Managing Conflicting Incentives in Academic-Health System Research Partnerships.
titre_fr: Good Science, Real Constraints: Ethics-Based Approaches to Managing Conflicting Incentives in Academic-Health System Research Partnerships.
auteurs: Prusynski Rachel A, Minick Kate I, Johnson Michael P
resume: Partnerships between health systems and external academic researchers are increasingly central to embedded and learning health system (LHS) research in rehabilitation. Such partnerships offer substantial promise, but they also introduce ethical and practical challenges arising from conflicting incentives related to research rigor, timelines, dissemination, financial sustainability, and academic freedom. This perspective examines these challenges through the lens of the Ethics of Research and Implementation domain of the LHS Researcher Core Competencies, grounded in the ethical principles of the physical therapy profession. Drawing on existing literature and the authors' experience as academic-health system research partners, this perspective contrasts academic incentives (ie, grant funding, peer-reviewed publication, and generalizable knowledge) with health system incentives focused on operational efficiency, return on investment, and organizational reputation. Because health systems vary widely in their capacity to support research, this perspective presents a typology of partnership contexts and describes where ethical challenges may arise in each. This perspective then proposes ethics-based strategies for mutually beneficial research partnerships that apply across the different partnership contexts. These include transparent alignment of research goals with organizational priorities, accurate differentiation between research and quality improvement, attention to oversight particularly when a partner has less research infrastructure, pre-specification of outcomes, interim deliverables for health system stakeholders, and data use and publication agreements that protect academic freedom while allowing health system input. It illustrates these strategies with a partnership in which protected academic freedom and collaboration on dissemination allowed findings to reach national policy audiences. The Ethics of Research and Implementation competencies offer a practical framework for anticipating these conflicts and addressing them deliberately, enabling partnerships that generate rigorous knowledge while remaining useful to the health systems and patients they serve.

titre: Differential Postsurgery Outcomes Across Physical Therapy Care Pathways in Lumbar Spinal Stenosis Surgery: Analyses of a National Registry-Based Cohort.
titre_fr: Differential Postsurgery Outcomes Across Physical Therapy Care Pathways in Lumbar Spinal Stenosis Surgery: Analyses of a National Registry-Based Cohort.
auteurs: Fors Maria, Öberg Birgitta, Enthoven Paul, Lundberg Mari, Schröder Karin, Lindbäck Yvonne, Svensson Jard, Abbott Allan
resume: Lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS) is the most common indication for spinal surgery. Physical therapist treatment is consistently recommended throughout the care pathway for LSS, including before and after surgical treatment. However, the effectiveness of pre- and postsurgery rehabilitation interventions are unclear. The objective of this study was to explore 1-year postsurgery outcomes associated with different physical therapy care pathways in patients who had undergone surgery for LSS. This was a registry-based multicenter study using data from the Swedish National Spine Surgery Registry. Swedish spine clinics participating in the Swedish National Spine Surgery Registry, with an estimated national coverage of 95%. Participants were patients surgically treated for LSS between 2021 and 2023 and with data on physical therapist treatment prior to a surgical decision, while waiting for surgery, and after surgery (N = 7969). Patient-reported exposure to physical therapy before and after LSS surgery, categorized into four physical therapy care pathways. Outcomes were patient-reported pain intensity, disability, health-related quality of life, general health, gait function, analgesic use, repeat surgeries, satisfaction with surgery, and perceived participation in decision-making. Multivariable logistic regression and univariate analysis of variance were used to assess differences in 1-year postsurgery outcomes between 4 physical therapy care pathways. Compared to patients who reported pre- and postsurgery physical therapy, patients with only presurgery physical therapy demonstrated better outcomes across all measures and had higher odds of reaching the thresholds for meaningful and acceptable outcomes at 1 year after surgery (odds ratio [OR] = 1.39 to 1.56). In contrast, patients with only postsurgery physical therapy had higher pain intensity, worse gait function and health-related quality of life, and less improvement in disability and gait function. They also had lower odds of reaching clinically acceptable thresholds in pain intensity (spinal OR = 0.83 [96% CI = 0.74 to 0.93]; leg OR = 0.78 [95% CI = 0.67 to 0.88]) and disability (OR = 0.83 [95% CI = 0.72 to 0.96]). Few differences were observed between patients with both pre- and postsurgery physical therapy and those with no physical therapy. The latter group was small, and comparisons should be interpreted accordingly. Presurgery physical therapy may be beneficial to consider for patients undergoing surgery for LSS, while additional postsurgery physical therapy may not be warranted for all. The results may inform the development of surgical care pathways for LSS.

titre: Post-Treatment Follow-up, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport: Proceedings of the International Consensus Meetings on Cartilage Repair of the Ankle.
titre_fr: Post-Treatment Follow-up, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport: Proceedings of the International Consensus Meetings on Cartilage Repair of the Ankle.
auteurs: Rubin Jared, Tham Alexander, Butler James J, Gauthier Paloma, Hedbany Davis, Kennedy John G, Smyth Niall A, Murawski Christopher D, Adams Samuel B, Berlet Gregory C, Buda Roberto, Labib Sameh A, Nunley James A, Raikin Steven M, Andrews Carol L, Angthong Chayanin, Batista Jorge P, Bayer Stephen, Becher Christoph, Boakye Lorraine A T, Brown Alexandra J, Calder James D F, Canata Gian Luigi, Carreira Dominic S, Clanton Thomas O, Dahmen Jari, D'Hooghe Pieter, DiGiovanni Christopher W, Dombrowski Malcolm E, Ferkel Richard D, Ferrao Paulo N F, Glazebrook Mark, Giza Eric, Gomaa Mohamed, Görtz Simon, Haleem Amgad M, Hamid Kamran S, Hangody Laszlo, Hannon Charles P, Haverkamp Daniel, Hertel Jay, Hintermann Beat, Hogan MaCalus V, Hunt Kenneth J, Hurley Eoghan T, Karlsson Jon, Kerkhoffs Gino M M J, Kim Hak Jun, Kong Siu-Wah, Lambers Kaj T A, Woo Lee Jin, Lee Keun Bae, Ling Jeffrey S, Longo Umile Giuseppe, Marangon Alberto, McCollum Graham, Mitchell Adam W, Mittwede Peter N, Nehrer Stefan, Niemeyer Philipp, O'Malley Martin J, Osei-Hwedieh David, Paul Jochen, Pearce Christopher J, Pereira Helder, Popchak Adam, Prado Marcelo P, Reilingh Mikel L, Rothrauff Benjamin B, Schon Lew C, Simpson Helene, Sofka Carolyn M, Spennacchio Pietro, Stone James W, Sullivan Martin, Takao Masato, Tanaka Yasuhito, Thordarson David B, Tuan Rocky, Valderrabano Victor, van Bergen Christian J A, van Dijk C Niek, van Dijk Pim A D, Vannini Francesca, Vaseenon Tanawat, Walther Markus, Wiewiorski Martin, Xu Xiangyang, Yasui Youichi, Hua Yinghui, Yoshimura Ichiro, Younger Alastair S E, Zhang Zijun
resume: BackgroundPostoperative follow-up, rehabilitation, and return to sport (RTS) are key components of recovery following surgical management of osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLT). However, substantial variability exists in postoperative protocols, with limited high-quality evidence guiding clinical practicesMethodsInternational experts convened during the International Congress on Cartilage Repair of the Ankle (ICCRA) in Pittsburgh, USA (2017), with subsequent ratification of recommendations in New York, USA (2025). The original consensus statements were developed using a modified Delphi process involving electronic surveys, structured questionnaires, and expert discussion. Consensus strength was defined as consensus (51%-74%), strong consensus (75%-99%), or unanimous (100%). The recommendations addressed postoperative follow-up, rehabilitation, and RTS following OLT management.ResultsA total of 16 consensus statements were developed and subsequently ratified, comprising 7 statements addressing post-treatment follow-up and 9 addressing rehabilitation and RTS. All statements achieved strong consensus, with agreement ranging from 75% to 98%. Follow-up recommendations emphasized standardized clinical assessment and patient-reported outcomes, with extended monitoring in select patients. Rehabilitation recommendations supported early controlled motion and progressive weightbearing, with individualized progression according to procedure and clinical performance. Return to sport recommendations emphasized functional recovery and individualized decision-making. Ten statements (63%) were classified exclusively as Grade E, highlighting the limited evidence supporting several recommendations.ConclusionThe ICCRA consensus statements establish a structured framework for postoperative follow-up, rehabilitation, and RTS following surgical management of OLT. Despite strong expert agreement, several recommendations remain supported by limited evidence, underlining the need for prospective studies to establish validated, procedure-specific rehabilitation protocols and objective RTS criteria.Level of Evidence:V, expert consensus.

titre: Lessons learned from developing serious games for upper-limb rehabilitation in children.
titre_fr: Lessons learned from developing serious games for upper-limb rehabilitation in children.
auteurs: Sanchez David Infante, Bourazeri Aikaterini
resume: Virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and serious games have demonstrated growing potential in physical therapy, exergaming, and the promotion of physical activity across diverse patient populations. However, the development of therapeutic games, particularly for rehabilitation in children, still lacks consolidated guidelines and structured frameworks. This study aims to document the design and development process of two gamified upper-limb rehabilitation systems for children, developed in collaboration with physical therapists, and to derive preliminary clinician-informed design recommendations. An iterative development process was carried out in close collaboration with clinicians. Feedback and observations from therapy sessions were collected and analyzed. These findings were contextualized through a targeted narrative review of relevant literature to examine their relationship with existing research. The comparative analysis produced actionable design recommendations regarding game mechanics, reward structures, adaptive difficulty, and feature extraction strategies. Key findings highlight the need to tailor gameplay to children's abilities through simplified narratives, therapeutic mechanics, consistent feedback, and adaptive difficulty. The results highlight the unique challenges and opportunities involved in designing serious games for therapy for children. It advocates for the development of preliminary clinician-informed design principles to support the creation of engaging, usable, and clinically grounded rehabilitation games for children.

titre: Sensorimotor rehabilitation and changes in upper limb function after acute cervical spinal disorders: a retrospective case series (n = 14).
titre_fr: Sensorimotor rehabilitation and changes in upper limb function after acute cervical spinal disorders: a retrospective case series (n = 14).
auteurs: Agostinho Inês Margarida Oliveira, Temudo Ana, Bacelo Sérgio Manuel Oliveira Gonçalves, Picoito Ricardo, Bernardes Rafael, Sousa Luís
resume: Upper limb impairment is a common consequence of acute cervical spinal disorders and can substantially compromise functional independence, highlighting the need for rehabilitation strategies that address sensorimotor and functional impairments. To describe changes in upper limb function following a sensorimotor intervention incorporating a viscoelastic product in individuals with acute non-degenerative cervical spinal disorders. Uncontrolled, before and after, observational retrospective longitudinal case series study with no comparator group, conducted over a 14-month period. Surgical inpatient unit. Fourteen participants with acute non-degenerative cervical spinal disorders receiving a rehabilitation nursing programme, with heterogeneous underlying diagnoses including disc herniation, fracture, space-occupying lesion, myelopathy, and spinal cord trauma. Spasticity assessed using the Modified Ashworth Scale, upper limb muscle strength assessed using the Medical Research Council Muscle Scale, and functional independence assessed using the Barthel Index. Statistically significant changes in spasticity were observed between baseline and discharge (Z = -3.093; p < .001; r = 0.83), together with significant changes in muscle strength across all assessed upper extremity segments: fingers (Z = -3.330; p < .001; r = 0.89), wrist (Z = -3.324; p < .001; r = 0.89), forearm (Z = -2.953; p < .001; r = 0.79), elbow (Z = -3.084; p < .001; r = 0.82), and shoulder (Z = -2.555; p = .008; r = 0.68), as well as in functional independence (Z = -3.297; p < .001; r = 0.88). Changes in spasticity, upper limb muscle strength and functional independence were observed between baseline and discharge. Given the uncontrolled retrospective case-series design and absence of a control or comparison group, these findings should be interpreted with caution, as they cannot be attributed specifically to the intervention and should be considered hypothesis-generating for future research. Further prospective controlled studies are warranted to evaluate the effectiveness of this approach.

titre: Menopause, Weight Loss, and Pelvic Floor Changes: Clinical and Aesthetic Considerations.
titre_fr: Menopause, Weight Loss, and Pelvic Floor Changes: Clinical and Aesthetic Considerations.
auteurs: Chirumamilla Varshita, Tyler Kelly H
revue: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
resume: Menopause is associated with hormonal, structural, and functional changes affecting the vulvovaginal tissues, pelvic floor, and urinary tract. Weight loss may further alter soft-tissue volume and body composition, although effects on pelvic floor function remain incompletely understood. The aim of this study was to review menopause-associated vulvovaginal and pelvic floor changes and discuss implications for dermatologic evaluation, weight loss, symptom management, and procedural counseling. A narrative review of literature addressing menopause, pelvic floor dysfunction, weight loss, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, pelvic floor rehabilitation, and emerging vulvovaginal therapies was performed. Menopause-associated tissue remodeling may contribute to genitourinary syndrome of menopause, urinary symptoms, sexual dysfunction, and pelvic floor disorders. Weight loss may improve obesity-associated urinary incontinence but can also reduce lean mass and external soft-tissue volume. titre: Adherence System Usability Patient Experience and Psychosocial Impact in Robot Assisted Gait Neurorehabilitation A Cross Sectional Study.
titre_fr: Adherence System Usability Patient Experience and Psychosocial Impact in Robot Assisted Gait Neurorehabilitation A Cross Sectional Study.
auteurs: Ketenci Pinar Gungor, Kaya Basak Bilir
resume: BackgroundAttendance, usability and rehabilitation experience may relate to perceived psychosocial impact in robotic neurorehabilitation.ObjectiveTo examine these associations in adults receiving robot-assisted gait neurorehabilitation, including diagnosis-adjusted and exploratory indirect associations.MethodsThis single-center observational study included 250 adults with stroke, spinal cord injury, multiple sclerosis or cerebral palsy. The System Usability Scale (SUS), Neurorehabilitation Experience Questionnaire (NREQ) and Psychosocial Impact of Assistive Devices Scale (PIADS) were administered in week two. Attendance covered the planned course; participation equaled attended/planned sessions × 100. Analyses included Spearman correlations, adjusted regression, indirect-association models with 5,000 bootstrap resamples, Kruskal-Wallis tests and Cronbach's alpha.ResultsMean participation was 86.35 ± 8.38%. Mean SUS, NREQ and PIADS scores were 72.79 ± 12.06, 27.84 ± 4.92 and 1.67 ± 0.74, respectively. Adherence correlated with SUS (r<sub>s</sub> = 0.41), NREQ (r<sub>s</sub> = 0.49) and PIADS (r<sub>s</sub> = 0.53; all p < 0.001). After adjustment for diagnosis, age, sex and disease duration, adherence (B = 0.0145), SUS (B = 0.0210) and NREQ (B = 0.0630) remained associated with PIADS (all p < 0.001; R<sup>2</sup> = 0.650). The diagnosis-adjusted indirect association through NREQ was 0.0252 (95% bootstrap CI 0.0178-0.0336). Scores differed across adherence categories (all p < 0.001). Cronbach's alpha values were 0.86, 0.89 and 0.94, respectively.ConclusionGreater attendance, usability and rehabilitation experience were associated with favorable psychosocial impact. Diagnostic heterogeneity, simultaneous questionnaire assessment and temporal mismatch with attendance limit interpretation. These findings establish neither causal mediation nor functional improvement.

titre: Diagnosis, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport after Athletic Hamstring Injury: An ICCUS Society Consensus Statement.
titre_fr: Diagnosis, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport after Athletic Hamstring Injury: An ICCUS Society Consensus Statement.
auteurs: Gilliam Brandon, Draovitch Pete, Malone Terry, Mangine Bob, Manske Robert, Page Phil, Silver-Granelli Holly, Tyler Timothy F, Voight Michael L, Weiss Leigh J, Wilk Kevin E
revue: International journal of sports physical therapy
resume: Athletic hamstring injuries (AHSI) remain a persistent challenge because recurrence is common and clinical decisions often depend on incomplete evidence. This consensus statement is intended to give clinicians a practical, unified framework for classification, rehabilitation, and return to sport after athletic hamstring injury. The purpose of this study was to achieve expert consensus on the management of athletic hamstring injuries through a structured, scientific survey approach. Delphi Survey. A modified Delphi process, aligned with CREDES guidelines, was conducted with an expert panel of sports physical therapists identified as having specific expertise in AHSI from the ICCUS Society. Consensus was defined a priori as at least 80% agreement or disagreement on a 5-point Likert scale. Statements addressed three areas: AHSI examination and classification, rehabilitation and management, and return to sport (RTS) testing. Sixty statements were developed across three domains. Seventeen experienced clinicians completed the final round. Overall, 54 statements reached consensus, with a mean Likert score of 4.56 ± 0.37 out of 5 (strongly agree), and mean agreement of 89.88% ± 12.1%. Experts supported standardized terminology, MRI and the use of diagnostic ultrasound for diagnosis when appropriate, individualized and criterion-based rehabilitation, progressive tissue loading and length restoration, early neuromuscular control, gradual running and agility progression, progression to pain-free sprinting, objective strength assessment, sport-specific workloads, and athlete readiness as key RTS criteria. The findings emphasize active rehabilitation guided by measurable progress rather than reliance on fixed thresholds. Clinicians should combine injury classification, functional presentation, symptom response, objective testing, sport demands, and athlete confidence when advancing rehabilitation and making RTS decisions. This ICCUS Society consensus statement offers a practical roadmap for managing AHSI: classify clearly, load progressively, monitor symptoms, test objectively, and return athletes only when sport-specific running, sprinting, strength, training tolerance, and readiness align. 4.

titre: Narrative review of non-pharmacological interventions for chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy: exercise, physical therapy, cryotherapy and acupuncture.
titre_fr: Narrative review of non-pharmacological interventions for chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy: exercise, physical therapy, cryotherapy and acupuncture.
auteurs: Li Lingjun, Fan Mingsi, Ni Li, Wang Jing, Qiao Li
resume: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a heterogeneous, treatment-limiting adverse event of cytotoxic chemotherapy that impairs sensory, motor, autonomic and balance function, and substantially reduces cancer patients' quality of life. Current pharmacotherapy options are limited: duloxetine is the only guideline-recommended agent for established painful CIPN, while no drugs are approved for primary prevention. Non-pharmacological interventions have emerged as promising adjunctive strategies, yet evidence strength varies widely across modalities and patient subgroups. This narrative review aimed to synthesize contemporary clinical evidence of non-pharmacological interventions for CIPN prevention, symptom treatment and functional rehabilitation, to deliver stratified, chemotherapy-specific clinical guidance and identify gaps for future research. A narrative review design was adopted, without pre-registration or standardized systematic review screening protocols. Targeted manual literature retrieval was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI and Wanfang Data for peer-reviewed human clinical studies published between January 2018 and March 2025. We focused on four core non-pharmacological modalities for CIPN: multimodal exercise therapy, physical therapy incorporating cryotherapy, acupuncture-based complementary therapies, and behavioral self-management interventions. High-certainty evidence was defined as consistent results from large multicenter randomized controlled trials and network meta-analyses; moderate/low-certainty evidence was derived from small single-center trials and observational studies. Cumulative stratified evidence demonstrates clear heterogeneity in intervention efficacy and clinical applicability. Multimodal supervised exercise and physical rehabilitation carry the most consistent high-certainty evidence for both primary CIPN prevention and functional recovery, with significant improvements in numbness, neuropathic pain, balance and muscle strength. Cryotherapy shows robust preventive efficacy exclusively in patients receiving taxane chemotherapy, with insufficient supportive data for platinum or vinca alkaloid regimens. Acupuncture, including warm needle acupuncture, TEAS and electroacupuncture, provides moderate-to-low certainty adjunctive relief for refractory established CIPN symptoms but is not recommended as first-line therapy. Behavioral interventions exert limited direct therapeutic effects on nerve injury, yet effectively improve symptom coping, treatment adherence and long-term self-management. All interventions exhibit favorable safety profiles with minimal severe adverse events when individualized to patient fitness, comorbidities and chemotherapy regimens. Non-pharmacological interventions cannot be considered uniformly effective for all CIPN populations; evidence strength and clinical indications differ markedly by modality. Supervised multimodal exercise and physical rehabilitation represent first-line adjunctive strategies for broad CIPN prevention and functional recovery. Cryotherapy is a targeted preventive option limited to taxane-treated patients. Acupuncture serves as secondary adjunctive care for persistent symptoms, while behavioral interventions function as supportive self-management tools. Clinical implementation requires agent-specific patient stratification, individualized intervention prescription, standardized validated CIPN assessment tools, and integrated multidisciplinary oncology rehabilitation pathways. Further large, stratified randomized controlled trials with long-term follow-up are required to standardize intervention protocols and validate sustained clinical benefits.

titre: Patient-Spouse Experiences of Post-Stroke Life Reconstruction: A Longitudinal Dyadic Journey Mapping Study.
titre_fr: Patient-Spouse Experiences of Post-Stroke Life Reconstruction: A Longitudinal Dyadic Journey Mapping Study.
auteurs: Li Wenbo, Ye Qingfang, Zhang Haiyang, Wang Meng, Fan Yuying, Li Qiujie
resume: Young and middle-aged stroke survivors with residual limb motor impairment continue rehabilitation while resuming employment, family responsibilities, and social roles. Their spouses often provide care and rehabilitation support, yet little is known about how partners' experiences compare and change within dyads over time. This study aimed to examine the experiences of young and middle-aged stroke survivors with limb motor impairment and their spouses across inpatient recovery, early transition home, and longer-term home-based life reconstruction, and to synthesize the findings into a patient-spouse dual-line journey map. This longitudinal qualitative study recruited 18 patient-spouse dyads using maximum-variation purposive sampling. Patients and spouses were interviewed separately 1-3 days before discharge (T1), 4 weeks after discharge (T2), and 6 months after discharge (T3), yielding 108 interviews. Data were analyzed using the Framework Method adapted for longitudinal and dyadic qualitative data. Longitudinal matrices and within- and between-dyad comparisons informed the visual synthesis of findings. Findings were synthesized across three phases: T1: Inpatient recovery and preparation for discharge; T2: Early transition home and emerging differences in independence and safety; and T3: Longer-term life reconstruction and varied dyadic adjustment. Five cross-cutting analytic domains informed this synthesis: patients' rehabilitation and everyday-life experiences; spouses' caregiving experiences; convergence and difference within dyads; emotional experiences; and stage-specific support needs and service gaps. At T1, professional guidance provided reassurance, while preparation for home remained incomplete. At T2, patients' attempts at independence coexisted with spouses' safety concerns and difficulties applying discharge guidance. At T3, negotiated goals and reassurance in some dyads contrasted with restricted participation, caregiving strain, or reduced communication in others. These findings informed a patient-spouse dual-line journey map. Patients' rehabilitation and everyday-life experiences and spouses' caregiving experiences changed across the hospital-to-home transition, with differing priorities within dyads and varied longer-term adjustment. Findings support involving both partners in discharge preparation and providing individualized follow-up, rehabilitation, and caregiver support responsive to changing needs.
