titre: The path to recovery: treatment adherence mediates the effect of subjective age on rehabilitation outcomes in older adults.
titre_fr: The path to recovery: treatment adherence mediates the effect of subjective age on rehabilitation outcomes in older adults.
auteurs: Mansour Asil, Hoffman Yaakov, Sasson Ady, Porat-Packer Tammy, Shrira Amit
resume: The current study aimed to test the effect of subjective age on rehabilitation outcomes in older patients following hip osteoporotic fracture or stroke. Additionally, we tested the hypothesis that adherence to therapy mediates the effect of subjective age on outcomes. Patients (N = 158, mean age = 77.15, age range = 64-98) reported their subjective age during the first week of rehabilitation, physiotherapists reported adherence to therapy throughout rehabilitation, and rehabilitation outcomes (rehabilitation effectiveness) were assessed by a multidisciplinary team of healthcare personnel using the Functional Independence Measure. As hypothesised, the results revealed that a younger subjective age during the first week of rehabilitation predicted higher rehabilitation effectiveness. Moreover, this effect of subjective age was mediated by higher adherence to the therapeutic protocol during rehabilitation. Our findings highlight the significance of subjective age not just as a predictor of health outcomes but also as an antecedent to coping with health crises, further elucidating the behavioural mechanisms underlying the link between subjective age and rehabilitation effectiveness.

titre: Comparison of robot-assisted gait training and visual feedback balance training on balance and gait outcomes in patients with stroke: a randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Comparison of robot-assisted gait training and visual feedback balance training on balance and gait outcomes in patients with stroke: a randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Erden Yakup, Mavuş Ahmet Burak
resume: Robot-assisted gait training and visual feedback balance training are technology-assisted approaches used to improve balance and mobility after stroke. Although both have demonstrated beneficial effects when incorporated into conventional rehabilitation, direct comparisons between these approaches under comparable treatment conditions remain limited. This study aimed to compare the effects of RoboGait-based robot-assisted gait training and ProKin-252 visual feedback balance training on balance, mobility, gait, motor recovery, fear of falling, and functional independence after stroke. This randomized, assessor-blinded, parallel-group trial included 50 participants with subacute or chronic stroke (mean age: 63.86 ± 9.06 years). Participants were allocated to RoboGait or ProKin-252 training. Both groups received conventional balance and gait rehabilitation for 40 min, 5 days/week for 4 weeks, with an additional 30-min technology-assisted intervention twice weekly. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and after 4 weeks. The Berg Balance Scale (BBS) was the primary outcome, analyzed using analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline BBS. Balance scores improved significantly in both groups (p < .001), with mean increases of 4.44 ± 1.71 points in the RoboGait group and 5.92 ± 1.91 points in the ProKin group. Adjusted post-treatment BBS favored ProKin, with a between-group difference of 1.43 points (95% CI, 0.37-2.49; p = .009). ProKin also produced greater improvements in fear of falling (p = .004) and forward-backward postural sway (p = .027). Functional mobility, gait speed, lower-extremity motor recovery, functional ambulation, and functional independence improved significantly in both groups without significant between-group differences. Both groups demonstrated improvements in balance and functional outcomes. ProKin produced a statistically greater improvement in BBS and additional advantages in fear of falling and forward-backward postural sway; however, the adjusted BBS difference was modest, with no significant between-group differences in gait or broader functional outcomes.

titre: Cochlear Implantation with Intracochlear Schwannoma In Situ in a Complex Mosaic NF2 Patient with Severe Visual Impairment: A Case Report and Literature Review.
titre_fr: Cochlear Implantation with Intracochlear Schwannoma In Situ in a Complex Mosaic NF2 Patient with Severe Visual Impairment: A Case Report and Literature Review.
auteurs: Zhuang Boxiang, Fu Linling, Wang Dandan, Hong Mengdi, Li Jianan
resume: To report the first Chinese case of complex mosaic neurofibromatosis type 2 (NF2)-recently reclassified as NF2-related schwannomatosis-in a patient presenting with concurrent severe visual impairment and an intracochlear schwannoma, and to evaluate the clinical efficacy and strategic priority of tumor-preserving in situ cochlear implantation (CI). The patient's clinical presentation, extensive neurosurgical history, genetic profile, and perioperative audiological data were retrospectively reviewed. Additionally, we analyzed the surgical approach-which involved localized microdrilling of the obstructed cochlear turn-and the subsequent one-year follow-up outcomes of auditory-verbal rehabilitation. A 52-year-old female presented with bilateral vestibular schwannomas and secondary profound sensorineural hearing loss. Peripheral blood genetic testing revealed no pathogenic NF2 mutations, strongly indicating somatic mosaicism. The patient also suffered from a concurrent profound visual deficit due to bilateral optic atrophy and exhibited a right-sided intracochlear schwannoma. Successful tumor-preserving in situ cochlear implantation (CI) was performed on her right ear by bypassing the tumor obstruction along the cochlear trajectory. At the one-year postoperative follow-up, the patient achieved significant gains in aided hearing thresholds, along with a disyllabic word recognition score of 22%. Furthermore, her Category of Auditory Performance (CAP) score markedly improved from 0 to 6, and her Speech Intelligibility Rating (SIR) score reached level 5. Cochlear implantation (CI) with tumor preservation in situ represents a safe, viable, and highly effective hearing reconstruction strategy for complex NF2 patients with intracochlear schwannomas. For patients afflicted with dual sensory impairment (dual sensory loss), a successful cochlear implant serves as a critical standalone interface that significantly facilitates auditory-verbal rehabilitation and restores social autonomy, even within an intricate oncological landscape.

titre: Floor-to-stand transition strategies observed in individuals with unilateral transfemoral amputation.
titre_fr: Floor-to-stand transition strategies observed in individuals with unilateral transfemoral amputation.
auteurs: Mizuno Yukihiko, Morishima Ryota, Katoh Shio, Hisano Genki, Hobara Hiroaki
resume: Lower-limb amputation is frequently associated with impaired mobility and an elevated risk of falls, making the restoration of functional independence a primary objective in rehabilitation. The ability to rise from the floor-referred to as the floor-to-stand transition (FTST)-is essential for post-fall recovery; however, the movement strategies employed by individuals with unilateral transfemoral amputation (uTFA) remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to characterize FTST strategies in a sample of individuals with uTFA and examine potential demographic differences between the observed strategy groups. Sixteen individuals with uTFA performed a single FTST trial from a long-sitting position. Movements were video-recorded and evaluated by independent reviewers. Two distinct FTST strategies were observed in the present sample: (i) a rise primarily supported by the intact limb with assistance from one or both upper limbs (n = 11), and (ii) a trunk rotation into a quadruped-like posture followed by bilateral hand support to achieve standing (n = 5). No statistically significant differences in demographic or clinical characteristics were observed between groups. However, participants who adopted the trunk-rotation strategy tended to be older and required more time to complete the FTST than those who adopted the intact-limb strategy, although these differences did not reach statistical significance. These findings highlight the compensatory biomechanical adaptations employed by individuals with uTFA in the absence of active knee control. Rehabilitation should therefore emphasize movement-specific training that accounts for biomechanical demands and age-related differences to enhance safety and efficiency during post-fall recovery.
resume_fr: Lower-limb amputation is frequently associated with impaired mobility and an elevated risk of falls, making the restoration of functional independence a primary objective in rehabilitation. The ability to rise from the floor-referred to as the floor-to-stand transition (FTST)-is essential for post-fall recovery; however, the movement strategies employed by individuals with unilateral transfemoral amputation (uTFA) remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to characterize FTST strategies in a sample of individuals with uTFA and examine potential demographic differences between the observed strategy groups. Sixteen individuals with uTFA performed a single FTST trial from a long-sitting position. Movements were video-recorded and evaluated by independent reviewers. Two distinct FTST strategies were observed in the present sample: (i) a rise primarily supported by the intact limb with assistance from one or both upper limbs (n = 11), and (ii) a trunk rotation into a quadruped-like posture followed by bilateral hand support to achieve standing (n = 5). No statistically significant differences in demographic or clinical characteristics were observed between groups. However, participants who adopted the trunk-rotation strategy tended to be older and required more time to complete the FTST than those who adopted the intact-limb strategy, although these differences did not reach statistical significance. These findings highlight the compensatory biomechanical adaptations employed by individuals with uTFA in the absence of active knee control. Rehabilitation should therefore emphasize movement-specific training that accounts for biomechanical demands and age-related differences to enhance safety and efficiency during post-fall recovery.

titre: Mobilization patterns and physical activity in hospitalized individuals with moderate to severe acquired brain injury: a prospective observational study.
titre_fr: Mobilization patterns and physical activity in hospitalized individuals with moderate to severe acquired brain injury: a prospective observational study.
auteurs: Wagner Vibeke, Kyed Bayram Berivan, Harboe Olsen Markus, Kruuse Christina, Gunge Riberholt Christian
revue: Annals of physical and rehabilitation medicine
resume: Upright time is an important component in early rehabilitation following moderate to severe acquired brain injury (ABI); however, objective in-hospital data are scarce. This study quantified upright time during inpatient rehabilitation using triaxial accelerometry. To characterize mobilization and physical activity during early and late rehabilitation phases in individuals with moderate to severe ABI. Prospective cohort study in a tertiary neurorehabilitation facility. Adults (≥18 years) with moderate to severe ABI (Glasgow Coma Scale score <13 or amnesia duration >1 h), admitted between Nov 2022 and Jan 2024. Accelerometer data were collected for 7 days (7 AM to 10 PM) at 2 time points: early (T1) and late admission (T2). The primary outcome was upright time. Other outcomes included associations between clinical characteristics and upright time, and between early upright time and functional outcomes at discharge. Ninety-nine participants were enrolled; 58 provided sufficient activity data at both time points. Median upright time was 8 min/day (IQR, 3; 30) at T1, increasing to 43 min/day (IQR 22; 131) at T2 (+6.6 percentage points, 95% CI 4.3 to 8.9). Shorter upright time at T1 was associated with the confusional state and medical device attachment, and at T2, with spasmolytic and sedative treatments. Longer upright time at T1 was associated with improved Functional Ambulation Category (β = 0.17 per % increase, 95% CI 0.08 to 0.27), and Functional Independence Measure, motor subscale (β = 3.01, 95% CI 0.77 to 5.25). Missing activity data were substantial (41% excluded). Upright time increased during rehabilitation but remained low overall. Medical devices were associated with reduced upright time, and more early upright time showed potential links to higher walking ability and greater independence in mobility at discharge. These findings underscore the need for tailored interventions, real-time feedback, and clinical guidelines to optimize mobilization during rehabilitation. NCT05571462.

titre: Effectiveness of dose-matched immersive virtual reality-stationary cycling combined with neurological physiotherapy versus neurological physiotherapy alone in individuals with chronic stroke (CIVIS): A single-blind, randomized crossover trial protocol.
titre_fr: Effectiveness of dose-matched immersive virtual reality-stationary cycling combined with neurological physiotherapy versus neurological physiotherapy alone in individuals with chronic stroke (CIVIS): A single-blind, randomized crossover trial protocol.
auteurs: Asensio-Perez Daniel, Lucena-Anton David, Moral-Munoz Jose A
resume: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide and frequently results in persistent motor and functional impairments, particularly affecting gait and balance. Given the high prevalence and impact of these limitations on independence and quality of life, innovative rehabilitation strategies are needed. Immersive virtual reality combined with stationary cycling (IVR-SC) has emerged as an innovative rehabilitation approach with the potential to improve mobility and functional outcomes after stroke. To analyze the comparative effectiveness of two dose-matched programs, one combining IVR-SC plus neurological physiotherapy (NP), versus the other consisting of NP alone, in individuals with chronic stroke. A randomized, single-blind, crossover clinical trial will be conducted. After calculating the sample size, a minimum of 8 participants with chronic stroke (≥6 months), hemiparesis, and gait and balance impairments will be randomly assigned to one of two sequences of intervention. Each participant will receive both neurological physiotherapy and IVR-SC across two 4-week intervention periods separated by a washout period (4 weeks). Each intervention period consists of 8 sessions delivered over a 4-week period, with each session lasting 60 minutes. The primary outcome will be gait quality, assessed using Wisconsin Gait Scale (WGS), while secondary outcomes will include walking endurance, balance, motor function, and muscle tone. Clinical outcomes will be assessed at baseline and after each intervention period. Satisfaction with using the IVR-SC intervention will also be evaluated. Statistical analyses will follow an intention-to-treat approach using a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) with treatment, period, sequence, baseline, and center as fixed effects, and participant as a random effect. Statistical significance will be set at p < 0.05. An individual responder analysis will be performed to determine if participants exceeded the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of 2.25 points on the WGS. This study will contribute to understanding the potential comparative effects of IVR-SC in stroke rehabilitation. Given the heterogeneity of individuals with stroke, which may limit the conclusiveness of findings in parallel-group studies, the crossover design allows each participant to serve as their own control, reducing inter-individual variability and strengthening the interpretation of the results. If effective, IVR-SC could represent a feasible and scalable option for partially replacing NP within standard neurorehabilitation, with potential for implementation in both clinical and home-based settings. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT07529665. Effectiveness of dose-matched rehabilitation with immersive virtual reality-stationary cycling combined with neurological physiotherapy versus neurological physiotherapy alone in individuals with chronic stroke (CIVIS): study protocol for a single-blind, randomized crossover trial. URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07529665. Date of registration: 2026-04-14. Version 1.

titre: Severe Rosuvastatin-Associated Rhabdomyolysis and Dialysis-Requiring Acute Kidney Injury in an Octogenarian Patient: A Case Report.
titre_fr: Severe Rosuvastatin-Associated Rhabdomyolysis and Dialysis-Requiring Acute Kidney Injury in an Octogenarian Patient: A Case Report.
auteurs: De Melo Luiza Mendonça Pessoa, Passos Mauro De Deus, Ferreira Dilson Palhares
revue: The American journal of case reports
resume: BACKGROUND Statins are fundamental to dyslipidemia management, but high-potency rosuvastatin can cause myotoxicity in vulnerable older patients. We present a probable case of rosuvastatin-associated rhabdomyolysis causing stage 3 acute kidney injury requiring hemodialysis in an 87-year-old woman with polypharmacy, highlighting clinical management and outcomes. CASE REPORT An octogenarian presented with progressive muscle weakness and inability to ambulate 20 days after starting rosuvastatin (20 mg/day), ezetimibe (10 mg/day), and evogliptin (5 mg/day). Laboratory tests revealed creatine kinase above 4267 U/L, serum creatinine 6.13 mg/dL, blood urea 220 mg/dL, severe hyponatremia (122 mEq/L), bicarbonate 15 mEq/L, and elevated transaminases (AST 419 U/L; ALT 342 U/L). Direct bilirubin (0.2 mg/dL) and gamma-glutamyl transferase (28 U/L) levels were normal, excluding primary hepatocellular or cholestatic liver injury. Urinalysis findings supported myoglobinuria. Refractory oliguria despite aggressive intravenous fluid resuscitation required emergency hemodialysis with sodium correction to prevent osmotic demyelination; rhabdomyolysis prompted rosuvastatin cessation. Concomitant nephrotoxic and renally cleared medications were temporarily withheld. During a 30-day hospital stay with 8 hemodialysis sessions, dialytic support was discontinued on Day 23 (serum creatinine 1.61 mg/dL). After physical rehabilitation, the patient was discharged on Day 30 with full motor strength (MRC grade 5/5). At 3 months, serum creatinine had stabilized (1.40 mg/dL; eGFR 38 mL/min/1.73 m²; creatine kinase 62 U/L) and independent ambulation continued. CONCLUSIONS Statin-associated rhabdomyolysis in older adults can be followed by renal recovery with dialysis independence and functional recovery through early drug cessation, fluid resuscitation, and timely dialytic support. Formal Naranjo assessment (score 5) classified the reaction as "probable," highlighting the multifactorial risks of geriatric polypharmacy.

titre: Caregiver agency in supporting children with deafblindness.
titre_fr: Caregiver agency in supporting children with deafblindness.
auteurs: Moroe Nomfundo, Masuku Khetsiwe, Moosa Humaira
resume: This study explored how caregivers exercise agency in supporting their children's academic, social, and independent development, alongside their overall well-being in South Africa. A secondary analysis of data from semi-structured interviews was conducted with seven purposively selected caregivers of children who are deafblind. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, guided by Braun and Clarke's framework. Three main themes emerged from the data. First, caregivers as advocates for their children's future captures how caregivers actively prioritised education, nurtured their children's unique talents, and encouraged play and skill development to foster independence and self-expression. Second, facilitating independence through environmental and sensory adaptation reflects how caregivers structured routines and familiar environments to support behavioural and sensory development. Third, fostering well-being through social and physical engagement highlights caregivers' efforts to promote social inclusion, physical activity, and holistic well-being. Across these themes, caregivers' agency was accompanied by considerable personal cost, including sustained time, vigilance, and sacrifice. The study highlights parental agency as vital in managing deafblindness challenges while highlighting the psychological toll on caregivers. It calls for enhanced systemic support, including specialised communication training, mental health resources, and inclusive education policies to strengthen caregiver resilience and improve outcomes for children with deafblindness.

titre: [Treatment of idiopathic inflammatory myopathies : Physical activity, nonpharmacological treatment and rehabilitation].
titre_fr: [Treatment of idiopathic inflammatory myopathies : Physical activity, nonpharmacological treatment and rehabilitation].
auteurs: Maurer B, Scheel-Sailer A
resume: Inflammatory myopathies are often associated with muscle pain, weakness, comorbidities and reduced quality of life. Physical activity and appropriate exercise programmes can effectively counteract the gradual loss of mobility and participation in daily life. At the same time, they promote independence, which subsequently contributes to an improved quality of life. It is important to explain to patients that the exercise programme will not cause any harm; on the contrary, it can, above all, bring improvements. The first step is to assess the status quo of disease activity and symptoms, so that targeted exercises can be prescribed which, on the one hand, alleviate existing symptoms and enhance functional ability and, on the other hand, help to prevent potential secondary complications. Naturally, the patient's limitations regarding the outpatient management of their condition should be taken into account. Although the evidence base is still limited, the results available to date suggest that many patients with inflammatory myopathy could benefit from a well-structured exercise programme.

titre: Severe delayed gastric emptying combined with enteroparalysis after pancreaticoduodenectomy: a case report.
titre_fr: Severe delayed gastric emptying combined with enteroparalysis after pancreaticoduodenectomy: a case report.
auteurs: Wan Zhili, Wu Dingquan, Yang Yuhang, Li Guizhong, Liu Bin, Chen Yongfan, Zhou Liangbi
resume: Pancreaticoduodenectomy is an important surgical procedure for treating diseases of the pancreatic head, periampullary region, and related conditions. However, due to its extensive surgical scope, long duration, and involvement of complex digestive tract reconstruction, postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction remains relatively common. Among these, delayed gastric emptying (DGE) is a common complication after pancreaticoduodenectomy, while the occurrence of severe DGE combined with enteroparalysis is relatively rare, and its diagnosis and treatment remain challenging. This article reports the case of a 69-year-old female patient who developed severe DGE complicated by intestinal paralysis after pancreaticoduodenectomy. The patient persistently experienced nausea, vomiting, and the inability to tolerate oral intake postoperatively. Although imaging studies suggested restricted passage at the gastrointestinal anastomosis, raising suspicion of obstruction, further laparoscopic exploration and gastroscopy revealed no definite mechanical obstruction. The patient received gastrointestinal decompression, nutritional support, internal environment management, and rehabilitation therapy. Enteral nutritional support was established through a jejunal feeding tube. After long-term comprehensive treatment, the patient's gastrointestinal function gradually recovered and eventually returned to oral intake. However, long-term follow-up showed that despite the recovery of gastrointestinal function, the patient still had a certain degree of decline in physical function and limited ability in activities of daily living. Severe delayed gastric emptying complicated by enteroparalysis after pancreaticoduodenectomy is a rare but clinically challenging gastrointestinal dysfunction. This case suggests that persistent postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction may present with clinical features resembling mechanical obstruction, therefore requiring comprehensive assessment integrating imaging, endoscopy, and dynamic clinical changes.

titre: Predicting Robot-Based Tracking Performance After Stroke Using Lesion Features and Clinical Assessments: A Pilot Study.
titre_fr: Predicting Robot-Based Tracking Performance After Stroke Using Lesion Features and Clinical Assessments: A Pilot Study.
auteurs: Azar Reem M, Waters Erica L, Opong-Duah Joana, Mendonca Rochelle J, Cacchione Pamela Z, Johnson Michelle J
revue: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
resume: Following stroke, motor and cognitive impairments often limit functional independence. Personalized rehabilitation requires comprehensive clinical assessments, which are costly and time-consuming. Imaging scans are routinely collected, but their predictive value in determining post-stroke function remains unclear. To determine the ability of clinical assessments, lesion features with medical chart information, and a combined clinical and biomedical model to predict kinematic outcomes from a robot-based tracking task in chronic stroke individuals. Eighteen participants (70±6 years) completed a robot-based tracking task and a battery of motor and cognitive assessments. Three elastic net regression models were developed: 1) clinical assessments only; 2) lesion metrics and chart information only; and 3) a combined model. Models were evaluated using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, bootstrapping, and permutation testing with false discovery rate correction. Robot-based outcomes included tracking error, normalized distance, velocity error response, and delay. The clinical assessment model significantly predicted tracking error (R²=0.45), delay (R²=0.22), velocity error response (R²=0.18), and normalized distance (R²=0.12). The combined model significantly predicted tracking error (R²=0.37), delay (R²=0.19), and velocity error response (R²=0.11). The imaging model did not significantly predict any outcome. Box and Blocks Test and Color Trails 1 were stable features. The right dorsal attention network was a stable predictor in several combined models. Clinical assessments outperformed lesion features in predicting tracking performance after chronic stroke. Attention- and motor-related measures were the strongest predictors, highlighting the importance of cognitive-motor interactions in function. A larger sample and more granular lesion features may improve prediction from imaging biomarkers.

titre: Predictive Value of Early Functional Improvement During Hospitalization for Intermediate-Term Functional Outcomes After Stroke: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
titre_fr: Predictive Value of Early Functional Improvement During Hospitalization for Intermediate-Term Functional Outcomes After Stroke: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
auteurs: Yu Qian, Gu Qinyi, Wang Jia
resume: To investigate whether early functional improvement status is associated with 3-month functional outcomes after stroke and to develop and internally validate a preliminary prediction model for poor outcomes. This retrospective cohort study included 150 patients with stroke who were hospitalized in the Department of Neurology and the Department of Rehabilitation Medicine at our hospital between March 2021 and December 2024 and who completed the 3-month post-discharge follow-up. Early functional improvement was defined by changes in the Barthel Index and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) scores from admission to discharge. The cohort-specific median values of ΔBarthel and ΔNIHSS were used as exploratory thresholds to classify patients into the functional improvement group and the insufficient functional improvement group. Baseline characteristics, early functional changes during hospitalization, and functional outcomes at 3 months after discharge were compared between the two groups. Poor functional outcome at 3 months after discharge, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score ≥3, was used as the dependent variable. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regression models were used to evaluate the association between early functional improvement status and poor functional outcome and its incremental prognostic contribution beyond baseline clinical variables. A nomogram was constructed based on the extended model. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, calibration assessment, and decision curve analysis, and internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples. In a sensitivity analysis, the categorized early functional improvement status variable was replaced by continuous ΔBarthel and ΔNIHSS values while retaining the same baseline covariates. The functional improvement group was slightly younger than the insufficient functional improvement group. During hospitalization, the functional improvement group had lower NIHSS scores, higher Barthel Index scores at discharge, and greater changes in both functional measures from admission to discharge. At the 3-month follow-up, the functional improvement group had significantly higher Barthel Index scores, a higher rate of functional independence, and a lower incidence of poor functional outcomes (all p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis showed that age, admission blood glucose, and admission NIHSS score were inde-pendently associated with higher odds of poor functional outcome, whereas admission Barthel Index and early functional improvement status were independently associated with lower odds of poor functional outcome. In the sensitivity analysis, each 1-point increase in ΔBarthel was associated with lower odds of poor functional outcome (OR = 0.936, 95% CI: 0.898-0.977, p = 0.002), as was each 1-point increase in ΔNIHSS (OR = 0.678, 95% CI: 0.524-0.878, p = 0.003). Adding early functional improvement status to the baseline clinical model modestly improved discrimination, with the apparent area under the curve (AUC) increasing from 0.809 to 0.852 (ΔAUC = 0.043, p = 0.037). After bootstrap correction, the AUC of the extended model was 0.827. These findings indicate modest incremental prognostic value within the present cohort, but external validation is required. Early functional improvement status during hospitalization after stroke was independently associated with intermediate-term functional outcomes and may provide additional prognostic information beyond baseline clinical characteristics. The prediction model incorporating early functional improvement status and baseline clinical variables showed preliminary predictive performance within the present cohort but should not yet be regarded as a clinically validated risk-stratification tool. External validation is required before its use in rehabilitation planning or clinical decision-making.

At the 3-month follow-up, the functional improvement group had significantly higher Barthel Index scores, a higher rate of functional independence, and a lower incidence of poor functional outcomes (all p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis showed that age, admission blood glucose, and admission NIHSS score were inde-pendently associated with higher odds of poor functional outcome, whereas admission Barthel Index and early functional improvement status were independently associated with lower odds of poor functional outcome. In the sensitivity analysis, each 1-point increase in ΔBarthel was associated with lower odds of poor functional outcome (OR = 0.936, 95% CI: 0.898-0.977, p = 0.002), as was each 1-point increase in ΔNIHSS (OR = 0.678, 95% CI: 0.524-0.878, p = 0.003). Adding early functional improvement status to the baseline clinical model modestly improved discrimination, with the apparent area under the curve (AUC) increasing from 0.809 to 0.852 (ΔAUC = 0.043, p = 0.037). After bootstrap correction, the AUC of the extended model was 0.827. These findings indicate modest incremental prognostic value within the present cohort, but external validation is required. Early functional improvement status during hospitalization after stroke was independently associated with intermediate-term functional outcomes and may provide additional prognostic information beyond baseline clinical characteristics. The prediction model incorporating early functional improvement status and baseline clinical variables showed preliminary predictive performance within the present cohort but should not yet be regarded as a clinically validated risk-stratification tool. External validation is required before its use in rehabilitation planning or clinical decision-making.

titre: Penetrating needling from Qiuxu (GB40) to Zhaohai (KI6) versus separate needling for post-stroke lower-limb motor dysfunction: an assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial protocol.
titre_fr: Penetrating needling from Qiuxu (GB40) to Zhaohai (KI6) versus separate needling for post-stroke lower-limb motor dysfunction: an assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial protocol.
auteurs: Zhang Jie, Wang Lin, Tian Zhen, Wang Meng, Fan Jing, Liu Xiaoxiao, Cui Chao, Qian Yulin, Zhang Rui, Liu Yi, Wan Chunxiao
resume: Post-stroke lower-limb motor dysfunction limits mobility, balance, and independence and remains a major target of neurorehabilitation. Acupuncture is widely used as an adjunctive intervention after stroke, but direct randomized evidence comparing penetrating needling with conventional separate needling at the same acupoints is limited. This protocol describes an active-comparator randomized controlled trial comparing penetrating needling from Qiuxu (GB40) to Zhaohai (KI6) with separate needling for post-stroke lower-limb motor dysfunction, with functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and surface electromyography (sEMG) included as exploratory mechanistic outcomes. This single-center, prospective, assessor-blinded, parallel-group superiority trial will enroll 130 participants with subacute post-stroke lower-limb motor dysfunction. Participants will be randomized 1:1 to penetrating needling from Qiuxu (GB40) to Zhaohai (KI6) or to separate needling at the same acupoints. Both groups will receive 12 acupuncture sessions over 2 weeks, delivered 6 times per week, with 30 min of needle retention per session, together with the same total rehabilitation dose of 30 min/day, 5 days/week. The primary outcome is the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Lower Extremity (FMA-LE) score at the end of treatment (T1). The primary analysis will use analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline FMA-LE. Secondary clinical outcomes include the Berg Balance Scale, Manual Muscle Testing, and Modified Ashworth Scale. Registered secondary neurophysiological assessments include fNIRS and sEMG; their derived measures will be analyzed exploratorily. https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/mgt/project/view/2037483478790045696, ITMCTR2026000773.

titre: The quality of life experienced by persons with spinal cord injury in Finland - a mixed methods study.
titre_fr: The quality of life experienced by persons with spinal cord injury in Finland - a mixed methods study.
auteurs: Eskola Kaarina, Tallqvist Susanna, Zechner Minna, Arokoski Jari, Koskinen Eerika, Rajavaara Marketta, Hiekkala Sinikka
resume: Spinal cord injury (SCI) affects an individual's quality of life (QOL) by impairing body functions and structures, which in turn lead to reduced functional capacity and participation restrictions. These outcomes are further shaped by environmental factors. The objective of this mixed-method study was to investigate the factors associated with QOL among persons with SCI in Finland. A convergent parallel mixed methods design with quantitative and qualitative data was used. Quantitative data were obtained from 879 individuals with SCI participating in the first nationwide community survey for the SCI population in Finland (FinSCI 2019). QOL was assessed using the PROMIS® Global Health survey question (Global02), and associations with sociodemographic and injury-related variables were analyzed using multivariable ordinal regression. Qualitative data were collected through interviews with 45 volunteer survey respondents and analyzed using inductive content analysis. Quantitative and qualitative data generated were then triangulated to develop a more complete interpretation of the QOL experienced by SCI population and integrated results were assessed for concordance, discordance or expansion during the discussion stage of this report. Impaired overall health and poor management of secondary health conditions (SHCs) were associated with reduced functional ability and poorer QOL, whereas SCI severity was not independently associated with QOL in the adjusted quantitative model. Factors associated with improved QOL included immediate social support, high self-esteem, psychosocial adaptation, and personal growth over time. Conversely, older age, secondary health problems, and inadequate services were linked to poorer QOL. High self-efficacy and the ability to function within personal limitations while maintaining autonomy were associated with good QOL, whereas poor QOL was characterized by reduced activity, constrained daily life, and lack of spontaneity. The findings highlight the complex interplay between health status, functional ability, psychosocial resources, and the adequacy of servicesin shaping QOL among people with SCI in Finland, whereas injury severity itself was not independently associated with QOL. Addressing these multidimensional factors is essential in rehabilitation and long-term follow-up to support well-being and participation in everyday life.

titre: Rehabilitation efficacy of neuromuscular training for individuals suffering from knee osteoarthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis based on randomized controlled trials.
titre_fr: Rehabilitation efficacy of neuromuscular training for individuals suffering from knee osteoarthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis based on randomized controlled trials.
auteurs: Bai Bihui, Gu YuBiao, Dingpeng Li, Xie Xingwen, Yao Fei
resume: This study aimed to comprehensively assess the efficacy of neuromuscular training (NMT) in function, symptoms, quality of life (QoL), pain, and safety in individuals with knee osteoarthritis (KOA), thereby providing evidence-based support for rehabilitation strategies in KOA management. This study was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from database inception to August 30, 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) assessing NMT for KOA were included. For multiple reports originating from the same underlying randomized trial, a trial family was established based on trial registration number, randomized sample size, baseline characteristics, intervention protocols, and follow-up duration to avoid duplicate counting. A random-effects model was applied for meta-analysis, and sensitivity analysis, publication bias assessment, prespecified subgroup analyses, and tests for subgroup interactions were performed. The certainty of evidence for primary outcomes and adverse events was evaluated using the approach proposed by the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) Working Group. A total of 17 study reports were included, corresponding to 14 independent RCTs with 1,029 participants, of whom 516 were in the NMT group and 513 in the control group. Compared with control interventions, NMT significantly alleviated KOOS Symptoms (MD = 4.44, 95% CI: 1.62, 7.26, P = 0.002), KOOS ADLs (MD = 3.94, 95% CI: 0.09, 7.79, P = 0.04), and KOOS QoL (MD = 5.59, 95% CI: 0.97, 10.21, P = 0.02). The between-group differences for KOOS Pain (MD = 1.95, 95% CI: -0.27, 4.17, P = 0.08) and KOOS Sport/Rec (MD = 1.64, 95% CI -2.24, 5.53, P = 0.41) did not reach statistical significance. The meta-analysis of adverse events showed no statistically significant difference in the incidence of adverse events between the NMT and control groups (RR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.50, 1.37, P = 0.46). Nevertheless, given the heterogeneity across studies in the definitions, monitoring, and reporting of adverse events, this result should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent safety between the interventions. The subgroup analyses suggested differences in certain specific subgroups. Most subgroup interaction tests were not statistically significant; however, a significant interaction was observed for mean age in the KOOS QoL analysis (P for interaction = 0.02), which should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of studies. NMT may partially alleviate comprehensive symptoms, facilitate activities of daily living, and enhance knee-related QoL in patients with KOA, whereas consistent benefits were not demonstrated for KOOS Pain, sport and recreational function, or most objective functional outcomes. No statistically significant difference in reported adverse events was observed; however, heterogeneity in adverse-event definitions and reporting limits conclusions regarding comparative safety. Additional well-designed RCTs with standardized NMT protocols, adequate sample sizes, and longer follow-up are needed to confirm the magnitude and clinical relevance of these effects. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251118258, identifier CRD420251118258.

titre: Next-generation control strategies for lower-extremity exoskeletons: State-of-the-art, limitations, and future directions.
titre_fr: Next-generation control strategies for lower-extremity exoskeletons: State-of-the-art, limitations, and future directions.
auteurs: Vespa Victoria, Kemp Stephen W P, Gates Deanna, Gillespie R Brent, Cederna Paul S, Kung Theodore A
revue: PM & R : the journal of injury, function, and rehabilitation
resume: Wearable powered exoskeletons are emerging rehabilitation tools for restoring gait in individuals with neurologic or motor impairments, including stroke, spinal cord injury, myopathy, and cerebral palsy. Lower-extremity exoskeleton-assisted walking can improve motor function, gait parameters, balance, and independence. Exoskeleton use has also been associated with secondary health benefits, including reduced spasticity and improvements in autonomic functions such as bladder and bowel control. However, despite these clinical benefits, exoskeleton control systems remain a central bottleneck limiting functional gains and widespread clinical adoption. The majority of clinically approved lower-extremity devices rely on weight shift triggers, predefined gait phase controllers, impedance-based assistance, or simple electromyographic signal activation. These approaches often feel unintuitive and require substantial user training. As a result, persistent challenges remain in detecting user intent, reproducing a user's expected dynamic behaviors, adapting to variable gait patterns and changing environmental conditions such as uneven terrain or inclines, and minimizing cognitive burden during everyday use. This review focuses on control strategies for lower-extremity exoskeletons used in gait rehabilitation and restoration of motor function. It summarizes current approaches in commercial and research systems and outlines why existing methods remain insufficient for seamless, user-driven assistance. We also examine emerging approaches for determining user intent, including brain-computer interfaces, peripheral nerve interfaces, novel biosignals such as ultrasound and mechanomyography, and regenerative surgical approaches. Together, these advances may help bridge the gap between human intent and robotic assistance, enabling more natural and autonomous mobility.

titre: Altered plastidial fatty-acid condensation is associated with changes in membrane composition and postembryonic leaf development in Arabidopsis.
titre_fr: Altered plastidial fatty-acid condensation is associated with changes in membrane composition and postembryonic leaf development in Arabidopsis.
auteurs: Angelos Evan R, Bagh-Abrishami Amirreza R, Gómez-Méndez María Fernanda, Gutbrod Katharina, Zanini Andrea A, Fan De, Choi Hee-Seung, Zeng Liping, Cheng Jiaxuan, Zhang Bailong, Chen Meng, Burch-Smith Tessa M, Dörmann Peter, Dehesh Katayoon
revue: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
resume: Membrane lipid composition is fundamental to organelle structure and environmental adaptation, yet how plastidial fatty acid metabolism influences developmental plasticity remains poorly understood. We examined the effects of sustained elevation of the plastidial fatty-acid enzymes KASII (β-ketoacyl-ACP synthase II) and SSI2 (Δ9 stearoyl-ACP desaturase 2) in Arabidopsis thaliana using lipidomic, ultrastructural, cellular, molecular, and physiological analyses. KASII overexpressing plants (KASIIox), but not SSI2 overexpressing plants (SSI2ox), increased carbon 18-containing lipid species and exhibited reduced plastidial galactolipids together with increased extraplastidial phospholipids. KASIIox plants displayed enlarged chloroplasts with disrupted thylakoid organization, impaired palisade differentiation, altered mesophyll patterning, and reduced seed coat mucilage. Under low light, KASIIox plants failed to exhibit the characteristic petiole elongation observed in control and SSI2ox plants, accompanied by altered phyB and PIF4 protein abundance. Exogenous gibberellin intensified, whereas inhibition of gibberellin biosynthesis partially alleviated KASIIox leaf and cellular phenotypes. Together, these findings associate sustained KASII elevation with changes in membrane lipid composition, chloroplast architecture, light-responsive growth, and postembryonic leaf development, supporting a link between plastidial fatty-acid metabolism and developmental responses to light and gibberellin availability.

titre: Decoding horizontal transposon transfer across plants through a comprehensive HTT atlas.
titre_fr: Decoding horizontal transposon transfer across plants through a comprehensive HTT atlas.
auteurs: Huang Yan, Sahu Sunil Kumar, Wang Hua, Lin Ziyu, Hu Jingjing, Zhao Yongfang, Varshney Rajeev K, Liu Xin
resume: Horizontal transposon transfer (HTT) plays an important role in genome evolution; however, its prevalence, evolutionary patterns, and potential mechanisms in plants remain poorly understood due to limited taxonomic sampling and challenges in distinguishing HTT from vertical inheritance. This study aimed to systematically identify HTT events across major plant lineages, investigate factors potentially associated with HTT, and assess the possible evolutionary significance of HTT in plant genomes. A total of 558 high-quality plant genomes representing 352 species spanning algae to angiosperms were analyzed. A conservative phylogeny-informed framework integrating transposable element (TE) annotation, orthology inference, sequence similarity analysis, and lineage distribution filtering was developed to identify putative HTT events. Co-transfer relationships, host gene enrichment, transport-related pathways, and exosome-associated sequences were further analyzed to investigate candidate factors associated with HTT. In total, 1,548 putative HTT events involving 684 TE families were identified across diverse plant lineages, indicating that both RNA- and DNA-mediated transposons contribute extensively to HTT in plants. Co-transfer analyses revealed widespread associations among TE superfamilies, whereas functional enrichment analyses highlighted chromatin-related and transport-related host genes frequently associated with HTT regions. HTT-related TE sequences were also detected in publicly available plant exosomal sequencing datasets, and several hotspot TE families showed homology to viral-associated sequences, suggesting potential involvement of vesicle-mediated transport and viral interactions in HTT processes. In addition, genes associated with cold acclimation and stress responses were enriched near several HTT regions, suggesting that HTT may contribute to environmental adaptation in some plant lineages. This study provides a comprehensive atlas of HTT across plants and establishes a scalable framework for HTT detection in large-scale comparative genomics analyses. These findings generate candidate hypotheses regarding the mechanisms and evolutionary significance of HTT and provide a resource for future functional and experimental investigations.

titre: Standing up against the silencer: Chromatin factors antagonizing Polycomb.
titre_fr: Standing up against the silencer: Chromatin factors antagonizing Polycomb.
auteurs: Lagarde Antoine, Jarry Lucas, Moissiard Guillaume
resume: Polycomb group proteins are central regulators of plant development, maintaining transcriptional repression through H2AK121 monoubiquitination and H3K27 trimethylation. However, Polycomb-mediated silencing must remain reversible to allow developmental transitions and environmental responses. Recent studies have uncovered a diverse repertoire of chromatin factors that restrict, remove, or counterbalance Polycomb activity in plants. These include histone deubiquitinases and demethylases, trithorax-related proteins, adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-dependent chromatin remodelers, transcription factors, and additional regulatory proteins that protect gene expression programs and chromatin architecture from inappropriate Polycomb recruitment or spreading. Their actions range from the direct removal of repressive marks to the inhibition of Polycomb recruitment and the remodeling of nucleosome accessibility. Importantly, some of these factors display context-dependent dual roles, acting either as Polycomb antagonists or facilitators depending on the locus, protein associations, or developmental context. Evolutionary analyses suggest that Polycomb regulatory networks and their antagonistic pathways have undergone substantial diversification and rewiring during Viridiplantae evolution. Extending functional studies beyond Arabidopsis thaliana will be essential to determine how these regulatory networks contribute to developmental plasticity and environmental adaptation in plants with agronomically-relevant traits.

titre: Comprehensive O-Phosphoproteomic Landscape of Corynebacterium glutamicum.
titre_fr: Comprehensive O-Phosphoproteomic Landscape of Corynebacterium glutamicum.
auteurs: Wang Yujie, Han Manman, Qin Peibin, Zhang Wenwen, Liu Qiyue, Cao Qichen, Sun Jibin
resume: Corynebacterium glutamicum serves as a pivotal industrial platform organism, accounting for an annual global amino acid output of several million tons. Elucidating its adaptive mechanisms under diverse environmental perturbations during high-density fermentation is fundamental to advanced metabolic engineering and strain optimization. Despite the critical role of protein phosphorylation in cellular adaptation, the phosphoproteome of C. glutamicum remains largely unexplored. With fewer than 50 phosphoproteins currently identified, this knowledge gap hinders the elucidation of regulatory networks underlying industrial stress tolerance. In this study, we implemented a highly robust workflow for O-phosphopeptides enrichment utilizing titanium-based immobilized metal affinity chromatography (Ti-IMAC). By integrating an offline reversed-phase prefractionation strategy and a combination of Electron-Transfer/Higher-Energy Collision Dissociation (EThcD) and Higher-Energy Collision Dissociation (HCD) mass spectrometry fragmentation techniques, we established the most comprehensive phosphoproteomic data set for this species to our knowledge. We identified 874 phosphoproteins and 2,137 phosphorylation sites, representing a more than 20-fold increase over existing literature. Furthermore, we delineated the dynamic phosphoproteome under nitrogen starvation, uncovering novel site-specific phosphorylation events on key proteins such as OdhI (Ser2/Thr7), FtsZ (Thr387), and EF-G (Thr48). This study provides a high-quality, global phosphoprotein resource, that elucidates the molecular insights into the orchestration of environmental adaptation and metabolic regulation of C. glutamicum.

Furthermore, we delineated the dynamic phosphoproteome under nitrogen starvation, uncovering novel site-specific phosphorylation events on key proteins such as OdhI (Ser2/Thr7), FtsZ (Thr387), and EF-G (Thr48). This study provides a high-quality, global phosphoprotein resource, that elucidates the molecular insights into the orchestration of environmental adaptation and metabolic regulation of C. glutamicum.

titre: Systematic Review of Smart Home Assistive Technology Devices for Supporting People With Dementia Living in Their Homes.
titre_fr: Systematic Review of Smart Home Assistive Technology Devices for Supporting People With Dementia Living in Their Homes.
auteurs: Han Oscar, Lee Reagan, Lee Anne, Thorpe Naomi, Tan Hui Zhi, Doh Changmin, Rajkumar Anto P
resume: Most people with dementia prefer remaining in their own homes as long as possible. Smart home assistive technologies are being developed to enhance safety and autonomy of people with dementia and to support their caregivers. However, evidence for their efficacy and effectiveness in community-based dementia care remains uncertain. Hence, we aim to systematically review the available evidence on the efficacy of smart home assistive technology devices for supporting people with dementia living in their homes. We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA-2020 guidelines (PROSPERO ID:CRD420251051358). We comprehensively searched four databases. Eligible studies examined smart home or wearable devices used by people with dementia in home or supported accommodation settings. We systematically performed quality assessment, data extraction, and the GRADE assessment. Meta-analyses were conducted when three or more studies investigated similar outcomes. We screened 3176 abstracts and identified 18 eligible studies that investigated 17 devices. There is level-2 evidence supporting the use of companion robots, electric calendar, a night-time home monitoring system and the People Power Caregiver system. Our meta-analysis did not find evidence supporting the use of the investigated devices for reducing caregiver burden (p = 0.68; Hedges's g = 0.01; 95% CI -0.14 to 0.17). Smart home technologies for dementia care are acceptable and feasible. However, current evidence for their efficacy remains limited. Larger clinical trials are required to strengthen their evidence base and justify their routine use in supporting people with dementia and caregivers.

titre: Host specificity, seasonality, and urbanicity shape the gut microbiome of a synanthropic insect.
titre_fr: Host specificity, seasonality, and urbanicity shape the gut microbiome of a synanthropic insect.
auteurs: Noyes Hanna, Anika Nur-E-Jannat, Combs Julia, Khan Tamheeda, Just Josefine, Fitzpatrick Su, Angelini Rowan Graham, Angelini David R
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: The soapberry bug Jadera haematoloma is a classic model of rapid adaptive evolution, with a well-documented host shift from native herbaceous sapinds to the introduced goldenrain tree (Koelreuteria spp.). This host shift has facilitated the insect's spread into novel anthropogenic urban habitats. Microbial associations are often critical to insect environmental adaptation. Here, we characterize the gut microbiota of J. haematoloma across native and introduced host plants, seasonal transitions, and a gradient of urbanicity. Our findings indicate that the soapberry bug gut microbiome is highly specialized, with a small number of core bacterial amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) primarily from the families Rhizobiaceae, Streptococcaceae, Enterobacteriaceae, and Lactobacillaceae. While traits such as sex and wing morph do not correlate with microbiome structure, the host plant acts as the primary determinant of community composition. Bugs feeding on the ancestral host plant maintain a more diverse and even microbial community featuring Enterobacteriaceae, whereas the gut environment of bugs on the introduced host is overwhelmingly dominated by a single unclassified Rhizobiaceae ASV. Furthermore, seasonal transitions drive significant turnover among accessory microbial taxa. Finally, we demonstrate that urbanization introduces a distinct ecological effect on the insect's microbiome. While the degree of local green space does not systematically alter within-host taxonomic richness, it is associated with modest change in mean community composition and significantly disrupts microbial community variance. Increased urbanization correlates with significantly higher beta dispersion, indicating that anthropogenic environments lead to more stochastic microbiomes, which may be an indicator of environmental stress. Together, these results illustrate how rapid dietary host shifts and the ecological pressures of urbanization interact to shape the microbiome of a synanthropic insect.

titre: Lectin-centered signaling networks orchestrate plant immunity, stress adaptation, and development.
titre_fr: Lectin-centered signaling networks orchestrate plant immunity, stress adaptation, and development.
auteurs: Yang Zihang, Wu Xinghan, Chen Yanjie, Pan Yuemin, Chen Jianping, Sun Zongtao
resume: Plant lectins are structurally diverse non-catalytic carbohydrate-binding proteins, some of which contribute directly to defense against herbivores and pathogens. However, emerging evidence suggests that lectins function far beyond passive defense factors and instead constitute a multilayered signaling system coordinating environmental perception, immunity, stress adaptation and development throughout the plant life cycle. Recent studies reveal that lectins perceive diverse endogenous and exogenous cues, including glycoconjugates, peptides and damage-associated molecules, and integrate these signals into conserved downstream signaling networks. In parallel, intracellular lectins contribute to pathogen restriction, physiological homeostasis and developmental regulation through direct modulation of cellular signaling pathways. Together, these findings position lectins as central components of a broader plant glyco-signaling framework linking extracellular information with adaptive physiological outputs. In this Review, we synthesize recent advances in lectin-mediated signaling across plant immunity, abiotic stress adaptation and developmental regulation, discuss how post-translational modifications expand lectin signaling plasticity, and highlight emerging translational opportunities in sustainable agriculture, including immune engineering, programmable receptor design and targeted biomolecule delivery. Finally, we propose that lectin-mediated signaling represents an underappreciated regulatory layer underlying plant environmental adaptation and outline key challenges for harnessing lectins in next-generation crop improvement.

titre: Plant Single-Cell Metabolomics and Metabolite Imaging: Current Advances and Future Directions.
titre_fr: Plant Single-Cell Metabolomics and Metabolite Imaging: Current Advances and Future Directions.
auteurs: Singh Yatendra, Chen Sixue
resume: Plants are multicellular systems composed of highly specialized cell types, whose distinct transcriptomes, proteomes, and metabolomes collectively shape growth, development, defense, and environmental adaptation. While single-cell transcriptomics has transformed our understanding of plant cellular heterogeneity, metabolites provide a direct and integrative readout of cellular biochemical activity and physiological state and can offer valuable insights into phenotype. They provide essential information that gene expression alone does not capture. Recent advances in mass spectrometry-based single-cell metabolomics (scMet) have enabled direct measurement of metabolic variation across individual cells and subcellular domains. In parallel, mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) has emerged as a powerful approach for mapping the spatial organization of metabolites within intact plant organs, offering new opportunities to connect chemical diversity with anatomy, cell identity, and biological functions. This review summarizes current technologies for plant single-cell sampling, scMet, and MSI for spatial metabolomics. It further highlights emerging efforts to illuminate the plant's cellular and spatial dark metabolome through spectral libraries, computational metabolomics, and AI-assisted annotation. A long-term objective is to build quantitative, spatially resolved, and biologically interpretable plant signaling and metabolic networks at single-cell resolution.

titre: Digital Masking Profiles and Academic Self-Concept Among Gifted Autistic Students and Students With Learning Difficulties: A Two-Wave Person-Centered Study.
titre_fr: Digital Masking Profiles and Academic Self-Concept Among Gifted Autistic Students and Students With Learning Difficulties: A Two-Wave Person-Centered Study.
auteurs: Almulla Abdullah Ahmed, Khasawneh Mohamad Ahmad Saleem
revue: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
resume: Digital tools can make academic participation more accessible while allowing effort or support underlying successful performance to remain unseen. This study examined configurations of compensation, masking, assimilation, and digital masking among gifted autistic students and students with learning difficulties and their associations with academic self-concept. The sample comprised 469 Saudi school students aged 16-18 years at Wave 1, with 394 completing Wave 2 approximately 20 weeks later. Participants completed measures of compensation, masking, assimilation, digital masking, and academic self-concept. Latent profile analyses were conducted separately at each wave using three Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire-Short Form dimensions and a six-item Digital Masking Behavioral Index. Academic self-concept was examined as an external correlate, while learner group and accommodation access were evaluated as predictors of profile membership. Four profiles emerged at Wave 1: Open Support/Low Masking, Supported Compensation, Hidden Digital Effort, and Pervasive Camouflaging. Three profiles emerged at Wave 2: Low Masking/Open Support, Moderate/Mixed, and Pervasive Camouflaging. Academic self-concept was highest in open-support profiles and lowest in pervasive-camouflaging profiles. Compensation alone was not associated with poorer academic self-concept, whereas masking, assimilation, and digital masking showed negative associations. Gifted autistic students had higher odds of Supported Compensation membership, while accommodation access was associated with lower odds of Hidden Digital Effort membership. GPA differences were smaller and less consistent. Similar academic performance may coexist with different patterns of compensation, masking, and digital effort. Findings support distinguishing supported compensation from masking-dependent compensation and highlight environments that facilitate accommodations.

titre: Multi-joint and multi-planar lower-limb moment prediction from four inertial measurement units with target-subject adaptation.
titre_fr: Multi-joint and multi-planar lower-limb moment prediction from four inertial measurement units with target-subject adaptation.
auteurs: Fan Xinyu, Ma Tao, Yu Ningbo, Han Jianda, Guan Jiayin, Ni Monan, Sun Tao
resume: Accurate and continuous prediction of multi-planar lower-limb joint moments is crucial for clinical rehabilitation, sports science, and assistive device design. However, gold-standard methods rely on bulky, expensive laboratory-bound equipment, and existing wearable solutions are often limited to single-joint or single-plane predictions, or require dense sensor arrays impractical for daily living. To address these limitations, we propose an end-to-end multi-task temporal convolutional network framework. Using only four inertial measurement units sparsely placed on the pelvis and lower limb, the framework simultaneously predicts five continuous joint moments: hip and knee moments in the coronal plane, and hip, knee, and ankle moments in the sagittal plane. A hard-parameter-sharing temporal convolutional backbone extracts cross-joint temporal features, while point-wise channel attention enables task-specific feature reweighting. Adaptive batch normalization (AdaBN) further enables target-subject adaptation using a 10-s segment of unlabeled level-walking data. We evaluated the model on 14 participants performing level walking, stair ascent, and stair descent under nested subject-level leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. The proposed model achieved the highest numerical overall R<sup>2</sup> among models evaluated without target-subject adaptation and significantly outperformed four of the six external baselines; AdaBN further improved the overall R<sup>2</sup> to 0.759 ± 0.032. Ablation experiments showed that hard parameter sharing, point-wise channel attention, and AdaBN increased the overall R<sup>2</sup> by ΔR<sup>2</sup> = 0.017, 0.026, and 0.032, respectively (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.05). Supplementary evaluation on an independent public dataset yielded R<sup>2</sup> values of 0.704-0.840 across four joint-moment targets. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of continuous multi-joint and multi-planar moment prediction using a sparse wearable sensor configuration under controlled laboratory conditions and support further evaluation in larger and clinically diverse cohorts and in out-of-laboratory settings.

titre: Transcriptional signatures associated with environmental and developmental variation in tobacco aroma-related pathways across cultivars and regions.
titre_fr: Transcriptional signatures associated with environmental and developmental variation in tobacco aroma-related pathways across cultivars and regions.
auteurs: Li Xiaoxu, Wen Yilin, He Xinxi, Yang Jiashuo, Wang Guoping, Peng Yu, Li Zhiyuan, Zhao Yu, Wu Dousheng, Xu Xiangli, Liu Wanfeng, Li Yangyang, Huang Pingjun, Gao Junping, Wang Yirong, Chen Long, Yang Xiaonian, Pu Wenxuan
resume: Tobacco aroma is a complex quality trait shaped by interactions among genotype, developmental progression, and regional environment, yet the transcriptional programs linking ecological context to aroma-related metabolism remain incompletely understood. We profiled the transcriptomes of ten Nicotiana tabacum L. cultivars grown in three representative regions and sampled at three developmental stages. Normalized RNA-seq expression, principal component analysis, differential expression analysis, soft clustering, pathway enrichment, gene-expression variability analysis, and protein-protein interaction network analysis were performed. Growing region was the major source of transcriptomic variation, followed by developmental stage, whereas cultivar effects were comparatively smaller. Leaf maturation from S1 to S3 was associated with repression of photosynthesis and carbon-assimilation pathways and induction of stress responses, redox regulation, cell-wall and membrane remodeling, amino acid metabolism, and secondary metabolism. Aroma-associated processes, including carotenoid-, phenylpropanoid-, and redox-related pathways, showed regiondependent expression patterns. Strong-aroma cultivars exhibited greater transcriptional variability across regions than light-aroma cultivars, suggesting stronger environmental responsiveness of their regulatory networks. Network analysis further highlighted candidate hub genes, including the heat shockrelated protein A0A1S4A548 and peroxiredoxin Q A0A1S4B900, in temperature- and oxidative-stress-related modules. These findings provide a transcriptome-level framework for understanding how environmental context and developmental maturation are associated with aroma-related metabolic reprogramming in tobacco and identify candidate genes for future functional validation.

titre: Designing Memory into the Medicine Box: A Call for Smarter Adherence Tools in Alzheimer's Care.
titre_fr: Designing Memory into the Medicine Box: A Call for Smarter Adherence Tools in Alzheimer's Care.
auteurs: Uludag Kadir
resume: Medication non-adherence is common among people with Alzheimer's disease (AD). In the study, it is argued that the pill container should be redesigned as a cognitive-support device rather than a passive holder for medication, and the cognitive, equity, and implementation considerations that this position raises are outlined. The study proposes matching tool complexity to disease stage and an individual's broader cognitive profile may support adherence: connected reminder devices where executive, sensory, and technological capacities allow, and simpler, high-cue designs where these capacities are more limited. The study emphasizes that personalization should apply to the medication-management interface. We conclude that redesigning the medicine box as an active therapeutic interface is a plausible, low-risk complement to pharmacological care that warrants comparative evaluation.

titre: Viral potential to modulate antibiotic resistance gene succession through host interactions during food waste composting.
titre_fr: Viral potential to modulate antibiotic resistance gene succession through host interactions during food waste composting.
auteurs: Zhang Liangmao, Luo Dewei, Yang Jing, Yang Meng, Yang Ying, Yao Rui, Zhan Min, Zhang Yuchen, Su Yinglong, Wang Binghan, Xie Bing
resume: Composting can mitigate antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) risks, yet viral contributions to their dynamics remain unclear. Using time-series metagenomics, we investigated viral roles in ARG succession during composting of two food waste types. In both composts, ARGs followed an enrichment-decline-rebound trajectory accompanied by substrate-specific ARG-host turnover. Particularly, the maturation rebound involved the re-enrichment of high-risk ARGs, including tet(L) and lnu(G). Procrustes analysis showed significant associations of viral communities with bacterial and ARG profiles. Meanwhile, virus-host networks were organized predominantly around Firmicutes, with both temperate and lytic viral abundances correlated with ARG-host dynamics during the heating-to-thermophilic transition. Viral auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs), annotated for central carbon metabolism, nutrient acquisition, and stress responses, may aid environmental adaptation in key ARG hosts, including Bacillus spp. Although mobile genetic elements (MGEs) provided important genetic contexts for ARG mobility, only four putative virus-mediated ARG horizontal transfer records were detected. Structural equation modelling suggested potential viral involvement through host interactions, while highlighting the importance of ARG hosts and MGEs in resistome succession. Further viral perturbation experiments are needed to clarify causal contributions in future. Overall, this study provides new insights into viral roles in resistome succession, informing resistance risk management during composting.

titre: Gait, cane loading, and usability after 1 month of Carbon-Curved Cane use in chronic post-stroke hemiplegia: A pilot study.
titre_fr: Gait, cane loading, and usability after 1 month of Carbon-Curved Cane use in chronic post-stroke hemiplegia: A pilot study.
auteurs: Kokuwa Ryu, Sakai Yuta, Ishikawa Junpei
resume: This pilot study examined gait, cane loading, and perceived usability after 1 month of daily Carbon-Curved Cane (CC-Cane) use in people with chronic post-stroke hemiplegia who habitually used a single-point cane (SP-Cane). Ten community-dwelling participants completed this non-randomised longitudinal pilot study, prospectively registered. Three-dimensional gait analysis and cane ground-reaction force measurements were obtained with the habitual SP-Cane, at initial CC-Cane use, and after 1 month of daily CC-Cane use. Participant-condition means were analysed with random-intercept linear mixed-effects models. False-discovery-rate correction was applied within outcome domains, and continuous cane-force waveforms were assessed with one-dimensional statistical non-parametric mapping. After false-discovery-rate correction, condition effects were observed for paretic and non-paretic step length, stride length, walking speed (q ≤ 0.009), and selected centre-of-mass outcomes (q ≤ 0.015). Post-CC-Cane values differed from both initial conditions for most of these outcomes. Continuous waveform analysis identified condition effects in mediolateral (24-85% of the cane-contact cycle) and anteroposterior forces (11-42%; corrected p < 0.001), but not vertical force. SUS and QUEST total scores did not differ between canes. One-month CC-Cane use was associated with changes in selected gait and centre-of-mass outcomes, whereas direction-specific cane-loading patterns differed immediately. These pilot findings support further controlled evaluation of mechanically adaptive canes and do not establish causality.

titre: Genome-wide selection signatures in Turkish Awassi sheep: uncovering the genetic basis of production traits and adaptation.
titre_fr: Genome-wide selection signatures in Turkish Awassi sheep: uncovering the genetic basis of production traits and adaptation.
auteurs: Meydan Hasan, Demir Eymen, Bilginer Ümit, Doğru Huriye, Kaya Sarp, Argun Karsli Bahar, Aktaş Yusuf, Atmaca Veli, Perini Francesco, Karsli Taki
resume: The Awassi sheep is one of the leading fat-tailed breeds of the Fertile Crescent, known for its high milk yield and resilience in arid and semi-arid environments. Despite its socio-economic importance, a high-resolution genomic characterization of selection signatures in Turkish Awassi populations remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the genomic diversity, demographic history, and selection signatures of Turkish Awassi sheep using double-digest restriction-site-associated DNA sequencing (ddRADseq). Genome-wide single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) discovery was performed on 40 unrelated Awassi sheep. Genetic diversity parameters, historical effective population size ( N e ), and linkage disequilibrium (LD) decay were assessed. Selection signatures were identified using both runs of homozygosity (ROH) islands and Tajima's D analyses, followed by functional annotation of candidate genes. A total of 397 315 high-quality SNPs were identified. The average minor allele frequency (MAF) was 0.333, and the ROH-based inbreeding coefficient ( F ROH ) was low (0.025), indicating high genetic integrity. The historical N e showed a consistent decline, reaching 147 in the most recent generations. Selection signature analysis identified 21 and 48 protein-coding genes by means of ROH and Tajima's D , respectively. The key candidate genes were associated with milk yield and lactation (AKR1C3, AKR1D1, OXT, AVP, ZNF131), meat production and growth (PBX1, KBTBD8, HOXA cluster, ADGB), fat-tail formation (HOXA cluster, HMGCS1, STARD4), and environmental adaptation (ABCB1, TSLP, IL6). Our findings reveal that the Turkish Awassi genome is a rich genetic reservoir shaped by combined natural and artificial selection. The selection signatures identified in this study provide fundamental genomic targets for future breeding strategies to enhance productivity without compromising environmental resilience. These findings support the use of Turkish Awassi as a genetic resource for breeding programs in arid and semi-arid production systems.

titre: Design and intelligent control of a low-cost, sEMG-driven, 3D-printed robotic hand prosthesis: A three-tier benchmarking framework with novel robustness metrics.
titre_fr: Design and intelligent control of a low-cost, sEMG-driven, 3D-printed robotic hand prosthesis: A three-tier benchmarking framework with novel robustness metrics.
auteurs: Shinde Anagha, Shete Virendra, Mehendale Ninad
resume: Upper-limb amputation and neuromuscular disorders impose functional limitations on millions of people worldwide. Commercially available myoelectric prostheses, controlled by surface electromyography (sEMG) signals from residual limb muscles, cost approximately USD 75,000-100,000 (about INR 62-83 lakh), limiting accessibility in resource-limited settings. We present a 3D-printed, tendon-driven research hand prototype with a component cost of USD 122-232 (about INR 10,100-19,300), built around a single MyoWare 1.0 sensor and an Arduino Nano, with gesture classification performed on a tethered host PC. Five classifiers-Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D CNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-were benchmarked across synthetic, Ninapro DB5, and live recordings of three gestures from ten able-bodied participants. Under subject-independent Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation, RF achieved the highest live accuracy (68.7%). Friedman and Nemenyi testing showed that RF was significantly better than SVM, KNN and LSTM (p < 0.05), while its advantage over the 1D CNN (60.7%) was not significant. Permutation importance identified waveform length, RMS and MAV as the most informative features. We further propose two metrics: the Robustness Degradation Index (RDI), which quantifies the synthetic-to-real performance gap and was lowest for RF (43.7%), and a Cost-Performance Index (CPI), which was 13.77 for the prototype. The hand achieved an end-to-end latency of 285 ms and reliably held objects of up to 200 g. These results demonstrate well-above-chance three-class control with minimal hardware in able-bodied users and motivate evaluation with trans-radial amputees.
