titre: A Randomized Controlled Trial Examining the Effects of Extended Oral Tranexamic Acid on Postoperative Pain and Range of Motion Following Total Knee Arthroplasty.
titre_fr: A Randomized Controlled Trial Examining the Effects of Extended Oral Tranexamic Acid on Postoperative Pain and Range of Motion Following Total Knee Arthroplasty.
auteurs: Grosso Matthew J, Panek Gina, Weinz Czarina, Hahn Alexander K, Bauer Jordan A
resume: The implementation of perioperative intravenous tranexamic acid (TXA) protocols in total knee arthroplasty (TKA) has led to improved outcomes related to decreased blood loss and decreased transfusion rates. A recent randomized controlled trial (RCT) demonstrated that there may be additional benefits to extended oral TXA (EOTXA) for improving pain and function in the early postoperative period. In this double-blind RCT, we examined the effects of EOTXA following primary TKA on postoperative pain, range of motion (ROM), opioid usage, and ambulation status. There were 86 patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty randomized to two groups: EOTXA versus placebo. All patients received one gram of intravenous TXA prior to incision and in the postoperative recovery area. Patients in the EOTXA group (n = 43) received 1.95 grams of oral TXA daily from postoperative day one through POD three. The primary outcome in this study was the visual analog scale (VAS) pain score in the three-month postoperative period. The secondary outcomes included ROM, ambulation status (assistive device usage), and opioid consumption. There was no statistically significant difference in VAS pain scores at any time point: POD one Placebo 4.7 versus EOTXA 5.4 (P = 0.16); POD two 4.1 versus 4.4 (P = 0.33); POD three 3.7 versus 4.0 (P = 0.49); POD7 3.6 versus 3.7 (P = 0.66); two weeks 3.0 versus 2.8 (P = 0.63); six weeks 2.2 versus 1.8 (P = 0.22); and 12 weeks 1.2 versus 1.1 (P = 0.86). In addition, there were no significant differences in ROM, daily opioid consumption, and ambulation status at two, six, and 12 weeks postoperatively (P > 0.10). In the largest RCT to date, this study found no significant difference in pain scores, opioid consumption, functional outcomes, or ambulation status with the addition of extended oral TXA following primary TKA. Based on these results, broad utilization of this protocol in primary TKA may not be warranted.

titre: CmALDH2B7 and CmALDH7B4 positively regulate the osmotic stress tolerance in melon (Cucumis melo L.).
titre_fr: CmALDH2B7 and CmALDH7B4 positively regulate the osmotic stress tolerance in melon (Cucumis melo L.).
auteurs: Zhu Kaidi, Yang Haiming, Zhou Shuxin, Yan Ruiyao, Du Jiawei, Gao Hongbo, Zhao Wensheng
revue: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
resume: Aldehyde dehydrogenases (ALDHs) play critical roles in detoxifying reactive aldehydes and maintaining cellular redox homeostasis under stress conditions. In this study, 17 ALDH genes were identified in melon (Cucumis melo L.). Most CmALDH genes harbor multiple cis-regulatory elements associated with abiotic stress responses and hormone signaling, implicating their roles in environmental adaptation. Subsequently, CmALDH2B7 and CmALDH7B4 were selected for further expression and functional analyses. Both CmALDH2B7 and CmALDH7B4 were highly expressed in flowers, flower buds, and roots, and were strongly induced by osmotic stress. Overexpression of CmALDH2B7 or CmALDH7B4 enhanced the osmotic stress resistance of Arabidopsis plants, while silencing of either gene compromised the osmotic stress tolerance of melon seedlings, as evidenced by accelerated wilting, elevated malondialdehyde (MDA) accumulation, and reduced activities of catalase (CAT), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and peroxidase (POD). Protein interaction assays revealed that CmALDH2B7 directly interacts with the catalase CmCAT1, whereas CmALDH7B4 does not. This study provides a foundation for understanding the functional diversification of the ALDH superfamily and identifies promising targets for improving drought stress tolerance in melon.

titre: Aquatic pelvic floor rehabilitation for persistent stress urinary incontinence after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a prospective single-arm study.
titre_fr: Aquatic pelvic floor rehabilitation for persistent stress urinary incontinence after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a prospective single-arm study.
auteurs: Iacovelli Valerio, Carilli Marco, Vittori Matteo, Schifone Simona, Antonucci Michele, Di Giovanni Giulia, Signoretti Marta, Maiorino Francesco, Bove Pierluigi
revue: Archivio italiano di urologia, andrologia : organo ufficiale [di] Societa italiana di ecografia urologica e nefrologica
resume: Persistent stress urinary incontinence (SUI) remains one of the most troublesome functional complications after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP). Although pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) represents the standard conservative treatment, a proportion of patients continue to experience bothersome symptoms. Aquatic rehabilitation may facilitate pelvic floor activation through reduced gravitational loading, enhanced proprioceptive input, and trunk stabilization; however, its role in post-prostatectomy incontinence has not been investigated. This prospective pilot study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and clinical outcomes associated with hydrokinesitherapy in men with persistent SUI following RARP.  Methods: Men with persistent pure SUI after rArP despite three months of standardized conservative management, including PFMT and biofeedback, were prospectively enrolled between January and May 2023. Participants underwent a five-week hydrokinesitherapy program consisting of ten supervised 40-minute sessions performed twice weekly. outcomes included the 24-hour pad test, International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-short Form (ICIQ-sF), Incontinence Quality of Life questionnaire (I-QoL), International Prostate symptom score (IPSS), IPSS quality-of-life item, and Patient Global Impression of Improvement (PGI-I), assessed at baseline, end of treatment (5 weeks), and 12-week follow-up. Twenty patients completed the rehabilitation program without treatment-related adverse events or dropouts. significant improvements were observed at the end of treatment in pad weight, IPSS, IPSS-QoL, ICIQ-SF, and I-QoL scores (all p ≤ 0.01). These improvements were maintained or further improved at 12 weeks, particularly for pad weight, QoL, and incontinence-related symptom scores. overall patient satisfaction was high according to PGI-I. Two patients (10%) subsequently underwent male sling surgery because of persistent bothersome sUI.  Conclusions: Hydrokinesitherapy was feasible, safe, and associated with clinically meaningful improvements in urinary continence and health-related QoL in men with persistent SUI after RARP who had not achieved satisfactory recovery following initial conservative rehabilitation. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in adequately powered randomized controlled trials.

titre: Clinical Outcomes of Zone I Flexor Digitorum Profundus Injuries: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of the Last 25 Years.
titre_fr: Clinical Outcomes of Zone I Flexor Digitorum Profundus Injuries: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of the Last 25 Years.
auteurs: Hones Keegan M, Lamprecht Chris, Wabnitz Patrick, Rakauskas Taylor R, Hao Kevin A, Yu Stephen, Hampton Hailey, El-Gammal Tarek Abdalla, Wright Thomas W, Kim Jongmin
resume: Zone I flexor digitorum profundus (FDP) tendon injuries, at the distal phalanx insertion, generally require surgery. However, outcomes may vary, and multiple surgical techniques have been described. This review sought to evaluate management, rehabilitation, and outcomes following zone I FDP injuries. Using Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, a systematic review and meta-analysis was performed. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane were queried for articles concerning zone I FDP injuries since 2000. Patients younger than 18 years of age and revision surgery were excluded. Demographics, strength, range of motion, outcome scores, therapy protocols, and complications were evaluated. Twenty studies met inclusion criteria and were stratified by treatment strategy into 31 cohorts comprising 669 fingers. The mean age was 36 years and 25% were women. Injury mechanisms included 348 lacerations (52%) and 234 avulsions (35%); 88 injuries (13%) were unspecified. Primary tenorrhaphy was the most frequently reported treatment (39%), followed by tenorrhaphy with a tie-over button (10%) and bone anchor fixation (10%). The mean time to surgery was 4 days. Range of motion or outcome measures were documented in 12 cohorts (39%) and strength in 10 cohorts (32%). Meta-analysis demonstrated postoperative FDP rupture, revision surgery, and tenolysis rates of 2.0%, 1.0%, and 1.6%, respectively. Lacerations were treated with primary tenorrhaphy more commonly compared with avulsions (59% vs 22%) and had higher revision rates (7.6% vs 1.4%). Surgical repair of zone I FDP injuries demonstrates low complication rates and generally favorable outcomes; however, inconsistent reporting of functional outcomes limits meaningful comparison between surgical techniques.

titre: Community-Based Physiotherapy Models and Neurological Trajectories in Infants at High Risk of Cerebral Palsy in Rural Tanzania: A Retrospective Routine-Care Study.
titre_fr: Community-Based Physiotherapy Models and Neurological Trajectories in Infants at High Risk of Cerebral Palsy in Rural Tanzania: A Retrospective Routine-Care Study.
auteurs: da Silva Fernanda Cordeiro, de Araujo Giovanna Dantas, da Silva Natany Carla Lima, Ribeiro-Samora Giane Amorim, de Lima-Alvarez Carolina Daniel, Pereira Silvana Alves
resume: Cerebral palsy (CP) refers to a group of motor impairments resulting from nonprogressive brain malformations or injuries that occur early in development. Limited access to rehabilitation services in low- and middle-income countries poses substantial challenges. This study aimed to describe the clinical and sociodemographic characteristics of children treated at a rural rehabilitation centre in Tanzania and to evaluate their neurological trajectories across three physiotherapy models. A retrospective longitudinal review (April to September 2025) analysed 126 medical records of children aged 3-24 months who underwent the Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination (HINE) at the beginning of the intervention and after approximately 3 months of care. Participants were categorized into the hope intensive programme (HPP; 40 h/month), early intervention programme (EIP; 16 h/4 months) or conventional physiotherapy programme (CPP; 16 h/4 months). Neurological function improved across all groups, with substantial raw neurological development gains reflected in the mean HINE scores, which increased from 41.6 to 55.3. Postintervention, the odds of infants remaining in the lowest HINE score range decreased significantly (OR: 0.07). The HPP group showed the fastest developmental progression. The study also supports the feasibility of using the Kiswahili-translated HINE as an excellent low-cost, responsive and context-appropriate tool for longitudinal tracking and clinical monitoring. Structured neurorehabilitation, particularly intensive intervention, was associated with significant raw neurological progression in this low-resource setting, highlighting the utility of the HINE for objective longitudinal surveillance.

titre: Mime therapy versus proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation exercises as adjuncts to clinic-based multimodal rehabilitation in Bell's palsy: a retrospective comparative cohort study.
titre_fr: Mime therapy versus proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation exercises as adjuncts to clinic-based multimodal rehabilitation in Bell's palsy: a retrospective comparative cohort study.
auteurs: Ercan Batı Buse, Ünlü Akyüz Ece, Batı Musa Alper
revue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
resume: To compare clinical and electrophysiological outcomes of adjunctive mime therapy and proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) exercises within a shared clinic-based multimodal rehabilitation program for Bell's palsy. This retrospective comparative cohort study analyzed routine-care records of 53 patients (28 PNF; 25 mime therapy; 40 men; median age, 39 years; median baseline Sunnybrook score, 30). Rehabilitation began 10-28 days after onset, after corticosteroid treatment, and comprised 10 sessions of low-level laser therapy and neuromuscular electrical stimulation plus the group-specific adjunct. Sunnybrook, electroneurography (ENoG), and needle electromyography (EMG) assessments were performed at baseline (T0), one month (T1), and three months (T2); T2 total Sunnybrook was the prespecified primary outcome. Formal assessor blinding was absent. Both groups improved. At T1, no secondary clinical between-group difference remained significant after Holm adjustment. At T2, mime therapy was associated with a higher total Sunnybrook score (p = 0.002; δ = 0.490; 95% CI, 0.211-0.736) and better resting symmetry (adjusted p = 0.021; δ = -0.389). The between-group difference in voluntary-movement scores was not statistically significant after adjustment (p = 0.0501). ENoG parameters did not differ at T1 or T2; T2 effects were small. T2 combined ENoG/needle EMG classification was mild degeneration in 48 patients and moderate in five, without a between-group difference (p = 0.201; Cramér's V = 0.176). Synkinesis occurred in 3/28 PNF patients and 0/25 mime-therapy patients (p = 0.238). Within a shared multimodal rehabilitation program, mime therapy was associated with higher three-month total Sunnybrook scores and better resting symmetry, while most outcomes showed no significant between-group differences. These findings require cautious interpretation given the small sample and retrospective, nonrandomized design.

titre_fr: Hybrid Osteosynthesis for Septic Humeral Shaft Nonunion in a Patient with Obesity: A Case Report.
auteurs: Chiquini-Ramírez Paolo, Villamues-Moreno Nancy Lorena, Ponce-de-Léon-Dominguez Jorge, Moreno-Degante Leonardo, Pettet-Ruiz Bernardo, Torres-Casado Ernesto, Reyes-García Héctor Mauricio, Garduza-Leyva Nelva
resume: Septic humeral shaft nonunion represents a complex reconstructive challenge in orthopedic surgery, particularly in patients with obesity, in whom increased lever arms and greater mechanical loading of the upper extremity substantially compromise fixation stability. Recurrent failure of isolated fixation constructs, including intramedullary nails or compression plates, necessitates hybrid strategies that combine enhanced biomechanical stability with effective eradication of microbial infection. This article presents the case of a middle-aged man with obesity and a history of a left humeral shaft fracture initially treated with intramedullary nailing in December 2020 who developed persistent nonunion. Following revision surgery with dynamic compression plating, fixation failure occurred secondary to implant fatigue. A second revision procedure was performed through a posterior approach, including nerve neurolysis, extensive debridement, and hybrid fixation using a 240 x 8 mm Targon™ H intramedullary nail (B. Braun, Melsungen, Germany) combined with a narrow 4.5-mm dynamic compression plate (DCP; DePuy Synthes, Warsaw, IN, USA). Cancellous bone chip grafting was also performed. Intraoperative cultures yielded Staphylococcus epidermidis, establishing the diagnosis of septic nonunion, and targeted oral clindamycin therapy was initiated. Despite transient postoperative radial neuropraxia, which resolved with pregabalin treatment and structured physical rehabilitation, the patient achieved complete osseous union, eradication of infection, and an Upper Extremity Functional Scale (UEFS) score of 69/80, corresponding to 86% of maximal functional capacity. In conclusion, hybrid fixation combining an intramedullary nail with a narrow 4.5-mm DCP, together with pathogen-directed antimicrobial therapy, provides excellent axial and rotational stability and represents an effective salvage strategy for septic humeral shaft nonunion in patients with increased biomechanical demands.

titre: Electroacupuncture Combined with Surround Needling for Acute Lateral Ankle Sprain in Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: Electroacupuncture Combined with Surround Needling for Acute Lateral Ankle Sprain in Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Hu Qimiao, Cai Qingzi, Qi Bonuo, Cai Jin, Wang Jue, Liang Yi, Lu Hui
resume: Acute lateral ankle sprain (ALAS) has a high incidence in adults. Improper acute-stage intervention causes prolonged pain, swelling and impaired functional recovery. Conventional ice plus brake rest has limited rehabilitation efficacy. This study investigated the clinical efficacy and safety of electroacupuncture (EA) combined with surround needling for adult ALAS. In this single-center randomized controlled trial, 95 patients aged 18-60 years with ALAS were 1:1:1 randomized to EA+surround needling (n=34), sham EA (n=32) or control (ice+brake rest, n=29) groups. Outcomes were the Kofoed score and musculoskeletal ultrasound, assessed at baseline and weeks 1, 2, 3 and 9. Adverse events were monitored throughout. EA improved Kofoed scores more than control or sham EA from week 2 to week 9 (adjusted mean differences 7.8-11.4, 95% CI excluding zero). Kofoed AUC (baseline to week 9, points × week) was greater with EA (675.5, 95% CI 658.3-692.8). AUC differences were 39.51 vs control (95% CI 19.32-59.70) and 24.76 vs sham EA (95% CI 6.05-43.47). EA reduced anterior talofibular ligament thickness more than both groups and calcaneofibular ligament thickness more than control. EA combined with surround needling was superior to sham EA and ice plus brake rest in improving ankle function assessed by the Kofoed score and reducing anterior talofibular ligament thickness, and superior to ice plus brake rest in reducing calcaneofibular ligament thickness. However, larger, longer-term trials are needed to verify these findings.

titre: Neuromuscular Determinants of Strength Training Response in COPD: A Multilevel Approach to Understanding Non-Response After Pulmonary Rehabilitation.
titre_fr: Neuromuscular Determinants of Strength Training Response in COPD: A Multilevel Approach to Understanding Non-Response After Pulmonary Rehabilitation.
auteurs: Desachy M, Héraud N, Oliver N, Lacombe J-P, Goesch J, Calvat A, Alexandre F, Varray A
resume: COPD is associated with significant lower limb muscle weakness, a predictor of mortality. Pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) incorporating resistance exercises is a key intervention to counteract this impairment. However, 50% of patients fail to improve muscle strength, classifying them as non-responders (NR). To understand this variability, this study aimed to assess all components of the muscle strength production chain before and after PR, and to identify predictors of non-response. 33 COPD patients completed a 4-week inpatient PR program including standardized strength training following ACSM international guidelines. Quadriceps maximal voluntary isometric contraction (Q<sub>MVIC</sub>), rate of force development (RFD), voluntary activation (VA<sub>cortical</sub>), corticospinal excitability (MEP/M<sub>max</sub>), and contractile properties were assessed before and after PR. Patients with a Q<sub>MVIC</sub> increase < 7.5N·m were classified as NR. Logistic regression analysis was used to identify predictors of non-response. On average, Q<sub>MVIC</sub> improved (+5.4 N·m; p=0.02), but 60.6% of patients were NR (despite comparable training metrics). Baseline VA was similar between groups. Responders showed a significant increase in VA<sub>cortical</sub> (p=0.03), while NR exhibited no changes (p=0.78). Corticospinal excitability and peripheral muscle adaptations improved similarly in both groups. RFD was lower in NR both pre and post PR (p<0.01), and was identified as a key predictor of non-response (sensibility: 95%; specificity: 90%). Both groups displayed comparable improvements in corticospinal excitability and peripheral muscle properties; however, only responders showed a significant increase in voluntary activation. Identifying RFD as a predictor of non-response provides a valuable tool for early patient stratification and personalized training strategies.

titre: Effect of a social participation redesign programme for stroke survivors: A randomised controlled trial.
titre_fr: Effect of a social participation redesign programme for stroke survivors: A randomised controlled trial.
auteurs: Zhang Huijing, Zhao Xuetong, Yang Yuhang, Wu Xi Vivien, Li Kun
resume: Stroke survivors encounter multifaceted barriers to physical, psychological, and social adaptation. Although social participation is a crucial long-term rehabilitation outcome, few interventions have addressed multi-dimensional barriers while redesigning daily lifestyles to enhance social participation. To evaluate the effectiveness of a social participation redesign programme for stroke survivors in improving social participation and related health outcomes. Assessor-blinded, two-arm randomised controlled trial. Department of Neurology of a tertiary hospital in Changchun, China. Stroke survivors aged ≥18 years with a modified Rankin Scale score <4 (N = 112). Participants were recruited using convenience sampling and randomly assigned to either an intervention group (n = 56) or a control group (n = 56) receiving usual care. The eight-week intervention comprised WeChat-based group sessions, group activities, and individual consultations. The primary outcome was social participation frequency. Secondary outcomes were participation satisfaction and restrictions, social support, functional and cognitive status, depression, anxiety, and intrinsic motivation. Data were collected at baseline (T0), post-intervention (T1) and three months post-intervention (T2). Generalised estimating equation models were applied to examine effects of the intervention on the study outcomes. Mediation analyses were conducted to explore the potential mechanisms underlying these effects. At T1, the intervention group demonstrated significant improvements in social participation frequency (β = 0.13, 95% CI: 0.05 to 0.20, p = 0.001). Significant improvement in social participation satisfaction (β = 0.11, 95% CI: 0.06 to 0.15, p < 0.001), social support (β = 0.08, 95% CI: 0.02 to 0.14, p = 0.005), intrinsic motivation (β = 0.10, 95% CI: 0.03 to 0.17, p = 0.003) and reductions in participation restrictions (β = 0.07, 95% CI: 0.00 to 0.13, p = 0.035), depression (β = -0.93, 95% CI: -1.68 to -0.19, p = 0.014) and anxiety (β = -0.92, 95% CI: -1.83 to -0.00, p = 0.049) was also observed. Improvements in social interaction and relationships (β = 0.09, 95% CI: 0.03 to 0.16, p = 0.007), and subjective social support (β = 0.08, 95% CI: 0.01 to 0.14, p = 0.016) were maintained at T2. Mediation analysis indicated that social support, depression, and intrinsic motivation were potential statistical mediators of the intervention effect on social participation. The social participation redesign programme was associated with short-term improvements in social participation and psychosocial health. Social support and psychological factors may represent potential pathways associated with improvements in social participation. This randomised controlled trial was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR.org.cn; ChiCTR2400084787). Registration date: May 2024. Recruitment commenced in August 2024.

titre: A New and Innovative Surgical Approach to Treating Haglund Deformity.
titre_fr: A New and Innovative Surgical Approach to Treating Haglund Deformity.
auteurs: Bhandari Hemant, Rathod Vishal Nitin
resume: Haglund's deformity, a posterosuperior calcaneal prominence, is a common cause of posterior heel pain, prominently affecting the Achilles tendon and supero-anterior bursa. First described in 1927, it is often idiopathic and may be exacerbated by factors, such as age, obesity, and systemic inflammatory diseases. Typically seen in active individuals, especially females, conservative management often resolves symptoms. However, in persistent cases, surgical intervention becomes necessary. This study presents an innovative sigma incision technique for surgical management, allowing for enhanced exposure and minimal tendon retraction, thereby reducing complication risks. Results from six patients showed significant pain reduction and improvements in function, with no post-surgical complications noted. This approach offers advantages over traditional methods, including quicker rehabilitation and lower risk of Achilles tendon damage, indicating a promising avenue for effective treatment of Haglund's deformity.

titre: Pain Management in Orthopedic Surgery: A Procedure-Specific Orthopedic-Anesthesia Approach to Perioperative Analgesia.
titre_fr: Pain Management in Orthopedic Surgery: A Procedure-Specific Orthopedic-Anesthesia Approach to Perioperative Analgesia.
auteurs: Bhadani Janki Sharan, Kumar Indrajeet, Kumari Priyanka, Kashyap Nishant, Kumar Santosh
resume: Introduction: Post-operative pain in orthopedic surgery is clinically important because inadequate analgesia can impair mobilization, sleep, physiotherapy and discharge, while excessive analgesia can cause sedation, motor weakness, drug toxicity and unnecessary opioid exposure. This narrative review uses a structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and targeted review of recent systematic reviews, randomized trials, consensus statements and procedure-specific recommendations, with emphasis on publications available through September 2026. Evidence is synthesized qualitatively according to procedure, analgesic strategy, functional outcomes, and limitations of the underlying evidence. Present evidence supports multimodal analgesia, but does not support a universal regimen or routine addition of every available intervention. Regional techniques can improve early analgesia, although benefits vary by procedure and may be offset by motor block, rebound pain, or limitations in post-operative examination. A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) provide opioid-sparing analgesia, but the relationship between NSAID exposure and fracture healing remains uncertain and appears to depend on drug, dose, duration, fracture type, and patient factors. Opioids remain appropriate as rescue therapy when clinically indicated. Persistent post-surgical pain is influenced by pre-operative and biopsychosocial factors and acute analgesia has not been shown consistently to prevent it. The practical framework proposed here therefore links the operation, patient risk profile, analgesic options, and rehabilitation task, with unexpected severe pain treated as a trigger for clinical reassessment rather than automatic escalation.

titre: [Optimization of rehabilitation program for abnormal gait in patients with knee osteoarthritis based on comprehensive assessment of muscle strength and joint stability].
titre_fr: [Optimization of rehabilitation program for abnormal gait in patients with knee osteoarthritis based on comprehensive assessment of muscle strength and joint stability].
auteurs: Zheng Guanghao, Li Haiqing, Wang Congxiao
revue: Zhongguo gu shang = China journal of orthopaedics and traumatology
resume: Based on a comprehensive evaluation of muscle strength and joint stability, rehabilitation protocols were designed for patients with knee osteoarthritis to investigate their effects on rehabilitation outcomes in these patients. A total of 110 patients with KOA were enrolled between April 2022 and April 2024 and randomly divided into control group and study group using a random number table. The study group comprised 55 patients, including 30 males and 25 females, aged from 45 to 77 years with a mean age of (63.28±5.32) years, disease duration ranged from 2 to 8 years with an average of (5.46±1.21) years. Among them, 26 had left-sided knee involvement and 29 had right-sided involvement. Patients in the study group received a rehabilitation protocol based on comprehensive assessment of muscle strength and joint stability.The control group included 55 patients, 28 males and 27 females, aged from 46 to 78 years with an average of(64.15±5.43) years old, with a disease duration ranging from 2 to 8 years with an average of(5.39±1.18) years old. There were 27 patients of left-sided knee involvement and 28 patients of right-sided involvement. Patients in the control group received conventional rehabilitation for knee osteoarthritis. Before treatment and after 6 weeks of treatment, pain intensity was evaluated using the visual analogue scale(VAS). Spatiotemporal gait parameters were tested in a three-dimensional gait analysis laboratory. Muscle strength was measured using an isokinetic dynamometer. Joint stability was recorded and determined with an infrared camera system. Knee function was assessed using the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities osteoarthritis index (WOMAC) and the Lysholm knee scoring scale. After 6 weeks of treatment, VAS in both groups were significantly lower than those before treatment, and the score in study group (4.15±0.54) was lower than that in control group (4.92±0.63), with a statistically significant difference (P<0.05). The percentage of support phase, cadence, stride length deviation, step width, and foot progression angle in both groups were significantly lower than those before treatment, and the values in study group were lower than those in control group. The walking speed in both groups was significantly higher than that before treatment, and the value in study group was higher than that in control group, with statistically significant differences (P<0.05). The maximum single repetition volume, torque acceleration energy, average power, and peak torque of the affected knee in both groups were significantly higher than those before treatment, and the values in study group were higher than those in control group, with statistically significant differences (P<0.05). The knee joint stability index in both groups was significantly higher than that before treatment, and the index in study group (0.97±0.13) was higher than that in control group (0.86±0.11), with a statistically significant difference (P<0.05). After treatment, the knee joint function scores in both groups were significantly lower than those before treatment, and the score in study group was lower than that in control group, with a statistically significant difference(P<0.05). The rehabilitation program based on the comprehensive evaluation of muscle strength and joint stability can reduce the pain degree of knee osteoarthritis patients, improve the spatiotemporal parameters of gait and knee function, and improve muscle strength and joint stability.

titre: Effects of extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training combined with iron supplementation versus iron supplementation alone on postural control in young women with iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Effects of extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training combined with iron supplementation versus iron supplementation alone on postural control in young women with iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Harrabi Mohamed Achraf, Fendri Thouraya, Ayed Rahma, Boughattas Wissal, Chaari Fatma, Mezghani Ines, Kallel Choumous, Rebai Haithem, Turki Mouna, Ayadi Fatma, Sahli Sonia
revue: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
resume: Recent research revealed postural control deterioration in young women with Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA). To address this postural deficit, it is crucial to develop intervention strategies for postural rehabilitation in these individuals. This study aimed to explore the effect of 8-week extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training (HIIT) based on plyometric exercises combined with iron supplementation versus simple iron treatment on postural control of young women with IDA. This randomized controlled trial enrolled young women with IDA aged 18-25 years, who were randomly assigned to a training group (TG; n = 16) or a non-training group (NTG; n = 17). All participants received oral iron supplementation (ferrous sulfate, 494.5 mg/day, administered as 247.25 mg twice daily), while the TG additionally completed an 8-week extremely low-volume HIIT program based on plyometric exercises. Hemoglobin (Hb) and serum ferritin concentrations were assessed, alongside muscle endurance, reaction time performance, and postural control. Muscle endurance was evaluated using the Killy test, reaction time performance using an online simple reaction time test, and postural control using a stabilometric platform under bipodal and semi-tandem stance conditions. Postural assessments were conducted with eyes open (EO) and eyes closed (EC) on firm and foam surfaces. All outcomes were measured at baseline and 72 h after the final intervention session. After the 8-week intervention, this study demonstrated significant improvements across both groups, irrespective of the intervention. However, TG showed significantly greater post-intervention improvements than NTG in Hb concentration (P = 0.042), muscle endurance (P < 0.001), and postural control. Superior postural control in TG was observed during a bipedal stance on a foam surface (EO: P = 0.001); EC: P = 0.035), as well as during semi-tandem stance on a firm surface (EO: P = 0.015; EC: P = 0.040) and on a foam surface (EO: P = 0.019; EC: P = 0.003), compared to the NTG. With a Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold for multiple comparisons (α = 0.00625), between-group differences in postural control remained significant for bipedal foam EO (P = 0.001) and semi-tandem foam EC (P = 0.003). The study showed that women with IDA improved their postural performance regardless of the intervention used. However, an 8-week program of extremely low-volume HIIT combined with plyometric exercises and iron supplementation had a more beneficial effect compared to traditional iron therapy. These greater improvements in postural control occurred alongside greater improvements in the Hb concentration and muscle endurance in the TG compared to the NTG.

Muscle endurance was evaluated using the Killy test, reaction time performance using an online simple reaction time test, and postural control using a stabilometric platform under bipodal and semi-tandem stance conditions. Postural assessments were conducted with eyes open (EO) and eyes closed (EC) on firm and foam surfaces. All outcomes were measured at baseline and 72 h after the final intervention session. After the 8-week intervention, this study demonstrated significant improvements across both groups, irrespective of the intervention. However, TG showed significantly greater post-intervention improvements than NTG in Hb concentration (P = 0.042), muscle endurance (P < 0.001), and postural control. Superior postural control in TG was observed during a bipedal stance on a foam surface (EO: P = 0.001); EC: P = 0.035), as well as during semi-tandem stance on a firm surface (EO: P = 0.015; EC: P = 0.040) and on a foam surface (EO: P = 0.019; EC: P = 0.003), compared to the NTG. With a Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold for multiple comparisons (α = 0.00625), between-group differences in postural control remained significant for bipedal foam EO (P = 0.001) and semi-tandem foam EC (P = 0.003). The study showed that women with IDA improved their postural performance regardless of the intervention used. However, an 8-week program of extremely low-volume HIIT combined with plyometric exercises and iron supplementation had a more beneficial effect compared to traditional iron therapy. These greater improvements in postural control occurred alongside greater improvements in the Hb concentration and muscle endurance in the TG compared to the NTG.

titre: Levodopa and Subthalamic Nucleus Deep Brain Stimulation Modulate Excitation/Inhibition Balance and the Neural Encoding of Isochronous Sequences in Persons With Parkinson's Disease.
titre_fr: Levodopa and Subthalamic Nucleus Deep Brain Stimulation Modulate Excitation/Inhibition Balance and the Neural Encoding of Isochronous Sequences in Persons With Parkinson's Disease.
auteurs: Criscuolo Antonio, Schwartze Michael, Schwarz Johannes, Strecker Karl, Hesse Swen, Kotz Sonja A
revue: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
resume: Temporally regular auditory stimuli, as found in isochronous sound streams, metronome beats, or music, are often used in rhythmic auditory stimulation (RAS) interventions to initiate and stabilize the temporal coordination of motor plans in persons with Parkinson's disease (pwPD). Research suggests that RAS promotes the recruitment of a cerebellar-prefrontal network and recalibrates abnormal β-band synchronization in the striato-thalamo-cortical pathway. These cuing effects can resemble those observed via dopaminergic treatments (e.g., levodopa) and deep brain stimulation (DBS) targeting the subthalamic nucleus (STN). Here, we investigated the influence of both levodopa administration and STN DBS on the neural encoding of isochronous auditory sequences in pwPD. A comprehensive analysis of electroencephalography (EEG) data revealed changes in β-band event-locked neural responses, as well as event-related potentials, neural tracking of rhythm (δ-band inter-trial phase coherence), and excitation/inhibition balance (E/I) as a function of these treatments. Furthermore, we characterized the link between changes in E/I and motor symptom severity (UPDRS-III) with levodopa administration. We suggest that characterizing individual responses to specific treatments is a fundamental step in tailoring rehabilitation protocols and optimizing intervention efficacy.

titre: Clinical Pathway Management for Platelet-Rich Plasma Therapy in Kellgren-Lawrence Grade I and II Knee Osteoarthritis: A Prospective, Multicenter, Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: Clinical Pathway Management for Platelet-Rich Plasma Therapy in Kellgren-Lawrence Grade I and II Knee Osteoarthritis: A Prospective, Multicenter, Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Yang Shunjie, Wang Hui, Liu Yan, Fu Fangang, Xu Peng, Li Qi, Li Jian, Tian Xiaohe, Chen Gang
revue: The American journal of sports medicine
resume: Clinical outcomes after platelet-rich plasma (PRP) treatment for knee osteoarthritis are inconsistent, and some well-designed trials show no benefit. Whether a standardized multicomponent pathway improves outcomes relative to conventional PRP care is uncertain. To compare the efficacy, safety, satisfaction, and costs of a standardized PRP pathway versus physician-directed conventional PRP care in Kellgren-Lawrence grade I and II knee osteoarthritis. Randomized controlled trial; Level of evidence, 1. At 3 hospitals, 240 patients were randomized 1:1 to a standardized PRP clinical pathway (PRP-CP; n = 120) or physician-directed conventional PRP care (PRP-C; n = 120). PRP-CP combined standardized selection, quality-controlled leukocyte-poor PRP, ultrasound-guided injections, staged rehabilitation, and systematic follow-up. Primary 12-month outcomes were visual analog scale (VAS) pain, Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) total, and International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) scores; secondary outcomes included achievement of the minimal clinically important difference, satisfaction, adverse events, and costs. At 12 months, PRP-CP produced greater changes than PRP-C in VAS (mean difference [MD], -2.98 [95% CI, -3.64 to -2.32]), WOMAC total (MD, -8.63 [95% CI, -11.35 to -5.90]), and IKDC (MD, 10.25 [95% CI, 8.37 to 12.13]) scores (all P < .001). Achievement of the minimal clinically important difference favored PRP-CP at 3, 6, and 12 months for the VAS and at 6 and 12 months for the IKDC and WOMAC (P < .05). Satisfaction was greater with PRP-CP (odds ratio, 1.79 [95% CI, 1.11-2.89]; P = .017). An adverse event occurred in 17 of 115 patients in the PRP-CP group (14.8%) versus 36 of 113 patients in the PRP-C group (31.9%) (Fisher exact test: P = .003). Mean costs were CN¥15,199.9 versus CN¥14,754.4, respectively; the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was CN¥66.0 per WOMAC point. Effects were generally consistent across centers, and blinding was maintained. The standardized multicomponent pathway produced greater 12-month improvements in pain and function than conventional PRP care, with fewer adverse events. Because components were bundled and no placebo group was included, the trial does not establish PRP efficacy or component-specific effects.

titre: Implementation of home-based Digital Rehabilitation in sub-Saharan Africa: a scoping review.
titre_fr: Implementation of home-based Digital Rehabilitation in sub-Saharan Africa: a scoping review.
auteurs: Arntz Angela, Vuori Mia, Oltman Renée, Handgraaf Marietta, Weber Franziska, Ngwakongnwi Emmanuel, Ames Matthew, Tawa Nassib, Mumbi Caroline, Jokinen Kaisa, Tumusiime David, Gasana Juliette, Urimubenshi Gerard, Amaya Nancy, Kingau Naomi, Juma Said Khamis, Khamis Abdulrahman, Mkenda Sarah Harry, Menuka Asteria Lawrence, Grüneberg Christian
resume: The need for rehabilitation in sub-Saharan Africa is largely unmet due to challenges such as limited access to rehabilitation, lack of healthcare professionals, high costs, challenging geographical distance and poor health infrastructure. Home-based Digital Rehabilitation may offer an opportunity to overcome some challenges. However, little is known about successful implementation of home-based Digital Rehabilitation in sub-Saharan Africa. We aimed to identify the technologies used and the important factors considered for the implementation of home-based Digital Rehabilitation. We performed a scoping review according to the framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley, with improvements made by Levac et al. The search strategy was developed on PubMed and translated to Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane, Web of science, IEEE, Science Direct and SpringerLink to identify literature published from 2018 to 2023 conducted in sub-Saharan African countries. We performed a gray literature search to supplement the results. We extracted data on technology and implementation determinants based on the domains of the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research 2.0 (CFIR) and summarized them narratively. In addition, 11 key stakeholders were consulted to explore their experiences with digital technologies and their perspectives on factors relevant to the implementation of home-based Digital Rehabilitation. We included 25 studies in the final set of papers. Technologies such as applications, web-based programs, videoconferencing, short-message-services, television/radio, social media, and 3-D printers are already utilized for rehabilitation in sub-Saharan Africa. Important implementation determinants were identified in three of five CFIR domains, including intervention effectiveness, relative advantages, costs and the design, client acceptability, the use of implementation frameworks, and appropriate implementation strategies. Barriers to and facilitators of implementation were reported across studies, including the need for sufficient technical infrastructure and ongoing technical support to operate the technology. The results of this study highlight the need to develop and implement sustainable Digital Rehabilitation approaches that consider all domains of the CFIR 2.0, including structural characteristics, religious and cultural factors, local conditions, local policies and legislation, and intervention financing. The implementation of home-based Digital Rehabilitation requires systemic adaptations, such as the development of an appropriate technical infrastructure and reimbursement mechanism, as well as increasing (digital) health literacy in society. Not applicable.

titre: Symptom Clusters and Quality of Life Following Breast Cancer Surgery: A Systematic Review.
titre_fr: Symptom Clusters and Quality of Life Following Breast Cancer Surgery: A Systematic Review.
auteurs: Jeyakumar Anita Kiruba, Kim Min Su, Orozco Ricardo, Chandran Shalini, Goldstein Ellen, Doorenbos Ardith Z
resume: Understanding the symptom clusters following surgery is crucial for developing targeted management strategies and improving postoperative outcomes. This systematic review synthesized evidence on the relationship between symptom clusters and quality of life (QOL) among women following breast cancer surgeries. The CINAHL®, Embase®, PubMed®, Scopus®, and PsycINFO® databases were searched for studies published from January 2015 to September 2025. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts for inclusion. The included studies were critically appraised using the appropriate JBI critical appraisal tools based on study design. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) methodology. Although there is low certainty in the evidence, symptom clusters, including breast and arm symptoms, lymphatic stasis, nerve injury, movement limitation, and emotional distress, are associated with reduced QOL for patients undergoing breast cancer surgery. Physical clusters impair mobility and self-care, psychological clusters affect emotional and social functioning, and less studied cognitive clusters influence role functioning and mental well-being. Early identification of symptom clusters may help provide interventions for patients at the highest risk for QOL impairment. Integrating multidimensional symptom assessment into routine care supports personalized rehabilitation and recovery plans.

titre: Rehabilitation Wearable Boots and Offloading Methods for Diabetic Foot Ulcer Treatment: A Systematic Review.
titre_fr: Rehabilitation Wearable Boots and Offloading Methods for Diabetic Foot Ulcer Treatment: A Systematic Review.
auteurs: Sabzehmeidani Yaser, Popa Andrei-Alexandru
resume: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are a serious and common complication of diabetes, primarily affecting the plantar surface and toes. They are associated with high rates of recurrence, amputation and mortality, making effective treatment strategies essential. This review explores the current landscape of offloading methods and rehabilitation wearable boots used in DFU management, with an emphasis on clinical efficacy, patient adherence and the integration of emerging technologies. Total contact casts (TCCs), the gold standard, achieve healing rates exceeding 80%-90% but face limited adoption due to discomfort, stigma, and lifestyle disruption. Meta-analyses indicate that custom orthotics may reduce ulcer recurrence by up to 50% compared with standard footwear, although the magnitude of benefit varies across studies. In contrast, recent advances in smart wearable devices, multimodal sensors, custom orthotics and AI-driven adaptive systems demonstrate potential to enhance patient compliance and therapeutic outcomes. Despite the availability of evidence-based guidelines, a significant gap persists in their consistent application in clinical settings. Bridging this gap requires the development of patient-centric solutions that integrate technological innovation with usability, comfort and accessibility. This review highlights the need and future for innovative approaches that integrate technology and design to support healing, rehabilitation, adherence and quality of life providing pathways for more effective and sustainable DFU management.

titre: Effect of robotic assistance on upper-limb sensorimotor recovery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effect of robotic assistance on upper-limb sensorimotor recovery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Choudhuri Ritwika, Solomon John M, Nehrujee Aravind, Sujatha S, Balasubramanian Sivakumar
resume: Robot-assisted upper-limb neurorehabilitation enables several beneficial therapy components, including repetitive task-specific practice, high training intensity, real-time feedback, gamification, and continuous physical interaction with the patient's limb. However, conventional comparisons of robot-assisted and therapist-delivered rehabilitation cannot determine whether the physical assistance provided by the robot contributes independently to recovery. This systematic review and meta-analysis, therefore, focused specifically on randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of upper-limb rehabilitation in which experimental and comparator interventions were designed to be similar except for the presence, or level, or mode of robotic assistance. PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched through November 2025 for eligible studies. Study screening and filtration were performed using Covidence software. Thirteen studies met the eligibility criteria for qualitative synthesis, and nine studies involving 272 stroke survivors provided Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA) data for quantitative synthesis. The standardized mean difference (SMD) between the control and the experimental group for change in pre-to-post intervention FMA score was calculated to perform meta-analysis. Heterogeneity computation, sensitivity analysis, risk of bias, publication bias, and certainty of evidence evaluation were also performed. The main meta-analysis pooled effect (SMD = 0.425) favored the experimental robot-assisted condition across disease stages, assistance levels, and targeted limb segments. However, this overall effect was imprecise (95% CI: [-0.007, 0.858]) and showed substantial heterogeneity (62.62%). In studies restricted to chronic stroke, the pooled effect was larger (SMD = 0.53), although imprecision [0.067, 0.992] and heterogeneity (60.72%) remained similar. Estimates for shoulder-elbow and hand-focused interventions were small and imprecise too. Sensitivity analyses showed that the direction of the pooled effect was stable across various considerations. The certainty of evidence was judged to be low, primarily because of risk of bias concerns (mainly lack of double-blinding), inconsistency, and imprecision. Exploratory meta-regression did not identify clear study-level moderators of between-study heterogeneity. In addition, no significant publication bias was identified. Although this study provides preliminary evidence suggesting a positive independent influence of the robotic assistance on upper-limb recovery, the limited number of studies with their small sample sizes and substantial heterogeneity preclude a firm conclusion. Larger, adequately powered RCTs that isolate robotic physical assistance while standardizing other intervention components are needed to establish its independent causal contribution to upper-limb sensorimotor recovery.

titre: Adjunctive extracorporeal shock wave therapy after botulinum toxin type A injection for post-stroke spasticity: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Adjunctive extracorporeal shock wave therapy after botulinum toxin type A injection for post-stroke spasticity: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis.
auteurs: Ke Weihao, Wang Lujiang, Shen Wenli, Chen Min, Wang Zhenyu
resume: Post-stroke spasticity is a common rehabilitation problem, and botulinum toxin type A (BTX-A) is a standard focal treatment. Whether extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) provides clinically relevant additional benefit after BTX-A remains uncertain. This systematic review and three-level meta-analysis evaluated the add-on effect of ESWT after BTX-A for post-stroke spasticity, with particular attention to impairment-level and activities-of-daily-living outcomes. Methods: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang Data, VIP, and CBM were searched from inception to March 2026. Randomized controlled trials of BTX-A plus ESWT in adult post-stroke spasticity were included. The primary quantitative synthesis was restricted to BTX-A-based comparators. Hedges' g was pooled with three-level random-effects models to account for dependent effect sizes. Seven randomized controlled trials with 377 participants met the qualitative criteria, and six trials with 242 participants contributed to the primary quantitative synthesis. Adjunctive ESWT was associated with greater reduction in Modified Ashworth Scale scores (g = 0.87, 95% CI 0.41 to 1.34; p < 0.001) and greater improvement in Fugl-Meyer Assessment scores (g = 1.11, 95% CI 0.45 to 1.76; p < 0.001). Activities-of-daily-living estimates favored the combined intervention but did not reach conventional statistical significance (g = 1.15, 95% CI -0.03 to 2.32; p = 0.056). Two participants developed transient erythema after ESWT, but adverse-event reporting was too incomplete for a comparative safety estimate. Adjunctive ESWT may improve short-term impairment-level outcomes after BTX-A, but certainty is limited and evidence for reliable functional independence gains is very uncertain. Modality-, target-, timing-, and dose-specific findings remain exploratory. Identifier INPLASY202630010; https://doi.org/10.37766/inplasy2026.3.0010.

titre: Global trends and thematic evolution in breast cancer and frailty research: a multi-database bibliometric analysis, 1973-2025.
titre_fr: Global trends and thematic evolution in breast cancer and frailty research: a multi-database bibliometric analysis, 1973-2025.
auteurs: Xiang Silu, Han Xu, Wang Xiaoyi
resume: Frailty is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant marker of vulnerability in breast cancer, with implications for treatment tolerance, functional outcomes, and survivorship. This study mapped the global research landscape and thematic evolution of research at the intersection of breast cancer and frailty. Publications were retrieved independently from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC), Scopus, and PubMed from database inception through December 31, 2025; publications from 2026 were excluded. After eligibility screening and three-stage cross-database deduplication, 1,003 records were included. Citation analyses were restricted to 591 eligible WoSCC records. Bibliometric analyses were performed using R 4.5.2 with bibliometrix 5.4.0, VOSviewer, and CiteSpace. Publication output increased over time and reached 115 records in 2025. Segmented Poisson regression estimated annual rate ratios of 1.133 (95% CI, 1.119-1.147) before 2018 and 1.151 (95% CI, 1.105-1.200) after 2018, but the change in slope was not statistically significant (P = 0.465). The United States ranked first in publication output, the Journal of Geriatric Oncology was the most productive journal, and the University of Toronto was the most productive institution. A title/abstract audit of the 1,003-record dataset identified 421 records (41.97%) mentioning both breast cancer and frailty, 83 (8.28%) mentioning breast cancer only, 361 (35.99%) mentioning frailty only, and 138 (13.76%) mentioning neither term category. Keyword and network analyses identified frailty, geriatric assessment, quality of life, comorbidity, treatment, and survivorship as major themes. Breast cancer and frailty research has expanded into an interdisciplinary field spanning oncology, geriatric medicine, supportive care, rehabilitation, and survivorship. The findings should be interpreted in light of the broader indexing contexts represented in the retrieved set.

A title/abstract audit of the 1,003-record dataset identified 421 records (41.97%) mentioning both breast cancer and frailty, 83 (8.28%) mentioning breast cancer only, 361 (35.99%) mentioning frailty only, and 138 (13.76%) mentioning neither term category. Keyword and network analyses identified frailty, geriatric assessment, quality of life, comorbidity, treatment, and survivorship as major themes. Breast cancer and frailty research has expanded into an interdisciplinary field spanning oncology, geriatric medicine, supportive care, rehabilitation, and survivorship. The findings should be interpreted in light of the broader indexing contexts represented in the retrieved set.

titre: Singing-based interventions for motor and non-motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease: a systematic review.
titre_fr: Singing-based interventions for motor and non-motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease: a systematic review.
auteurs: Trinchillo A, Suh J, Marcuzzo E, Vitale C, Li Ttle S, Morgante Francesca, Ricciardi L
resume: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by disabling motor and non-motor symptoms. Although pharmacological and rehabilitation interventions improve many motor and non-motor symptoms, persistent impairments commonly remain in domains, including speech, swallowing, gait, and balance, particularly as the disease progresses. For this reason, over the past few years, alternative rehabilitative approaches, such as singing-based interventions, have been used with the aim of addressing symptoms, such as speech impairment, swallowing difficulties, respiratory dysfunction, and mood. We aim to review the evidences on the efficacy of singing interventions on motor and non-motor symptoms in patients with PD. A comprehensive literature search of PubMed and Google Scholar was conducted for interventional studies published until December 2025. Results were summarized into five symptom domains: motor function, voice quality, breathing, swallowing, and quality of life. Twenty-six studies involving 1057 patients with PD were included. Singing-based interventions were associated with improvements in motor symptoms, gait, posture, voice quality, respiratory control, and maximum phonation time. Several studies also reported enhanced psychological well-being, social connectedness, and quality of life, with reductions in stress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. Evidence regarding swallowing outcomes was limited and inconsistent. Considerable heterogeneity in study design, intervention protocols, and outcome measures precluded meta-analysis. Singing is a promising adjunct therapy for PD rehabilitation, particularly in domains less responsive to pharmacological treatment. Further high-quality research is needed to establish standardized protocols and assess long-term benefits.

titre: The application of brain-computer interface on cognitive function and activities of daily living in stroke patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: The application of brain-computer interface on cognitive function and activities of daily living in stroke patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Luo Zijie, Yu Lei, Wu Meiling, Gong Xuan
resume: Nonmotor dysfunction is a common sequela of stroke, affecting patients across acute, subacute, and chronic recovery stages and significantly impairing their functional independence, psychosocial adjustment, and overall Activities of Daily Living (ADL). Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology has demonstrated effectiveness in motor function rehabilitation. The primary objective of this study was to assess the efficacy of BCI technology on cognitive function (as the primary indicator of nonmotor dysfunction) and ADL in stroke patients through a systematic review and meta-analysis. This review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines and registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261453809). Systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, CNKI, and Wanfang Data up to March 2026. Statistical analyses and the risk of bias were assessed using Review Manager 5.3. The quantitative synthesis focused on the effects of BCI on the cognitive function and ADL of patients with stroke. The meta-analysis reviewed 11 randomized controlled studies (RCTs) involving a total of 559 participants. Compared with conventional rehabilitation, BCI-based training significantly improved cognitive function (SMD = 0.634, 95% CI: 0.214, 1.055; p = 0.003) and ADL (SMD = 1.198, 95% CI: 0.079, 2.316; p = 0.036). Subgroup analyses suggested exploratory patterns of benefit in certain strata. However, subgroup analysis revealed no significant differences for most comparisons (including scale type, region, sample size, stroke type, BCI type, intervention intensity, and intervention duration; all p > 0.05), except for first-episode stroke in the ADL analysis (p = 0.001). BCI-based training shows preliminary promise for improving cognitive function and ADL in stroke patients. Current evidence remains insufficient to recommend BCI for emotion or speech rehabilitation. However, the GRADE certainty of evidence was rated as low for cognitive function and very low for ADL, indicating that further high-quality research is warranted. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, CRD420261453809.

titre: Effects of combined non-invasive brain stimulation and brain-computer interface on upper extremity motor function after stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effects of combined non-invasive brain stimulation and brain-computer interface on upper extremity motor function after stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Qiu Shutao, Zhang Li, Gao Qiang
resume: Non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) and brain-computer interface (BCI) training are both promising approaches for post-stroke upper extremity rehabilitation, and their combination has been hypothesized to produce synergistic effects. However, the efficacy of this combined strategy has not been systematically evaluated. We systematically searched EMBASE, PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from inception to October 2025 for randomized controlled trials evaluating NIBS combined with BCI in stroke rehabilitation. Mean differences (MDs) in pre- to post-intervention change scores and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted to examine potential moderators. Seven randomized controlled trials were included. Pooled analysis showed that NIBS combined with BCI did not provide superior immediate upper extremity motor recovery compared with BCI alone and was associated with lower FMA-UE improvement (MD = -3.67, 95% CI -5.32 to -2.01; I<sup>2</sup> = 0%). Subgroup analysis suggested that this effect was mainly driven by studies of tDCS plus BCI, while no significant difference was observed for rTMS plus BCI. No significant long-term effect of tDCS plus BCI or stimulation-site difference for rTMS plus BCI was identified. However, the certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low, and sensitivity analyses suggested that the findings were unstable. Current evidence does not demonstrate a clear additional benefit of NIBS as an adjunct to BCI for upper extremity rehabilitation after stroke. Given the limited number of studies and the instability of the pooled result in sensitivity analysis, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. More rigorous and adequately powered trials are needed to determine whether optimized stimulation protocols or specific patient subgroups may benefit from this combined strategy. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251151708.

titre: Analgesic efficacy of regional and local analgesic techniques for anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction in adults undergoing general anesthesia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Analgesic efficacy of regional and local analgesic techniques for anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction in adults undergoing general anesthesia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
auteurs: Xu Liaoyuan, Chen Kefan, Yang Chun, Jiang Peng
resume: Acute pain after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) can impair early mobility and rehabilitation. This network meta-analysis (NMA) compared regional and local analgesic techniques in adults undergoing ACLR under general anesthesia. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to February 18, 2026, for randomized controlled trials. Risk of bias was assessed utilizing the revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (RoB2), and a Bayesian random-effects NMA was performed. Thirty-one studies involving 2,470 patients were included. Only six were at low risk of bias. For oral morphine milligram equivalents (OMME) at 24 h postoperatively, femoral nerve block (FNB) [mean difference (MD) = - 30.31, 95% credible interval (CrI) - 58.02, - 6.79] and FNB with sciatic nerve block (SNB) [MD = - 40.42, 95% CrI - 80.42, - 5.79] were associated with lower estimated opioid consumption than control. FNB with SNB ranked highest for lower 24-h OMME [surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) = 87.44%]. FNB with graft donor-site infiltration was associated with lower estimated pain scores in the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) than local infiltration analgesia (MD = - 2.46, 95% CrI: -4.67, - 0.21). At 24 h, adductor canal block (ACB) with graft donor-site infiltration had lower estimated pain scores than ACB (MD = - 1.50, 95% CrI: -2.43, - 0.61). At 48 h, the 95% CrIs for all pain comparisons included 0. ACB with infiltration between the popliteal artery and capsule of the posterior knee (iPACK) had a longer estimated time to first analgesic request (TFAR) than ACB (MD = 7.50, 95% CrI: 1.92, 13.01). Regarding postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), the 95% CrIs for all comparisons included 1. In sensitivity analyses excluding high-risk studies, the CrIs for key comparisons regarding OMME and TFAR widened and included 0. Some treatment nodes were missing from certain outcome networks, and the rankings for PONV changed. Potential analgesic benefits varied across outcomes, but key estimates became less precise after high-risk studies were excluded. Functional outcomes were not systematically synthesized, and adverse event assessment was limited to PONV. These findings do not establish the overall clinical superiority of any single strategy. Not applicable.

titre: Virtual reality-based intervention in forensic mental health services: a feasibility study of implementation, acceptability, and clinical outcomes.
titre_fr: Virtual reality-based intervention in forensic mental health services: a feasibility study of implementation, acceptability, and clinical outcomes.
auteurs: Escuder-Romeva Gemma, Vorstenbosch Ellen, Olivé-Albitzur Aitor-Eneko, Tre-Ortega Verónica, Sanz-Heras Raquel, Luna-Rodríguez Eduardo, Civit-Ramírez Mónica, Brophy-Palma María-Cristina, Pérez-Sánchez Ezequiel-Jesús, Del Prado-Sánchez Noemí, Ribas-Siñol María
resume: This study evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary clinical outcomes of an immersive virtual reality (VR)-based relaxation program implemented as part of routine care in adult and juvenile forensic mental healthcare settings. A feasibility study was conducted in two forensic mental healthcare services: an adult prison-based rehabilitation unit (UHRPI; n = 21) and a juvenile justice treatment unit (UTJJ; n = 8). The 12-week study comprised a four-week pre-intervention phase, a four-week intervention phase including eight VR sessions, and a four-week post-intervention phase. Feasibility, comprising service-user acceptability and professional usability, was the primary outcome. Secondary exploratory outcomes included physiological measures (blood pressure and heart rate), state anxiety (STAI-State), and subjective emotional states assessed immediately before and after each VR session using visual analog scales (VAS). Participant-level behavioral indicators extracted from institutional clinical records were summarized descriptively. Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze repeated physiological and VAS measures, whereas state anxiety was analyzed using paired-samples t-tests. Acceptability and usability were high in both settings, and the intervention was generally well tolerated. In the UHRPI, significant reductions were observed in systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and state anxiety; no significant physiological or anxiety changes were observed in the UTJJ. In both settings, stress and anxiety decreased and relaxation and perceived connection with nature increased immediately following VR sessions, whereas changes in happiness and craving reached significance in only one setting. Participant-level behavioral indicators showed descriptive reductions in several indicators across study phases, with patterns differing between settings. The VR-based relaxation program was feasible, acceptable, and well integrated into routine forensic mental healthcare. The intervention was associated with improvements in immediate emotional responses across both settings and with favorable physiological changes in adults. Descriptive behavioral findings suggest potential benefits that warrant further investigation. Larger controlled studies with predefined clinical and safety outcomes are needed to determine effectiveness, establish causal effects, and evaluate long-term implementation.

titre: Assessment-need mismatch in discharge readiness among young and middle-aged stroke survivors: A mixed-methods study.
titre_fr: Assessment-need mismatch in discharge readiness among young and middle-aged stroke survivors: A mixed-methods study.
auteurs: Li Meng Wen, Zhang Man, Liu Xiao Mei, Zhang Pan Pan, Gao Yu, Liu Hong Mei
revue: International journal of nursing studies advances
resume: Young and middle-aged stroke survivors face distinct challenges when transitioning from hospital to home, particularly regarding disruptions to occupational roles, family responsibilities, and social participation. Examining discharge readiness profiles alongside patients' accounts may help clarify the specific support needs of this younger cohort. This study aimed to identify distinct discharge readiness profiles among young and middle-aged stroke survivors, examine associated factors and explore their anticipated transition needs, and examine how quantitative readiness scores correspond with patients' accounts of preparation for home. A rolling explanatory sequential mixed-methods design. Five neurology wards within a tertiary grade-A hospital in northwestern China. The quantitative phase enrolled 732 stroke survivors, from whom 11 individuals were purposively selected for the qualitative phase. In the quantitative stage, participants aged 18-59 years completed, 24-48 h before scheduled discharge, the Readiness for Hospital Discharge Scale (RHDS), the Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire (BIPQ), and the Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS). Latent profile analysis (LPA) of the three RHDS dimension item means was used to identify distinct patterns of discharge readiness, with multinomial logistic regression analysis examining associated factors. In the qualitative stage, semi-structured interviews were conducted before discharge with 11 purposively selected participants. These narrative data underwent inductive content analysis; Meleis' transition theory guided the interview topics and interpretation. Quantitative and qualitative strands were integrated through a joint display to evaluate how the identified profiles mapped onto reported preparation for home and anticipated care needs. Latent profile analysis yielded four distinct discharge readiness configurations: comprehensive vulnerability (9.84 %), high adaptability-low support (16.39 %), support advantage (20.49 %), and balanced preparation (53.28 %). Survivors in the high adaptability-low support subgroup reported high personal status and adaptation ability but low expected support. Multinomial regression indicated that age, education level, per capita monthly family income, SSRS, and BIPQ were associated with profile membership; the gender test was not significant. Qualitative analysis revealed seven care needs organized into four themes: changes in role identity and psychological support needs, practical self-management support needs, continuing support needs, and socioeconomic needs. Data integration linked readiness profiles to concerns about rehabilitation at home, continuity of care, returning to work, and family responsibilities. Discharge readiness in young and middle-aged stroke survivors is highly heterogeneous. Pairing RHDS dimension profiles with targeted, patient-centered inquiry can clarify life-stage-related concerns and support priorities, informing individualized discharge planning and continuity of care.

titre: Repositioning community-based mental health care for people with psychosocial disabilities: a physical health equity-oriented whole-health recovery framework.
titre_fr: Repositioning community-based mental health care for people with psychosocial disabilities: a physical health equity-oriented whole-health recovery framework.
auteurs: Zhang Yan, Cao Yunhua
resume: Community-based mental health care has expanded identification, treatment, continuity of care, and rehabilitation for people with psychosocial disabilities, yet physical health, functional capacity, and social participation remain insufficiently integrated into routine support. This Perspective proposes a physical health equity-oriented whole-health recovery framework that builds on existing community mental health services. The framework follows a single service logic in which routine contact identifies physical, functional, and participation needs; needs and support assessment considers clinical status, functional limitations, social barriers, preferences, and available resources; and needs-matched support facilitates participation, adaptation, and continued engagement. Its distinctive proposition is that disproportionate loss among people facing greater health or participation barriers should trigger further assessment, adaptation, or support with identifiable service responsibility. Equity is therefore examined across identification, assessment, matching, participation, retention, and benefit. Supported community participation provides one means of translating identified needs into everyday community life, with social prescribing representing one possible implementation mechanism. The proposed sequence is intended as a testable service proposition rather than a validated universal pathway, and its implementation should be examined across different service and policy contexts.

titre: Interactive Gardening Intervention for Preschoolers With Developmental Delays: A Family-Centered Feasibility Study.
titre_fr: Interactive Gardening Intervention for Preschoolers With Developmental Delays: A Family-Centered Feasibility Study.
auteurs: Pan Chieh-Yu, Tsai Yuan-Ching, Hong Jia-Pei, Kuo Fen-Ling
resume: This pilot study examined the feasibility and preliminary effects of an interactive, family-centered gardening intervention on social functioning, sensory integration, and caregiver-related outcomes among preschool children with developmental delays and their caregivers. A nonrandomized controlled pretest-posttest design was conducted in an outpatient rehabilitation setting. Sixty caregiver-child dyads were allocated to an intervention group (n = 30) or a routine-care control group (n = 30). The intervention consisted of 6 weekly 40-minute gardening sessions combined with home-based activities. Outcomes included caregiver stress (Parenting Stress Index-Short Form), parenting efficacy (Parenting Sense of Competence Scale), children's social functioning (Pediatric Evaluation of Disability Inventory-Chinese version), and sensory integration (Child Sensory Integration Scale). Program satisfaction and caregiver feedback were also collected following intervention completion. Social functioning improved within the intervention group (mean change, 3.34 ± 9.47; p = .007), but not in controls (1.72 ± 13.56; p = .269). No significant changes were observed in sensory integration or caregiver-related outcomes, although caregivers reported program satisfaction and perceived improvements in parent-child interaction and child engagement. The findings suggest that a family-centered gardening intervention is feasible, well accepted, and may serve as a complementary approach to support social participation in early childhood rehabilitation.

titre: Exploring internalized stigma among people living with psychosis and their caregivers: Insights from a community rehabilitation initiative in Malawi.
titre_fr: Exploring internalized stigma among people living with psychosis and their caregivers: Insights from a community rehabilitation initiative in Malawi.
auteurs: Buono Mia, Kulisewa Kazione, Pence Brian W, Gaynes Bradley N, Morrison Abigail M, Chienda Joshua, Stockton Melissa A
resume: People living with psychosis (PWLE) experience, anticipate, and internalize stigma. Over time, experienced and anticipated stigma can increase internalized stigma, negatively impacting health. However, predictors and outcomes of internalized stigma among PWLE and their caregivers remain unknown. We explore how stigma changes over time; the associations between hypothesized predictors and internalized stigma; and how internalized stigma influences mental health and functional outcomes. titre: The Responsivity Principle Among Justice-Involved Individuals: Conceptualization Through a Scoping Review.
titre_fr: The Responsivity Principle Among Justice-Involved Individuals: Conceptualization Through a Scoping Review.
auteurs: Wray Kate, de Vogel Vivienne, Stam Jeantine, Clercx Maartje, Keulen-de Vos Marije
revue: International journal of offender therapy and comparative criminology
resume: The responsivity principle has received relatively little attention in the scientific literature, despite being considered an important component of the Risk-Need-Responsivity (RNR) model. This scoping review aimed to synthesize how the responsivity principle has been conceptualized within the literature concerning justice-involved individuals and to identify the responsivity factors most frequently discussed across justice-involved populations. The scoping review was conducted in accordance with the JBI methodology for scoping reviews and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Most papers defined responsivity as adapting interventions to individual characteristics that influence an individual's ability to benefit from treatment. Motivation and cognitive functioning were the most frequently cited responsivity factors. Other factors included demographic characteristics, personality, mental health, socio-economic circumstances, and treatment-related variables, although these were discussed less consistently. Few papers considered practitioner, environmental, or organizational influences on responsivity. Furthermore, limited literature examined responsivity within specific subgroups of justice-involved individuals. The findings also revealed persistent uncertainty regarding the conceptual boundaries of responsivity, the status of proposed responsivity factors, and the position of the responsivity principle within the broader RNR framework. The primary challenge facing the responsivity principle is not the identification of additional factors, but clarification of their conceptual status, boundaries, and role within the treatment process. Further conceptual and empirical research is needed to support the implementation of responsivity among justice-involved individuals.
