titre: Co-development of an educational toolkit to support young adult women following stroke.
titre_fr: Co-development of an educational toolkit to support young adult women following stroke.
auteurs: Ghisi Gabriela L Melo, Ibrahim Sarah, Akingbade Adeyemi, Kocabas Emine, Schneider Nicole, Verven Angela, Pasagic Una, Zhang Jiayu, Vaz David, Sookdeo Vishma, Langlois-Horkey Shannon, Rac Valeria E, Pikula Aleksandra
resume: Young adult women who experience stroke face unique challenges related to parenting, employment, relationships, and emotional recovery, yet tailored educational resources addressing these needs are limited. This project aimed to co-develop, evaluate, and refine a patient-centered educational toolkit to support young adult women in navigating parenting roles, recovery, and long-term well-being following stroke. A multi-phase co-development quality improvement initiative was conducted between May 2024 and March 2026. Phase 1 involved virtual co-design sessions with women with lived experience of stroke (n = 6) to identify priority content areas. Phase 2 comprised development of an initial 90-page educational toolkit informed by lived experience and evidence-based literature. Phase 3 included: (1) readability assessment using the Flesch Reading Ease (FRE) formula and evaluation by healthcare providers (n = 13) using the Suitability Assessment of Materials (SAM) and Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials (PEMAT-P); and (2) focus groups with women post-stroke (n = 25) to refine content and usability. Phase 4 involved patient-partner review and refinement of the toolkit. Five overarching themes informed toolkit development: children's education and support, return to work, navigating healthcare, mental health and emotional well-being, and relationships and social roles. The initial toolkit demonstrated difficult readability (mean FRE=39.2), but superior suitability according to SAM evaluation (79.8%). PEMAT-P scores demonstrated high understandability (88.5%) and actionability (88.9%). Focus group participants emphasized the need for more practical guidance, simplified language, improved visual layout, and expanded women-specific content, including mental health, parenting, reproductive health, and menopause. Iterative revisions resulted in a final 151-page toolkit organized into six thematic modules. Final readability improved substantially (FRE=60.8), indicating standard plain-language readability. A co-developed, patient-centered educational toolkit addressing the multidimensional needs of young adult women following stroke was successfully developed, evaluated, and refined through iterative input from women with lived experience and healthcare providers. This toolkit has potential for integration across stroke care, rehabilitation, and community settings to enhance patient education and support more equitable, person-centered care for young adult women post-stroke.

titre: Living hi: GBMSM narratives of pleasure, risk, and everyday hi-fun (chemsex) navigation in Thailand.
titre_fr: Living hi: GBMSM narratives of pleasure, risk, and everyday hi-fun (chemsex) navigation in Thailand.
auteurs: Waratworawan Worawalan, Samoh Nattharat, Rodger Alison J, Prabowo Harry, Lai Gloria, Phanuphak Nittaya, Srichau Siripong, Ngamee Verapun, Bourne Adam, Guadamuz Thomas E, Witzel T Charles
resume: Hi-fun among gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM) is practiced across Southeast Asia. Yet research remains focused on epidemiological trends and health risks, with limited qualitative work capturing lived experiences, motivations and support needs. These gaps are pronounced in Thailand, where social, legal and cultural structures emphasise control and enforced abstinence over harm reduction and holistic support. This study aims to explore the experiences and perspectives of GBMSM who engage in hi-fun and other types of sexualised drug use, including their strengths and challenges. It seeks to identify the types of support they desire to contribute to the development of harm reduction strategies grounded in the everyday contexts of GBMSM communities in Thailand. This qualitative study drew on five focus group discussions (FGDs) and six in-depth interviews (IDIs) with 30 Thai and non-Thai GBMSM in Bangkok, Khon Kaen and Pattaya. Discussions explored the contexts, experiences, strengths, challenges and support needs related to hi-fun. Thematic analysis was conducted, and findings were reviewed with a community advisory board and partner NGOs. Participants described hi-fun as a distinct world enabling self-expression, pleasure, intimacy and a sense of being valued and accepted beyond what everyday life affords. This world was shaped through equipment preparation, participant screening and unwritten rules promoting trust and safety. Hi-fun offered emotional and social benefits, including connection and belonging. However, participants also reported risks, including mental health challenges, dependence, sexual performance difficulties, violence, non-consensual recording, financial strain and legal consequences. Hi-fun became problematic when individuals lost control, encountered police, were forced into mandatory rehabilitation, experienced health decline or struggled with daily functioning. Participants emphasised the need for sterile equipment, post-use care, accurate information, stigma-free environments and legal reforms aligned with lived realities. Supporting GBMSM engaged in hi-fun in Thailand requires moving beyond abstinence-focused approaches toward flexible harm reduction and structural reforms that uphold dignity, safety and equity.

titre: Exercise physiology and speech pathology support treatment engagement in forensic mental health in community health: evidence from a retrospective cohort study.
titre_fr: Exercise physiology and speech pathology support treatment engagement in forensic mental health in community health: evidence from a retrospective cohort study.
auteurs: Shawyer Frances, Wilson Kate, Dhungana Raja Ram, Atkinson Ben, Hipgrave Lyndsey, Dawadi Shrinkhala, Enticott Joanne, Meadows Graham
resume: Adults completing community-based orders (CBOs) imposed by courts in Victoria, Australia, often present with complex mental health needs and face barriers to treatment engagement. The Forensic Mental Health in Community Health (FMHiCH) program was established to address these challenges through multidisciplinary care within a community health model across multiple sites. At one site, exercise physiology (EP) and speech pathology (SP) were introduced to enhance engagement and support treatment success, however evidence for these interventions in forensic mental health settings is limited. Because the FMHiCH dataset did not contain a direct measure of engagement, this study examined whether EP and/or SP involvement was associated with two behavioural indicators of engagement: treatment completion and treatment goal achievement, and whether greater service dose improved these indicators. A retrospective cohort study analysed de-identified FMHiCH data (December 2018-June 2023) from 1,111 care episodes. Mixed-effect logistic regression was used to examine associations between EP and SP involvement and the two treatment outcomes, adjusting for demographic and socio-economic factors. Dose effects were explored using univariate logistic regression for EP and SP contact time and number of contacts. EP and/or SP involvement was positively associated with both engagement indicators across minimally adjusted (treatment completion: EP OR 5.65 [95% CI 2.41-13.23], SP OR 2.50 [1.18-5.33]; goal achievement: EP OR 6.67 [2.42-18.42], SP OR 4.05 [1.66-9.85]) and fully adjusted models (treatment completion: EP OR 5.68 [2.10-15.37], SP OR 2.44 [0.93-6.36]; goal achievement: EP OR 7.26 [2.32-22.66], SP OR 3.75 [1.38-10.17]). Higher EP and SP contact hours were significantly associated with treatment completion and treatment goal achievement. Demographic factors such as secure housing and employment showed associations with engagement indicators. Integrating EP and SP into community-based forensic mental health care was associated with improved behavioural indicators of engagement - treatment completion and goal achievement. The findings suggest that these allied health interventions may enhance engagement and rehabilitation for adults completing CBOs. Controlled studies, such as stepped-wedge cluster randomised trials, are warranted to confirm these associations, clarify dose effects and further explore the influence of social determinants of health.

titre: Digital Resilience-Based Course-Game Sequential Intervention for Social Participation in Stroke Survivors: Development and Usability Study.
titre_fr: Digital Resilience-Based Course-Game Sequential Intervention for Social Participation in Stroke Survivors: Development and Usability Study.
auteurs: Zhou Xuan, Lv You, Liu Runlin, Gao Wenjun, Zhou Lanshu
resume: Social participation is a key goal of stroke rehabilitation, yet effective interventions remain limited. Existing approaches focus largely on functional training or general psychological support, rarely targeting resilience as a modifiable mechanism for enhancing social participation. Most interventions are delivered face-to-face, limiting accessibility and scalability. A theory-driven digital intervention that integrates resilience training with contextualized practice may offer a promising pathway to support social reintegration in stroke survivors. This study aimed to develop a theory-driven, digital resilience-based course-game sequential intervention for improving social participation in stroke survivors and to evaluate its usability among the target population. This was an intervention development and usability study. Following the first 4 steps of intervention mapping, we completed the following steps: (1) conducted a needs assessment based on prior empirical evidence identifying psychological resilience as a key determinant of social participation; (2) defined performance and change objectives grounded in the Kumpfer resilience framework, which delineates 5 protective factors (cognitive, emotional, spiritual, behavioral, and physical); (3) selected theory-based methods and practical applications; and (4) developed an intervention prototype through 4 phases: initial design integrating course learning and gamified experiential modules, expert review and refinement by an 8-member panel, development of the digital system via a WeChat mini-program, and finalization of comprehensive intervention scripts. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling from a rehabilitation hospital in Shanghai, China. Usability was evaluated with 14 stroke survivors through 5 representative tasks, the System Usability Scale (SUS), and semistructured qualitative interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and qualitative data were analyzed using conventional content analysis. The intervention comprised 2 sequential modules: a 7-session course learning module targeting 5 resilience factors, delivered weekly via narrative audio and multimodal content, and a gamified experiential module featuring a supermarket shopping scenario that enabled contextualized skill application. Each weekly course session was designed to last approximately 60 minutes. The duration of a single game session was 20 minutes. Participants had a mean age of 65.4 (SD 9.75) years, and 78.6% (11/14) had experienced an ischemic stroke. All participants completed the usability tasks successfully. The mean SUS score was 73.6 (SD 12.2, 95% CI 66.5-80.6; median 77.5, IQR 61.3-80.6), indicating good usability. Qualitative feedback revealed 3 themes: perceived ease of use and accessibility, perceived usefulness and engagement, and suggestions for improvement. This study systematically developed a theory-driven, digital course-game sequential intervention that is innovative in targeting psychological resilience as a core mechanism for social participation, distinguishing it from conventional function-focused or generic resilience approaches. By integrating systematic course learning with contextualized gamified practice, it offers a scalable, low-burden tool that addresses key gaps in stroke rehabilitation. These findings support progression to feasibility and efficacy testing through randomized controlled trials in real-world settings.

titre: From virtual practice to real-world function the transfer problem in digital neurorehabilitation.
titre_fr: From virtual practice to real-world function the transfer problem in digital neurorehabilitation.
auteurs: Karadag Mustafa, Ercis Mehmet Bahadır, Alimoradi Mohammad, Karadağ Dilek, Kabal Ceyhun, Karakulak Izzet, Bayansalduz Mehmet, Ceylan Levent, Iranmanesh Mojtaba, Alghosi Mohammad
resume: Digital technologies have expanded opportunities for neurorehabilitation by enabling intensive, interactive, and adaptable motor practice. However, improvements achieved within virtual environments, rehabilitation games, or technology-based assessments do not necessarily translate into meaningful changes in everyday function. This Mini Review examines the transfer problem in digital neurorehabilitation and discusses key factors that may limit the generalization of training-related gains to real-world performance. We synthesize evidence regarding task specificity, sensory and perception-action differences between digital and physical environments, cognitive and contextual demands, practice variability, and patient-specific constraints that influence transfer. Based on these mechanisms, we propose a transfer-oriented framework consisting of five interconnected stages: skill acquisition, adaptive variability, cognitive-motor integration, contextualized real-world practice, and ecological evaluation. This framework emphasizes that transfer should be deliberately targeted rather than assumed as a consequence of successful digital training. We further discuss how virtual reality, augmented reality, wearable sensing, and hybrid rehabilitation models may support different stages of this process when integrated within adaptive and personalized approaches. Future digital rehabilitation research should move beyond evaluating performance within trained tasks and incorporate measures of functional and ecological transfer, including real-world mobility, activity, and participation. A shift from technology-centered rehabilitation toward transfer-oriented design may enhance the clinical impact of digital interventions and support meaningful improvements in daily life.

titre: AI Scribe in Specialized Rehabilitation: Usability Study of Perceived Usability and Usefulness Among Physicians and Psychologists.
titre_fr: AI Scribe in Specialized Rehabilitation: Usability Study of Perceived Usability and Usefulness Among Physicians and Psychologists.
auteurs: Engan Harald Kåre, Landstad Ingeborg, Sand Kari, Evenshaug Ståle, Henjum Halsnes Einar
resume: Clinical documentation in specialized, interdisciplinary rehabilitation is often time-consuming and complex and may contribute to clinician burnout and reduced time for patient interaction. AI-based scribes transcribe and summarize clinical notes and may reduce documentation burden; however, their usefulness and usability in specialized rehabilitation remain uninvestigated. This study aimed to assess the use of an ambient AI scribe tool among physicians and psychologists in specialized rehabilitation, focusing on perceived usefulness, usability, note quality, impact on patient interaction, perceptions of time spent on documentation, and documentation-related fatigue. Over approximately 4 weeks, physicians and psychologists at 9 specialized rehabilitation centers used an ambient AI scribe during clinical consultations. Usability and user experience were assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and a modified technology acceptance model (TAM). Participants rated an AI-generated note using a modified 8-item Physician Documentation Quality Instrument (PDQI-8) questionnaire to evaluate documentation quality. Additional questions explored perceived impact on patient interaction, documentation-related fatigue, and general attitudes toward AI technology. Thirty-one clinicians (18 physicians and 13 psychologists) used the AI scribe over approximately one month and completed evaluation questionnaires. The mean SUS score was 78.3 (SD 10.4), with 86.7% of participants scoring above the usability threshold. Perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) were relatively high (mean PU score 5.65, SD 1.33; mean PEOU score 5.56, SD 1.17), and 87.1% expressed intention to use the AI scribe in future practice. Most participants (80.6%) agreed that using the AI scribe reduced time spent on documentation, while 66.6% reported a reduced perception of documentation-related fatigue. The quality of AI-generated notes was rated relatively high, with a mean modified PDQI-8 score of 4.3 (SD 0.3) out of 5. Comprehensibility received the highest rating (mean 4.6, SD 0.6), whereas thoroughness received the lowest rating (mean 3.9, SD 1.0) among the note quality variables. Overall, 71.0% of participants expressed some level of agreement that the AI scribe enhanced attentiveness during patient consultations, while a similar proportion (70.9%) agreed that it made active listening easier by reducing distractions associated with note-taking. A few participants reported that some notes were incomplete, lacked biopsychosocial details, and contained inaccuracies. This study demonstrated broad acceptance of an AI-based ambient scribe among physicians and psychologists working in specialized rehabilitation. The AI scribe was generally perceived as valuable, easy to use, and clinically relevant. Most participants reported a reduced perceived documentation burden and improved attentiveness during consultations. These findings suggest that clinicians perceived the AI scribe as supporting more focused patient interactions. Some concerns were noted regarding completeness and occasional inaccuracies, highlighting areas for refinement. resume_fr: Clinical documentation in specialized, interdisciplinary rehabilitation is often time-consuming and complex and may contribute to clinician burnout and reduced time for patient interaction. AI-based scribes transcribe and summarize clinical notes and may reduce documentation burden; however, their usefulness and usability in specialized rehabilitation remain uninvestigated. This study aimed to assess the use of an ambient AI scribe tool among physicians and psychologists in specialized rehabilitation, focusing on perceived usefulness, usability, note quality, impact on patient interaction, perceptions of time spent on documentation, and documentation-related fatigue. Over approximately 4 weeks, physicians and psychologists at 9 specialized rehabilitation centers used an ambient AI scribe during clinical consultations. Usability and user experience were assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and a modified technology acceptance model (TAM). Participants rated an AI-generated note using a modified 8-item Physician Documentation Quality Instrument (PDQI-8) questionnaire to evaluate documentation quality. Additional questions explored perceived impact on patient interaction, documentation-related fatigue, and general attitudes toward AI technology. Thirty-one clinicians (18 physicians and 13 psychologists) used the AI scribe over approximately one month and completed evaluation questionnaires. The mean SUS score was 78.3 (SD 10.4), with 86.7% of participants scoring above the usability threshold. Perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) were relatively high (mean PU score 5.65, SD 1.33; mean PEOU score 5.56, SD 1.17), and 87.1% expressed intention to use the AI scribe in future practice. Most participants (80.6%) agreed that using the AI scribe reduced time spent on documentation, while 66.6% reported a reduced perception of documentation-related fatigue. The quality of AI-generated notes was rated relatively high, with a mean modified PDQI-8 score of 4.3 (SD 0.3) out of 5. Comprehensibility received the highest rating (mean 4.6, SD 0.6), whereas thoroughness received the lowest rating (mean 3.9, SD 1.0) among the note quality variables. Overall, 71.0% of participants expressed some level of agreement that the AI scribe enhanced attentiveness during patient consultations, while a similar proportion (70.9%) agreed that it made active listening easier by reducing distractions associated with note-taking. A few participants reported that some notes were incomplete, lacked biopsychosocial details, and contained inaccuracies. This study demonstrated broad acceptance of an AI-based ambient scribe among physicians and psychologists working in specialized rehabilitation. The AI scribe was generally perceived as valuable, easy to use, and clinically relevant. Most participants reported a reduced perceived documentation burden and improved attentiveness during consultations. These findings suggest that clinicians perceived the AI scribe as supporting more focused patient interactions. Some concerns were noted regarding completeness and occasional inaccuracies, highlighting areas for refinement. Future research should explore long-term implementation in routine rehabilitation settings and its effects on workflow, documentation quality, and patient experience.

titre: Comparing the magnitude of change in memory function following telehealth versus in-person delivery of a group memory skills intervention for survivors of stroke.
titre_fr: Comparing the magnitude of change in memory function following telehealth versus in-person delivery of a group memory skills intervention for survivors of stroke.
auteurs: Milligan Daniel Thomas, Wong Dana, McKay Adam, Stolwyk Renerus J
resume: Telehealth could potentially improve memory rehabilitation access post-stroke, but its suitability is underexplored. We aimed to characterize changes in stroke survivors' memory function and memory strategy use after completing a compensatory memory skills group intervention via telehealth, compared to in-person. Our retrospective study drew upon two previous parent studies, and examined change in memory goal attainment, everyday memory failures, and memory strategy use at program completion (T1) and follow-up (T2), relative to baseline. Non-inferiority analyses then compared change among in-person (n = 24) and telehealth (n = 30) participants. Among telehealth participants, repeated-measures ANCOVAs indicated goal attainment at T1 (p < .001, d = 1.08) and T2 (p < .001, d = 1.33), and reduced memory failures by T2 (p = .011, d = -0.58). Internal strategy use increased by T1 (p < .001, d = 0.89) and T2 (p = .003, d = 0.68), but external strategy use did not (pT1 = .079, dT1 = 0.43; pT2 = .319, dT2 = 0.25). While these findings were promising, non-inferiority analyses comparing telehealth and in-person delivery were inconclusive. Further research directly comparing delivery modalities is therefore needed. Offering participants their preferred intervention format in future trials may help further our understanding of how stroke survivors might maximally benefit from memory rehabilitation.

titre: Evaluating the effectiveness of digital and intelligent technology-driven rehabilitation training following radical prostatectomy: A scoping review.
titre_fr: Evaluating the effectiveness of digital and intelligent technology-driven rehabilitation training following radical prostatectomy: A scoping review.
auteurs: Wang Jinyang, Li Yao, Huang Mimi, Cao Xuefeng, Zhang Cuilian
resume: The rapid growth of smart healthcare has integrated digital and intelligent interventions into care models. However, the impact of technology-driven rehabilitation on recovery after radical prostatectomy remains unclear, especially from the perspectives of patients and healthcare providers. This scoping review investigates the effects of these interventions on patients and examines how digital and intelligent technologies are incorporated into rehabilitation plans. A total of eight databases, searched from inception to January 20, 2025. Based on an a-priori protocol the JBI methodology for scoping reviews was used and the review reported against the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews. A total of 43 effective indicators were reported in the 12 included studies, with the number of effective indicators ranging from 1 to 11 in individual studies, with the most frequently occurring outcome indicators being physical activity behavior, degree of incontinence, and quality of life. As advances in digital health continue to evolve, future research should be committed to combining postoperative assessment and rehabilitation training through digital and intelligent means to deepen the understanding of enhanced recovery after surgery in digital health, thereby further improving the ability of nurses to use Digital health technology and services to support care.

titre: The CheckBRAIN™ platform: architecture for post-screening brain health care across the Parkinson's disease continuum.
titre_fr: The CheckBRAIN™ platform: architecture for post-screening brain health care across the Parkinson's disease continuum.
auteurs: Bhidayasiri Roongroj, Sringean Jirada, Anan Chanawat, Phumphid Saisamorn, Laosombut Teerawat, Leabthong Natthaphat, Phokaewvarangkul Onanong, Panyakaew Pattamon, Khongprasert Surasa, Sukmueng Narumol, Dornbunlon Punkorn, Aksornpukdi Sirapatsorn, Jitpugdee Weerachai, Prasertpan Tittaya, Phonsrithong Aekamorn, Boonrach Grisada
resume: Parkinson's disease (PD) screening can identify people needing clinical assessment but does not itself provide continuing care. Drawing on Thailand's smartphone-based CheckPD implementation and selected literature, this conceptual review proposes CheckBRAIN, a platform linking screening to personalised brain-health care. All CheckPD participants would be offered voluntary entry, while clinician-led assessment would proceed without delay when clinically indicated. Concerning screening results, new or progressive symptoms, clinically defined high-risk syndromes, diagnostic uncertainty or medication-related problems would trigger clinical review, while people with established PD could enter directly. A personal brain-health portfolio links multidomain functioning, systemic and environmental context, priorities, actions, responsible persons or services and review dates. The six-domain SHAPES framework supports priority setting without creating another diagnostic score. Actions may include diagnostic assessment, medication review or pharmacotherapy, rehabilitation, cue-linked daily habits, social support, and service-level responses to practical barriers such as transport, digital access, referral navigation or unavailable services. Primary-care teams would coordinate longitudinal review, community workers would support assisted or non-digital participation, and specialists would contribute according to clinical need. Intended benefits include understandable next steps, fewer unresolved referrals, support for everyday function and participation, and clearly defined roles for care partners with the participant's consent. We outline staged co-design and evaluation of feasibility, safety, functioning, participation, caregiver burden, equity, service use and costs. CheckBRAIN is not intended as a population registry and has no fixed national enrolment target. It remains a proposed care architecture, not a validated intervention or evidence of PD prevention or cost saving. Its intended contribution is accountable continuity between identified needs, appropriate care and reviewed outcomes.

titre: Digital rehabilitation interventions for Fibromyalgia: A scoping review.
titre_fr: Digital rehabilitation interventions for Fibromyalgia: A scoping review.
auteurs: Bullón-Benito Elisa, Alcalá-Cerrillo María, Guillén-Rogel Paloma, Huertas-Hoyas Elisabet, Rodríguez-Pérez Ma Pilar, Poveda-García Ana
resume: Fibromyalgia is a chronic condition characterised by widespread pain, fatigue, sleep disturbances, and cognitive-emotional symptoms. Digital health interventions may help improve access to care and support self-management. To map the characteristics, delivery formats, outcomes, and assessment instruments of digital health interventions for adults with fibromyalgia. The review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched in February 2026. Eligible studies evaluated digital interventions in adults (≥18 years) with fibromyalgia. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. A descriptive synthesis was conducted to map intervention characteristics, delivery modes, outcome domains, and assessment instruments. Twenty-nine studies published between 2010 and 2025 were included. Four intervention categories were identified: emotional or behavioural programmes, exercise-based telerehabilitation, self-management or educational interventions, and multicomponent programmes. Interventions were delivered asynchronously (n = 16), synchronously (n = 8), or using hybrid formats (n = 3). The most frequently assessed outcomes were pain, fibromyalgia impact, fatigue, sleep, psychological variables, and physical functioning. Overall, digital interventions were associated with favourable physical and psychosocial outcomes. More consistent benefits were reported for supervised interventions, particularly exercise-based telerehabilitation and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy or Cognitive Behavioural Therapy-based programmes, whereas unguided app-based interventions showed more variable findings. Digital interventions appear to be a promising approach for supporting rehabilitation and symptom management in fibromyalgia. However, substantial heterogeneity in intervention characteristics, delivery modes, outcome measures, and study designs remains. Greater standardisation, longer follow-up periods, and more rigorous studies are needed.

titre: Digital Health Technologies for Mobility Recovery Among Intensive Care Unit Survivors: Scoping Review.
titre_fr: Digital Health Technologies for Mobility Recovery Among Intensive Care Unit Survivors: Scoping Review.
auteurs: Yan Yuhang, Zhu Jiayan, Peng Sining, Qiu Jin, Cheng Linghong, Ge Xiaohua
resume: Mobility recovery after critical illness is a complex and multidimensional process. Digital health technologies have emerged as approaches for delivering rehabilitation, monitoring recovery, and facilitating self-management among intensive care unit (ICU) survivors. However, the extent to which current digital health approaches address the multidimensional nature of mobility recovery remains unclear. This scoping review aimed to map the current evidence on digital health approaches supporting mobility recovery among ICU survivors and to examine the mobility domains, outcomes, feasibility, and acceptability associated with these approaches. A scoping review was conducted following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published from January 2016 to September 21, 2026. Studies involving adult ICU survivors that used digital health approaches to assess, monitor, support, or promote mobility recovery were included. Mobility outcomes were mapped to the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health domains of body functions and structures, activities, and participation. Clinical outcomes were synthesized separately from implementation and user experience outcomes. Twenty-seven reports representing 24 unique parent studies were included. Digital health approaches comprised telemedicine, telerehabilitation, mobile health, wearable monitoring, virtual reality, robot-assisted rehabilitation, and digital recovery platforms. Telemedicine and telerehabilitation were the most frequently reported approaches, and exercise-based rehabilitation was the predominant intervention component. Mobility outcomes were heterogeneous and concentrated on body functions and structures and activity-level performance, particularly muscle strength, exercise capacity, and functional performance, whereas participation outcomes were less frequently represented. Controlled and comparative studies showed mixed between-group findings, with clinical benefits not consistently demonstrated across primary or mobility-related outcomes. In contrast, feasibility, adherence, usability, and acceptability were generally favorable when assessed, although technical difficulties and incomplete device-generated data were reported in some studies. Digital health technologies offer diverse approaches to supporting mobility recovery after critical illness, but current evidence remains concentrated on physical function and activity-level outcomes, with limited attention to participation and long-term recovery. More rigorous and longitudinal studies using standardized, multidimensional mobility outcomes are needed to clarify clinical effectiveness and support sustainable implementation.

titre: Digital endpoints as outcome measures in orthopaedic care and their psychometric properties: a scoping review protocol.
titre_fr: Digital endpoints as outcome measures in orthopaedic care and their psychometric properties: a scoping review protocol.
auteurs: Fakak Reem, Aslam Sultan, Davies Benjamin, Hadi Saif, Gharooni Ali
resume: Digital health technologies, including wearable sensors, smartphone-based assessments and vision-based systems, are increasingly used to generate objective outcome measures in orthopaedic care. These digital endpoints have the potential to complement traditional patient-reported outcome measures by providing continuous, objective assessments of functional recovery in real-world settings. However, the extent to which these endpoints have undergone psychometric validation remains unclear, and existing reviews are limited to specific conditions or technologies. This scoping review aims to systematically map the range of digital endpoints used in orthopaedic care and synthesise the available evidence regarding their psychometric properties This scoping review will be conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology for scoping reviews and reported following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). MEDLINE (Ovid), Embase, CINAHL, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library will be searched for studies published from January 2005 to December 2025. Searches are expected to be completed in February 2026. Eligible studies will include paediatric and adult populations with orthopaedic conditions evaluating at least one psychometric property of a digital endpoint, including validity, reliability, responsiveness or interpretability. Two reviews will independently perform study selection and data extraction using a Consensus-based Standards for the selection of health Measurement Instruments (COSMIN)-informed extraction tool, with disagreements resolved through discussion or a third reviewer. Extracted data will be synthesised descriptively and presented using tables, figures and narrative summaries to map the current evidence base and identify research gaps. The review is planned to commence in February 2026 and conclude in September 2026. Ethics approval is not required because this review will synthesise data from published literature without involving human participants. Findings will be disseminated through publication in a peer-reviewed journal and presentation at relevant scientific meetings. Open Science Framework: https://osf.io/n4ctu

titre: Comparative Effects of Neurostimulation- and Technology-Augmented Robot-Assisted Training on Upper-Limb Motor Recovery After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
titre_fr: Comparative Effects of Neurostimulation- and Technology-Augmented Robot-Assisted Training on Upper-Limb Motor Recovery After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
auteurs: Wang Lin, Zhu Zhitao, Liu Yue, Qu Junjie, Li Ning, Liu Haitao, Cao Lei, Ma Zhenjiang, Wu Hao, Wang Jinwu
revue: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
resume: To compare robot-assisted training (RAT) alone with neurostimulation- or technology-augmented RAT for poststroke upper-limb recovery. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang were searched through August 1, 2026. Randomized trials evaluated RAT alone or RAT combined with virtual reality, a brain-computer interface, low-frequency electrical stimulation (LFES), transcranial direct current stimulation, or repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS). Two reviewers independently selected studies and extracted data; risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed with Cochrane and GRADE methods. Of 103 trials (5,251 participants), 84 (4,277 participants) entered restricted Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) Model E. Compared with usual care (UC), mean differences (MDs) were 9.56 points (95% CI, 7.18-11.93) for rTMS plus RAT, 7.52 (95% CI, 4.48-10.57) for LFES plus RAT, and 3.83 (95% CI, 2.69-4.97) for RAT alone. Heterogeneity was substantial (τ=2.79); global inconsistency was not detected (χ²(9)=3.64; P=.934). rTMS plus RAT ranked first (SUCRA, 96.2%), but its probability of being best decreased from 77.8% to 56.0% after predictive uncertainty was incorporated. Signals for stroke stage (P=.030) and total duration (P=.040) did not meet the multiplicity-adjusted threshold (P<.01). rTMS plus RAT yielded the largest FMA-UE estimate, followed by LFES plus RAT. Sparse head-to-head evidence, heterogeneity, and very low-to-moderate certainty preclude a definitive hierarchy and warrant comparative trials.

titre: Early-Stage Co-Creation and Human-Centered Development of Digital Therapeutics for Cognitive Rehabilitation in Early Neurocognitive Disorders: Convergent Mixed Methods Study.
titre_fr: Early-Stage Co-Creation and Human-Centered Development of Digital Therapeutics for Cognitive Rehabilitation in Early Neurocognitive Disorders: Convergent Mixed Methods Study.
auteurs: Rossetto Federica, Borgnis Francesca, Mangione Chiara, Serenelli Claudia, Isernia Sara, Baglio Francesca
resume: Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) represent critical windows for early neurocognitive intervention, although access to timely, personalized rehabilitation remains limited. Digital health technologies offer opportunities to deliver scalable and individualized cognitive care; however, their successful implementation depends on an understanding of users' needs, expectations, and barriers. Within a human-centered design (HCD) framework, actively involving end users during the earliest stages of development is essential to ensure that digital rehabilitation is acceptable, usable, and responsive to real-world rehabilitation needs. This study explores the experiences, rehabilitation needs, perceptions, and challenges of individuals with SCD and MCI regarding cognitive telerehabilitation. The findings are intended to inform the early-stage co-creation and human-centered development of digital rehabilitation solutions. The study is framed within an HCD perspective to inform the user-centered development of digital rehabilitation solutions. A convergent mixed methods design was adopted to integrate quantitative assessments with qualitative interviews. The semistructured interview explored 4 thematic domains: neurocognitive abilities, network support, user experience and engagement, and digital divide. Twenty-three individuals with SCD or MCI completed the interview together with measures including the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Cognitive Failures Questionnaire (CFQ), and an ad hoc Technological Expertise questionnaire. Qualitative interview data were analyzed using directed content analysis based on 4 predefined thematic domains by 2 independent raters, with interrater agreement assessed using Cohen κ. Qualitative and quantitative findings were subsequently integrated through exploratory Mann-Whitney U tests. Twenty-three participants (n=16 female participants; mean age 74.3, SD 7.35 y) were included. Participants reported preserved cognitive performance (MoCA: mean 24.9, SD 3.23), low-to-moderate perceived cognitive difficulties (CFQ: mean 22.4, SD 9.48), and moderate technological familiarity. Qualitative findings revealed memory (n=12, 52.2%), attention/executive (n=6, 26.1%), and language (n=4, 17.4%) difficulties during everyday activities, together with widespread use of compensatory strategies. Participants also described emotional vulnerability, social withdrawal, and feelings of misunderstanding, as well as delayed rehabilitation access despite reporting cognitive concerns to health care professionals. Although most participants had limited prior knowledge of telerehabilitation, they expressed a positive attitude toward home-based rehabilitation, valuing its convenience, flexibility, autonomy, and accessibility when appropriate technological and clinical support was available. Concerns mainly related to limited supervision, technical barriers, and digital literacy. Mixed methods integration showed that perceived technology-related barriers were associated with lower technological competence (median 1.88, IQR 1.69-2.56 vs median 3.06, IQR 2.75-3.59; P=.002), while no other significant differences emerged. These findings highlight that effective digital rehabilitation should be developed through iterative, user-informed HCD processes that simultaneously address cognitive, emotional, social, and technological dimensions of early neurocognitive decline. Integrated findings highlight the importance of addressing individual needs and incorporating users' perspectives from the earliest design phases to support usable, engaging, and accessible digital rehabilitation solutions.

The semistructured interview explored 4 thematic domains: neurocognitive abilities, network support, user experience and engagement, and digital divide. Twenty-three individuals with SCD or MCI completed the interview together with measures including the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Cognitive Failures Questionnaire (CFQ), and an ad hoc Technological Expertise questionnaire. Qualitative interview data were analyzed using directed content analysis based on 4 predefined thematic domains by 2 independent raters, with interrater agreement assessed using Cohen κ. Qualitative and quantitative findings were subsequently integrated through exploratory Mann-Whitney U tests. Twenty-three participants (n=16 female participants; mean age 74.3, SD 7.35 y) were included. Participants reported preserved cognitive performance (MoCA: mean 24.9, SD 3.23), low-to-moderate perceived cognitive difficulties (CFQ: mean 22.4, SD 9.48), and moderate technological familiarity. Qualitative findings revealed memory (n=12, 52.2%), attention/executive (n=6, 26.1%), and language (n=4, 17.4%) difficulties during everyday activities, together with widespread use of compensatory strategies. Participants also described emotional vulnerability, social withdrawal, and feelings of misunderstanding, as well as delayed rehabilitation access despite reporting cognitive concerns to health care professionals. Although most participants had limited prior knowledge of telerehabilitation, they expressed a positive attitude toward home-based rehabilitation, valuing its convenience, flexibility, autonomy, and accessibility when appropriate technological and clinical support was available. Concerns mainly related to limited supervision, technical barriers, and digital literacy. Mixed methods integration showed that perceived technology-related barriers were associated with lower technological competence (median 1.88, IQR 1.69-2.56 vs median 3.06, IQR 2.75-3.59; P=.002), while no other significant differences emerged. These findings highlight that effective digital rehabilitation should be developed through iterative, user-informed HCD processes that simultaneously address cognitive, emotional, social, and technological dimensions of early neurocognitive decline. Integrated findings highlight the importance of addressing individual needs and incorporating users' perspectives from the earliest design phases to support usable, engaging, and accessible digital rehabilitation solutions.

titre: Effectiveness of Non-immersive Virtual Reality-assisted Tilt Table Therapy on Vertical Orientation and Functional Outcomes in Patients Following Decompressive Craniectomy: A Pilot Feasibility Case Series.
titre_fr: Effectiveness of Non-immersive Virtual Reality-assisted Tilt Table Therapy on Vertical Orientation and Functional Outcomes in Patients Following Decompressive Craniectomy: A Pilot Feasibility Case Series.
auteurs: Bhoopathy Aravindh, Palanivel Om Prakash, Srinivasan Vignesh, Sharma Simran, Thirumalai Jeevarathinam
resume: Patients recovering from decompressive craniectomy commonly experience prolonged immobilisation, orthostatic intolerance and delayed functional recovery, which significantly limit early rehabilitation. Effective strategies to improve vertical tolerance and cardiovascular stability are critical in this population. The objective of this study was to evaluate the feasibility, safety and preliminary clinical outcomes of non-immersive virtual reality (VR)-assisted tilt table therapy in patients following decompressive craniectomy. This pilot feasibility case series included five adults recovering from decompressive craniectomy. Participants underwent 10 sessions of combined non-immersive VR and tilt table therapy over 2 weeks, alongside standard rehabilitation. Primary outcomes included maximum tolerated tilt angle, heart rate variability, blood pressure variability and orthostatic intolerance episodes. Secondary outcomes included functional independence measured (FIM) using the FIM and Modified Barthel Index (MBI). Outcomes were assessed at baseline and post-intervention. All participants completed the intervention with 100% adherence and no serious adverse events. The mean maximum tolerated tilt angle improved from 30.0° ± 4.1° to 65.0° ± 4.1°. Reductions were observed in heart rate variability, systolic and diastolic blood pressure variability and orthostatic intolerance episodes (60%-87%). Functional outcomes showed improvement, with FIM scores increasing by 30.0 ± 3.2 points and MBI scores by 54.2 ± 4.0 points. Non-immersive VR-assisted tilt table therapy appears feasible and safe in patients following decompressive craniectomy, with observed improvements in vertical tolerance, cardiovascular stability and functional independence. These findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger controlled trials.

titre: Virtual Reality Sickness and Safety During Use of a Purpose-Built Seated Virtual Reality System in Clinical Rehabilitation: Retrospective Single-Arm Cohort Study.
titre_fr: Virtual Reality Sickness and Safety During Use of a Purpose-Built Seated Virtual Reality System in Clinical Rehabilitation: Retrospective Single-Arm Cohort Study.
auteurs: Dobelbower Jaylen, Saadi Bilal, Galvan Ashley, Zhou Kevin, Fathima Zarqa, Pathare Dhroov, Murakawa Yuichiro, Tamaki Masatake, Hara Masahiko
resume: Virtual reality (VR) sickness is a recognized barrier to the clinical adoption of immersive rehabilitation. Evidence on the tolerability of purpose-built clinical VR systems used at scale remains limited. This real-world feasibility and safety study aimed to describe the frequency of recorded VR sickness in a primary cohort using a purpose-built, seated VR rehabilitation system (mediVR KAGURA®) integrating seven multisensory engineering principles, and to characterize serious adverse events in a secondary post-marketing surveillance (PMS) cohort, without assessing the causal effects of individual features. We conducted a single-arm, retrospective observational cohort study (no comparison group) of two cohorts, following the Journal Article Reporting Standards for quantitative research. The primary cohort comprised all 3572 unique users (patients and general public, aged 3-100 years) identified from company records and server logs between November 2023 and June 2025 at our rehabilitation centers (n=578), institutional demonstrations (n=1715), and academic exhibitions (n=1279); typical exposure was 20-60 minutes at our rehabilitation centers and 5-10 minutes elsewhere. Its primary endpoint was VR sickness (user-reported nausea, dizziness, or malaise during or immediately after a session); secondary endpoints were adverse events such as falls or injuries. The secondary PMS cohort comprised all 337,577 therapeutic sessions (approximately 9306 patients) at 170 medical institutions from 2019 to 2025; its endpoints were serious adverse events and VR sickness requiring medical intervention. Sex and diagnoses were not available. All eligible records were analyzed without exclusions, and no outcome data were missing. Analyses were descriptive (95% confidence intervals [CI] by Wilson score and exact binomial methods); no hypothesis tests were performed. In the primary cohort, 13 of 3572 users (0.36%, 95% CI 0.21%-0.62%) had recorded VR sickness, mostly mild and transient, and 1 user (0.03%, 95% CI 0.005%-0.16%) discontinued a session early. No user required medical intervention, and no falls or injuries were recorded. In the PMS cohort, no serious adverse events or VR sickness requiring medical intervention were reported across 337,577 sessions (exact 95% CI 0%-0.0011%), although mild unreported symptoms cannot be excluded. In this real-world dataset, recorded VR sickness was uncommon and mostly mild with a purpose-built seated VR rehabilitation system, and no serious adverse events or medically attended VR sickness were reported in PMS. Whereas earlier work mainly tested individual design features under controlled conditions, this study documents an integrated multisensory design at scale in routine practice. Because it was uncontrolled and applied all features together, it cannot establish causality, attribute effects to individual features, or support comparison with other systems; the findings are proof-of-concept evidence. They suggest that seated, visually stable, and predictable designs can be deployed safely at scale in clinical rehabilitation and motivate prospective controlled studies with standardized symptom measures. UMIN Clinical Trials Registry UMIN000056624.

titre: Pain in rare disorders.
titre_fr: Pain in rare disorders.
auteurs: Gazerani Parisa
resume: Rare disorders collectively affect more than 300 million people worldwide and often require lifelong multidisciplinary care. Although pain is not universal, it is a clinically important and frequently underrecognized manifestation in many rare disorders, contributing to impaired functioning, psychological distress, reduced participation and quality of life, and caregiver burden. Assessment and management are complicated by heterogeneous pain mechanisms, limited disease-specific evidence, fragmented care pathways, and a lack of standardized guidance. This Perspective proposes a clinically oriented framework for understanding and managing pain in rare disorders. Rather than reviewing individual diseases, it highlights the diversity and evolution of nociceptive, neuropathic, inflammatory, ischemic, nociplastic, and mixed pain mechanisms and the need for repeated, multidimensional, mechanism-informed assessment. Individualized management should integrate appropriate pharmacological and disease-modifying treatments with rehabilitation, psychological support, education, self-management, and multidisciplinary care. Digital health technologies may support longitudinal monitoring and access to specialist expertise, although their use requires appropriate validation and integration with clinical services. Literature was identified through searches in Oria, Oslo Metropolitan University's library discovery service, with no lower date restriction and including publications available up to June 2026.

titre: Understanding Changes of Emotion and Cognitive Effort in VR.
titre_fr: Understanding Changes of Emotion and Cognitive Effort in VR.
auteurs: Otono Riku, Moore John, Chen Jingruo, Karai Zane, Gupta Kunal, Murphy Peta, Nunnerley Jo, Billinghurst Mark
revue: IEEE transactions on visualization and computer graphics
resume: Understanding how cognitive and emotional states evolve during everyday activities is important for designing effective virtual reality (VR) systems for training and rehabilitation, such as for recovering from traumatic brain injury (TBI). However, less is known about how these internal states fluctuate during naturalistic VR tasks. In this work, we investigate cognitive and emotional state dynamics during a VR shopping activity designed for TBI rehabilitation. Twenty healthy participants performed budgeting, item selection, and decision-making tasks while interacting with a virtual coach in either a low-stimulus (quiet) or high-stimulus (busy) environment. During the task, participants reported on momentary mental workload while physiological signals were continuously recorded. After the session, participants retrospectively annotated perceived cognitive and emotional state changes over time. Our results showed higher perceived workload and physiological arousal in the busy environment, with galvanic skin response activity positively correlated with reported cognitive workload. We describe the implications of the research, its limitations, and directions for future work.

titre: Apprendre à gérer ses émotions, à faire des choix, à vivre ensemble… : l’ARS La Réunion accélère la mobilisation pour renforcer les compétences psychosociales des enfants et des jeunes
resume: Colère, stress, pression du groupe, conflits, manque de confiance en soi, capacité de dire non… Autant de situations auxquelles les enfants et les adolescents sont confrontés. Et si on pouvait leur apprendre à mieux y faire face et à devenir des citoyens éclairés et responsables ? C'est tout l'enjeu des compétences psychosociales (CPS), qui contribuent au bien-être, à la santé mentale et à la prévention des comportements à risque. À La Réunion, l’ARS et le rectorat, avec leurs partenaires (Promotion Santé Réunion et Santé publique France), souhaitent accélérer leur développement chez les enfants et les jeunes de 3 à 26 ans et donner à chacun des ressources utiles pour faire face aux défis du quotidien et préserver leur santé. Cette mobilisation a été notamment mise en lumière à l’occasion des rencontres régionales sur les CPS organisées du 27 octobre au 3 novembre 2026, en présence de Béatrice Lamboy et Dominique Jeannel, expertes de Santé publique France et de nombreux acteurs institutionnels et associatifs.

titre: Exploring Australian child and youth mental health occupational therapists' perception and utilisation of creative activities: A survey snapshot.
titre_fr: Étude de la perception et de l'utilisation des activités créatives par les ergothérapeutes australiens spécialisés dans la santé mentale des enfants et des jeunes : un aperçu de l'enquête.
auteurs: Forbes Hannah, Lo Adam, Steele Michael, Harrington Rosamund
revue: The British journal of occupational therapy
resume: Creative activities have traditionally been an important therapeutic medium in occupational therapy; however, research suggests a decline in their perceived efficacy, utilisation, and teaching. This study explored Australian child and youth mental health (CYMH) occupational therapists' perceptions and use of creative activities. A 31-item web-based survey, comprising quantitative and qualitative questions, was disseminated via convenience sampling to collect data from Australian CYMH occupational therapists. Descriptive statistics and non-parametric Mann-Whitney U tests were used for quantitative data, with inductive content analysis used for qualitative data. Analysis of 33 completed surveys revealed creative activities were perceived as a highly efficacious therapeutic medium (78%), utilised most frequently multiple times a week (66%). All respondents utilised creative activities, although 64% were not content with their current use. Although 67% rated confidence using creative activities highly, 97% identified additional training needs to feel more confident. Three main categories central to use of creative activities arose: 'creative activities as a therapeutic medium', 'legitimacy of creative activities within occupational therapy' and 'initial and ongoing professional development'. Australian CYMH occupational therapists perceived and utilised creative activities positively. Lack of discipline-specific evidence and unmet training needs impacted confidence in their use.
resume_fr: Les activités créatives ont traditionnellement constitué un moyen thérapeutique important en ergothérapie ; cependant, les recherches suggèrent une baisse de leur efficacité perçue, de leur utilisation et de leur enseignement. Cette étude a exploré les perceptions et l'utilisation des activités créatives par les ergothérapeutes australiens spécialisés dans la santé mentale des enfants et des adolescents (CYMH). Une enquête en ligne comportant 31 questions, comprenant des questions quantitatives et qualitatives, a été diffusée par échantillonnage de convenance.g pour collecter des données auprès d'ergothérapeutes australiens travaillant dans le domaine de la santé mentale des enfants et des jeunes (CYMH). Des statistiques descriptives et des tests U de Mann-Whitney non paramétriques ont été utilisés pour les données quantitatives, et une analyse de contenu inductive a été utilisée pour les données qualitatives. L'analyse de 33 questionnaires remplis a révélé que les activités créatives étaient perçues comme un moyen thérapeutique très efficace (78 %), utilisé le plus souvent plusieurs fois par semaine (66 %). Tous les répondants ont eu recours à des activités créatives, bien queCependant, 64 % n'étaient pas satisfaits de leur utilisation actuelle. Bien que 67 % des répondants aient estimé avoir un niveau élevé de confiance dans l'utilisation des activités créatives, 97 % ont identifié des besoins de formation supplémentaires pour se sentir plus confiants. Trois grandes catégories centrales pour l'utilisation des activités créatives ont émergé : « les activités créatives comme moyen thérapeutique », « la légitimité des activités créatives dans l'ergothérapie » et « le développement professionnel initial et continu ». Ergothérapeutes australiens spécialisés dans la santé mentale des enfants et des adolescents pont perçu et utilisé les activités créatives de manière positive. Le manque de données probantes spécifiques à la discipline et les besoins de formation non satisfaits ont eu un impact sur la confiance dans leur utilisation.

titre: The effectiveness of activities of daily living retraining programmes for older adults in hospital: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: L'efficacité des programmes de rééducation aux activités de la vie quotidienne pour les personnes âgées à l'hôpital : une revue systématique et une méta-analyse.
auteurs: Leong Clara, Donaldson Amy, Macasieb Celine Faye Espanol, Johnson Jessica, Lee Shuk Man, Clarke Laura, Harper Kristie
revue: The British journal of occupational therapy
resume: Older adults in hospital experience functional decline that affects their independence, quality of life (QoL) and health outcomes. This study aimed to examine the effectiveness of occupational therapy activities of daily living (ADL) retraining programmes on functional status, length of stay (LOS), self-efficacy and QoL in hospitalised older adults. A systematic review was conducted with three databases searched. Studies included older adults aged 65 years or above, in hospital where ADL retraining was explored. Meta-analyses of relevant studies were conducted with the random effect model at 95% confidence interval. Seven studies were included. ADL retraining programmes were delivered in either an individual (n = 7) or group format (n = 3). Intervention protocols and intensity varied across studies. Meta-analysis included four studies, which showed statistically significant improvement in functional status (effect size (ES) = 0.75, p = 0.03), but were insignificant for LOS (ES = -0.03, p = 0.84), self-efficacy (ES = -0.34, p = 0.08) and QoL (ES = 0.04, p = 0.71). ADL retraining in hospital had significantly large effects on functional outcomes, with no significant effects on LOS, self-efficacy and QoL. Further rigorous, large-scale research is needed to explore the impact of ADL retraining on rehabilitation outcomes.
resume_fr: Les personnes âgées hospitalisées subissent un déclin fonctionnel qui affecte leur indépendance, leur qualité de vie (QdV) et leurs résultats en matière de santé. Cette étude visait à examiner l'efficacité des programmes de rééducation en ergothérapie axés sur les activités de la vie quotidienne (AVQ) sur l'état fonctionnel, la durée de séjour (DdS), l'auto-efficacité et la qualité de vie (QdV) des personnes âgées hospitalisées. Une revue systématique a été réalisée à partir de trois bases de données. Les études portaient sur des personnes âgées ded 65 ans ou plus, à l'hôpital où le réapprentissage des AVQ a été étudié. Des méta-analyses des études pertinentes ont été réalisées avec le modèle à effets aléatoires à un intervalle de confiance de 95 %. Sept études ont été incluses. Les programmes de rééducation aux AVQ ont été dispensés soit de manière individuelle (n = 7), soit en groupe (n = 3). Les protocoles d'intervention et leur intensité variaient d'une étude à l'autre. La méta-analyse comprenait quatre études, qui ont montré des résultats statistiquement significatifsl'amélioration de l'état fonctionnel (taille de l'effet (TE) = 0,75, p = 0,03), mais étaient non significatifs pour la durée d'hospitalisation (TE = -0,03, p = 0,84), l'auto-efficacité (TE = -0,34, p = 0,08) et la qualité de vie (TE = 0,04, p = 0,71). Le réapprentissage des AVQ à l'hôpital a eu des effets significativement importants sur les résultats fonctionnels, sans effets significatifs sur la durée d'hospitalisation, l'auto-efficacité et la qualité de vie. D'autres recherches rigoureuses et à grande échelle sont nécessaires pour étudier l'impact du réapprentissage des AVQ.en fonction des résultats de la rééducation.

titre: Exploring occupational therapists' perspectives on the clinical utility of the Assessment of Client's Enablement (ACE): A qualitative study.
titre_fr: Étude des points de vue des ergothérapeutes sur l'utilité clinique de l'Évaluation de l'autonomisation du client (ACE) : une étude qualitative.
auteurs: Sawada Tatsunori, Sato Manae, Wakugawa Mikako, Ohno Kanta, Tomori Kounosuke
revue: The British journal of occupational therapy
resume: The Assessment of Client's Enablement (ACE) was developed to help occupational therapists address perceived differences with clients. However, its clinical utility in promoting collaboration has not been empirically studied. This qualitative descriptive study involved semi-structured interviews with experienced occupational therapists who had used ACE in clinical practice. Transcribed data were analysed using the Steps for Coding and Theorization (SCAT) method. Seven occupational therapists participated. ACE was perceived to facilitate mutual understanding and dialogue by making differences in perceptions of therapists and clients more visible. Three central themes were identified: (1) clinical characteristics and uses of ACE, including ease of integration into practice, provision of visual feedback and use as a complementary tool; (2) observed changes in both clients and therapists, including increased client insight, more active engagement and enhanced professional reflection; and (3) the promotion of collaborative processes, such as shared goal setting, improved communication and trust building. Participants emphasised the importance of appropriate timing and sensitivity to client characteristics to ensure ACE was used effectively and ethically. This study provides preliminary insight into how ACE may support collaboration in occupational therapy.
resume_fr: L'Évaluation de l'autonomisation du client (ACE, pour Assessment of Client's Enablement) a été élaborée pour aider les ergothérapeutes à gérer les différences perçues avec les clients. Cependant, son utilité clinique pour favoriser la collaboration n'a pas fait l'objet d'une étude empirique. Cette étude descriptive qualitative a consisté en des entretiens semi-structurés avec des ergothérapeutes expérimentés ayant utilisé l'ACE dans leur pratique clinique. Les données transcrites ont été analysées à l'aide des étapes de codage et de théorisation(SCAT). Sept ergothérapeutes ont participé. L'ACE a été perçu comme facilitant la compréhension mutuelle et le dialogue en rendant plus visibles les différences de perception entre les thérapeutes et les clients. Trois thèmes centraux ont été identifiés : (1) les caractéristiques cliniques et les utilisations de l'ACE, notamment la facilité d'intégration dans la pratique, la fourniture d'un retour visuel et l'utilisation en tant qu'outil complémentaire ; (2) les changements observés tant chez les clients que chez les thérapeutes, notammentnotamment une meilleure compréhension des clients, un engagement plus actif et une réflexion professionnelle renforcée ; et (3) la promotion de processus collaboratifs, tels que la définition d'objectifs communs, l'amélioration de la communication et le renforcement de la confiance. Les participants ont souligné l'importance d'un timing approprié et d'une sensibilité aux caractéristiques des clients pour garantir une utilisation efficace et éthique de l'ACE. Cette étude fournit un aperçu préliminaire de la manière dont l'ACE peut favoriser la collaboration dansergothérapie

titre: Comparison of occupational balance in high school students with different nomophobia levels: A cross-sectional study.
titre_fr: Comparaison de l'équilibre professionnel chez des lycéens présentant différents niveaux de nomophobie : une étude transversale.
auteurs: Tekeci Yasin, Ersoy Temiz Kübra, Pekçetin Serkan
revue: The British journal of occupational therapy
resume: The study investigates the relationship between nomophobia and occupational balance among high school students. Nomophobia, or the fear of being without a mobile phone, is increasingly prevalent among adolescents, potentially impacting their daily routines and well-being. This study aimed to examine the relationship between nomophobia levels and occupational balance among high school students. Sociodemographic data were obtained with a sociodemographic form. The Adolescent Occupational Balance Scale was used to measure occupational balance. The Nomophobia Questionnaire was used to determine nomophobia levels. A total of 258 students participated in the study. Findings reveal that as nomophobia levels increase, students' ability to manage time and participate in various activities significantly decreases. This study found that students with severe nomophobia showed lower scores in occupational diversity and harmony, indicating that excessive reliance on digital platforms may reduce participation in social and academic activities. The study suggests that high levels of nomophobia may limit individuals' ability to engage in a variety of meaningful activities, thereby disrupting their occupational balance. Considering occupational balance in future research and intervention strategies is crucial for promoting healthier technology use and improving the overall well-being of high school students. Clinical trial number: not applicable.
resume_fr: L'étude examine la relation entre la nomophobie et l'équilibre occupationnel chez les lycéens. La nomophobie, ou la peur d'être sans téléphone portable, est de plus en plus répandue chez les adolescents, ce qui peut avoir un impact sur leur quotidien et leur bien-être. Cette étude visait à examiner la relation entre les niveaux de nomophobie et l'équilibre occupationnel chez les lycéens. Les données sociodémographiques ont été obtenues à l'aide d'un questionnaire sociodémographique.graphique. L'échelle d'équilibre occupationnel des adolescents a été utilisée pour mesurer l'équilibre occupationnel. Le questionnaire sur la nomophobie a été utilisé pour déterminer les niveaux de nomophobie. Au total, 258 étudiants ont participé à l'étude. Les résultats révèlent qu'à mesure que les niveaux de nomophobie augmentent, la capacité des élèves à gérer leur temps et à participer à diverses activités diminue considérablement. Cette étude a révélé que les élèves souffrant de nomophobie sévère obtenaient des scores plus faibles en matière d'équilibre occupationnel.la diversité et l'harmonie relationnelles, ce qui indique qu'une dépendance excessive aux plateformes numériques peut réduire la participation aux activités sociales et académiques. L'étude suggère que des niveaux élevés de nomophobie peuvent limiter la capacité des individus à s'engager dans diverses activités significatives, perturbant ainsi leur équilibre occupationnel. Il est essentiel de prendre en compte l’équilibre occupationnel dans les futures recherches et stratégies d’intervention afin de promouvoir une utilisation plus saine des technologies.et améliorer le bien-être général des lycéens. Numéro de l’essai clinique : non applicable.

titre: Environmental sustainability in occupational therapy: Insights from Greek occupational therapists.
titre_fr: La durabilité environnementale en ergothérapie : points de vue d'ergothérapeutes grecs.
auteurs: Daskalou Symeon Dimitrios, Gerosideris Nikolaos, Stratou Elpida, Katsouri Ioanna Giannoula
revue: The British journal of occupational therapy
resume: Sustainable development in occupational therapy is primarily implemented through the integration and adaptation of sustainable occupations in occupational therapy practice. However, occupational therapy through the lens of sustainability remains underexplored. To explore the insights of Greek occupational therapists regarding sustainability in their practice. A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted using an electronic questionnaire distributed to 105 Greek occupational therapists. Findings indicate that the majority of Greek occupational therapists (91%, n = 95) acknowledge the importance of sustainable occupations in everyday life. However, only a small percentage (12%, n = 13) of participants have received training in sustainable development practices. Most participants reported engaging in practices related to sustainability, including frequent use of reusable materials (71%, n = 74), recycling (27%, n = 28), sourcing from local communities (40%, n = 42), and adopting eco-friendly products (50%, n = 52). This exploratory study highlights a substantial training gap regarding sustainability in occupational therapy. These findings suggest the need to integrate sustainability-focused content into occupational therapy curricula and continuing professional education as a priority.
resume_fr: Le développement durable en ergothérapie est principalement mis en œuvre par l'intégration et l'adaptation d'activités durables dans la pratique de l'ergothérapie. Cependant, l'ergothérapie sous l'angle de la durabilité reste peu explorée. Explorer les points de vue des ergothérapeutes grecs concernant le développement durable dans leur pratique. Une étude descriptive transversale a été menée à l'aide d'un questionnaire électronique distribué.distribué à 105 ergothérapeutes grecs. Les résultats indiquent que la majorité des ergothérapeutes grecs (91 %, n = 95) reconnaissent l'importance des activités durables dans la vie quotidienne. Cependant, seul un faible pourcentage (12 %, n = 13) des participants a reçu une formation aux pratiques de développement durable. La plupart des participants ont déclaré adopter des pratiques liées au développement durable, notamment l'utilisation fréquente d'articles réutilisablesles matériaux (71 %, n = 74), le recyclage (27 %, n = 28), l’approvisionnement auprès des communautés locales (40 %, n = 42) et l’adoption de produits respectueux de l’environnement (50 %, n = 52). Cette étude exploratoire met en évidence un important déficit de formation en matière de développement durable dans le domaine de l’ergothérapie. Ces résultats suggèrent la nécessité d'intégrer en priorité des contenus axés sur le développement durable dans les programmes d'études en ergothérapie et dans la formation professionnelle continue.
