titre: BOPPPS combined with case-based learning for occupational therapy clinical placements: a single-centre randomised controlled trial.
titre_fr: Le modèle BOPPPS associé à l'apprentissage par cas pour les stages cliniques en ergothérapie : un essai contrôlé randomisé monocentrique.
auteurs: Dai Yuhan, Ju Xiaowen, Xu Ying, Jia Geyang, Wang Xiaodan
resume: Clinical education is a cornerstone of occupational therapy (OT) training. However, traditional lecture-based learning (LBL) often fails to prepare students for the integration of theoretical knowledge, clinical reasoning, and clinical skills required in real-world practice. The BOPPPS model combined with case-based learning (CBL) has shown positive effects across various health professions, yet its application and effectiveness in OT clinical internships have not been evaluated. This study aimed to assess whether the multi-component BOPPPS-CBL educational prograrmme improved theoretical knowledge, clinical skills, and teaching satisfaction among undergraduate OT interns compared with traditional LBL. This randomized controlled trial was conducted at the Department of Rehabilitation Medicine, Suzhou Municipal Hospital, from November 2025 to March 2026. Sixty undergraduate occupational therapy interns were randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 30) receiving the multi-component BOPPPS-CBL educational programme or a control group (n = 30) receiving traditional LBL. The multi-component BOPPPS-CBL educational programme integrated structured pre-class, in-class, and after-class activities centered on authentic clinical cases. Primary outcomes were theoretical knowledge (0-100) and clinical skills assessed by an Objective Structured Clinical Examination (0-100). Teaching satisfaction (20-100) was a secondary outcome, assessed using a 20-item questionnaire adapted from the SETQ framework (Cronbach's α = 0.87). Between-group differences were analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with pre-test scores as covariates, with Bonferroni correction applied to the five satisfaction subdomains. No alpha adjustment was applied to the two co-primary outcomes.Due to a significant group × pre-test interaction for clinical skills, change-score analysis was used as the primary analysis for this outcome, with Bootstrap ANCOVA as a sensitivity analysis.The relationship between satisfaction and theoretical knowledge was examined using partial correlation controlling for both group allocation and pre-test scores. The trial was retrospectively registered (ChiCTR2600132112). The experimental group scored significantly higher than the control group on both post-test theoretical knowledge and clinical skills (both p < 0.001), with large effect sizes (partial η² = 0.91 and 0.895). The experimental group also reported significantly higher total teaching satisfaction (p = 0.001) and higher scores in all five satisfaction subdomains after Bonferroni correction (adjusted p < 0.05 for all, including Teaching Enthusiasm, adjusted p = 0.015). For clinical skills, change-score analysis was used as the primary analysis due to a significant group × pre-test interaction, and Bootstrap ANCOVA confirmed the robustness of the findings.The association between satisfaction and theoretical knowledge was strong but exploratory (partial r = 0.860, p < 0.001). Students assigned to the multi-component BOPPPS-CBL educational programme achieved higher immediate post-intervention theoretical knowledge and clinical skills scores and reported greater teaching satisfaction than students receiving traditional LBL. However, because instructor identity was completely confounded with group allocation and the educational dosage was unequal, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary, exploratory evidence for the potential benefits of the entire educational package, rather than confirmation of the BOPPPS-CBL model itself. Future prospectively registered, multi-center trials with validated outcome measures, longer-term follow-up, and factorial or multi-arm designs that can isolate active components and control for instructor effects are required before widespread implementation can be recommended. The trial was retrospectively registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) under the registration number ChiCTR2600132112 on September 9, 2026.
resume_fr: La formation clinique est une pierre angulaire de la formation en ergothérapie (OT). Cependant, l'apprentissage traditionnel basé sur les cours magistraux (LBL, de l'anglais « lecture-based learning ») ne parvient souvent pas à préparer les étudiants à l'intégration des connaissances théoriques, du raisonnement clinique et des compétences cliniques nécessaires dans la pratique réelle. Le modèle BOPPPS associé à l'apprentissage basé sur des cas (CBL) a montré des effets positifs dans diverses professions de la santé, mais son application et son efficacité dans la formation clinique en ergothérapieLes stages n'ont pas été évalués. Cette étude visait à évaluer si le programme éducatif à composantes multiples BOPPPS-CBL améliorait les connaissances théoriques, les compétences cliniques et la satisfaction à l'égard de l'enseignement chez les stagiaires en ergothérapie de premier cycle par rapport à l'apprentissage traditionnel basé sur les cours magistraux (LBL). Cet essai contrôlé randomisé a été mené au service de médecine de réadaptation de l'hôpital municipal de Suzhou, de novembre 2025 à mars 2026. Soixante étudiants en ergothérapie de premier cycleLes internes en thérapie ont été répartis aléatoirement dans un groupe expérimental (n = 30) bénéficiant du programme d'enseignement BOPPPS-CBL à composantes multiples ou dans un groupe témoin (n = 30) bénéficiant de l'apprentissage traditionnel basé sur les cours magistraux (LBL). Le programme d'enseignement BOPPPS-CBL à composantes multiples intégrait des activités structurées avant, pendant et après les cours, centrées sur des cas cliniques authentiques. Les principaux résultats étaient les connaissances théoriques (0-100) et les compétences cliniques évaluées par un examen clinique objectif structuré (ECOS).Examen clinique structuré (0-100). La satisfaction à l'égard de l'enseignement (20-100) était un critère de jugement secondaire, évalué à l'aide d'un questionnaire de 20 items adapté du cadre SETQ (α de Cronbach = 0,87). Les différences entre les groupes ont été analysées à l'aide d'une analyse de covariance (ANCOVA) avec les scores du pré-test comme covariables, et une correction de Bonferroni a été appliquée aux cinq sous-domaines de satisfaction. Aucun ajustement alpha n'a été appliqué aux deux critères de jugement co-primaires. En raison d'un signeinteraction significative groupe × pré-test pour les compétences cliniques, l’analyse des scores de changement a été utilisée comme analyse principale pour ce résultat, avec l’ANCOVA Bootstrap comme analyse de sensibilité. La relation entre la satisfaction et les connaissances théoriques a été examinée à l’aide d’une corrélation partielle contrôlant à la fois la répartition des groupes et les scores du pré-test. L'essai a été enregistré rétrospectivement (ChiCTR2600132112). Le groupe expérimental a obtenu des scores significativement élevésque le groupe témoin tant pour les connaissances théoriques que pour les compétences cliniques après le test (p < 0,001 dans les deux cas), avec des tailles d'effet importantes (η² partiel = 0,91 et 0,895). Le groupe expérimental a également fait état d'une satisfaction globale à l'égard de l'enseignement significativement plus élevée (p = 0,001) et de scores plus élevés dans les cinq sous-domaines de satisfaction après la correction de Bonferroni (p ajustée < 0,05 pour tous, y compris l'enthousiasme à l'égard de l'enseignement, p ajustée = 0,015). Pour les compétences cliniques, les scores de changementL'analyse de régression a été utilisée comme analyse principale en raison d'une interaction significative entre le groupe et le pré-test, et l'ANCOVA Bootstrap a confirmé la robustesse des résultats. L'association entre la satisfaction et les connaissances théoriques était forte mais exploratoire (r partiel = 0,860, p < 0,001). Les étudiants affectés au programme éducatif BOPPPS-CBL à composantes multiples ont obtenu des scores plus élevés en matière de connaissances théoriques et de compétences cliniques immédiatement après l'intervention etont déclaré être plus satisfaits de l'enseignement que les étudiants bénéficiant de l'apprentissage dirigé par l'enseignant (LBL) traditionnel. Cependant, l'identité de l'enseignant étant complètement confondue avec la répartition des groupes et la dose pédagogique étant inégale, ces résultats doivent être interprétés comme des preuves préliminaires et exploratoires des avantages potentiels de l'ensemble du programme pédagogique, plutôt que comme une confirmation du modèle BOPPPS-CBL lui-même. Futur essai multicentrique enregistré de manière prospectiveDes études comportant des mesures de résultats validées, un suivi à plus long terme et des conceptions factorielles ou à plusieurs bras permettant d’isoler les composantes actives et de contrôler les effets des instructeurs sont nécessaires avant de pouvoir recommander une mise en œuvre généralisée. L’essai a été enregistré rétrospectivement auprès du Registre chinois des essais cliniques (ChiCTR) sous le numéro d’enregistrement ChiCTR2600132112 le 9 septembre 2026.

titre: Balancing Security, Autonomy, and Dignity at the End of Life in Forensic Psychiatry: A Case Report.
titre_fr: Concilier sécurité, autonomie et dignité en fin de vie en psychiatrie légale : un rapport de cas.
auteurs: Yakubov Rose, de Lasa Cristina, Kravtsenyuk Maryana
resume: BackgroundAs forensic psychiatric populations age, clinicians are increasingly required to manage advanced medical illness and end-of-life care within secure psychiatric environments. The intersection of terminal illness, forensic detention, Medical Assistance in Dying (MAiD), and palliative care remains poorly described in the literature.Case PresentationWe describe the case of an adult forensic psychiatric inpatient detained under the Criminal Code of Canada who experienced progressive endstage alcohol-related liver disease complicated by hepatocellular carcinoma, hepatic encephalopathy, and increasing physical frailty. Despite longstanding psychiatric stability, his evolving medical needs required extensive collaboration among forensic psychiatry, hospital medicine, hepatology, radiation oncology, palliative care, nursing, pharmacy, occupational therapy, social work, and biomedical ethics. Throughout his illness, he consistently expressed goals emphasizing comfort, dignity, and quality of life, ultimately requesting MAiD.ConclusionIn this case, we highlight the unique clinical, ethical, and operational challenges of providing end-of-life care within forensic psychiatric settings. This case underscores the need for integrated forensic-medical models that can reconcile therapeutic security requirements with the principles of person-centered palliative care, ensuring dignity, autonomy, timely access to specialized palliative services, and appropriate support for complex capacity and MAiD related decisions. As medically frail forensic populations continue to age, healthcare systems must develop policies, infrastructure, and interdisciplinary models of care that better address the intersection of forensic psychiatry, complex medical illness, and end-of-life care.
resume_fr: Contexte : À mesure que les populations de patients en psychiatrie légale vieillissent, les cliniciens sont de plus en plus amenés à prendre en charge des maladies médicales avancées et des soins de fin de vie dans des environnements psychiatriques sécurisés. L'intersection entre la maladie en phase terminale, la détention médico-légale, l'aide médicale à mourir (AMM) et les soins palliatifs reste mal décrite dans la littérature. Présentation du cas Nous décrivons le cas d'un patient adulte hospitalisé en psychiatrie médico-légale, détenu en vertu du Code criminel.Code du Canada qui souffrait d'une maladie hépatique progressive au stade terminal liée à l'alcool, compliquée par un carcinome hépatocellulaire, une encéphalopathie hépatique et une fragilité physique croissante. Malgré une stabilité psychiatrique de longue date, ses besoins médicaux évolutifs ont nécessité une collaboration approfondie entre la psychiatrie légale, la médecine hospitalière, l'hépatologie, la radio-oncologie, les soins palliatifs, les soins infirmiers, la pharmacie, l'ergothérapie, le travail social et l'éthique biomédicale.Tout au long de sa maladie, il a constamment exprimé des objectifs mettant l'accent sur le confort, la dignité et la qualité de vie, demandant finalement l'AMM. Conclusion : Dans ce cas, nous soulignons les défis cliniques, éthiques et opérationnels uniques que pose la prestation de soins de fin de vie dans les établissements de psychiatrie légale. Ce cas souligne la nécessité de modèles médico-légaux intégrés capables de concilier les exigences de sécurité thérapeutique avec les principes deDes soins palliatifs centrés sur la personne, garantissant la dignité, l'autonomie, l'accès en temps voulu à des services palliatifs spécialisés et un soutien approprié pour les décisions complexes liées à la capacité et à l'AMM. Alors que les populations médico-légales médicalement fragiles continuent de vieillir, les systèmes de santé doivent élaborer des politiques, des infrastructures et des modèles de soins interdisciplinaires qui répondent mieux à l'intersection de la psychiatrie médico-légale, des maladies médicales complexes et des soins de fin de vie.

titre: A brief neuromotor-therapy-augmented pathway for pediatric functional movement disorders: a sequential historical cohort study.
titre_fr: Un bref parcours de soins renforcé par la thérapie neuromotrice pour les troubles du mouvement fonctionnels pédiatriques : une étude de cohorte historique séquentielle.
auteurs: Valentina Baglioni, Ilaria Notaristefano, Patrizia Maggiore, Sara Romano, Serena Galosi, Michele Tinazzi, Christian Geroin, Dario Esposito
resume: Pediatric functional movement disorders (FMD) often improve, but access to specialized motor rehabilitation is heterogeneous. We compared two sequential, non-overlapping care periods within one clinical unit: usual care (UC) and a neuromotor-therapy-augmented pathway (NMT-A), which added brief hospital-based neuromotor therapy before community referral. This retrospective, non-randomized historical cohort included 17 UC patients (June 2021-January 2023) and 29 NMT-A patients (February 2023-June 2025). The primary outcome was continuous S-FMDRS at 6 months; S-FMDRS-defined motor symptom-free status (score = 0) was secondary. Both were reassessed at 12 months, together with community-treatment engagement. At 6 months, the adjusted NMT-A-minus-UC S-FMDRS difference was -1.66 points (95% CI, -4.04 to 0.72). Motor symptom-free status occurred in 55.2% versus 5.9% (risk difference, 49.3 percentage points; 95% CI, 21.8 to 66.4), and in 86.2% versus 52.9% at 12 months (risk difference, 33.3 percentage points; 95% CI, 6.5 to 56.8). The pathway-by-time interaction was not significant. Sustained community physical and/or occupational therapy was documented in 75.0% versus 17.6% (RR, 4.25; 95% CI, 1.74-12.46). The NMT-A pathway-period was associated with more frequent motor symptom-free status and greater continuity of community motor rehabilitation, although the adjusted mean S-FMDRS difference was not statistically significant. Because pathway and calendar period were inseparable, these findings should be interpreted as associations with the overall later care pathway rather than as an isolated effect of NMT.
resume_fr: Les troubles fonctionnels du mouvement (TFM) pédiatriques s'améliorent souvent, mais l'accès à une rééducation motrice spécialisée est hétérogène. Nous avons comparé deux périodes de soins séquentielles et non superposées au sein d'une même unité clinique : les soins habituels (SH) et un parcours de soins renforcé par une thérapie neuromotrice (NMT-A), qui prévoyait l'ajout d'une brève thérapie neuromotrice en milieu hospitalier avant l'orientation vers les services de proximité. Cette cohorte historique rétrospective et non randomisée comprenait 17 patients ayant bénéficié de soins habituels (juin 2021-janvier 2022).2023) et 29 patients atteints de NMT-A (février 2023-juin 2025). Le critère d’évaluation principal était le score S-FMDRS continu à 6 mois ; l’absence de symptômes moteurs définie par le score S-FMDRS (score = 0) était le critère d’évaluation secondaire. Les deux ont été réévalués à 12 mois, ainsi que l’engagement dans le traitement en milieu communautaire. À 6 mois, la différence ajustée du score S-FMDRS entre le groupe NMT-A et le groupe UC était de -1,66 point (IC à 95 %, -4,04 à 0,72). L’absence de symptômes moteurs a été observée chez 55,2 % des patients contre 5,9 % (différence de risque, 49,3 %).tage points; 95% CI, 21.8 to 66.4), and in 86.2% versus 52.9% at 12 months (risk difference, 33.3 percentage points; 95% CI, 6.5 to 56.8). The pathway-by-time interaction was not significant. Sustained community physical and/or occupational therapy was documented in 75.0% versus 17.6% (RR, 4.25; 95% CI, 1.74-12.46). The NMT-A pathway-period was associated with more frequent motor symptom-free status and greater continuity of community motor rehabilitation, although the adjusted mean S-FMDRS difference was not statistically significant. Because pathway and calendar period were inseparable, these findings should be interpreted as associations with the overall later care pathway rather than as an isolated effect of NMT.

titre: Occupational therapy interventions for functional neurological disorder: a scoping review.
titre_fr: Occupational therapy interventions for functional neurological disorder: a scoping review.
auteurs: Nicholson Clare, Lorencatto Fabiana, Yogarajah Mahinda, Nielsen Glenn
resume: Functional Neurological Disorder (FND) is a common and disabling condition for which multidisciplinary rehabilitation is recommended; however, the specific contribution of occupational therapy remains poorly defined. This scoping review aimed to map and characterize occupational therapy interventions for people with FND, examine how these are delivered and evaluated within rehabilitation and identify priorities for future research. A scoping review was conducted using Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology. Peer-reviewed English-language intervention studies involving adults (≥18 years) with FND who received occupational therapy delivered independently or as part of multidisciplinary rehabilitation and reporting treatment outcomes were included. Descriptive analysis was undertaken. OVID Medline, Embase, APA PsycInfo and CINAHL Plus were searched from inception to July 2026, supplemented by reference list screening. Forty-one studies (n= 1,284 participants; sample sizes 1-201) were included, with only one randomized study. Occupational therapy was predominantly delivered within multidisciplinary rehabilitation; only one study included a subgroup receiving occupational therapy alone. Despite considerable variation in intervention reporting, common occupational therapy intervention components included facilitating occupational engagement, movement retraining and anxiety management, with symptom management strategies integrated into functional activities to promote confidence and independence. Improvements in symptom severity, functional ability, mental health, and quality of life were reported following multidisciplinary rehabilitation including occupational therapy. However, findings were primarily derived from uncontrolled studies, and interpretation was further limited by heterogeneity in intervention approaches, inconsistent use of outcome measures, and variable follow-up. Although occupational therapy was included in all eligible studies, occupational therapy-specific interventions and associated outcomes were inconsistently described and evaluated, limiting understanding of occupational therapy's distinct contribution within multidisciplinary rehabilitation. Future research should focus on clearly defining and evaluating the components of occupational therapy interventions.

titre: Exploring the Efficacy of Assistive Technology on the Quality of Occupational Performance: a Single-Case Experimental Design Study of the Use of the Activity Chair.
titre_fr: Exploring the Efficacy of Assistive Technology on the Quality of Occupational Performance: a Single-Case Experimental Design Study of the Use of the Activity Chair.
auteurs: Bjørnskov Stina, Mortenson W Ben, Petersen Kirsten Schultz, Helle Tina
resume: Assistive technology (AT) is provided to support occupational performance, yet evidence on the efficacy of different types of AT is limited. This study aimed to explore the efficacy of the activity chair in relation to the quality of occupational performance. This study used an alternating treatments design (ATD) within a single-case experimental design (SCED), involving six first-time users of an activity chair. Across five home visits, data on quality of occupational performance were collected using the Assessment of Motor and Process Skills (AMPS), alongside self-reported measures of effort, efficiency, safety, satisfaction, and independence, as well as data on the time used to complete the AMPS tasks. Data were analysed using visual inspection and statistical comparisons of differences between conditions (with and without the activity chair). No consistent pattern regarding the efficacy of the activity chair in relation to the quality of occupational performance was identified across participants. One participant demonstrated improved motor skills, whereas the remaining participants showed no clear differences and considerable within- and between-participant variation. Yet, several participants reported lower effort when using the activity chair, while process skills were often lower and task completion time was longer. Findings suggested that the activity chair may facilitate some specific performance skills, such as bending, reaching, lifting, and transporting objects, while making positioning and navigation more challenging. The findings indicate that the efficacy of the activity chair in relation to the quality of occupational performance may depend on the participant and the specific situation in which it is used. Individualised assessment and training should therefore include observation of relevant occupations in the home environment, with ongoing follow-up to address changing needs over time.

titre: A Two-Dimensional Perspective on Quality Of Life: Changes After the Balancing Everyday Life Intervention for Mental Health Service Users and Relationships to Everyday Occupations - An RCT Study.
titre_fr: A Two-Dimensional Perspective on Quality Of Life: Changes After the Balancing Everyday Life Intervention for Mental Health Service Users and Relationships to Everyday Occupations - An RCT Study.
auteurs: Eklund Mona, Argentzell Elisabeth
resume: A randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating the Balancing Everyday Life (BEL) intervention compared with care as usual (CAU) for mental health service users found no group differences when quality of life (QoL) was treated as a single construct. However, research suggests that (QoL) consists of two dimensions: a personalized life-and-health dimension (e.g., life satisfaction, health, leisure, and work) and an environmental dimension (e.g., safety, housing, and family situation). The current study re-examined data from the BEL study to investigate whether the BEL group and the CAU differed regarding improvements on the two aforementioned QoL dimensions and explore how changes in everyday occupations were related to QoL improvements. A total of 226 mental health service users were assigned to BEL or CAU. Data were collected at baseline, post-intervention, and six-month follow-up. QoL was measured using the Manchester Short Assessment of Quality of Life (MANSA) and analyzed as two dimensions. Everyday occupations were assessed through measures of actual participation and subjective experiences. Change scores were analyzed using t-tests and Pearson correlations. The BEL group showed significantly greater improvement in the life-and-health dimension of QoL after the intervention, with marginal significance at follow-up. Positive perceptions of everyday occupations were moderately associated with improvements in both QoL dimensions, whereas actual activity participation showed weaker associations. Treating QoL as a two-dimensional construct revealed intervention effects that were not detected in previous analyses. Interventions emphasizing meaningful everyday occupations may enhance QoL and recovery among mental health service users. Trial Registration The study was registered with ClinicalTrial.gov. Reg. No. NCT02619318. Retrospectively registered: 20-11-2015.

titre: Communication Education in Prelicensure and Postlicensure Occupational Therapy: Scoping Review.
titre_fr: Communication Education in Prelicensure and Postlicensure Occupational Therapy: Scoping Review.
auteurs: Shimada Ryuichi, Sano Yukiko, Sasaki Takeshi, Tanimura Astuko
resume: Effective communication, therapeutic relationships, and interprofessional collaboration are essential to high-quality occupational therapy (OT) practice. However, communication education across prelicensure and postlicensure OT training has not been comprehensively mapped. This review aims to identify research gaps and map communication education in prelicensure and postlicensure OT education according to content, delivery methods, assessment approaches, and outcomes. Following Joanna Briggs Institute guidance, this review was reported using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Literature Search Extension (PRISMA-S) frameworks. PubMed, CINAHL, ERIC, Web of Science, Ichushi-Web, and Open Access Theses and Dissertations were searched without publication year restrictions; the final search was conducted on May 25, 2026. Eligible sources were English- or Japanese-language publications that examined communication education involving OT students or practicing occupational therapists. The review protocol was developed a priori but was not registered. Two reviewers independently screened records identified through database and gray literature searches, whereas records identified through backward citation searching were screened by one reviewer and checked by the second reviewer. Data were charted for study characteristics, educational content, delivery methods, assessment approaches, and outcomes. Educational outcomes were categorized using the Kirkpatrick model. Formal critical appraisal was not conducted, and the findings were synthesized descriptively. Database and gray literature searches identified 10,243 records, and backward citation searching identified 9 additional records. After duplicate removal and screening, 55 reports corresponding to 54 studies were included. Of the 55 reports, 47 (85.5%) focused on prelicensure education and 8 (14.5%) on postlicensure education; prelicensure reports mainly involved OT students learning either within OT programs alone or with students from other health professions. Single-group pre-post studies were the most common design (n=22, 40%). Educational content was diverse and included interprofessional communication and teamwork, communication with specific client populations or conditions, model-based communication training, experiential communication skills training, and OT-specific therapeutic communication or therapeutic use of self. Outcome assessment relied mainly on learner-reported measures, including perceived competence, self-efficacy, self-reported communication skills, and attitudes. Objective or observer-rated assessments were less common. Across the 55 included reports, 15 (27.3%) reported reaction-level outcomes, 53 (96.4%) learning-level outcomes, and 5 (9.1%) behavior-level outcomes; no report assessed results-level outcomes, and reports could contribute to more than one level. This review maps communication education across both prelicensure and postlicensure OT education in the English- and Japanese-language literature. The findings highlight the need for more explicit occupation-centered education, including occupational history taking, values-based goal setting, therapeutic relationship development, and therapeutic use of self. They may inform curriculum design, continuing professional development, and outcome measure selection. Interpretation should remain limited to the included literature, which was dominated by single-group pre-post designs and learner-reported outcomes.

titre: Predischarge home visits: A survey of inpatient rehabilitation facilities in the United States.
titre_fr: Predischarge home visits: A survey of inpatient rehabilitation facilities in the United States.
auteurs: Russell Abigail J, Krauss Melissa J, Holden Brianna M, Woods GaResia B, Bollinger Rebecca M, Stark Susan L
revue: The British journal of occupational therapy
resume: Data on predischarge home visits (PDHVs) by inpatient rehabilitation facilities (IRFs) in the United States (US) are limited. We evaluated how often IRFs conduct PDHVs and factors influencing their use. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among IRFs registered with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS; 2024-2025). Among 1224 IRFs, a stratified random sample of 538 was selected by CMS region. One participant (occupational/physical therapist, case manager, director/program manager) per IRF was allowed to participate. Response rate was 11% (n=61/538). Forty-four percent (27/61) conducted PDHVs within the past 12 months. Among these IRFs, the median approximate percentage of patients receiving a PDHV (based on self-reported/calculated estimates) was 1% (range 0.1%-64%). Considerations for conducting PDHVs were home setup (26/26, 100%), physical impairment (26/26, 100%), social support (22/25, 88%), and cognitive impairment (22/26, 85%). Among IRFs not conducting PDHVs, barriers were staffing (16/34, 47%), budget (15/34, 44%), and time (14/34, 41%). Over half (32/60, 53%) of participants believed PDHVs are critical for inpatient care. PDHVs were infrequently conducted by responding IRFs despite many practitioners viewing them as critical. Given resource constraints, further research should determine patients who benefit most and evaluate alternative methods, such as telehealth-based visits.

titre: Feeding challenges at initiation and maintenance of the ketogenic diet in children with infantile epileptic spasms syndrome: 20 years single center experience.
titre_fr: Feeding challenges at initiation and maintenance of the ketogenic diet in children with infantile epileptic spasms syndrome: 20 years single center experience.
auteurs: Lowe Helen, Kaur Prabhjot, Dickson Jolynn, Fraser Erin, Owusu Karen, McRae Lyndsey, Zak Maria, Chau Vann, Jain Puneet, Donner Elizabeth, Kobayashi Jeff, Sharma Suvasini
resume: Infants with Infantile Epileptic Spasms Syndrome (IESS) are at high risk for feeding challenges such as aspiration. These vulnerabilities may be exacerbated by the ketogenic diet (KD), an accepted second-line therapy. Hormonal therapy (ACTH or oral corticosteroids), the first-line IESS treatment, may transiently enhance appetite and improve oral feeding performance, and hence mask feeding challenges. A retrospective chart review was conducted for infants with IESS who initiated KD between January 2005 and January 2025 at our center. Collected data included ages at diagnosis and KD initiation, comorbidities, clinical and video fluoroscopic swallow study (VFSS) assessments, timing relative to hormonal therapy, feeding method before and during KD initiation, and incidence of feeding concerns during KD. Feeding challenges included aspiration, confirmed by VFSS or occupational therapy clinical assessment of feeding (OCTA), or inadequate oral intake. Forty infants were enrolled. Twelve (30%) had previous aspiration reported in the medical charts or VFSS at baseline; nine were tube-fed prior to KD. Of the 31 (31/40, 77.5%) orally fed infants at initiation of KD, 23 were referred for feeding safety evaluation. Twelve of these had a feeding concern found on OTCA and/or VFSS, of which 3 presented with aspiration without a protective cough confirmed by VFSS. Nineteen babies were deemed safe to initiate KD orally; however, 5/19 (26%, 95% CI 11.8%-48.7%) went on to experience aspiration or aspiration pneumonia during KD treatment. Feeding challenges are frequent, dynamic, and under-recognized in IESS. Comprehensive feeding evaluation at KD initiation and maintenance is essential for safe treatment.

titre: Conservative management of closed extra-articular metacarpal hand fractures: A scoping review.
titre_fr: Conservative management of closed extra-articular metacarpal hand fractures: A scoping review.
auteurs: Naughton Mary, Morrissey Ann-Marie
revue: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
resume: Metacarpal (MC) fractures account for up to 44% of hand injuries, primarily affecting working-age adults. Despite their prevalence and significant socioeconomic impact, conservative management approaches vary widely. The current key concepts, gaps, and nature of existing treatment evidence for MC fractures are not clearly defined. To identify and map the breadth of literature regarding the conservative management of extra-articular MC fractures and identify existing gaps in clinical evidence. Scoping review METHODS: Following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a systematic search of five databases (CINAHL, Cochrane, MEDLINE, EMBASE, and PubMed) was conducted through September 2025. Research questions focused on the nature of evidence, types of interventions, and differences in treatment based on fracture location. Thirty-four studies were included (n=2857 participants), comprising eleven RCTs, fourteen observational studies, and nine secondary/qualitative reports. Narrative synthesis revealed significant heterogeneity in orthotic design, immobilization duration, and clinical governance. A key evidence gap was identified in therapeutic management beyond the acute (0-6-week) healing phase. Outcome measures were inconsistent, complicating the comparison of functional recovery across protocols. Conservative MC fracture management lacks standardization. Future research should prioritize methodologically robust trials using standardized core outcome sets, with a specific focus on the role of advanced practice hand therapy in late-stage functional rehabilitation.

titre: From Referral to Reality: A Mixed Methods Analysis of Barriers to Pediatric Rehabilitation Service Initiation.
titre_fr: From Referral to Reality: A Mixed Methods Analysis of Barriers to Pediatric Rehabilitation Service Initiation.
auteurs: Tanner Lynn, Grinde Kathy S, Gustner Kelsey J, Slater Nancy L, Thornton Adriene, Evans Stella, J Nickel Amanda
revue: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
resume: We investigated factors associated with pediatric rehabilitation service initiation through an integrated analysis of sociodemographic characteristics and parental experiences of non-initiation. Explanatory sequential mixed methods design SETTING: [Geographic area] pediatric healthcare organization comprised of six ambulatory rehabilitation clinics with physical therapy (PT), occupational therapy (OT), and speech-language pathology (SLP) disciplines PARTICIPANTS: We examined service initiation among 8,533 pediatric rehabilitation referrals in persons aged 0-18 years between March 2021 and February 2022 and sampled 12 parents from the quantitative cohort for semi-structured interviews. Not applicable MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Analysis included examining service initiation rates, patient characteristic predictors, and qualitative themes related to factors for service non-initiation. Parents described a complex interaction of barriers that inform our cohorts' service initiation rate of only 42.7% (PT, 43.0%; SLP, 37.3%; OT, 43.0%; Feeding, 55.2%). Contextual factors included geographic availability, scheduling challenges, and how professionals communicate the need for services to families. Individual factors ranged from prior rehabilitation experience and family competing priorities to access to early intervention services, financial and transportation challenges, and a "wait and see" approach. The qualitative findings contextualized differences in service initiation across patient characteristics. Parents described intersecting barriers of the child's age, cost, service availability, and need. Systematic changes are needed to address barriers to rehabilitation services with a focus on sociodemographic disparities, rehabilitation evidence, and shared decision-making between referral provider and family.

titre: Practices and Processes Supporting Goal Setting in Occupational Therapy: A Scoping Review.
titre_fr: Practices and Processes Supporting Goal Setting in Occupational Therapy: A Scoping Review.
auteurs: Bernie Charmaine, Kessler Dorothy, Lepage Shae-Lynn, Kirby Grace, Egan Mary
revue: Canadian journal of occupational therapy. Revue canadienne d'ergotherapie
resume: BackgroundGoal setting is a core component of occupational therapy. There is lack of clarity and consistency in the practices adopted by occupational therapists when goal setting with people accessing their services.PurposeThis scoping review explored goal setting approaches, tools, and processes described in current occupational therapy research.MethodsEnglish, peer-reviewed articles published between January 2000 and June 2024 with a focus on goal setting by occupational therapists were retrieved from CINAHL, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, ERIC, and Nursing and Allied Health databases. The results were presented descriptively and thematically.FindingsNinety-eight studies were included. While approaches and frameworks varied, collaborative (32%) and client-determined (49%) goal settings were commonly reported. Tools included the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (31%), Goal Attainment Scaling (17%), and Aid for Decision-making in Occupation Choice (10%). A number of supporting processes are utilized by occupational therapists to facilitate goal setting practice.ConclusionsThere is high variability in goal setting practices in occupational therapy research, often without theoretical underpinnings explicitly guiding tool and process adoption or research related to therapy outcomes.SignificanceIdentifying strengths and gaps in goal setting practices promotes more effective approaches to goal setting with people accessing occupational therapy services.

titre: From learner to trainer: efficacy of a wheelchair skills bootcamp with embedded learner teaching.
titre_fr: From learner to trainer: efficacy of a wheelchair skills bootcamp with embedded learner teaching.
auteurs: Worobey Lynn, Kenney Alan, Callahan Carrie, Eckstein Stacey, Romano Stephanie
resume: To evaluate a 2-day wheelchair skills bootcamp in which learners (licenced occupational and physical therapists) received train-the-trainer training, from instructors that included wheelchair users with lived experience, and then applied that training by teaching trainees (students and wheelchair users). Seventeen learners, 17 student trainees, and 5 wheelchair user trainees participated in a cohort study with pre- and post-training comparisons. Learners completed skill acquisition and train-the-trainer instruction during 6-hours of training on day 1, and then sequentially trained student and wheelchair user trainees on day 2. Wheelchair skill performance and confidence were assessed for all participants using the Wheelchair Skills Test Questionnaire (WST-Q). titre: Employment in Veterans With Mental Illness: An Exploratory Penalized-Regression and Random-Forest Analysis.
titre_fr: Employment in Veterans With Mental Illness: An Exploratory Penalized-Regression and Random-Forest Analysis.
auteurs: Umucu Emre, Koc Betul Bengusu, Cheever Kelly, Swan Alicia A, Rivas Velarde Minerva, Weichelt Bryan, Tansey Tim, Lee Beatrice
revue: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
resume: ImportanceReturning to civilian and community life after military service represents a critical and often challenging transition. Employment can contribute to social identity, financial security, social participation and community reintegration, and overall quality of life among veterans.ObjectiveTo examine candidate factors of employment among veterans who reported a current mental health diagnosis.DesignCross-sectional survey study.SettingOnline data collection.ParticipantsA total of 156 veterans who reported having a current mental illness were recruited; 151 with complete data (mean age = 37.85 years) were analyzed. Most participants identified as male (67%), White (70%), and married or living with a partner (62%).Outcomes and MeasuresEmployment status was the outcome, and candidate predictors included demographic and military characteristics, mental health, physical health and functioning, and psychosocial and behavioral factors.ResultsThe BIC-LASSO model revealed that greater disability severity and pain intensity were each associated with lower odds of employment, with moderate bootstrap selection recurrence (57.1% for disability severity and 56.9% for pain intensity) that remained robust after sensitivity analysis. The random forest model did not exceed majority-class accuracy.Conclusions and RelevanceGreater disability severity and greater pain intensity emerged as plausible, though not yet confirmed, correlates of employment status among veterans with mental illness. Because these exploratory findings require replication in larger, more diverse, and longitudinal samples, they do not yet justify changes to practice; in the interim, they support attending to everyday functioning and pain, alongside psychiatric symptoms, when occupational therapy practitioners evaluate work participation with this population.

titre: Staged orthotic intervention in line with hand therapy for functional recovery following replantation of a complete forearm amputation: A case undergone 2.5-year intervention.
titre_fr: Staged orthotic intervention in line with hand therapy for functional recovery following replantation of a complete forearm amputation: A case undergone 2.5-year intervention.
auteurs: Ishita Kohei, Tashiro Syoichi, Ikeda Mitsuyo, Harada Yusuke, Inada Narisaku, Yamada Shin
revue: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
resume: Replantation is the first-line treatment for upper limb amputations proximal to the wrist; however, detailed long-term reports describing specific occupational therapy content and clinical reasoning from the acute to chronic phase remain scarce. We describe a case with traumatic amputation at the level between elbow and wrist (S58.1) who underwent occupational therapy intervention over 2.5 years following replantation. Case report. A male mechanic in his 30s completely amputated right forearm at the middle third in a workplace accident and underwent replantation. Occupational therapy was initiated on postoperative day 8. Interventions included individually tailored finger orthoses, early active motion using Rubber Band Traction, graded sensory re-education, and a structured home exercise program, continued over 2.5 years. At 2.5 years, Simple Test for Evaluating Hand Function 97/100, grip-strength 13.6 kg (42% of unaffected side), Semmes-Weinstein monofilament test fingertip 2.83 (normal), Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand: disability 18, work 19, and Chen's criteria grade II were achieved; the patient returned to work in an administrative role following job redeployment. Long-term (2.5-year) occupational therapy combining graded orthotic intervention, early active motion, sensory re-education, and a home exercise program may contribute to functional hand recovery following complete forearm replantation.

titre: Burden of diseases and disease trends in the rehabilitation public health facilities in Gauteng Province, South Africa.
titre_fr: Burden of diseases and disease trends in the rehabilitation public health facilities in Gauteng Province, South Africa.
auteurs: Pilusa Sonti, Masuku Khetsiwe, Rabothata Simon, Mukheli Tshifhiwa, Naidoo Vaneshveri
resume: Rehabilitation remains an unmet need and a neglected health service in South Africa. To address the country's complex burden of disease, a skilled rehabilitation workforce is needed. This study aimed to identify prevalent medical conditions and disease trends among patients treated by rehabilitation therapists over a six-year period. It further examined whether these prevalent health conditions are represented in the rehabilitation health education curricula. The study was undertaken in public healthcare facilities within Gauteng province, South Africa. Secondary data on provincial rehabilitation data from April 2019 to March 2024 were analysed and categorised into non-communicable diseases (NCDs), children-specific conditions, injuries, and communicable diseases. Data were analysed descriptively. Lastly, the undergraduate rehabilitation health training curriculum (Occupational therapy, Physiotherapy, Speech therapy and Audiology) was reviewed to assess whether it covers the medical conditions treated by rehabilitation therapists. The most treated conditions were NCDs (44.1%), injuries (36.4%) and children-specific conditions (15.6%). All health conditions decreased during the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic, followed by an increase in NCDs and injuries between 2022 and 2024. The undergraduate rehabilitation health training curriculum covers the most prevalent conditions treated by public sector rehabilitation therapists. The burden of diseases treated in public healthcare rehabilitation departments aligns with the national burden of diseases. The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on rehabilitation services is evident in the trend analysis over the years. Continual review of the curriculum is needed to ensure local health responsiveness. This study highlights the burden of disease treated by the public health sector rehabilitation therapists, the trends over time and the importance of ensuring that the curriculum is locally responsive.

titre: Outdoor Fall Risks and Strategies Used for Prevention: An Exploratory Study of Rural-Dwelling Older Adults.
titre_fr: Outdoor Fall Risks and Strategies Used for Prevention: An Exploratory Study of Rural-Dwelling Older Adults.
auteurs: Chippendale Tracy, Hines Leah, Akey Christina, Bauer Michael, Gell Nancy
resume: Outdoor falls prevention research has focused primarily on suburban and urban settings. Further, hazards related to terrain have not been well studied. Therefore, to fill this gap, perceived outdoor fall risks, community resources to support falls prevention, and strategies used for safe community mobility in rural communities were explored through in-depth interviews with older adults from two rural counties. Themes that emerged from this qualitative study included: (a) physical and natural elements; (b) few proximate resources and available options underutilized; (c) instrumental activities of daily living (IADLs) as a key source of physical activity; (d) risk recognized and strategies implemented; and (e) living with fall risk. Results suggest occupational therapy practice implications to support the safety of older adults in rural communities.

titre: The Effect of Convalescent Nursing Combined With Occupational Therapy and Group Painting Art Therapy on Medication Adherence and Quality of Life in Patients With Schizophrenia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: The Effect of Convalescent Nursing Combined With Occupational Therapy and Group Painting Art Therapy on Medication Adherence and Quality of Life in Patients With Schizophrenia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Shi Lei, Liu Danhui, Zhao Jing, Zhang Yintao, Wang Hao, Wang Jiangyi, Feng Weiwei, Wang Zhenhui, Ma Tianhua
revue: The International journal of social psychiatry
resume: To evaluate an integrated intervention combining convalescent nursing, occupational therapy, and group painting art therapy for medication adherence, quality of life, and related outcomes in patients with schizophrenia. In this single-center randomized controlled trial, 150 patients with schizophrenia were randomized 1:1 to a control group (routine convalescent nursing) or an observation group (routine nursing plus occupational therapy and group painting art therapy) for 15 weeks; 146 participants (73 per group) completed the intervention. The primary outcomes were medication adherence (MMAS-8) and quality of life (WHOQOL-BREF); secondary outcomes were symptom severity (PANSS), social functioning (SFS), mood (HAMD-17, HAMA-14), and cognition (MoCA). Repeated measures were analyzed with linear mixed-effects models, and an intention-to-treat sensitivity analysis was performed. Group × time estimates favored the observation group for MMAS-8 (β = 1.46, 95% CI [0.98, 1.94]) and the study-defined WHOQOL-BREF composite (β = 12.34, 95% CI [8.77, 15.91]; both FDR p < .001). PANSS, SFS, HAMD-17, HAMA-14, and MoCA also favored the observation group (all FDR p < .001). WHOQOL-BREF domain changes were non-uniform. Recorded adverse-event rates were 16.44% and 19.18% (Fisher exact p = .829). In this single-center trial, the integrated program was associated with greater 15-week improvements in medication adherence, quality of life, and several secondary outcomes than routine nursing alone. Adverse-event rates were similar between groups, but the findings require confirmation in larger multicenter studies using standardized safety assessment.

titre: Severe Motor Deterioration of Young-Onset Parkinson's Disease in Pregnancy Following Medication Rationalisation: A Case Report.
titre_fr: Severe Motor Deterioration of Young-Onset Parkinson's Disease in Pregnancy Following Medication Rationalisation: A Case Report.
auteurs: Naing Ei Ei P, Ko Ko Naw Phu N, Phyu Mya K
resume: Parkinson's disease (PD) in pregnancy is rare, and there are no agreed guidelines for its management. We report a 34-year-old primigravida with a three-year history of young-onset PD who presented at eight weeks' gestation with an unplanned pregnancy. She had previously tolerated levodopa poorly, with nausea and early peak-dose dyskinesia, and before conception her symptoms were reasonably controlled on amantadine, selegiline and procyclidine. Because of the potential teratogenicity of amantadine and limited safety data for the other agents, her treatment was changed to co-careldopa (carbidopa/levodopa) with domperidone. Her condition deteriorated soon after the switch. Despite stepwise increases in levodopa to 400-450 mg/day, by 31 weeks she was wheelchair-dependent, with severe peak-dose dyskinesia alternating with "off" periods and freezing, and she relied on her husband for feeding and personal care. Other drug options and deep brain stimulation were deferred until after delivery. Her care involved neurology, obstetric medicine, obstetric anaesthesia, safeguarding midwives, physiotherapy and occupational therapy, and she received thromboprophylaxis for immobility. She presented in spontaneous labour at 37+5 weeks and underwent a category 2 caesarean section under general anaesthesia, as constant tremor precluded neuraxial anaesthesia. Estimated blood loss was 750 mL. Her daughter had Apgar scores of 4, 7 and 9 at 1, 5 and 10 minutes, respectively, and weighed 2250 g (3.4th centile). Postpartum, dyskinesia and tremor temporarily prevented her from holding her baby, and trihexyphenidyl was started; her symptoms were unchanged five weeks after delivery. In young-onset PD, withdrawal of an effective pre-pregnancy regimen may be followed by significant functional decline, and previous levodopa intolerance may be a warning sign. This case highlights the importance of pre-conception counselling, early multidisciplinary planning and postnatal support.

titre: Traumatic lumbar spondyloptosis, surgical challenges in a low-resource setting: a case report.
titre_fr: Traumatic lumbar spondyloptosis, surgical challenges in a low-resource setting: a case report.
auteurs: Sule Emmanuel L, Mparazo Madai, Massawe Honest H, Ncheye Mathias S, George Gosbert, Mrimba Peter M
revue: International journal of surgery case reports
resume: Traumatic lumbar spondyloptosis is a rare, highly unstable spinal injury caused by high-energy trauma and is commonly associated with complete neurological deficit. Management is particularly challenging in low-resource settings where access to timely surgery may be limited. We report a rare case of traumatic L1-L2 spondyloptosis managed despite a 2-week delay in definitive surgery due to financial constraints. A 26-year-old woman sustained traumatic L1-L2 spondyloptosis following a road-traffic accident and presented with complete paraplegia (ASIA Grade A). Computed tomography confirmed complete vertebral dislocation. Surgery was delayed for 2 weeks because of financial constraints affecting implant procurement. During this period, comprehensive spinal cord injury care, including pressure sore prevention, deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis, bladder and bowel management, chest physiotherapy, pain control, nutritional support, and regular neurological assessment, prevented major complications. Once implants became available, she underwent posterior open reduction and long-segment pedicle screw fixation from T11 to L4. Postoperative rehabilitation included physiotherapy, occupational therapy, bladder and bowel care, and psychological support. At discharge and 4-week follow-up, neurological status remained ASIA A; however, spinal alignment was restored, pain was controlled, the wound healed satisfactorily, and the patient achieved improved sitting balance and wheelchair mobility. This case highlights the importance of comprehensive multidisciplinary care when definitive surgery for traumatic lumbar spondyloptosis is unavoidably delayed. Standard spinal cord injury care prevented complications associated with prolonged immobilization and enabled safe, definitive treatment. Although neurological recovery was not achieved, surgical stabilization restored spinal stability and facilitated rehabilitation and functional independence. This case also contributes to the limited literature on traumatic lumbar spondyloptosis from sub-Saharan Africa. Traumatic lumbar spondyloptosis is a severe spinal injury requiring surgical stabilization and multidisciplinary care. In low-resource settings, appropriate spinal cord injury care during unavoidable surgical delays can prevent secondary complications and facilitate definitive treatment. Even when neurological recovery is not achieved, surgical stabilization can restore alignment, improve pain control, and support rehabilitation and functional independence.

titre: Try This at Home: A Systematic Review of Patient Satisfaction With Stroke Telerehabilitation.
titre_fr: Try This at Home: A Systematic Review of Patient Satisfaction With Stroke Telerehabilitation.
auteurs: Rakic Aleksandra, Fleet Jamie L, Bateman Emma A
resume: Stroke rehabilitation improves patient outcomes but requires timely delivery, sufficient intensity, and adequate participation in appropriate therapies for maximal effectiveness. Unfortunately, many patients experience barriers to accessing conventional in-person rehabilitation. Telerehabilitation may increase access to care and is increasingly used in clinical settings, particularly since the COVID-19 pandemic. However, little is known about patient satisfaction with telerehabilitation. The objective of this systematic review was to examine patient satisfaction with poststroke motor telerehabilitation. MEDLINE, Embase, and PsycINFO databases were searched from database inception to July 2025 inclusive. Two independent reviewers screened articles using the following inclusion criteria: English-language, full-text articles, reporting patient satisfaction outcomes with telerehabilitation for persons with stroke receiving upper or lower limb motor rehabilitation. Studies reporting only caregiver, but not patient satisfaction, were excluded. Study quality was assessed using the PEDro rating scale where appropriate. After removing duplicates, 225 unique articles were reviewed. Nineteen studies published between 2007 and 2025 met inclusion criteria, assessing 811 individuals (n = 4-188, median 24) across 13 countries. Most studies were conducted in the outpatient setting; 3 were in both outpatient and inpatient settings. Fourteen studies (74%) examined telerehabilitation in the chronic phase poststroke, 2 in the acute phase, 2 in the subacute phase, and 1 in both acute and subacute. Ten studies used telerehabilitation for upper limb motor impairment, 2 for lower limb, and 7 for both. Eight controlled trials (7 randomized control trials and 1 nonrandomized control trial) were assessed for quality with PEDro scores ranging from 4 to 8 (median 6). Assessment tools for patient satisfaction varied significantly between studies. Eight unique validated satisfaction tools were used across studies. All studies reported high patient satisfaction ratings with virtual motor telerehabilitation. Although this review found that patient satisfaction ratings were high among studies of telerehabilitation for poststroke motor impairment, there are few high-quality motor telerehabilitation studies, and none focused on satisfaction as their main outcome. Given the importance of telerehabilitation for removing barriers to care, future research should use standardized tools to explore patients' and providers' satisfaction in addition to evaluating efficacy.

titre: Impairment of Contrast Sensitivity Function and Stereopsis in Successfully Treated Bilateral Pediatric Cataract Patients.
titre_fr: Impairment of Contrast Sensitivity Function and Stereopsis in Successfully Treated Bilateral Pediatric Cataract Patients.
auteurs: Li Xin, Song Yunhe, Zhou Fengqi, Chen Hui, Chen Wan, Wang Qiwei, Ye Qingqing, Liu Yizhi, Li Jinrong, Chen Weirong
resume: To evaluate postoperative contrast sensitivity function (CSF) and stereoacuity in children with successfully treated bilateral pediatric cataracts who achieved excellent best-corrected visual acuity (≤0.00 logMAR), and to assess the impact of age at surgery. This retrospective cohort study included 45 children with bilateral pediatric cataracts (90 eyes) and 45 controls. Monocular CSF and stereoacuity were measured. Patients were stratified by age at surgery (<2, 2 to <4, 4 to <6, and ≥6 years) to analyze the effects of surgical timing. Despite a normal best-corrected visual acuity, the cataract group exhibited a lower area under the log CSF than controls (1.42 ± 0.20 vs. 1.49 ± 0.20; P = 0.04) and reduced CS at low-to-medium spatial frequencies (SFs) (1.0, 1.5, 3.0, and 6.0 cycles per degree; all P < 0.05). High SFs (12 and 18 cycles per degree) and cutoff SF were comparable between the groups (all P > 0.05). Age- and sex-adjusted CSF deficits differed across surgical-age subgroups for area under the log CSF, cutoff SF, and several CSF parameters (all P < 0.05), with the ≥6-year-old group showing deficits closest to zero. Stereopsis was significantly impaired in the pediatric cataract group (P < 0.01). Children with successfully treated bilateral pediatric cataracts may exhibit persistent deficits in low-to-medium SF CS and stereopsis despite excellent visual acuity. This pattern may suggest differential developmental trajectories or vulnerability of visual pathways involved in contrast processing. Comprehensive functional assessment and individualized visual rehabilitation are recommended.
resume_fr: To evaluate postoperative contrast sensitivity function (CSF) and stereoacuity in children with successfully treated bilateral pediatric cataracts who achieved excellent best-corrected visual acuity (≤0.00 logMAR), and to assess the impact of age at surgery. This retrospective cohort study included 45 children with bilateral pediatric cataracts (90 eyes) and 45 controls. Monocular CSF and stereoacuity were measured. Patients were stratified by age at surgery (<2, 2 to <4, 4 to <6, and ≥6 years) to analyze the effects of surgical timing. Despite a normal best-corrected visual acuity, the cataract group exhibited a lower area under the log CSF than controls (1.42 ± 0.20 vs. 1.49 ± 0.20; P = 0.04) and reduced CS at low-to-medium spatial frequencies (SFs) (1.0, 1.5, 3.0, and 6.0 cycles per degree; all P < 0.05). High SFs (12 and 18 cycles per degree) and cutoff SF were comparable between the groups (all P > 0.05). Age- and sex-adjusted CSF deficits differed across surgical-age subgroups for area under the log CSF, cutoff SF, and several CSF parameters (all P < 0.05), with the ≥6-year-old group showing deficits closest to zero. Stereopsis was significantly impaired in the pediatric cataract group (P < 0.01). Children with successfully treated bilateral pediatric cataracts may exhibit persistent deficits in low-to-medium SF CS and stereopsis despite excellent visual acuity. This pattern may suggest differential developmental trajectories or vulnerability of visual pathways involved in contrast processing. Comprehensive functional assessment and individualized visual rehabilitation are recommended.

titre: Validity and Reliability of a Thai Version of the Paediatric Haemophilia Activities List.
titre_fr: Validity and Reliability of a Thai Version of the Paediatric Haemophilia Activities List.
auteurs: Simiwanich Saran, Timdang Suttirat, Nuanta Wannika, Pinijpong Ruamporn, Pongtanakul Bunchoo, Kongkasuwan Ratcharin
revue: Haemophilia : the official journal of the World Federation of Hemophilia
resume: The Paediatric Haemophilia Activities List (PedHAL) is a self-administered instrument for assessing activity limitations in children with haemophilia, yet no Thai version has previously undergone psychometric evaluation. To evaluate the validity and reliability of a Thai version of the PedHAL. Following permission from the original developer, the PedHAL was translated into Thai using forward-backwards translation. Content validity was examined via the content validity index (CVI). Construct validity was determined by correlating PedHAL scores with the Functional Independence Score in Haemophilia (FISH) and the Haemophilia Joint Health Score (HJHS). Internal consistency and test-retest reliability were assessed with Cronbach's alpha and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), respectively. The participants were nineteen children with haemophilia who attended the Departments of Rehabilitation Medicine and Paediatrics, Faculty of Medicine Siriraj Hospital, Mahidol University, between June 2021 and September 2022. The Thai PedHAL demonstrated excellent content validity (CVI  =  0.99; threshold  ≥ 0.90) and good construct validity, as evidenced by a strong positive correlation with FISH (r  =  0.703; range 0.70‒0.89) and a moderate negative correlation with HJHS (r  =  -0.475; range 0.40‒0.69). Reliability testing revealed excellent test-retest reliability (ICC  =  0.955; threshold ≥ 0.90) and excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha  =  0.944; threshold ≥ 0.90). The Thai version of the PedHAL has acceptable-to-excellent psychometric properties for measuring activity limitations in Thai children with haemophilia. It may serve as a valuable instrument for both clinical and research applications.

titre: Best Evidence Summary of Phase II Exercise-Based Cardiac Rehabilitation for Patients with Dilated Cardiomyopathy After Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy.
titre_fr: Best Evidence Summary of Phase II Exercise-Based Cardiac Rehabilitation for Patients with Dilated Cardiomyopathy After Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy.
auteurs: Wang Xinglei, Liu Yunyun, Han Leyao, Wang Haixia, Zhang Meishan, Xi Yaya, Xiong Jingying, Dou Xinman
resume: This study aimed to systematically summarize the available evidence on Phase II exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation (CR) for patients with dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) after cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), so as to provide an evidence-based framework for clinical nursing practice. A comprehensive computerized search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, Web of Science, CNKI, WanFang, VIP, and SinoMed, as well as guideline repositories, evidence-based databases, and professional association websites. The included document types were clinical decisions, guidelines, expert consensus or consensus documents, evidence summaries and systematic reviews. Twenty-eight publications were included: 2 clinical decisions, 10 guidelines, 1 systematic review, 11 expert consensus or consensus documents and 4 evidence summaries. A total of 42 pieces of evidence items were summarized across 12 themes: multidisciplinary collaboration, indications and contraindications for exercise rehabilitation, pre-exercise assessment, pre-exercise preparation, exercise prescription, aerobic exercise, resistance training; pulmonary rehabilitation training, flexibility training, personalized adjustment, remote supervision and support, and emergency management. This study synthesized available evidence on Phase II exercise-based CR for patients with DCM after CRT. Most included evidence was derived from broader heart failure or cardiac rehabilitation populations; direct evidence specific to DCM after CRT remains limited. These findings may inform the development of individualized rehabilitation protocols, but recommendations should be applied with caution. This evidence summary was registered with the Fudan University Center for Evidence-Based Nursing (Registration No. ES202610091).

titre: [Treatment of patients with severe functional somatic disorder].
titre_fr: [Treatment of patients with severe functional somatic disorder].
auteurs: Petersen Marie Weinreich, Carlsson Rikke Hinge, Høeg Marian Dalgaard, Thastum Mille Møller, Severin Kåre Eg, Frostholm Lisbeth, Fink Per, Gormsen Lise Kirstine
resume: A national highly specialised inpatient service for patients with severe functional somatic disorder has been established in Denmark. The programme targets a small, highly disabled group not manageable in outpatient care. Treatment includes interdisciplinary assessment, up to 12 weeks of inpatient rehabilitation and follow-up. Among 22 admitted patients in the service centre in Western Denmark, 70% improved in functioning. Early experiences indicate that intensive, structured rehabilitation may improve function and quality of life in this complex patient group, as argued in this review.

titre: Using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health Framework to Document Real-World Functional Outcomes in Inpatient and Outpatient General Rehabilitation.
titre_fr: Using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health Framework to Document Real-World Functional Outcomes in Inpatient and Outpatient General Rehabilitation.
auteurs: Pawlak Karol, Kiedik Dorota, Raulinajtys-Grzybek Monika, Rzymski Piotr, Fal Andrzej
revue: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
resume: BACKGROUND The International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health (ICF) provides a standardized framework for documenting rehabilitation outcomes beyond diagnosis-based reporting. This study aimed to assess the use of ICF-based profiles for describing real-world functional outcomes in inpatient and outpatient general rehabilitation in Poland. MATERIAL AND METHODS A retrospective secondary analysis was conducted using anonymized implementation-pilot data from 674 inpatient and 601 outpatient general rehabilitation patients. ICF qualifiers were recorded at baseline and at the end of rehabilitation for Body Functions, Activities and Participation, and Environmental Factors. RESULTS In Body Functions, significant reductions were observed in both profiles for energy and drive (b130), sleep (b134), emotional (b152), pain (b280), exercise tolerance (b455), urination (b620), joint mobility (b710), and muscle power (b730). In Activities and Participation, inpatient rehabilitation showed significant reductions across all analyzed codes, including daily routine (d230), body position (d410, d415), transferring (d420), walking (d450), self-care (d510-d550), looking after one's health (d570), interpersonal interactions (d710), and remunerative employment (d850). In the outpatient profile, significant changes were observed in most codes, including community mobility (d460), transportation (d470), housework (d640), and assisting others (d660), but not d240, d550, or d920. Environmental Factors were analyzed as facilitators and were stable or changed only minimally over time. CONCLUSIONS ICF-based profiles captured multidimensional functional changes in routine general rehabilitation, while Environmental Factors complemented outcome assessment by describing supportive contextual resources.

titre: The disrupted navigational compass: pathophysiological mechanisms and clinical interventions for spatial navigation deficits.
titre_fr: The disrupted navigational compass: pathophysiological mechanisms and clinical interventions for spatial navigation deficits.
auteurs: Zhen Yuning, Zhang Kuo, Li Shengzhe, He Runnan, Pang Meijun, Liu Haofan, Czosnyka Marek, Czosnyka Zofia, Li Chunyang, Li Chenglong, Song Xizi, Liu Xiuyun, Ming Dong
resume: Spatial navigation is a higher-order integrative cognitive ability that supports environmental orientation, goal-directed route selection, and adaptive locomotion by integrating spatial memory, multisensory cues, attention, and executive control. Neural systems supporting navigation are also vulnerable to aging and neurodegenerative disease, making navigation a useful domain for linking basic mechanisms with clinically measurable functional impairment. This review summarizes spatial-navigation mechanisms across multiple levels. At the cognitive level, navigation depends on interacting processes including spatial representation, path integration, reference-frame transformation, landmark use, and route planning. At the network level, hippocampal-entorhinal, retrosplenial-parietal, scene-selective, and prefrontal systems contribute complementary functions. At the cellular level, place-, grid-, head-direction-, speed-, and boundary-related representations encode position, heading, self-motion, environmental geometry, and prospective behavior. Clinical and neuroimaging studies indicate that navigation impairment is associated with structural and functional abnormalities, with the strongest diagnostic evidence currently arising from Alzheimer's disease and its prodromal stages. VR-based behavioral assessment and electrophysiological approaches provide complementary means of characterizing navigation phenotypes: VR enables controlled, repeatable, process-sensitive tasks, whereas intracranial and scalp recordings provide neural information at different spatial and physiological scales. No pharmacological agent has been developed or licensed specifically for navigation impairment; current navigation-focused interventions therefore rely mainly on behavioral and VR-based rehabilitation, compensatory strategies, and emerging neuromodulation approaches. Future studies should integrate process-specific behavioral and physiological markers with biomarker-defined clinical cohorts, and use large, randomized, longitudinal studies to establish diagnostic validity, real-world transfer, and mechanism-informed intervention effects.

titre: Screening for rehabilitation needs in newly diagnosed breast cancer patients: exploring psychometric properties of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network<sup>®</sup> (NCCN<sup>®</sup>) Distress Thermometer and Problem List.
titre_fr: Screening for rehabilitation needs in newly diagnosed breast cancer patients: exploring psychometric properties of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network<sup>®</sup> (NCCN<sup>®</sup>) Distress Thermometer and Problem List.
auteurs: Velickovic Katarina, Bendahl Pär-Ola, Olsson Möller Ulrika, Rydén Lisa, Malmström Marlene
resume: Identifying and managing distress in breast cancer patients is a crucial element of adequate rehabilitation. Immediately after diagnosis, a brief instrument such as the Distress Thermometer has the potential to aid early assessment of distress. Similarly, the accompanying Problem List can aid identification of sources of distress. The aim of this study was to determine cut-off scores of the Distress Thermometer indicating patients with clinically significant impaired functioning which is likely to reflect distress, to investigate its validity, and explore the measurement properties of the Problem List. 634 Swedish patients participating in the ReScreen​ intervention study [NCT03434717] were included. ROC curve analysis was performed to explore cut-off scores of the Distress Thermometer in relation to emotional, social, cognitive functioning, and global quality of life subscales of the QLQ-C30. The factor structure of the Problem List was assessed using Confirmatory Factor Analysis. Content validity of the Distress Thermometer was assessed in relation to resilience, assessed using the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale. Convergent validity of the Problem List was investigated in relation to resilience and relevant QLQ-C30 subscales. The Distress Thermometer had acceptable accuracy in identifying clinically significant impaired cognitive functioning and global quality of life and excellent relative to emotional and social functioning. A cut-off on the Distress Thermometer between 4 and 5 was found to best balance sensitivity and specificity relative to impaired emotional and social functioning. The Problem List had acceptable model fit. The Distress Thermometer had good content validity and the Problem List convergent validity. The Distress Thermometer and the Problem List have the potential to aid screening for newly diagnosed breast cancer patients with clinically significant impaired functioning. To ensure the responses accurately reflect the patient's life, these tools should be used alongside a clinical interview when assessing dysfunction. A cut-off score on the Distress Thermometer between 4 and 5 best balances false negatives and false positives relative to impaired emotional and social functioning. However, before it is implemented in clinical practice, further validation in external and large cohorts is needed. A qualitative evaluation of the instrument would contribute to its utility.

titre: Digital health tools in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: a cross-sectional survey of orthotists' perspectives.
titre_fr: Digital health tools in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: a cross-sectional survey of orthotists' perspectives.
auteurs: Seng-Iad Sirirat, Poonsiri Jutamanee, Kanda Masaru, Wong Man Sang, Suda Hironori
resume: To explore orthotists' perspectives on the needs and preferences for digital health tools (DHTs) to support patient education, self-management, and treatment adherence in patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) in Thailand. A national cross-sectional survey using a convergent mixed-methods design was conducted among orthotists in Thailand. Quantitative data examined current AIS orthotic practices; perceived effectiveness of existing strategies in patient education, self-management, and treatment adherence; and perspectives on clinical requirements and prioritization of DHT platform features and content. Qualitative data explored clinical challenges, expectations, and implementation considerations. Both findings were subsequently integrated through triangulation for comprehensive interpretation. Ninety-eight orthotists participated in this study. Adherence and self-management monitoring were predominantly subjective and perceived as moderately effective. Participants strongly supported DHTs that enhance patient education, self-management, adherence monitoring, and clinician-patient communication. Participants consistently prioritized patient-centered functions, particularly self-monitoring and educational platforms, over system-level or technology-intensive solutions. Key implementation concerns included data security, clinical reliability, digital inequity, and integration into routine rehabilitation. Thai orthotists demonstrated strong acceptance of DHTs as adjuncts to current AIS orthotic management. The findings identified practice-informed priorities for contextually appropriate DHT design and development for future research, while emphasizing the need to further evaluate usability, feasibility, clinical effectiveness, and routine implementation.

titre: Musculoskeletal pain, functional limitation, and perceived performance anxiety across artistic disciplines: a cross-sectional survey.
titre_fr: Musculoskeletal pain, functional limitation, and perceived performance anxiety across artistic disciplines: a cross-sectional survey.
auteurs: Son Isaac, Gadikota Pranay, Viswanath Omar, Ganti Latha
resume: Repetitive loading and sustained postures can contribute to musculoskeletal symptoms among artists. Psychosocial stress may complicate symptom experiences and the ability to participate in artistic activity. To describe self-reported musculoskeletal pain, participation limitations, perceived relationships with performance anxiety, and openness to supportive care among artists and arts students. A cross-sectional electronic survey recruited 100 U.S. respondents who identified as active instrumentalists, vocalists, actors, or ceramic artists. A screening item and 13 survey questions assessed practice characteristics, pain, anxiety, participation restrictions, self-management, and care preferences. Responses were summarized descriptively. Forty-six respondents (46%) reported current activity-associated musculoskeletal pain. Thirty-two (32%) reported having reduced practice or withdrawn from a performance because of pain; 39% selected continuing to play despite pain as a management strategy, and 22% selected consultation with a physician or physical therapist. High pre-performance anxiety (ratings of 4-5/5) was reported by 58%. Forty-one percent perceived a bidirectional anxiety-pain relationship, while 76% were very or somewhat likely to use supportive services. In this exploratory sample, self-reported musculoskeletal pain was accompanied by meaningful participation limitations and a perceived psychosocial burden. Findings support further investigation of performance-specific orthopedic assessment and rehabilitation, but do not establish clinical diagnoses, causal relationships, or population prevalence.
