titre: Artificial Intelligence in Coronary Artery Disease: From Detection to Precision Management.
titre_fr: Artificial Intelligence in Coronary Artery Disease: From Detection to Precision Management.
auteurs: Garg Keshav, Bruich Landon, Enemark Luke J, Sawalha Khalid, Rana Aakash, Agrawal Ankit, Spraggins Robert F, Khalaila Osama, Shehadeh Mohanad, Alhwarat Buthainah, Johnson Carsten, Guha Avirup, Zhang Yiye, Pontone Gianluca, Dani Sourbha S, Chindambaram Vignesh, Baskaran Lohendran, Tayal Bhupendar, Al'Aref Subhi J
resume: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, yet the landscape is rapidly evolving as artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to its detection, diagnosis, and management. This review surveys the expanding role of AI across the full spectrum of CAD care. In screening, deep-learning electrocardiography and electronic health record-based digital markers enable earlier identification of clinically significant disease. In noninvasive imaging, AI-driven coronary computed tomography angiography automates calcium scoring, derives fractional flow reserve without invasive wires, and quantifies high-risk plaque features that predict incident adverse events. Within the cardiac catheterization laboratory, angiography-derived physiologic assessment and AI-guided intravascular imaging segmentation support real-time procedural decision-making. Beyond diagnosis, machine-learning models integrating multimodality imaging data improve risk stratification over conventional clinical scores, while pharmacogenomic algorithms and wearable-based digital rehabilitation platforms enable patient-centric secondary prevention. Despite this progress, significant challenges persist, including limited evidence from randomized trials, algorithmic bias in underrepresented populations, regulatory uncertainty surrounding software-as-a-medical-device frameworks, and the risk of clinician de-skilling. AI has the potential to act as a collaborative tool that augments-rather than replaces-physician judgment. Future directions include foundation models, multiomics integration, agentic AI workflows, and equity-centered deployment strategies to ensure that AI-driven advances benefit all individuals with CAD.

titre: Therapy onset and characteristics associated with improvement following HABIT-ILE in infants with unilateral cerebral palsy: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Therapy onset and characteristics associated with improvement following HABIT-ILE in infants with unilateral cerebral palsy: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Carton de Tournai Astrid, Herman Enimie, Ebner-Karestinos Daniela, Gathy Estelle, Araneda Rodrigo, Renders Anne, De Clerck Célia, Kilcioglu Seyma, Vandermeeren Yves, Bleyenheuft Yannick
resume: To explore the association between therapy onset and changes in motor and functional outcomes and identify characteristics associated with greater changes in infants with unilateral cerebral palsy (UCP) following Hand-Arm Bimanual Intensive Therapy-Including Lower Extremities (HABIT-ILE). This study included 38 infants aged 6 to 20 months (mean = 14.4 ± 4.3 months) with UCP. All received 50 h of HABIT-ILE and were assessed pre-intervention and 3 months later. Outcomes included Mini-Assisting Hand Assessment (Mini-AHA; primary), Gross Motor Function Measure-66 (GMFM-66) and Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM). Regression analyses explored changes in outcomes in relation to age at therapy onset, prematurity, type and side of lesion, and baseline motor abilities. Age at therapy onset was not significantly associated with changes in Mini-AHA or COPM satisfaction scores. However, younger age was associated with larger changes in the GMFM-66 and the COPM performance scores. Regarding baseline characteristics associated with greater improvement, the baseline GMFM-66 score was associated with changes in GMFM-66. These exploratory analyses found that younger age at therapy initiation was associated with larger changes in GMFM-66 and COPM performance scores, suggesting that early therapy onset may be associated with greater improvements in gross motor and functional performance. Baseline gross motor abilities were also associated with changes following HABIT-ILE, suggesting that these characteristics may contribute to variability in observed changes and warrant further investigation in larger studies. https://clinicaltrials.gov/, identifier NCT04698395.
resume_fr: To explore the association between therapy onset and changes in motor and functional outcomes and identify characteristics associated with greater changes in infants with unilateral cerebral palsy (UCP) following Hand-Arm Bimanual Intensive Therapy-Including Lower Extremities (HABIT-ILE). These exploratory analyses found that younger age at therapy initiation was associated with larger changes in GMFM-66 and COPM performance scores, suggesting that early therapy onset may be associated with greater improvements in gross motor and functional performance. titre: Arthroscopy Resources and Service Availability in Tanzania: A National Multidomain Assessment.
titre_fr: Arthroscopy Resources and Service Availability in Tanzania: A National Multidomain Assessment.
auteurs: Issa Samih, Nungu Kitugi, Zacharia Joel, Muhamedhussein Mohamed, Sabas Joseph, Fabian Francis, Hussein Adam, Kisanga Allen, Mrita Felix
resume: Background: Arthroscopy requires specialised personnel, equipment, and reliable supplies. Resource deficiencies have been documented in sub-Saharan Africa, but national data from Tanzania are lacking. Objective: To assess arthroscopy resources and service availability in Tanzanian hospitals providing specialist orthopaedic care and examine differences by hospital tier and ownership. Methods: A national cross-sectional survey was conducted between January and February 2025 using orthopaedic surgeons as key informants to provide hospital-level data from their primary hospitals of practice. The hospital was the unit of analysis. Arthroscopy-related resources were assessed across five domains: personnel, infrastructure, procedures, equipment, and supplies. Overall resource availability was summarised using a study-specific Arthroscopy Resource Availability Score (ARAS) and compared across hospital tiers. Findings: A total of 171 orthopaedic surgeons responded (response rate, 77.7%), providing data on 92 hospitals. Seven hospitals (7.6%) offered arthroscopy services, six of which were in Dar es Salaam. Arthroscopy surgeons were available in eight hospitals (8.7%). Although anaesthesia, rehabilitation, and supporting surgical infrastructure were widely available, 75.0% of hospitals lacked arthroscopy instruments. Arthroscopy-specific equipment, consumables, and implants were available in fewer than 15% of hospitals. Most facilities (83; 90.2%) had low resource availability (ARAS <50%). Median ARAS was 21.9% (IQR, 18.8-28.1), with higher scores in higher-tier than lower-tier hospitals (40.6% vs. 21.9%; P < 0.001). Hospitals offering arthroscopy were more likely to be higher-tier facilities (RR, 5.2; 95% CI, 2.6-10.4; P < 0.001). Conclusions: Arthroscopy services were uncommon among the hospitals assessed and concentrated in higher-tier facilities, predominantly in Dar es Salaam. Planning service expansion should consider coordinated workforce development, equipment maintenance, reliable supplies, and institutional support. Phased development through selected referral centres warrants consideration, although its feasibility and effectiveness require further assessment.

titre: Cervical epidural spinal cord stimulation is associated with enhanced voluntary upper-limb muscle activation in chronic post-stroke hemiparesis: a pilot feasibility study.
titre_fr: Cervical epidural spinal cord stimulation is associated with enhanced voluntary upper-limb muscle activation in chronic post-stroke hemiparesis: a pilot feasibility study.
auteurs: Wu Ciou-Chan, Huang Hsiang-Ling, Chen Yu-Chen, Wang Po-Kai, Wu Ming-Yung, Yan Lian-Cing, Lin Shinn-Zong, Tsai Sheng-Tzung
resume: Upper-limb hemiparesis is a prevalent and often refractory sequela of stroke, and conventional rehabilitation approaches often yield limited long-term gains in the chronic phase. Cervical epidural electrical stimulation (EES) has emerged as a promising precision neurorehabilitation strategy to amplify residual corticospinal drive through contact-specific modulation of spinal interneuron excitability. However, the relationship between individual cervical motor recruitment patterns and functional recovery has not been systematically characterized in stroke survivors. Therefore, the present prospective pilot study investigated contact-specific motor mapping and the acute effects of cervical EES on voluntary upper-limb muscle activation in four participants with chronic post-stroke hemiparesis. Four adults with chronic post-stroke hemiparesis (time since stroke 6-28 months; baseline Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity [FMA-UE] scores 6-35) underwent bilateral percutaneous cervical epidural lead implantation spanning C3-T1. Intraoperative contact-specific motor mapping was performed through bipolar stimulation at 2 Hz, yielding individualized cervical recruitment maps that informed subsequent parameter selection. Task-related surface electromyography (EMG) was then recorded under EES-On and EES-Off conditions across six standardized upper-limb movements; EES-On/EES-Off amplitude ratios served as indices of acute stimulation effects. Clinical assessments, including the FMA-UE, Action Research Arm Test (ARAT), and Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS), were administered at baseline and 12-28 days after implantation, with EES active. Intraoperative mapping showed a level-dependent proximal-to-distal pattern of muscle recruitment consistent with cervical somatotopic organization. EES-On was associated with higher voluntary EMG amplitude in most muscles and tasks, with EES-On/EES-Off ratios of up to 11.4 in the wrist flexor during grasping. All four participants had higher FMA-UE scores at the post-implantation assessment (range +4 to +8 points), with changes in three participants falling within or above the published minimal clinically important difference range, and ARAT scores increased in all four participants (+1 to +6 points). Elbow flexor tone increased in two participants, and no serious adverse events occurred. Collectively, these preliminary findings suggest that contact-specific cervical EES, informed by individualized motor mapping, may represent a feasible adjunct intervention for upper-limb rehabilitation following chronic stroke, and provide a neurophysiological rationale for future controlled trials. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05981989.

titre: Cerebral blood flow asymmetry in motor-related regions is associated with 30-day upper-limb motor recovery after acute ischemic stroke.
titre_fr: Cerebral blood flow asymmetry in motor-related regions is associated with 30-day upper-limb motor recovery after acute ischemic stroke.
auteurs: Shi Yongwei, Lv Yichen, Gao Shaoge, Bi Cancan, Hu Fangju, Zhu Xi, Zhou Hongyu, Wang Xin
resume: Upper-limb motor impairment is a leading cause of long-term disability after acute ischemic stroke (AIS), yet early prognostication relies mainly on clinical scales. Cerebral blood flow (CBF) asymmetry measured by arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion MRI may indicate recovery potential. We investigated whether acute-phase CBF asymmetry indices (AIs) in six motor-related regions are associated with 30-day upper-limb motor recovery. Sixty patients with AIS underwent pseudo-continuous ASL MRI within 72 h of onset and completed the 30-day Fugl-Meyer Assessment of the Upper Extremity (FMA-UE). Patients were classified into good (n = 30, ΔFMA-UE ≥ 10) and poor (n = 30, ΔFMA-UE ≤ 4) recovery groups; both thresholds lie outside the published minimal clinically important difference range, and no patient fell between them. Mean CBF was extracted bilaterally from the precentral and postcentral gyri, supplementary motor area, putamen, pallidum, and thalamus, and AIs were calculated. Regional AI-ΔFMA-UE associations were assessed with Spearman correlation, partial correlation, analysis of covariance, and linear regression. Precentral and postcentral gyrus AIs each correlated positively with ΔFMA-UE (both Spearman r = 0.30, p = 0.020; false-discovery-rate q = 0.020), persisting after adjustment for cognitive status, baseline FMA-UE, and lesion volume (partial r up to 0.326; all p < 0.05); other regional AIs showed negligible correlations (|r| < 0.09). In analysis of covariance (follow-up FMA-UE as outcome, baseline FMA-UE as covariate), precentral gyrus AI remained associated with the outcome (β = 0.13, 95% CI 0.01-0.25, p = 0.037; after cognitive adjustment, p = 0.045). A model combining the six AIs with age and cognitive status explained 29.7% of variance in ΔFMA-UE (F(8,51) = 2.69, p = 0.015), but adding the AIs to clinical variables alone did not significantly improve explanatory performance (ΔR2 = 0.048, p = 0.170); this R2 reflects the combined imaging-clinical model rather than ASL alone. Sensorimotor-cortex CBF asymmetry within 72 h of onset was associated with 30-day upper-limb motor recovery after AIS, robust to adjustment for clinical variables. Acute-phase ASL may serve as a noninvasive imaging indicator for recovery-oriented rehabilitation stratification, a hypothesis requiring further validation.

titre: Development of a Decision-Tree Model to Stratify Walking Independence at Discharge Using Admission Information in Patients with Stroke in a Convalescent Rehabilitation Ward: Evaluation of Its Validity as a Bedside Decision-Support Tool.
titre_fr: Development of a Decision-Tree Model to Stratify Walking Independence at Discharge Using Admission Information in Patients with Stroke in a Convalescent Rehabilitation Ward: Evaluation of Its Validity as a Bedside Decision-Support Tool.
auteurs: Ikeue Koichi, Funabiki Keisuke, Nakatani Yuya, Tanaka Hiroki, Toratsu Hiroshi, Mochi Shusuke
revue: Japanese journal of comprehensive rehabilitation science
resume: Ikeue K, Funabiki K, Nakatani Y, Tanaka H, Toratsu H, Mochi S. Development of a Decision-Tree Model to Stratify Walking Independence at Discharge Using Admission Information in Patients with Stroke in a Convalescent Rehabilitation Ward: Evaluation of Its Validity as a Bedside Decision-Support Tool. Jpn J Compr Rehabil Sci 2026; 17: 59-67. Early identification of the likelihood of walking independence at discharge after stroke is important for goal setting and discharge planning. Herein, we aimed to develop a decision-tree model to stratify walking independence at discharge using admission variables in patients with hemiplegia after a first-ever stroke and to evaluate its internal validity, agreement between predicted probabilities and observed outcomes, and group-specific patterns of attaining walking independence. This study included 228 patients admitted to a convalescent rehabilitation ward between January 2020 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a Functional Independence Measure (FIM) walking score of ≥6 at discharge. Candidate predictors included age, sex, stroke subtype, paretic side, days from stroke onset to admission, ability to sit up, lower-extremity Fugl-Meyer Assessment, Berg Balance Scale (BBS), and total motor and cognitive FIM scores. The model was evaluated using tenfold cross-validation and bootstrap resampling. For each terminal node, the proportions of patients attaining walking independence within 90 and 120 days after stroke onset were calculated. Walking independence at discharge was achieved by 116 patients. The decision tree stratified the patients into six groups with different rates of walking independence at discharge based on the total cognitive FIM score, BBS or total motor FIM score, and age. The optimism-corrected area under the curve was 0.888, the Brier score was 0.115, and the calibration slope was 0.893. The terminal nodes included groups with high rates of both walking independence at discharge and attainment within 90 days; a group with an intermediate rate of walking independence at discharge, no attainment within 90 days, but 46.2% attaining independence within 120 days; and groups with low or moderate rates of walking independence at discharge and little additional attainment after 90 days. This model could serve as a supplementary stratification tool by providing group-level information on differences in the likelihood of walking independence at discharge and the timing of its attainment.

titre: Readiness for stoma reversal in patients with a diverting stoma: a concept analysis.
titre_fr: Readiness for stoma reversal in patients with a diverting stoma: a concept analysis.
auteurs: Zhou Xian, Xu Wen, Zeng Yu, Han Sixuan, Hong Yanyan
resume: Readiness for stoma reversal is an important concept for patients with a diverting stoma during the transition from "living with a stoma" to "resumption of transanal defecation and adaptation to postoperative bowel function." However, its conceptual meaning remains unclear, limiting the development of related research and clinical practice. Therefore, it is necessary to clearly define the concept of readiness for stoma reversal in patients with a diverting stoma. To clarify the concept of readiness for stoma reversal in patients with a diverting stoma using Rodgers' evolutionary concept analysis. Relevant studies on readiness for stoma reversal in patients with a diverting stoma were systematically searched in PubMed, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, CINAHL, the Cochrane Library, Embase, CNKI, Wanfang Data, and VIP Database. Rodgers' evolutionary concept analysis was used to synthesize and analyze the included studies. The conceptual attributes, antecedents, consequences, and related concepts of readiness for stoma reversal in patients with a diverting stoma were extracted and summarized. The core attributes of readiness for stoma reversal in patients with a diverting stoma include pre-reversal assessment, physical and functional readiness, information and knowledge readiness, and psychological readiness. The main antecedents included rectal cancer control and anastomotic healing, systematic health education and health literacy, socioeconomic conditions and support systems, and multidisciplinary assessment and collaboration. For patients, adequate readiness may facilitate bowel function recovery, enhance engagement in rehabilitation and self-management, reduce anxiety and fear, lower the risk of postoperative complications, and improve quality of life. For healthcare systems, it may help shorten hospital stays, reduce readmissions and other unplanned healthcare use, and lower related medical costs. Readiness for stoma reversal is a multidimensional and dynamic state that develops before reversal in patients with a diverting stoma. It reflects the patient's ability to cope with stoma reversal, bowel function recovery after reversal, and related lifestyle changes. Clarifying the attributes, antecedents, and consequences of this concept may support the development of assessment tools for readiness for stoma reversal. It may also provide a basis for designing individualized and continuous nursing interventions.

titre: Self-Reported Handicap and Pain in Multiple Sclerosis: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of the London Handicap Scale and Disability Status in a Slovak Neurorehabilitation Cohort.
titre_fr: Self-Reported Handicap and Pain in Multiple Sclerosis: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of the London Handicap Scale and Disability Status in a Slovak Neurorehabilitation Cohort.
auteurs: Mikuľáková Wioletta, Pobrotyn Piotr, Paprocka-Borowicz Małgorzata, Rosińczuk Joanna
resume: Background/Objectives: Handicap (participation restriction) and pain are clinically important but under-investigated outcomes in multiple sclerosis (MS). We examined the London Handicap Scale (LHS) and pain (Visual Analogue Scale, VAS) in relation to disability and other clinical variables. Methods: This secondary, cross-sectional, non-interventional analysis included 65 Slovak patients with MS (study group, SG, n = 32, designated for a 12-week neurorehabilitation program; control group, CG, n = 33, waitlisted), all assessed before rehabilitation. Associations were tested with Spearman correlation (Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted) and linear regression; groups were compared with the Mann-Whitney test. Results: Disability (EDSS) correlated with LHS (ρ = -0.667) and VAS pain (ρ = 0.457; both p < 0.001), although SF-36 measures correlated more strongly. In adjusted models, EDSS was the only significant predictor, explaining 44.1% of the variance in LHS and 21.1% in VAS pain. LHS and VAS pain did not differ between SG and CG (p = 0.936 and p = 0.770) but differed across EDSS severity subgroups (p < 0.001 and p = 0.007). Conclusions: EDSS is a significant but partial correlate of handicap and pain, supporting their assessment alongside disability staging. The baseline group comparison is descriptive and provides no evidence about the effects of neurorehabilitation.

titre: Residual Postural-Control Differences After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: Dual-Task Postural Control and Associations with Time Since Return to Sport.
titre_fr: Residual Postural-Control Differences After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: Dual-Task Postural Control and Associations with Time Since Return to Sport.
auteurs: Alshehri Shaker Hassan S, Algarni Nizar, Alkhamis Batool Abdulelah, Koura Ghada Mohamed, Elshiwi Ahmed Mohamed Fathi, Kardm Saleh M, Alqahtani Amal Awad Saeed, Reddy Ravi Shankar, Gautam Ajay Prashad, Ali Zeinab A, Al Ahmari Maram Y
resume: Background/Objectives: Residual sensorimotor deficits may persist after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR), even after clearance for unrestricted sport. This study compared unilateral postural control between individuals after ACLR and healthy controls under visual deprivation and cognitive dual-task conditions and examined associations between dual-task cost and time since reconstruction and return to activity. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 35 physically active adults 9-24 months after primary unilateral ACLR and 35 age-, sex-, body mass index-, and activity-matched controls. Force-platform posturography measured center-of-pressure (COP) path length, ellipse area, and mean velocity during unilateral stance with eyes open, eyes closed, and concurrent serial subtraction. COP path-length dual-task cost (DTC) was compared between groups and limbs. Correlation and multiple linear regression analyses examined associations with postoperative and return-to-activity duration. Results: Eyes-closed COP path length was greater in reconstructed limbs than in control reference limbs (720.00 ± 118.00 versus 552.00 ± 92.00 mm; p < 0.001). Reconstructed-limb DTC exceeded control reference-limb DTC (17.45 ± 10.20% versus 6.97 ± 6.80%; p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.21) and contralateral-limb DTC (11.00 ± 8.40%; p < 0.001). Longer time since ACLR (r = -0.38; p = 0.024) and return to unrestricted activity (r = -0.44; p = 0.008) were associated with lower DTC. Both associations remained significant in a two-predictor regression model (adjusted R2 = 0.20). Conclusions: Postural-control differences persisted after ACLR despite clearance for unrestricted activity and were more evident under visual deprivation and cognitive loading. These cross-sectional associations support further investigation of dual-task posturography in postoperative assessment. The clinical significance and predictive value of these static posturographic measures for return-to-sport readiness and subsequent injury risk remain to be established.

Results: Eyes-closed COP path length was greater in reconstructed limbs than in control reference limbs (720.00 ± 118.00 versus 552.00 ± 92.00 mm; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Postural-control differences persisted after ACLR despite clearance for unrestricted activity and were more evident under visual deprivation and cognitive loading. titre: Variations in Assessment Methods of Heterogeneous Exercise Capacity Response After Cardiac Rehabilitation.
titre_fr: Variations in Assessment Methods of Heterogeneous Exercise Capacity Response After Cardiac Rehabilitation.
auteurs: Kurpaska Małgorzata, Piotrowicz Katarzyna, Kubiak Marzena, Alisz Katarzyna, Krzesiński Paweł
resume: Background: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) improves the prognosis of patients with cardiac diseases by, among other measures, improving exercise capacity (EC) as assessed according to different parameters. Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of phase II of CR on the different measurements of EC and to assess the distribution of changes in these measurements among patients who underwent the intervention. Methods: From a single-center retrospective registry, records of 295 patients who underwent the six-minute walk test (6MWT) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing twice during CR were evaluated. The distance of the 6MWT, peak oxygen uptake (VO2) expressed in absolute values and as a percentage of predicted values, and workload on a cycle ergometer were assessed before and after CR and then analyzed. Results: Among the 295 patients (228 men, mean age 62 years [range: 55-69 years]), CR resulted in improvements in the median value of peak VO2 (approximately 1 mL/kg/min, 3% of the predicted value), workload (by approximately 5 watt), and 6MWT distance (by approximately 24 m, 5% of the predicted value). A total of 53.6% of the patients achieved an improvement in peak VO2 of ≥1 mL/kg/min and 44.1% of the patients achieved an improvement in 6MWT distance of >30 m. Simultaneous improvement in both peak VO2 and 6MWT distance was observed in 23% of the participants, whereas 26% did not achieve clinically meaningful improvement in either parameter. Conclusions: CR improved exercise capacity, although the proportion of patients who achieved clinically meaningful improvement differed substantially across the exercise capacity measurements.

titre: Clinical Assessment and Exercise Rehabilitation of Sarcopenia in Cardiovascular Disease.
titre_fr: Clinical Assessment and Exercise Rehabilitation of Sarcopenia in Cardiovascular Disease.
auteurs: Jeong Soon Il, Baek Un Hyo, Bang Hyun Seok, Seo Dae Yun
resume: Sarcopenia complicates cardiovascular disease, but diagnostic definitions and outcome selection can substantially alter the interpretation of exercise rehabilitation. This critical review examines how these differences affect the translation of muscle biology into clinical assessment and treatment, with heart failure as the principal clinical setting. Targeted literature retrieval prioritized recent consensus statements, clinical studies, and intervention trials, while experimental evidence was considered separately. Human biopsy studies associate inflammatory and mitochondrial abnormalities with muscle dysfunction; causal manipulation of muscle-derived signaling remains predominantly experimental. European and Asian consensus frameworks differ in their thresholds and the diagnostic role of physical performance. These distinctions matter because trials frequently enroll patients with frailty or exercise intolerance without confirming sarcopenia. Resistance and combined interventions improve selected measures of strength or physical performance, whereas muscle quantity, diagnostic status, and clinical events may respond differently. A small coronary artery disease trial provides direct, short-term evidence in confirmed sarcopenia, but durability remains uncertain. Rehabilitation should therefore link an explicit diagnostic framework to individualized exercise, nutritional assessment, and repeated measurement of the intended outcomes. Future trials should establish whether improvements in defining muscle components persist and translate into sustained independence and fewer clinical events.

titre: Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis-Derived Phase Angle in Initial Medical and Nursing Assessment for Cardiac Rehabilitation: Association with Cardiac Rehabilitation Risk Category and Longitudinal Change During the Program-An Exploratory Prospective Observational Study.
titre_fr: Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis-Derived Phase Angle in Initial Medical and Nursing Assessment for Cardiac Rehabilitation: Association with Cardiac Rehabilitation Risk Category and Longitudinal Change During the Program-An Exploratory Prospective Observational Study.
auteurs: Rodríguez-Velasco Francisco José, Becerra-Mejías José Alberto, Lara-Godoy Luis Miguel, Yuste-Domínguez María, Carmona-Blesa Julio, Gil-Fernández Guadalupe
resume: Background: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) reduces cardiovascular mortality and improves quality of life in coronary patients. Risk stratification at program onset is essential for individualizing exercise prescription. Phase angle (PhA), derived from bioelectrical impedance analysis, is an index of cell membrane integrity that has emerged as a functional biomarker in various clinical populations. Its utility at the onset of a phase II CR program has not been explored in the Spanish context. This study evaluated the association of PhA with CR risk category, functional capacity and quality of life, its change during the program, and its incremental value over the Duke Treadmill Score (DTS) and clinical variables for risk classification in patients beginning phase II CR. Methods: This was an exploratory prospective longitudinal observational study with repeated measures. A total of 109 patients with ischemic heart disease (86.2% male; mean age: 60.2 ± 7.6 years) enrolled in an 8-week phase II CR program (Badajoz, Spain) were included. Phase angle was measured with a multifrequency bioimpedance analyzer (TANITA MC-780MA) under standardized conditions at baseline and program completion. Non-parametric tests (Wilcoxon, Mann-Whitney U, and Spearman correlation), multivariable models adjusted for potential confounders, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis with incremental-value metrics, and a classification and regression tree (CART) evaluated with standard, repeated and nested stratified cross-validation were applied. Results: Baseline PhA was significantly higher in the low-risk group than in the high-risk group (5.43 ± 0.65° vs. 4.98 ± 0.81°; U = 1568.5; p = 0.002; rank-biserial r = 0.38). PhA correlated positively with the Duke Treadmill Score (r_s = +0.268; p = 0.005), physical functioning (r_s = +0.291; p = 0.002), vitality (r_s = +0.265; p = 0.005) and grip strength (r_s = +0.196; p = 0.041), and inversely with age (r_s = -0.288; p = 0.002) and the comorbidity index (r_s = -0.198; p = 0.039). High-risk status remained associated with lower PhA after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, comorbidity, LVEF, diabetes, revascularization type and time since the event (β = -0.49°; p = 0.002). PhA alone showed moderate discrimination (AUC = 0.689; 95% CI: 0.574-0.803); adding PhA to the DTS did not improve discrimination (ΔAUC = +0.004; p = 0.748); and a CART model combining DTS, PhA and grip strength (cross-validated accuracy: 85.2%) classified patients identically to the DTS alone. Without the DTS, adding PhA to a clinical model improved model fit and reclassification (likelihood-ratio p = 0.003; NRI = 0.64) without a significant AUC gain (+0.067; p = 0.106). After 8 weeks, PhA increased slightly (5.27 → 5.33°; p = 0.016); the mean change was small (95% CI: 0.01-0.10°) and was not associated with functional changes, and its clinical relevance is uncertain because repeatability data were not available. Conclusions: Phase angle is lower in high-risk CR patients independently of age, sex, body composition and comorbidity and correlates weakly to moderately with functional capacity and quality of life. However, it did not add discriminative value to the DTS, and the clinical relevance of its small mean change during the program is uncertain. These exploratory findings show associations only: neither the standalone use of PhA nor its added value over the DTS for risk stratification has been established, and its use for monitoring the response to rehabilitation has not been validated.

titre: Comparative Outcomes of Surgical and Non-Surgical Treatment in Patients with Lumbar Radiculopathy: A Six-Month Analysis of Quality of Life and Functional Status.
titre_fr: Comparative Outcomes of Surgical and Non-Surgical Treatment in Patients with Lumbar Radiculopathy: A Six-Month Analysis of Quality of Life and Functional Status.
auteurs: Mahmutović Elvis, Safiye Teodora, Minić Slaviša, Zeljković Vesna, Bajin Zoran, Salihagić Zerina, Ajdinović Aldina, Komatina Hristina, Gusinac Bošnjak Medina, Sokolović Almasa, Dolićanin Zana, Biševac Emir
resume: Background/Objectives: Lumbar radiculopathy can be managed non-surgically or surgically; however, comparative changes in quality of life and functional status between these treatment pathways remain clinically relevant. Therefore, this study aimed to compare six-month outcomes in patients treated non-surgically and those treated with lumbar microdiscectomy followed by rehabilitation. Methods: A prospective, non-randomized comparative cohort study included 100 patients with discogenic lumbar radiculopathy: 50 treated non-surgically and 50 treated by lumbar microdiscectomy. Both groups underwent medical rehabilitation and were assessed at admission, three months, and six months using the Short Form-36 Health Survey (SF-36), including the Physical Component Summary (PCS) and Mental Component Summary (MCS), and the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Results: PCS improved from 35.5 to 50.8 in the non-surgical group and from 28.8 to 49.2 in the surgical group. PCS was significantly higher in non-surgically treated patients at admission (p < 0.001) and three months (p < 0.05), whereas the difference was not significant at six months (p = 0.064). No between-group differences were found for MCS at admission, three months, or six months (p = 0.104, p = 0.871, and p = 0.323, respectively). ODI decreased from 51.5% to 22.5% in the non-surgical group and from 56.1% to 23.7% in the surgical group, without significant between-group differences at any assessment (p = 0.109, p = 0.162, and p = 0.427). Conclusions: Both treatment pathways were associated with substantial improvement. The initial between-group difference in physical quality of life diminished during follow-up, while mental quality of life and disability outcomes were similar between groups.

titre: Association Between Daily Energy Intake and Cognitive Recovery After Mechanical Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
titre_fr: Association Between Daily Energy Intake and Cognitive Recovery After Mechanical Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
auteurs: Arnăutu Sergiu Florin, Arnăutu Diana Aurora, Patankar Tufail, Shariq Mohd, Qazi Hamood, Lewis Martin, Sciacca Sara, Jianu Dragoș Cătălin, Crețu Octavian M, Sandesc Dorel, Malița Claudiu-Daniel, Juratu Cătălin, Bernad Brenda-Cristiana, Lynch Jeremy
resume: Background: Post-stroke cognitive impairment is a common complication associated with reduced functional independence and quality of life. Although adequate daily energy intake is considered an essential component of stroke rehabilitation, its association with cognitive recovery after mechanical thrombectomy remains poorly understood. This study investigated the relationship between daily energy intake and 90-day cognitive outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke treated with mechanical thrombectomy. Methods: This multicenter retrospective observational cohort study included 100 consecutive patients undergoing mechanical thrombectomy between 1 April 2025 and 1 April 2026 at stroke centers in the United Kingdom and Romania. Daily energy and macronutrient intake were retrospectively extracted from routine clinical records and normalized to body weight (kcal/kg/day). Daily energy intake was evaluated primarily as a continuous exposure (kcal/kg/day), while the originally defined 31 kcal/kg/day grouping was retained for exploratory categorical analyses. Cognitive performance was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) at baseline and, among survivors with available cognitive follow-up, at 90 days. The primary multivariable model evaluated daily energy intake (kcal/kg/day) as a continuous exposure and adjusted for baseline MoCA, atrial fibrillation, chronic coronary artery disease, admission NIHSS, C-reactive protein, and PICA/AICA/SCA occlusion. HC3 heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors were used for robust inference. Results: Among patients with available 90-day cognitive assessment, those with higher energy intake achieved significantly higher 90-day MoCA scores than those with lower intake (24.2 ± 2.1 vs. 20.0 ± 1.5; p < 0.001) and greater cognitive improvement (ΔMoCA: 3.82 ± 1.08 vs. 0.48 ± 0.54 points; p < 0.001). In the primary continuous-exposure model, each additional 1 kcal/kg/day was associated with a 0.18-point higher 90-day MoCA score after multivariable adjustment (β = 0.179, HC3 95% CI 0.081-0.278; p < 0.001). The association remained similar in an expanded sensitivity model addressing available indicators of baseline severity (β = 0.176, HC3 95% CI 0.071-0.281; p = 0.002). Exploratory categorical analyses also showed higher 90-day MoCA scores in the higher-intake group. No significant differences were observed in NIHSS or mRS at 90 days. Conclusions: Higher daily energy intake was associated with higher 90-day cognitive performance among survivors with available cognitive follow-up after mechanical thrombectomy. Given the retrospective observational design, baseline differences between exposure groups, and potential residual confounding and reverse causality, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Prospective studies are required to determine whether nutritional optimization can influence cognitive recovery after stroke.

titre: Exploratory Evaluation of the Statistical Fidelity of Large Language Model-Generated Synthetic Rehabilitation Data for Patients with Hip Fracture.
titre_fr: Exploratory Evaluation of the Statistical Fidelity of Large Language Model-Generated Synthetic Rehabilitation Data for Patients with Hip Fracture.
auteurs: Momosaki Ryo, Ushida Kenta, Yamamoto Yoshinori, Shimizu Akio
resume: Background/Objectives: Synthetic data generated from aggregate statistics may support preliminary clinical research when patient-level data access is restricted. However, statistical similarity does not establish clinical validity, analytical utility, or privacy protection. We evaluated three datasets independently generated by large language models (LLMs) for patients with hip fractures. Methods: Of 26,637 hospitalization records, 12,130 complete eligible records were identified, and 1000 were reproducibly sampled. Aggregate statistics for 12 variables were provided to three LLMs, each generating one 1000-record dataset. We assessed fidelity to prompted marginal targets, preservation of unsupplied distributional and correlation structures, logical plausibility, and performance in an exploratory regression task predicting discharge Barthel Index scores. Results: Mean absolute standardized mean differences (SMDs) were 0.164, 0.027, and 0.001 for GPT, Claude, and Gemini, respectively. Mean absolute differences across 36 correlations were 0.090, 0.113, and 0.105, respectively; maximum correlation discrepancies were 0.411, 0.713, and 0.262. In train-on-synthetic/test-on-real evaluations, R2 values were 0.167, -0.080, and 0.146, respectively, compared with 0.262 for five-fold cross-validation on real data. Conclusions: The three individual LLM-generated datasets reproduced prompted marginal targets with varying fidelity but did not consistently preserve unsupplied multivariable structures or achieve comparable task-specific performance. These exploratory findings do not establish definitive model rankings, demonstrate clinical validity or privacy protection, or support replacing real patient-level data with synthetic data.

titre: An Integrated Dual Framework for the Design and Reporting of MI and SSVEP Brain-Computer Interface Studies.
titre_fr: An Integrated Dual Framework for the Design and Reporting of MI and SSVEP Brain-Computer Interface Studies.
auteurs: Chio Nayibe, Quiles-Cucarella Eduardo
resume: This article presents a framework for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) based on the motor imagery (MI) and steady-state visually evoked potential (SSVEP) paradigms, with a focus on rehabilitation and robotics applications. The development of this framework was based on a review of scientific literature looking for the best practices, common phases, and key components used in research projects and applications in rehabilitation and robotics. The main result of this work is an integrated and dual framework of 20 components organized into two primary sections: the experimental section and BCI system section. The experimental section formalizes the non-technical phases that are critical for a study's validity. The BCI system section describes technical architecture. Furthermore, derived from the framework, a taxonomy is proposed to structure language, and a checklist is provided as a practical tool to ensure all the elements are present. The proposed integrated dual framework offers a structure that overcomes the limitations of previous models by merging experimental design with the BCI system's functional components. Its main contribution is the formalization of all phases of a study, which promotes methodological consistency and facilitates the inclusion of ethical considerations and user characterization. This structure, along with the taxonomy and checklist, provides researchers with a practical guide for designing and reporting BCI studies; documentation assessment in three BCI studies demonstrates the applicability and value of the framework as a practical tool. This contribution aims to promote methodological consistency and comparability among MI and SSVEP-based brain-computer interface (BCI) studies in rehabilitation and robotics.

titre: Large Language Models in Shoulder Dislocation: Performance Across Medical and Rehabilitation Domains.
titre_fr: Large Language Models in Shoulder Dislocation: Performance Across Medical and Rehabilitation Domains.
auteurs: Ayas İnci Hazal, Sözlü Uğur, İnce Bülent, Kanatlı Ulunay
resume: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to obtain health information about musculoskeletal conditions. However, their performance across different types of clinical questions remains insufficiently understood. This study evaluated the accuracy, quality, information reliability, and readability of responses generated by three widely used LLMs (ChatGPT 5.2, Gemini 3, and DeepSeek V3.2) to questions about first-time traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation, with separate analyses of medical and rehabilitation questions. Sixty-five clinically relevant questions were categorized into Medical and Safety (n = 28) and Rehabilitation (n = 37) domains. Responses were independently evaluated by domain experts using a 5-point accuracy scale, the Global Quality Scale (GQS), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), and Flesch Reading Ease (FRE). Model differences were analyzed using Friedman tests with post hoc pairwise comparisons, and inter-rater agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients. In the Medical and Safety Domain, the models differed significantly in accuracy (p < 0.001), quality (p < 0.001), information reliability (p = 0.004), and readability (p = 0.011). ChatGPT 5.2 and Gemini 3 had higher accuracy and GQS scores than DeepSeek V3.2, while DeepSeek V3.2 showed significantly higher mDISCERN scores than ChatGPT 5.2. Gemini 3 demonstrated significantly higher FRE scores than DeepSeek V3.2. titre: Tongue ultrasonography as a quantitative biomarker for oropharyngeal dysphagia in neuromuscular disorders: a systematic review.
titre_fr: Tongue ultrasonography as a quantitative biomarker for oropharyngeal dysphagia in neuromuscular disorders: a systematic review.
auteurs: Maccarone Maria Chiara, Manocchio Nicola, Foti Calogero, Dionyssiotis Yannis
resume: Oropharyngeal Dysphagia (OD) is a prevalent and potentially life-threatening complication of Neuromuscular Disorders (NMDs). Tongue ultrasonography is an inexpensive, non-ionising, point-of-care technique that permits quantitative assessment of lingual muscle structure, but its value as a biomarker of OD across NMDs has not been systematically appraised. This systematic review aims to synthesize the available evidence on the diagnostic accuracy, reliability and clinical utility of quantitative tongue ultrasonography as a biomarker of OD in adults with NMDs. We systematically searched PubMed and Scopus for studies correlating quantitative tongue-ultrasound parameters, Tongue Thickness (TT) or Echo Intensity (EI), with instrumental swallowing assessment in adults with NMDs, following the PRISMA 2020 guideline. Study selection, data extraction and risk-of-bias appraisal were performed independently by two reviewers. Six studies (n = 10-38 per cohort) met the inclusion criteria. Reduced TT was a consistent marker of lingual atrophy in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) and correlated with oral-phase swallowing impairment, whereas functional measures of tongue strength were stronger predictors of aspiration risk. In Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), increased TT reflected "pseudohypertrophy" from fatty and connective-tissue infiltration rather than preserved function and EI provided a complementary index of tissue quality in myopathic NMDs. Tongue ultrasonography is a promising, disease-sensitive biomarker for monitoring bulbar dysfunction in NMDs, but morphological indices should be integrated with functional swallowing data to predict aspiration risk. Standardized acquisition protocols and larger, longitudinal, multicentre studies are required before clinical implementation.

titre: G-MCL: Gait-Oriented Multi-Criteria Design of Sparse Plantar Sensors for High-Fidelity Analysis.
titre_fr: G-MCL: Gait-Oriented Multi-Criteria Design of Sparse Plantar Sensors for High-Fidelity Analysis.
auteurs: Yuan Shiji, Ma Kang, Hu Chun, Zhang Feiyang, Liang Xiao, Tang Huaizhi, Li Dapeng, Sun Ying, Zheng Dezhi
revue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
resume: Scalable, reproducible gait monitoring is limited by the cost and integration burden of dense plantar pressure arrays. Sparse sensing reduces cost, but heuristic or uniform layouts may miss clinically salient spatial patterns. This study aims to derive an anatomically valid, non-uniform sparse insole layout that preserves gait-relevant biomechanics under a strict sensor budget. Using the high-resolution StepUP dataset, we propose the Gait-Oriented Multi-Criteria Layout (G-MCL) framework. It searches discrete candidate sensor positions for optimal configurations. The problem is formulated as a constrained optimization problem with a weighted composite objective that jointly minimizes pressure-field reconstruction error, center of pressure (COP) trajectory deviation, and gait-event timing error. A deterministic repair operator enforces boundary validity, minimum inter-sensor spacing, and regional coverage, providing design-stage geometric feasibility. In subject-wise validation, G-MCL achieved lower composite fitness than heuristic and penalty-based binary-GA baselines while maintaining a balanced trade-off among pressure reconstruction, COP tracking, and gait-event timing at the same sensor budget. Optimized layouts are biomechanically interpretable, allocating sensors to functional plantar regions and along COP progression while satisfying the encoded geometric constraints without manual tuning. Performance exhibits diminishing returns as the budget increases, with a practical knee around 48 sensors in the StepUP setting. G-MCL provides a robust and interpretable strategy for designing manufacturability-oriented sparse plantar sensing layouts that align low-cost hardware constraints with high-fidelity gait analysis. This data-driven framework has the potential to facilitate condition-tailored sparse insole development for rehabilitation assessment, screening-oriented gait monitoring, and longitudinal wearable studies, pending prototype-level and clinical validation.

titre: The assistive technology continuity framework: sustaining access through disruption and change.
titre_fr: The assistive technology continuity framework: sustaining access through disruption and change.
auteurs: Du Yiran
resume: Assistive technology research has extensively examined person-technology fit, service delivery, adoption, satisfaction, abandonment, and participation. However, less attention has been paid to the continuity of access amid technological breakdown, organisational transition, infrastructure failure, platform change, and changing individual circumstances. This conceptual paper develops the Assistive Technology Continuity Framework (ATCF) to explain how access to valued activities can be sustained or restored despite interruption and change. Drawing on established perspectives on assistive technology use and service delivery, the paper develops a conceptual framework that integrates temporal, relational, and infrastructural dimensions of assistive technology continuity. Assistive technology continuity is defined as the capacity of a bounded person-technology-service-infrastructure configuration to sustain or restore acceptable access to valued activities despite interruption and change. The ATCF distinguishes seven interrelated components: risk architecture, disruption and temporal fit change, continuity capacities and responses, proximal continuity states, activity continuity, distal consequences, and continuity labour. It identifies dependency concentration as an architectural condition that amplifies disruption when multiple essential activities or support pathways depend on a limited number of products, providers, people, or infrastructures. Six propositions specify relationships involving reliability, realised repair capability, portability, effective redundancy, personalisation, and continuity labour. The ATCF extends person-technology fit and abandonment perspectives by incorporating disruption propagation, substitution, migration, and cross-level dependencies. It provides a conceptual basis for evaluating assistive technology beyond initial adoption and use, highlighting the importance of lifecycle support, transferable configuration, acceptable alternatives, and the distribution of continuity labour in assessment, design, procurement, and policy.

titre: The Cylinder Test: Development and clinical validation of a tool for assessing hand opening.
titre_fr: The Cylinder Test: Development and clinical validation of a tool for assessing hand opening.
auteurs: Ramström Therese, Bunketorp Käll Lina, Wangdell Johanna
revue: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
resume: Impaired hand opening following neurological injury can limit functional grasp and object handling. Existing upper limb assessments do not specifically evaluate functional hand opening or distinguish between active and passive components. To describe the development of the Cylinder Test (CyT) and evaluate its preliminary face validity, manual clarity, feasibility, and perceived clinical relevance among clinicians and individuals with neurological upper limb impairment. Clinical measurement, cross-sectional study. The CyT was developed through iterative clinical refinement and literature review. The final CyT version comprises 14 plastic cylinders (20-150 mm diameter) and four subtests assessing active and passive functional hand opening. Face validity was evaluated in 33 individuals with neurological upper limb impairments due to cervical spinal cord injuries (cSCI) or spasticity and 31 clinicians experienced in neurological upper limb rehabilitation. Clinicians reviewed the CyT manual and completed a study-specific questionnaire assessing clarity, perceived clinical usefulness, relevance of the subtests, and scoring criteria. Participants performed the CyT and subsequently rated its relevance and perceived effort. Data were summarized descriptively. All clinicians (31/31, 100%) reported that the manual provided sufficient guidance for independent administration, and all considered the CyT potentially useful in clinical practice. The purpose of the CyT was rated as clear or very clear by 26/31 clinicians (84%), and no clinician rated any subtest or scoring criterion as inappropriate. All participants (33/33, 100%) rated the overall CyT as relevant or very relevant, and ratings of the individual subtests were predominantly relevant or very relevant. Six of 15 participants with spasticity rated the test as demanding compared with 2/18 participants with cSCI. Preliminary evaluation supports the face validity, manual clarity, feasibility, and perceived clinical relevance of the CyT for assessing functional hand opening in neurological upper limb rehabilitation. The CyT may provide hand therapists with a clinically feasible approach to assessing active and passive hand opening. Further evaluation of reliability, construct validity, and responsiveness is required.

titre: A COSMIN systematic review of performance-based assessment tools for mealtime performance in Parkinson's disease: a linking study based on the ICF framework.
titre_fr: A COSMIN systematic review of performance-based assessment tools for mealtime performance in Parkinson's disease: a linking study based on the ICF framework.
auteurs: Kim Bo-Ra, Hong Deok-Gi
resume: This study systematically reviewed performance-based outcome measurement instruments (PerFOMs) for mealtime performance in Parkinson's disease and appraised their measurement domains and properties using the ICF framework and COSMIN methodology. PubMed, Embase, ProQuest, and CINAHL were searched for studies published between January 2006 and July 2026. Eligible studies used observer-administered PerFOMs that evaluated comprehensive ingestive skills during meals. Patient-reported outcome measures and screening tools limited to isolated swallowing tasks were excluded. Instrument items were linked to ICF components, and measurement properties were appraised using COSMIN. Two studies were included, identifying two PerFOMs: the Mealtime Assessment Scale (MAS) and the modified Older Americans Resources and Services (OARS) scale. The MAS was linked to all four ICF components, whereas the modified OARS scale was limited to utensil use. Neither instrument had undergone independent content-validity testing. The MAS showed adequate methodological quality with sufficient results for measurement error and convergent validity, whereas the modified OARS scale lacked evidence for most measurement properties. The evidence base for comprehensive mealtime assessment in PD remains limited and preliminary. Existing instruments differ in ICF coverage and lack content validation. Further research should establish psychometric evidence and address multiple dimensions of mealtime performance in PD.

titre: Measurement Properties of Spanish Versions of Two Exercise Self-Efficacy Scales in People with Multiple Sclerosis.
titre_fr: Measurement Properties of Spanish Versions of Two Exercise Self-Efficacy Scales in People with Multiple Sclerosis.
auteurs: Santoyo-Medina Carme, Janer Montserrat, Lidón-Moyano Cristina, Meza-Murillo Edwin Roger, Galán Ingrid, Montalban Xavier, Bagur-Calafat Caritat, Sastre-Garriga Jaume, Amor-Barbosa Marta
resume: Regular physical activity (PA) is recommended for people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS), yet long-term exercise adherence remains suboptimal. Exercise self-efficacy is a key patient-reported determinant of exercise initiation and maintenance, making its assessment relevant for both clinical practice and research. Although the Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale (EXSE; McAuley et al 1993) and the Exercise Self-Efficacy (ESE; Neupert et al 2009) have been previously used, validated Spanish versions are not available. This study aimed to translate, culturally adapt, and evaluate the measurement properties of the Spanish versions of the EXSE-McAuley (EXSE-Sp) and ESE-Neupert (ESE-Sp) in Spanish PwMS. The EXSE-McAuley and ESE-Neupert were translated and cross-culturally adapted into Spanish according to Beaton's guidelines. Ninety-three Spanish PwMS completed both questionnaires twice, with a 7-10-day interval between assessments at the end of their rehabilitation program. Structural validity, internal consistency, test-retest reliability, measurement error, and construct validity were evaluated following the COSMIN framework. Both instruments demonstrated a unidimensional structure with adequate structural validity. Internal consistency was excellent for the EXSE-Sp (Cronbach's α = 0.977) and good for the ESE-Sp (α = 0.896). Test-retest reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.992 and 0.969, respectively), with low measurement error (SEM = 2.83 and 1.20 points; Smallest Detectable Change [SDC] = 7.86 and 3.33 points, respectively). Construct validity was supported by the expected moderate positive correlation between the two scales (r = 0.56, p < 0.001), indicating that they assess related yet complementary aspects of exercise self-efficacy. The EXSE-Sp and ESE-Sp demonstrate good measurement properties and are suitable for assessing exercise self-efficacy in Spanish PwMS. These patient-reported measures may support clinical assessment, patient-centred rehabilitation planning, and evaluation of interventions targeting long-term PA participation.

titre: A Novel DHX9 Variant Was Identified in a Patient With Developmental Delay, Facial Dysmorphism and Seizure.
titre_fr: A Novel DHX9 Variant Was Identified in a Patient With Developmental Delay, Facial Dysmorphism and Seizure.
auteurs: Li Xiaoyan, Chen Yong, Sun Xiaolan
revue: International journal of developmental neuroscience : the official journal of the International Society for Developmental Neuroscience
resume: The DHX9 gene encodes an RNA helicase belonging to the DExD/H-box family, which is highly expressed in the brain and nervous system. Pathogenic variants in the DHX9 gene are associated with neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD) and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT). Both loss-of-function (LoF) and missense variants can cause NDD, whereas CMT is associated with specific missense variants. Patients with DHX9-related NDD typically present with intellectual disability, language and motor developmental delay, and autism spectrum disorder (ASD). CMT patients primarily present with distal weakness, sensory deficits, variable muscle wasting, foot deformities and painful sensory neuropathy. Here, we report a female patient with severe DHX9-related NDD phenotypes, including global developmental delay, ASD, facial dysmorphism, epilepsy, microcephaly, abnormal brain MRI findings and clinodactyly of the fifth finger. She experienced her first febrile seizure at 1 year and 2 months of age. She developed frequent myoclonic seizures characterized by rapid nodding and upper body tremors lasting 3-10 s at the age of 3 years. Simultaneous electroencephalogram (EEG) revealed paroxysmal bursts of high- to very-high-amplitude sharp-slow waves, spike-slow waves and polyspike-wave complexes diffusely over bilateral leads. Clinical exome sequencing (CES) identified a likely de novo missense variant in the DHX9 gene in the patient (NM_001357.5, c.1540C>T, p.(His514Tyr)). Notably, this variant resides within the highly conserved DEIH motif (Motif II) of the helicase ATP-binding domain. This critical region plays an essential role in ATP hydrolysis and helicase function. Three-dimensional protein structure modelling suggested that the p.(His514Tyr) substitution may compromise local protein stability by altering hydrogen bond networks. Our study expands the genetic and phenotypic spectrum of DHX9 variant-associated disorders.

titre: Parentification, Sibling Relationships and Caregiving Intentions Among Siblings of People With Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities.
titre_fr: Parentification, Sibling Relationships and Caregiving Intentions Among Siblings of People With Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities.
auteurs: Sygon Noa Polliack-, Roth Dana, Karni-Visel Yael
revue: Journal of intellectual disability research : JIDR
resume: Adult siblings of individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) are often expected to assume greater caregiving responsibilities as parents age. Thus, their future caregiving intentions are an important consideration for these individuals and their families. Research suggests that childhood parentification and sibling relationship quality are associated with caring in adulthood, yet the nature of these associations remains unclear. In a cross-sectional quantitative design, 97 adult siblings of individuals with IDD (aged 18-50), who were not current primary caregivers, completed measures of parent- and sibling-focused parentification, perceived benefits of parentification, sibling relationship characteristics and caregiving intentions. Regression analyses indicated that, after accounting for childhood parentification, sibling closeness was positively associated with future caregiving intentions, whereas sibling conflict was negatively associated with these intentions. The final model explained 51% of the variance. Mediation analyses further showed that closeness linked parent-focused parentification and perceived benefits of parentification with higher caregiving intentions, while lower conflict linked perceived benefits with higher intentions. No significant indirect effects emerged through jealousy. The findings suggest that the associations between childhood parentification and future caregiving intentions should be considered in relation to the quality of current sibling relationships and the meaning attributed to earlier caregiving roles.

titre: Sex-specific effects of prenatal vitamin D supplementation on repetitive behaviour and neuroimmune mediators in the BTBR mouse model of autism spectrum disorders.
titre_fr: Sex-specific effects of prenatal vitamin D supplementation on repetitive behaviour and neuroimmune mediators in the BTBR mouse model of autism spectrum disorders.
auteurs: Bove Maria, Palmieri Maria Adelaide, Farrag Mariam, Sikora Vladyslav, Palmieri Rossella Pia, Tucci Paolo, Schiavone Stefania, Morgese Maria Grazia, Trabace Luigia, Gualillo Oreste
resume: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) are prevalent in males compared with females, possibly attributed to male-centric profiles diagnostic criteria. ASD pathogenesis involves neuroinflammation and altered immune signalling. Therefore, maternal vitamin D deficiency may contribute to ASD by impairing fetal neurodevelopment, promoting immune dysregulation and inflammatory conditions. Due to the difficult recruitment of the vulnerable paediatric population, we used BTBR T + tf/J (BTBR) male and female mice, characterized by core ASD-like behaviours, to investigate the effects of prenatal vitamin D supplementation. On gestational day 9, pregnant BTBR dams received a subcutaneous injection of either vitamin D<sub>3</sub> (400 ng·kg<sup>-1</sup>) or vehicle. At 8-week-old, offspring underwent a battery of behavioural tests, including Hole Board, Marble Burying, Self-grooming, Open Field and Social Interaction tests. mRNA expression and protein levels of tumour necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), transforming growth factor-β2 (TGF-β2), fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4) and resistin in prefrontal cortex and hippocampus were then quantified. Maternal vitamin D supplementation reduced BTBR stereotypies. Moreover, vitamin D decreased cortical and hippocampal protein TNF-α levels only in BTBR males. In addition, vitamin D upregulated hippocampal TGF-β2 gene expression and FABP4 gene expression and protein content in male offspring, whereas a down-regulation of TGF-β2 mRNA and protein levels was reported in females. Our findings indicated that prenatal vitamin D supplementation exerted beneficial effects on BTBR stereotypies, neuroinflammatory and neuroimmune signalling alterations, ultimately suggesting its potential as an early preventive strategy to target ASD sex-tailored biomolecular dysfunctions.

titre: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor cytoplasmic retention by p27^Kip1 in senescent astrocytes.
titre_fr: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor cytoplasmic retention by p27^Kip1 in senescent astrocytes.
auteurs: Juárez-Solano Alan Hipólito, Rosales-Hernández Martha Cecilia, Velazquez-Toledano Jazziel, Tenorio-Barrera Iván, Pérez-Osorio Iván Nicolás, Rodríguez-Pérez Citlali Ekaterina, Martínez-Coria Hilda, Escudero-Lourdes Claudia, Salgado-Delgado Roberto C, Torres-Ramos Mónica Adriana
resume: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) regulates neurodevelopment, immune responses, and cellular homeostasis. Despite increased availability of endogenous ligands during aging and neurodegeneration, AhR transcriptional activity may decline through mechanisms that remain unclear. We investigated AhR dysfunction and its association with the cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p27 in senescent human astrocytes. SVG p12 human astrocytes were exposed to hydrogen peroxide (50 or 100 µM, 30 min) to induce senescence-associated features and evaluated over 72 h. The AhR ligand indole-3-propionic acid (IPA; 200 µM) was administered after oxidative stress. Cellular assays included at least three independent experiments. AhR localization and signaling, p27 association, and senescence-associated phenotypes were evaluated using microscopy, gene expression analysis, protein assays, and molecular docking. Senescence was associated with cytoplasmic redistribution of AhR and reduced expression of its target gene, cytochrome P450 1A1 (CYP1A1). Increased cytoplasmic p27 accumulation coincided with greater AhR colocalization, and co-immunoprecipitation supported their association. Molecular docking suggested that acidic conditions could stabilize the AhR-p27 complex. IPA increased nuclear AhR localization, CYP1A1 expression, and proliferation while reducing senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity. These findings suggest that p27-associated cytoplasmic retention may impair AhR signaling during astrocyte senescence despite ligand availability. IPA treatment after oxidative stress attenuated the development of senescence-associated features. Modulating AhR localization and its association with p27 may offer a therapeutic avenue for age-related neurological disorders, although causality and therapeutic relevance require further investigation.

titre: The RNA and protein landscapes of mouse brain organoids.
titre_fr: The RNA and protein landscapes of mouse brain organoids.
auteurs: Fromaget Anne-Charlotte, Gonthier-Guéret Céline, El Koulali Khadija, Périllous Sophie, Gumpangseth Nuttamonpat, Montibus Bertille, Arnaud Philippe, Urbach Serge, Court Franck, Bouschet Tristan
resume: Organoids are powerful models of brain development and function. Mouse brain organoids reproduce the main steps of neurodevelopment in vivo and differentiate more rapidly than human organoids, making them scalable for screening applications. However, mouse brain organoids remain poorly defined. Here, we showed that the transcriptome and proteome of mouse brain organoids developed for three weeks are close to those of a neonatal mouse brain. Strikingly, organoids recapitulated the majority of alternative splicing and polyadenylation-site events that define neural identity in vivo. Proteomics revealed that most changes in mRNA expression were translated into proteins. Mouse brain organoids differentiated for only three weeks already harbored a complex network of synaptic proteins, including the ionotropic and metabotropic receptors for the neurotransmitters glutamate and GABA. To conclude, our study provides evidence that mouse brain organoids are a rapidly maturing and relevant model of mammalian brain development and function in a neonatal-like environment.

titre: Characterization of lysine methylation during neuronal differentiation of LUHMES cells.
titre_fr: Characterization of lysine methylation during neuronal differentiation of LUHMES cells.
auteurs: Hanquier Jocelyne N, Iyer Malini, Evans Taylor N, McCourry Devon L, Berryhill Christine A, Doud Emma H, Smith-Kinnaman Whitney R, Mosley Amber L, Cornett Evan M
resume: Over one-third of human lysine methyltransferases (KMTs) and lysine demethylases (KDMs) are linked to neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Changes in histone lysine methylation during neuronal differentiation have been reported. It is now recognized that KMTs and KDMs also target non-histone proteins, yet characterization of non-histone lysine methylation during neuronal differentiation remains limited. Here, we address this gap using quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomics to quantify changes in non-histone lysine methylation across three stages of the Lund human mesencephalic (LUHMES) neuronal differentiation model. We identify 70 lysine methylation events with significant differences in abundance across differentiation. Our analysis reveals lysine methylation on many non-histone proteins involved in neuronal differentiation, including signaling molecules, cytoskeletal proteins, RNA splicing factors, and transcription factors. This work broadens the understanding of non-histone lysine methylation in a neuronal differentiation model and provides a resource of lysine methylation sites on proteins of biological and clinical significance for future research.

titre: Optimized GENE TARGET framework characterizes barriers to therapeutic development for monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders.
titre_fr: Optimized GENE TARGET framework characterizes barriers to therapeutic development for monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders.
auteurs: Belanger Deloge Raymond, Sveden Abigail, Frazier Zoë, Osika Hailey, Byrne Charlotte, O'Toole Jillian, Bayraktutan Muhammed, Dies Kira A, Brewster Stephanie J, Trelles Pilar, Ryan Morgan E, Zhang Bo, Prock Lisa, Hubbs Jed, Buttermore Elizabeth D, Chung Wendy K, Thurm Audrey, Sahin Mustafa, Chopra Maya
resume: GENE TARGET is a previously published framework designed to quantitatively assess the suitability of a specific monogenic neurodevelopment disorder (NDD) for development of genetic therapies, addressing the need for a systematic and rigorous approach to research prioritization and resource allocation. Here, to keep pace with the rapidly evolving knowledgebase, we refined the framework with more nuanced scoring definitions and added a resource guide to standardize evaluation of each criterion. Interrater agreement was assessed and found to be substantial for most domain/criteria scores among experienced users, primarily genetic counselors with at least two years of experience in translational genomic medicine. Secondary scoring adjudication by experts with clinical/molecular genetics and preclinical modeling expertise is recommended. Cross-disorder analysis of 57 NDD gene-disorder pairs evaluated at the Translational Neuroscience Center was performed, which identified clinical considerations, including establishing endpoints, as the most common translational research gap. Common barriers across disorders also included generating natural history data, establishing an early diagnosis, understanding dosage sensitivity, and demonstrating phenotypic reversibility. We further discuss application of this framework for gene editing and small molecules approaches. Future goals include the validation of GENE TARGET beyond academic research settings and the use of artificial intelligence to aid in preliminary scoring.

titre: Protocol for construction of human neural tube organoids with dorsal-ventral pattern using synthetic organizers.
titre_fr: Protocol for construction of human neural tube organoids with dorsal-ventral pattern using synthetic organizers.
auteurs: Zhang Yujiao, Liu Cong, Xu Peng-Fei, Ji Junfeng
resume: Dorsal-ventral (D-V) patterning of the neural tube is essential for neuronal subtype generation during neurodevelopment. Here, we present a protocol to generate human neural tube organoids (hNTOs) with a refined D-V pattern by establishing opposing BMP and SHH gradients in human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived neural ectodermal aggregates. We describe steps for neural induction and fusion, embryoid body (EB) formation, and D-V patterning. We then detail procedures for detecting and analyzing D-V markers. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Luo et al.<sup>1</sup>.

titre: Oocyte lipid damage from maternal ageing marks neurodevelopment in mouse offspring.
titre_fr: Oocyte lipid damage from maternal ageing marks neurodevelopment in mouse offspring.
auteurs: Gulzar Hafsa, Musson Richard, Depciuch Joanna, Gąsior Łukasz, Bisogno Simona, Sarna Michał, Heber Maria Florencia, Skałka Julia, Molina Diego Alejandro, Kiełbus Michał, Bodzon-Kulakowska Anna, Suder Piotr, Alluhaibi Lulu, Maximenko Alexey, Ptak Grażyna E
resume: Is advanced maternal age (AMA) associated with lipid dysregulation in oocytes that correlates with the intergenerational persistence of altered lipid homeostasis and neurodevelopmental pathway signatures in downstream offspring? Lipid profile alterations characterized in AMA oocytes are associated with distinct lipidomic and spectral variations in the foetal brain and yolk sac, displaying intergenerational persistence that extends up to the fourth generation (F4), independently of the gestational uterine environment. AMA is a recognized prenatal risk factor for neurodevelopmental conditions in offspring. However, whether early-life oocyte lipid variations correlate with altered lipid profiles and molecular signatures in the developing brains of subsequent generations remain uncharacterized. This controlled animal model study compared oocytes, blastocysts, and foetuses from AMA mice (8-16 months old) to those from young maternal age (YMA, 3-4 months old) controls and featured an embryo transfer (ET) of AMA blastocysts into young surrogates and longitudinal, lineage-specific tracking up to the F4. Complementary approaches, including liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) proteomics and lipidomics, Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization-Tandem Time-of-Flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF/TOF MS), RNA sequencing, atomic force microscopy, Coherent Anti-Stokes Raman Scattering (CARS) chemical imaging microscopy, Raman and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopies, and histology were conducted on single oocytes, blastocysts, and foetal structures (brain and yolk sac) from AMA and YMA mice. ET was utilized to decouple the oocyte-derived phenotype from the effects of an ageing maternal uterine environment. AMA oocytes and preimplantation blastocysts exhibited significant lipid droplet and lipid membrane alterations, a higher relative absorbance of intracellular lipid bands, and altered expression of lipid-regulatory transcripts, corresponding to early embryonic pathway shifts. Following the ET of AMA blastocysts to young surrogates (ET AMA group), distinct lipidomic variations and structural alterations were observed in the F1 yolk sac and foetal brains. Furthermore, these lipid-associated spectral and molecular signatures displayed intergenerational persistence, tracking through the yolk sac, brain, and oocytes of the third- (F3) and fourth-generation (F4) descendants derived from the oocyte of AMA progenitors. The transcriptomic data have been deposited in the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) under accession number GSE349634. Processed transcriptomic, lipidomic, and proteomic datasets, together with the shared transcript-protein analysis, have been deposited in RODBUK under DOI https://doi.org/10.57903/UJ/LVQ7FU. All datasets are publicly available. This study was conducted exclusively in a mouse model. Given species-specific variations in baseline oocyte lipid content and developmental kinetics, these findings require cautious interpretation before extrapolation to human clinical contexts. Additionally, the exact molecular and epigenetic mechanisms underlying the intergenerational persistence of these lipid signatures warrant further characterization. These findings demonstrate an association between early-life oocyte lipid changes and downstream pathway-level molecular signatures of neurodevelopmental alterations. By establishing an intergenerational pathway that persists independently of the maternal uterine environment, this work introduces a novel framework linking metabolic programming at conception to neurodevelopmental outcomes, offering new directions for reproductive medicine and translational neuroscience. This research was funded by National Science Centre of Poland Grants 2021/41/B/NZ3/03507 and 2019/35/B/NZ4/03547 (to G.E.P.), 2022/44/C/NZ4/00076 (to M.F.H.), and 2019/35/N/NZ3/03213 (to Ł.G.), and the program 'Excellence initiative-research university' for the AGH University of Krakow (A.B.-K.). Proteomics was supported by the subsidy no 16.16.160.557 of the Polish Ministry of Science and Higher Education (to P.S.). Raman analysis at the National Synchrotron Radiation Centre SOLARIS was supported by the Ministry of Science and Higher Education, Poland, under contract no. 1/SOL/2021/2. The authors declare no competing interests.
