titre: Preinjury Employment Advantage and Early Return-to-Work: Identifying Influential Time Points for Employment Post-traumatic Brain Injury.
titre_fr: Preinjury Employment Advantage and Early Return-to-Work: Identifying Influential Time Points for Employment Post-traumatic Brain Injury.
auteurs: Barrett Pat M, Moore Graham E, Thompson Nicole A, Johnstone Brick, O'Neil-Pirozzi Therese M, Talley Kelli G, Anderson Raeda K
revue: The Journal of head trauma rehabilitation
resume: Analyze preinjury and postinjury predictor's effect on employment after traumatic brain injury (TBI) at 1, 2, 5, and 10 years postinjury to identify the most influential drivers of employment where vocational rehabilitation interventions are feasible. Community. Workforce-eligible persons enrolled in the TBI Model Systems National Database with data at injury and years 1, 2, 5, and 10 postinjury. Secondary analysis of longitudinal cohort data. Employment status at years 1, 2, 5, and 10 after TBI. Predictors included lagged preinjury and postinjury employment status, sociodemographic characteristics (age, sex, race, education), and concurrent postinjury features including marital status, transportation independence, and rural residence. Latent constructs of functional dependence were generated at each postinjury time point with rehospitalization history, Functional Independence Measure subscores, and the Disability Rating Scale. Generalized structural equation modeling found that prior employment had the largest positive effect on employment status at all time points. Being employed at injury increased the likelihood of employment at years 1, 2, and 5 postinjury. Employment 1, 2, and 5 years postinjury increased the odds of employment at all subsequent time points. Being currently married increased employment odds only for 1-year postinjury. Transportation independence increased the odds of employment, and greater functional dependence reduced employment odds for all time points. Employment prior to TBI improves employment chances for a minimum of 5 years postinjury, and early postinjury employment has even longer-lasting effects on future employment. Achievement of employment soon after injury can have long-term benefits in increasing the likelihood of employment at later time points. Results suggest that vocational rehabilitation interventions near the point of injury can have lasting positive improvements, including leveraging existing employer relationships. Practical policy approaches that support proactive VR at the point of injury are provided.

titre: Sex Differences in Rehabilitation Outcomes After Stroke: A Single-Center Retrospective Observational Study.
titre_fr: Sex Differences in Rehabilitation Outcomes After Stroke: A Single-Center Retrospective Observational Study.
auteurs: Małek Michał, Hozakowska Anna, Guzek Zbigniew, Stefańska Małgorzata, Kowalska Joanna
resume: Background/Objectives: The findings of studies that assess post-stroke rehabilitation outcomes according to sex remain inconclusive. This study aimed to assess the rehabilitation outcomes among patients after a first stroke according to sex and identify the factors related to functional status and independence in performing basic activities of daily living at discharge. Methods: The data from 527 patients, aged 69.1 ± 11.8 years, comprising 244 women and 283 men, were analyzed. The Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE), Barthel Index (BI), Trunk Control Test (TCT), Timed Up and Go Test (TUG), and Berg Balance Scale (BBS) were used at two measurement points: upon admission to the ward (T1) and at discharge (T2). Results: No significant differences between women and men at T1 were found. At T2, statistically significant differences in the length of stay in the ward, MMSE, BBS, TCT, TUG, and BI were observed, but the reported effect sizes were generally small. At T2, men had better rehabilitation outcomes, but they stayed in the rehabilitation ward significantly longer than women. The analysis revealed no significant effect of the time point of measurement (T1 vs. T2) and sex interaction on the test results. Greater independence in basic activities of daily living at discharge (BI > 15 at T2) depended on sex, age, MMSE, and TUG at T1. Conclusions: The results obtained do not provide conclusive evidence for differences in rehabilitation outcomes based on sex. Further research on the factors and mechanisms involved in stroke rehabilitation outcomes in relation to sex is needed.

titre: Functional Trajectories Following Clinically Selected Management of Concomitant Proximal Humerus Fractures in Geriatric Hip-Fracture Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
titre_fr: Functional Trajectories Following Clinically Selected Management of Concomitant Proximal Humerus Fractures in Geriatric Hip-Fracture Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
auteurs: Lara-Galdón Borja, Hernández-Mateo José María, Prats-Peinado Lourdes, Guzmán-Sánchez Álvaro, Begara-Bretón Carmen, Aburto-Bernardo Mikel, Pérez-Martín Ángel, López-Mombiela Fausto
resume: Background/Objectives: Concomitant hip and proximal humerus fractures create a demanding rehabilitation scenario in older adults. We described unadjusted functional trajectories following clinically selected proximal humerus management and explored the relationship between baseline independence and treatment allocation. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 4776 hip-fracture presentations (2011-2023); 55 patients aged > 65 years had synchronous proximal humerus fractures. All hip fractures were surgically treated; 13 proximal humerus fractures were managed operatively and 42 non-operatively. Barthel Index was assessed before fracture, at 30 days, and at six months. Results: Mean pre-fracture Barthel scores were 98.5 ± 3.8 and 79.5 ± 20.8 in the operative and non-operative groups, respectively. At 30 days, scores were 85.4 ± 6.9 versus 60.5 ± 23.9; at six months, scores were 93.5 ± 5.2 versus 70.2 ± 25.0. Mean absolute change from baseline at six months was -5.0 versus -9.3 points. Conclusions: Patients selected for surgery were more independent before injury and remained more independent at follow-up. Marked pre-injury differences and confounding by indication prevent any inference about the independent effect of proximal humerus surgery.

titre: IMU-Based Analysis of Postural Transitions: A Systematic Review.
titre_fr: IMU-Based Analysis of Postural Transitions: A Systematic Review.
auteurs: Buraschi Riccardo, Pullara Rosa, Amici Cinzia, Gobbo Massimiliano, Pollet Joel
resume: Postural transitions (PTs) are crucial for daily independence, but their assessment often relies on subjective observational scales. Inertial measurement units (IMUs) offer quantitative assessment, yet a comprehensive synthesis of methodological approaches for IMU-based PT assessment is lacking. This systematic review maps the methodological landscape of IMU-based PT studies. A PCC-based search queried PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for IMU-based PT assessment in adults. Methodological quality was appraised using design- and purpose-appropriate established tools. From 30,181 records, 35 studies were included, with heterogeneous study designs, purposes (e.g., detection, segmentation, validation), and analytical methods (e.g., threshold-based approach, model-based approach, deep learning method). Sit-to-stand was the most frequently assessed PT. Methodological appraisal indicated an intermediate robustness, with most studies showing moderate concerns. Sensor configurations, acquisition protocols, signal processing, segmentation, and outcome definitions varied substantially, and IMU-derived PT outcomes lacked standardization. IMUs offer significant potential for objective postural-transition assessment in rehabilitation, yet methodological heterogeneity and underrepresented tasks like bed mobility limit progress. Future research must prioritize standardized, validated, and clinically interpretable metrics to address reporting inconsistencies and establish a unified framework essential for widespread clinical adoption.

titre: Nursing Interventions Supporting Rehabilitation and Functional Improvement in Older Adults with Coronary Heart Disease: A Scoping Review.
titre_fr: Nursing Interventions Supporting Rehabilitation and Functional Improvement in Older Adults with Coronary Heart Disease: A Scoping Review.
auteurs: Ortega-Maldonado Alvaro, Chica-Perez Anabel, García-Lopez Dulcenombre de Maria, Gerez-De-Paco Miguel, Fernandez-Sola Cayetano, Hernandez-Padilla Jose Manuel
resume: Background/Objectives: Coronary heart disease (CHD) is a major cause of morbidity, disability, and loss of autonomy among older adults. Nursing interventions may support rehabilitation and continuity of care, although their characteristics and delivery remain heterogeneous. This scoping review aimed to map nursing interventions implemented and evaluated to support rehabilitation and functional improvement in older adults with CHD, focusing on how these interventions were organised and delivered, the roles assumed by nurses, and the outcomes assessed. Methods: A scoping review was conducted following Joanna Briggs Institute's guidance and reported according to PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane were searched between November 2025 and February 2026. Eligibility criteria followed the Population-Concept-Context framework. Quantitative and mixed-method intervention studies involving adults with CHD with a mean age ≥60 years were included. Study selection was performed independently by two reviewers. Results: Twelve studies were included. Most interventions were multicomponent (10/12), commonly integrating health education, exercise, psychosocial support, and self-care strategies. Nine programs combined face-to-face care with remote follow-up, and ten were directly led and delivered by nurses. Intervention duration ranged from four weeks to six months. Outcomes included functional, physiological, psychological, self-care, and quality-of-life domains. Favourable findings were frequently reported for functional capacity, anxiety and depression, self-care, self-efficacy, and health-related quality of life, whereas cardiovascular and physiological findings were less consistent. Conclusions: Nursing interventions for older adults with CHD are predominantly multicomponent and delivered across hospital and home settings. Further research should assess long-term outcomes and improve representation of very old, frail, and digitally vulnerable populations.

titre: Physiotherapy-Based Rehabilitation from the Perspective of Individuals with Multiple Sclerosis: Independence and Psychological Well-Being Beyond Physical Function-A Qualitative Study.
titre_fr: Physiotherapy-Based Rehabilitation from the Perspective of Individuals with Multiple Sclerosis: Independence and Psychological Well-Being Beyond Physical Function-A Qualitative Study.
auteurs: Erturan Burak Sinem, Burak Mustafa, Demir Caner Feyzi
resume: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic, progressive neurological disease with profound effects on physical functionality, psychosocial adaptation, and quality of life. This study aims to examine the perceptions, experiences, and factors influencing participation in physiotherapy-based rehabilitation among individuals diagnosed with MS. This qualitative study was designed using a descriptive phenomenological approach. Semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with 12 purposively sampled individuals with relapsing-remitting MS (10 women; mean age, 45.6 ± 6.4 years; mean Expanded Disability Status Scale score, 4.8 ± 1.5). Data were collected until code saturation was reached and analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. Two overarching themes were identified: living with MS and rehabilitation in MS. Most participants perceived physiotherapy as supporting their function, independence, and psychological well-being; three perceived no change or felt worse after sessions. A friendly, knowledgeable physiotherapist, individualized exercises, and easy transportation were described as facilitators, and physical symptoms, transportation difficulties, and lack of information as barriers. From the participants' perspective, physiotherapy-based rehabilitation was experienced not merely as symptomatic treatment but as support for function, independence, and psychological well-being. Structuring services around therapeutic relationships, individualized programs, and early information may facilitate participation; these perception-based findings do not establish effectiveness.

titre: Ethics in Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation: Global Research Trends and Thematic Structure-A Bibliometric and Science-Mapping Analysis.
titre_fr: Ethics in Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation: Global Research Trends and Thematic Structure-A Bibliometric and Science-Mapping Analysis.
auteurs: Erdem Sultanoğlu Tuba, Sultanoğlu Hasan
resume: Ethical issues in physical medicine and rehabilitation (PM&R) span autonomy, disability rights, decision-making, and equitable access. This study mapped the bibliographic and conceptual structure of the ethics-related PM&R literature. Web of Science Core Collection records published through 2025 were retrieved using PM&R-related terminology and field-restricted ethics terms. The refined search identified 110 records. Following post hoc eligibility reassessment, one veterinary rehabilitation publication was excluded, yielding 109 records for the primary bibliometric analysis. Publication characteristics, citation patterns, and standardized keyword networks were examined. Sensitivity analyses assessed keyword-source selection, keyword-frequency thresholds, and the exclusion of five potentially overlapping publications. The primary dataset comprised 109 indexed records published between 1986 and 2025, including 94 Articles, 12 Reviews, and three records with dual Article/Proceedings Paper classification. These publications received 1918 citations (h-index: 23). The keyword co-occurrence network contained 35 standardized terms and 187 links, forming five thematic communities encompassing care and rehabilitation access, palliative care and participation, informed consent and decision-making capacity, disability and quality, and physicians and AIDS. The sensitivity dataset contained 104 records and 1909 citations, with 33 keyword nodes and 180 links; five thematic communities remained identifiable. The findings characterize recurrent concepts within a defined bibliographic corpus rather than the entire PM&R ethics literature. The broad thematic structure was retained in sensitivity analysis, although publication indicators and detailed network characteristics were affected by potentially overlapping records.

titre: Nurse-Led Stepped Care to Reduce Fear of Falling After Hip Fracture Surgery in Older Adults: A Non-Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol.
titre_fr: Nurse-Led Stepped Care to Reduce Fear of Falling After Hip Fracture Surgery in Older Adults: A Non-Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol.
auteurs: Lv Shuangshuang, Wang Liulin, Wang Lei
resume: To evaluate whether a nurse-led stepped care protocol reduces fear of falling (FoF) among older adults after hip fracture surgery. A prospective, single-centre, non-randomized controlled trial protocol. A total of 124 older adults will be recruited by convenience sampling and allocated by ward. The intervention group will receive routine care plus a response-adaptive stepped care intervention, whereas the control group will receive routine care alone. Intervention intensity will be adjusted according to Short Falls Efficacy Scale-International (Short FES-I) scores and activity limitation. The primary outcome will be the Short FES-I score at 1 month. Secondary outcomes will include activity limitation, activities of daily living, hip function, anxiety, and depression. Short FES-I and activity limitation will also be reassessed during the inpatient stages to guide progression, while formal outcome assessments will occur at baseline and at 1 and 3 months. Statisticians will remain blinded to group allocation where feasible. Recruitment has commenced. Literature synthesis, expert consultation, and pilot testing were completed before the main trial and used to refine the protocol. Recruitment is underway, and no trial outcome analysis has yet been performed. The protocol integrates response-guided psychological support, rehabilitation, family involvement, and post-discharge follow-up within a nurse-led stepped care pathway. The pathway gives orthopaedic nurses a structured role in FoF screening, first-line intervention, reassessment, escalation decisions, multidisciplinary coordination, and post-discharge follow-up. This study addresses the lack of a nurse-coordinated, response-adaptive pathway for postoperative FoF and may inform staged care across inpatient and home-based rehabilitation. Reporting was guided by the Template for Intervention Description and Replication (TIDieR) and the Transparent Reporting of Evaluations with Non-randomized Designs (TREND) statements. Ten older adults and their family caregivers participated in pilot testing and contributed to refinement of the intervention materials and procedures. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2500107946.

titre: From Nosography to Biography: A Four-Level Framework for Evaluating Irremediability in Medical Assistance in Dying for Mental Health.
titre_fr: From Nosography to Biography: A Four-Level Framework for Evaluating Irremediability in Medical Assistance in Dying for Mental Health.
auteurs: Ramos-Pozón Sergio, Poveda-Moral Silvia
resume: The assessment of "irremediability" in mental health constitutes the most complex bioethical challenge within medical assistance in dying laws, given the structural uncertainty inherent in psychiatry. This article proposes a four-level analytical framework designed to transform diagnostic ambiguity into a prudent and auditable decision. In the first level (technical), "incurability" is delimited as a nosographic judgment based on treatment futility and traceability, as opposed to "irremediability" as a clinical-pragmatic judgment. The second level (phenomenological) defines irremediability as a 'frozen temporality' and a closure of the biographical horizon, where suffering becomes structural. The third level (ethical) advocates for "relational autonomy" and the two-track approach as safeguards against both therapeutic obstinacy and abandonment, ensuring that intensive rehabilitation coexists with the request. Finally, the fourth level (legal) analyzes how certain euthanasia legislations integrate biographical functionality, moving beyond a purely biological paradigm. It is concluded that the transition from a nosographic model to a biographical one allows for the respect of individual autonomy and life history without abdicating clinical responsibility, offering a decision-making standard that harmonizes technical rigor with compassion.

It is concluded that the transition from a nosographic model to a biographical one allows for the respect of individual autonomy and life history without abdicating clinical responsibility, offering a decision-making standard that harmonizes technical rigor with compassion.

titre: Effects of slow-belt split-belt treadmill training on balance, walking speed, and activities of daily living in patients with subacute stroke: A pilot randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Effects of slow-belt split-belt treadmill training on balance, walking speed, and activities of daily living in patients with subacute stroke: A pilot randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Oh Byeong-Hun, Kim Da-Sol, Kim Gi-Wook, Won Yu-Hui, Park Sung-Hee, Seo Jeong-Hwan, Ko Myoung-Hwan
resume: This study aimed to compare the effects of 3 weeks of slow-belt split-belt treadmill training (SBT) with those of tied-belt treadmill training (both belts driven at the same speed) on balance, functional reach, walking speed, and basic activities of daily living in patients with subacute stroke, and to evaluate the feasibility and safety of the SBT protocol. In this single-center, assessor-blinded, parallel-group pilot randomized controlled trial with 1:1 allocation conducted in the inpatient rehabilitation unit of a tertiary hospital, 30 patients with subacute hemiplegic stroke (median, 13 days after onset) were randomized; 26 participants (13 per group) completed the post-intervention assessment. Thirty 30-minute treadmill sessions (twice daily, 5 days per week, for 3 weeks) were delivered in place of the routine gait-training sessions of the standard inpatient rehabilitation program. In the SBT group, the paretic limb was positioned on the slower belt at a fixed paretic-to-nonparetic belt-speed ratio of 1:2; in the control group, both belts operated at the same speed. The primary outcome was the Berg Balance Scale (BBS) at 3 weeks, compared between groups using baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance. Secondary outcomes were the functional reach test (FRT), modified FRT, gait speed (10-m walk test), and Korean version of the modified Barthel index, with Holm adjustment for multiplicity. Both groups improved substantially (BBS, +18.8 vs +18.0 points; both P <.001); however, the baseline-adjusted between-group difference in the BBS was not significant (1.20 points; 95% confidence interval = -5.30 to 7.71; P =.706). No secondary outcome remained significant after Holm adjustment; a nominal difference in seated FRT (adjusted difference = 9.75 cm; P =.044; Holm-adjusted P =.355) was not robust in sensitivity analyses. Session completion was 99.7%, and no device- or protocol-related adverse events occurred. In this pilot trial of patients with subacute stroke undergoing inpatient rehabilitation, SBT was feasible and well tolerated but did not demonstrate superiority over tied-belt training for balance, walking speed, or activities of daily living. An exploratory signal in seated reach warrants confirmation in adequately powered trials.

titre: Physical and psychosocial morbidity in pregnancy and lactation-associated osteoporosis: a comprehensive mixed-methods study.
titre_fr: Physical and psychosocial morbidity in pregnancy and lactation-associated osteoporosis: a comprehensive mixed-methods study.
auteurs: Gak Nataliya, Teixeira Maria Joao Cardoso, Dhillo Waljit S, Abbara Ali, Keen Richard, Comninos Alexander N
revue: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA
resume: This study showed that women with pregnancy and lactation-associated osteoporosis (PLO) experience markedly impaired physical and mental health when compared to controls, with partners also affected. These findings highlight the need for multidisciplinary, patient-centred care with psychological support and rehabilitation, informing future clinical guidelines. To date, limited understanding of the physical and psychosocial impact of fractures secondary to pregnancy and lactation-associated osteoporosis (PLO) has hindered the management of this condition. To investigate the physical and psychosocial impacts of PLO on women and their partners, and to describe its clinical and radiological characteristics. A mixed-methods, single-centre, case-control study of women with PLO (n = 20) and healthy women (n = 20), matched for age and time postpartum. Participants completed four health-related quality-of-life (HRQoL) questionnaires. Women from PLO group also participated in semi-structured interviews. In addition, partners of women with PLO took part in qualitative interviews separately (not part of the case control analysis). The PLO group had significantly reduced physical functioning (SF-36 physical: 75 vs 100, p = 0.001; Qualeffo-41 physical: 16 vs 2, p < 0.001) and poorer mental health (SF-36 emotional wellbeing: 64 vs 88, p = 0.007; Qualeffo-41 mental: 42 vs 39, p = 0.06; PHQ-4: 3.5 vs 0, p < 0.01). Social life was also negatively affected (SF-36 social 75 vs 100, p = 0.06; Quallefo-41 social 38 vs 0, p < 0.001). Qualitative interviews revealed themes including loss of physical autonomy, chronic pain, delayed return to work, loss of motherhood experience, anxiety and depression, altered body image, poor healthcare support, emotional resilience, relationship strain, social isolation, online peer support, and impact of COVID-19. Partners reported emotional stress and difficulty balancing work and family responsibilities while adjusting to a 'new normal'. PLO has severe consequences on both affected women and their partners, highlighting the need for increased awareness, earlier diagnosis, improved management and holistic support.

titre: Multicomponent exercise intervention impact on recovery outcomes in frail older adult patients with trochanteric femoral fractures: a quasi-experimental study.
titre_fr: Multicomponent exercise intervention impact on recovery outcomes in frail older adult patients with trochanteric femoral fractures: a quasi-experimental study.
auteurs: Lin Hua, Wang Yang, He Yali, Zhu Ying
resume: This study investigated Trochanteric femoral fractures (TFFs) in frail older adult patients who are at high risk of complications and increased mortality, thereby imposing a significant economic burden on healthcare systems. The objective of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of a multicomponent exercise intervention compared with conventional care in promoting recovery outcomes in older adult patients with frailty post-TFF surgery. In this quasi-experimental study with a historical (non-concurrent) control group, we analyzed 120 frail patients with TFFs who were treated with intramedullary nailing between January 2023 and December 2024. Patients were divided into a control group receiving conventional care and an observation group receiving multicomponent exercise interventions, both receiving interventions for 3 months. The multicomponent intervention comprised strength, balance, flexibility, and aerobic exercises, was delivered by a multidisciplinary team, and was progressed from bed-based to standing and walking training. The modified Barthel index (MBI) and Functional Independence Measure (FIM) tools were used to evaluate the rehabilitation status of the two patient groups. The Harris Hip Score (HHS) was used as a secondary outcome to assess hip function. The Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) score was used to evaluate frailty. The 36-item Short-Form Health Survey (SF-36) was used to assess quality of life. After the intervention, the MBI, FIM, and SF-36 scores of the observation group were statistically significantly higher than those of the control group (P < 0.05). The CFS was significantly lower in the observation group than in the control group (P < 0.05). The HHS score was significantly higher in the observation group than in the control group (P < 0.05). These findings suggest the potential benefits of multicomponent exercise interventions in enhancing rehabilitation outcomes and reducing frailty in older adult patients with TFFs, indicating a promising direction for future clinical practice. Future studies should explore the scalability of these interventions across diverse settings and populations to refine and validate the therapeutic strategies identified in this study.

titre: Outcomes of elderly hospitalized patients with influenza after the COVID-19 pandemic: decline of functional independence and frailty.
titre_fr: Outcomes of elderly hospitalized patients with influenza after the COVID-19 pandemic: decline of functional independence and frailty.
auteurs: Ishida Tadashi, Ito Akihiko, Nakanishi Yosuke, Tateda Kazuhiro, Fujita Jiro, Izumikawa Koichi, Nagai Hideaki, Seki Masafumi
resume: Influenza remains a heavy burden to the elderly and the situation has been affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. The objective of this study was to clarify outcomes of elderly hospitalized patients with influenza after the COVID-19 pandemic. The clinical data of patients 65 years of age or older who were severely ill with influenza and required hospitalization in one center were gathered between September 2023 and March 2026 (3 influenza seasons after the COVID-19 pandemic). The outcomes, functional independence, and frailty of them were analyzed. A total of 210 elderly patients were enrolled. The median age was 79 and 32 cases were judged as having mild or more frailty by the clinical frailty scale (CFS) before admission. Pneumonia was the most common disease indicated as cause for hospitalization, followed by a poor general condition and heart failure. The median duration of hospitalization was 13 days and in-hospital deaths were recorded for 17 patients (8.1%). Sixty cases changed hospital due to further treatment or deterioration of activity of daily living, and the functional independence measure (FIM) of 37 cases (17.6%) remained under a score of 70 even after rehabilitation. The CFSs worsened in 19 cases (9.0%) at the time of discharge. Influenza infection remains a heavy burden among the elderly after the COVID-19 pandemic. The elderly tend to lose functional independence and fail to frailty even after recovery from acute illness. Preventive measures for influenza to avoid admission, including vaccination, will be essential. (Influenza Internet Survey, UMIN000015989).

titre: Cerebellar Intermittent Theta-burst Stimulation Reduces Dual Task Cost in Walking and Balance in Stroke Patients.
titre_fr: Cerebellar Intermittent Theta-burst Stimulation Reduces Dual Task Cost in Walking and Balance in Stroke Patients.
auteurs: Li Kai, Li Shijue, Huang Ziyan, Zhang Siyun, Zhang Xiangsheng, Lo Wai Leung Ambrose, Zhang Jack Jiaqi, Luo Qihang, Yu Qiuhua, Wang Chuhuai, Ding Minghui
resume: The cerebellum plays a key role in integrating cognitive and motor functions. After stroke, impairments in cognitive-motor dual task (DT) performance increase fall risk and limit functional independence. We aimed to investigate whether cerebellar intermittent theta-burst stimulation (CRB-iTBS) can improve DT performance in patients with subacute ischemic stroke. In this randomized controlled trial, 26 patients with subacute ischemic stroke and lower-limb impairment were assigned to receive CRB-iTBS or sham-iTBS combined with physiotherapy. Stimulation targeted the cerebellar hemisphere contralateral to the lesion. Cognitive task, single-task (ST: standing/walking), and cognitive-motor DT task (counting backward while standing/walking) completion pre- and post-intervention were compared. The primary outcome was the dual-task cost (DTC) of sway area. Secondary outcomes included DTCs for other balance and gait outcome measures, as well as balance and gait performance, electroencephalographic measures, and functional connectivity. CRB-iTBS significantly reduced the DTC for sway area, the primary outcome. DTCs for cadence and double support time were also reduced. Improvements in standing balance and gait performance were observed across ST and DT conditions. During DT walking, CRB-iTBS was associated with increased theta, alpha, and beta power and enhanced global connectivity. Increased frontal theta power correlated with a reduced DTC for cadence. CRB-iTBS improved DT performance, particularly balance as reflected by reduced DTC for sway area, in patients with subacute stroke. Cerebellar neuromodulation may be a promising adjunctive therapy during stroke rehabilitation.

titre: Genome-wide synthetic engineering identifies essential genes and host-specific factors governing tropism switching in mycobacteriophage D29.
titre_fr: Genome-wide synthetic engineering identifies essential genes and host-specific factors governing tropism switching in mycobacteriophage D29.
auteurs: Sakiyama Arata, Washizaki Ayaka, Naznin Most Hushna Ara, Ando Hiroki
resume: Mycobacteriophage D29 is a phage that infects mycobacteria and has been studied as a model since its isolation in 1954. It can infect multiple species, including Mycobacterium smegmatis, nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), and Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the causative agent of tuberculosis. D29 is now considered a potential candidate for NTM and tuberculosis treatment. However, 34% of its genes remain functionally uncharacterized. Recent advances in synthetic biology have enabled efficient phage engineering, reducing the challenges of mutant screening in bulk populations. In this study, we generated a set of single-gene deletion mutants using synthetic engineering techniques to identify genes required for phage propagation. Functional analysis of all 77 genes showed that 44 genes (57%) and all tRNAs were nonessential for phage replication. Furthermore, infection assays using the deletion mutants demonstrated that genes 55, 56, and 59 are required for efficient infection of M. tuberculosis H37Rv but are dispensable for infection of M. smegmatis, highlighting their contribution to host-specific phage infectivity. These findings provide valuable insights into D29 biology and phage-host dynamics. In this study, we employed synthetic biology techniques to construct a comprehensive library of the gene and tRNA deletion mutants of mycobacteriophage D29 to systematically assess gene essentiality. Notably, over half of the genes were found to be nonessential for the lytic cycle, suggesting potential roles in environmental adaptation and host-mycobacteria interactions. Furthermore, we found that the D29Δ55, D29Δ56, and D29Δ59 mutants showed markedly reduced plating efficiency on Mycobacterium tuberculosis although these genes were dispensable for infection of Mycobacterium smegmatis. Such differential genetic requirements highlight their potential roles in modulating phage-host interactions across distinct Mycobacterium species. These findings provide valuable insights into the functional genomics of D29 and phage biology and support its continued development as a candidate for phage-based therapies against nontuberculous mycobacteria and M. tuberculosis infections.

titre: Chiral-Regulated Kresling Structure for Reconfigurable Multimodal Motion.
titre_fr: Chiral-Regulated Kresling Structure for Reconfigurable Multimodal Motion.
auteurs: Tang Zhi-Chuan, Wang Anqi, Yang Yi-Zhou, Cui Zhi-Xuan, Sun Hui-Ling, Jiang De-Sheng
resume: Once geometrically defined, conventional Kresling structures typically exhibit a deterministic coupling path between axial displacement and radial deformation, which inherently limits their post-assembly reconfigurability under identical actuation inputs. We propose a mechanically actuated double-layer Kresling module, comprising a compliant inner layer with switchable chirality and a rigid outer shell featuring an expandable base boundary. By modulating the chiral state of the inner layer, the axial-radial coupling path of the assembled module can be dynamically reconfigured, achieving distinct rotational and radial responses under the same axial input without necessitating geometric replacement. The resulting coupling paths support compression, torsion, radial expansion, multidirectional bending, and a load-resistant state under mechanical constraints. A multi-module robotic system assembled from these units demonstrates locomotion in pipes with inner diameters from 84 to 140 mm and in a curved pipe, alongside inner-anchoring grasping. Furthermore, the system uses radial deformation to estimate the pipe inner diameter; this measurement provides a basis for future adjustment of the inner-layer configuration and driving parameters. By integrating reconfigurable axial-radial kinematics and radial measurement within a unified mechanical embodiment, this study establishes a mechanically programmable structural platform for future robotic systems with closed-loop environmental adaptation.

titre: GhILL8 Interacts With GhREF to Coordinate Jasmonate-Auxin Signalling and Positively Regulate Cotton Defense Against Verticillium Wilt.
titre_fr: GhILL8 Interacts With GhREF to Coordinate Jasmonate-Auxin Signalling and Positively Regulate Cotton Defense Against Verticillium Wilt.
auteurs: Zhang Lei, Wang Chang, Li Xinyi, Rong Kaikuo, Li Youzhong, Yu Yongang
resume: Auxin homoeostasis is a critical determinant of plant growth and environmental adaptation, yet its precise role and regulatory mechanisms in Verticillium wilt resistance remain largely unexplored. Here, we systematically characterized the IAA amidohydrolase (ILL) gene family across cotton species and identified GhILL8, a gene strongly induced by Verticillium dahliae infection and jasmonic acid (JA) defense-related signalling molecules. Functional dissection through virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) revealed that GhILL8 knockdown severely compromises cotton resistance to V. dahliae, as evidenced by elevated disease indices, exacerbated vascular browning, and significantly increased fungal colonization. Notably, the early transient burst of free indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) observed in wild-type plants at 1 h post-inoculation, a hallmark of pattern-triggered immunity was completely abolished in GhILL8-silenced plants, correlating with accelerated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and extensive cell death. RNA-Seq data analysis further revealed that GhILL8 positively regulates cotton resistance to V. dahliae by modulating both JA and auxin (IAA) signalling pathways. Conversely, heterologous overexpression of GhILL8 in Arabidopsis and tobacco markedly enhanced tolerance to V. dahliae, underscoring its evolutionarily conserved positive role in plant immunity. Mechanistically, yeast two-hybrid and luciferase complementation imaging assays demonstrated that GhILL8 physically interacts with the rubber elongation factor GhREF. Loss of GhREF phenocopied GhILL8 silencing, impairing defense gene activation and aggravating vascular wilt symptoms. Collectively, our findings establish GhILL8 as a pivotal metabolic rheostat that calibrates the free auxin pool during early fungal infection and uncover a previously unrecognized GhILL8-GhREF module that orchestrates JA and IAA signalling crosstalk to fine-tune crop immunity. This work provides new mechanistic insights and valuable genetic resources for breeding Verticillium wilt-resistant cotton cultivars.

titre: Carotenoid Metabolism in Plant Stress Adaptation: Pathway Regulation, Flux Distribution, and Stress-Adaptive Functions.
titre_fr: Carotenoid Metabolism in Plant Stress Adaptation: Pathway Regulation, Flux Distribution, and Stress-Adaptive Functions.
auteurs: Chen Panrui, Lin Zhengyao, Zhou Mingjian, Shen Jie, Liu Yinggao, Zhu Fuyuan, Xie Yanjie
resume: Carotenoids are plastid-localized isoprenoid metabolites essential for photosynthesis, photoprotection, and plant development. Their metabolism also provides precursors for abscisic acid (ABA), strigolactones (SLs), and diverse apocarotenoids involved in environmental adaptation. Both abiotic and biotic stresses can alter carotenoid biosynthesis, composition, and turnover, although the underlying regulatory mechanisms and physiological consequences vary with stress type. This review examines how carotenoid pathway regulation influences metabolite allocation and stress-adaptive functions, with particular emphasis on the control of precursor supply and metabolic branch points. We discuss the contributions of carotenoid metabolism to ABA-mediated stress responses, photoprotection and redox homeostasis, and signaling by carotenoid-derived metabolites, including zaxinone, β-ionone, β-cyclocitral, and SLs. The distinct and overlapping roles of these processes in abiotic stress adaptation and biotic defense are evaluated, while senescence is considered as a developmental process associated with changes in carotenoid turnover and downstream signaling. We further examine how functional specialization among pathway genes, transcriptional and chromatin regulation, RNA-mediated control, protein stability, and enzyme interactions influence pathway activity. Metabolite feedback and competition for shared precursors, particularly at the methylerythritol 4-phosphate (MEP) and geranylgeranyl diphosphate (GGPP) nodes, provide additional mechanisms for regulating metabolic branch allocation. The reversible interconversion between ABA and ABA glucose ester (ABA-GE) is also discussed as a mechanism of ABA homeostasis distinct from de novo carotenoid-dependent biosynthesis. Importantly, the extent to which changes in metabolite abundance reflect actual flux redistribution remains insufficiently resolved. Future research should therefore prioritize quantitative flux analysis, the mechanisms underlying tissue- and stress-specific regulation, the perception of carotenoid-derived signals, and strategies to improve stress resilience while minimizing growth and yield penalties.

titre: From Nitrate Perception to Environmental Adaptation: Functional Elucidation and Regulatory Networks of the Plant NLP Family.
titre_fr: From Nitrate Perception to Environmental Adaptation: Functional Elucidation and Regulatory Networks of the Plant NLP Family.
auteurs: Ahmad Hafiz Ishtiaq, Liu Ying, Chen Chunrui, Jia Lijie, Zhu Huihui, Yang Jianli
resume: Nitrogen is a necessary macronutrient that limits plant growth and crop productivity, yet excessive fertilizer application has resulted in serious environmental consequences. The NIN-like protein (NLP) family consists of plant-specific transcription factors that serve as central regulators of nitrate signaling. In 2022, the discovery of NLP7 as an intracellular nitrate receptor represented a major conceptual shift from transcriptional regulation to signal perception. This review systematically summarizes the molecular architecture of NLP proteins, focusing on the conserved RWP-RK DNA-binding domain, the PB1 protein-protein interaction module, and the GAF-like domain associated with the integration of multiple signals. It also examines the species-specific expansion and evolutionary diversification of the NLP family, as well as the multilayered mechanisms that regulate NLP activity, including phosphorylation as a signal-dependent molecular switch, SUMOylation as a negative feedback mechanism, transcriptional regulation of downstream targets, and PB1-mediated protein interaction networks. In addition to nitrate signaling, NLPs serve as central hubs linking nitrogen and carbon metabolism and mediating responses to abiotic stresses including cold, heat, salinity, and iron deficiency. Notably, the NLP7-NIGT1.3 module coordinates a growth-stress trade-off during iron deficiency by modulating nitrate signaling intensity, revealing a previously unrecognized mechanism for balancing stress adaptation with growth maintenance. NLPs also participate in developmental processes, including lateral root formation and symbiotic nodulation. Finally, this review highlights the potential of NLP-based approaches for crop genetic improvement, such as overexpression of key NLP genes or CRISPR/Cas-mediated editing, to improve nitrogen use efficiency, stress tolerance, and yield. Collectively, these insights provide a theoretical foundation for developing crop varieties with improved nitrogen-use efficiency and context-dependent stress adaptation, while acknowledging the inherent trade-offs between productivity and resilience.

titre: Clinical and Self-Care Factors Associated with Fear-of-Falling Avoidance Behavior in Older Adults with Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study.
titre_fr: Clinical and Self-Care Factors Associated with Fear-of-Falling Avoidance Behavior in Older Adults with Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study.
auteurs: Gezer Uluğtekin Elif, Arda Hamdiye
resume: Fear-of-falling avoidance behavior can restrict mobility and independence among older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This study examined associations of diabetes self-care behaviors and selected clinical and fall-related characteristics with fear-of-falling avoidance behavior. This cross-sectional study included 137 adults aged ≥65 years with T2DM attending Diyarbakır Gazi Yaşargil Training and Research Hospital between November 2023 and April 2024. Data were collected using the Patient Information Form, Fear of Falling Avoidance Behavior Questionnaire (FFABQ), and Summary of Diabetes Self-Care Activities (SDSCA). Correlation analysis and hierarchical stepwise regression were performed, with age and sex entered as prespecified covariates. Additional analyses included a clinically justified simultaneous-entry model and 2000 bootstrap repetitions of the screening and selection procedure. The final stepwise model explained 66.9% of the variance in FFABQ scores (adjusted R2 = 0.653). Higher age (β = 0.432), assistive device use (β = 0.408), diabetic foot (β = 0.235), and longer diabetes treatment duration (β = 0.159) were associated with higher scores, whereas higher SDSCA exercise scores were associated with lower scores (β = -0.246; all p ≤ 0.003). Sex was not significantly associated with FFABQ scores. The simultaneous-entry model yielded similar associations. Bootstrap selection frequencies were 100.0% for assistive device use, 97.80% for exercise, 86.55% for diabetic foot, and 45.05% for treatment duration. These exploratory associations may inform nursing assessment of mobility, diabetic foot status, exercise behavior, and fear-related activity restriction. The association with treatment duration requires particular caution because of selection uncertainty. Longitudinal and experimental studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships and evaluate the efficacy and safety of exercise interventions tailored to foot status and functional capacity.

titre: Genome Editing for Earliness and Plant Architecture in Cucurbit Crops: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives.
titre_fr: Genome Editing for Earliness and Plant Architecture in Cucurbit Crops: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives.
auteurs: Wan Lili, Wang Zhuanrong, Ren Jian, Wei Jiaqi, Zeng Hongxia, Li Xiaoyong, Qu Jiuhong, Xiong Jianshun, Tang Mi
resume: Earliness and plant architecture are major breeding targets in cucurbit crops because they influence crop duration, early yield, planting density, canopy management, and production efficiency. This review summarizes genetic, molecular, and genome-editing advances related to flowering, sex expression, fruit development, stem elongation, branching, and canopy architecture in cucumber, melon, watermelon, Cucurbita species, and other cucurbits. Current evidence shows that earlier flowering or increased femaleness does not necessarily lead to earlier commercial maturity, while compact growth must be evaluated together with yield, fruit quality, and environmental adaptation. CRISPR/Cas9 knockout remains the most established editing approach, whereas base editing, cis-regulatory editing, multiplex editing, developmental-regulator-assisted regeneration, and DNA-free RNP delivery offer promising routes toward more precise trait optimization. Major constraints include genotype-dependent transformation, pleiotropic effects, limited validation in elite germplasm, and scarce direct evidence for shortening fruit-development duration. An evidence-guided framework is proposed that links trait definition, functional genomics, target prioritization, tailored genome editing, whole-plant evaluation, and breeding deployment. Future progress will depend on quantitatively tuned alleles and coordinated optimization of reproductive timing, canopy architecture, productivity, fruit quality, and environmental stability.

titre: BZR1 and BES1: From Brassinosteroid Signaling Termini to Multifunctional Integrators of Plant Growth and Environmental Adaptation.
titre_fr: BZR1 and BES1: From Brassinosteroid Signaling Termini to Multifunctional Integrators of Plant Growth and Environmental Adaptation.
auteurs: Guo Fengxiao, Ge Shenghong, Lei Mingguang
resume: BZR1 (Brassinazole-resistant 1) and BES1 (bri1-EMS suppressor1) are the principal transcription factors that convert brassinosteroid (BR) perception into genome-wide transcriptional programs governing plant growth, development, and stress responses. Once regarded as end-effectors of a linear receptor-to-nucleus relay, they are now recognized as central hubs that integrate diverse endogenous and environmental cues into context-specific transcriptional outputs. We synthesize recent progress across four connected levels. Structurally, a modular architecture enables simultaneous target recognition, signal input, and output control. Mechanistically, the canonical BIN2-mediated phosphorylation switch is expanded by upstream regulators that couple membrane dynamics, carbon status, protein homeostasis, and nuclear import to BZR1/BES1, while ubiquitination, SUMOylation, redox modification, and acetylation form an interconnected post-translational network. During transcriptional execution, dephosphorylated BZR1/BES1 partition targets into activated and repressed sets through cis-element preference, corepressor recruitment, chromatin modifiers, and partnerships with factors such as PIF4 and ARF6. Physiologically, BZR1/BES1 coordinate anutrient-responsive metabolism, yield-related traits, and abiotic-stress tolerance, with marked functional divergence among crop orthologs. We highlight open questions in signal-integration specificity and discuss how BZR1/BES1 modules could be engineered for climate-resilient crops.

titre: Genomic Signatures of Independently Evolved Walking-Associated Locomotion in Fishes.
titre_fr: Genomic Signatures of Independently Evolved Walking-Associated Locomotion in Fishes.
auteurs: Wang Qin, Wang Bao, Zhu Chenglong, Yue Huishan, Fan Deqian, Xu Wenjie, Zheng Jiangmin, Ling Jianzhong, Zhao Liulan, Yang Song, Song Xiaojing, Tan Ling
resume: Walking-associated locomotion has evolved independently in several fish lineages through distinct anatomical and biomechanical mechanisms. The spiny red gurnard (Chelidonichthys spinosus) provides an experimentally tractable model for dissecting the genetic basis of walking-associated locomotor specialization. We assembled a high-quality chromosome-level genome of the spiny red gurnard and performed a comparative genomic analysis across five walking-associated fish lineages. An integrated protein-protein interaction (PPI) network revealed high clustering coefficients and significant enrichment in fin development and locomotion pathways, indicating candidate functional similarity of lineage-specific genes at the protein interaction level. Shared positively selected genes (PSGs), including jph2, ccdc80, lrrc7, and ap3b2, were identified as candidate genes potentially associated with neuromuscular function. Specifically, in the spiny red gurnard, cdh23, showed lineage-specific positive-selection signals and amino acid changes, suggesting a potential contribution to mechanosensory adaptation. Furthermore, we identified changed conserved noncoding elements (CNEs) in each lineage, with some showing convergent changes near wnt3 and cyp26a1 in specific species pairs. A species-specific CNE deletion in the tax1bp1b intron was tested in HEK293T cells using sequences from zebrafish and spiny red gurnard; the two sequences showed different heterologous reporter activities. Overall, our analyses provide exploratory evidence for a dual pattern of genomic variation potentially underlying walking locomotor evolution: functional association at the protein network level coupled with predominantly lineage-specific yet occasionally convergent regulatory changes. This work also offers insights into environmental adaptation in fishes and a valuable genomic resource for studying convergent evolution.

titre: Adolescent Gross Motor Function Classification System level and adult function in cerebral palsy.
titre_fr: Adolescent Gross Motor Function Classification System level and adult function in cerebral palsy.
auteurs: Verschuren Olaf, van Driel Marieke, van Rijssen Ilse
resume: The Gross Motor Function Classification System - Expanded and Revised (GMFCS-E&R) describes gross motor performance in cerebral palsy (CP), yet its oldest age band ends at 18 years. In adulthood, a reported GMFCS level may reflect either an adolescent classification or a current adult-derived rating using paediatric descriptors. These uses are not equivalent; neither captures the full range of change in adult functioning. Evidence shows heterogeneous trajectories: GMFCS levels may remain stable alongside shifts in mobility, pain, fatigue, independence, assistive device use, and participation. We recommend purpose-sensitive reporting of the adolescent GMFCS-E&R level, when known, alongside a dated profile of current adult mobility and functioning, with any adult-derived rating explicitly labelled. Research should first establish who uses the GMFCS in adulthood, how and for what purposes, and what additional information is needed before determining whether adult-specific guidance, adaptation, extension, or complementary assessment is required.

titre: Understanding Education and Training Needs in Rehabilitation Technologies Among Those With Lived Experience, Rehabilitation Health and Care Professionals, and Technology Professionals: Qualitative Study.
titre_fr: Understanding Education and Training Needs in Rehabilitation Technologies Among Those With Lived Experience, Rehabilitation Health and Care Professionals, and Technology Professionals: Qualitative Study.
auteurs: Thornton Angela, Horrocks Matthew, Abbott-Fleming Victoria, Blake Holly
resume: Demand for rehabilitation services and associated technologies is increasing globally due to population aging and rising chronic disease burden. Despite their potential to enhance access, efficiency, and outcomes, adoption of rehabilitation technologies in clinical practice is variable. Barriers include limited workforce capability and confidence, resource constraints, fragmented governance, and challenges integrating technologies into existing systems. Collaboration among health and care professionals, educators, technology professionals, and individuals with lived experience is essential to identify training needs and strengthen capability for technology-enabled rehabilitation. This study aimed to develop an in-depth understanding of education and training needs for rehabilitation technologies across 3 stakeholder groups-rehabilitation professionals, technology professionals, and individuals with lived experience to inform future training initiatives. A qualitative study was conducted, primarily across England, using purposive sampling to recruit stakeholders from each group. Data were collected through online focus groups and individual interviews and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Although thematic analysis is inherently interpretive, the initial analysis focused primarily on the descriptive content of participants' accounts. Subsequently, deeper theoretical interpretation was undertaken through application of the capability, opportunity, motivation-behavior (COM-B) model, selected domains from the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF), and the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). COM-B was used to identify behavioral determinants, with selected domains from the TDF used to clarify behavioral influences. CFIR was then applied to situate behavioral determinants within organizational and system-level contexts. A total of 50 participants contributed to 7 focus groups and 11 individual interviews. Following this, 3 overarching themes were identified: (1) perceived capability and confidence in technology engagement, (2) system-level resource constraints, and (3) fragmented governance structures and organizational decision-making. COM-B mapping indicated that capability-related influences were most prominent among individuals with lived experience, whereas opportunity-related and structural constraints were more influential for rehabilitation and technology professionals. CFIR analysis highlighted that these behavioral determinants were embedded within, and often constrained by, infrastructure, procurement processes, and wider National Health Service (NHS) policy. Individuals with lived experience require accessible, ongoing support to build confidence and skills in using rehabilitation technologies. Rehabilitation professionals and technology professionals emphasized the need for structured education on available technologies and practical training on integrating them into clinical workflows, particularly for telerehabilitation and emerging digital and AI-enabled tools. Findings indicate that training initiatives must extend beyond individual skill development to address organizational resources, infrastructure, and governance processes. Coordinated, cross-stakeholder education and training strategies are essential to support equitable and sustainable adoption of rehabilitation technologies within the NHS. Training programs should be co-designed across stakeholder groups, embed behavioral and implementation considerations, and align with NHS infrastructure and procurement pathways. Addressing both capability and system-level constraints will be critical for achieving widespread, confident, and sustained use of rehabilitation technologies.

titre: mRNA chemical modifications in model and crop plants.
titre_fr: mRNA chemical modifications in model and crop plants.
auteurs: Liu Xiaoye, Zhao Jie, Xue Xiaoming, Chen Mingjia
resume: Post-transcriptional RNA modifications have emerged as a crucial layer of epigenetic regulation in eukaryotes, profoundly influencing mRNA processing, stability, and translational efficiency. As RNA modification research expands from mammalian systems to plants, its significance for crop improvement and environmental adaptation is becoming increasingly evident. This review synthesizes current research on the plant epitranscriptomic landscape-primarily focusing on N6-methyladenosine (m<sup>6</sup>A), alongside N4-acetylcytidine (ac<sup>4</sup>C), 5-methylcytosine (m<sup>5</sup>C), 1-methyladenosine (m<sup>1</sup>A), 7-methylguanosine (m<sup>7</sup>G), and pseudouridine (Ψ). By exploring the dynamic machinery of specific "writers," "erasers," and "readers," we highlight how these epitranscriptomic marks orchestrate plant growth, developmental phase transitions, and adaptive responses to abiotic stresses in model species and major crops. Rapid advances in detection methods, from conventional chromatography to third-generation single-molecule sequencing, have largely driven these biological insights. Although regulatory mechanisms and cross-species conservation of most modifications beyond m<sup>6</sup>A remain poorly understood, their translational potential is undeniable. Ultimately, we discuss how leveraging gene-editing technologies to manipulate these epitranscriptomic pathways offers a transformative strategy for molecular breeding, aiming to enhance crop yield, nutritional quality, and abiotic stress tolerance.

titre: PHI: a Galaxy-based workflow for reproducible prophage-host interaction analysis and standardized viral-genomics reporting.
titre_fr: PHI: a Galaxy-based workflow for reproducible prophage-host interaction analysis and standardized viral-genomics reporting.
auteurs: Saraiva João Pedro, Borim Corrêa Felipe, Bernt Matthias, Ghanem Nawras, Nieto Esteban, Brizola Toscan Rodolfo, Wick Lukas Y, Chatzinotas Antonis
resume: Viruses that infect bacteria, known as bacteriophages or phages, are widespread in nature and play important roles in shaping microbial communities and ecosystem functions. Some phages can integrate into bacterial genomes as "prophages", where they may influence the biology of their host by carrying genes that affect metabolism, virulence, or environmental adaptation. Despite their importance, studying prophages and their interactions with bacterial hosts remains challenging because it typically requires combining many complex computational tools and can be resource-intensive. In this study, we introduce the Prophage-Host Interaction Toolkit (PHI), a user-friendly and automated workflow available through the Galaxy platform. PHI brings together multiple established tools into a single, reproducible pipeline that identifies candidate prophages, evaluates their quality, predicts host relationships, and characterizes key functional genes. Importantly, all results are summarized in an interactive report that simplifies interpretation. Applied to the MBARC22 mock community of 22 bacterial reference genomes as a workflow demonstration, PHI identified 41 candidate prophages across 14 hosts, including high- and medium-quality viral genomes. Most host genomes exhibited > 99% completeness and < 1% contamination, while DefenseFinder identified between 3 and 24 antiviral defense systems per genome. To further evaluate applicability to metagenome-derived assemblies, PHI was also applied to three MAGs and their matched reference genomes. resume_fr: Viruses that infect bacteria, known as bacteriophages or phages, are widespread in nature and play important roles in shaping microbial communities and ecosystem functions. Some phages can integrate into bacterial genomes as "prophages", where they may influence the biology of their host by carrying genes that affect metabolism, virulence, or environmental adaptation. Despite their importance, studying prophages and their interactions with bacterial hosts remains challenging because it typically requires combining many complex computational tools and can be resource-intensive. In this study, we introduce the Prophage-Host Interaction Toolkit (PHI), a user-friendly and automated workflow available through the Galaxy platform. PHI brings together multiple established tools into a single, reproducible pipeline that identifies candidate prophages, evaluates their quality, predicts host relationships, and characterizes key functional genes. Importantly, all results are summarized in an interactive report that simplifies interpretation. Applied to the MBARC22 mock community of 22 bacterial reference genomes as a workflow demonstration, PHI identified 41 candidate prophages across 14 hosts, including high- and medium-quality viral genomes. Most host genomes exhibited > 99% completeness and < 1% contamination, while DefenseFinder identified between 3 and 24 antiviral defense systems per genome. titre: Comparative Analysis of Phenotypic Characteristics and Antimicrobial Resistance Among Aeromonas veronii Strains Isolated from Different Farmed Freshwater Fish.
titre_fr: Comparative Analysis of Phenotypic Characteristics and Antimicrobial Resistance Among Aeromonas veronii Strains Isolated from Different Farmed Freshwater Fish.
auteurs: Yu Guina, Shen Mengli, Yang Wenjing, Lu Di, Fan Enguo, Wang Xiaolei, Sui Zhihai
resume: Aeromonas veronii is an important zoonotic pathogen causing severe diseases and high mortality in freshwater aquaculture. In this study, five strains (LY-3, JY-1, G7, G8, and WL-3) were isolated from different diseased freshwater fish in Linyi City, Shandong Province, China, and identified as A. veronii using phylogenetic analysis based on 16S rRNA and gyrB sequences. Five strains grew at 20-40°C, pH 5.0-8.0, and 0-3% NaCl, demonstrating strong environmental tolerance. Their optimal temperature and pH were identical, but optimal NaCl concentration was strain-dependent. Despite harboring the hemolysin-related genes act, aer, and hlyA, all strains except JY-1 exhibited β-hemolytic activity. All strains exhibited distinct flagella-driven motility abilities. Specifically, only strain G8 possessed two polar flagella and exhibited the strongest swimming motility. Similarly, all strains formed biofilms, correlating with the production of N-acyl-homoserine lactone (AHL). Worryingly, all strains exhibited multi-drug resistance to three penicillin-class antibiotics, midecamycin, clindamycin, three carbapenems, vancomycin, and polymyxin B. Additionally, five strains carried blaTEM and blaCphA3 genes, and four strains (excluding LY-3) additionally harbored the blaOXA gene. Encouragingly, most of isolates remained susceptible to florfenicol and enrofloxacin. These results indicate considerable intra-specific heterogeneity among A. veronii strains from different geographical origins and host sources, suggesting an urgent need for precise treatments.

titre: Computational functional annotation and structural modelling of hypothetical proteins in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia NCTC10958.
titre_fr: Computational functional annotation and structural modelling of hypothetical proteins in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia NCTC10958.
auteurs: Alnaqshabandy Iman Hussein Fadhiladeen
resume: Antimicrobial resistance represents a significant global health challenge, specifically concerning the escalation of multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria. Stenotrophomonas maltophilia has emerged as a prevalent pathogen affecting immunocompromised patients in intensive care units. Its incidence has notably increased, particularly during the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic, complicated by resistance mechanisms such as enzymatic degradation and biofilm formation. Despite its clinical importance, the functional roles of many genomic regions remain obscure. This study aimed to characterize 61 hypothetical proteins from S. maltophilia NCTC10958 to elucidate their involvement in virulence and adaptation. Functional annotation revealed that a significant proportion of these proteins are membrane-associated enzymes and transporters essential for environmental adaptation. Key findings include the identification of putative virulence factors involved in biofilm formation and motility, such as phosphoglycerate mutase and type IV pilus assembly proteins. Crucially, the analysis uncovered key functional determinants, including a ComEC/Rec2 family competence protein involved in DNA uptake and a mycobacterial membrane protein large family transporter linked to cell envelope processes and transport. Structural modelling validated high-confidence tertiary structures for these targets, confirming their biological feasibility. These insights provide a foundation for understanding the pathogenicity of S. maltophilia NCTC10958 and highlight specific HPs as promising candidates for therapeutic intervention.

titre: The fungal phosphate starvation regulator CtPHO4 couples nutrient adaptation to host colonization through the effector NFC1.
titre_fr: The fungal phosphate starvation regulator CtPHO4 couples nutrient adaptation to host colonization through the effector NFC1.
auteurs: Newfeld Jacy, Aoki Seishiro, Haba Hiromi, Takagi Momoko, Takahashi Nozomu, Kubota Akane, Endo Motomu, Hiruma Kei
resume: Plant-associated microbes must balance environmental adaptation with virulence and host colonization to survive in fluctuating ecosystems, yet the molecular mechanisms coupling these processes remain poorly understood. Here, we identify the effector NUTRIENT-DEPENDENT FACILITATOR OF COLONIZATION 1 (NFC1) in a conditionally pathogenic Colletotrichum tofieldiae strain, whose expression is tightly regulated by both temperature and phosphate availability. By leveraging plant phosphate starvation response (PSR) mutants and phosphate supplementation, we demonstrate that NFC1 expression is driven by the internal phosphate status of the host. Notably, the fungal PSR regulator CtPHO4 represses NFC1 and colonization during phosphate starvation, while simultaneously activating canonical fungal PSR-related genes. Conversely, under phosphate sufficiency, NFC1 is strongly induced and promotes infection. This host colonization and adaptation machinery is partially conserved in a beneficial C. tofieldiae strain. This study uncovers a molecular link between metabolic adaptation and host colonization, providing a conceptual framework for understanding fungal lifestyle transitions under changing environments.

titre: Spinal cord-computer interfaces for neurorehabilitation: Technical challenges and clinical perspectives.
titre_fr: Spinal cord-computer interfaces for neurorehabilitation: Technical challenges and clinical perspectives.
auteurs: Chen Hengshuo, Wang Yang, Chao Bo, Wang Zhonghan, Wu Minfei
resume: This Perspective aims to clarify the clinical and engineering scope of spinal cord-computer interfaces (SCCIs) in neurorehabilitation, distinguishing them from adjacent brain-computer interface, neuromodulation, and assistive-technology approaches while identifying the key barriers to translation. We synthesize evidence from epidural electrical stimulation, spinal bioelectronics, neural decoding, actuator control, brain-spine interfaces, and activity-dependent rehabilitation to define SCCIs as closed-loop or potentially closed-loop spinal interfaces. We then organize the major translational barriers into five interdependent domains: implantation strategy, long-term interface stability, spinal signal integration, actuator coupling, and activity-dependent circuit reconstruction. Our synthesis identifies five barriers that currently limit SCCI translation: surgical targeting and localization, chronic interface degradation, heterogeneous spinal pathophysiology, real-time decoding and actuator compatibility, and incomplete understanding of activity-dependent circuit remodeling. Although targeted spinal stimulation and hybrid brain-spine systems have shown functional benefits in selected populations, these advances remain difficult to generalize without adaptive, patient-specific system architectures. By distinguishing SCCIs from adjacent neurotechnology paradigms and linking engineering barriers to clinical decision points, this framework may support consistent terminology, calibrated translational claims, and the development of adaptive, patient-specific closed-loop strategies for restoring native motor control.

titre: Stigmatization and Self-Other Perception Profiles Amongst Adolescents With Learning Disabilities: A Mixed-Methods Exploration.
titre_fr: Stigmatization and Self-Other Perception Profiles Amongst Adolescents With Learning Disabilities: A Mixed-Methods Exploration.
auteurs: Goodman-Vincent Ella, Vaccarella Paige, Cunningham Todd
resume: This study explored experiences of stigmatization among adolescents with learning disabilities (LDs) in Grades 7 to 10 (N = 77). Two aims guided the study: (a) to examine how adolescents' personal views of their LD differed from expectations of how others perceive them, and (b) to investigate how discrepancies between these views relate to key psychological and educational outcomes. A three-stage approach was employed, involving thematic analysis, conversion of qualitative data into quantitative values, and statistical analysis. Thematic analysis showed overlap as well as divergence between self-perceptions and perceived societal views. Personal views emphasized academic ability (39.7%), difference (19.2%), and support (20.5%), whereas expected societal perceptions highlighted being seen as "stupid/dumb" (28.1%), concerns about social relationships (16.7%), and lack of LD awareness (12.5%). Quantitative conversion identified four self-other perception profiles, with the most common being balanced self/balanced other (37.6%) and balanced self/negative other (38.9%). Statistical analyses suggested these profiles were associated with perceived stigma related to assistive technology (AT) use, although not with frequency of AT use or academic self-concept. Implications for intervention, study limitations, and directions for future research are discussed.

titre: Field site-specific proteome remodeling under contrasting environmental conditions in Brassica rapa.
titre_fr: Field site-specific proteome remodeling under contrasting environmental conditions in Brassica rapa.
auteurs: Kurina Anastasia B, Hanschen Franziska S, Vahabi Khabat, Púčiková Vanda, Artemeva Anna M, Witzel Katja
resume: Plant plasticity enables adaptation to heterogeneous environments, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying long-term climatic acclimation in crops remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigated the proteome plasticity of Brassica rapa across three contrasting field sites representing subarctic (68°N), temperate (59°N), and subtropical (44°N) climate-associated conditions. Twelve accessions spanning three crop types were cultivated, and subjected to proteome analysis and protein-metabolite correlation analysis. Principal component and clustering analyses revealed a strong imprint of the field sites on proteome patterns. Functional enrichment analysis identified site-specific protein networks: subarctic conditions favored enrichment of proteins involved in photosynthesis, carbohydrate metabolism, and glycolysis, supporting energy capture and cold acclimation; temperate conditions induced proteins related to respiration and redox homeostasis; and subtropical conditions induced proteins involved in clade-specific metabolism, particularly glucosinolate biosynthesis, alongside amino acid and redox pathways. Based on proteome data, key adaptive responses to the three field sites included modulation of cellular respiration proteins, such as NADH dehydrogenase subunits, and shifts in phytohormone regulation, with cytokinins enriched under subarctic, gibberellin-regulated proteins under temperate, and auxin-associated proteins under subtropical conditions. Chinese cabbage accession A247 demonstrated the highest proteome plasticity, whereas root turnip accessions showed lower plasticity. Reaction-norm analyses across the latitudinal climate gradient revealed genotype and crop type dependent trajectories in mean protein Z-scores, which shows contrasting adaptive strategies across cultivars. B. rapa shows strong proteomic flexibility across different field sites, indicating distinct metabolic adjustments. These findings suggest that proteomic profiling aids in identifying adaptive traits and could guide crop breeding strategies to improve resilience under future climate change.

titre: Genomic epidemiology and transmission dynamics of Acinetobacter baumannii: Comparison of clinical and wastewater isolates.
titre_fr: Genomic epidemiology and transmission dynamics of Acinetobacter baumannii: Comparison of clinical and wastewater isolates.
auteurs: Wang Xiao, Zhang Yue, Liang Yanru, You Shuqi, Xu Tongsheng, Xu Yiying, Qiu Ye, Wang Yuanping, Feng Jun, Zhao Bing, Shen Yifeng, Ren Lili
resume: This study characterized the epidemiological, phenotypic, and genomic dynamics of Acinetobacter baumannii across inpatient, outpatient, hospital environmental, and diverse wastewater habitats from January to December 2025. Bacterial detection exhibited pronounced seasonal variations and habitat heterogeneity, with wastewater showing the highest prevalence and summer marking the peak period. High-touch surfaces represented the core hospital contamination nodes, and healthcare workers faced potential risks of carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii (CRAB) colonization. Notably, CRAB and multidrug-resistant strains appeared confined to clinical niches, where the dominant ST2<sup>Pas</sup> and ST164<sup>Pas</sup> clones stably harbored abundant carbapenemases, disinfectant resistance genes, and virulence factors. Anthropogenic antibiotic and sanitizer selective pressures likely drive their high multiple antibiotic resistance index (MARI) phenotypes. Conversely, wastewater strains were predominantly pan-susceptible (MARI < 0.2) but enriched with novel sequence types (STs) and rare resistance genes, suggesting their role as a natural reservoir for genetic diversification. Core-genome SNP transmission networks indicated high-density intra-hospital cross-transmission and occult inter-hospital dissemination, while capturing potential bidirectional cross-habitat spillover events. Mechanistically, conjugative plasmids, insertion sequences (IS256/IS3/IS66), and active prophages mediated resistance and virulence recombination in clinical strains. Meanwhile, wastewater strains might utilize the ISNCY family to undergo environmental adaptation, with integrons playing a minor role in resistance spread. This study uncovers the divergent evolutionary pathways of A. baumannii, providing critical genomic evidence for integrated clinical-environmental management to mitigate the cross-niche dissemination of antimicrobial resistance.

titre: Does sexual trait expression reflect adaptation in a wild insect?
titre_fr: Does sexual trait expression reflect adaptation in a wild insect?
auteurs: Rodríguez-Muñoz Rolando, Hopwood Paul, Tregenza Tom
resume: Sexual selection has the potential to accelerate adaption if males that are better adapted to the environment are more likely to mate. This requires that a male's degree of environmental adaptation is reflected in his expression of secondary sexual traits. To test this hypothesis, we created a population of crickets in a meadow in N. Spain where half of the individuals were expected to be well adapted to the local environment and half poorly adapted. We achieved this by replacing all the crickets in the natural population with individuals derived from replicate independent source populations. Half of the introduced crickets had parents from low altitude environments similar to the experimental meadow. The other half had parents from high altitude environments to which genetic adaptation in traits has previously been identified. After tagging every adult, we observed the lives of these common-garden-reared and either genetically well-adapted or poorly-adapted individuals. Using video from a network of 140 day/night cameras we were able to quantify sexual trait expression, mating success, lifespan and developmental timing. We observed differences between crickets from high and low altitudes in the date that they reached adulthood according to where they were reared. There were also complex interactions between genetic background, rearing environment and trait expression that affected mating success. However, contrary to the theory, we did not find any convincing evidence for differences in sexual trait expression between well adapted and poorly adapted males.

titre: Bacterial extracellular vesicles as carriers of genetic and regulatory messages.
titre_fr: Bacterial extracellular vesicles as carriers of genetic and regulatory messages.
auteurs: Kubler Loan, Vial Ludovic, Nazaret Fanny
resume: Although bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) are increasingly recognized as mediators of communication, the contribution of their nucleic acid cargo remains poorly understood. Providing an overview of BEV-nucleic acid content and their roles, this review first examines their true significance. In particular, it highlights why they should not be treated as bulk cargo, given that DNA and RNA contents exhibit various sub-vesicular localizations that may define their ecological roles. We propose that this heterogeneity allows viewing BEVs as distinct subpopulations. Furthermore, recent studies increasingly propose the involvement of DNA associated with BEVs in horizontal gene transfer between bacteria and that of vesicular small RNA (sRNA) during host-bacteria interactions. Overall, this review offers insights into considering BEVs in an ecological context based on notable recent studies.
