titre: Identifying workplace supports and interventions for employees living with neurodegenerative cognitive impairment: A rapid review.
titre_fr: Identifying workplace supports and interventions for employees living with neurodegenerative cognitive impairment: A rapid review.
auteurs: Kenny Kiera, Swarbrick Caroline, Holland Carol
resume: BackgroundAs people work to older ages, there is greater risk of age-related morbidities developing whilst in employment. Age-related dementia, cognitive impairment, or young-onset dementia may be diagnosed during an individual's working life.ObjectiveThis rapid review aimed to identify and synthesise the types of supports and interventions described or implemented for people diagnosed whilst working.MethodsA rapid review was conducted with searches across three databases: MEDLINE, PsycINFO and Scopus and grey literature sources. Articles were screened against the inclusion criteria.ResultsFifteen articles and five grey literature sources met the inclusion criteria. The literature originated from high-income settings in Europe, Canada, Japan, and Australia. The evidence base was predominantly qualitative and exploratory. Identified supports were grouped by type and level: individual (reasonable adjustments, assistive technology), relational (colleague, managerial and HR support; training), and organisational (policy, legal frameworks, multi-agency coordination, including occupational health). Identified support measures were either implemented in practice or recommended.ConclusionThe review identified a foundation of workplace support for employees living with neurodegenerative cognitive impairment. However, both the type of support available and its implementation varied across employers. Greater consistency in the provision of support is needed to ensure that employees' needs are met during a period of considerable workplace uncertainty. Individual, relational, and organisational supports may extend workforce participation and promote wellbeing among people living with neurodegenerative cognitive impairment. Embedding support across multiple levels may help workplaces advance inclusive employment practices that recognise and accommodate neurodegenerative cognitive impairment.

titre: Arthroscopic Double EndoButton Adjustable-Loop Plate Fixation for Acute Acromioclavicular Joint Dislocation.
titre_fr: Arthroscopic Double EndoButton Adjustable-Loop Plate Fixation for Acute Acromioclavicular Joint Dislocation.
auteurs: Huang Shenbo, Zheng Zhenxin, Qian Chao, Yuan Hang, Bao Huricha
resume: Acute acromioclavicular joint dislocation is a shoulder injury. Surgical intervention is typically recommended for Rockwood type IV to VI injuries with significant displacement. Both traditional open surgery and existing arthroscopic techniques have limitations in terms of trauma, stability, and procedural complexity. This article introduces an arthroscopic fixation technique using a double EndoButton adjustable-loop plate. It aims to achieve anatomical reduction and sustained compressive fixation of the acromioclavicular joint through a dual-EndoButton structure and an adjustable-loop design. This method is relatively straightforward to perform, minimally invasive, and biomechanically sound, offering a reliable new option for the minimally invasive treatment of acute acromioclavicular joint dislocations. Preliminary clinical practice has shown favorable reduction outcomes, stable fixation performance, and potential for early rehabilitation.

titre: Geminated Maxillary Incisors With Talon Cusp: A Case Report With Management and Narrative Review.
titre_fr: Geminated Maxillary Incisors With Talon Cusp: A Case Report With Management and Narrative Review.
auteurs: Al-Ak Hali Mohammed Sultan, Kelani Reem Hassan, Halawi Rahaf Ahmed, Alakhali Hani Saeed, Abueishah Atyaf Fassal, Peeran Syed Wali
resume: Recognition of teeth with gemination and/or talon cusp, along with early treatment, is important to prevent complications such as occlusal interference, malocclusion, the formation of caries and periodontal pockets, and esthetic issues. This case report is aimed at describing the multidisciplinary management of a rare case of geminated permanent maxillary central incisors associated with a talon cusp and to review similar cases previously reported in the literature. The diagnoses were determined through a combination of intraoral photographs, dental casts, periapical x-rays, and cone-beam computed tomography. A long-term, multidisciplinary treatment plan was developed for managing this geminated tooth with a talon cusp. This case report describes the successful diagnosis and management of an 11-year-old patient with Class II malocclusion and bilateral gemination of the two maxillary incisors. A unilateral talon cusp was erupting on the palatal surface of the malpositioned maxillary left central incisor, extending from the cervical area toward the incisal edge and reaching approximately two-thirds of the crown length. The talon cusp caused occlusal interference with the mandibular left lateral incisor, and a 5-mm periodontal pocket had formed at the distopalatal site of the maxillary left central incisor. The treatment focused on managing tooth gemination through a combination of occlusal adjustment, restorative procedures, and orthodontic therapy. The talon cusp was gradually reduced in size through selective enamel grinding to eliminate occlusal interference, followed by the application of topical fluoride. Teeth affected by caries were restored with appropriate fillings, and orthodontic treatment was provided as necessary. The rehabilitation of geminated maxillary anterior incisors with a talon cusp requires a multidisciplinary approach for optimal management and outcomes.

titre: Association of an Intensive Multimodal Perioperative Management Bundle With Short-Term Recovery After Surgery for Trimalleolar Fractures: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
titre_fr: Association of an Intensive Multimodal Perioperative Management Bundle With Short-Term Recovery After Surgery for Trimalleolar Fractures: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
auteurs: He Min, Chen Yongkang, Zou Xue, Zou Yamei, Ding Hui
resume: To examine the association between receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle and short-term functional recovery, pain, and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing surgery for trimalleolar fractures. This single-center retrospective cohort included 84 patients who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for trimalleolar fractures between September 2023 and September 2025. The intensive management bundle was a pre-existing standardized routine-care pathway rather than a research intervention developed for this study. Patients were classified retrospectively according to contemporaneous medical and nursing records: 43 patients who received routine management were assigned to a routine-management group, and 41 who received the intensive bundle were assigned to an intensive-pathway group. The investigators did not prospectively enroll patients, assign pathways, deliver study-specific interventions, or collect research-specific data. Primary outcomes were the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) Ankle-Hindfoot Scale and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores; secondary outcomes included first out-of-bed mobilization, length of hospital stay, hospitalization costs, patient satisfaction, and deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Unadjusted mean differences or odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and longitudinal AOFAS and VAS data were analyzed using mixed-design repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA). Because the components were delivered together, no component-specific effect was estimated. No baseline variable differed significantly between groups, although the absence of statistical significance did not establish covariate balance. In unadjusted analyses, receipt of the intensive bundle was associated with earlier first out-of-bed mobilization (mean difference [MD], -22.80 h; 95% confidence interval [CI], -26.48 to -19.12), shorter hospitalization (MD, -3.30 days; 95% CI, -4.14 to -2.46), lower hospitalization costs (MD, -13,114 CNY (1 USD = 7.1429 CNY); 95% CI, -14,979 to -11,249), and higher patient satisfaction (OR, 5.16; 95% CI, 1.04-25.56). VAS scores were lower in the intensive-pathway group at 1 week (3.9 ± 0.9 vs. 4.8 ± 1.0), 1 month (1.3 ± 0.7 vs. 3.2 ± 1.0), and 3 months (1.0 (0.0, 1.0) vs. 2.0 (1.0, 2.0)) postoperatively (all Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.001); RM-ANOVA showed significant group, time, and group-by-time interaction effects for both AOFAS and VAS scores. DVT occurred in 3/41 (7.3%) patients in the intensive-pathway group and 8/43 (18.6%) in the routine-management group, and the difference was not statistically significant (OR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.08-1.41). These findings represent associations with the integrated bundle and cannot be attributed independently to preoperative optimization, ankle-pump exercise, analgesia, mobilization, or follow-up. In this retrospective cohort, receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle was associated with earlier mobilization, shorter hospitalization, lower hospitalization costs, and more favorable short-term functional and pain trajectories. Because the bundle contained multiple simultaneously delivered components, the study cannot determine the independent efficacy of preoperative optimization, ankle-pump exercise, or any other individual measure. In addition, pathway allocation was non-random and the estimates were unadjusted; therefore, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than definitive causal effects.

titre: Comparison of Telerehabilitation and Face-to-Face McKenzie Therapy Following Unilateral Biportal Endoscopic Discectomy: A Multicentre Retrospective Matched Cohort Study.
titre_fr: Comparison of Telerehabilitation and Face-to-Face McKenzie Therapy Following Unilateral Biportal Endoscopic Discectomy: A Multicentre Retrospective Matched Cohort Study.
auteurs: Zhao Cheng, Zhao Ning, Lyu Yiming, Li Zhibin, Chen Jingfeng, Sun Jianfeng, Huang Lihua, Lu Shengdi, Wu Meng
resume: To compare short-term pain, disability, and functional outcomes between telerehabilitation and face-to-face McKenzie therapy following unilateral biportal endoscopic (UBE) discectomy for lumbar disc herniation (LDH). This multicentre retrospective matched cohort study included adults undergoing UBE discectomy for LDH at Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital and Xiyuan Hospital of China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences between October 2023 and December 2024. Patients received either in-home telerehabilitation (Tele) or in-clinic physiotherapy (Clinic) according to the standard practice of the treating centre rather than by random allocation. Propensity score matching (PSM, 1:1) was used to reduce confounding. Both groups completed a 12-week McKenzie programme. Primary outcomes were Modified Von Korff (MvK) pain and disability scales and the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) at 12 weeks. Secondary outcomes included visual analogue scale (VAS) scores, modified lumbar Schober (MLS), and the 6-minute walk test (6MWT). After matching, 122 patients were included (Tele: n = 61; Clinic: n = 61). Matching reduced between-group imbalance for every covariate, with all absolute standardised mean differences (SMDs) below 0.25, although modest residual imbalances remained for some covariates. For the primary outcomes, scores decreased significantly from baseline to 12 weeks in both groups (all time effects, p < 0.001), with no significant group × time interactions detected (MvK pain, p = 0.979; MvK disability, p = 0.794; ODI, p = 0.910). The between-group difference on the MvK pain scale at 12 weeks was substantially smaller than the established minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of 10 points. All secondary outcomes also improved significantly in both groups (all time effects, p < 0.001), with no significant between-group differences detected (all interaction p > 0.05). Overall adverse event rates were comparable between groups. Telerehabilitation and face-to-face McKenzie therapy were associated with comparable short-term improvements after UBE discectomy. These findings suggest that telerehabilitation may be a feasible alternative to in-clinic rehabilitation, although prospective randomised trials are needed for confirmation.

titre: What is therapy in physiotherapy?
titre_fr: What is therapy in physiotherapy?
auteurs: Nicholls David A
resume: The physiotherapy profession carries the word therapy in its name, yet has never subjected the concept to serious philosophical scrutiny. Where psychologists have interrogated the psyche, nurses the meaning of care, and sociologists the nature of medicine, physiotherapy has no equivalent tradition. It has taken for granted what therapy is in order to build a literature centered on what physiotherapy does. This paper aims to clear the ground so that a more fundamental ontological inquiry into what therapy is can begin. It concentrates on five commonly held assumptions (axioms) about everyday practice: that therapy is performed by people; that it is an intentional, deliberate and conscious act; that it is local; that it is immediate; and that it constitutes restoration, repair, and rehabilitation. I argue that all five derive from physiotherapy's long history of treating bodies as discrete, bounded, and static entities, situated in bounded clinical spaces, moving through linear clock-time, and returned to a prior norm. Each assumption is increasingly out of step with twenty-first-century healthcare, and with what physiotherapists already know: that the therapist is rarely the sole agent, that therapeutic effects exceed conscious intent and the clinic walls, and that no stable state of health awaits return.

titre: Barriers and Facilitators to Cardiac Rehabilitation Adherence in Post-PCI Patients: A Qualitative Study From an Implementation Science Perspective.
titre_fr: Barriers and Facilitators to Cardiac Rehabilitation Adherence in Post-PCI Patients: A Qualitative Study From an Implementation Science Perspective.
auteurs: He Xingrong, Wang Jing, Ye Lingyan, Tao Xuemei, Ruan Xiaozhu, Gao Jingquan
resume: To explore barriers and facilitators influencing adherence to cardiac rehabilitation among patients after percutaneous coronary intervention from patient and healthcare-professional perspectives. A descriptive qualitative study guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. Purposive sampling recruited 21 patients receiving Phase II cardiac rehabilitation and 15 healthcare professionals from two tertiary hospitals in Lishui, China. Face-to-face semi-structured interviews were conducted from May to June 2025. Data were analysed using a primarily deductive thematic analysis guided by the framework. Five themes and 11 subthemes were identified across innovation characteristics, inner setting, outer setting, individual characteristics and implementation process. Adherence was influenced by perceived evidence strength and cost; implementation climate, communication and resources; family and policy support; self-efficacy, health-behaviour change and fear of physical exertion; and geographical and scheduling barriers. Adherence after percutaneous coronary intervention reflected interacting patient, family, professional, organisational and health-system determinants. Contrasting rehabilitation infrastructure at the two hospitals helped explain differences in multidisciplinary support and continuity of care. Nurses can provide consistent risk communication, assess fear of physical exertion, involve families in education, coordinate referral and telephone follow-up, and escalate unmet nutritional, psychological and exercise-rehabilitation needs. This study addresses persistent underuse of Phase II cardiac rehabilitation. It shows that non-adherence cannot be attributed to patients alone and identifies organisation- and nursing-sensitive determinants. Findings can inform hospital services caring for patients after percutaneous coronary intervention where rehabilitation capacity is uneven. The study is reported according to the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research. Patients and healthcare professionals contributed interview data and participated in member checking; they were not involved in the initial study design.

titre: Concurrent functional impairment associated with multidimensional social capital among community-dwelling patients with schizophrenia.
titre_fr: Concurrent functional impairment associated with multidimensional social capital among community-dwelling patients with schizophrenia.
auteurs: Chen Yankai, Liu Yanli, Yao Hao, Zhou Yu, Tang Zixuan, Xuan Guo, Wang Lijun, Cai Jun, Zhang Weibo
resume: Social capital is a recognised social determinant of mental health, yet its multidimensional association with functioning in community-dwelling patients with schizophrenia remains unclear. In this cross-sectional study linked to historical records, we assessed social capital and perceived social support in 601 patients under Shanghai's standardised community management system. Observed 2026 functional scores were available for 599 patients. The primary analysis examined concurrent functional impairment; 2021-2025 records were analysed separately as an exploratory historical outcome. Each 1-SD increase in overall social capital was associated with 0.064 points lower concurrent impairment (95% CI -0.098 to -0.030; P < 0.001; standardised coefficient -0.142). The historical association was -0.057 points (95% CI -0.090 to -0.024; P < 0.001). Cognitive social capital, activity participation, social contact and perceived social support were associated with concurrent impairment after false discovery rate correction. Participation was not associated with the historical outcome after correction (q = 0.078). Confirmatory factor analysis did not support adequate structural fit of the social capital instrument. These findings describe concurrent associations in a selected community-managed sample. Reverse causation, measurement overlap and common-cause confounding cannot be excluded, and intervention benefits or future functioning cannot be inferred.

titre: Comparative Clinical Performance of Lingual Fixed Appliances and Clear Aligner Therapy for Esthetic Deep-Bite Correction in Adults.
titre_fr: Comparative Clinical Performance of Lingual Fixed Appliances and Clear Aligner Therapy for Esthetic Deep-Bite Correction in Adults.
auteurs: Özsoy Ömür Polat, Pamukçu Hande, Şar Çağla, Akpınar Nida Su, Akyalçın Sercan
revue: Journal of esthetic and restorative dentistry : official publication of the American Academy of Esthetic Dentistry ... [et al.]
resume: Adult deep-bite correction extends beyond orthodontic alignment because it directly influences anterior esthetics, incisal display, smile arc, anterior guidance, restorative space, and the interdisciplinary planning required for minimally invasive esthetic rehabilitation. Although lingual fixed appliances and clear aligner therapy are widely used esthetic treatment modalities, evidence directly comparing their effectiveness for vertical correction in adults and its potential restorative implications remains limited. Therefore, this study compared adjusted posttreatment overbite and selected cephalometric outcomes between these two treatment modalities in adult deep-bite patients. Pretreatment and posttreatment lateral cephalograms of 38 adult deep-bite patients were analyzed: 19 treated with lingual fixed appliances and 19 with clear aligner therapy. Skeletal and dentoalveolar variables were compared within and between groups. Adjusted between-group treatment effects were assessed using analysis of covariance models controlling for baseline values and age; a second model additionally adjusted for sex, malocclusion class, and treatment duration. Baseline characteristics were comparable, except for a smaller maxillary first molar angulation in the clear aligner group. Skeletal parameters remained generally stable. Both groups showed significant overbite reduction, but overbite correction was greater in the lingual group. Adjusted posttreatment overbite was significantly higher in the clear aligner group than in the lingual group (Model I: 1.03 mm and Model II: 1.05 mm; both p < 0.001). Lingual fixed appliances were associated with significantly greater adjusted overbite reduction than clear aligner therapy in this retrospective sample of adults with deep-bite malocclusion. Although overbite decreased significantly in both groups, the findings indicate a difference in the amount of correction achieved. This finding may inform appliance selection when planning vertical correction as part of interdisciplinary esthetic and restorative treatment.

titre: Giant cell myocarditis mimicking cardiac amyloidosis with apical sparing pattern in echocardiography: a case report.
titre_fr: Giant cell myocarditis mimicking cardiac amyloidosis with apical sparing pattern in echocardiography: a case report.
auteurs: Sawada Shun, Miura Masanobu, Endo Hideaki, Ono Sadahide, Nakamura Akihiro
resume: Giant cell myocarditis typically has a poor prognosis among the various types of myocarditis. Early diagnosis and treatment are essential to save lives. Immunosuppressive therapy is used for giant cell myocarditis; however, evidence in patients on mechanical circulatory support is insufficient. A woman in her 60 s with no history of heart disease or medication was admitted to our hospital because of congestive heart failure. Echocardiography revealed an apical sparing pattern suggestive of cardiac amyloidosis. However, owing to the rapid deterioration of symptoms, an urgent right heart catheterization and myocardial biopsy were performed. Right heart catheterization revealed a cardiac index of 1.20 L/min/m<sup>2</sup>, and rapid myocardial histology indicated inflammatory cell infiltration. She was later diagnosed with giant cell myocarditis with cellular infiltration of irregular multinucleated giant cells in the myocardium. Her condition improved after starting mechanical circulatory support and sequential immunosuppressive therapy, and after successful rehabilitation, she was discharged as an outpatient on Day 183. Early diagnosis and prompt initiation of immunosuppressive therapy are essential in giant cell myocarditis; however, specific findings are lacking. Early myocardial biopsy and prompt mechanical circulatory support initiation should be performed in patients with rapidly deteriorating heart failure presenting with amyloidosis-like echocardiographic findings and in cases where only troponin is elevated and creatine phosphokinase MB is not, considering the possibility of severe oedema. Combination immunosuppressive therapy under mechanical circulatory support is associated with a high infection risk, and starting with single-drug immunosuppressive therapy with careful haemodynamic monitoring is acceptable.

titre: The relationship between perceived social support and health-promoting behaviors among middle-aged and young patients after PCI: the mediating role of fear of disease progression.
titre_fr: The relationship between perceived social support and health-promoting behaviors among middle-aged and young patients after PCI: the mediating role of fear of disease progression.
auteurs: Li Yuxin, Zhong Xiaoli, Zhao Tianxia, Dai Ping, Yang Junrong, Fan Yuting, Wu Jijun, He Lin
resume: This study aims to investigate the mediating role of fear of disease progression in the relationship between perceived social support and health-promoting behaviors among middle-aged and young patients after PCI, providing a theoretical basis for developing targeted interventions to improve health promotion behaviors in this population. This cross-sectional study employed convenience sampling. Between April and October 2024, 265 middle-aged and young patients who underwent PCI were surveyed in the cardiovascular department of a Grade A tertiary hospital in Sichuan Province, China. Data collection utilized questionnaires on general information, the Health-Promoting Lifestyle Scale, the Perceived Social Support Scale, and the Fear of Disease Progression Scale. Data analysis was performed using SPSS 26.0 software for descriptive analysis, univariate analysis, correlation analysis, and multivariate stratified regression analysis. Mediating effect analysis was conducted using Model 4 in the Process v4.1 plugin. The mean health-promoting behaviors score among middle-aged and young patients after PCI was (88.09 ± 9.98) points. titre: Five-year outcomes after brace-free versus brace-based rehabilitation following isolated anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with hamstring tendon autograft: long-term follow-up of a randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Five-year outcomes after brace-free versus brace-based rehabilitation following isolated anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with hamstring tendon autograft: long-term follow-up of a randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Schoepp Christian, Praetorius Arthur, Tennler Janina, Raeder Christian, Schroeder Martin, Hax Jakob, Seelmann Christine, Ohmann Tobias, Efe Turgay, Dudda Marcel, Neidlein Claas
revue: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
resume: Postoperative knee bracing following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) remains common practice despite growing evidence questioning its clinical benefit. Previous studies demonstrated that brace-free rehabilitation was noninferior to brace-based rehabilitation one year after isolated ACLR using hamstring tendon autograft; however, its long-term effects remain unknown. The purpose of this study was to evaluate long-term effects five years after surgery. Patients enrolled in a prospective randomized controlled trial conducted between 2016 and 2019 were recontacted approximately five years after isolated primary ACLR with hamstring tendon autograft for a long-term follow-up. In the original trial, 139 patients had been randomized to postoperative rehabilitation without a brace (n = 71) or with a functional knee brace (n = 68). Participants completed several patient-reported outcome measures. Furthermore, a standardized telephone interview was performed. Changes between the one-year and five-year follow-up were analyzed. Ninety-seven patients participated in the long-term follow-up (n = 45 brace-free group, n = 52 brace group). Mean follow-up was 5.2 ± 1.0 years. No significant differences were observed between groups regarding subjective knee function, activity level, quality of life, rerupture rate, revision surgery, or persistent knee-related complaints at final follow-up. However, there was a significant interaction between treatment group and time for the subjective IKDC score. Patients treated without postoperative bracing showed stable or slightly improved subjective knee function, whereas patients treated with a brace demonstrated a significant decline between one and five years. Brace-free rehabilitation after isolated ACL reconstruction with hamstring tendon autograft remains safe and effective more than five years after surgery. Postoperative bracing did not reduce rerupture rates, revision surgery, or long-term functional impairment. Instead, brace-free rehabilitation demonstrated a more favorable longitudinal development of subjective knee function. These findings further question the routine postoperative prescription of rehabilitative knee braces following isolated ACL reconstruction.

titre: Ultrasound-Guided Pudendal Nerve Block in Elderly Pelvic Organ Prolapse Surgery: Impact on Anesthetic Consumption and Postoperative Recovery-A Randomized Clinical Trial.
titre_fr: Ultrasound-Guided Pudendal Nerve Block in Elderly Pelvic Organ Prolapse Surgery: Impact on Anesthetic Consumption and Postoperative Recovery-A Randomized Clinical Trial.
auteurs: Yang Chen, Lu Zhiying, Li Yannan, Yu Xiaojuan, Hu Changdong, Chen Yisong, Huang Shaoqiang
resume: Nerve block is often used for multimodal analgesia. Surgeries for pelvic organ prolapse (POP) in elderly patients are focused on the perineal area, where pudendal nerve block (PNB) can provide analgesia or anaesthesia. There are limited studies on PNB in POP surgery, mainly addressing postoperative pain relief. This prospective randomized controlled trial examined the impact of ultrasound-guided PNB on intraoperative medication and postoperative recovery in elderly POP surgery patients. Patients aged 60-70 undergoing total vaginal hysterectomy (with or without sacral fixation/colporrhaphy) under general anesthesia were randomized into two groups: PNB (pudendal nerve block) and NPNB (no pudendal nerve block). Anesthesia was induced with target-controlled infusions of remifentanil (3 ng/mL) and propofol (3 µg/mL). The study compared intraoperative anesthetic doses, hemodynamic changes, cardiovascular drug needs, wakefulness time, and post-op recovery quality between the groups. 58 patients completed the study. The PNB group required significantly less remifentanil (386.6 ± 239.1 µg vs 563.1 ± 235.7 µg, p = 0.005) and propofol (645.5 ± 315.2 mg vs 804.2 ± 297.2 mg, p = 0.028) compared to the NPNB group. Intraoperative hemodynamics were more stable in the PNB group, with a reduced need for vasopressors. The PNB group also exhibited faster emergence, lower postoperative pain, and less oversedation,with a non-significant trend toward higher QoR-40 scores. Ultrasound-guided PNB in elderly POP surgery patients reduced opioid and anesthetic doses, shortened awakening time, and produced clinically favourable improvements in postoperative recovery. Larger studies are needed to confirm these benefits for postoperative rehabilitation.

titre: Boosting Post-Stroke Recovery: The Role of Nutritional Supplementation in Reducing Fatigue-A Single-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: Boosting Post-Stroke Recovery: The Role of Nutritional Supplementation in Reducing Fatigue-A Single-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Giovannini Silvia, Pedico Alessandra, Malizia Anna Maria, Angelini Flavia, Assante Di Panzillo Giovanna, Loreti Claudia, Morciano Nadia, Frisullo Giovanni, Petrucci Martina, Biscotti Lorenzo, Biscetti Federico, Flex Andrea, Castelli Letizia
resume: Post-stroke fatigue (PSF) remains a debilitating barrier to recovery. Chronic inflammation and oxidative stress often create physiological plateaus that standard rehabilitation alone cannot resolve. This single-blind randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluated the efficacy of Food for Special Medical Purposes formulated with iron and other vitamins and minerals in Sucrosomial® form, allowing improved absorption, bioavailability, and tolerability, as an adjunct to neurorehabilitation. One hundred and twenty stroke patients were randomized into an experimental group (Sid-G) receiving the specific nutraceutical compound or a control group (CG) receiving standard care. Longitudinal assessments from baseline (T0) through 16 weeks (T3) measured clinical outcomes (including fatigue, motor/cognitive function) and physiological markers, specifically phase angle (PhA) derived from Bioimpedance Analysis, and key inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers (IL-6 and MPO). The Sid-G cohort demonstrated superior, sustained improvements in fatigue, motor, and cognitive function (p < 0.05). These clinical gains were reflected in the following physiological observations: the time × group interaction for cellular integrity (SPhA) was not significant, though within-group improvements were observed in Sid-G (p = 0.009); at the group level, significant time × group interactions were detected for key inflammatory and oxidative stress markers (IL-6, p = 0.001; MPO, p = 0.026). Correlational analysis revealed a significant association between changes in inflammatory markers and clinical recovery outcomes in Sid-G, a pattern absent in the CG. Adjunctive supplementation may support recovery by helping patients to overcome physiological plateaus. These findings support further evaluation of an integrated, metabolically focused approach to neurorehabilitation.

titre: TNF rs1800629 Genotype and Motor Response to Intensive Rehabilitation in Parkinson's Disease: An Exploratory Study.
titre_fr: TNF rs1800629 Genotype and Motor Response to Intensive Rehabilitation in Parkinson's Disease: An Exploratory Study.
auteurs: Agliardi Cristina, Guerini Franca Rosa, Bolognesi Elisabetta, Zanzottera Milena, Saibene Francesca Lea, Salvatore Anna, Arcuri Pietro, Castagna Anna, Cattaneo Davide, Bowman Thomas, Anastasi Denise, Navarro Jorge, Meloni Mario, Clerici Mario
resume: Rehabilitation is a key component of Parkinson's disease (PD) management, although individual responses differ substantially. Genetic factors involved in neuroplasticity and inflammation may contribute to this variability. We investigated whether selected polymorphisms in inflammation- and neuroplasticity-related genes influence motor outcomes following intensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation in patients with PD. Sixty-six patients with a diagnosis of idiopathic PD were consecutively enrolled and randomly allocated to an intensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation group (EXP-Group, n = 34) or a home-based stretching control group (CTRL-Group, n = 32) for six weeks. MDS-UPDRS III score was assessed at baseline (T0) and post-treatment (T1). SNPs in the TNF, IL6, IL6R, IL1A, IL1B, IL10 and BDNF genes were genotyped. Possible associations between genotype, treatment group and MDS-UPDRS III score at T1 were analyzed using ANCOVA and linear mixed-effects models, adjusting for baseline MDS-UPDRS III score, age, sex, disease duration and levodopa equivalent daily dose (LEDD). A significant treatment group x TNF rs1800629 genotype interaction was observed (p = 0.033). Among EXP-Group patients, GG homozygotes showed lower adjusted MDS-UPDRS III scores than did the A-allele carriers (29.10 vs. 36.11; p = 0.029). Longitudinal analyses revealed a significant time × treatment group × TNF rs1800629 genotype interaction (p = 0.010), with GG homozygotes showing an approximately 10-point reduction in MDS-UPDRS III score (40.87 to 30.87; p < 0.001). These findings suggest that TNF rs1800629 contributes to variability in response to intensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation in PD.

titre: Frequency-specific cortical swallowing-network responses following neuroengineering-guided individualized multichannel tDCS.
titre_fr: Frequency-specific cortical swallowing-network responses following neuroengineering-guided individualized multichannel tDCS.
auteurs: Muhle Paul, Khan Asad, Jung Anne, Vogenauer Nikolas, Wollbrink Andreas, Gross Joachim, Labeit Bendix, Dziewas Rainer, Wolters Carsten H, Suntrup-Krueger Sonja
resume: Neuromodulatory interventions for dysphagia are increasingly explored as adjunctive rehabilitation strategies, yet their efficacy may be limited by non-individualized stimulation protocols and insufficient consideration of network-specific brain dynamics. Advances in neuroengineering now enable individualized targeting based on functional neuroimaging and computational modeling, offering the potential for precision neuromodulation of swallowing-related brain networks. We investigated whether individualized multichannel transcranial direct current stimulation (mc-tDCS), optimized using magnetoencephalography (MEG)-derived target localization, MRI-based finite-element head modeling, and a distributed constrained maximum intensity (D-CMI) optimization framework, modulates the cortical swallowing network. In a randomized sham-controlled crossover design, eight healthy adults underwent three stimulation conditions: low-intensity mc-tDCS (1.5 mA), high-intensity mc-tDCS (4.0 mA), and sham stimulation. Swallowing-related cortical activity was assessed before and after stimulation using MEG source reconstruction of event-related desynchronization during uncued voluntary swallowing and a visually cued swallowing task requiring precise timing. A repeated-measures Dose × Task × Time model tested the hypothesized interaction separately in five frequency bands, with Holm correction across bands. No Dose × Task × Time interaction was significant after Holm correction across the five frequency bands (all adjusted p ≥ 0.274). Within-condition pre-post analyses identified alpha- and beta-band changes after 1.5-mA stimulation during challenged swallowing and a low-gamma change after 4.0-mA stimulation during uncued swallowing. Challenged-task timing accuracy increased over time, without significant Dose or Dose × Time effects. This study demonstrates the feasibility of integrating individualized MEG-based targeting, subject-specific head modeling, and optimized multichannel stimulation. The hypothesized Dose × Task × Time interaction was not significant. Exploratory within-condition pre-post differences were observed in alpha, beta, and low-gamma activity, but do not establish stimulation-specific effects. Larger controlled studies are needed to evaluate the physiological effects of this individualized approach.

titre: Chin Tuck Against Resistance Exercise With Feedback to Improve Swallowing, Eating, and Drinking in Frail Older People Admitted to Hospital With Pneumonia (CTAR-SwiFt): Randomized Controlled Feasibility Study.
titre_fr: Chin Tuck Against Resistance Exercise With Feedback to Improve Swallowing, Eating, and Drinking in Frail Older People Admitted to Hospital With Pneumonia (CTAR-SwiFt): Randomized Controlled Feasibility Study.
auteurs: Smithard David Graeme, Swaine Ian, Ayis Salma, Goubar Aicha, Gambaruto Alberto, Stone-Ghariani Aoife, Morgan Lydia, Hansjee Dharinee, Kulnik Stefan Tino, Lloyd-Dehler Elizabeth
resume: Community-acquired pneumonia in frail older people requiring hospital admission is considered to be commonly associated with swallowing difficulties (dysphagia). A rehabilitation program (chin tuck against resistance [CTAR]) targeting the anterior neck musculature involved in laryngeal movement can improve swallowing safety. We have developed a swallowing exercise rehabilitation intervention (CTAR-SwiFt [Chin Tuck Against Resistance Exercise With Feedback to Improve Swallowing, Eating, and Drinking in Frail Older People Admitted to Hospital With Pneumonia]) by adapting a previously established swallowing exercise. The CTAR-SwiFt intervention consists of a feedback-enabled exercise ball that can be squeezed under the chin, with real-time feedback provided via a mobile app. This study aimed to assess the usability of the CTAR-SwiFt intervention and the feasibility of recruiting participants to take part in a larger-scale multicenter randomized controlled trial. We recruited participants aged 75 years and older who were admitted with a diagnosis of pneumonia to the acute frailty wards at 2 participating hospitals in the United Kingdom. Patients had to be medically stable. Study participants were randomized to 1 of 3 groups: standard care (control), low intensity (once daily), or high intensity (twice daily) CTAR-SwiFt exercises. The intervention period lasted for 12 weeks; the final follow-up assessment was conducted at 24 weeks. Feasibility outcomes were assessed descriptively and included participant recruitment rate, retention, compliance with the exercise regimen, and adverse incidents. The Eating Assessment Tool-10 (EAT-10) and 4 Question Test (4QT) measures were used to screen for oropharyngeal dysphagia. Additionally, we assessed the usability and acceptability of the intervention device and performance of different clinical outcome measures (chin tuck strength, Functional Oral Intake Scale [FOIS], Quality of Life in Swallowing Disorders [SWAL-QOL] questionnaire, EuroQol 5-Dimension 3-Level [EQ-5D-3L] questionnaire, and swallow speed). A total of 24 participants were recruited, and 21 were randomized at the rate of 0.91 recruits per month (95% CI 0.59-1.0). Of those approached, 32% (24/75) were willing to take part, and of those randomized, 52% (11/21) completed the study. The major reason for failing to complete the study was medical, with people becoming unwell or being readmitted to hospital. The outcome measures assessed suggested that there was an improvement in the EAT-10 and 4QT and a minimal impact on FOIS. Quality of life as measured by the EQ-5D-3L showed improvement with time. The low-intensity intervention demonstrated the best improvement. Participants were able to partake in the CTAR-SwiFt exercises. There was an improvement in the consistency of ball squeeze over the course of the intervention and an increase in maximum chin tuck strength by a mean of 0.8 (SD 0.9) kgf. The literature supports the benefit of CTAR in improving swallowing in community-dwelling older adults. Our study has demonstrated that older, frail adults are able to perform CTAR and could use the ExerPhager. A future study should investigate the benefits of CTAR-SwiFt in community-dwelling older, frail adults after pneumonia. ISRCTN Registry ISRCTN12813363; https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN12813363. RR2-10.1186/s40814-022-01060-w.

titre: Ultrasound-Guided Focused Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy for Hemiplegic Shoulder Pain: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: Ultrasound-Guided Focused Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy for Hemiplegic Shoulder Pain: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Guo Kangxiang, Cheng Qinghua, Zhao Yinuo, Xiao Linlong, Tian Chao
resume: To evaluate the efficacy of ultrasound-guided focused extracorporeal shock wave therapy (fESWT) for hemiplegic shoulder pain (HSP) in patients with ultrasound-confirmed periarticular soft tissue lesions. This single-center, three-arm randomized controlled trial enrolled 114 patients with HSP, randomly allocated 1:1:1 to sham stimulation, conventional landmark-guided fESWT, or ultrasound-guided fESWT. All groups received standardized conventional rehabilitation. fESWT was delivered twice weekly for four sessions. The primary outcome was resting Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain score at 2 weeks post-treatment. Secondary outcomes included shoulder passive range of motion (PROM), Upper Extremity Fugl-Meyer Assessment (U-FMA) score, and lesion-specific ultrasound response rate. Intention-to-treat analysis was applied. At 3 days post-treatment, both fESWT groups had significantly lower VAS scores than the sham group (P < 0.01), with no difference between active groups. At 2, 4, and 8 weeks, VAS scores followed the gradient: ultrasound-guided group < conventional group < sham group (all P < 0.001). For PROM and U-FMA, both active groups improved more than sham. However, after Bonferroni correction, the difference between ultrasound-guided and conventional fESWT was significant for flexion (P = 0.009) but not for abduction, external rotation, or U-FMA. Ultrasound-guided fESWT achieved the highest response rates for tendinitis and bursitis; no significant between-group differences were found for tendon tears. No serious adverse events occurred. fESWT as an adjunct to conventional rehabilitation effectively reduces pain and improves function in patients with HSP and ultrasound-confirmed periarticular lesions. resume_fr: To evaluate the efficacy of ultrasound-guided focused extracorporeal shock wave therapy (fESWT) for hemiplegic shoulder pain (HSP) in patients with ultrasound-confirmed periarticular soft tissue lesions. titre: Web-Based Isha Kriya Meditation and Breathwork in Long COVID: Mixed Methods Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
titre_fr: Web-Based Isha Kriya Meditation and Breathwork in Long COVID: Mixed Methods Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
auteurs: Rayapuraju Akila, Mohamed Enas, Reed Preeti Upadhyay, Orui Hibiki, Pratt Morgan, Jafari Nashaw, Chase Tulsi, Ticotsky Amberly, Maley Jason, Subramaniam Balachundhar
resume: Long COVID affects millions of adults, causing fatigue, dyspnea, cognitive symptoms, and mood disturbances. Effective treatments are limited, and many patients cannot access multidisciplinary rehabilitation because of symptom fluctuation, distance, or specialist shortages. Web-based mind-body interventions may offer accessible, scalable support alongside existing care. We assessed the feasibility and efficacy of a 3-week web-based yogic breathing and meditation program for long COVID symptoms. In this completed, parallel-group, 6-week waitlist-controlled, mixed methods randomized trial, adults aged 18-70 years with physician-confirmed long COVID were recruited from US clinics and self-referral and randomized 1:1 to immediate intervention or waitlist control, crossing over at week 3. The program included live webinars and video guides for daily self-practice. The primary outcome was adherence, defined as practicing at least 1 of 3 techniques on ≥4 days/week across all 3 active-intervention weeks. Secondary outcomes included perceived stressmood, quality of life, dyspnea, and somatic symptom burden, assessed at baseline, 3 weeks, and 6 weeks. Quantitative outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Semistructured interviews and focus groups underwent conventional content analysis and were integrated with quantitative findings via joint display. Of 189 randomized participants, 1 was excluded post-randomization for a protocol deviation; 188 (96 intervention, 92 waitlist) began the study. Of these, 124 reached the active intervention period. Among 58 with complete adherence data, 55% met the adherence threshold (60% intervention, 50% waitlist). Secondary analyses included 185 participants with ≥1 assessment. No adverse events were reported. Compared with waitlist control, the intervention group showed greater reductions in total mood disturbance (MD=-10; 95% CI -19 to -1.6; P=.02), negative mood (MD=-7.5; 95% CI -15 to -0.44; P=.04), fatigue (MD=-2.9; 95% CI -4.6 to -1.2; P=.001), MDP immediate perception (MD=-5.5; 95% CI -9.4 to -1.6; P=.007), MDP sensory dimension (MD=-5.1; 95% CI -8.5 to -1.7; P=.003), and somatic symptom burden (MD=-2.0; 95% CI -3.6 to -0.38; P=.02), and greater increases in positive mood (MD=2.9; 95% CI 0.66 to 5.1; P=.01) and vigor (MD=1.7; 95% CI 0.18 to 3.2; P=.03). Stress and quality of life did not differ significantly. Qualitative findings identified medical-system struggles, digital delivery, online support, and practices' effects on resilience and identity. Integration showed convergence for dyspnea and mood, divergence for stress and quality of life, and expansion through themes of medical-system experience, identity, and social connection. This web-based yogic breathing and meditation program appears feasible and accessible for people with long COVID. By combining 3 practices in a brief protocol and integrating quantitative and qualitative evidence, this study provides novel insight into both symptom outcomes and dimensions of recovery not captured by standardized measures. Further evaluation should assess longer-term effects and integration into scalable telehealth and virtual rehabilitation pathways.

titre: Hand-Arm Bimanual Intensive Therapy Including Lower Extremities in Preschoolers With Bilateral Cerebral Palsy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
titre_fr: Hand-Arm Bimanual Intensive Therapy Including Lower Extremities in Preschoolers With Bilateral Cerebral Palsy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
auteurs: Araneda Rodrigo, Ebner-Karestinos Daniela, Paradis Julie, Saussez Geoffroy, Demas Josselin, Bailly Rodolphe, Bouvier Sandra, Carton de Tournai Astrid, Herman Enimie, Souki Aghiles, Le Gal Grégoire, Nowak Emmanuel, Sizonenko Stephane V, Newman Christopher J, Dinomais Mickael, Riquelme Inmaculada, Guzzetta Andrea, Brochard Sylvain, Bleyenheuft Yannick
resume: Intensive interventions for children with cerebral palsy (CP) have traditionally focused on the upper extremities, despite frequent impairments in gross motor function and the critical period of motor development occurring before age 5 years. Hand-Arm Bimanual Intensive Therapy Including Lower Extremities (HABIT-ILE) has demonstrated efficacy in improving manual dexterity and gross motor function in school-aged children, but evidence in preschool children with bilateral CP remains limited. To determine whether early HABIT-ILE improves gross motor function more than usual unstructured motor activities in preschool-aged children with bilateral CP. This multicenter randomized clinical trial was conducted between December 2019 and December 2021. Recruitment was from European university hospitals, CP-specialized centers, and spontaneous applications at 4 sites: Brussels, Belgium; Brest and Angers, France; and Pisa, Italy. Children aged 12 to 59 months with spastic or dyskinetic bilateral CP who were able to follow instructions were included. Exclusion criteria were uncontrolled seizures, scheduled botulinum toxin injections or orthopedic surgery during the 6 months before or during the study period, severe visual or cognitive impairments, and contraindications to magnetic resonance imaging. Data were analyzed in May 2024. Children were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive 2 weeks of usual motor activity, including usual rehabilitation (control group), or 2 weeks (50 hours) of HABIT-ILE (HABIT-ILE group). The primary outcome was Gross Motor Function Measure-66 (GMFM-66; range, 0-100, with lower scores indicating lesser gross motor ability). Secondary outcomes included Both Hand Assessment (BoHA), Melbourne Assessment 2, Pediatric Evaluation of Disability Inventory-Computer Adaptive Test (PEDI-CAT), and Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM). Assessments were performed at baseline (immediately before intervention) and 2 weeks and 3 months after baseline. Among 49 preschool children with CP (mean [SD] age, 40.18 [11.53] months; 18 girls [36.7%] and 31 boys [63.3%]), Gross Motor Function Classification levels were I in 5 children, II in 14 children, III in 17 children, and IV or V in 13 children and Mini-Manual Ability Classification levels were I in 10 children, II in 27 children, III in 7 children, and IV or V in 6 children. Change in mean (SD) GMFM-66 score from baseline to 3 months was significantly greater in the HABIT-ILE group (5.01 [2.52] logits) than the control group (0.70 [1.98] logits) (adjusted mean difference [aMD] in score, 4.33 logits; 95% CI, 3.03-5.62 logits; P < .001). Likewise, mean (SD) scores favored the HABIT-ILE group vs the control group for secondary outcomes of BoHA (5.32 [4.47] vs 0.13 [5.16]; aMD, 5.15; 95% CI, 2.23-8.08; P < .001), PEDI-CAT mobility domain (1.70 [2.18] vs -0.40 [4.38]; aMD, 2.27; 95% CI, 0.20-4.33; P = .03), and COPM performance (4.22 [1.61] vs 1.14 [1.35]; aMD, 3.55; 95% CI, 2.86-4.24; P < .001) and satisfaction (4.37 [1.38] vs 1.15 [1.63]; aMD, 3.11; 95% CI, 2.25-3.97; P < .001). In this randomized clinical trial, early HABIT-ILE significantly improved upper and lower extremities motor performance in preschool-aged children with bilateral CP at 3 months after the intervention. These findings suggest that HABIT-ILE is effective in improving gross motor function in preschool-aged children with bilateral CP. Clinicaltrial.gov Identifier: NCT04020354.

titre: Home-Based, Digitally Assisted Dyadic Tai Chi Intervention for Patients With Chronic Heart Failure and Their Caregivers: Development of an Intervention and Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: Home-Based, Digitally Assisted Dyadic Tai Chi Intervention for Patients With Chronic Heart Failure and Their Caregivers: Development of an Intervention and Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Zhang Yan, Ngai Fei Wan, Cao Lihua, Lu Xiaohong, Zhang Wenzhong, Wei Lili, Xie Yao Jie
resume: Chronic heart failure (CHF) imposes a dual and dynamically interrelated burden on patients and family caregivers, whose health and illness management behaviors are interdependent. Exercise interventions that actively engage the patient-caregiver dyad as the unit of rehabilitation in the home setting remain underdeveloped. This study aimed to develop a home-based, digitally assisted, dyadic tai chi (HDTC) intervention and evaluate its feasibility, acceptability, safety, and preliminary effects among dyads of patients with CHF and their caregivers. This sequential, multiphase study comprised intervention development followed by a single-center, assessor-blinded, parallel-group pilot randomized controlled trial. Phase 1 integrated literature review, theoretical frameworks, and stakeholder focus group interviews to develop and refine the HDTC intervention. In phase 2, eligible adults with CHF (aged 18-75 years; New York Heart Association class I-III) and their primary caregivers were recruited from a tertiary medical center in Qingdao, China, from October 14 to November 12, 2024, and followed for 12 weeks. Forty dyads were allocated 1:1 to the 12-week HDTC intervention plus usual care or usual care alone (n=20 per group). Outcome assessors and the data analyst were blinded to group allocation. Feasibility, acceptability, and safety were the primary focus of the pilot trial. Patient, caregiver, and dyadic health outcomes were preliminarily explored at baseline and 4 and 12 weeks. All 40 randomized dyads were included in the intention-to-treat analyses. The HDTC intervention comprised an online educational seminar, nurse-led dyadic coaching, preliminary face-to-face tai chi training, and supervised HDTC practice. The recruitment rate was 83.3% (40/48), mean session attendance was 73.7% (SD 8.6%), and 70% (14/20) of participants achieved high adherence rate (≥75% attendance). All intervention dyads rated the intervention as acceptable. No intervention-related adverse events were identified. Exploratory generalized estimating equation analyses suggested greater improvements from baseline to 12 weeks in the intervention group than in the control group in functional capacity (β=38.858; P=.001), together with greater reductions in Minnesota Living With Heart Failure Questionnaire scores (β=-1.850; P=.002), sedentary time (β=-1.025; P=.01), and fear of activity (β=-6.550; P=.01). Caregiver burden also decreased (β=-4.350; P<.001), while mutuality improved more for both patients (β=10.508; P<.001) and caregivers (β=6.450; P<.001). The HDTC intervention was feasible and acceptable, with preliminary improvements across patient, caregiver, and dyadic outcomes. By integrating shared patient-caregiver participation with digitally supported home-based tai chi, the HDTC intervention extends patient-centered rehabilitation toward a dyad-oriented model. If confirmed in a fully powered trial, this approach may offer a practical strategy for expanding home-based cardiac rehabilitation. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06876441; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06876441.

titre: Adjunctive Multisensory Passive Immersive Virtual Reality With Synchronized Plantar Tactile Stimulation for Gait and Balance Disorders in Parkinson's Disease: An Exploratory Randomized Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: Adjunctive Multisensory Passive Immersive Virtual Reality With Synchronized Plantar Tactile Stimulation for Gait and Balance Disorders in Parkinson's Disease: An Exploratory Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Shirolapov Igor, Natalevich Sviatoslav, Khivintseva Elena, Komarova Yuliya, Romanchuk Natalia, Sergeeva Mariya, Popov Nikolay, Kalinin Vladimir, Zakharov Alexander
resume: Postural-locomotor disorders, particularly freezing of gait and postural instability, are among the most disabling symptoms of advanced Parkinson's disease (PD) and respond only partially to dopaminergic therapy. Evidence for virtual reality (VR) approaches in moderate to severe PD remains limited. This prospective randomized controlled open-label exploratory trial evaluated the addition of multisensory passive immersive VR with synchronized plantar tactile stimulation to conventional rehabilitation for gait, balance, and freezing disorders in moderate-to-severe PD (Hoehn and Yahr Stages 2-4). In the study, 80 PD patients were randomized into an experimental group (EXP, n = 40) receiving standard pharmacotherapy and conventional rehabilitation plus 10 sessions of passive immersive VR with synchronized plantar tactile stimulation and a comparison group (COM, n = 40) receiving standard pharmacotherapy and conventional rehabilitation only. Because the VR sessions were added to an otherwise identical program, the trial evaluates the effect of adding this intervention rather than a VR- or tactile-specific effect. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and after 10 days using the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS), Berg Balance Scale (BBS), and Freezing of Gait Questionnaire (FoG-Q). The EXP group showed significant improvements in the UPDRS "Gait" cluster (an eight-item composite of UPDRS items 2.11, 2.12, 2.13, 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13, range 0-32; median from 12.5 to 8.0 points, p < 0.001), BBS (from 38.0 to 43.5 points, p < 0.001), and FoG-Q (from 9.0 to 6.5 points, p < 0.001). A formal group × time analysis confirmed a differential treatment effect for every outcome. For the main outcome, the UPDRS "Gait" cluster, the baseline-adjusted between-group difference was -2.48 points (95% CI -3.37 to -1.59; p < 0.001; Hedges' g = 1.16). Large effects also favored the EXP group for the FoG-Q (-2.14 points, 95% CI -2.62 to -1.66; g = 1.65), the BBS (+2.20 points, 95% CI 1.31 to 3.10; g = 1.06), the UPDRS freezing subscore (items 2.13 + 3.11; -0.89 points, 95% CI -1.13 to -0.66; g = 1.32), and the UPDRS postural subscore (items 3.12 + 3.13; -0.74 points, 95% CI -1.08 to -0.41; g = 0.93). Secondary outcome p-values were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg procedures. By contrast, in the COM group, no significant change was observed for freezing of gait (p = 0.083), and improvements in other outcomes were smaller than in the EXP group. No serious adverse events were recorded. The trial was exploratory, so the effect estimates require confirmation rather than supporting robustness in themselves. Overall, multisensory passive immersive VR with synchronized plantar tactile stimulation was well tolerated and shows preliminary promise as an adjunct to conventional rehabilitation for gait and balance disorders in moderate-to-severe PD. Wider clinical implementation requires long-term multicenter studies with standardized assessment criteria and analysis of long-term sustainability. These findings support integrating passive VR technologies into personalized neurorehabilitation programs.

titre: Patient Engagement in a Virtual Cardiac Rehabilitation Platform: Secondary Analysis of the ERA-Nudge Trial.
titre_fr: Patient Engagement in a Virtual Cardiac Rehabilitation Platform: Secondary Analysis of the ERA-Nudge Trial.
auteurs: Gupta Prerna, Durfee Josh, Waughtal Joy, Fletcher Dana R, Polsinelli Vincenzo B, Vathsangam Harsh, Hilton Joan F, Beatty Alexis L, Ho P Michael, Allen Larry A, Bull Sheana S, Peterson Pamela N
resume: Mobile health interventions have the potential to motivate healthy behaviors. Optimal strategies for engaging patients in cardiac rehabilitation (CR) through mobile health interventions remain unclear. This study aimed to examine patient engagement in a mobile app platform for CR across patient characteristics and by the method of delivery of nudge messages over the 12 weeks of CR. The authors analyzed data from the ERA-Nudge (Enhancing Rehabilitation Adherence Through Optimized Nudge) study, a pragmatic randomized trial conducted at an urban safety-net hospital testing nudges (short messages designed using behavioral economics to elicit behavior change) to enhance CR adherence and log healthy activity. Trial patients were given access to a smartphone-based app. Nudges were initially sent as app notifications. Later in the study, patients received nudges as text messages. We assessed patient characteristics associated with app engagement, and we compared time spent in the CR app among patients receiving nudges as app notifications vs text messages. The trial enrolled patients who could engage with messages in either English or Spanish at an urban safety-net hospital with a qualifying CR diagnosis and a smartphone from May 2019 to May 2023. We describe minutes spent in the app across patient characteristics and by type of nudge delivery, and we compare the 2 approaches using unadjusted and multivariate negative binomial regression over the 12 weeks of CR. In total, 223 patients received nudges: 74 via app notification and 149 via text message. Overall, patients spent an average of 219 (SD 328) minutes in the app, and 3 (1.3%) patients used the app for zero minutes. Patients receiving only app nudges spent a mean of 167 (SD 365) minutes in the app, and patients receiving text messages and app nudges spent 245 (SD 306) minutes in the app (unadjusted ratio 1.5, 95% CI 1.1-2.0; P=.02). After adjusting for age category, sex, primary language, CR location (hospital vs home), and highest education achieved, Spanish-preferring patients, patients with some college education, and patients receiving text messages spent more time in the app. Patients receiving nudges as text messages and app notifications spent an adjusted ratio of 1.8 (95% CI 1.2-2.5; P=.002) times as many minutes in the app compared to those getting nudges as app notifications. resume_fr: Mobile health interventions have the potential to motivate healthy behaviors. titre: Effectiveness of Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Post-Stroke Depressive Symptoms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials With Subgroup Analyses of Standard and Adapted Approaches.
titre_fr: Effectiveness of Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Post-Stroke Depressive Symptoms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials With Subgroup Analyses of Standard and Adapted Approaches.
auteurs: Pu Jie, Guo Wang, Li Hongxin, Wang Zhihao, Chen Jie, Guo Kailing, Li Hongyu, Tang Qiang
resume: Depression has ranked as one of the major complications after stroke, which reduced participation in rehabilitation, increased recurrence rate and mortality. Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) has been used in treating post-stroke depressive symptoms, although evidence regarding the effectiveness of CBT interventions for post-stroke depressive symptoms remains heterogeneous. Meanwhile, standard CBT typically involves structured cognitive restructuring and multiple therapeutic components, which may place considerable cognitive and practical demands on stroke survivors; several CBT-adapted interventions have been increasingly applied. Determining effectiveness of CBT intervention for post-stroke depressive symptoms and effectiveness of standard and adapted approaches for post-stroke depressive symptoms is warranted. This review was registered with PROSPERO (REG# CRD420251270950). PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov and Cochrane Library databases were systematically searched. Standardized mean differences (SMDs), and the 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using the random effects model. The Cochrane Risk of Bias tool was used. Altogether, 11 studies with 994 participants with post-stroke depressive symptoms were included and analysed. CBT interventions were associated with a significant reduction in post-stroke depressive symptoms compared with control conditions (SMD = -1.00, 95% CI -1.61 to -0.39, p = 0.001), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I<sup>2</sup> = 95%). In subgroup analyses, adapted CBT showed a significant pooled effect (SMD = -1.16, 95% CI -1.92 to -0.40, p = 0.003; I<sup>2</sup> = 94%), whereas the pooled effect of Standard CBT did not reach statistical significance (SMD = -0.58, 95% CI -1.52 to 0.36, p = 0.23; I<sup>2</sup> = 93%). However, the test for subgroup differences showed no statistically significant difference between standard and adapted CBT (p = 0.35; I<sup>2</sup> = 0%). CBT interventions may help reduce depressive symptoms after stroke. Although adapted CBT showed a statistically significant pooled effect, the test for subgroup differences did not indicate a significant difference between adapted and standard CBT. Given the substantial heterogeneity across studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further well-designed randomized controlled trials are warranted.

titre: Effectiveness of Digital Health Interventions on Rehabilitation Outcomes in Patients After Total Knee Arthroplasty: Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
titre_fr: Effectiveness of Digital Health Interventions on Rehabilitation Outcomes in Patients After Total Knee Arthroplasty: Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
auteurs: Zhang Wenhua, Mei Jingqi, Li Xun, Liu Jun, Chen Keliang, Zhang Dianbo
resume: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is the most effective treatment for end-stage knee osteoarthritis, but some patients continue to experience persistent postoperative pain, stiffness, and impaired functional recovery. Digital health interventions are increasingly used in rehabilitation after TKA, but their comparative effectiveness remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different digital health interventions on rehabilitation outcomes in patients after TKA and to compare and rank these interventions in terms of pain relief, active knee flexion range of motion (ROM), and knee function to provide evidence for selecting optimal rehabilitation strategies. We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Google Scholar, Scopus, CINAHL, MEDLINE (via OvidSP), CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) meeting the inclusion criteria. The RoB 2 tool (Risk of Bias 2; Cochrane) was used to assess risk of bias, and the confidence in network meta-analysis (CINeMA) framework was used to evaluate certainty of evidence. Traditional meta-analysis and network meta-analysis (NMA) were performed using Stata (version 17.0; StataCorp LLC). A random-effects model (DerSimonian-Laird method for estimating τ²) was consistently used across all analyses. For outcomes measured with the same or convertible scales, mean differences (MDs) with 95% CIs were used to pool effect sizes. Surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) values were calculated to summarize the ranking probabilities. A total of 36 RCTs involving 3067 patients after TKA were included. NMA results showed that compared with conventional rehabilitation (CR), for active flexion ROM, rehabilitation robot (RR; MD 8.96, 95% CI 5.86-12.05), mobile app-based telerehabilitation (MAT; MD 6.36, 95% CI 2.81-9.91), and virtual reality (VR; MD 5.92, 95% CI 2.94-8.90) were significantly superior to CR; for the Hospital for Special Surgery knee score, VR (MD 9.53, 95% CI 5.18-13.88), intelligent rehabilitation system-based telerehabilitation (MD 6.90, 95% CI 2.35-11.44), and RR (MD 5.32, 95% CI 1.61-9.04) were significantly superior to CR; for pain, RR and MAT had relatively high ranking probabilities, but the 95% CIs of most comparisons included 0; for the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index and Timed Up and Go test, only internet videoconference-based telerehabilitation and VR-based telerehabilitation, respectively, were significantly superior to CR. The certainty of evidence for most comparisons was low or very low. Digital health interventions may improve pain, active knee flexion ROM, and knee function in patients after TKA. In the SUCRA ranking, RR, VR, and MAT showed favorable ranking probabilities; however, because the network was predominantly star-shaped and the rankings were derived largely from indirect comparisons, these findings should be interpreted as suggestive rather than definitive. Further high-quality studies with direct head-to-head comparisons are needed.

titre: Digital health interventions for cognitive function in breast cancer patients treated with chemotherapy: a network meta-analysis of subjective and objective cognitive outcomes.
titre_fr: Digital health interventions for cognitive function in breast cancer patients treated with chemotherapy: a network meta-analysis of subjective and objective cognitive outcomes.
auteurs: Zeng Ruihong, Liu Xiangyu, Fan Yujia, Wu Sijie, Hu Yaxuan
resume: To systematically compare the effects of different digital health interventions on subjective and objective cognitive function in breast cancer patients treated with chemotherapy and to provide evidence for tailored supportive care and rehabilitation strategies. Eight databases, including the Cochrane Library, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CNKI, WanFang, VIP, and SinoMed, were searched from inception to March 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating digital health interventions for cognitive function in breast cancer patients treated with chemotherapy. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. A frequentist network meta-analysis was conducted using RevMan 5.3 and Stata 16.0. Interventions were ranked according to the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). The certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach. Twenty-two RCTs involving 1, 494 participants were included. Network meta-analysis (NMA) showed that digital exercise intervention (DEI) (SMD = 2.53, 95% CI 1.58 to 3.48) and digital psychological and behavioral intervention (DPBI) (SMD = 0.44, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.85) significantly improved subjective cognitive function compared with the control group (CON). DEI was also significantly more effective than digital multimodal intervention (DMI), DPBI, digital rehabilitation intervention (DRI), and digital cognitive training (DCT), and ranked highest (SUCRA = 100.0%). For objective cognitive function, DRI significantly improved cognitive function compared with CON (SMD = 2.59, 95% CI 1.17 to 4.02) and ranked highest (SUCRA = 85.5%), whereas no significant differences were observed in the remaining comparisons. The certainty of evidence was low. Digital health interventions may improve cognitive function in breast cancer patients treated with chemotherapy, with DEI showing the greatest potential for subjective cognitive function and DRI for objective cognitive function. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the low certainty of evidence. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261331780.

titre: Feasibility of High-Intensity Interval Training Before, During, and After Cancer Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
titre_fr: Feasibility of High-Intensity Interval Training Before, During, and After Cancer Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
auteurs: Karnarou Konstantina, Xanthopoulou Vasiliki, Skouras Apostolos Z, Holborn Catherine, Newton Emily, Tsamtsouri Lydia, Koulouvaris Panagiotis, Copeland Robert J
resume: To systematically evaluate the feasibility and safety of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) interventions in cancer populations across the cancer care continuum (before, during, and after cancer treatment). This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to 31 December 2025. Studies were included if they enrolled adults with cancer, implemented a HIIT intervention, and reported feasibility outcomes. Recruitment, adherence, and dropout outcomes were calculated as study-specific proportions with 95% confidence intervals and pooled using random-effects models with REML estimation. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 for RCTs and MMAT for non-randomized studies, while certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Twenty-two studies were included, comprising 559 participants in HIIT groups. Pooled recruitment across 20 studies was 0.57 (95% CI: 0.41-0.72), pooled adherence across 21 studies was 0.91 (95% CI: 0.86-0.95), and pooled dropout across 20 studies was 0.11 (95% CI: 0.06-0.16). Recruitment showed considerable heterogeneity, whereas adherence and dropout showed moderate heterogeneity. No statistically significant subgroup differences were observed by study design, intervention setting, treatment phase, or exercise frequency. Adverse events were reported in six studies, with no serious adverse events. HIIT appears feasible and safe for individuals with cancer, particularly after enrolment. However, recruitment remains moderate, and findings should be interpreted cautiously due to heterogeneity, risk of bias, and limited certainty of evidence.

titre: Effects of acceptance and commitment therapy on psychological and health-related outcomes in stroke patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
titre_fr: Effects of acceptance and commitment therapy on psychological and health-related outcomes in stroke patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
auteurs: Li Xiaohuan, Huang Weijin, Gao Ying, Wu Yu'e, Wang Ping
resume: Stroke is a leading cause of disability worldwide and is frequently accompanied by psychological and functional impairments. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), a third-wave behavioral intervention focusing on psychological flexibility, has been increasingly applied in stroke rehabilitation. Although previous reviews have suggested beneficial effects of ACT in stroke patients, whether these benefits persist in the short term after the intervention ends, and the certainty of the evidence, remain unclear. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261325108). Randomized controlled trials evaluating ACT in stroke patients were included. Pooled effects were calculated using random-effects models, with separate analyses for post-intervention and follow-up outcomes. Sources of heterogeneity were explored using subgroup analyses and meta-regression. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE framework. Twenty-two RCTs involving 1,975 participants were included. ACT may be associated with reductions in depressive symptoms (post-intervention: SMD = -1.32, 95% CI: -1.80 to -0.84; follow-up: SMD = -0.76, 95% CI: -1.07 to -0.45) and anxiety symptoms (post-intervention: SMD = -1.36, 95% CI: -1.90 to -0.82; follow-up: SMD = -0.51, 95% CI: -1.42 to 0.40, not significant); depressive symptoms remained statistically significant at follow-up. Heterogeneity was considerable for both outcomes at post-intervention (I2 = 93.68% for depression and 93.60% for anxiety), so the pooled estimates represent average effects across studies. ACT may also be associated with improvements in psychological flexibility, quality of life, and sleep quality; however, these outcomes were based on a limited number of studies and showed considerable heterogeneity (I2 = 74.68 to 92.26%), so they should be interpreted cautiously. However, no statistically significant effects were observed for activities of daily living, neurological function, or hope. ACT did not appear to increase dropout rates in the available studies (K = 16; RR = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.58-1.69). Meta-regression analyses indicated that intervention duration may not be a significant moderator of treatment effects. The certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate, mainly due to risk of bias and inconsistency. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy may be a useful adjunctive intervention for improving psychological outcomes in people with stroke. However, evidence for functional recovery remains insufficient. Future high-quality RCTs with standardized protocols, larger samples, and longer follow-up are needed to confirm the long-term effectiveness of ACT. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifer CRD420261325108.

titre: Effects of auditory sensory stimulation on consciousness and physiological parameters among individuals with disorders of consciousness: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effects of auditory sensory stimulation on consciousness and physiological parameters among individuals with disorders of consciousness: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Zhang Jinqin, Yan Xinyue, Huang Fubiao, Huang Yudi, Wang Jiawen, Zhang Ying, Taniguchi Takamichi
resume: To systematically evaluate the effects of auditory sensory stimulation (SS) on consciousness levels and physiological parameters in patients with disorders of consciousness (DOC). Furthermore, this study aimed to explore intervention characteristics based on the frequency, intensity, time, and type (FITT) framework that may influence treatment effects and to investigate potential sources of between-study heterogeneity. This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. The PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Scopus, and ProQuest databases were systematically searched from database inception to April 25, 2026. Fifteen randomized controlled trials involving 713 patients with DOC were included. Meta-analyses were performed using postintervention endpoint data (means, standard deviations, and sample sizes), and effect sizes are expressed as the mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Subgroup analyses based on the FITT framework, univariable random-effects meta-regression analyses, and GRADE assessments were conducted to explore potential sources of heterogeneity and evaluate the certainty of evidence. Auditory SS was associated with higher postintervention Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores and a lower postintervention pulse rate than control conditions. No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, or body temperature. Exploratory FITT-based subgroup analyses showed numerical differences in effect estimates across some intervention categories, but these findings did not establish an optimal intervention protocol. Univariable meta-regression analyses identified no statistically significant study-level moderators. According to the GRADE assessment, the certainty of evidence was low for GCS scores and very low for all physiological outcomes. Auditory SS may have potential as an adjunctive rehabilitation intervention for patients with DOC, although confidence in its effect on GCS scores is limited by the low certainty of evidence. Its effects on physiological outcomes remain highly uncertain. The available evidence is insufficient to establish an optimal FITT-based protocol. Future high-quality randomized controlled trials using standardized auditory SS protocols, comprehensive reporting of stimulation parameters (particularly stimulation intensity), and consistent outcome measures are needed to establish the optimal FITT prescription for auditory SS.
