titre: Psychological Care in Heart Failure Rehabilitation: A Meta-Analysis.
titre_fr: Psychological Care in Heart Failure Rehabilitation: A Meta-Analysis.
auteurs: Zheng Ruigui, Xue Zhe, Yu Yijian
revue: Journal of the College of Physicians and Surgeons--Pakistan : JCPSP
resume: This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy of psychological therapy versus conventional therapy within cardiac rehabilitation programs for individuals with heart failure (HF). The systematic review included 19 randomised controlled trials (RCTs), including 2,196 HF patients, of whom 1,060 were assigned to standard care, and 1,136 underwent psychological interventions. This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420250651620). The meta-analysis demonstrated that psychological interventions were not significantly more effective than conventional care in improving Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) scores (standardised mean difference [SMD] = 0.57, 95% CI: -0.61 to 1.75). titre: Effects of different durations of exercise-based pulmonary rehabilitation intervention in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effects of different durations of exercise-based pulmonary rehabilitation intervention in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Sun Yan, Yuan Jingmin, Li Meng, Fan Meng, Li Wenrui, Zhang Bo, Li Yan, Kang Zhenjing, Cheng Hao, Ren Hui, Chen Mingwei
resume: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a chronic and fatal lung disease causing progressive scarring, severely impairs respiratory function and quality of life. Although pulmonary rehabilitation is an important supportive intervention, the effects of different intervention durations remain uncertain. This study aims to evaluate the effects of exercise-based pulmonary rehabilitation at approximately 3 months/12 weeks, 6 months/26 weeks, and 9 to 12 months/52 weeks in patients with IPF. Systematic literature searches were conducted in the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, Chinese Science and Technology Journal Database, and CBM databases up until May 2024. Included studies assessed the impact of exercise-based pulmonary rehabilitation on patients with IPF, with outcomes measuring six-minute walk distance (6MWD), St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) or its IPF-specific version IPF-specific St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ-I), percent-predicted diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLco%), and dyspnea scores using the modified Medical Research Council Dyspnoea Scale. Only studies published in English or Chinese were included. Eight studies with 358 participants were analyzed. For 6MWD, pooled effects favored pulmonary rehabilitation at 3 months/12 weeks (mean difference [MD] = 35.98 m, 95% confidence interval [CI] 18.05-53.92), 6 months/26 weeks (MD = 36.53 m, 95% CI 19.62-53.44), and 9 to12 months/52 weeks (MD = 50.98 m, 95% CI 25.94-76.03). SGRQ/SGRQ-I improved at 6 months (MD = -8.16, 95% CI - 12.33-- 4.00) and 9 to 12 months (MD = -8.76, 95% CI - 13.06-4.46), but not clearly at 3 months (MD = -4.08, 95% CI - 9.61-1.45). DLco% improved only at 9 to12 months (MD = 7.85, 95% CI 2.80-12.90). mMRC data were available from 1 study at 12 weeks and 1 study at 6 months and were therefore not pooled within either intervention-duration category. Longest-intervention-duration sensitivity analyses supported benefits for 6MWD and SGRQ/SGRQ-I, whereas DLco% was not statistically significant and the longest-assessment sensitivity analysis for mMRC showed substantial heterogeneity. Exercise-based pulmonary rehabilitation was associated with improved exercise capacity across the assessed intervention durations. Improvements in health-related quality of life were observed at 6 and 9 to12 months, whereas evidence for lung function and dyspnea remained limited. The intervention-duration analyses were exploratory and did not establish a duration-response relationship.

titre: Effects of brain-computer interface output modalities on motor recovery after stroke: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effects of brain-computer interface output modalities on motor recovery after stroke: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
auteurs: Jiang Haoying, Zhang Xinzhao, Xu Jingying, Fu Yuyao, Jin Na, Xiao Yao, Fang Lili
resume: The relative effects of different brain-computer interface output modalities for post-stroke motor rehabilitation remain unclear. To synthesize randomized evidence on brain-computer interface-assisted motor rehabilitation after stroke, with emphasis on functional electrical stimulation-triggered and robot-assisted output modalities and the certainty of evidence. Sixteen randomized controlled trials published from January 2020 to October 2025 were identified from PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, IEEE Xplore, the Cochrane Library, and MEDLINE. Interventions included brain-computer interface-triggered functional electrical stimulation, brain-computer interface-controlled robotic rehabilitation, and conventional rehabilitation. The primary outcome was motor recovery measured by the Fugl-Meyer Assessment. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was performed, and certainty of evidence was assessed using CINeMA. No trial directly compared the two active brain-computer interface modalities, resulting in a star-shaped network. Compared with conventional rehabilitation, brain-computer interface-triggered functional electrical stimulation improved motor recovery (standardized mean difference 0.57, 95% confidence interval 0.12 to 1.01), whereas brain-computer interface-controlled robotic rehabilitation showed an uncertain effect (0.17, -0.25 to 0.60). The indirect comparison numerically favored brain-computer interface-triggered functional electrical stimulation over brain-computer interface-controlled robotic rehabilitation, but the confidence interval crossed the null (0.39, -0.22 to 1.01). Certainty was limited by indirectness, imprecision, and heterogeneity. Brain-computer interface-triggered functional electrical stimulation showed a clearer signal of benefit vs. conventional rehabilitation than brain-computer interface-controlled robotic. However, the comparison between the two active modalities relies entirely on indirect evidence from a star-shaped network, has very low confidence, and does not establish comparative superiority. P-score rankings are exploratory pending direct head-to-head trials.

titre: Comparative effects of different magnetic stimulation modalities on upper limb motor function and activities of daily living in patients with stroke: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Comparative effects of different magnetic stimulation modalities on upper limb motor function and activities of daily living in patients with stroke: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
auteurs: Yang Shuijin, Rao Yan, Wei Chen, Jia Shuqi, Liu Qiang
resume: To systematically evaluate the effects of different magnetic stimulation (MS) modalities on upper limb motor function and activities of daily living (ADL) in patients with stroke through a network meta-analysis. Embase, Web of Science, PubMed, Wanfang, VIP, and CNKI were searched from inception to January 2026 for randomized controlled trials evaluating MS interventions for upper limb motor function and activities of daily living (ADL) in patients with stroke. A frequentist network meta-analysis was performed using standardized mean difference (SMD) with 95% confidence interval (CI). The surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) was used to estimate the relative ranking probabilities of interventions. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. A total of 48 randomized controlled trials were included. For upper limb motor function, rPMS (SMD = 0.65, 95% CI: 0.19 to 1.12), rTMS (SMD = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.68 to 1.24), and combined MS (SMD = 1.01, 95% CI: 0.47 to 1.55) were all superior to conventional rehabilitation. SUCRA rankings suggested that combined MS ranked highest, followed by rTMS. However, pairwise comparisons among active magnetic stimulation interventions did not reach statistical significance. For ADL, rPMS (SMD = 0.60, 95% CI: 0.26 to 0.95), rTMS (SMD = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.56 to 0.97), and combined MS (SMD = 1.27, 95% CI: 0.94 to 1.59) significantly improved ADL compared with conventional rehabilitation. Combined MS was also superior to rPMS and rTMS alone. Sensitivity analysis excluding studies that reported only the Barthel Index showed broadly consistent results. No clear evidence of publication bias or small-study effects was detected. The certainty of evidence was rated as low. MS interventions may improve upper limb motor function and ADL in patients with stroke. Combined MS and rTMS showed relatively high ranking probabilities for upper limb motor recovery, whereas combined MS showed the highest ranking probability for ADL improvement. Given the heterogeneity among included studies, non-significant differences in some direct comparisons, and low certainty of evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed by high-quality head-to-head trials. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261302905, Identifier: CRD420261302905.

titre: XR serious games for phantom limb pain, neurofunctional recovery, and prosthetic adoption: a systematic review.
titre_fr: XR serious games for phantom limb pain, neurofunctional recovery, and prosthetic adoption: a systematic review.
auteurs: Farhan Muhannad, Khan Saad Jawaid, Yusuf Kehinde Quasim, Bari Abu Zeeshan, Siddiqui Muhammad Faisal, Alahmadi Maram Ali, Wang Joyce Zhanzi
resume: To synthesize evidence on Extended Reality (XR) serious games for Phantom Limb Pain (PLP), neurofunctional recovery, embodiment, and adoption following amputation. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched up to January 2026. Eligible studies included adults with limb amputation who received XR serious game interventions and reported rehabilitation or user-experience outcomes. Quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Evidence certainty was rated using GRADE across 5 outcome domains. 24 studies met the inclusion criteria. XR interventions showed consistent PLP reduction, with AR-based phantom motor execution systems reporting the largest effect sizes (d = 0.9-1.3) and preliminary evidence of reversal of cortical reorganization. VR exergames improved gait and balance in 2 RCTs. Immersive VR and EMG systems indicated improved object manipulation, performance time, and motor control. Neurofunctional and embodiment outcomes provided mechanistically plausible evidence regarding cortical activity, embodiment, and physiological adaptation. XR serious games show preliminary benefit in reducing phantom limb pain, improving functional mobility, supporting prosthesis control, and enhancing embodiment after amputation. Evidence linking XR-mediated sensorimotor feedback to cortical adaptation remains exploratory but is supported by neurofunctional findings. Usability and engagement outcomes were positive, although real-world implementation and scalability remain under-researched.

titre: Interval Between Injury and Surgery Influences Knee Biomechanics During Walking in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstructed Patients: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Interval Between Injury and Surgery Influences Knee Biomechanics During Walking in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstructed Patients: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
auteurs: Esmaeili Ali, Sajedi Heidar, Aka Serkan Tevabil, Jafarnezhadgero AmirAli, Dionisio Valdeci Carlos
resume: Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) is commonly performed to restore anatomical and functional knee stability. Although altered walking biomechanics have been observed post-ACLR, previous studies have not consistently accounted for the interval between injury and surgery. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to determine whether walking-related knee biomechanical alterations following ACLR are transient or persist over time, and whether the timing of surgery influences these alterations. Five electronic databases (Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, Physiotherapy Evidence Database [PEDro], and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials [CENTRAL]) were systematically searched from inception through August 2026. Studies comparing walking biomechanics between patients who underwent ACLR and healthy controls and reporting the interval between anterior cruciate ligament injury and reconstructive surgery were included. Biomechanical outcomes during the stance phase of walking were extracted and stratified according to the interval between injury and surgery: short term (0 to < 6 months), mid-term (6 to < 12 months), and long term (≥ 12 months). Standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals were calculated using a random-effects model. Study quality was assessed using a modified Downs and Black checklist. Of the 3522 identified records, 16 studies involving male and female participants aged 18-55 years met the inclusion criteria. The mean methodological quality score was 65%, indicating an overall moderate level of methodological quality. Compared with healthy controls, ACLR participants demonstrated lower peak knee flexion angle (SMD = - 0.33, 95% confidence interval [CI] - 0.64 to - 0.02, p = 0.03, I<sup>2</sup> = 57%), peak knee adduction angle (SMD = - 0.47, 95% CI - 0.92 to - 0.01, p = 0.04, I<sup>2</sup> = 66%), and peak knee flexion moment (SMD = - 0.64, 95% CI - 1.05 to - 0.23, p = 0.002, I<sup>2</sup> = 76%). In subgroup analyses, the long-term group (≥ 12 months between injury and surgery) demonstrated lower peak knee flexion angle (SMD = - 0.27, 95% CI - 0.54 to - 0.00, p = 0.05, I<sup>2</sup> = 8%) and peak knee flexion moment (SMD = - 1.97, 95% CI - 3.77 to - 0.17, p = 0.03, I<sup>2</sup> = 88%). The short-term group (0 to < 6 months) demonstrated lower peak knee adduction angle (SMD = - 0.79, 95% CI - 1.18 to - 0.40, p < 0.0001, I<sup>2</sup> = 19%) and peak knee extension moment (SMD = - 0.55, 95% CI - 0.93 to - 0.18, p = 0.004, I<sup>2</sup> = 50%). The interval between anterior cruciate ligament injury and ACLR was associated with differences in postoperative walking biomechanics. Delayed reconstruction (≥ 12 months) is associated with persistent sagittal plane deficits, which may reflect chronic neuromuscular adaptations or preoperative joint degeneration. In contrast, early surgery (within 6 months after anterior cruciate ligament injury) was associated with fewer long-term sagittal-plane deficits, although temporary frontal-plane asymmetries and extension deficits may persist during the early postoperative period and may improve with rehabilitation. These findings underscore the importance of considering the timing of ACLR when planning surgery and postoperative rehabilitation to support walking recovery.

titre: Blood flow restriction training for lower-limb function, walking and functional recovery after stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Blood flow restriction training for lower-limb function, walking and functional recovery after stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Kang Honghu, Yan Zhexuan, Zhang Zhongrui, Xu Yushan, Jiang Wenjing, Yang Zhongsheng, Zhang Qian, Yin Yu
resume: Blood flow restriction training (BFRT) is increasingly used as a low-load rehabilitation strategy after stroke, but the magnitude, clinical relevance, and certainty of its effects remain uncertain. We evaluated the effects and safety of BFRT on lower-limb function and mobility after stroke. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, CENTRAL, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and SinoMed were searched from inception to June 10, 2026. Randomized controlled trials evaluating lower-limb BFRT in adults after stroke were included. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, certainty using GRADE, and random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Nineteen randomized controlled trials were included. BFRT improved Fugl-Meyer Assessment of the Lower Extremity scores (10 studies, 646 participants; MD = 2.14 points, 95% CI 0.74 to 3.54) and Berg Balance Scale scores (8 studies, 581 participants; MD = 4.72 points, 95% CI 1.62 to 7.82). The 10-meter walk test analysis showed higher walking speed (4 studies, 322 participants; MD = 0.14 m/s, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.25), but the estimate attenuated after eligible grey literature was included (6 studies, 410 participants; MD = 0.09 m/s, 95% CI - 0.03 to 0.21). Six-minute walk distance increased by 8.01 m (5 studies, 271 participants; 95% CI 2.31 to 13.71). No clear pooled effects were observed for Timed Up and Go, sit-to-stand performance, cadence, or standard full-scale Barthel Index/Modified Barthel Index scores. FMA-LE and 6MWT effects were below reported clinically important thresholds; the BBS estimate was close to an approximately 5-point reference, with its confidence interval spanning effects below and above that threshold. Certainty was moderate for 6MWT, low for FMA-LE, and very low for BBS and 10MWT walking speed. No BFRT-related serious adverse or thrombotic events were reported among studies with explicit safety information, although reporting was limited. BFRT may improve selected lower-limb outcomes after stroke, but clinical importance remains uncertain for several outcomes and certainty ranges from moderate to very low. Better-designed trials with standardized BFRT protocols and more complete safety reporting are needed. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261477739, PROSPERO CRD420261477739.

Certainty was moderate for 6MWT, low for FMA-LE, and very low for BBS and 10MWT walking speed. No BFRT-related serious adverse or thrombotic events were reported among studies with explicit safety information, although reporting was limited. BFRT may improve selected lower-limb outcomes after stroke, but clinical importance remains uncertain for several outcomes and certainty ranges from moderate to very low. Better-designed trials with standardized BFRT protocols and more complete safety reporting are needed. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261477739, PROSPERO CRD420261477739.

titre: Postoperative Bladder Rehabilitation After Radical Hysterectomy for Cervical Cancer: A Systematic Review.
titre_fr: Postoperative Bladder Rehabilitation After Radical Hysterectomy for Cervical Cancer: A Systematic Review.
auteurs: Kuroda Kenji, Ito Keiichi
revue: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
resume: To systematically review the evidence on postoperative bladder management and rehabilitation strategies for women undergoing radical hysterectomy for cervical cancer. A systematic review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE. Studies evaluating postoperative bladder management or rehabilitation interventions in women undergoing radical hysterectomy for cervical cancer were included. Eligible interventions comprised catheter management, trial-of-void (TOV) strategies, pelvic floor exercises, integrated care, and electrical stimulation. Study characteristics, urinary outcomes, quality of life (QoL), and risk of bias were assessed descriptively. Eight studies were included. Interventions included intermittent catheterization continuity care, TOV strategies, enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS)-based pelvic floor exercises, integrated nursing care, early pelvic floor muscle exercises, transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS), and transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS). Intermittent catheterization continuity care was associated with faster bladder function recovery and improved QoL. Pelvic floor exercises and integrated care were associated with improvements in urinary symptoms, pelvic floor muscle strength, or QoL. TENS was associated with a lower urinary retention rate in a retrospective cohort study. In a randomized controlled trial, TEAS improved several secondary bladder-emptying outcomes and QoL, but did not significantly reduce the primary outcome of urinary retention. Heterogeneity in study designs, interventions, and outcome definitions limited comparisons across studies. Structured postoperative bladder management and rehabilitation may improve bladder recovery and patient-reported outcomes after radical hysterectomy for cervical cancer. However, the certainty of evidence remains limited. Further well-designed prospective studies and randomized controlled trials using standardized outcome measures are needed to determine optimal rehabilitation strategies.

titre: The Association of Cannabis Use With Pain, Mental Health Outcomes, and Medical Cannabis Legal Status in Persons With Chronic Traumatic Brain Injury: A NIDILRR and VA TBI Model Systems Collaborative Project.
titre_fr: The Association of Cannabis Use With Pain, Mental Health Outcomes, and Medical Cannabis Legal Status in Persons With Chronic Traumatic Brain Injury: A NIDILRR and VA TBI Model Systems Collaborative Project.
auteurs: Rabinowitz Amanda R, Vuolo Michael, Shankman Rebecca, Callender Librada, Pinto Shanti M, Juengst Shannon B, Neumann Dawn, Dubiel Rosemary, Corrigan John D, Harrison-Felix Cynthia, Hoffman Jeanne M
revue: The Journal of head trauma rehabilitation
resume: To examine associations between state-level medical cannabis policy, cannabis use patterns, and pain and mental health outcomes in individuals with traumatic brain injury (TBI). Data were drawn from a multicenter observational cohort study conducted within the Traumatic Brain Injury Model Systems (TBIMS) National Database across rehabilitation centers in the United States. Participants were 3365 community-dwelling adults with complicated mild-to-severe TBI, 1-30 years post-injury, who completed a follow-up evaluation between May 2019 and February 2021 as part of a nested study on chronic pain. Cross-sectional observational cohort study. Primary outcomes included self-reported current pain (binary), pain severity, and pain interference (Brief Pain Inventory Short Form). Secondary outcomes included depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 [PHQ-9]), anxiety (General Anxiety Disorder-7 [GAD-7]), and opioid misuse. State medical cannabis legality (legal vs. illegal) and individual-level cannabis use (binary and frequency) were the primary predictors. Cannabis use was more prevalent in states with legal medical cannabis (33% vs. 23%). Regardless of legal status, cannabis use was associated with greater pain, depression, anxiety, and opioid misuse. Significant interactions between cannabis use and legal status emerged for depression and anxiety, with users in illegal states reporting higher symptom burden, most pronounced among those reporting some use (PHQ-9 difference: 1.80 points, P < 0.001; GAD-7 difference: 1.58 points, P < 0.01). Effect sizes for state policy associations were small (eta-squared: 0.021-0.031). Less than 25% reported using cannabis solely for recreational purposes. Most individuals with TBI seem to use cannabis for symptom management regardless of its legal status. Our findings suggest that future work should consider whether legal barriers to medical cannabis access may contribute to mental health disparities in this population.

titre: Health-Related Outcomes of Stand-Up Paddle Across Diverse Populations: A Scoping Review.
titre_fr: Health-Related Outcomes of Stand-Up Paddle Across Diverse Populations: A Scoping Review.
auteurs: Bento Teresa, Frazão Henrique, Couto Nuno, Freitas João
resume: Stand-up paddle (SUP) is a rapidly growing water-based activity with potential physical- and mental-health-related outcomes. Although research on SUP has increased in recent years, the evidence remains dispersed across different populations and health outcomes, and no scoping review has specifically mapped its health-related effects. This scoping review aims to map the available evidence on the health-related outcomes of SUP across diverse populations and identify key directions for future research. A scoping review was conducted following the JBI methodology and reported according to the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were performed in PubMed, Web of Science, and RCAAP, including published and gray literature. Studies investigating the health-related effects of stand-up paddleboarding across any population were eligible. Data were summarized descriptively by main topics and health-related outcomes. Eleven studies published between 2013 and 2026 met the inclusion criteria. The evidence was mapped into four thematic areas: physical conditioning and cardiovascular health, musculoskeletal strength and balance, mental health and psychological well-being, and long-term impact and mindset shifts. The available evidence was limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous methodologies, and the absence of randomized controlled trials. The results from the present study identify research gaps on the health-related outcomes of regular participation in SUP and the underlying mechanisms that explain effects across multiple health domains. Finally, systematic reviews on the topic are recommended only if more robust and broader databases and search tools are used.

titre: Psychological Distress, Daytime Sleepiness, Fatigue, and Health-Related Quality of Life in Young Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study with Implications for Rehabilitation.
titre_fr: Psychological Distress, Daytime Sleepiness, Fatigue, and Health-Related Quality of Life in Young Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study with Implications for Rehabilitation.
auteurs: Torad Ahmed A, Alanazi Sulaiman, Elbosaty Reda Fathi, Essa Noran Abdallah, Hasan-Hafez Omar, Horváth András Attila, Boolani Ali, Singh Harshvardhan, Taha Mona Mohamed, Alawafi Rana, El Melhat Ahmed M, Torad Mohamed A, El-Saeed Tamer Mohamed, Emam Mohamed Abdelaziz
resume: This study examined associations between psychological distress, daytime sleepiness, mental and physical fatigue, and HRQoL in young adults and identified key predictors relevant for rehabilitation-oriented screening and intervention. In this cross-sectional analytical study, 371 university students (18-25 years) completed the Epworth Sleepiness Scale, Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21, Fatigue Assessment Scale, and 12-Item Short Form Health Survey. Descriptive statistics, one-way ANOVA, multivariate general linear models, multiple linear regression, and logistic regression were applied to evaluate associations with fatigue and SF-12 physical and mental health scores and categories. Most participants reported mild-moderate distress and fatigue, and about half of the participants had SF-12 scores below the sample median. Severe mental and physical fatigue were associated with substantially higher stress, anxiety, and depression than normal fatigue (all p < 0.001). Psychological variables explained 52% of the variance in mental fatigue and 30% in physical fatigue, with lower R2 for SF-12 physical (0.17) and mental health (0.29). Depression and stress were the strongest predictors of mental fatigue and low SF-12 mental health scores, whereas anxiety was more closely related to physical fatigue and physical health. Sleepiness showed weak, inconsistent associations after adjustment. Higher distress categories significantly increased the odds of HRQoL below the sample median. Psychological distress, particularly depression and stress, was strongly associated with fatigue and was also associated with poorer health-related quality of life, although the adjusted models indicated a more modest contribution to HRQoL. The findings support the value of considering psychological distress in rehabilitation-oriented screening while recognizing that HRQoL is influenced by multiple factors.

titre: Work-Caregiving strain among family caregivers of burn survivors: Occupational sacrifice and positive occupational appraisal.
titre_fr: Work-Caregiving strain among family caregivers of burn survivors: Occupational sacrifice and positive occupational appraisal.
auteurs: Zhao SiNing, Yu Yongpei, Zhou Zhiqing, Frey Katherine P, Wegener Stephen T, Castillo Renan C
resume: BackgroundFamily caregivers are often working adults whose unpaid care responsibilities can disrupt paid work, yet occupational impact is rarely examined beyond employment status or financial burden. Burn caregiving provides a high-demand traumatic-injury context in which prolonged rehabilitation, family reorganization, and support needs may conflict with caregivers' work lives.ObjectiveTo examine the occupational impact of burn caregiving over a 24-month recovery period and characterize two theory-informed patterns of caregiver occupational experience: occupational sacrifice and positive occupational appraisal.MethodsWe analyzed baseline and 24-month occupational follow-up data from 256 family caregivers in a burn survivor-caregiver cohort. Follow-up outcomes captured work participation, job change, caregiving-attributed workforce detachment, perceived career impact, and work-related barriers and facilitators post-baseline. Occupational sacrifice was operationalized as caregiving-attributed workforce detachment or adverse career appraisal among employed caregivers; positive occupational appraisal was defined as favorable perceived career impact. Baseline demographic, survivor-injury, and psychosocial characteristics were examined descriptively and in logistic regression models.ResultsAt 24 months, 71.5% reported ongoing work participation, 20.7% caregiving-attributed workforce detachment, and 7.8% other changes. Among employed caregivers, 32.2% reported job change, of whom 42.4% reported negative career appraisal. Occupational sacrifice was identified in 35.2% and was accompanied by functional, appearance-related, family-caregiving, workplace, rehabilitation-support, and financial barriers. Positive occupational appraisal was reported by 31.3% and was associated with lower baseline distress and higher posttraumatic growth.ConclusionsThese findings extend injury-related occupational health to family caregivers and support a theory-informed framework for studying work-caregiving strain, occupational sacrifice, and positive appraisal prospectively.

titre: Effectiveness of inpatient psychosomatic rehabilitation in Germany: protocol of a longitudinal study with a waitlist control group.
titre_fr: Effectiveness of inpatient psychosomatic rehabilitation in Germany: protocol of a longitudinal study with a waitlist control group.
auteurs: Schlett Christian, Lewandowski Fabian, Mack Julian, Streibelt Marco, Seifert Nico, Ottenstein Charlotte, Farin-Glattacker Erik
resume: In Germany, psychosomatic rehabilitation is widely used to improve mental well-being and promote social and occupational participation among individuals with chronic mental and psychosomatic disorders. Although previous studies have reported clinically meaningful improvements following rehabilitation, most have relied on uncontrolled pre-post designs, limiting the strength of the current evidence. The present study exploits the current long waiting times for psychosomatic rehabilitation to form a waitlist control group without influencing the timing of rehabilitation. Overall, the primary objective of our study is to evaluate the short- and medium-term effects of psychosomatic rehabilitation on mental well-being (primary outcome), return to work, and work ability (secondary outcomes). Additional objectives include examining treatment effects in relevant patient subgroups (e.g., diagnostic groups), investigating moderator effects, and analyzing determinants of waiting time until rehabilitation. We will conduct a prospective longitudinal study with a waitlist control group among individuals whose application for inpatient psychosomatic rehabilitation has been approved by the German Pension Insurance agency (Deutsche Rentenversicherung [DRV]). Participants will complete up to 12 online questionnaires at six-week intervals over a period of 16 months. Questionnaire data will be linked with routine data from the DRV rehabilitation statistics database to obtain objective information on rehabilitation and return to work. The effectiveness of psychosomatic rehabilitation will be examined using two complementary analytical approaches: a propensity score-matched waitlist control group comparison to examine the short-term effects of rehabilitation and a discontinuous growth model to examine the medium-term effects of psychosomatic rehabilitation. Both models will also be applied in the subgroup analyses and extended by the relevant interaction terms for the moderator analyses. Determinants of waiting time until rehabilitation will be analyzed using time-to-event models. The study will provide comparatively robust evidence on the effectiveness of psychosomatic rehabilitation in routine care. It may identify patient groups that benefit differently from rehabilitation and factors associated with waiting time until rehabilitation. These findings may inform future efforts to optimize rehabilitation interventions, improve equity in treatment outcomes, and reduce waiting times for psychosomatic rehabilitation. German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS): DRKS00038670 (9th December 2025; https://drks.de/search/en/trial/DRKS00038670/details ); WHO UTN: U1111-1332-6419.

titre: Efficacy of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in Preventing Poststroke Spasticity: A Sham-Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: Efficacy of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in Preventing Poststroke Spasticity: A Sham-Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Mupparaju Venkata Divya, Bhoi Sanjeev Kumar, Jha Menka, Samal Priyanka, Naik Suprava
resume: Poststroke spasticity significantly impairs recovery, yet preventive strategies remain limited. This study evaluated the effectiveness of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in reducing the development and severity of spasticity in patients with early subacute stroke, offering a possible early intervention. In this double-blind, randomized, sham-controlled trial, 70 patients with early subacute stroke (7-30 days) were randomized to receive 3 sessions of low-frequency (1 Hz, 1000 pulses at 90% resting motor threshold) rTMS over contralesional primary motor cortex (n=35) or sham stimulation (n=35), alongside standard care. The primary outcome was upper-limb spasticity assessed using the modified Modified Ashworth Scale. Secondary outcomes included handgrip strength, muscle power assessed by the Medical Research Council scale, pain assessed by the Visual Analogue Scale, modified Rankin Scale, and Stroke Impact Scale 3.0. rTMS therapy significantly lowered spasticity scores at 1 and 3 months across all assessed upper-limb joints (P=0.001), improved handgrip strength (P=0.01), and prevented pain (P=0.001). Stroke Impact Scale scores at 1 month showed greater gains in activities of daily living, mobility, hand function, social participation, and recovery in the rTMS group (P=0.001). Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale) was significantly better in the rTMS group (P=0.006) at 3 months. On binary logistic regression, sham stimulation was associated with greater odds of developing spasticity at 1 month (shoulder odds ratio [OR], 8.29 [95% CI, 1.95-35.27], P=0.04; elbow OR, 7.62 [95% CI, 1.69-34.35], P=0.08; wrist OR, 5.18 [95% CI, 1.60-16.78], P=0.06). At 3 months, sham stimulation remained predictive, with higher odds of spasticity at the shoulder (OR, 15.3 [95% CI, 8.26-28.43]), elbow (OR, 13.43 [95% CI, 3.94-45.78]), wrist (OR, 19.9 [95% CI, 4.9-80.96]), and fingers (OR, 26.25 [95% CI, 5.19-132.87], all P=0.001). Minor adverse events like headache and light-headedness were observed in 5 patients. Low-frequency rTMS over contralesional primary motor cortex significantly prevented spasticity, improved motor recovery, reduced pain, improved functional outcomes and quality of life in early subacute stroke, supporting its role as a promising adjunctive therapy in early stroke rehabilitation. URL: https://ctri.nic.in/; Unique identifier: CTRI/2024/01/061225.

titre: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis and comorbid anxiety and depression: advances in psychophysiological interaction mechanisms and integrated interventions.
titre_fr: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis and comorbid anxiety and depression: advances in psychophysiological interaction mechanisms and integrated interventions.
auteurs: Hou Zhaomeng, Wu Jiaojiao, Lu Hua, Chen Chaoqun, Wang Jing, Han Tingliang
resume: Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) is a common three-dimensional spinal deformity, and its comorbidity with psychological disorders such as anxiety and depression is increasingly attracting clinical and research attention. This narrative review aims to summarize the epidemiological characteristics of this comorbidity in AIS. It explores the complex underlying psychophysiological interaction mechanisms, including psychosocial stress, chronic pain, body image disturbance, and interconnected neuroendocrine and neuroimmune pathways. Based on this mechanistic understanding, the article further synthesizes and evaluates existing intervention strategies for this comorbid condition, encompassing psychological therapies, pharmacotherapy, physical rehabilitation, and emerging multidisciplinary integrated care models. Finally, the review outlines future research directions, with the goal of providing a theoretical foundation and a comprehensive management framework to improve the holistic physical and mental health outcomes for individuals with AIS.

titre: Associations between mental health conditions and outcomes of pain and function following upper extremity fragility fractures: A systematic review.
titre_fr: Associations between mental health conditions and outcomes of pain and function following upper extremity fragility fractures: A systematic review.
auteurs: Pepin Marie Eve, Chatterton Hannah G, Keinath Christiana, Mehta Saurabh P
revue: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
resume: Upper extremity fragility fractures (UEFF) are increasingly prevalent among older adults and are associated with functional decline, recurrent fracture risk, and increased mortality. While physical comorbidities influence recovery, the impact of pre-existing mental health conditions on pain and function following UEFF is less clear. To synthesize evidence examining associations between pre-existing mental health conditions and pain and functional outcomes following UEFF. Systematic review. A comprehensive search of MEDLINE, PubMed, PsycINFO, CINAHL, PEDro, SPORTDiscus, and the Cochrane Library was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Eligible studies included adults with UEFF that assessed mental health conditions (eg, depression, anxiety, and pain catastrophizing) identified prior to or within 2 weeks of fracture and reported pain or functional outcomes using validated measures. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Quality in Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool. Due to substantial heterogeneity in psychological constructs, outcome measures, and follow-up intervals, findings were synthesized narratively by short- (≤3 months), mid- (6-9 months), and long-term (≥12 months) follow-up. Thirteen studies were included [10 distal radius fractures (DRF), three proximal humerus fractures (PHF)]. In DRF, short‑term outcomes were primarily associated with anxiety and pain catastrophizing, which predicted poorer grip strength, range of motion, and upper‑extremity functional performance. Mid‑term outcomes were influenced by psychological distress, pain interference, fear of movement, and self‑efficacy. At long‑term follow‑up, depression was the most consistent predictor of persistent disability, with affected individuals demonstrating worse functional scores and slower recovery trajectories. Antidepressant use and registry‑defined common mental disorders present before fracture were associated with poorer long‑term outcomes. In PHF, pre‑existing mental health diagnoses and kinesiophobia were associated with worse mid‑ to long‑term disability and quality‑of‑life outcomes. Pre-existing mental health conditions are important prognostic factors for pain and functional recovery following UEFF. Incorporating early psychosocial screening and psychologically informed rehabilitation may improve outcomes.
resume_fr: Upper extremity fragility fractures (UEFF) are increasingly prevalent among older adults and are associated with functional decline, recurrent fracture risk, and increased mortality. While physical comorbidities influence recovery, the impact of pre-existing mental health conditions on pain and function following UEFF is less clear. To synthesize evidence examining associations between pre-existing mental health conditions and pain and functional outcomes following UEFF. Systematic review. A comprehensive search of MEDLINE, PubMed, PsycINFO, CINAHL, PEDro, SPORTDiscus, and the Cochrane Library was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Eligible studies included adults with UEFF that assessed mental health conditions (eg, depression, anxiety, and pain catastrophizing) identified prior to or within 2 weeks of fracture and reported pain or functional outcomes using validated measures. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Quality in Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool. Due to substantial heterogeneity in psychological constructs, outcome measures, and follow-up intervals, findings were synthesized narratively by short- (≤3 months), mid- (6-9 months), and long-term (≥12 months) follow-up. Thirteen studies were included [10 distal radius fractures (DRF), three proximal humerus fractures (PHF)]. In DRF, short‑term outcomes were primarily associated with anxiety and pain catastrophizing, which predicted poorer grip strength, range of motion, and upper‑extremity functional performance. Mid‑term outcomes were influenced by psychological distress, pain interference, fear of movement, and self‑efficacy. At long‑term follow‑up, depression was the most consistent predictor of persistent disability, with affected individuals demonstrating worse functional scores and slower recovery trajectories. Antidepressant use and registry‑defined common mental disorders present before fracture were associated with poorer long‑term outcomes. In PHF, pre‑existing mental health diagnoses and kinesiophobia were associated with worse mid‑ to long‑term disability and quality‑of‑life outcomes. Pre-existing mental health conditions are important prognostic factors for pain and functional recovery following UEFF. Incorporating early psychosocial screening and psychologically informed rehabilitation may improve outcomes.

titre: Impulse control as a mediator between mental health and substance use across diverse adolescent and young adult samples.
titre_fr: Impulse control as a mediator between mental health and substance use across diverse adolescent and young adult samples.
auteurs: Shelley Lillyan T, Yule Amy M, Wilens Timothy E, Morgan-López Antonio A, Ridenour Ty A, Stone Mira, Fiellin Lynn E, Ahrens Kym, Knight Danica K
resume: Substance use (SU) and substance use disorders (SUD) are common and often co-occur with psychopathology including depression, anxiety, and emotional dysregulation (ED). The specific role of ED components, including impulsivity, and their links to various substances has not been fully studied. This research examines how impulse control relates to anxiety, depression, and SU in adolescents and young adults (AYA). The study involved baseline data from 1246 participants aged 14-30 (M=20.07, SD=4.48) from behavioral health clinics, juvenile justice, juvenile rehabilitation, and high schools across four projects focused on opioid and other SU prevention. Analyses tested whether impulse control challenges mediated the indirect effects of depression and anxiety on SU (alcohol, cannabis, opioids). We fitted group structural mediation models in which mental health factors (depression or anxiety) predicted impulse control, which in turn predicted SU (alcohol, cannabis, opioids). Generally, AYA with high depression or anxiety had higher SU rates for alcohol and cannabis, and the associations were partly mediated by challenges in impulse control. AYA with depression or anxiety are more likely to exhibit increased impulsivity and SU, and impulsivity further raised the risk of SU among those with depression or anxiety. Hence, careful monitoring of symptoms related to anxiety, depression, and impulsivity may help identify AYA at the highest risk for developing problematic SU and SUD.

titre: Mental well-being and quality of life related to participation in leisure-time activities among people with spinal cord injury: A secondary analysis of a cross-sectional survey.
titre_fr: Mental well-being and quality of life related to participation in leisure-time activities among people with spinal cord injury: A secondary analysis of a cross-sectional survey.
auteurs: Skovbjerg Frederik, Stabel Henriette Holm, Wouda Matthijs Ferdinand, Stubbs Peter William, Nielsen Jørgen Feldbæk
revue: The journal of spinal cord medicine
resume: People with spinal cord injury (SCI) may experience reduced mental well-being and quality of life (QoL), as well as barriers to community and social participation. This study examined associations between social and non-social leisure-time participation and mental well-being, and between perceived participation restrictions and QoL, among people with SCI. Secondary analysis of a cross-sectional survey. Western Denmark. People with SCI who had previously completed inpatient rehabilitation. Of 1,157 invitees, 479 completed the survey, of whom 474 were included in the analyses. Not applicable. Mental well-being, QoL, and perceived participation restrictions were assessed using the WHO-5, SCI-QoL Basic, and USER-P Restrictions, respectively. Multiple linear regression analyses examined associations after adjustment for potential confounders. Compared with very low social leisure-time participation, low to very high participation was associated with WHO-5 scores 12.3-15.3 points higher. For non-social participation, differences ranged from 1.3 to 5.5 points, with all 95% confidence intervals including zero. Fewer perceived participation restrictions were associated with higher QoL; participants in the highest USER-P Restrictions quartile scored 26.2 points higher than those in the lowest quartile. Greater social leisure-time participation was associated with better mental well-being, whereas non-social participation was not clearly associated with mental well-being. Fewer perceived participation restrictions were associated with higher QoL. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal direction.

titre: COVID-19 Is Not an Independent Risk Factor for Post-Intensive Care Syndrome: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
titre_fr: COVID-19 Is Not an Independent Risk Factor for Post-Intensive Care Syndrome: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
auteurs: Antinoro Alberto, Leder Antonia, Grunow Julius J, Steinecke Karin, Boehnke Désirée, Denke Claudia, Weiss Björn, Spies Claudia, Schaller Stefan J
resume: BackgroundPost-intensive care syndrome (PICS) affects many ICU survivors, leading to persistent physical, cognitive, and mental health issues. The COVID-19 pandemic raised concerns about whether SARS-CoV-2 infection increases PICS risk. This study aimed to evaluate whether COVID-19 is an independent risk factor for PICS and to identify other contributing factors.MethodsThis retrospective cohort included 92 patients treated for respiratory failure in three ICUs at Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin between July 2020 and September 2021. Patients were divided into COVID-19 (n = 49) and non-COVID-19 (n = 43) groups. At three months post-discharge, outpatient assessments consisted of demographic data, ICU-related variables, and evaluations of physical (handgrip dynamometry, Timed Up and Go test), cognitive (Mini-Cog, Animal Naming Test), and psychological health (PHQ-4). PICS was defined as at least one abnormal test; severity was graded by the number of affected domains. Logistic and ordinal regression analyses assessed whether COVID-19 was independently associated with PICS prevalence and severity.ResultsPICS was present in 71.4% of COVID-19 and 62.8% of non-COVID survivors (p = 0.378). Multivariable analysis showed no significant association between COVID-19 and PICS or its severity (OR = 1.46; 95% CI 0.50-4.23; p = 0.486; and OR = 1.09; 95% CI 0.45-2.68; p = 0.845, respectively).ConclusionsCOVID-19 was not independently associated with PICS in ICU survivors. Both groups experience high rates of long-term impairments, highlighting the importance of rehabilitation and follow-up care for all ICU survivors.

titre: Physical medicine and rehabilitation clinics as transitional care hubs after stroke.
titre_fr: Physical medicine and rehabilitation clinics as transitional care hubs after stroke.
auteurs: Baratta John M, Harr Elondra, Cardoza Katherine, Jackson Mary, Bettger Janet P
resume: The transition from hospital-based care to community living is a vulnerable period for stroke survivors and caregivers. During this period, patients often experience evolving medical, functional, psychosocial, and social needs while navigating fragmented systems of care. Although guidelines emphasize timely post-discharge follow-up, coordinated discharge planning, rehabilitation continuity, and linkage to primary care and community resources, there remains no consistently implemented model for delivering transitional care after stroke. Outpatient Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PM&R) clinics are well positioned to address this gap because physiatrists routinely manage post-stroke disability, functional recovery, secondary complications, therapy coordination, equipment needs, caregiver concerns, and barriers to community reintegration. This Perspective proposes a PM&R-based bridge clinic model for selected stroke survivors discharged home from acute care or inpatient rehabilitation settings, particularly those without established primary care or with barriers to timely outpatient follow-up. In this model, a small interdisciplinary core team, including a rehabilitation physician, advanced practice provider, and social worker or care coordinator, provides time-limited post-discharge follow-up focused on medical, mental health, and functional stabilization, medication reconciliation, rehabilitation planning, durable medical equipment needs, social drivers of health, caregiver support, and primary care linkage. By embedding transitional care within existing outpatient rehabilitation infrastructure, PM&R-based bridge clinics may offer a practical and scalable approach to strengthening continuity across the post-stroke care continuum.

titre: Beyond Clinical Stability: Recovery and Reintegration Among Residents of a Psychiatric Halfway Home in India- A Qualitative Study.
titre_fr: Beyond Clinical Stability: Recovery and Reintegration Among Residents of a Psychiatric Halfway Home in India- A Qualitative Study.
auteurs: Subramaniam Sudharshini, Mariadharshini Ruffina, Puthalath Mariya, Thomas Mahima Mariam
resume: Halfway homes provide transitional support for persons with mental illness moving from institutional care to community living. However, there is limited evidence from India on how residents experience recovery and rehabilitation within these settings. Hence, this study was done to explore the lived experiences of persons with mental illness residing in a halfway home, understand its role in rehabilitation and recovery, and identify factors influencing rehabilitation outcomes. A qualitative study was conducted among residents of a government-run halfway home. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with eight purposively selected residents who had lived in the facility. Interviews explored experiences of rehabilitation, daily functioning, social relationships, occupational engagement, future aspirations, and barriers to reintegration. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke's approach. Five themes emerged: transition from institutional dependence to everyday autonomy; work, routine, and reconstruction of identity; relearning daily living and functional independence; social support, family estrangement, and reintegration challenges; and hope and future aspirations. Participants described halfway home as a space that promoted autonomy, privacy, mobility, and participation in everyday life. Work and structured routines contributed to identity reconstruction and purpose. Recovery was facilitated by peer and institutional support, while stigma, family estrangement, and medication-related challenges remained important barriers. Halfway homes play a vital role in promoting recovery, autonomy, and community reintegration among persons with mental illness and represent an important component of recovery-oriented mental health services in India.

titre: Rethinking psychosocial rehabilitation in mental health.
titre_fr: Rethinking psychosocial rehabilitation in mental health.
auteurs: Prina Eleonora, Asher Laura, Barlati Stefano, Chatterjee Sudipto, Cristea Ioana Alina, Ferreira Sandra, Hanlon Charlotte, Montague-Cardoso Karli, Sharma Parth, Purgato Marianna, Barbui Corrado
resume: Psychosocial rehabilitation is central to recovery-oriented mental health care, yet its uptake remains uneven because of persistent conceptual, methodological, organisational, and implementation barriers.Greater conceptual clarity is needed through stakeholder dialogue to establish a common set of core principles that can be adapted across diverse cultural and health system contexts.Meaningful co-creation with people with lived experience and their families should be embedded throughout the research and implementation cycle, from priority setting and intervention design to evaluation, scale-up, and dissemination.Evidence synthesis should adopt component-based and mechanism-informed approaches to identify the active components of psychosocial rehabilitation interventions and the mechanisms through which they produce change.Psychosocial rehabilitation should be recognised as a core component of mental healthcare, integrated from first contact and delivered across the continuum of care.

titre: [Potential of immersive virtual reality in the management of chronic low back pain : a narrative review].
titre_fr: [Potential of immersive virtual reality in the management of chronic low back pain : a narrative review].
auteurs: Scinta Vincent, Demoulin Christophe, Grosdent Stéphanie
resume: Low back pain (LBC) is a multifactorial condition with major impact. This narrative review analysed 16 studies evaluating the use of immersive virtual reality (iVR) in the rehabilitation of patients with chronic LBC. iVR interventions, focusing on pain education, relaxation, or motor tasks, appeared to be associated with significant reductions in pain and fear of movement. iVR improves adherence and satisfaction and could complement conventional approaches. However, given the variability of protocols and the limited number of studies, large-scale randomized controlled trials are required to confirm these findings.

titre: The Tinnitus Integrated Digital Ecosystem Model for Digital Tinnitus Rehabilitation: A Clinical Framework.
titre_fr: The Tinnitus Integrated Digital Ecosystem Model for Digital Tinnitus Rehabilitation: A Clinical Framework.
auteurs: Tubul Zahi
resume: Tinnitus rehabilitation has increasingly shifted from attempts to suppress the auditory percept alone toward interventions that address distress, attention, appraisal, coping, and daily functioning. However, evidence-informed components such as counseling, cognitive-behavioral strategies, mindfulness-based approaches, and sound-based interventions are often delivered as separate elements rather than as parts of a coherent rehabilitation pathway. This clinical focus article presents the Tinnitus Integrated Digital Ecosystem (TIDE) model, a clinician-guided framework for organizing established tinnitus interventions within an integrated digital rehabilitation structure. Drawing on contemporary clinical and research literature on tinnitus distress, digital health, internet-based tinnitus interventions, cognitive-behavioral treatment, mindfulness-based regulation, and sound-based management, TIDE proposes four interacting therapeutic domains: psychoeducation, cognitive-behavioral strategies, mindfulness and attention regulation, and sound-based strategies. The model further organizes these domains through four synergistic pathways: Understanding-to-Engagement, Appraisal-to-Regulation, Attention-to-Habituation, and Sound-to-Coping. Rather than introducing a new standalone treatment, TIDE clarifies how existing therapeutic components may reinforce one another when delivered through a structured, clinician-guided digital platform. The framework may support future intervention design; clinical implementation planning; and empirical testing of integrated, clinician-guided digital tinnitus rehabilitation.

titre: A central hub model for remote delivery of multisite clinical trial interventions.
titre_fr: A central hub model for remote delivery of multisite clinical trial interventions.
auteurs: Charvet Leigh, Pilloni Giuseppina, Becker Jacqueline H, Wisnivesky Juan, Federman Alex D, Pehel Shayna, Ko Timothy S, Koltai Deborah C, Knopman David S, Laskowitz Daniel T, O'Steen Ashley, James Melissa, Cox Wendy, Karwowski Jeannie, Zimmerman Kanecia O
resume: Digital health technologies enable remote delivery of clinical interventions, creating opportunities to redesign multisite trials. Traditional trials require participating sites to deliver interventions independently, potentially increasing implementation variability and operational complexity. Centralized models instead allow local recruitment and assessments while coordinating intervention delivery through one hub. We describe the feasibility of this model in RECOVER-NEURO, an NIH-funded, five-arm phase 2 randomized trial overseen by the Duke Clinical Research Institute. The trial enrolled 328 participants across 22 US sites with cognitive symptoms associated with long COVID. Sites conducted recruitment, consent, and clinical assessments, while an NYU Langone Health hub managed study kit preparation and distribution, device programming, onboarding, remote supervision, adherence monitoring, and equipment recovery. Participants were randomized to BrainHQ cognitive training alone; BrainHQ plus cognitive rehabilitation (PASC-CoRE), delivered via telehealth by Mount Sinai and Emory University investigators; BrainHQ plus active transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS); BrainHQ plus sham tDCS; or non-adaptive computer-based puzzles and games as an active comparator. Interventions were delivered remotely over 10 weeks using home-based study kits. Participants completed a mean of 44.0 ± 10.9 sessions over 68.8 ± 11.3 days. Of 320 participants who received intervention, 260 (81.3%) were consistently adherent. The hub initiated intervention within 13.5 ± 6.1 days of first participant contact, supported up to 168 concurrently active participants, and achieved a 96.9% equipment return rate. The intervention phase was completed in 375 days. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of centralized remote delivery of digital and device-based interventions in a large multisite trial and may inform future decentralized or hybrid clinical trials. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05965739.

titre: Stimulus-specific postural responses to optokinetic stimulation using a semi-immersive virtual reality system.
titre_fr: Stimulus-specific postural responses to optokinetic stimulation using a semi-immersive virtual reality system.
auteurs: Delap Celeste, Johnson Liana, Bautista Nicole, Keyes-Rhames Kaitlyn, Mork Gabriel, Denton William, Bolch Charlotte A, Zhou Tian
revue: Journal of vestibular research : equilibrium & orientation
resume: BackgroundVirtual reality (VR)-based balance assessment tools are increasingly integrated into vestibular rehabilitation, yet preliminary reference data for semi-immersive optokinetic stimulation (OKS) remain limited. The Computer-Assisted Rehabilitation Environment (CAREN), a semi-immersive projection-based system, may reduce the risk of cybersickness compared to head-mounted displays, but its utility for characterizing stimulus-specific postural responses in healthy adults has not been established.MethodsOne hundred healthy participants underwent 12 trials, including pre- and post-test eyes-open and eyes-closed baselines and eight directional OKS conditions (yaw, pitch, roll, tunnel flow). Postural sway was quantified via center-of-pressure (COP) metrics: mean COP position, mean distance, root mean square (RMS) distance, mean velocity, and 95% confidence ellipse area.ResultsOKS increased postural sway relative to the eyes-open baseline, but the effect was stimulus- and metric-specific. Roll-plane OKS (clockwise and counter-clockwise) produced the largest disruption, with ellipse area more than three times the baseline value (p < 0.001). Tunnel flow caused less postural disruption than roll. Sway increases were mainly anterior-posterior; ellipse area and medial-lateral RMS increased only during roll. Mean COP position showed a significant unidirectional lean only during roll (rightward with clockwise rotation, leftward with counter-clockwise rotation). Exploratory analyses found no association with age or sex.ConclusionSemi-immersive OKS elicits reproducible, stimulus-specific postural responses in healthy adults, with roll-plane stimuli producing maximal instability and tunnel flow engaging distinct adaptive mechanisms. These preliminary reference data provide benchmarks for characterizing healthy postural responses to semi-immersive OKS and support the design of future studies to validate stimulus-specific OKS paradigms in clinical populations.

titre: Digital twin technology in cardiovascular care: future perspectives for nursing practice, patient management, and clinical decision-making.
titre_fr: Digital twin technology in cardiovascular care: future perspectives for nursing practice, patient management, and clinical decision-making.
auteurs: Shafqat Naseema, Verma Veena, Naseema Saman
resume: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality globally and continue to impose substantial clinical, economic, and organisational burdens on healthcare systems due to increasing disease complexity, recurrent hospitalisations, and the need for long-term monitoring and personalised care. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence, computational modelling, wearable biosensors, telehealth, and digital health technologies have accelerated the emergence of Digital Twin Technology (DTT) as a promising innovation in precision cardiovascular healthcare. Although DTT has gained growing attention in medicine and engineering, its implications for cardiovascular nursing practice, patient management, and clinical decision-making remain insufficiently synthesised. This scoping review aimed to explore the current applications of DTT in cardiovascular healthcare and examine its implications for cardiovascular nursing practice, patient management, clinical decision-making, and future healthcare delivery. Review was conducted using the Arksey and O'Malley methodological framework and reported according to the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, Embase, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar was performed for studies published between 2020 and 2026. Eligible studies included literature related to digital twins, computational cardiovascular modelling, artificial intelligence-assisted cardiovascular care, wearable technologies, remote monitoring systems, and nursing implications in cardiovascular healthcare. Data were charted and synthesised narratively according to predefined research questions and thematic areas. Thirty studies met the inclusion criteria. The findings demonstrated that DTT is increasingly applied in heart failure monitoring, arrhythmia prediction, telecardiology, smart ICU systems, virtual cardiac modelling, personalised rehabilitation, and population-level cardiovascular risk prediction. Artificial intelligence, machine learning, wearable biosensors, cloud computing, electronic health records, and predictive analytics were the most commonly reported technological components. The review further identified important implications for cardiovascular nursing, including transition from reactive to predictive care, expansion of telehealth nursing, enhanced data-driven clinical decision-making, and the growing need for digital competency. However, ethical concerns, cybersecurity risks, interoperability challenges,infrastructure costs, workforce preparedness, and limited nursing-focused evidence remain significant barriers. DTT has the potential to transform cardiovascular healthcare through predictive, personalised, and continuously adaptive models of care. Strengthening nursing leadership, digital competency and interdisciplinary collaboration is essential for integration of DTT into future cardiovascular practice.

titre: Early ambulatory re-evaluation and follow-up of patients admitted in the acute cardiac care unit - Practical aspects on ambulatory follow-up of acute care patients: acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, ventricular arrhythmias, atrial arrhythmias, conductance disorders, myocarditis, pericarditis, other acute cardiac settings A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care of the ESC.
titre_fr: Early ambulatory re-evaluation and follow-up of patients admitted in the acute cardiac care unit - Practical aspects on ambulatory follow-up of acute care patients: acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, ventricular arrhythmias, atrial arrhythmias, conductance disorders, myocarditis, pericarditis, other acute cardiac settings A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care of the ESC.
auteurs: Roubille François, Lenz Max, Morosin Marco, Algalarrondo Vincent, Kalmanovich Eran, Schaubroeck Hannah, Sionis Alessandro, Vidal-Perez Rafael, Leonardi Sergio, Delmas Clément, Imazio Massimo, Ammirati Enrico, Aboyans Victor, Chapet Nicolas, Rosenberg Alex, Belohlavek Jan, Pavlov Marin, Vandenbriele Christophe
revue: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
resume: Early, structured ambulatory follow-up after hospitalization for acute cardiac events remains a key unmet need in cardiovascular care. This clinical consensus statement of the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care of the ESC provides pragmatic, condition-specific guidance on post discharge management and (early) ambulatory re-evaluation for patients admitted to an acute cardiac care unit. It complements existing disease-oriented guidelines by focusing on the vulnerable transition from hospital to home rather than on acute in-hospital treatment. The document first defines key concepts and outlines general principles regarding timing, content, and organization of the first post-discharge contacts, including risk stratification, medication reconciliation, symptom assessment, evaluation of psychosocial status and comorbidities, patient and family education, and integration of cardiac rehabilitation. In practice, the consensus statement discusses the patient's path after discharge: how should the follow-up team look like, when should the first and subsequent visits be planned, what should be done at each contact, and how can multidisciplinary teams and hybrid (in-person plus remote) models be implemented according to local resources. Supplementary material highlights major evidence gaps, including the optimal timing and intensity of follow-up, the composition of ambulatory teams, the role of telemonitoring and digital health, and the needs of vulnerable populations. Overall, this consensus aims to support clinicians in designing structured, individualized, and scalable ambulatory pathways after acute cardiac care.

titre: Effects of virtual reality-based exercise on biomechanical and functional outcomes: a narrative review of randomized controlled trials.
titre_fr: Effects of virtual reality-based exercise on biomechanical and functional outcomes: a narrative review of randomized controlled trials.
auteurs: Park Sang-Kyun
resume: This study was conducted as a structured narrative review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating virtual reality (VR)-based exercise and rehabilitation. PubMed and the Research Information Sharing Service were searched for peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025. Predefined search terms and eligibility criteria based on the population, intervention, comparison, and outcome framework were applied to identify relevant studies for narrative synthesis. Search terms were organized into three conceptual domains: VR, exercise or rehabilitation, and biomechanical outcomes. Of 2,138 records initially identified, 19 RCTs were included in the final analysis. Whole-body movement was the most common intervention (11 studies), followed by center-of-mass shifting exercise (three studies). Gait-related outcomes were investigated in 13 of the 19 RCTs, balance and postural control in 12 studies, and direct or instrumented biomechanical outcomes in 10 studies. Across the trials, VR-based exercise was generally associated with improvements in gait, balance, postural control, and selected neuromuscular outcomes; however, the direction, magnitude, and statistical significance of these effects varied across studies. Because substantial heterogeneity was observed in study populations, intervention duration and dose, VR modality, and outcome assessment, pooled effect sizes were not estimated, and definitive conclusions regarding the magnitude of treatment effects could not be drawn.

titre: Reliability and validity of a context-aware sleep holistic cycle gate algorithm for personalized digital healthcare and sleep prediction.
titre_fr: Reliability and validity of a context-aware sleep holistic cycle gate algorithm for personalized digital healthcare and sleep prediction.
auteurs: Kim Jaehoon, Pathak Prabhat, Shin Hang-Sik, Jin Youngsoo, Ahn Chang-Young, Jee Yong-Seok
resume: This study evaluated the reliability and validity of a context-aware sleep holistic cycle gate algorithm and explored its potential for artificial intelligence (AI)-based personalized sleep management in digital healthcare. A 6-week prospective observational study was conducted in 25 adults aged 20-65 years. Participants recorded daytime activities, evening behaviors, presleep environmental factors, sleep outcomes, and feedback adherence using a mobile application. Five sleep-related indices were calculated, and a context-aware gate algorithm comprising five domains was applied. Reliability was assessed through internal consistency and reproducibility analyses, while validity was examined using correlations with sleep quality indicators and receiver operating characteristic curve analyses. Data completion and adherence rates were 80.3%±9.8% and 72.7%±11.6%, respectively. The sleep readiness index was positively correlated with subjective sleep quality (r=0.53, P<0.01). The algorithm demonstrated moderate predictive performance (area under the curve=0.73), with the environment and presleep gates showing the highest accuracy. Following personalized feedback, sleep onset latency decreased by 12.6%, and perceived sleep quality improved significantly (P<0.05). In conclusions, the context-aware sleep holistic cycle gate algorithm demonstrated acceptable reliability and validity for predicting sleep quality. These findings suggest that the proposed framework may serve as a foundational platform for the development of AI-driven personalized sleep management systems and future digital healthcare applications related to sleep rehabilitation and health promotion.

titre: Association of eHealth Literacy With Cognitive Function, Frailty, and Functional Status in Hospitalized Geriatric Patients: Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
titre_fr: Association of eHealth Literacy With Cognitive Function, Frailty, and Functional Status in Hospitalized Geriatric Patients: Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
auteurs: Flemm Chantal, Wirth Rainer, El Bataioui Sarah, Daubert Diana, Haussleiter Ida, Hermenau Matthias Tristan, Dieris-Hirche Jan, Kuhlmann Judith Frederica, Kunde Katharina, Trampisch Ulrike, Ueberberg Bianca, Vollmar Horst Christian, Busse Theresa Sophie
resume: The rapid growth of digital health technologies has highlighted the importance of eHealth literacy, which is crucial for navigating health information and tools such as telemedicine and eHealth records. However, older adults often have reservations about digital technologies and face barriers due to cognitive, sensory, and motor impairments, which hinder their ability to effectively use digital health applications. Despite its relevance, research on eHealth literacy in older populations is limited, with a particular gap in understanding how self-assessments of eHealth literacy correlate with health characteristics. The study seeks to explore eHealth literacy among hospitalized geriatric patients in Germany. The main objective is to evaluate the eHealth literacy level within this particular group and identify the clinical and sociodemographic factors that may influence it. Data from this observational study were analyzed to explore characteristics influencing eHealth literacy in hospitalized geriatric patients. The study included patients aged 60 or older in the Department of Geriatric Medicine at Marien Hospital Herne and enrolled in the standardized early rehabilitation pathway. eHealth literacy was measured using the German version of the eHealth Literacy Scale (GR-eHEALS), a self-assessment tool. Sociodemographic and clinical data, including cognitive function (Montreal Cognitive Assessment [MoCA]), frailty (Clinical Frailty Scale [CFS]), and depression (Depression in Old Age Scale [DIA-S]), were collected. Statistical analyses involved descriptive statistics, t tests, chi-square tests, and regression analyses to examine the relationship between eHealth literacy and various factors. Sociodemographic and clinical data, including cognitive function (MoCA), frailty (CFS), and depression (DIA-S), were collected. A total of 244 participants (aged 60-97, mean 77.2, SD 6.9 years) were included in the analysis. Participants generally reported an eHealth literacy, with higher scores in "information seeking" (mean 3.64, SD 0.84) compared to "information appraisal" (mean 3.32, SD 0.80). Significant differences in eHealth literacy were observed by age, with older participants scoring lower on both subscales. Frailty was significantly associated with critical appraisal of online health information (B=-1.372, 95% CI -2.554 to -0.189), suggesting that individuals who are frail struggle more with evaluating health information. No significant associations were found with other sociodemographic variables, including MoCA scores, education, or gender. While the findings suggest a positive self-reported ability to engage with digital health tools, the selective sample and reliance on self-assessment limit the accuracy of these results. It also emphasizes the need for tailored interventions to support older adults in improving their eHealth literacy, particularly those with higher levels of frailty. Further research, including longitudinal studies and objective assessments, is essential to better understand and address the digital health needs of the geriatric population.

titre: From Bedside to National Conferences: Empowering Nurses Through a Clinical Nurse Mentor Program.
titre_fr: Du chevet des patients aux conférences nationales : autonomiser les infirmières grâce à un programme de mentorat infirmier clinique.
auteurs: McCray Sharee, Gilewicz Diane, Patton Rènee A, Hensley Amberly, Fernandini Christine, Bogumil Linda M
resume: This article describes how the clinical nurse specialist empowered clinical nurses in disseminating scholarly work by developing a structured evidence-based clinical nurse mentor (CNM) program aimed at enhancing abstract writing skills, building confidence in presenting, and fostering professional growth. Presenting at conferences supports professional development by enabling nurses to share expertise, contribute to their profession, and advance their careers. Limited time, resources, lack of confidence, and leadership support are barriers to presenting. In 2022, the clinical nurse specialist identified the need for mentorship to empower nurses to share clinical expertise internally and externally. The Iowa model of "evidence-based practice" was utilized to guide implementation of the CNM program in the rehabilitation hospital. Over the 4-year period (fiscal year 23 to fiscal year26), 41 abstracts were submitted to local and national conferences, resulting in an 80% acceptance rate. Since program inception, 33 abstracts were submitted by 18 clinical nurses, 3 nursing supervisors, and 1 occupational therapist. Postimplementation, it was discovered that once nurses acquired these skills, they consistently submitted abstracts. The CNM Program enhanced and fostered a supportive and healthy work environment for clinical nurses, enabling professional development, leadership growth, and empowerment in sharing clinical expertise.
resume_fr: Cet article décrit comment l’infirmière clinicienne spécialisée a donné aux infirmières cliniciennes les moyens de diffuser des travaux scientifiques en élaborant un programme structuré de mentorat des infirmières cliniciennes (MIC) fondé sur des données probantes, visant à améliorer les compétences en rédaction de résumés, à renforcer la confiance en soi lors des présentations et à favoriser le développement professionnel. Faire des présentations lors de conférences favorise le développement professionnel en permettant aux infirmières de partager leur expertise, de contribuer à leur profession et de progresser.leur carrière. Le temps et les ressources limités, le manque de confiance et le manque de soutien de la part de la direction sont des obstacles aux présentations. En 2022, l'infirmière clinicienne spécialisée a identifié le besoin de mentorat pour permettre aux infirmières de partager leur expertise clinique en interne et en externe. Le modèle de l’Iowa de « pratique fondée sur des données probantes » a été utilisé pour guider la mise en œuvre du programme CNM dans l’hôpital de réadaptation. Sur la période de 4 ans (de l’exercice 2023 à l’exercice 2026), 41des résumés ont été soumis à des conférences locales et nationales, ce qui a abouti à un taux d’acceptation de 80 %. Depuis le lancement du programme, 33 résumés ont été soumis par 18 infirmières cliniciennes, 3 superviseures en soins infirmiers et 1 ergothérapeute. Après la mise en œuvre, il a été constaté qu’une fois que les infirmières avaient acquis ces compétences, elles soumettaient systématiquement des résumés. Le programme CNM a amélioré et favorisé un environnement de travail favorable et sain pour les infirmières cliniciennes, ce qui a permisle développement professionnel, le renforcement du leadership et la responsabilisation dans le partage de l'expertise clinique.
