titre: 'I am sick of being told to breathe in and out for four'. Facilitating occupational engagement using virtual reality in inpatient palliative care.
titre_fr: « J'en ai assez qu'on me dise d'inspirer et d'expirer pendant quatre temps. » Faciliter l'engagement professionnel grâce à la réalité virtuelle dans les soins palliatifs en milieu hospitalier.
auteurs: Chamberlain Anne, Kinton Wendy, Smith Suzanne, Verdonck Michèle
resume: ObjectivesVirtual reality (VR) in palliative care settings is emerging as a therapeutic tool for symptom management and improving quality of life and well-being. This study explored the experiences of people receiving inpatient palliative care who used VR, and willingness to re-engage with the technology.MethodThis study was conducted in a palliative care inpatient setting in a regional health service in Queensland, Australia using an exploratory case study methodology. Seven participants engaged in ten VR trials over a four-week period. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, observations and field notes to record participant behaviour, technical assistance required, the frequency and nature of content selections and willingness to re-engage with the technology.ResultsReflexive thematic analysis of interview data supported by observations led to the development of three themes: VR in palliative care as meaningful engagement, Content choices impacted engagement and Using VR in an inpatient setting is challenging. Re-engagement with the VR technology after an initial trial was limited, with barriers such as content choice, expectations not met, technological challenges and VR being a lower priority occupation identified.ConclusionThe findings suggested that while people receiving care in inpatient palliative care settings reported positive experiences after using VR, it may not always be considered meaningful occupational engagement. Content should offer diverse experiences to accommodate individual preferences and ensure access to valuable and desired experiences.
resume_fr: Objectifs La réalité virtuelle (RV) dans les établissements de soins palliatifs s'impose comme un outil thérapeutique pour la prise en charge des symptômes et l'amélioration de la qualité de vie et du bien-être. Cette étude a exploré les expériences des personnes bénéficiant de soins palliatifs en milieu hospitalier qui ont utilisé la RV, ainsi que leur volonté de réutiliser cette technologie. Méthode Cette étude a été menée dans un service de soins palliatifs en milieu hospitalier d’un établissement de santé régional du Queensland, en Australie, au moyen d’une approche exploratoire.méthodologie d'étude de cas. Sept participants ont pris part à dix essais de réalité virtuelle sur une période de quatre semaines. Les données ont été collectées au moyen d'entretiens semi-structurés, d'observations et de notes de terrain afin d'enregistrer le comportement des participants, l'assistance technique requise, la fréquence et la nature des choix de contenu, ainsi que la volonté de se réengager dans l'utilisation de la technologie. Résultats : L'analyse thématique réflexive des données des entretiens, étayée par les observations, a conduit à l'élaboration de troisThèmes : la réalité virtuelle dans les soins palliatifs en tant qu’engagement significatif, les choix de contenu ont eu un impact sur l’engagement et l’utilisation de la réalité virtuelle en milieu hospitalier est difficile. Le réengagement envers la technologie de la RV après un premier essai a été limité, avec des obstacles tels que le choix du contenu, les attentes non satisfaites, les défis technologiques et le fait que la RV soit considérée comme une activité moins prioritaire. Conclusion : Les résultats suggèrent que, bien que les personnes recevant des soins en milieu hospitalierBien que les établissements de soins palliatifs aient fait état d'expériences positives après avoir utilisé la réalité virtuelle, celle-ci ne peut pas toujours être considérée comme une activité occupationnelle significative. Le contenu doit offrir des expériences variées pour répondre aux préférences individuelles et garantir l'accès à des expériences utiles et souhaitées.

titre: Winifred Conrick Kahmann: Shaping the Foundations of Occupational Therapy Practice, Education, and Leadership.
titre_fr: Winifred Conrick Kahmann : Shaping the Foundations of Occupational Therapy Practice, Education, and Leadership.
auteurs: Reed Kathlyn L
resume: This paper summarized the contributions of Winifred Conrick Kahmann, OTR, who was a member of the first generation of occupational therapy practitioners educated as an occupational therapist. As a pioneer in a new profession, her contributions included development of practice sites, educating students, promoting awareness of the role of occupational therapy and providing the management skills needed to oversee practitioners and students while interacting effectively with physicians, other healthcare workers, and volunteers. Kahmann excelled in all four areas: program development, student education, professional promotion, and management. With the development of practice sites, she provided fieldwork education for students, published articles and advocated for occupational therapy to professional and lay groups. Additional contributions included provided management skills as a department head to the hospitals with whom she was employed, as an officer to the American Occupational Therapy Association (AOTA) and consultant to the Army Surgeon General's office.
resume_fr: Cet article résume les contributions de Winifred Conrick Kahmann, ergothérapeute agréée, qui faisait partie de la première génération de praticiens en ergothérapie formés en tant qu'ergothérapeutes. En tant que pionnière d'une nouvelle profession, ses contributions ont notamment consisté à développer des sites de pratique, à former des étudiants, à faire connaître le rôle de l'ergothérapie et à fournir les compétences de gestion nécessaires pour superviser les praticiens et les étudiants pendant leur stage.interagir efficacement avec les médecins, les autres professionnels de la santé et les bénévoles. Kahmann a excellé dans les quatre domaines : l'élaboration de programmes, la formation des étudiants, la promotion professionnelle et la gestion. Avec le développement de sites de pratique, elle a dispensé une formation sur le terrain aux étudiants, publié des articles et fait la promotion de l'ergothérapie auprès de groupes professionnels et de profanes. Parmi ses autres contributions, citons la mise à disposition de ses compétences en gestion en tant que chef de départementse rendre dans les hôpitaux où elle travaillait, en tant que responsable de l'American Occupational Therapy Association (AOTA) et consultante au cabinet du médecin général de l'armée.

titre: A Standardized Occupational Therapy-Based Upper Extremity Assessment for Surgical Residency Onboarding.
titre_fr: Une évaluation standardisée des membres supérieurs basée sur l'ergothérapie pour l'intégration des résidents en chirurgie.
auteurs: Burnette Caitlin, Zeller Matthew, Dixon Austin, Chilcoat Angelina Romano, Feinman Marcie
resume: This initiative targets technical readiness and ergonomic awareness within surgical residents. By integrating occupational therapy (OT) assessment into resident onboarding, the evaluation identifies individual strengths and potential improvement opportunities before training. This approach aims to assist with proactive strength development, wellness, and sustainable surgical performance. To enhance early technical skill acquisition and ergonomic awareness, our general surgery residency integrated a structured OT upper extremity and hand functional assessment prior to onboarding. Each incoming intern underwent evaluation of ergonomic health, fine motor coordination, hand strength, dexterity, and peripheral neurological status. Residents received individualized reports with suggestions for exercises to maximize performance, promoting early awareness of hand ergonomics and strategies to reduce the learning curve in surgical skill development. Across 2 intern cohorts from 2024 to 2025 (n = 8), residents completed a follow-up survey 4 months into training, assessing the perceived value of the OT assessment using a 5-point Likert scale. They rated the experience highly, finding it helpful for residency preparation (mean 4.5 ± 0.5), useful during training (4.0 ± 0.8), positively impactful in the operating room (3.75 ± 0.9), and worth their time (4.9 ± 0.4); 75% implemented OT recommendations and 25% pursued additional follow-up. Feedback emphasized improved ergonomic awareness, confidence, and intentional self-improvement early in training. This project introduces an innovative, interdisciplinary approach to surgical ergonomic awareness by pairing OT expertise with resident technical development. The assessment encourages residents to consider their individual musculoskeletal strengths and ergonomic habits from the outset of training. Early integration of hand and upper-extremity assessment fosters technical readiness, enhances wellness, and may reduce overuse injuries throughout surgical residency. Potential barriers include limited OT staffing, time constraints, and cost for larger programs, which can be mitigated through streamlined protocols and involvement of OT trainees. Scheduling assessments before orientation avoids disruption to clinical duties and enhances feasibility across diverse surgical training programs. This baseline upper extremity and hand assessment was easily implemented at our institution and can be scaled to other programs with OT partnerships using standardized templates for consistent feedback and reproducibility. Minimal cost and scheduled evaluation time make it adaptable to diverse training settings.
resume_fr: Cette initiative vise à renforcer la préparation technique et la sensibilisation à l’ergonomie chez les internes en chirurgie. En intégrant l'évaluation en ergothérapie (OT) à l'intégration des internes, l'évaluation identifie les points forts individuels et les possibilités d'amélioration potentielles avant la formation. Cette approche vise à contribuer au développement proactif des points forts, au bien-être et à la performance chirurgicale durable. Pour améliorer l’acquisition précoce des compétences techniques et l’ergonomiesensibilisation, notre internat en chirurgie générale a intégré une évaluation fonctionnelle structurée des membres supérieurs et des mains par un ergothérapeute avant l'intégration. Chaque nouvel interne a fait l'objet d'une évaluation de sa santé ergonomique, de sa coordination motrice fine, de sa force manuelle, de sa dextérité et de son état neurologique périphérique. Les résidents ont reçu des rapports individualisés contenant des suggestions d'exercices visant à optimiser leurs performances, à favoriser une prise de conscience précoce de l'ergonomie des mains et à proposer des stratégies pour réduireréduire la courbe d'apprentissage dans le développement des compétences chirurgicales. Au sein de 2 cohortes d'internes de 2024 à 2025 (n = 8), les résidents ont répondu à un questionnaire de suivi 4 mois après le début de leur formation, évaluant la valeur perçue de l'évaluation en salle d'opération à l'aide d'une échelle de Likert à 5 points. Ils ont attribué une note élevée à l’expérience, la jugeant utile pour la préparation à l’internat (moyenne : 4,5 ± 0,5), utile pendant la formation (4,0 ± 0,8), ayant un impact positif en salle d’opération (3,75 ± 0,9) et valant la peine d’être suivie.temps d'héritier (4,9 ± 0,4) ; 75 % ont mis en œuvre les recommandations de l'ergothérapeute et 25 % ont fait l'objet d'un suivi supplémentaire. Les retours ont mis l'accent sur une meilleure sensibilisation à l'ergonomie, une plus grande confiance et un effort délibéré d'amélioration personnelle dès le début de la formation. Ce projet introduit une approche innovante et interdisciplinaire de la sensibilisation à l'ergonomie chirurgicale en associant l'expertise des ergothérapeutes au développement technique des internes. L'évaluation encourage les internes à prendre en compte leur santé musculosquelettique individuelleles points forts et les habitudes ergonomiques dès le début de la formation. L'intégration précoce de l'évaluation de la main et des membres supérieurs favorise la préparation technique, améliore le bien-être et peut réduire les blessures dues à une utilisation excessive tout au long de l'internat en chirurgie. Les obstacles potentiels comprennent le nombre limité d'ergothérapeutes, les contraintes de temps et le coût des programmes plus importants, qui peuvent être atténués par des protocoles simplifiés et la participation d'ergothérapeutes stagiaires. Programmer des évaluations avant l'orientationévite de perturber les tâches cliniques et améliore la faisabilité dans divers programmes de formation chirurgicale. Cette évaluation de référence des membres supérieurs et des mains a été facilement mise en œuvre dans notre établissement et peut être étendue à d'autres programmes en partenariat avec des ergothérapeutes, en utilisant des modèles standardisés pour garantir la cohérence des retours et la reproductibilité. Le coût minimal et le temps d'évaluation planifié la rendent adaptable à divers contextes de formation.

titre: Assessing quality of life during adolescence and adulthood following brachial plexus birth injuries.
titre_fr: Évaluation de la qualité de vie à l'adolescence et à l'âge adulte après des lésions du plexus brachial à la naissance.
auteurs: Ajayi Omotolani O, Gaskin Regan E, Zhai Guihua, Rocque Brandon G
resume: The objective of this study was to assess quality of life (QOL) outcomes during adolescence and adulthood following brachial plexus birth injury (BPBI) and to identify factors linked to poorer outcomes. Additionally, the authors aimed to determine the construct validity of the Impact of a Brachial Plexus Injury Questionnaire (Mancuso scale) for use in the birth injury population. This study utilized a cross-sectional, within-subject comparative survey design to assess the QOL outcomes of adolescents and adults with BPBI. Participants older than 13 years of age and with a history of BPBI were identified using the United Brachial Plexus Network Facebook group. QOL was assessed using the World Health Organization Quality of Life Scale-Brief Version (WHOQOL-BREF) in adults, Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL) in adolescents, and a brachial plexus injury-specific tool (Mancuso scale). To determine construct validity, scores from each Mancuso subscale were compared to the participants' overall WHOQOL-BREF scores. Adults (n = 59) who completed the WHOQOL-BREF had a mean overall score of 63.1 ± 22.2 (0- to 100-point scale). The scores of the Mancuso scale with regard to the symptoms, limitations, and emotion subscales were 45.8 ± 29.5, 35.2 ± 17.3, and 43.6 ± 25.3, respectively. These findings contrasted with the published values from subjects who had sustained a traumatic brachial plexus injury whose scores were 66 ± 18.7, 48.2 ± 22.3, and 39.5 ± 21.2, respectively. For adolescents (n = 4), the overall score on PedsQL was 63.7 ± 21.3. Adolescent scores on the Mancuso scale were 31.7 ± 26.9, 29.8 ± 20.7, and 39.7 ± 18.8, respectively. In adults, severe functional limitation and limited access to care were associated with poorer QOL (p < 0.05), whereas surgical history and occupational therapy attendance did not. Higher scores on the Mancuso subscales correlated with lower quality of life scores on the WHOQOL-BREF. Adolescent data analysis revealed similar, nonsignificant results. BPBI plays a role in long-term QOL, notably by the severity of functional limitation and access to care. The Mancuso scale shows promising construct validity in the adult BPBI population, but a larger sample of adolescents is needed.
resume_fr: L'objectif de cette étude était d'évaluer les résultats en matière de qualité de vie (QdV) pendant l'adolescence et à l'âge adulte à la suite d'une lésion obstétricale du plexus brachial (LOPB) et d'identifier les facteurs liés à des résultats moins favorables. En outre, les auteurs ont cherché à déterminer la validité de construit du questionnaire sur l'impact d'une lésion du plexus brachial (échelle de Mancuso) en vue de son utilisation auprès de la population ayant subi une lésion à la naissance. Cette étude a utilisé une approche transversale et comparative intrasujets.Conception de l'enquête pour évaluer les résultats en matière de qualité de vie des adolescents et des adultes atteints de BPBI. Les participants âgés de plus de 13 ans et ayant des antécédents de BPBI ont été identifiés grâce au groupe Facebook United Brachial Plexus Network. La qualité de vie a été évaluée à l'aide de l'échelle de qualité de vie de l'Organisation mondiale de la Santé - version abrégée (WHOQOL-BREF) chez les adultes, de l'inventaire de qualité de vie pédiatrique (PedsQL) chez les adolescents et d'un outil spécifique aux lésions du plexus brachial (échelle de Mancuso).. Pour déterminer la validité de construit, les scores de chaque sous-échelle de Mancuso ont été comparés aux scores globaux WHOQOL-BREF des participants. Les adultes (n = 59) ayant répondu au WHOQOL-BREF ont obtenu un score global moyen de 63,1 ± 22,2 (échelle de 0 à 100 points). Les scores de l’échelle de Mancuso en ce qui concerne les sous-échelles des symptômes, des limitations et des émotions étaient respectivement de 45,8 ± 29,5, 35,2 ± 17,3 et 43,6 ± 25,3. Ces résultats contrastaient avec les valeurs publiées.provenant de sujets ayant subi une lésion traumatique du plexus brachial, dont les scores étaient respectivement de 66 ± 18,7, 48,2 ± 22,3 et 39,5 ± 21,2. Pour les adolescents (n = 4), le score global au PedsQL était de 63,7 ± 21,3. Les scores des adolescents sur l'échelle de Mancuso étaient respectivement de 31,7 ± 26,9, 29,8 ± 20,7 et 39,7 ± 18,8. Chez les adultes, une limitation fonctionnelle sévère et un accès limité aux soins étaient associés à une moins bonne qualité de vie (p < 0,05), tandis que les antécédents chirurgicauxet la fréquentation de l’ergothérapie n’a pas eu d’effet. Des scores plus élevés sur les sous-échelles de Mancuso étaient corrélés à des scores de qualité de vie plus faibles sur le WHOQOL-BREF. L'analyse des données concernant les adolescents a révélé des résultats similaires, non significatifs. La BPBI joue un rôle dans la qualité de vie à long terme, notamment en raison de la gravité de la limitation fonctionnelle et de l'accès aux soins. L'échelle de Mancuso présente une validité de construit prometteuse dans la population adulte atteinte de BPBI, mais un échantillon plus important d'adolescents est nécessaire.

titre: Gait and Balance Disorders in Older Adults.
titre_fr: Troubles de la marche et de l'équilibre chez les personnes âgées.
auteurs: Russell Rebecca, Chamberlain Carly
resume: Falls in older adults are often the result of gait and balance disorders. These disorders affect a patient's quality of life, reduce their functional capacity, and increase morbidity and mortality. Common conditions in older adults, including arthritis and sarcopenia, contribute to these mobility disorders, but primary care physicians should also consider less common causes, such as neurodegenerative disorders (eg, Parkinson disease, Huntington disease) and normal pressure hydrocephalus. Physicians caring for older adults should ask patients about unsteadiness and falls at every health maintenance visit. Gait should be observed if there is a higher risk for falls based on patient or caregiver concerns. Several mobility assessments can be used to assess fall risk and gait disorders, including the Timed Up and Go test, the 30-Second Chair Stand test, and the 4-Stage Balance test. Fall prevention should include a multifactorial evaluation and individualized intervention strategies. Effective fall prevention involves increasing physical activity, using appropriate assistive devices, and strength training, ideally with physical or occupational therapy.
resume_fr: Les chutes chez les personnes âgées sont souvent le résultat de troubles de la marche et de l’équilibre. Ces troubles affectent la qualité de vie du patient, réduisent sa capacité fonctionnelle et augmentent la morbidité et la mortalité. Des affections courantes chez les personnes âgées, notamment l’arthrite et la sarcopénie, contribuent à ces troubles de la mobilité, mais les médecins généralistes doivent également envisager des causes moins fréquentes, telles que les troubles neurodégénératifs (par exemple, la maladie de Parkinson, la maladie de Huntington).et l’hydrocéphalie à pression normale. Les médecins qui prennent en charge des personnes âgées doivent interroger leurs patients sur leurs problèmes d’instabilité et leurs chutes lors de chaque consultation de suivi médical. La démarche doit être observée s’il existe un risque accru de chutes en fonction des préoccupations du patient ou du soignant. Plusieurs évaluations de la mobilité peuvent être utilisées pour évaluer le risque de chute et les troubles de la marche, notamment le test Timed Up and Go, le test de lever de chaise en 30 secondes et le test d’équilibre en 4 étapes. La prévention des chutesLa prise en charge doit inclure une évaluation multifactorielle et des stratégies d’intervention individualisées. Une prévention efficace des chutes implique d’augmenter l’activité physique, d’utiliser des dispositifs d’assistance appropriés et de pratiquer un entraînement musculaire, idéalement avec une kinésithérapie ou une ergothérapie.

titre: Exploring the COSA-t and Other Occupation-Based Assessments in Pediatric Occupational Therapy for Tic Disorders.
titre_fr: Étude du COSA-t et d'autres évaluations axées sur les activités dans le cadre de l'ergothérapie pédiatrique pour les troublesचना de tics.
auteurs: Schug Thaila, Martin Heather Simpson, Rowe Jan, Kramer Jessica M
revue: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
resume: ImportanceThere is a paucity of research describing the occupational therapy assessment process for children with tic disorders (TD) and the priority areas of occupational performance that should be considered during assessment.ObjectiveThis study aimed to (1) explore the content validity of the COSA-t items, as indicated by clinical importance and (2) understand how occupational therapists use the COSA-t and other occupation-based assessments to inform their Comprehensive Behavioral Intervention for Tics (CBIT) practice.DesignCross-sectional, qualitative study.SettingVirtual focus groups (Zoom) and asynchronous surveys.ParticipantsOccupational therapists were recruited through closed, professional networks. All participants were CBIT trained, had experience providing occupational therapy to at least one child with TD, and had training or experience administering the COSA-t or other occupation-based assessments with children with TD.Outcomes and MeasuresParticipants rated the clinical importance of each COSA-t item using a 0 to 10 visual analog scale. Five virtual focus groups explored participants' use of occupation-based assessments with children with TD.ResultsNineteen occupational therapists completed the survey of clinical importance and 18 participated in focus groups (17 female, 1 male, 2-20 years of experience). COSA-t importance ratings ranged from 5.95 to 8.95. Occupation-based assessments were a starting point, revealed the daily impact of tics, provided clinical discernment, and fostered motivation and insight.Conclusions and RelevanceThe occupational therapists found value in administering occupation-based assessments, such as the COSA-t. Therefore, there is a pressing need for further evidence to support the incorporation of self-reported, occupation-based assessments into interventions with children with TD.
resume_fr: Importance Il existe peu d'études décrivant le processus d'évaluation en ergothérapie pour les enfants atteints de troubles des tics (TT) et les domaines prioritaires de la performance occupationnelle qui devraient être pris en compte lors de l'évaluation. Objectif Cette étude visait à (1) explorer la validité de contenu des items du COSA-t, telle qu'indiquée par l'importance clinique, et (2) comprendre comment les ergothérapeutes utilisent le COSA-t et d'autres évaluations basées sur l'activité pouréclairer leur pratique de l'intervention comportementale globale pour les tics (CBIT). Conception : étude transversale qualitative. Cadre : groupes de discussion virtuels (Zoom) et enquêtes asynchrones. Participants : les ergothérapeutes ont été recrutés par le biais de réseaux professionnels fermés. Tous les participants avaient été formés à la CBIT, avaient de l'expérience dans la prestation d'ergothérapie à au moins un enfant atteint de TD et avaient été formés ou avaient de l'expérience dans l'administration du COSA-t ou d'autres évaluations en ergothérapie.évaluations basées sur les activités chez les enfants atteints de TD. Résultats et mesures Les participants ont évalué l'importance clinique de chaque item du COSA-t à l'aide d'une échelle visuelle analogique allant de 0 à 10. Cinq groupes de discussion virtuels ont exploré l'utilisation par les participants d'évaluations basées sur les activités auprès d'enfants atteints de TD. Résultats : Dix-neuf ergothérapeutes ont répondu à l'enquête sur l'importance clinique et 18 ont participé aux groupes de discussion (17 femmes, 1 homme, 2 à 20 ans d'expérience). COSA-t iLes notes d'importance allaient de 5,95 à 8,95. Les évaluations axées sur les activités ont constitué un point de départ, ont révélé l'impact quotidien des tics, ont fourni un discernement clinique et ont favorisé la motivation et la compréhension. Conclusions et pertinence Les ergothérapeutes ont trouvé qu'il était utile de procéder à des évaluations axées sur les activités, telles que le COSA-t. Par conséquent, il est urgent d'obtenir davantage de données probantes pour justifier l'intégration d'évaluations autodéclarées et axées sur les activités.des évaluations en interventions auprès d'enfants atteints de TD.

titre: Early Developmental Interventions for Infants Born Very Preterm: A Survey of Australian Physiotherapy and Occupational Therapy Practice.
titre_fr: Interventions précoces de développement pour les nourrissons nés très prématurément : une enquête sur les pratiques de physiothérapie et d'ergothérapie en Australie.
auteurs: Fehring Susan M, Eeles Abbey L, Hastings-Ison Tandy, Cameron Kate L I, Pascoe Jessica, Spittle Alicia J
resume: To describe clinical practices of Australian physiotherapists and occupational therapists providing early developmental interventions for infants born very preterm (VPT; <32 weeks' gestation) during the first year of life. A national survey was conducted with physiotherapists and occupational therapists who had cared for infants born VPT, under 12 months' corrected age. Clinician demographics and practice characteristics were summarized using descriptive statistics. Intervention descriptions (guided by the Template for Intervention Description and Replication for Rehabilitation checklist), and perceived barriers and facilitators, were analyzed using inductive content analysis. Of 114 responses analyzed (74.6% physiotherapists), representing all Australian states, territories and care sectors, most reported more than 10 years of clinical experience (65.8%), provided care during neonatal hospital admissions (65.8%), and worked within multidisciplinary teams (93.9%). Interventions encompassed multiple interacting components, described using varied terminology. Three categories of barriers and facilitators included: systems and structures, infant and family characteristics, and clinician capabilities. Physiotherapists and occupational therapists in Australia provide early developmental interventions across multiple sectors within collaborative practice settings. Variability in terminology and systems-level barriers highlight the need for greater consistency in clinical practice. Standardization of terminology and strengthening clinician capabilities are key priorities for the field.
resume_fr: Décrire les pratiques cliniques des kinésithérapeutes et des ergothérapeutes australiens qui proposent des interventions précoces de développement aux nourrissons nés très prématurément (NTP ; < 32 semaines d'âge gestationnel) au cours de leur première année de vie. Une enquête nationale a été menée auprès de kinésithérapeutes et d'ergothérapeutes ayant pris en charge des nourrissons nés GPV, âgés de moins de 12 mois d'âge corrigé. Les données démographiques des cliniciens et les caractéristiques de leur pratique ont été résumées à l'aide destatistiques descriptives. Les descriptions des interventions (guidées par la liste de contrôle du modèle de description et de reproduction des interventions pour la réadaptation), ainsi que les obstacles et les facilitateurs perçus, ont été analysés à l'aide d'une analyse inductive du contenu. Sur les 114 réponses analysées (74,6 % de kinésithérapeutes), représentant tous les États, tous les territoires et tous les secteurs de soins australiens, la plupart des répondants ont déclaré avoir plus de 10 ans d'expérience clinique (65,8 %), avoir dispensé des soins pendant la période néonataledes admissions à l'hôpital (65,8 %) et ont travaillé au sein d'équipes multidisciplinaires (93,9 %). Les interventions comprenaient plusieurs éléments interagissant entre eux, décrits à l'aide d'une terminologie variée. Trois catégories d'obstacles et de facilitateurs ont été identifiées : les systèmes et les structures, les caractéristiques du nourrisson et de la famille, et les compétences des cliniciens. Les kinésithérapeutes et les ergothérapeutes en Australie proposent des interventions précoces de développement dans de nombreux secteurs, dans le cadre d'une collaborationContextes de pratique collaborative. La variabilité de la terminologie et les obstacles au niveau des systèmes soulignent la nécessité d'une plus grande cohérence dans la pratique clinique. La normalisation de la terminologie et le renforcement des compétences des cliniciens sont des priorités essentielles dans ce domaine.

titre: Barriers to Implementing Sleep Interventions for Children With Autism: Malaysian Occupational Therapists' Perspectives.
titre_fr: Obstacles à la mise en œuvre d'interventions liées au sommeil chez les enfants atteints d'autisme : points de vue des ergothérapeutes malaisiens.
auteurs: Abu Bakar Muhammad Radhi Rahimi, Dahlan Akehsan, Zaini Zul-'Izzat Ikhwan, Mohd Rasdi Hanif Farhan
resume: Implementing sleep interventions for children with autism spectrum disorder remains challenging. This study identified barriers faced by Malaysian pediatric occupational therapists. A convergent mixed-methods design integrated quantitative survey data from 112 occupational therapists with qualitative data from two focus group discussions (N = 10). Two major barriers emerged: (a) inadequate formal training and knowledge gaps regarding evidence-based sleep management, reported by 76.8% and 67.0% of survey respondents, respectively, leading to reliance on informal practices; and (b) a lack of standardized resources (59.8%) and clinical time constraints, which limited intervention consistency. Malaysian occupational therapists face critical educational, resource, and operational gaps in pediatric sleep practice. Overcoming these barriers requires structured curriculum integration, continuing professional development, standardized clinical toolkits, and multidisciplinary practice frameworks.

titre: Development and Initial Psychometric Evaluation of the Family Life Impact Questionnaire.
titre_fr: Development and Initial Psychometric Evaluation of the Family Life Impact Questionnaire.
auteurs: Grady-Dominguez Patricia, Turel Aleks Anton, Mailloux Zoe, Smith Roley Susanne, Bundy Anita C, Schaaf Roseann C
resume: Occupation and co-occupation are central to occupational therapy, yet no standardized instrument exists to measure ease of participation in co-occupations for families with a child with sensory integration challenges. This study describes the initial development and psychometric evaluation of data gathered with the Family Life Impact Questionnaire (FLIQ), a parent-report measure assessing perceived ease of family participation. Using Rasch measurement methods, we iteratively evaluated the 43-item FLIQ with a sample of 62 parents of children with sensory integration challenges (n = 25) and typically developing children (n = 37). Analyses supported a two-subscale structure: Social Participation (nine items) and Daily Life Management (25 items), rated on a 4-point scale. Both demonstrated strong reliability (person separation reliability = .88-.95), good item fit, and large between-group effect sizes. FLIQ shows promise as a clinically meaningful, occupation-centered instrument for assessing and monitoring family participation outcomes.

titre: Task-specific training for upper limb rehabilitation after subacute and chronic stroke: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Task-specific training for upper limb rehabilitation after subacute and chronic stroke: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Berges Enrique Villa, García César Hidalgo, Zamorano Pablo de Blas, Sánchez Manuel González, Pérez-Cruzado David
revue: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
resume: Task-specific training is commonly used to improve poststroke upper-limb function through repetitive, goal-directed practice of meaningful tasks. To evaluate the effectiveness of task-specific training, alone or combined with adjunct therapies, on upper-limb motor recovery and activity/activities of daily living-related outcomes after subacute and chronic stroke. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and OTSeeker, through September 2025, for randomized controlled trials in adults with subacute/chronic stroke. Effect sizes were summarized as Cohen's d; random-effects pooling was performed when dispersion data allowed. In 24 randomized controlled trials of moderate-to-high methodological quality, within-group improvements were frequently observed in motor recovery and functional outcomes across both subacute and chronic stroke. Significant between-group effects favoring task-specific training were reported in five of 17 trials assessing upper-limb motor recovery, one of 11 assessing upper-limb function in activities of daily living, one of four assessing gross manual dexterity, one of six assessing amount of use, and one of seven assessing quality of movement. Significant between-group effect sizes ranged from Cohen's d = -0.12 to -0.97 for motor recovery, while effects of d = -0.39, -1.18, and -3.03 were reported for gross manual dexterity, amount of use, and quality of movement, respectively. Statistical heterogeneity across pooled outcomes was substantial (I² = 71% = 93%), and pooling was limited by incomplete dispersion reporting. Task-specific training may improve upper-limb outcomes in adults with subacute and chronic stroke. However, when delivered alone or in combination with adjunct interventions, the advantages over active comparators were not consistent across outcomes. Activities of daily living-oriented, meaningful task practice may promote functional gains, but current evidence does not support universal superiority of task-specific training over other active rehabilitation approaches.

titre: Mirror comfort and avoidance, contextual support, and illness acceptance after breast cancer surgery: a cross-sectional study among Iranian women.
titre_fr: Mirror comfort and avoidance, contextual support, and illness acceptance after breast cancer surgery: a cross-sectional study among Iranian women.
auteurs: Roudi RashtAbadi Omsalimeh, Kazemy Homayoon, Freysteinson Wyona M, Kalantari Khandani Behjat, Fattahi Toqroljerdi Mohammad Hossein, Seyfali Nasab Asma, Soleimani Zahra
resume: Breast cancer surgery can alter body image, mirror-viewing experiences, and illness acceptance. This study examined illness acceptance, body image disturbance, mirror comfort and avoidance, and contextual factors among Iranian women after breast cancer surgery, addressing limited quantitative evidence from Middle Eastern settings. This cross-sectional correlational study included 103 women after partial or total breast cancer surgery in Kerman, Iran. Participants completed the Acceptance of Illness Scale, Body Image Scale, Mirror Image Comfort and Avoidance Scale, and exploratory contextual items. Spearman's correlations, Kruskal-Wallis tests, and multiple linear regression were used. Illness acceptance was positively associated with mirror comfort (r = 0.452, p < 0.001) and negatively associated with mirror avoidance (r = -0.609, p < 0.001), but not with body image disturbance. In the regression analytic sample (n = 90), mirror avoidance, treatment-related personal/family disruption, and perceived usefulness of adaptation support were independently associated with illness acceptance (R2 = 0.632); mirror avoidance showed the largest standardized association (β = -0.562, p < 0.001). Mirror-related responses may provide rehabilitation-relevant information beyond general body image. Interdisciplinary, preference-sensitive preparation, and supported mirror-assisted self-care warrant evaluation in prospective and interventional studies.

titre: A Preliminary Study of Occupational Therapy Doctoral Students' Perception on AI's Application in Occupational Therapy Education and Practice.
titre_fr: A Preliminary Study of Occupational Therapy Doctoral Students' Perception on AI's Application in Occupational Therapy Education and Practice.
auteurs: Coppard Brenda, Qi Yongyue, Lampe Angela, Mu Jackson
resume: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing health care and rehabilitation, yet little is known about how occupational therapy students perceive its role in education and clinical practice. This survey study examined perceptions of AI's application in occupational therapy education and practice among entry-level occupational therapy doctoral students at a Midwestern university. Using a self‑developed 28‑item questionnaire (5-point Likert scale items) with three subscales-Knowledge and Understanding, Attitudes toward AI's Application, and Intention to Engage in AI's Application-researchers invited all 308 students across three cohorts to participate. The study also examined the psychometric property of the self developed questionnaire. Sixty-four students responded (20.8%). Overall perceptions were neutral to slightly positive (M = 3.16), with the highest ratings in Knowledge and Understanding (M = 3.73) and the lowest in Attitudes toward AI's Application (M = 2.84), reflecting concerns about academic integrity, privacy, clinical reasoning, and reliability of AI-generated information. ANOVA results showed no significant differences across cohorts, likely due to the absence of structured AI integration within the curriculum. The questionnaire demonstrated strong reliability (Cronbach α = 0.87). Findings highlight a gap between students' familiarity with AI and their comfort applying it in professional contexts. As AI continues to shape documentation, decision‑making, and client engagement, occupational therapy programs should intentionally incorporate AI literacy, ethical considerations, and hands‑on learning experiences to prepare students for evolving practice demands.

titre: Natural History of Prenatally Identified Children With 48,XXYY Syndrome in Infancy and Early Childhood.
titre_fr: Natural History of Prenatally Identified Children With 48,XXYY Syndrome in Infancy and Early Childhood.
auteurs: Nocon Kayla, Swenson Karli, Bothwell Samantha, Howell Susan, Davis Shanlee, Ikomi Chijioke, Ross Judith, Tartaglia Nicole
revue: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
resume: 48,XXYY syndrome is a rare sex chromosome aneuploidy (SCA) associated with a variable profile of neurodevelopmental and medical. The limited information available in the literature is almost exclusively limited to postnatally diagnosed cases. This study aims to describe the early medical and developmental features of prenatally identified 48,XXYY infants, The eXtraordinarY Babies Study prospectively follows children prenatally identified to be at high risk for SCA with annual medical and neurodevelopmental evaluations. Data presented herein include the prevalence of medical conditions, developmental milestones, developmental and adaptive functioning assessment scores, and therapy utilization in 15 participants confirmed to have 48,XXYY. Comparisons were made with 47,XYY and 47,XXY males also enrolled in the eXtraordinarY Babies Study, the general population and a 2008 cohort of individuals postnatally identified 48,XXYY. Infants and young chlidren with 48,XXYY exhibited a range of early medical features, including elevated rates of feeding and GI disorders (breastfeeding difficulties, gastroesophageal reflux, and eosinophilic esophagitis), allergic disorders (food allergies and environmental allergies), and hypotonia. Developmental and adaptive functioning scores identified variable delays in motor, communication, and social domains, with nearly all infants receiving speech therapy, physical and/or occupational therapy due to delays or proactive developmental care. Medical and developmental findings were more prevalent in 48,XXYY compared to the 47,XYY and 47,XXY cohorts, although considerable individual variability and overlap in developmental functioning were observed across groups. Compared to the 2008 postnatally identified 48,XXYY cohort, infants identified prenatally received earlier intervention services, and developmental outcomes in the first years of life were similar between the two groups. Prenatal identification of 48,XXYY provides opportunity for early developmental monitoring, anticipatory guidance, and proactive referrals for medical evaluations and intervention. These findings provide valuable insights for genetic counselors and healthcare providers, emphasizing the spectrum of medical and developmental findings and the importance of early and proactive care to support individual outcomes. Prospective study of this prenatally identified cohort will provide important data about the natural history and phenotypic variability in XXYY, as well as identification of predictors of health and developmental outcomes. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03396562.

titre: Development of the Children's Occupational Justice Scale Across Metropolitan and Non-Metropolitan Contexts.
titre_fr: Development of the Children's Occupational Justice Scale Across Metropolitan and Non-Metropolitan Contexts.
auteurs: Bektas Selen Aydoner, Bumin Gonca
revue: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
resume: ImportanceOccupational justice is a core concept in occupational therapy; however, no standardized self-report measure exists for school-aged children, limiting the identification of occupational inequities and evaluation of participation-focused interventions.ObjectiveTo develop and evaluate the psychometric properties of the Children's Occupational Justice Scale (COJS) and examine its ability to distinguish between children from metropolitan and non-metropolitan contexts.DesignCross-sectional scale development and psychometric validation study.SettingSchools located in metropolitan and non-metropolitan regions of Türkiye.ParticipantsA total of 873 children ages 11 to 14 years participated. Independent samples were used for exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n = 428) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n = 445). Test-retest reliability was assessed in 94 participants.Outcomes and MeasuresThe preliminary COJS was developed through literature review, expert evaluation, and pilot testing. Construct validity, reliability, and known-groups validity were examined.ResultsEFA supported a 23-item, four-factor structure explaining 68.47% of the variance. CFA demonstrated good model fit (Comparative Fit Index = .957, Tucker-Lewis Index = .949, Goodness-of-Fit Index = .918, Root Mean Square Error of Approximation = .054, Standardized Root Mean Square Residual = .047). Internal consistency was excellent (Cronbach's α = .94; McDonald's ω = .95), and test-retest reliability was strong (intraclass correlation coefficient = .91, 95% confidence interval [.87, .94]). Children in metropolitan regions reported significantly higher occupational justice scores than children in non-metropolitan regions (p < .001).Conclusions and RelevanceThe COJS demonstrated strong validity and reliability for assessing occupational justice among school-aged children. The scale may provide occupational therapy practitioners and researchers with a novel tool for identifying occupational inequities and evaluating children's perceptions of participation opportunities, inclusion, choice, and environmental support.

titre: Effectiveness of Drive-Fun Intervention: Randomized Controlled Trial to Reduce Driving Risks Among Adolescents With ADHD.
titre_fr: Effectiveness of Drive-Fun Intervention: Randomized Controlled Trial to Reduce Driving Risks Among Adolescents With ADHD.
auteurs: Keren Anat, Fisher Orit, Mahani Trepp Amit, Hamde Anwar, Tsafrir Shlomit, Ratzon Navah Z
revue: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
resume: ImportanceAdolescents with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) are more likely to be involved in motor vehicle accidents, highlighting the need for early intervention. However, there is a lack of evidence-based interventions addressing driving safety in this population.ObjectiveTo evaluate the effectiveness of the Drive-Fun cognitive-functional intervention on simulated driving performance, attentional control, and visual scanning in adolescents with ADHD.DesignRandomized controlled trial with three parallel groups: Drive-Fun, an educational intervention, and a control group.SettingA university research laboratory.ParticipantsNinety-three adolescents (M age = 16.8 years, SD = 0.52) diagnosed with ADHD.Outcomes and MeasuresPrimary outcomes were simulated driving errors; secondary outcomes included the percentage of time spent within the optimal Cognitive Effort Index (CEI) range and eye-tracking metrics.ResultsThe Drive-Fun group demonstrated significant time-by-group interactions: reduced driving errors, F(2, 89) = 82.65, p < .001; increased percentage of time spent within the optimal CEI range, F(2, 89) = 15.56, p < .001; fewer dashboard fixations, F(2, 89) = 27.65, p < .001; and more fixations on traffic lights, F(2, 89) = 7.61, p = .001, and pedestrians, F(2, 89) = 10.15, p < .001. Exploratory moderation analyses indicated greater improvements in driving performance among adolescents with lower Conners Hyperactive Scores and no regular sports participation within the Drive-Fun group.Conclusions and RelevanceThe Drive-Fun intervention improved simulated driving performance, cognitive engagement, and visual scanning, indicating its potential to reduce driving-related risks among adolescents with ADHD. Improvements were maintained at follow up, indicating sustained benefits. These findings support integrating cognitive-functional strategies and simulation-based training into occupational therapy to enhance adolescents' driving readiness and safety.

titre: Early intervention in children with fragile X syndrome: Prevalence, timing, and family perception.
titre_fr: Early intervention in children with fragile X syndrome: Prevalence, timing, and family perception.
auteurs: Dunajcik Alicia, McDonald Emily R, Summers April D, Esler Amy, Gonzalez Maria G, Thompson-Paul Angela M, Schweizer Marc, Tinker Sarah C
resume: Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is a genetic disorder that commonly leads to intellectual and developmental delays and disabilities. Early intervention (EI) services and therapies provided to children under 3 years of age aim to improve developmental outcomes. This analysis examines the prevalence of EI receipt among children with FXS, enrollment timing, services used, and parental satisfaction with EI services. Data were obtained from the Fragile X Online Registry With Accessible Research Database (FORWARD), collected from 2011 to 2021. Participants aged 3-21 years during at least one clinic visit were included. EI receipt and enrollment age were assessed overall and by demographic characteristics; services used and satisfaction with services were assessed in relation to EI enrollment age. All analyses were stratified by sex. Among 1114 participants, 86.0% of males and 59.6% of females received EI, with over 80% of parents reporting some level of satisfaction with services. EI receipt varied by household income, parental education, race/ethnicity, household language, and insurance. Among participants diagnosed with FXS at < 3 years, only 8.6% of males and 13.3% of females had a diagnosis before starting EI. Most EI participants received speech and language therapy (93.5% males, 90.3% females), occupational therapy (89.2% males, 72.4% females), and physical therapy (72.5% males, 50.3% females). Most children began early intervention before FXS diagnosis, showing that EI receipt may depend more on recognition of developmental delays than genetic diagnosis. Parental satisfaction with EI was high, though receipt varied substantially by demographic factors, identifying opportunities for targeted outreach.

titre: Feasibility and Preliminary Outcomes of Gardening-Based Immersive Virtual Reality Cognitive Training in Older Adults With Dementia: Single-Group Pretest-Posttest Analysis.
titre_fr: Feasibility and Preliminary Outcomes of Gardening-Based Immersive Virtual Reality Cognitive Training in Older Adults With Dementia: Single-Group Pretest-Posttest Analysis.
auteurs: Chuang I-Ching, Wu Hui-Ju, Wu Yih-Ru, Hsu Jung Lung, Wu Ching-Yi
resume: Nonpharmacological interventions for cognitive problems play a critical role in dementia care, yet maintaining engagement and adherence remains challenging. Immersive virtual reality (VR) provides a promising platform for cognitive training, particularly when integrated with personally meaningful leisure activities that may enhance therapeutic resonance. This study aimed to examine the feasibility of gardening-based immersive VR cognitive training and to explore pre-post changes in clinical outcomes among older adults with dementia. This study reports an analysis of intervention-phase data from an ongoing registered randomized crossover clinical trial (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07033468). For this report, the available data were analyzed using a single-group pretest-posttest approach; data from the waitlist-control period were not included. Between September 2024 and December 2025, 16 older adults with mild-to-moderate dementia were recruited through referral-based convenience sampling from a hospital and a dementia day care center in Taiwan. Participants completed a 15-session VR intervention over 5 weeks, involving gardening-based activities targeting multiple cognitive domains. Feasibility outcomes included VR acceptance, simulator sickness, and observed emotional responses during the first VR session. Cognitive outcomes included global cognition assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and domain-specific cognitive measures. Secondary outcomes included activities of daily living, depressive symptoms, behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia, quality of life, and well-being. Paired t tests were used to examine pre-post differences, and the Holm-Bonferroni procedure was applied to adjust for multiple comparisons. Sixteen participants (5 men and 11 women; mean age 78.12, SD 6.61 years) completed feasibility assessments, 15 participants (4 men, 11 women; mean age 78.57, SD 6.58 years) completed the intervention, and 5 occupational therapists evaluated the usability of the VR system. VR acceptance significantly increased after the first session (t15=-5.40, 95% CI -0.61 to -0.26; P<.001), while simulator sickness significantly decreased (t15=2.42; 95% CI 0.34-5.27; P=.009). Emotional responses indicated high levels of pleasure (mean 3.38, SD 1.63) and alertness (mean 4.63, SD 0.89) with minimal negative affect. Usability was rated as acceptable (system usability scale: mean 70.5, SD 12.17). Global cognitive performance was higher at postintervention than at baseline (MoCA: Cohen d=1.03; 95% CI -3.28 to -0.99; P=.001). No statistically significant pre-post differences were observed in domain-specific cognitive measures, activities of daily living, quality of life, or psychosocial outcomes. Gardening-based immersive VR cognitive training appears feasible, acceptable, and well tolerated among older adults with dementia. The program extends existing VR approaches by embedding familiar, goal-directed gardening activities within an interactive cognitive training environment. By combining participant-centered feasibility outcomes with occupational therapist-rated usability, this study provides preliminary evidence relevant to the development and implementation of person-centered VR cognitive training in clinical and community dementia care. The favorable pre-post change in global cognition further supports investigation of this approach in larger controlled studies.

By combining participant-centered feasibility outcomes with occupational therapist-rated usability, this study provides preliminary evidence relevant to the development and implementation of person-centered VR cognitive training in clinical and community dementia care. The favorable pre-post change in global cognition further supports investigation of this approach in larger controlled studies.

titre: Student Perceptions of Scaffolded Instruction Promoting Research Engagement for Future Evidence-Based Practice: A Forward Thinking Approach.
titre_fr: Student Perceptions of Scaffolded Instruction Promoting Research Engagement for Future Evidence-Based Practice: A Forward Thinking Approach.
auteurs: Modlin Ellen, Goldin Deana Shevit
resume: Occupational therapists are proficient in searching literature but struggle with complex research skills. This competency gap is an opportunity for occupational therapy education to promote greater student engagement in research activities to inform evidence-based practice (EBP) for future clinical decision-making and best practice in patient care. Our scaffolded, forward-thinking approach addressed this gap in a master's degree research course by conducting original systematic reviews. Students shared their experiences through an anonymous reflection assignment. Four major themes emerged from the students' reflective responses: 1) research engagement, 2) critical appraisal of evidence, 3) relationship between research and EBP, 4) supported learning.

titre: Who am I now? Experienced changes of occupational identity after spinal cord injury.
titre_fr: Who am I now? Experienced changes of occupational identity after spinal cord injury.
auteurs: Pettersson Sundberg Karina, Häggblom Kronlöf Greta, Antepohl Ulrica
resume: To explore the experiences of individuals in redeveloping their occupational identity following a spinal cord injury (SCI). This qualitative interview study included six adults with SCI and used an inductive design. Data were analyzed using latent qualitative content analysis. The findings indicate uncertainty and a dynamic process in redeveloping occupational identity through engagement in altered daily activities shaped by environmental and contexts. This is captured in the theme: "Landing or not landing in a new identity." Participants' experiences are expressed in four categories: Loss of identity sparks the fighting spirit; Challenge to maintain hope and faith in the future; The person I was - who am I now?; and Searching for my future self. Together, these illustrate the tension between holding on to a pre-injury identity and allowing a new one to emerge while navigating facilitators, barriers, and expectations. Following SCI, occupational identity undergoes a transformative process extending from rehabilitation into post-discharge life. Although individuals may initially strive to restore their pre-injury identity, redevelopment is influenced by self-worth and exploration of personal narratives. Findings highlight the importance of person-centered rehabilitation, coordinated interventions, lifelong follow-up, and further research to support occupational identity development following SCI.

titre: Eye-Tracking Use for Assessment and Rehabilitation of Driver Performance: A Scoping Review.
titre_fr: Eye-Tracking Use for Assessment and Rehabilitation of Driver Performance: A Scoping Review.
auteurs: Ghafari Ehsan, MacKenzie Diane, Holohan Quinn, Askari Sorayya
revue: Canadian journal of occupational therapy. Revue canadienne d'ergotherapie
resume: BackgroundDriving rehabilitation increasingly incorporates eye tracking to quantify visual-cognitive performance; however, its clinical relevance and patterns of use remain unclear.PurposeThis scoping review maps how eye-tracking technologies, metrics, and applications are used in driving assessment and rehabilitation, and characterizes the populations studied.MethodFollowing Arksey and O'Malley's framework and PRISMA-ScR, five databases were searched (January 2001-July 2026). Thirty-nine eligible studies were charted for population, driving task, eye-tracking metrics, and device type.FindingsStudy populations included older adults (24 studies), autism spectrum disorder (5), traumatic brain injury (3), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (3), visual field impairment (3), and stroke (1). Eye tracking was applied to hazard perception, visual exploration and scanning, visual-motor coordination, and cognitive workload. Simulator studies mostly used remote screen- or dashboard-mounted systems, whereas on-road studies mostly used head-mounted systems. Drivers in several populations showed delayed first fixation on hazards, fewer fixations on relevant targets, and narrower or spatially biased visual search than comparison drivers.ConclusionThese population-specific gaze signatures indicate that eye tracking offers an ecologically relevant complement to occupational therapy driving assessment. Normative gaze datasets, standardized reporting, and validated clinical thresholds are needed before eye-movement metrics can guide routine return-to-drive decisions.

titre: [The Montessori method for seniors in hospital settings - an innovative approach to the care of geriatric patients with cognitive impairment: a literature review and the authors' clinical experience].
titre_fr: [The Montessori method for seniors in hospital settings - an innovative approach to the care of geriatric patients with cognitive impairment: a literature review and the authors' clinical experience].
auteurs: Kożuch-Sajdak Katarzyna, Rataj Maria, Szymala-Pędzik Małgorzata, Sobieszczańska Małgorzata
resume: Due to population aging and the growing number of patients with neurocognitive disorders, there is an increasing need for effective non-pharmacological interventions in geriatric care. The Montessori method, derived from the pedagogy of Maria Montessori, is increasingly being adapted for the care of older adults with dementia. While predominantly used in long-term care facilities, this method represents a potentially valuable but rarely described tool in hospital settings. The work aims to review the current literature on the application of the Montessori method in the care of seniors with cognitive impairment, with particular focus on its effects on behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia, antipsychotic use, nutritional status, patient engagement and affect, and to present own experiences from implementing elements of this method at the Department of Geriatrics and Internal Medicine, Wroclaw Medical University. A narrative review of the literature from medical databases was conducted, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and clinical studies on Montessori based interventions for people with dementia published 2000-2025. The team's own experiences from >1 year of clinical practice were also included. The literature analysis confirms that Montessori-based interventions can significantly improve patient engagement, enhance positive affect, reduce challenging behaviors (agitation, aggression), and can improve independent eating ability. The authors' clinical experience supports a positive impact of occupational therapy with Montessori elements, cognitive prosthetics, the "hand-under-hand" technique, and modifications of the hospital environment on patient well-being and cooperation in the diagnostic-therapeutic process. The Montessori method represents a promising, evidence-based non-pharmacological approach in the care of geriatric patients with cognitive impairment. Its implementation in hospital settings, although innovative and beyond standard protocols, is feasible and warrants further prospective controlled studies. Med Pr Work Health Saf. 2026;77(4).

titre: Non-contact human activity recognition system for smart healthcare and elderly care.
titre_fr: Non-contact human activity recognition system for smart healthcare and elderly care.
auteurs: Xin Haitao, Cai Xiao, Zhu Fangzheng
resume: With the continuous increase in population aging, the demand for long-term health monitoring for elderly people living alone and patients with chronic diseases has been steadily growing. Human activity recognition is regarded as an important supporting technology for smart healthcare and elderly care monitoring. It plays a significant role in fall warning, rehabilitation assessment, and daily activity analysis. Traditional vision-based monitoring methods are limited by privacy concerns, illumination conditions, and occlusion effects. Wearable-device-based methods are affected by low user compliance and a high probability of device omission. To address these issues, a non-contact human activity recognition system based on WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) is proposed in this paper. Variations in multipath propagation caused by human movements are exploited to achieve passive monitoring of human activities. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, a CSI activity dataset for healthcare and elderly care scenarios is introduced. The dataset contains six typical human activities from 20 participants under the condition of three receiving antennas and 114 effective subcarriers. Considering that CSI signals simultaneously contain spatial scattering characteristics and temporal dynamic characteristics, a lightweight spatiotemporal asymmetric convolutional neural network is designed. An asymmetric large-kernel convolution structure is adopted to achieve effective decoupling and joint modeling of cross-antenna spatial information and long-term temporal features. As a result, model complexity is reduced while recognition accuracy is maintained. Experimental results show that an activity recognition accuracy of 96.85% is achieved on the dataset. In addition, favorable performance is obtained in terms of model parameter size and inference efficiency. The results indicate that the proposed WiFi CSI-based non-contact activity recognition technology can provide a low-cost, privacy-preserving, and easily deployable solution for hospital wards, elderly care institutions, and home health monitoring.

titre: Sensorimotor Impairments and Task-Specific Virtual Reality-Augmented Balance Rehabilitation in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Narrative Review.
titre_fr: Sensorimotor Impairments and Task-Specific Virtual Reality-Augmented Balance Rehabilitation in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Narrative Review.
auteurs: Lin Xuewen, Zhuang Jie, Jin Juan, Wang Tiantong, Rao Fen, Hu Zekai, Wang Jue, Long Junwen, Chen Jiameng, Yang Nanhua, Song Lei
revue: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
resume: Balance impairment in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) reflects interacting respiratory, muscular, sensory, cognitive, and behavioral constraints. Virtual reality (VR) and exergaming offer repeated practice and feedback, but technologies and exercise content vary substantially. This narrative review integrates COPD clinical and physiological evidence with indirect motor-learning literature to propose an impairment-oriented, task-specific rehabilitation framework. Study selection was performed by one reviewer, retrieval was selective, and no formal risk-of-bias or certainty assessment was undertaken. Direct VR-specific balance evidence in stable COPD remains sparse. A principal positive balance finding comes from hospitalized patients with acute exacerbation who received additional somatosensory game exercise alongside conventional therapy; it cannot establish effectiveness in stable outpatient or home populations or isolate a VR-specific effect. Pulmonary-rehabilitation outcomes, functional mobility, direct balance outcomes, and feasibility are considered separately. The framework links observed impairments to assessments, candidate tasks, proposed mechanisms, and outcomes, with explicit distinctions between direct COPD-VR evidence, non-VR COPD evidence, indirect evidence, and hypotheses. Current findings do not establish restoration of sensory function, durable sensory reweighting, or fall prevention. Dose-matched trials with mechanism-specific measures, retention, transfer, systematic safety reporting, and patient-relevant outcomes are needed before the proposed matching rules can be validated.

titre: Massive ascites with preserved serum albumin in adult anorexia nervosa: Impact on eating behavior and weight-based treatment assessment.
titre_fr: Massive ascites with preserved serum albumin in adult anorexia nervosa: Impact on eating behavior and weight-based treatment assessment.
auteurs: Mashimoto Masaya, Kora Toma, Sakamoto Yurie, Masuda Atsutaka, Chiba Hiromi, Ozone Motohiro
revue: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
resume: Ascites is a rare complication of anorexia nervosa (AN) and is typically associated with hypoalbuminemia. Its influence on eating behavior and on the evaluation of treatment response remains poorly characterized. A 30-year-old woman with AN presented with massive ascites despite a preserved serum albumin level, a presentation not previously reported in adults. Imaging, ascitic fluid analysis, and serological testing excluded cirrhosis, malignancy, infection, and autoimmune serositis. The fluid showed a high serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG, 2.1 g/dL) with preserved protein (3.1 g/dL) and normal lactate dehydrogenase. Although the SAAG was high, there was no evidence of portal hypertension, and the mechanism remains undetermined. Serum and ascitic carbohydrate antigen 125 were elevated and normalized as the ascites resolved. Ascites-related symptoms, including early satiety, abdominal pain, and nausea, further reduced oral intake, while fluctuations in body fluid obscured the weight gain expected from nutritional rehabilitation, making weight-based assessment of treatment efficacy difficult. The ascites resolved with nutritional therapy and diuretics. Ascites can develop in adult patients with AN even when serum albumin is preserved. Beyond the psychopathology of AN, somatic symptoms caused by ascites may influence eating behavior and contribute to weight loss. Because fluctuations in body fluid can confound weight-based assessment of treatment response, comprehensive clinical evaluation incorporating abdominal imaging, rather than body weight alone, is warranted.

titre: Normative Thresholds for Upper Extremity Functional Testing in Adolescent Athletes: Outcome Measures of Strength.
titre_fr: Normative Thresholds for Upper Extremity Functional Testing in Adolescent Athletes: Outcome Measures of Strength.
auteurs: Sloma Katie, Arvesen John, Erdman Ashley, Loewen Alex, Riesenberg Josh, Davis Ava, Ellis Henry, Wilson Philip, Ulman Sophia
resume: The use of functional upper extremity measures to guide rehabilitation, reduce injury risk, and inform return-to-play decision-making has increased. However, assessment of these measures has focused primarily on collegiate and adult athletes. Normative thresholds would differ by dominance, with stronger values exhibited on the dominant limb. Cross sectional. Level III. Healthy, adolescent athletes who reported participation in either contact or overhead upper-extremity sports completed an upper extremity functional test battery administered in a randomized order. Strength measures of internal rotation (IR) and external rotation (ER) as well as the athletic shoulder (ASH) test were collected in prone using a handheld dynamometer. Descriptive statistics were calculated for all outcome measures with separate analyses for dominant (DOM) and nondominant (NON) limbs. The 15th percentile was computed and used to establish performance thresholds. Strength measures were compared between limbs using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with effect sizes calculated. Descriptive statistics were computed to compare exploratorily male versus female and sport-based performance for all strength measures. A total of 156 participants (78.2% male; 60.2% contact athletes; age, 16.5 ± 1.2 years; weight, 162.8 ± 39.2 lbs) were included for analysis. Norms and percentile thresholds across tests are presented, with shoulder strength thresholds consistently greater in the DOM limb. DOM IR strength was significantly greater than NON IR strength (P = 0.002). ASH performance was greater in the DOM limb for the I position (180 degrees of shoulder abduction; P < 0.001) and Y position (135 degrees of abduction; P < 0.001). Performance in healthy, adolescent athletes is influenced by limb dominance and task-specificity and indicates that reliance on collegiate or adult-derived normative values may not be appropriate. These normative thresholds provide a clinically meaningful framework to guide rehabilitation progression and evidence-based decision-making and will serve as the foundation for future work establishing whether these measures are associated with or predictive of subsequent injury.

titre: Evaluation of Rehabilitation Outcomes Following Therapy With the Luna EMG Diagnostic and Rehabilitation Robot for the Upper Limb and Hand in Individuals in the Chronic Post-Stroke Phase.
titre_fr: Evaluation of Rehabilitation Outcomes Following Therapy With the Luna EMG Diagnostic and Rehabilitation Robot for the Upper Limb and Hand in Individuals in the Chronic Post-Stroke Phase.
auteurs: Leszczak Justyna, Pniak Bogumiła, Drużbicki Mariusz, Poświata Anna, Mikulski Michał, Pisz Anna, Guzik Agnieszka
revue: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
resume: BACKGROUND This study compared a rehabilitation program using Luna EMG biofeedback with conventional physiotherapy in patients in the chronic phase after stroke, focusing on hand motor function, upper limb proprioception, and functional ability. MATERIAL AND METHODS A total of 124 post-stroke patients aged 45-75 years were randomly assigned to a test group (n=63) or control group (n=61). Both groups completed a 3-week rehabilitation program. The control group received conventional physiotherapy, while the test group received Luna EMG biofeedback training for the same total therapy time. Outcomes included upper limb proprioception, Fugl-Meyer Assessment of the Upper Extremity (FMA-UE), Barthel Index, Box and Blocks Test, and Frenchay scale. RESULTS Both groups showed significant post-intervention improvements (P<0.001). Compared with controls, the test group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in upper limb proprioception, FMA-UE scores, manual dexterity, and grip function (all padj<0.001; rrb=0.40-0.89). The between-group difference in Barthel Index scores was not significant after Bonferroni correction (padj=0.138), although the test group showed slightly greater improvement. CONCLUSIONS Adding Luna EMG-based biofeedback to conventional rehabilitation may provide short-term benefits in upper limb proprioception, motor function, manual dexterity, and grip function after stroke. Further studies are needed to determine long-term effects and clinically meaningful changes.

titre: Pulmonary rehabilitation nursing improves outcomes in acute COPD: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Pulmonary rehabilitation nursing improves outcomes in acute COPD: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Liu Meicheng, Huang Yan, Huang Li, Luo Qiuyan
revue: The International journal of artificial organs
resume: To systematically evaluate the effects of nursing-coordinated pulmonary rehabilitation on exercise capacity, pulmonary function, dyspnea, and quality of life in patients with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD). PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Embase, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between December 2003 and December 2024. Eligible studies compared nursing-coordinated pulmonary rehabilitation with routine care. Outcome measures included the 6-min walking distance (6MWD), pulmonary function (FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC), modified Medical Research Council dyspnea scale (mMRC), and COPD Assessment Test (CAT). Eleven RCTs involving 986 AECOPD patients were included. Compared with routine care, pulmonary rehabilitation significantly improved 6MWD (SMD = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.62-1.16, p < 0.05), FEV1/FVC (SMD = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.18-1.06, p < 0.05), mMRC score (SMD = -0.64, p < 0.05), and CAT score (SMD = -0.93, p < 0.05). No significant differences were observed in FEV1 or FVC (p > 0.05). No significant publication bias was detected. Nursing-coordinated pulmonary rehabilitation effectively improves exercise capacity, dyspnea, and quality of life in AECOPD patients, supporting its integration into routine clinical nursing care.

titre: Venous flow dynamics in post-stroke hemiparetic lower extremity motor dysfunctions.
titre_fr: Venous flow dynamics in post-stroke hemiparetic lower extremity motor dysfunctions.
auteurs: Külekçioğlu Sevinç, Guven Hakan
resume: To assess venous flow impairments in post-stroke hemiparetic lower limbs by comparing venous pump capacity (VPC) and venous refilling time (VRT) between affected and unaffected sides, and to examine their associations with motor function, spasticity, and functional independence. Retrospective cross-sectional study. Outpatient Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation and Cardiovascular Surgery clinics at a tertiary care hospital in Türkiye. Participants: Forty-three adults (mean age: 62.6 ± 11.5 years) with hemiparesis persisting ≥ 3 months were included. Patients with hemiplegia, chronic venous disease, peripheral arterial disease, or systemic illness were excluded. Participants were identified via consecutive sampling from existing plethysmographic records. Not applicable. Primary outcomes were VPC and VRT, measured bilaterally using digital photoplethysmography (D-PPG). Secondary measures included Brunnstrom stage, Barthel Index, and Modified Ashworth Scale. titre: Does Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing Change Pulmonary Rehabilitation Decisions in COPD? A Critical Review of Incremental Clinical Utility.
titre_fr: Does Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing Change Pulmonary Rehabilitation Decisions in COPD? A Critical Review of Incremental Clinical Utility.
auteurs: Xu Yongquan, Dong Wenli, Liu Hai, Shang Ningxia, Jia Pengfei
revue: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
resume: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) provides integrated physiological assessment in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and can inform exercise prescription, exertional evaluation, and specialist referral. This critical narrative review examines whether CPET information improves pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) treatment allocation and patient outcomes beyond comprehensive conventional assessment. Targeted PubMed/MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov searches through September 5, 2026 were supplemented by focused revision checks; evidence directness was assessed at the claim level. Physiological measurement and clinically appropriate dose anchoring, diagnostic evaluation, and integrated care retain their established or context-specific rationales. The targeted searches did not identify a randomized COPD information-strategy or test-plus-treatment trial isolating additional PR allocation benefit; this does not establish absence of clinical value. We adapt test-utility methodology into an author-proposed, unvalidated research framework separating interpretation, recorded decisions, delivered actions, and measured outcomes. Four candidate questions identify settings for comparative investigation. Concordant conventional assessment is a comparison scenario, not a validated low-yield boundary or a rule to withhold CPET. An unchanged prescription may provide confirmation or reassurance; a changed prescription without detected benefit requires assessment of delivery, outcome sensitivity, follow-up, and statistical uncertainty. Prospective work should establish operational reproducibility and then compare complete strategies with domain-specific patient outcomes, safety, burden, and access. Clinically appropriate CPET remains part of individualized care, and lack of CPET should not delay indicated PR when assessment supports safe supervised participation. The framework organizes evaluation rather than selecting patients or prescribing treatment.
