titre: Muscle coordination networks during human walking revealed by graphical LASSO analysis at individual and population levels.
titre_fr: Muscle coordination networks during human walking revealed by graphical LASSO analysis at individual and population levels.
auteurs: Acuña Samuel A
resume: Understanding how the nervous system coordinates many muscles simultaneously during walking, and how that coordination breaks down in pathology, is a central challenge in gait biomechanics and rehabilitation. Existing approaches describe what muscles do individually or on average, but cannot reveal which muscles are directly coupled to one another at each moment of the stride. The purpose of this study was to establish the feasibility of graphical LASSO network analysis as a framework for characterizing muscle coordination at two complementary levels: stride-to-stride variation within a single representative participant, and between-subject variation across a healthy young adult population. Surface EMG data were collected from six lower extremity muscles in twenty healthy young adults during treadmill walking at 1.0 m/s. Sparse partial correlation networks were estimated among the six muscles at each of 101 time-normalized gait cycle points at both the individual and population levels of analysis. Networks varied systematically across the gait cycle, recovering expected couplings including plantar flexor pairing during stance and quadriceps pairing during loading response and terminal swing. At the individual level, networks revealed which muscle relationships are stable features of that person's stride pattern and which vary across strides. At the population level, networks revealed which muscle relationships are common features of healthy young adult gait and which reflect individual differences in coordination strategy. Centrality metrics further identified muscles as coordinatively important at time points where their absolute activation was low. The graphical LASSO framework produces muscle coordination networks that are interpretable, biologically coherent, and sensitive to coordination structure at two clinically meaningful scales. By characterizing which muscles are directly couples at each moment of the stride and how that coupling structure evolves across the gait cycle, the approach offers a rich description of the neuromuscular organization of walking and a promising foundation for future clinical assessment of gait coordination.

titre: Telerehabilitation and teleassessment in rare pediatric neurological disorders: an ERN-RND telerehabilitation working group systematic review.
titre_fr: Telerehabilitation and teleassessment in rare pediatric neurological disorders: an ERN-RND telerehabilitation working group systematic review.
auteurs: Maida Elisabetta, Dini Michelangelo, Medijainen Kadri, Kubica Jadwiga, Buizer Annemieke I, Timmann Dagmar, Wolf Nicole I, Bonavita Simona, Federico Antonio, Salamon András, Nonnekes Jorik, Graessner Holm, Vinciguerra Claudia, Ortigoza-Escobar Juan Dario, Leocani Letizia, Lavorgna Luigi
resume: Children and adolescents with rare neurological disorders (RNDs) often require long-term rehabilitation, but specialist access is limited by geography, medical fragility, and travel burden. Telerehabilitation and teleassessment may extend care into the home, yet evidence remains fragmented. We evaluated functional outcomes and summarized feasibility, adherence, acceptability, safety, and teleassessment measurement properties. This PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420251238931) followed PRISMA and SWiM guidance. PubMed, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar were searched through April 20, 2026, supplemented by citation searching. Eligible studies evaluated telerehabilitation or teleassessment in participants aged ≤18 years with Orphanet-classified RNDs and reported child-level functional outcomes. Mixed cohorts required separable data or ≥80% eligible participants. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias and certainty of evidence using design-appropriate tools. 2,260 unique records were screened and 71 full texts assessed; 16 studies were included. 13 evaluated telerehabilitation (316 participants: 203 intervention, 113 comparator/control) and 3 evaluated teleassessment (94 participants). Most studies involved neuromuscular disorders, mainly Duchenne or Becker muscular dystrophy; other conditions included Rett syndrome, Fragile X syndrome, Dravet syndrome, Canavan disease, Guillain-Barré syndrome, and rare pediatric ataxias. Technologies included videoconferencing, apps, wearable sensors, and video-based assessment. Telerehabilitation was associated with improvement or stabilization in selected motor, respiratory, cognitive, communication, and daily functional outcomes, whereas global measures often showed limited short-term change. Feasibility, adherence, and acceptability were generally favorable. No major telerehabilitation-related safety concerns were reported when assessed. Teleassessment showed good reliability or agreement with in-person motor assessment. In selected pediatric RNDs, telerehabilitation and teleassessment demonstrate strong feasibility, high acceptability, and meaningful clinical potential as effective complements to in-person care. These approaches offer valuable opportunities to expand access, enhance continuity of care, and support patient-centered rehabilitation. Larger multicenter studies should evaluate long-term outcomes and equitable implementation.

titre: Force and Power Testing in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Literature: A Scoping Review.
titre_fr: Force and Power Testing in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Literature: A Scoping Review.
auteurs: Compagnin Alessandro, Della Villa Francesco, Di Paolo Stefano, Hamrin Senorski Eric, Olivari Giorgio, Read Paul, Patterson Stephen, La Rosa Giovanni, Scavone Alberto, Buckthorpe Matthew
resume: Force and power testing has been recognised as a key aspect of anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) rehabilitation. However, a literature synthesis is required to examine how these physical characteristics have been assessed due to pronounced heterogeneity in the methods used. To synthesise and describe the existing literature on force and power testing post-ACLR. A scoping review of the electronic databases MEDLINE (PubMed), SPORTDiscus, Cochrane Library and PEDro was conducted including studies adopting at least one force or power test in patients post-ACLR. The search methodology followed the Joanna Briggs Institute Manual for evidence synthesis and included the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). In total, 1625 studies fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Seven main device categories were identified, with different rates of implementation over the years (1981-2023) and throughout the recovery process: (1) isokinetic dynamometry (IKD; 64.9%), (2) jump (without force platform; 32.2%), (3) force platform (28.0%), (4) traditional gym equipment and bodyweight exercises (6.2%), (5) hand-held dynamometry (4.0%), (6) manual muscle testing (1.5%) and (7) other devices (5.5%). Studies used 1.42 ± 0.62 devices, with 45 different combinations recorded. Various tests were conducted using different devices, ranging from 8 to 72 recorded tests per category. Only force plate assessments showed a linear increment in implementation from the surgical procedure (r = 0.86, p = 0.012). Significant heterogeneity in assessment device selection, metrics analysed, test implementation and protocols was observed. Most studies included a single device category to examine force and power characteristics of patients post-ACLR. The IKD remains the most adopted testing device in research, but current assessment practices are more varied than in the past.

titre: Orthotopic Neobladder after Radical Cystectomy: Contemporary Patient Selection, Outcomes and Survivorship.
titre_fr: Orthotopic Neobladder after Radical Cystectomy: Contemporary Patient Selection, Outcomes and Survivorship.
auteurs: Imperatore Vittorio, Coppola Paola, Sciorio Carmine, Di Girolamo Antonio, Romeo Giuseppe, Giannella Riccardo, Romano Lorenzo, Ruffo Antonio, Napolitano Luigi, Stanzione Francesco, Esposito Fabio, Spirito Lorenzo
resume: Orthotopic neobladder should be actively discussed after radical cystectomy, but it should not be framed as the routine default. The best candidates are patients in whom urethral preservation is oncologically appropriate, renal and hepatic function are adequate, cognition and manual dexterity are intact, and the patient accepts rehabilitation, nocturnal leakage risk, and the possibility of clean intermittent catheterization. Age alone should not exclude patients; frailty, limited life expectancy, major neurocognitive disease, severe baseline incontinence, and unreliable follow-up weigh more strongly in favor of an ileal conduit. Prior high-dose pelvic radiation and marginal self-management capacity call for individualized assessment rather than routine exclusion. Bowel considerations are also nuanced: severe intestinal disease or markedly limited bowel reserve may preclude bowel-based reconstruction, whereas lesser bowel concerns should be judged case by case. We do not regard orthotopic neobladder as oncologically superior to ileal conduit. Its value lies in preserving body image and urethral voiding in carefully selected patients. Counseling therefore needs to be explicit about the trade-offs-slower functional recovery, nocturnal leakage, retention, catheterization burden, and lifelong metabolic, renal, and oncologic surveillance. In women, bladder neck and urethral assessment are decisive, and pelvic organ-preserving strategies should be considered only when cancer control is not compromised. In older adults, diversion choice should follow physiologic reserve and goals of care rather than chronology alone. Overall, orthotopic neobladder remains a valuable option for motivated, well-selected patients treated in centers that can deliver reproducible reconstruction and deliberate long-term follow-up; ileal conduit remains preferable when simplicity, safety, or self-management limitations dominate the decision.

titre: Determining the Scalability Readiness of a Transitional Care Stroke Intervention for Older Adults With Multimorbidity: A Mixed Methods Study.
titre_fr: Determining the Scalability Readiness of a Transitional Care Stroke Intervention for Older Adults With Multimorbidity: A Mixed Methods Study.
auteurs: Northwood Melissa, Chambers Tracey, Ganann Rebecca, Bharatselvam Sharvika, Juneau Maxine, Markle-Reid Maureen
resume: Following a stroke, the transition from inpatient care to home is a vulnerable period for older adults with multimorbidity and their care partners. The Transitional Care Stroke Intervention (TCSI) is a patient-oriented intervention, shown to be effective in improving physical functioning, stroke self-management, and patient experience through a pragmatic randomized controlled trial. The objective of this study was to assess the scalability readiness of the TCSI in selected community stroke rehabilitation programs in Ontario, Canada. A convergent mixed methods design was used, guided by the Implementation Scalability Assessment Tool. Three diverse community stroke rehabilitation programs participated, including people with lived experience. Data were collected from relevant documents, meetings with working group participants in each setting, and interviews with key informants. Participants noted that the TCSI had many benefits for persons with stroke and their care partners, including the provision of system navigation and care coordination. Key considerations for scale up included interprofessional team development, local contextual adaptations, optimizing virtual care, provincial standardization for ongoing program quality monitoring, a digital health solution, and designated care coordinator roles. Supporting transitions in care for persons with stroke and their care partners continues to be a pressing issue in Ontario and in many other jurisdictions. Implementation of the TCSI has the potential to improve outcomes and foster integrated health and social care delivery for older adults with stroke and multimorbidity. This study improves our understanding of implementation considerations to inform future scale up of the TCSI.

titre: Impact of early severity of finger paresis on upper limb motor recovery and functional outcomes in people after stroke: a retrospective cohort study.
titre_fr: Impact of early severity of finger paresis on upper limb motor recovery and functional outcomes in people after stroke: a retrospective cohort study.
auteurs: Uehara Shintaro, Nagasaka Kasumi, Matsuura Daisuke, Maeda Hirofumi, Otaka Yohei
resume: Upper-limb hemiparesis is a frequent, disabling post-stroke complication. While initial severity is a dominant predictor of long-term recovery, performing complex motor assessments is often challenging during the unstable, very acute phase. To evaluate the association between very acute hand-finger paresis severity and subsequent subacute outcomes across multiple domains: motor impairment, motor capacity, and activities of daily living (ADL). This retrospective cohort study included post-stroke individuals (N = 473) receiving continuous rehabilitation from acute to subacute phases between 2019 and 2021. Initial hand-finger motor paresis severity was assessed using the Stroke Impairment Assessment Set Finger-Function (SIAS-FF). Outcomes at hospital discharge were evaluated using SIAS-FF, SIAS Knee-Mouth (SIAS-KM) test for proximal function, the Simple Test for Evaluating Hand Function (STEF) for motor capacity, and Functional Independence Measure (FIM) selfcare items for ADL. Multivariable regression models (ordinal logistic regression and generalized linear models) adjusting for age and length of hospital stay were implemented to test associations between the acute hand-finger paresis severity and subacute outcomes. Analyses included 356 participants (mean age, 66.7 years). Acute finger paresis severity (assessed at 1.7 days post-stroke) was associated with subacute outcomes (at 86.9 days) in multivariable regression models (p < 0.01). Participants with better SIAS-FF scores in the acute phase achieved better discharge outcomes across all measures, including SIAS-FF, SIAS-KM, STEF, and FIM selfcare scores, even after controlling for age and length of hospital stay. Severity of hand-finger paresis in the very acute phase is significantly associated with global upper-limb recovery. The SIAS-FF is a simple clinical tool that provides useful information for estimating post-stroke functional outcomes.

titre: Integrated rehabilitation for post-stroke anxiety: a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Integrated rehabilitation for post-stroke anxiety: a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Xu Shenglu, Ye Keqin, Zhang Shiyu, Chen Kaili, Zhou Jie, Hu Xiaohua, Li Liping, Zhang Zaifu, Gao Hong
resume: Post-stroke anxiety (PSA) affects approximately one-quarter of stroke survivors and impedes functional recovery, yet pharmacological options remain limited by inconsistent efficacy and absent standardized guidelines. This study evaluated an integrated rehabilitation program combining repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), acupuncture, and Chinese herbal medicine for PSA. In this multicenter randomized controlled trial, 188 participants with mild-to-moderate PSA were randomized 1:1 to standard care (pharmacotherapy, general care, and exercise therapy) or integrated rehabilitation (standard care plus rTMS, acupuncture, and Chinese herbal medicine) for 4 weeks, with an 8-week follow-up. The primary outcome was the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A). Secondary outcomes included the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), Activities of Daily Living (ADL), Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA), and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Analyses followed an intention-to-treat framework. The integrated rehabilitation group showed significantly greater reductions in HAM-A scores at Week 4 than controls (between-group difference, 2.49 points; 95% CI, 1.50 to 3.48; p <0.01), and this treatment benefit was maintained at week 12 (p<0.01). In supportive analyses of the secondary outcomes, Holm-adjusted group × time interactions remained significant for PSQI, MoCA, upper-extremity motor function, ADL, and SAS scores (all adjusted p<0.05), but not for lower-extremity motor function or IADL. The integrated rehabilitation program improved the primary anxiety outcome and provided supportive evidence of broader clinical benefits in sleep quality, cognition, and upper-extremity motor function, together with distinct patterns of functional change in ADL and IADL. Overall, these findings support further consideration of this integrated approach as an adjunct to pharmacotherapy for PSA. Biological mechanisms and contributions of individual intervention components remain undetermined. Further mechanistic investigations incorporating biological measures would help clarify the underlying mechanisms. https://clinicaltrials.gov/, identifier NCT05147077.

The integrated rehabilitation group showed significantly greater reductions in HAM-A scores at Week 4 than controls (between-group difference, 2.49 points; 95% CI, 1.50 to 3.48; p <0.01), and this treatment benefit was maintained at week 12 (p<0.01). In supportive analyses of the secondary outcomes, Holm-adjusted group × time interactions remained significant for PSQI, MoCA, upper-extremity motor function, ADL, and SAS scores (all adjusted p<0.05), but not for lower-extremity motor function or IADL. The integrated rehabilitation program improved the primary anxiety outcome and provided supportive evidence of broader clinical benefits in sleep quality, cognition, and upper-extremity motor function, together with distinct patterns of functional change in ADL and IADL. Overall, these findings support further consideration of this integrated approach as an adjunct to pharmacotherapy for PSA. Biological mechanisms and contributions of individual intervention components remain undetermined. Further mechanistic investigations incorporating biological measures would help clarify the underlying mechanisms. https://clinicaltrials.gov/, identifier NCT05147077.

titre: Making sense of chronic low back pain in later life: illness representations and coping among older adults in Ghana.
titre_fr: Making sense of chronic low back pain in later life: illness representations and coping among older adults in Ghana.
auteurs: Eliason Cecilia, Kponton Beauty Yayra, Avadu Patricia, Attafuah Priscilla Yeye Adumoah
resume: Chronic low back pain (CLBP) is one of the most common musculoskeletal conditions affecting older adults and a leading cause of disability worldwide. Beyond physical discomfort, CLBP has profound physical, psychological, social and economic consequences. Although previous studies have documented the burden of CLBP, limited evidence exists on how older adults in sub-Saharan Africa make sense of their condition and regulate their responses to it. Guided by the Common-Sense Model of Self-Regulation (CSM), this study explored the illness representations, emotional responses and coping strategies of older adults living with CLBP in Ghana. An interpretive qualitative design was employed. Sixteen older adults aged 60 years and above with chronic low back pain were purposively recruited from Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital. Data were collected through semi-structured, face-to-face interviews. The interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The CSM informed both data interpretation and the organisation of findings by examining participants' illness beliefs, perceived consequences, emotional representations and coping responses. Five interconnected themes emerged. (1) Constructing the Meaning of Chronic Low Back Pain captured participants' attempts to explain the causes of their condition. (2) When Pain Redefines Everyday Life illustrated how persistent pain disrupted mobility, independence, occupational roles, etc. resulting in diminished quality of life. (3) Emotional Responses to Living with Persistent Pain highlighted feelings of fear, sadness, frustration, anxiety and threatened identity. (4) Negotiating Control Over Chronic Low Back Pain described participants' efforts to regain control through medications, healthcare utilisation, activity modification, self-management strategies and reliance on family support. Finally, (5) Faith as the Anchor of Adaptation demonstrated that spirituality was central to participants' coping. Among our participants, CLBP was described in relation to illness beliefs, emotional distress, functional limitations, social participation and spiritual coping. These accounts suggest areas for person-centred assessment in this hospital-based sample. The potential value of integrating education, rehabilitation, psychosocial support and patient-preferred spiritual support warrants further evaluation; this study did not assess their effectiveness.

titre: Diagnostic pathways and unmet healthcare needs in rare diseases: a Romanian survey.
titre_fr: Diagnostic pathways and unmet healthcare needs in rare diseases: a Romanian survey.
auteurs: Dan Alexandra, Mocuțiu Ramona, Criste Cristina, Demjen Zelike, Damsa Larisa, Severin Emilia, Dan Dorica
resume: Rare disease policy in Europe increasingly emphasises not only timely diagnosis but also the integration of specialist expertise into sustainable national care pathways. We analysed a cross-sectional, network-based online survey conducted in Romania within the ECOU project to describe diagnostic trajectories and principal unmet care needs and to consider their relevance within the evolving European rare disease landscape. Of 799 exported records, 768 met the inclusion criteria and were analysed. The individuals represented included 291 children and 473 adults, with age category missing for four individuals. Amongst 763 responses concerning the diagnostic interval, 47.1% reported diagnosis within 6 months of the first medical consultation, while 32.9% reported intervals of at least 1 year. Two to three physicians were consulted most frequently (39.1%). Amongst 729 responses concerning principal unmet healthcare needs, rehabilitation (22.6%), access to available treatment (21.7%), expert-centre follow-up (14.7%) and psychological counselling (11.1%) were most frequently reported. These findings identify unmet needs extending beyond diagnostic assessment, particularly in rehabilitation, treatment access, expert-centre follow-up and psychological support. They highlight priorities for strengthening links between specialist rare disease services and local health and social care in Romania.

titre: Characteristics of interventions using barefoot and minimalist footwear in older adults: a scoping review protocol.
titre_fr: Characteristics of interventions using barefoot and minimalist footwear in older adults: a scoping review protocol.
auteurs: Oliveira Tiago, Fernandes Hugo, Galego Mariana, Kiszio Blanche, Ribeiro Catarina, Barbosa Pedro, Salgado Ricardo
revue: International journal of nursing studies advances
resume: Aging is associated with progressive neuromuscular decline and sarcopenia, increasing the risk of mortality. These changes may result in structural foot deformities and severely compromised stability, thereby increasing the risk of falls. Therefore, assessment of the foot and footwear interface is a fundamental component of multifactorial falls prevention strategies. Conventional cushioned footwear acts as a sensory barrier, attenuating feedback required for balance. Furthermore, barefoot and minimalist footwear may optimize sensorimotor function and biomechanics by allowing natural contact between skin and surface. Despite this potential, existing evidence regarding these interventions remains dispersed. To map the characteristics of interventions using barefoot and minimalist footwear in older adults. PubMed, CINAHL Ultimate (EBSCOhost), Embase (Elsevier), Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane Library, Scopus, JBI EBP Database (Ovid), PEDro and Epistemonikos. Gray literature such as master's and doctoral theses will be searched through ProQuest Dissertations and Theses and Google Scholar. The review will follow JBI methodology for scoping reviews. Two independent reviewers will screen and extract data, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Results will be presented in a tabular format, accompanied by a narrative synthesis, highlighting the characteristics of the interventions. www.osf.io 10.17605/OSF.IO/6QDEJ, registered 28/01/2026.

titre: Rehabilitating Sexual Offenders in Nigerian Correctional Institutions: A Multidisciplinary Evaluation of Current Practices and Pathways for Reform.
titre_fr: Rehabilitating Sexual Offenders in Nigerian Correctional Institutions: A Multidisciplinary Evaluation of Current Practices and Pathways for Reform.
auteurs: Aborisade Richard A, Adeleke Oladele Adelere, Osinibi Olusegun, Akindele-Oscar Yomi, Oladejo Segilola Y, Bawalla Oluwatoyin Gbenga, Babatunde Stephen, Ogunyemi John Ajibola
revue: International journal of offender therapy and comparative criminology
resume: Despite global advances in evidence-based responses to sexual offending, little is known about how individuals convicted of sexual offences are assessed and treated in Nigerian correctional institutions. This study addresses this gap through a multidisciplinary qualitative inquiry conducted across six states in South-West Nigeria, drawing on interviews with incarcerated individuals, correctional staff, health professionals, NGO practitioners and legal officers. Drawing on the Risk-Need-Responsivity model, the Good Lives Model and Cognitive-Behavioural Therapy, the analysis reveals fragmented and non-standardised assessment practices, limited psychological screening at intake and reliance on informal judgement. Rehabilitation is largely generic, focused on vocational and educational programmes, while offence-specific psychological treatment remains marginal. Structural constraints, weak inter-agency coordination, limited NGO collaboration and the absence of integrated reintegration planning result in minimal continuity of post-release programmes. The findings highlight systemic governance and policy gaps, underscoring the need for legally grounded, context-sensitive, evidence-based reforms to strengthen rehabilitation and public safety.

titre: Managing environmental enteropathy among Egyptian infants and children with growth faltering.
titre_fr: Managing environmental enteropathy among Egyptian infants and children with growth faltering.
auteurs: Nassar May Fouad, Emam Ehab Khairy, Allam Mohamed Farouk, Hamdy Ahmed Mohamed, Abdelhaleem Bassma Abdelnasser, Radwan Nehal Ahmed, Emam Abeer Mohamed, Ibrahim Haya Essam
resume: Environmental enteropathy (EE) is an acquired subclinical inflammation of the small bowel mucosa, leading to reduced nutrient absorption and increased intestinal permeability. There are currently no universally accepted protocols for the diagnosis and treatment of EE. The primary aim of this clinical trial was to assess the prevalence of EE among children with faltering growth (FG). Determination of the dietary requirements in pediatric FG with EE and highlighting the histopathologic changes in the small intestine in such conditions were the secondary objectives. The current study recruited 200 patients (their age range was 6-58 months) diagnosed as GF at the Pediatric Clinical Nutrition Clinic, Children`s Hospital, Faculty of Medicine, Ain Shams University (Cairo, Egypt), during the period from April 2022 till June 2023. The first phase of the study was a cross sectional interventional one where all patients underwent nutritional rehabilitation using diet regimen including polymeric milk formula. Patients whose weight z score was still below - 2 SD for age and sex after 12 weeks were considered as non-responders and were enrolled in the second phase, when esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) and mucosal biopsies were done. In the latter phase, patients with EE received nutritional rehabilitation regimen using peptide-based milk formula with assessment of anthropometric measurements after 8 weeks of follow up. Out of the studied cases, 170 were responders, and 30 were non-responders, 24 of the non-responders underwent EGD with biopsies and all were diagnosed as EE with prevalence of 12% among the studied patients with GF as the least possible prevalence. Total histology scores of the EE fell between those of the controls and celiac disease reference samples with cut off values > 3 and ≤ 14 for EE, ≤ 3 for controls and > 14 for celiac disease. There was a significant increase in weight and height z scores among patients of EE on peptide-based formula compared to polymeric formula. EE isn`t uncommon and should be suspected when provision of catch-up nutrients can`t correct FG. Peptide-based formula has a possible beneficial effect on growth of patients with EE. The clinical trial was registered at Protocol Registration and Results System with number NCT06497907 (12/07/2024).

titre: Rehabilitation Strategies for Upper Limb Function After Breast Cancer Treatment, with and Without Lymphedema: The Potential of Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation - A Systematic Review.
titre_fr: Rehabilitation Strategies for Upper Limb Function After Breast Cancer Treatment, with and Without Lymphedema: The Potential of Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation - A Systematic Review.
auteurs: Pezzi Letizia, Mastroberardino Ilaria, Cichelli Alice, Di Matteo Andrea, Pizzi Stefano Delli, Paolucci Teresa
resume: Upper limb dysfunction (pain, reduced shoulder mobility and strength, activity limitation) is common after breast cancer treatment, with or without breast cancer-related lymphedema (BCRL). Proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) has been proposed to improve upper limb function and range of motion (ROM). This systematic review evaluates PNF for upper limb dysfunction in women treated for breast cancer, analyzing women with and without BCRL separately. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement was followed. Four databases were searched without date restrictions. Randomized or quasi-randomized English-language trials of PNF-containing interventions in women treated for breast cancer were included. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool and certainty of evidence with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Six trials (366 women) were included: three enrolled women with confirmed BCRL and three women without BCRL. PNF was mostly part of multimodal programs, but the between-group contrast isolated PNF in four trials. In BCRL trials, limb volume decreased in all groups, with no consistent advantage of PNF over active comparators. In women without BCRL, single trials reported improvements in ROM, strength and function. Risk of bias was low in one trial, high in one and of some concern in four; certainty of evidence was low or very low. PNF may be a promising component of multimodal rehabilitation for upper limb dysfunction after breast cancer treatment; its independent effectiveness and its effects on BCRL remain unproven, and in women with BCRL it should complement, not replace, decongestive treatment. Trials in women with confirmed BCRL and standardized PNF protocols are needed. PROSPERO CRD42025641774, registered on 2 February 2025 (retrospectively registered).

titre: Can active bone conduction implant processors of two different systems be interchanged? A technical and clinical feasibility study.
titre_fr: Can active bone conduction implant processors of two different systems be interchanged? A technical and clinical feasibility study.
auteurs: Rahne Torsten, Brüning Dawid, Fröhlich Laura, Dziemba Oliver
resume: Active transcutaneous bone conduction implant systems are designed as closed hardware systems in which external audio processors operate exclusively with their corresponding implanted transducers. However, the electro-mechanical compatibility of components from different manufacturers has not previously been investigated. This study evaluated the technical feasibility, output performance, and preliminary clinical applicability of cross-system processor-implant combinations using the Bonebridge (MED-EL) and Sentio (Oticon Medical) systems. A Bonebridge BCI 602 and a Sentio Ti implant were coupled to a skull simulator and implant phantoms. Native and non-native combinations of the Samba 2 BB and Sentio 1 Mini audio processors were evaluated under standardized reference test settings. Force output characteristics were measured using frequency response and maximum output recordings. In addition, two implanted patients underwent acute experimental fitting with the alternative processor system. Audiological assessment included aided sound-field thresholds, speech recognition in quiet and noise, categorical loudness scaling, and the Speech, Spatial and Qualities of Hearing Scale (SSQ12). Cross-system activation was technically possible in all investigated processor-implant combinations. Skull simulator measurements demonstrated substantial differences in output force levels between native and non-native pairings, with 4PTA force-output differences of up to 21.6 dB, although feedback-related interference affected measurements at high input levels. Phantom measurements confirmed audibility for all combinations. In both clinical assessments, successful fitting and open-set speech understanding were achieved with the non-native processor configuration. Speech recognition performance, aided thresholds, and subjective hearing outcomes were generally comparable between native and non-native configurations, with both participants reporting a preference for the Sentio 1 Mini processor in at least some outcome measures. The tested audio processors were technically capable of activating non-native implants, and short-term speech perception was possible in two supervised clinical assessments. Nevertheless, substantial differences in output characteristics indicate system-specific electro-mechanical optimization. However, differences in output characteristics and the lack of systematic electrical, thermal, and long-term safety evaluations mean that clinical interchangeability cannot be recommended. Further technical and clinical evaluation is required before cross-system use can be considered.

titre: Eating behavior patterns and cardiometabolic risk in adults with obesity across care settings.
titre_fr: Eating behavior patterns and cardiometabolic risk in adults with obesity across care settings.
auteurs: Mazzola Giuseppe, Manzalini Sonia, Perna Simone, Rondanelli Mariangela
revue: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
resume: Assessment of altered eating behaviors may support personalized obesity care at the interface of nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular risk. This study compared Eating Behaviors Assessment for Obesity (EBA-O) profiles across inpatient metabolic rehabilitation and outpatient endocrinology care, and explored their cardiometabolic correlates. We assessed 115 adults with obesity (81 outpatients, 34 inpatients). EBA-O scores were analyzed as continuous variables and dichotomized at the clinical threshold of 4 or higher. Mean total scores did not differ significantly between inpatients and outpatients (3.85 ± 1.31 vs. 3.68 ± 0.99; Welch p = 0.500), nor did the proportion above the total-score threshold (55.9% vs. 37.0%; p = 0.068). Only binge eating differed by setting (55.9% vs. 27.2%; p = 0.005), the sole unadjusted comparison surviving Bonferroni correction. In age-, sex-, and BMI-adjusted models, inpatient status was associated with night eating (OR 7.14, 95% CI 1.99-25.61; p = 0.003) and binge eating (OR 2.80, 95% CI 1.02-7.69; p = 0.046). In inpatient women, EBA-O correlated with BMI, waist circumference, triglycerides, and LDL cholesterol; in outpatient women, it correlated with insulin and HOMA-IR. All subgroup analyses were exploratory and uncorrected for multiplicity. Altered eating behaviors were frequent across care settings, and the overall EBA-O burden was similar. In unadjusted analyses, the between-setting difference was confined to binge eating. Exploratory sex-stratified analyses suggested associations with adiposity, lipids, and insulin resistance; these hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation before EBA-O can be proposed for cardiometabolic risk stratification.

titre: Prevalence, progression and factors associated with contralateral rotator cuff tears in patients treated for unilateral symptomatic non-traumatic rotator cuff tears: A scoping review.
titre_fr: Prevalence, progression and factors associated with contralateral rotator cuff tears in patients treated for unilateral symptomatic non-traumatic rotator cuff tears: A scoping review.
auteurs: Littlewood Chris, Moffatt Maria, Winter Ashlie, Lalande Tacey, Rees Jonathan, Smith Toby
revue: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
resume: Rotator cuff tears are common in people with shoulder pain and disability. Although management typically targets the symptomatic shoulder, people with unilateral non-traumatic rotator cuff tears may be at increased risk of contralateral pathology. However, the prevalence, progression, and factors associated with contralateral tears remain poorly understood. To identify and synthesise published evidence on the prevalence, progression, and factors associated with contralateral rotator cuff tears to inform future surveillance, prevention, and management strategies. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute framework and reported following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. MEDLINE, AMED, Embase, CINAHL, and PsycINFO were searched from inception to 20 January 2026. Studies involving adults with unilateral symptomatic non-traumatic rotator cuff tears were included. Data were summarised descriptively. Fourteen heterogeneous reports from 12 studies (2001-2024) were included; 54% were based on surgical populations. Prevalence of contralateral rotator cuff tears ranged from 8.7% to 67.3%. Contralateral tear enlargement was reported in 39% to 67% of shoulders during follow- up to 13.1 years, while 26% to 57% of patients developed contralateral shoulder pain. Median time to tear enlargement ranged from 2.8 to 3.4 years; time to symptom onset ranged from 15.2 months to 3.0 years. Limited data suggests larger baseline contralateral tear size was associated with subsequent pain development (p≤0.001). Tear enlargement during follow-up was not consistently associated with symptom development. Factors associated with the presence of contralateral rotator cuff tears at baseline included older age (OR 1.1, 95% CI 1.05-1.18), increased BMI (26.1 vs 24.7 kg/m<sup>2</sup>, p<0.05), diabetes (23.1% vs 8.1%, p<0.03), and heavy repetitive work (31.8% vs 14.4%, p<0.05). Factors associated with progression included full-thickness contralateral tears (HR 2.93, 95% CI 1.71-5.03), dominant-side involvement of the contralateral shoulder (HR 1.70, 95% CI 1.2-2.4), and fatty muscle degeneration within the contralateral shoulder (OR 2.6, 95% CI 1.3-5.4). Contralateral rotator cuff tears are common and frequently progressive in patients with unilateral symptomatic tears, signalling a possible bilateral and multifactorial disease model rather than an isolated shoulder disorder. Research is needed to develop and evaluate clinically and cost-effective assessment and management strategies that extend beyond the affected shoulder and include optimisation of modifiable risk factors and consideration of bilateral rehabilitation approaches. resume_fr: Rotator cuff tears are common in people with shoulder pain and disability. Although management typically targets the symptomatic shoulder, people with unilateral non-traumatic rotator cuff tears may be at increased risk of contralateral pathology. However, the prevalence, progression, and factors associated with contralateral tears remain poorly understood. To identify and synthesise published evidence on the prevalence, progression, and factors associated with contralateral rotator cuff tears to inform future surveillance, prevention, and management strategies. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute framework and reported following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. MEDLINE, AMED, Embase, CINAHL, and PsycINFO were searched from inception to 20 January 2026. Studies involving adults with unilateral symptomatic non-traumatic rotator cuff tears were included. Data were summarised descriptively. Fourteen heterogeneous reports from 12 studies (2001-2024) were included; 54% were based on surgical populations. Prevalence of contralateral rotator cuff tears ranged from 8.7% to 67.3%. Contralateral tear enlargement was reported in 39% to 67% of shoulders during follow- up to 13.1 years, while 26% to 57% of patients developed contralateral shoulder pain. Median time to tear enlargement ranged from 2.8 to 3.4 years; time to symptom onset ranged from 15.2 months to 3.0 years. Limited data suggests larger baseline contralateral tear size was associated with subsequent pain development (p≤0.001). Tear enlargement during follow-up was not consistently associated with symptom development. Factors associated with the presence of contralateral rotator cuff tears at baseline included older age (OR 1.1, 95% CI 1.05-1.18), increased BMI (26.1 vs 24.7 kg/m<sup>2</sup>, p<0.05), diabetes (23.1% vs 8.1%, p<0.03), and heavy repetitive work (31.8% vs 14.4%, p<0.05). Factors associated with progression included full-thickness contralateral tears (HR 2.93, 95% CI 1.71-5.03), dominant-side involvement of the contralateral shoulder (HR 1.70, 95% CI 1.2-2.4), and fatty muscle degeneration within the contralateral shoulder (OR 2.6, 95% CI 1.3-5.4). Contralateral rotator cuff tears are common and frequently progressive in patients with unilateral symptomatic tears, signalling a possible bilateral and multifactorial disease model rather than an isolated shoulder disorder. Research is needed to develop and evaluate clinically and cost-effective assessment and management strategies that extend beyond the affected shoulder and include optimisation of modifiable risk factors and consideration of bilateral rehabilitation approaches. Level IV; Scoping Review.

titre: AI-Based Rehabilitation System for Congenital Muscular Torticollis: Formative Usability Evaluation.
titre_fr: AI-Based Rehabilitation System for Congenital Muscular Torticollis: Formative Usability Evaluation.
auteurs: Hong Seojin, Nam Heewon, Jeong Seongwoo, Choi Hyun, Kweon Hyosun
resume: Home-based exercise programs for congenital muscular torticollis (CMT) depend heavily on caregivers, yet adherence is often hindered by cognitive and emotional burdens. This study conducted a formative usability evaluation of an AI-based CMT rehabilitation system comprising a clinician web interface and a caregiver mobile app to identify usability-related issues and preliminary design requirements during early development. A formative usability evaluation was conducted with 8 clinical experts (rehabilitation physicians, nurses, and physical therapists). Participants engaged in focus group interviews (FGIs) following a demonstration of the system and completed the System Usability Scale (SUS) for the overall system, including a proxy evaluation of the caregiver mobile app. Qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis, and SUS scores were analyzed descriptively as a supplementary quantitative measure of perceived usability. The thematic analysis identified 2 core themes, "Usability Barriers of the CMT Rehabilitation System" and "Improvement Requirements," encompassing 10 subthemes and 21 concepts. Key findings highlighted concerns regarding the reliability and interpretability of AI-generated feedback and the need to simplify data visualization to reduce the potential cognitive burden on caregivers. The mean SUS score for the overall system was 73.44 (SD 18.01). This result was interpreted descriptively and considered supplementary to the qualitative findings. The formative evaluation identified preliminary usability strengths and areas for improvement from clinicians' perspectives, with particular concerns regarding the reliability and interpretability of AI-generated feedback. The experts emphasized that the AI-based CMT rehabilitation system should function as a therapeutic bridge between clinicians and caregivers. As actual caregivers were not included in this evaluation, the findings represent preliminary formative design inputs based on clinicians' proxy perspectives rather than evidence of usability for caregivers. Future iterations should incorporate the identified improvements and undergo evaluation with actual caregivers in home environments, along with separate technical verification of the accuracy of the AI feedback algorithm.

titre: Predictors of nurses' management of sexual health counseling after percutaneous coronary intervention: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
titre_fr: Predictors of nurses' management of sexual health counseling after percutaneous coronary intervention: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
auteurs: Oeychanai Arthit, Panruy Khemmarat, Injun Nipa, Funilkul Kriengsak
revue: International journal of nursing studies advances
resume: Sexual health counseling is a critical yet under-addressed component of cardiac rehabilitation following post-percutaneous coronary intervention. Although nurses' positive attitudes-particularly regarding role responsibility and comfort with sexual health discussions-and their readiness to provide clinical sexual counseling can facilitate patient care, translating professional knowledge into practice is often hindered by specific constraints and complex sociocultural norms. To use multiple regression analysis to identify individual and hospital ward-specific factors predicting cardiovascular nurses' sexual health care management among post-percutaneous coronary intervention patients, evaluating the incremental influences of nurses' readiness and clinical experience across departmental settings, sexual attitudes, sexual knowledge, problem-solving solutions, facilitators, and barriers. A cross-sectional, explanatory correlational study. Four tertiary-level percutaneous coronary intervention centers within the Bangkok metropolitan administration network, Bangkok, Thailand. A total of 118 cardiovascular registered nurses recruited through combined purposive and random sampling. Data were collected using validated, self-administered questionnaires. The binary sexual knowledge scale demonstrated a Kuder-Richardson Formula 20 internal consistency reliability coefficient of 0.82. The Likert-type scales exhibited Cronbach's alpha coefficients ranging between 0.89 and 0.99. Content validity indices ranged from 0.90 to 0.98. Pearson's correlation coefficients were first calculated to examine bivariate relationships, followed by a three-step hierarchical multiple regression analysis to evaluate the incremental variance. The mean participants' sexual management score was 35.22±14.88 out of a possible 60 points. In the final hierarchical regression model, the combined predictors accounted for 21.6% of the total variance coefficient of determination (R2) = 0.216, adjusted coefficient of determination (Adjusted R²) = .143, F-statistic (F) (10,107) = 2.945, p = .003). Positive sexual attitude (β = .217, p = .019) and readiness (β = .198, p = .030) emerged as statistically-significant positive predictors. Conversely, advanced sexual knowledge maintained a statistically-significant, counterintuitive negative association (β = -.274, p = .003). Ward-specific analysis revealed that assignment to the outpatient department (β = -.226, p = .020) and the cardiac catheterization laboratory (β = -.234, p = .025) negatively predicted sexual health care management practices. Experience, sexuality education, problem-solving solutions, facilitators, and barriers were not statistically-significant. Participants' sexual management was driven by attitudes and readiness yet constrained by ward environments. Poor sexual health counseling management practices in the outpatient department and cardiac catheterization laboratory, alongside knowledge's negative impact, highlighted a "theory-practice gap." To optimize post-percutaneous coronary intervention rehabilitation in Thailand, policies should consider shifting from traditional education toward modifying workflows, establishing private counseling spaces, and developing nurse-led transitional care protocols. Not registered. (Ethical approval was prospectively obtained from the Bangkok metropolitan administration human research ethics committee [approval number COA N002hh/68_EXP] and the faculty of medicine, Vajira hospital [approval number COA 013/2568] prior to data collection).

titre: HVLT-R process variables in neuro-oncology: relationship with measures of executive functioning and utility in clinical and research settings.
titre_fr: HVLT-R process variables in neuro-oncology: relationship with measures of executive functioning and utility in clinical and research settings.
auteurs: Aslanzadeh Farah, Zarrella Giuliana V, Gross Hana, Deo Natasha, Fox Amber, Dietrich Jorg, Loughan Ashlee R, Parsons Michael, Braun Sarah
revue: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
resume: Executive functioning (EF) is frequently impaired in people with brain tumors (PwBT) and may be reflected in neuropsychological "process variables" (e.g., semantic clustering) derived from verbal memory tasks. Although prior studies have linked these variables to memory performance, their construct validity and convergence with established EF measures remain unclear. This study aimed to: (1) replicate prior findings linking Hopkins Verbal Learning Test-Revised (HVLT-R) process variables with memory performance; (2) compare process variables between PwBT and healthy controls (HCs); (3) evaluate construct validity by examining associations with standardized EF measures; and (4) explore relationships with tumor location. PwBT (N = 127; M<sub>age</sub> = 56.7; 63.8% female) completed the HVLT-R and at least two validated EF measures. Process variables included semantic clustering, intrusions, and repetitions. EF test scores were converted to normative z-scores and averaged to create a composite EF Index. Spearman correlations examined associations between process variables and EF. Comparisons with published HC data used summary t-tests. Independent samples t-tests evaluated differences by tumor location. EF performance (M = - 0.75, SD = 1.53) was positively associated with semantic clustering (r = .397, p<.01), but not with intrusions or repetitions. PwBT demonstrated fewer semantic clusters than HC during learning and delayed recall (ps<.01), with no differences in intrusion rates. Process variables did not differ by tumor location. Semantic clustering was associated with EF performance, supporting its construct validity, and was used less frequently by PwBT. Reduced clustering may represent a readily available, low-burden, supplemental marker of EF with potential utility for rehabilitation planning and clinical research.

titre: The Coronary Artery Disease Education Questionnaire (CADE-Q) in Cardiovascular Care: A Scoping Review.
titre_fr: The Coronary Artery Disease Education Questionnaire (CADE-Q) in Cardiovascular Care: A Scoping Review.
auteurs: Vieira Ariany Marques, Benetti Magnus, Ghisi Gabriela Lima de Melo
resume: Patient education is a core component of cardiac rehabilitation (CR) and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease, supporting disease understanding, self-management, and adoption of heart-healthy behaviours. The Coronary Artery Disease Education Questionnaire (CADE-Q) was developed as a standardised instrument to assess disease-related knowledge among individuals with cardiovascular conditions. Since its development, multiple versions and translations have been created and applied in diverse populations and settings worldwide. This scoping review aimed to map the global use of CADE-Q instruments, including populations, contexts, knowledge outcomes, and psychometric properties reported across studies. This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Databases searched included Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central, Emcare, EBSCO CINAHL, Web of Science Core Collection, Global Index Medicus and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses. Studies were eligible if they used the CADE-Q or any of its versions to assess disease-related knowledge in adults. Data were charted using a standardised extraction tool and synthesised descriptively. Sixty-six studies involving 14,714 participants across 26 countries were included. The CADE-Q Short Version was the most frequently used instrument (n=36), followed by CADE-Q II (n=17) and the original CADE-Q (n=13), administered in 19 languages. Most studies were conducted in CR settings. Baseline knowledge levels were generally moderate relative to maximum scores. Lower knowledge was commonly observed in risk factor and psychosocial health domains, while knowledge related to nutrition and exercise was generally higher. In intervention and longitudinal studies, knowledge typically improved following structured educational interventions, particularly within CR programs. Twenty validation studies reported acceptable psychometric properties across versions and languages, including good internal consistency, test-retest reliability, and evidence of structural and construct validity. CADE-Q instruments are widely used globally to assess cardiovascular disease knowledge and demonstrate consistent psychometric performance across diverse settings. Moderate knowledge levels and persistent gaps in risk factor and psychosocial domains suggest a need for more targeted patient education. These tools may support personalised educational interventions in clinical practice, while future research should prioritise implementation and validation in underrepresented populations and regions.

titre: Inter-rater reliability of the ability for basic movement scale II-w: a revised clinical mobility scale adding a walking item.
titre_fr: Inter-rater reliability of the ability for basic movement scale II-w: a revised clinical mobility scale adding a walking item.
auteurs: Nakayama Yasuhide, Togawa Jukia, Ueda Ai, Yoshida Kentaro, Kinoshita Syoji, Abo Masahiro
resume: To verify the inter-rater reliability of the Ability for Basic Movement Scale II-w (ABMS II-w), a revised version of the Ability for Basic Movement Scale II that incorporates a walking assessment item. Cross-sectional reliability study. Setting: Department of Rehabilitation Medicine at a university hospital. Subjects: Fifty patients were enrolled, and 49 were included in the final analysis. Intervention: Not applicable (observational study). Main measures: Patients were evaluated by two independent physical therapists using the newly developed ABMS II-w. The scale includes a walking item (based on a 50-yard criterion) in addition to the original five basic mobility items. High inter-rater reliability was demonstrated for the overall ABMS II-w total score (ICC=0.92; 95% CI 0.86-0.95). Furthermore, the newly incorporated walking item exhibited almost perfect agreement (quadratic weighted kappa=0.99; 95% CI 0.97-1.00), and all individual items maintained substantial to almost perfect inter-rater reliability. The ABMS II-w possesses exceptionally high inter-rater reliability. By extending the evaluation scope beyond standing balance to include functional walking, it provides a seamless and practical tool for clinical rehabilitation medicine.

titre: Imagery ability in children with Obstetric Brachial Plexus Palsy and associations with clinical characteristics: a cross-sectional pilot study.
titre_fr: Imagery ability in children with Obstetric Brachial Plexus Palsy and associations with clinical characteristics: a cross-sectional pilot study.
auteurs: Şengün Nursena, Dilek Burcu, Ankaralı Handan, Kuru Çiğdem Ayhan
resume: The Movement Imagery Questionnaire for Children (MIQ-C) assesses children's imagery ability through three subcomponents: internal visual imagery (IVI), external visual imagery (EVI), and kinesthetic imagery (KI). The study aimed to evaluate the imagery ability and its associations with clinical characteristics in children with Obstetric Brachial Plexus Palsy (OBPP). Fifteen children with OBPP (mean age 10.67 ± 1.18 years; 8 males and 7 females) and 15 healthy children frequency‑matched for age and sex were included. Motor imagery was assessed using the MIQ-C. Motor and sensory functions in participants with OBPP were evaluated using the Active Movement Scale (AMS) and the Narakas Sensory Grading System (NSG), respectively. Mann-Whitney U tests assessed between-group differences in MIQ-C subscores; intraclass correlation coefficients (95% confidence intervals) evaluated test-retest reliability in both groups; and Spearman rank correlations examined associations with clinical characteristics in the OBPP group. Children with OBPP had significantly lower scores than the control group across all MIQ-C subscores (after Bonferroni adjustment to 0.0167; p ≤ .005). In the OBPP group, clinical type was strongly negatively correlated with all MIQ-C subscores. Higher imagery scores were observed in children classified as NSG = 3 than in those classified as NSG = 2. Positive correlations also were found between MIQ-C subscores and AMS scores. Compared to controls, children with OBPP demonstrated lower imagery scores, suggesting potential differences in imagery ability between the groups. Exploratory findings also indicated possible relationships between imagery scores and clinical characteristics; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size. Motor imagery assessment may offer complementary information about imagery ability alongside routine motor and sensory evaluations in OBPP rehabilitation.

titre: Concurrent Validity of the Process Analysis Scale for Shopping-Older Adults (PASS-OA).
titre_fr: Concurrent Validity of the Process Analysis Scale for Shopping-Older Adults (PASS-OA).
auteurs: Yuri Yoshimi, Kaneda Toshikatsu, Higashi Yasuhiro, Yuri Takuma
revue: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
resume: To examine the concurrent validity of the Process Analysis Scale for Shopping-Older Adults (PASS-OA) among community-dwelling older adults based on the Consensus-based Standards for the selection of health Measurement Instruments framework. Cross-sectional validation study. Community-dwelling older adults receiving rehabilitation were assessed between 2022 and 2025. The PASS-OA consists of 10 observational items scored on a 5-point scale (range, 10-50). Concurrent validity was examined by testing predefined hypotheses regarding associations between the PASS-OA and established instrumental activities of daily living (IADL) measures, including shopping-related items and overall scores. A total of 107 participants (mean age, 82.4 ± 5.9 years; 81 women) were included. The PASS-OA total score was significantly correlated with the shopping items of the Lawton IADL scale (ρ = 0.243; P = .011) and the Frenchay Activities Index (ρ = 0.275; P = .004). Significant correlations were also observed with the Lawton IADL mean score (ρ = 0.218; P = .024) and the Frenchay Activities Index total score (ρ = 0.450; P < .001). The PASS-OA demonstrated concurrent validity while capturing complementary process-level aspects of shopping performance. It may help identify specific difficulties relevant to rehabilitation planning and goal setting.

titre: Reliability and measurement error of a climbing-specific upper extremity testing battery for sports rehabilitation monitoring.
titre_fr: Reliability and measurement error of a climbing-specific upper extremity testing battery for sports rehabilitation monitoring.
auteurs: Ehiogu Uzo, Ng Hang, Buckthorp Matthew, Patterson Stephen
revue: Physical therapy in sport : official journal of the Association of Chartered Physiotherapists in Sports Medicine
resume: To establish the inter-tester, test-retest reliability and measurement properties of a climbing-specific upper extremity testing battery for clinical use. Repeated measures study. Sports injury clinic. Thirty recreational boulderers. Finger and shoulder peak force, mean work force, area under the curve (AUC), time to failure, repetitions to failure and fatigue index. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC 2,1), standard error of measurement (SEM), minimal detectable change at 95% confidence level (MDC95), coefficient of variation (CV%) and Bland-Altman limits of agreement plots. Finger and shoulder pull strength demonstrated excellent test-retest reliability (ICC 0.96-0.98). Finger strength MDC95 values ranged from 4.8 to 6.7 kg. Shoulder strength MDC95 ranged from 5.5 to 5.8 kg. Inter-rater reliability was excellent for finger strength (ICC 0.96-0.97) and shoulder strength (ICC 0.96). Mean work force for finger endurance was (ICC 0.99) and shoulder endurance (ICC 0.93-0.99), while time to failure, repetitions to failure, AUC and fatigue index demonstrated greater variability. Climbing-specific finger and shoulder strength testing is a reliable reassessment tool. Mean work force was the most stable endurance-derived outcome. MDC95 values provide preliminary thresholds for interpreting whether observed change exceeds measurement error during rehabilitation monitoring.
resume_fr: To establish the inter-tester, test-retest reliability and measurement properties of a climbing-specific upper extremity testing battery for clinical use. Repeated measures study. titre: Factors Associated With Suicidal Spectrum Behaviours in Women With ADHD: A Systematic Review.
titre_fr: Factors Associated With Suicidal Spectrum Behaviours in Women With ADHD: A Systematic Review.
auteurs: Hamilton Tamara, Johnston Bernadette, Nicholson Emma
resume: ADHD is a common neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by impaired impulsivity, hyperactivity and inattention. Adult females with ADHD are at heightened risk of engaging in suicidal spectrum behaviours (SSBs), including self-harm, suicidal ideation and attempts. However, there is limited knowledge of the factors that are associated with SSBs in adulthood. This systematic review sought to identify factors associated with SSBs in women with ADHD. A search was conducted using PsycINFO, PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus and Web of Science databases. Studies with data concerning factors involved in SSBs in females with ADHD over 16 years old were included. The literature search identified 1,661 articles for screening, of which 16 were included in the final review. The results demonstrated several individual and environmental risk factors associated with the heightened risk of SSBs in women with ADHD, including ADHD subtype, severity, persistence, executive functioning (EF) and response inhibition (RI), comorbidities such as depression and ASD, and childhood and familial factors, such as maltreatment, peer victimisation and parenting factors. Intervention and assessment processes require a more comprehensive and individualised approach to target underlying mechanisms that increase SSB risk in women with ADHD. Further longitudinal research is required to investigate the combination of these risk factors and their underlying mechanisms, such as emotion regulation and impulsivity.

titre: An apparently de novo UBE3A missense variant p.(Tyr777Cys) in the HECT domain in a child with an atypical early childhood phenotype suggestive of Angelman syndrome: a case report and focused literature review.
titre_fr: An apparently de novo UBE3A missense variant p.(Tyr777Cys) in the HECT domain in a child with an atypical early childhood phenotype suggestive of Angelman syndrome: a case report and focused literature review.
auteurs: Jiang Kai, Zhou Ying, Zhang XinYao, Qi Yangfan, Sun Liping, Lin Shuangzhu
resume: Angelman syndrome (AS) is a neurodevelopmental disorder associated with loss of maternal UBE3A function in neurons. Interpreting rare UBE3A missense variants can be challenging, particularly when parental origin and functional effects have not been established. We report a 30-month-old Chinese boy with global developmental delay, motor impairment, and severe expressive language impairment, without clinically observed seizures during the available follow-up. Genetic evaluation, including trio whole-exome sequencing and proband whole-genome sequencing, identified an apparently de novo heterozygous UBE3A missense variant, NM_130839.5:c.2330A>G, p. (Tyr777Cys), within the homologous to the E6AP carboxyl terminus (HECT) domain. Copy-number analysis did not identify a large deletion involving 15q11.2-q13. Electroencephalography (EEG) showed paroxysmal high-amplitude 2-3 Hz spike-slow and sharp-slow complexes, and the magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) report suggested delayed white-matter myelination. The variant was classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS) in the laboratory report and remained a VUS following reassessment using the UBE3A-specific ClinGen Variant Curation Expert Panel (VCEP) specifications. Its maternal or paternal allelic origin remains undetermined, and its functional effects have not been experimentally assessed. This report documents the rare, apparently de novo UBE3A HECT-domain variant p. (Tyr777Cys), together with detailed early developmental and electrophysiological findings. Substantial motor and expressive language impairment accompanied by EEG abnormalities suggestive of AS, despite no clinically observed seizures by 30 months, highlights the importance of considering AS during the evaluation of unexplained developmental delay. Integrated clinical assessment, EEG, and family-based genetic testing help identify candidate variants and guide further investigation. Although p. (Tyr777Cys) remains a VUS, the documented phenotype provides a reference for future case comparisons, parent-of-origin studies, and functional investigations.

titre: Beyond decibels alone: environmental noise, auditory diversity, and person-environment interactions in autism.
titre_fr: Beyond decibels alone: environmental noise, auditory diversity, and person-environment interactions in autism.
auteurs: Gao Xinping, Du Shuning, Zhang Xinming, Wang Jun
resume: Environmental noise is a ubiquitous physical exposure and a biologically active non-auditory stressor, yet its relevance to autism has received substantially less attention compared to chemical components of the urban exposome. Two questions are often conflated: whether prenatal or early-life noise contributes to autism-related neurodevelopmental susceptibility and whether adverse auditory environments increase functional burden after autistic characteristics are present. In this structured narrative review, we integrate environmental epidemiology, developmental and auditory neuroscience, sleep and stress research, and environmental acoustics within a two-pathway life-course framework. PubMed/MEDLINE and the Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception through 4 September 2026, supplemented by targeted Google Scholar searching. We included English-language peer-reviewed primary studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and authoritative guidance or standards documents and excluded conference abstracts, dissertations, and preprints. Evidence was prioritized by directness to the autism question, study design, exposure characterization, outcome validity, precision, and recency; the evidence matrix is intentionally selective. Direct human evidence that quantified environmental noise independently increasing the risk of autism diagnosis or persistently worsening autistic traits is sparse and inconsistent, and current data do not support a causal claim. A more direct functional evidence stream-studies conducted on autistic participants that experimentally manipulate auditory conditions and/or measure real-world functional outcomes-indicates that some autistic individuals show altered auditory responsivity, reduced or delayed habituation, speech-in-noise and selective-attention difficulties, and greater burden in noisy or unpredictable settings. We conceptualize this pathway as a person-environment interaction in which acoustic structure, sensory phenotype, task demand, and predictability or control jointly shape functioning. Standard metrics such as LAeq, Lden, and Lnight remain necessary for comparability and policy and are supplemented, not replaced, by multidimensional characterization. Event peaks and temporal fluctuation receive empirical support from studies on child neurodevelopment, whereas spectral content, reverberation, source multiplicity, predictability, controllability, and personal time-activity patterns remain framework-generated hypotheses requiring direct autism-specific testing. This framework separates etiologic inference from phenotypic modification and identifies testable priorities for early-life research and co-designed acoustic accessibility.

titre: TTC5 regulates γ-tubulin mRNA and is required for mammalian neurodevelopment.
titre_fr: TTC5 regulates γ-tubulin mRNA and is required for mammalian neurodevelopment.
auteurs: Rushforth Rebekah, Martin Alexia K, Cassady Kevin A, Stottmann Rolf W
resume: Tubulin autoregulation is an essential function that controls the concentration of cellular soluble tubulin. This process is mediated by TTC5 which binds the REI/C polypeptide sequence found in all α- and β-TUBULIN proteins. The recent discovery of TTC5 as the primary tubulin autoregulation pathway mediator and the identification of human brain malformations caused by TTC5 variants poses a need for an in vivo system to elucidate the gene-disease relationship. Here, we present an in vivo Ttc5 mouse model that phenocopies many of the human TTC5 clinical presentations. The brain malformations in Ttc5null/null mice are driven by neurogenesis defects, which are in turn caused by perturbations in mitosis. We found that increased γ-TUBULIN levels in Ttc5null/null brains likely facilitate mitotic errors. We posit that the paradigm of tubulin autoregulation should be expanded to include γ-tubulin and that this expansion provides a mechanistic base for tubulin autoregulation brain malformations.

titre: Deep Brain Stimulation of the Nucleus Accumbens and Anterior Limb of the Internal Capsule in Severe Autism Spectrum Disorder: Clinical Outcomes and Infralimbic-Accumbens Circuit Involvement.
titre_fr: Deep Brain Stimulation of the Nucleus Accumbens and Anterior Limb of the Internal Capsule in Severe Autism Spectrum Disorder: Clinical Outcomes and Infralimbic-Accumbens Circuit Involvement.
auteurs: Wu Yang, Pei Jia-Sheng, Guo Yi, Yin Sen-Lin, Xu Yang-Yang, Yin Li, Cao Yu, Gan Lu, Yu Hai-Fang, Yao Peng, Wang Meng-Qi, Deng Hao, Huang Xinyuejia, Xiao Ling-Long, Shi Yi-Feng, Xu Chong-Xi, Peng Hao-Ran, Ren Zhi-Yi, Lin Jian-Ping, Chi Bin, Chen Zhi-Ling, Lin Yang-Yang, Zhang Shu-Xin, Yuan Bang-Qing, Wang Wei
resume: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder with limited effective treatments. Deep brain stimulation (DBS) has emerged as a potential intervention, yet its efficacy and mechanisms remain poorly understood. We conducted a prospective, single-arm cohort study of nucleus accumbens-anterior limb of the internal capsule (NAc-ALIC) DBS in patients with severe ASD, observing preliminary safety and longitudinal reductions in repetitive-behaviour and social-domain symptom severity during follow-up. Exploratory sweet-spot analysis suggested a candidate medial-ventral NAc region associated with social-domain score reductions. In a maternal immune activation mouse model, NAc-DBS enhanced social novelty preference and reduced repetitive behaviours. NAc-DBS partially normalized aberrant oscillatory activity in the NAc and infralimbic cortex (IL), increased IL neuronal activity, and enhanced cross-frequency coupling. Chemogenetic activation of the IL→NAc projection enhanced social novelty preference, whereas inhibition of IL neurons projecting to the NAc attenuated the DBS-associated social novelty improvement without affecting marble-burying behaviour. NAc-DBS also increased glutamate, AMPA receptor, and brain-derived neurotrophic factor levels, consistent with enhanced synaptic plasticity. Together, these findings provide exploratory clinical evidence of longitudinal reductions in symptom severity during follow-up after NAc-ALIC DBS and suggest that NAc stimulation modulates IL and NAc neural activity, implicates the IL→NAc pathway, and engages plasticity-related processes.

titre: Proteomic Analysis of Plasma Small Extracellular Vesicles and Targeted Metabolomic Analysis of Plasma From Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
titre_fr: Proteomic Analysis of Plasma Small Extracellular Vesicles and Targeted Metabolomic Analysis of Plasma From Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
auteurs: Li Hang, Ma Wenhui, Zhao Yan, Dong Hangyan, Wang Jing, Wang Bin, Hu Jianxin, Yang Qianxu, Han Pengfei, Liu Xinyun, Luo Chuncai, Dong Bo, Xiang Xiaochao, Qin Weijie, Qian Xiaohong, Wang Yi, Zhang Wanjun, Li Shijun
resume: Autism is a neurodevelopmental disorder with deficits in social communication and interaction, restricted and repetitive behaviors, and unusual stereotyped interests or activities. With a lack of molecular information on the etiology of ASD, early diagnosis of this disease remains a challenge. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs), as extracellular vesicles containing various important biomolecules, have been demonstrated to have a functional impact on physiological processes in the central nervous system. Herein, we profiled the proteome of plasma sEVs collected from preschool children with autism and performed targeted metabolic analysis on their plasma samples. Screening of the differentiated proteins between autistic and healthy children revealed potential biomarkers, including those involved in calcium ion binding, such as MACF1 and CALM3. Bioinformatic investigation further identified 10 outlier proteins, such as EHD1 and ERF3A, strongly associated with autism. Targeted metabolic analysis and IPA prediction suggested the potential involvement of the PI3K-AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. The sEV proteomic and plasma metabolomic analyses were performed in parallel, and pathway-level findings from each dataset were compared descriptively. These results provide insight into the biological mechanism of autism and promise in determining biomarkers for the early diagnosis of ASD. Trial Registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry identifier: ChiCTR1800018616.

titre: Leucine exposure and neurodevelopmental outcomes in maple syrup urine disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic, longitudinal, and treatment-related evidence.
titre_fr: Leucine exposure and neurodevelopmental outcomes in maple syrup urine disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic, longitudinal, and treatment-related evidence.
auteurs: Dalili Setila, Nikpour Sara
resume: Neurodevelopmental impairment remains a major long-term complication of maple syrup urine disease (MSUD). Although leucine is a principal neurotoxic metabolite, studies have characterized exposure using clinically distinct measures, including diagnostic or acute peak concentrations and longitudinal indices of metabolic control. We therefore evaluated these exposure patterns separately and examined neurodevelopmental outcomes in the context of early diagnosis and liver transplantation. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to July 26, 2026. A total of 203 records were identified through database searching (63 PubMed/MEDLINE, 58 Scopus, and 82 Web of Science); 46 unique studies were included after deduplication, screening, full-text assessment, and supplementary reference-list searching. Leucine exposure was classified as diagnostic/peak or long-term/mean exposure. Quantitative synthesis was restricted to studies with sufficiently comparable populations, exposure definitions, outcomes, and effect measures. Correlations between long-term/mean leucine and IQ were transformed to Fisher's z, pooled using inverse-variance random-effects weighting with the DerSimonian-Laird estimator of between-study variance, and back-transformed to Pearson's r. Heterogeneous outcomes were synthesized narratively. Methodological quality and risk of bias were appraised with JBI tools appropriate to study design. Four studies (total N = 61) contributed to the long-term/mean leucine-IQ meta-analysis. Higher long-term/mean leucine exposure was associated with lower IQ (pooled r = -0.40, 95% CI -0.66 to -0.05; I2 = 39%; tau2 = 0.056). The 95% prediction interval was -0.77 to 0.17. Leave-one-out analyses identified the small le Roux study as influential; its exclusion yielded r = -0.52 (95% CI -0.70 to -0.27; I2 = 0%). Diagnostic/peak leucine showed a less consistent relationship with later neurodevelopment and was not combined in a single pool. The approximately 200 μmol/L value reported in longitudinal evidence is best interpreted as a study-level treatment-associated target in young children, not a universal neurotoxicity threshold. Newborn screening and early diagnosis were generally associated with more favorable clinical and neurological outcomes. Liver transplantation consistently improved metabolic stability, whereas neurocognitive improvement was variable. Longitudinal leucine exposure appears more consistently associated with neurodevelopmental outcome in MSUD than a single concentration measured at diagnosis or during an acute episode. The findings support early diagnosis and sustained metabolic control while cautioning against interpreting any single leucine value as a universal neurotoxicity threshold. Liver transplantation provides robust metabolic stabilization but may not reverse established cognitive impairment.
