titre: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence in Cerebral Small Vessel Disease: From Risk Prediction to Personalised Management.
titre_fr: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence in Cerebral Small Vessel Disease: From Risk Prediction to Personalised Management.
auteurs: Zhao Lei, Xie Le, Meng Pan, Liu Danhong, Li Yuxiang, Wu Bingqing, Yang Wanyao, Fang Rui, Ge Jinwen, Mei Zhigang
resume: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a major substrate for cerebrovascular and neurodegenerative conditions. However, its subtle and diffuse lesions hinder early detection and timely intervention. This clinically oriented review examines applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in CSVD, focusing on the integration of imaging with clinical, molecular or digital data. It covers three clinical areas: risk stratification and prognosis, diagnosis and quantitative assessment, and personalised management. We distinguish between findings in CSVD cohorts, evidence from other populations and proposed applications. We consider internal and external validation and evidence of clinical impact. Prediction models have been developed for CSVD screening and for estimating the risk of lesion progression, cognitive decline and vascular events. Selected studies have evaluated automated lesion quantification across multiple centres. Imaging and digital measures have also been used to assess current cognitive and gait impairment. AI-assisted treatment selection, remote monitoring and rehabilitation remain at an early stage, and their clinical benefits in CSVD have yet to be established. We discuss key requirements for clinical translation, including harmonised data acquisition, annotation aligned with neuroimaging standards, external validation and prospective evaluation of safety, equity and value in clinical practice. The review emphasises CSVD-specific phenotypes and longitudinal management, with outcomes extending beyond imaging to cognition, gait, affect and independence in activities of daily living. Future studies should establish whether these approaches improve clinical assessment and patient outcomes compared with current practice.

titre: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation combined with resistance exercise for knee osteoarthritis: randomized clinical trial protocol.
titre_fr: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation combined with resistance exercise for knee osteoarthritis: randomized clinical trial protocol.
auteurs: da Silva Andressa Costa, Duarte Gabriel Filipe, da Costa Souza Heloisa, da Silva João Guilherme Neiva Nogueira, Aguiar Camila Chaim, Dias Danielle Barros Ruffo, de Oliveira Leite Samuel, do Nascimento Bruno Fajardo, Felício Diogo Carvalho, Fonseca Diogo Simões
resume: Resistance exercise is the gold-standard conservative treatment for knee osteoarthritis (KOA). However, arthrogenic muscle inhibition and quadriceps weakness may limit the effectiveness of strengthening programs. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) has been proposed as an adjunct strategy to enhance muscle activation, yet current evidence in KOA remains inconclusive and methodologically limited. To investigate the effects of adding NMES, applied concurrently with voluntary contractions, to a resistance exercise program in individuals with KOA. This double-blind, parallel-group randomized controlled trial will include 84 participants with clinically diagnosed KOA, randomly allocated (1:1) to resistance exercise combined with either active or sham NMES. Both groups will perform supervised sessions twice weekly for eight weeks. The primary outcome will be knee pain assessed by the Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS). Secondary outcomes will include self-reported physical function, knee extensor torque, performance-based physical function, and adverse events. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and 12-week follow-up. Data will be analyzed using linear mixed models under the intention-to-treat principle. This study may clarify whether adding NMES provides additional therapeutic benefits in KOA rehabilitation and support evidence-based clinical decision-making. ensaiosclinicos.gov.br identifier is RBR-77f8rjq.

titre: Current Clinical Practice and Barriers to Instrumented Gait Assessment in Stroke Rehabilitation: A Cross-Sectional Survey.
titre_fr: Current Clinical Practice and Barriers to Instrumented Gait Assessment in Stroke Rehabilitation: A Cross-Sectional Survey.
auteurs: Araki Sota, Ikeda Takaaki, Wakida Masanori, Kitatani Ryosuke, Kubo Hiroki, Mizuta Naomichi, Yamamoto Masataka, Honda Keita, Nakamura Manabu, Takahashi Tadashi, Suzukamo Yoshimi, Sekiguchi Yusuke
resume: BackgroundObservational gait analysis is widely used in stroke rehabilitation but may have limited objectivity and reproducibility. Instrumented gait assessment may address these limitations, but its routine use and implementation barriers remain unclear.ObjectivesTo investigate gait assessment practices and barriers to routine instrumented gait assessment among physiotherapists treating people with stroke.MethodsA web-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among members of the Japanese Society of Neurological Physical Therapy. Respondents reporting limitations in observational gait analysis completed additional questions on instrumented gait assessment. Logistic regression examined factors associated with perceived measurement time burden among device users.ResultsOf 329 respondents, 95.4% used standardized clinical gait assessments, and 81.8% perceived limitations in observational gait analysis. Although 91.2% recognized the need for instrumented gait assessment, only 39.8% of the 269 respondents completing the second-stage questions used it routinely. Of 162 non-users, 80.2% reported that relevant equipment was unavailable. Device users commonly reported excessive measurement time, high equipment costs, and difficulty interpreting results. Measurement time ≥20 min was associated with perceived measurement time burden (odds ratio 3.59, 95% confidence interval 1.04-12.46; p = 0.044). Automated analysis (95.5%) and usability regardless of location (83.6%) were frequently desired.ConclusionsInstrumented gait assessment was widely perceived as necessary, but routine use remained limited. Improving equipment access and developing time-efficient, portable systems with automated analysis and interpretation support may facilitate integration into routine stroke rehabilitation and sustained clinical use.

titre: Patients treated with rehabilitation alone after anterior cruciate ligament injury display greater muscle strength symmetry, yet lower absolute muscle strength normalized to bodyweight compared to reconstruction: A Cross-sectional study of 3,093 patients.
titre_fr: Patients treated with rehabilitation alone after anterior cruciate ligament injury display greater muscle strength symmetry, yet lower absolute muscle strength normalized to bodyweight compared to reconstruction: A Cross-sectional study of 3,093 patients.
auteurs: Hamrin Senorski Rebecca, Thomeé Roland, Samuelsson Kristian, Hamrin Senorski Eric, Piussi Ramana
revue: Physical therapy in sport : official journal of the Association of Chartered Physiotherapists in Sports Medicine
resume: Younger patients active at a greater activity level are in general treated with anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) while older, less active patients receive rehabilitation alone as primary treatment. Objective of this study was to compare muscle strength, and patient-reported outcomes (PROs) between patients treated with rehabilitation alone and rehabilitation with additional ACL reconstruction (ACLR) during the first 12 months after treatment. Registry-based cohort study. Cross-sectional comparisons adjusted for age and sex using ANCOVA. 3093 patients (2707 ACLR; 386 rehabilitation), aged ≥15 years and registered in Project ACL. Muscle strength and PROs assessed at 10 weeks, 4, 8, and 12 months after ACL injury or ACLR. In the comparison between patients treated with rehabilitation alone and ACLR, patients in the rehabilitation alone group had greater muscle strength symmetry at all follow-ups but lower absolute strength normalized to bodyweight in the uninjured limb, except hamstrings strength at 10 weeks. Patients in the rehabilitation group reported higher KOOS symptoms at 8- and 12 months and sports/recreation at 10 weeks, present K-SES<sub>18</sub> was higher at 10 weeks but lower at 12 months, while future K-SES<sub>18</sub> was lower at all follow-ups. Patients in the rehabilitation alone group reported lower ACL-RSI was lower at 12 months and Tegner activity levels were lower pre-injury and at all follow-ups. Patients treated with rehabilitation alone had greater symmetrical strength, but lower uninjured limb absolute strength normalized to bodyweight compared to patients treated with ACLR. Patients in the rehabilitation alone group also reported less knee symptoms, but inferior present and future knee self-efficacy compared with patients treated with ACLR.

titre: Is Social Vulnerability Associated with Discharge Disposition After Trauma Laparotomy?
titre_fr: Is Social Vulnerability Associated with Discharge Disposition After Trauma Laparotomy?
auteurs: Rieger William D, Fajemisin Mokunfayo O, Martinez Ugarte Stephanie, Green Renee W, Kim Seokhun, Mankiewicz Kimberly A, Kao Lillian S
revue: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
resume: Social vulnerability may influence rehabilitation discharge after trauma independent of functional recovery needs. We evaluated whether neighborhood-level social vulnerability was associated with rehabilitation discharge and whether this association persisted when discharge appropriateness was assessed using objective mobility scores. This retrospective, single-center cohort study included adult trauma laparotomy patients receiving physical therapy from 01/2020-06/2023. Social vulnerability was assessed using the social vulnerability index (SVI) and area deprivation index (ADI). Rehabilitation appropriateness was defined using an Activity Measure for Post-Acute Care (AM-PAC) score ≤16. Primary and secondary outcomes were rehabilitation discharge and mobility-informed rehabilitation appropriateness, respectively. Associations were evaluated using binomial regression adjusted for prespecified covariates. Among 572 patients, 119 (20.8%) were discharged to rehabilitation, and 103 (18%) had AM-PAC scores ≤16. Median SVI was 0.75 and ADI was 63.0. Greater social vulnerability was associated with lower odds of rehabilitation discharge (SVI: aOR 0.17, 95% CI 0.06-0.53, P<0.01), whereas ADI was not (aOR 0.99, 95% CI 0.98-1.00, P=0.21). When accounting for AM-PAC scores, neither SVI (aOR 1.06, 95% CI 0.39-2.88, P=0.91) nor ADI (aOR 0.99, 95% CI 0.99-1.01, P=0.27) was associated with appropriate rehabilitation discharge. Greater social vulnerability was associated with lower rehabilitation discharge rates after trauma laparotomy, but not with mobility-informed rehabilitation discharge. Incorporating objective mobility assessments into discharge planning may help identify rehabilitation needs while limiting the influence of social factors.

titre: Sensorimotor recovery, neuropathic pain reduction, and neuroplasticity changes following cognitive multisensory rehabilitation or adaptive fitness in adults with spinal cord injury: a feasibility pilot randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Sensorimotor recovery, neuropathic pain reduction, and neuroplasticity changes following cognitive multisensory rehabilitation or adaptive fitness in adults with spinal cord injury: a feasibility pilot randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Van de Winckel Ann, Carpentier Sydney T, Bottale Sara, Blackwood Jena, Deng Wei, Zhang Lin, Hendrickson Timothy J, Mueller Bryon A, Nourian Ruhollah, Melander-Smith Sheri, Morse Leslie R, Lim Kelvin O
resume: Spinal cord injury (SCI) often causes partial or complete sensory and motor loss, disrupting the afferent integration needed for accurate mental body representations (MBR, i.e., body awareness and visuospatial body map). MBR deficits compromise sensorimotor recovery and contribute to neuropathic pain in about 69% of adults with SCI. Medications for neuropathic pain are often ineffective and can cause adverse reactions. Our previous pilot clinical trial showed that Cognitive Multisensory Rehabilitation (CMR), a physical therapy that restores MBR, produced significant, lasting reductions in neuropathic pain, improved sensorimotor function, and enhanced brain function. Building on these results, we examined feasibility and whether 8 weeks of CMR or adaptive fitness (1) improves sensorimotor function and reduces pain; (2) increases sensorimotor- and MBR-related brain activity and connectivity in adults with SCI. Sixteen participants (52 ± 8 years old, 13 ± 10 years post-SCI) were randomized to CMR or adaptive fitness (45 min, 3x/week, 8 weeks); one withdrew. Ten participants had neuropathic pain of ≥3/10. Pain and sensorimotor function were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and 3-month follow-up using the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), ASIA Impairment Scale (AIS), and Neuromuscular Recovery Scale (NRS). Functional MRI included resting-state and 4 tasks: imagining feeling the left leg, imagining moving the left leg, whole-body movement imagery, and a sensation task (i.e., gently brushing the big toes with a towel). Post-CMR (n = 8), participants showed significant large within-group AIS effect sizes (touch: d = 1.54; pinprick: d = 1.83; lower limb motor function: d = 1.32) and large (core: d = 2.19) to moderate (arm function: d = 0.69; leg function: d = 0.74) NRS effect sizes. Adaptive fitness (n = 7) showed non-significant small/moderate AIS (touch: d = 0.49; pinprick: d = 0.53; lower limb motor function: d = 0.74) and NRS effects (core: d = 0.73; arm function: d = 0.34; leg function: d = 0.00). Benefits persisted at follow-up. MCID was exceeded for average pain post-CMR and highest pain at 3-month follow-up. Pain virtually did not change after fitness. CMR increased brain connectivity and activation during leg imagery. During whole-body imagery, CMR increased widespread activation; adaptive fitness showed spatially limited increases. These preliminary results support CMR's potential to improve function and reduce neuropathic pain in adults with SCI, warranting larger confirmatory trials.Clinical Trial Registration: https://clinicaltrial.gov/, identifier NCT05167032.

titre: Physiotherapists' perspectives on delivering a specialist intervention for functional motor disorder in NHS settings in England and Scotland: a qualitative study embedded within the Physio4FMD randomised controlled trial.
titre_fr: Physiotherapists' perspectives on delivering a specialist intervention for functional motor disorder in NHS settings in England and Scotland: a qualitative study embedded within the Physio4FMD randomised controlled trial.
auteurs: Macklin Heather, Hornsby Claire, Nielsen Glenn
resume: This qualitative study explored physiotherapists’ experiences of delivering the Physio4FMD intervention and examined implications for integrating this approach into routine practice. Qualitative interview study using thematic analysis, informed by an interpretative phenomenological orientation. This qualitative study was conducted as part of the Physio4FMD randomised controlled trial (ISRCTN56136713) and is classified as a post-results publication. 11 National Health Service (NHS) neurology and physiotherapy services in England and Scotland. All 15 eligible physiotherapists who delivered the Physio4FMD intervention were invited; 13 participated. Four themes captured factors influencing implementation: different outcomes for different individuals; catalyst for change; the trial intervention was a roadmap for navigating complex health problems; and acquiring the skills and qualities of a competent physiotherapist in functional motor disorder (FMD). Physiotherapists valued the structured intervention and opportunities for professional development but identified variation in patient responses and challenges delivering the intervention within existing NHS services. While physical outcomes varied, clinicians identified meaningful gains in patient understanding, self-efficacy and emotional well-being, highlighting the importance of multi-dimensional treatment goals. Successful implementation was perceived to depend on patient readiness, clinician expertise and adequate service resources. The findings contextualise trial outcomes and underscore the need for careful patient selection, specialist training and integrated multidisciplinary pathways. Overall, the physiotherapists felt there was a need for greater investment in dedicated, well-resourced physiotherapy services for FMD within the NHS.

titre: FoRist: Three-DoF Soft Wearable Robot for Forearm and Wrist Assistance.
titre_fr: FoRist: Three-DoF Soft Wearable Robot for Forearm and Wrist Assistance.
auteurs: Su Huimin, Ye Seungmin, Lee Yechan, Lee Hojik, Cho Seongyun, Park Hyung-Soon
resume: The growing population of elderly individuals affected by musculoskeletal and neurological diseases experiences multijoint functional impairment, and individuals with compromised forearm and wrist function can lose independence and quality of life. However, most wearable robotic devices provide assistance for a single degree of freedom (DoF) and restrict other joint movements because decoupling multijoint kinematics remains challenging. This article introduces FoRist, a lightweight three-DoF soft wearable robot designed for forearm and wrist assistance. FoRist assists wrist ulnar/radial deviation, wrist extension/flexion, and forearm pronation/supination through a spring blade-based active-passive hybrid actuation mechanism using three motors. It integrates compact rail structures, soft tension transfer mechanisms, and a flexible twisted string actuation mechanism to assist forearm-wrist motion while preserving freedom of movement in the neighboring hand and elbow joints. The local wearable structure at the wristband rail-slider engagement has a maximum thickness of 16 mm. Its personalized usability features, including bioanatomical analysis-driven customization and user-friendly donning/doffing, support application to individuals with forearm and wrist impairments. User tests with stroke survivors showed that wearing FoRist increased the achievable range of motion and output torque across the forearm and wrist movements compared with unassisted movement. In a two-participant test of a simulated food-preparation sequence involving opening a jar, scooping jam, and spreading jam on bread, FoRist assistance increased task-relevant wrist motion and was associated with lower maximum shoulder abduction. These preliminary results support FoRist's feasibility and usability in short-term laboratory use. With its compact three-DoF architecture, low distal mass, and personalized fit, FoRist offers a promising avenue for extending rehabilitation training beyond clinical settings and has the potential to enhance independence and functional performance in activities of daily living.

titre: Structuring Exergame Program for Unilateral Cerebral Palsy with Multi Criteria Decision-Making: Randomized Trial Exergaming in Cerebral Palsy Rehabilitation.
titre_fr: Structuring Exergame Program for Unilateral Cerebral Palsy with Multi Criteria Decision-Making: Randomized Trial Exergaming in Cerebral Palsy Rehabilitation.
auteurs: Emir Ahmet, Tarakci Devrim, Karatekin Duygu, Gedikli Erman
resume: Objective: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of structured exergame rehabilitation program on upper extremity functions and trunk control in children with unilateral Cerebral Palsy (CP).Methods: Twenty-five children with unilateral CP in Gross Motor Function Classification Scale Levels I-III were included. Participants were randomly divided into two groups. First group (Exergame-EG) received 15 sessions of exergaming program structured by Analytical Hierarchy Process for 8 weeks in addition to neurodevelopmental treatment (NDT) sessions once a week. The second group (Activity-Based Exercise-AE) received 15 sessions of activity-based exercise program for 8 weeks with the same duration of additional NDT sessions. Assessments included 2D kinematic analysis, Upper Extremity Selective Motor Control Scale (SCUES), Jebsen-Taylor Hand Function Test (JTHFT) for upper extremity functions, Trunk Control Measurement Scale (TCMS) for trunk control, and Pediatric Evaluation of Disability Inventory Computer Adaptive Test (PEDI-CAT) for activities of daily living (ADL).Results: Both groups demonstrated significant improvements in SCUES, JTHFT, kinematic analysis, and TCMS after the intervention (P < 0.05, effect sizes: 0.54-0.652). There were no significant intergroup differences (P > 0.05). Only exergame group showed significant improvements in PEDI-CAT after the intervention (P < 0.05 effect sizes: 0.392-0.469).Conclusion: The structured exergame program yields comparable positive effects on upper extremity functions, trunk control, and ADL when compared with activity-based exercises.

titre: Effects of basic activities of daily living interventions in patients with post-stroke hemiplegia: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effects of basic activities of daily living interventions in patients with post-stroke hemiplegia: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Wang Qing, Xiong Jing, Lin Suzhu, Lin Xiujiao, Lin Feifei, Xu Yating, Yang Wenqi, Lv Wanping, Xie Baoyuan
resume: To systematically evaluate the effect of basic activities of daily living (BADL) intervention on patients with stroke-induced hemiplegia. Due to motor and sensory dysfunction, patients with stroke-induced hemiplegia are restricted in performing basic daily living activities, which seriously affects their ability to take care of themselves and their quality of life. BADL intervention, which involves training in basic self-care tasks such as eating, dressing, and bathing, and functional mobility, is an important measure for the rehabilitation of stroke-induced hemiplegia. This review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. The Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, CBM, Wanfang, Embase, PubMed, Web of Science, and CINAHL databases were systematically searched from 2015 to 2025 to identify randomized controlled trials. A total of nine randomized controlled trials were included, involving 521 patients with hemiplegia after stroke. The meta-analysis results showed that compared with conventional intervention, BADL intervention could significantly improve the self-care ability of patients [standardized mean difference (SMD) = 1.10, 95% confidence interval (CI) (0.64, 1.57), P < 0.00001] and significantly improve the upper limb motor function [SMD = 0.61, 95% CI (0.33, 0.89), P < 0.00001]. Basic activities of daily living interventions may improve self-care ability and upper-limb motor function in patients with post-stroke hemiplegia. However, given the limited number of included studies, methodological limitations, and heterogeneity across studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Further high-quality, large-scale randomized controlled trials with standardized outcome measures and longer follow-up periods are needed to confirm these findings.

titre: Employment patterns and correlates among young adults registered with autism or intellectual disability in South Korea.
titre_fr: Employment patterns and correlates among young adults registered with autism or intellectual disability in South Korea.
auteurs: Oh Miae, Ko Minsu, Chung Yeeun, Yoon Nan-He, Yoo Hee Jeong, Perera Bhathika
resume: Employment among young adults with developmental disabilities reflects individual and contextual factors. We described employment patterns and examined educational, caregiver-reported functional, and family correlates among young adults with registered developmental disabilities in South Korea. We pooled 2022-2024 nationwide survey data for 2688 adults aged 18-29 years registered with autism or intellectual disability who were no longer enrolled in education. Multinomial logistic regression examined four survey-defined labor-market categories (not in paid employment, sheltered employment, subsidized integrated workplace, and competitive employment). Overall, 53.4% were not in paid employment and 20.4% were in survey-defined competitive employment, representing mainstream private- or public-sector open-market work. In the adjusted multinomial model, better communication was associated with competitive employment relative to not being in paid employment (relative risk ratio [RRR] 1.39 per 1-SD increase; 95% CI 1.10-1.75), as was better functioning in activities of daily living (RRR 1.61 per 1-SD increase; 95% CI 1.29-2.00). School placement and contemporaneously reported family-system factors were also associated with labor-market status. Educational experiences, caregiver-reported functioning, and family characteristics were associated with employment status. Cross-sectional data cannot establish temporal or causal direction and may partly reflect employment-related differences in caregiver ratings. Longitudinal studies with independent assessments are needed to clarify these relationships and inform support planning.

titre: The Impact of Telenursing on Post-Operative Self-Care in Women with Breast Cancer: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
titre_fr: The Impact of Telenursing on Post-Operative Self-Care in Women with Breast Cancer: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
auteurs: Dos Santos Cristina Poliana Rolim Saraiva, Goyanna Natália Frota, de Freitas Corpes Erilaine, Yanez Romel Jonathan Velasco, Netto José Jeová Mourão, Castro Régia Christina Moura Barbosa, Dos Santos Neto Abilio Torres, Laranjeira Carlos, Saraiva Ana Fátima Carvalho Fernandes
revue: Journal of cancer education : the official journal of the American Association for Cancer Education
resume: To evaluate the effect of telenursing on postoperative self-care capacity among women undergoing surgical treatment for breast cancer. A clinical trial conducted at a specialist outpatient clinic in Brazil, involving 59 women with breast cancer, randomised into two groups: control and intervention. Telenursing via telephone contact was carried out on the 1st, 5th to 7th, and 30th to 40th post-operative days. During these contacts, self-care ability was assessed using the Self-Care Ability Assessment Scale in both groups. The intervention group had sole access to an educational telenursing programme, providing guidance on the surgical wound, suction drain, ipsilateral arm, lymphoedema prevention, diet, medication, and physical, social and psychological rehabilitation. Pearson's chi-squared test, the Wilcoxon test and Fisher's exact test were used to assess the outcome and investigate associations between categorical variables, with statistical significance defined as p < 0.05. The study adhered to the CONSORT checklist. No statistically significant difference was observed in the total self-care autonomy scores between the groups at the start of the study and at the last tele-nursing contact. However, this score was higher in the intervention group than in the control group, where changes in individual mean scores were statistically significant for two actions: ensuring good habits (p = 0.017) and body self-examination (p = 0.007). Although no significant difference was observed in overall self-care scores, participants receiving the educational intervention demonstrated significant improvements in selected self-care behaviours. The clinical trial described in this article was registered with the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry (ReBEC) under registration number RBR9xbptxt (Date of registration 11 August 2022).

titre: Medication count increase and in-hospital falls after hip fracture in older adults: a multicenter cohort study.
titre_fr: Medication count increase and in-hospital falls after hip fracture in older adults: a multicenter cohort study.
auteurs: Yoshimura Yoshihiro, Matsumoto Ayaka, Hikuma Masami
revue: Annals of geriatric medicine and research
resume: Medication counts change during post-acute care after hip fracture, but their association with inpatient safety is uncertain. We examined admission-to-discharge count changes and in-hospital outcomes. This retrospective multicenter cohort included 837 patients aged ≥65 years admitted to two post-acute rehabilitation hospitals in Japan during April 2023-June 2025. Net change in routinely recorded medication count between admission and discharge was categorized as decrease, no change (reference), or increase. The primary outcome was first documented in-hospital fall. Models adjusted for facility, age, sex, admission medication count, admission Functional Independence Measure motor and cognitive scores, premorbid modified Rankin Scale, Charlson Comorbidity Index, fracture type, and treatment procedure. Mean age was 85.4 years; 79.2% were women. Falls were recorded in 121/837 patients (14.5%): 11.8% in the count-decrease group, 10.5% in the no-change group, and 21.8% in the increase group. Compared with no change, increase was associated with falls (adjusted odds ratio, 2.22; 95% confidence interval, 1.28-3.84). A small association between count reduction and discharge motor function attenuated after additional length-of-stay adjustment; no clear adjusted associations with acute-care transfer or home discharge were observed. Admission-to-discharge medication count increase co-occurred with inpatient falls after hip fracture, but temporal precedence and causation cannot be established. Count change is not a validated prospective fall-risk measure; whether real-time medication monitoring improves safety requires prospective study.

titre: Addressing the goals and needs of people living with psychosis in Malawi through community-based rehabilitation: A mixed methods analysis.
titre_fr: Addressing the goals and needs of people living with psychosis in Malawi through community-based rehabilitation: A mixed methods analysis.
auteurs: Morrison Abigail M, Buono Mia, Tikhiwa Harriet Akello, Zumazuma Alex, Mortenson Hillary, Waddell Katherine, Dao Thuy, Chiliza Bonginkosi, Stockton Melissa A, Gaynes Bradley N, Kulisewa Kazione, Pence Brian W
resume: Psychotic disorders are a leading cause of disability. Community-based rehabilitation (CBR) interventions may improve psychosis outcomes. CBR is designed to reduce relapse, promote independence, and support people with lived experience (PWLE) and caregivers by identifying and working toward their recovery goals. However, the alignment between an adapted CBR and the specific needs and goals of PWLE and their family members in low-resourced settings remains unknown. To address this gap, we describe the needs and goals of PWLE and caregivers participating in an adapted CBR intervention in Malawi using a mixed methods approach. We analyzed qualitative and quantitative data from a CBR intervention as part of a pilot trial in Blantyre, Malawi (NCT06080477). Structured nurse-led needs assessments and goal-setting activities were completed during three phases (Phase I-stabilization, Phase II-rehabilitation, and Phase III-maintenance) over the 12-month study period. Thirty PWLE were analyzed. Qualitative interviews were conducted with a subsample of 12 PWLE and 14 caregivers and analyzed to contextualize quantitative findings. Many stabilization needs and goals were resolved by Phase III, suggesting they may have been addressed for most PWLE. In Phases II and III, PWLE frequently selected relapse prevention, well-being, and work goals. Social and work goals were less selected in Phase III compared to Phase II, indicating that some of these goals may have been achieved. Nurses identified the highest unmet needs in work, social life, wellbeing, and empowerment, with unmet needs decreasing across phases. Qualitative results align with quantitative findings suggesting that participants perceived the intervention helped to address their goals and needs. PWLE and caregivers reported a range of goals and described the CBR intervention as a key factor in achieving them. Findings suggest the CBR intervention was partially responsive to participants' needs and goals as perceived by participants, supporting broader implementation of CBR to improve psychosis recovery.

titre: Modeling common finger movement patterns in daily activities: A quantitative framework for adaptive rehabilitation interfaces.
titre_fr: Modeling common finger movement patterns in daily activities: A quantitative framework for adaptive rehabilitation interfaces.
auteurs: Suwabe Ryota, Saito Takeshi, Koizumi Kohei, Hamaguchi Toyohiro, Abo Masahiro
revue: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
resume: BackgroundHand movement involves complex joint patterns that vary across tasks and individuals, and identifying the components that underlie functional hand use is essential.ObjectiveWe aimed to construct a Commonality Model that decomposes real-world finger motions into dynamic forms and quantify probabilistic transitions to develop rehabilitation systems for post-stroke patients.MethodsFifteen healthy young adults performed upper limb tasks based on a Motor Activity Log (MAL), with hand motion captured using a camera and analyzed using MediaPipe. Joint angle data were extracted, k-means clustering was used to classify the movement patterns, and silhouette analysis was performed to determine the optimal number of clusters. Euclidean distance was used to identify overlapping forms across tasks grouped into Common Forms (CFs). A first-order Markov model was constructed to calculate the transition probabilities from CFs to unique task-specific forms.ResultsSeven operationally defined CFs were identified as recurrent image-derived hand-joint configurations observed across multiple activities of daily living (ADL) related tasks. Some tasks were largely composed of CF-associated transitions, whereas others showed higher proportions of task-dependent Individual Forms.ConclusionThe proposed Commonality Model provides an exploratory quantitative framework for identifying recurring and task-dependent hand-joint configurations during ADL-related movements in healthy young adults. Further studies are required to validate its reproducibility, generalizability, and clinical relevance in larger and clinical populations.

titre: Early Intensive Physiotherapy Drives Functional Recovery in Pediatric Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis: A Quantified Case Report.
titre_fr: Early Intensive Physiotherapy Drives Functional Recovery in Pediatric Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis: A Quantified Case Report.
auteurs: Muralidharan Kaviya, Govindhan Santhiya
resume: Structured physiotherapy protocols for pediatric acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) remain inadequately described in the literature, despite persistent neurological deficits occurring in approximately 20% of cases. We report a 13-year-old MOG-antibody-positive male with ADEM who presented with severe bilateral weakness (Manual Muscle Testing 1-3/5), ataxic gait, bladder dysfunction, and complete functional dependence (Functional Independence Measure [FIM]: 55/126). Following medical stabilisation, an 8-phase, 16-week intensive physiotherapy protocol was implemented alongside immunomodulatory therapy, incorporating progressive strengthening, proprioceptive training, balance activities, and task-specific gait rehabilitation based on neuroplasticity and motor learning principles. Outcomes were quantified using 6 validated measures. Walking speed increased by 316% (0.18-0.75 m/s); FIM improved by 60 points (55-115/126); Berg Balance Scale increased by 30 points (18-48/56); Functional Ambulation Category progressed from level 1 (non-functional) to level 5 (independent community ambulation); Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory increased by 40 points (45-85/100); and bladder dysfunction completely resolved. As spontaneous recovery occurs in up to 80% of pediatric ADEM cases and a control condition was absent, functional gains cannot be attributed to the physiotherapy programme alone; however, the breadth and pace of documented recovery across 6 validated domains within 16 weeks provides the first detailed, replicable phased physiotherapy framework for pediatric ADEM with quantified benchmarks that may guide clinical practice and inform future controlled trials.

titre: Feasibility of the outdoor mobility intervention for older adults after hip fracture: a randomised controlled trial with embedded qualitative study in England.
titre_fr: Feasibility of the outdoor mobility intervention for older adults after hip fracture: a randomised controlled trial with embedded qualitative study in England.
auteurs: Sheehan Katie J, Bastas Denise, Creanor Siobhan, Hulme Claire, Lamb Sarah E, Martin Finbarr C, Sackley Catherine, Smith Toby O, Milton-Cole Rhian, Hillsdon Melvyn, Cook Heather, Connors James, Taylor Ellie, Palmer-Welsh Adam, Carter Carina, Godfrey Emma
resume: To assess the feasibility of a randomised controlled trial (RCT) evaluating the clinical- and cost-effectiveness of an intervention designed to enable recovery of outdoor mobility after hip fracture (OUTDOOR). Multicentre pragmatic parallel group individually randomised (1:1 allocation), assessor-blinded, feasibility RCT with embedded qualitative study. Four community rehabilitation services in England, UK. Adults aged ≥60 years able to mobilise outdoors prefracture, surgically treated for hip fracture, returning to own home and with capacity to consent. Individuals requiring ≥2 people for mobility on hospital discharge were excluded. Participants were randomised to usual care or usual care plus OUTDOOR delivered by trained physiotherapists/occupational therapists/rehabilitation support workers. OUTDOOR comprised a goal-oriented outdoor mobility programme, motivational support, a peer-support video and signposting to additional services to support recovery. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, fidelity and acceptability. Patient-reported outcomes included health-related quality of life, activities of daily living, pain, community mobility, falls-related self-efficacy alongside healthcare resource use. Accelerometry data were collected for a participant subset. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, 6 weeks, 12 weeks and where possible, 6 months. Of 691 individuals screened, 250 were eligible, 180 approached, 46 consented and 39 randomised. Retention was 74.4% (29/39) at 12 weeks and 52.4% (11/21) at 6 months. Intervention fidelity showed that motivation and goal-oriented mobility components were delivered in 60.9% (42/69) of sessions, while 75% (12/16) of participants received goal setting, progress review and signposting at least once. Acceptability was high among participants (Theoretical Framework of Acceptability questionnaire median 34; IQR 30, 38; qualitative interviews) and therapists (focus group). Seventeen unrelated adverse events were reported among seven participants. The OUTDOOR intervention was deliverable with fidelity and participant acceptability was high. The trial identified feasible amendments to support progression including strategies to optimise recruitment and retention. ISRCTN16147125.

titre: Feasibility and acceptability of high-intensity interval training for apathy after deep brain stimulation in Parkinson's disease: the HIIT-ing apathy study protocol.
titre_fr: Feasibility and acceptability of high-intensity interval training for apathy after deep brain stimulation in Parkinson's disease: the HIIT-ing apathy study protocol.
auteurs: Musch Karlijn, Beudel Martijn, Gravesteijn Arianne S, van den Heuvel Odile A, de Bruin Jip, Krijger Hélène V, de Groot Vincent, Rietberg Marc B, van Wegen Erwin E H
resume: Apathy is a common and disabling non-motor symptom after subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation (STN-DBS) in persons with Parkinson’s disease (PwP), impairing daily functioning and quality of life (QoL) of both PwP and their caregivers. Pharmacological and stimulation-based treatments are often insufficient, highlighting the need for complementary non-pharmacological approaches such as physical exercise. In the outpatient rehabilitation clinic of Amsterdam University Medical Center (UMC), high-intensity interval training (HIIT) is part of routine rehabilitation due to its time efficiency, safety, tolerability and multiple health benefits. However, its feasibility and acceptability in PwP with apathy following STN-DBS have not been well explored, and its clinical effects are unknown. This pilot study therefore primarily aims to determine the feasibility, acceptability and safety of a structured HIIT programme targeting apathy in PwP following STN-DBS. Clinical outcomes will be assessed on an exploratory basis to inform the potential design of a future randomised controlled trial. A patient and public involvement approach, engaging clinicians, researchers, a patient-researcher and a PwP, informed the development of a protocol for a single-centre, open-label pilot feasibility study. The study will include 10 PwP with clinically relevant apathy (Starkstein Apathy Scale ≥14) following STN-DBS, who will complete an 8-week HIIT programme comprising two physiotherapist-supervised cycle ergometer sessions per week. The target intensity corresponds to a Borg rating of perceived exertion of ≥15 during high-intensity intervals, recorded at the end of each interval. Primary outcomes are feasibility (eg, recruitment and retention), acceptability (eg, tolerability and participant burden) and safety (adverse events and unintended effects), which will be analysed descriptively. As the study is not powered for hypothesis testing, clinical outcomes—including apathy severity, QoL, motor and non-motor symptoms, functioning, activities of daily living, mood and anxiety, fatigue and caregiver burden—are exploratory and will be assessed using pre–post analyses to estimate effect sizes, which will inform the sample size calculation for a future randomised controlled trial. This ongoing study is in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki. The non-WMO Committee of the Medical Ethics Review Committee of Amsterdam UMC judged that the Dutch Medical Research Involving Human Subjects Act (WMO) does not apply, as participants are not subjected to procedures or required to follow rules of behaviour as defined by this Act, and therefore waived formal ethical approval (reference 2024.0155). All participants and their caregivers will provide written informed consent prior to participation.

titre: Efficacy of action observation therapy in patients with dementia or cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
titre_fr: Efficacy of action observation therapy in patients with dementia or cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
auteurs: Lin Ho-Wei, Lu Ching, Chen Sheng-Chang, Liao Chun-De, Lin Lien-Chieh, Hsu Ting-Hsuan
resume: To investigate the therapeutic effects of action observation therapy (AOT) on patients with dementia or cognitive impairment. The authors performed the literature search in the PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases in August 2025. Randomized controlled trials comparing the outcomes of AOT with controls among patients with dementia or cognitive impairment were included. Nine studies involving 348 patients were included in a systematic review, of which seven were included in a meta-analysis. The meta-analysis results revealed that AOT was associated with significantly improved cognitive function [Standard mean differences (SMD) = 0.86, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.53 to 1.19], activities of daily living (SMD = 0.67, 95% CI = 0.22 to 1.12), and naming aphasia (SMD = 0.53, 95% CI = 0.01 to 1.05); with significantly improved motor function (gait velocity [SMD = 0.70, 95% CI = 0.24 to 1.16] and result on the timed up-and-go test [SMD = -1.05, 95% CI = -1.89 to -0.21]) in patients with dementia without stroke; and with significantly improved cognitive function (SMD = 0.96, 95% CI = 0.41 to 1.50) at the 1-month follow-up. AOT may exert beneficial effects for patients with dementia or cognitive impairment.

titre: Sensory-Perceptual impairments and adaptive functioning in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy.
titre_fr: Sensory-Perceptual impairments and adaptive functioning in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy.
auteurs: Cabezas-López Mercedes
resume: Cerebral palsy (CP) is traditionally conceptualized as a disorder of movement and posture resulting from early brain injury. However, increasing evidence highlights that sensory-perceptual impairments may play a fundamental role in adaptive functioning and social participation. Despite this, explanatory models of CP continue to focus primarily on motor dysfunction. To examine the relative contribution of neuromotor and sensory-perceptual impairments to adaptive functioning in children and adolescents with CP and related neurodevelopmental conditions. A cross-sectional retrospective observational study was conducted with 131 children and adolescents (48.9% females), aged 6-17 years (M = 11.18, SD = 3.59). Following their established medical diagnoses, participants were classified into CP and related conditions groups and were assessed using the Gross Motor Function Classification System and the Bobath Foundation Scale. Hierarchical regression analyses were performed to determine whether perceptual-motor functioning accounted for additional variance in functional autonomy, communication and language, and cognitive competence beyond neuromotor impairment. In the CP group, neuromotor impairment was the strongest predictor of functional autonomy (β = .624, p < .001), whereas perceptual-motor functioning made a smaller but significant additional contribution (β = .347, p < .001; ΔR2 = .058). In the related conditions group, perceptual-motor functioning showed a stronger association with functional autonomy (β = .597, p < .001) than neuromotor impairment (β = .287, p = .017; ΔR2 = .188). For communication and language, perceptual-motor functioning emerged as the only significant predictor in both groups (CP: β = .872, p < .001, ΔR2 = .367; related conditions: β = .984, p < .001, ΔR2 = .511), whereas neuromotor impairment was no longer significant after its inclusion in the model. A similar pattern was observed for cognitive competence, with perceptual-motor functioning accounting for substantial additional variance beyond neuromotor impairment (CP: β = .947, p < .001, ΔR2 = .433; related conditions: β = 1.041, p < .001, ΔR2 = .573). These findings suggest that adaptive functioning in CP is associated not only with motor impairment but also with sensory-perceptual functioning. Assessment and rehabilitation approaches should therefore address perceptual-motor processes alongside traditional motor-focused interventions.

titre: Evaluating and predicting independent gait recovery after stroke within the international classification of functioning, disability and health framework.
titre_fr: Evaluating and predicting independent gait recovery after stroke within the international classification of functioning, disability and health framework.
auteurs: Musilová Nicole, Kolářová Barbora, Marková Tereza, Šaňák Daniel, Hluštík Petr, Kolář Petr
resume: Restoration of independent gait is one of the primary goals of rehabilitation care in patients after stroke and significantly influences their functional autonomy and quality of life. Gait impairments result from a complex interaction between structural damage to the central nervous system (CNS), disturbances in body functions, activity limitations, and the influence of environmental factors. This narrative review summarizes current approaches to the assessment and prediction of independent gait recovery within the framework of the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF). Clinical tests such as the Functional Ambulation Categories (FAC), the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for the Lower Extremity (FMA-LE) for sensorimotor examination of the paretic lower limb, the 10-Meter Walk Test (10MWT) for gait speed, the 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT) for gait endurance, and the Trunk Control Test (TCT) for trunk function cover key ICF domains. These valid and reliable tools for evaluating gait also demonstrate substantial predictive value. According to internationally recognized consensus recommendations, a comprehensive assessment should additionally include tests evaluating stability and reactive postural control in standing and during gait, including the Mini-BESTest and the Dynamic Gait Index (DGI), when feasible. This standardized set of measures enables consistent evaluation of functional status in poststroke patients and supports its broader implementation in both clinical practice and research. Furthermore, structured prediction models that allow early patient stratification and improve the accuracy of estimating the likelihood of achieving functionally independent locomotion are increasingly used. The integration of clinical, imaging, and functional indicators within the ICFframework contributes to more precise neurological prognostication and supports individualized rehabilitation planning.

titre: The PagMYBS1-PagCKX1/PagERF113 Module Synergistically Inhibits Xylem Differentiation and Drought Adaption in Populus.
titre_fr: The PagMYBS1-PagCKX1/PagERF113 Module Synergistically Inhibits Xylem Differentiation and Drought Adaption in Populus.
auteurs: Qiao Yongqi, Yu Changhong, Zhang Wanqi, Li Na, Yang Mengxin, Wang Nuoxin, Kong Di, Du Shuhui, Zhao Kai, Wang Shengji
resume: Secondary growth in woody plants requires the coordinated regulation of vascular development and environmental adaptation, yet the transcriptional mechanisms linking hormone homoeostasis with wood formation remain poorly understood. In this study, we identified PagMYBS1, an R2R3-MYB transcription factor of 84 K poplar preferentially expressed in the stem endodermis. Overexpression of PagMYBS1 significantly inhibited vegetative growth, resulting in reduced plant height, xylem width, fibre cell length, and secondary wall thickness, while increasing vessel density. Integrated LC-MS/MS hormone profiling, RNA-Seq, and DAP-Seq analyses indicated that PagMYBS1 regulates stem development through modulation of cytokinin homoeostasis. PagMYBS1 was found to directly bind to the GATAA-box in the promoters of cytokinin oxidase/dehydrogenase genes PagCKX1, thereby activating its expression. In addition, PagMYBS1 directly induced the expression of PagERF113, a regulator of poplar growth and development. Drought assays showed that PagERF113 overexpression increased cellular damage and reduced drought tolerance, whereas PagERF113-RNAi lines displayed enhanced resilience. Further analyses identified a downstream regulatory module in which PagERF113 activates PagMPK3, PagWRKY33, and PagPR-3, linking MAPK signalling and amino sugar metabolism with cell wall remodelling. These results reveal a novel regulatory network involving PagMYBS1-PagCKX1/PagERF113 that plays a critical role in cytokinin homoeostasis, xylem development, and drought adaptation, presenting potential targets for genetic enhancement of stem growth and stress resilience in woody plants.

titre: Brain-computer interfaces in clinical translation: technological advances, clinical practice and future challenges.
titre_fr: Brain-computer interfaces in clinical translation: technological advances, clinical practice and future challenges.
auteurs: Deng Renfu, Deng Bin, Yan Xinwei, Liu Xionghaolan, Wu Canbiao, Liu Gexin, Li Guangli
resume: As a transformative technology in neuroengineering, brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) establish a direct communication pathway between the brain and external devices, independent of peripheral neuromuscular circuits by decoding neural activity and enabling bidirectional feedback. This capability fundamentally reshapes the paradigm of human-machine interaction. Based on the integration depth of neural interfaces, BCIs can be classified into invasive, semi-invasive, and non-invasive approaches, each supporting a range of applications from motor control to cognitive monitoring through multiple paradigms. Despite rapid technological advances, comprehensive reviews examining the clinical implementation of BCIs remain limited. Existing literature often focuses on BCI applications for specific disorders or introduces the recent technological innovations, yet lacks systematic synthesis and critical reflection on real-world clinical translation. To address this gap, the present review provides an overview of the latest clinical applications in BCI, centered on three functional domains: BCI assistive technology, BCI therapeutic and neuromodulation technology, and BCI rehabilitation technology. It further analyzes key challenges hindering clinical adoption, including hardware limitations, signal processing constraints, modality and paradigm design, and integration with neuromodulation therapies. Ethical and societal considerations are also discussed. Finally, we propose future directions aimed at advancing BCI clinical applications, such as the development of novel materials, multimodal fusion strategies, device miniaturization, and the establishment of standardized regulatory frameworks.

titre: Comparative genomic scans identify putative immune-associated candidate regions in Indian indicine cattle compared with European taurine cattle.
titre_fr: Comparative genomic scans identify putative immune-associated candidate regions in Indian indicine cattle compared with European taurine cattle.
auteurs: Ahlawat Sonika, Bagiyal Meena, Singh Ajay, Chhabra Pooja, Arora Reena, Sharma Rekha
revue: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
resume: Indian indicine cattle are adapted to diverse tropical production environments, but the genomic basis of these adaptive and immune-related traits remains incompletely understood. Whole-genome sequencing data from 34 animals representing seven Indian indicine breeds were compared with data from 30 European taurine cattle representing the Holstein-Friesian and Jersey breeds. Because evolutionary lineage, geographic origin and indigenous/exotic status were confounded in the sampling design, the comparative analyses primarily represent indicine-taurine genomic differentiation. Inter-population selection-signature analyses based on the fixation index (F<sub>ST</sub>) and cross-population extended haplotype homozygosity (XP-EHH) identified 825 candidate genes within highly differentiated regions and 500 candidate genes within regions showing positive normalized XP-EHH scores in the indicine group. F<sub>ST</sub> candidate genes showed nominal associations with metabolic and immune-related pathways; however, none remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction. In contrast, eight KEGG pathways associated with XP-EHH candidate genes remained significant after correction (BH-adjusted P < 0.05), including natural killer cell-mediated cytotoxicity, complement and coagulation cascades, graft-versus-host disease, ABC transporters, allograft rejection, folate transport and metabolism, and antifolate resistance. These pathways included candidate genes involved in immune recognition, cellular cytotoxicity, complement regulation and membrane transport, including ULBP17, RAET1G, RAET1L, CD96, KIR3DS1, CFH, CFHR5, C4BPA and TFPI. The detected genomic patterns may reflect a combination of indicine-taurine ancestry, demographic history, breed formation and selection, and therefore cannot be attributed specifically to indigenous status or environmental adaptation. However, these candidate genomic regions and genes may provide a basis for prioritizing genomic loci for future phenotype-association and validation studies, which may help identify informative variants for genome-enabled selection targeting immune-related traits.

titre: Conservation and diversification of pre-mRNA alternative splicing mechanism across kingdoms: A review.
titre_fr: Conservation and diversification of pre-mRNA alternative splicing mechanism across kingdoms: A review.
auteurs: Li Qi, Ma Ligeng, Cao Ying
resume: Pre-messenger RNA splicing is an essential step in eukaryotic gene expression, performed by the spliceosome-a large ribonucleoprotein complex. While alternative splicing vastly expands proteomic diversity and facilitates environmental adaptation, the underlying catalytic and architectural framework remains profoundly conserved across the eukaryotic kingdom. Recent high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy structures have established that the spliceosomal catalytic active site is built upon a conserved RNA triplex: formed primarily by U2 and U6 snRNAs, which supports the coordination of two essential magnesium ions, while potassium ions contribute to active-site organization and catalytic efficiency, reflecting an ancient RNA-based evolutionary origin. This catalytic core is surrounded by an evolutionarily conserved scaffold, most notably PRP8, and driven through a sequential series of ordered assembly, activation, catalysis, and disassembly transitions by conserved DExD/H-box ATPases and RNA helicases. Although the catalytic machinery and snRNP biosynthesis pathways are highly conserved, the peripheral regulatory network has undergone extensive lineage-specific diversification. The budding yeast has a simple spliceosome system dedicated to short, uniform introns; in mammals, a multi-level quality control and proofreading system regulates the splicing of numerous introns; the plants have some unique innovations for regulation, including redundancy of branch point recognition and diversification of catalytic components. Here, we review the chemical basis of spliceosome catalysis, detail the conservation of dynamic assembly cycles and core components, and explore how lineage-specific adaptations of spliceosome regulatory networks balance evolutionary flexibility and functional robustness in eukaryotes.
resume_fr: Pre-messenger RNA splicing is an essential step in eukaryotic gene expression, performed by the spliceosome-a large ribonucleoprotein complex. While alternative splicing vastly expands proteomic diversity and facilitates environmental adaptation, the underlying catalytic and architectural framework remains profoundly conserved across the eukaryotic kingdom. Recent high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy structures have established that the spliceosomal catalytic active site is built upon a conserved RNA triplex: formed primarily by U2 and U6 snRNAs, which supports the coordination of two essential magnesium ions, while potassium ions contribute to active-site organization and catalytic efficiency, reflecting an ancient RNA-based evolutionary origin. This catalytic core is surrounded by an evolutionarily conserved scaffold, most notably PRP8, and driven through a sequential series of ordered assembly, activation, catalysis, and disassembly transitions by conserved DExD/H-box ATPases and RNA helicases. Although the catalytic machinery and snRNP biosynthesis pathways are highly conserved, the peripheral regulatory network has undergone extensive lineage-specific diversification. The budding yeast has a simple spliceosome system dedicated to short, uniform introns; in mammals, a multi-level quality control and proofreading system regulates the splicing of numerous introns; the plants have some unique innovations for regulation, including redundancy of branch point recognition and diversification of catalytic components. Here, we review the chemical basis of spliceosome catalysis, detail the conservation of dynamic assembly cycles and core components, and explore how lineage-specific adaptations of spliceosome regulatory networks balance evolutionary flexibility and functional robustness in eukaryotes.

titre: Simulation-guided design of exotendons to reduce the energetic cost of running.
titre_fr: Simulation-guided design of exotendons to reduce the energetic cost of running.
auteurs: Stingel Jon, Bianco Nicholas, Ong Carmichael, Collins Steve, Delp Scott, Hicks Jennifer
resume: A passive device that attaches to the feet, called an exotendon, can reduce the energetic cost of running at moderate speeds, but its efficacy and optimal design parameters at higher speeds are unknown. Identifying optimal parameters at new speeds experimentally would require many experimental trials with different exotendon designs, which is challenging for participants at higher running speeds. We developed a muscle-driven simulation framework to predict the effect of various exotendon designs on the energetic cost of running at an experimentally untested speed (4 m/s). We used these predictions to select four designs, which we evaluated experimentally as users ran at this speed. The framework correctly predicted that an exotendon that reduced energetic cost at 2.7 m/s would also reduce energetic cost at 4 m/s (10% predicted vs. 5.7% measured) and that a short, stiff exotendon and a long, compliant exotendon would not significantly reduce energetic cost. However, exotendon parameters predicted by the simulation to maximize energetic savings did not significantly reduce energetic cost when evaluated experimentally. There was variability between participants in both the magnitude of maximum energy savings and the exotendon condition associated with those savings. In a 5-km time trial performed with and without the exotendon condition that elicited the largest energy savings for each participant during the experiment, we observed a lower average heart rate (-3.9 ± 3.8 beats/min; P = 0.03; mean ± standard deviation) and increased cadence (15.9 ± 9.6 steps/min; P = 0.002) when participants ran with the exotendon but did not observe a statistically significant difference in finishing time (-13.5 ± 24.6 sec; P = 0.3). These results demonstrate exotendons can reduce energetic cost across multiple running speeds and that predictive simulations provide a framework for guiding experiments to evaluate assistive device designs.

titre: Interventions to improve the safe and effective use of medicines among visually impaired patients: a systematic review.
titre_fr: Interventions to improve the safe and effective use of medicines among visually impaired patients: a systematic review.
auteurs: Habibullah Ahmed, AlHammoud Fadel Mohamed, Habibullah Mahmood, Al-Sallami Hesham S
revue: Journal of pharmaceutical policy and practice
resume: Visual impairment affects over 2.2 billion people globally, posing significant challenges in medication management due to difficulties in reading labels, identifying drugs, and following instructions. This affects adherence and potentially increases the risk of medication errors. Assessing the effectiveness of available interventions is essential to improve medication safety for this population. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, International Pharmaceutical Abstract, and Google Scholar following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A PROSPERO protocol was registered before the search (CRD420250649876). Studies were screened and evaluated by independent reviewers. Data was extracted into a standardised table, and study quality was assessed using study design-specific tools. From 2,112 identified records, seven studies met the inclusion criteria. These studies were conducted in the United States, India, Switzerland, and Thailand. Interventions included AI-powered mobile applications, tactile aids like Braille labels and 3D-printed adaptors, and wireless Radio Frequency Identification (RFID)-based systems. These interventions demonstrated improvements in medication identification, independence, and/or user satisfaction, although study quality and sample sizes varied. A range of innovative and accessible interventions can significantly support medication management in visually impaired populations. However, more robust, large-scale research is needed to validate long-term outcomes and scalability. Incorporating these tools into routine pharmacy practice, alongside regulatory support, could promote safer, more inclusive healthcare delivery.

titre: Genomic evidence of a single domestication origin for modern cattle.
titre_fr: Genomic evidence of a single domestication origin for modern cattle.
auteurs: Miraszek John L, Cooper Alan, Llamas Bastien, Chen Kefei, Mitchell Kieren J, van Loenen Ayla, Heiniger Holly, Souilmi Yassine, Gower Graham, Rowan Harly J, Wrinn Patrick J, Diaz Miranda Edgar A, Facioni Guimarães Simone Eliza, Vasil'ev Sergei, Ovodov Nikoli D, Taylor Jeremy F, Schnabel Robert D, Decker Jared E
revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
resume: Domesticated cattle occur as humpless taurine and humped zebu, historically explained as two independent domestications in the Fertile Crescent and Indus Valley. We question the validity of this model using whole-genome analyses of cattle and their wild relatives, including extinct aurochs. Zebu derives from admixture between domesticated taurine cattle and Indian aurochs and has elevated genomic diversity from an ancient introgression of a gaur-like or banteng-like population into Indian aurochs. We identify selective introgression in zebu from both 238 Indian aurochs-derived genes enriched for environmental adaptation, and 283 taurine-derived genes enriched for domestication loci. We suggest this process was shaped by polygenic selection. Modern cattle diversity traces from a single domestication event, followed by migration, wild introgression, and selection.

titre: Effects of walker grip angle on wrist biomechanics and functional efficiency during sit-to-stand and stand-to-sit transitions in older adults.
titre_fr: Effects of walker grip angle on wrist biomechanics and functional efficiency during sit-to-stand and stand-to-sit transitions in older adults.
auteurs: Yeh PoChan
resume: Walkers are widely prescribed to support sit-to-stand and stand-to-sit transitions in older adults; however, conventional grip designs may increase wrist strain and reduce movement efficiency. Previous studies have focused primarily on wrist loading, paying limited attention to whether grip modification also influences functional performance or produces consistent effects across different transitional movements. This study investigated the effects of walker grip angle on wrist biomechanics and task efficiency during sit-to-stand and stand-to-sit transitions. Thirty-seven right-hand-dominant older adults completed both tasks using a standard walker and a grip-modified walker in a 2 × 2 within-subjects design. Wrist ulnar deviation, wrist extension, peak reaction force, and task completion time were measured. Significant walker type × movement type interactions were observed for right wrist extension, left wrist ulnar deviation, and left wrist extension (p = .002-.008, ηp² = .179-.235), indicating that grip-modification effects differed between sit-to-stand and stand-to-sit. Across movement types, the grip-modified walker reduced task completion time by approximately 14% (p = .045, ηp² = .107) and decreased ulnar deviation in both wrists (p < .01, ηp² = .214-.233), while increasing wrist extension (p < .001, ηp² = .280-.557). Peak reaction force did not differ significantly between walker types. Grip modification improved functional efficiency but did not uniformly reduce upper-limb demand: it reduced frontal-plane wrist deviation while increasing sagittal-plane extension, with the trade-off varying by task. These findings support ergonomically optimized walker grips that account for movement-specific demands and multi-planar wrist biomechanics.

titre: Acceptability and Feasibility of myAccessibleHome: A Mobile Application for Consumer-Directed Home Assessment.
titre_fr: Acceptability and Feasibility of myAccessibleHome: A Mobile Application for Consumer-Directed Home Assessment.
auteurs: Burns Suzanne Perea, Pickens Noralyn Davel, O'Donnell Knudson Laryn, Blough Alethia, Smith Roger O, Mendonca Rochelle
resume: Older adults and people with disabilities overwhelmingly prefer to remain in their own homes, yet environmental hazards contribute to falls and functional decline. This study examined the acceptability and feasibility of myAccessibleHome, a consumer-directed home safety mobile application for people with disabilities and aging adults. A single-arm feasibility trial across four sites enrolled 22 end-users (mean age 69.8; 73% female). Participants completed a self-directed home assessment and received a personalized report and educational videos, followed by a professional in-home evaluation within 2 weeks. PROMIS Self-Efficacy was assessed at baseline, 2 weeks, and 6 weeks; the uMARS and Technology Acceptance Model items were administered at 2 and 6 weeks. uMARS scores averaged 3.91 (SD 1.13), highest for functionality (4.14) and aesthetics (4.08). Self-efficacy increased slightly (+0.11, d = 0.29); 95% would recommend the application and 23% reported minor technical issues. myAccessibleHome demonstrates initial feasibility and acceptability.

titre: Self-care interventions to reduce, prevent or monitor disability in those affected by leprosy: a systematic review.
titre_fr: Self-care interventions to reduce, prevent or monitor disability in those affected by leprosy: a systematic review.
auteurs: Willis Matthew, Asboeck Alexandra, Amorim Bianca B C, Deps Patricia D, Fastenau Anil, Boeckmann Melanie
revue: International journal for equity in health
resume: Self-care is a widely promoted strategy for the prevention and management of disability among people affected by leprosy. However, the content, delivery, and reported outcomes of self-care interventions have not been systematically analysed. This review aimed to identify and describe self-care interventions for people affected by leprosy, assess their outcomes, and map the interventions to the transtheoretical model of behaviour change. A systematic review was conducted across PubMEd, Medline ALL, Web of Science Core Collection, EMBASE, LILACS, and SciELO. Studies were eligible if they reported a peer-reviewed self-care intervention for people affected by leprosy, including self-care interventions delivered within broader interventions. Data were extracted and formulated in an extraction table. Study quality was assessed using the relevant Critical Skills Appraisal Programme checklist. Findings were synthesised narratively. PROSPERO (CRD42025649623). Twenty-four studies were included. The studies were conducted in Brazil, Ethiopia, Nepal, Nigeria, China, India, Mozambique and Indonesia. Interventions included self-care or self-help groups; structured self-care education programmes and prevention of disability programmes; family-based or integrated disability-management interventions; assistive technology or adaptive devices; and tele-health interventions or follow-up. Foot-care was the most consistently reported intervention, and was most often linked to measurable outcomes, including ulcer healing and ulcer prevention. Hand-care and eye-care were more often embedded in larger broad self-care packages and did not report measurable outcomes. Evidence for ulcer impairment and prevention was promising but largely derived from uncontrolled non-randomised trials. Cost evidence for interventions was limited and no randomized control trials for self-care were identified. This review shows that self-care interventions for people affected by leprosy may be effective in reducing disability, especially when they combine practical education, repeated follow-up, peer or family support, provisions of materials and devices, and access to wider health services. However, as shown by the review the evidence base remains limited by a lack of control trials and limited economic data. Future studies should use clearer intervention reporting, longer follow-up, and increased sample sizes to provide more evidence for which models are effective, sustainable, and transferable across leprosy endemic settings.

titre: Fungal laccases: a double-edged sword linking environmental adaptation and pathogenicity.
titre_fr: Fungal laccases: a double-edged sword linking environmental adaptation and pathogenicity.
auteurs: Sim Jahyeon, Kim Chaewon, Park Daul, Abbas Mustansir, Cho Seung-Yeon, Choi Jaeyoung, Lee Kyung-Tae
resume: Laccases (EC 1.10.3.2) are multicopper oxidases that oxidize diverse phenolic and non-phenolic compounds while reducing oxygen to water. Despite their highly conserved catalytic architectures, fungal laccases perform diverse biological functions depending on ecological context. In saprophytic fungi, they contribute to lignin degradation, nutrient acquisition, carbon cycling, and pollutant detoxification, supporting their application in bioremediation, wastewater treatment, biofuel production, and green chemistry. In certain pathogenic fungi, laccases contribute to lineage-specific processes associated with host adaptation and virulence, including melanization and resistance to host-derived stresses, as particularly well characterized in Cryptococcus neoformans. This functional duality highlights fungal laccases as a molecular double-edged sword linking environmental adaptation and pathogenicity. Here, we integrate current knowledge of their evolutionary distribution, structural conservation, regulatory mechanisms, and biological functions with comparative phylogenomic, domain, structural, and protein language model analyses. We propose that divergent laccase functions may arise from regulatory diversification, substrate availability, and ecological context rather than major changes in catalytic architecture. We also discuss advances in recombinant production, protein engineering, and laccase-targeted antifungal strategies, together with challenges limiting industrial implementation. This integrated perspective provides a framework for developing sustainable laccase-based biocatalysts and anti-virulence therapies.

titre: Design priorities for paediatric walkers in India: professional perspectives.
titre_fr: Design priorities for paediatric walkers in India: professional perspectives.
auteurs: Coutinho Franzina, Balaji Ananya, Ragunathan Shabiga, Ponnusamy Ramasubramanian, Krishna Dinesh, Babu Sarath, Prakash S Doss, Nowrouzi-Kia Behdin, Duncan Andrea
resume: Independent mobility is essential for children's participation in education, community life, and social activities. In India, no paediatric walker is specifically designed for Indian children or the contexts in which they live. This study explored rehabilitation providers' perspectives on the limitations of existing paediatric walkers and identified features that may optimise walker design for Indian settings. A qualitative study using reflexive thematic analysis was conducted across four cities in India. Rehabilitation providers, orthotists and equipment vendors, involved in the assessment, prescription, and provision of paediatric mobility devices were recruited through convenience and snowball sampling. Data were collected through focus groups and individual interviews. Fifty-eight participants shared their perspectives over nine focus groups and five individual interviews, in four different Indian cities. Six themes were identified (1): child-friendly design, emphasising attractive, engaging, safe, and easy-to-use walkers (2); customisation, including adjustability for age, diagnosis, growth, and terrain (3); durability, particularly for uneven rural environments and prolonged use (4); functional features, such as harnesses, splints, seating options, braking systems, and improved wheel designs (5); technology integration, including biofeedback, artificial intelligence, and GPS-enabled monitoring; and (6) lightweight construction, supporting portability, transportation, and everyday use. Rehabilitation providers identified several design priorities for a paediatric walker tailored to Indian contexts. These findings provide foundational guidance for the development of paediatric mobility devices that better meet the needs of Indian children and their families.

titre: Heavy Metal Uptake, Signalling, Detoxification and Environmental Adaptation in Plants: Mechanistic Insights and Emerging Mitigation Strategies.
titre_fr: Heavy Metal Uptake, Signalling, Detoxification and Environmental Adaptation in Plants: Mechanistic Insights and Emerging Mitigation Strategies.
auteurs: El-Beltagi Hossam S, Hassan Karim M, Rezk Adel A, Shehata Wael F, Nasser Mohamed A, Al-Dossary Othman, Alsubaie Bader, Abou El-Nasr Mohamed K, Shalaby Tarek A, Farag Reham, Abdelkader Mostafa, Ali Mahmoud A A
resume: Heavy metal contamination has emerged as a widespread environmental problem that threatens ecosystem functioning, biodiversity and plant performance across natural and managed ecosystems. Toxic elements, including cadmium (Cd), lead (Pb), nickel (Ni), zinc (Zn), aluminium (Al) and other potentially hazardous metals, can accumulate in plant tissues, disrupting growth, development, physiological processes and cellular homoeostasis while posing risks to ecological and human health through trophic transfer. Understanding the mechanisms underlying metal uptake, transport, sequestration and detoxification is therefore essential for increasing plant resilience in metal-stressed environments. This review synthesises current knowledge of plant responses to heavy metal stress, integrating physiological, biochemical, cellular, genetic and molecular mechanisms that contribute to tolerance and adaptation. Particular attention is given to the factors regulating metal accumulation and distribution within plants, including species and genotypic variation, soil physicochemical properties, rhizosphere processes, microbial associations and environmental conditions. This review also evaluates recent advances in strategies to mitigate heavy metal toxicity, including nutrient-based approaches, soil amendments, beneficial microorganisms, biostimulants, phytoremediation technologies, rhizosphere engineering and nanotechnology-assisted interventions. Emerging evidence indicates that plant responses to heavy metals are highly species-specific and strongly shaped by plant-microbe-soil interactions, emphasising the importance of integrated and context-dependent management approaches. Despite substantial progress, significant knowledge gaps remain regarding the regulation of metal partitioning, long-term adaptive responses, cross-tolerance mechanisms and the identification of critical thresholds for maintaining plant health under diverse environmental conditions. Future research integrating multiomics technologies, microbiome engineering, molecular breeding and precision remediation strategies will provide new opportunities to strengthen plant resilience and reduce the ecological risks associated with heavy metal contamination. By consolidating current advances and future directions, this review offers a comprehensive framework for understanding plant adaptation to heavy metal stress and for supporting sustainable ecosystem management in contaminated environments.
