titre: Artificial intelligence in diagnostic haematopathology: Current applications in lymph node and bone marrow biopsy diagnosis.
titre_fr: Artificial intelligence in diagnostic haematopathology: Current applications in lymph node and bone marrow biopsy diagnosis.
auteurs: Baloush Razan Abed
revue: Revista espanola de patologia : publicacion oficial de la Sociedad Espanola de Anatomia Patologica y de la Sociedad Espanola de Citologia
resume: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being explored as a supportive tool in diagnostic haematopathology, particularly for the assessment of lymph node and bone marrow biopsies. These specimens require the integrated interpretation of morphology, immunohistochemistry, flow cytometry, cytogenetic and molecular findings, laboratory data, and clinical context. Digital pathology and whole-slide imaging have enabled the development of AI-based methods for image classification, region-of-interest detection, tissue segmentation, cell identification, biomarker quantification, and workflow prioritisation. In lymph node biopsies, AI may assist in distinguishing reactive from neoplastic lymphoid proliferations, supporting lymphoma classification, quantifying immunohistochemical markers, and identifying diagnostically relevant areas. In bone marrow biopsies, potential applications include cellularity estimation, blast and plasma cell quantification, fibrosis assessment, evaluation of haematopoietic lineages, and detection of focal infiltrates. AI may also contribute to multimodal diagnostic models that integrate histological images with ancillary studies and clinical data. However, routine clinical implementation remains limited by the rarity of many diseases, small annotated datasets, variability in tissue characteristics and staining, limited explainability, insufficient external validation, and regulatory challenges. At present, AI should be regarded as an assistive technology rather than a replacement for haematopathologists. Its greatest near-term value lies in improving efficiency, reproducibility, quantification, and quality assurance within an expert-led diagnostic workflow.

titre: Evaluating use of an activity chair to facilitate daily activity engagement while seated.
titre_fr: Evaluating use of an activity chair to facilitate daily activity engagement while seated.
auteurs: Fei Yi Yang, Lefeaux Virginia, Miller William C, Mortenson W Ben
resume: Activity chairs are rehabilitation-grade ergonomic chairs with features such as braking systems and seat elevation. They are designed for individuals with limited standing tolerance or balance. Currently, there is limited research examining outcomes of their use. Our study used a mixed-methods, single-subject design to investigate the subjective and objective impact of activity chairs on activity engagement among adults with standing difficulties. Five people aged 21-65 with disabilities and/or chronic conditions participated, including two women, two men, and an agender individual. Performance measures (i.e., activity duration, fatigue, pain) were reported by participants in daily activity logs for five days prior to and five days after receipt of the chair. Pre-post semi-structured interviews were conducted. Activity chairs were used for dishwashing, cooking, and studying. Quantitative data included satisfaction rating with Wheelchair Outcome Measure (WhOM) and task demand rating with NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX). Qualitative data were analysed using inductive content analysis. Quantitative data were assessed using descriptive, visual, and 2-Standard Deviation (2SD) methods. Compared to baseline, three participants had increased satisfaction and reduced pain and/or fatigue using the chair. One participant had equal satisfaction and fatigue; another participant had decreased satisfaction and increased pain. Four participants had decreased total NASA-TLX score, indicating reduced task demand. Qualitatively, most participants were satisfied with seat elevation features but dissatisfied with mobility and navigation. Activity chairs may facilitate engagement in seated activities for short durations when limitations relate to musculoskeletal fatigue and pain. The device's compatibility with individual user's abilities and context warrants careful consideration.

titre: Complete genome sequence of Micromonospora costi NBMW051 isolated from river sandy soil.
titre_fr: Complete genome sequence of Micromonospora costi NBMW051 isolated from river sandy soil.
auteurs: Wang Yueying, Chen Ling, Luo Xiaoxia, Gong Yan, Wang Kaimei, Zhu Lei
resume: We present the complete genome of Micromonospora costi NBMW051 isolated from sandy soil samples from floodplain. The total length of the genome is 7,176,888 bp and possesses 6,583 protein-coding sequences (CDS). This first complete genome of the species supports studies of environmental adaptation and biosynthetic potential.

titre: DNA Methylation and Alternative Splicing: A Dual-Layer Regulatory Code for Plant Environmental Adaptation.
titre_fr: DNA Methylation and Alternative Splicing: A Dual-Layer Regulatory Code for Plant Environmental Adaptation.
auteurs: Li Min, Liu Yue, Wang Su-Hui, Li Fu-Tian, Tian Yuan, Ding Xin-Hua, Liu Ying-Gao
resume: DNA methylation and pre-mRNA alternative splicing (AS) regulate the expression of plant genes at the transcriptional level and the post-transcriptional level, respectively. Emerging evidence has unveiled an intricate bidirectional interplay between them, bridged by multiple molecular mediators. DNA methylation reshapes splicing patterns by directly modulating RNA polymerase II (Pol II) elongation dynamics and by targeting transposable elements (TEs) to generate alternative promoters, novel splice sites and termination codons, as well as to mediate exon disruption and intron‑exonization. Conversely, splicing factors reciprocally shape DNA methylation by governing the expression and isoform production of methylation-related epigenetic factors, and by engaging in the RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) pathway. This bidirectional regulatory relationship jointly maintains the homoeostatic balance of the plant genome at both the epigenetic and post-transcriptional levels. Furthermore, this review systematically synthesizes the synergistic roles of DNA methylation and AS in plant responses to diverse environmental stresses, as well as their significant contributions to stress memory formation and crop domestication. On this basis, this review discusses the potential applications of multi-omics-based bioinformatic analyses, the mining of epialleles and splicing sites, as well as targeted methylation editing and splicing-site editing in molecular breeding. Overall, the bidirectional regulation between DNA methylation and AS constitutes an important hub within the plant gene regulatory network; in-depth dissection of their synergistic mechanisms will provide novel molecular targets and technical avenues for enhancing crop stress tolerance and designing next-generation breeding strategies.

titre: Comparative genomics reveals contrasting candidate adaptive signatures in two ecologically similar plateau fishes.
titre_fr: Comparative genomics reveals contrasting candidate adaptive signatures in two ecologically similar plateau fishes.
auteurs: Wang Yibang, Huang Yuxiang, Sun Wenyu, Zhang Hui, Matsui Motomu
resume: Plateau aquatic environments expose fishes to chronic cold, hypoxia, ultraviolet radiation and low productivity, providing natural systems for studying genomic features associated with environmental adaptation. Whether related fishes inhabiting similar cold-water plateau environments exhibit comparable or divergent genomic responses remains unclear. We compared two plateau cypriniform fishes, Aspiorhynchus laticeps and Diptychus maculatus, within a 12-species phylogenomic framework, integrating orthogroup inference, gene-family turnover, coding-sequence divergence, chromosome-scale synteny and duplicated gene-pair divergence profiling. The strongest contrasts occurred in species-specific orthogroups and gene-family turnover. Aspiorhynchus laticeps had a larger set of apparent species-specific orthogroups, enriched mainly in oocyte and reproductive processes, and its expanded families and elevated-ω orthogroups were associated with immune, receptor-mediated and membrane-associated functions. By contrast, D. maculatus had fewer species-specific orthogroups enriched for neural and synaptic processes and a contraction-dominated gene-family profile involving host defence, mucosal immunity and chromatin-related processes. The focal contrast did not exceed empirical background variation, and expansion-related computational analysis of gene family evolution (CAFE) estimates were associated with assembly continuity and input-gene properties. These findings indicate that ecologically similar plateau fishes may exhibit different combinations of candidate genomic features, highlighting the joint influence of ecological adaptation and genome history.

titre: The CRISPR-Cas system functions a regulatory module in diverse cellular processes in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi and related Enterobacteriaceae.
titre_fr: The CRISPR-Cas system functions a regulatory module in diverse cellular processes in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi and related Enterobacteriaceae.
auteurs: Villasenor Tomas, Hernandez Victor Manuel, Aguirre-Partida Eira, Vazquez Alejandra, Rivera-Ramirez Abraham, Hernandez-Lucas Ismael
resume: The CRISPR-Cas systems have been traditionally viewed as adaptive immune mechanisms; however, increasing evidence indicates that they also perform broader regulatory functions. Here, we demonstrate that the Type I-E CRISPR-Cas system in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi modulates the expression of key transcriptional regulators, including OmpR and TviA. Furthermore, the CRISPR-Cas system controls critical virulence-associated phenotypes including intracellular replication within human macrophages, bile salt resistance, biofilm formation, and motility. Comparative analyses across members of the Enterobacteriaceae family reveal species-specific contributions of CRISPR-Cas to bacterial physiology and virulence. In Salmonella Typhimurium, its role is largely restricted to bile salt resistance, whereas in enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EHEC) it additionally regulates, bile resistance, biofilm formation and motility. In contrast, no detectable CRISPR-Cas-dependent regulatory function was observed in Citrobacter rodentium or Escherichia coli K-12 under the conditions tested. Despite these differences, CRISPR-Cas systems consistently influence core physiological processes associated with host adaptation and pathogenicity. Collectively, our findings support a model in which CRISPR-Cas systems function as global regulatory module that enhance bacterial fitness and pathogenic potential by fine-tuning traits required for host colonization and environmental adaptation. This expanded functional paradigm underscores the importance of CRISPR-Cas in enteric pathogens and suggests that its contribution to virulence may be more widespread than previously appreciated.

titre: Strigolactones as Integrators of Nutrient Signaling and Root-Microbe Interactions in Plants.
titre_fr: Strigolactones as Integrators of Nutrient Signaling and Root-Microbe Interactions in Plants.
auteurs: Das Abir, Adak Malay Kumar
resume: Strigolactones (SLs) are carotenoid-derived phytohormones that regulate diverse aspects of plant development and environmental adaptation. Beyond their endogenous roles in controlling shoot branching and root system architecture. SLs function as rhizosphere signals that mediate interactions with soil microorganisms. Expanding findings indicate that SLs act as key integrators of nutrient-deficiency signals. Specifically, under phosphorus and nitrogen limitation, they link internal plant signaling networks to external ecological responses. This review synthesizes recent advances in understanding how nutrient availability regulates SL biosynthesis, transport, and exudation, and how these processes influence rhizosphere communication and microbial recruitment. We examine the molecular mechanisms underlying SL-mediated signaling and its crosstalk with other regulatory pathways. These include auxin, abscisic acid, and redox signaling, which modulate root architectural plasticity. We also evaluate the role of SLs in orchestrating the selective recruitment of beneficial soil microorganisms, notably arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi and plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria. We pay particular attention to feedback mechanisms through which microbially mediated nutrient acquisition modulates SL signaling and systemic plant responses. SLs emerge as central coordinators of plant adaptation to nutrient-limited environments by integrating internal signaling networks with rhizosphere interactions. A conceptual framework is proposed in which SLs function at the interface of nutrient sensing, hormone crosstalk, and microbial recruitment to optimize plant performance. Understanding these integrated processes provides new opportunities to improve nutrient-use efficiency and develop sustainable strategies for crop management under changing environmental conditions.

titre: Efficacy of an automated vestibular function diagnosis and treatment system combined with habituation training in refractory benign paroxysmal positional vertigo.
titre_fr: Efficacy of an automated vestibular function diagnosis and treatment system combined with habituation training in refractory benign paroxysmal positional vertigo.
auteurs: Li Yanan, Liu Hui, Gao Yali, Jia Weihua
resume: To evaluate an automated vestibular function diagnosis and treatment system (SRM-IV system) combined with habituation training in patients with refractory benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). Clinical data were collected from 81 patients with refractory BPPV from December, 2023 to December, 2024. Thirty-eight received SRM-IV repositioning plus habituation training (intervention), and 43 received SRM-IV alone (control). Training was remotely supervised for three months. Follow-up was at six months. Residual vertigo duration was shorter in the intervention group (6.7 ± 1.4 vs. 8.9 ± 1.6 days, p < 0.001), and the Dizziness Handicap Inventory score reduction was greater (54.5 ± 12.0 vs. 42.7 ± 11.6, p < 0.001); both were confirmed after adjustment for baseline scores (analysis of covariance, p < 0.001). Recurrence did not differ significantly between groups (28.9% vs. 34.9%, p = 0.64). Hypertension independently predicted recurrence (OR 3.65, 95% CI 1.21 to 11.05, p = 0.022). After excluding hypertensive patients, recurrence was lower in the intervention group (10.7% vs. 33.3%, p = 0.04). Combined habituation training shortened residual vertigo and improved dizziness-related disability in refractory BPPV. The recurrence benefit became evident after excluding patients with hypertension. Blood pressure control may warrant attention in this population.

titre: JAK Inhibition in Refractory Ocular Surface Stevens-Johnson Syndrome.
titre_fr: JAK Inhibition in Refractory Ocular Surface Stevens-Johnson Syndrome.
auteurs: Shi Lisa, Samarawickrama Chameen, Hu Hannah, Wakefield Denis, Comsa Monica, Dai Pei
resume: Chronic ocular inflammation following Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) is a rare but devastating condition that can lead to progressive cicatrisation, corneal failure, and irreversible visual loss despite intensive immunosuppression. Increasing evidence suggests that persistent immune dysregulation, rather than residual structural damage alone, contributes to ongoing ocular surface inflammation in severe disease. We describe a young woman with refractory ocular SJS requiring escalation to JAK inhibition after failure of conventional and biologic steroid-sparing therapy. A 22-year-old woman developed severe mucocutaneous SJS of uncertain trigger, with differential diagnoses including oral contraceptive-associated SJS and Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection. Her disease course was complicated by bilateral ocular involvement with progressive right-sided scarring and persistent inflammatory keratoconjunctivitis affecting the left eye. She also developed small airways disease with ground-glass changes on high-resolution computed tomography consistent with SJS-associated bronchiolitis. Despite prolonged corticosteroid therapy, topical and oral calcineurin inhibition, intravenous Ig (IVIG), and high-dose mycophenolate mofetil, significant ocular inflammation persisted. Steroid-related complications included intractable glaucoma requiring tube surgery, further complicated by post-operative pseudomonal keratitis, as well as steroid-induced osteopenia. Etanercept partially improved her ocular inflammation and facilitated corticosteroid tapering; however, ongoing moderate chronic inflammation continued to prevent corneal graft surgery due to concerns about viability, delaying visual rehabilitation. Given refractory disease despite combined conventional and biologic immunosuppression, treatment was escalated to tofacitinib, which finally allowed tapering of oral prednisolone. We describe the first reported case of severe ocular SJS responding to JAK inhibition, highlighting a promising new therapeutic approach for this potentially devastating condition.

titre: Implementation of cognitive remediation in community care units.
titre_fr: Implementation of cognitive remediation in community care units.
auteurs: Dark Frances, Falvey Olivia, Hutchens Sarah, Higgins Niall
revue: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
resume: BackgroundCognitive Remediation (CR) is an evidence-based intervention targeting neurocognitive deficits in individuals with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. These deficits contribute to poor functional outcomes, yet CR offers opportunities for greater utilisation in routine care.MethodA survey was conducted across 14 Community Care Units (CCUs) in Queensland as part of service benchmarking and quality improvement to assess CR activity, barriers, and staff perceptions.ResultsNine of 14 CCUs reported currently delivering a formal CR program, with a further unit delivering structured cognitive activities without a formal curriculum. Four CCUs reported not currently delivering CR, most commonly citing resourcing and funding constraints, limited access to trained facilitators, and infrastructure limitations. Several sites noted that the cost of training and software licences limited their ability to continue or expand delivery.ConclusionCR is feasible and valued in CCU settings, but access remains uneven due to workforce, funding, and infrastructure constraints. Addressing these barriers may enhance access and sustainability within extended rehabilitation mental health services.

titre: Prosthodontic approaches for Class II malocclusion: A narrative review and proposed classification.
titre_fr: Prosthodontic approaches for Class II malocclusion: A narrative review and proposed classification.
auteurs: Alqarni Abdulaziz M, Babeer Walaa A, Marghalani Thamer Y, Ahmad Shakil
revue: Journal of prosthodontics : official journal of the American College of Prosthodontists
resume: The purpose of this review was to synthesize evidence on prosthodontic management of Class II malocclusion and to propose a classification system based on horizontal overlap severity. A narrative review was conducted on prosthodontic management of Class II malocclusion. Electronic databases (PubMed, MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and OpenAlex) and key prosthodontic journals were searched for English-language articles published between 1980 and 2026, that reported on full-mouth prosthodontic rehabilitation without orthodontic treatment or surgical intervention, as well as relevant narrative reviews addressing prosthodontic management of Class II malocclusion. Fixed prosthodontic rehabilitation may be considered an option for managing Class II malocclusion, but evidence is limited to case reports or author opinions with no strategies based on overjet severity data. A three-category system was proposed to guide restorative decision-making according to horizontal overlap severity. Class II malocclusion requires an individualized, function-driven prosthodontic approach. Conversion to Class I should be considered selectively in cases with favorable horizontal overlap, restorative space, and tooth position, whereas maintaining the existing Class II relationship may be more appropriate when the discrepancy is pronounced. Regardless of the occlusal scheme, rehabilitation should prioritize stable posterior contacts, appropriate anterior guidance, and freedom between centric relation and maximal intercuspal position where indicated. Further long-term clinical studies are needed for the prosthodontic management of Class II malocclusion.

titre: Open Extensor Carpi Radialis Brevis Debridement Augmented by Bioinductive Collagen Implant: Indications and Surgical Technique.
titre_fr: Open Extensor Carpi Radialis Brevis Debridement Augmented by Bioinductive Collagen Implant: Indications and Surgical Technique.
auteurs: Keinath Cassandra, Kasto Johnny, Andrews Erickson, Obinero Chimdi, Dalby Drew, Mahylis Jared, Muh Stephanie
resume: Lateral epicondylitis is a common cause of elbow pain that typically resolves with conservative management. For patients with persistent symptoms and failed nonoperative treatment, surgical intervention may be considered. We describe a surgical technique for open extensor carpi radialis brevis debridement with augmentation using a bovine-derived bioinductive collagen implant. The procedure involves direct visualization and excision of degenerative tendon, followed by extensor carpi radialis longus tendon repair using a suture anchor. A bioinductive patch is secured over the repair using absorbable staples and suture. This technique builds on principles established in rotator cuff repair, where bioinductive implants have shown increased tendon thickness, organized tissue regeneration, and reduced retear rates. Although no studies currently assess the efficacy of collagen augmentation in lateral epicondylitis, its hypothesized benefit lies in enhancing tendon healing and promoting growth of new tissue after debridement. Contraindications include active infection and allergy to implant materials. Postoperative rehabilitation includes early range of motion and gradual strengthening. This technique provides a reproducible approach to augment open extensor carpi radialis brevis debridement and warrants further studies to evaluate the effect of bioinductive patch augmentation and outcomes in patients with recalcitrant lateral epicondylitis.

This technique builds on principles established in rotator cuff repair, where bioinductive implants have shown increased tendon thickness, organized tissue regeneration, and reduced retear rates. Although no studies currently assess the efficacy of collagen augmentation in lateral epicondylitis, its hypothesized benefit lies in enhancing tendon healing and promoting growth of new tissue after debridement. Contraindications include active infection and allergy to implant materials. Postoperative rehabilitation includes early range of motion and gradual strengthening. This technique provides a reproducible approach to augment open extensor carpi radialis brevis debridement and warrants further studies to evaluate the effect of bioinductive patch augmentation and outcomes in patients with recalcitrant lateral epicondylitis.

titre: Advances in spinal cord injury therapeutics: integrating foundational research and clinical innovation.
titre_fr: Advances in spinal cord injury therapeutics: integrating foundational research and clinical innovation.
auteurs: Zou Yunlong, Zhang Qi, Xue Xiaoyu, Liu Zeqi, Yang Keni, Du Liangchao, Dong Jian, Han Sufang, Zhang Haobo, Zhao Jiakang, Shen Aling, Xue Weiwei, Xu Zhuo, Ma Dezun, Yin Huijuan, Li Xing, Shen He, Chen Yanyan, Xiao Zhifeng, Zhao Yannan, Gu Rui, Dai Jianwu
resume: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a devastating condition causing profound neurological deficits and significant global burden. Poor functional recovery stems from the limited regenerative capacity of adult central nervous system neurons and a post-injury inhibitory microenvironment featuring scars and molecular inhibitors. Recent multidisciplinary advances offer promising therapeutic avenues. Advanced multi-omics technologies provide unprecedented insights into spinal cord development and injury responses, revealing cellular heterogeneity and molecular dynamics. Progress in stem cell biology, functional biomaterials for lesion bridging and drug/cell delivery, spinal cord tissue engineering and physical neuromodulation techniques enables novel strategies to enhance regeneration and remodel the injury site. Clinical studies also show incremental progress. This review synthesizes foundational biology, pathophysiology, and these converging engineering and biological approaches, aiming to accelerate the development of effective regenerative therapies for SCI repair.

titre: Music Beyond Rhythm in Parkinson Disease Gait Rehabilitation: A Mechanism-Informed Narrative Review.
titre_fr: Music Beyond Rhythm in Parkinson Disease Gait Rehabilitation: A Mechanism-Informed Narrative Review.
auteurs: Chen Jiameng, Hu Yinhu, Song Lei, Jin Juan, Yang Nanhua, Wang Jue, Hu Zekai, Lin Xuewen, Zhuang Jie, Meng Tingting
resume: Rhythmic auditory cueing can improve selected gait outcomes in Parkinson disease (PD), but whether liking, familiarity, groove, or personal relevance adds benefit beyond matched rhythm remains unresolved. This mechanism-informed narrative review considers literature published through August 31, 2026 and distinguishes immediate on-cue response, off-cue response, delayed retention, and free-living mobility. Five small, single-session PD gait studies compared music with a nonmusical rhythmic cue while controlling at least tempo. Within-subject comparisons and tempo control strengthen interpretation, but incomplete matching of beat salience, expectancy, instructions, and cognitive demand limits attribution. Findings include acute advantages for selected music conditions and comparisons with no clear difference; nonsignificant differences do not establish equivalence. These experiments do not establish durable incremental benefit. Longer music-based interventions can increase walking during use, but their multicomponent designs do not isolate music from rhythm, adaptation, or feedback. No included study demonstrated a music-specific mediated effect on gait or established prospective mediation from liking through engagement and practice dose to retention. Evidence for auditory cueing as an intervention should therefore be distinguished from proof of a shared rhythmic causal mechanism. Incremental music-associated benefits remain possible and require rhythm-matched longitudinal comparisons and temporally ordered process measurements.

titre: Effect of suspension core muscle training versus pressure biofeedback training in the treatment of chronic mechanical low back pain: a three-arm randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Effect of suspension core muscle training versus pressure biofeedback training in the treatment of chronic mechanical low back pain: a three-arm randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Turky Eman Ramadan Abdelsatar Abo, Abdelmajeed Salwa Fadl, Abd Allah Dina S
resume: Chronic mechanical low back pain (CMLBP) is a prevalent musculoskeletal condition associated with impaired daily functioning, reduced work productivity, and poorer quality of life. To compare the effects of suspension core training, pressure biofeedback-guided core training, and advice-only care in patients with CMLBP. Forty-eight participants were randomly allocated to suspension core training (SCT), pressure biofeedback-guided core training (PBT), or an advice-only control group (n = 16 each). The SCT and PBT groups received supervised training three times weekly for four weeks. Primary outcomes were pain intensity and active lumbar extension range of motion. Secondary outcomes were active lumbar flexion range of motion, functional disability, core muscle activation capacity, core muscle endurance, and lumbopelvic movement patterns. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and after four weeks. After adjustment for baseline values, significant treatment effects were found for all continuous outcomes (all p < 0.001). Adjusted NPRS scores were 1.34, 1.87, and 4.54 in SCT, PBT, and control groups, respectively. Adjusted lumbar flexion ROM was 6.28, 5.82, and 4.68 cm in SCT, PBT, and control groups, respectively, and adjusted lumbar extension ROM was 2.75, 2.12, and 1.69 cm, respectively. Adjusted ODI scores were 11.47, 16.83, and 28.24, respectively. SCT showed significantly better outcomes than PBT in ODI, lumbar extension ROM, and all core endurance tests. No significant differences were found between SCT and PBT in pain intensity, lumbar flexion ROM, core muscle activation capacity, or lumbopelvic movement patterns. Both supervised groups showed clinically meaningful improvements in pain and disability, whereas the control group did not. Both suspension core training and pressure biofeedback-guided core training produced beneficial short-term effects compared with advice alone in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain. Suspension core training showed additional benefits in selected outcomes, particularly lumbar extension range of motion and core muscle endurance; however, it was not consistently superior across all outcomes. Given the small sample size, short intervention period, and absence of follow-up, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in larger trials with longer follow-up. Retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07448766; first posted/registered: 19/02/2026).

titre: Motor imagery-based brain-computer interface training for upper-limb rehabilitation after subacute stroke: A randomized sham-controlled trial.
titre_fr: Motor imagery-based brain-computer interface training for upper-limb rehabilitation after subacute stroke: A randomized sham-controlled trial.
auteurs: Tong Qifeng, Wu Jianing, Fan Pengcheng, Cai Sunyue, Wang Minzhe, Gong Jianqiu, Wu Fangchao
resume: To determine whether motor imagery (MI) based brain-computer interface (BCI) training improves upper-limb motor function in patients with subacute stroke compared with a high-fidelity sham-BCI control, and to explore accompanying structural and resting-state functional MRI changes. In this participant-blinded randomized controlled trial, 32 patients with subacute stroke were randomized to a MI-based BCI group or a high-fidelity BCI sham-control group (n = 16 each). Both groups received dose-matched training (30 min/session, 5 sessions/week for 4 weeks) in addition to standard rehabilitation. Upper-limb motor outcomes were assessed using the Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity (FMA-UE; primary outcome), Wolf Motor Function Test (WMFT), Motor Assessment Scale (MAS), and Modified Barthel Index (MBI). Structural MRI and resting-state functional MRI were acquired at baseline and post-intervention to assess gray matter volume (GMV) and functional connectivity (FC). Both groups showed significant improvement after the intervention. Compared with the sham-control group, the MI-based BCI group demonstrated greater gains in FMA-UE and secondary motor outcomes (WMFT and MAS), whereas the difference in MBI was not statistically significant. Voxel-based morphometry revealed a within-group increase in GMV in the contralesional supplementary motor area (SMA) in the MI-based BCI group; however, no significant between-group GMV difference was observed. The MI-based BCI group also exhibited increased resting-state FC between the SMA and the ipsilesional cerebellar lobule IX and fusiform gyrus. Changes in FC were associated with improvements in FMA-UE, WMFT, and MBI, but not MAS. Compared with a high-fidelity sham-control group, MI-based BCI group training was associated with greater upper-limb motor recovery in patients with subacute stroke, accompanied by changes in structural and functional neuroimaging measures involving motor-related regions and connections. Larger randomized controlled trials with longer follow-up are required to confirm durability and clinical relevance. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2100052452.

titre: A mHealth-Based Vestibular Rehabilitation Program for Postoperative Vestibular Dysfunction in Patients With Vestibular Schwannoma: Randomized Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: A mHealth-Based Vestibular Rehabilitation Program for Postoperative Vestibular Dysfunction in Patients With Vestibular Schwannoma: Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Zhang Dongmei, Zhu Furong, Wu Peixia, Cheng Guiqing, Ye Xiaonan, Liu Ying, Gu Xuyan, Ma Ziling
resume: Patients with vestibular schwannoma often experience postoperative vestibular dysfunction, including vertigo, dizziness, and imbalance, which severely impair daily functioning and quality of life. Effective and accessible rehabilitation strategies are needed to improve recovery after surgery. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a mobile health-based vestibular rehabilitation program in improving postoperative vestibular outcomes after unilateral vestibular schwannoma surgery. A prospective randomized controlled trial comparing a customized mobile app-based vestibular rehabilitation program with standard face-to-face vestibular rehabilitation was conducted at the Otology Center, Eye & ENT Hospital, Fudan University, from October 2023 to May 2025. A total of 60 patients undergoing unilateral vestibular schwannoma surgery were enrolled and randomly assigned to either an intervention group (n=30) or a control group (n=30). Both groups received a 90-day vestibular rehabilitation program. The intervention group received guidance, symptom recording, and adherence monitoring through a customized mobile app, whereas the control group received face-to-face guidance. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in the change in Dizziness Handicap Inventory (DHI) score from baseline (preoperative) to postoperative day 90. Secondary outcomes included visual analog scale scores for vestibular symptoms and the incidence of vertigo, dizziness, vestibulo-visual symptoms, and postural symptoms. Of the 60 randomized participants, 52 (86.7%) had DHI scores available at postoperative day 90, and 49 (81.7%) had paired baseline and day-90 DHI scores available to calculate the primary outcome. The adjusted between-group difference in DHI change from baseline to postoperative day 90 was not significant (adjusted mean difference -0.83, 95% CI -8.79 to 7.13; P=.84). No significant differences were observed in visual analog scale scores at postoperative days 7, 30, or 90 (all P>.05). Among the assessed vestibular symptoms, postural symptoms on postoperative day 7 were reported by 53.3% (16/30) of the intervention group and 83.3% (25/30) of the control group; the difference was not significant after Holm adjustment (unadjusted P=.03; Holm-adjusted P=.30). In conclusion, mobile health-based rehabilitation did not demonstrate greater improvement in postoperative vestibular outcomes than face-to-face rehabilitation following unilateral vestibular schwannoma surgery. The lower proportion of patients reporting postural symptoms on postoperative day 7 remains an exploratory finding requiring confirmation in future studies. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2200056123; https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=150939.

titre: Trigger-point injections for post-mastectomy pain syndrome: a randomized double-blind controlled trial.
titre_fr: Trigger-point injections for post-mastectomy pain syndrome: a randomized double-blind controlled trial.
auteurs: Leite Victor Figueiredo, Andrade Rodrigo Guimarães de, Siena Wilian Carlos, Freitas Rafael Pereira de, Resende Giovana de Andrade, Brito Christina May Moran de
resume: To evaluate the efficacy of trigger-point injections in individuals with post-mastectomy pain syndrome when combined with interdisciplinary rehabilitation and pharmacological treatment. Study design: Double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial. Participants with post-mastectomy pain syndrome were randomized to receive three weekly trigger-points, injections (active versus sham), combined with rehabilitation and pharmacological treatment. Primary outcomes included pain intensity measured by the numerical rating scale (NRS, 0-10), the number of active trigger points, and pressure pain thresholds across six predefined bilateral muscles. Assessments were performed at baseline and at 1 and 3 months post-intervention. Secondary outcomes included measures of neuropathic pain, central sensitization, disability, and shoulder range of motion. Seventy one patients were enrolled, with a median pain duration of 13 months. At baseline, mean NRS was 7.0±1.5, neuropathic pain was present in 74.7%, central sensitization in 78.9%, and patients had an average of 3.8±1.7 active trigger points. No between-group differences were observed in NRS at any time point. At 1 month, pressure pain threshold in the ipsilateral upper trapezius muscle favored the Control Group (active=0.12±0.89 versus control=0.71±1.02; p=0.048). Conversely, the number of active trigger-points. was lower in the Active Group (active=1.95±2.28 versus control=3.00±2.11; p=0.048). No significant differences were found in secondary outcomes. The addition of three weekly trigger-point injections to a rehabilitation and pharmacological treatment program for PMPS did not yield clinically meaningful improvements in pain or functional outcomes at 1 or 3 months. NCT04267315.

titre: Associations between white matter network alterations and visuospatial and social-emotional deficits in patients with right hemisphere tumors: a prospective clinico-radiological study.
titre_fr: Associations between white matter network alterations and visuospatial and social-emotional deficits in patients with right hemisphere tumors: a prospective clinico-radiological study.
auteurs: Lihi Abir, Clavreul Anne, Aubin Ghislaine, Besnard Jérémy, Girot Jean-Baptiste, Bernard Florian, Delion Matthieu, Allain Philippe, Menei Philippe, Lemée Jean-Michel
resume: Preserving neurological function is crucial in brain tumor surgery. Because the right hemisphere supports visuospatial and social‑cognitive abilities, damage may affect quality of life. This prospective study (TANGO; ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04288505) examined associations between visuospatial and social‑emotional deficits and tractography‑based white matter alterations in patients with right hemisphere tumors. Thirty‑four patients were assessed preoperatively and 22 postoperatively using diffusion magnetic resonance imaging and four neuropsychological tests. Tractography metrics were extracted for nine right hemisphere tracts. Thirty‑four Human Connectome Project participants served as controls. Preoperatively, deficits in visuospatial functioning, facial emotion recognition, and mentalizing were associated with predominantly right hemisphere microstructural abnormalities within distributed white matter networks. Visuospatial deficits were associated with alterations involving the frontal aslant tract (FAT), arcuate fasciculus (AF), superior longitudinal fasciculus (SLF), and SLF II; facial emotion recognition deficits with the SLF III and uncinate fasciculus (UF); and mentalizing deficits with the AF. Postoperatively, exploratory findings suggested associations between new social-emotional deficits and structural alterations involving the inferior longitudinal fasciculus (ILF), SLF, and SLF III, whereas new visuospatial deficits showed a trend toward reduced right FAT volume. Relative to controls, left hemisphere tractographic changes were observed regardless of the presence of visuospatial and/or social-emotional deficits, whereas right hemisphere alterations were primarily observed in patients with such deficits. These findings highlight the role of right hemisphere networks in supporting visuospatial and social-emotional functioning. Further characterization of white matter connectivity may help improve risk stratification, surgical planning, and rehabilitation strategies.

titre: Effects of telerehabilitation pelvic floor muscle training on urinary incontinence in patients with multiple sclerosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
titre_fr: Effects of telerehabilitation pelvic floor muscle training on urinary incontinence in patients with multiple sclerosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
auteurs: Yan Hui
resume: Telerehabilitation-based pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) may improve urinary incontinence in patients with multiple sclerosis (MS), but its effectiveness remains uncertain. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted, including randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with telerehabilitation PFMT as the intervention. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for eligible English-language studies published up to November 15, 2024. The revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials was used to assess the risk of bias, and data were analyzed using Stata 16.1. Three RCTs involving 100 participants were included in the meta-analysis, showing that telerehabilitation PFMT significantly improved urinary incontinence symptoms (weighted mean difference [WMD] = -2.53, P < .001) and bladder overactivity (WMD = -7.13, P < .001). However, no significant improvement was found in quality of life (WMD = -0.88, P = .002). Sensitivity analysis confirmed the stability of the results with no significant publication bias. Telerehabilitation PFMT demonstrated positive effects on urinary incontinence and bladder overactivity in MS patients, although its impact on quality of life remains unclear. Further large-scale, high-quality RCTs are needed to confirm long-term efficacy and guide the development of clinical guidelines for telerehabilitation in MS rehabilitation.

titre: Frailty management in patients with heart valve disease: a scoping review.
titre_fr: Frailty management in patients with heart valve disease: a scoping review.
auteurs: Yuan Wenhui, Han Qiong, Dong Peihuang, Zheng Xinglin, Chen Yuan, Wu Linjing
resume: This study aims to identify, evaluate, and summarise evidence on frailty management in patients with valvular heart disease to inform the development of frailty management programs for clinical practice. This study adheres to the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) framework and is reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines to guarantee methodological strictness and transparency. The system searched multiple databases and websites to gather evidence on the management of frailty in patients with heart valve disease. The search covered the period from the database's inception to October 2026. Literature screening, quality assessment, evidence extraction, and synthesis were conducted independently by two researchers, and the evidence was graded using the JBI Evidence Grading System (2014 edition). After a rigorous literature screening process, a total of 28 publications were included, comprising 3 clinical guidelines, 12 expert consensus documents, 1 systematic review, 1 evidence summary, 6 observational studies, 4 randomised controlled trials, and 1 quasi-experimental study. Through a systematic synthesis of the included literature, a total of 46 pieces of evidence were ultimately compiled, covering five areas: identification and screening assessment of the risk of frailty, comprehensive management, exercise rehabilitation management, multidimensional support management, and continuity of rehabilitation care. titre: Effects of exercise interventions on physical fitness, fatigue, and quality of life in adult hematologic malignancy patients receiving hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a network meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effects of exercise interventions on physical fitness, fatigue, and quality of life in adult hematologic malignancy patients receiving hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a network meta-analysis.
auteurs: Xiaoxuan Li, Shanshan Li, Huili Cai, Xule Zong, Rui Yan, Jiemin Qin, Xiaopeng Xia
revue: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
resume: Patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) experience significant declines in physical fitness, fatigue, and quality of life (QoL). The optimal exercise modality to address these issues remains unclear. This network meta-analysis (NMA) compared the effects of different exercise interventions on physical fitness, fatigue, and QoL in this population. We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and CINAHL from inception to January 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating structured exercise interventions in adult HSCT patients were included. A NMA was performed using Stata 19.0, with effect sizes calculated as standardized mean differences (SMD) or mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) was used to rank interventions. Twenty RCTs involving 1,886 patients were included. For QoL, inspiratory muscle training (IMT) was the only intervention showing significant improvement compared with usual care (SMD = 0.54, 95% CI [0.04, 1.04]), with the highest SUCRA value (0.455). For fatigue, supervised combined exercise (SCE) (SMD =  - 0.39, 95% CI [ - 0.67, - 0.12]) and multidirectional walking/exergaming/whole body vibration (MDW/EXG/WBV) (SMD =  - 0.66, 95% CI [ - 1.29, - 0.04]) were significantly effective; MDW/EXG/WBV ranked highest (SUCRA = 0.691). For physical fitness, SCE significantly improved 6-min walk test (MD = 46.24 m, 95% CI [20.87, 71.61]) and peak oxygen uptake (MD = 2.37, 95% CI [0.56, 4.19]), ranking first for VO<sub>2</sub>peak (SUCRA = 0.919). MDW/EXG/WBV showed the greatest improvement in handgrip strength (MD = 11.9 kg, 95% CI [6.34, 17.46]; SUCRA = 0.992). No intervention significantly improved 30-s sit-to-stand test. This NMA suggests that different exercise modalities may have differential effects on distinct outcomes in HSCT recipients. Supervised combined exercise showed the greatest improvements in cardiorespiratory fitness measures, while multidirectional walking/exergaming/whole body vibration ranked highest for fatigue reduction and handgrip strength improvement. Inspiratory muscle training was the only intervention associated with statistically significant QoL improvement, although this finding should be interpreted with caution given the moderate SUCRA value and wide confidence interval. These findings provide preliminary evidence to inform the selection of exercise modalities within individualized rehabilitation planning; however, the present analysis did not directly evaluate whether outcome-guided or individualized prescription strategies improve clinical outcomes compared with uniform exercise programs, and future confirmatory studies with head-to-head comparisons are needed before practice-changing recommendations can be made.

titre: Which elements of pulmonary rehabilitation improve physical activity and sleep in COPD? A systematic review and component network meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Which elements of pulmonary rehabilitation improve physical activity and sleep in COPD? A systematic review and component network meta-analysis.
auteurs: Orme Mark W, Manifield James, Latimer Lorna, Daynes Enya, Freeman Suzanne C, Xu Jason, Ward Sarah, Haris Muhammed, Bakali Majda, Reap Sophie, Iqbal Mamoon, Wang Lin, Mavilakandy Akash, Olaiya Aarinola, Aung Hnin, Harvey-Dunstan Theresa C, Whelan Maxine E, Singh Sally J, Greening Neil J, Evans Rachael A, Steiner Michael C, Sutton Alex J, Ward Thomas J C
revue: European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society
resume: Physical activity (PA) predicts both mortality and morbidity. Pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) is known to improve exercise capacity and quality of life, but it's impact on PA remains unclear. Likewise, it is uncertain which components of PR elicit the greatest response. To use component network meta-analysis (cNMA) to investigate the relative contribution of exercise modality and intensity, nonexercise components, type of supervision and programme duration of PR on PA and sleep behaviour for people with COPD. Medline, Embase, Cinahl and Cochrane databases were searched with no date or language restrictions. We included randomised controlled trials with an intervention involving exercise for people with COPD that measured PA or sleep behaviour as an outcome. A random-effects additive cNMA assessed the relative effectiveness of PR components on steps·day-1. Certainty of evidence was based on Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations (GRADE). 50 studies (n=4136) reported a PA outcome and four studies reported a sleep outcome (n=638). The 34 studies measuring steps·day-1 were included in a cNMA (n=3039). PA increased following lower limb aerobic exercise (695 steps·day-1, 95% credible interval (CrI) 510-898; high certainty), strength training (390 steps·day-1, 95% CrI 63-811; low certainty), PA tracking (e.g. pedometers; 938 steps·day-1, 95% CrI 688-1480; low certainty). In-person supervised (-669 steps·day-1, 95% CrI -845--452; very low certainty) and remotely supervised (-685 steps·day-1, 95% CrI -1124--174; low certainty) programmes resulted in smaller changes in step count than unsupervised programmes. A meta-analysis of sleep outcomes was not possible due to the low number of studies reporting sleep as an outcome and heterogeneity in outcome measures used.

titre: Long-term rehabilitation needs of survivors of conflict-related sexual violence in Kosovo: a scoping review of challenges and policy directions.
titre_fr: Long-term rehabilitation needs of survivors of conflict-related sexual violence in Kosovo: a scoping review of challenges and policy directions.
auteurs: Limani Merita, Istrefi Remzije, Limani Meli, Uwizeye Glorieuse
resume: More than two decades after the 1998-1999 Kosovo conflict, survivors of conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV) continue to experience profound long-term consequences across physical health, mental health, psychosocial wellbeing, economic stability, and social stigma. Despite landmark policy advances, including the 2014 legal status recognition, rehabilitation responses remain fragmented, under-resourced, and heavily dependent on the non-governmental sector. This scoping review maps the existing evidence on the long-term rehabilitation needs of CRSV survivors in Kosovo and identifies system-level barriers impeding access to comprehensive rehabilitation. A scoping review was conducted following the Arksey and O'Malley framework, with reporting guided by the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, supplemented by a targeted grey literature search using systematic methods Godin et al. across institutional websites and Google Advanced Search. Records were screened against Population-Concept-Context(PCC) eligibility criteria. Data were charted using a standardized extraction form and synthesized thematically across five rehabilitation domains. A total of 37 sources were included: 19 peer-reviewed studies and 18 grey literature documents, including research and policy documents, government reports, non-governmental organization (NGO) reports, UN reports, and program evaluations. Sources spanned 2000-2025. Thematic synthesis identified five domains of unmet rehabilitation need: mental health and psychosocial wellbeing, physical health, legal and rights-based access, economic rehabilitation, and community reintegration. Four cross-cutting structural barriers were identified: the gap between legal recognition and substantive rehabilitation entitlements; NGO-state service dependency; stigma as a structural barrier; and unaddressed intergenerational trauma. The findings further highlight delayed accountability for CRSV as a critical constraint on rehabilitation. Kosovo's CRSV rehabilitation landscape is characterized by substantial policy progress alongside persistent implementation gaps. Comprehensive survivor-centered rehabilitation requires institutionalization of services within the national health and social welfare system, a rights-based approach that links recognition to substantive entitlements, community-level norm change, and expanded attention to long-term and intergenerational impacts of trauma. Findings offer transferable lessons for other post-conflict settings where CRSV survivors remain underserved.

titre: Comparative efficacy of different rehabilitation exercise interventions on upper limb function and lymphedema in postoperative breast cancer patients: a network meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Comparative efficacy of different rehabilitation exercise interventions on upper limb function and lymphedema in postoperative breast cancer patients: a network meta-analysis.
auteurs: Li Fangyu, Long Yanmei, Deng Libang, Shu Qingxia, Peng Hui, Li Jinxiu
resume: While surgery is a cornerstone of breast cancer (BC) treatment, it frequently leads to postoperative complications such as upper limb dysfunction and lymphedema(LE). These sequelae are prevalent and profoundly diminish patients' recovery and quality of life (QoL). Although rehabilitation exercise has proven effective, the comparative superiority of different exercise protocols remains to be elucidated. This study aimed to first systematically evaluate the aggregate efficacy of rehabilitation exercise interventions for postoperative breast cancer patients. Subsequently, we employed a network meta-analysis to delineate the comparative efficacy of different rehabilitation modalities, with the ultimate goal of informing the identification of an optimal protocol. We systematically searched seven English and Chinese databases, including PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, from their inception to December 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating rehabilitation exercise interventions were included. The Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB-2) tool was used to assess bias risk, and R software was employed for the network meta-analysis. Continuous outcomes were expressed as mean difference (MD) or standardized mean difference (SMD), and dichotomous outcomes as odds ratios (OR). The Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking Area (SUCRA) was used to rank interventions. This study protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251243892). A total of 14 RCTs involving 2207 patients were included. For reducing lymphedema incidence, SUCRA-based ranking favored Structured Self-Management/Education (SSM/E, SUCRA = 98.5%), followed by Progressive Resistance Training (PRT, SUCRA = 75.2%) and Comprehensive Exercise (CE, SUCRA = 35.1%). Although SSM/E ranked highest according to SUCRA values, this result was based on evidence from only one small randomized controlled trial (RCT), and the certainty of the evidence for SSM/E was low. Network meta-analysis suggested that SSM/E improved upper limb function (DASH score), however, this finding was derived from only two studies. Due to substantial heterogeneity in measurement tools and reporting methods, other outcomes were synthesized qualitatively. The narrative evidence suggested that CE may improve shoulder range of motion, and that SSM/E, PRT, and CE may improve quality of life. The evidence regarding pain relief was inconclusive. Rehabilitation exercise interventions have been associated with improved functional recovery, reduced risk of LE, and enhanced QoL in postoperative BC patients. SSM/E showed potential benefits in reducing LE incidence; however, this finding was based on only one RCT and should be interpreted with caution. PRT showed more consistent effects across the included comparisons. More high-quality RCTs with standardized intervention protocols and outcome assessments are required to establish the relative effectiveness of rehabilitation strategies. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251243892.

titre: Pulmonary rehabilitation following exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
titre_fr: Pulmonary rehabilitation following exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
auteurs: Weber Manuel, Gimeno-Santos Elena, Wuyts Marieke, Herrero-Cortina Beatriz, Troosters Thierry, Puhan Milo A
revue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
resume: Guidelines have provided positive recommendations for pulmonary rehabilitation after severe exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), but results are heterogeneous and new randomised controlled trials (RCTs) continue to be published. To assess the effects of pulmonary rehabilitation after COPD exacerbations on hospital admissions (critical outcome) and other important and patient-centred outcomes (mortality, health-related quality of life (HRQL) and exercise capacity). We identified studies through searches of the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE ALL, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov and the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (WHO ICTRP). Searches were current to 2 June 2026. RCTs comparing pulmonary rehabilitation of any duration (at least exercise training but no minimum number of exercise sessions) after exacerbation of COPD versus usual care were eligible. Usual care groups received conventional community care without rehabilitation. The four main outcomes were hospital readmissions, mortality, HRQL and exercise capacity. We assessed the risk of bias in the included RCTs as high, low or unclear, using the Cochrane RoB 1 tool. We expected substantial heterogeneity across trials due to the diversity of rehabilitation programmes (i.e. number of completed exercise sessions; type, intensity and supervision of exercise training; and patient education), duration of follow-up (under three months versus three months or longer) and risk of bias (random sequence generation, allocation concealment and blinding). Therefore, we conducted prespecified subgroup analyses. We used random-effects models and standard Cochrane methods for this update, and assessed the certainty of evidence using GRADE. For this update, we added 20 studies and included a total of 40 studies (2825 participants). Rehabilitation programmes showed great diversity in terms of exercise training (number of completed exercise sessions; type, intensity and supervision), patient education (from none to extensive self-management programmes) and how they were organised (within one setting, e.g. pulmonary rehabilitation, to across several settings, e.g. hospital, outpatient centre and home). In 12 studies, participants completed extensive pulmonary rehabilitation, and in 25 studies, participants completed pulmonary rehabilitation ranging from not extensive to moderately extensive. We could not determine how extensive the programmes were in three studies, owing to missing information. Thirteen studies (1229 participants) contributed data on hospital readmissions, with follow-up ranging from three months to 18 months. Moderate-certainty evidence indicates that pulmonary rehabilitation after an exacerbation likely reduces the risk of hospital readmission when compared with usual care (pooled odds ratio (OR) 0.52, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.32 to 0.84; I<sup>2</sup> = 69%). Twenty-two studies (1677 participants) contributed data on all-cause mortality, but only 11 trials (1196 participants) were included in the pooled effect estimate because the remaining studies reported no deaths in either group. Follow-up in these studies ranged from the duration of the hospital stay to 48 months. Low-certainty evidence suggests that pulmonary rehabilitation after an exacerbation may reduce all-cause mortality slightly when compared with usual care (pooled OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.49 to 1.43; I<sup>2</sup> = 33%). Twelve studies (1118 participants) used the St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) to assess HRQL, with follow-up ranging from the duration of the hospital stay to 12 months. High-certainty evidence indicates that, when compared with usual care, pulmonary rehabilitation after an exacerbation results in a large improvement in HRQL, as measured by the SGRQ total score (mean difference (MD) -9.05, 95% CI -12.60 to -5.50; I<sup>2</sup> = 70%), exceeding the minimal important difference (MID) of four points. There was evidence of a difference between pulmonary rehabilitation and usual care for the SGRQ activity and impacts domains (effects exceeding the MID), but no evidence of a difference for the symptoms domain. Twenty-two studies (1464 participants) used the six-minute walk distance (6MWD) to assess exercise capacity, with follow-up ranging from four days to 208 weeks. High-certainty evidence indicates that pulmonary rehabilitation after an exacerbation results in a large improvement in 6MWD when compared with usual care (MD 57.79 m, 95% CI 41.68 to 73.91; I<sup>2</sup> = 89%). Heterogeneity appeared to be driven mainly by differences between studies showing very large effects and those showing smaller effects but still evidence of between-group differences. The overall results of this review have not changed to an important extent compared with results reported in the previous version of this review. Overall, the risk of bias was judged to be low or unclear across most domains. However, the lack of participant blinding raised concerns for subjectively reported outcomes (HRQL). High risks of selection bias and attrition bias were identified in a small number of studies, while a larger proportion of studies were at high risk for reporting bias. Egger's test indicated evidence of funnel plot asymmetry for hospital readmission (P = 0.02) and mortality (P = 0.02), but not for SGRQ (P = 0.45) or the six-minute walk test (P = 0.12). Visual inspection suggested that the asymmetry was more consistent with small-study effects than with clear evidence of missing negative studies. Moderate-certainty evidence indicates that pulmonary rehabilitation likely reduces hospital readmissions, while evidence for mortality is of low certainty. However, some recent studies showed no benefit of rehabilitation on hospital readmissions and mortality. Such heterogeneity of effects on hospital readmissions and mortality may be explained to some extent by the extensiveness of rehabilitation programmes and by the methodological quality of the included studies. High-certainty evidence shows moderate to large effects of pulmonary rehabilitation on HRQL and exercise capacity in people with COPD after an exacerbation. While additional RCTs comparing rehabilitation to no rehabilitation seem questionable scientifically and ethically, future research must investigate how rehabilitation programmes can be designed and implemented to be feasible, cost-effective and attractive and accessible for patients and healthcare providers in the long term. Research must also investigate how the organisation of such programmes within specific healthcare systems determines their effects after COPD exacerbations on hospital readmissions and mortality. This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding. High-certainty evidence indicates that pulmonary rehabilitation after an exacerbation results in a large improvement in 6MWD when compared with usual care (MD 57.79 m, 95% CI 41.68 to 73.91; I<sup>2</sup> = 89%). Heterogeneity appeared to be driven mainly by differences between studies showing very large effects and those showing smaller effects but still evidence of between-group differences. The overall results of this review have not changed to an important extent compared with results reported in the previous version of this review. Overall, the risk of bias was judged to be low or unclear across most domains. However, the lack of participant blinding raised concerns for subjectively reported outcomes (HRQL). High risks of selection bias and attrition bias were identified in a small number of studies, while a larger proportion of studies were at high risk for reporting bias. Egger's test indicated evidence of funnel plot asymmetry for hospital readmission (P = 0.02) and mortality (P = 0.02), but not for SGRQ (P = 0.45) or the six-minute walk test (P = 0.12). Visual inspection suggested that the asymmetry was more consistent with small-study effects than with clear evidence of missing negative studies. Moderate-certainty evidence indicates that pulmonary rehabilitation likely reduces hospital readmissions, while evidence for mortality is of low certainty. However, some recent studies showed no benefit of rehabilitation on hospital readmissions and mortality. Such heterogeneity of effects on hospital readmissions and mortality may be explained to some extent by the extensiveness of rehabilitation programmes and by the methodological quality of the included studies. High-certainty evidence shows moderate to large effects of pulmonary rehabilitation on HRQL and exercise capacity in people with COPD after an exacerbation. While additional RCTs comparing rehabilitation to no rehabilitation seem questionable scientifically and ethically, future research must investigate how rehabilitation programmes can be designed and implemented to be feasible, cost-effective and attractive and accessible for patients and healthcare providers in the long term. Research must also investigate how the organisation of such programmes within specific healthcare systems determines their effects after COPD exacerbations on hospital readmissions and mortality. titre: Employment in substance use disorders: A systematic review and mapping of associated factors.
titre_fr: Employment in substance use disorders: A systematic review and mapping of associated factors.
auteurs: Bardon Ludovic, Dambrun Michael, Chazeron Ingrid De, Miele Cécile, Marinho Gaétan, Brousse Georges, Cabé Julien
resume: Mental health and substance use disorders (SUD) have substantial individual and societal impacts. Their relationship with work is bidirectional. Recovery from SUD is increasingly viewed as a multidimensional process in which employment is a key component of social reintegration. Despite evidence that employment reduces relapse risk and improves long-term outcomes, the factors shaping vocational trajectories in this population remain insufficiently understood. This systematic review aimed to identify and synthesise the individual, clinical and contextual factors associated with employment among adults with SUD, with or without comorbidity. This review was conducted following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. PubMed, PsycINFO, Cochrane and Web of Science databases were searched for studies meeting the following inclusion criteria: (1) adults (≥18 years) with current or former SUD (any substance); (2) outcome(s) clearly capturing employment, defined as any indicator of engagement in paid employment (full-time, part-time, temporary, subsidised, etc.), including self-reported employment; (3) quantitative study designs; (4) articles written in English. From an initial pool of 7014 references, 60 articles were included. There were 23 randomised controlled trials, 23 cohort studies, 9 cross-sectional studies, 4 quasi-experimental studies and 1 case control study. A narrative synthesis identified 51 factors, 46 of which were statistically associated (positively or negatively) with employment in at least one of the 60 studies. These were organised across six domains: socio-demographic characteristics; substance use patterns and related risk factors; treatment and recovery-related factors; health-related factors; psychological factors; and social and environmental factors. Better employment outcomes were associated with prior employment history, higher educational attainment, engagement in treatment, supported employment and contingency management interventions. In contrast, substance use, its severity, psychiatric comorbidity and housing instability were associated with poorer employment outcomes. Findings were mixed for several factors, including age and criminal history. Most studies presented moderate to high risk of bias while a formal assessment of the overall certainty of evidence was not performed. There are 46 statistically significant factors either positively or negatively associated with employment among individuals with substance use disorders, showing that employment may be a multidimensional process shaped by individual, clinical and contextual factors. Supported employment and contingency management were associated with better employment outcomes, while persistent barriers such as housing instability, stigma and fragmented services suggest that sustainable employment depends on coordinated support across treatment, employment, housing and policy systems.

titre: Factors influencing health beliefs regarding facial nerve rehabilitation training in patients with peripheral facial paralysis: a qualitative study.
titre_fr: Factors influencing health beliefs regarding facial nerve rehabilitation training in patients with peripheral facial paralysis: a qualitative study.
auteurs: Shi Xiujun, Wu Ling, He Chunlin, Qiu Lingyu, Zhou Jingfeng, Luo Wenyu, Zhao Li
resume: To investigate the factors influencing health beliefs regarding facial nerve rehabilitation training in patients with peripheral facial paralysis (PFP), and to provide a reference for developing precise and individualized facial nerve rehabilitation training programs for this population. Guided by the Health Belief Model (HBM), this descriptive qualitative study employed purposive sampling to recruit 16 patients with PFP who had received facial nerve rehabilitation training in healthcare settings. Semi-structured interviews were conducted, and the data were analyzed using codebook thematic analysis. Through data analysis, five overarching themes and 23 subthemes were identified: Perceived Threat of the Disease (appearance impairment, emotional distress, disease course concern, diminished role functioning, disease burden); Perceived Benefits of Health Behaviors (improvement of facial paralysis symptoms, emotional improvement, social participation, image enhancement, reduced disease burden); Perceived Barriers to Health Behaviors (memory difficulties, inconsistencies in guidance content and methods, emotional interference, time-space constraints, low perceived importance); Cues to Action (professional guidance, post-discharge referral services, family support, stage goal setting, health benefits, peer support); and Self-efficacy (perseverance, ability to regulate training intensity). Health beliefs regarding facial nerve rehabilitation training in patients with PFP are influenced by multiple interrelated factors. Healthcare providers should promptly identify and respond to perceived barriers to health behaviors, reinforce the perception of disease threat and benefits of health behaviors, and utilize cues to action and self-efficacy as key entry points for intervention. Tailored rehabilitation guidance and recommendations should be provided to enhance patients' adherence to facial nerve rehabilitation training and improve their quality of life.

titre: IMPACT OF TRAUMATIC BRACHIAL PLEXUS INJURY ON QUALITY OF LIFE: A NARRATIVE REVIEW OF ASSESSMENT METHODS AND INFLUENCING FACTOR.
titre_fr: IMPACT OF TRAUMATIC BRACHIAL PLEXUS INJURY ON QUALITY OF LIFE: A NARRATIVE REVIEW OF ASSESSMENT METHODS AND INFLUENCING FACTOR.
auteurs: Hofmann Veronika, Maleki Maryam, Maufroy Christophe, Schneider Urs, Pott Peter P
resume: Traumatic brachial plexus injury (TBPI) is associated with substantial physical, psychological, and social impairment. This review aimed to summarize quality-of-life (QoL) assessment methods and identify factors influencing QoL following TBPI. A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. Studies published between 1990 and August 2026 assessing QoL in adults with TBPI were identified and analyzed. Twenty-six studies were included. Various assessment tools were analyzed, including QoL instruments such as the SF-36/12, WHOQOL-BREF, EQ-5D, FLZ-M, and Ulm Questionnaire, and disability-focused measures, such as the DASH/QuickDASH. Despite methodological heterogeneity, all studies consistently reported reduced QoL in individuals with TBPI compared with unaffected populations. Major factors associated with poorer QoL included greater injury severity, delayed surgical intervention, chronic pain, dominant limb involvement, psychological distress, and reduced social participation. Pain, anxiety, depression, and difficulties with occupational reintegration emerged as particularly important determinants of long-term outcomes. TBPI has a substantial and persistent negative impact on QoL. While functional recovery remains an important treatment goal, long-term outcomes are also strongly influenced by pain, psychological health, social participation, and occupational reintegration. Comprehensive rehabilitation strategies addressing these dimensions are therefore essential to improve QoL in individuals with TBPI.

titre: Relationship between the provision of procedures in psychosocial care centers and socioeconomic factors: an ecological study.
titre_fr: Relationship between the provision of procedures in psychosocial care centers and socioeconomic factors: an ecological study.
auteurs: Lima Anna Helen Silva, Coelho Ardigleusa Alves, Costa Gabriela Maria Cavalcanti, Olinda Ricardo Alves de, Silva Valdecir Carneiro da
resume: to analyze the correlation between the supply of procedures performed in the Psychosocial Care Centers and the socioeconomic indicators in municipalities with populations above 100 thousand inhabitants. this is an ecological study covering 312 municipalities and 1,127 services. In the modeling, data were extracted from the historical series of outpatient production of the Health Information System and socioeconomic indicators from the Atlas of Human Development. only 12 capitals recorded harm reduction actions; 93% of the records are more frequent in the capitals. A positive correlation was observed between home care and per capita income; and a negative correlation between psychosocial rehabilitation and illiteracy rate. It is noteworthy that the Municipal Human Development Index and per capita income were correlated with most of the procedures, while the illiteracy rate correlated with 64.7% of them. Statistically significant differences were found between medium and large municipalities. the relationship between the procedures recorded in the Psychosocial Care Centers and the socioeconomic indicators may indicate the influence of multifactorial issues on mental health care.

titre: Feasibility of a community-based physical activity programme in individuals with Long Covid: insights from the Hertfordshire longitudinal observational programme.
titre_fr: Feasibility of a community-based physical activity programme in individuals with Long Covid: insights from the Hertfordshire longitudinal observational programme.
auteurs: Logue M, Lyus R, Edwards B
resume: This study explores the feasibility of implementing and evaluating a community-based physical activity programme for individuals with Long Covid in Hertfordshire, UK. Long Covid presents unique challenges including fluctuating symptoms, post-exertional malaise and difficulties with re-engagement following symptom flare-ups. Developed collaboratively by the Herts Sports & Physical Activity Partnership and local NHS Covid Rehabilitation Services, the programme aimed to address these challenges through tailored physical activity opportunities informed by the lived experience of Long Covid. A longitudinal observational design was used to evaluate programme retention, symptom severity, health-related quality of life and physical activity levels among 62 participants over a 12-month period. Data were collected via validated self-report tools including the EQ-5D-5L, EQ-VAS, SBQ-LC and VAS pain scale. High initial engagement was observed, with 89% of participants completing the first follow-up survey and 52% remaining engaged through to follow-up 4. While average physical activity minutes remained stable, the proportion of inactive participants declined from 37% to 25%. Statistically significant improvements were observed in self-rated health (EQ-VAS), breathing difficulties, fatigue and brain fog. Weak but significant correlations were found between increased physical activity and reduced symptom severity in several domains, including mobility, self-care and musculoskeletal pain. No significant changes were observed in anxiety or depression, suggesting physical activity alone may not address the full spectrum of Long Covid symptoms. These findings demonstrate that community-based physical activity interventions are feasible for people with Long Covid, though sustained behavioural change and mental health support remain important challenges. This study contributes practical insights for service development while highlighting the need for more rigorous controlled designs and diverse sampling in future research.
