titre: Serum Vitamin D Combined with Obstetric Parameters to Construct a Nomogram Model for Predicting the Risk of PFD Disorders.
titre_fr: Serum Vitamin D Combined with Obstetric Parameters to Construct a Nomogram Model for Predicting the Risk of PFD Disorders.
auteurs: Li Jian C, Song Jun N, Liu Chuan H, Zhang Yong H, Qu Mei Q
resume: Postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction (PFD) significantly impacts women's quality of life and mental health. Although existing studies suggest various obstetric factors may contribute to PFD, there is a lack of early prediction tools based on readily available indicators. This study aimed to develop a nomogram model incorporating serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)VitD] levels and routine obstetric parameters to predict the risk of PFD. A total of 300 women who delivered and completed a 6-week postpartum follow-up were enrolled. Data on age, body mass index (BMI), duration of the second stage of labor, neonatal birth weight, and serum 25(OH) VitD levels within 24 hours postpartum were collected. Participants were divided into PFD and non-PFD groups based on follow-up outcomes. Logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent risk factors for PFD, and a nomogram prediction model was constructed. The model's performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Multivariate logistic regression revealed that age, BMI, duration of the second stage of labor, birth weight, and 25(OH)VitD levels were independent predictors of PFD (p < 0.05). The nomogram model achieved an AUC of 0.830 with calibration curves demonstrating good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities. DCA indicated substantial clinical net benefit across a wide probability threshold range. The developed nomogram model effectively predicts postpartum PFD risk using easily obtainable pre- and post-delivery indicators. This model may facilitate early identification of high-risk individuals, guiding personalized rehabilitation strategies and improving early intervention and prevention of PFD.

titre: Cervicothoracic sympathetic chain block Against placebo Saline injection Evaluation for post-COVID condition: a study protocol for the CeASE randomised controlled trial.
titre_fr: Cervicothoracic sympathetic chain block Against placebo Saline injection Evaluation for post-COVID condition: a study protocol for the CeASE randomised controlled trial.
auteurs: Chung Olivia S, Harvey Paula, Cheung Angela M, Chakraborty Praloy, Hulme Jennifer, Alomari Abeer, Meng Howard, Ladha Karim, Al Azazi Emad, Bhatia Anuj
resume: Post-COVID condition (PCC) affects a substantial proportion of individuals following acute COVID-19 infection, with manifestations such as dysautonomia, fatigue and brain fog. The cervicothoracic sympathetic chain block (CSB), a local anaesthetic block of the cervical sympathetic trunk, has shown preliminary promise in uncontrolled studies, but randomised evidence is lacking. This trial is expected to provide a rigorous estimate of the efficacy of CSB compared with a placebo saline injection for PCC. The CeASE randomised controlled trial (RCT) is a double-blind, parallel-group RCT enrolling 78 adult participants with PCC across two Canadian sites (Women’s College Hospital and Toronto Western Hospital). Participants will be randomised 1:1 to receive two ultrasound-guided injections of either 0.25% bupivacaine with epinephrine (active CSB) or 0.9% normal saline (placebo control), spaced 1–2 weeks apart. The primary outcome is a change in the Modified COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale (C19-YRSm) Symptom Severity subscale at 1 month following the final injection. Secondary outcomes include C19-YRSm scores at 3 months, cardiovascular autonomic function (heart rate variability, postural heart rate changes and blood pressure responses), serum proinflammatory cytokine levels (interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, tumour necrosis factor alpha), autonomic symptom burden (Composite Autonomic Symptom Score-31), mental health (Generalised Anxiety Disorder-7, Patient Health Questionnaire-9 and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale), quality of life (EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level questionnaire, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index), and actigraphy-measured sleep and physical activity. The sample size of 78 participants (39 per arm) was calculated for a target between-group difference of four points on the C19-YRSm Symptom Severity subscale, assuming an SD of 5.62, 85% power and a 10% dropout allowance. Recruitment opened in May 2026; final follow-up is expected by September 2027. Ethics approval was obtained from the University Health Network Institutional Review Board (25-6183). Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publication and presentation at relevant scientific conferences. Deidentified individual participant data will be shared, in accordance with the data sharing plan recorded in the trial registration, on reasonable request. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07468604

titre: Real-World Use and Effectiveness of Internet-Based Vestibular Rehabilitation Following Nationwide Implementation: Prospective Observational Cohort Study.
titre_fr: Real-World Use and Effectiveness of Internet-Based Vestibular Rehabilitation Following Nationwide Implementation: Prospective Observational Cohort Study.
auteurs: Ngo Hà Tn, Maarsingh Otto R, Blanker Marco H, Bont Jettie, van Vugt Vincent A
resume: Vestibular rehabilitation is a safe and effective exercise-based treatment for various vestibular disorders, yet it is underused by general practitioners. Following a randomized controlled trial demonstrating the effectiveness of Vertigo Training, an internet-based vestibular rehabilitation program, a nationwide implementation was initiated in the Netherlands. This study aimed to evaluate the real-world use and effectiveness of Vertigo Training on vestibular symptoms. We conducted a prospective observational cohort study by using anonymized data from Vertigo Training users (period 2023-2025). Individuals were eligible if they reported vestibular symptoms for at least 1 month, irrespective of the underlying cause. Main analyses focused on users who completed voluntary questionnaires, capturing demographic and clinical characteristics. We evaluated the effectiveness using the Vertigo Symptom Scale-Short Form (VSS-SF). Factors associated with treatment success (defined as ≥3-point reduction in VSS-SF score at 3 months) were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. To contextualize these outcomes, we used program-level data and additional voluntary questionnaires to describe engagement and adherence. A total of 2156 users were included for the main analyses (median age 60, IQR 48-70 years; n=1427, 66% women). The most frequently self-reported diagnoses were benign paroxysmal positional vertigo and vestibular neuritis. Median VSS-SF scores improved from 17 (IQR 12-22) at baseline to 11 (IQR 6-18) at 3 months, with 63% (155/247) achieving treatment success. Higher baseline VSS-SF scores were associated with a greater likelihood of treatment success (odds ratio 1.1, 95% CI 1.0-1.1), as was a diagnosis of benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (risk ratio 1.7, 95% CI 1.1-2.0). These outcomes were observed in a context where engagement declined over time, with 43% (1442/3367) of users progressing to week 2, and adherence to the recommended exercise frequency averaged 13%. In this real-world cohort, Vertigo Training was associated with meaningful reductions in vestibular symptoms following nationwide implementation. These findings confirm its effectiveness beyond the trial setting and support broader integration of internet-based vestibular rehabilitation into routine care. However, sustained engagement remains an important target for future research and optimization. RR2-10.1186/s43058-023-00524-1.

resume: BackgroundTechnology-assisted rehabilitation offers alternative ways to deliver exercise, feedback and pain-management strategies for adults with musculoskeletal (MSK) pain. However, its additional clinical benefits and implementation requirements remain uncertain.ObjectiveTo evaluate clinical outcomes, engagement and safety across virtual reality (VR), exergaming, wearable or sensor-based feedback, and robot-assisted rehabilitation for adults with non-surgical MSK pain.MethodsFive databases were searched on 26 September 2026 for English-language, peer-reviewed randomised controlled trials (RCTs) published from 2022 onwards. Methodological appraisal used the Joanna Briggs Institute RCT checklist. Findings were synthesised narratively because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity.ResultsThirty-six RCTs involving 2,084 adults were included: 25 evaluated VR or exergaming, eight wearable or sensor-based rehabilitation, and three robot-assisted rehabilitation. Selected trials reported additional improvements in pain, function or psychological outcomes, whereas others found no significant between-group benefits. Changes in movement performance or muscle activation did not consistently accompany broader clinical improvement. Participation varied: one short programme achieved complete session attendance, while another reported median completion of 61% of prescribed exercises. Usability and satisfaction did not consistently favour technology. Reported adverse effects included cybersickness, transient pain and device discomfort; inconsistent safety reporting limited comparative interpretation.ConclusionTechnology-assisted rehabilitation may benefit selected outcomes, but the evidence does not establish a universally superior technology, delivery model or dose. Clinical selection should consider rehabilitation goals, patient preferences, access and support needs. The proposed Tech-Care Biopsychosocial Framework organises these considerations but requires further development and validation.

titre: Oculomotor rehabilitation after concussion in adults (ORCA): a feasibility study.
titre_fr: Oculomotor rehabilitation after concussion in adults (ORCA): a feasibility study.
auteurs: Biscardi Melissa, Bayley Mark Theodore, Thorpe Kevin, Quaid Patrick, Colantonio Angela, Mollayeva Tatyana
resume: Oculomotor deficits are reported in up to 85% of adults after concussion and may contribute to prolonged symptoms and delayed return to daily activities. Oculomotor rehabilitation has been successfully implemented in younger age groups, however evidence in adults is lacking. Virtual reality (VR)-based oculomotor rehabilitation (OMR) offers a standardized and scalable intervention model; however, feasibility in adults with persistent symptoms has not been established, and it remains important to understand whether sex influences response to rehabilitation. The goal of this study was to assess the feasibility of a 6-week RCT on VR-based OMR in adults with persistent symptoms after concussion, using a sex and gender lens. Sex-stratified, two-arm randomized feasibility trial with 1:1 allocation. Adults (24 female, 16 male; all identifying as cisgender) aged 18-42 years with persistent (≥30 days) post-concussion symptoms suggestive of oculomotor dysfunction were randomized to six sessions of VR-based OMR with mobile application homework or usual care (UC, education only). The primary objective was to assess feasibility of a future fully powered randomized controlled trial, including recruitment, retention, perceived benefit and harms. Feasibility progression criteria were defined a priori using a traffic-light framework. Proof-of-concept was operationalized as participant-rated perceived benefit (0-4) at study completion. Forty participants were randomized (OMR n = 20; usual care n = 20); 39 completed follow-up (97.5% retention). All participants allocated to OMR attended six sessions and 94.7% engaged in prescribed home-based exercises. VR-based assessment and training were well tolerated; symptoms were transient and no adverse events occurred. Participant-rated perceived benefit was higher in the OMR group (mean 3.4/4) compared with usual care (mean 2.3/4). VR-based OMR with mobile reinforcement is feasible, acceptable, and well tolerated in adults with persistent post-concussion symptoms. Predefined feasibility benchmarks were met, supporting progression to a fully powered trial. Future adequately powered studies should evaluate clinical efficacy and consider sex and gender as interacting variables, in samples with greater gender diversity. Identifier, NCT07709936, https://clinicaltrials.gov/expert-search?term=NCT07709936.

titre: Digital Health Coaching in Adult Cancer Survivorship Care: A Scoping Review and Nursing-Oriented Evidence Map.
titre_fr: Digital Health Coaching in Adult Cancer Survivorship Care: A Scoping Review and Nursing-Oriented Evidence Map.
auteurs: Chen Tingting, Zhou Shiyu, Long Siyu, Chen Xiaohuan, Chen Xin, Zhang Yanzi, Chen Shiyu, Liao Zhenyu
resume: To (1) map digital delivery modalities and behavior-change ingredients used in adult cancer survivorship; (2) describe the distribution of evidence across cancer populations, intervention domains, and outcomes; and (3) identify nursing implementation functions and evidence gaps. A scoping review was conducted using JBI methodology, informed by Arksey and O'Malley and Levac et al, and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, APA PsycINFO, and CINAHL were searched from database inception through April 1, 2026, without language or study-design filters. Three reviewers independently screened records, assessed full texts, charted data, classified evidence, and grouped companion publications into intervention/study families; discrepancies were resolved through discussion and consensus. Critical appraisal was not undertaken because the purpose was to map the extent, characteristics, and gaps of the evidence rather than estimate intervention effectiveness. The search identified 1,197 records. We included 118 publications representing 90 intervention/study families; 104 publications representing 78 families formed the core evidence map, and 14 publications representing 12 families were summarized as peripheral evidence. Mobile apps and web platforms were the most common delivery channels, but active intervention content varied and included goal setting, self-monitoring, tailored feedback, action planning, problem solving, reminders, and human support. Nursing implementation functions additionally included symptom review, monitoring, triage, referral, and escalation. Evidence was concentrated in physical activity, lifestyle, fatigue, symptom self-management, patient-reported outcomes, and rehabilitation. Sleep-specific and metabolic-health-focused interventions were sparse, and few programs addressed sleep, physical activity, and weight/metabolic risk together. Reporting of intervention content, dose, fidelity, clinical responsibility, long-term maintenance, equity, and workflow integration was inconsistent. Digital health coaching is best understood as a set of blended digital-human support arrangements rather than as a technology category or a single survivorship care model. Its clinical value depends on the behavior-change ingredients, support intensity, nursing responsibilities, escalation pathways, and workflows connected to the technology. Oncology nurses can use the evidence map to match survivor needs with support intensity, define monitoring and escalation responsibilities, and design equitable digital-human survivorship workflows.

titre: Virtual Reality-Based Rehabilitation for Pediatric Acquired Brain Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
titre_fr: Virtual Reality-Based Rehabilitation for Pediatric Acquired Brain Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
auteurs: Centrello Justice, Zhang Minci, Smith Bradley, Startup Joshua, Issac Sony
resume: BackgroundVirtual reality and augmented reality (VR/AR) rehabilitation shows promise after adult brain injury, but its efficacy in pediatric acquired brain injury remains unclear.ObjectiveTo synthesize within-person changes in cognitive, motor, and functional outcomes following VR/AR rehabilitation in pediatric acquired brain injury and explore moderators.MethodsSix databases were searched through March 2026 following PRISMA guidelines. Of 373 records, ten studies (nine VR, one AR) were included: four randomized trials and six uncontrolled studies. Standardized mean changes were pooled using three-level random-effects meta-analysis.ResultsAcross 72 effect sizes, VR/AR rehabilitation was associated with significant pre-post improvement (g = 0.62, 95% CI [0.15, 1.09], p = .01). Improvements were significant for motor and functional outcomes, but not cognitive outcomes. Outcome domain, developmental stage, study design, immersion, assessment method, and treatment dose were not significant moderators. Longer pre-post intervals predicted larger changes (β = 0.01, p = .004), potentially reflecting natural recovery. Overall improvements remained significant across assumed correlations and when restricting analyses to VR, excluding mixed diagnostic samples, or clustering by research team. Funnel plot asymmetry suggested possible publication bias.ConclusionsVR-based rehabilitation was associated with within-person improvement, but comparative efficacy remains uncertain because evidence is limited, heterogeneous, and predominantly uncontrolled. Larger controlled studies should evaluate efficacy, safety, mechanisms, durability, and functional transfer.

titre: Virtual and Augmented Reality Feedback During Robotic Gait Training Acutely Modulate Paretic Muscle Activation, Limb Loading, and Propulsion-Related Mechanics in Chronic Hemiparetic Stroke: A Randomised Crossover Trial.
titre_fr: Virtual and Augmented Reality Feedback During Robotic Gait Training Acutely Modulate Paretic Muscle Activation, Limb Loading, and Propulsion-Related Mechanics in Chronic Hemiparetic Stroke: A Randomised Crossover Trial.
auteurs: Park Haesol, Kim Chaesu, Na Yujin, You Joshua Sung
resume: BackgroundVisual-feedback modalities, including virtual reality (VR) and screen-based augmented reality (AR), have been integrated into robot-assisted gait training (RAGT) to enhance engagement and gait control after stroke, yet their distinct and combined neuromechanical effects remain unclear.ObjectiveTo compare the acute effects of RAGT alone, VR-RAGT, screen-based AR-RAGT, and sequential combined VR + AR-RAGT on paretic gait mechanics in individuals with chronic hemiparetic stroke.MethodsTwenty participants completed four 30-min RAGT conditions (RAGT alone, VR-RAGT, screen-based AR-RAGT, and sequential combined VR + AR-RAGT) in a randomized within-subject crossover design. Paretic muscle activation, ground reaction forces and center of pressure (COP) were analyzed as time-normalized waveforms using one-dimensional statistical parametric mapping; robot-derived joint torque and torque-angle slope were analyzed as phase-averaged scalars using repeated-measures ANOVA.ResultsRelative to RAGT alone, VR was associated with greater swing-phase tibialis anterior activation and hip flexion torque, whereas AR was associated with reduced stance-phase co-contraction and greater late-stance gastrocnemius activation, knee extensor torque, and anterior-posterior COP progression. The sequential combined VR + AR condition produced the broadest acute modulation across swing- and stance-related outcomes, including reduced co-contraction-related EMG, greater paretic limb loading, and longer anterior-posterior COP progression.ConclusionsUnder identical robotic parameters and the task configurations tested, VR and screen-based AR feedback differentially modulated swing- and stance-phase paretic gait mechanics, and sequential exposure to both conditions produced the broadest acute modulation. Whether these acute, task-specific effects translate into longer-term functional recovery remains to be determined.

titre: Integration of sports and exercise medicine into Saudi primary care: a narrative review from family medicine perspective.
titre_fr: Integration of sports and exercise medicine into Saudi primary care: a narrative review from family medicine perspective.
auteurs: Althunyan Abdullatif K
revue: Frontiers in sports and active living
resume: Saudi Arabia faces dual pressures from a high non-communicable disease (NCD) burden driven by physical inactivity and accelerating sports participation under Vision 2030. Family physicians in primary health care (PHC) are central to both challenges but lack a structured framework for integrating sports medicine and exercise medicine into routine practice. To define core sports and exercise medicine roles for family physicians, identify barriers and facilitators using a SWOT framework, and propose a contextualized integration model for Saudi primary care. A single-author narrative review was conducted. MEDLINE (via PubMed) and Embase were searched for English-language publications from January 2000 to July 2026; Google Scholar and the official websites of Saudi governmental and sports organizations, WHO, ACSM, ADA, AMSSM, and IOC were also searched. Clinical guidelines and consensus statements from WHO, ACSM, AHA, ESC, ADA, AMSSM, and IOC were included. No formal quality appraisal was undertaken; evidence was weighted pragmatically according to study design and population relevance. Five core roles were identified: (1) preparticipation evaluation and cardiovascular risk screening; (2) exercise prescription for NCD prevention and management; (3) prevention of sports injuries and illness, including exertional heat illness and overtraining; (4) assessment and rehabilitation of acute, chronic, and overuse injuries; and (5) care of special populations, including youth, female, older adult, and para-sport athletes. SWOT analysis identified Vision 2030 alignment and digital health infrastructure as strengths; training and curriculum gaps as the principal modifiable weakness; expanding sports infrastructure and the NCD burden as opportunities; and geographic workforce concentration as a key threat. The Saudi Primary Care Sports and Exercise Medicine (SPCSM) Framework is a literature-informed, not-yet-piloted proposal comprising three pillars: Workforce Capability, Service Architecture, and Health Intelligence, with phased implementation from 2026 to 2032 within existing PHC clusters. Structured integration of sports and exercise medicine into Saudi family practice appears clinically rational and potentially feasible; empirical evaluation through prospective pilot studies and stakeholder co-design is required before conclusions about implementation readiness can be drawn.

titre: START-the Swiss tele-assisted rehabilitation and training program to support transition from inpatient to outpatient care in the subacute phase after a stroke: results of the feasibility, safety and performance evaluation.
titre_fr: START-the Swiss tele-assisted rehabilitation and training program to support transition from inpatient to outpatient care in the subacute phase after a stroke: results of the feasibility, safety and performance evaluation.
auteurs: Gäumann Szabina, Ziller Carina, Paulissen Nele, Behrendt Frank, Suica Zorica, Augstburger Mara, Matsushita Sarina Mai, Schneider Philipp Lars, Crüts Björn, Gammerschlag Luana, Parmar Katrin, Gerth Hans Ulrich, Bonati Leo H, Schuster-Amft Corina
resume: Intensive rehabilitation is crucial for functional recovery after stroke, particularly during the subacute phase. However, therapy intensity often substantially declines after discharge from inpatient rehabilitation. This study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and performance of the Swiss tele-assisted rehabilitation and training program (START) facilitating transition from inpatient to outpatient stroke rehabilitation. This single-center observational feasibility study enrolled 40 patients. START was introduced during the last two weeks of inpatient rehabilitation and continued for 12 weeks after discharge. START included daily exercise, coaching, monitoring and blood pressure measurements. Feasibility was assessed using predefined process-, training-, and mHealth-related criteria including recruitment, safety, acceptance, adherence, dropout, system stability, usability, quality, satisfaction, and perceived change. Secondary outcomes included disability, functional status, quality of life, life-space mobility, physical performance and activity level. Of the 94 informed patients, 40 were enrolled (recruitment rate 42.6%); 29 patients (59.7 ± 13.7 years, 11/29 females) completed the study. Dropout rate was 27.5%, exceeding the predefined threshold (≤20%). No serious protocol-related adverse events occurred. Training adherence was 65.1 ± 31.4% during inpatient and 66.7 ± 29.9% during outpatient rehabilitation. Adherence to blood pressure measurements was 79.0 ± 27.6% and 83.6 ± 20.3%, respectively. System stability was high (0.7 failures/week). Usability was rated high (System Usability Scale: 88.3 ± 10.7/100; German mHealth Application Usability Questionnaire: 5.3 ± 1.1/7), and application quality was rated 4.1 ± 0.5/5 on the App Quality Assessment Tool for Health-Related Apps. Patient satisfaction was high (median 8/10), and patients reported positive changes. Functional outcomes changed, including examiner-rated modified Rankin Scale (median 2 to 1), Timed Up and Go (13.7 ± 14.3 to 10.3 ± 8.9), Short Physical Performance Battery (median 10 to 11), Trunk Impairment Scale (median 17 to 20), life-space mobility (55.9 ± 33.4 to 80.1 ± 27.3), and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (58.1 ± 41.5 to 83.0 ± 46.4 min/day). START was well accepted, technically stable, and appeared feasible with an acceptable safety profile for supporting transition from inpatient to outpatient stroke rehabilitation. However, dropout and training adherence require optimization. These findings warrant further evaluation of START compared with conventional care in a randomized controlled trial.

titre: Preliminary postural responses to an immersive VR exergame in children with unilateral cerebral palsy: a pilot study.
titre_fr: Preliminary postural responses to an immersive VR exergame in children with unilateral cerebral palsy: a pilot study.
auteurs: Çavdar Senanur, Yazici-Mutlu Çiğdem, Çelİk Meltem, Doğan Osman, İnan Muharrem
resume: Game-based VR interventions have been proposed as a promising tool to enhance motivation and engagement in pediatric rehabilitation. However, there remains insufficient knowledge regarding the therapeutic use of immersive VR systems in this population. This study aimed to evaluate the preliminary postural responses to an immersive virtual reality (VR) exergame‑based intervention on postural control in children with unilateral cerebral palsy (UCP). Fifteen participants with unilateral cerebral palsy (UCP) (6 female and 9 male) were included in this pilot study. Static postural stability and foot contact area measurements were recorded before and after 15-minute sessions performed in both the real-game (RG) and immersive virtual reality (VR) environments. Linear mixed model analyses indicated that none of the pedobarographic contact area variables or center of pressure (CoP)-based postural stability measures showed significant effects of time (before vs. after), environment (immersive virtual reality [VR] vs. real-game [RG]), or their interaction (all p > .05). Although 64.3% of participants reported greater discomfort during the virtual reality condition, 86.7% expressed a preference for it. A single session of immersive virtual reality (VR) gameplay did not result in significant immediate changes in postural control measures in children with unilateral cerebral palsy (UCP). Despite reporting some discomfort, most participants preferred the immersive VR experience, supporting its feasibility and acceptability for further investigation in pediatric rehabilitation.

titre: Game-based digital interventions in pediatric hematologic oncology: a scoping review.
titre_fr: Game-based digital interventions in pediatric hematologic oncology: a scoping review.
auteurs: Hang Yujie, Ren Yulu, Chen Shenjie, Deng Jiayi, Guo Yanni, Shao Zhuoyi, Zhai Weicheng, Jin Zhizhi, Wang Runping, Zhang Chunmei
revue: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
resume: This review aims to map game-based digital interventions in pediatric hematologic oncology, describe their technological platforms and game elements, and identify the reported health-related and implementation outcomes. This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and was reported in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guideline. The Population, Concept, and Context (PCC) framework guided the definition of search terms and the development of the search strategy for PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database. This review included 19 studies from 12 countries, involving 932 participants, of whom 756 had hematologic malignancies. The studies evaluated game-based digital interventions in three formats: screen-based (n = 7), motion-based (n = 6), and virtual reality-based (n = 6). Applications included procedural distraction, treatment-related education, symptom management, and physical or cognitive rehabilitation. The studies reported symptom and psychological, functional, health-related quality of life, and implementation-related outcomes (feasibility, usability, and acceptability). Game-based digital interventions have been applied across diverse supportive care contexts for children with hematologic malignancies. Although a range of applications has been explored, current evidence is insufficient to determine which intervention formats or game elements are most appropriate for particular age groups or clinical contexts. Future research should focus on theory-informed intervention development, evaluate implementation in practice, and explore the potential of these interventions in long-term care.

titre: Perceptual but not motor predictions are altered in virtual reality: evidence from weight illusions and predictive grip forces.
titre_fr: Perceptual but not motor predictions are altered in virtual reality: evidence from weight illusions and predictive grip forces.
auteurs: Harris David, Arthur Tom, Kannan Dayanita, Buckingham Gavin
resume: Recent theories in cognitive science propose that prior expectations strongly influence how individuals perceive the world and control their actions. This influence is particularly relevant in novel sensory environments, such as virtual reality (VR). This registered report outlines a study examining the impact of VR on prediction-related sensory perception and motor control during object lifting. We tested two competing hypotheses: the low-precision priors hypothesis suggests reduced influence of prior expectations in VR owing to the novelty and uncertainty of the context, while the high-precision priors hypothesis posits increased reliance on predictions relative to current sensory information. We employed two weight illusion tasks (the size-weight and material-weight illusions) to isolate the effects of prior expectations on perception and action to test whether VR alters their influence on weight perception and fingertip forces. Results revealed a dissociation: perceptual illusions were significantly attenuated in VR, yet predictive grip force scaling showed no difference between environments. Exploratory analyses indicated initially elevated grip forces in VR, but similar motor adaptation profiles over time. These findings suggest perceptual inference is highly susceptible to 'virtuality' while motor predictions remain robust, challenging the use of VR as a neutral research medium and highlighting potential complications for applications in training and rehabilitation.

titre: Toward equity in health: A scoping review protocol for fifteen years of progress and gaps in disability-inclusive healthcare (2010-2025).
titre_fr: Toward equity in health: A scoping review protocol for fifteen years of progress and gaps in disability-inclusive healthcare (2010-2025).
auteurs: Makhado Lufuno, Makhado Thendo Gertie
resume: Persons with disabilities (PWDs) experience persistent disparities in accessing equitable and effective healthcare, despite the existence of global human rights frameworks. While previous studies have examined barriers to care, no scoping review has systematically synthesised disability-inclusive healthcare interventions using a structural competency framework, which emphasises how social, economic, and institutional structures shape health inequities. Structural, financial, attitudinal, and systemic barriers continue to impede the full inclusion of PWDs in healthcare systems worldwide. Over the past fifteen years, frameworks such as the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) have aimed to promote inclusive health reforms; however, implementation remains uneven and global evidence on effective interventions remains fragmented. This scoping review aims to map and synthesise global literature (2010-2025) on disability-inclusive healthcare systems. It focuses on structural competency, universal design, telehealth, and community-based rehabilitation (CBR), identifying key barriers and facilitators. The review will follow Arksey and O'Malley's scoping review methodology, incorporating guidance from the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) and PRISMA-ScR. Literature will be identified through searches in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Google Scholar. Eligibility will be guided by the Population-Concept-Context (PCC) framework, with studies screened and charted independently by two reviewers. Thematic synthesis and evidence mapping will be used to analyse findings. No meta-analysis will be conducted due to expected heterogeneity. The review is anticipated to categorise major systemic barriers (e.g., physical inaccessibility, provider bias, financial exclusion) and identify inclusive interventions aligned with CRPD principles. These insights will support health policy reform and training in disability-responsive care. This review will synthesise global evidence on disability-inclusive healthcare interventions to inform policy, practice, and training in disability-responsive care. No ethical approval is required. This protocol is registered with the Open Science Framework (OSF) https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/PWC92.

Santé publique France rappelle l'importance des effets sur la santé et des conséquences en termes de santé publique.

titre: Moi(s) sans tabac... en novembre, on arrête ensemble : déjà 110 000 inscrits sur tabac-info-service.fr
resume: Le grand défi collectif lancé pour inciter le maximum de fumeurs à arrêter de fumer pendant 30 jours a commencé le 1er novembre 2016. Déjà 110 000 personnes ont rejoint le mouvement et se sont inscrites sur tabac-info-service.fr pour participer à l'opération… Un nombre qui continue de croître de jour en jour.

titre: Journée mondiale sans tabac - 31 mai 2016
resume: A l'occasion de la Journée mondiale sans tabac, le ministère des Affaires sociales et de la Santé et Santé publique France lancent une nouvelle campagne de sensibilisation nationale du 23 mai au 30 juin 2016. Son objectif est de rappeler que fumer n'est jamais sans risque et de promouvoir de nouveau dans les médias le dispositif interactif d'aide à l'arrêt Tabac Info Service.

titre: Mois sans tabac, 2e édition : pour arrêter de fumer ensemble et en équipe
resume: Le Ministère des Solidarités et de la Santé et Santé publique France en partenariat avec l'Assurance Maladie lancent la 2e édition de #MoisSansTabac. Cette opération nationale, qui incite de manière positive les fumeurs à arrêter le tabac pendant 30 jours, se déroule durant tout le mois de novembre. Un mois sans tabac multiplie par 5 les chances d'arrêter de fumer définitivement. Le collectif est au cœur de cette 2e édition qui invite les participants à arrêter de fumer en équipe. Pour renouveler le succès de la première édition, qui a réuni 180 000 participants, de nouveaux moyens sont déployés : des équipes sur les réseaux sociaux, une Fan zone itinérante pour soutenir l'arrêt du tabac et un duo très médiatique prêt à relever le défi.

titre: Intoxications par le monoxyde de carbone. Adopter les bons gestes peut sauver des vies.
resume: À l’approche de l’hiver et de ses intempéries, le risque d’intoxication par le monoxyde de carbone (CO) augmente avec l’utilisation des appareils de chauffage non électriques, mais aussi d’appareils comme les groupes électrogènes ou pompes à eau en cas d’inondations ou de coupures d’électricité, et de tous les appareils dotés d’un moteur thermique.

titre: Zéro alcool pendant la grossesse : un principe essentiel de prévention pour protéger son bébé
resume: Santé publique France et le ministère en charge de la santé lancent jusqu’au 31 décembre une campagne pour rappeler les risques de la consommation d’alcool pendant la grossesse. En effet, aucun niveau de consommation ne peut être garanti sans risque pour le bébé (accouchement prématuré, malformations cardiaques, difficultés d’apprentissage…). Cette campagne rappelle le principe de prévention essentiel : zéro alcool pendant la grossesse.

titre: 20 ans de gestion de l'hépatite C chez les usagers de drogues en France
resume: L’hépatite C, qui affecte près de 50 millions de personnes dans le monde, est une maladie pouvant être mortelle. Les personnes consommatrices de substances par injection représentent jusqu’à 70 % des cas dans le monde. En France, depuis 2004, l’Inserm, l’ANRS MIE, Santé publique France et le CHU de Tours ont mis en place l’enquête Coquelicot pour estimer la prévalence et l’incidence de l’hépatite C chez les usagers et consommateurs de drogues pris en charge dans les structures de soin et de réduction des risques. Les derniers résultats de cette enquête viennent d’être publiés dans la revue Nature Communications du mois d’octobre. Ils montrent une réduction d’au moins 50 % de la prévalence et de l’incidence de la maladie dans ces populations. Pour les autrices et auteurs, cette baisse reflèterait probablement l’effet combiné de la généralisation des antiviraux à action directe et des politiques de réduction des risques. La France se situe actuellement à un tournant et pourrait atteindre les objectifs d’élimination de l’hépatite C en 2030 définis par l’OMS.

titre: Vaccination contre la grippe chez les seniors : 9 000 hospitalisations évitées par an
resume: Chaque année, les épidémies de grippe saisonnière ont un impact considérable sur la population ainsi que sur le système de santé, pouvant être responsables de plusieurs millions de consultations en médecine de ville et plusieurs dizaines de milliers d’hospitalisations. Plus vulnérables aux infections en raison de leur système immunitaire moins actif, les seniors sont particulièrement concernés. Santé publique France a ainsi estimé l’impact de la vaccination antigrippale chez les personnes de 65 ans et plus : depuis la saison hivernale 2023-2024, la vaccination contre la grippe a permis d’éviter environ 9 000 hospitalisations en moyenne par an. Ces résultats montrent que la vaccination des seniors est un moyen efficace pour réduire le nombre de formes graves de la grippe en France chaque année.

titre: Antibiotiques : baisse des prescriptions et de la consommation en 2025
resume: A l’occasion de la Semaine mondiale de sensibilisation à la résistance aux antimicrobiens (du 18 au 24 novembre) et de la Journée européenne d’Information sur les Antibiotiques (18 novembre), Santé publique France communique les dernières données de consommation et de résistance aux antibiotiques, en santé humaine. Même si elles restent à un niveau élevé, les prescriptions et la consommation d’antibiotiques en secteur de ville ont diminué en 2025 par rapport à 2024, ainsi que sur la période 2015-2025. Compte tenu du risque persistant de développement de bactéries résistantes aux traitements antibiotiques, il reste important de poursuivre la sensibilisation des professionnels de santé prescripteurs et des patients au bon usage des antibiotiques.
